_childDocuments_.review: As I'm writing this review, I have only done 1 out of 3 endings, which excludes the other alternate ending and the true ending because I'm burnt out from the game and can't get myself to keep playing. I would really give this game a mixed review because it feels very "mid". Putting a good review feels too nice and putting a bad review feels too harsh. It's not great but it's not bad either, but just OK. I have also watched (and really enjoyed) the Fate/Stay Night anime, so I am familiar with how the series works.The Bad:This combat gets stale and boring quick, especially if you've played other action RPGs, it feels very flat after a while. The different sword stances that you unlock doesn't really help either as the differences feel minimal against enemy types. The servant/master combat switch is fun at first but doesn't really matter when most special bosses/enemies are just HP sponges by mid-game to end-game. And the DPS difference between Iori and Saber is still there during end-game. Saber still hits like a truck while it feels like Iori tickles bosses. Toning down the difficulty to easiest doesn't help either, they're still HP sponges. Having to fight for like 5 minutes before I can switch to Saber is really lame, and the switch only lasts for like 20 seconds.The pacing of the story feels slow and the plot seems to just repeat itself over and over. Like Iori is helping Musashi for like the... 5th time to X enemy? How original... The early to mid game moves so slowly. It's just Iori and Saber going to small missions over and over until a major one comes up, and it ends quick and nothing interesting happens. The soundtrack is forgettable, the places you visit feel stale because the atmosphere barely changes, and the repeated boss fights against Rogue Servants are very irritating. No, I do not want to fight Rogue Berserker again, go away. And Rogue Archer is just an annoying fight.Don't get me started on leylines. Genuinely the worst puzzle I've ever came across in a game. It's boring and slow and just wastes your time in getting to the next place. And the game punishes you if you don't complete it in a number of turns. You expect me to beat it when it's so damn boring? No, I'm not going to pay attention to the map board.The Good:The character's sprites moving as they talk are cute. The relationship between Iori and Saber are cute. You can pet cats and dogs around the map. There's Jalter in the game and you can (eventually) play her a bit.)Conclusion:Repetitive combat, stale environments, and slow pacing drags the game down. Mechanics like leylines and HP-sponge bosses are frustrating. Character interactions are cute and the relationship between Iori and Saber is adorable but the gameplay feels very meh. You should only get this game if you are already a fan of Fate. I would really not start the series at this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fate/Samurai Remnant is a great Game. The Visuals and Soundtrack are phenomenal. The Plot is great and doesn't need any prior knowledge of the Fate Franchise. The characters might feel like a retreading of the characters in Fate Stay/Night but quickly throw away that notion past the prologue. The game encourages a 2nd playthrough as new missions and extra details that give more context to the events in your first playthrough. The gameplay's really fun. The gameplay is split into 2 main portions, Combat and Leyline capture. For the combat portion, you play as Iori Miyamoto, a ronin with access to several stances based on The way of the Two Swords. These stances allow quite a number of moves to fight with alongside some magic spells taught by his teacher. But if that's not enough, You can call upon your Servants, Heroes of the Past and Legends. You can summon them to perform special moves and if your gauge is full, You can take control of them for a set amount of time, often more than enough to defeat most bosses. While you are provided one for the duration of the game, you will meet other Servants who you can assist to get them to aid you in fights. Only issue I had is some enemies, namely the special monsters have a Shell gauge that needs to be depleted before Iori can deal proper damage, otherwise it's rather miniscule. The idea is to use your servants to shred through this or use spells but early on, this might take a while to fill up the gauge and spells are rather costly. This mechanic, while understandable to show the contrast in power between a regular human and a hero of yore, does feel like a rough gimmick. Though it does become less of an issue by the midgame.Moving on to the leyline capture gameplay, this segment comprises of Iori and his servant attempting to capture neutral zones while fighting enemies to protect the controlled zones. Iori can split with his servant and summon others to help with this fact. While it does start off easy, it does get tedious to do upon further playthroughs due to being unable to split Iori and his servant immediately. Otherwise, its a fun gameplay element that helps getting extra loot for upgrades or to sell. Overall, Fate/Samurai Remnant is a great game. Would recommend if you're into  Hack and Slashes or you're looking to get into the Fate Franchise.

Sure has some stuff to improve, but it's good we did get a quality game for this saga after so many years of gacha and cheap stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been in an on and off relationship with Type Moon works for quite a while now, however, I feel like that is no longer the case in last few years as I generally grew more appreciative of nasu and his writing quirks and the overall narrative of the verse. This game didn't really change my opinion of Type Moon and the overall verse as much as it only furthers my own appreciation of it. This game really does act as a definite Type Moon work, not because it is the best, but rather because it excels at creating the parallels that fans can notice and love, while serving as a nice starting off point for newcomers. Iori and Saber are an excellent example of this as their relationship is very clearly reminiscent of Shirou and Saber's in the original Fate/Stay Night. I perhaps shouldn't go too much into detail in a review but I should at least mention how they essentially have similar backstories, however, this is probably the more important part in the narrative, have wildly divergent aspirations and goals. This is great as it blends the comfortable and the uncomfortable in a seamless way without sounding stale and I absolutely love their dynamic in game. Even if one isn't aware of this as a newcomer, I feel their struggles, dynamic, and overall character is appealing enough to compel one to continue playing the game even after reaching the first ending as each route is different and new game plus offers more insight on the characters as well as a new ending. It is very difficult to separate this game from the mobile game, Fate Grand Order, as it simply would not have been made without it. At the very least, it would be remarkably different in terms of the characters as the developers made it very clear that they wanted FGO fans to connect with these characters as there is not only a lot of overlap with the characters we grew to love in both stories (Such as most of the rogue servants and Lancer), but even the new servants have some connection to the servants we know in FGO. Some of the connections are a lot less direct than others but everyone fundamentally can trace their origins back to a servant in FGO. What does this means to people who don't play FGO or worse, hate FGO? Nothing really, because while sure there are references and I personally feel you won't have solid basis for liking these characters (especially the Rogue Servants who are mostly there for fan service), I don't think not being a huge FGO enjoyer detracts from the overall quality of the game and the heroism of the servants. You will find reasons to like them and I think the digressions do a lot to even improve my own impression of characters I knew beforehand such as Rogue Caster for example, so they will certainly get someone to like them even if one is uninitiated in the gatcha.I really enjoyed this game a lot however, I feel like there is content missing in the game to get a completely satisfactory ending for the characters as while I love Entreat the Darkness as an ending, it does feel like there is another ending out there that deals with Iori's inner demons while also resolving it in a more healthy manner... this is also combined with the general lack of story relevance for Kaya despite clearly being a very important character in the grand scheme of things leads me to believe there will be a DLC ending that is her exclusive route which I am looking forward to.

But once you fill the substitution gauge you can play as up to 2 servants for a short  period of time. Servants can break enemies armor gauge more quickly and still dish out more dmg. You can mow down enemies more quickly than Iori but that's only for a short period which is what makes it balanced.But don't worry there's whole side quests where you get to play as almost all the servants ( so far I've played as all of them except 3) with each their own unique move sets alone. Even enemy servants. There's multiple opportunities to play as just servants themselves during spirit fronts If you're a fate fan this is a must buy. You'll see a lot of familiar faces and enjoy participating in a holy grail war. If you're not a fate fan but fan of samurais I recommend trying it out . You get to play as son of Miyamoto Musashi, Miyamoto Iori mastering Musashi's dual katana style. The dual different variations of dual katana styles really fun to play as especially the fire style where you do more dmg and hit faster the lower your health is.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, the game is nothing too crazy in terms of combat and questing.It can also be argued that some characters are underdeveloped in the grand scale of this  Waxing Moon Ritual, considering how many there are.But Fate/Samurai Remnant delivers an authentic Fate story with very enjoyable character and story arcs, delving deeply into the wishes of each Master and Servant, reminiscing their past or looking towards the future.The main story quests and character side quests (which the game calls 'Digressions') will have you play from the point of view of the other Master/Servant pairings, so you can get a glimpse at how their relationships are like and get the full picture of the events that unfold.A good amount of this content is locked behind the New Game Plus (NG+) mode, which unlocks right after beating the game once. But it is well implemented, allowing to skip through unchanged parts of the story and highlighting new dialogues.In particular, playing through this mode is necessary to witness all the endings the game currently has to offer.You will also find the combat very engaging from the start, because it constantly renews itself thanks to a plethora of different fighting styles and techniques to unlock, that each have their own unique animations and effects.Fate enjoyers and newcomers alike will surely enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Going in knowing nothing about Fate, this was a fantastic game that is now one of my all-time favorites. Incredible in all aspects, well worth the price, and I highly recommend it to everyone. I’ll rate  a - : Definitely the highlight of the game. An incredible story about the Waxing Moon ritual, bringing together people from across Edo and even some from other countries. I honestly can’t stress enough how much of a great story this game has, there were several points throughout where I just didn’t want to stop playing to see what would happen next. All the plot points tie together well, you get completely blindsided at times, and each of the endings has their own lead-ups and executions which are all incredible and have their own conclusions.- : Combat is pretty fleshed out, despite being built on only a few fundamental mechanics. You’ve got your sword stances, which each have their own playstyle as well as pros and cons, You’ve got the Magecraft spells which allow for healing, buffs, and even powerful attacks, and lastly there’s the Servants and the systems tied to them, affinity techniques (special attacks), link strikes with Saber (event attacks), and even temporarily switching to them to use their attacks or Noble Phantasm (ultimate ability). There’s a bit more you can do such as “Riposte” on perfect dodges, but it’s mostly minor. Overall it feels smooth in all aspects.- : Despite the game being segmented open-world, it’s quite nice as there’s not much to collect in each area. Despite all locations in the game being in Edo, each location manages to have its own theme among them all, so it’s not just copy-pasted towns everywhere. If I had to complain about something it’s the fact that sometimes certain areas will be blocked due to story reasons and aren’t unblocked until much later in the story or sometimes even NG+ entirely. - : Looks great in all aspects. The artwork present in the character dialogue bubbles and CGs. All characters have really beautiful, intricate designs (mostly) that really help them stand out from the crowd. The special effects in combat are great, and the cutscenes look beautiful. Impressive for the game only being about 20gb (25 with DLC).- : You’ve got your standard difficulty options (although renamed): Easy, Medium, and Hard, and then you unlock the ‘Ultra Hard’ upon starting NG+. Can be changed at any time throughout the game, so you’re free to play however you want. (Update: iirc, there’s also been one more difficulty added to both the bottom and top ends of the difficulty options, so more there)- : In my opinion, the $60 for the game is very much worth it for something of this quality, duration, and experience, but I know that it’s a pretty high price to pay for some people, so if you’re debating on getting it based on the price, if it’s not on sale on Steam you could always check .- : Quite decent, I recommend getting it. Not only are the DLC servants quite good and useful to have while playing through the game, the stories themselves are decently interesting. It’s honestly more of the same from the base game, just with a little break from the main story of the Waxing Moon Ritual. If for some reason you want to just get individual stories instead of the season pass, I’d rate them 3 > 1 > 2.- : The DLC achievements are vastly more easy in comparison to the base game, as it’s either a few hour playthrough of a new story or (in the first DLC,) seven quick playthroughs of a tournament (it sounds like a lot, it’s not really that bad), followed by some quick battle and workshop achievements relating to the new servants or mechanics. - : Mostly a very nice and easy 100% completion, unfortunately there are quite a few missable things that you likely won’t know about or find until looking it up, not to mention purchasing every workshop upgrade will require at least an hour or two of grinding materials, and even then there’s a monster that only spawns in story encounters so if you don’t get enough from them you have to replay the game again. Getting the 100% can take anywhere between 2-4 playthroughs, which sounds like a lot, but after you gain the ability to start in Ch. 2 and fast forward and/or skip through already-read dialogue, you can cut down the time each takes. For reference, my first playthrough took about 25 hours iirc, but when I had to do a third for some last things, I ran through it all in about one 4-hour sitting. No major downsides, minor ones were covered in their category.- : Once beating the story and getting any ending, you can carry over your progress and start the game again in Chapter 2. I highly recommend doing this as not only are there NG+ exclusive digressions (side quests) that further enhance the story experience and you can go for the other endings which are all good in my opinion.- : If you’re planning to buy the game and play it like a normal person, you don’t need to interact with anything online and can just enjoy the story, but if you’re cursed to want to 100% your games, I HIGHLY recommend using these guides ( & ) to help you as it will greatly cut down the amount of time you spend not only playing the game but also just wandering around aimlessly wondering why the Logbook achievement hasn’t popped up yet.- : Play with a controller if you can, it’s better, trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished all the endings, and I have to say I really enjoyed the game. This is not an in-depth review, just some general thoughts and opinions I have on the game. I think the gameplay is fine. It has the skeleton of a musou game, but isn't really one. It's more like a mix of NieR:Automata, Nioh, and musou. I thought it would quickly get old at first, but they managed to keep it fresh by introducing different stances and skills for Iori as you progress. Story wise, it is fine. I personally think it is okay to start with this as your first Fate media, but if you feel unsure, then go watch the anime adaptations by Ufotable to get a feel  of the series before spending money on this game. Anyway, there are 3 main endings and 1 joke ending. In normal Fate fashion, you play as a master fighting in a Holy Grail War. You will need to play through the game at least twice if you want all the endings and see the full picture of the story.  I think what the story does great is Iori's characterization, his interactions with Saber, the relationship with Musashi, and his twist. Every other important characters and their endings felt underdeveloped, and ends very abruptly, or at least leaves more to be desired. Only Iori and Saber got a somewhat satisfying conclusion in what seems to be considered the "bad" end by the community, but I personally consider that the true end since it gives a perfect closure to the story after playing the other endings first. Overall though, I'd rate it 7/10. I still found it to be very enjoyable and had a great time playing this game despite some of its flaws, so I do recommend it. I'm happy we finally got a brand new Fate game after Extella Link 4-5 years ago, along with news that the Extra CCC fan-translation will be releasing around Christmas!

_childDocuments_.review: Fate/Samurai Remnant is an exhilarating addition to the Fate franchise, seamlessly blending the series’ trademark rich storytelling with a captivating historical setting. Set in Japan during the Edo period, this game offers fans a unique perspective on the familiar world of Fate, bringing forth a fresh narrative while retaining the core elements that make the franchise beloved.Engaging NarrativeThe story of Fate/Samurai Remnant follows a new protagonist, who becomes embroiled in the legendary Holy Grail War, but this time, the stakes are heightened by the clash of samurai and mythical heroes. The narrative is deeply immersive, filled with twists and turns that keep players engaged. The game does a fantastic job of intertwining historical figures and lore, presenting them in a way that feels both authentic and fantastical.The character development is another strong point. Each servant you encounter has a unique backstory and motivations, which adds depth to the interactions and the overarching plot. The dialogue is well-written, striking a balance between serious themes and lighter moments, allowing players to connect with the characters on a deeper level.Gameplay MechanicsFate/Samurai Remnant introduces a dynamic combat system that feels both fluid and responsive. The battles are fast-paced, allowing for a mix of strategy and action that keeps players on their toes. The incorporation of a "Battle System" where players can chain together combos and utilize unique abilities makes each encounter thrilling and satisfying.One of the standout features is the ability to summon and control various Servants, each with distinct fighting styles and powers. This adds layers of strategy to combat, as players must adapt their tactics depending on the Servant they choose. The skill tree system further enhances customization, allowing players to tailor their characters and combat style to fit their preferences.Exploration is another key element, with beautifully designed environments that encourage players to interact with the world around them. From bustling towns to serene landscapes, each location is rich in detail, immersing players in the Edo period. Side quests and optional missions provide additional content, ensuring that players have plenty to explore beyond the main storyline.Visuals and Sound DesignVisually, Fate/Samurai Remnant is a treat. The character designs are stunning, reflecting the distinct aesthetics of the period while incorporating the fantastical elements of the Fate series. The animation quality during battles and cutscenes is top-notch, making each action feel impactful.The sound design is equally impressive, with a soundtrack that enhances the overall atmosphere. The music complements the emotional beats of the story and ramps up the intensity during battles. Voice acting is excellent, featuring a talented cast that brings the characters to life, adding depth to their personalities and motivations.ReplayabilityFate/Samurai Remnant offers substantial replay value. With multiple routes and endings influenced by player choices, each playthrough can yield a different experience. The game encourages exploration and experimentation with different Servants and combat styles, making it worthwhile for players to return and uncover all that the story has to offer.Final ThoughtsFate/Samurai Remnant is a standout entry in the Fate franchise, successfully marrying rich storytelling with engaging gameplay. The unique setting, combined with well-developed characters and a dynamic combat system, creates an experience that feels both fresh and familiar. Whether you’re a longtime fan of the series or new to the world of Fate, this game is a captivating journey that offers both excitement and depth.In conclusion, if you’re looking for a game that combines action, strategy, and an intriguing narrative set in a beautifully realized historical world, Fate/Samurai Remnant is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: this one's pretty good. no spoilers.in terms of genre, it's something like a warriors game, with a bunch of other mechanics like active skills and character swaps and super moves. at first i felt like it was somewhat overwhelming, keeping track of so many bars and meters, but it's ultimately fine? you get used to it. spells are kinda meh overall though, since you have to craft a resource to keep using them. the enemies can kind of be health sponges, and a lot of the time you can mitigate this by getting your perfect dodges down, but this strat doesn't really work for enemies that mostly use ranged attacks.the story is about a proper holy grail war, no less than the ones in the other fate side novels, like fate/apocrypha or fate/requiem. the real highlight is the characters, and the dynamics they have. saber & iori have a great dynamic that runs parallel to shirou and saber's relationship from fate/stay night. the other masters, in particular, archer and his master, also play off each other fairly well. the villains of the story are a little... thin though. they lack the same depth that the heroes have. graphically... it's fine? no complaints. the noble phantasms are cool, and the properly animated cutscenes are a treat to see. iori and saber's animations in particular are a nice spectacle to see.audio... also fine? no stand out audio tracks, but nothing terrible. the voice acting is great. DO keep in mind that you'll have to play the game twice to get the true ending of the game. you'll also want to drop a save towards the end if you want to avoid playing it a THIRD time. i lost patience with the game during my new game+ playthrough and didn't end up doing the extra "super boss" fights that unlock exclusively in new game+, but the game isn't too hard to go through a second time if you do just ignore those fights and focus on the story ones.overall, pretty solid game. i'd recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: While I looked into the game for the promise of hack and slash antics with a little thought behind it necessary for success, a step up from the kind of mindless slaughter you can ascend to in a Musou title after putting some work in, I was also interested in the premise of the game's protagonist because I enjoy a good underdog. Keeping things relatively brief, Iori does serve as an interesting and engaging protagonist and the combat is likewise engaging enough to entertain; but things go off the rails from there as virtually everything else is stupendously bland.If one is familiar with FATE as a series and if you're playing this game at all, you almost certainly are, the plot and characters presented here are dyed in such incandescent shades of "This is a FATE property" as to plunge into the realm of self-parody, as though there's some ironclad checklist that needs to be adhered to, regardless of the setting. I can't really be interested in the story if I see everything coming several chapters off. While this is probably entirely tolerable and perhaps even a cause for enthusiasm among some (you play FGO), I found it thoroughly diluted the initially interesting premise. What's the point of changing up the time and place if all of the same characters are essentially going to be accounted for? Remember when notoriety was an element of Servant strength? Too bad, here's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ baguette in 1600s Japan.Even putting all of that aside, my entire experience with the game was made more laborious by magnitudes by the incessantly obnoxious presence of Iori's booby prize Servant, who we will call Remnant Saber to avoid spoilers; though if I'm being perfectly frank, I don't know who among FATE enjoyers would not have deduced his identity at the moment of his introduction. Remnant Saber is the worst elements of a vindictive younger sibling who both insults and constantly tries to one-up you, while simultaneously imposing upon your good nature and making demands, and a viciously jealous ex-girlfriend who is deeply invested in sabotaging all of your relationships going forward, personal or otherwise. Positively charming. What a great character dynamic. Does he have other traits? Sure he does. He's got a "Saberface", so he likes to eat of course. All of the time. Everything. Remember what I said earlier about checklists? Thinking about this absolute walnut again makes me want to give the CCIS agent obligated to read all of my communications a reason to increase my domestic threat level.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually only fully judge a game after I've completed it at least once, but my god, this game is so f@cking sh!t that I can't force myself to play it any longer.Most of the game is actually just running around town going from point A to point B to trigger the next story events and most of the side stuff are so painfully time-wasting fillers like pet the dog/cat, visit certain locations, buy food from this store from that part of the town, etc... For the combat, the game employs the standard Musou format with flashy attacks that cover the whole screen, but instead of putting the player in the middle of a massive battlefield to make the best of the combat, the game has tiny ass areas with barely anything in them, and the combat focus more on boss/mid-boss fights that have the enemies hyper-armoring through most of your attacks. This combined with the fact that the main character, Iori, has such long animation for his attacks mean that the majority of his movesets are outright useless unless you really want to have your face smacked mid-attack.Speaking of character, I bet the biggest selling point of the game to a lot of players is the appeal of playing the Servants, but guess what? You spend 95% of the game as Iori, with 3% as Saber and 1% as the Rogue Servants via spending a gauge in battle, and the rest are playable at certain points in the story in like 5 minutes, 10 top.And the story is just characters constantly info dumping stuff on you and you just have to take whatever the characters say at their face values because otherwise the plot just completely falls apart. I'd like to give egregious examples, but will settle for the least spoilery stuff: When Iori first met Berserker, he immediately knows that Berserker is in fact Miyamoto Musashi with the sole reason being that he recognizes swordstyle. The first thing that came to his mind wasn't "Oh, this person must have studied under the same dojo as my teacher/father" or "Oh, my teacher/father must have had another pupil that I didn't know about" but "Oh, my very very old teacher/father who passed away years ago is this big-titted silver haired woman". _childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of the fate franchise, and while not a huge player of kingdom warriors style games I have played a couple including the Fate/Exstella series. This game is a massive step up from those games both by trimming the fat that was present in the very repetitive style of map and fort based combat and instead make combat isolated arenas of small enemies and one central boss enemy. The closest you get to the map based tactical system is the leylines which themselves are not a fight but more of a strategic pathing kind of thing. Combat actually feels ironically more akin to an actual duel as most large enemies don't go down easy at most levels and you have to actually be careful with your attack timing, dodging, and parrying.That being said, what they trimmed in combat they added in other pointless mini-games and mechanics that even 15 hours in are still cropping up at random. Did we NEED fight mediating, statue carving, and sword maintenance? Not really and they just seem to be there just to give you stuff to do with no real end or point or notable benefit. Maintenance at least gives you an exp multiplier but the other two mini games don't really give you anything of note.The game is good and has clearly put some effort into making the experience more diverse and fun, but sometimes it just feels tedious to have so many elements that exist for clearly no reason at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I may like this series and there are some good elements, but honestly, my experience with Fate/Samurai Remnant was just painful.I will start with the good. For one, the core combat mechanics are actually pretty good, great even. You get a handful of stances to swap between and are actually encouraged to do so depending on your HP level, how many enemies you are fighting, and what stats you want to prioritize. It adds a good bit of depth to the otherwise mashfest that is Musou-style gameplay. There is still a bit of mashing, but I liked the extra layers added here.It is just unfortunate that this combat is stuck with some incredibly repetitive and tedious mission design. The game literally opens with you helping a guy collect debts from random people around town. That’s how bad it is.When you are not running random errands as main story quests, you are dealing with this absolutely tedious turn-based board game style travel system. You have to travel between nodes to get to your destination and if you run into an enemy along the way, jump into a copy-paste arena to fight them in.And the enemies are copy-paste too. You will be fighting the same type of samurai and a handful of monsters the entire game. You occasionally get some new, interesting ones, but it just becomes tiring spamming buttons against the same enemies battle after battle. Especially so given how this game manages its difficulty level: by simply raising enemy HP. Bosses especially, since they get an extra armor meter that just takes forever to break before you actually do damage. It’s not like the bosses are even hard, just boring and time-consuming.The gameplay is only about half of the experience, maybe just 30-40% of it. The rest is visual novel style storytelling, which I honestly don’t mind as a VN fan, but not so when it is as wordy and full of fluff like it is here. For every actual cutscene, you get a full 30 minute dinner dialogue scene. One cool character reveal, and then an info dump where a character explains a simple concept to death as if I was five years old.It’s just frustrating. Boring and frustrating. I know the Fate franchise is full of lengthy stories, but I don’t recall ever being as bored with them as I was here. The pacing is just far too slow.I had no issues playing at 4k 120fps, although it was a bit weird that the game is divided into performance and quality modes on PC, the latter of which listed a 60fps limit. The game still looked fine in performance mode - at least, for this developer’s standard - so I can’t say I minded all that much. There are a bunch of video settings to change too, so props to the devs for that instead of just leaving it as one slider as they have definitely done in the past.I cannot recommend Fate/Samurai Remnant. There are obviously some good ideas here, especially with the combat mechanics, but the gameplay loop, the mission design, and the story full of filler really sour the experience. The Fate/Extella games may have their issues, but they are at least better than this.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this one's a treat for me.Preface: I'm a Fate fan, even if I've not been around the EXTRA side of the franchise, or the Strange Fake one. My experience with the franchise is with the Stay Night shows and movies, the Apocrypha anime, and most notably the Grand Order mobile game as well as what anime adaptations are currently available for Grand Order. So while I'm not the world's biggest Fate fan, I am familiar with the franchise. I'd been waiting for this game to come out for months, and I'm happy that it didn't disappoint. I'm also only on Chapter III, and while I'm not sure how many chapters there are, the fact that I'm 33 hours into the game and still haven't seen the end is encouraging. For reference, if this game was made into an anime, that's 66 episodes already, and yet the show isn't over yet.The game is pretty story-heavy - it's best to get that out the gate early. You will be reading and listening and watching. A lot. This isn't something that's new to franchise veterans, especially ones who read the Stay Night visual novels, but for newcomers, this can be a dealbreaker, so just be aware. I estimate the game is 50/50 between cutscenes slash dialogue and gameplay. The good news about this is that from what I've played so far at the time of this review, the story is shaping up to be a good story for a Fate entry. I don't think it beats out some of Grand Order's story chapters, but the story so far hasn't gotten close to annoying me enough to take even one break from playing the game.The characters are a large part of what carry the game. In this one, you're playing as Miyamoto Iori, disciple of the famed Miyamoto Musashi, as he comes to terms with his role in what is effectively a battle royale between him and six other Masters, each Master in command of a Heroic Spirit - an incarnation of a hero from human history. While he's rather flat as protagonists go in the prologue and the first two chapters, he gets a bit more fleshed out past the second chapter. His Servant, Saber is cold and slightly condescending toward him at first, but as the two of them share travels and fight together numerous times, he/she learns to respect and even like Iori. Yes, Saber is ambiguous as to whether or not he/she is male or female, at least from what I can tell. The two's relationship is the highlight among character relationships, in my opinion, though there are plenty of other characters with backstories and their own relationships with Iori.There are also side stories called Digressions, which deal mostly with exploring side characters and other Servants, for that extra bit of Fate lore. I highly recommend doing these as soon as they become available throughout the story, as proceeding with the main storyline too much will lock you out of these entertaining bits of side story that give insight to the world and the characters involved in the main story. For franchise veterans, many of the side characters will be familiar fan favourites, but there are a few that to my knowledge, haven't been in any Fate literature, game, show, or movie before.On to gameplay, I'm not sure what to call it. I've heard people call it a musou(?) game, but basically it's a bit of a hack and slash, with abilities tied to each of the controller face buttons. There is a dodge feature that, with a skill upgrade, can be timed just right to slow down time and counter at the attacker with a riposte for increased damage and stun time. There is a sort of heavy finisher attack for Iori called Valor Strike, which deals a ton of damage and stuns affected enemies as well. Iori also has a total of four stances, something that vaguely reminds me of a similar mechanic in a game called Nioh. Iori has two stances unlocked from the start, one for defensive play that can employ blocking, or counters if you time the release of the block correctly. The other is a more crowd control-oriented style that deals less overall damage than the first stance, but excels in knocking weaker enemies around and giving Iori a lot more breathing room in a fight. His Servant, Saber, fights alongside him most of the time, and can be commanded to perform certain actions to turn the tide of battle in Iori's favour, as well as work in direct tandem with Iori to launch debilitating attacks against enemies. Later on, one other Servant can be chosen in addition to Saber to assist in fights, and so far, I've unlocked four.There is also some light customization involved in the game. For example, the twin swords that Iori uses can be customized in terms of scabbard, handle, and guard. These options are unlocked via drops from completing fights, or can be purchased from general stores in the towns scattered throughout the region. There is also a base of sorts where you can craft items to help in your journey, maintain your swords (QTE minigame where success leads to experience gain buffs for a number of fights), carve statues that can sold for currency, or read up on tutorials and the lore.In terms of level design, there's nothing super fancy. You'll nearly always be at some town and travel to and from each one is done by going into the overworld and practically fast traveling where you want or need to go. It's not open world where you'd need to get on a horse to get anywhere with any modicum of speed, but really, that's not a bad thing. It keeps the focus of the game on the story, which is what people come to Fate for. I will say that the locales are adequately designed and really give off that 1600s Japan aesthetic very well. NPCs are dressed the part and the buildings really evoke a feeling of an era in the distant past.Graphics are... well, I'll admit that they could do with a bit more work. And the art style is serviceable at worst and good at best, but I wish the developers made the art style look more specifically Fate-like, rather than "just generally Koei Tecmo-ish". I recognize the art style Samurai Remnant uses in a couple other titles Koei Tecmo released in recent years. These two criteria are easily my heaviest criticism of the game, and when these are the harshest I can criticise the game for, that's saying something about the fun I've had and continue to have with the game.The soundtrack is a banger, which you'd come to expect before even booting up the game if you've been around anything Fate a good while. As a player of the Grand Order mobile game, I instantly recognized familiar and slightly remixed versions of classic tracks in Samurai Remnant that were in Grand Order, such as the Shimousa theme from the Epic of Remnant Pseudo-Singularities, and Miyamoto Musashi's own Slash the Void/Beyond Zero theme music. Speaking of sound, the voice acting is pretty good. There is no English voice acting, but I have zero issues with any of the JP voice actors so far. Subtitles are there, naturally, to ensure you understand what's being said.That should be about all I can stand to say about Fate/Samurai Remnant at this moment. Like I said, I've yet to finish the story, and the game is such a treat that I can scarcely write any more on this review because I want to get back into the game and experience more of it. The fanservice, the references, the easter eggs, the laughs and the stakes... Words alone cannot adequately express how much this game and everything that comes together to comprise it make me smile.Truly, this is one of my favourite games of this year, and a must-play for any fan of the Fate franchise, and for newcomers, it's not a bad place to start going down the Fate rabbit hole.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll recommend it because it does hold the attention, but after the first ending I was just playing to justify my purchase. The story ranges from mediocre to weak; not something I expected with Nasu's involvement, although to be fair he wasn't a direct writer. The actual combat is fun, but later on in the game enemies become incredible tanks that take a lot of punishment yet, due to their agonisingly slow movement, you can dodge all their attacks with ease and there's little challenge to be had. Plus, when you unlock void stance, you won't be doing any more stance dancing - there's little reason to use any other stance but void.The environments range from dull and brown to breathtakingly gorgeous, but the maps are little more than a selection of corridors bridging obvious arenas where enemies spawn.It's not BAD, mind, just... average. The combat system has a massive amount of potential that more polish and alterations to the scaling could have brought out; I'd have preferred shorter, faster and more dangerous fights, and more focus on stance-dancing.Also, the third ending unlocked in NG+ is atrocious and needs a complete revision.Also, since when can a human fight toe-to-toe with a servant without another servant bolstering them in some way?

_childDocuments_.review: When you're one as deep delved into the Fate franchise as me, this can only be described a love letter to nearly all of the games and stories that came before it. With what I can only call the arguably best Fate gameplay and visuals I have ever seen from this franchise as a game. There's just too much to like as a well versed Fate fan. You like Fate Stay Night? This game's story plays out a lot like it. You like the Extraverse?(My favorite Fateverse personally) we got a certain little fox who uses her predecessor's theme from Extella when she gets introduced, albeit differently mixed since the setting of the game is different, You like FGO? Guess what, we have Musashi-Chan in all her happy go lucky glory. They have somehow found what I can call the perfect way to give us old favorites back in these stories, as well as introduce us to new servants like Saber and Archer. I am not currently done with the story as of yet since I'm trying to 100% in my first playthrough, but I have no complaints about what the story is doing or how it has evolved.To say one last thing:Get this game if you are a huge Fate fan who is well versed in a lot of the Fate franchise. You don't even need to be a big Fate fan to enjoy the hell out of the game! Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to say about this game.For people out there (like me) who bought the game for Jeanne forget it you won't get to play her everytime and just for that the game is ass.Now for the real review (I've been playing it in the hardest difficulty available at the beginning)Omega Force are well known for their Musou games, they've been doing it for a while.For the past few years they've been doing games for other studios or licences like Hyrule Warriors, One Piece Pirate Warriors (The second one being the best one btw) and having some succes because they managed to implement the fun aspect of musou within those licences.Now for this game, they did some good ♥♥♥♥ and when I say good it's not in the right way.You have the gameplay element of a musou which is made to face hords of ennemies with stronger ones but nothing that forces you to rely on dodging etc...In this game you have this specific gameplay but it is more focused on defeating small troups with one boss that has an armor and you can't attack him unless you wait for his patterns to be done.So you have to play arround the dodge system that is completly ass and a stance where you can counter ennemies to deplete their armor thus making them vulnerable to normal attacks without having the need to wait for their patterns.On paper it looks fine but in reality it's horrible to play, the patterns of ennemies are so poorly made so dodging them is almost random, it's like they wanted to go for a Nioh formula (Stance, dodge, parry) without the gameplay elements that made these games fun to play. While the gameplay doesn't help the level design is also really bad, it's just a bunch of hallways with some random square zones where you can have fights with random monsters/ronins and that's it, the exploration is pretty weak and you will spend most of your time petting cat and dogs because that's the only thing they made up for covering they emptiness that this game has to offer.You're force to play as Iori the MC for mostly all the game because playing a servant requires to fill up a gauge and use it to have the privilege of 15 seconds epic musou gameplay that allows you to stagger ennemies with normal attacks (something Iori can't do) and then going back to Iori where you have to bear with his two non fun to play stances for the first 10 hours before unlocking other stances that "helps".Speaking of which they give some BS stances (Void/Fire) that makes servants look like they're coming from a Cosplay Convention.The story doesn't have much appeal to it either I won't spoil it but it is poorly written while having some interesting characters that felt rushed, it doesn't have any meaning and while it's fine to have multiple endings, some of them felt like the trip wasn't worth it but it's subjective and I won't go further into it.To end this review on a good note, the animations are really amazing and the art style was really good, the artists did a good job for the artworks and they created some nice pieces.TL DR : The gameplay is bad because they didn't know what game they wanted to make (souls like one or musou), you won't play all the time as the servant you want like Extella Link, some characters are good but story is meh it feels like they were wasted.If you're coming from FGO (This game was made for FGO fans), you might enjoy it if you put aside having fun while playing it and only reading some dialogues, if you're here to feel the servant Experience you might wanna play Fate Extella Link.

_childDocuments_.review: Buyer beware - while this may seem like a Fate musou game, it is... very much not one. It's closer to an action-RPG with light musou elements, while borrowing some pretty bad mechanics from the souls franchise in ways that detract from the experience.Of note, do keep in mind that while the advertising of this game largely features gameplay from a lot of the different servants, the reality is that for the most part, you will be playing as Iori instead. While his kit is more or less fine, it is *not* a suitable musou kit - a lot of his attacks suffer from low damage and pretty hefty endlag. This means that you'll be constantly fighting with the controls to get any damage done to even the most basic of mooks.By contrast, the Servants are where all the effort lies although it is... a rather puzzling type. The most fleshed out one is easily Saber who more or less controls like how you expect a musou character to control - they have big sweeping attacks and specials that deal strong damage - the problem is that the game treats him like an Install; you have to spend several minutes playing with Iori before you can play with Saber and it only lasts for a few seconds. The most fun I've had playing this game is with Saber.The other servants literally have single fights that last for maybe 5 minutes at most. Where this gets puzzling is that every servant has a full blown x/y button kit and specials yet they only get used for a single fight. It makes absolutely no sense. All the stuff you've seen in the ads of controlling servants? Yeah that's often just their one single fight you get to see.Maybe I just don't get it, but this was a cold shower if you're expecting a Fate musou game. Even if you were expecting a Fate action game, this feels like it misses the target audience by a mile and then some. Masters are the emotional core of Fate, but in terms of gameplay... Servants easily ought to take priority because Masters tend to just be regular guys with minor magic spells. Servants get to do crazy ♥♥♥♥.The game isn't entirely bad if you know what you're getting into but given who made this and how it was advertised, I just cannot recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fate/Samurai Remnant

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get the point of a fate game like that (especially a muso) where you play as a human.It feels like you spend so much of the game fighting ennemies designed (in lore and in gameplay) to be fought by servants but you are stuck as a master who somehow manages to fights 20 ennemies at once and servants by himself, your servant will, most of the time, just stay there not doing much and you will only really feel powerful and have fun when you can control them for 15 seconds during a fight.It just feels wrong to attack human beings who can withstand all your blows and cancel you any time they decide to attack.It kinda seemed to me like the game was trying to be a muso in which you attack hordes of ennemies and some sort of souls game (idk) where you need to just not do anything and focus on counterattacking an ennemy that takes way too long to die.I honestly think I missed something in the gameplay that made my experience more miserable than it should have been (I played the normal difficulty sword fighter and didn't really have much trouble, it was fine)This may also be more personal but the main character always felt so lifeless, it seems like he is never bothered by anything that happens around him but I haven't played through the whole game so it may get better later on (we need to be careful to not hurt people around but let's kill hundreds of people that are in our way ???).I'd rather replay the other fate/extella games. Fighting was kinda stupid and had problems but it was more fun to me.Kinda have to give them props for making the game playable on mouse+keyboard, only problem was the game not showing the binds you want (it show the keyboard binds for attacking like I & J instead of mouse buttons but it's fine).Also who's idea was it to have secondary quests where you need to pet a bunch of cats and dogs during free roam in an interaction with them that lasts like 20 seconds everytime and heals you barely 15hp (at least you can ignore that)

_childDocuments_.review: The Fate franchise continues to be a parody of itself. Once again, our beloved FGO writers have decided that fighting is more important than having interesting characters. There's absolutely no emotion. Maybe it's stuck behind the NG+, but I'm not replaying a game that pissed me off during its first run. As far as combat is concerned, the base is very good, but totally undermined by its shield system. Enemies are bags of HP, and battles drag on and on, despite near-perfect dodging. I have absolutely no problem paying 70€ for a 10h straight experience. But the game refuses to accept this and prefers to slow down its pace. Too bad, but let's hope studio BB can save Fate's videogame future.

_childDocuments_.review: A very shallow musou game where your character Iori hits like a limp noodle. “He’s a master though and servants are stronger anyway”, I thought to myself. But 98% of your fights will be as him, not even your main servant will you get to control much due to the time it takes for affinity bar to come back.Speaking of playable servants, Musashi the character that was advertised as playable and even had DLC outfits is only playable for 5 minutes. I don’t get the point of doing such a thing unless there were nefarious reasons into tricking the player that the game is something that it isn’t. Gameplay is dialogue>run to marker>fight repeat with sometimes a fetch quest or leyline mini game added in the mix. Story is decent at best, but compared to the VNs is just a basic story.Not worth $60, and the game having day 1 season passes/DLC should’ve been a warning too. Game also doesn’t feel the best optimized with how the fps flickers and CPU fan revs up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an absolutely critical flaw in it, where cutscenes are skipped over. Supposedly you can fix it, but none of those fixes worked for me. I had to go watch the cutscenes later on youtube.This game would only be worth suffering through if the gameplay were good, but it is not. The boss battles are so dreadfully tedious that I do not recommend this game. Each boss and miniboss has this extra HP called a shell. It's basically an HP bar on top of their normal one. When you break the shell, then you deal lots of damage to their real HP bar. But even if you stack buff spells and anti-shell spells, the shell takes so, so long to degrade that probably 1/4 of my playtime is just mashing attack buttons on boss monsters.  I'm not kidding. It takes so long to chew through them. There's no depth to the gameplay. It's just wailing on a shell enemy and dodging their very telegraphed attacks over and over.It all works well in a technical sense. I only had one freeze (right after a tough optional boss, resetting my progress. That was annoying) and one time where I accidentally deleted an item I invested materials into (it wasn't obvious that it was no longer equipped), but otherwise, the mechanics and buttons work well. There's good Quality of Life and the game is pleasant to look at. But that just means it's worth watching Game: The Movie - it's not worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game that's marred by repetitive combat and a lackluster story. I came into this with an interest in Edo-era Japan and no real exposure to the Fate franchise or to anime games in general, so maybe that gives me a more critical lens than others.Beat it in 27 hours doing all side quests, which felt a bit short for a $60 RPG. I won't spoil the ending, but the game just kind of...ends without any closure between its two main characters. Huge letdown because the character building and development was pretty good.I also played on "hard" and only needed to load a save after losing a fight twice. Final boss went down easily on my first try. Never felt challenged at all.5.5/10. Worth picking up for 25 or 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of missable things with no proper automatic save system. They should have made the save system from Langrisser 1+2.Game and DLC are completely overpriced. Upgrades require a lot of grinding the same maps over and over, lots of mobs are not farmeable and item drops are really scarce even with 200 bonus drops.The soundtrack is complete forgettable garbage. The story is super shallow and contrived and includes a few arbitrary deaths that make no sense, the few story paths change very little but require tons of hours of investment from the playerThe game can freeze sometimes when loading the game, due to issues with steamYou are forced to finish the game twice to see most of the contentThe gameplay loop is very basic, you can spam X for most of the game, and spam phantasms the moment you get them. Casting magic is super limited and barebones, magic only gets good near the end of the game after you max affinity with certain servantsThe good:Graphics are quite decent and the game runs normally very wellVoice actors in English are quite good which is rare in videogamesThe game has its fun moments, it's not a total waste of time and if they could put the whole content into a single gameplay like the YS game this game would have been much betterGet is on a sale if you're a fan of the Fate anime and Dynasty warriors gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not too far into the game but I think it's a tenative recommendation. Before going into this game understand YOU PLAY THIS GAME AS A SINGLE DUDE AND THE SERVANT SECTION IS A POWER UP MID FIGHT.I've seen lot's of upset people you can't swap between numerous servants on the fly for this game's combat and I don't want to mislead people. You play as a single voiced protagonist with a single servant, and later on I imagine you unlock the ability to fight with other servants. Mid fight after raising a special gauge you switch to controlling your servant for a time before swapping back. This is pretty much Fate Warriors but with a lot more stuff to do outside of beating people up. If you like warriors, yay. If you don't like warriors... well you may hate this game or be meh about it.Story I'm barely into it so far but if you've watched one Fate property, you've seen them all. This series quite literally has one plot it constantly reuses but with new masters and servants, and this game is no different. Don't go in expecting an amazingly unique experience unless you have never seen Fate in your life, in which case you can go into this game perfectly fine and will probably find it interesting.As of how far I am in the game, this is like a 7/10 as someone who likes Fate, and as someone who is FINE with warriors gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: While I managed to complete the game and I am a Fate/ fan, I have some big gripes with this title.However, I will go through my points in order first:- Responsive gameplay, the main character handles well and the strikes have impact and flair- Great music, as expected from a title of this franchise- Good character design and art- Fully voiced dialogues, in japanese dub only- Less focus on the Musou fighting styleThe fights can be quite fun, especially as you unlock more ways to fight.However, that's sadly where the good points end for me:- Dragged out fights through super armored enemies- Gameplay gets repetitive fast, even while fights tend to be fun- The graphics aren't up to par compared to other anime-centric games- The story feels like it's been stretched too thin almost all the timeand takes way too long until it starts to get interesting.- Loose threads and at times some disconnect between plotpoints- Predictable story and outcomes- Some minigames have little to no merit or don't come up more than a few times- Too many servants/characters don't get enough spotlightSuper armor in boss/mini boss fights is the worst thing. It always feels like you first have to chip away at them long enough without any effect until you actually do damage. Not only that, but at times this super armor refreshes multiple times within the same fight. It feels like a drag. Adding to that is the fact of the lack of enemy variety, especially in terms of bossfights. After fighting the same servant 3 times, I don't really feel like bothering anymore.I sadly can't recommend Fate/Samurai, because for every one thing this game does right, it does two or three things wrong. It does not stand out in any particular way, the story isn't very emotional or engaging. My biggest gripe was how otherwise climactic bossfights are dragged out by boring super armor which also refreshes multiple times in a fight. There has to be better ways to design a bossfight.I did like the fighting system in general, just mechanics like those suck the fun right out of it. Adding the sheer repetitions and lack of variety into it, you sadly get a game that gets boring fast.And the story doesn't pick up until the last two chapters it feels like, which adds to the drag.I had hoped for more. Fate fans might as well skip this one, you won't miss much.

_childDocuments_.review: Fate is my favorite franchise, and I really like musou games so I thought this was a match made in heaven. As of finishing the game and all it's branching paths (there are no routes, just mildly different endings), the game has a satisfying conclusion and my purchase does not feel wasted. However, the lack of free play and/or being able to play the literal reason why you got into Fate anytime is a bummer, Iori turns out to be a cool character but I sure as s*** didn't start Stay/Night because I thought Shirou Emiya was the goat of gods and I needed to see what franchise he was from. You definitely get to play with servants way more than what people exaggerated it to be but it is not far fetched. This game's first half is slow as f***, where there were times where I forgot this was a Fate game. The story is fresh and quite "intriguing" but forgettable. They ain't making an anime out of this one any time soon, as a matter of fact, the mobile game's samurai chapter where a lot of this game's inspiration comes from is WAY better. Relying on playing the game multiple times for it's routes instead of making fun combat with whatever character you wish especially with some multiplayer company was a bold but unfortunately very boring move. I won't be replaying this game as much as I would if it it's missions were repayable with any character I wanted like previous Omega games. We really went from Zelda on a bike with a Death Star laser to this. I would recommend this if you're a fan of Fate but definitely at a lower price.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I wanted something to satisfy my "samurai game" desire after playing Like a Dragon: Ishin. Ishin wasn't a great gream by any measure, but I would have to say it's considerably better than this game. Fate/Samurai Remnant feels like a hollowed out version of Ishin in both world-building, activities, battle, graphics, and personal relationships. Don't be fooled by the movie-cutscenes into thinking that the game will be beautiful. It's not. The graphics during regular gameplay are very, very, very dated. It reminds me of EARLY PS2 games......and not top quality early PS2 games at that. Not only is the world of Fate/Samurai incredibly barren of things to see and do, but also barren in overall fun. The towns are largely non-interactive and I can't recall a single interesting thing to do in any of them. Even the "side-quests" aren't really side-quests.....but simply achievements that you will be awarded without even knowing that you were on the path to be rewarded for it until you get the alerts that you completed something. An example of this is "beating 100 enemies".The battle system is like Ishin......hack-and-slash......but less deep(which is saying something) and grows very tiresome. However, what makes Fate/Samurai even worse than Ishin is how far you have to travel on a map in order to fight a battle in the hopes of leveling up. Typically, for each map, you will have 2-3 battles available to fight a battle....and those locations are often as far away from each other as possible. It's VERY draining and tedious to fight one battle and then run across the other side of town to fight that 2nd fight. And no, the opportunities to fight do NOT respawn unless you leave the town completely. After you beat 2 or 3 fights...........you don't have the option to fight anymore unless you travel to another map (if it's available at that time). Between the bland and shallow hack/slash fighting and the time it takes to get to another battle.....you would not want to fight if you didn't have to. Let that sink in. This is a samurai game that you don't want to fight if it's not necessary. The leyline grid system that you will be FORCED to partake in is a chore and ultimately makes me question the decision to include it in this type of game. It's so ill-conceived that I think that even the Junction System from Final Fantasy 8 is a better idea and better applied.There are elements that are borrowed from other games, such as "improve your base"........but it adds nothing new to the concept, nor does it feel rewarding enough to invest in. I do have to laugh at one function that is available at your "home base"....it's the polishing of your sword. By the simple timing of stopping a circle in time you can be rewarded to have 1.1 experience up to the next 8 battles. This also feels pointless compared to the earlier issue I mentioned of the sparse battles on the maps. Also, in order to partake in this "mini game", you have to have certain materials. If you don't have the materials on hand, you won't likely feel compelled to go get them. The voice acting is wonderfully done........but that's about all the good I can say about the game.  5 out of 10. Fyi, Like a Dragon: Ishin is a 7.5.

_childDocuments_.review: Good 3rd person action with great music and an interesting story set in a feudal Japan time. Combat isn't overly difficult, but at higher levels still provides a good amount of fun. Gamepad usage preferred. For Fate franchise fans it has some familiar faces, but most of them would be known from later and extended installments. Although this game can stand on its own and doesn't really require familiarity with all-things-Fate.  If anything I would even say this is a good intro to Fate universe or at the very least a rather pleasant one-time venture. Apart from action combat mechanics game also offers a mini-strategy game implemented, where characters are moved on the map of Edo and require capturing points along the way. With a number of special items and turn limits it can be a nice break from the predominant 3rd person running around. Gets tedious on second and further playthroughs though. Which leads to the point of endings. Yes, the game has several of them and the one you get on the first playthough id downright inconclusive. That's probably the only big downside I found with the game. Even though the alternative endings build up upon the first ending, they basically make it somewhat obsolete this way. Apart from that it's a solid 8/10 for me.Oh, and Deluxe isn't really worth it. Unless the publisher decides to actually provide soundtrack and artbook as separate items you can listen or read wherever you like. As it is you pay to listen to soundtrack inside the game. And scrolls through the artbook that way too. It is... a very unfriendly gesture towards the paying gamer, in my opinion. Best to buy the full soundtrack on CDs, honestly. It is kinda worth it.DLCs are separate adventures and they don't influence main story in any way.  Just some nice extended time with the characters and additional Servants to boot.

Do not worry people who have not touched any other fate related material, it explains the basics of the grail- I mean, Waxing Moon ritual and the servant / master thing. And for those who have played FGO, yes, that is THE dual wielding best girl Flower at the Apex of Heaven herself (pre-Olympus) and she does make a couple references especially in one of the DLCs. Please support this game so Type-Moon makes more fate games and I have more fate related content besides a new chapter in FGO every 9 months. But also its a hidden gem that deserves more attention (:

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the fate franchise this story takes a lot of aspects from stay night and rehashes them with a couple of big differences. You play as Iori a guy who wants to improve their sword skills, the only person who your actually close with is your self proclaimed grandpa who resides inside a magic tomb. Kaya is your sister who you seem to have been close to in the past but don't really interact with much in the story. What's true is chosen by the player, however you make the dumbest choice imaginable to try and make your wish come true instead of being smart in any fashion.  The story falls apart at the finish line, but it has some good moments and strong characters. The presentation of them feels rushed at times and a lot of the best character interactions seems to have been glossed over.Combat isn't fully explained specifically special techniques granting afterglow which can be placed on the same type of element, or how mounting stances can effect that. Lancers SA is fire style which adds atk up but is the weakest. Unless your in fire stance with extremely low hp stacked with other buffs, and make no mistakes then it could be okay but functionally it's never something you want to rely on or use.Riposte is pretty scuffed, and there's no damage numbers to really intuit things. Mounting effects for certain parts are not listed anywhere. No presets for spells or katana mountings means everything is done manually which can get annoying. Dismantling 100s of parts is all done manually, and trying to get the right effect for fully powered gear isn't fun. A way to easily end the story early before the best gear drops, a hidden mountain shop and shops that help early players are removed from use.I didn't realize how good loot up on mounting upgrades were till way later and it didn't help me have a great experience early on.I had fun with the game in spite of that but the key word is in spite of all it's flaws and issues.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm already a huge fan of the fate series and other type-moon works, but this is still wonderful all on its own. This could even be a good starting point to the series as a whole, it introduces you to the concepts of the universe and magic systems wonderfully. The combat is surprisingly deep for a musou type game (you fight like a hundred people at once like nothing) and has some super difficult bosses that will catch you by surprise if you don't learn the mechanics. Speaking of, there's so many you can play however you want, maybe even go the entire game without using certain playstyles or attacks because there's just so many options.Story wise, it's Fate, and a masterpiece of storytelling is the norm, with this being no exception with incredible characters and depth given to everyone.It is a longer game than some would expect, since it has many jrpg / visual novel elements, including very long parts of the story where there is no gameplay other than cutscenes and dialogue, but not dreadful like some other popular jrpgs. This is being posted when I have beaten the game elsewhere, not on this account and I am replaying btwTLDR; musou with depth. Spectacular story and visual style. Definitely pick this up when on sale if you're interested in Fate in any way shape or form, love the idea of getting to know historical and mythological characters, or are just a weeb for historical japan.

I do not count the mobile gacha games simply cause I refuse to play any gacha games lol.  So with that being cleared up lets get to the pros and cons. Pros -- Voice Acting - Stellar Japanese voice acting from top to bottom- Combat - Very RPG and multi dimensional on the combat. You will find the style that best suits you. (Personally for me Void and Water Stance)- Story - This is the closest you will get to being in the War for the Grail. The story also really should be replayed as there are multiple endings There is a chapter selection after beating the game the first time to make this easier.- World themes - It gets the world themes for the place and time it happens in well.- Music - Best thing is that fits the game world though I will say open theme that plays is pretty catchy- Graphics - some story elements are told in a water color style  as being written in a book which are nicely done. It plays into a story element that will make sense as you play the game. Oh also the Noble Phantasms are amazingly done. - Boss battles - Fighting other Masters and Servants and some of the other big bads in the game is amazingly fun, you can even redo them with Battle RecollectionsCons -- Enemy Design - the normal monsters and men you fight will pretty much stay the same from beginning to end design wise.- Animations - Character animations with the in game engine can be a bit rough transitions in character movement arent smooth and are noticeable- World Exploration - The various areas you will visit all feel the same design wise, long corridors with bigger middle sections  and the environments are all the same design with some but very limited variety Overall if you always wanted to play a Fate game and the musou style of the other games weren't your style of games. This is the fate game to get if you want to feel like you are in a Holy Grail war. 40 our of 50 (8 out of 10 or 4 out 5 for you traditionalists)

_childDocuments_.review: As peak fate, I could go no further...Fate/Samurai Remnant was an enjoyable foray into everyone's favorite history mythstory blender, borrowing the subversive formula of Redline, and the FGO gag event that inspired it (i.e what if FSN broke the golden rule of the holy grail war as envisioned, western hero focus) expect a fair amount of flash cutting, quick sword draws, and dramatic self introductions.The protagonist this time around is Iori Musashi, who was real, and unfortunately, seemingly only a genius in mid level administration, and not being an awesome reality defying swordsman, teamed up with a not quite saberface who was generally pretty fun, and even more entertaining paired with our straight man player character. Surprisingly for a fate ip, I didn't find myself rolling my eyes every time specific servants or masters showed their face, and found most of them to be either interesting enough, or fitting in their role in the story. Most importantly the females were far too bad this time around, and would gladly be selflessly liberated. Gameplay wise the basic combat mechanics of dodge like hell, and stance systems were enjoyable, however can devolve into spam consumables and servants if you don't self impose a challenge, jealously hoard said things, or crank up the difficulty. It also becomes quite repetitive, and although the variety is decent, they usually are just permutations of the same couple types of enemies that you will have to fight rather than anything particularly groundbreaking, with servant fights feeling like a slog and making me think about how seppuku maybe really wasn't so bad after dying on the opponents last sliver. Exploring the world generally is the same collectathon you have played before, this time simply picking up glowing things off the ground, punctuated by yakuza style dialogue bubbles, or saber running off to look at something particularly interesting, despite the amount of stuff to interact with, and npcs doing things, it feels rather sterile. I personally did enjoy it, and even considered it fun, but can see how people wouldn't with how many alternatives there is out there.Story wise, it is similar to strange fake where it is basically a grail war in everything but name being ran by someone else, this time, not the definitely not CIA. Nothing too unpredictable, but enjoyable nonetheless, with a couple different endings and some new game plus elements.Graphics wise it looks nice but on lower end systems will be extremely sluggish (I upgraded my PC mid play through, and realized I really was just self flagellating), with really nice sprite work, in engine cutscenes are okay, in game cutscenes tend to be the same couple animations but that is par the course, and the intro animation is basically amazing. Sounds, voice acting, and music are all generally pretty good, in my opinion particularly the music.Its price point is high, as proud samurai don't sell their wares cheap, so if you only buy games that are absolute must plays, I would only recommend it to fate fans, but if that is a nonissue it is as decent an entryway into the setting of fate as ufotables stuff was, with a relatively self contained story dangling threads here and there that link to a wider world of multimedia merchandising.Oh, and you can pet the animals.

It's nothing all that special, but I also couldn't find anything negative about the graphics, and it runs smooth without any issues.I also especially like the designs of the characters!The only big negative I can definetily see is the price... 70€ for just the base game is pretty high.But in the end, I think it's still worth the money.All in all, it may be related to my relatively low expactations when starting to play, but I really love this game a lot. _childDocuments_.review: is a very successfully crafted game based off  franchise. I may be biased because this is the first  game that I have ever played. But I know that previous  games were not well received in terms of gameplay. , however, has no outstanding flaw in any aspect of game development, be it gameplay, character development, writing, etc. I also liked that the developers invested extra efforts to create characters related to 17th century Japan. Knowing little to nothing about Japanese mythology and history during the time, it was a pleasantly educational experience for me.I'd also like to note that the writing of the game seems more mature than other  franchise works that I know of, namely  and . Both of those stories had very different tone from that of . The overall tone of  was that of an adolescent boy wanting to find out what he has to do with his life, and the overall tone of  was that of a pilgrim in search of answers to his spiritual pursuit of truth. However, the writing of  reads like grown-up adults of distinct philosophies and beliefs competing with each other over their wishes. As such, the Masters in this game are very calm and determined in what they do. This is very different from previous stories that I know of; both  and  were stories primarily led by the Servants, not by the Masters. But in , it is the Masters who lead the story all along up until the end, while the Servants are in general more or less instruments of war, or mere advisors at best, despite that some exceptions to this trend do exist here and there.Clearly, this game is a product of significant innovation in the franchise. Not only the gameplay, but also the writing feel very new and fresh. I have to admit that It might be because I did not play , and skipped significant portion of the franchise. However, there is no question that this game is more accessible and innovative than , which is widely known to be suboptimal in the gameplay department, and also overflowing with mind-blowingly complex premises and overwhelming number of characters. Therefore, I recommend this game to anyone who is interested in the franchise. Beginners will have easier time learning the franchise, and veterans will be able to appreciate artistic advancement in both writing and gameplay.
