_childDocuments_.review: A 1980s vibe? A killer on the loose? A decades-old mystery to solve?Forrest Nash, fallen-from-grace DJ extraordinaire, is on the case!When the Gallows Creek police department is down for the count and the town's 911 dispatcher is on the road to get help, what else can you do at midnight on a Thursday but route the calls to the local 24-hour radio station? Talk to frantic residents, solve puzzles to save them from certain doom, all while unraveling the secrets of this sleepy town's past.What's fascinating about Killer Frequency is that you don't actually meet any of the Gallows Creek residents. Yet you form relationships with them, you worry about them, and you feel compelled to do your best to save them all despite even your character not having any particular buy-in on the town.And this is all thanks to the amazing cast, who quite frankly carry the game through to its success. The concept here is unique and compelling, but could have easily fallen flat with mediocre voice performances. Thankfully not so here! Every player nails it, including the breathing, the screaming, the (not necessarily inevitable) dying, with many deftly juggling multiple characters. Kudos to all the performers and their director!What's more, despite a lot of VO the game nimbly balances the dialogue with puzzles and exploration. The station is opened up to you bit by bit over time and you take those opportunities to look around, finding clues or information you might use to help residents. As you assist folks the layers of the onion are peeled back, uncovering more of Gallows Creek's shady past, and the game uses this to its advantage when it comes to urging you to save the citizens. People have information, and it would be a terrible thing for them to die at the killer's hands before sharing it with you, wouldn't it?The puzzles are clever, well laid out, and all solvable with careful thought - some more easily than others. A lot of logic is at play here and the game doesn't rush you in even the direst of moments. Need to go wander to find that bit of information to save this person? No problem, take your time. While this is partly a relief it's also a bit of a pitfall as greater tension would've come from worrying someone might die in the meantime, which generally isn't the case. Any timed portions are in dialogue  and you're given an indicator to show if you need to reply in a hurry (or, perhaps, not reply at all.)That said, your choices do matter.You will determine if people live or die.No pressure.Overall Killer Frequency is, well, killer! What starts as a simple "murderer on the loose" becomes so much more, as the threads are woven together around an event years gone by, how it happened, who was there... and why people are being stalked and killed on this night of all nights.Time to tune in to 189.16 - The Scream! It'll be a graveyard shift you won't soon forget.

Within the confines of your radio station, you'll have to do some sleuthing to solve the puzzle you're presented with, all while listening to the back-and-forth banter of the two radio cohosts. Killer Frequency has a lot of heart, and just the right amount of campiness, so if you're a fan of 80s slashers and synth-pumping music, this is one game you'll want to tune in for.

_childDocuments_.review: You should really only buy this game if you like walking simulators and mysteries or if you get it on sale. It's not much of a horror game, though. It's more of a thriller. It's a decent game, the story is interesting and I love the environments but it struggles with keeping my attention. There's quite a lot of downtime with characters talking and there's not much to keep busy during it other than throwing paper into a hoop over a trashcan. I technically have seven hours in the game but some of that is just from me leaving it open, getting bored and going to check twitter. This game would have been so much cooler had we swapped between the POVs of the victims instead.I had seen a few people play this game and it sat on my wishlist for a while. It never seemed interesting enough to prioritize, though, until it was like 13 bucks. I had seen one of the reviews call it a walking simulator so I knew kind of what I was getting into. It's not even really a walking simulator because most of the game is played from your desk, with little options to alter the story.There's also some little issues like weird pauses between voice lines or some of the audio balancing. I know the main focus is the killer and the whistling but does it have to be that loud? Don't get me wrong, I liked it, but it could have been improved quite a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: So well done! The comedy, the suspense, the voice acting all keeps you engaged throughout the whole game. The puzzles aren't very difficult, but you're just a radio show host, not a rocket scientist. :) I was able to get everyone but two on my first pass, so there is definitely some replay value for those achievement hunters too.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game, even though it's more like a walking simulator with some puzzle and slight horror element. Very impressive that it's fully voiced also. Frequently on sale for 30% off or more, so I'd wait for that to be worth the price.However I thought that the character of Peggy was insanely annoying and useless considering because of her we waste a lot of time looking for something that wasn't her's to toss in the first place. Her voice was also pretty aggravating since she sounded smug/arrogant the entire time to me. I also thought she was never much use for extra hints to be honest. I also think aside from the amazing music/funny callers and ads you play that the DJ character was not fleshed out enough because we don't find out exactly WHY he got booted from his hot shot gig in Chicago or how he ended up in the middle of nowhere. Other than that, good spending of 5 hours with me walking around and checking a lot of the objects you can randomly interact with.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Needs more music tracks and ad tracks but in all its one groovy game.At first its a bit "meh" but once the killing starts, the fun begins.For game play the controls are a little wonky but you get use to it but, other than that. I'd give it a solid 4.5 out of 5.The only down side is that there could so much more added to make the game longer and or possibly make a part two , say its 20 years later where tech is more "updated" (instead of floppy disk, every is in the era of the cd and sd card.) Maybe if say someone dies, the killer sends you there death tape and gives it that sense of "your are responsible" thing.None the less its a awesome game and when for a ten dollar price tag, this is a must have.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Great short game, about 4 hours more or less if you explore more or not.The non VR version is nice, it doesn't feel awkward and is controlled pretty good.Is a story with some "puzzles" but the best part is the voice acting of the main characters.I would say it is a thriller narrative game with decision making!But is not really a horror game! I would recommend it for a fair price!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! It’s not your regular chase, jumpscare game. This requires using your head to solve puzzles to save innocent victims. The graphics are amazing, the soundtrack is awesome, voice acting is right on. I find myself with every caller to do the best I can to save them. If you wanna see what this is about before buying, check out my YT video!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game on playstation and it took my around 5 hours.This game can be alot of fun, but you have to know what you are getting into.  It is not a walking simulator where you explore, you are mostly confined to one room listening to phone calls and making choices on how you want to answer / proceed.  It is very much like a choose your own adventure novel.  The graphics are passable but they are a bit cartoonish.  What saves the day is the Amazing Original story, that requires your patience and attention.7/10 from me!I wanted more action! ... but the story kept my interested...
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an awesome game. Prefect blend of horror and comedy, the characters were engaging, the dialog was great and well-written (which was important because since you don't really do much, just talk). Also the overall story was just really good, probably might had enjoyed it even if it was in a different type of media. Would love a sequel but just hope that Team 17 does some more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A great horror-puzzler, more the the side of solving puzzles which are a lot of fun. The game never pressures you with a time limit nor do I feel that any of them are unfair with their solutions, and it still maintains tension because you grow to care about the people who call you up and you really don't want anything bad to happen to them as you try and navigate them on the path to surviving a serial killer.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: more radio drama thriller than traditional horror, though still playing out in first person. tons of clever puzzles and wandering around a lovingly crafted early 80s radio station, talking callers through classic slasher scenarios. had a ton of fun with this one. also fully (and impressively) voice acted,
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a qualitative slasher with good music, thick atmosphere of a grim night in a small american town (local radio station KFAM's building, lit with bright neon lights, greatly contributes to it) and a typical for the genre, regular story, which is neither good nor bad. It's kind of 911 operator simulator (whose responsibilities are delegated to Forrest Nash, radio host) with a few story-related riddles to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game! I think it was the perfect amount of gameplay to remain thrilling without dragging anything out unnecessarily. Really enjoyed the voice acting and back-and-forth between Forrest and Peggy, as well as little things like being able to choose what record to play while trying your best to help the callers survive the night. A great game for a night or two if you love small town vibes and murder. It's reminiscent of Gone Home and Firewatch to me in terms of a walking simulator, with the ability to pick up objects and hunt for clues. Great buildup and ending, too!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is one of those games that i had recommended to me by a friend. I fell in love with the concept immediately and man did the developers deliver. Killer Frequency is a good time, I had friends with me while i was playing and we managed to get quite a laugh out of numerous sequences. The concept itself is phenomonal, A radio station host acts as a 911 caller as a string of murders leaves a quiet little town split open as you uncover the towns biggest kept secret. If you enjoy conspiracies, Govt Coverups, serial killer ghosts (Possibly), Late night radio vibes and PIZZA FROM PONTYS PIZZA WHERE THE DEALS ARE DOWN RIGHT ILLEGAL, Then you will very much enjoy this game. Best play it blind though. its one of those games where the less you know the more fun you will have.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a fantastic story, that I did not expect to be so intricate. Expect some plot twists, few jumpscares and just having a good time playing it. And your choices really matter! Your callers' lives depend on you.I would like to replay it in the near future to explore the other choices.I received this product for free, but was not asked to promote or review it. I genuinely like the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: If you are bored of the usual horror/survival games and want one that switches it up, this is a good game to pick up. It is a more relaxing horror game, where you are simply helping others through the night... the victims or the killer.The suspense building will only last the first round, and the game is more or less intended to be around 4 hours.Some of the puzzles will easily catch you off guard and are intensely unfair if you weren't paying attention. The puzzle comes in and hits hard and fast just like a real 911 call. Rather unfair but also realistic given the scenario, so I give this game points for sticking to its guns - you aren't a 911 operator and you quickly realize your shortcomings and the consequences of somewhat goofing off when you should be taking notes.The studio arrangement is at the same time quite well done and poorly executed. There are times plots are made while still on air and the killer could reasonably be expected to be listening in... oops. The host cannot hang up calls, and the producer often doesn't, and the producer can play music without having a music playing device while you are out of the studio. It could use some cleanup on those rough edges.At one point I had backtracked all the way to the studio, missing an intercom on the wall. I couldn't speak with the producer until I ran back down to the specific intercom to relay updates, the others did not work nor did trying to call the producer from the studio.Overall expect a good 4-5 hour game but it doesn't bear repeating unless you like to chase trophies or see alternate endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast playing through this game! so many small details to explore, great character growth/design, Engaging puzzles and best of all a good twist!I think this is a great game to pick up for anyone who enjoys games like "What Remains of Edith Finch, Stanley Parable, Firewatch Etc." Achievements also aren't to challenging so even if you are not normally an achievement hunter its still quite fulfilling to try and get them all!Overall I would definitely give it a try! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: An homage to 80s horror flicks, told through the medium of call-in radio show chatter and a handful of puzzles. Killer Frequency at first appears to be slight and simple, but you really do need to pay attention. Lives are on the line, after all, and your mistakes have consequences!With decent, characterful writing that alludes to stock characters without relying upon them and some talented voice acting, this dialogue-heavy game is easy to listen to and to follow. It dragged me in and if not for other commitments I could easily have finished this game in one sitting.A few moments were scary, but Killer Frequency most effectively wields tension and dread as its bloody knives. It makes you care for the people of this nowhere town, then threatens to hurt them. The oldest trick in the storytelling book? Maybe, but it works!You should absolutely give this unique and charming horror story a try. Maybe you'll be able to do better than I did and save everyone. Good luck.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but awesomely sweet. I loved playing this.It had been on my wishlist for a while now, and I'm so glad it went on sale for me to get.The voice acting was amazing, and the look and feel of it all was incredible, also.9/10, just wished it was longer, so I could feed my dreams of being a disc jockey.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: First person horror/comedy adventure exactly to my taste. The game is outrageously fun and offers the right amount of tension with real-time problem solving, a great atmosphere and 80s aesthetics, and the voice acting is also really good. You can also get up to some hilarious nonsense in the game, like throwing paper balls at a basketball hoop and moving, rearranging or throwing all sorts of objects into the toilet. If you want some examples, take a look at my screenshots.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: At first glance Killer Frequency by Team 17, gives the impression that it’s going to be a game full of jumpscares, as is usual with a horror game. We are immediately greeted with a terrifying masked figure that, if I can be totally honest, scared the absolute crap out of me. Who is this masked individual? Will they be stalking us throughout the game?When the game gets going properly you find yourself in a radio studio. You play as Forest Nash, a DJ who used to work in the big city but these days he’s on the graveyard shift at the local radio station for Gallows Creek, a backwater town with a small population. In a complete change of pace you find yourself in….a radio simulator? It took me by surprise and at that point I was half ready to turn the game off. But I gave it a chance, and thank God I did! Things start to ramp up when the station receives a call from a 911 operator. There’s been a murder and her colleague has been attacked by a masked, whistling man. She needs to go and get help from the next time over but there’s no one to man the 911 phone lines.Except you.This is where things start to get interesting. You begin to take calls from people who are being attacked by this mysterious killer. It is your job to help them escape and your choices will mean the difference between life and death. On top of this you find yourself investigating just who the killer might be. To do this you find yourself investigating the radio station and solving puzzles.Let me be clear – there are very few jump scares in the game. Instead the horror comes entirely from the atmosphere created by the environment, the tension and the incredible music. It relies on these and the gripping story to keep you well and truly on the edge of your seat.This has to be one of the most original horror games that I have played in a very long time. It is a murder mystery slasher horror that does not have the overused trope of unnecessary jump scares. Instead it is the atmosphere that makes it scary as well as the masterful use of music. Not only that but the tension is broken up by some well timed comedic moments – kudos to the excellent voice cast for how well they did this. The voice acting was worthy of a AAA title!Highly original with a tense atmosphere, fantastic score and top tier voice acting, this is a title that would suit anyone who loves the slower burn of murder mystery stories and the tropes of slasher horrors. It is a mix that shouldn’t really work but it does, and it does so brilliantly.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little first person interactive story game. The atmosphere is on ponty.....just like the slice and beer deal from Ponty's Pizza! (god I hate myself for that one). Overall one of the better story/ adventure games. It oozes the 80's with lots of blunt horror movie references and decent (yet cliche) story and characters. Liked the Radio DJ angle but felt like I wanted more of a challenge in the puzzles and mystery parts. It's a great introduction game for people that want a good puzzle/ story game. Replay value isn't there however which is where this game could improve towards if they ever do a sequel. Felt simplistic in parts but I enjoyed this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. It's lots of fun and scary moments. Puzzles are just enough to get you thinking but not enough to make you want to ram your head thru a wall. Really love playing this game. Also there are some real funny moments that had me laughing. I am not the most serious gamer which is why I probably love it so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I love 80s music, 80s horror movies, and I love this game. My only complaint is that I wish it was longer. It took me around 6 hours to complete, and I was in no hurry. So, in my opinion, the price is a little too high compared to that. But it's a good game, and if you love 80s music and horror movies, definitely give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good concept for a game, and a good execution of it. Some weird audio issues though, like some sound effects being unreasonably loud while others are very quiet, and like how other character voices are much louder than the voice of the player character, I don't know if this is just on my end though.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.... It plays somewhat like an interactive graphic novel with different choices. There are free roam periods where you can explore a bit more each time. I like being able to replay the game and choose different responses, like instead of allowing them to all live, I can say things to cause their demise. Its fun to hear the voices and story play out. I thought there would be a lot more records to collect but there wasn't much collectibles. Still fun to play tho! loved the voice acting!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Talk about a stripped down, living your 80s/90s horror trope fantasy with this game. It was awesome, sometimes truly creepy, sometimes suspenseful, and sometimes funny. I loved it. I poured over this game in two days. I enjoyed the Forrest and Peggy. My only gripe, literally only, is the voice actors for the extra. A little more variety would have been nice. I understand being on a budget, but your teen sounded like she has had one too many cigs. That is literally my only complaint. 9.5/10. Really, really great. Adding Whistling Man to the list of slashers for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite a novel horror-puzzle game.Like all good puzzle games it uses good writing and characters to keep you immersed and motivated to keep going.The voice work is serviceable. The puzzles are easy but occasionally can be obtuse and a little obscure on the correct answer.7/10, would like an extra level of complexity and it's a bit overpriced but the novelty adds a lot
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game!!! Great graphics, music that really goes hard, and a story that pulls you in. I started playing this on stream yesterday, and I couldn't get it out of my head, so I had to finish it today! Definitely recommend, only minor complaint is I feel like the story isn't long enough! I wish it had so much more, I fell in love with this atmosphere and I can't wait to go back in for more runs to get different endings and more secrets!!! I will say, for the price I do really wish that there was more content as it's only a 5.5 hour game when I was kind of mulling around, but that's really not the end of the world to me as a lot of studios and developers have raised prices recently and that's just par for the course. I do recommend this game, especially if you stream!!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. The mechanics are used very well and surprisingly don't get repetitive. It's not a game that relies on jump scares to scare you but the actual atmosphere. the only time I felt safe was when I was in the actual room. All the characters had so much personality and there were some actual funny parts to clear out the scares. With that also came some very well designed puzzles that had me actually thinking at times.      Obviously there are some bad parts to the game. Firstly I got the game on sale but spending $25 on a 6 hour game seems very steep. Another issue is that some dialogue is unneeded and just got annoying. They over explained things or added pieces to information in intense moments and made it hard to really be intense. Some parts of the story didn't add up, but they may explain it in different endings.     Other than that it is definitely good game to play when you want a bit of thrill.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved playing this game, every single detail I experienced in this game was amazing and it ran very well with my old computer. But if you're looking for a game with a unique charm that can both have its comedic timings and unsettle you again and again with its atmosphere then look no further because you've found your match. All in all I think this has turned into one of my favourite games and I hope it becomes yours too.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Might have been fun if I had the patience to get to any fun parts... But there is SO MUCH unskippable endless slow talking that you have to get through before being able to complete one puzzle. The idea is pretty cool but the pointless and corny lines exchanged between characters is insufferable. Refunding after this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying I don't often play horror games but I'm glad I got this one. I went in mostly blind so didn't know what to expect. I love horror movies and this really scratched that itch. I saw different names/writing that were like easter eggs for horror fans. Overall I had a fun experience, had some jump scares and screams.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game earlier today, and I have been thinking about it a lot since. The mystery of it all keeps you truly engrossed with all its twists and turns, and the entire story was something I think most people will have a good time playing through. While the story feels satisfying and complete, I still found myself wanting more by the end, and I really hope this game gets an opportunity to make some sort of prequel(s?) because I think there is a lot more lore they hint at that could be dug into with the Whistling Man and even Forrest's past. He seems like a fun guy and I'd love to hear him on the radio again!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and quirky retro-themed puzzle game with a dash of light, cheesy thriller elements. The story is casual and easy to follow, with great voice acting that adds charm to the overall experience. I was pleasantly surprised by how enjoyable it was, and there's even an achievement for completing the story within 4 hours so its not the longest game. While it's not groundbreaking, it's a solid, enjoyable experience. I'd give it a 6.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most entertaining games I've played. The story feels like an 80's horror B-movie but manages to rise up and provide a great mystery with some bits of humor thrown in here and there. I was guessing up until the very end as to who the Whistle Man actually was and what his motive could be. The "revelation" was not one I was expecting -- especially with everything that unfolded with it.You have to save various citizens during the night while being a radio DJ/host, and while some situations have obviously solutions, others...not so much. At times, I was not sure which option would be best, and sometimes I made some bad choices by mistake. But that's part of the fun: you have to rely on yourself to put the pieces together and make the right decisions. The game saves after key moments and events, so you're stuck with whatever you pick unless you want to start over from the beginning.The voice acting is great, and there are some nice 80's beats to listen to. The graphics aren't anything remarkable, but they have a sort of comic book style, which fits the type of story the game has. It's serious but with a tad bit of camp and humor thrown in for good measure. The replay value is high despite knowing the story and characters. It's just so well-done and so much fun to play. You can play it multiple times to get different achievements, different endings, or just to see if you can pick out some clues sprinkled here and there that hint at what may truly be going on. Definitely give this game a try. You won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Very good story game. Has a striking visual and very likeable characters. Puzzles are overall very good, with me only getting stuck on the newspaper board one. Having the extra features of being able to wander the studio as well as play around with the soundboard, records and cassettes add a lot more substance to the game and put  it above regular visual novel type games. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A sort yet thrilling game of deduction. It's like a true crime story that you get to be a part of. The setting is well done. This game is by no means scary but there were many tense moments while playing. The puzzles weren't very difficult but they were satisfying whenever you figured it out and saved another person. Actively piecing together this mystery unfolding in front of you is such a great experience. I would highly recommend this to anyone who enjoys a good mystery.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This game is clearly made for VR and I personally found that it didn't work well and the game seems to just talk at you rather than with you. I felt like I didn't make any meaningful decisions.  The controls are awkward and I tried with both a keyboard and mouse and a controller and it wasn't the easiest ( I dropped so many items) . You also start the game in a room where you can get up and walk around while apparently running a radio station but all of the responses to pick for dialogue is in a set location over the desk. I even missed a timed decision, from not standing in the correct position during the scene. As a player I felt like I wasn't actually needed and I could play stupid sounds and music over the radio callers with no reaction from other characters. I also felt like we are the only intelligent people in the area and some of the options felt obvious and felt forced.  It's a shame as this feels like it had a lot of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A fun slasher/thriller game with a cool premise executed fairly well. Playing as not the scared teenager but the person that gets called for help breathes new life into an otherwise tropey game.This isn't my usual kind of game but I enjoyed it. It feels a bit livelier than your typical interactive fiction/choose your own adventure style game, which is what this is when you boil it down. The most critical gameplay moments are about picking the right choices from a branching dialog path. But they do a lot with the formula to make it feel fresh. You need to find clues around the station and decipher them. Often it's up to you to decide what to do without a perfectly clear "right choice." The game rewards paying attention to small details (and a bit of save scumming).  Sometimes it seems pretty unfair and the only way to get things totally right is to save scum and guess. I feel like there is a trade off here. They could have made the kind of game that is easy to beat perfectly on your first try, but they instead made a game where the correct answer isn't always glaringly obvious and you have to listen to your gut at times. It was pretty gratifying at times to decide to do what I felt was the correct answer even though I couldn't point to a specific clue that told me so. Some felt cheap and I did shamelessly scum twice to save a victim. But that's okay.I also wish there was some sort of journal of the people who called. Does that name sound familiar because it was a call I really took, or is my mind playing tricks on me?And I think the interface could use some work. I felt for the largest part of the game I was trapped behind my desk because decision prompts would pop up there, sometimes with a limited window to act in. It was especially infuriating and broke immersion at times when I was *supposed* to be hurrying to another office to find a piece of information but couldn't because Peggy was still telling me that "time was running out," and I had to run from the door back to the desk to reply. Couldn't they just put the prompts right next to my head?The story isn't super original either, it's mix of several slasher films. I'm not a fan of the genre but I figured it out pretty quickly. But the perspective of being neither victim nor killer, and being on the sideline, working in a support capacity lends some freshness to a story I've heard a dozen times before.Really fun. I might play it again next October once I've forgotten a lot of it and see if I can save everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and engaging game that really makes you feel like you are in control of the story. And that is because you ARE. Everything you do while trying to solve this mystery has an impact and if you mess up you really feel it. So if you want a intriguing horror, problem solving game based on 80s slashers this is the easiest recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple and not complicated, you get the game that goes as detective/slasher sort of 80s movie. As of:  it's all about finding more information around the radio station and give the right answers for saving victims basically, nothing special, or active, or super entertaining. (Quite a lot of talks for fans of action i have to say). But my opinion, that the main reason to play is not for the sake of the gameplay, all thing worth the:  i'm fan of old school stuff, and music is my everything, so i have to say, they got it, you have not much space and locations, but belive me, in those spaces with theirs sounds and special 80s touch and design to it you get this 80s slasher/detective movie feel in interactive form. I definetly didn't regret playing it since again i'am fan of old school vibes and music. I would recommend this one for fans of 80s and atmospheric interactive movie sort of a game fans to play. In a few words: nothing special about the gameplay or graphics, but those vibes totally works for a fans of that era or fans of so called immersive sims. Go play for And of course sound effects and music is a seperate and huge THANK YOU to the devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun surprisingly chill puzzle game. Some of the puzzles could be a bit difficult, but solving them felt really satisfying especially the more complex ones that require you to pay attention to smaller details or make full conspiracy boards! The atmosphere is fantastic and DRIPS classic 80s neon-colored charm. Though the game is horror it's pretty light on the scares, leaning towards being more of a horror comedy. The voice acting from all the characters is great, and I would definitely recommend this for a fun spooky time following a cast of eccentric and charming characters!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for a Birthday Stream. I'm not one for horror games, but decided to try this out when a friend recommended it to me.The horror element relies more on the atmosphere and intensity of the plot. For those who don't like jump-scares, this game is mostly friendly to this preference. The closest thing to one happens in the prologue. Afterwards your experience will be focused on the "dread" you face when aiding the callers.The game itself is straightforward. Controls are intuitive and fluid, though they could get some getting used to at first. The calls are unique in their own way with various puzzles, and are enough to pick your brain while decently easy. The only confusing part is with a certain puzzle in which you have to "piece together" a lead. You'll know which one that is when you get there.FINAL THOUGHTS: I love the retro aesthetic of this game, and the music selection adds to the feel. There are good moments of levity to balance the dread, leading to a satisfying experience overall. If you're looking for a modern game that *doesn't* suck in current era, Killer Frequency is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocks. Super suspenseful for a game where you basically never leave your tiny radio room, at least to start. It's quite similar to the classic horror game Do You Copy, but with a significantly expanded scope in all the best ways. Great voice acting and the dialogue gets everything that's happening on the phone lines perfectly, without sounding corny. The humor was overall good, and decently spread out, and best of all it knew when it was time to put the clown horn away because the story was getting too juicy to have another pizza break.The one thing that's a bit irritating is that the first two calls are significantly more complicated to run through than the others, ESPECIALLY the second one which borders on Keep Talking And No One Explodes. Once you realize  the game gets much less nerve wracking. But that doesn't make it any less suspenseful. Super great stuff. Highly recommend, worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Saw the great reviews and figured I would check it out. Big mistake. Probably some of the worst writing and voice acting I have heard in a while. Story is laughably bad and incredibly boring. Tried to push myself through the intro and refund window, but could not bear anymore. Avoid this if you value your time and money. Even on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: About 80 min in, I like it, but don't love it. It's a little too silly for me so far. The radio callers fall into typical tropes (blustery old reporter, exercising mid-western housewife, etc.). The voice acting is very animated, going hard into these tropes. This is a turn-off for me. I wanted something that felt ... a little more authentic and frightening.The puzzles, though they might get better and more difficult later, have been simple at best thus far.  One was so easy it didn't require any thought at all. The concept is really cool, and to some extent, I'm sure it's meant to be super campy. This goes beyond camp though, delving into silly shenanigans and dialogue options that just don't make sense for the killer-on-the-loose concept. I'll update this further as I play more. But, over an hour in, I'm a little disappointed. Is it worth buying? Depends on what you go in expecting. For the price, maybe. For the interesting concept, yes. For the horror? No. For a meticulous and well-crafted plot and challenging puzzles? Also no. For strong, unique, and believable characters? Not at all.Edit:I've switched my recommendation to a "no" and will be attempting to return the game (just about at the two-hour mark). I can't get over how, if you fail and a character dies, you and the other host freak out for about a minute and then go back to their radio-host BS and silly humor. Ridiculous. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because of the initial game jam concept that I watched a few YouTubers play of this game, and I can tell you I was not disappointed.  Overall, I thought the game was great.  The voice acting was top notch, and overall it was a very fun experience.  I do think a lot of the puzzles were a little too on the nose, and easy to figure out how to solve them, the story and your first gut reactions through it are what really make the game worth playing.  The only thing I wish was implemented, would have been an easier system to go back to specific people who you might have failed to save.  I ended the game with 1 person not making it, assuming they could be saved, and unless 1 of my 3 save files would've been able to get me back to right before that exact part, I'd have to play through either my earliest save, or the entire game again to try and get a different outcome for that person, and then again play through the entire rest of the game again.  While, I think playing through the rest of the game would have been reasonable to get certain endings/dialogues, I at least wish the game would have had chapters or something equivalent, to be able to at least start back at a certain part of the story, and play through from there, instead of starting fresh, or hoping 1 of my 3 save files would have taken me back to that point.  Either more save file slots, or a chapter select would have been better...but all the same, I cannot recommend this game enough even with my small gripes, and really think if you enjoy narrative driven stories, that have some light game play outside of puzzles/choices within it, you need to give this game a try!  Or simply...just give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: The day after I streamed this, my throat was sore. Good lord why? The game is fully voiced, I didn’t talk all that much…Just realized it’s cause I was laughing so much! It did start out slow, for about the first hour, but stick with it. My community was a bit hard on the writing, and I didn’t like myself at first. This made us all determined to kill people, and we stuck with our bloodthirst as we met new characters and grew more conflicted. After the initial premise we all know going in of radio 911, the devs did their homework, and the story was realistic as the writing improved.I do think it’s made for horror fans, cause we’re more forgiving of the tropes. Even if you’re not a fan of horror, it’s not super scary and you will enjoy the calls and puzzles. The atmosphere outside the DJ room is surprisingly creepy. It’s nice to have a game that didn’t rely on jumpscares, but that did raise goosebumps and made me hesitate around corners. And for my favorite part…The devs gave us a fidget toy! For those of us who have ADHD and still love a good story, this was epic.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10This is a fantastic idea that has all the pizzazz of a wet towel. The music is great, some of the plot elements, and humorous bits are well written. HOWEVER...-The puzzles were either a bit too simple or non existent. Many times you would just have to make a lucky guess to get things right. -You can't skip dialog and there is a LOT OF DIALOG.-sometimes you have timed prompts but the prompts only physically pop up in one spot.-Most of the smaller story or character motivations were terrible. It's hard to tell how campy this game is supposed to be at times.  Why am i answering questions about co-workers Peggy has known for years? Why is a police officer asking me what weapon to choose? it's a short game but its also sort of cheap.  Idk, its decent enough if you like 80's slasher films.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely thrilled with "Killer Frequency"! This game masterfully blends the nostalgic 80s vibe with an engaging and suspenseful storyline. _childDocuments_.review: Aw man this game was completely amazing and unique. You can't get much cozier than behind the electronics at a radio station. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 8/10 One of my favorite puzzle thrillers in a while, but a few weird story choices keep it out of my Best of All TimeSince the bulk of this review is going to be kinda of spoiler-y (not gonna spoil the twists or the endings), let me get gameplay nitpicks and other praises out of the way first; The game is accessible to the ley person, even those who aren't super big on puzzle solving, and a generically-good ending can be achieved simply by following instructions and using a little intuition. It's kind of annoying how you often can't leave the area you're currently standing in until whoever's speaking is done doing so. Definitely makes Killer Frequency more annoying to replay, but different dialogue options keep things fresh enough that it's bearable.Now, on to the meat and potatoes of this review. The weird story beats and inconsistencies that made some elements feel... not very well fleshed out.  And that's all well and good, but what that little twist  adequately explain is With all that said, the game was genuinely fun the first time and I've happily replayed it trying to get different endings. It would be nice if getting everyone killed had a more interesting ending, because right now it only yields an achievement, and that's not really enough to justify another 5-hour playthrough that is surprisingly difficult to get right. Checkpoint saves on more than three slots would be nice. It's a pain in the ass to realize that a decision I made two and a half hours ago has porked my challenge run and I can't un-do it without starting all over.

_childDocuments_.review: This is why I love indie games!I'll start off by saying I'm not someone who likes horror games, generally. However, this game is very light in the 'horror' it uses, and it has more of a  'creepy' vibe then anything. But even then, the comedic undertone throughout the game is just so great that you quickly forget all about the creepy vibes! It also helps that your recording studio, the place you spend most of the game, is very warm and cozy. There is also a fun co-host character who's there to keep you company through most of the game.Onto the rest of the game then! I finished the story in in about 6 hours and was completely captivated all the way through. The story is told in a very fun and engaging way, even though you get to hear it mostly through phone calls to your radio station. The voiceacting is great and very fun which is a must for a game with this kind of premise. The puzzles are also engaging and mostly really fair. They're not an extreme challenge to the avid puzzler, but you do definitely need to do some lateral thinking. I was afraid that I'd feel rushed to solve the puzzles as the game uses them as a way for you to help characters escape a killer in real-time, but luckily the game gives you as much time as you need to figure them out. Some might say this is unrealistic, but I think the contrary would not have worked as well.There are real consequences to your actions, and whether you solve the puzzles or not decides the outcome of the story. I liked that, especially after I had my first "Oh no, I really messed that up and now someone actually died" moment. I loved that there is this co-host character called 'Peggy'. She not only keeps you much needed company throughout the night, but also adds some comedic relief where necessary. I think this was a great addition to the game and made it so there was always something that was happening, even in between the radio callers.I'd definitely recommend playing this game if you like mystery puzzle games with a strong sense of atmosphere! If you can get it on sale at all, it's even more of a steal. You'll love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little adventure/horror/comedy game. Does more with its premise that you might initially expect, and has some memorable sequences that make it a fun little ride.As an audio person, it does bother me that I can't fade out the music before entering a fade out sequence, and that you have to just jarringly stop the vinyl before things can progress, but having the rudimentary usage of the equipment probably makes it more accessible to most folks- it would be nice to have either option though.Music's good, atmosphere is good, and the game is doing it's best when it leans into kooky, over the top characters (a love struck boy in a a cornfield, or a jazzercise queen are the winning supporting characters imo). And the radio advertisements are simply glorious. The game has a reasonably predictable overarching plot, and the voice acting for the main two characters can seem woefully disconnected from the tone of the narrative from time to time- Peggy can be overly perky while people are getting murdered, and the player character is supposed to be progressively getting more comfortable airing the radio show as the night progresses, but it comes off feeling forced; the movie Pontypool, this is not.About 5-6 hours for a playthrough, plenty of incentive to replay it a few times to see how branching scenarios go, overall a fun little gem that the asking price might be a bit high for, but is still a worthwhile experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An unusual and brilliant adventure game that takes place (almost) exclusively in a radio station and most of that in a single room. The interplay between acting, in a very minor capacity, as a radio host while also trying to advise people in truly harrowing situations as a *surprise* emergency call operator was marvellous. This is all about the story - virtually no jump scares - just you, a switchboard, callers in distress and your trusty producer, Peggy, in the booth. The chatter is great; the characters are charming and layered; the story is intriguing; and the game mechanic is simple, inspired and elegant.I also really appreciated the touch of being able to throw balls of paper into the hoop bin - just the thing to keep the hands occupied in what is essentially an audio 'choose your own adventure' story.This game is a delight: a strong, thriller, narrative story, with enough interaction to keep you engaged for hours. I loved the fact that it was possible to save everyone but it was far from a guarantee, especially as the game progresses.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been drawn to games that push the envelope and introduce innovative concepts. Much like "Not For Broadcast," which had its share of merits despite some shortcomings, "Killer Frequency" arrives with a novel packaging yet struggles significantly in execution. Set against the backdrop of a pseudo-horror thriller set in the 80s, it places you in the role of a radio DJ, a premise brimming with potential…had it been done correctly.The initial thrill of engaging with your producer and getting the hang of your space is captivating, but the game stumbles in maintaining its momentum: the pacing is unnecessarily laborious, ruining what should have been an exhilarating experience. Further dampening matters, moving within the studio and building feels cumbersome, and the puzzles, rather than encouraging creativity, confine you to a stringent, seemingly random narrative framework that feels punishing if you deviate from the exact path the writers had conceived. Despite my enthusiasm and desire to embrace this game, these elements hold me back from recommending it, but I must commend Team 17 for trying something different and hope that more studios take such risks.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style, the music, the story, the voice acting, the puzzles, the comedy- all of it is a perfect amalgamation that makes for an enjoyable experience.Despite it's generally linear story-line, it still manages to be a replayable experience that is almost as enjoyable the second, third (and so on) times. _childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! The unique retro aesthetic and corny horror jokes everywhere made this an instant hit with me. The voice acting was fantastic and I really enjoyed the back and forth with Peggy and Forrest. The game isn't particularly long (first run was a leisurely 6-7 hours), and I found that to be perfect. The game is more or less a walking simulator with puzzles, and if you're a fan of campy horror, 80s aesthetic, and story-telling through radio (like Welcome to Nightvale) you may enjoy this.I've really taken to radio station games lately (re: Life is Strange: True Colors), so that paired slasher tropes was amazing. Complete with slasher logic that was reminiscent of the Scream franchise, a personal favorite, this game could do no wrong by me.I will say there are a couple instances where the sound EQing is painful and Peggy is louder than she should be and I found one typo during dialogue, but overall the music, atmosphere, and story was very fun and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. Its very audio heavy, and the devs knew this, so they put extra work into the audio of this game. The soundtracks are banger and the actors are ALL incredible talented and believable. The graphics are stylized in a pleasant, fitting style.This game made me laugh and made me jump in my seat. It was a great experience. Thank you, Team17!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed this game, i didn't know anything about the game, besides the first video on the steam page..i had not the slightest clue it was VR as i played in the dark over a few nights on a controller, looking back at some of the puzzles it makes sense, cant believe it never dawned on me!as someone who works in radio as both a board operator and now a broadcast technician, (i loved the "generic equipment racks very cute, i would of loved to see a silly little transmitter, or roof top access to stare at the tower but that's me) i really enjoyed the whole idea of the story, as well as the game environment, and the jabs at the station manager and the dead air jokes! either some one on your team has worked in radio or you really did your research into the dynamics of this type of office space, as my boss always says "it takes a special kind of crazy to work in radio"! this is a really a great murder mystery, with great replay value! the game looks great! the controls, wile unique, once your into the rhythm, are not an issue, which looking back is rare for VR games played on a monitor! the few puzzles in the game really make you think, but they are not so difficult that you need to resort to a guide, tho i felt lost at first for a few, i felt like i was tossed into a box with some pocket lint and was told to make art, a good hard think can get you where you need to be, and the rest from there slowly falls together!voice acting was also great, Forrest Nash, turning on and off the radio voice felt right to me, it was proper! and his "BIG HEAD" spot on! one game mechanic that i thought was really clever was using the time between cut ins or "talking/taking calls" as the time to leave and run around! again, very accurate, you dont just want to up and leave in the middle of a show unless you KNOW EXACTLY how much time you have to be gone, and you know exactly what your going to do, (make a coffee, warm up food, step out back for some air) so keeping the player within the studio until such a time made sense to me! overall i really enjoyed the game! would recommend to anyone! with or without radio experience!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: script is too corny for me, I got bored and stopped caring about the plot, final reveal was midKiller Frequency has an interesting premise and initially it appears that you would be able to fully immerse yourself as a radio host; however, there were several things that made it hard for me to get into playing. I did complete this game once.You don't do much as host besides taking calls and making dialogue choices. I expected more "puzzles" but I mostly just felt like I was walking around looking for papers which give you really obvious solutions. Most of the gameplay is akin to a visual novel. I don't mind the visual novel genre and I never skip dialogue, but most visual novel games you can  speed up the text/skip the audio to get through the script faster. You are forced to listen through all dialogue with Killer Frequency, which was a pain for me because I unfortunately found the script/voice acting to be too corny.I have nothing against the actual voices of the actors as they were pretty good, but I personally felt the script was so corny it was painful to listen to after getting through most of the game (if you have ever seen memes making fun of Marvel movies for corny lines, it's like that. I did find the advertisements and a certain pizza parlor amusing.) It also doesn't help that the plot is somewhat unsatisfying so I found it hard to stay motivated to find out what was going on. I didn't care when the killer's identity was revealed because
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I will be refunding this game the moment I hit post on this review I had this game on my wish list ever since it came out, I thought the idea behind it sounded really cool. And of course with the winter sale, when else is a better time to pick it up to try. I am beyond disappointed, to how far fetched the premise this game was set on at the start. I seriously don't understand how phones can call but only locally, or why they would have a radio host be a 911 dispatch replacement. What about people who are calling for an ambulance or fire fighter, do they just not exist in this world? The radio host has no way to reach them if someone did call for that matter.  I thought the victims were calling the radio host because they wanted to give their part of a story of a murderer. Along with the first video showing you being outside, however this is not the case at all. The outside play is the tutorial in the beginning as you go into the radio station. You continue to stay inside the building, mainly at the desk. You can't answer or decline the calls on your own accord, you have to actively tell your partner to end the call. (and wait for the option to come up before you can decide even if you want to sooner )  That extra step also makes no sense to me, and is irritating to deal with, while people are prank calling. I feel like it could have been so easy to start this game off, people are calling because they want to share their story. That makes sense regardless what time frame you're in. Have people call in for that reason alone, don't try to give this insanely far fetched back story to the plot. That alone took me out of the game, the reviews made me wanna keep going in hopes it just gets better, at least give it 2 hours. However a mixture of trying to ignore huge story plots to play the game, and also the idea of not being able to return it is making me stop playing before it's too late. I really wanted to like this game, but I can't recommend this to anyone. It feels like it should be a VR game, and gets tedious very fast. This is my longest review I've ever written but I'm just so upset about this game. The description should say clearly what you're doing, because it's unclear enough to make the game sound better.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a thrilling walking sim puzzle game where you play as Forrest Nash a midnight radio show host in a small city. But on this special night, a serial killer known as The Whistling Man returns. Your mission is to guide these potential victims to safety, by finding clues around the station. Like for example, read a book and relay the info to the caller. There are multiple dialogue choices, and picking wrong ones can result in their death.I really like the atmosphere of this game, which takes place only in the radio station. You don't get to explore other places, but the station itself is pretty decent-sized. It's quite creative and feels like a reverse-escape room, where you're in a small area and must find clues, but instead of helping yourself, you help other people. Despite seeing almost no characters the game managed to make you feel empathy for these unseen people, helped by great voice acting.I think Killer Frequency is a pretty unique puzzle game with lovely retro aesthetics, and obviously influenced by slasher films of that era, especially the Scream movies. If you're a fan of those you'd most likely enjoy this game's purpose of making you a slasher victim's savior. I do wish we got to explore more areas though, but that'll kinda ruin the tense, isolated feeling this game has.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I love nearly everything I've played out of Team17, but this one misses the mark by quite a bit. Simply put, the gameplay loop is not exciting enough to float the rather uninteresting story. If one or the other were great, it would carry the title, but sadly both are pretty dull. Another game with a rather simple gameplay mechanic but an incredible story, for example, is Arctic Eggs. Both are interesting enough that it was a title I simply couldn't put down. I really tried to like this one, but I find myself itching to press Exit and find the next title to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: + A fun 6 to 7-hour game by Team17+ A simple and well-designed UI. It makes you feel like an actual radio host with all the buttons and controls. I certainly enjoyed trying every button.+ A spooky intro and good tutorial+ Solid voice acting is what makes the game pretty good+ It does have some interesting escape-the-room-like puzzles (Maze puzzle, deducing the next target..etc)+ Ponty's pizza was the spotlight of the game+ The game had me taking notes and trying to connect the dots+ A fantastic OST is always a win for me- Some parts of the game suffer from pacing issues however it gets back on track towards the last phase of the game.Side Notes:- It was Team17's first VR game before coming to PC and console
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 I can't say much about the plot without ruining what I would definitely recommend for lovers of story games, but it's either an homage to, or very derivative of, the 80s slasher flicks it's inspired by. The only thing I can compare the gameplay to is the Wavelengths DLC for Life Is Strange: True Colors, where you're mostly in a radio booth. In this case instead of a cat companion you have a producer named Peggy, who assists you in trying to help you save some people being hunted by a serial killer. Horror fans might find this game light on the scary, but for this scaredy cat, there's as much spook as I would want in the sections where you have to leave the safety of the radio booth. Any more and I might not have wanted to keep going. To be honest I was expecting more visual puzzles like the maze shown in the trailer, but it's mostly narrative puzzles. However, that didn't turn out to be a detriment. I really enjoyed my short time with Killer Frequency, and played it in one session. To get all the achievements I'd have to play it twice more. Achievement hunters might finish in 2 total runs, if they did everything exactly right. I won't rule out revisiting this game in the future, but my backlog is so large, I may have to be satisfied with playing just once.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I have a better record collection at my house than this 80s radio station.Killer Frequency is, on paper, my kind of game. You're a radio DJ who has to also pull double duty as the town's 911 operator while a killer is on the loose.  I feel like there's a lot of potential for a subversive game about using the tools at your disposal to pull some really cool tricks. And I enjoy the game encouraging the player to think about what horror movie tropes to avoid when trying to save people. I also generally enjoy the game's vibe. It's cheesy but still manages to have tension, especially when you leave the DJ booth. However, there are some glaring flaws that keep me from really loving Killer  Frequency. First, interactivity is heavily limited. It's primarily staring at documents and selecting dialogue options. The DJ booth itself has very little mechanical importance which feels like a major loss when compared to games like Not For Broadcast. The game is also VERY handholdy and doesn't really push the player to think much. I wish there were more challenges that forced the player to really think outside the box. Lastly, while horror slashers of this ilk are often quite cheesy, the dialogue and voice acting is atrocious. It feels so phoned in and dull and it sucks all of the tension out of some potentially creepy scenes.I still enjoyed the game and wanted to see it through. I liked unraveling the mystery, helping save people, and interacting with the DJ booth. But there's definitely a major opportunity here to come back with a more ambitious game that dares the player to multi-task and actually outsmart the killer. I'd score it 7/10.Decent recommend FFO: 80s era slashers, Not For Broadcast, choose-your-own adventures, and dialogue so wooden it feels like it was written by a tree

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a horror game where a serial killer is systematically trying to murder residents of a small town. With the emergency services out of action, you as the towns radio DJ must field emergency calls and solve puzzles to save the residents from the killer... or they die.This game is quite simply one of the best and most unique horror titles out there. You field calls from the towns residents all of which involves you using your deduction skills and exploring the radio station building to find clues to solve said puzzles and save them.As an example one puzzle has a young teen trapped in a hedge maze with the killer, you must over the phone use a map you find given to the station for promo material to guide him through the maze to the exit away from the killer. It's simple, but tense as you take into account his position, the way hes looking, the description of landmarks with the map you have. It's one of many excellent puzzles you will partake in while piecing together the killers motive and uncovering some small town secrets that have stayed buried for a long time. The game is carried by excellent voice acting from all the cast, you spend four hours+ inside one building listening to people talk but it's done so well and the puzzles are so well executed this doesn't matter. Killer Frequency is a must play for all horror fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This was one slow game. I first tested it on January 3 and finished it on April 8. It's around 5 hours long.You spend the entire game in one location, in and around a radio station with tons of dialogue. For a walking sim this means that you never see any of the action, it is all told through voice and the radio station feels more like a backdrop to a "choose your own adventure" text book.I managed to save most people on my first attempt, but that definitely makes it replayable. I would, however, argue that the game is too long. Most of the voice actors aren't that interesting which is a shame. For a voice only type of game they needed more interesting characters than what we got.The game does get points for originality though and it's probably the "okayest" game ever made. For me it barely nudges over to "recommended", but could just as well have gone the other way if it only had made one more error.I don't know... it's one of those games you should definitely pick up on a 75% sale, but there are way better walking sims out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever felt compelled to give a game a standing ovation before? Me neither, but probably 7.5 actual gameplay hours later, having reached an/the(?) ending, I am here doing just that. The approach was kinda simple: a Borderland's style graphics (big-ass outlines), a relatively contained setting, a buttload of linear dialog that both contributes to and confounds the narratives in question, and a somewhat simplistic (hey, like, all of the SCREAM movies are arguably simplistic) plot. But each of those marks were met. This game is exactly what it claims to be, what it wanted to be. There are few bugs (don't worry -- it's kinda like the soundboard faders don't actually have an effect on the "audience"; you can reset object positioning from the ESC menu for that pesky pizza box that's missing) to trip you up. I mostly went with my intuitions (with augmented wit from our protagonist) and found that, as long as I had correctly digested the clues thus far, I wasn't being left behind for being annoyed at this or that caller. ...Jesus, I've never thought about the life of a radio DJ before, so... one more first for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a FANTASTIC story, and subsequently a fantastic game! If you love the vibe you get from the screenshots or game play you've seen, you're gonna love the game, I guarantee it. This game has an engaging plot with equally engaging mechanics. The concept of being a DJ on a late night show is so novel, and incredibly entertaining. I'm only left wishing there was more! It fits perfectly with the 80's slasher horror genre, this game is truly retro aesthetic heaven. I encountered only one small glitch, my tape player stopped accepting ad tapes, which was quickly remedied by a setting called 'Reset All Objects', seemingly integrated for a scenario just like mine. So to same the game was extremely well optimized and bug free is an understatement. All the tracks you could play were bangers! Just as you'd expect from a game so centered around music. Do your best to avoid spoilers before playing, as the story is a mystery and I often found myself having the most fun trying to piece together the mystery while I collected documents or searched around the station, it really puts you into the game. Lastly, I wholeheartedly recommend playing as much as you can in uninterrupted sessions, so you can immerse yourself the story, and feel like you're actually on the job. With all that said, if you're on the fence, get this game! One of my all-time favorites and my personal winner for horror game of the year so far! Thank you Team 17 for an amazing title!

It has everything.Teens, Adults, Murder, you're responsible for the well being of an entire town and it certainly feels like it.This is a lovingly crafted experience where nearly all of your dialogue choices matter. Gallow's Creak feels vibrant, and lived in, this makes every person whose life you're responsible for feel real and believable as a member of this tiny little backwater town.I really hope we get a sequel at some point, because this game is killer.

_childDocuments_.review: I downloaded Killer Frequency based on the description and a few screenshots alone on Steam, as well as the fact that it was apparently a horror game and it was late in the evening, and I was tempted to be scared at the time, which is an urge I'm sure some of you can relate to.The main thing that appealed to me instantly was the setting of the game. It was clear in the screenshots that you played as a radio DJ, and some part of the game consisted of running a show in first-person format. You know, announcing the songs, choosing the records, and coming up with cheesy banter with your producer. This has been a longtime dream of mine, so I was sold on the DJ simulation aspect alone.Killer Frequency does a lot of things right, and near or at the top of that list is the voice acting. All of the characters are relatable and engaging. This is a requirement based on how this game plays, functions, and intends to capture you through the narrative. If you've played this game, I'll challenge you to try to imagine it with just the subtitles and without the acting, and tell me something isn't lost. I found myself quite endeared to the DJ, Forrest, his producer, Peggy, and even the likes of Ponty of Ponty's Pizza by the end of the game. There's the odd character or situation that may break your immersion at times, but I think the game's narrative is partially at fault for this.Though the game's narrative is also at the top of my list for compliments, it just so happens that narrative is prone to a kind of tonal whiplash. I think this is somewhat of a necessary evil, though.See, the game is about a serial killer striking during a well-known prank night where people try to scare each other in the name of local horror myth and legend, The Whistling Man (this character is a clever construction because, as the name implies, his trademark is whistling, which can be heard over the numerous calls of the evening and early morning).The story starts with The Whistling Man killing the sheriff and several of the police at the local station, causing the local emergency operator to leave her post as she goes to find help. Subsequently, Forrest needs to field the 911 calls, as he is one of the few places in the small town equipped to handle them.So with this setup, a kind of paranoia seeps into everything. Is it all an elaborate prank? Can everyone you're talking to be trusted? Who is The Whistling Man, and what's their motive? You don't know if the next call you're going to answer will be a 911 call or a caller asking to place a request. And, in a well-directed sense, the game leans into this feeling.You'll get calls from potential victims, prank callers, and Ponty of Ponty's Pizza, trying to get free advertising. You'll play the most absurd ads during ad breaks and go from violent slashing to introducing the next song in your cheesiest DJ voice. The game also manages to walk the hard-to-balance line between comedy and horror. So that tonal whiplash is more like a feature than a bug.I found myself thinking of the mysteries involved, where they were going, and how everything would end several times in between play sessions. This is one of the highest forms of praise I can give to a piece of media in a world and time where so much is competing for our attention and how easily media can be forgotten.I love the aesthetic of the game. The graphics are cel-shaded 3D, which seems to hearken back to a pulp comic-horror style. Which is fitting because the game takes place in the chronological analog horror capital of "The '80s."The game's got a style I'd probably call something like horror vaporwave. I also love that almost everything that has a name is on-theme. You're on a radio station called "The Scream" in a town called "Gallows Creek." It has stores with names like "Price Slashers Groceries," "Little Shop of Flowers," or my personal favorite, the Mexican restaurant "Chalupacabra's."The game-play itself generally consists of three phases. During phase one, you'll be stationed at the DJ booth, awaiting a 911 call. This typically involves filling time with tasks such as playing ads and music, answering calls, engaging in conversation with Peggy, and throwing paper into the wastebasket from downtown.Then phase two is exploring the rest of the radio station, which is completely empty except for you and your producer. You're usually looking for something at this time to help a caller avoid an attack by The Whistling Man.This is where phase three comes in, and it is Killer Frequency at its best and at its core. You head back to the DJ booth and use all of the information at your disposal to guide a caller, hoping to save their life in the process. During these times, the game feels very tense. It feels like something akin to a hostage negotiation. You don't want to take too much time either, lest you give an alternate definition to the term "dead air."This calls back to my praise of the voice acting because it really shines in tense moments like these. It differs from the typical adventure game because you're usually giving instructions by proxy and, often times, not 100% sure if you're right and hoping for the best. And unlike other adventure games, when you're wrong, you don't always get a second chance.From here, the narrative and game-play play off each other, continuously reaching an inevitable climax. The game is, of course, a horror game. But I think the term suspense or thriller might be more fitting. Don't get me wrong, there are, without question, moments in the game that will have you on the edge of your seat. And the game knows how to slowly heat up the tension to a boil.The game intentionally has each scenario put you further and further out of your comfort zone, and it knows how to make the empty radio station feel like The Whistling Man is with you, watching you. Returning to the DJ booth always brings a sigh of relief after you rummage through who knows what, searching for a record, a crossword puzzle with a clue, or some other ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Killer Frequency also appears to be designed with some level of replay-ability in mind. You have various dialog options and choices, and of course, your decisions will have life-or-death effects on the town. The game has multiple endings, and I think the one I got was middle-of-the-road. It's a shame I probably won't have time to play through again to see what the best ending is. I recommend you save liberally because there isn't a chapter select.  Though I'm tempted to replay it, I'll probably just Youtube the better endings, making it only good for a single play-through for me.Without belaboring the point any more, I can give a strong recommendation to Killer Frequency. It's probably not for everyone, but if you like a blend of narrative-rich dark comedy and suspense, have ever imagined yourself as a radio DJ, or would like to see an interesting and exciting spin on the adventure genre, then I can't recommend it enough. And I think the story of the lost '80s horror icon, The Whistling Man, and the town that created him, will leave an deep and lasting impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my FIRST play through of this game and I don't always take the time to review something, but this game is worthy. Do you like campy horror? Do you like references to lots of other horror games and movies? Do you enjoy a good mystery? Give Killer Frequency a go. The game is very simple in its premise, you end up taking 911 calls in place of the local police dispatch during your radio show, which is silly, but it's great. Every character that calls in is memorable and unique and if you aren't able to guide them to the best possible outcome, you feel terrible. Even characters that aren't in danger you grow to love and hope you'll hear from again, like Ponty. Exploring the Radio station and trying to find all the records while unraveling the story is rather enjoyable and you want to check every nook and cranny for a chance of finding another interesting tidbit. My only complaint - I want to listen to the music more, haha. Every time Peggy told me "Wanna turn off the music now?" I was like, "NO PEGGY, OKAY, I'M VIBING".My first run through took about 6 hours and I looked through every thing I possibly could.
