_childDocuments_.review: In this 80's thriller game, you play both radio host AND detective! While taking control of calls and tunes, you are also controlling and aiding victims of the re-emerging urban legend, The Whistling Man. Using what you know, what is revealed to you, and what is discovered in your surroundings, you decide who lives and who dies! Killer Frequency has so many layers to it. It hits all of the marks while blending a beautiful combination of atmosphere and immersion with nostalgic music, refreshing art style, and in depth story that will leave you DYING to discover the truth. While it isn't all that scary, there are moments where the anticipation and dread is intense! It is replayable due to the fact that it offers multiple endings based on the decisions you make. For me, someone who has seen just about every horror movie known to man and played a lot of games in the genre, I did NOT expect the ending or what I was uncovering during my first playthrough.  To put it bluntly, I got this for free originally but ended up loving it so much that I purchased it on Steam and on my Switch! This is a game you definitely don't want to pass up! My only complaint is that I wish there was more games out there like this! This game leaves you wanting more, and after binging it to the end, I was so upset it was over!

_childDocuments_.review: You play as the radio host of a small town late night talk show in the 80s while a serial killer is on the loose. Due to circumstances, 911 calls are routed to you throughout the night and you need to help the citizens of the town survive the night (or not) until help arrives. I really enjoyed this one, it has a lot of tension at points, a few jump scares but not too many, and a lot of comedy. The voice acting is top notch, and only took about 5 hours for a playthrough. It did have some things I wish it could have done differently (like being able to respond to prompts not at your desk), but as a whole it's a phenomenal game with a fun story that was not too punishing and the puzzles are relatively easy to solve. If you want something light to play without too much thinking, and just want to enjoy the story, I highly recommend Killer Frequency.

If you are not into listening in conversations and learning the story from this way only, you should skip this game. Also, I saw a few review about this version of the game don't have the VR version, which is a bit shame.I really don't want to tell more about the game, because I would spoil something but in my opinion Killer Frequency is a surprising and really fun title for those who gets sucked in the base situation and they are okay listening in conversations. I can definitely recommend playing this game, 25€ is a bit overkill to me, but getting it around 8 - 10€ would be a steal.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency was such a fun little horror puzzle game to play during October, leading up to Halloween. The plot is simple but thoroughly enjoyable; it leaves the player guessing during their first playthrough and has a couple of twists to keep one on their toes. The art style and setting were fun to interact with. During my second playthrough, I'd turned the suspenseful horror show into a laugh-out-loud comedy with the use of the soundboard and Teddy Gallows' ad . The dialogue between characters seemed genuine thanks to the wonderful delivery of the voice actors, and it was neat to see the changes in said delivery that took place during my "worst" playthrough, where I killed everyone for my last remaining achievement. I have to say, playing as a darker, sarcastic Forrest Nash was something to be remembered. All in all, I played this game three times from start to finish and had a great time. If you're an achievement hunter, it is easily doable in two. It's a casual game, with uncomplicated puzzles, a single jumpscare , a plethora of characters and suspects full of colorful, comical personalities, a mysterious plot that takes the player through the history of Gallows Creek and its residents, all leading up to answers about what happened on that dreaded Whistling Night, many moons ago. It seems like the developers put a lot of thought, time, effort, and love into creating this game, and I truly hope they decide to make another similar in style in the future. _childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game. Not much more, not much less. Supposedly this game was intended for VR, but you can only get that verion on the Oculus store. If you have a headset, I'd probably do that. That said, you spend a lot of time sitting in one place just listening...I can tell this was optimized for VR...but kind of an odd choice for a VR experience.It's an engaging story and the voice acting was excellent. It was fun coming up with different timings and cues to DJ the radio show, but the puzzles weren't particularly complicated or difficult...they also weren't particularly explicit...there were quite a few where it really wasn't clear what the puzzle was...so I just started save scumming...which I hate doing. In hindsight many of the solutions became clear, but the game could do a better job of making the hints or context of the puzzle more obvious.The game has great vibes which is probably excellent in VR, I don't have my headset set up, otherwise I probably would have bought that version, but this was more than playable. It's really more of an interactive novel than it is a game, but if you like that kind of thing, I think you'll get a kick out of this. It's kind of like a Firewatch in a radio station. It's not as rich, nor as engaging, but that's the kind of "game" you'd be getting yourself into. If that's what you're into, I can recommend this game. Otherwise, I'd probably skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game on steam I was immediately intrigued for many reasons. The beautifully designed logo along with the charming almost hypnotizing draw of the 80s synth-wave. I'm gonna leave this review spoiler free as I highly recommend you play at on your home. The game is quite short, only taking around 4-5 hours to finish. You'd think this wouldn't give it enough time to quite get through but it manages to keep up the pace amazingly without feeling rushed and without feeling boring. Many of the calls you receive over the night will leave you at the edge of your seat with the not only  frightening puzzles and decisions but also with the amazing ( all be it a bit cheesy) voice acting and dialogue. The voice actors do an amazing job portraying each of their characters. Special kudos to Forrest's voice actor Josh Cowedry who really sells the "Fallen from grace celebrity". Because not only does the game let you follow the story of the town and it's killer but also you follow Forrest as he get a bit more humble which I personally find very endearing, and the back and fourth backtalk's between him and Peggy are just delightful. Forrest and Peggy's friendship have to be one of my favourite parts of the game, as it really sells them as real people. And the actual fear they have when being on call with the victims. The game may get repetitive according to some people but I personally didn't experience that. You start with just your recording booth and as the game goes on, you unlock new areas of the studio allowing for more exploration and scenery of this amazingly put together radio-shack.Now as far as replay ability  I wouldn't say the game is that repayable. Most of the games charm comes from that first play through but of course you can at least replay it once to get both endings. Which I do recommend. In conclusion, Killer Frequency a great game with amazing visuals, sound design and story writing. It's definitely worth is price and I'm looking forward to seeing what Team17 has to offer in the future.

The Whistling man is one of my newer favorite slasher characters in all of media right now and I wish this game got more praise then it already has because it definitely deserves it! I actually had a few moments where the game spooked me pretty good and hooked me onto the story with ease. I cannot recommend this game enough for everyone who enjoys horror and butterfly effect story telling. it was a real treat. Hunting all the horror references was one of the highlights and once again, the killer was amazing. This game was quite the Scream!

_childDocuments_.review: I always hate to look at a game like this, an ambitious indie title that was clearly already kind of stretching what their budget can do, and say "Man I wish there was more here" because that's just not a fair comment to make, but that's how I feel about this one. What's in the game is great and you should check it out but some of the puzzles and especially some of the setups and clues really feel like they could have been used more. As an example: there are huge maps of the city all over the place in the radio station and, given the nature of the game, I expected to be consulting the map a LOT more often than I actually did. Just things like that; what's here is great but I would've LOVED to see what this game could've looked like if it was 10 hours instead of 4.But still. Play it. It's fun. You'll solve interesting puzzles and meet interesting characters and hear some GREAT music.((And yes I know the plot of the game is written to justify it being 4 hours long and that 10 hours of gameplay would make the actual story feel kind of weird but that's beside the point))

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: I didn't finish the game. I think I need to point that out to be fair. Maybe I only finished the first half and the second half is the best game ever made. But unfortunately I have no desire to find out.I really wanted to like this. I enjoyed Firewatch and this gave me similar but cozier vibes. While this game is well executed and the concept is interesting, I just found it boring. I was hoping for a game where I slowly accumulate clues and start putting together a grand theory of solving the crime, all from the cozy atmosphere of a radio station. I wanted that feeling that Charlie Kelly felt when he discovered Pepe Silva while also making sure I'm keeping my listeners entertained. I wanted to get attached to a character so I felt some kind of stake in the universe. But instead, it seems like I got a half-assed radio-host-simulator between a series of mediocre, disconnected mini-games of no consequence while ankle-deep characters force you to press buttons to talk to them.While the radio host aspect was cozy, it left me feeling like I wished there was something more. There isn't really much there; you sometimes have to put a record on the record player (or a cassette in the tape player) and hit the play button. It seems like it doesn't matter which record you pick; it's just an inconsequential chore you have to do. It would have been cool if your choice of song actually mattered; perhaps if you pick a song that's relevant to the last caller, something good happens? I don't know, anything would have been nice. There's a mini basketball hoop across the room that you can mindlessly throw papers into. But to me this just felt like fluff to keep you occupied as a substitute for making the game more interesting. Which brings me to my next point.I found the core mystery of this game to be shallow and boring. I was hoping to have a list of suspects that I can narrow down over the span of the game, but instead I got a series of boring mini-games that don't seem to have any relation to each other. It seems like these scenarios don't give you clues, even when you complete them successfully. Maybe I'm an idiot and there's clues that went over my head, but it didn't seem like it. I put 2.5 hours into this game and I feel like I'm no closer to solving a crime than when I first started. This might be tolerable if the scenarios contained interesting problems, but even the problems themselves were mindlessly boring. I sincerely would rather do a crossword puzzle. What made it worse is sometimes the rules themselves were hard to understand. For instance, one of my characters died because I told them to go to a room that the killer already checked. How does that mean the character dies? It felt arbitrary and half-assed. Even for the problems I was successful in, it wasn't rewarding because they took no effort to solve -- most of the time it felt like I was just following a series of instructions off a piece of paper in front of me. I like problems where I feel like I'm forced to be creative or think outside the box to solve them. But I didn't find that in this game.I feel conflicted about the atmosphere because while it's aesthetically pleasing, somehow it's hard to get immersed into it. For one, there's some immersion-killing aspects of this game that don't make sense. While you're helping these people escape the killer over the radio, you think the killer wouldn't be tuned in on the night of their killing spree? There are ways that could be explained away, but the game doesn't even try. That kind of unrealism I can live with if it's all in good fun, but what makes it worse is that it actually works against you. There's a part where one of the characters verbally gives you a list that you need to memorize to complete the task successfully. What's the reason I can't simply ask them to repeat the list? I think if you're going to expect the player to memorize something, at least warn them in some way that they're about to part-take in some kind of memorization game. Even a simple "pay attention, because we don't have time for me to repeat myself!" would have been enough. But it leaves a really bad taste in my mouth when it seems like a game is trying to punish the players for simply zoning out for a few seconds (and with a game this boring, can you blame them?)Overall, the game has ok vibes and atmosphere, but that alone isn't enough to make me want to finish this game. If you want to play records in-between some mini-games, then this game is for you. But for me personally, I feel disappointed; on the outside, the game seems to have everything I like in a game, but I definitely didn't get $25 dollars of worth of enjoyment out of this. I don't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect. It is a 10/10 game from the audio, to the visuals, and to the feeling when the game scratches your mind and gives you unpromised shivers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.  It's a very unique take on the horror genre, with a great story and very entertaining characters. It took me just over 8 hours to beat, which really feels like the perfect length for the story.  Atmosphere is great, the story devices are great, the puzzles are fun and not BS. _childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game! You really feel like you're inside some slasher film. The gameplay and story were incredibly engaging. I wanted to find out who was behind the killings and save as many people as possible in the process. The atmosphere shifts between cosy (when you play music records, chat with a colleague or answer prank calls) and anxiety-inducing, when you explore the dark corners of the radio station or try to pick the correct line of dialogue extremely carefully, as one mistake will lead to your caller's immediate death. And voice actors did such a great job - you really root for all of the characters to survive this one long night. Overall - I would recommend Killer Frequency to everyone who likes narrative games, puzzles, crime stories and horror films. It's truly a unique experience and one of the best indie games I've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A really well considered, neatly presented and tidy little horror/puzzle game. Voice acting was excellent, the puzzles were good and there was a fun, campy, 80s B-movie tone throughout that really added to the character of the game. Very smartly designed and edited, doesn't feel like there's a wasted moment anywhere in this.Short enough to finish in an evening, very well executed theme and an excellent choice for Halloween; strongly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: This was so good.If this game looks familiar, you might have played the proof-of-concept release from a while back. It was a much simpler title, based on the idea of a radio host helping callers evade a serial killer with the aid of a town map. It was quick but creative and very fun. I had no idea it would ever grow into something more until I happened to see this game listed in the Steam New Releases. Killer Frequency is a ton of fun. It looks sharp, it's fully voice-acted, and it has a compelling, fun story with twists and turns to keep you guessing. It's the kind of puzzler where the puzzles don't just sit out on a table waiting for you to solve them. Instead, you have to piece together clues from dozens of lore documents scattered throughout the office building to assemble useful information for people calling into the radio station. There are elements from that earlier version of the title, but the full game includes much more than simply guiding people through a street map.Overall, this game is well worth full price. If you're looking for a creative, intuitive horror puzzle game with clear effort and love put into it, Killer Frequency is for you. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I usually watch let's players for horror games but I'm really glad I got too impatient and ended up buying this one to play myself! So much horror recently leaves me unsatisfied, with lack-luster sequel-bait endings or expecting 'deepest lore' to carry the lack of an actual preconceived narrative.This game is a full meal start to finish. A fun romp that doesn't leave any questions unanswered, but leaves just enough room for you to try and figure things out on your own before revealing its hand. Nothing too new for slasher lore but honestly there's not much new ground to tread there, so the game devotes that energy to the novel setting which I think was a good choice- You may know the slasher story but there's no media you can fall back on to assume what your role will be in that story now.I didn't find any of the puzzles too hard, but they weren't so easy I got bored, either. In one puzzle I actually got 'punished' for letting my guard down and not really thinking through all the 'clues' I had access to, but it felt fair and definitely made me second guess all the decisions in the future I assumed were 'easy'. I would have loved a few more segments that scratched that rare itch the cork-board segment did but I think the games difficulty was well designed for a fun experience.One caveat is that this definitely does have a lot of 'listening' segments as one would expect in a game about radio broadcast. I saw another review saying that as someone with attention problems they struggled because of it, and I can definitely see that happening as someone with ADD myself. It's such a small thing but the paper ball basketball 'minigame' worked perfectly for me and I really leaned into it. Had a few hundred baskets by the end.Jump-scared myself by accidentally knocking things off counters 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: What a crazy unique and insane game. 10/10 genuinely.I'm someone who hates horror and jumpscares but this one had to be played (it helped that my bestie recommended it to me and bought it for me). It barely had any true jumpscares but it had me tense the entire game.The lore was so fascinating and well thought out, the twists (while i could predict some) still had me reeling! The pace was perfectly built and every step was amazing. Genuinely, there's nothing I like more in a video game than profound and layered lore with little holes in it!The music? Great, catchy when in the studio and freaking terrifying in the basement and outside.The artstyle? Phenomenal. Literally gorgeous.Characters? 10/10, would die for Roller Ricky and Max. Plunker was also a surprising delight. Twists? Shaking in my boots with my jaw on the floor.Gameplay? Smooth as hell! For a point and click ish thriller game it felt soooo interactive and cool!Best part... TRASH CAN! The way i was so obsessed with throwing the paper balls. I'm very upset there was no achivements for it. I threw EXACTLY 200 into the hoop and I'm very proud of that.100/10 game must play!

_childDocuments_.review: So played this game, though missed out on the achievement to finish in 4 hours, bleh. It was actually pretty enjoyable, a lot more so than I'd have expected given the subject matter.I had no bugs. Graphics had no issues. Sound had no issues. All in all, very smooth. Though the art is good, there are a few things that standout for me:- This is something easy to miss, but the subtitles were very good. Font was very clear and easy to read, it had a good background behind the text that allowed you to read the text easily in all situations the game presented without actively blocking anything. I was very thankful for this.- The music is great, and I would buy the soundtrack in a minute if I could. This is the kind of music I really wish was in other games, especially after the trash music in Cyberpunk. This was such a nice change.- Dialog options were good and were often sort of what I was saying outloud, which was fun. - I feel three save slots are a bit few, but when I needed them they were there and I REALLY appreciated it. So many other games of this type block saves and require replaying entire chapters/sections. I was very happy to be able to reload the two times I needed.What I didn't like:- Peggy was sometimes annoying. I get she couldn't cut callers off, and I get WHY she was how she was... but, just as an existence she was annoying. - I wish we had a flashlight. I kept hitting F to try to light things up a bit. >_<- I wish we could skip ahead at conversations at times. When I already knew where I had to go and was being blocked by an invisible force bubble from exiting to the room - it felt like a time gate or something and was unnecessary. I understand not wanting 'speedruns', but just let me out. Bleh.All in all, a highly recommended game. The annoyances are exactly minor. The story was mildly predictable, but the annoying characters were appropriately recognized as annoying. The story puzzle comes together nicely. Would I play again to get the rest of the achievements? No. I don't think so as I don't want those endings, but I definitely enjoyed the full play through I had.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game to play, but it will set you down for a good few hours in the first run. Your other runs will be much quicker though should you decide to replay.Things I liked:- The great atmosphere and storytelling the game puts you in- The small details, such as Peggy's visible reactions to in-game events as they happen- The easy to use controls and detective style mindset- The amazing amounts of humour you can have if you mess up by shooting out an absolute satire one-linerThings I wished could be improved- Despite this being a game about radio hosts, the audio can be imbalanced, especially with Forrest being quiet- No chapter select- No dialogue skip for subsequent runs (I assume this is because of the speedrun achievement)- Other minor bugs (looping voicelines when played during autosave, songs/ads not recognised as being played before a voiceline finishes)A very solid game, the positives greatly outweigh the negatives. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to 189.16- The Scream, and I'm Forrest Nash.An immensely interesting and well voiced game, Killer Frequency is an absolute blast to play through. If you're aware of Do You Copy, this is very much an excellent spiritual successor, as you play a radio host who has to take 911 calls for the night and their fates are now within your hands. You'll be making critical decisions in life or death situations, determining who survives the Whistling Man and who falls. I love this game through and through, and even though your playthrough will average about 5 hours unless youre speedrunning for the achievement, i think the writing, voice acting, and dialogue is all superb enough to enjoy it. Every puzzle feels compelling and a good blend of difficulty and intuition, bar one puzzle involving a corkboard late in the game which i personally didnt really understand the solution to until it was pointed out to me. The plot feels logical and satisfying, and the twists make sense in hindsight and make you wonder how you didn't see it before.I would very much recommend this, it was a great game.

_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this a reluctant recommendation. "Killer Frequency" is a serviceable game, but I definitely liked the idea more than the execution. You play the host of a radio show who suddenly has to take on the role of a 911 operator, helping out the citizens of a small town survive encounters with a masked killer. Taking on emergency calls on live broadcast is a funny concept, but to be honest I think it deserved to be played straight. Playing up the absurdity is, to me, less preferable then straight-faced deadpan delivery. One thing that particularly frustrated me was the puzzles: the game creates the illusion of time pressure, but also forces you to solve puzzles that drag on for minutes on end. It quickly became obvious that the person waiting on the other end of the line would have wound up dead five times over while I was laboriously going over the reference materials and documentation. A more snappy pace would have worked better, I feel. All in all, "Killer Frenquency" is OK. Not great, but not terrible. If you enjoy the premise, you may give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: One word: tedious. I was really looking forward to this game, but it bores me out of my mind. I've been playing for three hours hoping I'd eventually find myself entertained, but I give up.The pacing: 15 minutes of slow, uninteresting dialogue, hokey "jokes", and theater kid "characters" before you're presented with a puzzle for a child. Ok, now it's time to leave the room... you know where you need to go. Nope, f-you, stay in the room while the last 30 seconds of dialogue play out about why you're doing the thing the game has already asked you to do.The voice acting: The acting is 97% of this game, and it is BAD. You play a "legendary DJ" who for some reason has absolutely no radio presence. He's tasked with handling emergencies by phone for the night, and has two total modes: 1) a REALLY bad attempt at "dj voice" and then 2) a cloying, sarcastic, annoyed regular voice actor voice. The callers are the absolute worst. Sure they got bit parts, and yes, it's supposed to be a little silly and corny to fit the motif, but you'll be begging for a skip dialogue button within 20 minutes.The puzzles: Anywhere between square-peg-square-hole games for toddlers to profoundly un-fun games of "guess what they must have been thinking".I really wanted to like this, but do not buy.

That makes it a really good intro to horror games, or for people who just want a spooky game but mostly G rated.Gamplay is straight forward. You basically play as a late night radio host in a small town who is attempting to solve the mystery of who the masked man is terrorizing the town. It's best to experience the story first hand and not be spoiled since it has linear gameplay moreso like a movie with controls. The experience is pretty short. _childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is exactly what you'd expect: a walking simulator version of an 80's slasher flick, where most of the action happens off-screen through victims-to-be calling in to your radio station.  Everything here is competently done, though nothing went beyond my expectations to move the game from good to great, for me.There are light puzzles, but once you've found the right clues, everything is pretty obvious.  The couple of times I was momentarily confused about how to progress, it was because I missed an interactable object in the environment which wasn't intended to be hidden, but I just overlooked it for some reason, and once I found those, I was smoothly back on the storyline.  There are no brain-burning logic puzzles here.A full playthrough is about five hours, and since it is unlikely that you will save all the victims in your first run, you may want to replay to get the achievement for saving all victims (and the alternate one for failing to save any victims), but personally I was satisfied with a single run, so if you are price sensitive in terms of hours for your money, take the length into consideration when deciding whether to wait for a sale.On the default graphical settings, I did experience some motion sickness.  This happens occasionally to me with first person games.  I took a break, and when I came back I tweaked the field of view as well as lowering the multisampling settings to get a higher frame rate, and after those changes it was no longer a problem for me.So, if the core concept of the game is appealing to you, and the content for price ratio not a deal breaker, I'm recommending.

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun, and I really did feel like I was solving a mystery! This is an excellent puzzle-forward interactive fiction adventure game, perfect for fans of retro horror. You play as a radio DJ who gets stuck manning 911 calls for the night when a serial killer is on the loose. Much of the game is based on choosing dialogue to help guide the potential victims to safety, so do be prepared to stand in one place for most of the game and click dialogue options to move the plotline forward.But in between those long sections of dialogue (which are very good, super interesting, and fully voice acted, by the way), you get to explore the studio and find clues that help you solve puzzles that lead you to solve the mystery behind this serial killer, how to help the victims, and how to (hopefully) survive the night. What I loved about this game is that you needed to actually pay attention, solve puzzles, and make deductions in order to get the best outcome. So many adventure games are focused on randomly trying things until you figure out what works, but this game features a series of distinct puzzles that feel more akin to what you'd do in an escape room--you really have to work out the answer on your own in order to progress the plot in a favorable way.I've played this game twice through already, and the dialogue tree feels pretty rich, giving you very different results when you do something wrong vs. when you do it right. There's a bit of leniency here and there, where your colleague will give you a chance to revise your answer if something seems horrifically off, but you can absolutely crash and burn by making the wrong choice. But what I love about this game is there are VERY few leaps of logic--if you're paying attention, the clues are all there! I missed a few things the first time through and just happened to choose the right answer on instinct, only to discover on a replay that all of the info I needed was totally in the game. I love all the attention to detail. Overall, it's just a great adventure gaming experience with a very well-composed story and sequence of puzzles... except for the fact that I really can't envision how most of these characters are able to be on the phone as they run from a serial killer in 1987. I guess technically some of the first cell phones were introduced around then, but... suspend your disbelief, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played only one play through so far, I have to recommend this game to anyone who loves 80s vibes, serial killers and the ability to hit keys on a soundboard at inappropriate times. Not only is it very immersive as a puzzle game, it hits all the sweet spots of horror without being too much. There's a very intricate mystery to solve, plenty of important choices - with sometimes startling consequences - and a really good chill to go up your spine. At the same time there's a lot of levity in the form of playing tunes, hoarding everything you can pick up at your desk and using a sound board to amuse yourself. The dialogue choices, along with the important puzzle choices, dictate tone and results in the game that feel true to their weight. You can be under pressure sometimes but nothing's too hard to solve. Just... make sure to examine your clues thoroughly so you don't end up answering a quiz with only half the data. Speaking from experience. #sorryscottI'll be playing through at least 2+ more times for achievements, so the replay value is already astonishing. It took me about 6-7 hours for one play through and so that's the one thing I have to say about this game: it isn't short, and you don't feel short changed. It seems to have a lot to go through and is well worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: I originally had no idea such a game existed. You see my morbid curiosity caught "Autopsy Simulator" in my radar. When I went to buy Autopsy Simulator I saw that for a little bit more money I could get the bundle which had Killer Frequency in it. I'm always down for a mystery thriller and was excited to try it out after finishing Autopsy Simulator.You play as Forrest Nash a radio host who with the help of his producer try and stop the WHISTLING MAN from claiming more victims. I was seriously impressed by the story that slowly unveiled itself over a 4 hour play through. The game makes you feel like you're never alone even when you think you are. The killers telltale is a haunting whistle that's drawn out and is quite unsettling. This game is not a run from the monster and hide but more of a psychological horror. It has a decent replay value not that I think I will be replaying it any time soon, but you may want to save more people knowing what you find out at the finale. I found it a bit of hilarity in joking with the producer when ever another victim was killed and turned to the soundboard to play a funny noise. I was surprised that it was not going to be all fun in games. The safety of you're station is taken away multiple times and you are tasked with exploring the building by yourself to figure out what is going on. Overall without spoilers I'd recommend if this is your slice of genre to go and get this game. Especially if its on sale as it's definitely worth a play through.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game since playing the original game jam version on game jolt 3 years ago and it didn't just meet my expectations, but it vastly exceeded them. Killer frequency EXCELS at crafting a tense, tight atmosphere where it really feels like every decision matters, and is overall an incredibly enjoyable game on every front. The main characters have a wonderful synergy and consistently interesting banter, the radio host idea is executed extremely well, and the game manages to be absolutely TERRIFYING in the moments you're given control outside of your radio booth. A good majority of the time I knew I wasn't in any real danger, but the excellent audio design made me feel completely terrified anyway. The game's only real flaws I've dealt with are the fact I had a caller die and had absolutely no idea it happened until the end of the game tally (And had no idea what I had done wrong in that encounter considering every other member of the group was alive) and that caller retention seemed to be very minor outside of a select few, however with how many branches the game's choice making has it's completely understandable. I played the game completely in one sitting and can't recommend it enough, and will definitely be playing again.Now please put the soundtrack for sale because I really want to throw my money at it!!!

I had so much fun when I originally didn't think too much of the game at all but the voice acting was amazing. Each phone call felt different. I actually felt suspense in it, and no, reader, i'm not saying you'll feel suspense but lemme say that I rarely feel suspense or fear in a game but this time it got to me. When you're walking around late at night at your radio station and its quiet, it'll get to you! I am however incapable of giving a really positive review without a complaint (that's how you know I LOVE it), we start off with a phone call from a police officer. I will be somewhat understanding that even police officers can forget stuff when stressed and scared but during the phone call it didn't make sense, it's like this character had no common sense. I get that the point of the game was us to tell each person what to do but she really didn't think! but yes, i love this game. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: There’s limited freedom to roam in "Killer Frequency", and not much to being a DJ, but the variety of gameplay kept me entertained and being an interim 911 operator sure is exciting, whether I played the hero or villain. Lives are very much at stake, but the great part is, you don’t need any action game experience to succeed. This is a more passive survival horror experience perfect for those who don’t like blood and gore, where all it takes is your brain and the ability to see solutions in all the clues provided. Every caller brings new elements that pose a challenge, but without being overly difficult. And even though you don’t see – or perhaps because you can’t see – what’s happening to the people in your care, there’s still a great buildup of tension. And it’s equally fun no matter which mindset you choose: being the grand savior is very rewarding and satisfying, but intentionally screwing up is just too tempting not to give it a go. I highly recommend it even to those who can’t bear to watch a horror movie – it’s perfect for a home-alone, late-night gaming session with the lights off and a bowl of popcorn at hand.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this one was excellent. it does a lot with very little; the Steam description is exactly what you get. You're a late-night DJ in a small backwater town, and have to use dialogue and research to save about half the town from crazed killer. Sometimes, you wander around the station and gather information or solve little puzzles to figure out how you'd do it. There's no action gameplay or platforming or anything like that, and mostly, it's just you and your very well voiceacted voice.The game practically drips with vibes. The soundtrack is great and as far as I can tell, custom made for the game, to emulate various styles popular in the 80s. It's also fairly replayable... once... because you  could also, if you're a sadist, make sure everyone dies instead.It took me about 6 hours to finish one way, saving everyone. Maybe that's a little bit steep for $25, but I think it's still worth getting. If it's on a sale or in a bundle and the premise interests you at all - or you, like me, are nostalgic for retro radio DJs and late night FM - then it definitely is.

While the voice acting direction can be a bit loopy at first, the actual quality of the performances are fantastic. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful indie discover.I had a lot of fun fitting the role of a radio host, who conveniently and against his will has to take on the role of a 911 operator at the same time, deciding the fate of the scared-to-death callers (and sometimes the prankcallers)... I never expected the atmosphere to work so well despite the fact that all of the violence and being chased by a serial killer doesn't happen directly to you. The puzzles are diverse, creative and you enjoy solving them under the pressure and knowing that the slightest mistake can cost the life of the caller. Shame that there probably aren't different versions of them so you could play the game multiple times. Peggy was a great sidekick to you, I just hoped the will be a little more of it, than just sliding the keys under the doors, but that's alright. The dialogues with her and the callers are niceely written and the voice acting is just as well performed on a level of an indie game, so another props to that. The visuals have a great style, the strong colorful lights from the neons outside just set the perfect vibe to it. I really dig this "Stranger Things" (retro/spooky) atmosphere, combining both comedy and horror at the same time, and this game got plenty of it. The studio itself is a pleasant environment, I enjoyed myself messing with the sliders, the soundboard, tape deck, swapping colored vinyl records on the turntable, exploring other rooms and just everything, maybe even more than the game itself wanted me to. (WHY IS THERE NO PAPER BASKETBALL ACHIEVEMENT??).. except all that, all I needed was a lava lamp and it would be perfect. In 5 hours you're done and it's absolutely worth it. Hope there will be another game like this, maybe even the KF2, I wouldn't be mad at all, it's a great concept that really could use more detailed mechanics.Plus there simply has to be the vinyl release of the soundtrack. Pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ please.

_childDocuments_.review: I used to co-host a late night local radio show, so maybe I'm biased, but this is easily one of the coolest and most unique horror games I've played ever, maybe. The fact it lets you manually fade in and out the music, load up tracks, play sound bytes and channel stings is so cool. I had an absolute blasting hosting my own little virtual radio broadcast while saving a small country town, one song request at time... and thats a level of detail and polish that the devs didn't need to include, but it does make the game significantly cooler! So huge props for that.The game has a really polished and pretty visual style, and it made great use of the its setpieces. Even though the entire game takes place in a single location, you really do get the feeling you're in the centre of a living, breathing town, gripped in the glove of a masked serial killer. Theres a lot of tension as you realise the killer is growing closer, and closer, mapping out the locations they appear at manually on a map of the town.Its also got incredible voice performances and audio that massively elevate the experience, literally every characters performance is good to excellent and it really sells whats going on. Essentially, think of this as an interactive horror audiobook with fun performances, nail biting puzzles and some genuinely gruesome consequences for failure. While not too scary, there are some fun intense moments and I think its honestly a really cool and accomplished experience that I would recommend to anyone that loves horror and wants something different from the standard fare.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles that make no sense- For example, the puzzle where the guy has to bait the killer by ringing telephones in different rooms and then slowly move through rooms while he's distracted to escape. The options for you to move, don't change based on which room you call first even though there are many other rooms to move to. You can be stuck with the worse possible options for no reason (forced to move to the room the killer is in or the room opposite the killer). - The maze directions making no sense. Saying to turn in one direction, and the guy on the other end has taken like 20 turns... its not even like following the road, taking every possible turn in the stated direction either. Makes absolutely no sense. The chemistry between the two main characters (you the radio host, and the lady working all the audio) was quite poor, which is pretty bad since you spend the whole game with those two. The jokes in general weren't funny either. Having unlikable main characters is one of the worst things you can do in a narrative. The premise is interesting, though the game didn't feel like it thought out how it was going to support that premise with its dialogue and tone. For example, right at the start with all 911 calls being rerouted to the radio show, the host still introduces each call like it is a radio call despite predominately receiving calls of people who are about to be murdered by a serial killer. This is a much more minor point, since I think its supposed to be light-hearted and whimsical but it definitely wasn't fully thought through. Another minor point but simple oversight is you can only carry two items at once, which can sometimes be annoying as you take multiple trips to gather all the relevant items. The graphics and whole look of the game look quite nice... that's about all the positives. Overall, I do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Went back and forth on this for a while, but I'm gonna say , due to the following:   Majority of the playtime is spent listening to conversations. Games are an interactive medium, and the older I get, the more I dislike experiences that take interactivity away from the player, through cutscenes, text, or conversations in this case. I suspect the devs recognised this issue, and added some dialogue choices, but these are rare and mostly inconsequential.   Some unintuitive puzzles. To its credit, one of the game's biggest strengths is the variety of puzzles, which aren't all bound by a single framework. The downside of this is that it's not always made clear how to work out the answers, and I felt frustratingly cheated a few times, which is the worst type of game; an unfair one. A single puzzle at a turning point around 3/4 of the way through, really cemented my thumbs - down. I think it's telling that 45% of players finished the game, yet only 18% nailed every puzzle (according to achievements). They all feel either dead easy, or unintuitive.   It's quite expensive given the experience it offers, even when on sale.In fairness, I enjoyed much of it, and it's a well - realised and presented vision. I'd go for a neutral / mediocre rating if Steam had it, but I think the '94% Very Positive' rating is quite misleading, and I was also bored for an equal amount of time, owing to all of the listening.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you play as Forrest Nash who moved to the small town of Gallows Creek after he left his job in Chicago. In a bizarre turn of events it turns out an old town legend known as "the whistling man" has began to kill again 20 years after his disappearance. The first victim is the towns sheriff, so her assistant needs to drive to the closest town for help. Sense all of the members of the police station are gone for the night you need to fill in for 911 and take in calls of desperate victims in need of help. It feels really fun playing as Forrest who's just trying to adapt to his new job and save callers from the town. All of the puzzles are unique and fun in there own way. I really enjoy the graphics as well, its like if borderlands was a horror franchise. The music to this game is outstanding and by far the best part of the whole game. It really feels like music that was made in the 80's. The dialogue is witty and fun, although a few jokes did fall flat for me. The game is decently scary thorough the whole game. When your not trying to save callers who are desperate for help, your exploring more creepy areas in the old radio station. The game is pretty long (taking me 5.2 hours to beat) and super small at only 2 gigabytes required for the whole game. I would give this game an 8.5/10 and if your looking for an entry to the horror franchise I absolutely 100% recommend this game. But if your a horror veteran looking for something extra spooky that will make you cry yourself to sleep, I would recommend something else. But if your looking to have a great time than this game is an excellent choice.

_childDocuments_.review: As you can see from the number of hours I've played this game... I'm in LOVE! It's been years since I've played such a satisfying mystery that filled me with urgency, fascination, and a feeling of accomplishment. Most mysteries nowadays tend to be over-complicated(with gotcha endings), filled with ghosts, cheap horror tropes/scares, and use poor lighting the whole time to make the environment tense. While these horror/mystery games are classic and have their place, with the space being so saturated with such games, this one is such a fresh breath of air. It is RARELY dark during the game, and when it is, it's intentional. KF relies heavily on its storytelling to frighten you. The environment itself felt cozy, but the serial killer on the loose disrupts that feeling and makes it eerie and unsettling all the time. The Live Studio with Peggy is one of the only places in the game I felt was "safe".The voice acting was hilarious and perfect for a 1980s slasher film-inspired game. I've seen some people criticizing it, and as welcome to their own opinions as they are I've noticed many of them haven't even finished the game (speedrunning the game takes at least ~4hrs to finish and many only played  ~1.7hrs). As long as you understand the inspiration behind the game, it's exactly as expected and better.I found myself playing this game over and over again just because I wanted to spend more time with the characters. They're just wonderful, and all of them felt unique.The game's puzzles were unique to each other, and many involved different skill sets to solve. None of them (in my opinion)were the annoying shape/number escape-room-esque type, which made me very happy. I felt like everything we were doing to problem solve was intentional and fairly realistic. They(the characters) used what they had at their disposal to do the best they could for their community/callers.The atmosphere was masterful! I wish I could work at KFAM honestly(minus the Whistling Man of course XD)! Totally modeling my at-home office after it. As an aspiring game dev, I hope I can one day make a cool mystery slasher game like this that mainly uses its riveting, gripping story to affect the player's emotions, and has the environment as simply a beautiful tool to help bring that story to life, just like Killer Frequency!

_childDocuments_.review: In Killer Frequency, you play a big-town radio DJ playing to a small town, on a night where a masked murder comes back to seek revenge. There's a paperball-basketball mini-game in the studio, and you will be hitting that during the long, repetitious "what's" being repeated by the DJ and his producer. Despite the less than fun gameplay experience, there IS a good story here, with an awesome setting and visual style, and there were moments that made me genuinely laugh out loud. The scares are pretty weak though. Buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Intro:Killer Frequency by Team17 is a unique blend of horror and mystery, set in the late 1980s. The game places you in the shoes of a radio DJ who must help callers survive a night of terror as a serial killer lurks in the shadows. Pros:- Immersive Atmosphere: Killer Frequency excels at creating a tense and immersive atmosphere. The late-night radio station setting, combined with the eerie soundtrack and ambient sound effects, keeps you on edge throughout the game.- Engaging Puzzles: The game’s puzzles are well-crafted and require critical thinking and quick decisions. As the DJ, you must guide callers to safety by solving clues and piecing together information in real-time, which adds a layer of urgency and excitement to the gameplay.- Strong Voice Acting: The voice acting in Killer Frequency is top-notch, bringing the characters to life and adding depth to the narrative. The DJ’s interactions with the callers feel genuine, making you care about the fate of each character as the night unfolds.Cons:- Limited Replayability: While the story is engaging, the linear nature of the game limits its replay value. Once you’ve solved the puzzles and experienced the narrative, there’s little incentive to play through the game again.- Short Playtime: Killer Frequency is relatively short, While this makes for a tight, focused experience, which may make some people reconsider paying full price- Lack of Variety in Gameplay: Although the puzzles are engaging, the gameplay can feel repetitive after a while. The game mainly revolves around solving similar types of puzzles and guiding callers,.Closing & Rating:Killer Frequency is a chilling and unique horror experience that shines with its immersive atmosphere and engaging puzzles. I personally think it is well worth the time and money to play and lives in my mind rent free. It’s a killer choice for a night of suspense, but you might find yourself tuning out after the first playthrough.Rating: 9 out of 10 records. 🎧

_childDocuments_.review: Mystery investigation in a radio station. You are the host of a show one night and everything goes south when a killer appears. You make choices and try to save people and solve the case. The game is played from first person perspective and you have some abilitiy to interact with many of the objects in the world. You solve puzzles and explore the radio station, piece by piece.It is hard not to think of Firewatch when playing this game. The graphics are similiar and suffers from the same problem of telling, instead of showing. There is too much handholding in this game for my taste, but I think it is still worthwhile. Some of the puzzles are pretty good and fresh, while others are hardly puzzles at all. The voice acting and sound effects are good, but some of the dialogue is hammy and could have been removed without making the game worse. You do alot of listening in this game and there are some funny moments and some moments that tries to be funny.  The game took about 5 hours to complete the first time. You might want to play again to see some other ending or get an achivement, but there is not much replayability. TL;DR: Firewatchesque radio murder mystery with some puzzles. Given everything I have written, I will still recommend this game for people that enjoy investigation games. There is no hurry to play this so make sure to buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: My best description of this game would be: "interactive podcast". I expected a walking simulator, but there's just not much gameplay. The dialogues are great, the atmosphere feels spooky, and the story makes sense (if far-fetched), but the game felt really long because of the lack of action. Overall, I'm happy I played, but not sure I recommend it unless you like podcasts.

_childDocuments_.review: A horror puzzle game where you're tasked with helping 9-1-1 calls that are being fed through your late night talk show? Conceptually it's a pretty interesting game. Unfortunately, while I really wanted to like the game, it falls flat in it's execution. For example, the game is audio based (due to the phone calls) and while that grips you for the first two 9-1-1 puzzles, after that the game really starts to show how slow it moves from moment to moment. Make a choice, wait for the results, have the characters make some sort of "witty" banter-- then rinse and repeat. The tension felt like too much of a slow burn for the horror aspect to be captivating, and the story felt obviously inspired by 80s slasher flicks making a story that's pretty corny when I really wanted it to spook me.TLDR; Rough experience, could be way scarier and faster paced (5/10)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an actual IRL Radio Personality that has worked in small/medium/large markets with 3 decades of experience. (And I'll say I recommend this game, it's a blast)I'll focus on the small market because holy moly this hit really close to home.Few of the misses: Small town late night show wouldn't have a 2 person crew, it'd be the DJ only to save $$$. Also, knowing "about 35 listeners" would be pretty rare, didn't seem like they had competition so odds are they wouldn't be paying for the analytics with no local competition... but this is nitpicking no big deals.Wondering where a few folks got their phones to call in, especially in the Maize Maze.  I've had businesses just like Ponty... and have taken some of the weirdest phone calls so this was spot on.I'm happy there wasn't a specific state this was located in, I had Ohio/Illinois/Indiana vibes but those call letters would've started with a W instead of a K. (East v West of Mississippi...weird fun fact for y'all)There's a few other bits I'd nitpick but it's a video game, and a fun one at that. Fun story, great horror references. The puzzles are a hoot...also I'm amazed how well a video game actually uses real First Aid information and not the usual flubbing that games do. Lot of love went into this game.The fact you can save/lose everybody is fantastic, love that it is not just a hard game over, and thank you save states! Only a few timer/quick moments really helps as well, and jumpscares are at a minimum! Love it. Is my type up of this all over the place? Yes. Should I re-do it? Probably. Am I going to? Nah.Just pick the game up. It's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a super neat indie game that puts you in the shoes of a late night 80’s radio DJ in a small town that’s being plagued by murders. Seeing that you’re the only one available and qualified to take calls, you're tasked with answering 911 emergencies when the police department becomes indisposed of. As a rogue whistle-happy killer descends on the town it’s up to you and your producer Peggy to use your wits and quick thinking to solve puzzles, suss out lies, stop the killer, and ultimately lead people to safety as you simultaneously put on an equally killer radio show. The gameplay mostly consists of choosing dialogue options while at your desk, inspecting clues, and occasionally going outside your room to explore the radio station or retrieve an item.The radio layout is delightfully comfy, and the DJ setup is fun to interact with. I do wish they leaned more into it. Implementing some more radio mechanics and giving more to do than clicking the call button and putting on records would have been ideal. Not to say it should have been a realistic simulator game, just a bit more underlying connection to the actual work of a radio DJ is all. The soundboard was a start, but entirely cosmetic and easily forgettable. What we did get I loved, but it left me wanting slightly more, indie game or not. Even without that though Killer Frequency did a good job of immersing you into the mind and world of late-night hosting. It’s less a dysfunction of the game’s offerings and more so my own desire to get greater engrossed in the world.I’m particularly impressed by how Killer Frequency is able to instill a sense of persistent isolation, with all the lone wandering you do around the station ratcheting up the tension effectively. I especially like the pace in which it slowly reveals more and more questionable parts of the locale in an organic way, going from benign to increasingly sinister. All in the purview of a small radio station at the dead of night. Each room is a new place to investigate, even letting you find hidden records and clues early if you look hard enough. In its totality the game is neither big nor a Sherlockian challenge, but it does a great job at making you feel like it is. Barring one exception, the game is remarkably proficient at hitting above its expectation in mood and pacing. We’ll get to that exception in a minute.The story, writing, and voice acting give light to the rest of the game, making it more of a dark comedy soup than a horror title. The actual mystery and killer themself are given a proper breadth of seriousness, but folks like Ponty of Ponty’s Pizza and jazzy Sandra are there to break it up with some much welcome comedy. That’s to say the game is legitimately superb with its comedic timing, and quite well voiced all around. Every character knows when to be silly and when to be serious. It never feels kitschy or ill-timed, playing perfectly into the 80’s over-the-top slasher aesthetic. The dialogue choices also let you play into the comedy or go for a more straightforward approach, giving you a degree of control over the tone of the story. Of course that doesn’t mean the dialogue options are superficial, you’re just not punished for making light of the situation unless you’re doing so during a time-sensitive choice.The actual bread and butter of the game, its puzzles, are just the right amount of accessible. One could argue they hold your hand a little too much in finding clues, but you’re just as likely to find them beforehand anyway, and you could always decide to not accept hints for where something is. The puzzles themselves range from straightforward to moderately tough, a scope that works well here. Thankfully, you’ll never be asked to memorize something unreasonably long or constantly make timed choices, but I’d advise reading everything twice to make sure you’re getting the full picture. A lot of choices come with hidden caveats and clues that can be easy to miss, and in a game where every choice may be life or death it’s important to dot your i’s and cross your t’s.This leads me into the only disappointment I had with the game. All throughout the game there’s a constant invisible threat of the killer showing up on your doorstep. With little to defend yourself with and having to venture out further and further away from your safe broadcast room, it’s all but spelled out this would lead to confrontation eventually. I thought for sure there would be at least one tense situation where you’d have to evade the killer as you sneak from hidden corner to hidden corner. There were more than a few clear moments where this could happen near the end but the time never came. The focus on dialogue and puzzle-solving is fantastic, yet I really think they missed an excellent opportunity to capitalize on the tension building with a little one-on-one traditional encounter.Nevertheless, when push comes to shove the strengths of Killer Frequency far outweigh its weaknesses. While it won’t take longer than a day to finish it’s more than worth the pickup. I finished it in one marathon sitting around the same time of night the game takes place, no doubt helping immerse myself even more into the world. Truly all you need to have a good time is an appreciation for groovy music,

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 8/10I've been reviewing a lot of stuff accessible at my level of content creation, which means a lot of indie horror.  On top of that I play a lot in my own right.  This game while sitting firmly in the Thriller side of horror  Overall this goes into my highly recommend category.  Definitely fitting more into the visual side of video games  I will be going into SPOILER-ISH territory in the following.You take the shoes of Forrest a fallen big time radio host in the year 198X.  Being moved to a small town after an unnamed scandal he is paired with the chipper Peggy as his producer.  A murder occurs and its revealed the towns legendary serial killer the Whistler is possibly back from the grave.  Events turn and leave Forrest and Peg as the replacement for the 911 dispatch.  The bulk of the story is you guiding people to their success or demise at the hands of the Whistler as you uncover the story of this small town.Graphically the game has a great aesthetic doing fun stuff with the neon 80s vibes.  The voice acting is on point and the levity in which the situation is handled is very well balanced.  There are definitely parts that made me cackle, Ponty might be the best written and voice acted character.  Seriously some of the funniest tension breaks I've ever seen in a game.  Gameplay wise the game was designed with VR in mind which I wouldn't have known playing on mouse and key though I've heard gripes from controller users especially in the switch port.  Puzzle elements if you want to even call them that are very light and mostly come down to reading information and answering appropriately.  As stated earlier this is much more close to a visual novel than a true puzzle adventure game, with minimal collectibles.  None of this is to a detriment as everything is paced out very well and the game actually seems to unintentionally remind you to take breaks every couple hours as Forrest is encouraged to stretch his legs.All in all one of the best indie experiences I've had recently, even though I received the key for this due to my work I think I will pick up a physical copy just to have for collectors purposes and to support the creation of such a good piece of media.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic interactive story in a unique style. If you like mysteries and story games, this one is a good choice. It has a very cozy 80s atmosphere that's perfect for some late night gaming.  7.5/10It's a murder mystery game, played from the perspective of a radio host in the studio, gathering information by carefully questioning callers. It's pretty linear, each caller is like a puzzle that needs to be solved with the end result being whether they live or die.The puzzles are pretty simple, a lot of the time you'll just have to rely on intuition, there's room for error, I only ever felt like I was rolling the dice on an option twice in the whole game, and while it did annoyingly get two people killed, it wasn't a big deal. When you're not relying on intuition you're usually exploring the studio for bits of info that might help the caller like a magazine or a set of notes, and from there it's a pretty standard puzzle, nothing complicated.The plot is fairly predictable if you're paying attention, if you're a fan of the mystery genre it shouldn't be hard to solve the mystery as you go along, but regardless of your experience you should take note of the hints that come to you, if you're not following the plot after the first 70% or so you might run into questions you don't have the answers to. Gameplay wise if you're expecting something like Not For Broadcast you'll likely be disappointed, the most you do with the radio is pause and unpause the record player and occasionally play an advert and get a handful of song requests. There's a soundpad but they're purely for your own entertainment, they have no affect on the game.Overall it's very story focused, you have a map board that you'll use sparsely, I checked it often just to mark where calls were coming from but you only really need it a couple times in the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been really fun to play and also very challenging with some of the puzzles, the story line for kill a frequencyIs very old school slasher vibes and also being quite unique as well.If you are a big fan of slasher movies and puzzle/ story games then this is definitely the game for you.Also might take A few play through's of this game, if you like collecting achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let Max and Roller Ricky die genuinely one of the worst character deaths I've seen in a video games.  Also the hard carry of this whole game has to be Forest Nash (played by Josh Cowdery) his dialog is one of the only bits of comedy that doesn't fight with the overall theme.  Peggy has a very short bit of saving dialog and is arguably the easiest to kill or save without realizing what happened.  Another weird part of Dialog is the saving of Max and Ricky as it is really hard to tell that what you should do is the opposite of what you first believed.  Murphy was a great additional character that had great dialog and was interesting for his whole sequence.  Its easy to hate our living plot device Marie Campbell and her son but Teddy Jr is also a very easily hated character with him being the reason the killings happen again 20 years later.  I was sad when I realized that only Katherine could save Murphy but its not any major issue.  John Hedges is easily my favorite character who assists you in saving Jason for a reason that is not biased by his name.  All the songs match the feeling of being a late night radio host perfectly and the credits song is a great way to close out all the great tracks.  I love having the ability to build up my office with all the thing i find on my searches outside of the studio.  This game was great sober and i could only imagine a first play through would have been greatly improved if I had the foresight to drink but I likely would have ended up with no one surviving and not the other way around.  To finalize my thoughts, the game is exciting never jump scares you always gives you an eerie feeling and you will always be looking for the next major plot twist.  R.I.P. Clive and Forest Nash is the best radio host this close to nowhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game at the recommendation of a friend who knows I like 80's styled games. I'm a retired 911 dispatcher, and I have horrible PTSD. I can't hear a call, interact with police, etc. without getting incredibly agitated and having a mental health emergency. So I play video games to relax and distract myself, but I avoid any sort of material of that nature. My friend really dropped the ball, since you have an incredibly poorly voice-acted 911 dispatcher that calls into the radio station for an extended sequence. There were a massive amount of inaccuracies that really made the story unbelievable and ridiculous (911 centers are hard-lined with back-ups that automatically roll over to the next closest place, they can't be forwarded to just any phone line), but I was just trying to tough through that sequence to get to the game itself. Then the actual gameplay is you being a substitute dispatcher. The parts where you're wandering or exploring the office are the best parts, and effectively scary. It's a super cliché story, with overly elaborate voice acting, aside from the male lead. Music was great, environment was even cool when you explore it. This would be a good game if you're a younger person, into light true crime detective adjacent stories, or are looking for a short VR experience. Also, I can absolutely destroy anyone with a single galvanized trashcan lid, let alone two. So that initial reveal made me call BS before I even got to the title screen. Hard pass if you are a dispatcher, retired, or know one, because it's immersion-breaking in a way that can't be overlooked.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cool. It's very fun to play blind, so I will spoil as little as possible. The whole game is pretty much done without seeing what's actually happening, and it does an amazing job at taking full advantage of this by letting you figure things out and piece things together that might not be visually obvious. The dialogue options will often become more and more important as the gameplay progresses, and you'll almost always have more reasons to select any given option by the end than just what you feel like saying. It uses the dialogue and audio medium to its fullest potential.In terms of flaws, the game is a little odd in that it all takes place in one night, meaning anything you do to the station will still be that way, which does not mesh well with the ability to pick up objects very well. Often items that were important become harder to find if you moved them at all. Also, the game often requires you to have a lot of information to make good decisions when it's hard to tell if you have everything you need. You often are expected to go fetch things, but don't know exactly what, or how much you need, and the fetching itself can just be grueling.Overall though, this is a super well-thought out and designed game that evidently has a lot of passion and effort put into it. Many of the dialogue options actually have a pretty big impact, even if it doesn't look like it, so this isn't necessarily a game you'll just want to watch a playthrough of online in my opinion, it feels incredible to actually experience the consequences of your actions.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency was an unexpected gem that left me completely hooked from the get-go. The captivating story took me on a wild ride, surprising me at every turn and keeping me on my toes. The graphics were delightful, adding to the immersive 80s theme that made me feel like I'd traveled back in time.Being a radio host in the 80s was a dream come true, and the unique point of view made the experience all the more special. The game struck the perfect balance with its intricate puzzles, challenging enough to keep me engaged without becoming frustrating.The isolation factor was a stroke of genius, focusing the action in the radio station and the nearby alleyway, creating an intense and atmospheric setting. The memorable side characters, especially the quirky bloody Ponty and his pizza place, added depth and charm to the game. The music in Killer Frequency was a standout feature. The nostalgic tunes perfectly complemented the 80s theme and left me yearning for the original soundtrack. The horror elements were expertly executed, providing just the right amount of scares to keep me on the edge of my seat.Kudos to Team17 for another fantastic game! The voice acting and sound environment were top-notch, immersing me further into the game's world. The dialogue options, akin to those in Telltale's The Walking Dead, offered diverse endings that added to the replayability.While there are some minor downsides, such as the initial price being a tad high and the story being on the shorter side, Killer Frequency's overall experience more than compensates. The desire for a sequel or DLC speaks volumes about the game's appeal.All in all, Killer Frequency is a groovy adventure that ticks all the right boxes. If you're a fan of 80s nostalgia, thrilling stories, and unique gameplay perspectives, this game is a must-play. Just keep an eye out for a sale to get the best bang for your buck. I can't wait to see what Team17 has in store next!

_childDocuments_.review: "Killer Frequency" stands out as an exhilarating and unique gaming experience that masterfully blends suspense, mystery, and interactive storytelling. This game captivates right from the start, offering an adrenaline-fueled journey that keeps you glued to the edge of your seat.The game's narrative is a high point, engaging players with its compelling mystery and interactive elements. You're constantly challenged to piece together clues, adding an addictive layer of problem-solving to the gameplay. The game mechanics are straightforward and intuitive, allowing you to immerse yourself fully in the unfolding story without unnecessary complexity.Visually, "Killer Frequency" is a feast for the eyes. The game's design and graphics are exceptional, with meticulous attention to detail in the environments, making you feel like you're the protagonist in a high-stakes thriller. The sound design is another highlight of the game, with a soundtrack that amplifies every suspenseful moment. The audio immerses you in the game's world, enhancing the overall experience significantly.One of the game's most appealing aspects is its replayability. With numerous paths and choices available, each playthrough offers a fresh and engaging experience. The joy of discovering new secrets and outcomes is a major draw, encouraging multiple playthroughs.The voice acting deserves special mention for its quality, despite the large cast of characters. Characters like Roller Ricky and Max are particularly memorable, making you genuinely care about their stories as they unfold over the phone. The puzzles in the game are logical and satisfying to solve, contributing to the game’s overall enjoyment.Gameplay in "Killer Frequency" is simple yet effective. The basic mechanics include walking, picking up items, and selecting dialogue options. This simplicity ensures the focus remains on the story and player choices, rather than complex gameplay elements.The achievement system in "Killer Frequency" is well-thought-out, with most achievements offering a sense of accomplishment. However, some achievements, like getting everyone killed, can be emotionally challenging, adding depth to the gameplay.In conclusion, "Killer Frequency" is more than just a game; it's an immersive experience that combines mystery, suspense, and interactive storytelling in a way that is both engaging and entertaining. Whether you're a fan of thrillers or looking for a unique gaming experience, "Killer Frequency" is an absolute must-play. It's a testament to the power of audio-driven storytelling in video games, making for an unforgettable adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets horror done right.  It sets up an absolutely wonderful atmosphere that lets the game speak for itself.  As a child of the 80's, this hits especially hard in the nostalgia.  The music was great, the ambiance was VERY good, the dialogue was a bit cringe, but it wasn't terrible.  The game follows particular tropes, and some of the tropes that you expect to happen, it flips on its head and just lets your mind do the spooky stuff.  Horror doesn't need to be hack and slash and gore.  Get the atmosphere right and the rest falls into place.  This game NAILS that on the head, so VERY well.  Score? At least a 7/10.   Pretty good, would absolutely play again.  Recommendation though - try to play it through a single sitting if you can.  The story is best experienced in this fashion.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this was a great game.The narrative was great, exploration was good too and the story was really good. Gameplay is mostly talking to NPCs, a few light puzzles and a lot of character development while trying to figure out what's going on. The story was done really well as were the characters. You really ended up liking Peggy and felt both the playable character and Peggy were written to compliment each other very well.
