_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a really good story rich horror game, now then the story. It has been a week since famous radio show host Forest Nash’s career blew up and he was forced to take the job of a small radio host in the quiet and sleepy town of Gallows Creek, fortunately for Forest he has been doing quite well and has been settling in thanks to his co-host Peggy and the rest of the staff at KFAM.Now for tonight show Forest was going to host the contest guess that scream, a nice silly game to win two tickets to the annual corn maze but soon the station gets a call from 911 dispatch, the sheriff is dead and it looks like an old evil the whistling man a serial killer from the '50s has returned.But now the 911 dispatcher has left Gallows Creek in order to get reinforcements and all 911 calls have been directed to the station, so it's up to Forest and Peggy to save Gallows Creek, in a show that's going to be a real scream.Okay the likes, the story is absolutely fantastic it's a kind of spooky yet kind of cozy story that you can just settle down with a nice drink. It has an interesting premise, a good mystery, an interesting killer and well written characters, it also has very good jokes/wordplay, plenty of funny moments and a lot of great references to classic works of horror from Friday the 13th to Killer Klowns from Outer Space.The characters are all really fantastic each one quite distinct with an interesting personality, even if they're just callers probably my favorite characters has to be Nash he has the right balance of sarcasm without being a jerk and Ponty of Ponty's pizza that guy was such a delightful jackass. The whistling man is really good; he's quite menacing and has quite a memorable and stylish look with his jacket, the creepy mask and the hair, as well as the whistling. The comedy is very good sometimes it's clever wordplay like the name Roddy Snatcher or Church of Jason, to just the funny interactions with the characters like Ponty being a quite funny running gag.The graphics are really good it has a beautiful shell shaded look with a great use of colors, scenery and character designs and designs that makes everything just stand out. The levels or level in this case is quite good, the station is richly detailed that it feels like a real station from its designs, the '80s decorations and set pieces, each one is quite distinct and memorable.The gameplay is very good basically you play as a radio host and your main objective is just answer calls and guide the collar to safety with either giving them directions, giving them suggestions on what to do or even just distracting the Killer, each call feels like a puzzle, you also have to play songs and such it all makes you feel like a real radio host. You also have to solve the mystery of who the whistling man is, so not only you're playing as a radio host, a rescuer but also an amateur Detective too, but it's all really well balanced without one aspect overshadowing.The voice acting is fantastic each voice actor definitely brought their A-game you may even recognize a few of them, I think the best ones were for Forest Nash you may recognize his voice from playing the main character in the Beast inside, Peggy and Ponzi of Ponzi's pizza were also vary good. The music is absolutely fantastic  with an incredibly good tracks that fit the game so well, probably the best track is the ending song it's really good to the point I wish it was longer.Okay the dislikes, now as you know this is the part where I talk about the dislikes, but honestly this game is absolutely perfect its one of the few games I can't really think of anything to really dislike about this game.Alright then now that I have told you all this Killer Frequency is a really good story rich horror game, it has an absolutely fantastic story, really fantastic characters and very good gameplay. So I absolutely recommend this game and I really hope the creators of this game either make a sequel or spin off.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a masterpiece.The story is phenomenal and really hooks you in. The story is told in such a way that it's not all told to you flat out, it's told in a way that has you work to find answers and takes a lot of twists and turns to try and stop you from figuring out the truth. The gameplay here is really simple; answer questions, play records and save lives. The gameplay relies more on your problem solving skills more than anything else. This can be both a positive and a negative in games but in Killer Frequency, it's absolutely a positive. Having to think about how to save lives and use objects in the environment to help you problem solve is so fun, it allows you to take a moment before answering to make sure that what you picked was the right option.The game doesn't really have much replayability outside of achievements, unfortunately. I really wish this game had some sort of incentive to replay it outside of achievement hunting. I really wish this game had some sort of side mode or additional gameplay tweaks to make every experience fresh. I would absolutely kill for some DLC for this game, just saying.Killer Frequency is a game that you have to experience blind and it's a game you can only play once every couple of years. It's more than a game, it's an experience. It's an experience that everyone should have. Buy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever played another game that relied so purely on real world judgment and skills while still being fun. It would be interesting to see more like this. The other thing I really appreciated is how Killer Frequency balances tension with its more relaxed silly moments between saving people- I feel like it would be tempting with a game like this to make it all tense all the time, but the silly moments make it so much more playable.The only issue I had is that the controls feel rather clunky. You can only have one object in each hand and you can only use the object in your right hand, so I was always a little afraid that I would fail something important based purely on a necessary object being in the wrong hand. This added to the tension, but it didn't seem very intentional or immersive.Speaking of immersion, it is awfully convenient that you get basically infinite time to search for useful information in the office. I appreciate this as something that makes the game more accessible, but I think it would be cool if maybe there was an optional mode where there was a time limit on finding things and overall getting through dialogue during the emergency calls.Anyway, I definitely recommend Killer Frequency. Given that it doesn't demand many gaming-specific skills, it could be a fun one to show your older, non-gamer family members if you're into that.

As a radio host, you have to act as the town's emergency line to accept calls from people who are being attacked by a serial killer. Solving puzzles will help you guide victims to safety, and can reward information on the killer. _childDocuments_.review: This game looked very promising with very good reviews, though I cannot say that I agree with most reviews. I really love the aesthetic of the game, these visuals however cannot make up for the absolute lack in story and dialogue. As some other people have pointed out, this game tries to balance horror and comedy and manages to fail in both aspects in my opinion. Most calls with the victims who are about to be murdered have people trying to hide but then talking with you while they would likely be in or close to earshot distance from the killer, describing everything they are doing in minute detail which also feels like a very lazy and unsatisfying way of storytelling. There are no real time limits for the puzzles, you are told to find something around the office to help the current caller but can take literally however long you wish to find these things - even though the caller is supposedly in mortal danger. The most egregious thing about the game that basically completely ruins the immersion for me is the fact that your character knows that people are literally being murdered right now and that he is the stand-in for the 911 operator, but still opening every call introducing himself and the radio show as if it's a normal Tuesday afternoon, sometimes not even mentioning that he is the stand-in for 911, causing people to waste more time being confused of reaching some random radio-show. You can literally hear people being murdered on the other end of the line and your character and your partner are shocked for about 10 seconds, but as soon as the call ends they are basically like "Too bad for that guy." and continue with their banter/jokes between themselves and playing music or ads on the radio. Some of the jokes like the calls from Ponty's Pizzeria are fairly decent but it simply does not do enough for the experience.I do believe that this game had potential to be a thrilling experience with a unique gameplay style, but it simply fails to deliver. For these reasons I cannot, in good faith, recommend this game, especially at a price of 25€.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is a unique horror experience that seamlessly blends 80s slasher tropes with modern interactive storytelling. As a late-night radio DJ, you find yourself thrust into a terrifying situation where you must use your wits and communication skills to save the lives of your listeners amidst a string of murders.What Works:    Immersive Atmosphere: The game expertly captures the vintage horror vibe, with its synth-wave soundtrack, grainy visuals, and chilling sound design. The radio station setting provides a truly immersive and claustrophobic environment, making every call feel tense and suspenseful.    Engaging Gameplay Loop: The core gameplay loop of receiving calls, gathering information, making choices, and navigating the radio station is surprisingly engaging. Balancing multiple callers in distress, managing resources, and trying to deduce the killer's identity keeps the player on their toes.    Intriguing Story and Characters: While the story isn't groundbreaking, it effectively builds suspense and features a cast of memorable characters. The interactions with callers, coupled with the unfolding mystery, keep you invested in the narrative.    Multiple Playthrough Value: The game encourages replayability with multiple endings and branching storylines depending on your choices. This adds a layer of depth and encourages exploration of different paths.What Could Be Improved:    Technical Issues: Some players have reported encountering bugs and glitches that can impact gameplay. While not widespread, these issues can unfortunately disrupt the immersive experience.    Limited Interaction: While the radio station setting is well-utilized, the physical environment feels somewhat limited in terms of interactivity. There are few opportunities to explore beyond the immediate surroundings of the station.    Pacing Issues: The initial few hours can feel a bit slow, as the game builds its tension gradually. For some players, this might lead to a loss of interest before the story truly picks up.Overall:Killer Frequency is a solid entry in the horror genre that successfully leverages its unique premise. The retro aesthetics, gripping narrative, and engaging gameplay loop make for a genuinely thrilling experience. However, some technical issues and occasional pacing problems might hinder the overall enjoyment for some players.If you're a fan of horror games with a strong narrative focus and enjoy a retro vibe, Killer Frequency is definitely worth checking out. Just be prepared for a few potential technical hiccups along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the 80s slasher movie vibe and synth music available in game. The voice acting was pretty good and didn't feel too over-the-top and each character felt unique in their own way even if you couldn't physically see them in game. A very good use of "less is more". The puzzles were pretty fun and aren't super difficult, though it can be trial & error for some of them, but it feels very rewarding once you solve it. There was a lot of good humor and there are definitely some tense moments, not overloaded with cheap jump scares either. While there definitely a few tense moments there was a good flow to balance it out. Overall I definitely enjoyed this game and hope they make a sequel! If you're a fan of puzzle-solving, 80's horror, synthwave music then this game is definitely for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: The unique premise - a late-night radio DJ becoming a lifeline for callers during a murder spree - is instantly compelling. The atmosphere, visuals, and voice acting are superb, pulling you into the suspense. The 80s-inspired soundtrack perfectly complements the retro vibe and the chilling narrative.The execution initially shines. Tension builds organically, the voice acting makes you care about the characters, and the retro aesthetics create an immersive backdrop. The puzzles offer an engaging challenge, even if they're simple.  The desperation, urgency, and the weight of your decisions are exhilarating and heart-wrenching. The soundboard, with its quirky effects, adds a touch of dark humor, though not always perfectly executed.However, the game falters as you progress. While the puzzles themselves offer variety,  Furthermore, some characters, particularly those you interact with regularly, are excessively berating and obnoxious, making them grating to listen to. Attempts at humor often feel jarring and inappropriate, trivializing the serious themes. Unskippable dialogue disrupts the pacing, forcing you to endure lengthy, pointless conversations. *  A fresh and intriguing take on the horror genre*  The setting, visuals, and voice acting create genuine suspense*  The 80s-inspired music enhances the retro vibe and suspense*  Guiding callers and using the soundboard is thrilling and immersive*  The game severely restricts exploration, particularly early on, hindering the sense of freedom and discovery*  Some characters are overly berating and difficult to tolerate*  Attempts at humor often feel jarring and inappropriate*  Unskippable dialogue disrupts the pacing*  The narrative loses steam and the conclusion feels rushed and unsatisfying*  Limited incentive to play again after completing the story*  The game's potential for deeper exploration of the setting and lore is not fully realized Killer Frequency has a captivating concept and exceptional atmosphere, but stumbles in its execution. The caller interactions and the creative use of the soundboard are the standout features. However, the excessive confinement, obnoxious characters, tonal inconsistencies, predictable plot, underwhelming ending, lack of replay value, and missed opportunities detract significantly from the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I knew it was going to be a good one. Recently I've watched Texas Chainsaw Massacre II and I really liked the part where people were calling the local radio station when they were approached by Leatherface. It was really well-made. And to be a part of situations like those in the movie but in the game? Count me in.So, in Killer Frequency you play as Forrest Nash - a former DJ, who now hosts a podcast in a local radio of a small town. Said town is a playground for a mysterious killer - The Whistling Man. Your job is to help people calling the radio escape death. Those calls are mainly puzzles and some of them were really surprising (for example when you can save Roller Ricky - really clever!). In breaks from calls, you will wander the station's building in search for clues that can help you save callers. Also, you are a DJ so your job is to play music (the OST is AWESOME!!!) and ads for the audience.Even though it's a horror game, many calls are here to lighten up the mood or make you laugh. I genuinely laughed in some moments. I think those calls are perfectly placed, so after a murderer gets his victim, you can take a break and speak with someone who just wanted to thank you for everything you've done so far. Also - there is just a 1 or 2 jumpscares so you don't have to be afraid of that.I really enjoyed playing this game, it's on a nice discount until 11th November, so if you like light horror games and solving a few not so hard puzzles - I can recommend this game to you. A casual playthrough of the game should take you about 5 hours so it's no too long. It ends exactly when you could start getting bored.

But that doesn't mean the story building isn't good, its definitely good if you're into the more lore heavy aspects of a game. The actual gameplay is about what you'd expect from this kind of game and the puzzles are really cool but the game just made them far too easy to figure out. Peggy the in-game show producer holds your hand the entire way through and makes it impossible to get stuck with unprompted clues. even as i write this im not sure 100% how i feel about the whole experience, overall it was a really cool story puzzle game, but as a puzzle game, there's not much of a challenge.OVERALL: 7.5/10if the puzzles were harder i'd probably have it up around 8-9/10Thanks for coming to my Ted Talk.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this tactile and campy horror/comedy game!  It's not scary, and I'd recommend it to folks who get stressed out by survival horror games.  It's almost more of a radio drama than a video game, just given how much of the action happens through voice acting over... the radio!  The writing is cheesy, but it fits with the theme of 80's horror.  From a game play perspective, I think that it is almost like an Escape Room.  Not only do you slowly unlock broader and broader access to the rooms within the radio station as you search for keys, tapes, and materials to help you, but every call has a puzzle element to it - you know that there's some combination of things you can say that will allow the caller to survive the night!  But I thought that it got pretty hard by the end.  I don't want to spoil anything about the scope of the story but according to the cork board in the credits sequence, I was able to save less than 50% of the people it was possible to save!  So if you try it out, make sure to think twice about your answers!  The game is very short, I don't know if I'd pay a full $25 for it given that I probably wouldn't play it a second time, but I got it in a recent Humble Bundle, and it's worth it if you can catch it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun, although short (comedy?) horror game. If you're fine with the price tag it's an amazing experience and you should absolutely go in blind. I also advise not save scumming unless you're dead set on getting all achievements (Be advised this WILL need two playthroughs MINIMUM.)The way situations play out as they happen can be either intensely rewarding as you successfully solve how to save your callers in jeopardy from the stereotypical slasher villain, or incredibly hilarious as they die in various gruesome ways. My only real gripes with the game were some puzzles being a little confusing initially with it not clarifying which options help you figure out clues being mixed in with actual results for progressing (or failing) a call, and not being able to finish the game in a single playthough due to one of the achievements. Besides that, Killer Frequency is an easy recommend for a fun couple of hours spent solving high stakes situations while listening to smooth tunes.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This was most entertaining. Great concept and execution of a idea where a killer is loose and you as a local radio host in a somewhat secure location have your part in assisting people in a small town to get away from the killer while you do some DJ work at the side. And other things that come along.  One of those games where guides are to be avoided and played as-is as you go. Pro: - Love the small details with actual DJ work. You got the laugh buttons, the commercial tapes and records. - Smooth interface. Started with game pad but realized mouse and keyboard work even better. - No padding on the game play time e.g. It is not a long game but time is used effectively. Some 6 hours and it is done but there are no forcefully extended moments just to get more game play hours. Some nice smooth moments when you listen to some music and toss a few hoops with paper balls. All part of the experience. Con: - Could have had more of the more routine DJ stuff too. I consider it a important part of the game play somehow. I can imagine if they had removed all of this from the game then the puzzles parts would not have lifted this game enough to get a positive scoring. Particularly with the price being somewhat high for a game so short so i am glad they avoided a direct competition with 'real detective/puzzle games' and instead had their own unique thing going on.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like slasher movies and 80's neon aesthetic, this game will probably please you in a lot of ways. The visuals are quite pleasing and the soundtrack is really fantastic. But all that being said, there's are some significant errors int the pacing of this game that prevent me from a full recommendation. By all accounts the game has some shining spots, but its Achilles Heel is that the game is too long. Normally that wouldn't be a bad thing, but because the game has to pad out so much time, much of the intrigue is replaced by boredom. To give credit where credit is due, the game has really good atmosphere and has its tense moments. There is a lot of room for potential here, but repetition works against it. You end up doing the same thing over and over again and those bright moments become significantly more dull about the 4th time seeing them. I feel that if the game cut out about about an hours worth of playtime, it'd be a much tighter experience. Certain plot points seem to come out of or go nowhere, and many of the interesting parts of game play either don't return, or as stated, you repeat them over and over until intrigue is lost. It's a shame, because this game could be a lot scarier than it is. But as it stands right now, the game just under delivers. It's a decent game and I could go on about my specific grievances, but I don't to spoil and I'd hate for this review to drag. All in all, it's not worth its price tag. Get it on a significant sale if you can, because as it is, it's just not worth it.

Perhaps the later puzzles really ramp up, or the story gets really compelling, but ultimately I just got bored listening to the filler between scenarios and I wasnt confident payoff would be worth the time sink.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the rare cases where I wish I could just give a neutral review. I wanna write about this game without boosting or harming its review score. But since that isn't possible, I'll go with "recommend" since it's slightly above the tipping point.The game tells a great crime story with many branching and reconnecting paths from the point of someone who spends most of the time in one room. Only hearing about what is going on out there and speaking to people instead of directly being there greatly benefits the vibes this game is going for, although I suspect it is partly born of a limitation.Sadly, throughout the game there are minor issues that all detract a tiny bit from the overall experience. The voice acting is sub-par. It's unclear if the voice actors themselves are to blame, the direction they were given or if anything else went wrong. Also, while the overarching story was honestly great, and had a good mix of high and low tension moments, the moment to moment writing was sub-par too. The two main characters listen to someone get slashed on the phone, with it being partly their fault, and they just shrug it off in one sentence and move on with the radio program. However, this stems partly from the many branching paths this story has, many people can die or survive and in connecting those threads back together, something probably had to give. I cannot fault the devs enough to push it into a negative review, but I still feel like it could've been handled a little bit better.Also, if you're a puzzle game veteran, most if not all of the puzzles this game has to offer should be fairly simple, so don't expect anything mindbending. They could've gone much much harder on almost all of them. I don't think it would make for a better game though because one wrong answer usually means someone dies. There not being any trial and error (assuming no savescumming) keeps the tension high even if the solution isn't incredibly hard to figure out. Lastly, as a minor nitpick. After a few callers that make sense in the time period, only being able to call with a landline phone at hand, there are two callers that make it seem like they have mobile phones in 1987. While not impossible, it would be unusual for some random people in a random 1000 people town. It felt more like the writer(s) just forgot or ignored the time this was set in for a moment to make for more tense scenes. Not the end of the world, but it did break my immersion for a moment.To sum up my thoughts. If you're into interactive stories, crime stories and/or unique ways of storytelling and are looking for a 4-8 hour experience, you can do MUCH worse than Killer Frequency. I think the overall "gimmick" could've been handled better, but if you're in the aforementioned groups, pick it up on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is Firewatch meets Pontypool meets 80's slasher.Even though this is only a 4-6 hour story, it was worth every dollar I paid for it.  I am excited to play through again and finish the rest of the achievements.  This is a great game for the Halloween season, both in genre and story content.If you are hesitant about picking up this game due to the divisive tropes in other horror titles (chase/hide sequences, cheap jump scares, combat), please rest assured that this is an atmospheric choices matter and puzzle-based exploration game.  While you should dread every door you open and check over your shoulder constantly, this game is approachable for casual horror gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, the story itself is amazing but then additionally the sound and details takes the experience up to several levels! Despite the fact that you are answering calls and really don't experience the attacks yourself, it still gets your heart pumping and concerned for the characters on the other line. The details even on the front screen puts you in a mood to play the game and it is a master piece of a game.i admit to sitting there and listening to the detail and going back to look at all the small details, the music is also pretty good, its very groovy. Additionally the characters are well written, they all have different personalities and react differently.it pretty re-playable. Even if you know how it ends, for example if you had watched a play-through before playing, (like i did) it is still so enjoyable and fun to play!5/5 all the way, would recommend buying and playing it.

It leaves a slight desire for more content. But that's just me.-1: . I'm gathering the strength to play the  to get the Forrest Dash achievement to get them all.When's Killer Frequency 2 coming out soon? Another station? Another killer? Halloween special?

_childDocuments_.review: Beaten - about 8 hoursA really well made "Walking Sim" where you play a new radio DJ who is tasked , in lieu of the limited police offers being unavailable, with taking 911 calls for a night.  You will solve issues , many of which involve a murderer, by exploring the radio station.  In between talking to callers and solving their issues, you will be playing songs, ads, and talking to your producer.The game is elevated by its art style and voice acting.Overall, a very fun Halloween game.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in a humble bundle and played it alongside some friends. Truly recommend this, its super super fun and very similar to games like "firewatch" or even "in sound mind" if youve enjoyed either of those. Its unique, has a compelling story, and manages to be humorous while balancing an impending sense of nervousness 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit confused as to why the reviews are so good here. The novel concept of the game wears thin after an hour or two. The writing isn't great and it's difficult to get invested in the story due to the sheer lack of logic. Peggy, the character you spend most of the game with, doesn't even have an actual character model. She is just a grey shape. This seemed lazy to me. It's not an awful game, but 96% positive reviews? come on now.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this! It's campy and fun with a great environment and awesome voice acting. The radio mechanics (especially the soundboard) are really entertaining. I probably could've finished the game faster than 5 hours, I played at a really leisurely pace. Overall a very rewarding campy slasher style game with awesome aesthetics!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: It doesn't have much in the way of replay value, and it's a little short (beat it in a little over 5 hours), but the core concept is exceptionally done. Each of the "puzzles" feels unique, and scouring the environment for means to help solve them is great. If they do a sequel or an update, I'd like to see the ability to skip lines of dialogue (this might help with replaying the game, as there are large stretches just talking to people on the phone), also the ability to select dialogue choices no matter where you're standing so you're not stuck near the main station while talking. Would also like to see a larger, more intricate environment if they do a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't quite finished this game yet but so far, it's already a favorite. There's something terrifying about only being able to hear what is going on over a phone compared to having the killer right in your face. Every time I had to leave my safe little recording booth, I was on edge that something was going to get me, even though I knew that there probably wasn't a jump scare around every corner. I am very excited to finish the game and more than likely, I will end up replaying it for both the story and to get all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an art piece. Everything about this game was so well put together, the visuals, music, voice acting, everything. I have played this game over a few sittings, but each time I stepped away I couldn't wait to come back to it. I scare easily, but the tension build up was immaculate. I missed a few clues so ended up not saving everyone, but that's all me. Even having a feature like this, to put together clues and solve mysteries and help people survive is so cool. If you couldn't guess, I would definitely recommend this game. I look forward to seeing what the developers come out with next!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play-through at the time of this review and i only have good things to say. The story is Perfectly written and pulls you in more then you would ever expect. I found myself being invested into characters and events like never before. 10/10 would recommend to ANYONE looking for an afternoon of thrill and entertainment. It was a....Scream
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good!A fun and engaging take on the 80's slasher flick with a lot of personality and heart.Some of the puzzles could have done with a polish and on at least one occasion I felt like the game was punishing me arbitrarily, but I would strongly recommend to anyone who loves something a little dark and quirky and has a spare six hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I think this might be my first review for a game, which is saying something, considering the size of my library. I'm not really a big fan of horror games, but I do like a good walking simulator with a good story, much like Firewatch.Killer Frequency's story captured me early on, and made me want to play "just a little more", dying (sorry) to find out how each call ended, and how the story progressed. Thoroughly recommend for anyone who is a fan of walking simulators, addictive stories, the 1980s, or games where you don't have to worry about getting killed every two seconds. Definitely need a prequel, and many sequels. 10/10, will play again soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm in love with the game's concept and its dark sense of humor, and I believe the execution is really well done.Regarding the reviews that claim the voice acting is supposed to be bad, they have no idea what they are talking about. The voice actors employ some heavily animated character tropes, but they do a great job at it and I think it benefits the intended tone of the game.Even though the game is quite funny at times, it still manages to create a mysterious and tense atmosphere when needed. So, if you also like the concept and are undecided about getting it, just go for it. You'll quickly see if it's for you or not, if not you can still refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I played Killer Frequency over the last few days... Only took about 4.5 hours or so. I very much enjoyed the vibes, it was a nice little horror mystery comedy thing. You are a late night talk show host in a tiny town where a string of serial killings is going down. The police are soon out of the picture, so it's up to you to field the 911 calls, help save the citizens of Gallows Creek, and still manage to run an entertaining show.It's not a terribly deep or complex narrative, and I think this concept could have been down in a way that makes it more bite sized. It feels like a one long sitting type of game, since there are not really major breakpoints. Honestly, the little game of trying to save the people is fun, but wears thin rather quickly. This is saved by the fact that the game is too short to make it tiresome, and because the game gives you access to a record player with music, a cassette player with ads, and a goofy soundboard; not to mention the addictive trash-ball-in-the-basketball-hoop game. You can use these at any time, which leads to some really great comedic effect. I do very much wish these affected how much people enjoyed your show, but alas. The voice acting is also quite good, which helps with the whole vibe.Speaking of the vibe, I love it. The 80's aesthetic, the neon, the music you get to play, the Stranger Things small town, it all works together perfectly. This was what made me click on the game on Steam's store page, and it was the standout feature throughout.I think this game is certainly worth your time, but it is $20 even on sale atm, and despite the game having "endings", I don't foresee myself replaying this by myself. I give it a genuine 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's clever, fun, with great voice acting and an interesting story. I like the characters and their interactions. Especially how some conversations change depending on what you say. "Don't be a Ponty, Forrest!"You'll need a small chunk of "Suspension of Disbelief" for it to work, but let's be real: Slasher fans have that in abundance. ^.~I originally played the first few calls in german, but would advise anyone who can to play it in english. (Sometimes wonky translation and unimersive overlays of translated text for maps, magazines and notes)Also, there's a dog! All love to Maxy!
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: It's like if Firewatch was reimagined as a radio show and you had to save all the kids from Until Dawn remotely from the station. As restrictive as the premise seems at first, its really alot more dynamic than it lets on. The puzzles are well realised in the writing and the environment. Its just so well thought out, some of the twists might feel predictable but it is always fun and the voice acting is some of the best going. Very well paced, nothing ever outstays its welcome and I kind of already want to go back in and try to save everyone. Seems there is alot of ways this thing can go down and there are also mini games and collectables but they are relevant to the game so it doesn't just feel like an unnecessary add in.A really good game worth your time. Very tightly made, there is alot to admire about it
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: A real example of how horror should be. With only 1 light Jumpscare at the beginning and at the end it still manages to be a very scary game. It manages to perfectly build up the tension and only drop it right at the end. With a rich story and choices that matter I will be sure to revisit the game in the future to see the other paths. I must say though 25 Euro is a bit to ask for a game that only takes around 4-5 hours to complete, but if It is on sale it is 100% worth your purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: Killer Frequency is another one of those games where it is best to avoid any and all videos on it. The more blind you go into it, the better of an experience you will get out of it and I am a sucker of those sorts of games. Those nicely condensed, narrative focused, information gathering types of games and Killer Frequency is just that. I will make this as short and sweet as possible. What do you do in Killer Frequency? Well, you play as a radio host Forest Nash and due to rather dire circumstances, you (along side your trusty co-host) are in charge of taking the calls of the frantic denizens in a small remote town as a killer is on the loose. You are in constant intense situations as each choice matters. How many are you able to save by simply being behind a desk? Whats best advice can you give? How much information can you gather to figure out who the killer is? The team behind this game have done an amazing job recapturing that neon 80's vibe and aesthetic as well as achieving that cosy "one man show" radio desk feel with all the little dials and buttons you can fiddle with throughout your game time. There are so many items that are intractable just for the sake of trying to immerse you in this unique job environment. The sound and mostly importantly the music is a joy to listen to. Synth waves, 80's rock and almost aerobic-esc dance music, the vinyl records you can play are absolute bangers with a few scattered through out to find as you play.An intense, gripping thriller from the get go and never lets up. Was truly hooked from the moment I picked it up. An amazingly unique and creative game and is one I wholeheartedly recommend to all.
_childDocuments_.name: Killer Frequency

_childDocuments_.review: You know how in heist movies the characters do a voice-over of their plans on top of footage of them executing that same plan to break into the bank or the museum or whatever? There's a reason they do that. It's so you don't have to waste the viewer's time by showing them the exact same information twice.More than half of this game is standing and doing nothing while the game forces you to listen to things you already know. You'll pick up a piece of evidence, inspect it, and then listen to a character tell you exactly what you just read. Or the reverse, where Forrest and Peggy come up with a plan, then reiterate it to the caller unabridged even though you, the player, just heard Forrest and Peggy come up with the plan.You cannot skip past any of this.You must wait for Peggy to finish talking before you go through the door to investigate the radio station, even through there's an intercom she could use to talk to you from anywhere in the building. You must sit and listen to ads that are twice as long as any radio ad would ever be in real life because the writers think they are very funny and they want you to listen to their bad jokes. You cannot hang up on any caller for *any* reason, even though you have buttons explicitly meant for doing that. You can't even hang up when someone is being killed live on the air or it's obvious you're being pranked. You just have to sit there like a useless fish and wait for Peggy to do it 60 whole seconds after it was obvious to anyone with a brain that you needed to cut the live feed. You are not a player in this world. You are a fair-goer waiting for the slow carnival ride to move to the next vignette in the dark ride.It's clear the developers received some kind of feedback about how boring it is to sit there and listen to actors give poorly-directed reads about an uninteresting story because there is a basketball hoop across the room and an endless pile of paper balls to throw into it. Thank god for this, because I cannot imagine playing this game without something to do during those long stretches of nothing. I found every object I could find and threw it. I collected mousetraps. I learned the different weight of objects, like how paper weighs nothing but a mannequin head is as dense as a neuron star and drops like a brick the moment it leaves Forrest's hand. But even these stopped being enough to hold my attention around hour 3.It's crazy to think of this as a VR, game because most of what you do is stand still and wait in front of a line of buttons that do nothing. The only benefit of playing it in VR is that your feet might hurt.It's even crazier that in a game where 95% of the game is just a radio play, there's such a poor performance from its cast. For many of them this seems to be a direction issue. There are little delivery mistakes *everywhere* where people enunciate incorrectly or say things wrong (i.e. Forrest telling a girl to send her friend Lisa to do a task and the actor reads the line "Yes, Lisa!" as in "Yes, Lisa, I heard you, calm down!" rather than "Yes, Lisa!" as in "Yes, I could send Lisa, of course, that makes sense!")Not to mention, almost every actor in this game is pulling double, triple, quadruple, quintuple, and, at times, sextuple-duty as multiple characters. Dawn's voice actress sounds convincing in all the roles she is given, but Joshua Manning and Rachel Handshaw are simply not strong enough actors to pull this off. Joshua's reads are cartoonish and tonally backwards while Rachel's are all so obviously the same actress that I was genuinely getting confused because I thought I was talking to the same people I just rescued.It seems like a very odd development choice to save budget on hiring more voice actors for your game when 99% of your game is an audiodrama where voice actors talk to the player while they stand there and do nothing. I'd also like to suggest they hire a better vocal director next time so the comedy reads actually sound like comedy and Peggy's lines aren't so atonally chipper and irritating that I'm actively hoping the killer will finish her off by the end of the game.As for the plot, the 911/Radio Host setup is too goofy and convoluted to believed for even a singular second. This might've worked if the game veered all the way into comedy, which I was expecting, but after its 20-minute-long "final confrontation" sequence where everything is played dead straight, I have no choice but to think they really did want this game to be scary. It is not scary. It is often a little embarrassing.It's also clear they wanted this game to be set in the 80s America for aesthetic reasons, but they didn't really think about anything beyond that point. You get calls to the radio station from people out in the woods, parking lots, or abandoned buildings and guide them across ridiculous distances, even through an entire hedge maze at one point. I assume they are calling into the station on 80s landlines with four hundred feet of extension cords. These people sure don't have cell phones! And if they did, they wouldn't be getting reception in a town of 1000 people that's nearest neighboring town with a police station is *a 2 hour drive away*. That's also nonsense, by the way. There are entire states you can cross in 2 hours time. Speaking as someone who's driven cross-country multiple times, even in the 80s the only place that remote would have to be up in northern Alaska, the mountains, or the far reaches of the Mojave desert, which this town is definitely not. The only time you go outside it's very clearly a normal suburban Podunk in, like, Ohio or something where another town would surely be like 25 miles away at most.I know these things sound like nitpicking and you can always poke at loose threads, but this game is nothing but loose threads. It's a whole sweater of loose threads. The puzzles are alright (sometimes), but nothing else is.Is this an irreverent black comedy about a stylized 80s radio station carried by its comedy? No.Is this a scary horror game that you can play if you want to be scared? Definitely not.Are the story or characters intriguing at all? Absolutely not.Well, then I don't know why you would play this thing. So you shouldn't.

_childDocuments_.review:
It's a late night at KFAM radio station in Gallows Creek, mid-west USA. You can feel something's in the air. You've just started your shift and someone calls in with a horrifying discovery. The next turn of events will be life-changing

Become a radio DJ in this 80s slasher shredded adventure that's certainly not child's play. As summer turns to fall and the countdown to Halloween continues, will this be a silent night, deadly night? Or will the airwaves scream?

Killer Frequency is a first-person horror adventure that puts you in the shoes of Forrest Nash, a late-night radio host whose callers are being stalked by a mysterious killer. Solve puzzles, save lives and run the switchboards, all while listening to a jukebox of retro '80s tunes!

name: Slave Zero X
detailed_description: From the top of Megacity S1-9, the Sovereign Khan rules with fists of iron and flesh. Beneath the city’s rotting foundations, a vengeful warrior embarks on a journey to murder him. 4 years prior to the events of Slave Zero, Slave Zero X brings new life to a world where horrific, living machines known as Slaves are primed to become the latest tools of war in humanity’s long and bloody history. A secret band of warriors known as The Guardians hope to stop these biomecha from being unleashed upon the world, but one swordsman among their ranks has a different idea: use the enemy’s own weapon against them. By merging with a stolen Slave Unit Prototype, Shou will become a furious Devil in pursuit of killing a false God. KILLER COMBOS: Use swift swordplay, explosive ordnance, and stylish combos against an army of meat and metal. DEATH FROM ABOVE: Air juggling, dashes, and frequent target switching allow for you to take down foes of any size while wall-jumping and platforming can help you outmaneuver your enemies. FIGHT FOR YOUR LIFE: Conquer mini-bosses, set pieces, and climactic 1-on-1 encounters that offer intense challenges against unforgettable villains. STRENGTH IS NOTHING WITHOUT CONTROL: Use the Training Room to hone precise and powerful moves to string together devastating attack sequences. BATTLE TO THE BEAT: A 90s-inspired soundtrack features heavy Drum’n’Bass and funky industrial music that adds to the thrill of combat. FEAST YOUR EYES: A unique visual aesthetic combines nostalgic 2D sprites with an advanced lighting system and stylized 3D environments. THE END IS NEVER THE END: After completing the campaign, further challenges await in an expansive and frenetic ‘Crimson Citadel’ procedural challenge tower with an online high score leaderboard and an unhinged, ultra-hard battle with SovKhan in his ultimate form, a.k.a. “SovKhan 300%.”

short_description: Slave Zero X is a stylish 2.5D character action game set in the biopunk world of Slave Zero (1999). Run & Slash your way through a dystopian future in this character action game which will resonate with fans of Devil May Cry, Strider, and Guilty Gear.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot emphasise enough how much I wanted to love this game. I also want to make it clear that, as of writing, I haven’t finished the game. I believe I stopped just before the Regent boss.--Bloody and Brilliant--I adore Fighting Games, Spectacle Fighters, and sprite-based artwork. Slave Zero X combines and draws inspiration from all of these, and hits it out the park. I’ve been following the art director (Francine Bridge) for years, she’s one of my favourite artists in the world. Her work, and the efforts of the entire art/animation team, cannot be understated. Bridge’s visceral art style blends beautifully with the biopunk aesthetic, resulting in a goreish gorgeous look. The way 2D sprites move around the 3D background is pure magic.Also huge compliments to the life bar. I wish more games had creative life bars like in Slave Zero X.The inclusion of the original Slave Zero with the purchase is awesome. I love when developers include previous games in a series for free. It’s brilliant that Poppy Works/Ziggurat are bringing attention to a hidden gem.--A Chipped Blade--While the combat can feel very satisfying and viscerally pleasing, the encounter design is quite frustrating. Initially, encounters have a fair spread of enemies. Enough for a challenge, but also enough to go a little crazy with your Fighting Game inspired movelist. But as the game goes on, the screen gets flooded with so many enemies that you can quickly get overwhelmed and completely lose control of the fight. You do have a Burst which can knock enemies back, but this is a finite resource.The difficulty does not benefit from reused enemies. I don’t mind when a game reuses basic enemies a lot, you gotta give the player stuff to gib. But there is one particular mini-boss that is so overused, I thought the game was spawning him by mistake. At the point I stopped playing, said mini-boss was reused 8 times.Additionally, your defensive options are very limited. The parry timing is too tight, I found it more reliable to counter attacks by clashing (although this isn’t much easier). You also have a dodge, but it has very limited i-frames. I actually don’t mind that, however. I think too many action games rely on dodge mechanics with over-lenient i-frames, making defence a bit brainless. However, it means that getting swamped by enemies is very difficult to get out of without Burst.The game also doesn’t have a movelist. Shou (the protag) has quite a robust set of attacks, but you won’t know without an internet guide. Now, I can see what Poppy Works is doing here. I love 2000s era video games (the PS2 is my fav console), and the devs are trying to recreate the thrill of discovering hidden moves. But I still think it does more harm than good to not include a movelist.It would also be nice to have health bars for some enemies, but I recognise that’s less important.Other miscellaneous notes: it would really reduce frustration if checkpoints were put directly before boss fights. And since your health is automatically refilled when you die, what’s the point of buying refills from the shop?--Conclusion in Good Faith--I have nothing but respect for everyone working at Poppy Works, and I hope Slave Zero X becomes a huge success for them. But I can’t ignore the frustration I feel with the encounter design and limited defensive options. I would love to see an update or revision that fixes these issues, but I understand if Poppy Works want to move onto other projects. Wish the best for you all.

_childDocuments_.review: This game started out pretty amazing with really fun combat and showed a lot of promise, but fell off really hard in the second half, especially towards the final missions. There are other more detailed reviews which go into this, but to sum it up:The good: Excellent music and visuals, core gameplay is fun when it worksThe bad, reason for this negative review: The latter half of the game has far, far too much enemy spam, especially these mini-boss type enemies which are used over and over. The playable character's defensive abilities are too lackluster to escape the constant stunlock & juggling you have to deal with when trying to make sense of all of the enemies on the screen. I'm open to someone telling me I have a skill issue or something, but I saw enough reviews agreeing with me to be sure that something went wrong here.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd actually like to give this a "sideways" thumb more than a straight up negative, but I feel like, even though I really enjoy a lot of what this game is doing so far, it's got a few too many things that stick in my craw in order to enjoy it fully.The art is amazing and inspired, and a sprite based action game like this being made nowadays is basically unheard of. The music is alright, not quite as intense as i'd like for this type of game and a little too videogame-y for me, but it serves it's purpose and is pretty catchy. Put on some HEALTH or NiN or even some hardcore or industrial hiphop for a better feel if you ask me.And the story, so far at least, is genuinely interesting and fun. Definitely gives 90's anime OVA vibes, which is a good thing. MC is the world's strongest femboy this side of Alucard.No, most of my problems, unfortunately, and importantly, lie with the gameplay.The game's defensive mechanics don't gel well with the gameplay from my pov. This is a game that's built like an anime fighter, with twitchy, fast paced combat and moves that come out in sub-10 frames. But even the fighting games it's based off of, namely Guillty Gear, have consistent damage mitigation. Blocking. But the best you'll get in this game is the "parry" function, which is...not great. Far too strict for a game with such fast windups and no combo limits. What this means is that you're forced to be hit over and over again if you don't properly defend the first attack. I actually got stuck in an infinite with one of the mini-bosses and his add(boo to adds in bossfights btw) and was killed this way. And that sucks. There's a little "dodge" move, but it's inconsistent in it's ability to avoid damage from my experience. Half the time I just got hit halfway through my dodge.Despite invoking Strider, there's essentially nothing of the sort here. There's limited mobility, and even more limited world design. Which is a shame because the cool, FEZ-like 2.5D world is such a killer idea, but so far through my adventure it's been pretty much entirely for show. There's no metroidvania elements outside of some minor secrets if you go backwards every once in a while, nor real reason to move in any way other than running and jumping 90% of the time, and moving to the right 90% of the time. I'd kill for a game to have really satisfying character action combat that also had the buttery smooth movement of Strider.The tutorial is bad. Period. The game just infodumps your moves on you right at the start before you get control of your character, and then tells you to fight. I suppose if you're especially nostalgic about the way some old games did tutorials then it might be cute to you, but let's remember that that way of teaching the player stopped being a thing FOR A REASON. It's easy to forget what button does what and what random obscure move you have available or what the conditions are because it all got dumped on you at once right at the start hours ago. Sure you can check your controls, but I kind of find that to be a bit of a failure of the game to properly explain itself. Like idk, it seems obvious to me at least that the way to do this is to have the game tell you "This is light attack" and then throw a guy at you, and then you walk forward and "This is heavy attack" and another guy, and you beat him then it teaches you how to run, and then jumping, etc.And lastly, I really don't like when supposed "character action games" don't give you more moves to buy. At least, from where I am I haven't seen any in the shop. Which is a bummer. If there are some later then I supposed that's fair, but i'm not sure if it makes much sense to go through multiple bosses and not see any new moves if there ARE new moves.The game is really COOL, and pretty interesting, and when you're just wailing on scrubs it's fine. But whenever you're up against an opponent that can't be stunlocked it starts to show some cracks. Attacks are too fast to warrant giving you so little defensive ability--mind you, LESS defensive ability than the notoriously aggressive Guilty Gear that this is clearly inspired by. And a lot of enemies just run up and instantly attack, or even have cheapshot attacks as you're moving through the level which is lame. Sometimes they'll even be offscreen, and you can't even see what they're gonna do in order to defend(or the game will inexplicably place something in the foreground so you can't see). The big heavy guys have like, no startup command grabs with SUPER ARMOR. Imagine a FG character like that. Picture Potemkin or Zangief with a command grab that comes out in like 5 frames, WITH superarmor. Honestly kind of hilarious if it weren't so annoying. But it is annoying, and that sucks, because man do I really really wanna love this game.If anything here sounds like a dealbreaker to you, then i'd tap out for now until the game is on sale for ~10-15 bucks. And if the game ever gets patched or these issues become alleviated in some other way, then i'll add that to my feedback here and possibly change my rating.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOOD:-Fun combo system, lots of mindless violence if you're into that.-Beautiful sprites. The backgrounds and general vibe remind me of Strider 2-The story's pretty good. Definitely more engaging if you've played the original and the Quake mod.-The soundtrack and voice acting are pretty good too.-Taunting wallbounces and it's very humorous.-Legally distinct Morshu NPCTHE MAYBE:-Until the end of February, purchasing this game comes with a free copy of the original Slave Zero, which in itself is a good game. However, the Steam version of that game has a bunch of issues and it's generally recommended to get the GOG version instead.THE BAD:-No move list-Tutorial is very brief, doesn't go in depth on what you're capable of doing.-You can Roman Cancel by accident as Fatal Sync is mapped to the same button and the latter can only be activated in a neutral state.-Fatal Sync (the game's Devil Trigger) only replenishes health upon dealing damage instead of regenerating over time. (Might be a personal issue tbh)-You can get juggled very, VERY easily, leading to a quick death, even with the game's defensive options.-Some enemies and bosses have super armor until they get hit enough times. From there you'll be able to combo them. Most of the time it's very hard to get a hit in, though.-The hit detection can get weird-Objects in the foreground can obstruct what you're doing in certain stages.-Atavaka's entire boss fight.I really want to like this, but for now I can't recommend it as there are too many glaring issues that makes the game a frustrating slog to go through. If you really want to try it, please wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: About as beautiful as a kusoge can get, but a kusoge nonetheless. Not the first time a game has deliberately broken itself in order to seem more "retro," and it probably won't be the last. This one stings a bit though, since the beautiful artwork and characters get completely swamped in the drudgery of moment to moment gameplay. No business in something that's allegedly based on fighting games to have 0 defensive options whatsoever, especially when you can't manually save. You're telling me that I'm *supposed* to not be able to get up, and not be able to get out of being stunlocked? And there are supposed to be invincible, instant command throws? And I can't even block? If this were an actual fighting game, at least when you have to eat a long combo you know that it's because somebody else has the execution to do it, hell they could even drop it, but here? You miss one parry--a unidirectional parry with like an i4 window mind you, that could very well be your only defense against something completely off-screen that kills you instantly--and you just get to watch a nice long cutscene of something supposedly cool happening, and then its back to the checkpoint with you. Not that the density of enemies on-screen usually allows you to actually see anything cool happening.I feel like this is misguided, is what I'm saying. Misguided, under-tutorialized, buggy, and also weirdly slow? The movement feels awful in this game, super sticky, and cancelling things with jumps or EX moves works maybe a third of the time. Plus, on top of all of that, this game commits one of my personal cardinal sins, which is including references to internet memes. Please don't do that! This is a lot of wasted potential, but it has some really effectively cool moments and gimmicks in it. Probably the most unique art style in any game I've ever seen, which is actually why I bought it (shouts out to Francine Bridge @Personfaces on Twitter.) Maybe if you like DMC and for some reason want a 2D imitator, this will scratch your itch?

_childDocuments_.review: Great artstyle, cool premise, but there are some bugs and weird design choices that make this game so frustrating to play that I genuinely might be done. In a game so difficult and reliant on precision, who decided it be a good idea to have you NOT SEE during large sections of the game should really rethink what constitutes fun. Also I don't know if this is an audio bug or how it's meant to be (and if so... why?), but the ambience and soundtrack are often drowned out by the noise the drone thing that follows you around makes, which for some reason is 10x louder than everything else around it. Sometimes it isn't even on my screen and I can STILL hear it over everything else. Like I'm sure the soundtrack you made/chose for the game is awesome guys - would be even better if I could actually HEAR IT. The tutorial is virtually useless - explains little of how you're actually meant to play the game. There's some VERY noticeable clipping issues with the sprites. Overall, pretty disappointed, especially since the core game loop and style are actually pretty good, but there's so many things that detract from the experience that I just can't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm truly glad to see we have learned NOTHING from Ninja Gaiden 3. This game's base combat is amazing. Fluid, fun, and flashy. However, as is all too common nowadays, the variety is genuinely *pitiful*. One weapon, one moveset, ZERO new moves for the entire game. What you begin the game with is what you end the game with. I guess you can buy upgrades for more health and meter, truly the pinnacle of variety. 24.99 is highway robbery for this amount of content. The level design is non-existent, the bar for variety is below the floor, and the length is barely passable. This is a game that stakes everything on gameplay, and then proceedes to give you a sandbox for ants and say "good enough". But hey, at least it has depth! Yep, we got the Kola Superdeep Borehole of gameplay over here, the evil version of No Mans Sky, if you will. Btw developers, adding a leaderboard doesn't suddenly make your game "like an arcade" and isn't an excuse for designing zero progression. Depth is not variety. Stop homogenizing the two, because good action games need BOTH. Maybe that "leaderboard replacing progression" garbage can fly for the two billion low effort, sub-$5 arena shooters plaguing the FPS tag, but not here. Not for 25 dollars. This review has been a little mean spirited, mostly because I'm so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ disappointed. The developers are clearly passionate, and seeing drip Morshu made me genuinely laugh out loud the first time. They're funny too. But this is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unacceptable. I hope we get the Razors Edge treatment, but I don't think that's going to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so so close to being a masterpiece.the offensive side of the combat is fantastic. Fun and satisfying with room to just make it up and still get rewarded with dopamine. There really should be an option to bind EX moves to a button in my opinion. I struggle to do them when i want to and accidentally do them all the time from just inputting quickly.Visuals I have no notes. Looks peak. Sound is similarly no notes. Its not the music i would choose for a game like this but I cant say whats there is bad. Voice acting is also phenomenal.The issue is there are several points this game is lacking in, and they are lacking HARD. There's an overall sense of jank to a lot of things that really could use polishing, but you would hope this polish should be able to be fixed via a patch. Some crashes, weirdness in AI, and some other The game is hard as balls, but most of that comes from the lack of defensive tools. You have a dodge with limited Invul frames, and a parry which you need to input using the stick. The dodge is unreliable and doesn't really help when you are sandwiched, and the parry is way too risky to be used in those same situations. This leads to frequent moments of getting knocked down one time and just being put into a situation that feels unfair and leads to you getting hit a tonMy hope to fix this would be to please for the love of god, add a block button. Make it so you can guard attacks with chip damage as a low risk option to deal with the absolute bombardment the game throws at you. It could also act as a potential input to parrying which would make it easier to do than needing to use the stick to parry. I get you wanna be third strike, but this game does not work with a 3s style parry. Another thing that i genuinely do not understand, why do boss-like enemies not have collision? I can understand why groups of enemies don't, but the bosses that require you to dodge from side to side and parry very precisely do not work as well when you are able to side swap by just doing a standing combo or a heavy move. Its a minor annoyance, but they do add up.Also please add a DP cuz i think it would be funnyI wanna say this game is something special, but as of now it feels like a cool idea that someone else could do way better. There is so much potential in this concept, world, and system, but I can't say its fully there. Please don't abandon this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The demo for this game was fun, and I enjoy challenging action games.  The reason this review is negative is because the game is not hard in a fun way.  It's extremely frustrating to play due to bad level and enemy design.A more interactive tutorial would have been helpful.  It tells you the controls and what stuff does but doesn't let you try it out.  You're thrown to the wolves with a difficulty level that's sometimes like playing another action game on the highest difficulty.Normal enemies flinch when hit and are easy to combo, which is fun.  However, some enemies have super armor.  The sword captain guys like from the first level are fine imo, but the super armor hammer guys in particular are completely overpowered.  it's awful fighting these things when other enemies are present.  They have a very quick, high damage combo attack and an essentially fullscreen clothesline rush that knocks you down in the corner, where you may end up getting gangbanged by a zillion enemies.  Armorbros don't flinch unless you've hit them a certain amount, after which you are allowed to combo them.  However, other enemies can interrupt your precious opportunity to finally combo these damn things.  In many areas of the game there are objects in the foreground that can block the view of the player and enemies.  That stuff should either turn transparent or not even be there.  I'm baffled the developer thought this was fine.  There are also some annoying platforming parts.  The jump controls feel awful, with slow activation and poor control while airborne.  You can walljump on a single wall infinitely like Megaman X so that's usually what you're supposed to do.Bosses are mostly badly designed but not difficult, with one exception.  The bosses that fly feel weird to fight due to the janky jumping controls.  There are also large bosses in the background that can only be hit while they use certain attacks where they move their body onto your plane, but the graphics do a poor job conveying when the bosses are on your plane.  It mostly involved a lot of swinging to see when my attacks would hit or not cause I couldn't tell by looking at the boss.  The only boss that I found to be difficult essentially felt like playing a Guilty Gear match where I can't block and the opponent has super armor.  Burst doesn't even save you when you're being comboed because he has super armor and keeps attacking.  He also has several attacks that are too fast to react to even if you were good at parry timing.  The final boss was much easier but revealed that you cannot wakeup with a crouch instantly after being knocked down which is silly.  There's a laser you need to crouch to dodge, but if it's already on the screen while you are waking up you can't crouch under it and get hit.  The game is fun to play at times so it's a shame the ball was dropped in many respects.  There's a lot of other things I didn't cover that were also annoying.  As it is, I wouldn't recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Balance Issues and Bugs.This could be good, is the problem.For the most part it is, even.However there are several aspects that have been negative enough for me to just drop this despite being at the penultimate level. Lets do the bugs first:The game will occasionally lock up in an 'eternal loading screen' which is an annoyance when it happens but usually not the worst as those typically are between autosaves. Still this shouldn't happen in the first place. Occasionally, if you run past enemies instead of killing them and then get into a 'fight arena' those enemies sometimes count as being part of the fight arena and despite killing all the arena spawns, prevent progress despite the game locking them out of the room when one would expect them to file in easily. Like, the door is right there, my dude. Didn't even lock it. As for the balance issues.Recovery, especially air recovery, is a joke. When you start getting to the larger or more aggressive crowds, you can actually get juggled to death from full if you are just unlucky enough. Yes you do get an on-charge 'get away from me' but maybe you spent that for meter or maybe you spend it and some other enemy literally a pixel out of the range of your shockwave just initiated a dash and hits you anyways because they could avoid the wave.  Actual recovery is a TRAP option. Yes, you heard me right. Air recovery especially is a trap as there are no accompanying I-frames after the recovery to let you recenter/hit neutral again so it is actually legitimately the best option to let yourself hard fall and hope that you have enough screen to dash back make space so you aren't swarmed. The sheer lack of almost any recovery frames for the player when even the mooks you are up against get them is frankly an incredible oversight. Basic mooks get this. You don't. Not really. Also I have no idea if the dodge actually has i-frames or not either. It feels like it doesn't and I would be surprised if it does or if it's more than a literal frame as it feels like it was not made. There are seemingly zero safe wakeup options as well other than the secret moves and those cost a full bar of meter to use. Enemy Super Armor is *♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Obscenely Overtuned*. Like, I understand bosses and such but they should at least still either obey your 'Get away from me' resource that you spend or not just muscle through your clashes and parries with their combo so that what would be a skillful riposte in other games is just "Oh I see you tried to use skill and cancel my attack. Cool, that does nothing to my momentum so ♥♥♥♥ you eat my followup attacks anyway." When the game itself feels centered around controlling a crowd, running into an enemy that flatly ignores your only options you actually have to do this to grab you and throw you across the room is not so much a challenge as just a middle finger. Sure, hit them until you 'poise break' but the actual hits to do that feel equivalent to a health-bar on it's own. I get the impression these are supposed to be 'Duel' foes with their appearances and presentation early on and that's mostly fine aside from those hammer bastards with the huge shoulderplates (those ones feel particularly inexcusable with how much agency they rip out of your hands), and there is an niche for that! And then late in the game they throw a highly mobile, rapid attacker in with one of those hammer bastards and then it's good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck I hope you liked your health bar because I can and have lost tens of attempts to their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ from being juggled to death from FULL HP between them. Because, remember, you don't get the same super armor or recovery like the enemies do.Both of these issues are at their apex at the penultimate boss. He attacks just as fast if not faster than you, will keep attacking through your parries and clashes despite you being unable to do the same to him/his combos are longer so you are going to have to hope he does a string that ends early or moves himself away before you run out of attacks, his super armor recovers extremely quick and you don't get a full combo off of him either, he goes flying after one hit, it seems like, and his already fast attacks get lighting trails behind him as the fight goes on so that you can just get pulled into one hit from a clash and boom you no longer have agency in the fight until you hit the ground again. Assuming he doesn't do the right strings to keep you juggled as if he's trying to do an infinite or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You have no recovery options here. Other than him throwing you clear and thus its safe to do the ground-hop instead of a hard landing, he ignores the pushback due to super armor and you have no safe options or.. The ability to actually put in any inputs anyway. And  you may ask 'but what about the 'Get away' charge?' Guess what! I can and have several times tried using it, the resource disappears, and because you don't get any I-frames, he super-armors and ignores you did anything to try and get control back. Or maybe it's just his attacks are so wide in coverage that your other option to move still whiffs and you get hit and looks like you just burned meter for nothing. Just a total lack of respect for agency. Straight up, it feels untested, almost. Like.. This fight feels like it's built for you to have some kind of i-frame or similar thing to recover but it's just not in the game. Maybe I got this far in through bull-headedness and maybe I missed a literal fundamental part of the game but, if so, then it's not in the tutorial. A few thoughts on controls before closing:Your super mode should not be on the same button as your 'spend meter to dodge' action. Why? Because maybe you want to use that super mode and ♥♥♥♥ YOU FOR HAVING THE CONTROL STICK TILTED HALF A DEGREE! YOU GET FIVE INCHES OF MOVEMENT AND A CHUNK OF METER GONE SO NOW YOU'RE JUST ♥♥♥♥♥♥! Change this or allow remapping. Similarly, 2H (up+heavy on the ground) has this animation lock that feels abysmal. Like, you made the attack and now you have to wait to do anything. Sure, heavy attack so you typically don't want to allow to combo after that, I get it. But I honestly feel like there should be a chance to follow up in the air given how the rest of the animation flows. Like, you are hitting them into the air and you are moving with them so you can follow up with more hits. That is what it looks like you should be able to do with the animation. In actuality you just kinda uselessly throw them in the air with a hit and then it's the wait for them to stand back up so you can hit them again. Doesn't feel good. In closing, I was feeling much more heated while writing parts of this but now I can come back with a more tempered expression. I do think there is a lot of good in the game but it is marred by the bugs which should be polished out and the issues of both balance and the hard removal of player agency to actually interact with a fight. I feel the super armor especially needs to be looked at and reduced greatly. I think bosses of all kinds should respect the tools given to the player to regain footing and breathing room. I think the player should actually have i-frames and recovery options. Heck, give the super mode some super armor or something. This game could be a blast to play.But currently what was fun became frustrating from what frankly feels like a double standard of rules for the player and the enemies with the player at a disadvantage here. Time to put this one down and walk away.
