_childDocuments_.review: Got this game super excited due to the graphics style and description...TLDR: They tried, but the game has an identity crisis and honestly is not very good.This was not playtested, straight up. The mechanics work in such a way that you are truly a glass cannon, however, I don't think that design was intentional. You either walk in, group the enemies up and land a massive combo due to how gold burst + fatal sync works (as the devs call it, The Golden Circle), or you get hit once and stunlocked for several seconds while enemies (or sometimes just one boss) deal large chunks of your health. In some cases, this means spending your burst and doing your best without it, in others, it means you drift slowly towards the enemy once you're up - no air control, no air dash, nothing of the sort to get over full screen projectiles. Very odd choice for a game meant to appeal to fans of Devil May Cry and Guilty Gear. This would be more acceptable if they were just trying to appeal to a niche audience, but it is further hindered by abysmal performance. Roughly half the time I play I experience drops below 30 FPS - my computer can run most games on the highest quality without issues. This, of course, messes with inputs, making it even harder to fight. The story is cool as far as I've seen, but I am not sure I will experience the rest of it. Even after learning cool combos in training mode, all you really need to know is how to abuse The Golden Circle and spam EX moves as hard as possible. Normal combos just fall prey to the fact that you:- Cannot block- Are almost always outnumbered- Can die in two or three interactions - Many enemies have very long super armor, meaning no matter how great your combo game is, you get tapped once and it doesn't matter any more. Should've spammed EX moves.The game also has a very well structured tutorial - for people that skip tutorials. If you actually want to learn the game, third party tutorials are required. This is not an exaggeration, the game has many important mechanics (read: you cannot realistically beat the game without knowing them) that the game never teaches you. No mention in the tutorial, no characters hinting at it, nothing. Air teching, ground teching, super moves, how to break armor, specifics on how combos work - none of these come up in the game, and not knowing them can easily mean getting locked out of progressing through some levels.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Slave Zero X is a sensational game with an even better story but with such glaring flaws it becomes almost difficult to reccomend. 7/10starting with the goodThe story is genuinely sensational, it has fully enthralled me all the way to the end and i love the story progression with shou and isamu and shou and x. this games combat is amazing* but with a massive asterisk. When you're in control you are an unkillable demon with some of the most fun beat em up moves ive ever played, but you have almost no defensive options other than parry and parry doesnt even work when most enemies have meaty attacks that linger past your parry timing. The graphics speak for themselves, the style is so stand out beautiful and the game takes clear inspiration from devilman, guilty gear, dmc, and all the maps were made in the quake engine afaik which honestly helps the style even morethe sections for each calamity really show the calamities characters well, and add a new challenge, thorman is a barebones section as it teaches you the game, enyo has the sniper on you so you're constantly moving, uriel has mostly chase scenes and it really just enhances the games storytelling through gameplaynow the negativeThe difficulty: i dont think the game is too difficult, but the game doesnt scale difficulty well at all. The way the difficulty works is instead of giving you more chances to outplay the opponent, the game just spams enemies and minibosses with super armor that will lock you in hit stun until you die. it is insanely frustrating and doesnt actually make it more difficult to win, just more infuriating to play against. secondly, the game doesnt have great save points, as you finish a section and die 2 sections later and it will reset you to the beginning of the level in some levels instead of the section you died on. In all, I hope this game gets a DLC, I hope it gets updates to add a difficulty selector, I hope that X-Shou is a guest character in a fighting game or that they make their own spinoff fighting game as its clear that fighting games inspired the combat heavily, and I generally do recommend the game to anyone looking for a beautiful spectacle beat em up with a great story, but I cant recommend the game to anyone getting it for the difficulty because it wont challenge you, but just make you irritated in the later levels with enemy spam and hit stun

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, the demo was super fun and the combat is very entertaining and fluid. Unfortunately, among other things, it keeps shoving in stupid platforming stuff on the most janky and awful feeling jumping controls ever. Yes, these work great when you're fighting, it's responsive, floaty enough to get hits, combo loops, and extensions the air, and cancelling into and out of them into attacks is great. When you're faced with platforms and climbing though? This falls apart hard. The collision, acceleration and jump height is all ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, you need to predict when you're stepping off a platform weirdly due to the 2D/3D graphics, and you have to walljump but the walljump is out of a double jump in the right direction, and you sometimes just don't make it over obstacles because the game doesn't feel like it. This can waste a lot of time which in turn makes you rank lower, or get you hit by a stupid hazard which again ruins your ranks.Beyond that the game has only one tool to effectively get away from damage temporarily, that being the Burst mechanic which depletes your Special gauge. The Special Gauge is something you also use to do Special attacks that you can extend combos and do more damage with but it's also used to dodge attacks (think Dark Souls rolls or Trickster in DMC), What this means is 3 mechanics are tied to this gauge and 2 of them are used defensively. Since enemies can stunlock/juggle you forever if they want to because there's always too many with active hitboxes out you need to either be dodging all the time and depleting your gauge, or bursting. Every enemy has enough health to survive a few juggles and they have air recovery just like you with instant attacks right after, this means you'll almost always take a stray hit, meaning you need to burst or be dodging, meaning your gauge is not being used to put out damage and extensions with specials, which gets you hit by recovering enemies, which then means enemies aren't dying before they get to attack. which becomes a loop of sorts soon and then you die. The mechanics are solid on their own but in practice they're not gelling together. There's technically a directional parry but it's very close to frame-perfect, as it should be, but because enemies come at you from both directions and above it's worthless in practice, Royal Guard this is not. Oh, and enemies also like to spawn in with active hitboxes out which is really annoying.This is a really cool looking game, the visuals are great, the sound is great, the combat and combos are great although I wish it had "more" to it. Like DMC-like combo upgrades or stuff like that, but that's asking a lot. If the encounters were less overtuned for that "Arcade" feel which is really just bad design made to waste your money and time, I'd recommend it wholeheartedly. I'll probably end up finishing it and grinding out ranks anyway in the future but it doesn't feel that great right now. The demo conveniently was just the first level which didn't have the ♥♥♥♥ platforming or the more annoying enemies. Blech.

_childDocuments_.review: Less than an hour in and I can see the amazing potential this has to hold my attention for a long time. Tons of skill expression here that I'm excited to explore. Most of the negative reviews that say there are "bugs" are vague so I take that with a grain of salt. Most of the other complaints about the game boil down to frustration over the game's difficulty or an unwillingness to play the game as it is rather than how they expect it to be. I think Dark Souls fans will know the age-old phrase for that - hell, they're watching it play out in real time with all the negative reviews for Shadow of the Erdtree. Only spent about 45 minutes playing, a little over half of that in training mode. Here are my immediate positive takeaways:Very fun and expressive freeform combo system. Like, actually super rich with combo options, I can't stress that enough. Great visual design and art. Fun characters I enjoy so far. Extremely gay story going on there, or at least it looks that way, and also I hope it is, lol. And a few negatives, none of which are experience ruining by any means: Tutorial is bad. Training mode doesn't have a stage without walls to practice on. Had to look at a few combo videos to get an idea of what some basic combo routes could look like, would have been nice to have at least  instruction there in order to get us started. Personal peeve is that jump is a button and not up, but it makes sense for this game so I've just gotta do as we do here and adapt. Overall this looks like a great pick for anyone who loves fighting games. I'll be sure to come back after sufficiently more time and edit this is as necessary but I doubt I'll need to add much unless that one boss I keep seeing in the reviews is actually as hard as they say. Even that will probably just need practice.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game a lot.I'm typically a mechanics-first type of player. The combat system will challenge you at first but will absolutely reward your experimentation as you learn your moveset and the interplay between your meter and burst ability. If character action games and fighting games speak to you, you'll find a lot to love here, including a training room for honing your combos, juggles and wallbounces. In no time at all you'll be parrying and corner-carrying whole hordes of enemies across the screen.From a presentation perspective, the art and aesthetics of the game are extremely striking and really tie together the transhumanist / biopunk atmosphere of the game. This is further buoyed by the writing and wonderful performances from the English and Japanese voice casts. There's really not much else that plays, looks and sounds like this out there.In short: Fun to learn and improve at, great to play and wonderful to look at. You should give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really like the game, the aesthetic is cool and the combat can be really fun. My only major gripe is that some of the combat encounters are straight up just not fun; when you have a large group of enemies combined with one or two that have stagger that you have to work through before they actually get stunned by hits it isn't fun, it's frustrating. There's simply too much stuff happening on screen during these fights for a person to be able to reliably attack or use their defensive options since you have enemies that can actually be staggered mixed in with ones that can't, and their animations blend together so you can't see an attack coming.I don't know what could be done to fix these encounters other than reducing the numbers of enemies for these fights or reworking how the armored enemies work, maybe adding a visible stagger indicator like a bar or making them change color so the player can accurately predict when they'll actually get the stagger.Additions: After playing some more, I've decided to change my recommendation to a not recommended. The issue of the armored enemies only gets worse the longer the game goes on to the point where it's just not fun. It works fine for bosses, but having normal enemies with this armor mixed in with a horde of other enemies on screen does not work and does not make for fun gameplay with how tight your window to parry or dodge is.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 7.5/10. I have never played a more disappointing 7.5/10 in my life. With time to think I actually think less of the game and its sloppily designed moveset that has redundant moves and awkward overlap. I had fun in spite of its design and not because of it.If you like what the Steam Page says this is influenced by, you can find something to enjoy here, but only on a surface level and only if you're ready for a game that expects you to play a certain way. The game's penultimate boss took me over 4 straight hours of attempts, and I did not find him fun. The final boss took me one attempt, and I did not find him fun. While I don't regret buying at launch (since I got the original Slave Zero), I do think this game is not worth $25 as it is; $15 would be ideal. It is, to put it nicely, a game that doesn't feel like it was playtested for balance even once.The good first: This game's presentation is mostly incredible. The Strider 2/Full Metal Forth-esque PS1 graphical style with Dreamcast-level fidelity is pulled off to perfection, the sprite work is on par with early ArcSys titles, the low-poly work is some of the best of any modern release (doubly so in the Quake mod Episode Enyo), the art direction is insane, the voice acting is extremely well-done, the story is simple but effective with a great build to the final area and bosses, the music is consistently good, and the menus/UI are solid. For every frustration I had a moment where the game just looked or sounded incredible to push me forward to see more. I also appreciate a lot of the little touches, like the multiple attack Taunts or the cavalcade of palette swaps/filters.In terms of things that aren't bad but weren't exactly to my taste: Corpse juggling serves zero purpose beyond getting the blood & guts kill animation off of certain moves which only ever matters for a single enemy type that will otherwise explode with a hitbox on death. The lack of any new attacks becoming available besides Ordinances throughout the campaign was a bummer, especially since three of them are variants on the same thing. The tutorial is better than the lack of one in the demo, but there are still several techniques it does not tell you about, though I can tell this was more for the sake of old-school "figure it out" mentality and nothing omitted is THAT integral to playing. The Morshu shopkeep is funny but every time I finished a major plot beat and went to the shop he basically reset the tension as a result, but that's a nitpick.In terms of technical stuff, while I haven't experienced the slowdown people mention, I do have to rebind my controls every single time I boot the game. The game doesn't read my Options button or Touchpad so I need to set Taunt to R3, and the game does not save this setting when I close it.The rest I have to say is negative, and it's entirely on the combat mechanics, balancing, bosses, and encounter design. If you're into this game primarily for the aesthetic or to mess around in Training doing combos forever, then you can just get the game knowing you'll be satisfied. First and foremost, the game says it's inspired by Devil May Cry, but the only real connections are surface level given that there is no visual indication of Style being calculated at all, and taking more than 1 damage in a given encounter will tank your overall Rank even if you have good Style. The combat is significantly more focused on the Guilty Gear end of things, which means the closest thing I can compare it to is Guilty Gear Judgment, which ends up being a great comparison for both the good and bad.That brings me to problem 2: Slave Zero X is nearly impossible without looping Gold Burst into Fatal Sync. Gold Burst, will fill your meter to the maximum on hit. Fatal Sync restores your Burst. Fatal Sync is also your ONLY source of healing outside of the rare mid-stage shop. The insane offensive and mobility options you have when in Fatal Sync allow you to deal with what would otherwise be tedious enemies by overwhelming them. Without Fatal Sync your EX options are very limited and you can regularly waste meter by dashing during normals and getting a cancel, and honestly some of your heavies are kind of bad without the EX, particularly the Air Down. There are some rooms and bosses that I think are a dozen times more difficult if you are left with no meter or Burst, and in times where I somehow get a Blue Burst over a Gold one when I thought I had fully recovered from a knockdown or gotten a Fatal Pulse instead of a Fatal Sync activation (I have never once intended to Fatal Pulse outside of Fatal Sync, needing to be neutral to activate FS has lead to me wasting meter or being hit dozens of times) I usually get mauled and die.That goes into Problem 3: Your defensive options are woefully weak. I genuinely was saved from damage by the Clash system more than Dashes, Parries, & Ukemi combined. The dash has good i-frames but oftentimes trying to dash past some enemies or bosses will get you caught in a hitbox that's way wider/further back than the animation implies. The parry is clearly pulled from Third Strike in terms of its input/function/visual, but it missed the part where the 3S parry has a generous 10f window while I would be shocked if the window here was greater than 3f. This would be much more understandable if the "forward" input wasn't involved in a game where you can freely change direction and multiple enemies can be on either side with unsynced attack patterns; Lieutenants & Atavaka seem clearly built around parrying them to force openings but between odd timing, the short window, and how often you can end up overlapping them to the point where you can't tell if they're even facing you I was never able to consistently get the parry timing down. Ukemi is useful against some enemies in some rooms, but other enemies and bosses either lock you into combos that need to be Bursted which ruins your GB/FS looping or put you in situations where Ukemi just puts you into another attack anyway unless you instantly parry. None of your EXs seem to have i-frames, and your only option that covers both sides is the sadly slow EX Spike.Compounding the defensive issues is just how difficult it is to read the action at times. I already brought up how the parry system completely breaks when your sprites overlap with an enemy, and that just gets worse in the rooms that throw a dozen or twenty or even more enemies at you at once. I will say that the armored enemies have clear visual tells on their strong attacks, but these can easily be obscured in crowds. Enemies with ranged attacks like guns can fire from offscreen, including the Lieutenants' massive fire waves that you NEED to parry (because every time I try to dodge through them the backend clips me). Fights that happen near corners can lead to extremely awkward-looking attack angles and juggles, enemies can be too far offscreen when the camera is locked into an arena, and fights with foreground elements are just plain unfair at times, particularly one near the end of the game in a long hallway.All of this is compounded into Atavaka, who despite incredible buildup throughout the game and a super slick design, is one of the worst-feeling bosses I've ever fought. All of your defensive options are worthless against him besides dodging away, he WILL combo you even if you Burst or Ukemi, you have no breathing room, your parry is a hail mary at best, he WILL meaty you with his hitgrab on your wakeup, he has an actual invincible reversal, his lightning teleports are near-impossible to dodge or parry on reaction, and worst of all, the only thing you can do to maneuver him is to run. He will run at you full force if you create distance, giving you openings to get in potshots with your Light string and Ordinances until he Guard Breaks after which you can Fatal Sync to dump your damage. That is the lamest way to handle such a cool boss but it was the only one that worked

_childDocuments_.review: I want to state my purpose here up front: I want to praise Slave Zero X because I think it’s the kind of game I’d like to see more of made. It’s a genuinely impressive package, but I also think there are a lot of glaring issues with the title that will make many people hate it. So let’s do a compliment sandwich and do some constructive criticism.Slave Zero X is, if nothing else, oozing with style. The art is full with biopunk monstrosities and sexy twinks. The music is brimming with cyberpunk arpeggios, wailing guitars, and thumping breakbeat. The spritework is beautiful and intricate, and watching this game in motion (especially a skilled player) can be a thing of beauty. You can unlock special shaders, which I think is a fun touch. This is a small easter egg, but I also think it’s really cool that the levels in the Episode Enyo prequel are actually based on the 3D environments you move through in this game.I also love the boldness of its narrative. It is unabashedly gay, for one, but I also think there is a deeper subtext of sex and gender here, of being at war with ones own body and seeking to reshape it. There is also an anarchist bent to its politics, which tie into Hegelian dialectics of power and rejects all authorities it can, be it government or gods. I don’t want to make it sound like it’s super highbrow. It’s all over the place. The lore bites range from some silly notes to eerie eschatological poetry. It’s very brash and loud. There’s a vulgarity to it, both in its satire and in its visuals, that feels like this hideous, pulsating mass of raw anger.Okay, let’s change gears. Most people who say they like hard games are kind of lying, including me. What they mean is that they want games that are hard in specific ways. They want games that challenge them in familiar ways. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve seen people say, “I like hard games, but this is just unfun”; sometimes it’s coming from my own mouth. Games like Volgarr the Viking come to mind, unrelenting and unorthodox challenge boxes. Ugh, I’ll try to keep this short. The point is that “hardness” is a nebulous and subjective thing that is seen as something that we can mark objectively and quantitatively, even though the exact ways in which a game is hard or unfair depends on so many variables intersecting. I’m not making a novel point here, but that’s why some games get lauded for their difficulty and others are scorned.I think that’s what Slave Zero X is. A game that is hard in ways people usually don’t want. That’s partially because of its ambition: it wants to be a fighting game and an action game in one. I think Slave Zero X wants to be Strider 2 but ends up being more like Ninja Warriors Return. And hey, that’s not a bad thing at all. What I mean is that combat in Slave Zero X, like in Ninja Warriors Return, tends to be very flat. You can launch and juggle people in the air, sure, but the majority of the game is forward movement. I really think the game could have done with a lot more verticality, but that also might have resulted in new issues. But it also ends up feeling a bit repetitive at times.But if you run through this game mashing the light attack button, you will eventually hit a brick wall, and wonder why the game is punishing you. That’s partially because the game isn’t very good at communicating to you what’s going on. The tutorial is quite bad; it just throws a dozen pages of text explaining the mechanics at you once and then sets you loose. But it goes deeper than that, I think. For example, you have a parry that you execute by pressing a direction toward the attack, but since it has no animation and is in a very small window, it’s often not clear when or why you’re missing the mark with your timing. And while there’s a training room, all that really helps you with is comboing. And comboing does feel great here, it really does. But that’s also not the thing you need the most practice on in order to beat the game.I think the key issue with Slave Zero X comes down to encounter design. One of the common action game design paradigms right now is a style that sees players progress through a series of arenas where enemies funnel in as you fight through them for some amount of time before eventually moving on. This is often paired with a combat system that produces self-sustaining feedback loops (recovering health or ammo, that is) that sort of dictates the flow of combat. As pointed out by one Campster, this kind of structure often lead to combat feeling pretty samey, as the pace of combat is entirely determined by the player and thus does not often get disrupted. But this trope has its place, and can be done well, but in order for it to be fun for long periods of time, you often need to be introducing new mechanics and enemies on a pretty frequent basis, which doesn’t really happen here.Slave Zero X’s arenas end up feel awfully repetitive. New enemies aren’t introduced often, and you have to fight hundreds of them. The screen will often be filled with dozens of identical enemies for you to hack away through, which can be okay as fodder, I guess, but these masses can combo you, often for a long time. If you don’t have Burst up, you just have to lie back and take it for however long they juggle you. And getting combo’d is one of those classic things thats fun to do to an enemy but never for an enemy to do to you. It’s no coincidence that Slave Zero X is at it’s best when you’re fighting a small number of enemies rather than in its massive cavalcades of fodder.A lot of the tougher enemies have attacks with insanely fast windups that lead into combos; even in a one-on-one fight I couldn’t really counter them consistently. They’re so fast that I think they may be literally impossible to parry reliably, and even if they’re not, they might as well be for most players. This is all exacerbated by the encounter design, which means that will all the enemies being thrown at you, it is often hard to tell what’s hitting you, let alone predict it and counter.So when you’re not successfully juggling armored cops and parrying like the cyberninja you’re supposed to be, you’re often getting bodied and juggled in a way that makes you feel powerless. The result is a game that will frustrate most players. I’m not going to backseat game design and act like I know exactly how to fix it, though I definitely have ideas. But that is the reality: this is a game that’s hard in a way that many people will reject. It’s unfortunate, because I think with changes, it could be a much stronger and approachable game with a wider appeal.But despite all these issues, I can’t say I think it’s a bad game. It’s a mess, yes, but it’s got so much style, so much ambition, and it’s combat does feel great when it works. During the right boss fight or the right set up of enemies, it feels like a dynamic flurry of blades, and you’ve somehow mastered it at the center of it all. While you’re not given a lot of opportunities for customization of your kit, your kit feels good to begin with. X-Shou feels sort of sticky and rigid in a way that is very novel, making in a distinctive feeling combat where a lot of your movement is done through attacks and dashes rather than running or walking. You juggle and bounce and parry and slash and gib fascists. It can be a blast.Again, this is a game I want to see more games like. I want to see games that take inspiration from the arcade era, that are ambitious in their design, that go hogwild on their fiction, that inexplicably reboot forgotten titles as completely different games, that are gay and radical and flashy and deranged, that are extra in every way possible, that are like Slave Zero X is.

_childDocuments_.review: You know that horse meme where the horse is split into 4 separate drawings? The first part is beautifully drawn, and it just progressively gets worse until the 4th part, where it's essentially a crappy stick figure.That's how I'd describe my time with Slave Zero X.It starts off incredibly strong but somewhat ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed halfway through. Gameplay starts to feel like a chore. I love fighting game mechanics but it doesn't all mesh well here. Third strike Parry is too strict and the overall feeling is janky. The amazing first half is canceled by the piss-poor second half resulting in Slave Zero X being a very mid-tier title. Feels like some amazing ideas clumsily strung together.Hopefully there's a patch soon to address things but until then - Pick it up on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding game. Maybe not the most approachable, but absolutely worth playing if you like getting your ass beat so you can feel really good when you win.Beat-em-ups with fighting game mechanics have been done before, but Slave Zero X really makes a beautiful and functional marriage out of the two genres that doesn't compromise one for the other, and asks a lot of attention and experimentation of the player to boot. It feels good to control, the freedom of the combo system is dizzying, and if you really want you can pop Devil Trigger and turn yourself into a chainsaw, too. There isn't a single wasted enemy slot, with every one filling a certain purpose and requiring at least some adjustment on the part of the player, so with the right strategy even encounters that initially appear overwhelming can be cleared with style.While all this would be good enough to get a good score from me on its own, this game also has absolutely killer art direction and a banger soundtrack; "awful cyberpunk dystopia" isn't exactly a rare thing to see in media nowadays, but the biomechanical designs throughout (as well as the unbelievably cool protagonist) really make this one feel even more awful, to the point it feels fresh. There's so much effort put into the presentation that I'm actually glad a game is going for retraux PS1 era graphics for once, since it works well with the almost alien environments and characters.It's addicting enough to actually warrant replaying levels for a better score, which I feel a lot of these stylish hack-and-slash games fail at. It's short enough that it's lightning in a bottle, but not so short that it feels fleeting; it's brutal, but there's ways to make it easier. Everything you can do is geared towards making you feel as cool as humanly possible, as long as you put in the effort to earn that coolness. With only a few bugs that I'm sure will be patched as time goes on, for me this is probably one of the best games that'll come out all year. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings towards this game but i think its charm just barely outweighs its faults.The story, music and graphics are all great and made me want to dive deeper into this universe, and i was fairly invested by the end of it, The story of a human's fusion with a weird sentient armor thirsty for blood was entertaining and even quite touching at times, and the wonderfully rendered 3-D backgrounds and dopamine-inducing animations make for a lot of memorable moments,The combat on the other end is voluntarily made obtuse and can quickly turn into a mess where you either juggle every enemy on screen or get juggled yourself until your health bottoms out, It's fun when it works, but expect cheap deaths and plenty of restarts with some frustrating checkpoint placements to boot.It's entertaining, clunky and very unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically, it's a sidescrolling beat'em-up with extra fighting game flair, including combos, cancels and evens parries. Thematically, it's a 90's OVA with beautiful sprites and a great soundtrack. Surprisingly robust yet unobtrusive narrative too.Personally, I love it. Yeah, it has flaws if you were to, say, dissect it with your FGC PhD but that would be missing the point pretty hard.e: If you're struggling - you can use burst to fill your meter and then use Fatal Sinc to build burst (and heal) back, pretty much having infinite meter. Just make sure to burst while you're attacking (as opposed to when you're getting hit) and that you're completely neutral when using FC.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: If you thought Panzer Bandit on the PS1 should've should've been a bit more like Strider 2, you need to play Slave Zero X. Right now. Don't wait. Just buy it.As for everyone else... it's a big maybe, at least for now. It's exciting, challenging, and deep, but it's also a bit rough around the edges.At the time of writing, there are a few softlock and hard crash bugs. This is on top of weird little combat bugs that, depending on your playstyle, could result in some frustrating moments. I'm confident these issues will get ironed out pretty soon, so no biggie there.And when they do get ironed out, people with even a passing interest in stylish hack and slash beat em ups should really give it a try! Until then, only hardcore folks that can forgive some technical jank should dive in. I will edit this review when I feel this no longer applies.What's less likely to change much with patches is the pacing of the game and its overall difficulty.It's short enough that if you're a gamer that highly values the time/money proposition, you may be disappointed. Yet it's also long enough that if you're expecting an arcade-like experience, you're in for something that will feel like it's dragging a little. The variety in enemy behaviors and encounters is just enough to entertain enthusiasts of the genre, but I can imagine a lot of players finding them to be repetitive.And man, a lot of players will STRUGGLE with this game. Maybe that appeals to you. It sure appeals to me. But be warned, this game intentionally does not explain itself well. You must experiment and dig at its mechanics, dying over and over to enemies until you finally figure out how the game wants you to play. You WILL be swarmed by absurd amounts of enemies. You WILL get juggled to death. You WILL get attacked after your air recovery if you can't time a parry. You WILL be shot at by an offscreen enemy. And by god, I hope you enjoy it.And I did enjoy it! There's a chance you'll enjoy it too! Games like this don't come around often, so if you think you're in the target demographic, I can only give the highest recommendation possible for this truly remarkable game.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, but its abit hard to recommend. its very stylish, art and music are strong, and I dont see much mentions about it, but I like the story and dialogue. I like the banter with X and shou. Especially X, she can be kinda funny at times. The world building and lore and excellent, especially if you read the data entries. The game has one fatal flaw but it can be overcome, and I will dub it as.... NEVER STOP STYLING. The game basically has zero defensive options and you get swarmed by crowds, no air dashing, you can be punished for doing an ukemi (recovery) you can be punished for bursting, and lets be real parries are cool, abit hard to tell what you can parry when theres a crowd of 20 sprites stacked on top of each other. the parry isnt good either, it doesnt cause an enemy to reel, it doesnt push them back, and for some enemies, their attack hits multiple times (looking at you hammer guy where your SPARKS do damage).   The remedy? NEVER STOP STYLING. The games biggest feature is its robust combo system. If you can juggle like a CHAMPION, this game devolves into one big combo lab. you can totally juggle 20 people. And in this sense, the game is actually good if you treat it like a zen combo lab. You need to have smokin sick style BY DEFAULT to have a good time here.with this being said the game has fake difficulty. and by that I mean in order to add challenge the game likes to put foreground elements, and make some rooms really dark, and in one case in area 6....Put shadow people in a room with a black background. THANKS SLAVE ZERO. "You cant parry what you cant see butt lord!" says the game devs.Overall I liked my experience, because I AM A GOD COMPARED TO YOU. I am a FREAK. That plays combo trials in fighting games for fun EVEN FOR CHARACTERS I DONT USE. I did the abel trials in SF4, AND THE DAHLSIM ones! My default state is SSS! And if you cant do that you probably wont have fun, you'll probably just be really frustrated. In the future if they ever do slave zero 2, probably balance the game abit better, maybe use something like the ninja saviors or hell double dragon gaiden as a template and not...one on one fighting  a genre distinctly not one on one.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay of Slave Zero X is incredible, and the art and music is second to none. It could genuinely be one of the best action games ever, but there are so many weird decisions holding it back:- Enemies start appearing in huge, unmanageable hordes on third level and beyond. It's a complete visual cluster****. Enemies that explode or have armored attacks get mixed into the mayhem and make it impossible to consistently deal with the large groups.- In some areas, enemies can go off the side of the screen, outside of your attack range but still able to attack you. In other areas, they wallbounce. Just make the side of the screen always wallbounce!- Weird scoring system (you'll either get an S or an E, nothing in between).- Perspective shifts around corners and behind foreground objects, obscuring enemies and making combat confusing (even though it's visually cool when not fighting).- Obnoxious flashing sniper reticle in level 2 obscuring the action. - No airdash, tiny hitbox on izuna drop and meat spike attack.- You can easily get juggled for almost your entire health bar. If you already used your burst, there's nothing you can do.- The window to perform ex attacks is too small (this could be a skill issue on my part lol).- Can't preview costumes and filters before buying.- Bad tutorial and no combo challenges.- Devil trigger and roman cancel are both on the same button, so you'll often do the wrong one by accident (change it so you hold down the button for devil trigger!).- You can't exit and save your progress in the Bloody Palace-like mode, so you have to do the entire thing in one sitting (also, I got to round 13 and no more enemies spawned, so I couldn't progress anyway).This game is ALMOST a masterpiece, but it has some critical mistakes that I'm shocked were overlooked. I'm only listing nitpicks because it seems like the devs are reading the reviews. If these issues get fixed, we are looking at a perfect action game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent art, gameplay, sound design, ost, voice acting, etc, and all for a cool $25.  This game is really indicative if that 90s to early 2K era of gaming.  Honestly recommend giving this one a look if you're even kinda interested.  It's totally worth, and if you're a Blazblue fan it's the closest you're ever getting to playing Hakumen ever again. However...I'm putting a thumbs down until some MAJOR issues get fixed, unfortunately.As a bit of a disclaimer, I'm going to put my summarized adjustments I would put in the game here, and if you want to see my pathos you can see my MLA format essay below:-Adjust Shou Air mobility (steerable jump, airdash (maybe?) or air special with horizontal momentum)-Adjust Burst to work on armored enemies, either a full armor shred or just a knockdown (perhaps make blue burst fullscreen)-Slow some enemy attacks and attack timings-Reduce Shou's hitstun, so you don't die from 1 infinite-Move the giant objects from the foreground-Increase visibility in dark rooms/on black enemies or make those sections purely setpieces with an invul Shou-Give Shou invincibility options (get up tech roll, aerial tech roll, up special working as an invincible reversal, better dodge)-Make enemy heavy attacks have a flashing effect to see them in a room full of people-Boss healthbars-Reduce importance of taking damage in rankings, actually put emphasis on style and what is stylish-Reduce enemy armor, (only the general mini boss and super heavies should have neutral state super armor imo, attack hyper armor should stay)-Fatal Sync health applies instantly-Use attack button to recover since there's no blocking anyway, or just add a block buttton-Checkpoint reset-Move list-Fixed ranking system, you can't even style on Herc technicallySmall issues:-Bugged Atavaka boss, chance the game softlocks when you beat him-Bugged izuna drop that sometimes does no dmg/has no FX, enemies never died when that happened so unsure-Bugged Uriel boss fight where if you skip the dialogue your UI will not load-Bugged stage 2-1, cutscene where Shou stops where the jumbotrons in the BG are causes softlock from unclear circumstances-Sound mixing needs work-Platforming in a game with a crap jump-Enemy hard knockdown takes too long-Shou down special doesn't hit up top-Softlock on Crimson CItadel stage 6-Crimson Citadel stats carry back into main game-No variable enemies in training roomBIG issues:-Too many rooms have GIANT objects that obstruct your vision or set pieces that use the color jet black to ♥♥♥♥ with you, whether that's the room itself going black or enemies being that color with silhouettes running around, I respect the artistic vision but for a game this unforgiving you either need to sacrifice the vision or add some player leniency-Enemies layering on top of eachother in rooms where you're getting jumped is purely a death sentence.  Not only can you not see enemy attack tells, but when an enemy decides to get your back, you may as well put your controller down.-Enemy tells are not strong enough.  Paired with the visual problems above the lack of strong sounds and flashing visuals to tell you "this is the BIG one, get away" (like the first mini-boss' giant sword swing), sometimes you will just get hit with a stray grab that will just put you from full to half even with a decent number of health upgrades.-Some enemy attacks are entirely too fast for the reward, my specific cited example is Herc and Aratavaka, the both have jab strings they hitconfirm into that chunk your health and juggle you way out, in the latter's case it leads to an infinite but I'll get to that later-Shou's defense is not good.The parry's window of activation is so tight that unless you're buffering it during hitstop it's unreliable at best, but once I learned that trick it's clear how centralized of a defensive mechanic it is, as in the game WANTS you to parry everything like it's MGR but the enemy tells and nature of the 2D doesn't allow for that very often outside of the odd 1v1.Outside of that, the dodge is nigh useless; as a "get me the hell outta dodge" mechanic, it's trash as using Shou's fwd heavy attack is a better evade button in terms of pure distance.  As an invincibility mechanic, it's also trash as it either has a negligible number of i-frames or just doesn't work sometimes, I have taken more hits trying to dodge than just mashing forward during hitstop.His jump is also not much better as you can't control the jump trajectory outside of double jumping and the height doesn't clear most attacks you really wanna get away from, so even if you do jump away you'll probably land on something else.  This also makes the Enyo fight very tedious,And Burst fills two major purposes; "get me outta this mook enemy infinite" (in which it does superb work) or "I need Fatal Sync rn."  Outside of that, it may as well not be there.  You WILL get your burst baited by enemies with armor on because they literally don't care (lookin at you super heavy) and as if this is an actual fg with fg balance, you cant burst throws??  The same throws that are parryable??-Enemy attack timing is way too fast.  If even TWO enemies decide to stagger their attack timing even slightly, you are subject to their mercy until one breaks the chain.-You take entirely too much hitstun.  I feel like every hit is the GGStrive counter hit with how LONG you're just no longer allowed to play the game.  Every enemy is playing the game by your rules so essentially (sometimes literally) you're just in a room with 20 Shous and if even one lands a hit, see above.  There really should be an invincible techroll option since this game already wants to be singleplayer GG in a lotta ways.-No enemy healthbars.  This is more QoL than anything, but optimizing rooms in a game this volatile would go a lot smoother if you could see enemy health at LEAST on heavy units.  Bosses should have one you can see though, there's no real reason not to.-Scuffed ranking system.  Basically this game doesn't really give a damn how cool you look beating it as long as you do it without getting hit and relatively fast.  TOO much value is put on getting hit in a game this volatile with constant pot shots that you just can't react to.  This means you make less money, you get less upgrades, it takes longer to hang with the later levels.  The progression feels like Gungrave GORE.-You are ultimately thrown to the wolves.  I get the retro game feel you're going for, but that tutorial in the first 10 mins of the game is just not enough.  There are so many things ab the game that go unexplained like the clash system which seems to be a superior alternative to parrying.And this section is specific beef with design choices I don't agree with but is largely more subjective:-There are SO many attacks that give so much reward with crazy disjoint; Hercules ground slam,  Super Heavy throw, Atavaka's whole kit, mind you he WILL just take you to the corner and infinite you to death.  Disjoints in a jumping simulator is just not necessary.-If you run sometimes you miss dialogue, pet peeve.-Enemies can WALK OFFSCREEN and start mixing you, the walls should apply to them as well.  Better yet, the DMC rule should take effect, where if the are no longer visible, they are not allowed to start attacking.-Perhaps this will make cheese too simple, but fatal sync health should apply instantly or you should just get more health from fatal sync.  You can't turn it off in hitstun and I'm assuming that's so enemies can waste your timer, which balances it out.-Blue Burst should be fullscreen, get away from me.-Genuinely, this game's difficulty can be summed up as "well it WAS going well but then they gave this enemy armor," and if it were MY game no enemies would have armor outside of some attacks.  It's a cheap way to spike the difficulty, and it's just as bad in every other game it's in, like DMC, MGR, Bayo, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely not for everyone. If you like fighting games or beat em ups, you won't necessarily enjoy this game. I love this game though. The art, the presentation, the story, the characters, and combat are all great. This does not play like a traditional 2D side scroll beat em up. This game focuses a lot on crowd control and juggle combos. To put it frankly, you have to play as cheap as possible, while your enemies are just as cheap. You can keep enemies stun locked for as long as you want, besides bosses and mini bosses. The enemies can do the same to you. This can be frustrating at times, but it's about learning how to group and control enemies. You are given defensive options with a burst, parry, and dodge, but they don't feel very strong overall. They exist to help you narrowly avoid attacks but if you're surrounded then outside of burst, you're gonna get juggled to death. I didn't find this game too hard. I struggled a little bit at first but once I learned how to properly keep fatal sync up at all times, then the game really opened up. You activate fatal sync in neutral, then you have faster attack speed, infinite EX moves, and life regen. I always tried to end fatal sync with an aoe super. This is extremely helpful for bosses because the super will almost always put them in a break state. Once it's over, you just burst an enemy for full meter again and then you can go right back into fatal sync. This is the loop I imagine the devs wanted for combat. My only complaint is I wish there more moves you could use with button inputs. The only ones that require some sort of input are the two secret special moves. I feel like with more move variety, the game would allow more expression for combos.All in all, this is a niche game for a niche audience. I personally loved it, and will probably pull my hair out trying to get S rank on all stages. Here's to hoping we get something like this again in the future or a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is most certainly one of my picks for game of the year 2024.  It's basically what happens when you fuse Guilty Gear with Strider with a heavy dose of classic Devil May Cry, and yes, it's as awesome as implied.  If anyone's played a character action game like Devil May Cry or Ninja Gaiden, you know what you're expecting and what you're expecting is top flight gameplay from the very same people that brought us one of my favorite shmups Devil Engine.  Then of course there's the storytelling, which is genuine late 80s/early 90s cyberpunk anime as hell.  It's basically a prequel to the OG Slave Zero, and of course I love that game to death, especially for the late 80s/early 90s cyberpunk anime aesthetic nowhere outta place in works like Ghost in the Shell and Neon Genesis Evangelion (two of my absolute favorite anime btw), but the basic setup is still the same in that you're a warrior of the resistance fighting against a totalitarian tyrant named SovKhan that rules the dystopian future world with a fist of IRON & FLESH (yeah, that sounds way too metal for words to describe).  One minor criticism I will levy at the game would be the rather homoerotic romance subplot, while not terrible and would totally not be outta place in a 90s boys love visual novel, just ain't to my taste and it's really more a me issue than anything.  But overall, this game is certainly a well crafted love letter to not just classic video game design philosophy but a very much well crafted love letter to classic cyberpunk anime like Bubblegum Crisis, Bio Booster Armor Guyver, Tekkaman Blade, and of course the aforementioned Ghost in the Shell and Neon Genesis Evangelion.  So if you haven't gotten this game already, do so ASAP.

_childDocuments_.review: - It's a single-player fighting game that lets you combo the ♥♥♥♥ out of anyone and everyone,- It's got a fast paced, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story,- The art both in game and in cut-scenes are phenomenal, - It's a challenge             - Overall, not detrimental to the fights, it makes them a little unresponsive, in my opinion, but it could definitely be adjusted to if the devs consider no healthbars to be critical to the style of game. I just think that it's a bit weird that the ONLY place you can obtain damage and health numbers is in the training room. IMO this discourages me experimenting anywhere that is not the training room, especially bosses, as lack of feedback means I can't really tell what's effective and what's not.           - Overall, they're great, but one flaw holds it back for me: you can't turn around while attacking. It just makes the combat a slight bit more sluggish, and not feel quite as smooth as it possibly could. Again, if considered critical to gameplay, it could be overlooked. (this is where the rant begins)Up until this point, all of the game's difficulty spikes have been due to stronger and stronger enemies appearing, forcing the player to utilize the mechanics they underuse. This is genius. This is good game design. However, what is not good game design, is the current roadblock of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, which has almost led two perfectly good playstation controllers to their demise, Enyo. This boss is an amalgamation that shows you exactly what your limitations are by exploiting every single bit of muscle memory the game has built up by this point. This is where everything that could be overlooked for the sake of creating a unique style of game turns into a detrimental flaw that makes you want to break things. Enyo is the culmination of all the minor annoyances I have with the game, but let's go one at a time.Lack of air mobility:When you are in the air, you are locked into your current trajectory, and the only way to alter it is to land a parry or grab. This becomes painfully apparent when Enyo starts to juggle the ♥♥♥♥ out of you because you recovered in-air out of muscle memory. You cannot move in the air. Enyo is in the air. If you jump to attack her, and she lands a single hit, she can and will juggle the ♥♥♥♥ out of you, regardless of whether you jump to recover or not. The only way to avoid getting juggled is by parrying her attacks, however, only two of the attacks she will use at close range are parryable. Her multihit moves are basically a death sentence. The lack of a air-dodge, or i-frames while falling makes her fight miserable.Wonky hitboxes:Enyo's hitboxes are ridiculously large, and linger for far too long. The only two things I will say is that guns do not shoot backwards, and bullets are usually no longer dangerous after you hear them hit the ground.Camera issues: It seems like all similar games are plagued by ♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera systems. This one isn't bad, but there is one huge flaw: ENEMIES SHOULD NOT BE ABLE TO BE PUSHED OFF SCREEN. It is an easily fixable issue that has no reason to exist in the first place.Overall, great game tho, would recommend. 8/10, but has potential to be a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very interesting I personally still like it regardless of the issues it has but that definitely isn't a excuse for the handful of bugs/issues this game has like the jumping when platforming, how the wall jumping interacts at times, and for this game being a hack n slash no command list which most if not all the most popular hack n slash games have a command list it's just obviously something you should have. the parrying in this game i feel could be better it feels hard in a sense which I enjoy the challenge but theres a difference betweeen games that have a hard parry = nice reward and then just this game not having any reward for the most part for parrying, the timing to hit the parry feels hard in a bad way i dont wanna say its impossible to parry but i mean there is no huge reward for parrying despite how hard it is to land a parry and because of that you're better off just continuing to slash through enemies and not care about parrying. I won't rant more than I already have but I will say I think this game needs to quickly try and resolve these issues because its luckily not a huge issue but rather this game has a lot of small issues that could be fixed but due to the big amount of small issues that overwhelms this game as a whole. Though despite all of this good ost, I love how this game tilts towards juggling your enemies thats always fun level design is really nice as well and all the characters are good the movement in this game is fine and thats all i gotta say.

_childDocuments_.review: Even as a fan of most of everything this game is inspired by, I got filtered.The brutal difficulty curve that hits as early as the third or fourth stage was frustrating enough that it drained any enjoyment I got from the parts of the game that I did like.This is a game that actively delights in trying to gut you and string you up from the rooftops by your entrails. It does not ease you into anything, offers very little to help you, and demands a lot from you. If that sounds good to you, you'll probably like it more than I did.I think "single-player fighting game" is a niche that has a lot of potential, but I didn't have a lot of fun with what I played here and didn't expect that to change if I kept at it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so many bugs and issues, and after almost killing Atavaka (who is the penultimate boss) he disappeared and basically "noped out" when he realised I was about to win. So honestly, I had to just uninstall lmao I do think that the game is actually quite fun early on if you like beat em up style combat and don't mind being ganged up on as its all about crowd control. But later on the game gets tedious and frustrating and I just was not enjoying how each combat encounter would recycle the same enemies and there are some REALLY annoying enemy types, most notably these "gold" hammer captain guys (legit harder than half of the bosses in the game lol).That brings me onto the bosses, they all suck after the first boss (gimmick boss fights), that's about all really. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely bonkers 2D action game. Tough and not at all fair, but the protagonist is overtuned to hell and back to make up for this game's bs.Divekicking resets your double jump infinitely, both taunts have a hitbox that leads into juggles, you got loops, restands, wallbounces, groundbounces, dash cancels, the list goes on. Plus! This game essentially gives you infinite meter 100% of the time if you play it right, so you can go crazy with all the most powerful tools you have (which are MANY). It's a combo playground of the best kind.It's a little rough right now though. It has a handful of bugs (raging demon will glitch your game out at some point for some reason), performance problems and overall some gameplay quirks gotta be ironed out, but overall it's an extremely enjoyable experience. It's definitely a game that caters to a very, very specific audience, but if any of this sounds exciting to you, yeah. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Slave zero x was a game i was extremely hype for as the art and design just screamed it very much my vib, So much glorious bio-horror goodness as well as fun hacking and slashing but what i didn't know was just how hard it was going to be as well as it having some sad gays in a dystopia.Playing the demo i expected a bit of difficulty and work that any real game would ask ya to do but in reality's playing the full game ask you to really deep dive into it combat to make sure you get an edge in and don't get rocked and socked by some baddies. that is both it greatest strength and frustration as the game has the best and worst aspects of playing a fighting game with others. as the depth of the combos and systems make you feel amazing very easily but if you come up against a few enemies that will test your understanding and timing. this can end up feelin like your pop into play a game with some rando and then just get destroyed were you cant even move sometimes as they end up locking you down via stunlock.There is a parry and burst mechanic that is meant to elevate this problem but the parry unlike the burst/gold bursting that you use to break out of a attack string is very difficult to wrap you head around at first and only really did i start to get it going consistently on the last few levels. So the games skill asks are very much up there and that is definitely going to turn off a lot of folk. the training mode is definitely a big plus in trying to help people deal with getting a ahold of some mechanics but lacks a dedicated move list to help getting time and some other combos so it has a limited for help if you not sure what to do sometimes but in the end since it can just be out right frustrating were i ended up just walking away for a few hours sometimes (looking at you super hammer bros, i eventually got your number but you still a ass)Alongside that just some minor hiccup with performance in some stages or the camera getting caught up in the air for a but are more minor bug and don't really hurt the over all experience of playing the game. the only semi major bug/glitch i found was one enemy accidently being nocked outside of the world when knocked into a corner during one fight but that only happened once, so i cant say for sure how prevalent that can be with out doing some testing to find out if it do-able or a one off.Story and visual wise the games soundtrack and art direction is great and really hit that biopunk itch that is very underused in well most media. so it was extremely nice sight to see as as you make your way through this grungy post apocalyptic city. animations are equally great to see as thing are flued and well rendered to help ya get each ones place in combat as well as the sort of solider or weird flesh monster they are in a big ol blob of dude your about to style on. the games story was one you can kinda really easy pick up on what there going to be going for but is still carry well but some great casting and performances and some well written if flowerily dialogue. I say flowerily but i don't mean that in a negative and it not all the time but the way the story is written it really want to hit the dramatic beat really well. the only area the game somewhat flounders is when it does these big ol dramatic beat it really lack having a few distinct track's to help the more dramatic scenes really hit that BIG dramatic crescendo or really to give a boss fight a very specific vib that unique to them, it all sounds good but i wish there a few one off tracks is all in the end.Still the story of shou and X's quest for vengeance is well told and by the end both this angry pretty boy and his bloodthirsty biomecha lady come out better and as over come the anger at the word to become something more together. also dang if i had a nicked for indie developed games that has sad gay leads that use a lot of really popping red in the character design and are scifi dystopia's with some biohorror elements to them, I'd have two nickels which is great. I need a lot more more nickels please.I Would definitely recommend the game as it's good parts make the annoying or frustrating parts are worth dealing with and overcoming in the end. the combat feel fun as hell and the story is fun and well made and just pack one wallop of style in for face. Just very much be prepared for a game that ask you to really dig into itself as it a tough one.

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: The controller input mapping is horrible and does not let you remap controls if your pad does not have enough buttons to map the taunt button; this is unfortunately the case of standard arcade sticks (Hori, Qanba).You can simply use Steam's own controller remapping feature to work around it; I almost wish the game remapping tool was a simple screen that said "just use Steam's remapping".As for the game, it's great. However, I find giving DMC and GG as influence make the comparison frustrating. These games are very "flowy", whereas SZX has some old-school clunkiness. Finding which attacks can be canceled into which ones, also feels clunky as the input system that feels much less logical than either reference. Guilty Gear Judgement is by far my favourite beat'em up of all time because of its expanded Roman Cancel system that gives it unequalled freedom and depth; yet GGJ is lacking in other aspects (story and design) so there's room to improve. SZX seems more like an alternative evolution to 90's Strider. An interesting take into its own conventions that needs to be learned.

_childDocuments_.review: Flawed masterpiece of epic proportions, worth the admission price simply for the graphics, music and the incredibly robust yet very flawed combat, let me talk about it.The first thing that hits you is nostalgia, this game reminds me of 2 games from the ps1 era, mostly STRIDER 2, a rarely talked about game and also SILENT BOMBER, another even more obscure title.This game used the same style of graphics as STRIDER 2 , sadly doesn't use the same amazing combat in that game.The art is just sublime, very organic and metallic at the same time, reminder of HR GIGGER work and a lot of early 80s anime like GUYVER.Didnd't care much for the girly looking characters that tried to mimic VAMPIRE HUNTER D but failed, the music and sound effects are great also.The combat, it is clear they tried, but it feels more like luck more than skill, it pains me when i parry most moves by mistake, and it looks damn cool.Lack of training mode kills the game , i hear about EX-MOVES and PARRIES and yet, it is not well explained, and i still look at the HUD and can't make heads or tails from it.The game is downright brutal where u get stunlocked a lot, the only way to even stand a chance is to use the old DOUBLE DRAGON technique from the 80s, make sure to put all the enemies on one side.Also , for such a primitive game, seeing the frame rate drop a lot is insane, at one point, i paused the game, went back and it was like 1fps....shameful. BUT, and here what it counts,  U WANT MORE, U CRAVE MORE, each time u play, u get a bit better, a bit wiser, a bit more aggressive, a bit more on the defence and when it clicks.............IT WILL ROCK YOUR WORLD.Highly recommended if u are the kind of person that appreciated a once in an era game and a lot of jank.

_childDocuments_.review: Slave Zero X is a side scrolling beat em up, that serves as a prequel to 1999's Slave Zero, which was a third person mech shooter, so already, there is an issue in terms of who this game is for. No doubt, fans of the original would be curious to check out what was done with the IP after 20 years of disuse, and I have to assume this would be a sizable chunk of the game's audience. This didn't necessarily have to be a problem, provided that the game made any attempt whatsoever at being accessible, but no, Slave Zero X has a massive problem catering exclusively to the type of gamer that enjoys memorizing long frame perfect button input combos. Right from the get go, I tried to approach the game on it's own terms, I entered the training dojo to see if I could start memorizing combos, and selected the moves list from the menu. Except, that there is no moves list. Slave Zero X not only refuses to throw you a single bone when it comes to figuring out how the ♥♥♥♥ to even play it, but the difficulty curve is insane. Unlike basically every other game in this genre, you don't get any sort of tutorial, or intro gameplay to get a feel, instead you get a series of noninteractive splash screens that quickly and without embellishment, tell you what the buttons do, but don't bother too hard explaining anything beyond the mechanical function of it. I learned I could do light attacks, heavy attacks, burst, i have an item meter, a burst guage, a health bar, I could do EX moves, I could parry, go into overdrive, jump, and dodge, like damn, you think that's enough things to throw at me in the first minute? Level 1 begins with a few mooks, nothing too bad, but it isn't long at all the game throws the first enemy at you that has super armor, basically, an attribute that prevents it from experiencing knockback or flinching. I have no idea how you are supposed to deal with these enemies later on, when they throw multiple tanky super armor foes at you and you just end up being juggled, literally unable to do anything but watch as your lifebar depletes faster then you could throw an expletive out. Slave Zero X then has an annoying habit of chucking your ass right back to the beginning,  because who needs checkpoints, right? In the final stages it's very difficult to make any kind of progress because of all the super armor enemies, and even when I am able to get past them, the next battle kills me and then I get to start all over, and hear intro cutscenes 20 times over. It's not annoying at all!I would like to stress, that everything mentioned above, did not even have to be a problem, if only the devs would have included a difficulty option. I'll play on easy, I don't care, and Hardcore combo experts can keep their more difficult challenge. I don't have time or energy to try to beat Atavaka or whatever the hell his name is for the millionth time. Visual design is the only thing this game excels at, and I'm talking mainly from an environmental standpoint. The backgrounds are striking futuristic cityscapes, and they do a good job of evoking the original game. Character and enemy designs however, range from bland soldier recolors, to somewhat interesting but also somewhat out of place feeling experimental monstrosities. The gameplay loop boils down to feeling repetitive, made worse by the fact that the arenas are linear and the enemies tend to be simple recolors. Combined with it's high difficulty and inaccessibility to newcomers, at least to me, and probably to other fans of the original, this game just felt like a kick in the teeth. With this line of reasoning, the Episode Enyo Quake add on starts to make a lot more sense. Here is a visually appealing shooter, not too complicated but a great time overall. I think that it was developed for fans of the original since this new game is just too far removed from everything I liked about the original. I can't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those reviews I wish I could properly give a percentage or some other review system than just would I recommend this to others. If I'm being quite honest, I wouldn't recommend this to anyone with the amount of anti-fun mechanics and clearly not thought through ideas. This game is not for everyone. I'm vaguely enjoying Slave Zero X because of my years playing fighting games and other games like these.There's a few things to just point out, the story just simply exists, It's not good but it's not bad either. Cringe the protag is in yet ANOTHER gay relationship, if I wanted a story about a gay revenge story I would read my hentai again. But that's just my taste and style.On something that's actually objective;Does the dev team not have playtesters or something to help you out on certain enemies or mechanics?There is alot of things that just are plain unclear or button configs that are just awful. I get that might be the only way you can do the button layout on the controller but making the F-Sync and the "Roman Cancel" the same button is plain bad game design. The fact I have to sit still for a split second to pop the F-Sync just to then be combo'd or grab combo'd (something I'll get into) and wasting more time of my F-Sync. It's genuinely bad.Remake the heavy destroyer enemy, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is a terrible enemy. Having terrible hurtboxes, multiple combo moves that just go on forever and if you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ unlucky another enemy happens to catch you. The big guy can continue his combo. Not a fun enemy at all. Can't get up close as he's got super armour, bosses were much easier to fight than having to fight them AND STOP ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ CHUCKING THE ♥♥♥♥ IN EVERY OPPORTUNITY YOU'VE GOT. I shouldn't have to spend 15 minutes on a stage because of this horribly designed enemy.Those mutant dog enemy types I would say aren't terrible but feel like they need a touch up, being able to have super armour on certain moves like a shoriuken, while versing maybe one or two of them with a small amount of enemies is fine. But the game spams them and in fights that already have a stupid amount of other enemies on the screen to keep track of.Which leads into my next point, once there is a huge and large amount of enemies. Most of the time you can't see the next attack as they're all the same colour and they basically turn into this massive ball. Can't tell when an attack begins or it's about to finish.Now the most terrible of them all, the grab combo. The amount of times there have been enemies that hide within the ball of mass and suddenly I'm grab. Which I'm flung into the air to be then GRABBED BY ANOTHER ENEMY and then by ANOTHER and so on and so forth. Waste of my time and my health. I hope the devs fix this design, it's just plain not fun at all.STOP PUNISHING THE PLAYER FOR DOING DODGES. You're not adding to the overall ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the game already throws at the player and then punishes them by taking your meter away by dodging these enemies.Overall, again I enjoy this game and I want to love it but I can't simply because of terrible design flaws. I love the world, the art, the level designs (how they look, some of them are not fun gameplay wise), the overall feel of the game but it feels like you wanted to make a fighting game but instead did a beat'em up. And that's the problem, you made a beat'em up that is more of a fighting game than a beat'em up.TL;DR version:I came to play an awesome looking beat'em up with fighting game mechanics. Instead, I got a fighting game with beat'em up mechanics that looks cooler than it plays. And ffs, studios need to hire playtesters again. If this isn't a fantastic example of why you shouldn't skim out on playtesters then ♥♥♥♥♥♥ if I know then.Update: I've finished the game, I've got to say the last two final boss fights are great but at what cost?I feel very frustrated not at the game but the potential this game could of been. Astrava felt like a great boss because I was able to finally use the game's parry mechanic,clashing and dodge effectively since it was a 1v1 and not "how many enemies can we fit on the screen" sort of situation. Such a great fight and I would rather have the entire game feel like that and not just a slog of a couple of enemy designs/placements.It felt like a fighting game, and that's my problem. The game feels like it was meant to be exactly that, but at the last minute they decided to change the direction to a beat'em up. So I don't know if I can play the QA-folks/play testers on this one or if it simply need maybe a couple more or it could just simply be more complicated than what I'm outlining I have no idea but this game feels like it needed more substance than that.For story, honestly I think it just plain stinks by the end of it. _childDocuments_.review: Slave Zero X is an interesting blend of its inspirations, and the finished product is a unique and very satisfying experience... which is honestly a pretty high bar when so many conventions of the "spectacle fighter" genre had been hard-codified by countless titles.Shou has good running and jumping, but in spite of Strider being one of the main advertised influences this game doesn't really care that much about platforming outside of a single sequence.  Combat is the order of the day, with you ideally carving a bloody path through everything in your way, but you do need to understand the general flow of the game through its systems to maintain yourself.  It took me admittedly way longer than I would've liked to realize that, and I blame it on a tutorial that introduces the crucial mechanics in a non-intuitive way.tl; dr: You have a health bar and an EX bar, which is used to fuel special moves and normally only fills up as you do damage.  You ALSO have a Burst orb, which can let you recover from beatdowns and getting wombo-combo'd, but more importantly COMPLETELY refills your EX meter if you use it from a neutral or attacking position.  This is important because when your EX meter is full you can enter a Devil Trigger-like state, giving you unlimited use of EX moves until the time runs out (or you use one of the two super-duper secret moves) AND damaging enemies while in this state refills your health.So with optimal play you can spend the majority of your time in the so-called Fatal Synch mode, and indeed you're encouraged to since opportunities to conventionally heal at item shops are few and far between.  This is *not* a game of "oh I should save this for later".  Shou's defensive options (a VERY short dash with a few i-frames, along with defense and attack parries that require perfect timing) are all very limited and lack the same kind of infrastructure that his offensive options do.There are also Projectiles, an assortment of consumables that serve as your only means of ranged combat.  They are not super important but holy crap do those compound grenades shred things.The story is fairly straightforward, if a bit rushed at times.  This is made up for the style that oozes (sometimes literally) from the mix of polygonal environments and stellar 2D sprites, along with an amazing techno OST.  Nothing but bangers here.Probably my two big complaints are thus:1. The enemy diversity is fairly stunted.  You spend the bulk of the first half of the game fighting hordes of goons and soldiers, holding back a big chunk of their enemy roster until you go after the third Calamity, Uriel.  But other than that the only real changes in enemy lineups besides a few miniboss-grade incarnations of enemies is different color schemes.2. The game's loading screen tips reference special techniques by name, but there's nowhere else you can go to in order to understand what those techniques *look like*, let alone how to perform them.  While most of Shou's moveset is pretty easy to intuit, the two super-secret moves *aren't*.Still, had an absolute blast playing through this for an evening and the music has been living in my head rent-free since then.  It's good stuff.
