_childDocuments_.review: A sidescrolling, 2.5D hack and slash brawler, featuring some vaguely fighting game style mechanics and combos, with a healthy dose of Devil May Cry style attacks. You go to the right (usually), you kill the hordes of enemies in your way, and you buy upgrades to make your stats better to allow you to do a better job of killing more enemies. Very occasionally, you do a wee bit of platforming. Very little going off the beaten path to find secrets (though they do exist), and no multiple paths, or choices, anything like that. This game wants you to slice up enemies and look good while doing it. In it's own loading screen tip: "Remember. Looking cool is only second to being alive."This game is one of those flawed gems. Aesthetically, this game rocks. It has beautifully horrifying yet insanely cool designs for it's characters and monsters, nailing the "Biopunk" aesthetic (first time I'd heard the term). The music, while not insanely remarkable, is very fitting and sets a great pace for slicing your way through hordes of futuristic enemies. The sprites look great, and the animations are excellent. Gameplay is the meat of the game though. There is a story, but it's fairly straightforward, and told in that "Jump right in and it's gradually made more and more clear what's going on as you proceed" style, which works fine, because this isn't a game where you'll be feeling like sitting around for long conversations. Combat feels, MOST of the time, really, really good. You mix light attacks and heavy attacks to build combos, and they did manage to make them feel very much like an anime fighting game. You've got things like comboing an enemy in to the air, jumping after them, doing an aerial combo, complete with jump cancels, and then slamming them back down to the earth. It feels great to kill things here. And honestly, that's most of what's worth considering; the game looks great, and it feels awesome to slice things up. HOWEVER, this game has a few small problems that stop it from being truly great. It's still very good, but the glaring problems are kind of problematic. First of all, and most predominantly, this game, as they say, is really !&#@!ing hard sometimes, and it's mostly due to getting hit being simultaneously not a problem at all, but also a complete death sentence. See, you have a lot of life. You can take a lot of hits before dying, and you have ways to heal yourself even. So getting smacked a few times isn't the problem. This game will wombo-combo the ever living hell out of you if you give it the chance. There is ALMOST nothing stopping you from getting hit by one enemy, and while in hitstun, getting hit by another, and this can basically extend over and over again as long as there are enemies bunched up who can all hit you. And trust me. There will be MANY, because this game likes to throw a LOT of enemies at you at once. When you're the one on the offensive, this feels extremely satisfying. But if you slip up and get caught with enemies on both sides and get hit, knocked into the air, there's a high chance you'll just get knocked around for quite a while. You have a Burst that you can use to escape these scenarios, but early on, this only charges up every once in a while, so you can only do it so often. Also, much like a real fighting game, if you just mash out your burst in a panic while getting hit, it's entirely possible to get hit during the recovery animation of your own burst by any enemies that happened to be spaced out well enough that the shockwave of the burst didn't reach them, but are still close enough to threaten you instantly afterwards.Against hordes of normal enemies, this isn't such a huge problem, but sometimes it will happen, and especially so when you're fighting mini-bosses that also spawn normal enemies to attack you while you're trying to focus on dodging or parrying the mini-boss. I'm willing to stomach this, but I can see how it would massively frustrate many players. I'm totally fine with getting punished hard for getting hit; I actually think you have an absurdly generous amount of health in this game. The problem is just that it feels REALLY AWFUL to get combo'd by hordes of enemies and not be able to do anything about it if your burst isn't up. Even when I knew it was my own fault, it just feels terrible to have all control taken away from you as you get used as a ping-pong ball by 15 different guys. The game being hard is not the issue, and it's not even any individual enemy that's the problem. It's just that when there are so many enemies at once, and they can all hit you at once, it just feels really nasty. Most games will give you an invincibility moment, or some kind of cap on how much you can get smacked around before falling out of getting hit. This game doesn't FEEL like it has those. Once they stop hitting you and you're lying on the ground you're invincible, but you have to then stand back up and instantly they can have at you again. There is a parry system reminiscent of Street Fighter Third Strike, but the thing with that is it's really hard to observe and time a parry with an enemy attack, when there's 15 of them all in the same spot doing different things. I write a lot about this because it is by FAR the most frustrating part about the game, and it almost certainly WILL frustrate you. I enjoyed the game a ton regardless, but you are going to have to deal with that pain as you learn the game, unless you're absolutely godlike and just perfect it from the start. Other than that, it does feel really good when you're the one winning. It's not an overly long game, and while the levels visually varied a lot from one another, there isn't a huge variety of types of enemies. If you love a challenge, and like those insanely over the top slashers like Devil May Cry or Metal Gear Rising, then this is strongly worth a shot if you can take the beatings the game will send your way. It's got that great feeling of when I first played Devil May Cry, where at the start you barely know anything and will probably be fine with the normal enemies up until the first boss kicks your ass around enough that you actually get a bit better at the game, and by the end of the game, the challenges and experience will have sculpted your skills enough that you're on a totally different level to when you began. For me, this game felt like it was hand-crafted to appeal to my tastes, so I loved it and will be replaying it. If you're not a fan of challenging games, or, and I cannot stress this enough, if you're prone to getting really angry when the game is kicking your ass, perhaps this isn't the one for you, because this game will test you.Also, devs, if you're out there reading this, I would pay good money for a DLC that lets you play the game as Atavaka, in the same kind of light as playing as Vergil back in Devil May Cry 3. Doesn't need to change the story or anything, just lemme play as him. He looks cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels so good to play and demands you learn to play it well to even clear it normally. Forcing pinpoint dodges and and parries, constant meter management, enemy grouping and CC, getting full damage combos on high priority targets while dealing with other mobs and stage gimmicks, etc, etc.It feels so good when it goes right and is the kind of game that makes you feel like the biomechanical terror of the main character not by just showing your character do cool things but making you have to really actually do all the cool things and smashing your face in if you don't.Thanks in part to the grueling difficulty I certainly feel like I'm getting my moneys worth, this isn't a beat-em-up where you just press continue a bunch and beat in in two hours to never touch again unless you are going for 1CC or high scores. Without the complicated fighting game inspired systems this would be a pretty mashy generic beat em up but it doesn't let you play it like that.I can't give this a 100% thumbs up because, well, this is a cool looking game with flashy animation and anyone who is just looking for that way to see the story and set pieces and clear in in two hours is absolutely not going to have fun with this game. The challenge is still fun to me, but it comes constantly close to pushing past the boundary to frustrating, and depending on where your line is this might push right past it fast. Especially in high chaos fights with lots of enemies it can be hard to tell why one try goes bad when another one goes well. And the boss fights (including mid-bosses) feel like the cheap final bosses from a fighting game in a good way and also in the too-much-super-armor and delete half your lifebar combo bad ways. Also the enemy variety isn't great.Also for some reason despite not having a japanese localization yet this has an incredible japanese dub? The voice work is incredible and I've only notices one or two very minor translation mistakes in their script.I still haven't beaten this or even got that far, and I am very afraid i'm going to get beaten down by the difficulty and not be able to (currently writing this review after giving up on a mid-boss that destroyed me 5 times), but 4 hours in and its the most fun I've had with a flashy action game since DMC V. I'll close the game in frustration but I keep wanting to go back for more. I already feel I got my money's worth.edit after beating:Everything I complained about it still true, and especially the bosses where often disapointing (the mid-bosses where usually better bosses), but still. So much fun. Maybe one of my favorite games of all time. I also ending up being way more invested in the story than I expected. Probably going to buy the limited special physical release now if I can.

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, this game is absolutely incredible both visually and audibly. If you've looked at the trailer/screenshots on the store page, it's incredibly apparent, not just in the psx era backgrounds and well animated sprites to match, but in the character portraits in art cut-ins that usually appear to punctuate major boss fights. The music is very good, and the voice acting is very well done, both in the performances themselves, but in how the frequency of battle voicelines has been tuned to be somewhat infrequent, as not to be annoying with the amount of moves happening at a given moment. It is quite clear how much the developers care for this game's inspirations, which can be seen in decisions like the spritework/voicework, and also in more overt ways such as the copious references, ranging from the game having the ps2 era "This game contains scenes of explicit violence and gore" screen and references to many fighting game round intros. It's quite charming.As for the gameplay, it is something I quite enjoyed, but it has a very specific quality to it that I feel it would be beneficial to know before playing the game. The best way I would sum up the main gameplay loop is that it is very snowball-y. The general feel of Shou's moveset is somewhat deliberate without using EX moves, but becomes very quick and powerful with them in play, and with the game promoting a gameplay loop where you use your burst to gain full meter and enter Fatal Sync to have infinite EX move usage for an amount of time, there is a very stark difference between when you're in this loop and out of it (not to say that you're completely helpless outside of the fatal sync loop, at least at most moments in the game) This, combined with the density of enemies the game ends up throwing at you, makes a very satisfying experience scooping up masses of enemies and hearing the very satisfying combo noises pop off. Enemies themselves are farily aggressive, but generally, your own moveset is enough to overpower them given that you don't get yourself surrounded, but the game does try to throw some wrenches in the way, both in enemy and level design. The main one which I feel is somewhat contentious is the use of super armor, which comes in two forms: enemies that have super armor applied to specific moves, and the stagger mechanic minibosses and bosses have in which they have super armor until staggered/broken/whatever, in which they can be comboed. The first type I'm perfectly fine with, seeing as it encourages paying attention to enemies, and the enemies that have the super armor generally aren't the ones that populate the majority of the bigger enemy floods you have to deal with. The second type is definitely harder to deal with, especially combined with the enemies associated with them also having the ability to do some evil mixups, but once I realized how powerful the ability to cancel EX moves into each other during fatal sync was, they generally became manageable enough as long as you really focus them down.As for defensive mechanics, what you have at your disposal are a set of powerful defensive mechanics that for the most part all have some really tangible risk/reward element to them. I'll fully admit that I never fully relied on the parry mechanic aside from maybe the projectiles on the first miniboss type enemy, but when I did manage to pull one off, it either saved my hide or had me realize I was gonna take every other hit of a multi-hit attack, but I'm overall positive on it. Clashing is another mechanic that while being similarly tight timing-wise, actually ends up being much more useful considering how many moves you can end up pulling off during fatal sync, though once again it does fall apart a bit against enemies with multihit attacks, making them higher priority targets. The burst is a mechanic that I honestly didn't use defensively as much as I thought I would considering I constantly got greedy with the thought of "oh but if I stay alive I can just get into fatal sync with this burst and heal this all off." The defensive burst seems like a tough proposition when you might not hit every enemy around you or hit an enemy with super armor and leave you high and dry, so it requires a lot of though, but I do feel it is important to note that the offensive burst does have some iframes, so you can get away with a lot using that, though of course you have to be careful with your timing so you don't accidentally get hit and use a defensive burst instead. The getup/air tech situation is another situation that requires a lot more thought with the 2D beatemup format, because while you can airtech and start attacking before you hit the ground, that generally doesn't leave you in an ideal situation, and even if you tech on the ground, techning left or right has a somewhat floaty arc to it, leading to similar consequences. Thus, it is really important to remember two things: if you hold down and jump, you do a quick getup in place which lets you gain movement control much more quickly, and if you just hit the ground and lay there, you'll have a very generous amount of iframes, just like the enemies do. This whole system ends up being very interesting, since you can end up getting comboed for a good while if you get more than one enemy on you, but doing nothing can still be the best decision, which is an interesting thing to grapple with. Finally, you have a dodge, which involves you stepping forward/backward, an action that has some iframes, and can be done while in attacking animations at the cost of some meter. As with a lot of the defensive mechanics here, the dodge doesn't have a super huge amount of iframes it feels, but it is really useful for positioning, which is of course super important defensively. Ultimately, I feel like the dodge is a reminder that this is still a beatemup, which means positioning is is very important, and ties back into how exactly you pull off combos, since you don't want to pull off a sick-nasty air juggle and then land between two hordes, so the defense and offense play together pretty well.The last things I'll mention is that generally the levels are pretty well paced and the game length is satisfying and replayable, with enyo's stage with the sniper gimmick probably being the most potentially annoying stage, and the Atavaka fight being a major highlight for me, very well done rival fight. Another miscellaneous thing I should mention is that the general way inputs are handled and the way EX move inputs work feels like you'd get the most out of this game with an arcade stick or a hitbox, though I used a normal gamepad and had a smooth experience regardless. Overall, I enjoyed the game enough to write all this, which I don't do too often, so I think that speaks fairly well to the game's quality.

_childDocuments_.review: This is masterpiece if you're a fan of fighting games, simple as.It's a beat'em up with burst roman cancels, ex moves and endless combo possibilities. It can be a bit difficult as you don't have a block, you can only dash and do a 3rd Strike style parry by pushing forward, which has very small frame window. And the very generous juggling rules that allow for your own ridiculous combos also apply to you, so you can get absolutely destroyed by groups of enemies comboing you. The game should probably explain this a bit more, but you can always use your burst aggressively to fill up your super bar and enter a super mode, "Fatal Sync", which gives you free ex moves and, more importantly, converts your damage into health that gets recovered when the super mode ends. This mode also charges your burst, which means you can use it to fill up your bar again and continuously stay in that super mode. That seems to be the expected gameplay loop, but it's definitely not immediately obvious and you have to execute the burst a certain way for it to fill your bar.The fantastic gameplay aside, the pixel art is gorgeous and the setting is some juicy cyberpunk, obviously nostalgic for those that played Slave Zero in the past. The PS1 style 3D backgrounds are also very beautiful and varied. Top tier.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Above all else this game succeeds on an aesthetic level. Detailed pixel art on 3D backgrounds that have change angles is a late 90s look that not a lot of modern games follow. The character designs are also great, committing to that biomechanical look the original had to move away from.On the gameplay side, the initial impression is pretty positive, enemies and player alike have no invincibility frames until they hit the floor so you can get into lengthy combos, as can enemies. Unfortunately throwing more enemies at you so they can stunlock you is where most of the difficulty comes in. You can escape this with a burst mechanic straight like Guilty Gear, but the fact that most fights increase the difficulty by piling more enemies on rather than increasing complexity is unfrotunate, I feel the game could've benefited from more enemies/enemies having more abilities. On the defensive side, you get a brief invincibility dash and a SF3 style parry. The dash doesn't function so strongly as other invincible dodges in modern action games so that's nice, some attacks have long enough reach that you'll just dodge into them if you're not careful. The individual zones associated with each boss do feel like they set themselves apart enough that they stand out, as do each of the bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: Slave Zero is a game very few people who play this one will have ever heard of. Originally released for the PC and the Dreamcast in 1999 (you can actually buy it here, though I recommend  because it's easier to tweak), it didn't review or sell amazingly, but it was a neat third-person shooter that took place in a giant mech that towered over everything. The franchise faded away and didn't come back until Ziggurat Interactive picked up the right and released this, a prequel to the 25 year old original, this time as a beat em' up with fighting game elements.There is a story and it's fully voice acted (pretty well too), but it's anime AF and I couldn't begin to tell you what's happening in it, beyond the fact that your character is a human who is bonded to a sentient mech suit (which is where the Slave part comes in) and you're trying to defeat the overlord of your city who is oppressing everyone. There's more to it that you might be able to glean, but the gameplay is largely why you're here. The game aims to take the tradition button mashing elements of a brawler and combine them with the more combo driven, precise input demanding elements of a fighting game.I want to preface by saying that I don't play fighting games, principally because I'm not good at them and too impatient to get so. But I have played a lot of character action games and am decent at those. While I did finish Slave Zero X, I hit my wireless controller against my desk several times with enough force to pop the batteries out, and I'm not the type of person who normally does that. Many encounters feel like the game is writing cheques that its fighting engine can't cash and other times, it just feels like there's some petty design at play. Quick examples:Some players won't mind this and will just see it as a challenge. I finished the game so indeed, I did to a point myself, but I also rage quit numerous times, not because things were hard (I can manage that) but because they seemed rather obviously unfair, which to me, is not fun.There is an upgrade system plus additional ordinance weapons of various types you can use (though you can't throw ordinance when stunlocked) and you can go back and grind previous levels to get all the unlocks, though the higher levels cost enough that you'll be doing that a lot if you need to. There are also hidden "golden enemies" throughout the levels that give little lore unlockables if you defeat them, though these didn't help me understand the story any more.So despite all those criticisms (some of which could be patched, some of which couldn't), why am I still giving this a thumbs up? Simply because even when this game was driving me up the wall, it also kept driving me to want to best it, which I eventually did. I didn't buy this, I got a press code for it and could have just dropped it at any time with no money lost. But I was determined to not let it get the better of me, and I think that does say something significant about it. I also think the Slave Zero universe is a really cool concept that never got the chance to really flourish and I hope that with this, we might see Ziggurat do more with the franchise, maybe even a remake of the original mech-style shooter or even a sequel.There's great potential here and I think the right kind of player will really enjoy this. Me personally, I'm glad to have it behind me, but I also want to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: in short :BUY IT! you wont regret it!! and its definitely worth the money.- very easy to pick up, but hard to master with a high skill ceiling.- Audio, Music and visual style is SO sick! faultless.- Gameplay is snappy and responsive, and the game mechanics / abilities are from a bunch of different fighting games, (guilty gear / Street fighter / mugen / Devil May Cry / etc ) crammed into a hack and slack. it works really well! the things you can pull off are amazing and really rewarding.- no hand holding here, what you know is what you've practised, (there is a dojo-like practice mode. spent WAY too much time here).nothing gameplay related is locked behind progression or anything like that, all moves and mechanics are available form the start. its up to you to find them, and decided for yourself what links best when and for what scenario.-best way to get the maximum fun out of a game like this (in my opinion) is to try S-rank the stages.its an endless cycle of "this is impossible", to "wait, i can do that?", to "omg! that combos into that?!!", until finally ' i'm a god!! who can stop me!"  game isn't perfect, needs some tweeks here and there (i frames on parry! please!!) amongst other things, and how the game handles difficulty needs work (higher difficulty areas = more enemies on screen. sometimes i cant even see my character ).turns the game into a spamfest for some encounters.I personally would prefer fewer enemies on screen, but more complex enemy designs / abilities, and encounters.but the game is still getting patched regularly at the time of writing this, so it only gets better from here.but overall as a package, very well done!!ALOT of potential, and easy top 3 hack and slash games of all time. still got alot more hours to get out of this game, and for this price, im a happy man :)
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game and I would have 100% recommended to anyone who enjoys harder games, exhilarating tough as Nails fast-paced gameplay that once you Master it, will feel like a demon for freeing Humanity from its shackles of religion. And with plenty of cosmetics you can be any kind of devil you want, on top of that the the game's art style is spectacular and is sure to entice anyone who's into horror. The art directors Twitter is @Personfaces for anyone who interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Slave Zero X delivers on being a game released in 2024 that makes me nostalgic for its big PS1 sprites and chunky textured 3d elements. It oozes transhumanisim cyber punk in a grimy dystopian world. It delivers on sounds and sights.This game is brutal in the mechanics department. It has a high skill ceiling with no way to get you there. It demands practice to learn how to juggle, parry and dash. It also holds you back with a few frustrating choices. Looking at you wasted Fatal Sync meter because the fatal sync button does multiple things. This game suffers terribly from a lack of a real tutorial (and a 20 page slide show).  It has lots to offer to anyone who is a fan of Strider or Muramasa Demon Blade. If you don't like flashy hack and slash combo games, this may not offer enough to keep you in it to finish.Feels like a real love it or hate it game. I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Slave Zero X is difficult to describe. It takes clear inspiration from fighting games and beat em ups, but I've never seen gameplay like this anywhere else. Throughout the course of the game I went from completely incompetent to being forced to master both Shou's controls and the enemy's movesets. I enjoyed the punishing difficulty that actually failed me if I didn't learn what to do, unlike many action games these days. My fighting game experience pretty much begins and ends with Guilty Gear Strive but I was able to clear the game in about 12 hours (plus several hours on the demo).Beside the gameplay, the stunning artwork and haunting setting are equally unique. I could write a whole review just about how much I love the art, but I'll keep it short.There is really nothing else like Slave Zero X being made anywhere on the planet. This is an experience you can only get here. So yes, as other reviews point out, it could do with a little extra polish, and it doesn't hold the player's hand. But if you like what you see, buy the game so you can enjoy it and hopefully we can get more of this crazy stuff in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: After finally finishing the game, I can say it will make you rethink your purchase whenever you get grabbed by the fatass hammerman with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fullscreen grab twice in a row. But the game does (mostly) tell you every important mechanic. (down, down, down, light atk, heavy atk really helps whith mini/boses). Just dont forget you have several types of granades, spam the ♥♥♥♥ out of EX moves (light atk, charge(hold) heavy atk and forward light atk, heavy atk for i-frames), and you'll manage.The adrenaline rush when you gib 5+ enemies at once and the implied gay sex barely make up for the frustration, but at the end you'll be glad you stuck with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real fighting game.Punishing and challenging but ultimately very rewarding. The art and music pair with the gameplay perfectly. Do yourself a favor and watch a few videos explaining how to stay in the Golden Circle - this unlocks a big jump in mechanics and is required past a specific part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: I actually like what this game is going for with it's style and art direction. But the team needs to keep working on it because they were so determined to make it like a fighting game that it needs buffs and nerfs. Hit and hurt boxes, enemy placement and behavior, overly committal attacks, no grab, and a parry that doesn't stagger don't lead to the type of combo variety the devs were going for. It'll also bug out on you here and there. It's a good base, but it needs work. I love the pallets though.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost or TL;DR: If you think this looks and sounds cool, you should buy it. You can feel how much the team cared about the worldbuilding and storytelling, you can tell it's a biopunk dystopian future setting and that you gorily kill things in it in very flashy ways. We need more stuff like this out there and it's a solid game with fantastic art direction.This is, however, a tough one to recommend to your average gamer while more experienced beat-em-up players or older Guilty Gear/fighting game fans will have immediate leveraging on it's systems: Mostly to their benefit, sometimes not so much due to tiny inconsistencies.The difficulty especially is a tough topic to chew on; I'd say love it or hate it, but they really are sides of the same coin here.For the beat em up mechanics, this game lets you (and expects you) to overcomplicate your combos and move usage for faster clearing, better crowd control and mobility, flashy and satisfying strings that route into desireable outcomes that suit your needs: Whether it's recovering life, building meter, repositioning, faster damage or more efficient slower damage etc etc. But, if you already have a solid beat em up background, you'll notice this game won't really push you into doing those things or learning anything *specifically* new. You can keep your crowd control quite simple and still do quite well without diving into said additional options, which unless you deliberately try to explore for fun, might make your experience compared to other games like Fight N Rage, stretched out.For the fighting game mechanics, your ability to combo is truly legendary: Enemies remain in hitstun or juggled for very long amounts of time, giving you a sense that your character is just extremely fast, which is great! You'd be lying if you denied not wanting a side swap combo that costs no meter that just involves you literally running to the other side after a launch to then launch them again.However, FG combat mechanics are hard to pull off (especially within this context) which makes the combat rarely buggy or inconsistent at times or with hit/hurtboxes that will make you scratch your head for not fulfilling their intended designed purpose. Many are just oversights to be worked in future patches so it's not that big of a deal, but the meta enjoyment of the genre will definitely elevate the experience here.Now the abstract stuff, it's hard to find words to describe how awesome the character designs, environments, sound design and music truly are. I did not know how much I liked this biopunk aesthetic until it was presented like this and it sparked my interest in their inspired media.The story playing out in Slave Zero X is obviously dark and well introduced by the characters' expressiveness, making you want to see more of the dystopian setting presented that made them that way. The style of the dialogue (mainly later on) might be a little too on the nose for me as if it's lacking any subtlety, but at the same time it's reminiscent of older dubbed anime, so it might even be considered a plus depending on your perspective.If all of this sounds interesting, then by all means give it a fair and dedicated shot; It's a hard game.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Savagely intricate, intricately savage. The game is very challenging, but in a way that feels like I need to hone myself instead of just looking up what to do. The artwork is stunning, and the blend of 2d sprites with polygonal environments brings me back to the turn of the century, while the music is engrossing and strangely calming.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: im no fighting pro expert. just your regular casual gamer with a huge nostalgic crash on the old slave zero. game presentation, voice acting, story and lore is pretty good, but my main problem is the tough gameplay. sometimes hit boxes are non responsive, enemies spamming attacks without letting you recover for even a micro second. bosses are epic but suffer from the same issues. i felt like instead of enjoying a fluid ninja gaiden like fighter, i was more focused on struggling with the controls and the spammy enemies, hoping to survive the unfair spamming of enemy attacks. this game could be amazing but it needs some balancing and tweaks. in this state it feels untested regarding the combat. i would also recommend adding an easy mode or cheat codes for us filthy casuals. some of us like the option of a power fantasy.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant combination from a clearly passionate team.  Set in a dystopian future, you play Shou who has stolen a living armor on a path of vengeance against a cavalcade of bosses on the way to the penultimate SovKhan.  This game is packed full of feature including a gallery, alternate colors, training mode, and even menu color customization.Fans of fighting games will find satisfaction in a deep and entertaining combo system.  Including mechanics like a parry, roman cancel, super moves, and various other combo extending bounces you will constantly find yourself discovering new moves to take to the training room and get the swaggiest combo you can.The art to Slave Zero X is something to behold.  Each character is engaging and intriguing making you want to study them for hours.  The world is developed in a way that balances nostalgia and grit of the 80's and 90's while finding something inspired by a desolate waste of Tsutomu Nihei.  Slave Zero X is the best game of 2024 and makes large shoes to fill for the rest of the year
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Alright folks. This game has a lot of pros, and a few glaring cons!I really enjoy all of the artist design choices in the story, characters, levels, and enemies. The sound effects and music are absolutely top-tier, and overall the aesthetic of the game is completely amazing. If you weren't hooked by the trailer, then I guess it's not for you, but it absolutely WAS for me.The cons are pretty big. As other reviewers say, a shallow tutorial is fine, but a more in-depth tutorial would've been nice. The BIGGEST two problems are:1. Not enough enemy variety. Devil May Cry had at least a couple new enemies to fight each stage. Here, it's not quite the same. Enemy variety makes beat 'em ups good and unique; this was somewhat lacking.2. Bursting is really cheap. Okay, so there's a "gold burst" that you can do if you cancel your attack into a burst, and it refills all of your meter. There's also a "devil trigger" of sorts that allows you to spend all of your meter to get health back on hit and have infinite EX moves. Do you see the problem here? I'll spill the beans: wait for burst to charge up, use gold burst, immediately use devil trigger, and repeat. You become unkillable; the only way you're ever losing is if you're forced to fight airborne enemies (which Shou has a hard time fighting unless you're very precise).The pros are legendary though. I absolutely recommend playing this game because it's awesome, and I'm sure these things are gonna be fixed. Currently there's a frame rate issue with the game, but it should also get fixed sometime soon.Slicing people up with a vengeful Shou is extremely fun, and taking out the Calamities one-by-one makes you feel like you're re-enacting Kikokugai: The Cyber Slayer or something. I love it.Bottom line is: Slave Zero X is a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: this game is like a mix of dmc street fighter and guilty gear . If you plan to get this game just go in with a mindset that this game will push you ( it's very challenging ) you wont be able to button mash your way through, so really mess around with the mechanics in training if you have trouble. my only input that could help this game is a difficulty select for people who are new to the hack&slash genre, it would be a great update and address the frame rate issues. I also encountered several bugs, but nothing really game breaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed my time a lot. Where the portions I had difficulty with? Absolutely. But save for a few instances, there was never anything that I couldn't beat by learning. It's hard. Very very hard. But that doesn't mean impossible or unfair. Stuff like the penultimate boss and super heavyweight enemies were manageable after I stopped flinging myself into enemies like a rabid dog. The graphics speak for themselves naturally, and I loved the music. If you can handle tough as nails gameplay, this is a special, special game.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Found this game through it's art director, i follow them on social media and have been a fan of their work for some time. I'm not good at fighting games so this game is pretty hard but man i do enjoy it. Even a buttom masher like me can feel cool pulling off some of these combos, its fast fluid and responsive. I haven't played all that much but from what i saw the story looks very interesting as well. All in all would recomend. Also played it on Steamdeck in docked mode with an Xbox controller and had no issues performance or gameplay wise.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I’m not into side scroller hack and slash games, but 3 things caught my attention.1. I heard Miles Luna was writing for this game.2. The action looked pretty good from the trailers.3. The soundtrack sounded good in the trailers.After playing for a bit HOLY COW, this game is amazing. The writing is so good, the dialogue is serious, funny, and gets your attention. The combat is super fun. You learn the combos pretty easily but the enemies/bosses they throw at you are ever changing so you’re forced to adapt your fighting style to each one. The fights can be pretty hard (in my opinion) but there’s frequent checkpoints so even if you get destroyed it’s not a huge pain of having to get back to where you died at. And last but certainly not least, the score is SO GOOD. The soundtrack for this game is mostly what sold me on it and it’s amazing in every way. If you’re into fast paced fights with awesome music and witty commentary I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Slave Zero X is, at its core, a beat 'em up game, but also has a very strong visual design, a good soundtrack (Enyo's theme stuck out for me), and, most surprising, a really moving story and compelling set of characters.Fair warning, I found that the game got genuinely hard at around the halfway point. It feels bad to get on the backfoot in a fight. Bosses will lock you in nasty combos, and big mobs will collectively juggle you. You won't be able to beat the game with just button mashing, you need to use dodges, parries, and all the weird special moves that the protagonist has. I found this frustrating at times, but eventually you just get better at fights, and what was previously unbeatable in a level just becomes one stepping stone as you grind through the fight afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review: Cool bio suit. Horrible future. Beautiful animation. Great 2d brawler with a deep combo system really interesting push-pull between it's burst gauge and special meter. (Burst refills special meter, then you burn your meter on the "Fatal Sync" mechanic to refill your health, then live long enough to burst again) Lots of unlockables. Juggles for days. TIGHT controls. A soundtrack you can wake up to. It's all I'm going to think about for a while, I suspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Slave Zero X

_childDocuments_.review:
From the top of Megacity S1-9, the Sovereign Khan rules with fists of iron and flesh. Beneath the city's rotting foundations, a vengeful warrior embarks on a journey to murder him.

Slave Zero X is a stylish 2.5D character action game set in the biopunk world of Slave Zero (1999). Run & Slash your way through a dystopian future in this character action game which will resonate with fans of Devil May Cry, Strider, and Guilty Gear.

name: Football Manager 2023
detailed_description: Join the managerial elite by writing your own headlines, earning the love of the fans and dominating the competition in Football Manager 2023. Football management is not just about picking tactics or crafting a team. It’s about taking on challenges and breaking new ground. Game Description Find the club that’s right for you. Meet board and fan expectations before beating the best on your way to winning football’s top prizes. Don’t just sign superstars, create them. Level up your recruitment with the help of your backroom staff and provide pathways to the first team for your wonderkids to develop a world-class squad. Your team’s playing style is down to you. Create a unique strategy on the tactics board to deliver big wins and memorable matchday moments. New this season BIG EUROPEAN NIGHTS Experience a greater sense of occasion with the UEFA Champions League, the UEFA Europa League and the UEFA Europa Conference League all fully licenced. Remodelled Cup Draws and officially branded team sheets, scoreboards and goal graphics vividly bring to life UEFA’s Club Competitions. BUILD STRONGER SQUADS Power your transfer activity with revamped scouting and recruitment meetings, a closer relationship with agents and brand-new squad planning tools. With a better oversight of your prospects in the pipeline, it’s never been easier to meet long-term club ambitions. OUTSMART YOUR RIVALS Test your managerial skills against the most realistic AI managers in the history of the series. An overhaul of your opponents’ decision-making has made them smarter, while new out of possession tactical instructions make defensive and counter-attacking football more viable. As you’re pushed harder in every game, you’ll notice further match engine advancements, including changes to the way wing-backs and double pivots operate and a range of new animations. GET THE FANS ONSIDE Become closer to the fans than ever before with the new Supporter Confidence system. Get to grips with their expectations on and off the pitch to ensure a bright, long-term future in the dugout. SAVOUR YOUR SUCCESS Relive the milestones and achievements of every career with the brand-new Dynamic Manager Timeline. Whether you’ve given a youth player their first-team debut or won the UEFA Champions League, it’s never been easier to savour and share your Football Manager story. Countless more features, big and small, designed to improve your game experience are ready for you to discover in every career.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't ask me how many hours I have on fm (been playing since fm 2012) for even idk lolEver since the beginning of my fm days, I've felt the devs have added something to the game in terms of features that, in tandem with features from past iterations, added a sense of depth and REALISM to the game. Small yet significant stuff that may not even be marketed as a feature for that yrs fm; such as subtle match engine improvements (adding cutbacks 2-3 iterations ago), UI improvements/tweaks (done each yr), improved animations (only significantly marketed this yr I believe), fm's version of twitter, better dialogue, better interactions in terms of contract and transfer negotiations, or press conferences etc etc. However this yr I can confidently say that, aside from UEFA licenses, nothing major OR minor of significance was implemented that added to realism. Each marketed feature except for licenses was just a glossy deception at worst or terrible implementation at best - like the tactical tweaks, scouting tweaks, animations, match engine changes etc.In terms of realism, this fm is a HUGE step backword for me. I get the idea that they want to capture football's sometime unpredictable nature but cmon......Rashford scoring like prime CR7, Haaland becoming Lukaku/Morata, top lvl CBs dealing with aerial balls like amateurs and making 2-4 mistakes per game, players with 16+ rating on penalties missing 3-5 pens a season, Leipzig winning Bundesliga first season, Leeds finishing top 3 first season, Chelsea/Arsenal stuck relegation battle or bottom half first season.....like wtf? 3-6 seasons down the road maybe I can see this but really? Leeds and Leipzig over-performing like that first season? gtfoThis game at its core is supposed to be a football SIMULATOR. But its more like a random, free for all. No logic, No Realism.Only fm where I legit wish I could get my money back. Fm 22 was AMAZING. Idk how they could get this one so terribly wrong.... 0/10EDIT:Played an additional 300 hrs. Fewer issues but still braindead AI, same scripted stuff. Game just feels repetitive and like a chore. My tactical inputs don't feel responsive and to top it all game now crashes. Still bugs. Feels like an alpha release. Disgraceful. Never supporting this company again after being a loyal customer for 10+ years. Do NOT buy even if its 50-60 or even 90% off.Edit 2: Game legit broken. Crashes after every couple in-game months of playing.

_childDocuments_.review: My hours played say it's worthy the buy. But I just want to tell you (probably too late), don't buy it, at least not every year, not much changes let's be fair. Once every three years is my recommendation.- Some things they 'improved' this year I ended up ignoring. I used squad depth screen in previous FMs so much. Now I hate it, and I use my notebook again.- Champions league feature I don't care much about, I usually play in Lower leagues or outside of Europe.- Scouting, pretty much the same.- Tactics, pretty much the same.

_childDocuments_.review: I never leave a review but it's time to on this shambles mess of scam game where heads need to roll in SI studio as they've become too complacent, arrogant, lazy and conceited in how they develop this half baked money grabbing con game. _childDocuments_.review: This game compared to FM22 is nothing but a expensive database update plus a new FM23 skin.Some minor extra features are added and there are the official licences for the European competitions.There are many unfixed issues from FM22 in this version. Defenders and goalkeepers are still doing very strange stuff.Stadiums are the same as in the first version of the 3D match engine. The match experience is therefore nothing you would expect after ten years of development time.If you have FM21 or 22 just download a free databse update and you will miss nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this game for 8 months now and whilst I do have periods where I get fed up, I always come back to it. Whether managing Chelsea in the EPL, St Albans City in the VNS or even a minor team in Iceland. The thrills and spills of managing a football team remain.The thing that makes this game unique is the modding community. Without this the game would be very plain, but the ability to add proper logos, player faces, stadium backgrounds, which have been meticulously created by numerous creators make the game. Also there are numerous data updates that update your game to the latest data including the ups and downs and player transfers.What to expect from the match engine? It isn't cutting edge put it that way. If you are used to the flashy graphics of the latest FIFA, then look away now. The game doesn't aim to woo you with the flashy graphics but it does represent a good representation of a standard football match. Providing your players are good enough and smart enough, you'll see back heels, overhead kicks and stepovers among many other animations.Is the game different from previous incarnations? Yes and no. The game features a brand new squad planner which is useful, but not wholly necessary. Also now included is official UEFA branding for the first time along with other branding SI have acquired over previous iterations. These additions add an air of atmosphere around the draws and those big European nights under the floodlights. But in all honesty if you already own FM22 at this point in the game cycle, I'd wait and get FM24 or else get this one in a sale. Really only the 'die-hard' FM'ers will likely purchase this every year.Is this game easy to get intp? In a word no. However. There are numerous YouTube creators and Twitch streamers who provide great information and guidance. Take a look at BustTheNet, lollujo, DrBenjy, RDF Tactics, and TomFM just to name a few. But by far the best is BustTheNet if you want to learn the tactical side of the game.It is a game that takes a while to master, but when you do, it is very gratifying.FM scores again!!!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: An enormous waste of your time. SI have mutilated the game over various iterations through the years, gradually hard coding fix after fix to the point where the game is unrecognisable and makes zero sense.In good form? the slightest issue with a squad member will derail the season and send your team into a tailspin. Playing a worse team with higher reputation? You'll lose repeatedly despite creating better chances consistently. Performing above expectations in the league? Found a tactic that actually works in this "match engine"? Your players will start missing easy chances and the AI teams will continually outperform their XG against you.Read up on these issues online and defenders will say "tactics" or "the AI teams have adapted". This isn't true. Your games when you're winning will look extremely similar to the games when you're losing - you'll create the same chances each game. You'll concede the same chances each game. You'll have just as much of the ball. The only difference? The final score and outcome of these chances. Your players will hit the bar 4 times a game (you think I'm joking, I'm not) whilst AI players will perform like Messi even at the lowest level of football. It's the illusion of AI adapting to your tactics. Another example of SI slapping tape over a glaring issue. Nonsensical obstacles for you to overcome which just so happens to increase playtime. They've created a game they have no control over beyond these fixes. Twenty years of muddled, half baked interpretations of what football is, thrown into a blender.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game if you are playing FM 22.  If you are coming from an earlier version it probably has enough tweaks and changes to justify the upgrade.  The only major changes from 22 are the new animations and general chaos in the match engine and and updated scouting system.  People will have different opinions but I don't feel those two changes justify picking this up.  Unfortunately Sports Interactive is more interested in sticking to a yearly release as opposed to taking the time needed to really improve the game.  I stopped playing FM 22 after a bug destroyed my save - took over a club after their season ended in relegation and the save broke when the "new season" started and the board blamed me for the relegation I had nothing to do with... a bug which still hadn't been patched nearly a year after release!  Similarly FM 23 has been shown to have several bugs and signification issues which despite being in the beta state is still insane for a game that hasn't really changed that much year on year.  This really feels like the sloppiest roll out for a new game and I just can't recommend it unless you've been playing on older versions for a few years.  Yes I will probably keep playing but I've certainly not been as compelled to play it as I have in the past.

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 23 is the weakest iteration of the series in recent memory.- No notable game-changing feature additions outside of a more balanced match engine that allows for defensive play to be viable too- No fixes to any of the major concerns players had (international management, set pieces, poorly written player interactions)- The graphics are horribly outdated. Many people will say they don't care, but I think that's a very lazy excuse to not update the graphics on a game we pay full price for every year.- The scouting rework is weird, unnecessary and features very clunky UI, and weird bugs. The time spent on this should have been invested in some new features instead. Stop reworking the same stuff over and over and calling it something new.It's concerning that I thought about starting a save in FM20 instead of the newly released game, but I can't think of any features I would miss.Skip this year if you've played FM in the past. For new players it may still be worth it, but know that this is the weakest and most uninspired I've seen this game in a long time.Edit: Oh and don't let them fool you with the idea that this is the result of Covid as an excuse. Other companies have released perfectly fine games during the pandemic, and if the game just isn't as good because of Covid, perhaps delay it until it's good?

They have reskinned FM22 with almost no major additions or improvements, and it just isn't worth wasting your money on.Women's football is still missing, its still not possible to be a U20 or U18 manager, the social media section still adds nothing to the experience, the press conferences still repeat so often that they're boring - these are things fans have been calling to add/change for years.Frankly SI are just phoning it in at this point - which is even more obvious given that games in other genres have been so keen to engage with, and listen to, their fans.Do yourself a favour and skip this year's game until SI offer you something worth spending your money on.

_childDocuments_.review: During the past year I have been a researcher of my local team, so as a thanks, I got the game for free from SI.Also, bare in mind that this is a review during the beta, so everything is not finalised and can be improved upon launch.Football Manager have been my favorite video game-series for many years. I have always looked forward to the new editions and this year was not any different. FM22 was a fantastic game, imo the best ever FM at that time. There have been several improvements to FM23. I am gonna list the biggest ones below.1. The match engine was already good in FM22, but this year it's even better. It looks a lot more like real football is being played with the new animations and ball bounces.2. I really like the new feature called "Squad Planner". It gives you a better overview of your squad and you can more easily find where you need to improve in the future. It also gives you a good idea of if a certain player would fit your team or not, because you can add any player to your Squad Planner at any time.3. The scouting system has been greatly improved as well. It's easier to set up the scouting structure, where you want your scouts to travel and what kind of players you want them to scout.4. The UEFA license is a great addition. SI have done a great job in making the new match layout for the UEFA competitions and also making the live draws a lot more appealing to be a part of instead of just skipping them as in previous years. It adds realism to the game. Yes, you have been able to download third party mods that can add all the real competitions and logos, but imo it's never the same as when it's fully licensed.5. They have made the pressing system in your tactics much better, now being able to choose a "low-block", "mid-block" or "high press" instead of just "lower", "standard", "higher" and "much higher". This has also made defensive tactics more useable and more effective than in previous editions.There are however still a few things that SI haven't improved that I would have liked them to be focusing more on. 1. The set-piece management is still the same as it has been for the last few years, and it's not good. It's too finicky and often it's not set up as you did it when you are playing a game. I think this has to be completely revamped in future editions.2. International management is still pretty pointless and very boring. You can't do team training and rest your players, which is very weird, because that is exactly what you can do in real life. This has to be improved.3. The game should have better graphics. I am not that bothered about the graphics in FM to be honest, because I don't think that is the main thing as in other games. But it should be better than it is. I do not expect FIFA-graphics, but there has barely been any improvement in this area for many years.Summary:For me, Football Manager 2023 is the best FM so far. There haven't been any big new features, which is a bit disappointing. But there is a lot of smaller improvements that just makes the experience better. The Squad Planner and also the improved match engine is the two biggest improvements this year imo.I'm gonna be honest though. If you have Football Manager 2022, and you like it, it's maybe not worth getting FM23 at the moment. I would have bought the game even if I didn't get it for free, but I think a lot of people that plays FM22 wouldn't notice that big of a difference going to FM23.If you still are interested in FM23 though, I fully recommend it. It's a fantastic game and many hours will be put into it, as always!

_childDocuments_.review: As usual, the AAA price tag, plus 9€ for the editor (which should be in the game anyway, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ console), doesn't come close to being justified by the "new features" and "upgrades" that this edition brings to the table over last year's. Precisely because of this do a lot of people only get every other game, such as every even numbered edition, rather than get every single one.With that said, I do love the visual improvements to the matches. In terms of graphical fidelity, it's literally the same: looks like FM (like ♥♥♥♥). However, the new animations are really good and make the game feel incredibly more immersive. It's something you really have to experience for yourself to really notice. The sad part is, for someone that has never played FM before, if they were to start now, with FM23, they'd still think the animations look ancient; because they do. At any rate, the new animations added to things like keeper distribution, heading, dribbling, touches, and even the net actually having physics now, make the game feel a lot more realistic. Regardless; yes, the new animations are a massive improvement, but the game still looks like it should've come out 15 years ago.In terms of actual gameplay... it's still the same old FM. It doesn't feel much different. There are some match engine issues that still need fixing (especially on defense), but overall I do feel like this year's edition is slightly better than the previous one. You can still 4231 Gegenpress your way to the top with any team, but it does feel like the series is continuing down a trend of making life harder for the human player, tactically speaking, which I appreciate; although, of course, it's still largely the same FM veterans have come to expect, and won't really pose much of a challenge for any type of playthrough that isn't journeyman, or something thereabouts.There's the new UEFA competitions license stuff, but who really cares about that? The music and fanfare around UCL competitions is nice and all, but it's a minuscule thing, and most people already used all kinds of packs and mods to make the game more realistic, by adding realistic competition names, logos, etc.The main criticisms, by far, have to be the complete lack of changes to set pieces (unbelievable that they haven't been touched in years, and the current system doesn't even work properly), and the similar total absence of changes to international management, despite the game coming out weeks before a World Cup. It's baffling that neither of these features were touched, and, to me, really just shows how much the execs. in charge of decision-making care about the series and its playerbase. We are cows to be milked, and nothing more.I got the game for around half-off (waited for sale + had a gift card lying around), and I think I'm fine with paying €30-something for the minor upgrade that is 23 over 22, since I know I'm gonna be getting hundreds or thousands of hours out of it.To sum it up: for me, it's definitely an upgrade over 22, but it's a minuscule one that definitely doesn't justify the AAA price tag in the slightest. Even €30 might be pushing it; the only reason I think €30 is about fair is because I'm sure SI paid quite a lot for the UEFA licensing, but were we to talk solely about the effort put into new features and upgrades, even €30 might be a bit too much. So, in short, if you're a die-hard fan of FM, you'll feel at home, but if you get it at full price you'll probably feel robbed, like most people do.If you're happy with 22, and/or the game doesn't get a big sale within the next 2 or 3 months (any more than that and the release of 24 starts to be close enough to justify just waiting for it), I'd probably just skip this edition. Of course, that is the exact same advice everyone gives everyone else, every year.As always, I wish Steam had a "meh" option, rather than Yes or No. I'll give it a Yes, purely based on the fact that I am enjoying myself (it's FM, I love FM, what can I say?...), but the review speaks for itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long term Championship and Football manager player. I really enjoy the games but often end up picking up every other iteration due to the length of my games and the minimal changes between each one. So my path thus far has been FM19, 21 & now the FM23 beta. When the features were released I was a little bit disappointed. There didn't seem to be that many new aspects that weren't, in my opinion, a little superficial. Squad planner seemed just a extension of the squad depth tool and the new licensing is just graphical at the end of the day.I really think not addressing international management before an impeding World Cup seems like one of the biggest promotional own goals of the series. I also wanted to see much more content on the business side of things. We have all seen "Man UFC" fail on the pitch over this decade, but still make massive strides financially. I want to be more supported by the game to make strategic decisions about where to tour, social media impact of signings and how affiliates can support income. It is all hinted at under the hood, but it would add another style of management to the series.As a Steamdeck owner, I wish there was more official support with how the game appears on the system. Nonetheless, it works absolutely fine (faster than my PC) and I will enjoy customising the controls and taking FM out and about! Let's hope the steam cloud based saves hold up as I have heard they can be difficult at times.However, despite these reservations, I have had a blast playing the game. I guess the team prioritised the core mechanics in terms of the match engine and the AI, and my experiences so far have been fantastic. Graphics are much less important for me personally, as long as the animations look realistic, natural, and fluid, which they do. Dribbling is much more dynamic now and you can easily see the difference when following an elite player like Neymar. Players take more realistic and intelligent (stats permitting!) first touches and this makes pressing feel grounded too. I have reflected how often I complain about FIFA wasting time on silly game modes and graphics, instead of addressing the core gameplay issues. So can I really be that dissatisfied with what is on offer here? This may be because I did not play the last title however. But for £32, and knowing how much I will play the game, I am very excited to play the full game this season.Drop a comment if you feel the same or disagree. Would love to hear about other people's experiences (especially Steamdeckers!)

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2023 is the latest iteration of the popular football management simulation game developed by Sports Interactive and published by SEGA. In football manager 2023 this year I challenged myself to successfully complete the glory hunter challenge in which you have o win every trophy in the top 5 leagues plus all the European trophies in the first 20 years of the save. I started Glory Hunter with Lazio.Lazio- I only stayed at lazio for one season however my impact there was not forgotten, In that season i had a terrible time in the Serie A finishing 7th however i managed to get an 8-0 win over Inter Milan and a 4-0 win against AC Milan on the first game of the season. Hats off to Ciro Immbile as he over performed and was the main reason for the clubs successful season. Despite poor league form i rallied the team the win the copper Italia against Napoli 3-1 after being 1 nil down. I also won the europa league with Lazio to fnsih of my last season in Italy. FOR NOW.Valencia - I then moved to Valencia in the preseason of the 23/24 season. When i joined there squad was struggling ith there best striker being 36 year old Edinson Cavani (terrible striker by the way). After a poor start to the season by getting 2 red cards against Barcelona and eventually finishing the game of as a 6 - 1 loss. I had to get my squad in line and with very little transfer budget that was going to be difficult, however i eventually didn't sign anyone as i changed my tecticular thinking and we started winning more and more games. We finished the season off in 3rd place even though the season preview predicted us to finish 11th overall a good season however only winning the Spanish Super Cup. Man United -   I had my heart set on staying at valencia however when the Manchester United job became available it was just to good to turn down. They sacked there previous manager (Erik Ten Haag) after a 7th place finish in the premier league. I joined to a team that looked to good to have finished 7th, at this point Manchester United had Christiano Ronaldo. In the 24/25 season when i first took over as manager there was 113 million pounds in the transfer budget. As you can imagine i spent all of the transfer budget very quickly on one player in particular Patrik Schick who is a wonderkid striker from RB Leipzig. I guess you can say that he was money well spent, between him and Rashford they scored a combined total of around 70 goals in the season . With conference league being our only European trouble this season it seemed like a good opportunity to tick of some silverware from the list. In this season we destroyed the conference league beating former team Lazio in the final 2 - 1 in extra time. In the premier league we had a successful season not losing to rivals Manchester City or Leeds United once however silly results led to us finishing second just 2 points behind Manchester City. We also won the carabao cup during my time at Manchester United so that was another trophy ticked off the list onto 25/26 season.Real Madrid - Another season , another club and we are back in spain for the second time in this save this time with spanish and European Giants Real Madrid. This was going to be a guaranteed trophy season and we even managed to go unbeaten the entire season with 33 wins and 5 draws and you guessed it 0 losses. We won La Liga and Copa Del Ray with a 3 - 1 final win against Barcelona however was sadly knocked out to them in the quarter finals of the champions league at camp Nou 4 - 2 over two legs . So that is officially the spanish leagues completed in the 25/26 season moving on.Thats It For Now

_childDocuments_.review: It is the FM we all know and love. No big upgrades from the last games. If you like the idea of the FM series, this game will not disappoint you. If you have FM22, you can skip FM23 completely and carry on with up-to-date databases. If you have not purchased FM in quite a while, then buying FM23 can make sense since you will catch up with the latest advancements (if you call them advancements) that the new game brings in terms of match engine, AI and, overall feeling. However, if you are someone who is not familiar with the FM series, there is one thing that you must know before you even consider buying this game. It is highly addictive and it will take a lot of your time. FM offers you a never-ending journey in which you decide what the ultimate challenge is. If you want to take a team from semi-pro leagues and bring them the Champions League glory, you will need a lot of TIME. Yet, you do not have to do this. You can just take PSG, for instance, and dominate the world football without even putting any effort into it. That is what makes FM beautiful. You are free to play this game in whatever way you will have fun. Either way, be prepared to put long hours into this game. There is a lot of content available online that will add real player faces, real team and competition logos, and real team and competition names to the game. I suggest you to play the game with these aforementioned add-ons since they will enhance your gameplay considerably.  Either way, FM is pretty clear on what it offers and what it doesn't. If you have the unpreventable desire to manage a team in deep detail that games like FIFA cannot satisfy, then FM is probably the right choice for you. You will not find a better option since there aren't any (I wish there was).

_childDocuments_.review: Football Manager 2023 (FM23) continues the legacy of the popular sports management simulation series, and it doesn't disappoint. The game, developed by Sports Interactive and published by Sega, offers an incredibly immersive and realistic experience for soccer fans who want to take the reins of their favorite clubs and lead them to glory.Graphics and Presentation:FM23 maintains its classic 2D and 3D match engine, which is a staple of the series. While the graphics may not be on par with modern video games, they are more than sufficient for the type of gameplay offered. The user interface has been refined, making navigation and information management more user-friendly. The game's attention to detail is remarkable, with everything from club logos to player likenesses being accurately represented.Gameplay:The heart of FM23 is its deep and engaging gameplay. Managing a soccer team is a complex task, and this game truly captures that essence. You have to handle various aspects such as tactics, training, scouting, and transfers, all of which are integral to your team's success. The game also offers a variety of realistic challenges, from league management to international competitions, ensuring a broad range of experiences.Player Development:The game's player development system is incredibly intricate. You can mold young talents into world-class superstars by giving them the right training and opportunities. This adds depth and satisfaction to your long-term gaming experience.Realism:FM23 is renowned for its realistic portrayal of the soccer world, and this edition is no exception. The in-game database is extensive, with player and team data meticulously researched. The inclusion of data analysts, sports scientists, and other backroom staff highlights the modern soccer world's complexity. The game also reflects real-life events, transfers, and changes in the soccer industry, making it feel incredibly current.Challenges:FM23 presents new challenges and scenarios to test your managerial abilities. This keeps the game fresh and engaging, even for long-time players who might have felt like they'd seen it all. The "Create-A-Club" feature allows for even greater customization, letting you design a club from scratch, adding another layer of depth to the gameplay.Multiplayer Mode:The game's multiplayer mode allows you to compete with friends or other FM enthusiasts. The online feature adds a social dimension to the game, letting you prove your managerial skills against others.Conclusion:Football Manager 2023 is a must-play for any soccer enthusiast or fan of management simulation games. Its deep gameplay, attention to detail, and commitment to realism make it a highly addictive and rewarding experience. While it may not be for everyone due to its complexity, for those who are willing to invest the time and effort, FM23 offers an unparalleled and immersive soccer management experience. If you're a fan of the beautiful game, this is as close as it gets to living the dream of managing your favorite team.

_childDocuments_.review: For new features this edition, we saw an overhaul of the scouting system, a new way to interact with the board of the club you’re managing and the fans too, and that’s it. In terms of quantity, it truly is an underwhelming feature list.However, in terms of quality of life, immersion, and how well they’ve been implemented, I really think each one was a success. I especially like the increased fan interaction and clear depiction of what they want and how satisfied they are with your performance, the goals the fans set differ from the board and their outlook on the transfers you have made go in the exact opposite direction, while the board are completely satisfied and maybe even give you an A+ grade for your financial prudence with you selling a long term squad legend who is well past their best, the fans will be in uproar with a definite F grade. The ability to manage on two fronts is a definite improvement to me.The new scouting system is a middling change for me, like many new features in recent years, it unfortunately only changes things at a superficial level and once you dive into even the slightest of depths you notice it’s purely a reskin of the previous iterations’ systems with some aspects even removed. I can understand the idea behind attempting to make it more realistic but at the same time this is a game, and the primary purpose of gaming is entertainment.What the game does badly is really it is a reskin of Football Manager 2022 in many ways. There just isn’t the need to put in the work required to overhaul it year on year when there are no competitors, people will still buy it. However public opinion is beginning to change though with the majority leaning towards this game being an insult for this price with its lack of changes.Overall I would recommend getting the game on sale if you enjoyed the previous game or it is your first foray into the series but avoid paying full price. Series stagnation is the main drawback and immersion is the main pull to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a reasonably negative review of last year's game, and my closing line was something along the lines of, "you can copy/paste this review for the 2023 edition". And really, you could, because that's exactly what they've done with the game.Perhaps gradual improvements, in yearly increments, to a winning formula would be no bad thing at all. As players, we shouldn't necessarily demand wholesale changes to a game that people have already grown to love. And I don't think my expectations are ever for the development team to re-write the game every year.But to be clear, we're not getting gradual improvements. We're getting basically nothing, year in, year out. Having played over 150 hours of the 2023 edition, I couldn't tell you what changes they've made this year. They're so insignificant to how you interact with (and play) the game, that I just don't think you'd notice them unless they were explicitly pointed out.Worse than this, though, is the refusal to fix things that never worked in the first place. Experienced players will know what I'm talking about, but a cursory glance at social media memes will show you how familiar we all are with the more obnoxious elements of game play. To name just a few:• Player interactions are an awful, half-baked feature. It's total pot luck how a player will respond, often defying any logic and with extremely long-lasting consequences. • Club and fan expectations are extremely unrealistic. For example, take your un-fancied team to an unexpectedly high position in the table, and they'll start being disappointed that you draw 0-0 away to Man City. • The conversations still use exactly the same text as multiple previous iterations of the game. Not even a couple of extra lines thrown in, just for variety. Not to mention that some of the lines sound like they asked your dad to chip in, and he was positively chuffed to do so.• Good players still make unfathomable decisions. 2vs1, through on goal, still won't square a pass. CBs told to play it short, take fewer risks, with a CDM right in front of them, team set to 'play it shorter' = still lump it forward to nobody in particular.The list really could go on, but this is not to say that FM is a bad game. I've put a lot of hours in to this game, and even more into the preceding titles. But the more time that passes, the more it feels like I'm playing this game because it's really addictive, not necessarily fun. Why do I say this? Because after 150 hours and taking a club to unrealistic heights, I just got the feeling that I'd done all this before. Same game, same graphics, same text, same broken elements. Just different player stats. So at this point, we might as well just call the game Football Manager, strip the year, and have it as a subscription service. You pay £40 a year and they update all the stats for you. And when you put it like that, it leaves a bit of a bitter taste in the mouth.Having said all this, I'll almost certainly be back next year. Though I think this is more a reflection on how much I want to enjoy this game, rather than how much I really get out of it. That, and there just isn't any competition; maybe it's time there was.
