_childDocuments_.review: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Hercule Poirot, the famous Belgian detective, is urgently requested to return to London. Unfortunately, he is stranded in Istanbul, but thanks to Mr Bouc, an old friend and line director of the all-mighty train, the Orient Express, Poirot is offered a compartment to travel from Istanbul to Paris. There is plenty of time for both men to catch up during the upcoming voyage, but fate will not allow it, as a mysterious businessman is killed on the first night of the trip. This is a game set in 2023 where Hercule Poirot even uses a mobile phone to his advantage.Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express is a point-and-click adventure with puzzle elements game developed and published by Microids on the 19th of October 2023 on the Steam platform. The game is also available on PS4|PS5, Nintendo Switch and Xbox Series X|S.The game consists of 13 chapters in which you will play the famous detective in Istanbul, Venice, Geneva and, of course, on the Orient Express. Although the game is faithful to the original story, a couple of twists have been introduced, such as a female American detective, which you'll also be playing in the Boston and Geneva chapters. I will leave the other twists for you to discover. They cleverly implemented these elements into the game, making perfect sense and prolonging the story.  The gameplay is what you would expect for the genre. I like how easy and comfortable the view movements are in this game, which enhances the ability to search areas and pick up and view items. Mind maps will appear in each chapter, which you can access anytime using the TAB button on your keyboard. On these maps, it will tell you who you need to interrogate next to move forward. But, at a particular stage and after gathering information, you will be prompted to make a deduction about what happened at a precise time, or to recreate a sequence of events, or perhaps to confront a character about a lie. For the latest, you'll be given four sentences to choose from, while the other two will be mini-puzzles. These puzzles are among many others in the game, and for the most part, they are decent and well-structured. I struggled with one puzzle towards the end of the game in Geneva - it took me a while to figure it out. But you don't have to sweat if you don't want to, as you can access up to three tips per puzzle, which will give you the answer. The characters' looks, personas, animations, and voiceovers are excellent. The fact that you will also be playing the Boston female detective gives you a bit of a breathing space, and is implemented at the right moment. They realised that it needed something other than moving back and forth between six wagons. I was truly entertained all the way through my 14 hours of gameplay. I also like the informative anecdotes on Agatha Christie and Hercule Poirot between the loading screens, which were quick. However, I encountered a weird issue in chapter two. At one point, you have to interview Mrs. Hubbard and search for clues in her compartment. Up until then, as I was away from home I used my laptop, promptly got stuck, and couldn't search her cabin. When I got back home, I tried with my desktop - I could click on a couple of places but then got stuck again. So I swapped back to the laptop, clicked on a few places, and - you guessed it - got stuck again. I went back and forth between both devices at least five times before I could finally exit the room. And yes, I did verify the integrity of the files on both devices. But from then on, it was smooth sailing. The graphics are fantastic, and I enjoyed the background music. The voiceovers are spot on, and overall, I am happy to say that this is probably the best Agatha Christie game I have ever played. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great graphics and background music+	Faithful to the original story, with a couple of twists+	Good camera angle movements+	Well-detailed characters' looks, persona and animations+	Decent puzzles all the way through, with tips if you get stuck+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	A very odd bug encountered in chapter two which stopped my progress-	No trading cardsA modernised, stylised version of the game, faithful to the original story with a couple of twists. It's probably the best game of the Agatha Christie series from Microids.8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: The game follows the familiar story line of the famous story, but adds small independent intrepretations that gives that little extra feeling of familiarity combined with uncertainty. This is of course not to say that M. Poirot, with his charismatic moustache and accent, is not single handedly capable to carry the game on his own.Though the plot is very similar to the original, it is set in a modern setting with mobile phones and other equipment. This aspect is well integrated as a plot device, which doesn't simply feel forced in for the sake of nothing but formulates an intriguing story of deduction.The game itself, while excelling in the 'feeling' of the plot, still plays a bit uncomfortable with slow movement with relatively large maps, making it frustrating moving from one side to another when you forgot to speak to a single person, resulting in sighing and loss of interest. Therefore, the deduction and other vital investigative parts of the game remain pristine, according to my experience, but the room between these seem simply annoying, and something as simple as making the doors inbetween the train wagons open with you moving into them rather than activly opening them with interactions would have made it more tolerable.Overall a great detective game, that captures the spirit of such games, but an annoyance in navigating between these scenes of deduction.

Changes noticeable would b ethe inclusion of cell phones, modern police car, and modern glass ouse setting. Most of the game is set in the fabled Orient Express and is a nice change. I love the addiitonal content and twist at the end. That was honestly surprisinging and unexpected entirely. Graphics are decent enough, and rough estimation are from the late 2000s and early 2010s. Not too bad, but are ok and acceptable. That is not a distraction from the game. The story pacing is fine, and the prologue got me hooked, even though its slow and does slow start. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved the Murder on the orient express part of this game. It's flawed, skipping key moments, somewhat weird characterizations, oddball modernizations, but overall great. But the original mystery is solved halfway into the game. You even get a creditroll, which is interrupted by the doctor absurdly declaring that he found "a small wound inside a big wound".At this point the game completly derails. The narrative doesn't just fall flat, it's absent. They don't bother about establishing characters, build up the plot or anything. You are just slapped with a endless series of quicktime events and "crack-the-code-to-open-door" crap.I understand the problematic aspects of a mystery that *everyone* knows the answer to. But at the very least they could keep it within the same genre. I still love the first part, and would be a fanboy if they opted to flesh that out more, but the latter part is so awful that I cannot recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this, not being too familiar with the original story (I know, I know - where have I been?!).  I recommend this to players who want a (somewhat forgiving) puzzle game with a large cast of characters (2 playable) and a lot of charm.Performance was fine.  No bugs or crashes.  I think I had to turn down the mouse sensitivity initially.The graphical style was really appealing to me.  Some scenery objects block you when it looks like they really shouldn't (invisible walls), but this did not actually deter from the experience.There is a hint system and multiple attempts at answers so having a perfect run of correct answers mainly matters if you're going for all achievements (or for personal satisfaction of course!)(My 32 hours played includes two full runs of the game)
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing the game. They tried to stay close to the book but added the elemtents of the "new world" nicely. It felt like this game was made with love. Some puzzles were really hard, some really easy.   Having to walk the train up and down countless times was a bit tiresome, but well... it's a train. So I guess, they did their best not to make it into a complete walking simulator.Finding the golden mustaches makes the exploring of the world fun and I still have to find a lot of them. I'll surley replay this game and try to find everything.The style and the scenery are nice and I forgive them, that Poirot is a tall, well build man. Character design overall was interesting.If you suffer from motion sickness the sensitivity of the mouse might throw you off. I read that some people have problems with it.Overall: good game.

_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Hated it.Boring, too long (it WOULD NOT END, meaningless chapters over and over again), glitchy and stupid riddles, the ending doesn't make sense, it's like they wanted to find a scapegoat aka villian and neither wrote nor explained it properly.And - cherry on top - russian propaganda. _childDocuments_.review: A character late in the game remarks how "somehow this all seems so familiar..."  It is certainly the bones of the original story and characters, but with an updated modern coating. When you reach the conclusion though, you'll discover that an additional mystery remains and your adventure along the route of the Orient Express isn't over by a long shot.This addition, as well as the fleshed out backstory of the central mystery are well thought out and work seamlessly into the grand design without detracting from the original plot.A new version of a classic that retreads the same familiar rails, but then jumps the tracks for some added excitement.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Some parts were a little annoying - opening the carriage doors on the train! But overall a fantastic game interpretation of the excellent classic detective story. _childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: -wayyyy too expensive-uneven voice acting-lackluster graphics and presentation-weak introduction and first hour-weak "detective" and guesswork gameplay structure (the game holds your hand way too much)-do not play this game if you've read the bookand despite these massive flaws, I still recommend it (on sale) because the story itself is just so good, and the way the murder unravels is so satisfying and multilayered. the few twists they've seem to add on the original story work not as good but are still engaging enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Good overallGraphics are so so/passable for 2024no bugs which is good.Characters movement seems stiff.Some of the dialogue seems unnatural. Also the main female American character (Locke), she said some words wrong. eg. instead of 'shame', she pronounced it 'sham'.The twist/extra at the end seemed odd, seemed to drag the game and tone out further than needed.If you get this game on sale, it's worth it. _childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: i was a bit hesitant in buying this game because the story and the outcome is so well known but i have no regrets, they made it so that you have to pay attention to what is being said in order to make the right conclusions and even if you make wrong conclusions/deductions, this doesn't change the ending of the game, only your/poirot's ego is on the line here and, without giving to much spoilers, this game has an extra.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: After playing and enjoying the ABC Murders and the Hercule Poirot First Cases and enjoying both, I of course had to try this one also. Murder on the Orient Express is one of Agatha Christie's classics that everyone knows and adores, so it's certainly a big title to take on.Fortunately, they do it fairly well.There are of course differences between the novel and the game, and they decided to throw in their own twist as well that adds something new even for those that know the story. (Whether or not it will be a positive addition or not will however be up to each person. I for one thought it was a little cliched but still found enjoyment in figuring it all out.)The game mechanics are easy to understand and straight-forward. The puzzles are simple enough while being fun, though some seem very unnecessary and could have been handled better imo. (Basically you have to help people before they answer your questions sort of thing, but really on the nose to the point where Poirot himself mentions it in-game.) Still, again, they were enjoyable.So was the collecting of the golden moustaches, though I find it funny that nobody ever mentions them. They just exist for you to collect. Nice.The achievements were also rather easy to get, you could probably get all in one playthrough, though that does take away some of the replay value. In general, I only replayed select levels again afterwards to look around even more because I really enjoyed the graphics.However, I did have a pet peeve. The game constantly has you running back and forth through the train, from one end to the other, and every time you have the little animation of going through a door, which involves opening the door and stepping through it, before you can go on. There are a lot of doors. It drags it out quite a bit and gets annoying fast.The other detective was nice also and added a bit more background info to the story, though it feels like she could have been better fleshed out as a character. I liked the bits where you had to work as both of them to progress. It was rather well done without being too confusing or either dragging on or being too quick to follow.All in all, it was a great and fun game, and I liked this depiction of Poirot and how he handled things and dialogues. It felt very Poirot to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Poirot game I have ever played. It has a great hint system if you get stuck but the puzzles are just the right level of difficulty. The voice acting is great and the mechanics of the game work flawlessly. Best of all, this iteration of Poirot takes place in the present day and Poirot is hot!
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much that I played it a second time. Hercule Poirot seems a bit old-fashioned for the way the game is implemented in today's modern times, but overall it's a charming signature style of Agatha Christie's character. The journey on an old train is exciting and changes in perspective and location give the environment a perfect variety along the ride. The difficulty of the puzzles is easy. However, the story involves murders and several extremely sad family tragedies. That's why I don't think the game is suitable for children, even though in Germany it's supposed to be suitable for children.It is a great game for everyone aged 12 and over, especially for adults who love crime stories and lores including extraordinary detectives and thrilling cases combined with lots of varied neat puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this game. Mysteries are my favorite genre. The only complaint I have (which isn't really a complaint at all), is that the loading screen was too fast and I couldn't read the interesting facts about Agatha Christie.  I am thinking of doing another play threw so i can get all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable experience start to finish. The snowed in Orient Express setting is a classic, and I really enjoyed the graphics style of this game, it really adds to the ambiance. The interior of the train is also gorgeous. Several chapters take place beyond the train, in the US and in Venice. Beyond that, the story takes the original book story and expands it across continents, and then just when you think you've solved it (around the halfway point), it adds an interesting twist on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Save system is greatly improved compared to the other games in the series. I also liked the general graphics and color scheme more. Music is better, voice acting is very good as usual. Overall probably the best game in the series so far.I have to say I hate WASD. this is not something I like to do when trying to relax. Other than that all is well. And there is a lot more personality to the game. Which is good. But WASD! and no way to avoid it. still no skip button for cutscenes... and what's worse now even casual dialogues are unskippable line by line making this last forever - you can only skip the line if you have heard it already but if it's long and you read the subtitles you have to actually wait for it to end. mandatory tutorial should also be illegal.The mindmap logic seems improved to me.What I also value is that no matter how high I set the video quality my pc stays cool. This is quite rare especially in WASD - first person walking simulator games.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Well written, with puzzles that stretch ones memory, but all the required information is available.  There's plenty of it too.  I thought I was getting to the end around 10pm, and decided to finish it off.  I was still playing at 2am and was rather tired the next day.  There are a few scenes that are not on the train, but most of the plot is, given the subject matter, on the train, and resulted in walking up and down the carriages rather more than I fancied.  Overall a worthwhile purchase.  More of this quality please Microids.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: There are two halves to this game. The first half is based on the book. The second half is original work. The first half is better, but the original story fits as well. Microids knows how to make amazing point and click adventures! I really hope they make another Agatha Christie game like this. I recommend this to anyone who loves mystery games.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: As someone new to the Agatha Christie stories I enjoyed this a lot! I think it's a nice way to tell the story in a more modern way. Puzzles are engaging without feeling like they're impossible to navigate. The plot is also quite nice to follow along, although at some points I felt like I had been better off if I had written down everyone's stories somewhere. The timeline along which the story progresses didn't help me there. All in all I definitely recommend this if you enjoy detective games :)
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 14 hours to complete "Murder on the Orient Express", and I had lots of fun questioning all the suspects on the train and solving the occasional logic or mechanical puzzle as Hercule Poirot, as well as getting to investigate the story behind the motive as police detective Joanna Locke. While the game offers perhaps too much guidance on where to go and what to do, making it a very linear experience without any alternative outcomes based on your decisions, it’s awesome to live through one of the best works in literary fiction in this interactive way. The Orient Express becomes your home for a while, its occupants almost a family – if a rather dysfunctional one – as you immerse yourself in discovering every clue and fitting all the puzzle pieces together. Even if you can’t really fail, earning that approving nod from Poirot or Locke when you’ve made a correct deduction filled me with pride and a feeling of accomplishment, and the entire experience made me wish there were more games of this quality out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game.  Finally, a game that is perfect for me.  I love Agatha Christie.  I love the story, characters & puzzles.  I played the older Agatha Christie Murder on the Orient Express & enjoyed it too.  The graphics are very good.  The game played smoothly with no glitches.  I would definitely recommend this game.  It took me 20 hours to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Tale as old as time....7/10 Do recommend, great for newer gamers because it's easy and also satisfying for experienced mystery gamers because the way they've handled the story is engaging, just go into it knowing you're going to have your hand held a lot. I'm a lifelong mystery/adventure game player and I love the 2006 Orient Express game, but have grown impatient with old school P&C, so a new telling of the story was a no brainer for me.This is a modern update to a story all mystery fans know. It would be easy for it to feel stale, but it doesn't. The original story is both honored and updated, and I can't say much more than that without spoiling it.Gameplay-wise it's standard fare. Controls are smooth, it's nice to have open movement in a Poirot game (I previously elevated this game above the other two newer Poirot games here due to their P&C, but I gave those games another chance and discovered they do enable keyboard controls and are much better with them, so am editing my review to remove that criticism). Voice acting is nice and I'm no graphics afficionado but the game is very pretty. The puzzles integrate well and aren't difficult if you've been paying attention.I'm quite pleased with this entry in the Agatha Christie franchise and I hope this studio develops more. It's certainly the best since the AWE games of the aughts.  I have only two suggestions for improvement. The first is ditch the mind map unless it's actually going to be used like a mind map - this game just has a task list that looks like a mind map. I promise you don't have to do it just because it's become common. I would rather have just had a notebook. Mind maps make sense when you have to make choices or deductions that actually affect the story - this one just tells you where to go and occasionally gives you a multiple choice question that you can't get wrong.  And that brings me to the second suggestion - less hand holding, please! It's not pixel hunting when you don't have to hunt but rather are shown anything/one you need to interact with. This is a game that is nearly impossible to get stuck in, and for me that's not a dealbreaker if everything else is good, but it's not a positive either.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first ever playthrough of this game and i'm impressed! I've struggled to find story rich games that pull me in recently but this one hits the spot! The graphics are beautiful and satisfying, the story is well written and puts a few twists and turns on the original Agatha Christie story to keep it interesting! I love the character design and development. The puzzles and tasks were a mixture of easy and some a bit complicated but I got there eventually. The music was great and helped to secure the desired atmosphere. Makes me want to go on a real journey on the Orient Express! If you're unsure if you want to buy this game, I recommend you do and just let yourself become enveloped in it.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game overall but damn am I fighting to not write a negative review based off of Bouc's annoyingness alone!!! Lol Early game you have to open a suitcase and Bouc literally will not shutup, it gave me so much anxiety, I can't even tell you! Otherwise great game lol. It is a lot to remember though, I do recommend playing it one or two sittings if possible because even your mind map does not recall/record everything you need to remember. ie conversations with passenger's that are important etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good remake of the original game. The story is Murder on the Orient Express in the modern day. The developer mixes the original story well with new and contemporary elements. More than that, a new character and a new ending are added to the story, making the game feel more like it is in the current day, but the original storyline can still be maintained. This is a successful remake.There are some minor imperfections. Most of the puzzles are not challenging enough. But the last chapter (which is the added new ending) brings a few real challenges so it's somewhat of a make-up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I like this version of Poirot better than any other in game adaptations.  Easy game mechanics, mostly decent voice acting (with exception to the last chapter), puzzles were easy save for the last chapter where there are several of progress stoppers.  The last puzzles felt like the game's death toll - where you can see the finish line and there's just a few hurdles to jump and with every jump you're actually transported into a dark maze with a matchstick for light.  There's at least one surprising dexterity mechanic that took me completely by surprise and I had to do it 5 or 6 times as my character would get stuck against a wall at a particular spot, I don't know if it was a pathing issue or a weird FPS drop during scene transition but it was reproducible.I do like difficult puzzles and felt that the game could've used more but I really like the way the game was designed.  All integrated well and didn't hold up the story.  Some were ehh and telegraphed but usual fare, Poirot even calls out the goofiness.  There are manual saves which is great.  I found the rework of the mindmap a delight, some may not like it but I thought it to be better than the previous Poirot games.  I haven't completed the game just yet as I'm stuck on a tandem puzzle and I think there may be another surprising game element lurking that I'm pretty sure I'm going to find irritating beyond measure, I certainly hope it's not what I think.  At first I found finding the golden mustaches fun but overall it was distracting for me and tone deaf at times to the point where I stopped bothering unless one was in plain sight.  I was into the story and having to remember there are also lil' mustaches to find was just a burden despite my moderate completion compulsion.  I kept going back and forth with effort to find them and then it would detract from the agenda and I'd forget what I was supposed to be doing.  Could be my old brain - anyway, recommend...I hope to see this version of Poirot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: I will only recommend this game because adventure/puzzle games are a niche product nowadays and you don't get as many new releases per year. This game was somewhat fun to play and the story was interesting, however, there are some major issues I want to point out.Firstly the game looks and plays like it was created in 2005, not 2023. Graphics are very outdated, even for a point and click game, and animations/physics are close to nonexistent/very bulky. It's been a while since I've seen an invisible wall in game. I would really love to play more games like this, but in 2023 I would expect a slightly better graphics/gameplay.Some gameplay aspects were a bit wierd/childish as well. Like Hercule saying "I am right" every time you solve some puzzle, this is rather annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game! A well paced mystery with twists and turns. The only feedback I could give is to add a menu that keeps track of details that we have discovered/transcripts such as alibis because unless you are playing the whole game in one sitting it can be tricky to remember all details when coming back to it a day later - not that the game punishes you for not remembering, the only thing this would effect is missing an achievement or two for the perfect playthrough.Overall loved this game and really hope to see more in the future! Hopefully that end credit scene was a hint that more is to come ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review: A simple yet effect detective game, so far I'm only frustrated by the movement of the character (sprint is buggy) - but so far it is much better than the other Agatha Christie game that I played this year.The only cons is that it's simple to master, like if you get something wrong you get a slap on the wrist until you do get the right answer. I feel like this game is meant to be experienced like you're watching a film or show because of how linear it presents itself, which isn't bad as this is a modern adaptation of a classic story.In truth this game knew it was kind of game it was before it was finalised, which is a big plus - it's meant to be light and enjoyable, a nice distraction while you're having some down time with a cuppa tea.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Agatha Christie - Murder on the Orient Express

_childDocuments_.review:
Set in 2023, Murder on the Orient Express brings the classic tale to life in a way that will surprise even the most dedicated fans. With brand-new elements added to the original story, experience the mystery and suspense like never before and rediscover one of the most famous case of Hercule Poirot.

A crime is committed on board the Orient Express. Hercule Poirot, during this trip, is surrounded by a group of singular characters, all suspects, each with their own secrets and motivations, and will then try to elucidate the murder that has just taken place.

Solving the mystery won't be easy. Through numerous twists and turns, you will have to use your little grey cells and your detective skills to unravel the truth and bring it to light.

Whether you're a fan of the iconic book or movies, a lover of murder mysteries, or just looking for a thrilling adventure, this new proposal has something for everyone. So step aboard the Orient Express, and let the journey begin!

_childDocuments_.review: Having read the more negative comments before making my purchase I was somewhat dubious about whether this game would be of the quality I've come to expect from Ironhide. Having played plenty enough already to make up my mind, I can tell you the answer to that question is an emphatic yes.The best way I can explain this game is as a sort of choose your own adventure turn based isometric roguelite. You control a party of three adventurers each with their own abilities, strengths and weaknesses and along the way pick up a fourth. By playing the game you gain access to new party members to choose from and new upgrade choices for the characters you use the most. Once you've selected your party you will embark on an adventure which brings you to a map dominated by nodes, without going into exhaustive detail this is where the choose your own adventure aspect comes in with the added spice of a little RNG. Personally I like this, each adventure is somewhat randomised in terms of nodes and random encounters giving the game a huge amount of replay-ability. The boss fights are tough and if you make a mistake the game isn't going to forgive you. The humour still gets the odd chuckle too.I'm not going to sit here and tell you that this game is super deep and it'll consume your life or that the controls on PC are perfectly intuitive. However, it is a really solid game to play while you listen to an audio book or to use as a break from work or study and I've already found myself spending hours engrossed in it half-oblivious to the outside world, something I haven't experienced in a game for what feels like years. If you like this sort of game or you're really into Kingdom Rush like me you will probably love Legends of Kingdom Rush. If you're the kind of gamer who wants really tough in-depth turn based strategy games it may not be for you (but give the demo a shot, it might surprise you).
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: The mobile game aspect of this game shows its face once you have completed the main questlines. It's only been updated once with the Moonlight Grove map and then...that's it, you just do the same game over and over again. I love Ironhide studios, their TD Kingdom Rush Games have been a stable of my childhood for the art styles, heroes and stories. But this game falls short in both the Story catergory and the replayability. I like the "idea" of this game but the clear "start this game over and over for replayabilties sake" is not the hook Ironhide thinks it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I was iffy about this game as it's not the typical tower defense that Kingdom Rush games have been known to be. In my opinion I was right to be iffy, this game gets so boring so fast. Not only is there very little variation in enemies as well as tactics, but the difficulty doesn't seem to matter. In fact I do better on the harder difficulty which makes no sense. I hit a plateau where the game got insanely harder and I cannot honestly figure out how I'm supposed to progress. From what I can tell they expect you to figure out exactly which combination of fighters you need to progress. But doesn't that defeat the point of CHOOSING your fighters? It's not just the progression plateau, I found the only reason I played beyond the first 2 hours was because there were some easy side achievements. I'm past 2 hours so I can't refund the game, but I honestly have no itch to reopen and continue playing it. I've done the same 5 fights over and over and over. I've beat the dead horse and see nothing more of interest in this title unfortunately. I guess it's not the worst $15 I've ever spent, but I certainly wouldn't recommend it to anyone either. _childDocuments_.review: So, I'm in the first battle of this adventure. I kill most of the enemies with all my heroes' health remaining. Then the enemies reach us and each one one-hit-kills each of my team. Game over. Maybe I'm just a novice? Except... this is the first battle of this adventure, but not my first overall. In fact, I've completed this adventure and the others in under 20 hours, I'm just trying to get the remaining achievements. So why is it still so hard? Because they haven't balanced the difficulty to work with their randomised battle mechanic. The first battle of each adventure could be harder than any others, just depends how they land. And with only 3 levels to get on the basic heroes, it's not a case of levelling them to improve your chances. By the end of the adventures, all the basic heroes I'd acquired were maxed out. It's no indicator of how well they'll do.But rather than work this out, they've chosen to just put on a loading screen that you might not win first time, keep trying! Idk, I love their tower defence games, but this attempt at a turn-based strategy feels a little unsophisticated.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but it's also pretty shallow. That's fine if that's what you're looking for -- otherwise, there are better games in the same genre, like Wildermyth -- and even better games by the same studio, like their tower defense games.

_childDocuments_.review: is not like any other  game, it is not a tower defense game. Just because you like those games, does not mean you will like this one. You were warned!Legend of Kingdom Rush offers 4 different adventures and these differ in both tactics and theme.The player controls a group of heroes as they embark on a journey to defend their kingdom against various threats. The game features a variety of heroes(18 total), each with unique abilities and skills, that players can collect and unlock possible upgrades as they progress through the game. We start our selected adventure with 3 of these heroes, setting up your roster is up to you, so the characters you control are not randomised. Feels exciting right? Sadly, it isn’t. Despite the variety of party setups, the combat ends up feeling pretty dry and mindless once you get the average knowledge about the basics. Each hero is also very simplistic as during adventures you can level up each only twice and during each level up you could choose one new ability only from 2 and you can’t decide what stats to increase.The nodes in these adventures are randomised, so it is still offering some replayability and you can also reach the final boss on the map by choosing different paths. While you can see what the upcoming nodes offer to you, like combats, events, a vendor or some other stuff, there are still random encounters that might stop you between 2 nodes. In case a node or an event ends up as a combat, then the turn-based gameplay allows players to carefully plan out their moves and make strategic decisions in combat. Fallen heroes losing one maximum health for the rest of the adventure, well, if you win the battle with your other heroes…Some items could help you out during your adventure. Potions with various effects or healing, items which help you out during some events (or you can roll with a dice to see different outcomes if you don’t own the required item) or consumables which increase a stat of your champions.Adventures ends upon beating the boss at the end of your journey and these battles are the most interesting part of the game, at least here we can find some creativity.Other than the 4 boss battles at the end of the adventures the arena and daily challenges are the most interesting part of the game because of additional mechanics and randomness to the otherwise boring and predictable combats.Because of the limited content and the repetitive and somewhat boring gameplay I personally don’t recommend the game. It is not a terrible game, but it really doesn’t bring anything notable to the genre. There are tons of better games out there if you want to play something similar. (and this is the same probably what i would say to tower defence game which is not Gemcraft or tower defense versions of Kingdom Rush :-D)  7/10.  5/10.  4/10. Not experienced any, I played this game only on steam deck. Not experienced any. Playable by using the touchscreen and because of that somewhat longer gaming session not comfortable in most body positions. Finish all 4 areas on normal difficulty and then only the grind remains. Need to finish (you don’t need to win, but you need to either lose or win it, so forfeiting does not work) 25 daily challenges. Don’t forget that if you going to a specific achievement, which require killing X enemy in Y amount of turns, or something similar, and you finally found the required node for it, then you can just quit the game in the middle of the game if you failing with the requirement and upon starting the game again then you will continue that node from its first round, not from the point where you quitted. This makes annoying achievements more obtainable. 5/10. Normal difficulty might be hard for some, but I nearly never lost a run, so it shouldn't be too difficult. If it is for you, then remember: stack ranged units. Oloch-Ranger-Bombardier was my favourite setup. ~30h+

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Game is fun, with bugs that could ruin a run. Lacks content atm with only 5 maps. Pros: - Easy to pickup once you are familiar with game mechanics - Decent replayability- Good character selection/Team Composition Cons: - RNG could be a real bummer sometimes- Controls takes time to get used to - Beginning of the game will be difficult with limited characters- Only 5 mapsThis game is honestly a good simplified roguelite for people that likes Turn-based combat, Random Encounters, and planning a path through a dungeon. To me it's a Slay The Spire path finding plus FF Tactics type combat. Character progression might seems pointless since leveling and progressing through a dungeon is difficult in the beginning. This is due to the initial learning curve of understanding of the enemy types and counters. Once you are past that initial bump, progressing will feel more natural. You will get frustrated as the game tends to up its difficulty with random events or encounters that could wipe your team before you're 2 tiles in. Which could discourage new players, especially if you have a good start/RNG. But I assure you even with my best team it happens, and it's something I eventually learned to accept. Now the real thing that almost turned me away from the game was the controls. Which is a mix of point and click plus keyboard (I haven't played with a controller yet). I initially played it as I did with most ironside mobile games, with point and click, but soon found it is far too unreliable as I find myself using the wrong ability from time to time. I soon adapted to using 1,2,3 for the abilities and E for end turns, which basically completely solved my control problems. Replayability will differ from person to person. I personally enjoy rerunning a dungeon with a different team just to try different combos. The game does a good job of mixing up encounters along the way and providing different daily/challenge dungeons for quick play. But I do find the weakness of the game to be it's lack of maps. I feel like there could be more, but I suppose for it's current price tag, it provides just enough content for a good 6-8 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, of course, the tower defense games from Ironhide are all masterpieces! But, but... this is no tower defense game. To my suprise this is a turn-based strategy game in the Kingdoms universe. You control up to 4 heroes on small maps in turn-based battles. Move, attack, and use spells and abilities to kill your foes. If all your heroes become unconscious, you lose. If you win, your heroes continue the game, but with wounds from the previous fights (until you can heal them). Decide whom of the around 15 heroes you include in your party - a paladin, dark assassin, evil demon, ranger, sorceress, or knight? All have unique abilities, so you have plenty of options. You have to find them before you can recruit them, of course. Between the combat you move your party over a map with nodes - not all of them lead to combat, some may lead to treasure, new heroes or other events. There are 3 adventures until you reach the final boss -  fight orcs in the forest, trolls in the mountains and demons in the wastelands. The story is not too long, you can finish it in a few hours. Defeat your foes in short turn-based fights on a hex-based grid in this casual strategy game. It's core mechanics are easy to understand, but still with some depth.

While it's fun to experiment with different combinations of characters, you'll always end up defending your starting position because you're always outnumbered and all enemies are coming straight towards you. Staggering most enemies while killing the closest one is the only effective way of winning the game that I could discover. The second problem is far worse: the game is rather hard, and winning or losing a campaign depends a lot on the outcome of random events. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: the game has good design, but is dragged down by bad UX and lack of polish.the game features several rogue-like campaigns within which we navigate a nodes map. combat encounters take the form of hex-based tactics-lite gameplay. the nodes are procedurally shuffled each time you start a new campaign.at the start of a campaign, you select a hero and two nameless sidekicks. you wil be able to recruit a third sidekick (total 4 party members) during the campaign. as you progress the game, you will unlock new starting characters.each character has 3 tiers of skills, and starts with their two tier 1 skills. the characters can be leveled up during campaign, unlocking one tier 2 and one tier 3 FOR THE RUN'S DURATION ONLY.campaigns are short, like 30min to 1h. the meat of the game is to complete achievements that unlock new characters, then to level up those characters' mastery level to unlock all their possible tier 2 and 3 skills.at the core, this system is nice because it plays into the rogue-like philosophy of the game where you are expected to do multiple runs of each map (the game even tells you that in the loading screen). it feels a bit grindy but I like it and find it okay since it is optionnal.the tactics gameplay is fun and nicely ballanced. careful placement and playing with freeze/stun/root and knockback are required in order to keep you units alive, which I enjoy. very well done.my real issues with the game lie in UI/UX design, reinforced by the lackluster PC port.- there is no option to show enemies' danger zone. you need to check the range of each of the enemie's skills, remember it, and sum it up yourself.- during a character's turn, YOU CHARACTER IS ALWAYS SELECTED. so you can not click on an eneny to see its traits, this shows you the path to move/attack. you need to select them in the "turn queue".- the hitbox when targeting a hex seems to be bigger than the ground and/or extend with the unit that is on. I had several misstargeting when a small enemy is next to a tall enemy. it could be even more cumbersome on mobile's small screen with touch controls less precise than a mouse.- there is no preview of the stats that will be gained when leveling up a character during a campaign.- BIGGEST QOL MISS: a common feature in tactical games is to allow movement cancellation until a skill/attack has been used.- the game does not let you restart an encounter. it is "unofficially" possible by quitting to desktop then continuing the campaign where you left at, which will resume the run at the start of the encounter. as a result of the previous two bulletpoints, it happens that a fight is doomed by an unintentionnal error. do you really want to play by the game's rules and restart you whole run in those cases ?- there is no encyclopaedia to easily access the enemies' stats, skills, etc. which is a huge  let down since all previous kingdom rush instalments had this feature.in the graphics department, like every ironhide production, the game is absolutely gorgeous to look at. every sprite and animation are so lively, it really shows the mastery they accumulated from doing this artstyle for over a decade 👌for the PC port, it would have been nice to have a borderless windowed display that does not go in background when the windows is not focussed, it is very anoying for dual+ screen setups.also the startup ironhide logo plays sound even if the sound is set to 0 in the game's settings. not that big of a deal though.

_childDocuments_.review: Ironhide Game Studio continues their 'but what if the towers moved' experiments with Legends of Kingdom Rush. Everything should be pretty familiar for fans of the franchise, our old favorites have simply stepped down from their respective towers, and the heroes didn't even do that much. The character designs are instantly recognizable from previous games, they've even kept the same voice clips, so you should have a good idea of what each unit is about at first sight. That brand recognition is important as you'll only be able to select three units yourself, the fourth being a random tag along picked up mid-adventure. There's a good variety between units and you'll be trying out most of them due to the aforementioned party quirk. Thankfully, explicit stats and descriptions make it easy to see what a character is capable of, including the conditions needed to trigger the more powerful 'epic' version of their moves. Though this can lead to some deceptive tooltips, when those characters have some kind of damage scaling due to distance or something else the game has a hard time calculating on the fly.Feedback in general is something Legends struggles with. The hex overlay, for example, is limited by how a character can move or attack, as that's the only time it's shown. Planning a move ahead or judging an enemy's attack range, extremely important parts of this genre, require an unnecessary amount of guesswork. The character models themselves can also block hexes even when they are shown, making some moves difficult to judge or simply impossible to execute. Speaking of difficulty, the only difference I could find between 'casual' and 'normal' is the items you start with and the experience you're granted, leaving the encounter challenge more a product of RNG than the setting I would have thought controlled it. That sense of randomness is clearly intentional as Legends is designed around replayability. The course of an adventure is determined as much by the outcome of dice rolls as it is by the path you choose. This, along with a single defeat booting you clear back to the overwold atlas, make adventures a fairly rogue-like affair. Which only rubbed me the wrong way before I realized you could simply leave a battle that wasn't going your way, restarting it and avoiding an untimely end to a surprisingly long adventure. As long as the adventures themselves are, Legends as a whole feels very short. Shorter than it actually is, in fact. Story beats only really happen at the opening and climax of a particular adventure and, with only three of the current four adventures moving the Kingdom Rush plot forward, it seems like you've barely begun before it's all over. The games Ironhide puts out usually get a few additional areas and heroes during their lifetime, an expansion this game in particular needs. In addition to needing some more flesh on its bones,  Legends is a great vehicle for getting attached the increasingly large cast of goofy characters and settings the series is known for. These games are always pretty solid, but what carries them is their sense of humor and playfulness. That characterization is somewhat damaged, along with the replayability aimed for with this title, by having the same lines spouted by very different characters during the handful of climaxes you'll be experiencing over and over again. While I've always enjoyed being handed a bit more of a good game to play, I'm especially hoping this one gets some more attention as I have not seen nearly enough of the Legends of Kingdom Rush.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually really like Ironhide's games. They're chill and fun, you're always in for a good time. Unfortunately, this game was not balanced well, ruining a lot of the fun. The art-style is, as always, very cool and engaging, reminescent of the old tower defenses. The similarities stop there. The game is a semi rogue-like, where you build a company of heroes to venture into territories. Character progression does not transfer from one zone to another, so any sense of progression is lost beside the ongoing story. On top of that, it means retraining the same heroes each time you go into a new territory. It gets boring very quickly. Finally, the main thing that made me stop is the unbalanced fights. Fights were not thought out at all it would seem. It's mostly kill first before they kill you. Just like Slay The Spire, your hitpoints carry on outside of fights, but in STS, your character has 70 hp. here your heroes have 6 hp, which means they die in 2-3 hits. It also means that if they get hurt, they keep their near-death status for the next fight, even if it's the second fight in the map you're currently doing. Any heal is seldom found and you'll often manage an party on the brink of death from the first fight unto the bosses. It is not fun. Partway through zone 3, I found an Ice troll that could one shot my ranged units (they mostly die in 1-2 hits) from afar, without any counter play. The ice troll was just there, pressed a spell, and killed my archer and shaman in one spell. Once they die they are removed from the fight, so you found yourself fighting 5 huge trolls with 2 knights and no backup. It's frustrating, made by an uncomprehensible gameplay decision and absolutely not fun. If you're really into turn-based strategy games, I'd say give it a shot, but beware that the balance of this game is from hell itself. Also take into consideration that the game is 5-6 hours long, try to get it on sale. It is not worth more.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the casual, simple, and clean gameplay from Ironhide games. _childDocuments_.review: Legends of Kingdom Rush is a turn-based boardgame-esque strategy game, significantly different from the traditional Tower Defense that Ironhide is known for. However, at the current moment, I really can't recommend the game for a couple of reasons.The first reason is that the game has too little content. There's only 4 campaigns to choose from and they aren't particularly that interesting by themselves, as well as a randomized arena mode. Another big dealbreaker for me was the small pool of Heroes and Companions to choose from when building my party. It felt like I was encountering the same random companions to join my party every playthrough, and my options were very limited to choose beforehand. Not to mention that some companions are locked behind difficult achievements so you can't choose all of them from the very start. While I did enjoy the various characters, and admittedly they are somewhat unique and complex individually, there wasn't enough variety to warrant me playing through the campaigns again after I unlocked them. The game is in desperate need of more campaigns, enemies, and playable characters, which I would consider the main issue that this game faces.My next issue was the difficulty. Difficulty felt completely random and excruciatingly brutal in some areas. I would consider myself a decent player, and I had to retry the Stormcloud Temple campaign over 20 times to finally beat it. In comparison, I rolled through the next and "final" main story campaign literally second try. The random encounters in a campaign are also bizarre. Sometimes they are way too easy and just a waste of time- sometimes, you get an impossibly difficult encounter that you have no chance of beating. Since you can't retry encounters, having to restart an entire campaign, this completely random difficulty can be very frustrating. Not to mention the large amount of RNG in your character's skills, from damage to bonus effects, it is very probable that you will lose to straight up bad luck, which isn't fun at all.The last main issue I have with the game is the lack of QOL features. There isn't a way to look at all the various enemies outside of combat, like with the tower defense games, and read lore or compare stats. You rank up and unlock new character abilities incredibly slowly. There isn't a way to speed up combat animations once you've seen them a million times. The UI is frustrating and will close itself as the game moves on. You can't undo a character's movement to move them somewhere else during their turn. The biggest unfortunate detail is the lack of a proper tutorial, as there are a lot of mechanics to learn in this game, from different statuses, obtaining epic effects for skills, character turn priority, character archetype bonuses, and the list goes on. While these seem minor, I guarantee you will eventually run into something that could easily be changed to improve the QOL as you play through the game.While I understand that story isn't important to many people as much as gameplay is, it's really a tragedy when the coolest setpiece in the entire series ends up severely underutilized. Characters use generic, repeated dialogue at the beginning of encounters, there's almost no voice acting, too many lame references, and the voices of many characters sounds completely different from their parent game, even relatively new ones like the Dark Knight. In addition, the lack of storytelling throughout a campaign really does detract from the cool units we've seen throughout the series. There are so many interesting conversations and quips that could be made by allowing the player to mix the different heroes and villains we've seen throughout the series together. LOKR really misses out on a lot of cool moments by having no time for conversation outside the generic intros to various encounters. Most of the interesting characters we've seen throughout the series are just kind-of thrown in, too. Why exactly is Reg'son here? Shouldn't he be on the southern continent as the ruler of the twilight elves? The main characters, Denas and Vez'nan are literally entirely absent save for a comic cutscene at the end of the game. Why don't we see the diplomacy that comes with subjugating a human nation with non-human species? So much is missed out on in this game, and it really is a shame from a storytelling perspective.For these reasons I would not recommend LOKR. It can be a decent 10-20 hour experience, but I wouldn't buy this game at full price, even if you are a diehard fan of the Kingdom Rush series like I am. Wait and get it for 5-10, and even 10 is pushing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very nice turn-based strategy roguelike game. While there are only four adventures plus a tutorial, and an arena where you can play fights, the true content of the game is its replay value. With six legends and twelve companions, you can select a lot of different party options. And unlike a few reviews seem to claim, you can beat almost any encounter with almost any party, even if the party is pretty bad. There are definitely some balance issues, but part of this is also that some characters need to be upgraded very quickly, because they are above average at high levels and below average at low levels, making them approximately average overall. That said, an additional adventure would be a great idea.The controls are slightly clunky, and I definitely hope they will be improved in the future. There's a button that shows all hp bars (the ones with full hp are normally omitted), but there's no button that shows all grid tiles, even though you need to count tiles all the time. You cannot hover over enemies to see their stats, however, you can right click on them in the queue to see their stats. You can similarly right click on any ability, enemy or ally, to see what it does. However, the game does fail to communicate this to the player, but once you know about this, it is a godsend. There is definitely room for improvement there.As touched upon above, there are balance issues, and a few egregious ones really should be addressed. You need to kill all enemies coming in, so you basically need some sort of damage per turn to stay safe, as well as some tanking. Characters with fancy mechanics that neither tank nor deal good damage therefore just won't cut it most of the time, which is a bit sad.Overall, I would still say this is a very enjoyable game (8/10 or so), and while not yet at the level of polish that the first two Kingdom Rush games had (I'm not including Origins here, due to its balance issues), some continued support should get it there. I would highly recommend trying out the demo to see if you even like the concept of a turn-based strategy game, but know that the demo is absolutely not representative of the difficulty of the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.6/10I actually think this is a good attempt by Ironhide. _childDocuments_.review: Its a decent rogue-lite game.You pick a group of 3 units (out of ~20 available), pick a map you want to run (5 maps available) and go on an adventure. Each map consists of several nodes - fights, shops or events (dice roll). You pick up any route you want, and in the end of the map fight boss. Fights are happening on various grid-based arenas, turn-based (similar to king's bounty series, HoMM, etc,etc,etc)When you kill the boss (or lose all your units in a single fight) you are awarded some EXP for each of your units, which is used for some very basic meta-progression on a world map (unlocks couple of new skills for each unit).You can also do some arena battles - randomized PVE encounters with preset parties and monsters on different layouts.PROS:+ silly and adorable graphics+ rather challenging gameplay - you wont steamroll every combat encounter, have to use your head+ SOME replay valueCONS:- very short campaignIf you are somewhat familiar with the rogue-like genre,it probably wont take you longer than 7-8h (mb 10h, if you really want to take your time) to clear the whole game, unlocking every unit.After you finish the last boss,there is not really much to do, except for achievement grinding and arena battles, but it gets old pretty fast.TL;DRGood rogue-lite game for an evening or three. Definitely not a must-have, but a solid entertainment for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: First time leaving a negative review for an Ironhide game. The game is well made, but needs some balancing. The game is too hard and it relies too much on luck. I got to the 3'rd area and can't beat the last stage, even on Casual difficulty. Seeing other reviews, I came to the conclusion that I am not the only one with this problem. Besides this progression issue, the game has everything I love about Kingdom Rush. Until the next patch (that I hope will fix this problem) my review will stay negative, but I'll keep trying to progress throught the game.Edit :  After playing 10 hrs and finishing the game. Now I'll change my review to a positive one. The game is not hard, but it feels this way. The thing is, you are predestined to lose your first playthrough on any adventure (except the first one, that acts as a "tutorial"). The first area, the "tutorial" is so bad designed because it teaches you the basics (1% of the core gameplay) and nothing more. In the second area you meet the deep combat they are talking about and literally need to figure everything yourself. No further help from the game, it doesn't explain you any status (bleeding, poisoned, froze, can't move but attack, stunned etc), there is just an icon that you need to understand by playing and failing yourself. Even the bosses, there is no way you can beat the boss your first time. You need to fail 5 times before you understand how the ♥♥♥♥ you should be able to kill him (for example, 3rd area boss is targetable, but he can't receive any damage, so you need to understand how the crystals work to be able to use them in your advantage etc). I can't lie, it feels rewarding after you figure it out and beat them, but 5 predestined loses before this, it is enough for me to drop the game and never play it again.  My point is, the game is great and has a deep combat system that is pretty enjoyable, a lot of heroes to try together. Even if it is too short (5 areas), you will be able to play them again, taking new paths, There are daily challenges and arena mode too. I won't spoil anything, but Vez'nan will appear in this game at some point, and that's a big reason itself to play the game till the end. BUT, Ironhide should make a real tutorial, or at least, when you encounter something new the first time around, explain it to the player.

_childDocuments_.review: Good battle gameplay brought low by RNG between fights.Arena mode is the peak: single fights with many heroes / enemies where you can get straight into it with all skills unlocked.The game isn't that hard overall, but can be made much easier / harder by which random events you get, and which dice challenges you get -- even beyond "do I have the right characters", some events give bonus attack or armor or invigorate units, all of which are vast bonuses compared to the normal XP. And the game won't tell you what you get for various options up-front, so you have to try them to see.The game is missing many conveniences common in other games of this genre: you can't revert back to the start of your turn after moving if you're not where you expected, you can't see units' move / attack ranges on the hex grid, only in their character portraits, you can't see enemy cooldowns, you can't see the hex grid explicitly, having to figure it out from the graphics. It's a straight port from mobile, with mobile-style controls.Levelling up your heroes doesn't make them stronger, merely give you access to more skill choices on level-up. Going all the way to 5 is a slog, and some units have their best skills earlier.Achievements are generally well-designed, except for "Late to the Party" -- I can see how beating the map in 3 turns is a neat challenge you might want to aim for, but to do that you have to:* actually get the map, which is a 1/3 chance for a node in the middle of the map, and* have your randomly chosen fourth slot actually be useful (ideally ranged / magic), and* have Orc Cleaver start in one of the forward slots (1/2) because otherwise he can't move forward far enough to counter-attack soon enough, and* have the enemy leader take his turn fairly late, as otherwise he'll buff the enemies around him instead of advancing forward which means he won't be in range soon enough to kill him.If the stars align and you get invigorated on one of your units this gets easier, but it's a bit of an RNG-fest. Good thing you can restart the map by closing the game if you happen to get a bad layout / turn order.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything feels pretty well-balanced overall until the Wild Moon adventure. You don't get enough time to level up your heroes, and the map is extremely unforgiving. Sometimes, you can die in the first encounter just because the enemies casually outnumber you. Or you die repeatedly at the boss, because who thought it was a good idea to put a melee, ranged, and summoner boss on the same map while it's slowly being covered in minions?Want to kill the minions first? You die because the bosses drain your health too quickly, or they snipe one of your heroes to death because you either missed your attack or the trees block your path, preventing movement and a potential kill.Want to rush the bosses? Nope, too many minions on the board, and the bosses just get stronger. That's another game over. (And don't tell me the healing orbs are enough to save you—1 HP regain per turn is just straight-up petty.)I've tried over and over again on CASUAL difficulty, and it's breaking my mind. It's extremely unforgiving to have to redo the campaign over and over just to die at the boss because of ONE misplay or not being at a high enough level.I seriously love the combat and design overall, but there are so many little flaws that are really hurting my enjoyment beside the last chapter.Such as:Enemy's dodging your attacks 24/7 or just straight up missZero to no way to heal in combat (Yes I know there's a healing hero, But he's not doing enough to keep my team alive)Some hero's just die from a enemy sneezing on themEnemy's able to move to other side of the board in a single turn and casually doing 6+ magic damage Tanks just being awful at tankingAnd worst of all, The amount of rng when it comes to the map layout.Readed the entire thing or just scrolled down and now you want to post a salty comment?Go ahead, Waist your time writing on this review. Call it a "skill issue," "git good," or tell me "Uh, actually use the RNG meta/Reddit looking ass response". Save it for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR i recommend but maybe in a year or so if you want a better experience (i would say wait for a sale but even when ironhide does do sales; theyre rarely big discounts)based on the kingdom rush series; but its a grid turn based strategy game with roguelike elements (so dont expect a kingdom rush tower defence game)its cross run progression systems (you can level up units to unlock more skill options for them... but honestly these options -with a couple of specific exceptions- are often extremely niche/underpowered compared to their original offering so i end up taking the first one anyway) are almost non existent (less existent than core tower defence kingdom rush games) so i wouldnt really call it a 'roguelite'currently short on content (my playtime is not at all reflective of the amount; i have a tendency to just leave games -especially rogues- running in the background between doing other stuff); theres 4 maps (not counting tutorial) and you can bash them out really quickly (couple of hours tops)... that said; Ironhide has a longstanding track record of free content expansions so id expect this (and unit options) to grow)... some of the achievements for a completionist take some time (either because theyre specific scenarios you have to keep rerunning for or because theres an awful timegated one that you need to play 25 daily arena challenges for)party, you build a team of 3; one 'legend' (these are named characters returning from previous kingdom rush games and tend to be stronger) and 2 'companions' (you get a random 3rd companion part way through a map for a full party of 4)... each of them feels unique and whilst i didnt like some at first (reg'son, sasquatch, arcane wizard and barbarian); once i figured out how best to use them they felt good; theyve all got strengths and drawbacks to put together in interesting waysaesthetics/animations are charming; but this is going to be a subjective matter and i may be tainted by kingdom rush nostalgiaUI is poorly explained, right click icons to view tooltips/stats/movement/abilities but nothing ever tells you this is an option (also ive seen people struggling to figure out how to change their party members so evidently thats a poorly explained system too)difficulty is kind of a joke; atleast if you're familiar with these kind of games and read the information provided... though only 2 difficulties currently exist (ive seen some grumblings about easy mode not being easy enough but i just think theyre unfamiliar with the genre and trying to LEEEEROOOOY everything) with a conspicuous space for a 3rd; so i am expecting that to come in a later updatearena system exists if you want to just do random encounters; theres also daily arena challenges that you only get one attempt/day at

_childDocuments_.review: It's Kingdom Rush universe but as a tactics game! Reminds me a bit of Gloomhaven in how much you think through enemy actions, or like Slay The Spire in your ability to see exactly what enemies can do (by checking on the initiative tracker). It's a short experience if you 1-shot each adventure and don't redo any... but the enemies and character combinations you can run into give you lots of cool things to try out. I really hope the somewhat "mixed" response from Steam reviews doesn't deter Ironhide from making DLC or more in this series since it's a fun experience that I'm happy to support for its cool ideas and humour along the way! Indie studios like this, creating wholesome, fun content -- regardless of "$ per Hour" metrics -- deserve our support!

Starter ranger has great ranged anti-armor dps without being super squishy like the starter mage.

_childDocuments_.review: You adventure begins with you chained up in the bowels of the citadel’s dungeon within the Linirean capital which is under the control of the Dark Army. While the guards attend a briefing about them marching out at dawn to stop the invasion, a mysterious figure sneaks into the dungeon. You ask what’s going on but they tell you there’s no time to explain and you must escape now as they unlock your chains. They slink off as quickly as they arrived but they left you with a parting gift, your trusty sword and gear. You make your break for freedom against the single guard making his rounds. It’s from here that you will go over the basics of the game in a same tutorial.  After leaving the dungeon you find yourself on a path which leads through the citadel’s grounds and out into the unknown world beyond. The path leading out of the citadel only consists of one path, although new areas you enter will have multiple paths all leading to the same final destination (boss fight), which paths you chose to travel along is up to you.  At various points along the paths are event points, you can get a gist of what is at each event, banners indicate if it’s a combat, dice rolling event or may be a traveller such as a merchant. Sometimes while on the road to a new event point you will come across an encounter, these are similar to the event points however, you won’t know what is going to happen upon a random encounter until you enter the event. Entering in to a combat even will place you somewhere on the combat map which has a background display of your current location. The map is divided in to hexagon tiles and you’ll be able to move a number of tiles each turn. On the combat map there are some obstacles here and there, some of the obstacles can be used to your benefit, obstacles such as mushrooms, training dummies and TNT barrels. Attacking these obstacles will make them explode or spin around allowing you to damage multiple enemies at once, if they are in range of the effects the obstacles.  Enemies can be placed anywhere on the map, sometimes you find yourself at one side of the map with your enemy the other side, however, you can find yourself in the middle of the map and the enemy surrounding you on both sides of you. You and your enemy will take it in turns to move and perform actions against each other. Attacking will deal damage and lose health, although some characters are adorned with armour. Any damage dealt to an armoured character will lose damage to their armour first, then once the armours health is gone any further damage will result in losing health. Once your health is depleted you will be removed from the combat, defeating the rest of the enemies and completing the level will bring your characters back to life. However, you will now be suffering a crippling injury lowering your total health by one bar, this will be indicated on your health bar and be red instead of green. You can recover from the injury by finding or buying from a trader a bandage. Once all characters are defeated on the same event then it will be game over. After defeating all enemies in an event, you will gain some experience points, orb points and some other rewards, you can also gain rewards from other events. Collecting enough Orb Points will allow you to promote your characters allowing them to improve their stats and gain new abilities. All party members will start each new adventure from Level One so as to experience a fresh new experience from beginning to end. Upon total defeat and end of game you will gain experience points depending on how well you and your party did, number of enemy defeated etcetera. This will Rank Level up your characters which is a permanent level up, each time your rank level up your character will unlock new abilities. You will unlock new characters as you progress; these characters can be recruited to help you on your journey. On some events you may also have some characters which will aid you until the end of the combat event. In total there are eighteen characters to unlock including Gerald your first character from the dungeon. Each will have their own traits and skills and to begin with the first couple characters are the Ranger and Arcane Wizard who will join just after you break out of the dungeon.  I have tried to add different characters to my party however, the only character I can seem to select and change is Gerald. This I thought was weird only trading one character not being able to swap out the other characters especially as I was hitting a brick wall in my progression and wanted to try something new but also wanting to keep Gerald in my party. Maybe I'm missing something or I haven’t completed something yet in order for me to change multiple party members. Not all events you enter will have you fighting someone or at least not to begin with but there are events where you will have to roll dice to determine the outcome of a scenario. The dice is a plain six-sided die with either a Star or Cross on each of its side. Rolling a star is what you want when rolling a dice, rolling a cross is bad news and you’ll have some sort of forfeit if you do depending on the current scenario. While on the world map which shows you the paths you can travel as you make your way to the final event, you are able to use some items you collect from combat or other events. These items could help you as you travel the paths and some of the events, items such as the Pick Axe which can be used to help dig your way out of somewhere, Rope to tie stuff, Supplies will help you replenish health as you travel, a Tent can help your party to rest and replenish up to three health, there are also potions to replenish health, cure exhaustion and bandages to help with those crippling injuries. The game also has a quick play arena mode where you will get instant action playing with a random team. You can choose the games difficulty (Casual and Normal) and randomise your Party and Diversifiers. There is also a Daily Challenge where you will have a pre-made party and diversifiers to play as. Positives  + Great looking artwork + Enjoyable game + Story, arena modes and daily challenges + Has achievements Negatives  - Frustrating at times - Stuttering - No cards currently Prove yourself a Legend along with your party of heroes as you set off to try and save the Kingdom against the menace that threatens it in Legends of Kingdom Rush. 6/10
