_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this game because it's worth a try, but I'd rate it a 7/10. It's a turn-based game, but it takes on a more "rougelike" approach since your heroes don't carry over the skills they learn from previous maps. In addition, the map itself changes. The biggest positives is the art and the simple and yet robust combat. A few things I'm mixed on: - There's a slew of characters to play, your starting party has a named "legendary" hero and two generic heroes. You will always get a 4th party member as you travel the map. Now, each character has their own style, theme, etc. However, some are clearly stronger than others. My issue is that there too many underpowered heroes, I tried finishing each map with a different legendary hero but I always come crawling back to the first legendary hero for later maps. - The map. Think of the overworld map like the nodes in Slay the Spire or Curse of the Dead Gods. Each node is either a combat encounter, a "roll the die" encounter, or a merchant encounter. My issue is with the roll the die encounters because it relies to heavily on RNG. Yes, you can get bonuses to skew the dice your way but most of the time you're flipping a coin for these events and sometimes you're locked out of the one option because you didn't take certain heroes into your party. - The random combat encounters. I cannot tell you how many times I lost  the FIRST combat because the encounter was clearly suited for higher level characters. Remember, you're starting over when you enter each map, albeit high level characters do have more option on skills later on. It came to the point where the game was just outright unfair. Now, those are just mixed. I don't hate the game because of that, I just wish they approached it a little differently. However, despite all the lost battles and encounters I always found myself going back for more. I haven't played a game for 6 hours straight in a long time, but for some reason Legends of Kingdom Rush hooked me in.

_childDocuments_.review: I support these developers, but this game isn't fun. I enjoyed Iron Marine and the first 2 Kingdom Rushes in particular (GREAT games). However, the last two (Vengence, and now this) I think are a step in the wrong direction. I've never played a game before in this turn based RPG style, but I do love strategy games. Unfortunately, if this wasn't in the Kingdom Rush lore/world, I would hard pass on this. I do not enjoy the randomness to it, the way you die and have to start over, the way your progression doesn't save. It's OK for $15, but I won't have anywhere near the replaybility as the other ones, and to me it is SUBSTANTIALLY less fun. I feel the difficulty is also out of wack in that you'll steamroll everything and then run into random spikes where you'll die fast and lose everything. There's also too many times your weaker units will just get 1 shot. It's just a way less fun format to me overall.It's just not a very good game. Honestly, I don't think it's worth buying.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Ironhide's best game. Ever. And by a large margin.The game is short, yes. But it has lots of replayability to it. The amount of party combinations is insane, and while some might be OP, others will be challenging. Also, every time you play the game, the adventure is going to be different, because events and fights are random throughout the map.Also replaying the game unlocks new abilities for your heroes to try out, which gives even more possibilities for future playthroughs.If you're tired of replaying the adventure though, there is the arena which has special rules and can be really fun, too!I love how the strategy is handled here. My first playrhrough on the first map was really easy, but then I tried several different parties and found out that some combinations can be really fun but harder to use. I really love how the game is like a sandbox to try out different teams. It follows well (and improves) the concept that Vengeance had, even though LoKR isn't a Tower Defense.I'm excited to see a new Ironhide RPG game like this in the future, like Legends of Kingdom Rush Frontiers or whatever they come up with. This is an awesome game.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent King's Bounty-lite game, but there's not enough content. You only have 5 roguelite adventures and 2 difficulty modes. The harder difficulty isn't that challenging, so there's a lot to be desired for more hardcore strategists and veterans such as myself. Sure, the game has lots of playable characters, but this doesn't mean much when there's not a lot of content to use them in. It's a fun game for about 5 hours, but for this major reason, I can't give it a recommendation -- especially at the price point. Things get too stale after you finish all 5 adventures (which I already did), so most of the "content" in the game thereafter is just tedious achievement hunting.Additionally, the game has a few problems design-wise. For one thing, the UI is kind of clunky. Keyboard support is wonky, you can't scroll the map with your keyboard, and tooltips don't display. Thus, it's needlessly obtuse because you can't see units' abilities and traits during battle. The second major problem is the overreliance upon luck at certain points: magic missiles strike randomly, dodge/block skills only activate 25% of the time, and in-game "dice events" are luck-based. The game's core systems are fun enough, but it could've been better. Couple this with the pronounced lack of content, and you get a game which is pretty hard to recommend.Get it on sale if it's $3.50 like I did, but otherwise, there are better ways to spend your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out there, because a lot of players seem to be confused with the idea of the game. This is a game of trial and error. The idea here is  to get straight to the last level on your first try, while having only 4 level 1/2 characters unlocked. This is a game where you have to unlock and assemble the correct team for each stage. You do that by completing each hero's achievement and then leveling them up by bringing them to your squad. So figuring out what's the best team for each stage and assembling it is going to require some re-runs (which are different every time).I wouldn't call the game hard. Its difficulty increases in a linear and fairly easy to keep up way. It definitely becomes more challenging the more you progress and requires you to prepare well before each stage (see the previous paragraph), but I believe this is the beauty of it. Of course, this wouldn't seem appealing to some players and that is fine, but it's definitely very possible to beat the game with the proper squad. For those having rough experience at the start I'd recommend switching to casual difficulty and picking heroes which synergize well. The game is pretty well executed. I haven't had any issues with understanding and playing it. I've always loved the style KR games had so I'm enjoying the way they managed to keep the atmosphere of the previous KR games. That being said, I think it would be awesome if they cover all the lines characters say before battle. It just seems a bit unfinished that only some phrases were voiced over.

It goes without saying but look at the screenshots, videos and game tags: this is NOT a TD game; it's a turn-based RPG. Buy it if you enjoy these types of games; it has no TD elements!

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 36.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for several hours, completed it, and earned all the achievements. During this time, I found out some game combat problems: Every time you try to inflict an enemy with poison, bleed, etc. you never know whether the enemy has resistance. Sometimes the debuff is simply canceled, which can completely ruin your strategy. I would add resistance icons for every enemy in the game. These could be displayed in the statistics window that can be opened for each unit during combat.  Sometimes, when you have two units near an enemy at the same distance, you can't predict which unit the enemy will attack. This can quickly lead to a lost fight because, instead of targeting your tank unit, the enemy might target your mage or other fragile characters. I would create an target order where the enemy would attack clockwise from the first unit in its path. The priority would be the unit on the bottom if the enemy is looking forward and the unit on top if looking backward. This could be explained in the starting tutorial.  In every biome, there are special environmental structures like fireworks, TNTs, spikes, etc. and you don't know how much damage they deal or if they have any debuffs. This information is sometimes important when deciding whether to destroy a TNT or directly attack an enemy.I would change the statistics window so that it opens by right-clicking on an enemy or structure to show its stats directly, rather than in the attack queue at the top, so you could see even structure stats.These are the main features that could improve the game. I really like this game, but these issues often frustrate me. If the developers add these features or find better solutions, I will revisit and update this review. Until then, it's not a good idea to do all achievements, or you might end up writing a negative review like me.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I want to warn: Accessibility Issues. There are many sounds in game, such as the opening jingle and the spikes in the Arena, that *are not affected by the volume sliders in-game*. They are ludicrously loud and surprising. I recommend avoiding this game if you had auditory issues. It's an extreme lack of polish on the dev's part.Speaking of lack of effort- the game is just not very good. It's only a couple hours long with barely any content. The lack of story can be excused as Kingdom Rush just never having a *good* story, but in a game trying so hard to be story centered the writing is especially harsh. The tactical complexity is mid and prone to randomness. The game lacks a general index or any sort of information, so it can be easy to simply be jumpscared by something you didn't see coming. You didn't know that the Troll Chieftain had a ranged attack that covered the whole map even though it only says "range 4"? You didn't know that "weakened" is any status effect that deals damage over-time? This problem would be solved by making menu items larger and having an actual index for the player to familiarize themselves with rather than being jumpscared by something bad. The UI is prone to bugging out- don't check a unit's information while the enemy is acting, it will break the initiative UI and take a few seconds to fix itself which is just a frustrating little oversight.The challenges of the campaign are interesting. Boss fights are fun in concept- a lot of elements are in play and you have to carefully maneuver everything- but are again brought down by the game's ability to jumpscare you with new mechanics. If you do a phase-change in a boss fight, you have no ability to reposition units, so they may already be caught in a boss's powerful AOE with no chance to even react. It's not fun. That's the main takeaway from the game- it's just not that fun. It shows a lack of care that's normally shown to the studio's Tower Defense titles. This is just a cheap phone game.

_childDocuments_.review: Legends of kingdom rush is a game that i've been looking forward to playing ever since the first trailer dropped in 2021 but never got the chance to play it until now because it initially was an apple arcade exclusive but now in 2023 i finally played it for the first time and although i was skeptical to buy this at first, seeing the mixed reviews, but for me personally i find that this game is a lot of fun!Now if you are a fan of the kingdom rush series and you're expecting more tower defense gameplay then sadly this game is probably not for you (go play KRV's Revengance mod instead!). HOWEVER if you're a fan of games strategic roguelike games like FTL, Into The Breach, Alina of the arena, and etc. Then this game might just be for you!The gameplay is fun, the artstyle is (as always) cartoonishly pretty and amazing! it has quite the wide roster of heroes and companions to choose from, and the few campaigns that are in the game are good and has decent bossfights aswell. The resource management and in-game events are also fairly balanced.The difficulty of the game however is kinda weird, the early fights that you'll have will probably be the hardest fights in that campaign, however once you have a few charcters get that level 2, the game becomes somewhat easy and i rarely ever lose any bossfights because most of the time once your dps get that sweet level 3 the boss just go byebyeAnd although i said that there are quite a lot of party members to choose from, the selection feels underwhelming and this is part of the reason why i wrote this review in the first place. - For starters, no hero with artillery trait? and even then there's only 2 companions who's artillery based and one has little to no damage in the early game(bombardier), and the other is essentially a pseudo mage with many stuns (zapper), i mean like where's bolin when you need him???- Going into the agility based Characters, while yes asra and reg'son are unique and offers 2 quite differing play styles that is fun to use, the agility companions are just lackluster, sylvian elves have underwhelming damage, while the ranger while yes is good and i've clutched multiple battles with him being the sole survivor of the party with 1 hp, doesn't really have any "good" skills and feels lacking, as his level 2 abilities are just trashy and his level 3 upgrades aren't really worthwhile - The amount of slow, tanky melee companions in this game is a lot, perhaps too much, Im not saying that's awful in its own right, the variety of it is good and provide a lot of strategic diversity, and the tanks are some of the more balanced and fun party members to pick and it's just saddening that most of the fun party members are just, well, slow tanky melee heroes. It is, however, fun to play with 4 melee with bravebark leading the charge, however i wished we have more agility based melee companions (pls giv me my assassins) instead of just damage sponges (barbs are an exception cus they rly cool)- the mages are decently made though,the heroes (oloch and bruxa) are extremely good and fun to play!, but we really only have 1 companions with magic dps (arcane wiz) and the 2 other are just supports. with witch doctor providing useful healing, while sorceress are just hot garbo.But at the end of the day, the game is gud, while i have commplaints for the roster and quite frankly lacking amount of campaign, and some bad QoL for the UI and Achievement hunting. Overall, the gameplay feels good with and offers a wide range of variety in strategy and party management. As of writing this review i have completed all achivements for the campaign and now just playing daily for the arena achievements. but i think i'll still be returning to this game for time to time. So if you're looking for a strategic roguelite game like Into the breach, the last spell, and etc, im sure that you'll find this worth your time!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, being as I am a long-time fan of the Kingdom Rush series. Unfortunately, the recent dip in design quality in the series continues with this game - but unlike the main Kingdom Rush series, there's no strong core gameplay to carry it.Instead what we have is a dull, shallow little turn-based strategy game which would have been uninspired twenty years ago. Indeed, were it not for the solid visual design you could be forgiven for thinking this was an old school Flash game (and even if it was, you wouldn't be impressed). Core gameplay has next to no strategic depth, very little to interest the player, and attempts to use 'it's a roguelite!' as an excuse to explain away poorly designed mechanics. The characteristic touches of the Kingdom Rush franchise, such as cute little dialogue moments or referential voice lines, are all missing. This could all be reasonable were the game some kind of experiment, but it isn't - there's absolutely no innovation on display here, nothing noteworthy or untested. You could get virtually the same game a dozen times over on any phone game store (which is what this is, to be clear - the interface is terrible specifically so that it can be played on a phone). I realise that Ironhide has been going downhill for a while now, being far more concerned with pushing questionable mobile gaming cashgrab practices instead of making strong niche games - but the fact that this one got through quality control is a real danger sign. I sincerely hope they rethink their strategy and release something with some design talent behind it on their next outing.

I encountered no bugs, and the art and music are great - particularly the comic strip intros to each level.

_childDocuments_.review: A spin off to the Kingdom Rush tower defense games that still retains the charm, references and easy to pick up harder to master gameplay. Heroes have two ways of improving; leveling up within the adventure currently going (doesn't carry over). Second way is what I'd call a rank system where permanent options unlock from exp earned after an adventure that is finished (won or lost). I've found it fun overall, however I'd like a better way to see range and move distance of enemies. It's the only real issue I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so the thumbs up is deceiving. The game is pretty fun, BUT and a big but, it is not worth $15 AT ALL. I got it for cheaper than that which made it worth it. On steam this is just not worth that. It has the play time like a mobile game you'd pay $3 for. Just like their other games. Find it somewhere else for 1/3 of the price. I have 7.4 hours on play time and I beat the entire "campaign" in like 6 hours on the highest difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great. Unlocking skills is rewarding, and the negative reviews are from  people complaining about the difficulty. They must not be used to SRPGs.A lot of replay value as there are multiple toons to unlock and level up. The group leaders have a lot of skills to unlock. By the last biomes you need toons with synergies to fare well. Its a great game for the cost.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets boring very quickly. Leveling characters grants them new abilities to choose from, but you have to start from zero every round. I regret I´ve paid money for it, because it is totally different from all the other kingdom rush games. It is NOT TOWER DEFENSE, but round-based strategy. Even for fans of this genre, I wouldn't recommend to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what all the complaints are about.  The game is good!  The battles are short TBS, there is plenty of different party types.  The roguelike part is very minimal but nice to have.  Honestly I think people are just upset that TD dev just made something other than another TD game. The only complaints I have are the controls can be a little wonky and there could be a few more campaigns.But if you are a TBS fan and looking for something light and fun then this is a good game to grab on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Several combinations of heroes to play with. Highly addictive. Need to have more details such as first row is for only few heroes. Second and Third row are for secondary heroes in "Select a party" option. Also, Its bit confused to maintain the order. which is round 1 to round 5 etc. Overall, A very good game from IronHide
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: its a... fine game. there is a bit of strategy into it but for the most part just looks like a normal turn-based strategy RPG game with a lot of RNG into it.The game is more "Roguelite" than "Roguelike" because you dont really progress into the game, every game looks almost the same. i mean you get new heroes but to some extent, and also you can level up heroes, but leveling up only opens new ability paths that shouldnt be locked in the first place, they just locked it so later they can be unlocked, so levels dont really matter that much. you dont really get a sense of progression in the game. you dont get upgraded, the difficulty doesnt change and the game is very RNG based. like your runs there are sometimes that even if you took the best option possible you can still lose fights because of imbalancements and things similar. but... i cant really say its a bad game it is still fun but i dont think the price is fair. im sure they will update the game a lot but right now in its current state i would say its either an incomplete game or if its already complete, a bad game.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Played Kingdom Rush first time on ArmorGames and I was  instantly in love ... Tbh the prices here are insanely high. I have every game on my phone would never pay that amount here. Liked Legends of Kingdom Rush alot but Normal is like super hard if you compare it to easy in normal you have luck if you dont get killed sometimes on the first stage on easy you dont even need a good team ... yeah Im a wussy but the content is too little omg like 5 worlds or something and then the game is done.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Storywise, the game is a continuation of Kingdom Rush Vengeance. So you are going to know what happened to the great Lineria after you helped Veznan to acomplish his goals.Then, obviously, it is main appeal to the fans of Kingdom Rush. I was sceptical about this hex-based RPG idea but it turned out great. The thing I like the most about this game is how they transformed towers into heroes. Some of the most iconic towers like Tesla, Arcane Wizard, Ranger Hideout are playable as characters.Even if you are not familiar with the franchise, this game is a typical Ironhide title - amazing scenery, great story, charming music and plenty of entertaiment.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved the past Kingdom Rush games and I love this game too. I understand where some of the negative feedback is coming from, this game plays completely differently from the past games that were strictly tower defense and so past fans may dislike the change. However as someone who is very accustomed to turn-based adventure games having played Pathfinder and D&D this game is awesome! The attention to detail and art in this game really brings me back to the first Kingdom Rush as well as Fronteirs. Highly recommend for all Kingdom Rush fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve played Legends of Kingdom Rush on Apple Arcade. Kinda disappointed this version doesn’t offer something new or unique compared to the Arcade version. I always feel the graphics in 4K aren’t as good as on my iPad Pro, but this isn’t a big deal. Regardless of those, Legends is a solid game. It’s definitely a turn-based and not TD, and I think it’s a better twist compared to Vengeance vs previous KR games. Replayability is a love-or-hate situation because the nodes keep changing and in each node there’s an RNG factor too. I wish I can have a “checkpoint item” in journeys but there’s always a trick for that. Fan of KR & turn-based games? Buy it, unless you already played it on Arcade.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is a quick fun game, there's not too much stuff to do but it should give you around 20 hours of enjoyable gameplay. Due to randomness this game could be annoying sometimes but not too much, unless you have really bad luck, it is easy to learn most of the stuff about characters and enemies, if you can read that is..., and arena is nice addition if you are bored and got nothing to do. I'd say that the game itself is worth the money if you are into KR lore and RPG games.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Kingdom Rush fan for many years. I was really excited to check this game out even though it's not my typical genre. I tried the demo & bought the game as soon as it came out. It's fun, simple and includes many nods to the things we love from Kingdom Rush while being a different game. It's not a brain-melter which makes it fun to play on a lunch break or while doing another task. The game has some quirks & there is definitely room to add more (if they wish to), but if you enjoy the demo then I'd recommend buying!It's honestly pretty disappointing seeing all the negative reviews when those folks could've easily played the FREE demo before buying the game to see if they'd like it. Instead they buy the game w/o playing the demo & complain. Pretty unfortunate & not fair to the game or devs imo.Thank you to the Ironhide devs <3
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Game feels very polished and the art style is top notch. My only complaint is the difficulty spike? I mean what the hell. I understand the training mission is supposed to be easy to help learn, the next level I get my ass destroyed EVERY time. Are you just supposed to keep trying and dying until your heroes level up and actually stand a chance? So far I would recommend the game. I will update if the whole point is just to keep failing over and over until your heroes are leveled or the RNG map is on your side.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Utter disappointment.Next to no content, you have "leader" type heroes and "secondary" heroes, the latter of which can gain a total of TWO levels over all campaigns... Apart from the fact that this kind of distinction is completely arbitrary and doesn't mean that a hero is good in any way just because they are a leader type hero.  Most of the secondary heroes are way more useful 90% of the time.Add to that a general lack of mechanics, lack of content, a sh*tty mobile feel, horrible UI and tooltips and you have what this game really is. A soulless, overpriced cashgrab with nothing to do. This game would've been OK if it was ~5 bucks, but for what they are asking, the game is in a ridiculous state, both design and content wise.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a disappointing game. Even the fifth one was better than this one.It has the worst traits in Kindam Rush but bigger.Slow limited. Separately boring, poorly balanced.I bought most of the series right away and this one.This is the only one I am returning and I will wait for a big discount to get it.This is a pretty poorly made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: One of the worst turn based games i have played.-Difficult to keep track of bonus/epic attacks.-Difficult to find out a strategy that suits you. The map and enemies change and you get different characters as you go along.-User interface is uncomfortable.I dont like that you have to 'fail' your way through the game instead of finding out what works. I have only gotten so far by chance, not by skill or using the game mechanics properly.The Kingdom Rush universe is surely suited for a game of this type, but the way it is made has let fans and the game itself down.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzler from Ironhide again, if you've played any of the Kingdom rush series and know that you're going to replay, replay and replay some more then this is a great game to fill 30 minutes to a few hours. The game does require a level of patience as you unlock characters and understand the game mechanics. Some are saying that the characters don’t keep level - which is kind of true, each character will unlock abilities as they earn xp from each mission, however they will start at level 1 on each mission and gain in-mission xp to unlock said abilities - basically you pick your team so that you aim to unlock certain abilities to progress. As per usual for an Ironhide game it comes with all the cultural references and jokes you'd expect, plus there is plenty of replay if you're a compulsive and want all the achievements!
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: A qualified yes - it's fun, but the campaign is desperately short (5 hours?) There's only two difficulty settings, easy and normal, so after 12 hours of enjoyment I'm wondering what else there is in the game. I've already basically been through the campaign twice with different units, done a few daily challenges and now....nothing? This is in need of more content, otherwise it's an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great concept in my opinion but there are so many things that bother me while playing like the fact that you can have only four party members and not more, or that you cannot go to all the nodes on the map, or that you do not have a bigger capacity for your inventory, and can't carry more useful tools or potions or things to boost your stats. In conclusion  it is fun to play but it could have been much better if you ask me. And i really thought that Ironhide would have made a new great game like the tower defense games we all know and love.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much finished the game on the harder difficulty in 7 hours. Would honestly not recommend it. I feel like there should be a progression system like in the TD games where you unlock stronger stuff and the fights get harder. Unfortunately, in this game you could easily beat it with all lvl 1 characters since the only power gain is within campaigns rather than between campaigns.However the game looks good and it is pretty tactical which I like. It definetely has potential to be good after a few updates of extra campaigns and systems. I really hope the game gets some updates since its not far from being a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and charming game, especially for old Warcraft fans since the inspiration is obvious..However it's just way too punishing to the point where winning an encounter has less to do with whether you've played well or not, and more to do with whether you were lucky enough not to have enemies eat half of your tank's HP in one round and the rest in the next, leaving your off tank and squishes to fend for themselves. Enemies deal essentially as much damage as you can do to them, you're able to oneshot their squishes and they're able to oneshot your squishes, however they will overwhelmingly outnumber you in every encounter.The game suggests moving your glass cannons away from enemies, which on paper is fine, however that leaves your tank or tanks having to fend for themselves against upwards of three melee enemies rapidly chipping away at their guard, and any number of ranged units with guard penetration.Now, "The game is a roguelite" I hear you say "You're supposed to die and try again" and that's absolutely true, however usually games like this would offer some sort progression system outside of runs that makes you stronger for when you try again, and there *is* a *technically* a leveling system for each hero, however leveling up after a run only unlocks more ability options for when you level up during a run, and these are sidegrades, not upgrades.It's a very charming game that I was drawn to because of some obvious D&D inspiration too, it feels like you're going on an adventure with your little group of guys, but it's not something I can see myself playing any further.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: It's the charming art style and characters from Kingdom Rush in a combat game featuring some lite-rp and roguelike elements. Once I thought of it as a fantasy-themed FTL it became more fun. I've been enjoying zoning out to some podcasts and trying various combinations of party members, skill selections, and random events to break through the next map.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, and worth it for the price. Its a simple turn based tactics game with some variety stage to stage. Found you could win every mission on normal with the three starting characters. Feels like melee needs a small buff, and if there was a longer stage, or higher level cap I would give it a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still giving this a thumbs up because it's a really enjoyable game with classic Ironhide's polish and humor and a well-designed strategical nature. The huge thing missing is just one: content. I'd be fully satisfied with this game if it had AT LEAST twice the levels it currently does. 4 levels in total feels like a demo of the proper title. It's so saddening to see a potentially great game being dragged down just by mere lacking of content. Please Ironhide, you have to drop way more adventures than what we have right now. Additionally, you should definitely add pop-ups and an encyclopedia for both the enemies and the keywords. It's frustrating having to learn mechanics through gameplay alone without being able to read what they do beforehand.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: The thing i like from this game is that  (Auto Generating Mission in every Campaign) with this type of game, player will have to fight the same enemy which have the same value whatsoever and also a different path way with a different event in it, and the profit from is that you get an free orb level (or whatever it called) to increase level and upgrading the damage of your heroes.Even thought you choose the path for not fighting, every path for you there will be no way without war.For IronHide, we beg for you to make a more Tower Defends game. and not RPG GameYou're style on art and drawing is 100% beautiful, your game has inspired many Dev in everyworld to create the Tower defends game the same as you. but they cant copy the Best MasterPiece Tower Defends game maker, Yeah its you IronHide.You can just look by people making their thumbs up down, cause the game was too borring and so i do.Keep Up the good work Ironhide, Best Indie game Developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I still resent IronHide a bit for releasing this on Apple Arcade first, I gotta admit, it was worth the wait. Be aware that the game is technically short, but the roguelike elements allow for decent replayability and the sheer quality of gameplay, animation and artstyle makes it well worth its price.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing, funny and beautiful game. I just love it! This new formula is great, I hope they will do more games like this oneUnfortunately it has a BIG downside: it has almost NO content. Except the tutorial map you have 4 more mission maps that are 1-1.5 hours of playtime. The game is 5-8 hours long depending on your playstyle. After that, it's grinding the same all content for achievements or the arena, but it's getting pretty old pretty fast. There are no more adventures/missions or harder play modes to unlock (A hard mode would be welcomed). Basically there is no fun and engaging endgame content after a very short story mode that is amazingly good.If the game was 3-4 euro it would have been priced right as it is more like a larger demo than a full game. I can't recommend it at this price. Unless they add 3-4x times more content just buy it on a sale if you are not a hardcore fan.Other then the lack of content the game is amazingly good. Hope they will add more content in the game for this price. Even the overall map is more than half empty after you finish the 4 mission maps + tutorial. They could have added so much more to make it a full game with at least 20-30 hours of new content/adventure stories/missions playtime. Let's hope they will soon do. Right now you don't even get 1 hour of playtime (fresh content) per euro
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, there is a need for improvements. Some part of the Italian translation is VERY bad with lots of errors. The user interface is not so good, the keyboard is not used at all. Keywords are not clear. Graphic and the rest is very good as always. Strategy is "good" but sure there is large room of improvement. Some heroes seems like unplayable like Sorcerer and Shaman compared to others. Could be nice to add also a wait button to delay some character? It seems like you need a bit to "farm", and i do not like so much this aspect of the game. Some combats/events are quite random and can change a lot the sort of the run.Anyway, Let's hope it will get better in time...For now is more a no than a yes. And.... I LOVE Kingdom rush. I have all the series on IPAD and i have the complete boardgame experience. So i'm very disappointed that this game is just a 6 for me.Update: Some new heroes and characters are well designed and funny to play. The games still need to have some useful QOL improvements like numbers of life, Un-do action when misclick (since you cant exit the combat) some other more deep strategical stuff. But i will raise the game to a 7. It's pretty funny in the overall game. I wait for some imrpovements to increase the number and put a thump up.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: Its fun. I'm an old gamer, and much of my gaming when I was younger was turn based, strategy games. This definitely takes me back to a time when games were fun, but also punishing if you didn't have your strategy right. I'm enjoying it but I do see why some Kingdom Rush fans don't like it. I do recommend if you like turn based combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: This game plays more like a tabletop rpg than I expected, and I love it. The art style is great and it has a great sense of humour as every other Kingdom Rush game. Although this is not a tower defence game, I do get the sense that they have worked very hard on this game. It can be tough at times and I enjoy the challenges that can come up with random encounters. This game does have the same sense of repeating as any other game in the same genre, it is as 'repetitive' as the tower defence genre. The roguelite nature of it means that every single time you play it is different. Sometimes repeating actions and strategies is enjoyable, and learning how to overcome obstacles by doing this can be very rewarding.The only negative thing I have to mention is that sometimes I find the camera in the fighting scenes to be a little annoying, if you move it to the left or right, it stays there and you can't move it while the enemies are moving around so you can't see what they are doing etc. That is my only criticism so far. Give it a go if you enjoy casual games.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review: It's good for a casual strategy rp roguelike thing. Emphasis on casual. Also, If you're a fan of the style it might be for you. It's pretty same-y so far in my playtime. I agree with most of the negative reviews saying it is shallow only in lieu of having a 'neutral' option. The game lacks depth, Caveat Emptor.
_childDocuments_.name: Legends of Kingdom Rush

_childDocuments_.review:
An extraplanar menace of unprecedented proportions is attacking the realm! Lead a party of heroes to stop this foe in a highly engaging combat system that is easy to learn but hard to master.

5 Legendary Heroes, like the mighty paladin Gerald Lightseeker or the cunning shadow assassin Asra Daggerfall, will be awaiting your command.

11 Companion Heroes, with different skills and powers, like the resourceful forest ranger, the volatile dwarven bombardier, or the menacing dark knight will follow your Legends to victory!

Embark on an epic journey through the medieval fantasy world of Kingdom Rush in this amazing RPG game with roguelike elements!

name: Greyhill Incident
detailed_description: This story-driven Survival-Horror game is about a classic Alien-Invasion which takes place during the early 90s. As Ryan Baker, equipped with a baseball bat and a few bullets in his revolver, the story takes you across the atmospheric neighborhood of Greyhill which is invaded by UFOs & Grey Aliens. EXPERIENCE A CLASSIC ALIEN INVASION STORY It's the early 90s in the US, the media talks about weather balloons and conspiracy theories. But residents of the small neighborhood soon realise! THE GOVERNMENT IS LYING. The recent increase paranormal activities over the last few days have convinced the scared and now paranoid residents of Greyhill, that the Government are somehow involved. They trust no one. The small neighborhood of Greyhill are afraid to speak up and fearing being sent to the psychiatric ward, they avoid calling the police. Alone, they prepare by boarding up their windows and founding a neighborhood watch. GET ACROSS THE NEIGHBORHOOD AS AN AVERAGE GUY As Ryan Baker,'an average guy' equipped with a baseball bat and a few bullets in his revolver, your path is to get across the atmospheric neighborhood of Greyhill to save a neighbor who is in serious trouble. Find useful items, solve puzzles and you meet other neighbors as you fight to survive the invasion and guide Ryan through the Neighborhood. INVESTIGATE AND UNCOVER THE TRUTH Sneak through the open areas of the atmospheric US Neighborhood which has been invaded by Aliens & UFOs. Investigate houses & barns and search for ammo while you work up your way through the village and uncover the Alien Conspiracy. AND BE AWARE OF THE SMALL GREEN MEN A constant threat which invaded the village with their flying saucers.'They' are trying to abduct everyone in the village, taking samples of everything, making experiments and probing people. Sneak, Run or fight to get through Greyhill and beware of 'The Greys'. Feel free to add Greyhill Incident to your Wishlist.

_childDocuments_.review: The Horrible:Run for 5 seconds, catch your breath for 90 seconds.Turn volume up because you can't hear the voices, jump scare blasts your speakers into tiny pieces.Game is a chore simulator and they all take 20 minutes because you move so slowly.The game is 25 dollars toooooooooooo expensive.Very Shorrrrrrt (Only takes long cause of run speed)The Bad:Wildly incorrect subtitles.The Good:Maybe they will patch the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the worst game I have ever played. There is no sense of direction, you are going to be lost 90% of the game. I tolerated this because it felt like it was leading up to something. But then you reach the point where there are tens of tiny aliens waddling around grabbing you making it miserable, repetitive and boring. The entire mystery disappears and it just turns into a shooter where you shoot aliens to kill them. But there is barely any bullets so the game expects you to be stealthy. But because there is literally nothing to look forward to you have to be jesus christ himself to have enough patience to be stealthy in this game.It almost sounds like a "so bad it's good" kind of situation but I can assure you it's not. I LOVE "bad" and funny horror games, even yanky games are lots of fun to just laugh at. But that's not this game, this game feels like grinding your teeth. I received it for free. I can't imagine paying 25$ for it. There is no way they can fix this with updates. The whole game is just messed up.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: The game is kind of all over the place. The aesthetics are probably the best part of the game. The atmosphere, lighting, de-saturated dark windy forest vibes works pretty well for Alien Abduction. Honestly though, after the initial kind of buildup it starts to get a little wacky fast. It's insanely apparent that the voice acting was all done separately and without any idea of cadence or enthusiasm they should be doing their lines with. Sometimes a character will just YELL a line when someone asks them something in a regular tone. The alien hunting mechanics are OK, but lack the OOMPH or spookiness after the first area.This all being said, the design decisions around the stamina is weird too. It takes FOREVER for your stamina to come back. You can tell they made the decision almost actively to pad the game out, forcing you to walk all over the place and sit around to recover stamina. You will be running around a lot too because you'll probably have NO idea where to go. Paths open and close behind you or in front of you depending on your current objective, and I honestly got lost many times not knowing where to go in this extremely short game. I played it all the way to the end. The ENDING is atrocious. It feels like it completely blue-balls you after setting up certain things, and then just literally ends as if the devs ran out of time or something. Tough to get a good Alien game, and this is still not it. Not recommended at all, especially at the price. This should be like 10 dollars max.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: Dont buy this unless you can get it on sale for 5 dollars or less. its more of a demo than a game, its a 30 minute game, and it would be a 15 minute game if your character didnt walk like he had 2 broken legs. i hope the dev continues to make games, because it shows a lot of potential, but i would not recommend buying this game for more than 5 bucks. its a shorter game than the fears to fathoms games but with a criminal price for what you get. that all being said the atmosphere and the potential is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: Three aliens sucked me off in a cornfield at the same time. They spun me around like the dirty tinfoil dreidel I am and absolutely went to town. No amount of mashing "e" would stop the alien fraternity's initiation ritual from commencing. It was the perfect payoff to having this game in my wish list for over a year. God bless the Alien Fraternity.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: I requested a refund for this game. While the concept is interesting the game feels unfinished. Game crashed once (which not the biggest deal). The real issue lies in the lack of objective tracking and vague directions on where to go. Then at least to me the smash E to escape from Aliens was just not really letting escape. Even with me practically smashing my keyboard down. I cannot recommend this game at all with its current state and its disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Greyhill Incident

_childDocuments_.review: Yet I was hyped and eagerly awaiting it.Now I'm all the more disillusioned. On the positive side, the layout is quite impressive, especially considering that the game was developed by a single person. Graphically, it's not bad at all, with the main environment lit up by a greenish moon to great effect.The tension is well conveyed, with indirect witnesses reporting disturbing events via walkie-talkie. It's a highly effective way of stirring the imagination: there's a strong sense of imminent threat, with strong inspiration from M Night Shyamalan's Signs.What's more, the iconography inspired by UFO testimonies from the 50s to the 80s is very well rendered.That's all well and good, but once you've actually played the game, it's a disaster. The sound design is poorly calibrated, with voices that are sometimes barely audible, and the overall game design is no slouch either, with vaguely defined objectives that regularly lead you in circles where you shouldn't be.There's no pleasure to be had in exploring such a dark game, where interactive objects are indistinguishable from the rest and environmental interactions are ultra-limited.Our avatar suffocates as soon as he runs for 14 seconds, with an indecent recovery time. The torch is an abomination (just like in Amnesia The Bunker, except that here it shines even less brightly and for even shorter periods). Fight doesn't work (8 bullets for the whole game and 2 bullets per alien), stealth doesn't work any better and escape and hiding are useless with an almost asthmatic character.In fact, it's terrible, but the conclusion is clear: Greyhill Incident doesn't feel like a game once you've got the controller (or keyboard) in your hands. It's neither fun nor particularly scary, but rather frustrating and boring.Another cold shower for indie games, as far as I'm concerned. And I can only regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has fantastic atmosphere, graphics, sound and lighting. The premise is interesting. The opening reminded me of the movie Signs, and I got a bit excited. But it all falls apart when people start talking. The voice acting is all over the place, severely lacking voice direction. All the characters are just line reading in seemingly random or improvised moods and tones, often completely unrelated to what is happening on screen. When this is the case, due to budget or whatever, don't make 60% of your game listening to dialogue. Also the writing is just strange, the game sets up for a mysterious, cosmic horror thriller. But nearly ALL dialogue is quirky and silly about how the aliens are an*l probing, how they probe you, how it hurts, they show probes all over. It gets old quick and the comedy doesn't do anything for me. It might have been a funny comedic relief if 1 or 2 lines of dialogue somewhere was about probing. But  every person you talk to has something to say about an*l probing, except the 2 child characters. Basically a strange clash between how the game presents itself and the characters, dialogue and writing. The gameplay is alright, but extremely simple. The aliens rush toward you and lock you in a grab once they get close. Forcing a button mash. That mechanic is just frustrating and boring.  The game could have been a hit if they focused it more around avoiding aliens, exploring and finding your son through your own means. The railroaded story and dialogue is so cheesy it ruins the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the trailer for this game, I was genuinely interested to see what this game could turn out to be. This game LOOKED promising with its premise and seemed to be executing it well graphically. There really hasn't been a good horror entry that involves the traditional aliens that are portrayed in media by conspiracy theorists. I was very wrong. This game disappoints in all fronts. Its premise is very promising, and the first five or so minutes of the game are actually gripping with suspense, but after you start the gameplay portions the curtain falls away from the game and reveals how unfinished and unpolished it really is. There are several portions where you are asked to walk around and "find" someone or something, but not given any indication on where to. Exploration is punishing to the player as you have a stamina bar that stops you from going more than 10 feet without your player getting tired. You are given a bat & a gun in the beginning of the game, which ruins any suspense you may feel as you can literally knock over the aliens after 3 hits with the aforementioned bat, and KILL the aliens with 2 shots. The aliens do not feel like a horror aspect of the game, but rather an inconvenience to you as you complete whatever monotonous task the game gives you. As well as that, on the off chance that you cannot hit the alien with either weapon you are given - you can escape from the aliens by mashing "E" if they ever grab you, and you can do this over 3 times without dying. The dialogue is not believable, nor is it acted well. During the game, you are expected to care for characters you are saving including your son and other townspeople without having any real connection established to them. They are more objectives than anything of substance. Once they have given their bit of dialogue or given you an item, you do not see 95% of characters again. The level design features multiple areas where you are required to get a key or WAIT for the dialogue to finish to progress - this leads the player to walk past areas that they will need to proceed to, disregarding that passageways use to your overall progression. This leads to numerous amounts of backtracking, which is increasingly frustrating given that you a limited amount of stamina. There were multiple instances in my playthrough where dialogue overlapped to a frustrating degree. Two characters would be having a conversation and then more dialogue would overlap their conversation from the same two characters. At times the game felt like a satire of what it was originally attempting to portray, but only with one foot into committing into that idea, leaving it feeling muddled and half baked overall. Some of the tasks you have such as "fixing the telecom box" were literally to stall time for the player and boost overall playtime - this was not hidden at all. The "fix" for this portion was to open a random shed and find a conveniently placed circuit breaker. This, as well as having doors be locked for the sake of finding a key without a real reason for the player or protagonist to open said door left me feeling as though as I were constantly being stalled to the next portion of the game. This is normally something I could overlook - however the game did not ever satisfy with a conclusion or resolution to anything at all. Several plotlines and narrative choices yanked the story in different directions without ever actually answering the questions the player has, instead leaving them with more. I genuinely wanted to like this game, but I was left severely disappointed. I hope that the developers take some of the critiques of this game into account and improve upon them, because the premise to this game could genuinely make one of the best horror games of all time. Sad to see it go to waste.

Or "they must be outta towners stopping for gas" when it wants you to go to the gas station.  Sure, the word gas is in that sentence but I didn't see a gas station at that point, so to me they could have drove through to anywhere.  And am I suppose to go find them?Game ends with a "guess we'll never know what happens, hope you guys had fun" when the the only fun idea the game had doesn't even happen.Here's the gameplay loop for anybody out there listening,It's go from point to point as the most out of shape main character you've ever played, get lost for a long time, maybe find enough ammo to shoot an alien (two headshots per), try to stealth and try to set off the next trigger.There's walking simulators out there that do this kinda thing, typically their story is engaging enough to hold it up. _childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game was great and I was super excited for this game to release as it was on my wishlist seemingly forever, but after playing it, I am super disappointed. The game lacks clear direction for the player, leading to an overly frustrating experience. Poor stamina and combat mechanics further increase the frustration.Pros: - Great concept of an alien invasion game. This had a lot of potential.- Nice ambiance. Overall creepy feel to the game. Seeing the alien ships come/go was pretty cool.Cons: - The script and voice acting aren't great. Lines don't really make sense, break the immersion, or just overall sound ridiculous. If you ever played old school Resident Evil games think "Jill sandwich" and that's what you get here. Unsure if this is intentional or not. Voice lines also don't necessarily always match up with what you need to be doing. You'll be told to prep your bat and board up your doors, but what you REALLY need to do is go across the street to where the cows are in order to progress the story, which is super unclear and confusing.- There is a severe lack of cues and clear instructions for where you need to go or what you need to do. You'll find yourself lost a lot. While some lights indicate POIs, they're all over the place so you're not always sure which spot you need to be at and when. The game could use some additional timed voice cues to better direct the player to the right area. If you insist on trying to play/beat this game, make sure you have a walkthrough on hand to refer to in order to stay on track.- Walking speed is incredibly slow, and recovery time due to lack of stamina from running is overly long and feels bad.- The aliens themselves are disappointing. From how they look to how they react (barely moving or only temporarily falling over when being hit or shot, then running up and holding the player). It really makes them not scary, and breaks the immersion.- Melee combat needs a lot of work. Swinging the bat feels sluggish and weak, especially considering this guy is supposed to be a "pro" with the bat. Bat swings also have an incredibly long cool down period. Since the game wants you to focus on melee combat more than guns (due to alerting aliens and lack of bullets) melee feeling so terrible just adds to the frustration as it's forced upon you to use.I hope that there will be future updates to address some of the things mentioned above, as the game has a lot of potential. It just feels unfinished and unpolished currently, so I can not recommend it at this time.

_childDocuments_.review: The majority of reviews on Steam seem to be negative, and yeah the game kind of deserves it.  It is not very good.  Graphically it does look nice, albeit an oddly sort of dark that makes everything feel somewhat artificial.  The aliens themselves look decent enough, no real complaints there.  Character models are ok, though their animations often do not match what they're saying and seem to spend most of their time looking elsewhere.The story is... Minimal at best, with far too much focus on anal probes as this one very long joke that falls flat.  The story has plenty of set up and reason to care, but it completely fails to deliver.  The short version is your son ends up being abducted and you want to save him.  But, it feels like an afterthought and just a bunch of stuff tossed around in an attempt to give people something to say.Voice acting and sound/music are all overall decent.Gameplay is... Middling.  You have the stamina of one of the people from Wall-E.  You simply struggle to run more than 10 feet, which is a common complaint and well warranted.  Aliens take 2-3 shots to kill with the gun you find, but there are very limited amounts of ammunition.  The AI is... basically completely absent.  They'll find you, walk to you, and you can mash E to escape.. It ultimately means the Aliens are completely devoid of any real threat.  You also have a baseball bat which allows you to down them temporarily but they won't die from it.Travel around the town is sometimes an exercise in confusion as you're not sure where you're going until you hit an invisible wall that encourages you to look elsewhere.  The town itself is mostly devoid of life, with barriers like 2 inch steps or fallen trees.Ultimately the game could probably be finished in 2 hours or slightly less, but I got stuck/lost.  I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Slow walk/run. No jumping. Pressing “F” constantly to keep flashlight charged.  Low stamina. No consistency with accessible areas during triggered events. Aliens spawn behind you. Run/hide game. Pay attention to dialogue, no log or waypoints, you must follow the random lanterns or light sources to figure out where to go.Added this to my wishlist in 2022, and had “mostly negative” reviews only days after its 9 June 2023 launch. Still wanted to try it and streamed it for my friend to see.The concept and atmosphere is pretty cool, but the game/gameplay/controls are horrible. Controller map in options didn’t match what it said, cant change it. While a lot of folks complain that there are no waypoints or indication of what you need to do, that’s true; however, this game uses lanterns or other light sources to give you a clue on where to go.I hate the flash light. I spent the majority of the game pressing “F” to charge up the flashlight, which quickly dims. What an annoying requirement. Also, stamina is a joke. I ran from my front door to across the street and was already out of breath. It recharges faster if you just stop moving, otherwise it takes a while. He walks and runs slow. Another downside was this game’s love for triggers. I opened one fence (had to click only on top of fence to open. Took me a while to figure that out.)  I found another area I couldn’t get to, so wondered around. I triggered an event, which made the original entry point secured with no option to open. But the area I looked at before had a portion of the gate that disappeared. I did that scene and then that new opened area was closed again. the game forces you in certain areas with no consistency on how it works. Once the aliens showed up, they spawned behind me once I hit the trigger area. Example: I looked behind me, nothing. Then walked 2 steps and an alien grabbed me from behind. Cool. Tried hitting it with the bat twice, but it just kept grabbing me. For me, this is a run and hide game. An offensive approach didn’t really prove effective. It’s a slow game, and if you’re not paying attention to the story, you will wonder around until you figure it out or find the right light areas to follow. Not worth the price tag in its current state. Feels like the developer made the game for themselves without thinking about how players would go through it (not knowing exactly what to do next).

(maybe?)Cons:- The price is utterly insulting and along with how deliberately your progress is restricted, it (funnily enough) will have you exceed the 2 hour mark thus making refunding this "game" impossible (I have seen some people refund their purchases with 3 hours of gameplay however I am on my 3rd attempt at getting my money back with no success)- Character restrictions deliberately used to lengthen game-play (even after the update 1.0.2 your stamina is just not realistic and just all round bad)- Poor quest guidance (even after the update 1.0.2 - Areas seemingly irrelevant previously suddenly require back tracking to after witnessing, for instance, a barn door being closed now suddenly being wide open.)- illogical environment restrictions (knee high fencing/gates that don't work but are clearly gates)- Environments being Invisibly or visually locked to fit poor quest narrative and then becoming miraculously open/closed to further push the poor story/quest lines along.- Nonsensical decisions being made/restricted despite the situation (poor writing/design, not picking up the officers fully working flashlight despite your own being a wind up flashlight???) - INCREDIBLY DULL fetch and carry quests (nothing exciting at all considering ET's have landed)- Lack of weapons/ammunition in a rural setting of Texas (makes zero sense considering the whole town is aware of these visits)- Non existence of self navigation/map (even after the update 1.0.2) The fact that every square ft in Greyhill looks the same as the last it becomes immensely difficult to follow quest tasks such as "go to field" at this point you've been through a number of fields with NO DISTINGUISHING FEATURES to set them apart, and seeing as you have needed to back track in the past, its never EVER obvious and you could end up wandering around for 40+ minutes with no obvious indicator (even after the update 1.0.2 *i will keep stressing this devs) - Non threatening protagonists. The Aliens have been modelled off of The McPherson Tape (1989 found footage movie) entities, you can tell this from the red lasers they use and that well, they're identical in every-way . Why on earth was it not considered to allow the entities to use these devices to shoot at/burn the player? resulting in much more exciting combat and the need to actually make the game feel Intense and immersive like its in a rural setting. THIS WILL CREATE EXCITEMENT (slams head on table) more reasons for stealth, more ability to question your tactics/approach to a quest. How lazy can these devs be?Summary: With such relevance in the public sphere with regards to Aliens it was hard to think that such an idea could be executed so incredibly poorly in every aspect of the word. The setting, mood & tone makes sense, but everything else that should help to immerse you in those 3 things just doesn't exist at all. _childDocuments_.review: **UPDATE**: The one thing I can say to the developer's credit is that they are moving FAST trying to fix what they can. I think that says A LOT about them and their dedication to making a better experience for their gamers. You love to see it.Deeply unfortunate experience.The best part was honestly the menu. They nailed the James Newton Howard 'Signs' theme, it looks gorgeous and creates the right mood and then the game starts and it's all downhill from there.Played with a gamepad and honestly don't understand what happened. The menu shows a fully mapped gamepad but none of the functions with the exception of like, three, actually correspond to the image shown. You literally have to split actions between the controller, the keyboard, AND the mouse. No option to remap anything. You can't even navigate through the menus with the controller. And what I find most bizarre about this is that the game is about to drop on consoles so it's not like this was never intended to have controller support. The writing, both from a narrative and a grammatical standpoint was...abysmal. Everyone is on 11 from the moment the game starts and there's no real reason for it. You're just plunged into a world where all of your neighbors are already conspiracy theory fanatics. There's no real escalation. The kid is just hanging out watching TV snow talking about imaginary girls while you hang out with your two 10-second crank flashlights that look like those little hand-held piss buckets you get at the hospital. The kitchen is in a bedroom. The bathroom is in the foyer. You're across from the trailer, now you're behind the trailer. The cows have no skin but then the greys kneel down to investigate as though they have no idea why the cows don't have skin. WHO SKINNED THESE COWS????? My dude can run for 4 blocks sometimes and then become breathless after 30 feet. Is that tiny tiny TINY little circle around the reticle his stamina meter? "Put the cat on the table..." WHERE??? On top of the book? Or the meth lab? Oh, the BENCH is the "table"????? This was all in the first 30-ish minutes of the game. And it only took THAT long because I was trying to figure out how to do, well, ANYTHING. I've really been looking forward to this one as a fan of aliens, UFOs, abduction/invasion stories, and things set in the early '90s. They really had the mood and aesthetic but everything else fell apart. Big disappoint.2*/10*

_childDocuments_.review: Upon seeing the trailer, I didn't know whether to laugh or be disturbed. It does a great job highlighting the idea of the game, but once you play, that all disappears quick. The game starts out with a painfully slow intro to the action. My early days of game development taught me to use lights and colors to lead players through your level, this game follows that pretty painfully well. If you can't figure out where to go next (which you won't) follow the lanterns or blinking lights. Combat is insanely frustrating, it takes about 2-5 seconds (or more) from mouse click to actually seeing a baseball bat swing animation so trying to time your attacks is out the window and impossible. I couldn't even get past the first alien. I understand stealth is part of the game (Alien Isolation hiding in a cabinet) however the option to fight is still present and proved to be useless. Struggling against getting grabbed is a gamble so good luck if you make it further into the game against more than one of those greys.Graphics and cinematics do a great job setting the mood and it had everything going for it except the mechanics make the game impossible to play without infinite frustration. I loved everything about how the stage was set and even organized a premier streaming night with friends just to embarass myself in front of them trying to figure out how to get to fighting my first alien. And even that ended in several abduction game over screens.The game has old school horror game puzzle mechanics that seem out of place in this game because of the way that it's made out to be. Going into this thinking it's going to be an action-packed thriller is a mistake because the pacing of the game is thrown off when you need to examine objects where most of them have nothing to do with progression and about 99.8% to do with steam achievements. It would have succeeded more if it was focused on the act of surviving against the alien invasion rather than a Blair Witch (2019) x Signs scenario. I want to see this game tightened up because this was a great premise and concept, if only they could update the combat would it be playable even with the hilariously lame dialogue. I had to request a refund because I spent $25 on a game that did a good job of playing off a well-done trailer when in virtual reality it felt like everyone on the team held up their part except the programmer and script writer.Really good sources of inspiration, great setting and environment design. Excellent animations and effects, however poor character movement and script.This game almost had a spot in the top games of the year for me but fell short with how insanely awkward the character moves. I love stealth games but this premise was too good to ignore the opportunity to smack around some aliens with a bat.

_childDocuments_.review: Greyhill Incident has the potential to be a great game, but unfortunately it falls flat for a few reasons. Typos and grammatical errors, inconsistent dialogue and subtitles, and unintuitive controls are issues that should've been ironed out before being released. The objectives and story-line itself leaves you with a lot of questions. With the largest one being, "What's the point?" After overcoming an obstacle you're immediately given another odd task with little rhyme or reason, and they all loosely connect to one another before ending in an unexplainable ending. All coming together to formulate a mediocre alien abduction story featuring quirky, stereotypical characters with little depth. A few of the game's redeeming qualities are it's graphics and suspense. The lighting does a great job masking the aliens which makes you really have to slow down and look. The game's audio ques do a great job adding to the suspense of encountering an alien. While there aren't any intentional jump scares, I often found myself turning a corner or looking over my shoulder only to find a grey stalking me. Even though the enemies themselves aren't necessarily the hardest, the game's ambience helps you constantly be afraid of them and your environment. I'm only recommending this game based on the fact that I bought it for roughly $10, and I'd suggest anyone else interested in trying out Greyhill Incident not pay anymore than that. If I could give this game a middle of the road recommendation, I would. This game, or a redone version, has a lot of potential to be a unique addition to the horror game scene.

This game isn't the easiest and poses a challenge when the grey's lock on to you. I did have some moments of frustration when I couldn't get past certain points. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, I've read the reviews, and I think some people are being overly dramatic. While the game certainly has its flaws, which I'll mention shortly, it's not terrible overall. With a few tweaks, it could actually be a better game.Personally, I found hiding from the aliens to be quite thrilling, and it requires some skill to evade them successfully. I appreciate the challenge of escaping from them, as simply pressing a button to be freed would make the game boring. The spooky yet goofy blend in the storytelling is something I enjoy. However, the delivery of the story through the characters could use some improvement.Unfortunately, there are some negative aspects to this game. The voices of the characters are often too low, and I had to manually increase the volume in a video editor while rewatching my Twitch VOD. Sometimes, the main character's voice doesn't match the situation, which is more annoying than anything else. It feels unnatural and unnecessary when my character starts yelling at someone who is calm. There are occasional glitches in AI movement, but nothing severe enough to break the game. I've also encountered instances where characters talk over each other.Personally, I don't mind the difficulty of escaping from the aliens. In fact, I enjoy it. It adds a sense of accomplishment when you succeed, and it also creates a consequence for being caught. After all, it's a survival horror game, and simply shooting your way through enemies to beat the game wouldn't be appropriate. It's important to preserve resources for moments when there's no chance of escape. The lack of quest markers also encourages exploration, although I would appreciate a hint or some sense of direction to help with finding certain things.Overall, I'm enjoying this game. It definitely needs some work, but I can't understand why someone wouldn't find enjoyment in it. I like sneaking around corners and feeling my heart race when an alien spots me. The story is mostly enjoyable as well. The developers should definitely update the game, but that shouldn't discourage anyone from appreciating what it already offers: an Alien Survivor Horror experience.I'm well aware this goes against the grain of other reviews. I'm not playing Devil's Advocate. I just wanted to give a different perspective on a game that someone worked really hard to give us. Is it perfect? Negative, but it is enjoyable. Take the good with the bad. Don't come into this game reading all the negative comments, and solely focus on that. FOCUS ON THE CHALLENGE AND HOW YOU CAN OVERCOME IT! THOSE DAMN ALIENS NEED TO GO AWAY, AND NOBODY CAN STOP IT BUT US!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so i try to find the good in most games i play before looking at the bad, sot that gonna be how this goes with the Pro's and Con'sPro's:Interesting Premise and Alien Invasion where we are one of the Regular humans not a Bad ass Soldier/Super Soldier and the Aliens seem to be smart enough to knock out communication when arriving Funny Characters Most of the characters in this game made me chuckle with their comments on what was going on or how they get takenTense Atmosphere at first just you and a bat trying to avoid being captured by the Grey Aliens Decent amount of game time not the shortest but not the longest in terms of gameplayeNow Onto the ConsCons:Poor Horror experience, once you get the gun AND the bat you quickly learn you can knock out or Kill the aliens so they quickly lose their terror and sure can surprise you if you don't see them but even that quickly vanishes awayvoice quality is very poor at times, lines running over one another difficulty figuring out where to go the lamps that tell you where to go didn't always work as they should and voices that were meant to play when you went the right way wouldn't play leading to getting lost and wanderingLack of varity of enemies at some point it like 'oh look another grey BAM and he is dead' No reason to replay the game, unless to secure any missed achivements/awards quickly uninstalledHonestly and as a personal comment not everyone will agree with this i'm sure but the ending to a game should at least leave me satisfied and happy with what transpires good or bad, this just left me..Empty is the best word? no resolution on the MC and his son who was the mystery man? why did the cat get probed? WHY did the gov allow aliens to land and kidnap people when they are easily killed. Way to many questions for me left unanswered maybe if this game got a DLC or a sequel to answer these questions, my feelings on the ending might change but until then it is the way it is.Overall as it stands i cannot suggest this game after playing it, a single session is not worth taking up storage space and i had higher hopes for this game. If you want to see for yourself if this game is for you or not then by all means but do take this recommendation into consideration.
