_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I really did. But it just has such bad design choices and implementation that I just can't.Firstly, enemy detection seems very off. My first death was to being detected through a wall and having the spot I was hiding in instantly detected.Secondly, there is not much you can do once detected unless you have ammo. The baseball bat takes too long to down an alien, 3 swings, costs stamina that limits how far you can run away in the time. Not only that but it takes longer to knockout an alien than they will actually be knocked out for. The way I feel this could be improved is having it either last much longer than in does now, or have it actually kill an alien. I don't think this would be too much because you could not do it to more than one alien at a time.Finally, the game does suffer from the occasional frame rate stutter. Other people seem to be having more issues than I did, but I still had issues. Even if the first two issues were fixed, the game does also suffer the problem of coming out only a few days after the new Amnesia game. Which has very similar game play just executed far better. The second issue is the most important one I feel to resolve at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: The Greyhill Incident is a survival horror in first person view.The story is simple, the small town of Greyhill is subject to paranormal phenomena, very quickly we understand  that an alien invasion is underway. It is not possible to contact the authorities or the government at the risk of being taken for a madman. The solution found by the inhabitants is to create a civil militia and patrol the city.You are one of these civilians, Ryan. And, everything is not going to go as planned, one by one your neighbors are abducted and you must fight your way to find a solution to this insavion.Here no highly trained soldiers, no merciless hitman, you are a simple civilian in an invasion of unprecedented magnitude.To give you an idea, there are only 17 revolver bullets and only 13 aliens in the whole game. By using all the bullets you will still have 5 aliens left, and you will have to play stealth towards the end of the game. What are you going to do? Play stealth and save your ammo for the end? Or eliminate as many aliens as possible?You are plunged into almost total darkness, for only source of light your torch and the streetlights of Greyhill, each step is a danger, stay in the shadows to not get kidnapped, study the movements of the aliens to find a flaw and take advantage of a moment of inattention.All this on paper sends a dream, BUT it is nothing. Greyhill remains a banal FPS without flavor, and which is very short in terms of its solo campaign. Its strong point is its unhealthy atmosphere and scenario but which do not hold up because the game ends too quickly, no real antagonist, no real stakes. In short I am impatiently waiting for They are here to maybe finally have a real game about an alien invasion.My rating 10/20It's really a shame because the atmosphere was really distressing.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't leave reviews often but felt I needed to say what I think.The idea and atmosphere is amazing! I love what this game is trying to be, but it isn't. I was super excited to experience it but the gameplay is atrocious and gets in the way of the experience. I feel if this game was made by the outlast team it would be a world wide success because of the idea alone, but the execution is flawed so badly. The developers have alot to learn and will definitely gain alot from these reviews and hopefully fix this game and release better games in the future because they def have the potential.criticism:I like that they placed lights to try and help direct the player but you can see all the lights at the same time and have no idea which one is the one you should actually be going for. I spent a long time just walking in circles trying to interact with every little thing cause I had no idea what I was actually supposed to be doing.the walking was way to slow and way to long. I felt like I had to walk back and forth and back and forth for way to long and the stamina was pretty much useless. I also smacked an alien about 20 times with a bat and it never died. I wish I could have killed them without the gun even if it was a chore and took a while similar to atomic heart. the crank light was a good idea and really makes you feel a bit more immersed in the world, sorta like how in gta 4 you would spam the run button to run. BUT!! and this is a big but, It didn't stay lit for long enough given the amount of spamming needed to turn it all the way on. I think it should have slowly dimmed over time at least 3 times slower.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a Recommended, but with a disclaimer that you MUST fit the target audience. This is a very specific experience, and I honestly don't know who it's for. It's a bit shy on the hitting the humorous beats it needs to be a comedy, and it's a bit too simple for it to scratch some combat itch. As for survival horror, the map is too confusing and the mechanics too opaque to compete. It's not Dead By Daylight versus AI. It's none of these things, though you get the sense that it could almost fit the spot.But what I will say, is if you're looking for a schlocky alien B-movie experience, this is the place to get it. Yes, I recommend having a guide at hand (my Twitch chat did), as the map can be overly large and a bit confusing. That said, once you get into the rhythm of hiding, running, whacking and shooting these grey bastards, you've got a good time on your hands. Honestly the ammo concerns of other reviews are overblown; you cannot shoot every alien you see, but you really don't need to. That's what the bat is for. Maybe, like, git gud.Also, the ending is a real jaw-dropper.i don't love it for the price, but if it's on sale and you're looking for something like .. this. well, you've got it !!

_childDocuments_.review: Like many I had high hopes for this game.  However, ultimately I was quite disappointed with the final result.First, the good: - Overall Concept (Yes, a survival horror game with aliens!)  - Art direction, atmosphere, sound, lighting, attention to detail (love the 90s memorabilia) - Was genuinely very spooky at the beginning.  Made me shout out loud several times.The bad:- The dull pacing (super slow after the first 30 minutes.  You basically walk from house to house on fetch quests...very...very slowly.   You can't run for very long, meaning the Aliens always have an excellent chance of catching you.  - The lack of guidance.  There is no map, no objective markers, not even any on screen text instructing you to find what you need to find.  This means more aimless wandering as you stumble around in the dark.   I was always very confused as to what I needed to be doing, and where I needed to go.   For a while it was tolerable, but then became incredibly boring.  I spent 20 minutes looking for aluminum foil in Bob's caravan (very had to see or know what you'd looking for).-The combat mechanics.  Why can't you kill the aliens with the baseball bat?  They get right back up again.  This seemed unfair as you have to it them three times.  At least make them stay down until you can escape.  That's it in a nutshell.  Interesting idea, but needs more work.

_childDocuments_.review: I read reviews but never let them to shape my thoughts. I always try and see myself and make my own decisions. This is the my approach to games, movies and books. I suggest you to do the same.Here is the my opinions:As a person who likes UFO stories and movies since my childhood, I always waited for a horror game about alien abductions and greys. I think it is a shame gaming industry hasn’t discovered it yet except this devs. I was waiting this game from the day which I saw it on steam and bought it when it was released. I couldn’t try the 1.0 version but as far as I see people doesn’t like it and become too harsh on the game. Luckily devs listened the people and fixed some issues regarding path finding and some bugs about audio etc.I played version 1.0.2 and really liked the game. The atmosphere is really great. Open night sky with full moon and foggy weather really gives scary and mysterios atmosphere. Greys are wandering around and trying to abduct you at first sight. You can try to escape them or kill them with your gun. Its your choice but don’t forget you have limited ammo. As greys my childhood nightmare, they gave me chill in every encounter even if I have gun. Game has no quest marker or a map. Because of lack of map, you should memorize the town and find your way by following the lights. If there was a town map, it would be great to find the places in the town. Otherwise you are wasting time to find the places in the foggy night and somepoint it become boring. Devs might have thought that the character is living in the town and know the places where to go but missed the point that player is totally strange to the town and need some advice or hint. I say again town map would be great. Otherwise finding Brandon became boring in quest "bring the cat to Brandon" and other example go to the dinner etc.You can use revolver with few bullets and also have baseball bat. Revolver is fine but baseball bat is too slow. When I hit alien I have to wait some time to hit again and it kills the reality I think. It could have been better to wait some time after 2 or 3 swing not at first swing.I haven’t encountered any FPS or crash problems. I have played it on both my desktop (rtx 3080) and laptop (rtx 3060). I was able to play smoothly on both systems without any drop or crash. But I have found out 2 bugs on ver 1.0.2. In caravan I couldn’t pass the backroom door without crouching. Also have the same door problems in some houses. Other bug is I wasn’t able to climb the ladder on the first barn after caravan. Restarting game was fixed the issue.For me this is a good experience and I think people who likes UFO’s, The X-files and greys will love it. Game is not too much scary or not just walking simulator. It has good balance between them. If you approach this game without high expectations, you will like it. I beat it in 3 hours but it is enough for me. I thank to dear developers for this game. Please continue to make UFO horror games. Maybe you should consider to make outlast style horror game inspired from Travis Walton Incident.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played $6.99 indie dev games on Steam that offer triple the production, writing, and gameplay value this game has. $25 is valuing itself at half the content and value that Alan Wake 2 offers. Does this dev really think they've produced half of Alan Wake 2?The beginning portions are entertaining in how unintentionally funny some of the eventing is, like how unbothered the MC's kid is about literally anything going on before  But overall the writing isn't very good. Character logic and reasoning is just absent for entire portions of the story when you meet NPC's and gain objectives. The save system is janky. You can complete an entire objective, talk to an NPC, acquire a new objective, close out the game and when you go to replay it you will have lost all that progress and be sent back to the previous objective. Is this probably designed to be played in one sitting? Most likely, but the gameplay is so frustratingly bad I needed to stop and pick it back up another time. And on the note of being played in one sitting, if it's designed that way why the $25 price tag? This doesn't offer any replay value, and as far as I can tell the assets aren't original, they're purchased, so again, why the $25 price tag other than to be a cash grab?This game feels like it's half passion project, half scam. I recommend avoiding. Even at a 50% discount, it's still not a $12.50 game, it's a sub $10 game, and $10 would be .There's one good thing about the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to play this game under patch 1.05. "Tried" because I lost heart after one hour and half.The game is more like a digital novel. You follow a crumbs trail and are rewarded with the next event. So, let's start with the story.The plot of this game is the sum of everything banal about UFO abductions. Nuts with tinfoil hats, lack of faith in the government, cattle mutilations... and of course Grey aliens.Our hero can smash SOME things with a baseball bat, but more often that not he is blocked by the classic impassable things in this kind of games: low fences, bins, tree branches... and the most powerful obstacle of them all: the psychological inability to go in a certain direction. You want to explore? No, you don't want to go there. Why? No reason at all.The developer is fixing the stamina problem, which makes you run like a 60 years old out of shape. It is still not enough. You move around a murky landscape like if you have to wade across mud in Vietnam.An then there are the aliens. I won't spoil, but let's say that there is a terrifying event involving the main character. What should cause panic and anxiety is immediately forgotten - because you have to find some nails to board up your house.The aliens chase you and you can end up abducted. Somehow, by then I didn't really care. Yes, the alien encounters are moderately scary, but you whack them with the baseball bat and run (a bit). Also, the aliens have psychic abilities that allow them to get to the next story beat faster than you. Maybe you need a tinfoil hat too.The "found footage" mode does seem to be an homage to the classic "The McPherson Tape" and it is interesting for all of five minutes before you turn it off. Also: we have this "found footage"... how? It isn't that the player has a camera with him.I was really waiting for this game but it is so bad that, even if reportedly very short, I don't even care to finish it. I'll watch a speedrun. Pity.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the bad reviews:This game actually is pretty good, it requires a more keen mind to play (if a bumbling buffoon like myself can have fun, anyone can lol)I've looked over some of the reviews and it seems the highlighted problems are;-No objective marker (which I understand but it doesn't take a genius to find your objective)-Quiet voices (I personally don't have a problem with it, and I'm recording my playthrough which would make the voices even quieter, little tip fellow gamers; the volume control panel exists on your PC for a reason)-A lack of interaction indicator (spoiler alert, the indicator is the white dot on the center of your screen, it will become slightly brighter when you can interact with something)-You can't bind certain keys (Practice with default controls makes perfect)-Performance (dude just lower the specs, I turned mine down from ultra to medium and the game runs smoother than a knife with butterSimply put: All the negative reviews are from people who seemingly got frustrated after the first two minutes of gameplay then took to the comment section to crap on the hard work of a very good indie team, which in turn leads to a human placebo effect ruining other potential players experiences.Shame on you party poopers.

_childDocuments_.review: Had high hopes for this from the moment it was announced, and they kind of delivered on the promised concept, but it's an extremely short lived experience that runs pretty poorly for a game of it's kind. The game is extremely confusing. Most of the time you have no idea where you have to go and what to do. There is the occasional lamp or some kind of light indicator of where to go next and some of the metal fences that can be opened have yellow paint on them, but apart from that you really have to figure everything out by yourself. Prime example of that for me would be in the trailer, when you deliver Bob his cat and then he asks you to pick up some foil from the kitchen desk. That entire trailer is literally filled with all kinds of foiled objects. Took me quite a bit to find that, ironically, the piece you need is the tiniest piece of foil in his entire trailer that fits onto your walkie-talkie's antenna, so aliens can't listen in on your comms.  I could see it work for about 10-15 dollars at the most, but at 24.99 it's a big ask for a three and a half hour "experience" at best if you are really slow. At this price tho, I can't recommend it. Really wish the devs the best, as it's a unique and interesting concept, but the longevity and bang for your buck just sadly isn't there.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game's atmosphere is good and the voice acting isn't that bad. Besides that every thing else is bad. Lots of voice lines will play over other voice lines and you haft to wait for voice lines to end a lot in order to progress for example a door may be locked but right after a voice line the door magically opens this ruins immersion and shows the game is scripted which it is. The Game is very linear and not in a good way. If you try to walk down a road you will hit an invisible wall and a text that says "I shouldn't go that way". It's extremely annoying! You will constantly be having to walk down these narrow scripted paths where gates magically open after a voice line. The Game doesn't allow exploration at all you will constantly be blocked by trees and 4ft gates which the player should be able to jump over. Every place you haft to go to you can only go one way you can't jump over a fence and go another way you can only go down the scripted path where aliens are spawned right where the objective is. There are only two weapons in the game. Baseball Bat and The Revolver! The Revolver feels good but the bat is awful it would be cool if the player was allowed to go off the beaten path and find weapons that other less adventurous players would miss. For example you will come across a police car it would be cool if the player could open the trunk and find a shotgun without the game telling them to do so. The game also lacks any re play ability as the game is only allowed to be played one way down the same exact scripted paths. It would be cool if you could actually explore the town of Grey hill and find supplies but instead your locked to a scripted path. Silent Hill 1 is a great example the game came out in 1999 and has more atmosphere, exploration and re-play ability than this. Now I know this is Indie but this game is just lazily made. 25$ is over priced should be a 5$ game at most the game only takes an hour to beat and the only reason I have more hours is because I beat the game twice. _childDocuments_.review: Special Thank you to Perp Games and Refugium Games for sending me a key to this long awaited indie hit!Let me start off by saying a small team making a game like this, a genre we don't get enough of, with graphics this impressive is incredible and fresh!If you've ever wanted to live in the alien horror of M. Night Shyamalan's SIGNS, then this is the game for you!The sound design grips you in, beefs up the anxiety and causes you to feel like theirs nowhere to run.Many of the jump scares do work and in my opinion do not overstay there welcome, being such funny looking designs you gotta take what you can get in that departmentBut something occurred to me playing thisThis isn't just SIGNS, this is its parodyThere are moments that are shocking, terrifying, memorable and leave you frozen in panicBut there are just as many moments of you saying....this is a troll game right?Certain dialogue choices leave you scratching your head, but they knew what they were doing.Now the bad- There are many bugs from invisible walls, stuck glitches (for all characters)- Dialogue overlaps that feel like your at a UN meeting- The weapon options glitch out and don't work correctly- Some of the controls tend to stick- And no way of leaping over easy to climb areas in my opinionBut the lack of stamina, no way points, no clue what the hell is going on, may turn off a lot of a peopleI feel this is its strength.The single most terrifying moment in this game I had no idea where I was going and all I heard were screams and the corn shifting in the windOne thing I cannot forgive, is the endingShort, sudden and left me with more questions than answers. Plus gave me a bad WTF instead of WTF NO WAY VIBE! Unless the developers are creating a sequel or even a trilogy, I want answers....what the hell happened?!So to summarise a beautifully crafted experience from people who really do care.A great first outing for Refugium GamesMoments that are genuinely terrifyingBut lacks quite a bit to warrant a replay and desperately needs some bug fixesTreat this as a movie that we get once in a lifetimeYou are hyped and excitedIt releases, it wasn't as good as you thought, but you are glad you saw it and there are times you remember certain moments that gripped you in and made you realise why you were happy to see it!I'm just glad we finally got a little grey men story instead of snarling beasts and run and gun shootersWe need more of these and soon! If this was the first step of Alien conspiracy stories, than there is a long, bright road ahead for this genreBut this one will hold a special place in my nostalgic heart6/10 An invasion that lacks supervisionTwitch Play Through: YouTube: COMING SOON!

_childDocuments_.review: I was absolutely thrilled to finally embark on this otherworldly journey. Counting down the days and months until its launch felt like waiting for a close encounter of the gaming kind, especially since I've been deeply captivated by movies like "Signs" and "Fire in the Sky," which clearly left an indelible mark on this game.Ultimately, this game beamed me up to only let me down. The objectives provided in the pause menu were frustratingly vague; I found myself resorting to YouTube walkthroughs, seeking guidance even for seemingly simple tasks like opening a gate I had mindlessly passed by numerous times.Technical issues further marred the experience. The initial sensitivity and volume settings were off-kilter, making me feel as if I were fumbling through an alien control panel. Dialogue delivery suffered from synchronization problems, with characters speaking and subtitles appearing simultaneously, resulting in a dissonant cacophony rather than a coherent narrative.I genuinely hope the developers will address these issues through updates, rescuing the game from its current state. While I can see the potential beneath the surface, the frustration I encountered overshadowed any enjoyment I could derive from it. Considering its current price, it's difficult for me to justify recommending it as is.

name: Gravitar: Recharged
detailed_description: A lone pilot, far from home, must navigate an abstract universe of uncharted planets and space stations guarded by mysterious, hostile aliens in Gravitar: Recharged. You must complete missions in each solar system, navigating a variety of challenging environments, each with varying levels of gravity that will test your skills as a pilot. Complete each mission within a solar system and you will be transported to the next through a massive black hole. Will you ever make it home? With Gravitar: Recharged Atari revisits an incredibly ambitious arcade title. The 1982 original took the rotate, thrust and fire mechanics of Asteroids and Space Duel, combined them with the gravity of Lunar Lander, and added exploration and elements of cave flying. The result was an extremely challenging arcade game that was eventually ported to the Atari 2600. The game, which did not achieve broad commercial success, has become a cult classic among Atari enthusiasts. The visual aesthetic of Gravitar: Recharged takes the Recharged series in a new direction, with expansive environments rendered in painterly style and pastel tones. In the capable hands of industry-veteran composer Megan McDuffee, the original soundtrack complements the art style with soothing, atmospheric tracks that evoke a sense of wonder. Key Features: - Arcade mode: fly from planet to planet and progress through ever-more-challenging solar systems in a quest to get home. - Missions: 24 taxing challenges with global leaderboards. - Power-Ups: Pick-up power-ups with your tractor beam, including homing missiles and EMP disruptors - Co-op: Play with a partner in each game mode, which connects two players on a tether, requiring a significant level of coordination. - Get in the Groove: Megan McDuffee continues to deliver with an ambient score that transports you into the depths of the unknown.

_childDocuments_.review: I was 14 when this game hit the arcade in 1982 and I absolutely loved it! It was so hard, which is why we all wanted to prove we were skilled enough to beat it. I remember actual rumors going around that it was deliberately designed so that you couldn't win just so we would keep plugging quarters into it. Silly conspiracy theorists. They just couldn't grasp the concept of multitasking.  This version is a blast from the past. Just as challenging as the original but buffed to a level of shininess that will hurt your brain. By far my favorite so far from the "recharged" series of ATARI classics. It is side-scrolling arcade action with a gravitational twist that will frustrate you to no end but in a good way!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on the Steam Winter Sale. I have fond memories of playing a version of the original Gravitar on a floppy disk that my parents got me. I looked for it on Steam and thought this was it with updated graphics. I was disappointed to find that this game was quite different, and in my opinion does not capture the fun of the original.This game has similar asteroids-style mechanics as the original. You go around shooting enemies that shoot back, and you need to dodge and maneuver to stay alive. This version has powerups and different objectives, but I don't feel like they really add anything. The game still feels very repetitive after the first few levels, especially arcade mode. The original game was simple but challenging, with each level having the objective of either kill all enemies or destroy the core and get out within the time limit. The variety came from the different levels, which each had their own unique layout and provided a unique challenge in maneuvering.I found that I couldn't complete levels quickly without losing lives to random stuff. The reason for this it that enemies can shoot you from off-screen. The shields would help with this, except that the bullets have knockback, so you get hit and lose your shield, then get knocked into something and lose a life. In the original game all enemies with few exceptions had fixed positions and you got a view of the whole level before moving closer and zooming in, so you didn't have to worry about running into enemies you didn't know were there. As for the powerups, some of them don't feel exciting to get, since they're inferior to the basic weapon in some ways and they're more like sidegrades than powerups. In particular, the spread shot gives more bullets but greatly reduced range. Some of them also make it easier to destroy fuel tanks on accident. That's another thing, fuel tanks are objects that can be destroyed with your shots now, rather than spots you hover over and collect with your tractor beam like in the original.Also I encountered a bug. I entered a planet as my fuel was running out, and my ship died and didn't respawn. I was just stuck looking at the planet, and I had to exit out and lose my progress.If you're looking for a simple asteroids-style shooter to mess around with and don't mind paying a few bucks for it, then you might like this game. If you're looking for a recreation of the original Gravitar, then I think you're out of luck, sadly.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: A great reboot of an old ATARI arcade classic, Gravitar: defy gravity while completing missions.This new version sports great retro-stylish graphics and a beautiful electronic soundtrack (Megan McDuffee), simple controls yet challenging gameplay.All that for a modest price tag, by the way... In case it wasn't clear, I love this game!Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought all of the recharged series of games as they are a lot of fun to play. I wasn't a really a big Atari fan back in the day or anything, but this is a great way of playing some old school games, jazzed up for the current gen.Gravitar is a lot of fun. Its like playing Asteroids with a campaign. Once you get the hang of how to control the ship you will be flying about with ease. There are some weapons that you can pick up during missions, which help you out and there is a nice set of achievements as well which always helps.If you love Asteroids then you will definitely enjoy this game with its mission structure and different objectives that you need to achieve on the different planets. I would say the skill level to complete the game will be quite high as you don't get many lives for the main campaign, but its an old-school game and that's how they were designed back in the day so you have to put the practice in to get the rewards!
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Skill-based shooter with atmospheric retro vibes, mainly relaxed but sometimes challenging and with 24 missions, some of which are also suitable for joypad masochists.  Co-op missions provide fun for two and an arcade mode offers a hunt for high scores. Overall, the gameplay is repetitive and offers little variety, but is quite entertaining for a quick session.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Hard, especially in beginning you have to do subtle pumps on the accelerator or you will quickly spin out of control, and you always need to pay attention which direction the gravity is coming from. Also not bad for co-op if you can get your co-player/GF to relax and teach them how not to spin out of control and bump into everything ;->
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Gravitar: Recharged is a great update to a classic game. I like the modern look of the game, while keeping some of the classic concepts of the game. If you loved the original Gravitar, then you will enjoy the updated version, because it is challenging and addictive. It is multi-player, so grab a friend when you play it. I applaud Atari, Adamvision Studios, and Sneaky Box for this great updated version!
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Although smoothly made, in many ways this is a backward step from the classic. The multiple shots per button press makes it hard to aim accurately. Black objects on the background layer appear like solid foreground objects to be avoided and are needlessly distracting. The UFO death is totally unrewarding, fading out rather than exploding. Chasing round the sun to find the last planet is boring. The guns and antennas are crudely drawn and ugly. The pickups are unrewarding. So sad, as this had real potential if the designers had made better choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Key obtained via Keymailer for streaming purposes.i admit, i thought this game would be allot of fun to play. and well it is but... it's lacking.i thought this game would have story or some form of progression unfortunately i was mistaking.most of the game is arcade based fly fly shooty shooty bang bang in a way. there are roughly 4 or 5 different mission types.destroy reactordestroy enemiessteal intel,activate beacons.earn points.i believe that's all the mission types. the only reason i figured that out is because i just started to do missions instead of the arcade. which honestly. is better than the arcade. mainly because the solar system is pointless and lacking.the music isn't bad but nothing memorable.the gameplay is rather simplistic and often times you're fighting against yourself trying to keep your ship lined correctly to take a shot.some of the weapon upgrades are questionable.the worst ones are the spread shot, it's good yes but it limits your bullet range significantly to the point u are using it as a shotgun.i hate the shield generators. i understand why they are there but between that and having the generators often hidden behind other invulnerable objects/enemies it becomes a pain in the behind.honestly the game is fine but... it needs more to keep you playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Gravitar is extremely difficult. This gameplay mechanic will provide the challenge you.You explore solar system, with planets and space stations. Land on one of planets and complete missions (power-up the beacons or destroy the enemies/generator). It takes time to get used to the controls. A ship movement requires precision and patience. The physics/gravity makes the gameplay more difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really surprising, excellent game!  it is super difficult and yet calming at the same time.  It takes patience and a steady hand but, after many hours and weeks, I was able to finish all four systems.  Excellent game.  (I play it on the Atari VCS rather than Steam because I love their classic controller).
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually really great. I've played Gravitar on the Arcade1Up Atari cabinets. It's a challenging game, but definitely one of the better ones. All of that is back in this version: variable gravity, fuel consumption, and everything that made the first one challenging, but with better graphics, more enemies and obstacles, and other new tweaks that add to the challenge. This is very well done and a worthy sequel to the original, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a new and challenging arcade game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I think objectively this is probably the best of the Recharged series so far, it has an amazing soundtrack which contrasts with the game play, because the music is calming I find myself not getting frustrated like with the old arcade version, adding shields to the ship definitely is a good thing for Gravitar and even has an option to play the game without shields so it's just like the arcade version.                                                                                                                                                                                    The backgrounds are just absolutely beautiful and gives you the feeling that you are truly in deep space alone and the power ups aren't op because the level design countracts the power ups somewhat but feel useful at the same time. One complaint I do have is I wish the buttons for exit and retry were like the older Recharged titles because it got you in the game faster and kept me immersed which was probably a mistake on the developers end but ended up being better unintentionally which was cool.The price is also good, cheap enough for an impulse buy while I still prefer Asteroids Recharged myself I would say that if someone could only buy just one Recharged game, I would have no problem recommending Gravitar Recharged.The developers did a really great job with this game and maybe we could get a Quantum or Lunar Lander Recharged game just food for thought I feel those would benefit a lot from getting the Recharged treatment some of the other titles got but that's just my opinion
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Having loved the original for too many arcade hours, I am loving this recharge!  It carries much of the spirit of the original, including the no-holds barred hardcore pull no punches approach of the environment. Yes, you can get clobbered by an asteroid just after you successfully clear a planet. Too bad. What, you wanted fair? The universe is not fair. You wanted to restart the mission where you left off? What part of 'destroyed' did you miss?Overall, the physics of move and control are well done here. When you get hit, you serious get the "I screwed up" feeling, not the "the game screwed up feeling" feeling. Like a good classic arcade game, it is responsive and consistent.My one serious complaint rather leaves me puzzled. Original Gravitar players can remap controls to Space-K-O/Tractor-Thrust-Fire for the right hand, but you cannot remap the left controls to make A-S/Left-Right. You are stuck with A-D which is s wide spacing for the index-middle fingers. I remapped the keys at the Windows layer, and using a classic arcade layout restores the rapid 'wobble fire' capability that the original had. Given that the other keys can be remapped, I don't follow why the left/right cannot also be remapped. It would be interesting to set up an original console size and button layout with USB keyboard controller to drive this from! I previously found that playing the original 'restored vector' emulation using a D-pad has the same problem - you cannot wobble left/right on a D-pad anywhere near as quickly as with closely paired left-right buttons.Overall though - lots of fun, a nice challenge, and good value for money!
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: A lone pilot, far from home, must navigate an abstract universe of uncharted planets and space stations guarded by mysterious, hostile aliens in Gravitar: Recharged. You must complete missions in each solar system, navigating a variety of challenging environments, each with varying levels of gravity that will test your skills as a pilot. Complete each mission within a solar system and you will be transported to the next through a massive black hole. Will you ever make it home? The visual aesthetic of Gravitar: Recharged takes the Recharged series in a new direction, with expansive environments rendered in painterly style and pastel tones. In the capable hands of industry-veteran composer Megan McDuffee, the original soundtrack complements the art style with soothing, atmospheric tracks that evoke a sense of wonder.
_childDocuments_.name: Gravitar: Recharged

name: ONE BTN BOSSES
detailed_description: ONE BUTTON BOSSES: ⬇️Push. Tap. Bash: A 4 hour campaign, a concise roguelike game mode and just one button. ❤️ Heart-pumping Strategy: It’s harder than it looks; pilots better be ready for a fight! Unlock upgrades and customize your ship to win. 🔥 The Grind: Brag to your friends, laugh at enemies, and compete for the best times on the leaderboard. 🎹 Get in The Zone: A legendary synth-wave soundtrack accompanies pilots' many, many losses. 🚩Rise up and Resist: Follow the story of Ace, an unpaid assistant, as they resist the big bosses for a fair paycheck. 🚀 Play Your Way: Each of the bosses needs to be beaten in a best of 3, 5, 7 … meaning you will never be hard stuck on a boss fight as there is always a different level to try. THE SHIP You pilot a ship that orbits the BOSS automatically. PRESS the button to change the ship’s direction 🔄. But the less you change directions, the faster the ship goes. The faster you go, the faster you shoot. The faster you shoot, the faster you WIN! Make sure to WIN before the BOSS gets too angry and wipes you out! CUSTOMIZE ATTACKS There's depth to the simple controls! You can customize the ship, mixing ATTACK and MOVEMENT upgrades to find the best builds to beat bosses. DASH instead of changing directions, fire a LASER instead of bullets. There’s over 100 different combinations you can try out to suit your playstyle! A MEAN STORY ACE THE ASSISTANT will loop you into the 50 handcrafted levels of bullet hell action. The bosses will taunt you as you lose, but if you persist you will rise up the ranks, progress the story, earn GRIND POINTS and unlock new ways to play! Are you ready? ROGUELITE R&D (RIFTS & DEVELOPMENTS) Fly your ship into the R&D (RIFTS & DISCOVERIES) department. Where you will face insanely challenging RANDOMLY GENERATED BOSSES and earn new upgrades and power-ups after every fight.

short_description: It's One Button Bosses, it's all in the name. You have one button. There are big bosses to beat. Push, tap, and bash in the handcrafted campaign or in the roguelike rifts.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really simple to pick up. You press only one button! Its in the title!!! But its anything but easy. The difficulty throughout the campaign has been very well balanced so far. It's never impossibly hard, but it also doesn't hold your hand.The rift mode also adds a ton of replayability. There is SO MUCH to try out with all the potential weapon and build combinations. I'm really impressed they managed to incorporate so many complex movement/attacking mechanics, while being restricted to only one button.If you're a fan of bullet hell or rhythm type games, or just want something a bit more accessible, then this game is a perfect fit.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: An arcade game that reminds me of Just Shapes and Beats. Very minimalisting dodge-em-up, I suppose.The central gimmick of the game is that you only have one button to perform actions with. The game isn't particularly different from level to level, placing you on some kind of loop where you continuously move. Clicking or pressing a button will turn you around by default, but you can choose your manner of attacking (which is by default automatic, you shoot stronger bullets with more speed) and what the action button does.As you would probably expect, the game is fairly difficult, and if you're very into arcadey titles provides you with ranking after each level. Around halfway through the campaign it also unlocks a roguelike mode where you choose levels on a Slay the Spire-like map and choose upgrades after each smaller battle. It doesn't feel as replayable as a roguelike mode should be, but I think I've enjoyed it more than the regular game thanks to randomness involved.Points you get acts as exp, unlocking new methods of play and new color schemes, and this is probably the only thing where game feels a little undercooked. Despite being called a Grind, you can unlock everything halfway through the campaign if you've tried the roguelike mode a few times. Wish there were more colors or options, as if you don't care for rankings the game goes by fairly quickly, taking me 2.5 hours. Granted, I haven't finished some of the levels since thankfully the "worlds" of the game only require some victories. Still, I very much had fun figuring out each of the game's short levels.I also was not a fan of most color schemes. It's cool to see so many of them themed around progressive ideas: many are queer flags, and there's a Free Palestine one, but I found most of them to be almost painful to look at, so I stuck with the basic Dark theme for my playthrough.I don't think this game is exactly for me, but if you're into arcade action titles like Shapes and Beats, shmups, and maybe rhythm games, check this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: This looked like a really cool game when I first saw it. I love boss rush games like titan souls, and the 1 button twists on games like Rhythm Doctor or Rhythm Heaven made me think this would be similar. After beating the campaign in under 3 hours, while getting top times on most of the levels, I found that ONE BTN BOSSES is an unpolished, unplaytested, poorly designed game, that rides on an enticing premise.----------Good stuff:-The premise is great. There's a lot you can do with this one button, on-rail movement type of stuff.-The shooting mechanics based off of speed are great too. Creates that nice depth with a balance between dodging and DPS.-I found the dialogue funny at times, and the office premise surprised me.-The build mechanics are cool. You get a module for movement, damage, and a supporting one, and there's potential for cool synergies between all of these. There's also room for building around bosses, using certain movement and damage abilities that work well with the bosses attacks. Unfortunately, despite all the potential here, I rarely found moments where I had to swap my build to counter a boss, and there is one build that 200% outperforms any other build.-I like that the game focuses on time to defeat a boss, rather than just defeating the boss. This gives room for casual and hardcore players.-I couldn't find any bugs related to gameplay. I only found one minor UI bug that doesn't impact the game experience.That's really all the good stuff I could find.----------Bad stuff:-There is a huge lack of polish and content throughout the whole game. This will be expanded on in the rest of the review, but also this is the 1.0 release, and there is a feedback google form in the pause screen. I understand the desire for feedback, but just plug socials or a discord, or be in early access. A google form in your *pause* menu is embarrassing.-Despite being a boss rush game, there is only 5 unique bosses. Now, each of these bosses do have multiple encounters and if you consider all of that it's probably around 30-40 bosses. But most of the encounters on the same boss are the same attack styles over and over. Many of the attacks are uninteresting, and they will mix and match attacks together only to create walls and poorly telegraphed messes. Despite the on-rail restrictiveness of the movement, it's clear the devs did not think about how the player is supposed to dodge some of these attacks, and instead just put stuff they thought was kinda cool. Compare this to other boss rush games like Titan Souls or Rabbit And Steel, which have many more boss designs, with varied unique attack patterns, that are all well telegraphed, and there is thought put into what the player is supposed to do. If there was more thought put into these attack patterns, with a clear goal in mind of how each attack/phase in a boss is supposed to challenge the player, this could be really really fun. But instead it feels random, like not even unfair random, it just feels like spam. If they went with a more reactive approach with boss design, rather than set pattern attacks for each boss, that would service the movement mechanics much better. -There are these HR fights before each boss that teach you the attacks of the boss. This seems like a cool idea, it lessens any BS of "wtf is going on." But there are already infinite fast retries with no consequences, so you could just play the boss once or twice and get the gist of the attacks. And the learning phase of a boss is one of the most fun parts of bossfight games. The learning is part of why soulslike games, Hollow Knight, shmups, are so fun and exhilarating. You get to the hard part, freak out and go "wtf is going on" and die, and then you slowly learn the patterns and realize that everything is actually pretty simple. In ONE BTN BOSSES, you don't get any of that learning experience, and rather you just memorize un-telegraphed patterns and it's just tedious.-There is a lack of QOL throughout the game. There are some obvious changes that should be there but aren't: there's no "fully charged" indicator for the reverse module, there's no way to change your build in the pause screen, there's disappearing telegraph for the drop attacks but not for the similar bomb attacks, you can't see your time in game, you can't see the time to get certain ranks, you can't find damage numbers for your attacks, there's no additional damage stats in the roguelike pickups so you can't minmax your build, and more small things that add up and break your immersion.-I think the art style is cool, but the way it's executed is honestly ugly. Everything looks very jagged when there are off-angled shapes: many outlines, like the arc attacks in the first level, have this problem. The victory and defeat screens look blurry. The symbols in the grind rewards don't fully fill the outline, so there's some empty pixels that look weird. When choosing your supportive item on the build select, the lines in the middle don't reach the info box and just float there. Also, every fight has the exact same background. There is absolutely no styling or other distinctions for each stage, besides the boss sprite and attack patterns. -I saved the biggest one for the end, the worst part about this game are the modules and the builds. There are 3 movement options, 5 attack options, and 7 utility options. Here are the useless ones:    -I could not find a use for reverse movement. It's clunky and doesn't synergize with any of the attacks. You deal much more damage and have much more mobility with turn or dash.    -Pickup attack is overcomplicated and useless. It deals no damage and requires you to have perfect position to grab the pickup as much as possible, but there's always something in the way and the damage is weak. I think it's supposed to synergize with dash but for some stupid stupid reason you can't pickup the pickup while dashing???    -Juggler attack has the same problems as pickup but at least it scales.    -Shooter attack is fine but laser is a direct upgrade.    -Slower not weaker is a complete debuff and I don't even know why it exists, you don't even get a damage buff.    -Phaser is situational and underwhelming.    -Basically all utilities are weaker than thick hull and invincibl-erThe laser attack is a million times better than 3/4 of the other attacks, and then that last attack is completely busted and untested. How the reload attack is supposed to work is you click, it charges up, and then it shoots once its fully charged, or you click again to shoot it prematurely. The fully charged attack does a lot of damage, but because of how poor the boss attacks are, you can't get a full charge. So how you're actually supposed to play reload is by mashing your mouse and space bar as fast as you can, melting the bosses with a ton of small bullets with a high minimum damage. They somehow did not test this and it completely ruins the whole game if you decide to play like this. It's 30 seconds faster than any other build and when combined with thick hull or invincibl-er, it's just a button mashing simulator.----------Basically, a combination of bad boss patterns and unbalanced untested builds creates a very brainless, poorly thought out experience. Even if you play without an overpowered build, the way the bullet hells are designed makes it a frustrating memory-fest. Most of the potential in this game is squandered due to the exact wrong decisions being made. Because of how great the base concepts are, a lot of this could be fixed in patches and this could be a really great game. That's the only reason I wrote this review, because this game could be super fun if they actually paid attention to how they designed the game. So please release many many patches, and then I'll recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Super good. Dope music. Many different playstyles available. Weapons are all very different, so choice of weapon will influence a lot how hard a level is to beat. Levels can feel very claustrophobic sometimes. When enemy hitboxes are fading away it can be difficult to say when exactly it's safe to pass through as the sprite gets transparent. Despite this, the game is very lenient and usually in favor of the player so one still has a chance in hectic situations.And remember kids: 1, 2, 3 ... kill the Bourgeoisie.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying so far. I am wondering if perhaps the devs or another player could chime in on how I can tell when an attack has ended? I think the game would be better if there was either a very clear sign (like rather than starting to fade, which is not immediately identifiable, maybe changing color and then fading?) or if there was a timer on the attacks.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: While a cool idea of a simplistic bullet hell game, I don't think there's enough game here to really justify more than about a 5 dollar purchase... I smashed the entire game in about 2.5 hours (including the "rouge-like" mode and the "progression path"). There honestly aren't very many bosses at all, at once you figure out the loadout that each boss segment is weak to it's pretty much over. None of the bosses are very challenging and the minimal presentation leaves a lot to be desired, with many of the color pallets rather grating on the eyes. I used to play browser games with more depth than this.  I'd wait for it to be at least half off.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: ONE BTN BOSSES has to be one of the most creative games I've played in awhile, in such a easy concept of literally only having one button, it's amazing on how many different ways you can play with the weapons provided, and the movement as well. My favorite has to be juggler because it reminds me of playing Draven from League of legends. This game is certainly one for the books, it has the challenging levels you are looking for in each boss section throughout its main campaign, the challenge to get an S on all levels was pretty fun. It even has a rouge like option for when you beat the game, that makes each run a unique experience which is pretty cool.Speaking about the rouge like game mode, did you know there is an achievement where you need to collect the same rare option 5 times? Fun fact, apparently your chances increase when you have even one of them. However after doing many, many, many runs, I can NOT get this achievement. This has to be the most insane luck based achievement, I've had to go for in awhile, but thank god I get pacifist offered to me 3 times each run. (Which is a rare btw that ruins my chances for the achievement) I am gonna keep bashing my head against this wall, despite the fact that on average, i'll do two complete runs, and not even see it offered once, despite going to every elite/rest/shop option available. If you are a completionist, do yourself a favor and turn back now, it is not worth it, you will think the other achievements are so easy, fun, so why not get them all. Not this last achievement. Other than that great game overall, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that becomes really enjoyable once you start experimenting with all the different weapons and load-out combinations. Although you only use one button... there's a lot more to it than meets the eye, some weapons can deal a lot more damage than you would initially expect and you can find some very clever techniques to defeat bosses really quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent bullet-hell game. It's difficult, but very satisfying to thread the needle. There is an interesting game theory element to deciding whether to press the button to stay more stationary and dodge or to not press the button and let it ride for a faster fire rate. The roguelike mode is fun and provides good value after finishing the campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little game.  Developed by 3 people it's clearly a labor of love.   I am a huge fan of minimalist visuals and this is so aesthetically pleasing in that department.  I also get home from work sometimes and I am just dead tired and need something to play for a few minutes before bed that doesn't take much exertion, and this has been perfect.  Just one mouse click is all that is needed.  I haven't played much so far, but I love what I have experienced.  The gameplay is tight, fast paced, challenging, and is 144+ compatible no 60 fps lock!  The soundtrack is dope and the humor is on point about the corporate "rat race".  Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the hunt for a game that offers a real challenge without the headache of complicated controls, ONE BTN BOSSES It's a game that shows how less can definitely be more when it comes to having fun.So stop wasting time and give ONE BTN BOSSES a shot! Are you ready to become the boss master with just one button?
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: One Btn Bosses is one of those games that takes a simple idea and builds an entire experience around it. As the name implies you only need to use one button to fight bosses - all it does is let you reverse directions in order to dodge projectiles. From here the base of the game is built around as each level is a mini-bullet hell around this simple mechanic.The highlights of the game where the majority of the content lays is the boss fights and the Roguelike rifts. Each boss fight has a corporate theme as you try to climb the ladder and fight your way through bureaucracy, which led to some moderately funny dialogue. The Roguelike mode has you climb floors as you and enemies both continually get stronger, but done in ways that make it so each run feels challenging in a different way. While I feel it was only scratching the surface with these runs being on the short side, each one was definitely unique and a blast to do.This game clearly has a high quality of care put into it. While there is a shorter playtime everything I experienced was very solid. If my biggest complaints is that I want  of a game, that means I definitely recommend it. Lots of fun powerups to try out, cute inclusive themes and challenging levels all coming together to make for a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: One Btn Bosses is a minimalist concept done right. As the name implies you only press one button to play. However don't expect a simple game or a button masher, it's a hard skilled game where you need to react to imminent danger and optimize your movement to defeat bosses quickly.The game has a minimalist look as well which helps to read the game and while it's simple there's a ton of details on the animation and sound design that makes it very lively and fun.The story mode introduces you to the mechanics with challenging bosses and variations, while the roguelike mode that you unlock after a few bosses features randomized and always different experiences.This game is a unique gem, if you're up for a challenge get it! It also works perfectly on Steam Deck which is perfect for quick bite sessions.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I haven't play it much but from what I have seen now is absolutely enough to say that I can recommend it. It is a very simple but also very nice game concept that features a campaign mode and also a rougelike mode. Even with the simple controls you have to manage your speed and use your abilities at the right moment, the more you play the more playstyles you unlock. But for me the best feature is the darkmode, thank you for implementing it. Overall I would say it is a very nice little game and can recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept a lot, but the execution is poor.ONE BTN BOSSES is a very minimal abstract videogame, where you automatically shoot at the bosses at the center of your screen with a firerate inversely affected by the amount of times you press a button. A button constitute some kind of evasive measure as you move over the fixed trajectory: a dash or a change of direction. The concept is awesome, with innate risk/reward and a high skill ceiling despite consisting of pressing a single button.The problem is: minimal abstract games require A LOT of precision in implementation. Any minuscule flaw stands out immediately. ONE BTN BOSSES unfortunately falls victim to this pretty badly. The color coding is great: contrasting, consistent colors are used to depict obstacles from the background and yourself. The problem lies in communicating when an object will appear and where: how do I know the projectiles are going to be fast? How do I know how fast an indicator has to flicker before an obstacle occurs on my path? Some obstacles move along a predetermined path: with multiple moving around, how do you expect me to determine which indicator is the next path this obstacle will take? These are all arbitrary, poorly communicated hazards the player unfortunately has no real chance of understanding without playing the boss a couple of times over.And the game recognizes this as  problem by including mini-tutorials prior to fighting each boss. Unfortunately the bosses themselves still throw these at you with variable parameters as described above, making them nearly impossible to read during a level even if you understand the intention.Another big problem lies in attack patterns: out of the three bosses I defeated all of them felt like the player could end up in a very bad spot by simply existing somewhere along the path. Attack patterns are highly asymmetrical and can "trap" the player.I like the idea a lot, and it requires a great deal of confidence and expertise to make something so astoundingly simple - but unfortunately it falls short in the implementation.More reviews at:

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a pilot that automatically orbits and shoots the boss, while the gameplay revolves around changing speed/direction of movement with your one button of choice. Not pressing the button gradually increases your movement speed and damage, which creates an interesting risk/reward dynamic. If you get hit by stuff three times, it’s game over. Pretty simple, yet effective design. To spice it all up, there are upgrades available, split into three categories (movement, weapon, utility) that automatically unlock with progress in any game mode (I wouldn’t mind if unlocks were a bit faster to give some more options during the early and mid-campaign).Speaking of the campaign, every chapter starts with a few levels that introduce new attack patterns that you will face in the boss fight at the end of the section. Interestingly, boss fights are a best of X format, with each of the battles offering a different design of the arena(s) (orbit route) and attack pattern sequences. What that means is that if you ever get stuck on a specific fight, you can still progress by completing one (or more) of the alternative versions for that boss that might suit your build/playstyle better. Difficulty progression feels good and there was a lot of effort made for boss designs. There is a light corpo-themed background story with some robot humor that ties everything together. The length of the campaign will mostly depend on your skill level, but I’d say it will take anywhere from 2 to 5 hours to complete.The whole vibe is really cute, the art is simplistic and well done. Later fights sometimes get a bit hectic when the screen becomes more clustered, although some colour palettes definitely provide better readability (there are a lot of them; I was just going with the latest unlock that is assigned automatically for my playthrough). Enemy actions also have audio cues which help with that. I would definitely recommend playing with sound as the soundtrack is good as well.A rift (roguelike) mode where you progress through randomly generated floors is also available. Similar to Slay the Spire you choose your own progression path and upgrades after each completed fight. I only played a few runs so far, but it looks like the upgrades are diverse and depend on your base build of choice. This mode should provide a lot of end game content and challenges in addition to speed running campaign bosses for best grades.TL;DR: Inventive game design and good application of a one-button control scheme. Can be played in short sessions. Recommended for everyone who likes challenging rhythm games.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the modules are useless unless you are doing a challenge run or need something specific.All but like four color schemes burn my retinas as if they were a well done steak. Content is lacking severely for the campaign and roguelite making it hard to stick with playing either.Concept great, game okay at best.
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: Skeleton of the game seems fine but it seems like the rest wasn’t fully thought out:1) Most of the weapon upgrades are useless, you will find it's only worth cheesing everything with a single combo you get near the start and maybe a secondary one for specific cases. The rest could have used a damage buff at least.2) Utility upgrades are unlocked late for some reason? Would have been good to intersperse them throughout the game evenly alongside weapon and movement tech to create deeper strategy.3) It’s cool that there are many attack patterns but I do not feel like they were deployed in a meaningful enough way. The difficulty ended up being all over the place and didn’t feel like there was cohesion moving stage to stage. Half the patterns with more thoughtful execution would have gone much further.4) Aesthetic quip, but the anti-capitalist stuff is a bit too over the head. I get that you are very passionate about your socioeconomic beliefs but it feels like you are force feeding the player with no tact the entire way through.5) UI and polish: Play button should preferably be front and centre instead of to the side, restarting level should be just as fast after dying as doing it manually mid-level, etc.I believe you have potential to make good games, but there has to be a greater focus on the design making sense.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that requires you to press only one button, it is surprisingly difficult. However (at least in my experience), the difficulty lies in being able to achieve the best times for each level as opposed to actually beating them. If you're not grinding achievements or the leaderboard, it can probably be fully beaten in a couple of hours.Very simple and arcade-y fun, and would recommend if you're looking for a challenging 100% (hardest achievement is RNG-based though, so keep that in mind).
_childDocuments_.name: ONE BTN BOSSES

_childDocuments_.review: One BTN Bosses is a compact treat of a video game. There are hundreds of bullet patterns, dozens of arenas, and a handful of playstyle modifiers packed into a gameplay format that truly does only use one button. Each fight is a timing challenge that is affected by player choices, and those choices have obvious ripple effects as the player gets further and further into any one fight. The cute art, the bumping soundtrack, and the amusing character quips round out the package into something that almost anyone can pick up and enjoy. The roguelike mode can get a little repetitive, but variety of upgrades offer an unexpected depth.

Its mega simple, and thats why its great! <3

detailed_description: Wishlist Now In the same universe About the Game Who will be the fastest Smurf in town? That is the question you will need to answer in this dynamic kart racing game in the world of Smurfs! The whole family can choose one Smurf, its kart and special power, then you’re ready to go on wild races! Make the best start, find shortcuts, and use the right items at the right time to pass your opponents! Play solo or with friends and family, should you be a beginner or the most trained driver… you can get 1st place and show others who the fastest Smurf of all time is! FEATURES 12 tracks taken from the Smurfs’ universe: the village, the forest, the dam, the swamps… even Gargamel’s house! 12 playable Smurfs: chose the Smurf you want to drive with. Each Smurf has its own kart and a very handy special item to help you breeze past your opponents. Reach 1st place by using the environment around you: bonus items, boosts, ramps, destructible boxes, shortcuts and more! Play solo or with family and friends, up to 4 players in split-screen local multiplayer game mode. Try to beat every Smurf at their own racetrack in the “Time Challenge” mode and reach the top of the online rankings with your best time! Unlock original bonuses race after race, win after win, and try to Smurf them all in your personal album!

name: Trinity Fusion
detailed_description: Take control of your parallel selves on a mission to save the dying multiverse. Explore dark, sci-fi worlds and engage in fast-paced, smooth and precise combat. A rogue-lite journey through the multiverse The various branches of the multiverse are always changing. Fight through a combination of procedurally-generated levels as well as hand-crafted challenges and arenas that will put your skills to the test. Levels with 3D graphics are seamlessly constructed out of hundreds of custom-made rooms. High-intensity combat With weapons and attack systems that leverage our previous experience working on fighting games. You’ll slide, dash and dodge between enemy attacks and strike back with an arsenal of satisfying special weapons and abilities. Three characters, three universes to explore Each of your parallel selves has their own world with multiple biomes to explore, as well as their own sets of unique abilities and weapons. Travel through a universe of desolate wastes and caverns roamed by mutant creatures, escape the endless forges and labs of a world ruled by machines, and survive the dangerous sky cities of a post-human society. Constant Progression Unlock permanent upgrades in the Hub and discover new starting points for your run as you reclaim major locations in each universe. Finding yourself getting stuck in one area? Start your next run in a different one! No matter where you die, or which starting point you pick, you're making progress somewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this on Skill Up's "Put this on your radar" section. I'm glad I saw it.So far enjoying it. Plays like dead cells. Feels smooth and responsive. Still in early access and could do with a little polish but otherwise really good. Addictive and gives me that magic feeling you get when you want to play just one more time to push further after a death.Fun.Plays great on PC with high frame rates.Just tried it on Steam Deck. There are graphics settings with a quality setting specifically for the deck. However, I've found (so far) that I can crank up the settings with no detriment to the performance, although battery life is slightly impacted. I at least recommend low shadows as the game loses something without them.Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I had been trying to decide on a metroidvania to scratch that itch...after roughly 2 days of research, I am so glad I decided on this game.  Even in early access, I see the vision.  The polish is pretty much there.  Got it on sale, and would assume this is worth it at full price as well.Edit:After 7 hours, I can't recommend this game enough!  It is EXACTLY what I was looking for, and it feels like it's going to be the Hades-type "Game of the year" contender when it's complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Trinity Fusion is a lot like Dead Cells, but with a more sci-fi theme and 3D models instead of pixel art.+ Fighting is fast and attacks feel punchy, but it can be a little clunky if you time your attack incorrectly.+ All the models and animations look great!+ Lots of variation in enemies, really fun to fight them!+ Abilities and powerups are nice, adds a lot of variation between runs.~ The game is not really clear about the difference between the three characters. One can double jump, one can walljump, one has a grappling hook. The grappling hook needs to be unlocked in a later stage, so until that time one character feels very weak.- Progression is also not quite clear, as far as I know you need to keep track of which bosses you defeated and the path to get there by yourself. This is especially confusing because every stage has two exits.- Some bosses are pretty annoying, move sets that are near impossible to dodge or impossible to beat  without a range weapon.Overall a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Trinity Fusion is a buttery smooth, action-packed bundle of awesome!  I've only played it for about 3 hours and I'm honestly hooked.  The game plays similarly to Dead Cells, but the fusion system is imaginative and fresh.  It is apparent that the devs draw big influence from games like Hollow Knight, Dead Cells, and the Metroid series, and I am 100% here for it.  Love those games, Love this game.  There is also "Streamer Mode" which gives your chat the ability to choose your Amplifiers and Curses, super pumped to give that a try!  I can't wait to see what the devs have up their sleeves for Q1 of 2024.  (If they see this, keep up the good work, yall are amazing and have created something I'll play constantly)
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely an under-appreciated gem, in the vein of Dead Cells / Rogue Legacy / Skul et al. TLDR: It's an absolute cracker of a 2D roguelite action platformer in a sci-fi setting with some incredible visuals and fun, new mechanics.Visually it's amazing; some of the enemy animations are just insanely detailed and they're all smooth (wait until you encounter the "juggernaut" robot mobs, they're _gorgeous_ models). Sound design also stands out, particularly with the mechanised enemies.Challenging without being frustrating, and there's a ton of builds to try out (and I've only used the one character and one fusion so far). There's some interesting and novel mechanics at play here too. Between these mechanics and the sheer number of build options already present, combat feels tight and varied every run.If you like roguelite platformers even a little bit, Trinity Fusion is already worth purchasing in early access.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Seems more like a proof of concept at this point as there's a lack of story or progression.  So, it seems cobbled together and disjointed.  It's like a cross between Dead Cells (upgrade system) and hack and slash sidescrollers.  I'm not sure medtroidvania is appropriate.  Graphically, it looks OK. The videos at this point are misleading as they make the game look much more detailed than it is.  NotesYou have a melee weapon and a secondary weaponPretty tight controlsDouble jumpTitle screen is very basic (I just mention this because it feels like it cheapens the game)Apparently there's three characters (hence Trinity...)Music is OKNo ultrawide screen supportRight now, it definitely needs more time to cook.  I think this has potential though, but not at it's current price point.  It's a thumbs sideways, but more positive than negative.

The gameplay is not responsive, everything has a delay, and is very floaty (jumping, attacking, etc).And nothing is clear; when you select or fuse with a character, you don't see their stats or ability, or what world you are going to. _childDocuments_.review: It's an ok roguelike/metroidvania but extremely buggy. You get permanent traversal abilities from beating bosses, but several players on the forums have reported bugs where the traversal abilities inexplicably disappear after getting them, leaving the player unable to progress. This appears to have been reported for months with no real response or fix from the developers. The exact same thing happened to me. The game was decent up to the point that my progress was halted by this game-breaking bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Identity crisis! The game is playable and within reach of a polished offering, but the presentation can't mask the flawed core. It seems that the core gameplay was never clearly established and stuck to, and each feature that was tacked-on pulled it in a different direction. A slew of nonsensical design decisions early on made it tedious to play and player-punishing for no reason other than to frustrate players. It's a cobbled together pile of features that still doesn't know what it wants to be, but the definite answer is not "FUN". Play Dead Cells :)
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a lot of things right. This is the only rouge-lite that I have stuck with because this game is very good.- Being that its a “metroidvania” style, there is not a steep curve in platforming as the run progresses. The levels are enough the same that you don’t feel like you are having to go through 15 minutes of pretty easy gameplay in order to get to the same part you died at last time. Might be a negative in some people’s eyes, but this encourages me to play another run instead of thinking about having to play for however long before I get a chance to play the hard parts (just to die again lol).- Abilities/items are scattered throughout levels instead of only getting them at the end of levels. This makes you feel continually stronger as you go.- The designers give an option for your defense to go up with every failed run (Hyper mode I think its called). WHAT A GREAT IDEA. This might be the most important reason I will keep playing this game. I don’t have to spend hours and hours dying at the same spots until I get better. With every run, I get better and it gets a little easier because of the defensive increase notwithstanding the other upgrades you can buy in between runs. For players that want a harder experience, this option can be turned off.- The combat has a good feel. Yes, you are often hitting the same button over and over again, but the attacks are slow enough so you aren’t quickly button mashing, yet fast enough that it feels good.- Enemy attacks are fair. Sure, there are a few times where enemies can gang up and you get bounced around taking a lot of damage before having a chance to do anything. But almost every time I get hit its my fault because I didn’t time the attack right to dodge or parry.- The designers keep putting out free DLC and improvements. The content keeps increasing and its a good quality.There are some things you could nitpick about the game if you wanted, but the overall experience is polished and a lot of fun. As I said at the beginning, this game does a lot of things right and it is worth your time. I would definitely encourage fans of the genre and those that want to try a rouge-lite with a metroidvania feel to play it.
