_childDocuments_.review: A bold rogue-lite with enjoyable combat but some major kinks that could have been better. The grind for upgrades is pretty bad considering that some essential's like parrying are locked behind it. It's not just about power, the game quite literally feels unfinished and doesn't gel well untill you are down the upgrades a bit. Without synergies between the weapon traits, upgrade stations before bosses etc. the game feels empty this will forever sour my first impression of it. Some enemy designs are pretty good and mesh well, others are outright bad. For the amount of projectiles the game throws at you in some arenas I expect no cooldown on my parry or directional dashing. Speaking of the arenas:I am not sure how the game algorythm works, but the enemy groups seem to be picked halfhazardly. Sometimes you are trashing through an entire map against basic enemies, other times you end up in arena-enemy combinations that feel annoying and out of place. More care needs to be put in encounter design for the future and more arena combinations/map variety is a must.Even with those issues I can still recommend it, since the combat really clicks after a while and the moment to moment flow is very enjoyable. I hope Angry Mob Games will reflect on what worked and what didn't to make a potential sequel truely great.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy companion to Dead Cells. While there are a few bugs and the platforming/combat isn't quite as smooth, I'm enjoying TF just as much as I did DC with some aspects I find more enjoyable. I'll update my review once I've completed the game.Just finished this last night. I mostly enjoyed it and I think it does bring something a little different to the roguelite action platformer genre with the blend of character's abilities and a decent combination of melee and ranged weapons. I also really like the perks system and the randomization of them and weapons can sometimes turn you into an overpowered juggernaut able to take down standard enemies in 2 hits and groups of enemies in no time. I do think there is room for improvement though.Pros:- Decent variety of weapons and attributes, though not nearly the amount given in DC- I love the perks system. Combing them with certain weapon attributes can make you feel super strong.- Combat is pretty smooth with only minor complaintsNeutral:- Story is very copy-paste.Cons:- A few bugs. There were times when certain attributes would not do what they said they would and I'd have to restart. I also experienced a few crashes on loading, and action inputs not working (though that only happened once).- I think the aerial combat needs a lot of work around melee weapons. Yes you've got a grapple hook but the actions of it are inconsistent and it did not work on at least 2 bosses I remember.- "Evade" window for effects to be applied is way too narrow IMO. I can dodge during the start animations of an enemy's attack and not have it applied. It might be the difficulty setting but I think that window should be the same regardless of difficulty.- Permanent upgrades cost too much. I put 20 hours in and still a lot of stuff wasn't unlocked which is a little disappointing.If you're a fan of the action roguelite, I'd say it's definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Average metroidvania roguelike. The game in normal dificulty isa good starting points for newcomers to the genre, veteran is more suited for ppl used to it or can be quite easy, beating bosses and progressing the story before intended. And then there is the 3º dificulty option for biger challenge runs.I enjoy it but sadly the metaprogresion is slow enough to make it repetitive, even when there are a good amount of diferent biomas, they barely change from one visit to another, having only a couple of changes betwen runs. But as said, is compensated with a large number of diferent biomas.Enemy variety is good and most of them have their own particuliaritys, bosses feels good too. but idk how many are there yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS FIRE!! Takes me back to the old days of Sega Genesys Rogue styles. This one just more modern. While there are some things I would change, I won't list them here because it truly doesn't matter. The game is good as it is IMO and I'll be waiting for the expansions and sequels coming in the future. Good work..
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I started out really enjoying this game! The fighting, abilities, being able to traverse by grabbing up walls, or being able to parry- oh sorry that's no longer part of the standard combat abilities. I've been  really hooked-until I started noticing some interesting events as I progressed. Below are just a few and I haven't bothered to proofread this so know that as you go in. Most of the skills are insignificant and confusing. Gain a 3% chance to do 5% damage with alt weapon while jumping above enemies who have been hit with elemental and are at or below 10% health.   While you are in Citadel, you have the ability to chat  with NPCs who give you stat chance increases or minor abilities, for you. You'd think they would be permanent Nope you have a power gauge to use certain number of skills-Parry being the MOST EXPENSIVE ability to equip.  weapons at the end of a subsection cost too much to afford most of the time. if you were not able to obtain a high enough level weapon for the next stage, you end up not being able to do enough damage to enemies. countless times have I lost almost all health because of a triple team up of unavoidable attacks by enemies because I can't dish out enough damage before another enemy becomes aggroed-and that is on the Survivor mode!offensive/defensive consumables pale in comparison to health quick slot. Most are severely under powered and feel meaningless to bother obtaining. If you find health, you have to use the previous health consumable before you can obtain it. Not being able to properly aim and hold yourself properly sometimes does not aim the way you'd expect and you end up wasting shots.  This happening with said 3 enemy gang ups a lot of times, causing you to get trapped in 3 hit combo by enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: My first time playing this type of game and I'm really enjoying it. The controls, music, visuals are all awesome. This game is great. I play it on my gaming laptop as well as my Steamdeck. Very smooth gameplay and it's easy to get lost after a couple of hours of playthrough. Good Job Developers. Keep up the good work and the content coming!
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: For a platformer it managed to pull me out of my nerves several times, especially with 3 of the achievments...Hardcore mode - 1 playthrough - this is insane...  you have hp as well as max 5 hits (that recharge on mob kill + 1).. also the mobs get buff on a time period... The in between doesn't help that much honestly on hardcore... insane.. and you need to kill at least 2 bosses ... The other 2 achievements seem to be a bit bugged - the kill 3 mobs with glitch dash and the kill a mob with dash effect... the later one i managed to do with burning weapon and the exposives that stick on the mob after perfect dash... it didn't work only with the dash.. the mob burned and it gave the achv.Overall:gameplay - 8/10story - 6.5/10mobs - 9/10 - hate them buggersachievements 7/10 - doable .. kindaeffects - 7/10 - the purple balls that the flying ones shoot are a bit invisble on some parts of the map due to the brightness of the background.. as well as the ice spikes of the drones - this may need to be checkedWorth playing - Yes!Good platformer - Yes!Should you try it if you like platformers? - Bet, definitely
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: The game is ok! I like the idea behind it, 3 characters with semi-distinct abilities sharing a connection in a roguelike/metroidvania, however, playing the game does feel a bit clunky, and I think it comes down to feedback. Did I evade that attack? Am I losing my health? Am I locked into these attack animations?These could use some polish, but I think if you're interested in another roguelike (with metroidvania-style platforming and level design) with cool melee and ranged weapons, this game can scratch that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: - Fully playable on Steam Deck - Gotta say that I bought this game on a whim, after reading another review that said the combat has the same flow of Dead Cells, and it's actually true. It's fast-paced and very challenging, where the foes AI act in a very aggressive way, but not in a cheap manner, allowing the player to act accordingly. Although I said that the difficulty per se doesn't feel cheap, one thing that bothers me slightly is how enemy bullets and bombs can pass through platforms and doors, but even so the game offers specific boons and other tools that help dealing with this kind of situation. In terms of level design and visuals in general, I like it a lot actually. Very futuristic setting, but not exactly flashy and neon-ish, which is actually a plus because I can see what's going on in the screen without being overwhelmed by flashing lights or way too colorful backgrounds and whatnot. And the soundtrack, even though it's more on a weaker side, offers a nice ambiance to it, allowing the player to explore the maps for hours without feeling annoyed.  I can't say much about the end game content, since this is merely a first-hours review, but I'm very satisfied with everything that Trinity Fusion is offering.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: They ask for a review so here we go.Its a good combat Focused Roguelike, controls and graphics are clean, areas look good. Weapons are varied enough to provide interest. The Higher of the two difficulty settings is actually difficult, ressources are kinda sparse. Sometimes i feel like getting a good weapon end/start of biomes is toooooooo crucial for the flow of the game, maybe there is some wriggle room for scaling nuances.I feel that the whole Storyline is a bit... disjointed so far (yeah great joke haha) but i honestly wish for a bit more guidance to where i am supposed to focus my efforts to make progress, it is not at all obvious to me. It just gets dumped on you at some point (or i missed interactions not honestly sure) Or maybe i just play so bad that the higher difficulty is slowing me so much I don't know.Anyhow if you like some decent cutting up of foes, this can be given a try for sure
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t played many roguelites, but I enjoyed the ones that I have played (Hades, Darkest Dungeon 1 and 2, Dead Cells), and while there are some flaws here and there, I can safely say that this is another that I liked as well.The gameplay is very fun to play, specially once you start to understand how to take advantage of the fusion mechanic, combining weapons and abilities. There is a good variety of enemies, and while the game can be hard, is not unfair and you can clear everything once you realize how to play, even if you have bad luck with amplifiers.In terms of graphics, the designs and visual aspects are good, with a unique look for each faction, but some human faces don’t look right, specially as they don’t move their mouth. However, given the indi nature and being a small team, I can forgive that.The story and the characters are ok, but nothing groundbreaking, although it has some interesting characters and I like the dynamic of the  Selves having very different personalities. I did genuinely like the lore, but I feel that it was a bit hard to find and it would have been better to find it in the Citadel, maybe as we progress the story.I did have a couple of bugs, one in the Amalgam where my character was unable to do anything (I could go to menus) and the enemies ignore me, forcing me to reboot the game. And another, in the same area, that was a crash. But on the rest it was a very fluid experience.So in summary, while it is not a perfect game, is an enjoyable one that did not bore me during my playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful futuristic locations, smooth and accurate controls, teleports placed correctly. Those ambient sounds (influenced from Blade Runner and Deus Ex) evoke a sense of loneliness and epicness. Tough at first but acquiring and combining multiple significant powerups will make each ride very enjoyable. A fantastic game overall and a very polished one.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play Roguelike's (bought it when I had a few beers) but this one got under my skin, the mechanics are so smooth, makes the combat a joy to learn.  Levelling up can sometimes be a grind and probably should have been balanced a bit more.The bosses are not too difficult, the difficulty comes from trying to get to the boss area with enough health & upgrades to slay them.I would highly recommend just on the combat alone, really enjoyed that aspect.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Updated 2 minutes after review: What I said earlier still stands, but they are releasing free DLC, it is only $20 full retail and they put a lot of heart into it. Still wait for a sale, and know what you are getting into.Original review: I wanted to, but here are the reasons I did not:1. Weak story2. Repetitive 3. Great ideas that fall short and lead to a "meh" experience. 4. They literally beg for a good review.There are "3" characters, but really they are basically the same with some minor differences. The combat is simple and fun enough for the first 10 hours or so. I beat it on hard mode and it was challenging at first, but I got to credits in only 14 hours. The game is just meh. If you get it on sale and just are really hankering for a metroidvania, then yeah, it is worth it. In most other cases, there are just a lot of better games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play it the more I like it, it's good but maybe it's not for everyone.  It has a lot going for it but I'm sort of weary about the action roguelike genre where you gain power through repeated attempts.  I wouldn't really call it metroidvania either because the obstacles that block you from accessing different zones are nonexistent.  You just need to find the door and there are no powerups beyond power scaling that allow you to do that.  I do think the music, effects, and look of the worlds are cool and each of the three characters have a unique playstyle.The story is very cool and it has a really good beastiary too which means a lot to me.  Gameplay is smooth and I like the mechanic of playing 3 different characters who can potentially merge to become stronger.  As with most games that have powerups, there are winners and losers.  For me, I'd say powerups like "glass cannon" are essential to progress which can suck if you don't get the necessary ones early enough, making a run pointless.  This is probably the biggest drawback to the game.  However, there are clear signs of passion and devotion from the dev team and that's endearing for me.If you like this kind of genre then I'd say it's a good buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I am a really big fan of side scrolling Rlite games and this one is quite fun.  I haven't found anything yet that I have a problem with.  Good graphics, good loot, good progression, cool idea about being able to meld toons together while you are going through the levels.  The power ups are good the skill tree is good.  Looks like in the skill tree you can unlock the ability to more effectively put together "builds" like running an all acid build or fire etc....  and not be married to random rolls and drops of weapons but this is something I am still looking into.  If it turns out that I am wrong then that is definitely something they would need to add to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Plays well, looks good. Needs work on tutorial as travelsal skills weapons and abilities are not very well presented and/or explained. lots of walking around to just find the way forward. I'm still confused what I need to do in the main hub after I die... Buy skills and items, boost my ability and weapons ? How where and when with what materials and currency and where to find it ... No clue.Still solid gameplay and awesome graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I love Metroidvanias. I love bashing my head against a single boss that is extremey hard and needs 50+ pulls to get it perfect. While I am generally not a big fan of Roguelites like Hades (partly because I got into controller based input very late in my life, and I like the aspect of a very tough boss with save points as I come from World of Warcraft Mythic raid background), Trinity Fusion has been a good experience so far. At the end of the day, it has a good balance bringing some aspects of Metroidvanias into Roguelites (not having to slog through tough levels just to reach the boss with almost no health and make absolutely no progress). While I would never recommend a Roguelite over a Metroidvania, it has been a fun experience playing Trinity Fusion.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAMEEEi had this on my wish list thinking ohh its just another platformer made by some devs.. I WAS WRONG!!this game is incredibly funnnnnn to play, at first it was super hard but keep on playing its ok to lose and try again.. this experience in unlike any other, big thanks to the dev team making me love gaming againpros:- great soundtrack - characters are interesting and fun - gameplay is funnnn- bosses are unique - many weapon combos - i really loved the storyline and the cyber apocalyptic worlds- the background art and enviroment is just something elsecons: - the final boss was a huge disapointment... it was easy and boring - wish the ending was different (my ending: all Maya alternatives disappear accept the one you were playing as and Sendara living with the pain of losing og Maya) - the Melee alternative should have a shield as a heavy weapon option - sadly no character animation during the cut scenes that would have been soo cool - you should be able to buy weapons for the character you fused with and have items drop for them
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun rogue-lite with an innovative "fusion" system which allows you to combine advantages of the 3 protagonists.  Each one plays similar enough to not alienate you, but different enough that you can tell they're different.  Things like double-jump (or not) and wall-cling (or not) help them to feel different and make interesting choices when you decide which ones to fuse.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for the first time during Pax East a few years ago.  Of all the games I played, this one stood out the most, even though it was in very early beta.  I love metroidvanias like this: The initial failure is harsh, but you get better over time, bit by bit, and end up doing stuff that really impresses yourself.  Sometimes, you just get on a run that makes no sense, and you plow through enemies like they're nothing, and others you just try super hard and fail in no time flat.  The variety and variability in runs makes this like seeing the game through fresh eyes every time.  Replayability is getting better, and better, and more and more fun.  In the time since my first play through at Pax, there has been so much world building, story development, and variety in the 3 main characters.  There's even more coming, meaning that I'm about to put a LOT of hours into this game.  Keep it up, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun side-scroller. I haven't been paying attention to the story - something about multiverses, engineers, and harmonizers? And what exposition there is sounds like it was voiced by Tannis from Borderlands, so I keep expecting some sarcastic quip from the science lady. Anyway, the music is rad. The art and animation are silky smooth and top-notch. Some parts could use some polish though - like it's not clear when or how you get the grappling hook, or drone. Also seeing which character has what before you merge would be helpful. Progression feels a little too open-ended and unclear about which characters get what and how. Which some balancing fixes and little more guidance, this game could be great.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: The game's obsession with putting enemies right at the top of ladders or on the edges of platforms aside, I enjoyed my time with this game. It started out tough, but eventually I got into a groove and managed to beat it on the Veteran difficulty without lowering it or using the Hyper Mode at any point. The game is visually impressive with tight controls and a decent variety of combat tools. It's short but not so short that I felt I didn't get my money's worth. I probably won't bother with higher difficulties as I think I've seen enough and the weapon variety isn't enough to compel me to take it any further right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: solid game!! especially for such a small team!! i am a big fan of rouge like games coming from titles like dead cells and when well done they make for hours of fun and a good challenge to boot. this game is a strong contender in the genre for sure. really creative worlds, awesome weaponry and power ups, and very satisfying combos make for a great time so far. also to story is pretty interesting and leaves you wanting to unlock its secrets. definitely gonna be putting some time into this one :)
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game at version 1.2 without real expectations and mostly for the tag "metroidvania". Trinity Fusion is much more of a "rogue lite" with some exploration than anything else, hower. It has quite some potential to entertain. The following critics are in consideration of the team size (4 people) and the problems connected to it:First off, the game is full of flaws, design errors, numerous translation/localization mistakes (german) and the level design has some questionable decisions. I don't want to list it all because I don't get paid for QA and working on the game. The efforts made by Angry Mob Games are great, though. It deserves respect.Yes, Trinity Fusion can be some fun when you don't expect perfection. Although I am close to calling the controls near perfect. The graphics are somewhere between good and fair. It's stable, solid and there are no troublesome bugs. In fact, the game has a nice cyberpunk / sci-fi setting and the concept itself is promising. You will encounter enough variation, randomness and options to adapt the game to your taste. There's alot of fighting regular and "veteran" units and it's doing a good job. The boss design could use some improvements but they are okay. If "rogue lite" is your favorite style, you might like Trinity Fusion for a change and give it a try.Unfortunately, you cannot choose weapons and skill trees. You get a random selection at each start. New weapons are either random drop or the choice 1 of 3 for skills. While unpredictable pattern can add some spice, the chaotic tendency can be very draining. I also miss some functionality of the area for choosing characters, doing upgrades and so on. That area is one big and time consuming graphic blender. Yes, it looks cool but it has some errors and it doesn't really help the game. It would be better of with a functional and pretty menu instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so great! I am very glad that I found it!It is a nice action 2.5D platformer with algorithm-generated levels. Unlike many other similar games, this one has several distinct advantages:1. The enemies and weapons are very diverse. As you play through the game,  the enemies change almost every 10-15 minutes. 2. I really like the "hyper mode" which decreases the game difficulty. I do not want a souls-like experience, I just want to crush some beasts for fun, and this "hyper mode" is perfect for me. I wish "Elden ring" had a similar "loser switch"!3. There is only little platforming, only few sections in which you have to jump here-and-there with perfect timing. When I played "Grime", some platforming sections made me crazy, and in "Trinity fusion" you find platforming only in the Lands in-between, and the puzzle are simple. Perfect for me :)))4. The overall flow of the game is nice. You run, meet the enemies, smash them alternating your weapons, and repeat the cycle. Just what I want!5. It is relatively easy to avoid damage. Only few enemies can get you if you are above the floor (in mid-air or on a ladder). You have evasion and parry. The enemy moveset is predictable. However, the combat is both challenging and fun.Overall, "Trinity fusion" is a very nice game. I strongly recommend this game to everyone who likes action platformers and metroidvania-like games.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: It's more a rogue-lite than metroid-vania, though as you progress you gain new abilities that get you access to areas of the map that you couldn't get to before. You'll obviously need to replay it a couple of times to get to all the secret areas. Combat is smooth and the comparison to Dead Cells is fair. They made more combat abilities which means more options to win your fights, if you can manage fiddling your controller to activate the right things at the right time. Weapons are well designed, though I'd like to see more differences in playstyle between them. Again, think Dead Cells or Spiritfall. Overall, I like it
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, first one I put on my steamdeck and I find I play it more than any other game. Sometimes I feel there's so much, with 3 different characters as I've still felt like playing 2 of them and just keep playing the same one. But with randomly generated levels it never seems to get old. It's a great game for my busy life, especially paired with a steamdeck, as I can pick it up and play a round or two and then easily(well not so easily as I have lost a couple hours unintentionally before) put it down and go on with whatever I need to do. It does have a downside or two, which for me is that with it being so new it's hard to find any tips, how to's, or guides to help me out with some of the power up choices. But it's not so hard that I can't figure it out, just with a busy life sometimes it's nice to get a little bit of help to get the most out of the game. I can't recommend this enough, I played Hollow Knight on the switch, and then Deadcells on my phone, and got Trinity Fusion on a whim since it was supposed to be like Deadcells, and like I said pairs perfect with the steamdeck. I do find myself playing this more than Deadcells, or Hollow Knight, though I haven't hit the total playtime for Hollow Knight yet, I'm sure it won't be far away.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy rogue-likes/-lites from time to time, post Dead Cells & Hades just couldn't enjoy anything as much until now. Trinity Fusion looks good, sounds fine and game-play wise mixes the Metroidvania and Rogue-Like genres perfectly (my PoV). If you like fair combat design with multiple starting paths and an interesting mix of characters this is definitely worth every penny. Keep up the great work, Angry Mob Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest, the entire concept of 'The Multiverse' has worn extremely thin on me. And my initial expectations were not good, but it had a demo, still one of the only reasons i ended up buying it. Story wise, even though i'm not done with the story, i already appreciate the concept they're going for. It's not the cringe inducing swill i thought it would be, i.e: 'haha totally endless multiverses bro we're all just apes on a floating rock nothing matters haha BUUURRRP' Maya's alternate selves are well-thought out, and i warmed to the idea much faster than i expected to. It's a joy to see the mechanics blended with the story in a mature way. The mechanics felt a little clunky at first, it's true when the game starts appearing in souls-like categories for being stuck in animations and having to commit to attacks. But, once you get the basics down, the experience becomes very fluid. I appreciate the thoughtful blend of rogue-lite and souls-like mechanics. My favorite feature is the drawback items, in this game 'cursed loot'. The curse isn't permanent, and gives a nasty debuff with a quest to kill enemies in a specific way to lift the curse, and keep the reward. I can imagine doing a run where you have three or four curses at a time, and have to prioritize cursebreak quests making the entire run feel that much more fresh, i've already had two on at a time. Overall good game, good choices and good mechanics, look forward to seeing what comes next. My only tiny gripe with anything is the 'feedback' tab taking you to discord, but i'm just a grognard that wants to have old-school forums back, so it's not really anything you'll probably care about.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania(ish) game with upgrades ala Vampire survivors (a choice of 3 at different stations rather than leveling). The game is VERY similar to Dead Cells but with different (very pretty) graphics and a more Sci-fi setting than what DC had. If you liked Dead Cells you will like this. It doesn't have near the content that DC has butit is newly released and there is a big content upgrade coming this quater (Q1 2023) according to the devs. I'm excited for it and cant wait to check it out. The only downsides I can think of are the tools you unlock (like in any metroidvania) are just kind of glossed over or not made out to be a big deal and arent really pointed out what all they unlock when you get them. I had zero idea I could use the blue ords with this teleport ability I unlocked and, likewise, was unaware for a good while that I was in possession of the handy drone that also could teleport me to impossible to reach spots. This wasn't really a big deal though. The only thing truly bothering/confusing me is what the point of fusing with other characters is. I now know to fuse with the character who has the drone so I can use that on my others but is that the only reason for it besides unlocking the other characters secondary attack weapon also? I just wish it was a little more fleshed out or at least described in MORE DETAIL on what its for and why/when I should do it.Like I said though, the game is still excellent and I highly recommend it. It's only 4 devs on the team for this so this is very impressive for such a small team. Can't wait for the content upgrade!
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: My first game was the original Super Mario Bros. but I took a "platformer" break for about twenty years.  Now, I'm back.  Trinity Fusion is a platformer in the style of a "souls-lite" game with a Sci-fi "Vampire Survivors" aesthetic.Loot and some enemies are random.  The levels themselves change slightly or flip.  Gameplay is tight and smooth like a [______].  Movement feels like Smash Bros.  Great sound score.  The different Weapons and attacks also remind me of [For Honor.]  Bosses and levels are challenging with a variety of difficulty and doesn't feel like cheap shots occur.  Power-ups and leveling are substantial.  There is a multiverse of platforming levels and three versions of the character, with separate abilities you combine.Additional content enroute.  The Mario Bros. smoke a crack pipe to feel this good.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying playing so far, lots of weapon variety and powers. Great art and voices too. I really love how stylish every zone is so far. Looking forward to the first big patch! I want to see where the story goes, the premise (and waifus) is what got me to buy the game.I'm still unable to win a run on the lowest difficulty but i'm usually a turn based / mmo player so my action game skills are low. The runs are still fun though, I'm glad you can remap skills ingame as they change from run to run.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: Trinity Fusion is not unlike Rogue-like games inspired by Dead Cells. In fact, in many ways you could say this game is a very light version of Dead Cells.Just like Dead Cells, it has some metroidvania-esque abilities to unlock to help improve travelling, and it also has the usual rogue-like you can expect in that sort of game, such as various upgrades to permanently unlock and extra passive abilities to use.Gameplay-wise, the game is very smooth and pretty responsive. There is a relatively decent variety of enemies as well.Graphics-wise, it's looks quite great too, with each enemy type and regions being quite unique in their appearance.It has a relatively simple story, with the neat fact that it takes a little bit of inspiration from Hades in the way that you can have conversations with NPCs in the hub area each time you come back from a run.  Not always though. It should be noted that since you technically can play as 3 parallel versions of the main character, each of them have a different personality and will definitively give them different conversations with the NPCs when you return from a run. So for those interested to trying to get as many tidbits of conversations, that's a thing you can go for.Also I think it bears mentioning. This is not a really big game overall. But it seems the four devs that worked on this game are planning to add extra content down the line.So if you feel like wanting a bit of a shorter kind of Dead Cells-esque game, that's a game you can pick up. And at least the price tag definitively reflects the smaller size of the game. So I'd say you should be getting your worth in money spent. Or wait for a sale. Your choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Trinity Fusion

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Refreshingly funIt took a bit of ramping up, but it's a lot of fun to smash through enemies with all kinds of crazy combos. Quite smooth.I very much enjoyed the scenery. Some of the music really stands out. I also enjoyed the lore even though I didn't find main plot even a little intriguing.It's not a long game and could use some refinement. But the fun I had was well worth the purchase, especially at the relatively low price point.

Enough story to hold interest as you progress through the runs. Fun finding lore bits or hidden rooms. Lots of fun combinations of getting augments during a run. Cons: Really bad luck HURTS. Enemies scale with power level but you have to find weapons to match it. There are still some bugs that can end runs, mostly going out of bounds.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun rougelike game with great replayability and that "one more run before going to bed" loop, which is a winner for a game like this. The combat is fluid once you learn its rythm. All 3 characters revolve around melee and ranged weapons and spells with each having strengths and weaknesses offering a more varied gameplay. Fans of Dead Cells or Skul will feel at home. Two hours in as of writing the review and I am still unsure how the fusion of characters works, but I am eager to find out in my future playthroughs. The levels are procedurally generated for the most part and there are currently 3 biomes as far as I've seen. You have your standard meta progression and upgrades for the current run. I read that some other players complained about character upgrades during runs being rather boring, and I'd say it's your standard rougelike ordeal. What surprised me most is that this game has cut scenes and it's fully voice acted, which is rather unusal in this genre, but a welcome addition nonetheless.Most importantly, the game is fun and addictive and with the devs' promise of adding more content I can only look forward to investing more time into this little gem. I am unsure about the ''metroidvania'' tag as it may confuse a lot of people expecting something like Blasphemous, Ori, Last Faith or Grime.

_childDocuments_.review: Loads of fun. Took me roughly 45hrs to get all achievements. Well worth the asking price. Weapons, combat and movement are satisfying (like a 7/10). Movement in 2.5D games is sometimes hard to get right but this is pretty solid and feels good. Decent variety of melee weapons and guns to finish the game. For more replayability you'd probably want more for variety. Endless mode is a nice addition. I was glad it was there for a few extra hours of play. But it can become monotonous so it might not appeal to everyone. The items you pick up on runs are satisfying and not just simple stat increases. If you've played roguelites like Fallback Uprising or Deflector, the items function a lot like those games in the sense that the items are less about deep, specific synergies and more like they're just good to have regardless of build. For example, if you wanted to create a high damage/attack build, you can pick all the attack items but you'll still have a ton of slots for health, crit, energy and retaliation items. You'll be able to pick up the majority of items every run (which can feel samey) but it will never negatively affect your build.

name: Atari Mania
detailed_description: 150 levels of microgame madness! Play as your favorite Atari characters as you solve puzzles, vanquish foes and race your way through lightning-fast mini games and boss battles based on classic Atari games. Key Features Play as Pete, the gunslinger from Outlaw Mashups : Levels based on Asteroids, Circus Atari, Dodge’ Em, Missile Command, Yars' Revenge and many more combine and twist into tons of crazy new games. Puzzles: You won’t get far if you cannot solve some tricky puzzles using tools you find along the way, and some smart thinking. Easter Eggs: Special surprises are hidden throughout the game. Find them all and collect trophies along the way. Chiptunes: Groove to a propulsive soundtrack of retro-inspired chiptune jams.

short_description: A wild journey through videogame history, Atari Mania is a microgame collection wrapped in a hilarious retro-driven narrative of exploration and surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to give this game a bad review, I was really looking forwards to it. But this is just not worth the money, at least not at the moment.I was expecting to play a game that I could have fun for hours and hours, like the classic Atari games it's based on. But it just has nowhere near the replay value of those. The concept is great, I liked the idea of a microgame collection based on Atari games, but the exeuction just... lame. Yes, there are around 150 microgames here, but they are really short and they have no replay value individually. Some of them change a little bit each time you play, but the change is so minimal it's barely noticeable.Atari devs from back in the day used to talk about how randomness is really important for the replayability of a game, and it's really ironic that this wasn't really taken into consideration here. Once you've played a microgame 2 or 3 times, you know how to beat it each time, whenever the game doesn't glitch out or the controls don't work, of course (yes, the glitches are minor, but when you're playing games that last for seconds and you can't afford mistakes, it is quite noticeable). And the thing is, even if there are many microgames, many of them are just slight variations of one another, I mean, I've lost count of how many Pong variations there are. Sure, you get to play as different characters and stuff, but it doesn't make much of a difference.Some of the minigames are also so easy to beat, like, just press the button a couple times at the start and you've won. Great...The "caretaker" section of the game isn't that great either. There isn't much to do aside from getting to section to section. You solve some puzzles but they're pretty mindless, and there's an attempt at exploration by locking certain sections with items that you find later on, but it's so simple it's barely anything worth noting. You can't interact with the scenary around you, and the characters you meet just repeat the same text once you're done with their cutscenes. A really big missed opportunity, it would've been so neat to learn about the games by talking to characters or inspecting furniture, but no. Nothing.And then there's the collection aspect. It's... barely worth mentioning, honestly. You can find box art lying around, and you get the manuals for the games if you beat the mice's minigames (which aren't unique at all, they're the same ones you play when fighting the bosses or when using the arcade machines). But... you can just easily find this stuff online. Like, great, I get to read the same manuals I've read over a hundred times already. Was it too much to ask to let us unlock the actual games this is supposed to be celebrating? Of course, that's reserved for the upcoming Atari 50 collection, no way they could've included it here!And this costs 20 bucks! That is, quite honestly, way too much for what this game has to offer. About 150 minigames that don't play that great, don't really look that great either (am I the only one who's really tired of this "neo-retro" style? It's just so generic and overused, I would've quite honestly rather get graphics based on the original games), and most of them are just slight variations of one another. You get to see boxart and manuals, which you've probably already seen a dozen times, and you don't even get to play the actual games. Until this drops in price, it's just not worth the asking price, I'm sorry.For 10 bucks it might be a good deal. But for this price you may aswell just get Atari Vault, where you actually get to play the games you see here. Without any time limits, without broken controls and collision, and you even get the manuals and boxart there too! I think I'll be getting a refund...Honestly, this game would've been better if it was just actual, full remakes of these original games. You know, without the time limits, with all the game modes and features of the games, not just simple microgames.

_childDocuments_.review: Sooner or later, you are going to realize the controls for nearly every mini game in this package are total garbage and that winning any of these games is 90% luck and 10% skill.  All the games are timed to only last seconds, requiring you to stay alive or defeat something before the timer hits zero.  These games would be awesome with a nice tournament stick, but the gamepad sticks, and D-pad are not responsive enough.  You’ll die or lose a lot and most of the time it will be control related.  When the game is working (when I’m not losing} Atari Mania is pretty fun, and with each mini-game lasting less than a minute there is definitely that “one more time” mentality.  The game randomizes the mini-games and their order if you do have to replay a boss fight, etc., so this adds a bit of luck to the equation if you are better at some mini-games than others.Read full review at - More Steam reviews on our Curator page -
_childDocuments_.name: Atari Mania

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game another compilation of emulated Atari VCS games? Or maybe some remakes of classic Atari VCS games? Absolutely not, this is a modern pixel art game, containing a large number of very short microgames, inspired by old Atari VCS games. You take the role of the caretaker in the Atari museum when something evil happens. It seems the museum is under attack by a dead pixel. You have to fight through the microgames to advance in the main game. The Atari VCS (Atari 2600) was the first really successful gaming console that ruled the world for many years (from 1977 to 1984) until the great industry crash. Hundreds of games were released, and many of these old games are featured with tiny action sequences (often mixing various games) in this game. Some of the old games were ports of coin-ups, but most were original cartridge games. You will meet some of the most famous characters from the games and have to save them from the dead pixel. The microgames are short, but not so easy.Play hundreds of tiny microgames inspired by VCS classics.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari Mania

_childDocuments_.review: The easiest way to sum up this game is that it's the atari version of warioware, where you play minigames based on classic atari games and/or combinations thereof.Although by any means it's definitely not a bad game it however does have a few problems:- It doesn't take very long to complete the entire game and unlock everything (however when you do you can always (re)visit the things you unlock, whether they be games or collectibles such as game covers and manuals)- what you're supposed to do in some minigames isn't always very clear at first, leading to a guaranteed loss- the controls in some of the minigames are very stiff and these minigames become very difficult merely for that very reason (although not a completely irrational decision by the devs, for it's based on remaining loyal to the original game, it's just that limiting controls doesn't fly very well with newer generations of players as is reflected by some of the reviews)- then some things about the game are just very tedious; such as for example when you go against the mice to unlock game manuals, whenever you lose you have to go back to get the cheese only to again give it to the mouse so you can play him again. There is no reason for why in some cases I have to keep walking back and forth a few rooms just to get the cheese and to play the mouse again because I keep losing. Especially considering the fact that the mouse only eats the cheese after you win. So as is the case with all the bosses in the game, I should just be able to step up to the mouse immediately and try again instead of having to walk back and forth over and over again.Likewise having an in game map displaying the locations of all the things in the rooms I have already went through (except for the game covers as they are supposed to be hidden), would have just made it more convenient. Instead of having to have to go through all the rooms to see if a mouse is located there.Furthermore I think it would have helped to give players a trial option for the minigames, which would have helped with the unintuitive nature of some of the minigames (since you could just try the minigame first before taking on an opponent), as against some opponents (particularly the mice) you have only 1 life, and so if you lose 1 minigame you have to try all over.So there are a bunch of somewhat annoying/frustrating elements in the game that could have easily been avoided.Other than that I think it would have been fun if they also added longer versions of each game that could have been unlocked. So for example you could have a crystals castles arcade where you could just play levels of crystal castles as an actual game, but based on the way it's presented in this game (so with the newer graphics and possibly levels in which they add elements from other games).So I can somewhat sympathise with some of the bad reviews, in that I think their reviews contain genuine grievances, even though I don't think it's actually a bad game. A game having some problems doesn't make it a bad game, and hence why I gave a positive review, while leaving some comments about things I hope the developers take into consideration.So overall; great addition to the atari library and great way to commemorate Atari's 50 year anniversary, it's just that some of the mechanics in the game could use some adjusting, while I also hope they add some more content in the way I described above.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari Mania

_childDocuments_.review: What, a WarioWare Atari style game!? Yeah well sortof. You do get mini games like WarioWare based on Atari games, but that's about all there is to compare.Pros:-Atari nostalgia.-Mini games like WarioWare, and the closest you can get to such a game on PC.Cons:-Biggest issue, NO ORIGINAL GAMES to unlock.-Crash/Bug often, every so few rounds especially with the arcades my screen went black, and had to restart the game.-The mini games are sort of linear, so in the arcades, if you are bad at 1 particular game in the end, you have to keep redoing the same easier ones in the beginning each time.-The mini games per set (3-4 games) are just slight variations of eachother, making it a bit boring.Sidenote:Some people say the game is hard, i am not an Atari pro, and didn't found it difficult at all, and completed the main game in about 5-6 hours? However the last few achievements, where you have to finish the arcades without dying once is a big big pain in the b..t, not because it's difficult but annoying, as with about 20 mini games you are mostly bound to make a mistake and thus it becomes a very tedious and long task.For the length of the game and what you not get (the original games) plus the bugs, this game is worth only half it's price.And then i would say wait on a sale or i think this will get bundled. About 5-7 euro and you will have a decent time. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Ashamed to admit I looked forward to this game. What I thought it would be about was a sim to unlock some cool Atari minigames -- 150 of them from the ads -- and yes, there are minigames that are sort of mashups of games we're familiar with but many of them look terrible. I mean Asteroids on the Atari 2600 is a visual improvement to what is seen in this. Why?Style? No.No scores anywhere? Really? Surely there must be some score on some games, yes? No. Without scores, no leaderboards. I see a key that looks like the one from Adventure? It unlocks a door for the custodian/caretaker to go to a new area to play more weak minigames. Don't get me started on the custodian/caretaker. Why is there an obsession with cleaning stuff in games in 2022? I mean we get Powerwash Simulator and then Arcade Paradise cleaning up junk and now we get it in Atari Mania? At least in those two games it made some sense, but what is some old Atari custodian doing cleaning up trash? How is that relevant here? I get it, include cleaning and gamers will flock to your game? Come on.This is one of the worst games of 2022 I've played.  I want to wash my memory of playing it and wait for the vastly better 50th anniversary where we can play actual Atari games not this mashup minigame mess.

_childDocuments_.review: My dad got me an Atari 2600 for my birthday when I was 10 years old and I spent hours playing this game. You had to use your imagination because the differences were huge from the cover art and the pixels on the TV screen. I liked that you could play any of the 100 games with different characters from all eras, like Asteroids, Breakout, Centipede, and Super Pong.I also like that it is not forgivable and when you lose you lose. The only thing is that the mini games are too short and easy to win after few tried. I also missed the old joystick game play; for example with the tanks and asteroid space craft, I find it was easier to control the original game than this version.The nice feature I like is that they mesh up the games into one. Like the tanks in a breakout game, or the spacecraft in Adventure layout etc.I loved the old games and I am glad they have brought back some of them. I was a kid in the 70s and they made me feel like a kid again.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun microgame collection with an interesting storyline attached. The dialogue is humorous and the characters have unique personalities. _childDocuments_.review: It's like NES Remix and the Warioware franchise but for Atari.  Really enjoyed it.My two biggest criticisms; 1. you can't play the original at all, or these "remastered" versions in any capacity aside from the microgame playlist format.  You can't just pick one to play it specifically, but that's pretty standard for the microgame genre.And 2.  some of the "remastered" versions are just a bit too remastered, in my opinion, and there is some inconsistency in how they looked.  Some games / environments / characters have some more definition but are still very much blocky pixelated early-mid 80s Atari graphics, but others are somewhat too detailed, as if they are from a different era entirely.Still had a lot of fun, found the games very enjoyable, and really liked finding all the classic cover art (which is gorgeous) and manuals.  Microgames; here for a good time, not a long time.Regarding other reviews complaints about controls?  Or supposedly too much luck / randomness involved?  I assure you, 100%, "skill issue".

_childDocuments_.review:
A wild journey through videogame history, Atari Mania is a microgame collection wrapped in an hilarious retro-driven narrative of exploration and surprise.

You play as the Caretaker of the Atari Vault, the storehouse of classic Atari games. One night, a dead pixel appears and soon enough, all heck breaks loose!!

Familiar and beloved games begin to warp, mutate and combine into a series of increasingly crazy challenges. It's up to you to fight back the pixels and other surprising villains, and restore order to the Vault!

name: Soccer Story
detailed_description: It's been a year since The Calamity™ tore apart the very foundations of soccer as we know it, and since then, Soccer Inc. has made dang well sure that not a soul has been allowed to even look at a soccer ball, let alone kick it. Soccer may have been banned across the world... but now there is hope! A magical soccer ball has chosen you , our Savior of Soccer! Soccer Story is a physics-driven adventure RPG, where every problem can be solved with your trusty magic ball. Along the way, you'll need to best bad guys in 1v1s, compete in a range of different sports (with your soccer ball, of course), and sometimes use your brain just as much as your balls In a world that has long forgotten The Beautiful Game, can you remind them why soccer is top of the table, and best the most formidable teams, including the local toddlers and a group of sharks? Drop your soccer ball and play anywhere! The world is full of goals, puzzles and secrets - it's up to you to find them! Play a single-player story full of quirky characters, quests, rogue refs and wacky soccer-adjacent sports Build your soccer career and do battle against the fiercest soccer teams like literal sharks, toddlers, old-age pensioners and ninjas Save soccer and restore peace and harmony to the world Grab a friend for a four-player local multiplayer match mode with a full roster of teams and animal captains Yes, Soccer Story has multiplayer matches too! Grab up to 3 friends, and convince them that soccer is the ultimate sport by challenging them to local multiplayer matches! With a whole host of teams and captains to choose from, find your personal playstyle and hold your own tournaments at home across the many pitches, from home matches at Soccertown to the vast Soccer Inc Stadium!

_childDocuments_.review: Game has some decent aspects going for it in the world design and content. I like the world's mechanics and the quests in general (though a bit heavy on the fetch quest side it also mixes it up with some well designed challenges). The soccer match gameplay though, is horrible. You spend most the match just dealing with it wrestling control away from you. If you get touched at all, you get stunned and lose the ball. Every time the ball changes owner, you get juggled control to that new owner which 90% of the time is positioned badly and will get promptly touched and again be stunned immediately. If you're stunned, you can't switch control to a different character either since it uses a proximity to the ball system to determine who you switch to. And then there's the shooting the ball... no matter what it seems to take at least 5 attempts to make it into the goal, regardless of quick passing. That's on top of the fact your goalie is so useless they can't block shots from half the field away but the opponent's goalie takes multiple attempts at a shot to potentially get a goal.I liked the RPG elements and world design decisions made, but the soccer match gameplay is so horrendous I had to stop playing cause of how frustrating it is getting control wrestled away from you and the incompetent positioning/blocking by your team mates. Do not recommend this title.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game, albeit with some MASSIVE caveats. Soccer Story is inevitably going to draw comparisons to Golf Story, a cult hit for the Nintendo Switch, given their similar titles.  They share pretty similar DNA. They're both lighthearted sports-based RPGs, centering around a washed-up dweeb following in their father's footsteps. I'm pretty sure they have the same fonts for their "Success" and "Failure" notifications, a detail which makes me think, simultaneously, that there was some shared talent between the two games, and that I should probably go into therapy. The similarity is not a bad thing; after all, Golf Story was a legitimately great game! Problem is, Soccer Story comes up short. The primary downside of the game is that the AI for the sports minigames is somewhat frustrating and pretty samey . When you're learning the ropes of the game, you'll be foaming at the mouth as the literal toddlers on the opposing team manage to orchestrate a Patton-like level of strategy, while your computer-controlled teammates are sitting around sniffing glue and eating crayons. You eventually learn, however, a game plan: the instant you get the ball, juke down and to the right, pass to whoever's available (even if it's your goalie), and the instant you cross over into the opposing team's side and get a clear shot at the goal, take the shot. This, as far as I can tell, is the _only_ way of reliably winning, and it works every single time (at least, up until the second cup, which is where I left off). Similar strategies exist for the volleyball minigame (cheese the opposing player into getting close to the net, wait for them to hit the ball into the net, and then let the points roll in). The game itself is also rather janky. While you're dribbling your ball around the worldmap (a thing I have separate gripes about), you can very easily get hung up on world geometry for a few seconds until you panic-kick the ball away from you and free yourself from the all-consuming prison that is the Gate in the Starting Zone. The camera and the collision detection often don't gel particularly well together; both I and my opponent in the volleyball minigame dropped the ball despite being in direct contact with it. As another reviewer mentioned, the shark minigame is also a pain in the neck to complete. There's a bunch of smaller game-design elements that I profoundly disagree with; your sprint mechanic in the real world is tied directly to your character's Speed and Energy mechanics, which means that if you want the convenience of getting from Point A to Point B in a reasonable length of time, you're gonna have to squander a few upgrade points on your MC. Last, but certainly not least, there's the writing.  My biggest disappointment with this game is that, while Soccer Story is certainly lighthearted in the same vein as Golf Story, it's not nearly as funny. The characters feel like afterthoughts, the jokes are fewer and further between, and it feels ultimately less like a Paper-Mario esque romp and more of a mid-budget Saturday morning cartoon. The writing isn't _bad_, but it feels like it's there as an excuse for the gameplay. At the end of the day, I still enjoyed Soccer Story. The graphical style is charming, the world itself is still whimsical enough for me to overlook the game's many flaws, and most of the sidequests and minigames (particularly the drone-hunter sidequest) are legitimately pretty fun, although occasionally heavy on asset-hunting. If you like sports-based RPGs and have the time, I'd give Soccer Story a try. That being said, if you have a Nintendo Switch and enough cash for only one game, I'd probably swing towards Golf Story instead. Or wait until December for Sports Story to come out.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two game modes - either a single player story mode, or a quick match for 1-4 local players.In single player story mode you play a young girl called Kai on her quest to bring back soccer into a world where soccer is banned. There is only a professional league, but noone outside it is allowed to play soccer. Suddenly a magic soccer ball appears, and guides you to the soccer field... which is of course closed. Unlock the soccer field, and you will always have a football with you, which you of course need for a lot of challenges. Reminded me of Soccer Kid (Krisalis, 1993), even though this was a 2D platformer.The game plays a bit like the old Zelda games (ok, without the combat...), and is actually quite fun. Slide of the grass to uncover hidden coins, talk to the many NPCs, do little quests in a world that looks like straight out from minecraft. Do the inhabitants of Soccertown a little favor, and they might help you on your main quest. A considerable number of miniquests await you in Soccertown - destroy "no soccer" signs, score secret goals, pass the ball into overturned waste baskets, find ticket stubs, score (secret or closed) goals, hit targets with your ball, unlock challenges, destroy stone towers, improve your player(s) by collecting/buying medals or getting new soccer boots (with special abilities) and most importantly, gather a soccer team... including an animal captain. There is a lot to do and you unlock new regions (beach, woodlands, gym, fishing lake, golf course...) soon.  The world really is full of goals, puzzles and secrets, and it's up to you to find them.You have a map, a list of all quests, an inventory screen, a stats screen for all your players (improve their speed, shooting, energy, strangth). The single player exploring/action rpg part of the game is really nice, even the soccer matches in this mode are... ok. Especially when you play vs weak teams like the Toddlers. That's why I upvote the game. The local multiplayer part, on the other hand... is not the game's stongest point. I would not recommend to acquire this game to play that mode (only). The matches are really... strange.To get the goal from an opposing player, just touch him. He will fall down and you have the ball. If you have the ball, it will stick to your player like it is fixed by glue. The only way to lose it is if you are touched by a player from the other team or if you shoot/pass. You can shoot with B, the longer you press the button the harder you kick. You can alos pass the ball to your nearest friendly player by pressing A. Pressing Y lets your player magically dash (teleport?) over maybe 15 meters. This is an arcade soccer, not a faithful recreation of the sport. Arcade soccer is ok, but in this game they have gone a bit too far. This has hardly any similarity to soccer. No fouls, no refree or linesman, no free kick, no penalty, no corner ball, no offside, no substitutes, the ball will never go out of play (just bounces back), no own goals (actually, you can shoot only in the direction of your opponents goal, no passing/shooting back), no headers, no throw in. Even the famous and realistic banana shot (invented by Microprose Soccer) is not possible. Goalies cannot leave a small semi-circle around the goal (mini penalty arena?), field players cannot enter it. You will very often hit the crossbar. The goalie is controlled by the computer. There are 4 field players. They look differently, but I had problems recognizing the dress and never knew if a player was from my team or the other team.I wouldn't care for some unrealistic features, I wouldn't care for some simplified or different rules... as long as the game is still fun and highly playable. The soccer part of this game was not fun and not really playable. Tried it with friends that play FIFA, they hated it. Tried it with friends that prefer simple arcade soccer games, they also hated it. Tried it with my wife, she refused to continue to play after 10 mins. Maybe you should play the local multiplayer variant only with friends who already played (and enjoyed) the single player mode before?Nice little soccer-centric action prg, and a local multiplayer arcade soccer that really needs getting used to.

_childDocuments_.review: 1 year ago, The Calamity tore apart the foundations of soccer and ever since that fateful day, people have been banned from even looking at a soccer ball. But that all changes when a magical soccer ball chooses you to be the savior to bring the sport back. Now, in Soccer Story, you will use your trusty ball to best bad guys, compete in other sports, and solve any puzzle and problem that comes your way just by dropping a soccer ball. Put together your team, upgrade, and bring soccer back to the glory it once had.Playing through Soccer Story felt reminiscent of the Switch-exclusive game Golf Story. This one does have a similar premise, though it uses soccer instead of golf, and they are made by different developers. Regardless of this, Soccer Story is beaming with charm and a great mix of 2D and 3D graphics. The gameplay is simple, but very enjoyable and the humor was on point. Overall, for a small RPG, I loved playing this and it felt right at home in short bursts.For the most part, Soccer Story runs fantastic without any changes! Was able to keep 60 FPS the focus with around 9W - 11W of battery drain for around 4 - 4.5 hours of battery life! This wasn't completely unexpected due to the nature of the game, but it was still wonderful to see. While it was like this most of the time, I did notice a couple spots that would drag the game down to 50 FPS and shoot the drain up. I decided a TDP of 8 would be best. Soccer Story can handle a lower limit, but keeping it at 8 allows the little areas that are harder to stay above 50, which still feels quite smooth. If left without a cap, these areas can go up to 17.5W drain, which I feel is way too much for a game like this. Luckily, these areas aren't huge and the cap, while it will bring framerate down, won't over draw your battery. The soccer games themselves have no issues running at 60.I did also notice a small stutter when going into new areas, but it was only 1 spike and then back to normal.Soccer Story doesn't have many graphical options to choose from, but it isn't necessary. The game runs great out of the box and other than those small areas, which don't last very long or break up the smoothness of the game, runs just fantastic.I didn't notice any other issues in-game during my playthrough, but the main menu take more power than most of the game. Keeping the TDP limit on will curb this, and it goes away once you enter into the game, but it is still worth noting that it could drain to 14W - 15W until you get in-game.As a game, I enjoyed my time with it. I am a fan of RPGs, especially small ones like these, and had a great time kicking the soccer ball at people and pandas alike. It isn't too detailed in its RPG mechanics, but I feel it does a good job managing all of it and putting all the pieces together for a good time. On the Steam Deck, the game works really well and feels fantastic most of the time. _childDocuments_.review: This game is NOT the buggy mess the other reviews claim it is. I played 6 hours and did not encounter any bugs. The people saying it's too hard are just bad at the game, it's actually way too easy.The game may not be buggy but that doesn't make it any less boring. The gameplay understandably starts off simple, but it stays that simple for the entire game. After 6 hours I had only just unlocked my first power which just lets me tackle from further away, hardly game changing.There is no team building, you are stuck with your starting team but you can upgrade them by doing fun little minigames to increase their stats. These minigames are the most fun you will have in this game and even they get boring eventually.The football gameplay is just watered down fifa and for some reason there's no music so it's even more soulless. The matches are incredibly easy but last five minutes so you have a massive lead in the first minute and have to suffer through 4 more of mindless winning. You can change the difficulty which I forgot about but the gameplay is so bland I doubt it improves much.The open world exploration is much more entertaining than the football. At first I really enjoyed completing minigames and finding collectables but after 6 hours it got very tiring.The graphics and music are charming, I have no complaints there.Buy this game if you must but I would refund after the first area unless you really want to do the same thing three more times. The game isn't terrible but it's definitely one of the most "mid" games I have ever played. 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Would pick a side-thumb if I could. The premise is good and it's a charming game but the soccer gameplay isn't fantastic and there are quite a lot of bugs and things not working quite right. Although none of the bugs stopped me from completing the game, I did have to force quit the game and lose some progress once and also there was a story mini game where I had to turn off Vsync or otherwise it didn't work. Besides this, there are general issues with collision detection throughout the game, and there are quite a few side missions, which isn't a bad thing, but some of them just feel like a waste of time - I created a few Steam guides for some of the more annoying side quests to save someone else's time in future. Also a real lack of music (e.g. soccer matches have no bgm) doesn't help.The game's biggest issue is that it just needed a bit more playtesting. Many NPCs show a Talk button but say nothing at all, some issues are just a lack of care e.g. an NPC standing next to a graveyard saying "the graveyard is locked" after you've already unlocked it, or the shopkeepers saying they are in trouble even after you've just finished the story quest to solve their problems. I could accept an NPC on the other side of the world not saying the right thing based on the story's timeline, but when an NPC literally involved or next to a thing says the wrong stuff, it breaks the game's immersion.All these sorts of issues make me feel the game isn't worth the asking price. I got the game on sale at 75% off and I feel that was ok all things considered.

It's been a year since The Calamity tore apart the very foundations of soccer as we know it, and since then, Soccer Inc. has made dang well sure that not a soul has been allowed to even look at a soccer ball, let alone kick it.

Soccer may have been banned across the world... but now there is hope! A magical soccer ball has chosen you, our Savior of Soccer!

Soccer Story is a physics-driven adventure RPG, where every problem can be solved with your trusty magic ball. Along the way, you'll need to best bad guys in 1v1s, compete in a range of different sports (with your soccer ball, of course), and sometimes use your brain just as much as your balls

_childDocuments_.review: POSITIVE-WITH HEAVY CAUTIONI'm reviewing as positive, because there is a great foundation here, and I want to see the game grow. BUT, there is ALOT that needs to be done by the devs to get it there. So, let's get the positives out of the way. The meat of the gameplay is great. Controls are responsive, and everything mostly makes sense. Fight Forever has struck a perfect balance between the pure spectacle of the 2K series, and the pure arcade feel of FirePro. There are however some glaring exceptions. It should be possible to put someone into a seated position from the ground (you can only do that with certain moves), and there was no reason why we can't have additional slots for rear grapples and corner grapples. The graphics are....... 'not great, not terrible'. People have been unfairly throwing around N64 or PS2 graphics. And they're only that bad when you compare them to 2K23. Take that out of the equation, and it would be fair to say they're on par with earlier 2K games from early in the PS4/Xbone era. They're...... acceptable. What's NOT acceptable however, is the creation suite. I heard rumours that the creation suite was going to be mid. Mid would be a compliment. What we have, is embarrassingly lacking. And I have examples. Oh boy do I have examples......*We have the barest of bare minimum sliders. You get 4 preset body types, and you get to change height, bodyfat, and musculature. THAT'S IT! You have very few preset faces, which you can't edit in any way! Oh, and let's talk about hair. Female hair presets have 2 pieces repeated 3 times per piece. You could have saved 4 slots just by giving us a length slider. *We have so many merch shirts. Basically, the same T-shirt repeated over and over again but with different logos on them. Why? Why can't we just put decals on the one shirt? Why are we being lazy and wasting clothing slots? *On that note, why don't we have a socks layer? Or an accessory layer for lower bodies? (belts?) Any reason we can't throw a shirt or a jacket over that one piece leotard as entrance attire? Why can we only have a single basic tattoo? This is stuff Yuke's were doing for WWE cas during late stage THQ. Why is none of this here? An arguably as equally egregious offender is the lack of moves available for your moveset. The way moves are categorised are poor at best, or non-existent at worst. And even how you can build your moveset. Your controls in a grapple are bound by high strikes-which can only be punches, low strikes-which can only be kicks, and throws-which can only be well, throws. You want to create a pure grappler? Or a boxer? Or a brawler? Maybe a fancy-pants martial artist? NOPE! So the barebones creation kit extends to your moveset as well. And the worst part: certain things like slots for signatures or finishers are locked off until you play path to elite. So to unlock those slots, or even simple attributes, you have to take 'some guy or gal' through a boring ass story mode which...... I just don't care for. And then if that wasn't salt enough, Yuke's has sealed away any hope of modding-something that 2K seem to no longer give a ♥♥♥♥ about in comparison. OK, I get that they want to protect their DLC model. That's fine. But then if that's the case...... open up the workshop. That way, they can actively police and curate community content. Buuut hey. You can do full contact intergender matches-something that you haven't been able to do in WWE games for over a decade. Also Cody's now in both companies current games, so that's nice. Y'know what? On that note, let's make him the guest character for Tekken 8. And Mortal Kombat '1'. And SF6. AMERICAN NIGHTMARE EVERYWHERE!Despite this mostly scathing review, I'm marking this as positive. Because, I see potential for the series to grow. And it NEEDS to grow, because WWE need a fire lit under their asses on all fronts. Even on video games which they have lorded a monopoly over for FAR too long.

_childDocuments_.review: I was super stoked about this game all the way up to launch. Unfortunately the experience has been lack-luster. It seems with this game Yuke's ( Who previously worked on nearly all WWE games ) have taken a huge step back in their ability to produce a game that has the content to reflect the idea of supporting this game for, well, ever. The arenas and most storylines date back to the 2019 era of AEW. This game has clearly been in the work for a very long time. So much so that they have failed to keep up with the level of detail that most modern games bring. This is not detail as in texture models or what have you, but more detail in the fine working of the gameplay flow itself. One on One matches flow near perfectly when playing on the ELITE difficulty. However as soon as you add more than two characters in the ring, the system gets confused and clunky. I hate to leave a bad review for this game but there HAS to be a push for better content if they want this game to continue living. They even sold out to the BATTLE ROYALE gameplay loop to try and appeal to more casual players, just as most other companies have, but due to the lack of sense of achievement these lobbies are literal ghost towns. I personally didn't want the Royale gamemode, but I tried to load a couple games of it anyway and got nowhere with it. It seems AEW as a whole needs to reassess their priorities to appeal once again to their hardcore fan base. No WWE fan will play this game and considering the limitations in the creation modes I can't imagine any casual player wanting to pick up this hot piece of garbage for half off let alone full price. This game is now on my books as yet another let down from the corporate gaming industry. Until they overhaul this game I can not in good faith recommend it to anyone.I also forgot: There is no support for remote play with friends on steam. As someone whole enjoys playing wrestling games with my brothers across country, i consider this is a MAJOR over site that should be immediately remedied as a step in the right direction if the developers want to show they're paying attention. This may unfortunately reach a void but steam asked me for a review so here it is.Also Also: I will be leaving the comments open for anyone to throw in idea's of what they're missing with this game. Or tell me I'm stupid and don't know what I'm talking about. Let me have it!
