_childDocuments_.review: The bones of a good game are here. The actual mechanics are extremely reminiscent of old THQ N64 qrestling games, which I believe was the goal, and they met that. There's a decent smattering of modes, lots of fan service. The skeleton of a good create-a-wrestler is here too, though with...we'll say not enough options.There's good things here. I want to like this game, desperately. Love AEW. Love WWE No Mercy from way back. This game should be a hit, at least for me.$60 is an embarrassing amount to charge for what's here. The game's not even out a year, and we're already on Season Pass #3. We get DLCs for characters that are already different in real life, game modes no one asked for, but very little updating of existing wrestlers or building-out of customizations. The initial cost is too high, the ongoing cost is too high, and the game just isn't built out enough to warrant this cost.There was a decision made at some point to release this game last June, and that was clearly 6 months (12 months, even?) too early. I don't think anyone's complaining about the overall quality of the game (which isn't bad, at least for what it's trying to be), just that it's nowhere close to justifying its extremely steep cost.If the customization had more options, or the career mode had more depth, or the wrestlers were kept more up-to-date, or the graphics were a touch better, or the animations were a bit crisper...maybe a cost this high, equaling the most expensive games on the market, is justified. As is, this game is likely worth half, or less, what's being charged.If the DLC prices and frequency hold, I wouldn't pay more than $5 for the base game. If $60 is the base game asking price, I would expect the DLCs to be free, if only to buy goodwill for what's clearly an unfinished game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time fan of Yukes's work for the earlier WWE games, I knew I had to get my hands on AEW Fight Forever. Unfortunately it didn't take me long to see their craftsmanship of making entertaining and content-packed arcade wrestling games is showing ring rust and it doesn't look pretty. - Plenty of weapon variety. - Moves sound and look impactful - Focused more on arcade wrestling which is refreshing from playing WWE 2K.  - Simplistic creation lessens the time it takes to create wrestlers, arenas etc. and get into the action sooner - Mini-games - Mixed gender matches - The Road to Elite story mode is short and can be finished in under 15 matches. Official wrestlers cannot have their stats altered in this mode thus making playing it as one is completely and utterly pointless. - "Branching story-lines" are not affected by your win ratio as advertising says, but they're activated by RNG.  - Created wrestlers are unfairly broken online.  - It's a signature move spam fest. Build up your momentum bar once and you can use Signature moves infinitely until you get hit or decide to do a Finisher. - Extremely limited creation suite and match types. No custom matches. - No way to manage win/lose records for the roster. - Created wrestlers stay weak as paper until you run them through the story mode.- Some tweaks are desperately needed such as button mashing either not working or not building enough escape progress to escape a pinfall. To tell how bad it is, it took just 1 non-finisher move on me at full health and all the buttons I can mash to lose.  - Referees are awful because when you go for a pinfall attempt, instead of running towards the pin like a normal referee, they need to do 2-3 short bursts towards the pin. This only prolongs the pinfall and this is annoying if you are in a multi-man match.I've held my hope for half a year for Yukes to make the proper adjustments and fixes to improve AEW: FF into a game it should've been. Into a game they advertised and promised us. But it's time to throw that hope away because Yukes have more or less adopted modern gaming practices of releasing a broken promise of a game, adding numerous expensive DLCs, forgoing patching the things that NEED to be patched to add new things that weren't asked for and pretty much abandoned ship offering ZERO post-release support.

_childDocuments_.review: -5 MONTH REVIEW-I grew up in the golden era of wrestling video games, and when AEW Fight Forever was announced, I was ecstatic. Boasting old-school vibes, mechanics and art style, this is everything I wanted from a video game.Unfortunately, the lack of content, support and features is overwhelming (yes - I am genuinely stunned how barebones this is) to the point where this game is a must-miss.I purchased the Elite Edition. This gave me the impression that I am supporting a grassroots game from the start, and that I would get additional content whilst the game matures & improves over the coming years. This is the impression AEW Games/THQ gave when they talked about this as well. Evil Uno also said this on a live stream several times also.I get none of the above. I got Matt Hardy (????????? great) and I still have to purchase additional DLCs in future despite supporting the game from the beginning.Outside of the lack of transparency of bundles, the game has fundamental flaws in terms of actual play-ability. For example, if you somehow win the Battle Royal at the very, very start of Road to Elite mode, and then go on and win the AEW world title, the game completely ignores the fact that you've won the title and they don't acknowledge it or have you defend it. Your journey continues on as if you're STILL going after the AEW title... What??Weapons constantly fall over and bug out, it is IMPOSSIBLE to kick out and THEY WON'T FIX IT. You can spam as fast as you can despite only taking one signature move from your opponent and lose. This is an ongoing issue they literally won't fix.The images in Road to Elite are genuinely flat PNG files with absolutely no thought put into them, the commentary (particularly JR) are lax at best, the little sentences above wrestler's names that are usually witty are basic, bland and not updated, and - for whatever reason - they haven't enabled crossplay so this game is completely and utterly dead on PC.I am based in Ireland and I have been trying to play online for months, and I literally have never been able to find an online game despite owning this game on release.In amongst all of the negatives, there are positives! Such as:Despite the small positives above, it breaks my heart to say that this game - as of right now - is a 100% miss. I know you want to give it a chance because you'll think you'll like it more than I do, and you might, but I don't think that's the issue. I think it's a fundamental issue and I would wait to buy this game heavily discounted or not at all.I think the issues are so blatant and unavoidable that they're impossible to ignore. I have no faith in this game's improvement, and I wouldn't be surprised to see Fight Forever 2 announced in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever is a divisive game, just like AEW itself is. It's not going to win everyone over and (as you can probably tell from the comment section) pissed a lot of people off. Ultimately, I'm going to go over why I decided to give the game a recommendation.Personal background:I've been playing wrestling games all of my life. My first was WCW/NWO Revenge and from there branched out to pretty much everything forward and backward. From WWF Wrestlemania on the SNES, all the way to Smackdown Vs Raw 2006. I attempted to play a few of the games after (such as the 2K games) but quite frankly I didn't feel they were fun to play, I really hated how wrestling games went more to simulation than arcade style. Also, the few times I played online were dreadful. Some people really enjoy this, I've always hated having people who used the exact same spammy moves (ala a Spike headbutt or Triple H knee lift), so my experience has always been local co-op or single player.Cons:First and foremost, I'm not sure what is causing it, but there are people who literally cannot play the game based on something in their setup conflicting with the game. I've had a seamless experience so far, but someone who bought it with me to play on Steam as well, literally can't play three minutes into any match with the game either crashing to desktop, or crashing then bluescreening their PC. I have an Nvidia card and they have an AMD card, maybe that's why? Who knows, but that needs fixed ASAP.The only really major thing I consider a detraction from my experience is, the game feels unfinished in many regards (but I'll get to why I don't think that's a detraction for me, yet) but the one part of that that's kind of egregious are the moves when making a custom wrestler. In classic Yuke's style, the game has multiple ways of doing moves. The thing is, some of these moves just don't look good or are almost identical. Most of the character specific versions look good, but they are definitely pulling from older animations for others and they didn't look good then, and including them in a game that already has an extra level of jank to it just makes it feel very weak, like why not just put the best looking ones in the game?And really the price. Again, I'm having fun with the game, but for 60 USD (70USD if you bought the Elite Edition) you're asking a lot of people with the state the game is in currently to shell out that much, and for two of the DLC packs in the Season Pass it wasn't even clear whether they were ready now or would be coming out later.Middle GroundI wanted to include things that to me might be a con to some but aren't really a con to me in the greater scheme of things or that don't detract from my experience.When this game shines, it really shines, which is why I put the overall quality in the middle ground. Many moves look awesome, I like some of the customization options, things I would never have thought of to play around with such as the custom effects on entrances and controlling those entrance effects. Same thing with a lot of characters, there are some characters that actually look really well done. Most of the women in the game actually look pretty good. But then you have some, like the Young Bucks, and you think sheesh what happened? Some things have a ton of options, but then others are non-existent. Some minigames are awesome like Shida baseball, the fan catching game or the bomb throwing game) but then others like guess the card that flew by or the trivia game are dreadful because they just go way too fast.The game just feels like it needed another two years and either AEW, THQNordic or both said "It has to come out now". And what we got is what is here. There's one or two spelling errors in the moves as well as extraneous spaces that show me this was a decision made very quickly. I'm reserving final judgment because like Cyberpunk or No Man's Sky, or any game that gets post-launch support, maybe THQ and AEW will really put in the work to make this game great, they've at least hinted that they were more interested in that then doing a yearly release.Pros:The thing that you've probably seen mentioned if you've looked at other reviews is, this game takes great inspiration from wrestling games of the past. WWF No Mercy, WWE Day of Reckoning and Here Comes the Pain, etc. It wears these inspirations on its sleeve, and if you're from that time, if these games were your favorites growing up? You're more than likely going to have a much better time with it. Road to Elite especially reminds me of a combination of No Mercy's championship mode and Smackdown: Shut Your Mouth's career mode. It has very tongue-in-cheek writing that doesn't take itself too seriously and works with the game.Most importantly, it's just fun. That may sound like a broken record to some looking to quantify in these reviews why "fun" supercedes all of these possible negatives but it just does. I bought this game at full price even with the mixed reviews coming out and with all of the jank and things I wished were currently in it. It's obvious the people who worked on this game had a passion for it, the foundation for a truly great game is here, it just needs both more time and content to get there.Final notes:I didn't bring up jank or glitches as positives or negatives because ultimately, every wrestling game has had them. There are a few that bug me, but nothing worth rage quitting over. Also, to any possible comments of "Well they had X amount of money and Y amount of time" or "But these games they're taking inspiration from are better". Listen, in the same way that AEW has only existed for four years as of this review and WWE for 50, Fight Forever is the very first console game AEW has ever made. It took 3 years to get from Smackdown 1 to Here Comes the Pain. Fight Forever has the potential to fix, change, and add a lot of things in that time to address concerns. Will they? That remains to be seen, but I'm personally willing to give them that chance.To the devs:If you are looking at reviews, here are some personal suggestions:

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the mid-2000s, Yukes' wrestling games became annualised with the release of 'Smackdown vs Raw 2006'. This began a long period where Yukes would crank out a new WWE game every year (under the banner of Smackdown vs Raw, WWE or WWE 2K) and they'd all be pretty much the same, with the same bugs, gameplay issues, dodgy animations and so forth.That's why I was so excited about AEW Fight Forever, because for the first time in nearly 20 years Yukes finally had an opportunity to take the time to craft the best wrestling game they possibly could. They could finally take their wrestling game formula and give it the 20 years worth of polish and improvement that they weren't able to do before... or at the very least, give us a nice polished-up version of Smackdown: Here Comes The Pain (PS2).At least, that was the theory.The first thing you notice about this game is that, even though it looks nice and sharp on a 4K monitor, the actual character models look like something from the PS2 era. This is especially noticeable with the facial expressions on the character select screen, which range from 'passable' to 'nightmare fuel'.Once you've gotten used to the facial expressions, you may notice that the roster is woefully incomplete (even if you take DLC and unlockable characters into account). Major stables like House Of Black and Blackpool Combat Club are woefully under-represented, and I noticed a lot of my personal faves were missing too (including ones that were with the company from the start). Notable omissions IMO include Christopher Daniels, Claudio Castagnoli, Evil Uno, Stu Grayson, Private Party, Jake Hager, Kip Sabian, both Santana AND Ortiz, Shawn Spears, Swerve Strickland, Austin Gunn, Penelope Ford and Toni Storm. So... yeah.But none of that matters if the game plays well, right? Well, let's get into that now.Unless you've been living on Mars for 3 years, you'll know that the main objective of this game was to replicate the gameplay of WWF No Mercy (a classic N64 wrestling game for those who don't know). But for some reason, this game also insisted on copying some of the worst parts of that game, things that only existed because of technical limitations. Entrances consist of a 5 second pose on the stage, so if one of your favourites has a really cool entrance or song (such as Hikaru Shida, Kenny Omega or Adam Cole) then you're fresh out of luck because you only get to see/hear a tiny sliver of it. You also don't get to hear Justin Roberts' amazing introductions during the entrances, there's no commentary during matches, and matches are limited to 4 wrestlers at a time which not only makes the Casino Battle Royal less fun but also prevents you from having 3 on 3 tag matches, even though AEW literally has a title belt for Tag Trios.The game itself is an odd hybrid that tries to merge the basic gameplay mechanics of No Mercy with the look and feel of a Smackdown or Smackdown vs Raw game. And just like the old SDvR games, a lot of the animations and mechanics are disjointed and awkward (which was, ironically, never an issue in No Mercy even though it is the older game). Some of the moves are difficult to connect with (such as Hikaru Shida's finisher which I missed with twice before finally landing one), hopping over a prone opponent is laggy and clunky and you never end up where you were aiming (again, not an issue in No Mercy), and while the strikes are pretty responsive there seems to be massive input lag when trying to grapple (especially if you try to do a light grapple straight after a strike).Ah yes, the famed Grapple System. An archaic relic of the past that demands that you do a collar-and-elbow tie-up before executing most of the moves in the game, even the ones that are NEVER preceded by a grapple IRL. It ensures that not only does most of the game not look or feel anything like real wrestling, but that all of the characters play pretty much the same since a high-flyer like Penta is just as reliant on standing grapples as a big guy like Miro is.In the past, some wrestling games have tried to do away with this system. We saw that TNA game which, for all it's other flaws, at least showed that it was possible to do standing grapple moves without standing grapple animations in a videogame. We also saw WWE All-Stars introduce a system where technical characters could chain 4 or 5 grapple moves together (in a way that almost resembled actual chain wrestling) and high-flyers had a style of play that felt more natural. Well you can forget about all that, because the 'classic' grapple system is back with a vengeance whether you like it or not. And even if you DO still like the grapple system, this incarnation of it feels slow, clunky and un-intuitive compared to a game like, say, Def Jam: Fight For NY (which actually WAS made by the studio that made No Mercy and felt extremely polished too).As you play longer you'll see other issues pop up too. When I tried to pause the game to see Kenny Omega's move list (because I was playing as him) it instead gave me Adam Cole's move list, which is extremely unhelpful when trying to figure out what they've picked as his 'signature moves' and how to position yourself to execute them. The camera likes to zoom in during big moves to make them look more impressive, but sometimes it zooms in so much that you miss part of the move and lose your bearings in the process (which matters if you want to follow up with something that requires specific positioning). The soundtrack seems to consist of about 5 songs that play on an endless loop, including during matches, so within an hour you'll start getting bored of them. And yes, the 'mini-games' suck which probably explains why some reviewers don't even bother mentioning them (and the one I actually wanted to play- the Home Run Derby one- is not unlocked from the start for some reason).I understand that most people will love this game, because all they want is a wrestling game that plays like an upscaled version of No Mercy or Here Comes The Pain, and that's fine. But even if that's all I wanted from a wrestling game, I still feel like this one is too slow, too laggy, too clunky and too janky to be consistently fun (not to mention the poor presentation and small roster), especially for a game that was being promoted as an arcade experience rather than a true sim. I already played an upscaled version of No Mercy's gameplay with DJ: FFNY and I got an arcade wrestling experience with WWE All-Stars, and this game doesn't feel like a step up from either of those. After an hour of gameplay I felt like I'd seen pretty much everything that the game had to offer, and I had no desire to jump back into another match.If you're a fan of Yukes' PS2 wrestling games or AKI's N64 games and this is somehow the game you've been waiting for, then I'm happy for you. Play it and love it and get years of joy out of it. But for me, this feels like an average, unpolished attempt to recall an era of wrestling games that I was ready to move on from 20 years ago. I will continue to wait patiently for my dream wrestling game, one that feels like a true evolution of the genre while also being a polished and feature-complete product at launch... and if that game ever arrives, I'm pretty damn sure it won't be developed by Yukes."Elite"? More like "Obsoleeeeeete!"

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now, this game is no where near worth the $60 price tag.  - Lacks content (roster, story mode, creation suite, entrances, etc)- No community creation page and no custom image uploading- Outdated roster attires- Outdated roster in general- Pinfall/Submission mini game lacks responsiveness- No commentary makes matches feel boring and dead- Graphics aren't consistent (some wrestlers look fine, others look horrible)- Already announced DLC is very weak- Voice overs in game are terrible- Matches either last 2-3 minutes, or drag way past the point of enjoyment A lot of these issues can be resolved over time, but to have this big of a list on day 1 is disappointing, especially after so much time and hype being built up. I didn't even add the amount of bugs I've experienced just because the list was already so long. When/if they decide to update the game and add more features then maybe it will be worth it, but for now you're better off picking up a WWE2k game on sale and downloading the AEW roster and arenas.Update: it's been almost 6 months since I first played this game and it hasn't gotten better. AEW just announced a new season pass that features content that we should've gotten at launch, but now is lock behind a yet another $25 pay wall. I wish I refunded when I had a chance because at this point I only see a modding community saving this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: I'm 50. I've been playing video games in a big way since I was 7. Also, I don't mean to piss and moan here, but like many of you, even after reading the reviews, I seriously wanted AEW FF to be even just "okay." And it isn't.I grew up in the glory days of Hulk Hogan, Andre, and the rest, and I went through college absolutely loving the AKI N64 wrestling games (WCW/NWO Revenge, WWF Wrestlemania 2000, No Mercy -- including the later Def Jam games [chef kiss]). Like many folks buying AEW FF, I would bet.So, okay. AEW FF feels a lot like those games. With a few changes, the controls are right there. The models, animations, move schemas -- that's all there. I loved how fast it all came back.And yes, it is seriously bare bones; it has so little to do. But since my friend and I bought the game just to get our wrassle on for a bit, I'm not concerned with that issue here. (The lack of features has been addressed by better minds than mine, anyway. And besides, the game wouldn't let me play it enough to even try the different match types, so I can't form an opinion. More on that directly.)Holy humping hotdogs. This is absolutely THE buggiest game I've ever played. (See preface.) Like, THE worst. Think of a bug, and this game has it. Constant missed collisions, weird UI glitches, and net code that combines with lag to produce some serious headaches: random loss of character control, and significant character teleporting and invisibility. Then the true game-breakers: Incessant match start failures, an invite system that just doesn't work half the time, and then a terrible tendency for characters and/or the camera to get stuck in the geometry. And these pop up in every match. All the time. Constantly. It's like the game doesn't want you to play it.It's a huge disappointment, and -- no hyperbole -- it is a true kick in the nuts for those of us who adored the old titles and spent our money on this. The reviews are right, if not even understated. This game is unplayable. Literally. If you try to play it, it gives you a giant "F**K YOU" and pooh-poohs you off to play a game worth your money and time.Please, please don't let nostalgia get the better of you. This game shouldn't even be listed in the store, let alone paid for.As other have astutely advised: Find a way to play No Mercy.Sorry for the whining.~ DU

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for what it is. If you are a fan of AEW, there's $$ of value....but wait a minute.First, discard the idea of Stadium Stampede ever happening. It's sad but it won't happen on PC.  I think I got two, maybe 3 stadium stampede matches because no one is EVER ONLINE.(btw developers - wtf, enable bots for this mode. I mean I can wrestle against the CPU in anything but SS...i can't imagine this to be difficult)Having said that, if you're just looking for a fun game that will bring you back to the days of WWE No Mercy gameplay-wise...it's easy to learn.As far as Create-a-wrestler, I mean, I can make silly characters all day long. Getting them to feel like an actual wrestler....you might find it in this suite if you really search for it. Not enough options though, and even more infuriating to refit a current wrestler.Overall, I believe it was built from the ground up, but it feels like a skin of WWF No Mercy/Virtual Pro Wrestling 2 with a few goofy minigames and some AEW centric video. I actually like AEW, but when this game chooses CM Punk....wowio. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game more but the rate at which they are fixing things post launch, let alone releasing newer content/patches feels underwhelming.I'll start with some quick positives:  I like the arcade-like feeling of combat/presentation.  Sounds are good, and the general back and forth between fighters feels good for the most part.  I like the old-fashioned style of momentum that charges your signatures/finishers.  Its exciting when you nail a reversal at the right time and turn a match around.  Overall, its a fun enough experience...but it leaves me wanting so much more.Annnnnnnnd now for the cons.-The customization for characters feels woefully lacking (unless you like dozens of T-shirts with lackluster junk on them) and match customization feels rigid and lacking.  Unless it is something that is in their presets, you can't tweak rules/settings to your liking (like making a 2v2 into elimination, or tornado, or only pins or submits, etc).  --CAW move assignment is DREADFUL.  As it is, you typically look for a move in a list that is usually very long.  You can assign "favorites" but that simply adds them to a new list that you get to sift through once more.  This becomes especially apparent if you are assigning a signature or finisher move.-The AI feels stupid/rigid.  I know there are settings in CAW that make them act differently (supposedly), but they don't generally feel particularly different or smart from one another.  They generally feel far to predictable (e.g. strike strike grab is a favorite go-to for them regardless of profile).  They rarely mix up assigned signatures/finishers, seemingly defaulting to forward grapples (if available) simply because it is the easiest thing to set up.-Cash for the shop feels worthless with how much they dump on you... Stats on Custom characters is locked at "crap" until you beat the story mode with them...which is fun the first few times but feels tiresome after your 4th-5th go.Now if you were to allow spending that overflowing cash on stats/abilities outside of story...well then....you might have a "two birds one stone" situation.They propose that they are going to release content gradually over a few years+  which sounds fantastic, but if this is the rate they are going to release stuff, and if this is the variety of options/customization/content they are going to release...well...I guess I can say that I'm not optimistic quite yet.I truly hope I am wrong and things look up soon, but here we are for now.

_childDocuments_.review: My first wrestling game was WCW/NWO Revenge and I was still playing it up until 6/29/2023. The only times I stopped in the past was for Here Comes the Pain and for a brief time with Fire Pro. The simple pick up and play aspect of this game is spot on with what I loved about those games. Matches are fun. That should always be the primary focus. So for that alone I recommend this game. Every match type in the game is fun because the base game is fun. My favorite mode is probably lights out with the Ladder match a close second. I do wish a cage match was in the game.If you are into creating robust CAW then you will be disappointed by the creation suite. I was able to make a decent Bret Hart though so it isn't un-workable. Just not up to the level we have been accustomed to since SvR 2011. Road to Elite (the story mod) is fun. I have been in some pretty entertaining stories. I played first as Kenny Omega and became the first AEW Champion and re-wrote history. Now I am playing as Bret Hart and just joined the inner circle. Some of the activities can get repetitive but I do think it is more fun when playing with a CAW as you have more to do with building up your character.For me this is a game that I will keep coming back to over and over again just to play a fun wrestling game for 5-20 minutes a match. Its not a simulation and it wasn't trying to be. Although I did discover in my last match before this review that if you kick out at 2.99 it will flash that up in a cool way similar to how Fire Pro does. 8/10 from me with hopes that the creation suite and match modes can be expanded upon in free updates down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: AEW: Fight Forever

_childDocuments_.review: The physics and controls are abysmal; laggy, and unresponsive. The underlying button presses are similar to the N64 era games, but they missed the mark with everything else. Oh, except for the multi-person slow down that existed in the AKI games, that's also present in Fight Forever...and man do they love dumping you into multi-wrestler matches in career mode, where the game's already janky and busted controls begin to feel like you're wrestling underwater when it has to animate 3 wrestlers doing something.And don't even get me started on the AI. It's not broken in the "it cheats to win" sense...it's broken in the "it barely does the things it ought to do" sense. There's a strong slap to the jaw that the AI will NEVER block, reverse, or move out of the way of. You can literally just spam it until the AI is in an injured state. Of course this is partially on the player for spamming one mover over and over again to exploit terrible AI, but come on...one well timed AI block would fix this, and it just doesn't do it.The creation mode stuff I can forgive/overlook because that will hopefully get better over time as they add things and update the game, it's very easy to add a handful of items or whatever, but it'd be a disservice to people reading the reviews to not at least mention that out of the box, your creation options are laughably small.I don't understand how people are saying this is a solid foundation, it's flawed in every place where it would need to be good to be a foundation for another game. I'm not an AEW fan, and someone said to me "Carl, you'd be more enthused if it had a roster you were more interested in...", and that's true, but Showdown: Legends of Wrestling had a roster I was super into, and that game was still terrible, much like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Thank you very much, for the Steam peeps who gave the awards. It's supposed to be funny, but the game being dead right now isn't a laughing matter to me, and I know, neither is it for all those who paid for the Elite edition. The highest count of concurrent players was 2,210, and as of August 9, 2023, it's a meager 59 concurrent players. Even avid fans of AEW are voicing out their frustrations in Reddit. They all said it better than me. No roadmap for improvements, delays for DLCs you've already paid for, very barren CAW selections, online quitters not being given a penalty, and the list goes on.Laugh as you may, slow clap as much as you want, simp all you want for the company, but if you're not getting your money's worth, what's the point of playing this game? Oh, and again, thanks for the awards, just keep 'em coming, I'm more than happy to collect points either way, even if you don't agree with my review.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As an AEW fan, I would not recommend this game for now. It pains me to say this but there are just so many things wrong with it. Many of you know about the noticeable absences, in terms of its rosters, and while I thought I may be able to overlook that aspect, it still boggles my mind that many of their mainstays aren't even in the game. Heck, Evil Uno, who's been promoting the game non-stop isn't even in it. That already says so much.The game also has many bugs and glitches. For the clowns who are going to say "Duh, I haven't even experienced one crash or glitch since I started playing it," well, good for you. Congratulations! Here's your medal, get the hell off my review cause it ain't for you. But seriously, the most irritating ones include:*A crash during the RTE Casino Battle Royal, just when I was about to win.*Your wrestler would randomly look and focus on other wrestlers who are outside the ring. I was about to pin the legal man in a tag match, but my wrestler looked at his tag partner outside instead and did a random punch instead of a pin on the legal man. Long story short, lost the match after the legal man stood up and clotheslined me at the back of the head, followed by a beatdown.*They say it would somehow replicate the fun aspects of No Mercy, but unlike No Mercy, this game:-Lacks a robust CAW option. Way less moves, taunts, customization options, etc. It feels like a mobile game.-Has no cage match option. That is one of the most basic aspects of a wrestling game nowadays, and for that to be missing in this game? A big no-no for me.-Lacks a guest referee option.-Lacks a tornado tag match.-Lacks an interesting and fun storyline in RTE. Like, wth?! No Mercy was released decades ago and I've had more fun with that.*I have to say, one thing this game inherited from the No Mercy game was the problematic way of doing tag team finishers. Instead of simply setting up your opponent for the tag move by pushing them in your corner where your tag partner is waiting and pressing the finisher button with a direction button, you would have to guess the convoluted ways of doing your finisher. It took me 30 minutes to do the Buck's Meltzer Driver.*Speaking of wrestling moves, the instructions in doing the signature and finishers are vague. Besides that, you wouldn't even be able to see the full moveset, unless you dig into the complicated options. They couldn't even organize it well, unlike the WWE games. SD vs. Raw and WWE 2k did it way better, and even I am not a fan of those repetitive games.*Your wrestler would randomly act dazed for a long time, even when all your opponent did was avoid a punch or a kick. I kid you not, my wrestler was selling a head injury, grasping it for a full 3-4 seconds, giving the opponent CPU enough time to do their moves in rapid succession. Here's the thing, YOUR WRESTLER SHOULD NOT BE SELLING EVERY COUNTER AS IF THEY WERE HIT BY A STEEL CHAIR!!*The tag matches are broken. Your tag partner would not stop the opponent's partner from breaking up pins. Yes, they would try, but if you're in the way, instead of jumping over or going around you pinning your opponent, they would just stand next to you while the opponent's tag partner would break everything up.*I can't even play online as there are usually problems with their servers. My internet speed is good. 100+mbps, yet, the game would disconnect from time to time.There are a lot more that I haven't even mentioned here yet. The point is, it isn't a great game, and neither does it fully capture the enjoyable aspects of WWF No Mercy. There are way too many problems with it. If they update it in the foreseeable future, then good. But for now, spend your money somewhere else because all you'd get from this game are frustrations, unsatisfying gameplay and mechanics, and glitches.

_childDocuments_.review: As many reviews here show, AEW Fight Forever isn't a bad game gameplay wise. It's a nice throwback to the N64 WCW games. But is that worth its price? Simply put: no.Why not?- Few game modes. No hell in a cell, no backstage areas, no first blood, no match types with more than 4 wrestlers at once...- online is death. If you manage to find someone to play with, they'll be using overpowered created wrestlers or trainers- Create a wrestler is extremely limited, to the point of being useless.- No creation suite. Nope, you won't be able to share your created wrestlers or arenas online.- Developers seem to have abandoned the game. DLC is too late, no updates since over a month, no new anouncements...- You want to play Owen Hart? You might! Maybe... If you aren't among the majority who aren't able to unlock him due to a bug. But hey, the developers promised they are working on a fix for this! At least, that's what they said over a month ago...There are plenty of other issues, but the main thing is: this game had tons of potential, but was dead on arrival thanks to the developers making every single wrong decision, mostly not communicating with the fans. Sure, they have a discord, but not everyone uses that. Even if they add new futures and fix all issues, I'm afraid it will be too late as most people will have moved on by then.It's still fun to play, but get it on sale or get a steam key. It's worth maybe 30, not 50 or more!

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an acceptable game. Also, a lot of you are being very weird wrestling nerds invaliding this for asinine reasons. **A lot of this was posted in the discussion board, but I realize that is not active anymore so I'm tweaking this to now just be my review**I'm currently playing through a few wrestling games at the moment. Most are ones I invested time into from nearly 20 years ago (Day of Reckoning 1-2, Smackdown Vs. Raw 06-09, Wrestlemania X8/XIX, Backyard Wrestling 2, DefJam) and wanted to play a more modern game with the brand I favored. Given the company/team behind this I figured this was actually similar to Day of Reckoning which is actually my favorite out of the mentioned titles so I went in aware of negativity(which seems to just be like the usual territoriality wrestling fans) but with an open mind.Create a character:The most exciting option for me in every wrestling game. I have been going into every game through my little run doing the same thing: make the closest version of myself. This sets a standard for every game to follow and see what I can manage to do or not do. This game for whatever reason limits character clothing options in three ways: In-ring, Entrance, and casual/outside clothing...What this means is that something as simple as wearing a shirt is something you are not to do when actually wrestling. You would only be able to see your character in these clothes while in their cutscenes(which i'll get into after this).Wrestling games are known for their extensive and wacky creation options. If you are playing this game for the create a character mode. DO NOT BUY THIS.There's also a general lack of options and just odd decision making choices that will turn off most players wanting to just spend a little extra time messing with designs. Created entrances are also extremely buggy and brief. **The (insert wrestler) is #allelite flashed for like a second and went away and I haven't found a way to see it again. I didn't realize that would happen and when I missed it I wished I had captured it as a screenshot.**Story Mode/Career Mode(Whatever it's called):-Career mode is done from an extremely embarrassing fan point of view. Regardless if you choose to be a babyface or heel the result is you are basically a super hyped fan who joins AEW and is just super excited to be best buds with all your favorite wrestlers. It's tough to read the dialogue of beginning to take pictures of every wrestler and just kiss their absolute asses. I stepped away multiple times for this. They also play the entirety of CM Punk's return which...LMAO. Come on man. If i'm playing the role of a wrestler I would want to be a wrestler, not some redditor with backstage passes. I can't stress enough, you're just a prime ass kisser.This isn't really something to be patched but it can be tough wanting to push through when its just like over the top ass kissing(I also chose the heel option and still end up with these results). Comparing this to GameCube titles(which this has more similarities than no mercy) the short and silly story within Day of Reckoning or the beat em' up of Wrestlemania XIX manages to be more entertaining. I listened to an interview with the writer for this just because it urked me so bad and come to find out, it was an overhyped fan basically without supervision and crunched on time.  If you're looking for a fun story. DO NOT BUY THIS.Gameplay: Wrestling games are not Tekken and nor do they need to be. This game has some strong similarities to Day of Reckoning but with some odd choices. Rolling out of the ring is usually bugged with the wrestlers rolling out nearly in the middle of the mat. This happens several times in a match. It doesn't take anything away from the match but can be a visual annoyance.Moves are dependent on the side of the wrestler which can get awkward. Most of the options all come out awkward or clunky. It feels like the game is not refined at all. In singles matches, this is fine. In every other option this is abysmal. Yet again, if you are looking to do non-singles matches...DO NOT BUY THIS.Visuals:Game doesn't look great by any standard but that's honestly the least of the worries here. It's passable in comparison to everything else. Overall:I'm close to hitting 8 hours. Just playing to complete the story mode while not using the stat points. Maybe i'll do the create an arena mode. Maybe i'll try a minigame. I have no want to do either at the moment and once this story is done I'll probably sign off and buy the more evil companies game and see how that is. Unfortunately.No matter how much of a fan you are I can't recommend this. It's not worth giving your money to say this is a video game you would like to support. You deserve a better game than this. DO NOT BUY THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is terribly disappointing to cut a long story short.While this game aims to emulate the style of WWF No Mercy, it fails to match up in quality and polish and makes very little attempt to innovate or improve upon the archaic design choices and limitations of an over 20 year old game, and falls short of it's inspiration in all aspects.I went in to this game with some hope and expecting to be surprised by how fun it would be, but I felt deflated immediately after playing my first singles match.The gameplay is okay but not up to scratch with No Mercy, or any of Yuke's previous WWE games in the past 20 years, there's less depth and polish here than other titles. Worth noting is the hit detection isn't great and you'll feel bewildered when your strikes and grapples miss for seemingly no reason, you have to be on-point with your positioning here. The AI can also get stuck unable to move around downed wrestlers, and they seem to spam taunts alot. The blind button mashing for pins and submissions, while paying homage to No Mercy and present in many older wrestling titles, feels outdated here. TNA Impact managed to implement a nice visual for the button mashing to indicate how close you are to kicking out and added some great tension to pinfalls, something that could be easily implemented and disabled for those who want a more classic experience. My feeling while playing this was that, while this plays like No Mercy, why would I pay so much money for a game to do a poor job replicating it rather than innovating it? Outside of new moves and weapons there is nothing new to experience here. The short entrances I feel also exemplify the fact that this is taking too much in the way of inspiration rather than trying to improve on the game they've pulled from, the short entrances were seemingly a space limitation of the N64 game, as No Mercy's predecessor, Wrestlemania 2000, featured full entrances, but had much less in the way of visual quality and overall content to it's sequel. Here it seems like the entrances are like this to save time and money, under the guise of paying homage.I'd say my biggest gripe with the gameplay is the match length, my singles matches ran around 3-4 minutes every time, and there are no settings or adjustments you can make to dictate whether your matches will be long or short. When you or your opponent are in the "danger" state, and a pin attempt is made, consider the match over. I think a big reason for this is the incredibly fast rate in which the momentum meter builds and falls, which feels like a poor and simplistic implementation compared to No Mercy.There is so little content in this game, there's a Season Mode called "Road to The Elite", which from what I've seen doesn't interest me personally but you may get some enjoyment out of it. From what I've played of the mini-games available at the start, they are just a novelty, something you will play once or twice and laugh at, and never come back to. The creation tools are quite frankly embarrassingly limited as you just chose from a very small selection of preset faces and generic clothing, and there is no Universe or GM Mode which while not mandatory, are the most popular and requested modes in wrestling games. Then there's the shockingly low amount of match types, there are no Tables matches, no Iron Man matches, no Submission matches, and most surprising of all, no Multi-Man Ladder matches or 6-Man tags, both of which are staples of the company. There's so little to do here and it is so incredibly unacceptable for a game of this price that took so long to develop.It's also important to mention the bizarre omission of wrestlers who should have made the cut, notably there's a huge lack of tag teams, with only 4 in the base game, and people who have been with the company for years who deserve a spot on the roster. And it's incredibly shameful to split Matt Hardy and FTR into DLC, and I don't see any good reason for it other than they wanted to make some extra cash.So what is there left to do? I love to boot up random wrestling games and play exhibition matches, but when every match lasts only a few minutes, and there is so little polish, so little to do, and so little variety, it's not at all worth playing over the plethora of great wrestling games out there. There is the upside of the AEW branding and roster, but sadly I can have a much better time just downloading creations or mods of those things in the WWE 2K series, some of which can be much higher quality than the character models on offer here.This is the result of 2-3 years of development from a company who has been making these kinds of games since 1995, yet this feels like a first outing in the genre. There's alot of hope going around for future updates and DLC, but how much of this game will change? What's the roadmap outside of the first batch of DLC? Not to mention that the DLC packs are shamefully small, will all future wrestlers be drip-fed in packs of 2 to maximise profit? We know nothing right now and while there is room for improvement and a possibility for a great game buried in here, this is a terrible package that does not in any way warrant charging full AAA price for so little. Personally I can't see this game getting a complete turn around, and I have a bad feeling that from here on out we're just going to be receiving small updates and character packs, but I'd love to be proven wrong and will gladly re-review this game if that ends up being the case. I'd say for $30 or even less this would be a much more justified purchase, I probably would be much more forgiving if that were the case, but in it's current state and at it's current price point, it's not worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I write this review with the full knowledge that making a video game starting from almost scratch is hard.It is entirely too hard to time a counter. It is entirely too hard to kick out of a pin. Even with 'feedback' turned on it is not useful in showing you how and when to counter, or how effective your button mashing is to get out of a pin. I honestly think that the button mashing to get out of a pin is bugged as I have yet to kick out of any single pin I've ever been covered with. Training mode is very bare bones, does not offer near enough options, and does not offer basic training scenarios to help with any of this. I understand that rosters have to be locked in at a certain point, but even at the certain point they were locked in, there were not nearly enough wrestlers to justify some of the 'stables' that were set up in game.   They are obviously going to sell them later as DLC in bite size chunks at an inflated price.Every wrestler you create yourself needs to go through Road to Elite to have any chance of competing with the pre-made roster. There's not a whole lot of customization options, and even the power fantasy of creating your own move list is severely limited because most of the options for your character are locked behind a Road to Elite playthrough. All that said, and despite the game needing a LOT more work, the framework of what they have to work with is promising, and I have hope that further iterations, whether they happen with patches or a future release, will live up to the vibe they were attempting to recreate as an alternative choice to the options currently available.Thumbs in the middle.

_childDocuments_.review: LETS GET WEIRDLETS GET WEIRDI dont generally review games and if I do its normally because its so good, but this game... God, I'm a huge AEW fan been to all their local events, been a fan since day one and that is the only reason I find joy in this game. I can't recommend this to new wrestling game players or old wrestling game players, its a true shame whats been produced here it feels like they thought since they'd been calling it an arcade game all this time they could just release a less polished featureless lump of dung. Lets get to the pros and cons for me.PROS - Characters are fun, all of them play nice and feel like the talent.  - Most character models look really good, (except for poor Aubrey (the goblin) Edwards, and Nick (pancake face) Jackson) - The career is cute, but short - Mechanics, they're fun, basic but thats ok I guess since its "arcade style"  - I cant help but have fun until I leave a match and thats where the fun ends. CONS (buckle up) - No cage match, death match, special referee, or any custom match settings - All arenas are exactly the same just reskinned and if you want a thematic arena you have to build it yourself.   - its not crossplay (this is a sure fire way to kill the potential feature of an "arcade game" somehow Fortnite managed to create a crossplay game that was arcade and weird, it was a huge success, so what I'm saying is Queues are dead especially if you want to play with a friend.  - In pins count anywhere they just mean outside of the ring, because you can't leave the arena for anything no street fights, no locker room brawls, no stadium stampedes, no dropping darby over the railing in a warehouse or any of the wrestling around a stadium that AEW loves to do in the stands and in concessions, (its like the people who made this game don't watch AEW) you can barely even utilize the arena as it is with the props for the ppv this is especially annoying if you take time to build an arena.  - the blood while it exists is momentary its not permit on the ring or the floors, and the blood effects on the character hit are full back or full frontal ZERO in between, and you can't bust someone open with out a weapon and the weapon typically needs to be sharp to even produce a blood effect - There are like 40 mini games in this featureless cesspool and even though you may complete and even win some in your limited run in Road to the Elite those wont unlock for you, so if you for whatever reason bought this game for the odd choice of mini games, you don't even get the joy of playing them with out playing the career so that means generally speaking you can do 1 mini game in between each career match... disappointing.  - Can't setup chairs, can't setup tables in the corner of the ring, no special ways to setup ladders - the mechanic to undo the casino chip in a ladder match is a sequence of mashing 4 buttons, it takes like 10 seconds to rip that chip and win the game after climbing which is insane considering I watch wrestlers bumble with that on tv for a minute like they are toddlers so it makes ladder matches VERY brief.  - Character customization is a joke, you cant wear pads over jeans or anything, if you want pads you have to wear spandex... I dont know why some of these choices were made..  - weapons disintegrate after 2 uses... thats it, you hit someone with a bat twice and poof your bat is gone. - Bugs Bugs Bugs, and I dont mean the bunny, I've had characters float in the ring before me, I've had ladders disappear, friends unable to move their characters in online, inability to walk past a character laid out in the middle of the ring. - The community support is horrendous, the campaign ends after 1 year when I talked to a THQ Community rep about this (attempting to open a dialogue about a poor feature choic) I was informed that it was a bug, so not only are there loads of bugs but also a team of THQ Community representatives that have never even spent the 3 hours it takes to beat the campaign to know that in fact, its not a bug but a feature that when the first year ends thats the end of your career and you need to start a new character all over again. (be better THQ)I think thats the end of my experience so far in this game. I feel like what I got is an early access window at a featureless, road-map-less demo and unfortunately thats just the game. I feel like AEW is going to bamboozle me take my money from this game and put it right into development of another game (looking at you Dynamite and Collision IYKYK).I bought the elite version.. I sure hope they dont think the only path forward is releasing the handful of price gated characters they shared for those gutsy enough to give them extra money for this heap of crap. Truly I wish I could mark this a recommended game, or that I could even call it a mid game, but this is at best is a tech demo and its a real shame, I wish there was more features and less mini games... (This isn't Mario Party, I'm looking at you Kenny Omega.)I wouldnt buy this game until it was on sale or they improve it, as of right now the only fools silly enough to enjoy this game are die hard AEW fans, this concludes my rant, I hope it saved you from making a purchase you may soon regret.

The gameplay in the matches feels solid for a while, but it doesn't even measure up to Wrestlemania XIX - the game it ACTUALLY emulates gameplay most closely; all the promotion of being inspired by the AKI engine games was purely nostalgia bait - and the excuses you'll get from the global CM for THQ Nordic - the ONLY person between AEW Games, THQ Nordic, and Yuke's combined that gives ANY communication with the public  - will be "studio of almost 200, nowhere near the budget of WWE games," as though better hasn't or can't be done under a smaller budget.For the base game, it was alright enough to start. _childDocuments_.review: I just couldn't help but feel disappointed by this game... It was exciting to get a new wrestling game other than WWE and it was exciting to have THQ & Yukes back as they have made most all the great wrestling games of my childhood.  It is just unfortunate that this failed to capture any of the magic of those games. I may be being a little harsh given this is AEW's first game but for a game charging the price it does, with the devs it had, I would've at least expected a product that felt somewhat complete.The game advertised to be a throwback to the old days of wrestling video games (specifically n64 era games) and not chase the simulation based style 2k has been offering for years. Overall, I think that is a cool concept, but I feel the concept may have been taken too literal. There is one particular example of this that stood out... The controls felt dated.... It truly captured the old style wrestling game controls with little things such as a single tap sprint button where you could only sprint in a straight line. The controls seem to go after a easy to learn simple basics, hard to master the fun stuff concept. It took me a while to learn how to a finishing move. Now, I will admit, I only have played two and a half hours of this game, and I am sure it would've felt better over time, but I see no reason not to at least take some inspiration from the WWE franchise whose controls have rarely been a week point for 15+ years. I would hope that future games in the series decide to smooth these out and start to modernize it. It would also be cool if the controls where explained better in the pause menu. Now, instead of being Mr. Negative, for at least one point I would like to praise the arcade like nature of this game. It is nice to have some fun over the top stuff in wrestling games that are completely optional for those who want it. I remember having my mind blown playing WWF Smack-Down: Just Bring It on PS2 as a kid and loving things like brawling to the backstage, the streets, downtown, the parking lot, the locker room and just having a grand ole time. I would always go back stage and hop in a jeep and run it at my brother (Who i would play with a lot back then.) It was cool seeing little things in this game like riding Darby Alins skateboard around the arena and doing tricks off wrestlers heads. I would love to see more fun concepts like this and concepts of past wrestling games. It looks like this will continue has the trailer of the stadium stampede mode showed wrestlers driving golf-carts and riding horses and shooting fireworks at one another. It is just a shame that that mode will still have the outdated controls the main game has.Early on when the game was announced and shown off, it showed an over the top, cartoonish, art style. This on its own would be fine, however, the game that shipped showed a clear art direction change half way through development. On one hand you have wrestlers such as Jericho & Omega exhibiting this original style but on the other hand, you have wrestlers that aim to be more on the realistic side of things. The models are proportioned realistically and have good resemblance to their real life counter parts. With the mixture of character models exhibiting different art directions and it shows the devs never bothering to go back and update older models to create a sense of consistency. Its baffling Kenny Omega has the worst looking model in the game considering he apparently had a hand in the direction of the game. Again, I do not care if the game has some poor looking models that have exaggerated body shapes. I just thought the inconsistency of the wrestler designs really clashed with one another.The DLC is so far proving to be a huge disappointment. the $30 price tag to get 6 wrestlers and a few mini games is a bit steep. However, It is not one of my main complaints. I was hyped to get the FTR DLC as FTR/The Revival are my all time favorite Tag team ever. This being said, It sucked to see that the game does not automatically make them a tag team in game. You have to go through the extra work to create the team. It is a somewhat minor complaint but it seems like something THQNordic could have done easily. The same could be said about the hardy boys with the Matt Hardy DLC. This leads me to my next point. Matt Hardy being locked as a Pre Order bonus while Jeff Hardy is on the main game is wild to me considering Matt has been with the company for years while Jeff is still relatively new to the company. This felt like pulling a character from the game just to entice people to buy the game early. This also leads me to my next point... The steam version of the game never was up for pre-order. You could only buy the game post launch meaning if you wanted the Matt Hardy pack, you had to fork over even more money.  (Also to note I didn't spend too much time trying to figure this out but I could not figure out how to access the other Matt Hardy attire... That was weird to me.)Entrances not showing the full entrance is not a huge issue. Especially for a first in franchise game. However, The game goes as far as to add options to change camera angles and set off various pyro during each entrance DURING the entrance, which is a cool feature if the entrances where longer than a few seconds. This leaves the feature to feel kinda pointless. The creation suite seemed really bare bones and not even worth using much. Only having a handful of options for attires and call names was disappointing but again, something I hope gets better with future iterations of the game.These are my main gripes and I know I only have a few hours of play on this. I didn't even touch road to elite. I just knew very quickly that I wanted to refund this game and wait to catch it on sale in a year or so. I felt really disappointed. I love AEW, THQN, and Yukes, so I just hope the next game is better. TLDR, this game is a promising start but not worth its current price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but I'm immensely disappointed with this.I played through a couple of matches, and found the controls to be clunky. The game isn't as responsive as I'd expect in some situations. The gameplay is slow. I'm a huge fan of the WCW/NWO Revenge style of games from back in the day, but this ain't it. These are things that can be patched.As of right now though, the game is in an unfinished state. The rumors that came out that the EVP working on this and THQ not getting along seem to have been true. And THQ's developers stating that the game wasn't finished. It seems like AEW rushed the game out, and said, "We'll patch it later." Which is disappointing.It *is* cool that the entire AEW music library is in there. Big up.The severe lack of content in character creation (there was more variety in Legends of Wrestling), the lack of a *cage* match, the fact that ladder matches are only 1 on 1 affairs, the story mode is very linear. I'm just very whelmed by this game at the moment.Maybe I'll come revisit it in a year or so when it's received patches and more content, but right now I can't recommend this. If you want to support AEW, cool. _childDocuments_.review: Well, to be honest I'm divided on my decision but have to give this a thumbs down...for now. AEW: Fight Forever clearly has effort put into its content from what I witnessed and played, but frankly not worth the full price as it stands at this time. Let me start with the positives:The controls are great, not what I'm typically use to with other wrestling games but when you get past that learning curve its rewarding with fair but challenging fights. Create-a-Wrestler is always welcome in a game like this, and the match types available are pretty fun too. When it comes down to fighting the matches can be a blast and reminiscent of earlier generation wrestling games.The big negative: the drawback is the anemic amount of content. Everything I saw in AEW was well polished in presentation and in execution...but compared to even WWE games from five years ago it feels like you have an unfinished but well crafted game on your hands. The entrances only go so far as to the start of someone's entrance with no flashy stuff walking on down to the ring or getting in to hype up the crowd...the arena customization options are about as limited, and match types underwhelming in number. Even character customization feels like a 4th of the options the average WWE game has. There is a career mode, however it doesn't particularly stand out to me...and the lack of a mode equivalent to WWE's Universe mode with managing entire shows worth of matches really demonstrates how bare bones the content is at the moment.I really want to like this game more, but the limited content for a full AAA price tag just doesn't seem worth it. Maybe this review will change over time, pending further updates and additional content, but for now this game comes off to me as a discount buy.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't ever write reviews but I feel the need to leave a positive review for Fight Forever.This game is very weird in the best kind of way.Spiking Kenny Omega in the face with a giant bouncy ball. Being able to spam insane pyro during the very brief entrances. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:Gameplay is fun and generally quick-paced. It's so good I can almost overlook all the glaring issues.Cons:I really wanted to like this game. I've been a fan of The Elite for a long time and AEW since it's inception. Character creation is way too limited for a modern game. I get the appeal of making it look more cartoony, but sometimes it looks like modelers/texture artists were given no direction for continuity. Sting looks very impressive, and Pac looks awful. Nick Jackson doesn't even begin to look like himself.I can forgive the roster not being up to date since the game started development years ago and they have to build a lot from scratch, so I'm hoping that a patch will introduce the BCC and HOB. For a company with such a stacked tag team division, it's WOEFULLY underrepresented here with just a few tag teams included at launch.Entrances are just really sad. They're too short. The trailer shows almost the entire entrance for any given wrestler.Voice acting is almost non-existent. I don't know if it's better or worse than hearing the same three lines from Michael Cole or not.Theres a lack of a constant body injury indicator along with a lot of other QOL problems that I hope are addressed via patches or future releases.For such a fast-paced game the characters get winded VERY quick. The casino battle match lasts the longest and 5 min in even a high-stamina wrestler like Kenny Omega is already spending 30 seconds on the mat. Other matches last around 3 minutes and that's a bit too short.I haven't played a 2K game since 16, but it looks like the best AEW game might be a 2k games with mods to skin it as an AEW game.The community manager said mods are welcome for this game, but it's still a question IF the game can be easily modded. Most of the issues I have with the game can be fixed by the community. I hate that it would come to that, but I'm a fan of Bethesda games so I also am just accustomed to it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid first step for AEW.  Let's get the bad stuff out of the way:It needs more. More of the roster. More CAW options. More moves. More customization. MORE MORE MORE. That just tells me that they're on to something.  The framework is great. Controlling your wrestler and doing larger than life moves is attainable. Most times the things I want my wrestler to do is what happens.  (Minus AI BS shenanigans and cheat to win.)  The mix of the nostalgia from WWE No Mercy / Smackdown series and previous THQ and Yukes games is here and mostly improved.  But it's all about more.  Upcoming season passes and character unlocks will make or break this.  Even releasing videos and music of potential CAW wrestlers missing from the roster would be fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever, is it All In? Or All Out?In terms of gameplay, it proves itself to be a bunch of wacky fun. Playing singleplayer against AI bugs weren't noticeable yet many of the clunky mechanics that have been in other pro-wrestling videogames for decades once more make their appearance.*Opponent Targeting*Stiff Controls*Lack of Direct Gameplay Guidance (Not Tooltips)For Gamemodes there's a mere handful, making it feel like a games conference tech demo instead of a fully-fledged finished product. 1v1 is probably the best option, with tag-team bouts proving capable too... But that's about it.*Ladder Matches 1v1 Only*Battle Royale Can't Be Customised (Females/Males in the same match)Looking at the roster, it's certainly not broad... Which was expected, but when John Silver is included yet his tag team partner Alex Reynolds isn't, that makes you scratch your head.*Huge Lack of AEW Talent (Evil Uno, Ethan Page, Claudio Castagnoli, Jake Hager, The Acclaimed, Billy Gunn, Brody King, Buddy Matthews, Shawn Spears, Diamanté, Penelope Ford... The list goes on)Customisation is also a feature and is sadly lacklustre, if you're a casual gamer not wanting for much you can create a decent looking character but probably keep it to one, since they'll all look similar.*Severe Lack of Options and Variety This is only after a short while with the game, and I certainly hope Yuke's manage to use this as a base to build upon. But, as the game itself is complete there's no improving the janky gameplay and that might mean that this is not revolution we hoped for but rather a downgraded knock-off version of the already quality devoid WWE2K games.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever is a special game. It’s the first major wrestling game to compete against WWE and while it doesn’t offer every bell and whistle that it’s competition offers, it does provide a game that is a welcome change of pace. Sadly there are some drawbacks. -PROS-The gameplay is extremely fun. And on initial play it’s confusing, especially if playing WWE 2K for a long period of time. It isn’t quite No Mercy, but it is reminiscent of the game where you can pick up and play it and after a few games you should get the hang of it. Road To Elite is very interesting. A single player campaign with branching story paths based on your wins and losses. A great tool for familiarizing yourself with the game. Graphics are an interesting bag. While nowhere close to the hot realistic nature of WWE 2K23, it does a pretty good job giving us an arcade-y look into some wrestler. Biggest drawback is character portraits not looking the best, but when they are in game they look better. Overall fun with weapons seems to be a big topic here. Moxley must’ve had input in this department because this game has tons of blood. Weapons are varied from the funny like just throwing a football at someone, to the awesome additions of thumbtack tennis shoes and thumbtacks to lay about on the ground. Yes, they do stay into the character that takes the bump. -CONS-While the gameplay is a fun arcade experience, the tutorial doesn’t provide everything needed to understand how certain mechanics work. I only started understanding the gameplay more as I played road to elite. The CAW suite is very underwhelming. I think this is a big drawback for a lot of people. The movelist section is expansive and the entrance section offers nice options for variety. But there isn’t enough parts to make your wrestler standout. It’s also weird that some parts can’t work together for attires that should (kick pads and knee pads).Match variety is an odd one. There are a good number of matches to play and it’s a fun time. However, there are handicap matches in road to elite but not in exhibition. Ladder matches & Barbwire Death matches are only 1v1. There’s also no cage match surprisingly, especially since the company has several week before the release of the game. -CONCLUSION-Is this game perfect? No. Is it fun? Absolutely. While there are complaints on my end with mini games being fun only for a brief period, caw needs more assets, better tutorials, etc. I can stop thinking about and playing this game. It’s online is pretty good for the little bit I played of it, but couch co-op shines in this game. There are also easter eggs I didn’t mention that are best experienced while playing the game. If anything, the game leaves room for improvement while laying down an enjoyable groundwork. Of you love wrestling games, pick it up to support the devs. Competition is good for this genre and this could be a better game series in time with the right backing. 7.25/10

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I started watching AEW in early 2020, I immediately wanted a game.  I soon found out that they were making Fight Forever, and I was extremely excited.  Although that was 3 years ago, the game finally came out and I honestly think it delivered.  However, there are cons.Starting off with the pros, I like the graphics.  I personally don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about graphics, but these really aren't as bad as everybody's saying it is.  They look like realistic arcade graphics.  AEW also specifically said they are going for an alternative to the WWE games, which is an arcade game.  They did not plan on making FF have 2K like graphics.  The mechanics are also very fun to play around with.  95% of the moves actually look great, and I haven't had an issue with any of them.  Entrances being short is both nice but also a little annoying, but I'll get into that later.  Having the ability to control the camera angle and the pyro is really cool and a fun little idea.  Road to Elite is fun so far, but I haven't fully completed it yet.  The weapons are great, thumbtacks being in a wrestling game is a great addition, and the blood to go along with it is great as well.  Not having commentary isn't really a big deal either.  I would've loved the AEW commentary team being in the game, but the commentary being repetitive is something that did bug me in the 2K games.  The roster is alright, but I will elaborate more.  I haven't played any of the minigames, I don't really care for them but I like the idea of there being more to do.Onto the cons.  To start off, the roster is way too small for AEW.  There's less than 30 (pretty sure there is less than 30), and they aren't up-to-date.  It took 3 years for the game to be developed, it would've been nice to have an up-to-date roster.  There are certain wrestlers on the AEW roster that should have been included too, like the Dark Order faction, the full Blackpool Combat Club, Samoa Joe, Toni Storm, Jamie Hayter, Saraya even, and a bunch of other AEW originals.  The fact that the Women's Champion (Toni Storm) isn't in the game is a huge problem.  AEW desperately needs to add more roster members, as the DLC's haven't fully come out yet either.  Most of the roster has their early AEW look too.  Jericho is still dressed like he was in 2019, Sammy still has his old stupid haircut, Trent? has hair, the Young Bucks have their old 2019 attire, but you can just buy the newer one with ingame cash.  There is barely any women on the roster as well.  I don't usually use the Women's Roster, but there's less than like 10 women on the roster.  The referee mechanics are also just very painful.  They count slower than my grandmother walking down the stairs, and once they get near the wrestlers, they start to slowly walk, then they get down on their knees, get into position, and begin the count.  Thats their only job too.  They can't get hit, they don't seem to get involved, and they're slow.  It makes it painful to have a long match, or just a fun one.  The running also just looks hilarious.  Entrances are fine short, but I love some of the themes in AEW and would've loved to hear them longer than in the menu.  The creation suite was honestly a complete let down.  There is ♥♥♥♥ all else for creation.  There's like 10 hairstyles, barely any attires, and you can't do much with that.  There's no community creations either.  Community creations would be great to have.  There should be many more match types than given, like Blood and Guts, Steel Cage Match, Tag Match modes, Stadium Stampede, 6-Man Tag, the World Trios Championships should be in the game, the International Championship should be in there as well.  GM Mode was also promised (at least rumored) and there is nothing of the sort. Collision should be added, Forbidden Door should've been here on release, and the new Dynamite/Rampage stage design should have also been here on release.  Dynamite Grand Slam, Fyter Fest, Road Rager, Fight for the Fallen, Christmas themed Dynamite. Thanksgiving themed Dynamite,  New Year's Smash, Beach break, St. Patrick's Day Slam, and Winter is Coming should all be there as well, as these have been in AEW for a few years now.Although these are stressful issues, I would say this game is a major hit for me and it was worth the wait.Solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Man. I knew I should've listened to my gut in not getting this game til 6 months later to at the very least give them time to work on some of the game mechanics more.I've NEVER once refunded a game. I cannot recommend this game in the state is in right now. I've been playing wrestling games since they first appeared and though lots of them as of recent have been less than stellar, I used to love it when Yukes / THQ did them back in the day. Now I love my nostalgia like the next oldie and all, but we did NOT need the clunkyness to come along as well. Here's a brief breakdown. Graphics: Everyone asked for the nostalgia that was in the old WWE games from the PS2 era and you got them on here. Not the best graphics compared to the recent WWE2k games, but they were ok. However there are A LOT of clipping issues.The controls: Oh boy where to begin. If you're expecting a smooth counter transition on here like on the WWE games? Well let's just say if you have hair or any hair left on your head, then you're gonna be bald by the time you even remotely learn the counter mechanics on here. The hit boxes themselves are seriously off. So even though you know you've connected with certain attack combos, the game doesn't register them correctly. Or at the very least fast enough. If you're screwed up and are at the receiving end of getting pinned and getting counted, forget about mashing the 4 keys / buttons it places on the screen. I've tried everything from mashing all button at the same time, mashing them separately along with just moving you analog sticks (I play with controllers) around and you still lose bouts. Oh and also, if you're in a 3 / 4 way match? Forget about any hopes of winning when even you knowing the patters of each opponent and they still manage to pull a move on you. They hella team up on you HARD in this game instead of focusing on each other mostly like the other wrestling games. And if you're in a handicap match? put the controller down, you ain't doing jack-shish.I played each mode on the game in order to take a break from the aneurysm that was the career mode and still most of the headaches you go through on the career mode in regards to the fighting mechanic is a lot worse on exhibition. The only thing I didn't touch was online. If it was bad offline, I could imagine the migraine that would ensue IF it would be online.
