_childDocuments_.review: The game is hot trash. I played for about a half hour before I gave up and refunded. People keep saying it's a spiritual successor to No Mercy, but it plays more like Day of Reckoning or the Def Jam games. I played the N64 AKI games like my life depended on it when I was growing up, and this isn't even close to any of those games. Just because Fight Forever has a spirit meter and a vaguely similar control scheme doesn't make it PLAY like No Mercy. Those N64 AKI games had weight and impact to them. They were deliberate and brutal when you wanted them to be. Fight Forever plays nothing like that. Even when you consider the difference in pacing between the games, the actual meat of the N64 AKI games just isn't there. That visceral, weighty feel is totally absent.I always loved beating the life out of my opponents in those games. Leaving them seizing on the ground unable to get up was brutal. Cracking opponents arms and watching them hold it with the other hand for the rest of the match. Hitting a brutal, realistic-looking piledriver on a chair and watching them try and fail to get up again. I felt it, and it was awesome. Absolutely none of that feeling is in Fight Forever. Instead, everything feels like a Yukes knockoff attempt at the early AKI games. There's a lot more that could be said here about the really deep fundamental differences between the two games (even when only considering pure gameplay and nothing else), but I'm not going to bother. The point is, it feels totally different. Too much Yukes flavor, not enough retro AKI flavor.With everyone hyping this game to be the next diamond in the rough, and a true throwback to the glory days of wrestling games, finally playing the game just pissed me off. I don't care for the DoR games, or the Def Jam games, so anything reminding me of those is a real turn off. All the people comparing this to No Mercy have no idea what they're talking about.I won't even get into all the missing content, match types, bare bones CAW, etc. This is mobile game tier stuff. Really made me appreciate WWE 2k23 more, so thanks for that I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW Fight Forever is a fun, arcade style wrestling game that has good ideas which if built on could be great.I've played through what Fight Forever has to offer and I've had fun doing so, I'd recommend watching some clips of the gameplay to see if you like the style, as the enjoyment does come from the style being a little different to the WWE 2K games series. However there is more that AEW FF has to offer.AEW FF has standard exhibition modes, singles, tag, along with barbed wire death match, lights out matches, falls count anywhere, and casino battle royale. The match types are quite limited honestly, handicap matches do exist in the Road To Elite mode, but you can't play it outside of the mode unfortunately. The matches are a little too quick due to the pin system being a weak point. It's a button mash but you can't see how far you are from reaching the kick out point, usually you can't kick out of a finisher, if you do, you'll be pinned off of the next move anyway.The gameplay is really easy to get into, hard to master reversals, but very fun to experience, especially the lights out matches due to the massive variety of weapons such as thumbtacks which make for some really insane spots. Along with the standard exhibition matches or speciality matches, you have the Road To Elite mode, this is the career mode which has "blocks" where you enter different scenarios based on match outcomes and character choices. This is very much like No Mercy on the N64, that's what they're going for.The RTE is the main mode of the game as it's the only other mode besides the exhibition and the few mini-games you start with. There is an achievement for playing through the mode with 10 different wrestlers but by the 4th or 5th run you've likely done everything unless you haven't followed a specific story path. There is some fun dialogue and interactions here, it doesn't take itself seriously and gets some laughs, if you play Orange Cassidy for example he'll have some unique dialogue which was fun but it's also inconsistent.There are some perks in the game that are OP, and if you want to play it online you can't turn off the CAW (created wrestlers) so you'll likely bump into spamming, but if you leave nobody wins so there is that, you can simply leave which is a problem in ranked obviously. But I don't think in this games state that a "ranked" mode works, it relies on exploiting and it's just CAW's.The music library is good, it's massive. It's just odd that we have some new music and some very outdated entrance music, that might be a licencing thing.Roster is good, but could do with more people, Uno & Reynolds for example should be on the roster. Overall, fun gameplay but very limited on the good ideas the game does have. You can't help but feel like "that would be good if they added more" to a lot of the content in the game. You can't really edit the actual wrestlers attires which is really lacking. Some wrestlers have multiple attires but you wouldn't know because you have to actually go into "edit" on the wrestlers, create a new attire, and select it for it to show. If you have multiple attires and you wanted to switch through them in RTE mode, if you go into "edit wrestler" you actually can't change the attire, despite it showing you all your attires and it showing that you can, this just seemed like an oversight on the main story mode. It feels like the game itself just wasn't finished, despite it having a lot of time to finish after all the delays. I recommend based on gameplay if you're into the style, worth getting on sale. They are bringing out a Stadium Stampede online mode which looks very fun in theory, but they really need to keep updating this game to get it to where it needs to be, and most importantly they need to add cross-play to keep the Online modes active.

_childDocuments_.review: Wrestling games are a wildly subjective thing and everyone enjoys them for slightly different reasons.As someone who continues to replay old games like Virtual Pro Wrestling 2, it's safe to say online play and expansive amounts of gimmick matches aren't what I'm looking for. That's good, because none of that really seems to matter here, anyway. Wrestling games live or die with core gameplay and creation modes. The core gameplay here is... fine? It's fun to some degree, but the CPU doesn't seem particularly intelligent, which means matches can be hilariously quick, or tedious. The story mode has these "branches" to them, but in reality, there's barely any meat on the bones there and a few plays through will likely take similar, uninteresting paths. That's not to say the career mode doesn't have some fun stuff in it. The cutscenes and random asides have the same kind of humor you'd expect in say a Yakuza game's side quests, but they tend to be repetitive here. If the story mode was more fun, it could be a saving grace, but it's simply not. The core loop is dull and lacks any challenge, to the point where you wonder why you need to eat, workout, do a secondary match, sightsee, do the main match every time. It's just... that, on repeat. Why does the story mode matter? Because otherwise your player creations suck. That's right, to apply stats and certain move types to your created wrestler, they need to go through a few-hour long career mode. Every time. You could play with a real wrestler, but then none of the little things would matter at all. What fun.The creation suite is just the barest of bare bones. Of course there's no online sharing because there's nothing worth sharing. There's so few options for faces, bodies, hair, facial hair and clothing that no matter what, your character will look like someone already in the game no matter what. Moves are uncategorized, which means when you're assigning signature and finishing moves you just get a scroll of every move in the game. No, seriously. Every move in the game. That may seem like an arduous task, but in truth, there's not enough moves to make it that painful. What's painful is trying to remember what it's named, or if the move you're looking for is even in the game. Simple moves like, you know, a superplex, just aren't in the game. For a game that had a massive delay, it sure seems like there could be more content and polish here. Sometimes I want to praise the little details, like the loading screen will show a character and then when you get to the menu the character is the one on the screen. That's neat. The only problem is the loading screens are lazy. Static images that were clearly a template with a random quote from Excalibur that's usually not even complimentary, but just mentioning this person exists. I'm not sure if this game will be one of those post-launch success stories where they add in all the missing content and make it worth playing, but somehow I doubt the planned DLC wrestlers and 'Stadium Stampede' mode are going to be enough, if delivered. The core gameplay remains fun, but considering how difficult it is to find other players, a lack of cross-platform play and the world is simply not built on local couch multiplayer anymore, I'm not sure how helpful that is. I'd love to recommend this game, but at this point I wouldn't recommend it for anything over $15 for a few throwaway hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan and player of the classic N64 and PS1/PS2 WWE games. No Mercy, Smackdown 2,3,4,5 were just spectacular overall. I remember that Kenny Omega had talked about wanting Fight Forever to play similarly to those games and have that kind of feel to them.I've played for 13 hours as I write this review. I created my own wrestler, went through the career mode once already, and I've had a really good time. The very first match I played, I was Adam Copeland against Christian Cage and he whooped my ass. I was caught off guard slightly by that, because difficulty was only on Normal and I'd like to think my years of wrestling game experience would've come in handy, but it's still a new game. It doesn't play quite like No Mercy or like Smackdown. But it plays similarly, and it's quite fun.There are things we could wish were in the game and hopefully more will be added. The Create a Wrestler mode is perhaps the most bare, but at the same time I've seen great mods already of wrestlers. So, PC master race wins again because PS and X-Box can't do that :)Ultimately though, I think for AEW's very first video game, this is a smashing success. Compare this to the very first games WWE or other promotions have put out in the past (or even some that weren't the first...) and I think Fight Forever holds its own. I am hopeful that Fight Forever will be like WrestleMania 2000 was for the N64. It was great, but No Mercy was the follow up and took Wrestlemania 2000 and made everything better, more CAW stuff, more wrestlers, more match types, longer career mode...so I think, if we've gotten all this out of Fight Forever already, the follow up is going to be even better.For now, Fight Forever is fun as heck. I personally bought the deal with the season pass and DLC included, it was on sale at the time for about 60% off. Definitely worth that.

_childDocuments_.review: is the first virtual offering for the wrestling promotion of the same name.I genuinely, sincerely wanted to like this game, but taking two  entire decades back is more of a detriment in this instance. I'm impressed with how forgiving people are being with the technically messy barebones offer here.+Taking us back to the halcyon days of console wrestling titles, I love the "if you're on the roster, you're in the match" philosophy here. I stopped playing WWE games way back in 2007/2008 when they started gender-locking the roster (until PC and mods worked around it). It is SO refreshing to not only see that not an issue here, but it's treated like how it's supposed to be treated: no big thing. Because it isn't. I love it, and that is what initially drew my attention.+Perspective is a big deal, and I was pleased to see the Titantron-facing perspective. After seeing the same NPC animation loops in WWE2k series, I've been YEARNING for this perspective forever. In addition to being the classic, it's just visually more appealing, I feel.+If you've played any wrestling game from N64/PSX/GC era, then you've played this title. It sidesteps the sim approach in favor of FUN, and we're all better for it.+Honestly - I'm happy to see Steam folks are being generally open and mostly positive of this title. I do not wish to bombard with a review bomb with my own opinion, so I am glad to see there is enough perspective that the average consumer can make their own informed decision. I genuinely thought this was gonna go ugly real quick just playing it. I guess people are more forgiving than I gave them credit for.+I just feel that the overall outlook from AEW talent is that they are doing what they enjoy. It makes for more a more interesting atmosphere and product, and I feel like they have not forgotten the reasons I loved wrestling as a kid, as WWE has in fashion of an "accessible brand".-Okay, wait - there were more genuine amounts and different types of options for No Mercy on the N64? I've replayed some of the classic titles after absorbing WWE2k and was shellshocked with some of the creation suite limitations, and mostly think No Mercy, HCTP, and even Day of Reckoning had more options. This game has nothing. Like, 8 or 9 hair options (no afros or anything with texture really - just all glamgirl hair), Ring/Entrance/Street attires, and they all have limitations outside of a smattering of options. The items locked in the shop are scarce and scarcely of any interest to anything I want to create.I wasn't expecting the levels 2k has FINALLY achieved (2k16 was bare compared to where they are now), but MAN I was not expecting it to be less than No Mercy. I was hoping for at least No Mercy's # of options. Can go into no filters for moves, but I lost all interest just making a boring male and female custom wrestler. I rode the game for still having 100 character limit, but after seeing the options - I wouldn't even fill 2 of those slots.-Only 4 people in the ring at a time? I don't care how fun the gameplay is, only 4 people in the ring when I am used to ... well, much more is just another thing I cannot support. One of the reasons I stopped playing the classics is because the limitations felt even more real in 2023 than they did when I was living with them in 2005. But this is just ... I am astounded this was their thinking for providing WWE2k solid competition.-Exhibition or ... Road to Elite (or whatever they want to call their MyCareer). Select a known star, and lose an entire section of mode mechanics. Those are the option, and it's kinda heinous. This game was intended for 4 friends or someone with a high threshold for terrible AI coding. I know there are mini-games, too, but that is not a valid mode option in my mindset, so onto the next:-This is what development resources went to? How many headblows and Bud-Lites were assumed to get a group of adults to decide this was a good idea, and what they offered further worked to reinforce that?-I kept checking my GFX settings as I wasn't confident they were on ultra, and looked like they were still loading mipmaps. They weren't. That's how the characters look. I'd give it to them if there was a decent creation suite, but seeing how the models on the actual reps look and seeing the creation suite so barebones, this is unmissable.-Okay, this was a REALLY good inside joke someone came up, to have every single loading screen need to have "A" pressed to continue. Moments I sit there thinking it's still loading, but no - it loads pretty fast! Hell, it's only, like, 19gb for the game cos there's not much in it! Why is it taking so lo... o, I see, I forgot to press "A" to continue again.There are more thoroughly documented reviews as to why  may or may not be the wrestling game renaissance for you. I thought it would be for me - I prefer the arcade action, the quick hits, the crazy weapons and match types.But I also enjoy the creation suite that matches that stuff. That is what gives these titles any form of longevity for me.I want to encourage YUKE'S and AEW to keep it up, because I sincerely want titles like this in our modern day, and maybe I'm naive, but I believe YUKE'S has the experience to do it. Had YUKE'S not been the devs on this, I wouldn't have even considered this. But I fall on the side of "best avoided" if any of the things I have mentioned put you off. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the N64-era of wrestling games i was pretty hyped for this game. I checked several reviews and i saw, that there is a lot of modding done in the background. So i was hooked.So i went and bought the game. Do i regret it? No - i spent more on worse. Do i wish the game was better? Definately. Do i recommend it: in the state it is right now? No.While you feel the good intentions of making a game in the same vain like WWF No Mercy, this game is not quite there yet.Let me list you some of my personal PROS and CONS:PRO:- fun, arcady gameplay resembling the golden N64-era- creation of wrestlers and arenas-a lot of weapons- familiar faces who were also present in the WWF-games (Hardy Boyz, Goldust, Sting, Big Show etc.)- interesting game modes (barbed wire death match, some fun mini games)CONTRA:- a lot of gameplay stuff (random buffs) that really annoys me. You either get first strike buffs and almost have a special right away OR you pummel your enemy into oblivion landing several specials only to see "injury buff" or "desperation buff" and the enemy now has a special (even though his life was absolutely drained), he "specials" and pins you and you lose the match because you can´t kick out (somehow mashing all face buttons as prompted does not work very well) - thats super annoying!=> you win either very quickly (my fastest was 45 seconds) or you lose because of some random buff stuff- localization of some splash screen and meter stuff (example: german words even though i selected english as language)- lackluster character creator (few options for faces and attire)- some match types are dearly missed (cage match, TLC, Tornado Tag Team, Handicap)- no backroom brawlsVerdict: the game has the base of being something great, but there is still a lot of work to be done. Concentrate on the core, balance the gameplay better and add the stuff people want to see (match types, wrestlers, customization for CAWs) and we might have another great and fun wrestling game to sink our time in.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW - 14/12/2023I don't think I had played a game previously that had soured my opinion of it over multiple updates, but there's always a first, and that game is AEW: Fight Forever.I believed they had an amazing foundation to build upon and while the initial content was lighter than expected, there was hope. Now after seeing what they're doing with the latest season pass, it has become obvious that they'd rather nickel and dime you for lacklustre content than actually provide a cool experience and work with the community to make the best wrestling alternative video game.The new season pass is a joke;  giving you half the amount of wrestlers than was in the first (which was already lacking compared to its price point), a "new single player" mode which is just a fighting game tower with little variety and bad unlockables, and a new arena which is just an updated version of one already available (and should have just been a free update for the community).What makes it worse is that the game is still massively lacking in the features players actually want, and if the current season pass is anything to go by, the publisher is going to keep making lousy decisions and piss off their community more and more (which right now, is a very small group after they broke the trust of those who were looking forward to supporting them).ORIGINAL REVIEW:There are some great foundations set up here for what could be an absolutely fantastic game with continued support from Yukes/AEW/THQN over time. As a big fan of the older wrestling games, Fight Forever has definitely scratched that itch and hopefully continues to get better with updates and content added. PROS:+ The gameplay is a lot of fun and builds on a modernisation of the classics like the N64 AKI wrestling games.+ Personally I enjoyed using Road to Elite to build up my created character, and there's enough content in the mode to check out branching paths making each run feel a bit different.+ The match types included in the game are quite varied and have some nice gimmicks to them.+ The roster has a lot of the big names present, and the arcadey feel to the game makes them all feel fun to play as no matter who you choose.+ Entering the match carrying up to 5 different belts can be funny to see.CONS:- Creation suite is a little limited in the content present and how you can modify what's available. This does primarily affect the visual side of things as there are a large amount of moves available to select.- Steel Cage match not being available is a bit of a baffling choice considering how much it has become synonymous with the more "hardcore" side of wrestling which this game does lean towards.- Road to Elite while fun, is a little on the shorter side, even with the branching paths. NOTE - I cannot comment on the online side of things as I don't really care for multiplayer, so I would say check out other reviews if you want more info on that.

_childDocuments_.review: Was fairly hyped, thought I set myself some realistic expectations for the game, where I wasn't quite jumping into the "OMG NEW GAME!!!" train, while at the same time not being overly negative about the small things I was noticing in the trailers and gameplay. Somehow, I still overhyped myself.I do havesome positives that I'll try to start with here. The game has potential to improve at least some of the gripes I have, so it can become an OK game that I'd recommend on sale. I think the blood is fairly decent, there's some nice stuff in the way moves and the combat feels, it's just that it's a bit bare bones (I'll explain below,) there's a nice little charm to a lot of the game that you can tell there was some love in parts of the game.The gameplay...it's somewhere between a 4 and a 6 out of 10. The moves feel like what you're normally used to, however because of how the controls are mapped and how the mechanics of certain things like grappling work, I feel like it's really limited and almost clunky. I don't know how to express this properly, but there's just no polish or depth to the combat. You'll hear that a lot in reviews I would say. Not just in the combat.The movement is horrendous, your character feels like it's old, tired and works with children, it's sooooo slow. To multiply this as a problem, the run/sprint button is a one press - one direction run. You cannot run in multiple directions. The graphics are mostly alright to me, however there are just certain parts and certain characters that just look like they're not even in pre alpha. I think it has a charm to it overall that I would've been onboard with - had the gameplay been a 7 or above.Match types...I don't want to say I'm disgusted, but literally every major wrestling game for the last...I don't know how long, has had a good variety of match types. This game just feels like there's about 3 or 4. I haven't counted them, and I dare not look into it, or I'll just get depressed. Again. The match types that it does have, are almost as depressing as the lack of quantity of them. The Casino Battle Royal match cannot hold more than 4 people at one time. It only spawns the next person when someone gets eliminated. The way to eliminate people or get eliminated is atrocious too. So heavily disappointed with this match in particular. I think this one sums up the game, there's so little polish and depth put into the game modes, that one of AEW's flagship matches gets put into the game, but it's like it's explained by some lad down the pub who barely speaks the same language as the person putting it together. The career mode feels like it's not even in a pre-alpha stage. This one was going to be the saving grace for me. Then I played it and I can see why Cody jumped back to WWE. It's like they played Wrestling Empire for a day, then tried to put it together on the last day of the college deadline. D-von - Do NOT touch that table. If you touch a table in this game, even by brushing off of it by the slightest of touches, it will fall over, and that lovely table spot you were hoping to do, will be ruined. This deserved it's own little paragraph. Referees are atrocious (lol AEW refs bad.) Worse than their real life counterparts. Don't get me wrong, I don't like to hate on the refs in AEW, I quite like some of them, but they do some awful indie stuff in real life. In this game, the refs are so slow, they make the snail that's chasing me from Earth 118-49-C look fast. I don't have a clue - with all of the delays this game had - how this game released in the state it launched in. I wanted it to be good, and I have some hope that the devs can turn it around into an alright game. Don't think they'll fix the core issues, however, it's Yukes, they're normally great, so they do have some credit in the bank so to speak.One last detail as well that sums up the game. The commentary in the game is only in certain parts in cutscenes etc. It's for some reason not in all cutscenes, even ones that are almost the exact same as one you'd have watched a minute before, but honestly, I wish it was disabled altogether. They get JR and Excalibur to read out their lines like "It's Saturday Night, you know what that means" as if they're at the commentary table. Well that's how it's supposed to sound. The way they actually do it however... They basically get JR to read out something as if it's him reading a prayer at a funeral. I don't know how it got past the recording booth, let alone how it was allowed into the release or past QA. (Would love a refund if any devs are looking xoxo, need to fund AEW for All in)

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people by default are going to compare this game to WWE 2K series and that'd be way wrong.  AEW: Fight Forever is truly a title onto itself.  This game has loads of fun and potential for party style gaming, where you're sitting around with friends and just enjoying beating up on each other's characters.  The one thing that I really like is the features of the characters.  They look more artistic instead of photo-realistic.  I didn't know how much I'd like it, but I think it's really cool.  I also like how the entrances aren't overly drawn out.  Most of us skip the entrances anyway, but with the length they are in AEW: Fight Forever, it makes more sense to just let them play through. You can also control the pyrotechnics during entrances which is really cool as well.  The create-a-character suite is pretty awesome too.  It's not as robust as WWE, but it really doesn't need to be.  The one thing I found comical is how they have a lot of the mannerisms from certain talent on the other wrestling promotions, which just inspires you to emulate your favorite wrestlers who may not be (or cannot be) featured in the game.  I recommend this game for people who miss the days of No Mercy, Wrestlemania 2000, and WCW vs NWO on N64.  The game feels like that, plays like that and I am happy to live through that experience again with AEW: Fight Forever!

_childDocuments_.review: Steam Deck Preview Here: It's been a bit since I last jumped in the ring with a Yuke's wrestling title. It feels like it was Wrestlemania 2000 on the N64, but most likely 2k16. Regardless, AEW Fight Forever feels just as solid as my 90s brain remembers, and that's what I was looking for in this game. I have been unhappy with the mainstream wrestling games that 2K has been kicking out annually for quite some time. I had stepped away from playing them, partly for the source material and partly for the gameplay, so you could infer that I had stepped away from watching wrestling for that period. AEW Fight Forever didn't require me to be a franchise fan to enjoy the game. I picked up the controller and felt like I had already played it, which in some ways, I had so many years ago. The hit and grapple timings felt familiar, the maneuvering in and out of the ring was solid, and it was essentially pick up and play for me, and that's what I remember from their games on N64 and PlayStation. There are various match types, a decent Career mode along with w/customization, and online. Overall, the game shines in areas that are important to me, like the actual wrestling mechanics, and for the not-so-important parts, like the Career mode, it still does a serviceable job. The Seasons Pass and the Matt Hardy DLC feels a little lite for the price unless you buy the Elite Edition up front, but even then, I'm not sure I see the value. Why was Danhausen not able to be unlocked for free in the main roster? I'm looking forward to seeing what else they bring to the series, but as it stands, all bases have been covered on this initial outing. In the end, its nice to see more competition in the genre.RoG Ally Preview Here: Enjoy!🎮eeFoGee🎮

_childDocuments_.review: Hidden master piece that requires time.  The fighting system is outstanding once you figure it out.  Blocking and timing are the hidden most important part of this game.  It's confusing for wrestling you would think offense would be the key.  Like:Hidden Depth - there is a constant record system of all matches and history of highest ranked matches  (it will be neat after a year or so to see how insane some Win/ Lose records will be)Fighting system - blocking is all timing based and it's skill based, so a skilled player will beat a button masher but the button masher can also be competitive  Fun - it had a video game vibe, it takes it self serious where it should and has fun with everything else (you pitch a wrestler as a baseball c'mon that's awesome)   Dislike:  AI -  The AI has been either dumb or god mode.  I've only played normal and easy so far.  The AI needs some tweaking.  No GM Mode -  WTF Tony Khan this is literally the Tony Khan mode.  Some GM/Franchise type mode should be playable.  It's a 1st game so simple is fine but a let down.  Glitches - it's day 1 so it's expected nothing bad but theres some that shouldn't have made it this far  Overall -  Could be a CHAMPion with some work but bare bone day 1 it's really good and fun.  Really fun with a group of 3 to 4 people.   IT'S INCREDIBLE IF YOU ARE A AEW FAN, N64 WRESTLING FAN, or a WRESTLING FAN.  BUT there is a learning curve and adjustment time needed to get a feel for the fighting system.

_childDocuments_.review: Review: The fact they did not even give us all the roster parts makes no sense. What is worse is that half of what they give us is colour locked or you cannot add layers to them. Why can I not put horns on most of the full-face masks (why are body art/tattoos so limited)? The more I think about it, the less I can defend it. No way they sat there and thought this was okay... right?I did not buy the game thinking it would be on the level of 2K. But this is silly levels of lacking in major areas. The fact you cannot respec after finishing RTE also seems silly. It is not like we're gaining more points from it, and it is annoying to go through a second time with the same guy (now reset) if you want to change their stats. There is also the chance they won't get as many points as the first time around.Add on the freeze bugs online, the broken moves and skill combos (lack of match types, even if some are in RTE but not the main game). It makes the game a chore more than anything, and when it is hard to find any online games due to the PC player base not being as big as the others, it becomes far more annoying than fun (if you even get a game that is not a maxed out super CAW or the like).I think it is fair to call this game massively overpriced. Look at the DLC. It's £10 for two wrestlers and some mini games and £4 for one wrestler (two versions of the same guy. A guy who should have been in the base game. Matt Hardy).While I like the game as an idea, this is stupid levels of pulling the leg here. The fact they have not even patched the game to make us at least have the full roster parts unlocked in Creations is questionable, and the fact CAW layering is a mess still is dumb. Add on the bugs and brokenness (online and offline), like getting stuck inside the ring or frozen in an endless grapple, or annoying parts of the game. It makes you wonder if removing stuff like mini games from the creation process would have done the game a world of good.4.5/10If it is on sale for £25 at some point (plus DLC) buy it then.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to think of this game. I want to enjoy it, but there's so much lacking and so much wrong. *Character creation in 10 year old mobile games have more options. This is perhaps the best part of any wrestling game and they've really dropped the ball here. I loaded up No Mercy just to compare and even still No Mercy has more/better options and the process is far more streamlined on NM. *Computer controlled wrestlers have the worst AI. I did Road to the Elite and started the Casino Royale. John Silver entered and did the same school boy roll up 16 times in a row (I counted). Would have been more but I eliminated him. I thought this may be a one character bug, but Miro, Scorpio Sky and Moxley did the same thing and just repeated the same move. Doesn't seem like intelligent programming.*Lack of match types makes no sense. You get like what, 6? 6 match types and most are just 1 on 1, 2 on 2, 3 on 3, 4 on 4. That vanilla mess is what makes up the majority of the match types.*Only 6 tag teams. There are 7 belts (5 singles and 2 tag team belts) in the game. That means we have more belts than tag teams and one of the tag teams is Anna Jay & John Silver. I mean, what? They have 4 real tag teams: Best Friends, Bucks, Lucha Bros and Death Triangle and 2/3 of Death Triangle IS Lucha Bros. So, 3 real tag teams. Then the Anna / Johnny and Jericho / Guevara*Health, health bars, signatures and specials are completely baffling and make no sense. I enter the ring, do one arm drag, one strong kick and one taunt and I already have a signature. AND, after I do 2 or so signatures then have to taunt to get my special, I can just repeat the signature/special loop over and over as long as I do 1, maybe 2 moves. And the health. I get hit maybe twice and I'm down on the mat writing in agony and cannot get up for 30, 45, even 60 seconds. This game is  utterly random.* Entrances are a big deal in wrestling. Wrestling games have worked hard to make you feel like you're right there with incredible, life-like entrances, music and other aspects. Fight Forever, on the other hand, might be the worst modern wrestling game with entrances. Yea, eventually you'll skip them of course. But these are already half skipped to begin with. * No Acclaimed. Massive fail.*The reverse and strike guard is so wonky and feels horribly random. * Sending an opponent into the ropes has the worst controls. You can direct them to go, lets say, left and they just randomly go whichever way they decide. Sometimes it goes where you direct them, sometimes random other directions. It's so frustrating to attempt to fire them into the ropes and they take two or three steps and just stop. *Instead of working on improving the game play, adding more match types and story modes or enhancing the character creation, they decide the best use of their development time and money was to add mini-games. Stupid, pointless, mini games. Is this Paper Mario or a wrestling game?There's a lot more, but I think you guys get the idea. I am utterly unimpressed and disappointed, and I'm having buyers remorse with this terrible game. I hope there's improvements down the line, but right now there's no possible way I can suggest this unless you can find it for $9.99 or less. It's hard to believe they spent years in development and this is the product they released. I got a few hours in and I can't go any longer. After my lackluster character creation and that abomination that is Road to Elite or whatever and the utter mess that is the games AI, there is no way I can stomach any more of this mess. While I have No Mercy loaded up, I'm going to play a real arcade style game and at nearly 24 years old it's still vastly superior to this garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever strikes a great balance between retro and modern wrestling games. It successfully harnesses stylized graphics and a punchy animation system akin to the Def Jam games. It borrows the momentum system best known from WWF No Mercy but the gameplay feels closest to something like Day of Reckoning.Certain wrestlers have distinct traits such as scenario specific momentum buffs (i.e. receive a temporary buff to momentum when your opponent kicks out of a pin or after a springboard attack, etc) and the chosen roster is a great start with more wrestlers to come via DLC. The result is a fun game that encourages you to play it like a fighting game, as opposed to a spot simulator. This is driven home with things like Ranked online multiplayer and over-the-top weapons and match types. Experimentation is encouraged here and doing so is quite rewarding.Whether or not you like the nuts and bolts of Fight Forever will largely be based on preference. The game feels simultaneously limiting while delivering various quality of life changes from 2K that will ultimately result in you having to decide what matters more to you. For example, Create-A-Wrestler is stripped back and lacks a reasonable amount of options/customizations but entrances can be controlled in the moment with self activated pyro, smoke, lighting and camera changes. Grapple moves can't be interrupted but you can self interrupt your own taunts so you're not caught in a long helpless state. Selecting moves when altering a moveset is troublesome due to the giant list of moves with no filtering, but a clickable scroll bar on the side makes navigation much easier than scrolling with the thumb stick. The UI is clean and communicates well, which results in less situations such as 2K's famous "Copy to" and "Copy from" options or accidentally backing out of a creation and losing everything. As another example, the story mode is short and lacks much ability for the player to make decisions, but the progression system and outside-the-box RPG elements create a truly fun experience. Speaking of the story mode, RTE mode is closer to an on-rails season mode than it is a full fledged story mode. It's not afraid to show some personality and lean into what makes wrestling wrestling in the first place. It has a certain retro feel to it, while still being unique and engaging. It's short and lacking a ton of content, but pushing forward feels fun and after one playthrough I'd honestly give it another go around. Sound design is excellent. Each wrestler's grunts and groans sound great, as does mat impact and weapon sounds. The jukebox is filled to the brim with theme songs and even 8 bit versions. The one exception here is the eating noises during Dining side activities. Seriously, Yukes, we don't need to hear all that chewing so vibrantly. The groundwork is there for AEW to create some modern classics moving forward and I feel like this title is close. With the rumored features to come (Traditional BR mode with vehicles, Battle Pass, etc.), this game has the potential to be truly great and unique. But as it stands, it positions itself as a valid alternative with a unique, fun and nostalgic playstyle that feels great as a brawler or as a multiplayer party game. It's safe to say that your friends that don't care for wrestling would still have a laugh and some fun in an Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch. There are even casual control modes for the uninitiated.All in all, Yukes has definitely proven that they still know how to make a good wrestling game. Fight Forever is at its best when it separates itself from the pack and the result is a clear path forward to a competitive market in professional wrestling video games.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: It's a positive review, but only just. Ideally, wait until it's on sale.AEW: Fight Forever is the first game for All Elite Wrestling, and is heavily inspired by the classic wrestling games of the 90s. Matches are fast paced (most are over within a couple of minutes) and hitting a finisher is an almost guaranteed win. First the positives:- The actual wrestling is really fun. It's built on a momentum system where being aggressive and using taunts builds your meter. Once full, you can hit any of your signature moves, or taunt again to activate special mode (where you can hit a finisher). Failing to use a finisher within a few seconds of this will cause you to lose some of the gauge, so you do need to use your finishers carefully. There's also a ton of weapons, and the move list is absolutely massive.- Road to Elite is a somewhat interesting mode where you play a year in AEW, going through Dynamite shows and PPVs. While it's somewhat entertaining, it does get repetitive very fast and you can probably complete a run of it in maybe 2 hours.Now for the not so good:- The creation suite for custom wrestlers is, to be blunt, garbage. There are barely any options for faces, accessories, clothing etc. You can unlock some, but even with those the list is tiny. Add to this the fact that there's loads of arbitrary restrictions (for example some long hair styles prevent you from...wearing glasses?) and it's just a complete disappointment. However, the customisation of your character's moves and entrance is pretty impressive. It's just the appearance that's very substandard.- Another thing that's substandard is the match types. The only match types in the game are: 1 on 1, 2 on 2, 3-way, 4-way, ladder match, casino battle royale, lights out (basically a no-DQ match), falls count anywhere and an exploding barbed wire deathmatch. The latter is entertaining the first couple of times, but it's what's NOT there that's surprising. There are no tables matches, no trios matches, no tornado tag... One of the reasons for no trios matches is because there's a 4-wrestler limit (so no 8-man or 10-man tags either). This limitation also extends to the casino battle royale match. In AEW this is essentially a royal rumble, which can end up with 20+ wrestlers in the ring. In Fight Forever, there are 21 entrants, but only 4 can be in the ring at once. The remainder file in once someone gets eliminated. It just feels like a very arbitrary restriction that shouldn't be in a game from 2023.- The roster is a weird one. While there are fan favourites (Moxley, Omega, Lucha Bros, The Elite etc), there are also odd omissions (Toni Storm, Jamie Hayter, Claudio to name a few). I realise we're going to get DLC, but when even FTR are added as DLC, I do have to question what Yukes were thinking. There's also only 4 recognised tag teams in the base roster (Young Bucks, Best Friends, Inner Circle and Lucha Bros). You can make additional ones like Jurassic Express, The Hardys etc, but many tag teams have half of the members missing. For example, if you want to play as Dark Order, you can only choose from Mr. Brodie Lee or John Silver. There's no Evil Uno, Stu Grayson or Alex Reynolds. Overall it's just a very strange roster choice that isn't necessarily terrible but could've been a lot better.- There's no commentary at all in matches. In fact, voice overs are extremely limited. It would've been nice to have Excalibur, Schiavone, JR and Taz calling the shots.- Entrances are very short, like some older wrestling games. I would've liked longer entrances but with an option to use shorter ones, as I feel the existing ones are way too short. On the plus side, you do get to control the pyro which is a neat touch.Overall, Fight Forever is tough to recommend in its current state, but I will based purely on how fun the actual wrestling is. If you play with a few friends it'll be a blast, but there's no doubt that the rest of the game is pretty underwhelming. I hope Yukes continue to work on the game and improve it over time, as it has a lot of untapped (tapped, get it?) potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game ever since AEW started. They said they were gonna put a heavy focus on the gameplay mechanics, and it shows with this game. The wrestling is fantastic and every move feels like it has a weight and impact to it. When set to ELITE difficulty is when the game really opens up, and every match becomes a challenge. It provides a any given Sunday feel when any wrestler can beat you, so you must be on your A game as it only takes a few moves for them to get back into it. I love the challenge and emphasis the game puts on the player to learn a wrestler's move set, be strategic and creative with how it's used, and provide an arcade experience all at the same time. The game mode you're gonna play the most is Road to Elite. It's a great game mode that combines a wrestling game with a Visual Novel narrative, light resource manager mechanics, and multiple story lines. I know it sounds weird but it works amazingly as this mode plays into creating your CAWs stats and abilities. Winning and losing in this game mode not only matters for growing your CAWs stats and abilities, but also what storylines you get to experience. I love that the game mode can be completed in a few hours, and it leaves you wanting more. Be warned though if you take the same CAW back into RTE everything stats and abilities wise will be reset. But with the focus being mainly on the gameplay other areas of the game aren't so developed, creation suite, arenas, and match types.Now onto the area I feel is the 2nd most important thing in any wrestling game, the creation suite. Kenny Omega has said multiple times that the main focus of the game was the gameplay mechanics, and it shows with this creation suite. It is very bare bones, offering limited options for customization of the wrestler and their personality. When a game gets away from sliders for setting facial features, and offers a selection of preset heads there needs to be at least 20+ different options provided to the player. Fight forever only has 6 male heads and 4 female heads not leaving much options for the player to choose from. The gear isn’t very customizable either as you can only change the color of the gear, and for some you can only change overall color. The hair options feel lacking too, they look alright, but again there are not many options. I can go on for everything else in the creation suite with the lack of options and customizing options but you will be here all day. The one big thing this game has going for it is it won't be a yearly release. Yes you heard me right it won't be a yearly release. The game is supposed to have support for years to come, or until they say they are done with this game. This offers hope for many things to be added like more support for the creation suite, match types, roster expansions, move sets, and many more.  Now you may ask what about graphics, you haven't talked about the graphics. GRAPHICS ARE NOT THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN GAMING. Yes graphics should be eye pleasing I won't argue there, but graphics should not be placed in a priority above gameplay. When game studios get away from just trying to do 4k graphics, and focus on the gameplay the MEAT of the player's experience you get Fight Forever. The graphics are easy on the eyes, not gaming industry redefining but they don't have to be. The art style fits right at home with this game.Now to wrap it this game has a solid foundation to build upon with patches, free content updates, and DLC. Is this game worth 60$ at release, no. But with everything that is rumored to come I say it's worth getting especially if you're looking for a wrestling game that feels amazing to play by yourself or with friends. Scores:Gameplay: 10/10 Amazing and stands out from other wrestling gamesGraphics: 6/10 Not anything to write home about, but easy on the eyesStory: 7/10 Good, short, and corny. It never takes itself to seriously and offers different experiences for multiple playthroughsValue: 5/10 60$ is steep for what’s there right now but I think it’s worth the investment as Yukes and AEW have my trust for right nowOverall: 8/10 Offers a feeling that most sports games are missing the arcade vibe of old. With the emphasis on being a simulator nowadays most sports games have become bland, repetitive, and unimaginative. Not having to learn complicated systems to play Fight Forever offers a smooth entry for all but still provides a good learning curve to become great at the game.

I'm only going to list the deal-breakers that resulted in the kiss of death for this game (and resulted in a refund request.)-The gameplay is just really outdated. That so called classic charm is just an excuse for clunky movements. Ironically, this feels less arcade-like than a modern WWE 2K game. For example, running is assigned to the press of a face button—and you can only run in a straight line. No visual cues for countering kills the pick up and play fun. Targeting is an annoying mess. You'll often find your wrestler picking something up or reaching for a weapon when you're just trying to grab you opponent. -No commentators during matches. What? It's okay if you don't like commentary, but commentators are often a huge part of what breathes life into a wrestling match.-The graphics look horrible.  We're not talking about mid-tier graphics here or even low-end graphics with a passable art direction—the game just looks uncannily bad. The animations aren't good enough to carry because they're either too stiff or dull.I really wanted to like this game, but I could tell immediately that fundamentally, some very poor design choices were made.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun thus far.  When it comes to game play, I absolutely love it. The variety of weapons is a superb. Skateboards, pizza boxes, barbed wire bats, propane tanks, hockey sticks, thumbtack shoes, and so much more. You can utterly obliterate your opponents with a myriad of weapons. You can create some really fun sequences.  Also, SO MUCH BLOOD (if you want it). The Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch also deserves a brief mention. It's a fun match type and should continue to be a staple. I hope Blood&Guts gets added eventuallyThe game play is not like No Mercy, contrary to belief before release, so don't go in expecting a No Mercy clone. The game is way more enjoyable when you don't even think about NM. Let those comparisons come organically. The game seemed inspired by the simplicity of No Mercy more than anything. The fighting works differently.Road to Elite could use some more depth and a padded runtime but the ideas presented worked well. They provided an enjoyable career mode despite a short length. The story line for a created character was fun at times but I wish there were more branching stories and opportunities at championships. However, there is a small bit of variety. And the story does change depending on your wins and losses.  I've also played a Yuka Sakazaki RTE and the story was different but, again, I would like to see some more depth in the story lines. Some all out wacky and insane stuff would be appreciated. Or, even better, have certain branching paths that can give you heated rivalries or mind-boggling supernatural stuff. It's just an idea. The stories are fine for now but some variety would be appreciatedEntrance customization is rather deep, however, the same can not be said for character customization. While there are certainly decent options and you can create an okay character, it lacks worthwhile options. This area better be improved in the future. The options can't be left like this forever. While there are certainly a lot of t shirt options, we need more variety in types of shirts, elbow pads, kick pads, boots, etc. I find the entrance attire customization to be the most atrocious aspect of the customization's low depth. Only tops and jackets are available at the time of this comment and that shouldn't fly in a time when customization is desired by most consumers. GIVE US MORE CLOTHING OPTIONS, GIVE US MORE TATTOOS, GIVE US MORE FACIAL HAIR, GIVE US MORE CHOICES I'm hoping that since a new game won't be created in a long time, Fight Forever will be given new content. It's very fun, especially with friends, but it needs to be built upon. It's a solid foundation. Let's see where they go with it. As of 2 days after launch, i'd say I recommend AEW: FF. _childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever is AEW's first attempt at a branded video game and with WWE2K pushing out games that have been riddled with bugs and content the past few years, I (among others) have been very excited about it's release. So, I was quite happy when Terminals.io gave me a free review key and 18 hours in, I think I've got my thoughts in order.First and foremost we have to talk about the elephant in the room: CAWs. The creator is lacking. It has only the bare essentials needed to customize a wrestler and even with those you are severely limited in your options. As someone that loves to experiment and create wrestlers for my friends streamer league, this is a major setback on every front. After this creation, you have the joy of assigning every single move to your wrestler in an effort for further customization. Being able to mimic known wrestlers moves or styles with a single choice would be a great starting point that was missed. And I don't even think I need to talk about the lack of graphics...On the plus side though, gameplay is actually really fun. It's reminiscent of some of the wrestling games from a decade ago and the "Road to Elite" game mode has some fun interactions that follow AEW's first year with bridging story lines. The play through I started with Abadon is different than that one I started with a custom wrestler... though there are some similar themes with who you wrestle in certain matches so you don't stray too far from the story line. (Join the Dark Order!)The music catalog in game is top notch! Not only can you customize what songs you hear while playing the game, it also makes it so that streamers can ensure non-DMCA music is being played. Add into it the fact that all the intros are super short, the jukebox feels like it was made for the streaming community in mind.There is a bunch more that should be covered, but know that overall AEW:FF is a decent game. The lower end graphics and chopped wrestler entrances make load times much quicker and keep the game file size down. And though there is a good amount of repetitiveness in training (we need variation there) and games with the Young Bucks, the controls are very responsive with the ability to work a nice flow into each match. I look forward to content updates and minor bugs to be fixed as things progress!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED AFTER 13+ HOURS OF GAMEPLAY:DON'T BELIEVE THE WWE FANBOY/TROLLS DOWN-VOTING THIS GAME.IF YOU'RE ALREADY FAMILIAR WITH AEW: Here's your confirmation bias! This game is for you, or should I say US (because I am a definite AEW fan). You can remake your favorite matches, or create matches you WISHED had happened. The characters and arenas are obviously from the 2019-2021 pandemic era, so we get a heavier Jericho, we still have Cody Rhodes and William Regal, and we can even play as the late, great Brodie Lee. You will love this game, the mini games, and the "Road to the Elite" campaign. If you're an AEW fan, you are a fan of great in-ring wrestling. That's what this game is about - fun, over the top, wrestling, with a deceivingly deep and re-playable story mode (more on that below). You can play multi-player vs players all around the world, but across platforms at the time of review,FOR THE REST OF US: This is a fun, old school wrestling game, like WWF No Mercy, Def Jam Vendetta, and WCW vs NWO: World Tour. If you know and love those games, you're going to love this game as well. Pure Nostalgia with updated graphics. DO NOT EXPECT a wrestling tv show simulation, like the WWE 2K series. But hey, you also don't have to pay $300 in real money to get all the content on this game. As of today, you pay $63 to get absolutely everything (the "Elite" edition). You won't have to pay anything else for any unreleased upcoming DLC. STORY MODE: The story struck me as simple at first. And it was short. But then I realized that I hadn't actually played the whole thing. What you see depends on your wins and losses and maybe even which character you play it with - as you replay the short "story" to unlock hidden rewards, including hidden wrestlers (NO SPOILERS), and earn more in-game currency you use to purchase them. The story mode also allows you to develop and build your Custom wrestler's stats and attributes and test them out in matches. So the STORY MODE actually has infinite replay value for that purpose alone.EXHIBITION MATCHES AND ONLINE PLAY: At this time both work and are LOADS of fun. You can eve use your Custom Wrestlers, which means that you should actually think and strategize about how you BUILD your custom wrestler, so you can create an absolute BEAST adapted to your play-style, or build an all around juggernaut. Plus, all matches reward you with n-game currency that you can use to unlock rewards.MODDING SUPPORT: That's right folks. They've UNLEASHED THE KRAKEN! The devs announced support for modders, and set up modding channels on the AEW Games Discord server. The game already included move-sets and assets (like audible names) for all kinds of wrestlers that weren't on the initial roster. Now, modders will be doing God's work, and adding everything to AEW Fight Forever that we added to 2K23 to simulate the AEW experience. Only this time, with ACTUAL bloody matches. MOD SUPPORT makes this game a MUST BUY. IN CONCLUSION: Yes, I recommend this game for any fans of wrestling games. If you love the old school wrestling games, or you're an AEW die hard fan, or you're just tired of 2K gouging you $300 per game to get all its content, then pick this title up now.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: AEW Fight Forever: A Spectacular Showcase of Professional Wrestling ExcellenceRating: ★★★★★ (5/5)AEW Fight Forever was an electrifying, groundbreaking, and awe-inspiring event that redefined what professional wrestling can achieve. _childDocuments_.review: Foundation really polished.Game has potential to be one of the best wrestling games.Road To Elite seems shallow, but if it is a foundation of the mode. It is really strong one.4 Acts, has 4 PPV, those have 4 Dynamites each. So in those 4 weeks leading to the finale of the act, you get to choose how you deal with your time (get 4 turns every week), you can do minigames (earn cash, exp), go fight on AEW Dark/Rampage (money/exp), eat (energy/random interaction with wrestler is possible which can lead to challenge, or just a specific text written for let's say Omega, that actually fits what Omega would say). You can go to Gym (exp, also can find wrestlers), you can go Sightseeing (mental health, also interaction with wrestler), and you can also do a press conference (mental health, energy, interaction). After you complete all 4 acts, the story mode ends. You have to start again, with another wrestler. Point of this mode is to unlock hidden wrestlers. Not easy to unlock, as every act is random. There are 4 acts, every act has 3 stories each. And you can get act 1A, act 2A, act 3A, act 4A. Or you can get Act 1C-2A-3A-1B (it's rng, while certain wrestlers have higher chances, and win/loss also give you branching out on ACT you are in).It seems the devs might update this mode with endless feature. As there are mechanics that would made more sense to be in endless run. I expect if the game sells well, that they will eventually add even more branching out acts. And that will open up possibility for continuation of seasons. Similar to Smackdown 2 on PS1 where you had Main story repeat every year while everything else was randomised.Combat: At first I thought it was really clunky. But, after I learnt how to move I noticed that the combat has great depth. You actually have to move around, use tactics, learn defence and right offence timing. You also learn about different and unique wrestlers. The styles that combined with their stats makes each wrestler encourage a specific tactic. From agile luchador like Rey Fenix to immovable wall Wardlow, from aggressor Lance Archer to cheater MJF. You learn about each wrestlers strengths and weaknesses, you find opportunities and threats that you have to acknowledge.Customisation: Lacking a lot of ways of creating your wrestler, you can still make something if you are creative (for example Roman Reigns), but as of now there are not many choices. But, yet again, the creation suite if it is a foundation upon which they add content. I can see it being really good. Right now, the create a wrestler seems like a template for a create a wrestler mode. I wouldn't buy this game for create a wrestler. 2K far superior in that case.Lack of Features: Lack of modes, only 4 wrestlers can be in the ring. That is what I heard so far. I don't think 4 wrestler limit is a negative. I think it is a really big positive. Think about it, when you played 6 man, 8 man matches. How much control you had. For me, it was fun to play once or twice. After honeymoon phase passed, and I learned how to play, those modes looked broken and unbalanced to the point they were just annoying to play. That is why 1v1 and 2v2 always were more fun to play. 3 way and 4 way matches are already really chaotic, so why add even more chaos. In 4 Way even when  it is chaotic, you can at least do something without everyone constantly getting in your way (or camera view going as high as the sealing).The choice to keep this game a Balanced Arcade Fighter really shows. As the matches flow fast and when you know how to do what you want, there will not be ton of things you can't control getting in your way. Matches last around 3min. But if you are a good player, you will avoid getting hit with a finisher or a signature (make sense for a wrestling game).I wish there would be more modes like 4 way Ladder, 3 way ladder, Steel Cage (pin/submission), Iron Man, Two out of Three falls. I can see them adding those matches later on in few years. Depends on how much devs and publisher listens to the feedback.This is where the price tag comes, it's a lot of money. Still, we all know Pro Wrestling is a niche culture, and Pro Wrestling Games aren't most popular fighting games (Tekken,MK,Street Fighter). It's expensive to keep servers running, and you can't keep a product alive if it only costs you money without returning anything for your investment. It can't be just good faith, I can see the price tag validated for those who want to support the development of this game. It's not called early access, as it is finished and can be played and enjoyed. But, if they do actually intend to add more content to it, then DLC and the Price tag is the only thing that will give them a reason to keep it going. Smaller audience, bigger price.I bought a game, that I a AEW total Mark really like. And I also wanted to support the product that I got a bit of faith in. I knew it will be bad as it's their first game, but now when I play it, it is actually a fun game. By the way, for those who want to play online, go join AEW Fight Forever Discord group (just get Discord, do that for all Online games, best place to find normal non toxic people to play any online games with). Devs encourage to join the Discord as well, because you can find Online matches, but it takes a lot of time to search via game. And there are ton of people in official Discord group that wants to play against anyone and just have fun.I gave a long summary about this game and why I see ton of potential in it, while it is also a good game already if you know how to play. But, that summary (that took 2 hours to write), got deleted after I clicked Allow Comments.... Anyone want to destroy me and my Main Eddie Kingston are welcome to invite.I recommend this game to those who like to learn the mechanics of a game. There is actual depth that is hard to see at first. Great foundation game-play wise

_childDocuments_.review: FOR THE FULL REVIEW CHECK OUT MY VIDEO? :) //Graphics, Sound & Artstyle//The graphics make some of the wrestlers seem almost like action figures, it reminds me of a modern take on WWE All Stars- which is something that is very welcomed after the blunder of WWE's Battleground game. The music in the menus isn't very loud & the entrance music seems like an afterthought.//Gameplay//Some are hailing AEW FF as an arcade game and while that may be true that the unlimited stamina & spammable dodges can seem like so, at it's core it's still a wrestling game. You have a health bar that also coincides with the momentum you have, the more on the offensive you are, the more momentum you have, the easier it is to pull off a Signature+Finisher to beat your opponent. Something I really enjoyed was being able to change the controller layout. I couldn't find my footing with B as a sprint button to I changed it to Left Trigger, made B my grapple button, A my kicks, X my punches and Y my irish whip. Left bumper & Right bumper account for grapple reversals & strike reversals. and right joystick will taunt. It's a very simplified system, that is, and I know this sounds cliche but easy to learn hard to master.Road to Elite- what I think is the absolute best thing going for FF. It's essentially a season mode. You pick a wrestler, & you start the first year of AEW. It shows an amazing video package that I can't show you for copyright reasons- & has you answer the call from Tony Khan to be announced in the infamous press conference.From there you enter a Casino Royale, if you win- you get a title shot. But unless you pick someone OP like Matt Jackson, more than likely you'll lose and the game will trigger one of three storylines or "blocks". There are four major PPVs, and you'll be going week after week throughout the map having matches, going to dinner, hanging out, doing meet & greets, working out & everything else a pro wrestler does. Every week you get 4 turns before you have to show up to Dynamite & wrestle there. How you choose to spend your time, will effect everything going forward (mainly for Created Wrestlers since AEW Wrestlers cant gain anything new to their repertoire). When you win a match or work out you can get skill points that you can spend on buffs, or stat boosts for your run. NOTE THAT ALL CAW will not be able to have any buffs, extra finishers/signatures unless you grind it out on RTE.//Is it Playable on Steamdeck?//No unless you have windows installed, it is not playable. Might be the anticheat or the Epic connection, i really wanted to try it but could not. Instead I played it on my Asus ROG Ally like a peach. Actually my preferred way of playing it was with the handheld. //Final Thoughts//Gameplay is loads of fun! Creative mode doesnt have enough for a wrestling game, 100 CAW slots, move sets need to have menu options like in WWE games, too many moves will have you scrolling nonstop for your favorite moves, and some moves like the F-5 are named something else. I kept saying the word underwhelming, and it still feels that way. Road to Elite needs more than 16 weeks especially considering whatever your CAW finishes with stat wise, that'll be theirs forever (unless you beat the mode all over with em but it resets your skills). If you're a wrestling fan you're more than likely gonna buy this, but if you're on the fence, 60 USD is NOT worth it. Wait for it to go on sale. //Wait for Sale//

_childDocuments_.review: Simple Answer: AEW: Fight Forever is one of the best wrestling games made in the last ten years. It's certainly better than anything WWE has released in the last decade.  More Detail: I'm going to date myself here. Think about the first time you played WCW/NWO World Tour. It was amazing! No wrestling game had ever been like it before. Did you ever go back and play WCW/NWO World Tour after WWF No Mercy came out? Complete opposite reaction. The game looked, and played terrible. You where amazed you put so many hours into it just a couple years prior. That's how I feel about AEW: Fight Forever. It's a good start, but as the series develops, I hope we can look back on this game to see how much the series has progressed. I bought this game when it game out, and I regret doing that. I should have waited until it was priced around $30 - $40. There isn't much content here, and there are still game play issues that need to be patched. If you're a wrestling fan, pick it up when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: While it might feel a bit bare boned to it's competitors, it's a great start. Graphics a lot better than WWE 2K games. For someone who spends a lot of time in creation suites, I appreciate who more detailed your wrestler is in AEW over WWE games. You might have more options to customize in WWE, but more isn't always better. Looking at my character's build, they actually have anti aliasing on the majority of their body. Also, I've dumped a ton of hours in to it so far and I haven't had any game crashes. That in itself is worth the price of admission for me. I don't know how many times I've lost hours in WWE creation suites to fine tune my gear for the game to crash.. and lose like an hours worth of work. Plus, save scumming is horrendous and not suggested in WWE 2K games either, because of the horrid loading screens. Meanwhile, AEW has like 2-3s.I like what they've tried to be different on. I like wrestling games in general, I've been playing them since the 80's. This isn't a WCW Nitro or WCW Thunder throwaway arcade button masher. You can be very exact if you want to be in your attacks/strikes. I like the fast paced action, even WWE games have been trying to speed things up on their end from the ultra realism with adding striking combos for pickup style button mashers and even sped up animations.I don't need full entrances or 2000 pieces of gear to be satisfied. Sometimes we lose sight in what's fun. WWE games, I spend more time in creation suites and loading screens than I do in matches. I wish AEW's creation suites had more meat on them, but I like what they've done so far. It just means for the first time in a long time, I might play as the actual wrestlers in the game.. crazy concept I know!Also, it doesn't have the 300 person roster that WWE touts around these days, but the reality is any die-hards download or make their own "superstars", they might play with less than 10 of the pre-built characters. Again, more doesn't mean better. As a wrestling fan, comparing WWE 2K to Fight Forever isn't equal. One is arcade, the other is simulation. I wouldn't review Streets of Rage the same as Diablo or Marvel Ultimate Alliance.AEW fans will like this. Older fans who have nostalgia for late 90s to early 00s will like this. It's a fun pick-up game. Plays well on Steam Deck as well. While I like the depth WWE games can have in modes, I don't like the technical issues that seem to come along with it. If lesser is better in that regard, AEW is your champion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little tricky to rate at the time of this review. A lot of the gripes I think are legitimate. Not having full entrances that you can skip at your leisure is an egregious misfire. A major part of the pro wrestling experience is the entrance. Not having enough of the current roster available, especially the women, is another glaring omission. The match types available are a lot of fun. Lights Out and especially the barbed wire death match are unique, brutal, and fun, but not having a standard cage match? That's awful. It's risky to make promises based on the sales of the game. It's what killed Retromania Wrestling. If they end up scrapping this game and making a sequel, I hope some lessons will be learned. I'm recommending this because the controls and gameplay itself are something that's been missing from wrestling games for quite some time. It handles just like the N64 games and the graphics are not a legitimate complaint. They look like action figures which fits perfectly with the arcade vibe of the game. Playing matches is so fun and addicting that it would be difficult for me to tell someone not to play it. It's good, but with an asterisk.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun pick up and play AEW pro wrestling game that mechanically lands somewhere between older Smackdown games, Day of Reckoning, and some light homages to the AKI games. Very little meat on the bone, but what's here has been fun and stable, Anyone who doesn't care much about CAW. Any passionate AEW fan. Anyone looking for a wrestling game that doesn't take itself too seriously. Anyone demanding deep CAW. Anyone who demands a serious tone in their wrestling. Anyone who demands endless modes like Universe, or things like GM mode. Anyone who wants crossplay, rollback, etc. Anyone looking for true AKI style gameplay and mechanics. To be clear, this game  play like No Mercy or the other AKI games. It plays like Yuke's games but with some AKI elements sprinkled in.I've been having a lot of fun with it. Matches flow well, weapon spots are incredibly satisfying, the quick pace of the story mode is refreshing, and the skeleton Yuke's and AEW have crafted here is solid. It's definitely nowhere near as mind numbingly frustrating in terms of  as 2K22 was (see my review of that game if you're curious as to what I'm talking about, and many of the same issues persisting in 2K23 is why I'm not buying it,) other than limited CAW.  An issue which still persists.The game needs more content and quality of life improvements. More CAW parts, changes to entrance attire, improved AI in some areas, and an expansion of RTE's branching elements to provide more awareness of players' choices. If they can actually pull all of those things off, this could be one of the most enjoyable wrestling games I've played in a long time.For now, it's a fun but flawed alternative to the 2K games, and a good representation of AEW's product, generally speaking. I will happily update the review to Recommended if the Owen Hart unlock issue is addressed. (Thus far it hasn't been.) For now, the game is fun enough for me to recommend it with caveats, but only if such issues are addressed. The pricey DLC that doesn't really address other shortcomings also gives me pause. The game  though. I want to underscore that.
