_childDocuments_.review: People anticipating this game: I'm so excited, we're getting a return to No Mercy!!!People when this game came out: wtf this is exactly what I asked for, I rather spend 200 bucks on Bugfest 2K23 with the invisible man showcase, now THAT is somehow worth money, the lovely unfinished mess that it is every year.Okay, I did the jokes that hopefully drove away the empty headed dumb ♥♥♥♥♥, so let's talk. First off, I did get a review code for this on PS5, but truth be told, I don't think I was even able to fully discuss the game due to a few issues I'm not sure I can discuss publicly, but now that I've played the game more now that it's officially out(and love it enough that I bought it on PC), I feel I can be more accurate about this game.To get this aside, I tried the game on Steam Deck. Despite them saying it runs fine on there, you're gonna have to set up Proton 8.0-2 to get it to run, and even then it's gonna take a bit to boot it up. Other than that, it runs great, but MAN is it a battery drainer. In addition, no, your Epic Games account login info is not malware like that one guy said, it's literally just asking for your account so you can play with people who got the game on EGS. "Oh no, I have crossplay with Xbox? But they're GREEN!!!"Now onto the game. The gameplay is an almost full return to No Mercy and encompasses what made it great. The action is a fresh take on wrestling games that DESPERATELY has been needed with WWE 2K having been on top for so long that people like me play 3 modes and then abandon it till the next entry. The modded CAWs of MyRise characters upped the replay value, but 2K hates replay value for some reason and put a lock on them. Money is such a burden, really.The Create a Superstar mode is largely what it was in No Mercy, but that doesn't exactly mean it's good, cause I'm sorry to say it's not. I'm a minimalist with this mode. I choose whatever face is the first one, put on facepaint, and then choose the attire I want. Every other CAW is downloaded online. However, for the people that aren't like me, this sucks. I personally hope they're able to patch in more options, but I also wouldn't be surprised if they pull a Bungie and just make a sequel with most of the problems fixed and then continue to support that entry.Create a Moveset is better, but I personally think it's lacking in a few move categories, and it would definitely benefit from a better search mechanic. Create an Entrance is short and sweet, like the entrances. I love how you can just use pyro in every entrance(except for Malakai who just uses groundlights), I admittedly have fun just mashing the buttons to make the pyro go crazy. The match type selection is admittedly lacking, but....no, it just is. The Exploding Barbed Wire Deathmatch is neat, and the Lights Out match is fun even if they're sanctioned despite the entire point of that match existing is to not sanction it for the record books as AEW would not want any part of the bloodshed that match is known for.The Ladder Match is okay, but sadly, you can't do a diving finisher off a ladder through a table. Hell, you can't do a diving finisher off a ladder, period. AND you can only set the ladder up in the middle of the ring. Some have set every weapon you get from under the ring is a ladder, but in my experience, most of the time I wasn't able to get a ladder. I then found there was a prone one on the opposite side of the ring. Still dumber than Ryback.Road to Elite is an interesting story mode that you can use to bulk up your CAW, but big warning. You are NOT going to be able to upgrade everything and get every single skill, as the mode only lasts 1 in-game year, which is technically only 16 in-game weeks because of the 4 PPVs. No Fyter Fest, no Grand Slam, and no Fight for the Fallen(bring that one back please, btw). Plus, if you use the CAW again, you don't get to keep what you unlocked as they don't exactly overlap, but you can have your extra signatures and finishers. You just can't upgrade their strength without officially unlocking the slot for them. I have no idea if anything unlocked from the first playthrough sticks around after the 2nd playthrough, and I don't wanna test it so as to risk losing any skills. It's also how you unlock the late great Mr. Brodie Lee(how you get the match against him is admittedly funny, if not a bit messed up), and Paul Wight.Paul Wight hates you, the storyline you unlock him in hates you, and no matter how much you try to show it love, it is going to freaking suck. Long story short, you're stuck having to beat him in less than 3 minutes, and he's insanely unfair. It also doesn't help that because he's a giant, he's mostly resistant to strikes at first. I heard the best way to win is via count out, but every time I tried that, I had to close the game and restart it(you can't just restart the match, and quitting the match itself counts as a loss), so in one of my failed attempts, I felt I roughed him up enough outside that I could affect him with my strikes, spammed signatures for a bit, and hit him with 2 finishers straight. I might have needed a 3rd, but I was too miffed to register that moment.I have not tried the online yet, and I admittedly have no interest in it. On top of that, intergender wrestling is back in AAA wrestling games!!! If you face a woman as a man to vent frustrations or just for the sake of having power over one, please seek help or never interact with society, ya sick bastard. There's also an in-game shop you spend in-game money on, with ZERO microtransactions btw(thank Christ), and the money is earned at such big amounts and so quickly that not once does it feel like a grind. Oh, that reminds me. You don't actually unlock Brodie and Paul, you "unlock" them in that you unlock the right to buy them in the in-game store. Veerrrrrrrry stupid, if you ask me. Oh, and you get the right to unlock Owen Hart by doing 100 Exhibition matches. even with this game not feeling like a grind when you play it, that DOES feel like one. Now, in all fairness, this is how games used to be before publishers had greedy ideas to fatten their wallets just a bit further, in that you had to work to unlock the content, so....yeah. *So retro* or whatever.Of course, like with every WWE release since the HD gaming era started, there are bugs that will need to be patched out, and it includes a weird one where some wrestlers don't have their full signature list visible in the pause menu section, affecting but not limited to Lance Archer, Nyla Rose, and even CM "I'm gonna cause AEW to die because I don't know how to own up to my actions, aren't I?" Punk. Weird alias, if you ask me. I ain't gonna pretend others' experience are bs, but all I can say is I haven't experienced anything major or gamebreaking. Mostly just stuff you tend to see in a WWE release.In conclusion, this game's worth your money, as the gameplay has me coming back with such an amazing fresh take on it, to the point that on PS5 I've beaten Road to Elite 4 times, and plan to play it more. It feels fresh to do it with different wrestlers cause of the different things they'd say as well as the different interactions you'll have in it for some of the storylines. I honestly don't understand why everyone is crying about "no content" like a parrot when they probably buy the same game every single year with no changes outside of a roster update. And yes, I do mean Madden.I look forward to what this game will offer in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review With Positives & Constructive CriticismA Good Wrestling Game. A solid foundation to start for AEW games. The game has great gameplay, just wish that matches went longer. RTE is a good mode with many different outcomes. Character Models look great, but we need more updates and attires. Stadium Stampede is a pretty cool and innovative mode. Another thing that’s innovative is characters having voice lines and special abilities for themselves (Orange Cassidy’s Sloth Style). Blood and gore in this game is incredible, no other wrestling game has it at this level. Unfortunately, their are a lot of limitations. Creation suite is sadly disappointing. Barely any faces and attires to use. Lack of body sizes and face morphing is not there. Customization of actual wrestlers are limited as well. I want to change the colour on an attire and want to switch a wrestler’s tights to trunks, and can not. Also, the game absolutely needs a Community Creations. We need more match types: Cage Match, Casino Gauntlet, Handicap match (which is in RTE, but not on menus), Blood And Guts, Table Match, Backstage, etc.  More modes as well. Continental Classic, Owen Hart Tournament. GM mode would be fun in this game.Overall this is good foundation to start a wrestling game franchise on. I can’t wait for the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: I do think it is a good game. You do get to do things in this game that you can’t in the 2K games. And its nice to have a wrestling game from a major promotion that does not give me trouble on the PC, like the 2K games have. But its not without its issues. The various criticisms of the game are reasonable, considering it was promised that “the game would have all the modes it’s supposed to have” and it supposed to “be like No Mercy”.  This is how the game was marketed.The developers idea of “sensibilities” are as follows:- Lots of minigames- A passable career mode and creation suite- A limited number of match types, with no ability to adjust the ruleset.- Controlling pyro in entrance (which is creative, I’ll give ‘em that)- Short entrances (which, in hindsight, was a good choice for matchtypes such as exploding barbed wire deathmatch)- A UI that’s like No Mercy- Can only boost CAW stats in RTE- Freedom to map controls to your liking (another cool feature)My idea of “sensibilities” would be as follows:- Tournament of 16 singles or 8 tag teams (choose between Eliminator, Owen Hart, Tag Team, Championship); byes possible- League mode of 16 singles or 8 tag teams (aka NJPW’s G1 & World Tag League)- Ref control; playing as Aubrey when she refs the match and playing as Aubrey when she wrestles against an opponent are two very different things.- Select entrants and suits in Casino Battle Royal- Trios matches, singles and tag team Iron man, singles and tag team parking lot brawl, tag team and casino ladder matches, 2 vs 1, gauntlet, singles and tag team backstage brawl, singles and tag team steel cage as matchtypes alongside the current selection. Maybe even a coffin match.- Control length of matches with short play, normal and long play- More CAW parts, faces, and moves in CAW- More freedom in CAA (why can’t I select the color tone of the canvas and turnbuckles, but I can select the color tone for the spotlights and the ring ropes? And why tease NJPW style turnbuckles if I can’t choose the turnbuckle for each corner?)- More CAA decals, logos & matchup screens (Dynamite ’19 &’20, Beach Break, Battle of the Belts, Blood & Guts, Fight for the Fallen, Fyter Fest, Grand Slam, St. Patrick’s Day Slam, New Years Smash, Holiday Bash, Road Rager, Collision, ROH PPVs, factions such as the BCC, etc) - An image uploader if CAA will remain barebones- Jericho Cruise, Daily’s Place, Nightmare Factory, TIAA Bank Field and Tokyo Dome as alternate venues to the standard venue in the game- Better AI (COM vs COM is disappointing to watch most of the time, to say the least)- Give people a Create a PPV mode if they aren’t going to be given a GM/Universe/some type of management or calendar mode- A DLC roadmap for new AEW stars, arenas, moves for create-a-moveset, mode like create-a-championship, and other goodies- Able to boost CAW stats outside of RTE- Ability to turn off replay- Be able to climb the tables that are set up- Palette swaps when editing the roster- Electric chair move; I can’t even set up my own variation of the Doomsday Device like in the AKI games- An extra 25-50 CAW save slots- An accountability system for online, to deal with quitters- Adjustable Ruleset from the AKI games (the most stunning omission of all): Pin: Y/NSub: Y/NTKO: Y/NCount out: 10 count, 20 count, none, no exit, falls count anywhere, lumberjackRope break: Y/NDQ: Y/NInterference: Y/NBlood: Y/N/First BloodTime limit: 5 min, 10 min, 20 min, 30 min 60 min, no limitTag help time: 5 sec, 10 sec, 20 sec, 30 sec, 60 sec, no tagMMA/Shoot: 1 round, 2 rounds, 3 rounds, 4 rounds, 5 roundsI enjoy this game. But I’m also not going to pretend it’s a 10/10 or even a 7/10. The game lacks depth. and in its current state is not worth the full price  Hopefully future updates make it a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and the Road to Elite mode has some nice replayability but thats where most of the pros end. The amount of match types you can play are few and they leave you unsatisfied as even just a table match isnt an option. The Road to Elite mode is good, but the story is weak. Once winning a title or making a story changing move nothing happens. You dont delve deeper into the storyline and instead just move on to winning another title. It would be nice to linger on stories longer and fully go through with one instead of just racing through the brands titles. I'd reccommend anyone who wants to buy it to wait for more content to come out or for the price to drop under $40.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing: If you enjoy AEW, more than likely, you'll enjoy this game. If you already have a problem with the SHOW, you will LOATHE this game because (spoiler) it features the same wrestlers and feel of the show.Like AEW itself, this game shines best between the bells. Unfortunately, (like AEW) outside of the in-ring action, it leaves a bit to be desired. With how obscenely bloated AEW's roster is, the pittance on disc is not okay. Beyond this, those who ARE in the game are painfully outdated i.e. Alien-face Kris Statlander, Le Champion Jericho, etc. There is no clear timeline cut off, and I'm baffled how The Acclaimed didn't make the cut, but Yuka Sakazaki did? I personally wonder if they didn't just drop the game so it could start making money, because it feels unfinished (looking at you junky, janky, trashy minigames).Overall, I do recommend this game as a GAME. By that I mean, it's a whole lot of fun. Even with the lacking match types and - Ugh, SERIOUSLY! THIS ROSTER!!! - anyway, sorry - It's way more fun to play than WWE 2kAnything. My hope is they make good on the premise of Fight Forever and release a healthy helping of FREE DLC. I get there will be paid expansions down the road, but I feel there's a bit of a good-faith lay away going on here.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a wrestling game in 4 years and this is definitely becoming one of my favorites because of the easily learned yet challenging combat, the entertainingly over the top and goofy mini-games, and the amount of personality in AEW's roster and the references or appearances of wrestlers I recognized from my WWE fanboy days. My only gripes would be how short and repetitive Road to Elite mode felt once I came back to it to farm in game currency, the somewhat small list of Exhibition match modes (mostly overshadowed in my opinion by exciting Exploding Barbed Wire matches), an in game store that feels a little dead and empty until more items are unlocked for purchase, and a severely  lacking set of customization options when creating custom wrestlers. _childDocuments_.review: The game is far from perfect, and one can't help but see where bugs or little annoyances that really shouldn't be there. These include relatively small things the mouse pointer not disappearing, limited (and sometimes confusing) physical and clothing customisation in created wrestlers. There are also bigger issues like the limited online player base, lack of crossplay, and lack of a lobby system, which together makes it hard to find online matches. That said, there is also a lot to love about this game if you are a fan of AEW. Lots of love went into the wrestlers and the career mode, and it really celebrates the rise of AEW. There is a pretty deep roster, and the wrestlers feel and look as they should. I can have a lot of fun even playing against CPUs. Although the physical customisation is lacking for created wrestlers, the movesets, traits, and skills go pretty deep, and you can end up with a very authentic feeling wrestler.The game could be a little or even a lot better with the right patches and some potential add-ons, but even as it is, I think it is pretty good, and I keep going back to it.
_childDocuments_.name: AEW: Fight Forever

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Fight Forever is a great game. There's a good selection of characters, an easy to pick up (yet hard to completely master immediately) grappling system and the little references, taunts, and weapons that AEW fans will love. Older fans will love how familiar AEW:FF feels to N64 wrestling titles, like VPW2, WCW: Revenge and No Mercy. The only major drawback is the lack of unique match types -  more options, rule customization and gimmicks are desperately needed. I have not tested online as no players were available when i attempted to match. I preferred playing through the ROAD TO ELITE mode with AEW characters. Having said that, the create-a-wrestler mode is anemic and should be completely re-done/revamped/reimagined as it's impossible to create unique characters with such a limited selection of assets. Body parts, body morphing, clothing types, etc are all pathetic here. The mode should've been held until it was ready for prime time. Visually, Fight Forever is adequate. The animations, however, are simply impressive, and the game is running smooth as Orange Cassidy on my PC. i7-9750 6 core CPU, 32GB RAM, Nvidea RTX 3060Ti 12GB.Wish list: -Ability to slow matches down or change damage sliders to create more epic, drawn out matches. Since the core mechanics of a great wrestling game are here, I believe this is possible. AEW on TV is known for wrestlers sometimes kicking out of multiple finishing moves/after big spots, so the game should have this too. -Table improvements-CAW revamp/assets added-Match variety/options accessible: 3 and 4-way matches aren't an option but appear in the ROAD TO ELITE mode. -Longer entrances, even if its just the wrestler walking down the ramp, into the ring/through the ropes.I really enjoy AEW: Fight Forever, I just hope some quality of life and overall updates/fixes are coming along with new DLC

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This review was previously positive. This is no longer the case, as the realization has hit that AEW has no real incentive to make this game better over time, only to drain the money of its players. Season Pass 2 is a joke. Charging $30 for a new gamemode when your game is already believed as being not worth its base price tag for its lack of singleplayer content is a joke. Charging money for an arena, something purely cosmetic that even 2K doesn't charge for normally, is a joke. Please don't encourage them continuing this behavior by giving them your money.My previous review preserved for archiving purposes.---I will start by saying Fight Forever has its problems, that much can't be denied. At launch state, it's got its glitches, random match types (Gauntlets and multi-man ladder matches) are locked behind Road to Elite for seemingly no reason, there's an arbitrary limit of 4 people in a match at one time, and its creation suites also have some unfortunate limitations, like not being able to add custom logos or even use all the same attire parts that the base cast have; if you're expecting it to look anything like 2K creation suites, you're gonna be disappointed.On the other hand, what it does right, it does damn right. The core gameplay is really good - I've been having a blast through every match I've played (even the ones where I got my ass kicked) - and while many groaned at first when they heard you had to do Road to Elite to build custom characters' stats, it definitely has more than enough ways to keep you entertained for a while, with each runthrough getting different storylines and such at random instead of a predetermined path, keeping it feeling fresh every time you go through it.Overall, if you know you're gonna be disappointed by the limitations it has right now, I'd say not to buy as-is right now; wait a little while for new content patches to come out, hold out for it to start getting discounts and then consider it. But, I've been having a blast with it personally even despite its problems, so when a discount does roll up, I'd recommend it.

I enjoyed it more with my Created Wrestler because the stat points you accumulate actually were of use.If you're on the fence about purchasing, I would strongly suggest waiting for additional content to be added, and picking it up when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoy this game. It reminds me of some of my favorite wrestling games in the 90s and early 2000s. There are a couple of standard match types that are not available as of this review but the ones that were added in are exciting enough to keep you busy like the exploding barbwire deathmatch. Road to Elite is short but fun. I hear a lot of gripe about graphics but this game looks fine to me. The art style here looks great IMO! Its definitely more on the  'arcadey' side but it looks great. The subtle touches like the sloth style fighting stance or 'heel begging' only to lure you in are awesome!!! Its been a while since a wrestling game has made me pop. I have to give this game extra points for the thumbtacks. literally made me jump out of my seat. You get to ride a skate board off of MJFs forehead... enough said. I do wish there was a a little more to the CAW mode. Also a Universe type game mode would be nice. The roster is a little outdated but I noticed that it can be user updated and modified. I cant wait for STADIUM STAMPEDE!!! The reveal had me intrigued.All and all its been a great game so far. I wanna see this game down the road once we get a few more updates. i definitely recommend this game especially if you are an All Elite Wrestling fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be fun, though I don't care about depth when creating a wrestler, and I know that's a major point of contention for many players. However, I have one huge issue that doesn't seem to come up much: the difficulty, even on Elite mode, is insanely low. It's hard for me to envision ever losing a 1v1 or tag team match to a computer opponent; occasionally, there are scary moments in 3-way and 4-way matches, but they almost always work out. Even 2v1 handicap matches (which only show up in the game's decent, but not outstanding, story mode) feel like a tossup, though 3v1 is a nightmare. The single player game can't be fun if there's not even a small amount of drama after playing a game for a few hours...and I'm not even an experienced wrestling gaming fan. I'll give the game a Yes, but it's a very soft one because of the lack of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW Fight Forever lacks depth but is still very fun to play and is probably the most pure fun I've had with a new wrestling game since WWE All-Stars. It won't be for everyone (at least not at launch) but for those craving a new wrestling game that turns away from sim style gameplay for something a little more fast and fun then it's worth giving a shot.+Gameplay is great! Easy to pick up and play but with enough depth for more experienced players to really enjoy.+Each wrestler really feels unique and a great reflection of their real-life counterparts.+The animations are fantastic and add to the impact of the gameplay.+Road to Elite single player mode is short but has different paths to explore that encourage multiple playthroughs. Plus the RPG-very-lite between match stuff reminded me of the Yakuza games a little so that's cool.+Lots of weapons, crazy matches and blood!+Great to play with friends!-The creation/customization suite absolutely sucks right now but THQ is planning on expanding it (and the game a whole) with updates so hopefully any big gripes will be fixed over time.-Roster has some notable absences-RTE might be too basic for some people and the cool Yakuza-like stuff can get repetitive after several playthroughs.-Ranked online matches are fun but there are too many people cheesing them or quitting.-Odd quirks like moves not being sorted, match types in RTE that aren't selectable in VS, "customizable" wrestler attire thats limited to t-shirts.

_childDocuments_.review: Good old AEW: Wait Forever... is it worth it ? The short answer is yes, it is and it can and is very much so an enjoyable experience.  It has some nods to the old school n64 titles while existing in a more present atmosphere.  Are the graphics pore visible realism ? no.. it is far from it.  Are they better than PS2 as often compared to ? of course! People grab for low hanging fruit usually and intent was never hyper realism by any stretch and that was communicated early, so as for visible presentation.. as expected and met my expectations. I have 2k series if i am looking for a more realistic experience and on that same note a deeper creative experience.  AEW lacks in the creative department, did not keep me coming back.Online when you can get a match, smooth so far, the odd laggy match but that faults the peer to peer portion imo.Content, it also lacks which is where in it's current state paying full price for it may be a sore spot, i did not mind as i was under the impression it was going to be built upon.  I just hope that remains true going forward as there is a lot of faces missing that should be features in this game and would be a shocker if some never get included IE: Private Party, Acclaimed, Butcher and Blade, Evil Uno, Sonny Kiss, The Factory, etc.  The game play is really where i enjoy it a lot and it does keep me dipping in for some matches, albeit limited at the moment and in hopes of getting more variety, it still plays very nice.  I definitely recommend if you enjoy wrestling and you like a more arcade approach that has nods to some old school favorites, just know it is more of an investment than a full toy box.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun but not perfect by any means.  The game play is sort of a blend of the old PS1 Smackdown! and N64 No Mercy / Wresltemania 2000 games, which for me is exactly what I wanted in a wrestling game.  This is the most important thing to me, the core of the game is excellent.  On the downside - The AI is a bit of a pain during Tag, Ladder, 3 way & 4 way matches.  1 on 1 and the Battle Royal matches seem to work out the best.  There's not as many match types as I'd like, should be a steel cage one for example.  The CAW is limited and the main roster is out of date and seems to be missing a lot of wrestlers that should be included.  The pinning / kick out system is not good, it needs to be much easier to kick out of pins both for the player and the CPU.  You can get pinned without ever taking a signature move or finisher, the button mashing system for kicking out favours the person doing the pin far too much and need re-balancing to get longer matches and avoid cheap early wins/loses.  All the downsides are fixable IMO, it's already much more fun than the WWE 2k games and with some tweaks would wipe the floor with it.
_childDocuments_.name: AEW: Fight Forever

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta get this out straight away.This is legit the most fun that I have had with a wrestling game since...WWE 2K15???It brings back that love that I have had for wrestling back when I was no-lifing SvR 2011 and copying all of the CAWs from online forums and trying to get platinum (which I never could after the servers shut down). The gameplay is fun and chaotic, the models look WAY WAY WAY better than the goofy portraits that they chose for the game menus, and I really don't mind the visuals at all. They really make the game stand out from 2K's clearly visual focused titles. (I'm sorry, I don't enjoy the "simulation" gameplay that every sports games are leaning towards.)THAT BEING SAID.This game is absolutely overpriced for what we have at the moment.I wouldn't say it's UNFINISHED but MAN do I wish there was more...stuff. This creative suite is actually quite laughable, the match types have a lot left to be desired and the main campaign is silly but goodness could they have gotten a better performance from JR or just use Excalibur? AND MORE ACTUAL VOICE ACTING? I mean, they have all of the wrestlers VOICED IN COMBAT. Would I recommend this game RIGHT NOW?If you are an AEW fan or a fan of the old N64 games, go for it! Other than that, wait for a sale and more content. They definitely seem like they have a road-map and I think I trust them to add more to this title. All in all, I am thoroughly enjoying it and can't wait to see what else AEW and Yuke's has in store.

_childDocuments_.review: For the hour and a half I played, I did think the game was fun. However that's all I really have to say about it. The matches were fun to play, but with the amount of match types there are, it's hard to want to play it again, and I can't not mention the how the game looks. I really don't like how the game looks. The models to me look like action figures, The arenas feel empty and straight up boring. I didn't feel compelled to pick a specific arena over another. The entrances being short also is a bummer, I find it more immersive to see the full entrance, I'll skip it if I don't want to see it, just let me be able to see the entrances. Lastly, I really got annoyed with the music playing during the match. Maybe there was a setting to change it, honestly I didn't look. It's such a minor problem compared to everything else but I felt like mentioning itall in all, this game could be an all time great game, but the game as it is? It simply disappointed me

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a middle of the road option. The mechanics play like a PS1/2 wrestling game which is good but there are several issues with it those games didn't have. The targeting system is pretty wonky. In old wrestling games you'd hit the target toggle and it would swap easily. This one will only swap if you are close and a downed wrestler's position can make it impossible for you to target them in a safe position. I honestly don't think the difficulty slider works! Like the ai seems to be supper tweaked in aggressive if you are targeted by 2 or more wrestlers. The counter system will just stop working then and you will just lose. Single player content is lacking, the create a character's are extremely limited with so many parts being unavailable in matches and parts being gender locked (especially hair styles). The story mode is insanely basic and none of the stories have a satisfying conclusion and arcs don't have any carry over. I became the AEW champ and then it never was brought up again. I do like that all the wrestlers are voice acted in matches though.I can't recommend this game for it's full price, not with it's lack of content. I'd wait for a sale of no more than 30 bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, no major complaints here. Although customization and match types are the only thing holding it back from being worth the full $60 for more casual players. Updates to the game are coming, so current/future players should be on the look out for more content in the works. My wish list would include longer entrances, a universe mode of some kind, logos for caws, props for arenas, and an increase in CPU's in match to allow more than 4 at once. Hopefully a Blood and Guts match is doable as well.With all that said, the game is still a blast to play. It's an 7.5-8/10 for me. I'll update the review once more additions get released.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW Fight Forever is a really good wrestling game that I'm having a lot of fun with.  I do think it's price is pretty steep given some of it's faults.Game-play is easy to pick up and learn. Move animations look good, although they're not perfect and there are times when you can notice that. The roster isn't as deep as I'd like it to be. Most of my favorite AEW wrestlers are there, but there are some who are noticeably absent. Game matches and types are fun, but I do wish there were more match types and stipulations. -For example; Ladder Match, Falls Count Anywhere Match, Lights Out Match & Exploding Barbed Wire Death Matches are exclusively 1v1.-There does not seem to be any special match types for 2v2, 3-way, & 4-way matches outside of normal exhibition matches. There is also a Casino Battle Royal match which is fun but there are definitely bugs. -I had duplicate wrestlers come out during the match.  -I had a bug where wrestlers stopped coming out unless there was only 1 person left in the ring. There were many wrestlers who could have come out and filled the ring, but they trickled in allowing only 1v1 at a time.Road to Elite mode was more fun than I was expecting. I am still on my first playthrough, and I am enjoying the experience so far. I am definitely going to play this game mode a few times.The minigames are a fun addition, the few that are included in the base game are OK, but I understand the season pass will be adding more as time goes on. The FTR DLC is weird because you getting a tag-team DLC, but they don't come into the game as a tag-team that you can select. -I had to go to the Creation part of the game to create a "custom" tag team, but really I was just pairing Dax and Cash together for the game to recognize them officially as FTR. -I had to make sure I selected the correct entrance animation, video, finishing tag move, etc. It would be nice if future DLC like this did this process for you for tag teams.I think what will "make or break" this game is how they handle this coming season pass of content, and what their long term plans are.  I would be a little annoyed if a newer, better version of this game came out next year (like WWE's 2k Series), but if they support this game for 2 years or so with updates, roster additions, new matches & minigames. If you enjoy wrestling games, this will be a good casual gaming experience that you can enjoy by yourself or with friends, this game just feels like it should be ~$50.
_childDocuments_.name: AEW: Fight Forever

_childDocuments_.review: Got a bit of gameplay under my belt on this now and have some comments.TL;DR - The game is fun, and it is an excellent baseline for what could be a fantastic sequel. This game is not much more than arcade fun though. If you're looking for a decent Create mode, you're going to be disappointed. If you're looking for heavy storylines, the career mode is woefully short. It's fun but far from perfect.Long one:The game is fun. When you are playing it, it is easy to pick up, feels familiar if you played any of the N64 games in the Yukes pedigree, and has a good sized (though limited) roster. Unlike many AAA games released these days, this one released without crippling performance issues. It is easily playable right out the gate. Pop in a controller and play a game that feels like a direct descendant of many great games of the past.It has excellent bones, and is an excellent first product in that regard. I have high hopes for it as a series or at least with solid expansion pack like DLCs that aren't just roster expansions. As is, I had a great time hooking up 4 controllers and playing it with my kids. Which just made me feel young again.The bad though... The creation suite is awful. It has less options than things like No Mercy, let alone modern offerings from other companies. I hope this changes.The graphics are fine. Nothing amazing, but it works and in game it's not really noticable.Some control interactions are funky. I dislike the autotargeting system. Just a couple quirks to get used to.The limitation of only having 4 characters in the ring feels odd for a modern wrestling game, Especially for a company that regularly has 6 man tag matches. We especially are going to have an issue if they try to implement the Blood and Guts match.The game modes are good, but I wish there were more. Like a Cage match, or a coffin match. Anything more than what's here. The roster is solid, but is missing a lot of the depth of the actual roster and is very out of date. There are a couple of neat includes too.But, that said, it is fun. Worth picking up on sale. Full price...? Probably not unless you're a massive fan of the company and don't want to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge AEW fan and lover of the N64 style wrestling games, I was incredibly excited about this game.  Unfortunately, I would have to call it disappointing.  Its a game with a ton of potential but unfortunately its stuck at potential.  The game is plagued with bugs ranging from AI that gets stuck to it crashing the SteamDeck to the point of requiring a hard reboot when trying to exit the game.  Speaking of the SteamDeck, it runs great but unless you knock the settings down to 45FPS, it will eat through your battery like it was RDR2 and the game doesn't look good enough to justify that kind of power draw.  There is a big element of fun with the game but it has so many issues and it feels like half a wrestling game that I just can't recommend it as much as I wish I could.  I wish I hadn't got a key from a 3rd party marketplace because I would get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Base game is fun to play, with a good selection of characters and weapons.Tables fall down far too easily, chairs cannot be wrapped around the limbs of a fallen opponent. Weapons do not have grapple attacks.Surprising lack of tag teams and female wrestlers.Women can win men's titles, but men can't win women's titles.No trios matches, or even the ability to form a faction of more than two people.Only up to four wrestlers at a time in a Casino Battle Royale.They claim "Deep Career Mode" but Career Mode is very short and hollow, with no choices of any kind. The characters and stories don't even reference your prior achievements. A total of 30 matches in a career, including Dark matches. Necessary for leveling up created wrestlers, results in AEW wrestlers having terrible Win-Loss records.Character creation is extremely limited.AEW wrestler customization is almost nonexistent. Even the few attires they do provide have to be found and added manually.Stadium Stampede is Online only. It has a first-person camera which can't be inverted.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few of flaws with the game, but I have been having fun with it. This is the first wrestling game (not counting Wrestling Revolution) I have played since WWE 2k16.  The gameplay is amazing, the minigames can be fun when played during Road to Elite (Never really played them outside of that game mode), it runs great on my PC and I only had 1 crash.  The controls are straightforward and easy to grasp. The create a wrestler could use some love, it lacks a lot of features.My biggest issue is Road to Elite. It is fun to play and reminds me a bit of Here Comes the Pain when I was a kid. It goes on for 1 year and has storylines leading up to each PPV. My issue is that it can get very repetitive and for some reason some of the snapshots don't appear when I do the correct event before a match. From what I have heard, there is a glitch with Road to Elite where it resets your custom wrestler's stats when you start a new playthrough of it.I haven't done online yet so I am not sure how it plays, but from what I have read it is peer 2 peer connection which isn't the best. The game was made using Unreal Engine 4, which means it uses the Epic Games Online service which asks you to connect an Epic Games account every time you log in if you don't. I haven't tried yet but I read you have to link an Epic Games account in order to play online but I'm not sure. I should mention this as I have seen people complain about the Epic Games account issue, you  need to install the Epic Games launcher to play this game. You just need to link your Epic account if you have one.Overall I would recommend this game for AEW fans and fans of wrestling games in general. In the current state that it is in I would probably wait until a sale to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game should show why the No Mercy style of wrestling games just doesn't work in modern day. The controls& the reversal mechanics are just bad. All this game tells you are the very basic buttons that need to be hit, but then everything else you just have to figure out for yourself. Running is a joke as you are stuck & committed to run in one direction once you press the button & cannot change your direction mid run. Some of the controls are also incorrectly given to you & i'm shocked nobody caught that b4 release (For example: Manual Targeting tells you to move the L stick + face buttons to select your target when that is clearly false, as it ACTUALLY is just pushing in the L stick w/o even using the face buttons at all). Normal Tag matches are the worst aspect about this game b/c it truly shows how awful the mechanics work, especially if you aren't the legal person. It gives you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in ring timer that once it runs out, takes away all control you have & forces you out of the ring & into your corner. There should be no reason that feature to exist in a modern day game. It doesn't help that playing Road to the Elite constantly puts me in Tag Matches & Tag story lines that I wan't nothing to do with. What's even worse is the AI obviously knows how to abuse this to it's advantage, so you'll wind up losing most of your matches unless you just take full control & never tag out. Speaking of the AI, sometimes it is super dumb or it has physic powers & reverses almost every other move you throw at it & lands the most ridiculous moves on you b/c of how weird the hit boxes are sometimes. The momentum meter is outdated af b/c it does not seem to matter at times, you can be in the green & still lose to a simple move b/c the game only flashes for a few seconds which body part is damaged, yet I've wrestled almost a full Casino Battle Royal Match w/ an injury and almost won (Which I definitely would have won if this game didn't make eliminations so easy for all shapes & sizes, regardless of how great your health is). But once you're momentum is in Danger, YOU'RE FINISHED, doesn't even matter if you barely have any body damage as you will never kick out. So it can really be 50/50 that you'll get a squash match or at least a half decent match out of the game. Create a Wrestler is very limited, although I'm sure there will be more added overtime, but it's kind of a joke what is available at launch. Road to the Elite feels kind of cut & dry for a "story mode" & they were hyping this up alot upon release, but you just repeat the same things over & over again. I'm rarely ever given "choices" to make in this game, as it constantly throws me into Tag feuds that I want nothing to do with. I was looking forward to a great alternative from 2k, but sadly Wrestling Empire is somehow slightly better & more fun than this game & it's only $20 compared to the $60 they're charging for this unfinished product. This game obviously needed WAY more time to be polished & patched up before slapping that price tag on it.

_childDocuments_.review: AEW: Fight Forever truly shines as a highly replayable 9/10 quality game at full price for diehard AEW fans - and the minor flaws literally melt away like CM Punk's ice cream bars on a summer's day in this deep, goodies bag full of easter eggs for long time fans of AEW and BTE. edit: I just had a super fun online match. The core fighting mechanics are legit, and will keep you playing for a long time. The more I play, the deeper the game feels.However, in the eyes of the casual gamer, AEW: Fight Forever may prove to be more of an exciting rollercoaster ride that more likely captivates your imagination for an extended period of time if the game evokes idealised memories of wrestling games from childhood, and moreover, if philosophically you feel the video game industry's obsession with graphical realism has come at the expense of legitimately fun game play. Surprisingly, my closing thoughts on AEW: Fight Forever is that the launch version of the game echoes vibes of much-loved classic "arcade sports games" such as Tony Hawk Pro Skater 2 in terms of the cheeky vibes, humour, stat building, fun-focused spirit of creativity, and most of all the fast paced story mode designed to be replayed with multiple characters using everyone's unique stats and moveset to progress not only in a light-hearted journey across hotstops in the US, but mostly in your mastery of the core game play mechanics.What are you waiting for? Buy in, have fun, and support AEW!

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10 has a couple things going for it right now and thats it.Considering this game has devs from previous WWE games it really lacks any depth across the board.CAW is limited and lackluster with what it has, only stock body types and faces, no way of editing them like you can in WWE games (individual sliders for body/face parts) next to no gear to choose from either.Games modes are also limited (custom, online and Road to elite) Custom only has a few match types which is pathetic, not touched online but id assume the same and probably with a fair amount of lag, road to elite is very gimmicky and very short, around 6hrs. No way of rotating gear presets during this either which is crazy despite having the option to choose which one is your default preset, it just doesn't change.The before match antics are dumb especially the mini games (go away nobody wants them)How are we in 2023 and a career mode in a sports game ends when you win the main title, thats like playing career mode in fifa, you win the league and its over, whats the point? also pretty sure WWE games of old had road to wrestlemania which once you win the title at WM it continues on with you as champ (wrestling games need to bring this aspect of career mode back as it gave you more to play and strive to keep the title)The actually gameplay is kinda mid comparing it to WWE games of present and old tbh which is a shame, it has a couple things going for it like certain wrestlers have unique things about them that they do during matches but otherwise its not as fluid as it has been made to look.Graphically the game is something from the early 00's, now yes i know they wanted this to be arcade kinda game but please these graphics are awful which if the game was better i wouldn't mind as much but its not so its noticeable how bad it looks.Now obviously this has only just come out and all of this can hopefully change and they'll add more to the game in the coming months but off the bat its a mid tier game that on release should've been £24.99All in all get rid of the gimmicky crap from road to elite, add more to the mode and continue it on after you win the title to give the game some life for those who want the solo experience.Add more match types to the game in general.More customisation to CAW (gear, body/face types/sliders)

_childDocuments_.review: So first up a potted history - Yukes exited producing the WWE franchise games after finishing 2k19, they then got snapped up by AEW to produce a wrestling game that's more about bringing back the look and feel and accessibility of the retro wrestling games such as of Kenny Omega's favourite N64 wrestling games (as he is the director of the games division for AEW). So start off knowing that AEW Fight Forever plays as more pacey arcade style fighting game, that doesn't bury the controls under a lot of complicated button combos... i's very much cleaner and simplistic but just as effective controls although does have a reduced move sets.... instead it relies on more of positional context to pull off moves rather than deep combo pressing, so that's much easier for pick up and play type folk.So that all said how does does it fair?Pros:1. Simpler pick up and play control system, that doesn't sacrifice too much depth2. Fast and fluid animations3. Uses Unreal Engine, so hopefully easier to bug fix and mod.4. Uses Epic Game's Anti-Cheat system (might be a deal breaker for some), personally doesn't bother me.5. Game Performance is great at launch (was getting 175fps on <30% usage on my rig)6. Mini-Games adds a new side mode to the campaign mode, reminds me of Wii Party games.7. Music in-game, the extremely vast music library can be background soundtrack during matches, this contains a lot of themes, alternative mixes, even 8-bit retro remixes, including nearly all the missing roster too. Oddly the only one that couldnt be used as a soundtrack was Jericho's Judas, as seems to be exclusive to only his ring entrance (bit like WWE did on Cody's theme).8. Long term support, this is not a yearly game, this is a game as service method so should be support for five years with streams of addons and dlcs to keep roster updated and all the outfits etc.9. Priced below the going rate as it's first outing for AEW (I paid £40 for Elite edition on Shopto) which seems about right to me, expect the base game to drop in price fairly quick as dlcs roll out.10. Has DLSS support (although tbh runs so well never needed to use it, but nice anyway).Cons:1. Roster on launch is disappointing, many of the missing ones will be dlc addons due to the new game as a service model (think how they did this on Fire Pro).2. Only 4 players in the ring at once (although could change in time with new modes being planned), but seriously needs even that forced to be allowed for other modes as ladders matches is only 1vs1 currently.3. Lack of play modes for online, with some off restrictions on the modes that are there.4. No crossplay at launch, despite being on the Epic store online system.5. it requires a Epic Store login attached to your Steam (much like Rocket League does).6. New game, new bugs.... expect that... but needs to be said.7. Ring Entrances and end of match celebrations are far too short and cropped, needs to have the full length versions added as an option, 7 seconds just isn't enough and abrupt exits to menu on match end is poor.8. Create a wrestler is extremely bare bones, needs a hell of a lot of work done, this will may well be the biggest deal breaker for many. Just seems daft they added so much customisation for entrances and real time triggering of effects that you barely get time to even see them??? WHY ??? this makes zero sense.9. Missing support for 21:9 Ultrawide which is surprising given how easy this should be to fix and that it's been a PC standard feature for nearly a decade, so for now you will get black borders.10. Some of the wrestler models look quite weird, while others look spot on.... so needs to have more quality passes done there. 11. Zero and I do mean ZERO in-match commentary.... very surprising given the quality commentary team they have at AEW, expected a lot there, and didnt even get the basics, just some phoned in read out intros in story mode and pre-match menus.Final Thoughts - On Launch week.Overall going to give this about 70% score, it's fun and decent but still needs a lot of work, and over time as patches and content roll out I do expect this score to improve, it's obviously not as polished as the rival brand's game which Yukes used to make, but its doing things in a different way and does feel good to play (see my Casino Battle Royale footage below). The teething problems on Multiplayer side probably need to be the first addressed, as simply needs more control over match types and vastly more match types. I am aware there is a 30 player stampede mode coming in due course, but we need match maker options that are more flexible for online, including options to block custom created ones that have stats modded etc. and also why can I not have my mate in a group and then join a online 4 player mode other than 2vs2 modes? seems a of bit of a silly limitation.

_childDocuments_.review: As fan of the older N64 games I can see their influence. I think the game came out of the oven to early. I think most of us were hoping for a a hybrid of N64 and HCTP style wrestling games. There is very little depth to keep you coming back. The matches them selves seem poorly research on pace and depth. There is little thought given to the ability to make a come-back. Resilience and lack of counter to a hot streak leads to short one-sided trades with little suspense of tension unless your on the end of the squash match. This feels like a "WCW Goldberg" simulator where a long match with not stipulations in 5 min or less lol. There is a good foundation but this outing did very little to bring the N64 concepts to a modern context were there is an expectation for more elevation of the art form. Others have even stated it is just lean in all places...heck just as I start sinning along to Judas...the entrance is over and well....as an AEW experience it falls short on even scratching the itch. I'm surprise for how long this was in development and the delays that this is all they have to show as of 7/1/2023.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit ♥♥♥♥ isn't it?I honestly thought is was crap after about 45 minutes but I kept going back to give it another go, and another one.... and another one because I really wanted to like it having been a massive fan of the N64 games, I still own them.Lets start with create a wrestler, extremely bare bones, I dunno how you mess this up but they did, just a complete lack of options.AI is awful, anything more than one v one is an absolute cluster, as soon as you hit your finisher the other computer goes for your pin before you get a chance so you hit your finisher and have to break up the pin EVERY TIME in a 3 way. In a 4 way the only way top win is to delay your pin until the computer starts a grapple move and hope it takes long enough for the animation to finish so they don't break it up.  For some reason when you tag in that's free game for the other side to come in too. Then there's just weird issues where the AI gets stuck in a loop of movement.Career mode... more like part time job mode, some good ideas but totally let down in execution, some real corner cutting, same cutscenes and same backgrounds, not even a minigame for the workout, some of the backgrounds are blurry jpegs by the looks of it. Story can be funny in a daft way but also really it's shallow, boring and nonsensical and none of it connects together.Matches are personally too fast paced, you can normally finish a 1 v 1 in under a couple of minutes, damage seems WAY too high, after a few hits you find yourself laying on your back for an eternity which doesn't make for fun gameplay, love it when they throw you out the ring too and your character is on their feet dazed for 30+ secondsIt's a £20 game at best in it's current state, it's not beyond saving at all, there's a fairly decent base to build on, whether they choose to or not though remains to be seen, it is THQ after all, they'll probably charge for patches

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT JANUARY 2024: Sad to say this, but avoid this game. Everything they could do wrong, they did wrong. They're charging for the most basic stuff possible, and adding over-priced DLC (They sold us a season pass and there was a second season pass like 3 months later! Awesome!) that is also terribly outdated, and even paying the DLC you're still missing like 60% of what you'd imagine a finished AEW game would be in the year 2024. This could've been great but it's the most disrespectful and greedy I've seen a company be towards its customers in a VERY long time. Keep in mind that as of July 1st 2023, this game is VERY barebones. It has a lot of work to put into it, and practically feels like a more solid tan average Early Access.That being said, just with the very base skeleton it has right now, this is till the most fun I've had with a wrestling game in MANY years. My first wrestling game as a kid was Smackdown vs. Raw 2007, and this totally scratches that itch for me in how arcade-y, non serious and just silly it can be at times. It never tries to be realistic or serious, it's just pure fun, and very quick paced, making it perfect to play one or two matches or do a couple weeks of Road to Elite during a break, or just to kill some free time.I'm a bit skeptical about how much of what's left to add will be free, because I can see them charging for very basic features, but for now I'm loving it and it was a promising future if handled right.

_childDocuments_.review: *EDIT*I left my original review below, but I am no longer recommending this game. We are now (as of tis edit) into "Season 3" of their DLC packs. This is basically 3 wrestlers, a ring, music and costumes/skins. Of these, you may get 2 of those 3 at once as a tag team, which feels like we got cheated a bit. Cheated? Well, that is because the original promise of free updates/content has yet to ever happen. Each "Season" is around $9.99 US. I understand that constant development and content is not free...but a lot of the things being added to an already $60/$70 game feels like gouging. A lot of this content should have been included at the get go.*Original Review*I recommend this game, but with a warning. It does have some quirks. Initially the game felt like it was rushed out, and it probably was as the rumors said. Thankfully AEW said that this game will be intended as a game that gets updates with new content and dlc over whatever its life span.  That should mean patches, new "arena's", new wrestlers, hopefully an expanded CAW, and I would LOVE to see longer intros. Yeah, intros are extremely short. Most importantly, some commentary from Tony, Excalibur, and Taz. There is no in match commentary. Even if it was just some basic commentary stuff. Even wrestler audio is not here. No grunts or groans either. Crowd noise and the brutal sounds of contact with the ring environment are here.With all of that said, it is fun. You get a decent amount of moves for the wrestlers, which are easy to pull off. The crowd is interactive with the cheers and boos and chants. The chaos you see on tv and ppv's is right here. And, anything that comes up short will get ironed out as more and more fans show support for the title.

_childDocuments_.review: You NEED to give this a chance. Seriously! It's a different timing than 2k, but once you learn the reversals a bit, and how to grapple and do chain moves and go behinds, you will have so much fun online and be bodying noobs! Look, this isn't WWE2k23, and to me, that's a good thing. It brought back the key things I enjoy from the N64 classics, AND a few elements I enjoyed from "Day of Reckoning" for Game Cube. It's not meant to be a wrestling sim like 2k. It's meant to provide a FUN wrestling game. Not a game that you have to be a brain surgeon to master. Once you push past the small learning curve, online ranked is so fun. So, So fun. They're already taking bug reports very seriously on their discord, and a rep from the dev team was there on launch day to take reports, answer questions, and give support. The odd bug that there is doesn't effect gameplay, and at worst are funny to watch. and clip for content. These are bugs that they are already working on the patches for. It's a highly dedicated team, behind this game. A quick visit to the discord showed me that much. One thing I will say is that their story mode "becoming elite" or whatever (I forget the name) leaves a lot to be desired. It feels like a dating sim with all the times you have to take your wrestler to dinner. XDSome expected an AEW version of the 2k series. It's not, and thank god for that. That's not to say it doesn't feel like a wrestling game. Getting into the more chain wrestling elements of the grapple system is so satisfying. Entrances are short, which is good, because we usually skip them on the 2k series anyway. Tell me when i'm telling Lies! :P Not only that, but you get to make different pyro explode whenever you want, as often as you want, and toggle camera angles. It deepens the immersion for me, without going overboard.All things considered, I can confidently give this 7.5 stars. (Eat your heart out, Meltzer). While I enjoy the depth of the 2k series, sometimes I just want a quicker, fun experience, This game scratches that itch. It's something your friends who don't like wrestling can enjoy. I mean, Electrified barbed wire ring? Being able to throw an exploding propane tank at your opponent? Slamming someone into tacks and seeing them wince as the tacks visibly stick in their back? Enough blood loss to warrant a plasma transfusion? (You can turn that off if you're squeamish homie, don't worry).The gameplay won my heart, and assuming things will be patched and added to an already FUN game, I'm ALL IN, Bay Bay!

_childDocuments_.review: [Update re: Stadium Stampede at the end.]WITH RESERVATIONS:I will start off this review with the same general sentiment of the major review outlets: "It's a fun game, *but*..."If all you want out of an arcade [not simulator] wrestling game is to get in the ring with your favorites and hit buttons and get a fun surprise or two it's a fine, and fun wrestling game. The core combat is satisfying enough. There are a lot of secret features and crazy moments to create by paying attention to details and experimenting in the ring. Though. in regards to the creation suites it simply must be conceded that they don't have 20 years worth of existing work to keep importing like the 2K games (I will expand on the CaW later). I never expected that level of depth, and I don't think anyone should have.The game runs great, and includes DLSS. The game is playable on Steam Deck, even mostly hanging around 60fps on High settings during 4-Ways (4 + Ref onscreen), although it may require one or two launches before functioning because EGS and EAC need time to configure. The EGS DRM is odd because the game isn't actually available to purchase on EGS? At any rate while they claim they are still working on deck verification, but it *does* work as of this writing. The controls are a bit different than 2K, and will require a little getting used to. I think the controls could use a little finessing in regards to setting up tables and ladders (I also think they need to up the weapon durability; I get why it's low, the matches are short enough already, but TWO hits is kind of sad) -- The tacks are fantastic though -- huge feature that has been mostly absent from wrestling games for decades. It is also cool to take control of your wrestler after the bell, where you are allotted a few extra seconds for manual celebrations, shows of sportsmanship (RB ;] ), or beat-downs.I will encourage more hardcore fans to go into the menu and calibrate some of the enabled-by-default beginner/basic control settings for more precise-but-challenging controls. Consider Hard difficulty, as the AI is a little clumsy sometimes; in either case remember the matches are intended to be a few minutes long like Smash or Fighter matches, not 10-20 minute sims like 2K.There was a pleasant surprise of a Jukebox menu where you can edit the menu and match music rotation. There is not-named-as-such streamer function in that you can remove songs from rotation for copy strikes, and you can calibrate the menu and match music volumes separately. It's crucial to make use of this if you don't want to hear Max Caster and Sony Kiss' original tracks over and over again.I will say that I am neutral on the short entrances and lack of commentary. I bet like 95% of players turn off entrances anyway in 2K. I get whey they wanted to save the resources, and also cut down on the time from menu-to-match; remember they also had to make them all from scratch, they are not importing an existing, 90%-complete roster year-to-year. They also do not call out a cool feature they have, where the player can control the Pyro and Camera during entrances, so some may assume there is not even pyro which is not the case -- it's just player-controlled. Some commentary would have been fun, but I guess I don't miss it too much. The crowd chants are good, I was happy with those.That said, I will echo what everyone else is, and it pains me: The CaW suite is SO EMPTY that they might as well have left it out until the sequel. We're talking 5-10 items in Tops, Bottoms, Boots categories; and a ton of flag-motifs and clunky-looking T-Shirts. Most of the items will clip so they disable them in most combinations. As far as I can tell you cannot edit your facial features outside of the 4 presets -- and there are like 8 hairs. The Main Roster Attire Editor is more-or-less identical but limited to putting existing T Shirts over wrestlers ring gear. Of note, for some reason this is also the menu you select Alt Attires, rather than in the match's selection menu.As far as the rest of the editors: The move-set editor is actually fairly robust, given the circumstances, despite the relatively slim, as compared to 2K/FP's library of 20 years of additions. The entrance creations are nice, despite what I said before about their length. Create-an-Arena exists also, but I never really mess with those. The Team editor is a little wonky; you can't make or edit Trios, so AFAICT, Death Triangle is stuck in the game permanently, and you can't make teams like JAS or CMFTR even though many of the mates are in -- I wish it functioned like the old SD2 Create-A-Stable (Freebird style) instead of whatever it is now. All-in-all, the creation suite is verging on net negative... it's JUST good enough to feel super disappointing, which is almost worse than being bad enough to ignore entirely.The mini-games are neat, but not my thing probably; notable that more are unlocked in Career mode, but most of the casuals playing the mini games are probably not doing multiple career mode runs. The career mode is decent, and evokes a loose rogue-lite feel (not to overuse the term) where you have a few branching paths depending on wins/losses and how you are meant to manage your energy and free time. You are intended to play multiple times to see all the scenes and develop CaWs, but given the lack of enticement in the CaW suite I would have preferred to have a longer story with more scenes and less replay value, if that makes sense, like the old Jaccob Cass WCW story (IYKYK).Menus need a pinch of work. They are missing simple things like quick-scrolling with triggers/arrows in some of the menus, the ability to select a Random ref [you pick Aubrey or Knox in the menu, I feel like it should offer a Random option]. While it's good you can access the whole menu from the match screen, it defaults to the graphics settings tab rather than Match settings. Stuff like that, little oversights that shouldn't take much dev power. These things can also be addressed with patches.I think they either could have shaved $10-20 off the price or let the suite cook another year and either add it as a DLC or keep it for the sequel -- this game is arcadey enough to have been presented as a Select a Fighter MK/SF/Tekken screen and people wouldn't have been expecting an actual editor. Unless they are planning a massive asset dump in the coming months, I don't think this creative suite is going to give people the legs that 2K and FirePro have on YouTube feds.Ultimately even as an AEW Enjoyer of PSX SmackDown-age, I will have to concede the pricing is not great for what is offered, given the Day One DLC and curious roster, without having a good enough editor to make the rest of the roster. I did get the Elite Edition cheaper than the base game on GMG. I don't know why people pay full price for PC games when there are so many options. Perhaps off-topic to this paragraph, but it's important context that what you get for the money was budget a new franchise with a new studio, and everything being hand-modeled and hand-animated for artistic licenses instead of existing content rehashes, body scans, and standard mo-cap. We are paying for the venture, and paying for the vision, rather than paying for content, in a way. Decide if that bothers you before buying.[Given that last paragraph, it should also be noted that there is the free addition of Stadium Stampede and several free attire updates. Both of these are welcome additions, but each still include that *"but*" from earlier: Stadium Stampede is fun and free addition, *but,* there is no crossplay and sooner rather than later you just will not be able to find a match on PC. Attire is nice *but*, you have to save your own Edited stars.TLDR: Fun game, maybe not for $60, but it's a solid foundation for the franchise, at least the in-ring stuff. It is not 2K, and it's not FirePro; don't buy it if you want those. Buy it if you want SD1 or No Mercy -- I did.

_childDocuments_.review: If you value the creation suite in any current wrestling game(fire pro, wrestling empire or the 2k series) do not get this game. I think 6 for men but I could be wrong. Male CaWs have to be shirtless. Female CaWs have to wear a brazzier or a one piece(or a maid outfit).  Every part of the creation suite is lacking in some way. Also, your CaWs start off weak, and you have to play the Career mode to make them more on par with the base roster.If you like entrances, the entrances in this game are ~7 seconds. While an interesting idea, they're often too short for the entrance music to even really hit(see Cody Rhodes).If you like universe mode, do not get this game unless you want to run one yourself with pencil and paper. There is not a universe mode, nor will there ever be, according to the devs from what I understand. On a similar note, there is no GM mode either.If you like Career mode, this game does have a somewhat decent career mode, with some branching paths. It also only lasts about 3 hours(or 4 months worth of matches). Its not something that has endless playability. I think the only real way I could recommend this game to someone was if all they wanted to do was play exhibition matches against the AI or with friends. Thats not a terrible selling point of a game, and the gameplay does feel fun enough. _childDocuments_.review: I can't describe my disappointment after spending these first few hours with Fight Forever. The core gameplay is fine, if not lacking polish. But the real letdown is how underdeveloped the Create a Wrestler mode is (and, by extension, the lack of a community workshop). A fully-featured CAW mode is a foundational piece of wrestling games and to see it so poorly fleshed out here is truly puzzling. - There are only 8 (EIGHT!) faces to choose from.- You can't change the size, shape or position of any facial/body features.- The eye colour choices are horrendous - you have your choice of black or various shades of neon or pure white.- There are only 5 eyebrow types to choose from.- There are only 17 hair styles to choose from. There are 47 non-DLC wrestlers at launch. Where are the other 30+ hair styles that are already in the game but missing from CAW??- Facial hair: 8 styles, and 3 of them look exactly the same.- Body types: Jacked, Skinny Jacked, Fat Jacked, or The Incredible Hulk- Body Settings: changing the Fat or Muscle sliders only affect the body and thighs. You can try to look lean, but your head, hands and feet will still be enormous. The Weight slider doesn't affect anything visually.- Headwear: NONE of the choices are actually viable, except for maybe the ballcaps and toques. The rest are a joke, especially the flag themed hats which are purely there to be filler.- Why are there SO MANY options for facial/body scars? There are 21 face scar choices - more that double the number of FACES.- Why are there SO MANY options for arm/knee sleeves and wrist bands- You can't wear shirts/tops in ring - only as part of your Entrance Attire, for some inexplicable reason.- Bottoms are mostly awful camo-themed pants/shorts or flag shorts. There a 2 Omega pants, a Nakamura ripoff and that's it.- There are 100 (ONE HUNDRED!) tattoo options. This would be fine if they gave us more than 8 FACES and ZERO SHIRTS to work with.These choices and omissions would be tolerable if this was Yuke's first time making a wrestling game but all they had to do was cherry pick the best parts of their past games and slap an AEW sticker on it. How hard could it be?

_childDocuments_.review: Changing my review from positive to negative, due to the game being imbalanced, poor communication from THQ Nordic. Please don't waste your money on this, until changes are made.Firstly, the positives:Great fundamental gameplay (offline). Strikes and grapples have a great slam, and hit detection from top rope and springboard moves feel great. Those familiar with the No Mercy games will enjoy this. The pace of the gameplay is very much like that, and it rewards patience over mindless mashing (most the time) and you have to watch what your opponent is doing before deciding on if to grapple or strike. Reversals are RB for strikes, LB for grapples - this is how reversals should be, unlike 2K's convoluted system.The career/Road to Elite is decent for what it is. Simple but charming in a weird way. Not much of a storyline but you have to be mindful or your energy and motivation, as this effects how productive your workouts are, as well as your health within the matches. Not much of a story tree here, but if you put it on "Hard" mode, the career mode becomes more enjoyable and rewarding. You can use your created wrestler or real wrestler. If you opt for created wrestler, you can build up your stats, attributes, and skills (more on this later) and can make a very OP that can be currently used for Online play. I recommend adding basic things like Springboard to your skills (it will then let you add the moves to your wrestler) and also maybe upping your movement speed and strength.Creation suite, although basic, is simple enough to make your own wrestler. This does need to have more granularity (more face and body types) but it is straight-forward enough. My favourite part is making your own entrance and adding in your own props, production (screen shakes, etc) and pyros that you time yourself every time.Negatives:Where to start. The online portion of this game is DEAD, and for good reason. Put simply: the game has been ill-thought out for online play, and is completely imbalanced. Those that have created their own CAFs and went through the Road To Elite, can completely max out their players. So, for example, they can add traits called "Unyielding Poise" which allows them to absorb your strikes for a decent amount of time. By this time, the match could already be over (due to how short matches are). Unfortunately, that's not all. There is another trait called "Bail Out" - it basically allows them to get outside the ring, at ANY time, and is completely unlimited. They can also use irreversible foot sweeps, Extended Combos, Signature Moves that stand your straight back up on your feet (so they can spam it over and over again). I'm not even mentioning half of the traits and skills that you can add, but once you add all of this up, it equals imbalance. The only way to compete is if you add all these traits to your own guy (you will have to create Road To Elite) and do this yourself. however, most people have the self-respect to not do this. THQ Nordic need to fix this, but there is no sign of them doing so a month in. It should not have even been released in this state. It's just not fun and THAT is why the game is dead online. And when you add the very limited game modes (no tornado tag) and no lobby online system, the game is more dead than it should be.Communication from THQ Nordic is appalling. The employees on their Discord act lawlessly and enforce whatever rules they can pluck out their butt. It is evident to anyone that has tried to communicate with them that they are not a serious company. The mods are basically glorified Reddit mods. They have mislead people about DLC expectation timelines. They are more interested in superficial updates over quality updates. They shouldn't even be thinking about DLC at this stage.The pin system is also garbage and results in matches being about 3 minutes long on average. There needs to be a skill-based system, so that matches can be a bit more back-and-forth.On the surface, it seems like they have tried to cash in and run, on the back of people's sentiment about the old No Mercy games. It's evident by their communication, lack of updates, and also by the price that they have tried to charge (for such limited content). Ultimately it is a waste of decent gameplay mechanics. Please don't waste your money on this, until they have both lowered the price and provided any meaningful updates to the GAMEPLAY online imbalance and match type variation.
