_childDocuments_.review: Capcom dethroned. For years now, it's been Capcom working with Digital Eclipse, the studio that made Atari 50th, and by far the greatest studio for retro collections in the world, to put out the best retro collections on the market, from Megaman to Disney to Street Fighter, each and every one was chock full of care and supplemental material in addition to the games. Atari 50th blows that level of respect for the source material out of the water. Interacting with the content via a series of timelines with the usual text blurbs and photographs in addition to the games, Atari 50th also includes documentary video interviews with the various people relevant to the content, as well as original period videos from the 70s. The games included are something like 90 titles picked from early arcade, 2600, 5200, Jaguar etc, in addition to modern reinventions of certain classics, and most of them won't surprise you, but they play great and in addition to selecting them from a dedicated games list, you can play them as you come across them in the museum timelines. This is just a very very well done celebration of the origins of our favorite entertainment medium. Every game company with an extensive history owes it to themselves to hire Digital Eclipse to do a collection. Nintendo?
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: For the price of the older ROMs alone, it's worth it if you're a retro games nerd, especially for the more rare games like Waterworld or anything on the Jaguar. However, the amount of work and clear love put into the Re-imagined series like Vctr-Sctr and the long-lost Airworld blows any other game compilation out of the water. If you're a game history buff like me, it's pretty sweet to see the corporate timeline of Atari put together with interviews and to be able to not only see, but play the history being shown is a great time! I wish this could be the new standard for games preservation for every company with a significant back catalog. Cannot recommend this little gem of a compilation higher!
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: If you are an atari fan, its an easy recommendation. It has the feel of something crafted for fans by fans. However, i'd get it on sale. There's not that much too it, and every time i pick up an atari collection I quickly remember that all my favorite games of this era were by Williams and Activision. Obviously, those games are not included. If you are a gaming dinosaur like myself, I also recommend picking up the art of atari book.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Not a ton of PC settings at launch, sadly, so you're maxing out at 1080p until further notice. Otherwise, the emulation is top-tier, especially for Lynx and Jaguar fare, and Atari's historical context is presented in a way that shames pretty much any other retro game collection ever released. Also, only here will you find documentary videos with titles like, "Did they do drugs at Atari?"--with fantastic documentary footage and interviews to match.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I love the combination of historical info and archival images with the games.  It creates a context that makes each of these (obviously and unexpectedly) dated games more interesting through a modern lens.  The inclusion of unreleased games and re-imagined updates is a bonus.  Anyone who has a remote interest in video game history owes it to themselves to check this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best compilation collection from any company I have ever seen, you get 104 games for 40 USD which is a great deal and is great to play with people, the major issue I have with this game is you can't save in SwordQuest: Airworld which does greatly hamper the playability of the game significantly but other than that this an excellent collection
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I've written quite a few reviews on Steam and I have a very low opinion of "retro" gaming and older games... not because I "hate" old games, but reviews must be written for the gamer .Pac-Man was a wild success in the early 1980's.  That doesn't mean I'm going to tell gamers to drop Black Myth Wukong and play Pac-Man instead.  Just because it was good then, doesn't mean it's good now.   The industry has moved on.I was there then, in the dark ages, the 8 bit age, and I loved those games then.  But I was also there to see why those games became obsolete, and I was there to celebrate every new advance in gaming technology, from 3D acceleration, the impact of the internet of gaming, how every advancement has made things better and better for gamers.From that, I know we can't go back.  And nor should we.  Hillary didn't get halfway up Everest and say "Wow, I really miss the foot of the mountain, let's go back there and hang around for a while".  The industry, and gamers, have to keep climbing higher and higher, doing better and better.But the Atari 50 is far more than just a retro game or two.   This is more than just 90 carefully curated emulated games (that pretty much any PC will play flawlessly).   This package is a celebration of a once great and now obsolete gaming legend, the technology, and the people behind it.The game includes a clever interactive launch menu that lets you see photos and biographical information about each curated game, where it came from and where it fits into the history of gaming.  If you're a gaming history buff, this quite simply is a must-have.It is overpriced, however.  This has gone on sale as low as $14 USD for 90 games plus the additional "virtual museum" data, which is the time to consider to buy.  I will make an exception to my general rule about retro gaming because this is a product that does have significant value for retro gamers.   It's more than the sum of the collected games in the bundle.  This is how retro gaming should be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I like this "game." It has a bunch of classic games, some with enhanced graphics. It goes through most of Atari's history and features stuff like the Atari arcade games, the Atari 2600, 5200, 7800, Lynx and Jaguar consoles, the Atari 400 and 800 PC's (among other Atari PC's), and more. It kinda reminds me of Microsoft's "Power On: The Story of Xbox" documentary, where they go through the history of Xbox, but their's one difference between that and Atari 50 that I wish Atari 50 had, and that difference is that in Microsoft's documentary, they bring up their failures, like how the system didn't turn on at E3 2001 or how the first models of the Xbox 360 were prone to the Red Ring of Death. While Atari 50 does mention things like the Atari 5200 controller and the Atari Jaguar CD, they didn't go over how they were extremely prone to hardware failures and almost none of them work. They also briefly bring up E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial for the Atari 2600, which is one of the worst games ever madeBesides that, I like Atari 50! I actually had more fun playing these games than I have had in some games of today.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: The presentation and interviews with Atari personnel are the big highlights.  While the controls are not perfect, they are an improvement over the previous emulation efforts of the past few decades. _childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: The first of four (at the time of this review) "game collections" where the games are actually the "extras" instead of being the main draw, which is  a negative in  way. It's more so a documentary or museum exhibit about the history of Atari where you can actually  some of the games as they're mentioned.Also for the paddle games, get the Wireless Classic Joystick made for the modern Atari VCS consolized PC. _childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal interactive museum and absolute blast from the past!  VCTR SCTR is worth the price of admission on its own!  Also love Yars Revenge Enhanced and Haunted Houses!  Of course, the greatest arcade game of all time, Asteroids Deluxe is on here as well! _childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool little museum-style collection of Atari history.Now I was born in the mid-80s, so I really don't have much nostalgia for anything Atari at all. My first console was an NES. My only real exposure to anything Atari back then was while on vacation in the mid 90s. We were at my grandparent's lakeside cabin, and I found an Atari 2600 with a few games in a closet. I fiddled around with Battlezone, Pole Position and Asteroids. They felt primitive by my standards, but it was a fun distraction for a few moments.One thing I didn't expect in this collection was the vector-based games. It was also in the 90s that I first saw a real vector-based game in an arcade. Something about the way those crispy, bright-white lines appeared on the black background was mesmerizing. No pixels to be seen anywhere, just sharp, crisp lines, like laser beams. I'm playing this collection on a Steam Deck OLED, and the brightness of that display plus the true and honest black levels absolutely replicates that feeling. Vector-based games are absolutely beautiful on an OLED screen.One disappointment is the feeling of games originally designed to use a trackball. While games like Breakout and Tempest work fine moving with a joystick, you really need a trackball for the speed and precision these games require. I haven't quite looked into it yet, but I expect there must be some way to simulate a trackball using the Steam Decks trackpads.For the moment, I'm enjoying just going through the timeline, watching the video interviews with people who were involved in the industry back then, and marveling at how sharp they all still seem mentally even though they're getting old, not to mention the drug use that occured in the Atari offices. (A topic they discuss in this collection.)
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Atari must really respect their past and appreciate the value of the historical preservation of videogames they have made. Not only do you get complete access to over 90 games, but a there are some pretty nifty remakes in here too. And on top of that, there is a fantastic museum-like experience where you can read high quality scans of documents, sometimes view 3D scans, and also plenty of actual bits of documentary footage, complete with historical footage or interviews with prominent people. I wish more game companies did something like this for their history. Bottom line is if you like learning about videogame history, you need this.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first retro collection that far surpasses what any kind of emulation can offer. It's the games, it's a guided historical tour, it's a museum piece, it's everything. Truly a masterpiece by Digital Eclipse.If you're into retrogaming and/or have any interest in the history of how this gigantic gaming enterprise of today came to exist, you need to see this thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest gripe is that Activision is sadly lacking from the titles represented in the collection. I would this day buy a DLC if it had Fishing Derby, Battlezone, River Run. I also am sad to not see Joust, Pole Position II and Berzerk.  I have had fun revisiting games I played when I was a kid, and if you love Asteroids and Missile command this pack has a lot of fun there. I also own a classic 7800 and just upgraded to the 2600+ this pack is not a replacement to a good game collection. It is an fun addition. Also Ninja golf was so very very funny I will need to see if I can find a used copy for my 2600+ think my wife would have a good laugh at that one. I also wish the for the 7800 games and the 2600 games in the collection it would keep the high scores I know the they did not happen in the past. I also think there should be a achievement to loop the score counter in the 2600 asteroids, it is not hard to do more funny.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I'am really interested in the history of videogames. But didn't had the chance to get some deeper informations about Atari. Until now. This Anniversary Collection is full of knowledge about the history of Atari and I think some of the best games from Atari. So yeah, if you are just a little bit interested in video game history or Atari itself, this is a must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say this is a fantastic collection, but calling it a "collection" is such an understatement as to do it a disservice.  Another reviewer said it's more like an interactive museum, and I think that comes pretty close to the mark.  Any which way, if you're an Atari fan, or a fan of video game history, this is a must-have and is worth full price.  The entire presentation is slick and polished, the game emulation is spot-on with excellent controls, and the package taken as a whole sets a new standard for how to present old games to audiences new and old alike.  Highly recommended.  (Note:  don't be concerned about my playtime at the time of review, I have this on the Switch and have spent the majority of my time with it there.  I'm now playing it mostly on Steam because it's even better here; the mouse is a far better substitute for trackball and spinner games than the Switch's joycons are.)
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Atari 50 is everything I could hope a retro video game collection to be and is truly a work of passion. While Atari 50 might not be the best way to play these games due to all the speciality inputs the originals had like trackballs, Digital Eclipse did their best to translate these game to work with modern controllers. There is also a lot outside of the games to make up for any faults.  Atari 50 features an array of video content and images that add important context to games that, lets face it can be kinda bad. Sadly, the video are not in HD, I can understand not wanting large files for the Switch port but this is PC. Other than that minor problem I really like Atari 50 and highly recommend it to any one wanting to learn more about this pioneer in video gaming. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like a majority of the games in here kinda aged like milk and I was always more of a Midway fan but I'm still recommending this purely because the actual collection itself is really good for those who already know what they're getting into.They did a really good job adding enough bonus content and making the arcade games more accessible on modern hardware that I'd say it's worth getting this over emulating. They also added some remastered versions of games I really like as well as a new game Vector Sector which combines a lot of Atari's good arcade games into a single sort of "rush" mode.I wish more collections were like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this awesome collection!  There should be more virtual exhibits like this.  Frankly, the best part of it is the explanation of the history; the games were incredibly influential, but they don't hold a candle to the story of the whole thing.  I highly recommend checking out the video where they interview all the old programmers on the subject of drug use at Atari.  It's a phenomenal collection and an absolute necessity for anyone who seriously likes video games.  (I think my favorite game in the collection may actually be Yoomp, but VCTR-SCTR is a close second.)That said, this collection is a history of a company, told by the company.  It absolutely goes further than most companies would, but they probably couldn't talk about Pac-Man (2600) due to rights issues, and they certainly couldn't talk about Tengen Tetris.  They don't address that Atari split into multiple companies, and they paint the programmers who speak to the documentarians in an immensely positive light, while painting everyone else in the story as, at best, vaguely small-minded.  There's pages upon pages of marketing materials in this collection, but they didn't interview a single member of the marketing team, and some of the programmers outright talk trash about them.  It is a good collection, and I absolutely adore it, but I encourage you to read more about the history of Atari.I will continue to go back to this collection on a regular basis.  I'm definitely going to try to get my friends and play some of the multiplayer games in it.  Thank you to everyone at Digital Eclipse; you're a great team, and I hope you continue making great works like these.  Other companies, take note!
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Many of the games in this collection are sure to bring back fond memories for Atari fans like myself. Having owned an Atari 400 and an 800 XL, as well as spending far too much time in arcades, a lot of these games are like old friends.They are faithfully recreated and as challenging as you remember them. In fact, they are even more challenging due to the games one serious drawback: There is no good way to emulate the controllers used on many of the games. Keyboards and mice struggle to match the fluidity of a trackball or joystick. While the game does allow configuration of the controls, which helps some, it can't recreate the setup on the original machines.Despite that, this is a great collection that includes a lot of vector graphics games like Tempest, Major Havoc, Asteroids, and more that faithfully represent the amazing visuals that were present on vector graphics games. If you temper your expectations just a bit, you'll find this collection to be a great trip down memory lane.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting to get this because my internal voice was telling me I have Too Many Games. I was young (born back in the summer of '69) when the Atari 2600 came out and my family was too poor to get one, so I was left with a lot of longing. I had a few friends who had one, so I got to enjoy it that way. One was wildly rich compared to my own situation, and it seemed he got every game he wanted, so I got to see and play a lot of it. The other friend had a 2600 and I only remember Pitfall!, which he had mad skillz playing.Anyway, the desire and nostalgia were cranked way up for me, so I finally bought it last night.Atari 50 is really well done, and the fact that new games are being added periodically makes it exciting on top of everything else. I justified my purchase by thinking of it as rewarding such a sensible attitude. If Steam has taught us anything, isn't it that if you give people what they want, they will heap oodles of cash upon you? (May Gabe shine blessings upon your gaming sessions.)I have a deep appreciation for the people of that era who participate in interviews in this title and elsewhere, so we can experience what was happening and understand why it was so unique. I am a programmer, so I love the wizardry the software and hardware people talk about, but I am especially in awe of Nolan Bushnell. Some of the business shenanigans he got into were amazing and it is miles from the technical world I know so well. It is clear that Atari was a stellar combo of technical and business skills, from the right people at the right time.Anyway, I eat these collections up because I like having the games to play without finding the original equipment. I also love rewarding the people and companies for having created something that is standing the test of time. It is special this is more that just a typical collection of games with a chooser menu.Ah, heck. I am getting a little too wistful here. Thanks for continuing to inject joy into this hurting world, Atari.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5 stars)Atari's 50th Anniversary Celebration on Steam is not just a collection of vintage games; it's a meticulously crafted interactive journey through the heart of gaming history. What truly sets this celebration apart are the masterful documentary films that accompany the games, offering a profound and captivating look into the evolution of Atari and the gaming industry as a whole.From the moment you embark on this interactive journey, you're transported back in time. The menu screen alone, with its retro-inspired design, evokes a sense of nostalgia that is beautifully complemented by the timeless Atari logo. It's like stepping into a virtual time machine that propels you straight into the gaming world of yesteryears.The documentary films featured in this collection are nothing short of masterpieces. They provide a comprehensive and insightful exploration of Atari's history, from its humble beginnings to its groundbreaking contributions to the gaming industry. Each film is expertly crafted, combining archival footage, interviews with key figures, and a rich narrative that captures the essence of the Atari story.These documentaries go beyond mere retrospectives; they are educational and enlightening. They shed light on the challenges, innovations, and cultural impact of Atari. You'll gain a profound appreciation for the pioneers who laid the foundation for modern gaming.The storytelling in these films is so compelling that it fosters a deep emotional connection with the subject matter. You'll find yourself empathizing with the visionaries who dared to dream in pixels and vectors. The triumphs and tribulations of Atari's journey become your own, making this celebration an intensely personal experience.What's remarkable is the seamless integration of these documentary films with the gaming experience. As you explore the extensive library of Atari games, you'll stumble upon nuggets of history and trivia that resonate with what you've learned from the films. It's a harmonious fusion of entertainment and education.Atari's 50th Anniversary Celebration isn't just a collection of games with documentaries tacked on. It's a meticulously curated, immersive experience that envelops you in the world of Atari. Whether you're a die-hard fan, a casual gamer, or a history enthusiast, there's something here for everyone.In an era when gaming has become a global phenomenon, Atari's 50th Anniversary Celebration reminds us of the humble origins of this cultural juggernaut. If you're looking for an unforgettable trip through gaming history that will leave you both enlightened and inspired, look no further. _childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true celebration of not just Atari but the early history of video games and computers as a whole.Not only do you get a vast selection of Atari's classic home console and arcade games, you get unreleased prototypes, remakes/re-imaginings of classic Atari titles, and even a few third party titles. The best part is that it really is a interactive documentary, you see interviews with the former staff, classified memos, design docs, commercials, etc. This is the best way to learn about the history of AtariEven better is they still update this game every now and then with new Atari titles, so there's always something to come back toHappy 50th birthday Atari

_childDocuments_.review: Works great on Steam Deck.  I haven't seen any problems while going through the menus and a few videos, and the games I tried so far work great.  I put this at the top of my review for all you Deckies!Just bought this on a Steam sale, with tax it came to just under $30.00.  I bought this solely for the arcade version of Tempest, to play on the Steam Deck and my PC.  If I were playing this in the arcade back in the day, I just need to play the game 120 times to get my money back for this entire collection.  For those interested in playing Tempest, I found in the Steam discussions that you need to go into the settings on the main menu and turn down the mouse sensitivity, and the game plays great.  You don't need a spinner controller to play this!  I nearly cried when I found I could play this game again!I was also excited for all the new games included in this, especially Akka Arrh and the reimagined Yar's Revenge.  With those two games along with the arcade version of Tempest, I bought Atari 50 with no hesitation.I have a lot of videogame documentaries, and even though I have a bunch of Atari ones, this collection had new video material.  Atari has a lot of history, and they are so important to the gaming world, that you can never have too much Atari history stuff.  The layout of this game - the timeline you can walk through - is so good.  This is a really satisfying experience.I actually have my original Atari 2600 and all the cartridges.  I have an Atari Lynx with about 2 dozen carts for it.  I traded off my Jaguar because I wasn't too into it, but it's nice to have the important Jaguar games in this collection.I haven't gone through most of this collection yet, but I don't have to, before leaving this review.  This collection is on sale right now at its lowest price ever, and if you're on the fence about getting this, I bought it and I recommend it for the current price.Tempest itself.  So worth the price!Watched all the videos in this.  So good!  Nothing is recycled from the other documentaries I have on Atari.  Lots of new insight to the inner workings of the company.  This was such a good purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great collection full of games, videos, and images. This is how a collection should be. I love the fact that it not only focuses on the successes but also willing to acknowledge the mistakes and failures. Well presented and fun to play. Anyone who grew up with these games will defiantly get a lot out of it. I have always been a fan of the work Digital Eclipse does, and here they go above and beyond.

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice collection of great Atari games.  The videos are actually interesting.  Enjoying this more than Lies of P, Starfield, Diablo IV, and Baldurs Gate 3.  But then I'm old.  Played these games in the arcade when they were new.  Its the same thing as hearing someone who didn't see Star Wars in the theater in 1977 have an opinion that would matter to me.  This was the golden era of gaming.  Love this anthology.  I was in Vegas in '79 at Circus Circus playing these games, and '80, '81', '82 etc.  I got to play them all.  If you didn't play them when they came out this may be a boring collection.  Go play Starfield until your face gets tired.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: An interactive museum exhibit - probably the best presentation a retro collection like this has ever received.You would be mistaken thinking this is just another dump of ROMs being resold. Atari 50 manages to do what other collections have rarely done, providing historical context to set the stage for every game and piece presented here. Be it flyers, commercials, interviews, design docs or other material, every game here is given a bit of a spotlight to tell the journey of the company using its games as a throughline. The context definitely helped me engage in the mindset that the games were created in and get a lot more out of this compared to any past experiences I’ve had with anything here.In terms of games, the highlights for me include Breakout (there’s so many versions here), Adventure and Yar’s Revenge on the 2600, the arcade versions of Warlords, Missile Command and Asteroids and both Tempest and Tempest 2000.Not every game is a winner, but they’re all worthwhile from a historical perspective. There’s a few notable omissions - anything based on licensed properties or created by Activision is of course missing, which is a shame, and it’s unfortunate that Battlezone isn’t able to be included here either.  The 2022 reimaginings are hit and miss. Don’t buy this for those or expect them to be super fleshed out, but at worst they’re extra bonus curios and at best they’re as good as their source material. If you’re at all interested in the roots of arcade and home video games, this is an incredible package. If you just want to play the games then you probably already know whether you need this or already own the ROMs in some other format. Nonetheless I can highly recommend Atari 50. It has been a wild ride to experience the highs of the iconic arcade hits and path all the way to the lows of the Jaguar (besides Tempest 2000 of course, a true gem)As a side note, I experienced this entirely through a Steam Deck docked to my TV and had zero issues whatsoever. Even if it’s not “verified” at the time I write this, it may as well be.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Atari 50 is one of the best games I have ever played. It's not just a collection of Atari games, but a foundation that sets a new standard for retro game collections, and I mean that. Rare games, prototypes, remakes, enhanced versions, interviews, high quality art & manual scans, and a library of over 100 games (plus a few secrets, but don't tell mr atari or ill get in trouble >:(   ). This is not just a bunch of Atari games. It is an exploration of their history and development of the company and an astonishing achievement in the preservation of video games and their history. Well done Digital Eclipse, well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing compilation of classic (and even some new) Atari games at a reasonable price. I spent hours alone just going through the interactive timeline of the history of Atari, which includes concept ideas of now classic games, and how they came to be, as well as culture at the Atari offices in the 1970s. "Far out man" This really is a no-brainer if you're a fan of video game history.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best retro game collection I have ever gotten my hands on. It's really well crafted, with interviews, design documents, comic books, concept art, manuals and lots of other cool stuff to look at. Not all the games you'd hope for are in there, but honestly this collection is still well worth the money with all the cool extras that come with them.There's also a couple of (I assume) unreleased games and remastered versions and mashups of old games that are mostly super cool! Go check out VCTR-SCTR on youtube if you need more convincing!I really REALLY hope that Digital Eclipse gets to do more cool collections like this for other companies in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: This is how games preservation should be done! This is not just a random collection of 40 year old roms bundled together, instead this is much more like a curated museum collection with incredible work to bring together a collection of interviews, old adverts, promotional images and of course the games (emulated extremely well with great presets for modern controllers) that helped shape the games industry over the last 50 years. All presented in a slick UI that is fairly easy to navigate and very pleasing to look at. I have nostalgia for the Jaguar as I was suckered in by their 64-bit adverts and it was the first console I owned that was not a family machine. I wish the collection for Jag was a little larger in here, but that's just a personal thing and so glad they included Tempest 2000. The re-imagining of some old classics are also great and remind me of Astro Bot on the PS5 and what that did for Playstation history. I wish more publishers would produce museum style collections of their back-catalogue like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never had much nostalgia for the Atari era outside of a few PC titles and plug n plays I owned when I younger, I think I  can say with confidence that Atari 50 might one of the best retro game compilations to date right up alongside Rare Replay. What elevates this collection above previous Atari compilations is that it doesn't feel like another collection of ROM dumps but more like one giant interactive museum of Atari history. It really feels like a gaming history buff's wet dream especially considering how Atari's history and impact on the gaming industry is often overlooked in this day and age, The historical content on offer here is staggering ranging from high quality artwork and arcade flyer scans, documentary footage, retro commercials, magazine ads, trivia, historical quotes, design documents, video interviews, and even 3D recreations of the original boxart for the Atari console titles all presented in a clear easy to read timeline that I highly encourage you go through in chronological order.Now for the games themselvesThe Arcade titles are probably the strongest of the lot with all of Atari's most well known hits here and accounted for. On top of that you also have their lesser known, rarer, and more obscure titles including some that have never before been released. I think I even may have managed to find some new favoritesThe console titles (2600,5200,7800, Atari 8 Bit computers, Lynx, and Jaguar) tend to be a bit more mixed probably cause of the fact a lot of the 2600 titles haven't exactly aged the most gracefully and I do find the choice of included titles a bit odd at times. Did we really need 6 versions of Centipede and Missile Command? The 8 bit computers clearly got the short end of the stick here. However the role Atari 50 is playing in game preservation can't be ignored here considering how for a lot of these titles especially for the, 400/800, Lynx, and Jaguar as this is essentially the 1st time these games have ever seen a proper re release on a modern platform in any capacity and this isn't even touching on the number of never before released prototypes that are included in the collection.  The emulation is top notch and Digital Eclipse has clearly put their past experience with previous Atari compilations to good work here. as well as including a number of nice QOL improvements to boot. One improvement I enjoy is that  the keypad commands for 5200 titles have been thoughtfully reworked into a more traditional controller configuration which goes a long way in making titles such as star raiders much more accessible for new players.And they actually went and included a replica of one of Atari's electronic handheld games called Touch Me which is probably the most horny sounding name for a Simon clone game you will ever seeLast but not least we have 6 completely original games created for this collectionHaunted Houses a 3D re imagining of Haunted House with new locations and mechanicsNeo Breakout An updated version of breakout with new modes and competitive multiplayerQuadratank A 4 Player multiplayer oriented re imagining  of TankSwordquest Airworld based off the unreleased 4th installment of the Swordquest series for the Atari 2600VCTR SCTR A mashup of Asteroids, Lunar Lander, BattleZone, and Tempest and probably the highlight of the bunchYars Revenge Enhanced Basically just Yars Revenge but with an HD graphics filter option slapped on.Of course there are a number of notable games that aren't included likely for obvious legal reasons. Sorry Pitfall and Star Wars fans. But hopefully if this game does well enough we might even get DLC for more games in future.At the end of the day this is a must buy really not just for Atari fans but also for anyone who is into early gaming historyI give this game 9/10-1 point for no Attack of the Mutant Penguins
_childDocuments_.name: Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration

_childDocuments_.review: Atari 50 is the best game compilation ever made. The attention to detail and story telling is unmatched by any other product. In a true and just world, nothing less than this should ever be acceptable again. Companies can complain about the roms folder on our hard drives or they can let a company like Digital Eclipse access and present these games and their development with the care and detail they deserve; they can't do both.That's not to say this collects the best games ever made. In fact, sometimes it's quite the opposite. But no other collection takes the time to illustrate why these games are here and why they are important. The only flaws in the presentation come down to corporate politics—the dawn of third party developers is a huge part of the Atari story and while that's covered here, you can't actually play Pitfall or Kaboom or whatever. You can play Ninja Golf though and that's something I didn't even know existed before this collection.The reimagined games are a lot of fun too and a tremendous example of going the extra mile. Those are probably the games I'll come back to the most—I have unfinished business with Neo Breakout. It's nice to see some Jaguar games on here too, as I actually had the system back in the day, but never got anything for it but the Cybermorph pack in. Turns out my Cybermorph skills have stayed the same over the last couple of decades (they were bad then, and they are bad now).If you have any interest in gaming history, your money is well spent here. I believe they may have created a new genre with this one: playable documentary.And if any suits are reading this review please just let me say these five words: Digital Eclipse Mortal Kombat Kollection

_childDocuments_.review: This is much more than just a large collection of games, which I normally would have wanted. For Atari's 50th Anniversary, Digital Eclipse and Atari went all-out;  with developer interviews, covering all the pivital moments in the history of gaming's originator. From the seedy bars, to the dedicated gaming rooms, to the living room, to the PCs, even to the dumping grounds in the middle of nowhere, you get everything one would expect in a museum. Interviews, technical specifications, even the source code to one of Atari's launch titles, and you can even play the games as you go. The whole presentation makes me smile. You'll never see Nintendo doing something like this, or SEGA, or Capcom, or Konami, or Commodore, or Sony, or Electronic Arts, all with an equally-rich history in gaming culture. This is perfect. Well.........almost.Please don't look at me like that, you knew this was coming.The Cons: It was expected that due to licensing costs, Raiders, Gremlins, Superman nor E.T. would make the cut, that's not where I take issue with this collection. While I enjoyed the Reimagined versions of several Atari classics, it would have been nice to include the various remakes on XBLA/PSN, flaws and all. But that would be more of personal expectation with the momentous occasion.As of this writing, there is a very nasty bug with the UI when sharing the screen via Discord; The screen flashes a seizure-inducing green. The control loses its grip on my gamepad and reverts to keyboard control when alt-tabbing out and coming back. And when screen-sharing, the reimagined games do not show at all.Finally, and this might be an issue with the compression involved, the video interviews stutter on occasion. It's not often, but when they do, it's very apparent.Overall, while not perfect, Atari 50 comes pretty close, and raises the bar in what should be expected of dynasty companies when putting out collections for public consumption.

_childDocuments_.review: Only 2.8 hours in and ive only completed the first section of it. Far and away one of the absolute best retro game compilations in existence and easily *the* best interactive/virtual museum experience money can buy. There's just so much to dig into and enjoy in this package, regardless of if you are here for the games or for the documentary/museum aspect. The game selection is fantastic (though there's *always* room for improvement; DE lads, if you're reading, *please* convince Atari to let you do DLC.), the emulation is top notch and all the scanned documents and artefacts are high res enough for you to zoom in and see lots of details. I guarantee you have never seen this much love, care, attention and effort put into a game compilation, an "anniversary" release or a virtual museum. Ever. Full stop. Including for the next 5-10 years. Absolutely worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Kudos to Digital Eclipse and Atari for this one. They've really took the time and effort to put together a great retrospect on this iconic institution. Bringing the player through most of the good times and the bad of Atari. My only gripe is how little is mentioned about the home computer era. Yes, they did mention the 8-bit era, which coincidentally is where I began my history with Atari as a teenager. But everything about Atari and computers during Tramiel's ownership was barely mentioned at all, with maybe two or three brief mentions about the ST line, not one mention of the TT, and a very tiny blurb about the Falcon and nothing else.That said, it does a very good job everywhere else. My only tiny gripe is the emulation is a bit off with Tempest 2000. Many of the attract mode and Game Over screens run way too fast compared to the original hardware, but that's just a small gripe. Despite the relatively high price tag there is a lot of value here. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: More an interactive documentary on Atari's history than simply a collection of games, this makes for a fascinating read if you have an interest in gaming history. The games cover a wide chunk of the company's lifespan for better or worse. There are a lot of big games, but some notables are missing like S.T.U.N. Runner, and Hard Drivin'. (Perhaps I'm mistaken and those ended up with Williams?) Jaguar missing licensed games like AVP isn't shocking, but titles like Super Burnout and Ultra Vortek would've been welcome in lieu of partial games like Club Drive. Emulation seems fairly good to me. No noticeable lag across the various systems. Some kind of option to upscale the 3d games would've been welcome as would 4k support in general. (Maxes out at 1080) Save states are also supported. In all a very nice package.

_childDocuments_.review:
It has been five decades since a small team in Silicon Valley first combined their creativity, curiosity and passion into making video games and hardware. The result of their efforts was Atari, one of the most recognizable and enduring entertainment and pop culture brands in the world.

Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration takes players on an interactive journey through 50 years of video games via interviews with designers, developers and industry leaders, documentary footage, product design documents, high-resolution original artwork, and a specially-curated list of more than 90 playable games.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, if possible pls buy this game only on sale. NBA 2K23 is a yet another follow-up in the long-standing 2K basketball franchise that continues to release repeated versions of the same game, re-skinned and re-titled to fit the year, and the real-life players drafted that year, it represents. As expected the core gameplay has been worked on to perfection for years now so players know what will be brought to the table - just an overall smooth and crushingly-detailed basketball simulator. This isn't the first time Micheal Jordan has graced the cover of a 2K sports game, but a lot of time has passed since then and things have changed for the good and for the bad.If you look to play this, you have to consider many things: do you care about the you-against-the-AI aspect of it all or do you really crave that online player-vs-player feel. If your heart lies somewhere in the middle, you have to choose a side here because there's no in-between. Playing online-only means that you will have two years at max before the servers are shut down intentionally, forcing you to pay top dollar for the inevitable next installment. Playing against the AI means 2K can't do s**t to you if you want to stay in 2K23, having fun at the various modes it has to offer - NBA 2K23 will be playable even after the specific game has been deleted from the store. So choose carefully... when it's on sale (don't feed the pigs even more).On PC, this game is fun to play against the AI - no bugs, no glitches and an overall satisfied experience playing completely alone. Do I recommend NBA 2K23? Yes, if you play against the AI, If you aim to play online - please read the other reviews of players who've had an even greater experince than me there. It's a lot to unpack there, for sure.Follow your heart <3

_childDocuments_.review: I hopped on 2k23 late in the game, so this review is with the context of not having to deal with any launch issues, first season bugs, or exploits / toxicity in the early, more populated community.Pros:-Good graphics and animations.-Fun online play with friends.-Lots of customization options for your MyPlayer.-A pretty solid story line for the MyCareer.-MyGM and MyLeague are still incredibly fun, especially with the retro rosters. Cons:-Monotony sets in fast in the game play loop.-The good animations sometimes bug out and look stoppy and awkward.-Keyboard smashing Hall of Fame difficulty.-The crowds are still cardboard and the announcers usually aren't even talking about whats actually happening.-Random performance dips that happen without any rhyme or reason.-Can you even make 3 pointers without a 99 3pt shot?**Lots of TL/DR below.**The last 2K game that I played was 2k18 and I'd played almost all of them since 2k13, with a pause between when the originals were first coming out. Immediately, I was impressed by this game and that's probably just because it was the first one I'd picked up in years. For people who play this game every year, it makes sense how they'd be frustrated with only small changes but if you're gonna pick this game up on sale (which I did and recommend) then it is absolutely night and day. Graphics, animations, features, and the feel of the game on both keyboard and controller has absolutely evolved. There are some big problems though with 2k23 and most of it stems from progression in this game. Having your progression constantly stall out while you grind points till your next overall is a feature I'm pretty sure isn't new, but it really does add to the monotony of playing an 82 game season especially when you play it on Hall of Fame where every single game is a DRAG to complete with how insane the cheese from the CPU and computer is. Missing wide open layups with a 95 overall slashing forward is INSANITY. _childDocuments_.review: (I have spent way too many hours on 2k20 when I was younger, so I have played this kinda game for more than the 12.1 hours stated above).Unless you bought this game from CDKeys for cheap, or some other site - it's not worth it - and maybe not even at the discounted price you get.I've always found playing as a player in 2K to be monotonous if you do not spend money on the game - it costs way too much money (if you pay) to even be able to become a starter! I've always found MyPlayer the most enjoyable part of the series as a whole but now I've decided the investment in a sub-par game for £60 to not be worth it anymore. (For the record, I got it for a lot cheaper.) Whilst you can play online with your character if you feel they are high-level enough to compete with the toxic and dedicated players who are way too good for you - you can try and play in the Rec. Or don't - if you want to touch the ball. Queues in my experience can take upwards of 10 minutes, and people can leave if they judge you too be 'not up to their standards.' The experience of the career outside of playing I've also found to be incredibly boring and annoying and a the pre-NBA stuff is just prolonged time waste until you get drafted. You also always have a nickname the commentator calls you, and it's MP in this one. How unoriginal!And that's just MyPlayer.One bit of praise is that playing offline against the CPU is fun for a bit whilst you play as All-Star level players.Speaking of All-Stars, the dunk contest is awful. Don't recommend. Three point contest is good but often unrealistic.It also automatically sets your nationality to America, and as far as I am aware, you cannot change it. This means you only play for the American team during the young rookies matches in the All-Star games.The MyTeam process is also incredibly pay-to-have-a-somewhat-enjoyable-experience, and opening packs to get players costs WAY too much. (Spot the recurring theme?)I haven't played much at all of MyGM and MyLeague, you might find enjoyment but I find it to be the most boring of them all.At the end of the day, 2K does reward you for skill with green-light (perfect timing) shooting, but when you play online everybody can do it with ease. However, you have to grind/pay for your shooting (mid range and 3 point) so that it is easier to get the perfect timing.Building a MyPlayer has gotten a lot more freedom and something really I like about this game - it adds a lot of diversity to your character's strengths and weaknesses that just weren't possible before with the skill pie charts in earlier games.Also, I've noticed you cannot access other windows when playing unless you exit the game in full. WHY 2K? (You might be able to, I just haven't been able to do so).2K, I'm done wasting money on this forsaken game.TL;DR: If you want to spend too much money to get a somewhat enjoyable time, look right here. Looking for a fun basketballl game that can be won through skill without grinding? Tough luck. Look elsewhere - its better than here :)Do yourself a favour and go play actual basketball. You'll see what fun it is actually meant to be. Or watch basketball! Much more entertaining.Good luck :D3.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you're anything like me and have a passive interest in picking up sports games when they hit the 20$ and below price range just because its nice to have something to shut your brain off and play sometimes, this is the review for you.NBA 2K23 is far from my first NBA game, let alone 2K/sports title. I've played loads of FIFA, Madden and NBA over the years, and I've done everything in every mode in each of those games. As far as 2K goes, the main draw is usually one of a few things. MyPlayer, Franchise mode or MyTeam. I'm in the MyPlayer camp, and if you are also debating buying this for the MyPlayer, uh, don't.Consumers in general are to the point that even Call of Duty has realized that as a franchise, taking a little more time per title is necessary and they're spending time updating their current release rather than forcing a new one out within 12 months. 2K hasn't gotten the message yet, and I don't think the audience that plays these games seem to care much either. As far as new things go, the gameplay is essentially unchanged from every other NBA game I've played, which is mostly fine. Its basketball, the rules and game played doesn't change. That being said, there have been zero improvements in how the game feels or plays since I last played 2K21, and the NBA games from 2020, 2019, 2018 all the way back to 2009. Since around 2017 it feels like they are still using the same engine. The game looks remarkably bad for a sports "simulation" game. Character models are awful, the crowd might as well be wooden cutouts and the animations are pretty much the only part of this game that looks good. Keep in mind that everything gets 10 times worse once you enter multiplayer and have to deal with their horrible netcode. Somehow, they continue to make the game more frustrating to play. There's a lot of small annoyances that add up to being very unfun. To start with, theres a ton of things that you just can't skip in the "simulation" parts of the game. You have to wait 5 seconds to skip a timeout, you can't skip the halftime animation (roughly 30 seconds), you can't skip the ref bouncing the ball to the player during foul shots. You can turn off a lot of the post shot and highlight replays, which I do, but there are a ton of little things that just slow the games down a ton. Beyond in game annoyances, out of the game they are still trying to push this stupid player hub for everything. 2K23 has you on a cruise instead of in a neighbourhood, and having to go into the hub for everything is obnoxious. Did a sponsorship? Go in to the physical office to pick up the VC check. Want gear for your player? Go to the physical store. Haircut? You get the drill.They also yet again make the game unfun for anyone that doesn't purchase VC, it takes forever to grind out VC regardless of how good you are. I play on HOF and average a double double a game and I'm still barely making enough to get one upgrade per full game. You really are incentivized to pay to skip having to play as a bad character.This year, the shooting is much more difficult than past years. I don't know how to put my finger on it, but it is. This shows a lot in team modes where the release timers for all 5 players plus your bench are different, and unless you memorize all of the shot timings... well, good luck hitting a 3 with a bench player.I don't really know where else to fit this too, but the game runs fast on PC, load times are good, but any time your MyPlayer gets subbed out and the game slows down to give you the option to skip to your next appearance, if you have your framerate uncapped the game won't let you. You have to turn Vsync on, make your game borderless and limit it to 60fps or it won't work. Wish I was kidding.Everything about this port and just the game in general is lazy. The MyPlayer, which could be such an awesome thing to do, ends up being annoying as hell. The writing is bad, the cutscenes take too long, the characters are annoying, and all of this happens with basically no music, sound effects or production value. I think they stuck one guy in Blender and said "make our cutscenes for us" and left him with a Papa Johns pizza as payment. Thats the quality level on show here.Do yourself a favor, even as a nostalgia trip or just to have something to play, don't buy this. If nothing else I've said convinces you, this game that looks awful, has all kinds of game breaking bugs and is just annoying to play also takes up 130 GB on your hard drive. Yup, 130 gigabytes. Thats all, follow my curator page for more reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I know there are a lot of terrible reviews out there for this game, and a lot of the criticisms are somewhat fair, but so far at least, it seems to me that the negatives have been greatly exaggerated. I've never played NBA2k before so it doesn't bother me that it's similar to previous versions. (I can see why that would be very frustrating if you're someone who buys the game every year.) I play on PC without a controller (which the game warns you not to do for optimal gaming experience). Nevertheless, by playing with the key binding quite a bit at the beginning till I got comfortable and memorizing the mapping, I haven't had many ongoing problems from there. I've had only very minimal performance issues with the game (I know that was a common complaint.) And personally, I don't think the story cut scenes are nearly as bad as some say. It's not great, but it's not THAT terrible. A lot of people also complained that its pay to play, which is somewhat true. However, I've enjoyed playing so far without spending any real money, and I expect I will be able to slowly grind my character without spending money and still mostly enjoy the game. Between each game I do all the drills available and focus on getting better at one new skill each time. The games are then kind of like a test to see how well I can execute the new skill. All the games as well as side quests, daily rewards, etc. rack up enough VC to improve the character a bit between each game. Yes, it's slow improvement, but I don't mind that. It seems to me that you should expect a rookie player in the NBA to take a few seasons to turn into a superstar. I can see why that's annoying for those who just want to play a superstar from the start, but for me, it's still been fun to work on getting better at a new skill or two each game. The players stats matter, but I've found that at least at my low stat level, my skill as far as timing, choice of play, etc. matters probably almost as much. Finally, I read a bunch of negative reviews about how you just really can't play multiplayer modes with random players because there is no level matching. That very true. It's other than fun to face off in an REC game with players who are level 40 plus when your level 1...and there's very little participation reward if you don't get the ball much in those games (which you won't with higher level players). I only play the multiplayer modes for the initial quest rewards. After that, I expect I likely won't attempt them again until my player is MUCH better. In summary, as someone who has never bought a sports related game before, I'd give the game a B. It's certainly not worth $60, but if you can get it for $20 on sale like I did and don't have anything like it in your playing arsenal, it might be worth a go. I've enjoyed it as a change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: The last 2K I played was 2K17 and I had a blast with it. I was excited to pick up 23 and immediately noticed how the game took a turn for the worse.For starters, it seems like the gameplay has been complicated for no good reason. I want to be able to call a Pick and Roll, but instead I get a drop down menu of plays. When I was able to call a PNR, I could only call for the pick with one player. Your player will lose stamina for moving around the court--not using sprint, not using dribble moves, but for simply going from one spot of the floor to the other. I think this is ridiculous. These are NBA players, not average Joes at a YMCA game. I've noticed an issue that was in 2K17; the floor spacing is awful. Players will bunch up on one side of the floor and take awkward and bad angles. The gameplay doesn't feel fluid and simple. It feels like there are so many needless complications that took a fun, simple basketball game into an algorithmic game of metrics, calculations and other small things that took the fun out of it. I don't know, it feels like the game takes away your freedom to just hoop.There are some other things. Simulating a season is slower, and for some reason, they took out the facial sculpting feature. The soundtrack is also horrible. "Rocket Man" is one of the worst songs I've ever heard. There are a few gems in there, but I'm going to mute the soundtrack the next time I play it. I don't play online. I love MyGM and taking my MyPlayer offline, where I have no cap limitations and can make up storylines on my own. But I don't enjoy the gameplay. It feels far too complicated, and for no good reason.I'm only hours into it and yeah, there's going to be a learning curve, especially when my last 2K was over six years ago. I'm also not a basketball expert, but I love the sport and love playing 2K. That said, 2K23 has so many negatives that I can't recommend anybody pick this up.UPDATE: The shooting has been horrendously nerfed. Timing plays way too much of a factor in hitting open looks. Timing is an important part of shooting but if you're .001 second early or late, it's a miss. 2K nerfed shooting because the online players complained, understandably, but it's an unfair tax on offline players, IMO. For best experience, turn on "Real Player %" so you don't have to worry about this garbage mechanic.Defense has been buffed, which is fine, but players will stick to you like glue no matter how quick/shifty/agile you are. It doesn't help that the dribble moves have been overly complicated. In the old games, a crossover was a quick flick of RS. Now, you need to hold RT, move, and release RT quickly. It's more "realistic" but for me, it takes out most of the simple fun prior 2Ks had.Again, this complaint came at the hands of the online community. But they're not the ones to blame. Why can't 2K make a separate setting for offline players? I guess that's too much to ask. I can't wait to see how 2K makes the game unplayable with a series of patches that ruins the game.

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K23 is a prime example of a series that has lost its luster. While it offers a visually impressive basketball experience, the game is plagued by a host of issues that detract from the overall enjoyment.One of the most glaring problems with NBA 2K23 is its overreliance on microtransactions. From card packs in MyTEAM to VC for progression in MyCAREER, players are constantly bombarded with opportunities to spend real money. This aggressive monetization model feels exploitative and can significantly diminish the sense of accomplishment and fairness.Despite improvements in some areas, the gameplay still suffers from inconsistencies and frustrating mechanics. Defending can be a hit-or-miss affair, and AI teammates often make questionable decisions. The shooting system, while improved, can still feel overly sensitive or inconsistent, leading to frustrating misses.MyCAREER, the single-player mode where players create their own player and journey through the NBA, has become a tedious grind. The progression system requires an excessive amount of time and effort to unlock meaningful upgrades and content. This can be especially frustrating for casual players who simply want to enjoy the game without feeling pressured to invest countless hours.The NBA 2K community has been vocal about their dissatisfaction with the series, expressing concerns about issues such as server stability, matchmaking, and a lack of meaningful updates. These ongoing problems have eroded trust and left many players feeling neglected.NBA 2K23 offers a visually appealing basketball experience, but its flaws far outweigh its strengths. The excessive microtransactions, inconsistent gameplay, and lack of meaningful updates make it a disappointing entry in the series. Until 2K addresses these fundamental issues, fans will continue to feel let down by a franchise that once held so much promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin with this one...Man, back in the days, coming from NBA Live from uh.. some other big gaming publisher, I discovered the NBA 2k series back in 2006 and it was...a revelation. Miles ahead already back then in terms of both presentation and gameplay. I've kept in touch over the years until NBA 2k16. After that, I merely watched the yearly trainwreck unfold on social media when thousands, no millions of people again flocked around the yearly NBA 2k Update. The core of the game is still there. The animations are mostly good, the gameplay is mostly solid, apart from when it's not. Overall, on the court, you still can't find a better virtual Basketball experience to this day. Maybe that's part of the problem. Lack of competition makes things stale. Uninspired. Atriously bad. Oh my god, so bad. I've always loved the idea of playing my own character and getting a feeling for how an NBA career might feel like. My go-to fantasy was always: Simon Jordan, a nephew of the great His Airness. Same family name, huge burden. He understands the implications and he's not a copy of the original, he's a great player in his own right. No, he grows into one. This is what I am looking for, by the way, Visual Concepts, if you are reading this. The journey, the growth from a talented rookie with clear weaknesses, into a hall of fame candidate. What are you giving me here? The weirdest, pointless, annoying, mood-killing cut-scenes I have ever had to endure in any game. They're so bad, you can hardly even meme on them. My player, young Mister Jordan is already in some big fancy apartment somewhere, clearly a millionaire. Surrounded by an annoying manager, girlfriend and social media lady. "That's why your fans hate you probably, lol", my rival Shep tells me. I didn't ask btw.  No idea why this douche is my rival at all, why he seems like he is about to stab me on the way to the lockerroom. Or why my player first shrugs it off with a coolness, until my "rival" says: "ha, the sun even shines on a dog's ass sometime!" - and oh boy, suddenly my character gives him a look that should kill him, but sadly doesn't.What the ♥♥♥♥ am I watching? Skip. I play my first game. My player has an average rating of 70. Not great, not terrible. I somehow shoot 70 % from mid-range, but I don't know why. There is very little shot-feedback. Clearly, a step back. Let alone the fact that I am being benched for most of the 4th quarter despite having scored the most points on my team. After the game, the season is supposed to start! Yay! Except, no, first, I am being invited to a special club, of which only the best players can be a part of. Clearly, that's me... Mister draftpick number 18! This is where I can satisfy all my shopping needs! ...My dudes, I just want to play Basketball and have a succesful season. What is this? Metabook? Disgusted, I try to upgrade my first ability with the 850 Virtual Coins I have earned. There is no real money involved, yet I feel like I just got my lunch money taken from me. I feel... disillusioned. NBA 2k 23 is a pale shadow of it's former gloryful self. The music, the menus, the lack of meaningful improvements in gameplay, a backstory that could have been done better for 5 $ by some guy/gal from Fiverr in 10 minutes. I really really wanted to like this game, I really wanted to play some virtual basketball in 2022 (btw after 2k Games made 2k16 literally obsolete and unplayable even offline!) but I just can not stand this piece of ♥♥♥♥ garbage. For the love of Kobe Bryant (<3 rip) please stop buying this garbage game, show the developers that this is not what we want in a game! Or maybe it is me? Am I so out of touch? No, it's the children who are wrong!

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K23 on PC, a cursed artifact that shattered the very essence of my existence. Its arrival marked the beginning of my descent into an abyss of eternal sorrow, where joy ceased to exist and anguish became my constant companion.From the moment I launched the game, a heavy cloud of melancholy enveloped my soul. Each pixelated basketball player seemed to taunt me, their flawless digital forms amplifying my own inadequacies as a human being. I spent endless hours chasing victory, seeking solace in a realm where success was nothing more than a cruel illusion.But the game's malevolence extended far beyond its deceptive allure. The glitches and bugs, like sharp knives, lacerated my fragile hopes and dreams. Every step on the virtual court was met with frustration and disappointment as the game twisted and contorted itself into an unplayable mess. How could I find solace in such a broken world?And then there were the microtransactions, those insatiable monsters lurking in the shadows. With every transaction, a piece of my soul was sold to the highest bidder. I watched helplessly as my hard-earned money vanished into a void of emptiness, leaving me destitute and hollow.Suffocating in the toxic fumes of the online community, I found no refuge from the relentless torment. Harsh words and relentless vitriol were hurled at me, piercing my heart with each cruel insult. Loneliness consumed me as I realized that even in this virtual realm, human connection was an elusive mirage.NBA 2K23 became the catalyst for my undoing, a relentless force that stole my dreams, crushed my spirit, and left me a mere husk of a person. Its grip on my soul tightened with every passing day until hope was extinguished, leaving only a desolate wasteland of despair.Beware, dear reader, for NBA 2K23 is not a game—it's a descent into an abyss from which there is no escape. Approach it at your own peril, for its embrace will bind you to a lifetime of sorrow. May you find solace where I could not.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Pros:Stunning Graphics & Presentation: NBA 2K23 continues the franchise’s legacy of top-tier visuals, with lifelike player animations, detailed arenas, and dynamic lighting. The game captures the energy of an actual NBA game, complete with realistic crowd reactions and commentary that make every game feel immersive.Gameplay Improvements: 2K23 refines many core gameplay mechanics, adding smoother dribbling, more realistic player movement, and more intuitive shooting. Defense has also been tweaked, making it more challenging to exploit easy plays and forcing players to strategize on both ends of the court. AI has seen improvements as well, with smarter team play and opponent behavior.MyCareer Mode: The career story mode this year is well-crafted, offering a fresh storyline with a "rising star" feel, full of customizations and new quests. The RPG elements add depth, allowing players to make choices that impact their career and relationships, making it feel like you’re shaping a true journey.MyNBA Eras: This new feature is a standout addition, letting players explore different NBA eras with unique visual filters and rule sets. It's a treat for fans interested in experiencing the evolution of the league, complete with authentic rosters and courts from the 80s, 90s, and 2000s.MyTeam Updates: MyTeam mode has removed contracts, making it easier to play with favorite cards without the grind of micromanaging. The seasonal format continues to offer new content, and card art is better than ever.Cons:Microtransactions & Pay-to-Win Elements: Like previous entries, NBA 2K23 is loaded with microtransactions. Whether in MyCareer or MyTeam, progression can feel heavily gated without VC purchases. For those who want to level up quickly or build a competitive MyTeam, spending real money often feels necessary.Server & Connection Issues: Despite being a yearly title, 2K's servers still struggle, especially during peak times. Matchmaking can be slow, and there are occasional disconnects, which can be frustrating during competitive online play.Repetitive Grind in MyCareer: While MyCareer is fun, the grind for VC and badges is still real. Players without VC investments may find progression sluggish, especially when competing against others who have boosted stats.Slight Gameplay Staleness: While improved, the core gameplay is still familiar. Players returning from recent titles might not notice dramatic changes, and certain animations can feel recycled.Verdict: NBA 2K23 is a solid basketball game with impressive visuals, refined gameplay, and engaging modes. However, its reliance on microtransactions and recurring online issues slightly hamper the experience. If you're a basketball fan or franchise veteran, this year’s installment is worth a look, especially for its nostalgia-rich MyNBA Eras mode and the immersive MyCareer journey.

_childDocuments_.review: NBA 2K23 is a yet another follow-up in the long-standing 2K basketball franchise that continues to release repeated versions of the same game, re-skinned and re-titled to fit the year, and the real-life players drafted that year, it represents. As expected the core gameplay has been worked on to perfection for years now so players know what will be brought to the table - just an overall smooth and crushingly-detailed basketball simulator. This isn't the first time Micheal Jordan has graced the cover of a 2K sports game, but a lot of time has passed since then and things have changed for the good and for the bad.If you look to play this, you have to consider many things: do you care about the you-against-the-AI aspect of it all or do you really crave that online player-vs-player feel. If your heart lies somewhere in the middle, you have to choose a side here because there's no in-between. Playing online-only means that you will have two years at max before the servers are shut down intentionally, forcing you to pay top dollar for the inevitable next installment. Playing against the AI means 2K can't do s**t to you if you want to stay in 2K23, having fun at the various modes it has to offer - NBA 2K23 will be playable even after the specific game has been deleted from the store. _childDocuments_.review: Title: Disappointing Performance and Ban Issues in NBA 2k23As an avid basketball fan, I was eager to try out the latest release of 2k23. The game promised to bring the excitement of the NBA to my fingertips with unparalleled realism, engaging gameplay, and cutting-edge graphics. Unfortunately, my experience has been marred by constant lag, settings issues, and an unwarranted ban. Despite its potential, this game has left me feeling frustrated and disenchanted.Starting with the positives, 2k23 delivers an impressive array of features that cater to both casual and hardcore gamers. The roster is up-to-date, and the player models are incredibly detailed, capturing the essence of each athlete. The game also boasts a wide range of customization options, allowing players to build their dream teams and take on others in online multiplayer matches. Additionally, the career mode is highly engaging, letting users create and develop their player from a rookie to a legendary superstar.Unfortunately, the game's performance on PC leaves much to be desired. From the moment I launched it, I encountered persistent lag, making the gameplay experience unbearable at times. Even on the lowest settings, I struggled to achieve a smooth, stutter-free experience. The game seems poorly optimized, which is highly disappointing given the caliber of its developer.Furthermore, the settings issue is beyond frustrating. Every time I start the game, I must manually adjust the settings to make it playable. The game consistently reverts to the default settings upon launch, which is incredibly inconvenient and tedious. This is a basic feature that should have been sorted out during the development stage, and its absence is inexcusable.What has been most disappointing, though, is the seemingly random ban I received while playing online. Without warning or explanation, I found myself unable to access the game's multiplayer component. Contacting customer support has been a slow and unhelpful process, leaving me feeling ignored and undervalued as a consumer. This ban issue has soured my entire experience with NBA 2k23.While this game offers an impressive array of features, its laggy performance, settings issues, and unwarranted ban overshadow its potential. The game could have been a slam dunk, but instead, it feels more like an airball. I sincerely hope that the developers address these issues in future updates, but for now, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend this game to fellow basketball enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: Been a 2K person since the beginning but always gamed on console. This year is my first ever on PC and I have to honestly say the game plays a pretty good game of basketball. To anyone wondering NBA 2K23 on PC is "last gen" meaning it is the same version that's on PS4 & XB1. So there is no "next-gen" version available for the PC. For some this is a deal breaker and I understand but for me the modding community has made this game better than the "next-gen" console version. On PC you can basically change up the whole look of the game, like change the broadcast presentation to ESPN, TNT, NBATV etc. Update the player faces, jerseys, courts, shoes that were not included with the game originally. You can even mod the lighting in the stadiums to make it look better & more realistic than "next-gen". So needless to say I am loving this game. And NBA 2K23's gameplay is waaaay better than any previous version. Animations on PC play out much smoother, you will see animations you've probably never seen before on console once you tinker with the sliders a bit to get everything dailed in. There are videos on YouTube to help with this.In conclusion I love this game. Its not for everyone and there are no shortage of folks who are going to complain about 2K no matter what (mostly the MyCareer mode which I don't play as it is a pay to win mode) ...but if you are knowledgeable about the game of basketball and really understand the game, and have the ability to adjust the settings and sliders you can thoroughly enjoy this game to the fullest. My advice don't waste your time with MyCareer or Online play as it's nothing but pure frustration. The sweet spot is offline play and franchise mode. Get on YouTube and learn how to add mods and this game will transform into a true NBA stimulation. I would NOT recommend paying $60 for the game though, wait on a sale, I got mine for $25.
