_childDocuments_.review: The basic game-play is still pretty good, but it hasn't changed in a long time and 2K continues to provide last-gen versions for PC. So, some of the most exciting new features? Yeah, nowhere to be seen.MyLeague is still fun.MyCareer is still a disaster. Everything is balanced around the online component, and you're constantly thrust into an online lobby even if you're only trying to play it single-player. It's one of those areas of the game that has gotten progressively worse with time, so here are a few highlights of issues I personally have with it:1) Progression is designed to be punishing to encourage people to buy VC. This probably ties into the online portion of trying to get people to fork over a ton of extra money so they can stop losing all the time. The result is that if you don't want to pay to win in an 80 dollar (CAD) game, you get to be a first overall pick who's so bad they've got dramatically worse attributes than the 15th man on your average MyLeague team. Hell, some of them don't even start with basic dunk packages.2) Story. I'm sorry, but the stories on 2K have never been good. The fact that they're mandatory, that there's no option to just make a player and play a career without having to skip 8 cutscenes before and after games because it has to introduce so many side-characters--it's a bit ridiculous. The worst of it is, because of the cutscenes--you have to hear the announcers talking not about what you're doing in the games, but about how great a guy you are.3) Bugs. The game has bugs in it, like the vsync sim-to-next-appearance bug, that were reported back in like 2K21. In 2K12, the career mode had:1) The draft.2) Sensible progression. Your player didn't start terrible, and it didn't take a ton of meaningless grinding to get them up to the level of an actual good rookie player.3) Less noise. The training facility and the various boosts and stuff are just time-wasters: they add nothing, and actually detract from the experience.4) Free dunk packages, lay-up packages, and shot styles that you could play with before you started, rather than needing to get games-and-games worth of VC to play with.5) Quick turnover to get into the action -- hit 'play next game' or 'play next key game' and you're there. No cutscenes to worry about.6) Post-game interviews relate to what you did in the game, not what your player did when he was on his phone in a cutscene.I dunno. I just want to play sports games to play sports, but I guess that doesn't convince people to hurl money at 2K so they can shoot a little better in a game that's already full-price when you buy in.

_childDocuments_.review: 1. **Gameplay Mechanics**: The on-court gameplay is praised for its realism and depth. The new offensive and defensive mechanics provide a more immersive basketball experience².2. **Historical Content**: The inclusion of the Michael Jordan Challenge and various retro modes is a hit among basketball history enthusiasts¹.3. **Variety of Modes**: With MyCAREER, MyTEAM, MyGM, and MyLEAGUE, there's a plethora of content to keep players engaged for hours².### Cons:1. **Lack of Next-Gen Graphics**: One of the biggest disappointments is the absence of next-gen graphics and features on the PC version. Players expected a visual upgrade similar to what is available on consoles, but the game falls short in this aspect¹.2. **Microtransactions**: The heavy emphasis on microtransactions, especially in MyCAREER, has been a major point of contention. Players feel that the game pushes them towards spending real money to stay competitive¹³.3. **Repetitive Content**: Despite the variety of modes, some players find the content repetitive and not significantly different from previous iterations⁵.Overall, while **NBA 2K23** offers a solid basketball simulation with rich historical content and engaging gameplay, the lack of next-gen graphics and the pervasive microtransactions detract from the overall experience. detailed_description: ~A tragicomedy in your smartphone.~ Backfirewall_ is a first-person tragicomic adventure that takes place inside a smartphone. As the update assistant, you hold the fate of the System in your hands. Will you counter the update and save the chatty operating system OS9 from deletion? Begin a humorous escapade through various areas of the phone and solve clever puzzles. Meet colorful apps that inhabit the smartphone and have their own opinions about their boss, the update, and the godlike user. Clever puzzles 👁️‍🗨️ Review terminal errors in RAM, party in the Speakers’ exclusive nightclub, navigate through the Wi-Fi bureaucracy, and explore other areas of a smartphone. Cheat-codes to manipulate the environment 👁️‍🗨️ Hunt down or create bugs, trim binary trees, master music-controlled platforms, collect errors, and delete data using special cheat-codes. A variety of app-characters 👁️‍🗨️ Gossip with quirky pieces of software—the sassy Photos, the insecure Social Media F, or the neglected Health, among others—and uncover their distinct side stories. Numerous collectibles 👁️‍🗨️ Collect emails scattered about to discover a parallel story of the mysterious phone User. Unproductive and useless humor 👁️‍🗨️ Enjoy meta satirical humor and breaking the fourth wall.

short_description: Hello and welcome to Backfirewall_, a first-person tragicomic adventure set inside a smartphone. You are the update assistant. Solve wacky puzzles to counter the update and save the previous operating system from deletion. The fate of the System is in your hands!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, but hear me out: this is the closest thing to SOMA I've played, and I've tried many a time. Insanely, comparable drama came in the form of this comedic game that kicks the fourth wall left and right and is closer in tone to  than any sci-fi game I tried.Don't get fooled by the wacky characters: it's a game about death — and coping with the understanding that your God is a scammer.You play as an update assistant that tries to install a new OS to a phone. It turns out, however, that this process is supposed to end with your erasure, and the old OS doesn't want to die as well, so the two of you join forces to resist the update. You proceed to travel through the system, getting to know its many inhabitants.The painful truth, however, is that the system IS shabby, laggy, and old. It DOES need an update. It's crumbling around you. And while the system's inhabitants have different opinions on whether the update would help, it soon becomes apparent that your and the OS's selfishness is bringing pain to those around you — and also kind of leads nowhere. There is no endgame. No solution to planned obsoletion — the mortality of programs. As it dawns on you that you can't escape the inevitable, the tone of the game becomes more and more tragic. And while the style is still whimsical and it still cracks jokes, the ending bears uncanny similarities to SOMA — .Notably, the gameplay is also fun here. It's not an overly complicated puzzle —  is first and foremost a narrative game — but you can do a lot with four types of interaction. It never felt like I was ploughing through gameplay sections to get the next piece of the story — the pacing in particular was done well. Each level is relatively short and has a theme, and recurring characters, while not too deep, are endearing enough that losing them matters. The game also plays with meta — for example, some characters can speak and some can only communicate through text, and it's an in-universe thing.The comedic tone makes it easy to get into  (and some jokes had me chuckle out loud), the puzzles are fun enough to make you stay, and the final chapters actually felt unironically heavy. It's a damn shame that this game has 160 reviews. It deserves way more attention.

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ is a game that will take you on a journey inside a smartphone that is nothing short of extraordinary. The highlight of the game is its story. It is well-crafted and takes you through all sorts of emotions. It's a touching, captivating, humorous, and entertaining tale with twists and turns! What appealed to me the most was the attention to detail. There are many characters and most of them are well-developed. Heck, even characters that seem unimportant can hide a nice little story. This makes the whole smartphone ecosystem feel real and alive. The alternate endings add even more depth to the experience and replayability. The level design is original and filled with hidden places to find, and the puzzles, while on the easier side, serve the story perfectly. The gameplay is easy to handle with the functions (powers) introduced throughout the game. It's also quite an original way to solve puzzles. The sound design is fantastic. I love OS9 (the main character) with his humor and British-like manners. The other characters also have excellent voice acting with very distinct personalities. I also enjoyed the hilarious sound effects, like when you turn on a light or trim a tree. These are the little details that give this game an edge over other narrative games.If I had to list a few problems (although they are NOT significant), I would say that you cannot revisit previous areas to collect missing items. You have to collect 100% of the items in one playthrough, and sometimes the text is not clear enough (for example, when you want to buy collectibles, you do not actually pay with the messages, you still have them in your collectibles).To conclude, this game is like a Pixar movie in the form of a video game, with well-developed characters and a story that will keep you entertained from start to finish, and again all the little details everywhere make it amazing. Moreover, it also makes you reflect on your actions as a protagonist of the system. I highly recommend Backfirewall_ to anyone who wants to live an incredible, carefree adventure. Now the question is: will you update?

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ is a first-person adventure game that takes place inside of a smartphone on the verge of...updating? As the update assistant who has now gained full autonomy, you hold the fate of the system in your hands. Will you save OS9, a chatty and humorous interpretation of the old OS, or will you let the update happen and give the world a fresh reboot. Traverse through the smartphone and solve puzzles, meet unique characters, find bunches of collectables, and save the phone from impending "doom".Before 3 weeks ago, I had no idea this game existed, but I am so glad to have discovered it. I enjoyed the humor and setting, as well as the minimalistic graphics compared to the more complex 3D games. In the end, this unknown game captured my attention and I loved the experience I got. And the best part about this, enjoying this on the Steam Deck is almost a guarantee!When first booting up the game, I was delighted to see it running better than I expected. 60 FPS with no setting changes (the game starts on max settings) was wonderful to see. It did hold up for awhile too, but I did start to notice some slowdowns later in the game. This started after getting out of the first area. I did have to change a couple settings at that point, bringing quality to medium and a FPS cap of 55, but I had no more issues after that! You could increase TDP and keep at 60, but the battery savings were much more appealing with 55, which felt just as smooth.Other than that, there are a couple of little trouble spots I found that took deeper looking to find. The most obvious was actually a single standing light in the first area. Walking around was completely fine, but going up to it would cause dips to 14-20 FPS. As soon as I walked away though, the game would go right back up to the correct framerate.I did feel the camera movement speed was a bit on the slow side for my taste, but overall, I had no issues running the game. The controls worked fine, with a slight adjustment to camera speed, and no graphical problems at all.Backfirewall_ is a fantastic first-person game with a story that shines with its humor and setting. The puzzles require some thinking, but won't completely break your mind. I loved seeing this interpretation of what it would be like inside of a smartphone. Thanks to how the game is made and how easy it is to run, Backfirewall_ also feels amazing on the Steam Deck. I wish I had known about this game earlier, but I am so glad I do now!

_childDocuments_.review: Embracing change can be difficult. Especially so when the changes seem to overhaul established norms which weren't in dire need of "fixing". Already described as a tragicomic adventure, Backfirewall_ is indeed a bittersweet manifesto against the absurd concept of planned obsolescence. An economic strategy envisioned by certain corporations and manufacturers long before the dawn of tech companies. It's developer Naraven Games' second project released on Steam after their F2P bite-sized forray called "Answer Knot". Give that one a try and you'll be able to understand some of the internal conflicts that are present in Backfirewall_ as well. The latter is published by All In! Games as yet another indie gem for their growing portofolio.You might be tempted to draw some narrative comparisons with the Portal series. After all, we also have social comentary on tech industry corporate greed in Backfirewall_ alongside sarcasm and snarky remarks from a constant companion to an otherwise silent protagonist. There's even an evil Operating System trying to push for total control (she's also female, but definitely not GLaDOS). Manipulative as she may be, you won't fall for that scheme and instead join a resistance movement fighting against sudden, deliberate changes. Without spoiling anything, imagine the real life counterpart of a software update on your mobile devices. They are meant to be seamless changes, but sometimes they can still cause faulty apps that aren't yet updated themselves to handle a new OS version.Some applications might even require uninstalling if the long-awaited updates won't be implemented at all. The smartphone is a clever metaphor in Backfirewall_. You role play as the Update Assistant, a software protocol which serves as the catalyst for the updating process. By seeing all steps followed to completion, you inadvertently cause your own deletion in the process.  A Unity project which still has some install size issues (currently occupying around 34 GBs), the performance was spotless at the very least. It won't turn any heads, but the graphics are serviceable as they convey the dystopic insides of a smartphone. Visual metaphores are the best kind. A minimal design in regards to the textures, yet still colourful enough to contain eye-catching set pieces.The HUD is clean for the most part, minus the permanent presence of a yellow eye sprite etched on the upper right side of the screen. Haven't found a way to make OS9's gaze become less intrusive, though it does occasionally blink. I appreciate any title which lets me fiddle with the subtitles far beyond just font size. I want them purple too and Backfirewall_ catered to my "burning desires".Here is where the story truly shines. Clever voice acting for the deuteragonist, the aforementioned OS9 struggling to keep both himself and the silent protogonist alive and relevant. Wheatley was a clear inspiration, yet the sardonic outlook has been tempered enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation. The majority of NPCs only communicate through repetitve buzzing and clicking sounds, so the few characters that are fully voiced, have to stand out.No Portal Gun, obviously. You will instead manipulate certain objects within the environment through actions mimicking software command lines. Some puzzles are complex, but solutions can be found thorough inspection of the level or by receiving hints from an omnipresent rubber duck. Plenty of collectibles tied to Steam Achievements can be found on every level section.Half the fun of Blackfirewall_ is finding connections to tech jokes and elements which are sometimes tied to pop culture references as well. Imagine "The Big Bang Theory" at its finest, during the first couple of seasons. No time constraints per se, feel free to explore every nook and cranny, the map is filled  with everything from funny messages to creative doodles acting as pure satire. It might not push the story forward, but it will provide context.Multiple endings are a treat, since they provide some replayability to an otherwise brief experience of around five hours per standard playthrough. In fact, you can get one particular ending in less than 15 minutes and all you have to do is reach a certain point and do nothing but wait. Reminded me of some Far Cry endings following that same path of inaction. The collectibles themselves range from messages you need to decipher, to certain action figures rewarded for helping out characters and finding "bugs within the system". A glitch or two in the Matrix never hurt anyone. Many achivements can only be gained by venturing well beyond the beaten path, but you've got time to burn unless you're into speedrunning. Reaching the more fleshed out conclusions will require certain choices made along the way, as you explore new sections of the smartphone layout and interact with NPC routines. A few fetch quests here and there, while you can safely assume Occam's Razor is the best course of action. "The simplest explanation is usually the best one." Hidden in plain sight and quite ironic given the constant scrutiny of that eye companion of yours. Eyes wide shut.Overall, there are plenty of aspects you can appreciate about Backfirewall_. It strives to be original and its satire isn't too blunt. Given the early tech exposure for younger generations, I think this title can be enjoyed by almost any gamer, regardless of age bracket. It's definitely something worth considering if you want a more peaceful experience without mind-numbing brain teasers at the same time. It's fully worth it as far stability and current pricing are concerned. The change in the System starts with you.+ Amusing collectibles.+ Steam Achievements.+ Pleasant graphics and sounds.+ Replay value through multiples endings.- No Steam Trading Cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ is, in a word, brilliant. You play an Operating System Installation Protocol who has been loaded into a cell phone to start an upgrade to a new OS. Upon arrival, you meet OS9 (the old operating system) who, out of self preservation, convinces you to sabotage the upgrade. Thus begins a romp through the bowels of the cell phone - a journey filled with bits, logs, processes, pointers, and a host of applications. You travel through familiar features  (Recycle BIN, RAM, the Battery, Messages, Photos, WiFi, etc.) that are presented in a creative and colorful way.The sound track is superb, with delightful voice acting. OS9 is witty, sarcastic, and one of the best traveling companions you'll find.  This is a good thing because you can't click through dialog and sound is essential to problem solving. There are phones to answer, bugs and cookies to find, user messages to read, and toys to collect. Much of the problem solving requires creating system errors in each area you pass through. While some thinking outside the box is required, this is not a difficult game. The environment is a labyrinth of tunnels, hidden rooms, and multi-level work spaces. You are armed with 4 cheat codes that allow you to manipulate the environment to meet your needs.  If you are stuck, there are rubber ducks who will give you hints and OS9 is generally helpful. I played with a controller which worked best for me (although I did use the keyboard to solve a dance puzzle).Backfiirewall_ is a 3D platformer with some stealth to avoid Security Guards. The penalty for getting caught is minimal... you just return to try again. While moderately precise platforming is required, you usually don't fall to your death and there is minimal jumping.  If you are killed, you are immediately returned to the same place to try again.The only complaint I have is that the game auto-saves to a single slot. If you are not an achievement hunter, this will not matter to you. But, it will drive completionists crazy. Your path is fairly linear and you cannot circle back to look for missed items. Bypassing a collectible means starting a new game, from square one (tutorial and all). In my second play-through, I am copying my save files to back-up folders before moving to a new section to avoid multiple restarts. Collectibles are not retained when a new game is started and some actions for achievements already earned must be repeated  in order to qualify for the 'good' ending. Those seeking 100% might consider checking out the guide  posted by Carrot Helper. Separate from the video, the list of timestamps can be used to count the items you are looking for in a specific area.I highly recommend Backfirewall_ to those who enjoy an engaging adventure through a world that is beautifully crafted and quite clever. Although not required, those with knowledge of computers will probably laugh the hardest. Forget about achievements and take time to read everything and talk to everyone you meet. It will be time well spent.An added note: Looking back at the games I've played this year, Backfirewall_ remains my most memorable and most delightful experience!

Not too much else to say about it really other than it's worth a playthrough for sure and deserves more attention that it currently has.------------------------------Control Scheme I Used:  Default Binding Keyboard and Mouse.  Supports controller. _childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall is the kind of game that clearly has a lot of effort, but not a lot of direction. You play as an update assistant inside a phone trying to stop the system from updating by following the instructions of the current operating system. To do this, you go through a bunch of abstract representations of the phone's internal processes, use a few cheat codes to manipulate the system, and cause errors to clear the path ahead. I was drawn to this game by the clean art style and cool premise as well as the solid voice acting in the trailer. I thought this would be a game similar to Portal with a chipper character by your side making for some fun dialogue and interesting puzzles. That's not what I got.The game unfortunately fails to accomplish any of its goals. The visuals are fine and the voice acting is still decent, but nothing is ever utilized in a new or clever way. The comedy is predictable and boring, the dramatic moments don't leave any impact, the character dialogue ranges from boring to bland, and the overall story beats are mostly just confusing and made me want to rush through by the end. And the gamepaly doesn't fare any better. You have four cheat codes you can use to cause errors and find collectibles, but they ways in which they're used is obvious from the outset of each new puzzle you encounter. I can't imagine anyone struggling to find solutions to these problems, none of them have clever utilizations of the powers to make you feel smart, and it mostly just boils down to wandering around until finding the next highlighted object to click. Putting all of that aside, the game also constantly takes away your control for boring cutscenes, the controls are stiff as all hell, you get locked out of collectibles if you get past certain points in the game, and worst of all- the game deleted my save file as I was nearing the end. I did still finish the game, but reluctantly to say the least. In the grand scheme of things, there's nothing particularly awful about Backfirewall, but unfortunately, there's nothing particularly special about it either.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start by saying that I don't necessarily despise the game.My problems deal with the accomplishments and slow paced / jerky movement.I shouldn't have to replay 4 hours of content just to obtain one accomplishment, and I shouldn't be unable to save scum. It just creates a chasm between what a player is allowed to do and what a developer tells them they can do."You are not permitted to save scum; we want more hours spent playing our video game, so do it on your first run or try again!" That's how it feels, and it's not something I enjoy doing. In comparison to another game I have played, it had three separate achievements at the end of the game, the game was eight hours long, and it automatically removed your save. It's not a good feature. On the surface, the game plays like The Stanley Parable, with nods to other games like Super Hot (Telephones), unless I'm mistaken. Internet references, for example. It's fantastic to be able to connect with some of these well-known allusions.The opening is excellent, and there appear to be several endings from what I can tell; nonetheless, there is much more to be desired.After a few hours, the humor begins to fade, and the game appears to run at low frame rates with no way to change this option. It feels like I'm playing at 26-28 frames per second at times, or there's a lot of motion blur that skips I do not believe this to be a hardware issue. It aspires to be like Stanley, but fails to truly immerse you in the tale and puzzles.It has fantastic character design and moments where it sticks out, but overall I felt denied and pushed away because I didn't know every single ASDF reference and had to restart because I couldn't re-load a save. It's been overwritten.It's enough to drive me away from the game for good. It may appear stubborn or ridiculous to negative a game for this, but it's more or less a personal thing, similar to having a parkour game prevent you from climbing a specific landmark or site. It simply makes no sense and only serves to punish someone for such a trivial thing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, the unforgiving nature of the story progression and inability to access or create backups within a game about backing up a phone is incredibly ironic.Steam Backup will be your best friend because sometimes the dialogue tree progresses itself, or alt-tabbing progresses it like say when coming back from reading the guide, and there's absolutely no way to restart the conversation and that's critical achievement content wasted an hour into the level. There are a few complaints on the discussion board about being like 10 hours into the game and having to restart the entire thing due to corrupted backups. I don't understand what the point of the OS making a huge deal about the auto save or what the point of having it deal out checkpoints every few seconds or clicks is if you're not going to give anyone access to the checkpoints in the menu OR the steamapps file. In my 2nd play through- at the very end of the night club scene- Podcast and Music's dialogue tree bugged out and wouldn't let me collect the last figurine, which also makes you miss the Data Jesus achievement. I had to restart the entire level and collect every stupid ass text message all over again. ASDF God gets messed up by this, as well. For this annoying reason alone I almost hit do not recommend. The bugs along the way impeding achievements have been infuriating. Try not to do too many things at once or progress too quickly or the dialogue will end immediately and trigger the next set and you'll miss some hilarious quips. It's worth listening to everything the first time.Edit: Steam backup doesn't work for this very well, it keeps crashing Steam and then uninstalling itself, the one time it backed up the file was corrupt. I still recommend the game, I'm just going to play it a 4th time through for that last achievement, nbd.HOWEVER...The game is just too good to put down. Simply put, the story is brilliantly crafted and really creative for such a short game, and my Portal loving heart was pleased. The cheat codes given to manipulate the environment were a lot of fun. I love a game that makes me laugh the entire time and this was it. The music, sounds, and voice acting aspects were all expertly done. Unzipper x Cache Cleaner forever!!

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ is a story-centered puzzle-adventure. The plot is one of the highlights of the game. It has some beautiful twists, the game filled with a lot of humour, satire and even has some dramatic moments. Naraven Games were able to deeply develop the characters, even some that doesn't have an effect on gameplay, and environment. So the game is truly captivating and as it's not fully linear, there's a good replayability.Backfirewall_ has some interesting gameplay mechanics that I didn't meet in other games. Puzzles are quite simple, and even if you stuck, you can always use rubber duck helper that can particularly describe what you need to do. The game has a great level design with secrets and easter eggs. So you can just go through levels or explore them completely and have more entertainment.The game has nice graphics. It's a little bit of cartoon style and simplified. By the way, all characters look absolutely gorgeous and unique. And additions of real-life pictures and videos are also help to immerse into the game.The sounds are great too. Backfirewall_ has a little soundtrack in techno style that suits it very well. And also voice acting is top-notch.I didn't have real problems with UI or controls. All elements are on their places. Just maybe in a couple of times I fell from heights due to several restrictions. And thanks to the developer that have added hints in a last level. It helped to move through it without deceleration.Verdict. Backfirewall_ is a very captivating, funny and dramatic puzzle-adventure game with some amazing gameplay mechanics. It's well-made, has great graphics and sound, and is a great way to spend some spare time. Definitely yet one of the best games of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: A young woman has a phone.  The phone needs an update to the OS. But the OS.... doesn't want the update to go through, because... that would destroy  it. You are the update program. And somehow, you end up breaking the update, going against your protocol, and trying to prevent the update from ever happening. The User is not happy, and the other programs are... confused. The game is most reminiscent of Tron 2.0, but it's a 1st st person puzzler. You do some stealthing, some jumping, but mostly, you find things in the thematic levels to interact  with, to move the story along, and also to find bits of messages on the phone, to figure out what the user is up to, which is a whole different aspect of the story. There's several endings depending on your actions towards various programs, and how much exploring you do. Overall, the game's pretty fun, and there's some real creativity with the concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, it's complicated.There should be a tragicomic story, but there is something missing. The story is not very well-written, dialogs are kinda wacky. There are some good story bits, but overall it doesn't play like a tragicomedy.There should be wacky puzzles, but there is something missing. I've played the game for 5 hours during the week, but it felt like I was playing for 15, and not because the puzzles were ridiculously hard. Some of them are just hard to follow due to lacking of basic logic (and a game test pass). Some of them are so easy that they can be solved by just clicking around. There are some good puzzles, but overall it doesn't play as the puzzle game.There is quite a good amount of side quests which shapes the in-game world, and they are mostly fun. You will probably skip most of them, because you have to actively scout for every single point of interest, which is quite tedious.BUT, if you have 6 hours to spare, consider playing this game despite all written above. This game is crafted with passion and love, and it shows. Especially because of the amazing art, good voice acting and 100% certified banger of a soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: I just did my play through of Backfirewall_, and, wow. I was not expecting such an amazing story. The graphics may not be the best, they don't need to be, its a perfect style and I love it! I will not spoil any of the story, but let me tell you this, your actions, do have consequences.Overall 10/10, Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Good premise- Well written funny dialog and very well voice acted.- Good story.- Simple but engaging game-play. Its basically a walking simulator with some light puzzles. You unlock a handful of basic powers as your progress through the game and use them to solve environmental puzzles mostly.- Lots of Collectibles and achievements if that's your thing.Cons- Some choppy fps in a few sections- Sometimes after saving and returning to the game later certain things may not have saved state correctly.- Basic controls are fine although the abilities you unlock get bound to the number keys which was not really to my taste.Overall its a really well presented game, a definite thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I had a fun time with this game and would still recommend it despite my main issue outlined below. It's fun and cute and doesn't take itself too seriously. The main thing I found frustrating and disappointing though is that the "good" ending of the game demands essentially perfection from your play-through. You have to check every box, get every little thing, explore every little nook and cranny. I got pretty close but ultimately fell short on a rescuing a few of the characters.I really wish there was a way to go back and finish up the things I missed. Some kind of chapter/level select or a way to "glitch" the system and "go back in time" before the ending to make sure I was able to save everyone. If that were the case I'd be coming away from this game feeling even better about it.Unfortunately that's not the case, my only option is to completely restart which is a big ask for a game like this. Maybe I'll come back in a year or two and finish this up but I'm not particularly excited to dive right back in. I'd be running through 5+ hours of content that I've already seen and explored pretty extensively just trying to find the last few bits and pieces. At that point a walkthrough is probably the best option but then is that even playing the game?Still, I hope that doesn't dissuade anyone from playing. I really did enjoy my time with Backfirewall. I'm just not a fan of "perfect" endings that require you to play back through the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: An orignal and unique game in the classic "first person narrative puzzle" genreFrom setting/narrative premise to gameplay/puzzle mechanics this title sets itself apart from the others I played: it's a very solid and fun experience overall (even if it doesn't excel in anything), but it really shines for the novelty of the ideas contained in almost every aspect.Entertaining and amusing, doesn't overstay its welcome; definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game interesting because of the trailer and the visual style, so i just bought it. and i wasn't disappointed. I will definitely play it again. (One of the things I liked about this game and the older I get the more important it becomes ... that it doesn't take forever to play through but only a few hours. That is a very positive point)
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: WOWOWOW I LOVED this concept so much!! What a FUN game, but also HEART BREAKING! omg I keep thinking I can never update my phone or get a new one hahaha. I really loved the story, and learning about the user (oh my gosh) and wow, I truly loved this. Conceptually it was very creative and awesome. Loved every second.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: A funny and rewarding puzzle game with lots of little things to find and explore. The puzzles have a good bit of variety to them that keeps the pacing steady and not repetitive. The characters and world are very charming as is the story that pulls you through the game. The emphasis is more towards the story and progressing than it is tricky puzzle solving, so don't expect to get really stumped or be overcoming very difficult puzzles. What the puzzles lack in difficulty they do still feel rewarding with the way they are fun to figure out and solve without slowing things down and adding to the overall experience bringing just enough to see, find, and do for those that don't care for purely narrative/"walking simulator" games without as much interactivity.My main complaint would be the lack of chapter selection combined with the missable content leading to the consistent feeling that I am overlooking something that I may not be able to get back to.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Q - Would I recommend Backfirewall_?A - MaybeUnfortunately for me, the more of the game I played, the less I enjoyed my time with it. As such I recommend this as a “maybe” as I feel it will be very hit or miss, but because it will be “really” worth playing for the right person, I will not give the game a thumbs down.The games strengths are in its visuals, it’s story, it’s voice acting, the package and experience as a whole are lovely and the nerdy nature of traversing the inside of a phone seeing Ints, chars, along with all the techy references will without a doubt put a smile and some people’s faces.There are two stories in this game, the story you play through as an update package for the phones operating system which is presented in a fairly witty and humours way with dialogue from your companion the current OS and meeting apps on the phone such as social media F, I and T to health app and photos app. And then the story presented to you from the collectible chat messages through the games stages by the user of the phone you occupy.The first for me was entertaining to start, but the more I played the less I unfortunately cared about it. It does, or can have a deeper meaning if you wish to experience the story that way about change and the meaning of change or staying still and how that can affect your life. But to me the layers of a story shouldn’t be what make the story good (but can elevate the story to be better), it should be entertaining in itself.I personally found the secondary story told through collected messages to be more entertaining as it was revealed, but these messages can be missed and even though I felt I was leaving no box unturned in my play through, I did miss a number of these and missed out on the end of this story having not collected the last messages.As you can see most of my review is on the story, that’s because this is what I feel this game will be about and be the appeal for those who will enjoy it.The gameplay itself is simple and the puzzles are not to challenging, they are simply a means to an end to get you to progress through this 7-8 hour experience.And that gameplay starts to feel repetitive mostly as you get further, though does thankfully near the end throw a few more interesting ideas at you for the final stretch.So in summary, if you liked games like portal, fire watch and similar titles in walking sim and “puzzle” adventure genres you could like backfirewall_ though your experience won’t be as good as those titles.Get on sale if that sounds like it appeals to you.——I played this game via a steam deck to completion of the main story, but not replaying for completion of its secondary story.The game had performance issues after the first zones which did impact enjoyment somewhat but not to the extent the game could not be finished. (I don’t feel this was a steam deck issue and more a game optimisation issue but cannot be sure.)
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ isn't a terribly difficult puzzle game, but its unique setting, cool visuals and well told and acted story more than make up for aa lack of challenge.The premise is that you're a software update for a cell phone, whose current OS is fighting to not get overwritten. You have to interact with a number of different apps and services, all of which have their own unique, voiced characters. It sounds goofy, but ends up put together really well and it's funny and even a bit heartwarming in places. You'll go to various different parts of the phone, all of which are fully realized and present different challenges and missions to do for characters.I didn't get stuck in the game at any point, and I'm both not good at puzzle games and get impatient with them quickly. That should give you an indication of the level of difficulty here. This game's far more about experiencing the world, characters and story than it is about challenging puzzles. Personally, I don't mind that in this case and really enjoyed myself, but if you are someone who thrives on challenge and the mental stimulation offered from puzzle games, you won't find that here.The experience is linear and has no real replay value so it's a one and done affair. It took me about four and a half hours from fromt to back, but I think at the price being asked, you will get good value out of this. It's a cool and different experience that I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: The game is terribly lovely and so are the characters! I could hardly stop myself from interacting with every NPC I would encounter! The graphics are not AAA level, of course, but damn are they good!The only pebble in my shoe, and the reason why I give it an 9/10, is that there is no easy replayability to get the achievements you're missing... Its not that big of a deal for most, but I can see completionists getting outraged by that.All in all, an amazing game, story, and experience! I really wish for a continuation in the -----ERROR-----. ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: You will get attached to the characters in this game and it will get you to laugh and cry, even if you haven't cried in many months. Very glad I had therapy scheduled today!12/10 I'm gonna go through it all again. Devs if you see this review; how does it feel to inflict pain? How does it feel knowing people love your characters? This game is a masterpiece!
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the hidden gems that you find and you are amazed how good quality it is.Think of the game as Portal 2 and Stanley Parable had a baby together and from it this masterpiece came out.The game has amazing narration and every character in the game has their own unique personality.The story is really good and it can be actually emotional. It is surprising how a game can give you such emotions and Backfirewall_ absolutely does give them really well.As last thing I want to mention is that the game has so many references packed into it that you will have an absolute blast if you know a bit about internet, gaming or tech history.Of course the game has of course issues as well. A lot of players got softlocked because they left on the wrong moment. I even got softlocked once because I left the game in the wrong place on a wrong time.Another issue is for completionists, because you can't go back to previous levels you must to collect everything in the level first try. The game also doesn't tell you how many hidden things you can collect making it quite hard to 100% it.Luckily because the game is short you can play the game multiple times to complete it all. You can also ask the community or the Devs itself on their Discord server for some help as well making it actually not as a big hassle.The developers mentioned that they are working hard to fix the softlocks as well that's why the issues I mentioned above should be fixed soon.Overall I can say is that if you enjoy narrative games with puzzles and you love when developers put small references in the entire game then Backfirewall_ is absolutely for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The narrator is lovely, hilarious, and emotional. There's a rich cast of characters, a compelling story, and really fun gameplay. The graphics are beautiful and there's tons of replay potential though I've only played it through once as of writing this, I plan on replaying soon. Amazing game and a short play. 10/10. Did make me cry twice though so take that as you will
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: This game has way more to offer than you think.Backfirewall_ is a very basic game with a simple premise: Trigger some elements in the map, move forward, go to the next puzzle.The first 30 minutes of gameplay can feel repetitive, but if you push through the repetition and advance the plot, you end up with one of the most refreshing stories I've come across in years.It's not necessarily a game for everyone, but if you enjoy games like Portal and don't mind exploring maps and going off course, you will definitely not regret spending your money on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Sincerely, I liked this game even if i finished it in around 3 hours. _childDocuments_.review: A genuinely witty and charming puzzle game that I enjoyed playing from start to end.The puzzle were, even if on the easier side, creative enough that they were never boring or tedious.There was so much personality baked into the world and characters that I found myself far more attached than I had expected to be by the end.For a humorous, casual puzzle game this ticks all the right boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: What I liked:- Quirky humor- Feels a bit like Supraland, Psychonauts, There Is No Game, Life is Strange,  and The Stanley ParableWhat I didn't like:- There is a game breaking bug which initially prompted me to leave a negative review. In the WiFi location, if you quit the game after visiting Frank, autosave is screwed and the game won't let you progress.- Apparently, there is another autosave bug which prevents you from giving Hector to PID101 if you quit the game after picking Hector up?- Story is too sad and melancholic :(- I wish there was chapter selection or at least save/load with multiple savesOverall, I liked the game
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: at first blush, Backfirewall_ seems a lot like The Stanley Parable. and there are definitely parallels to be made, sure. the narration, humor, and attitude definitely have that TSP pizzazz to 'em. but Backfirewall_ is a lot more of a first-person puzzler, with plenty for secret hunters to unearth. the puzzles are never really all too threatening, allowing you to pace yourself comfortably, and they're quite inventive and satisfying. the game has a built-in, optional hints system so you don't really need to consult a walkthrough if you get stumped or confused. the voice acting and low-poly visuals are marvelous, and the writing hits the mark (although I am not sure yet if I would hold it up to TSP).minor quibble would be that jumping honestly feels really bumbling and bad. this is not a platformer, but it has some occasional moments where you do need to platform, and they stink.for more thoughtful recommendations of the best games on Steam, check out my curator, .
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Fresh from a first run, a couple of initial thoughts.Having spoken to the devs at Gamescom, I was looking forward to this one and it did not disappoint.There are obvious influences from Portal and The Stanley Parable, even going as far as making a cake joke and dabbling in multiple story cut-off points. But what about the core gameplay loop? It's not a puzzle game at it's core, but neither is it a complete story subversion. It's smack dab in the middle and the game knows it. Sure some of the jokes are dependent on memes and tropes, but there are a lot of sensible chuckles to be had with some social commentary. Other than a laugh, the game did even evoke a spark well timed melancholy.Aside from some audio jabber after more than three hours of playtime (which may be my laptop's fault), I only have one small point on which I'm having double feelings about:...We're getting into spoiler territory now for this point of feedback, so alt+f4 now if you want to be surprised.Don't say I didn't give fair warning.Here goes.After Cloud 42, before the actual end credits, there is a lovely sequence of polaroids of the characters, some of whom are missing. A simple yet effective way of tugging on the heart strings to say "Hey, maybe you should replay this thing, you didn't save them all."Alright. Cool. Mind is already working on 'what did I miss'. Very effective. Well done, devs.Don't undo that moment by then showing each of the branches and the particular path we picked for each character. At least let me have a sulky minute or two before you open up your secrets.But then again... Knowing who I saved and what other possible outcomes I can still explore does make for a nice challenge for a second run, albeit a tad spoiled.Again again, there is the matter of the rubber ducks for those that don't like spoilers and who knows... Maybe the devs are a step ahead of me and you can play a complete guided route to save everyone on NG+5 or something like that. And thinking about it a little longer, the first time seeing the artworks and noticing some are missing and piecing it together that you didn't save them all... Well that loses its impact for each subsequent time it comes around, I'd imagine.Overall: Great game, happy they didn't put out a longer demo and released when they were ready.Going by the formula of "Does this game's purchase cost bring me joy at the rate of 1 hour per euro spent?" If I do another run where I try to save everyone after the first, yes.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the beta and was waiting for this to release. They did a great job of polishing it up since then, and it has a real Stanley Parable feel to it now. By the end I was emotionally invested in these stupid little characters and their problems, and I mean that in the most endearing way. I have got to replay it at least once more to get the best possible ending, at least I have got to get Hector back to his owner for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAME!!This game does a great job at having you build all sorts of attachments/connections to the characters. The puzzles are unique and not too challenging! From the start it creates an atmosphere that is surely to get you hooked right away! Story is new and refreshing. If you are a fan of portal and stanley pleaseee give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ has certainly been a game that has surprised me! It’s similar to A Stanley Parable, Portal, and other such games, but even with it’s similarities, it stands on it’s own entirely (apart from a few references to said games). There’s no true right or wrong answers, tons of little easter eggs and characters to learn about, and the story really makes you think “Am I really doing the right thing?” So many times, but the answer may never be found. For an indie game by a small team, it is a true work of art. And the price is also worth it! Honestly, it’s quite a low price for a game like this. Gameplay wise, it’ll be about 10 hours to play through once, and 20 or more to collect everything and all the achievements. The game’s difficulty feels like a really good blend. It’s not too easy where you know what to do immediately, but it’s not so hard that you need to look outside the game for answers (let’s just say, the game helps you out if you wish). I liked this because it made it feel far more fulfilling to be able to stay in the game and never have to look for answers outside of it, unlike a couple levels in Portal 2, where I just felt dumb because I had to look up solutions. The tools the game gives you seems like it would be so OP, and even though the tools aren’t, it doesn’t mean they feel repetitive. Using the tools (or cheat codes, as the game calls it) feels fun every time. They’re not overused or underused. I also enjoy how the characters all have their own issues and personalities. There’s variety in it and quite a few characters have a disability of some sort that makes them even more unique. It’s played as a bit of a joke but it isn’t offensive at all. As someone with most of the disabilities mentioned in the game, I found no problem with them at all and I liked the way the jokes flew by, as I make many of the same jokes myself!The puns are, well, they definitely didn’t have me laughing for hours, but they did make me smile or groan, and I appreciate the effort greatly. Oh, and the OST is pretty sweet! All in all, if you want a quick game that gives some replayability, Backfirewall_ is certainly a game that anyone can play (except those with photosensitivity. The game gave me a migraine or headache when it would take over the camera, but it only happened 3 times and it was very short. No major flashes as far as I know, though! The camera movement was smooth but fast, like Subnautica for reference).
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: I played all of 5-10 minutes of the demo and just from the opening sequence I was like yep I'm buying this. It's hilarious, has fun puzzles and hidden areas, dialogues, and secrets to find. I haven't gotten too far in it yet but can't wait to finish it and already am planning to replay for a completionist playthrough.It checks all the boxes for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: This was such an amazing game. In my mind, this was Stanley Parable's bigger (and better) brother. I loved Stanley Parable, and this one blew me out of the water. Beautiful game, fantastic humor, and such great attention to detail for this type of game (). I've never felt more involved in a game, and the story was great. I felt so immersed the entire time. I'm actually really sad that it's over. Now I have to go find another similar game :(
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say: I'm digging it! The Update Assistant/OS9 dynamic is SO reminiscent of the Chell/Wheatley dynamic early on in Portal 2, including the silent protagonist. There is also a very subtle The Cake is A Lie reference in the GPU Art Gallery.The world of this game looked a bit corporate and simplistic at first, but the gameplay, world building, such as characters and lore, sure made up for it. Puzzles really reminded me of Portal to some extent despite the games having very little in common in terms of gameplay mechanics.Game was good and I liked that the tech terms weren't too overwhelming or overdone as I first expected when seeing this game in an ad on Instagram long ago. TL;DR: This game was very fun and well made, being the first puzzler game I've found reminiscent of Portal's gameplay, Definitely recommend it to anyone who's played Portal, even in full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review: Backfirewall_ is a reeeeeally interesting way to aproach puzzles, storytelling and philosophical questions. Since this game hides quite a lot behind it's first impresions I'll separate the review in "aspects of the game" (audio, etc).The story is good AF, it ends when it has to do it and in a sort of unexpected way so you'll be at a 100% during the entire playthrough (awesome ^^). Despite being an "straight forward" story since there's mostly no backtracking (maybe you can do some a few times but in the same sections of the game) there's a lot of ways of altering little parts of the outcome of the story or it's end itself. So yes, there's some replay value here and it doesn't feel like it's just there to make the game longer since the game make every conversation fun and interesting and being able to know every character and more about the world felt really nice. You could finish the game in around 3h, but if you want you can squeeze more of it as I've said.Not much to say here, looks really nice and the art direction it's what makes it outstand. I'll say that between settings there wasn't a huge difference, but the performance of the game felt a little bit of a letdown since I expected better optimisation.Noice, voices are awesome, effects on point, and I think that they made a really interesting implementation with the audio design and gameplay mechanics/world building as the audio remians pretty dynamic during all the playthrough.10/10 no complaints, no spoilers, all I want to tell you is that every playable aspect here is perfect. I really loved how the game evolved and how the gameplay mechanics where always a really good way for the player to interact with the level design instead of just a way to get from point A to point B.Thanks, at this price point is hard to see games putting some effort in this aspect at all, but in this game there's a good implementation of the accesibility options and the ones included manage to be there for the player without disturbing the experience at all :).A joke, I would have paid easily double the price for the game. It's just a bargain get it and try to get the 100% of achivements you'll love it.Here you have some footage of the game: I'm also making a guide for the puzzles in case you need some help ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Backfirewall_

_childDocuments_.review:
Hello and welcome to Backfirewall_, a first-person tragicomic adventure set inside a smartphone.

You are the update assistant. Solve wacky puzzles to counter the update and save the previous operating system from deletion. The fate of the System is in your hands!

name: River City Girls 2
detailed_description: The River City Girls are ready for round 2! When an old foe returns for revenge, Misako, Kyoko, Kunio, and Riki - joined by newcomers Marian and Provie - hit the streets for an all-new beat-'em-up adventure packed with new abilities, enemies, allies, locations, and more! Team up for local or online co-op, then pound punks into the dirt with brand-new guard-crush attacks, lift-off combos, elemental status effects, and other knuckle-busting techniques! Level-up to earn new moves, buy items and accessories in more than 40 shops, and recruit defeated foes and hired heavies to help you on your way! River City is bigger than ever, offering more areas to explore, more objects to destroy, and a day-night cycle! With nonlinear gameplay, character-specific VO, and another epic soundtrack by Megan McDuffee, River City Girls 2 will keep you brawling until all your enemies yell 'BARF!' Key Features: • Six playable characters, each with their own fighting styles and upgradable move sets! • Enhanced combat: guard crushes, lift-off combos, elemental attacks, and more! • River City is bigger than ever! New locations with multiple routes and secret areas! • Play solo or team up with a friend, locally or online • New 'hired heavies' aid you in battle! Have two recruits at once! • Loads of NPCs to meet, interact with, and punch in the face - including surprise cameos! • Awesome anime intro, comic book cutscenes, English and Japanese voiceovers, and a spectacular soundtrack featuring RCG1 composer Megan McDuffee!

short_description: The River City Girls are back! Misako, Kyoko, Kunio, and Riki - joined by newcomers Marian and Provie - hit the streets for an all-new beat-'em-up adventure! Team up for local or online co-op and explore a massive world packed with new abilities, enemies, locations, and more!

_childDocuments_.review: This used to be the most helpful rated review but it was negative. At the time, I honestly wouldn't have recommended this game to people and that was fair. Maybe I could have changed the content and left it negative and it would have stayed at the top of the list, but that didn't really feel fair to the game given the changes that it's made. I haven't played the game since the changes though, due to my brother being my co-op partner and him simultaneously having no interest in playing the game again and telling me he'll hold a grudge if I beat it without him so consider this a placeholder for now. I initially wrote that it was a great game, that I liked the characters, I love the style, the writing, the soundtrack, the variety of their move lists, there's a lot of cute environmental stuff and I appreciate how the move lists have opened up from the first game with more stuff being able to chain into combos. It even has cross play available between PC and consoles and a cameo from good old Matt McMuscles. But a friend asked me if he should get the game and I could not honestly and wholeheartedly tell him "yes.". I had to tell him "It's got some problems at the moment.". And they were some serious problems so at that time I told him and anybody else that I could, as a friend, to wait on this game. Those problems seem to be a thing of the past now however and as I've even been trying to get that same friend to pick the game up recently with the addition of four player online co-op it seems only fair that I can tell you now that the time of waiting is over. If you happen to see this game on sale (because 39.99 is still a lot to ask, imo) or you have deep enough pockets I'd tell you to pick it up without hesitation. Just... not on switch as that's still locked to 30 fps.As a final note, I would say to the devs, you bungled this game's launch badly. Not only did the game launch in a state you should honestly be ashamed of but then you paired months of silence with months of "soon"s and offered garbage excuses like "None of use could tell the difference between 30 and 60 FPS" to anybody waiting for those desperately needed fixes. I still hope you get a chance to make a River City Girls 3 though and I hope you give THAT game the development and QA time it actually needs.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE UPDATE: Since writing the first update, there has been a NEW beta patch released that reverts a lot of what I talked about in the first update. The game feels mostly like it used to be. However, unlike the first beta patch, they haven't done anything to prevent beta players from playing online or even crossplay. They're just going wild west with things at this point, so I guess expect lots of weirdness if you're playing someone with a different version of the game than you. -shrug-UPDATE: Since writing this review, there has been a performance patch released that fixes the 30 FPS issues mentioned in this review. However, the patch also did a lot of changes to the gameplay, physics and flow, making the game feel very off to many players, myself included. With the exception of 60 FPS online, which you probably aren't going to find games in the lobbies to join anyway, I'd say the game is probably worse now than it was when I originally wrote this.Getting the obvious question out of the way, the vast majority of my play time has been making mods for the game. I've only played the story around 2.5 times and have yet to 100% a save file.If you liked the first RCG, this sequel expands on the game world, side quest, better accessories, playable characters and improved combat. On the other hand, this comes at the sacrifice of being more directionless, less polished, more buggy and mostly less funny. There are moments where everything clicks and comes together but it's too often a slog to get to those moments.There are many instances where the execution doesn't match the ambition. An example is the way the middle story missions can be tackled in different orders. It's a nice idea but it's fairly clear that there was a default order in mind and what areas got worked on first. If you don't follow that order, you risks losing out on dialog and context. If you do follow the order, it becomes obvious that the backend is full of filler locked-screen fights and forced fetch quests that involve repeated globe trotting back and forth between the same screens.The dialog system is weird and it seems like it really handcuffed the writing. You can play as multiple characters but for the most part, there are two talkers, speaker and responder. Speaker lines are almost always something Misako might say and responder lines are almost always something Kyoko might say. Speaker and responder talk to each other quite generically, in a way that prevents their words from needing context to who they are talking to. At its best, the dialog falls flat and provides no insight to the characters speaking it. At its worst, characters speak nonsense that doesn't fit them or their context at all. An adult woman worrying about being late for high school class, for example.This might seem like a costs cutting measure but I'm not sure. In order to make this system work, the majority of the characters had to record both speaker and responder lines to avoid conflicts between combinations of characters. It's hard to imagine this was the most efficient use of resources. Considering the manga cutscenes are always told from the perspective of Misako and Kyoko, I'm not sure doing things this way made any sense.There are other areas of the game where it just feels like different parts of the development were not communicating with each other. Story dialog that makes references to side quest that you may not have done. A sprite of a character crying in peril, only for the joke of their rescue dialog to be that they were oblivious to being in mortal danger because they were too busy being an airhead. One character's entire introductory manga sets up a story that is instantly resolved the second she joins your crew and no story dialog follows up on it afterwards. There are multiple collectibles in the game but you can't start collecting most of them until you start the quest, which may be several hours into the game, depending on your route. It might seem like little stuff but there's a whole lot of it and it adds up.The game was released with a 30 FPS cap but not even in the way you'd expect it. Elements related to the gameplay are locked at 30 while the rest of the game runs at 60. This includes menus, transitions and particle effects. This means you're seeing things run at both 30 and 60 at the same time, which is even worse than just seeing things at 30.There is a "beta" branch that band-aids this problem but only this problem and only for offline play. A proper patch has been "almost ready for certification" for two months as of this writing and has yet to be submitted for approval by the console manufacturers. Because the game supports cross-play across all platforms, everyone has to get the patch at the same time.Little information is available about this patch and communication from Wayforward is very sparse and what little we get involves a generous amount gaslighting, hand-waving and absurdist claims. As mentioned, I have spent time modding the game which required getting familiar with its code. While I'm not an expert on the engines of the game, I can say confidently that the manner in which this cap has been presented as nothing more than "error in the code" that went unnoticed for the entirety of the game's development is nonsensical. The evidence within the code is that this cap was put in intentionally. Why? Can't say for sure. Was the plan always to go back and change it? I think it's probable. It sure feels like a stopgap solution to get a game out before Christmas. I would love to hear a believable explanation that contradicts this evidence but I am not holding my breath.There's a good game buried beneath all of this and if you liked the first game, it's hard to imagine you'd outright hate this one, if not like it more depending on your tolerance of certain flaws. If you do get it, I wouldn't pay the $40 asking price again and certainly not the much higher regional prices I've heard about. 50% sale, at least and if you do grab it, go check out some mods! :p

_childDocuments_.review: I gave River City Girls 2 (RCG2) a brief try before I was provided with a review copy for the first game. Having finished a playthrough of the original and better understanding how it was meant to be played, I believe I'm well-prepared to do a solo run of its sequel, although it has the benefit of online coop. Either way, I'm curious to see what changes were made.  Shocking nobody, much of how RCG2 works is similar to the first game. Beating enemies earns experience and money, you'll rarely have the screen lock preventing you from moving on until each foe is defeated, and there's shops and side quests available. However, many small changes have been made, which add up to a gaming experience that feels significantly better. Having played both games on normal difficulty, peons take significantly less damage to be defeated, when they were gluttons for punishment previously. They get stunned less often, but it's not an issue due to better balancing. Additionally, although many moves are the same, you can string them together with more flexibility. For instance, starting with an aerial attack, transitioning into a regular combo, and throwing in special moves to finish. It leads to combat that feels a lot more satisfying and snappy, with Marian having some of my most favored moves.  Using the same controller across both games, I still find it works well with the d-pad. If you don't string your moves together right, enemies can block in the middle of a combo, although I'd abuse the timing to repeatedly punch the last enemy around and force them to fight for me. After getting used to the pacing RCG2 is going for though, I think most would agree that the beat-'em-up controls here are tight and responsive.  This game opens up as a very direct sequel to the first, making numerous references and connections to prior events. It definitely would make someone who hadn't played the first game curious about what had taken place prior. Ironically, after tying the plots together so well, it skips ahead two months as an excuse for the characters to forget all of their moves and soften up. Curse youth, lax parents, and couch surfing! Looking at the two games side by side, I was slightly surprised that they're nearly identical. Perhaps due to bias from the gameplay or purely from it being the sequel, I had thought there had been some tweaks to improve RCG2's visuals over the first game. However, the comic book panels, enemy designs, backgrounds, shop pictures, and character portraits all appear unchanged, notwithstanding any new content of course. I don't believe there's anything wrong with maintaining fidelity from one game to the next, as drastic changes in style can harm branding, but I would have liked to see some degree of improvement.  With all the songs available from the first game, and being based around the same city, I decided to compare the two soundtracks to see how many songs they kept or changed out. Looking at each by name, I didn't see any repeats, though a couple could have been remixed for all I know. Each section of River City has a boss, and all of them have their own Noize track, with related lyrics. At first, I was really confused, because I couldn't understand the relationship between the pop musician Noize and using magic to keep people off her lawn, leading to lore that's a bit at conflict with itself. Although an interesting way to develop an area, many of these songs seemed to be on loop far more than necessary, and seemed to go against what I thought was one of the strengths from the prior title.  🌟 Side quests don't only take place in the form of fetch quests or going somewhere to defeat specific enemies. Quite a few involve a short mini-game, providing a little bit of diversity in the gameplay.  🌟 If you play local coop, up to four people can play at once. Online coop allows two people to play together. 🌟 It's largely unnecessary, but many background objects can be destroyed. Just a bit of silly fun.  ❌ Boss battles had odd pacing or balancing in comparison to one another. Ken and Marian took a good amount of time to beat, but Primo and Provie's fight took little time at all. Even the last boss fight was over pretty quickly. ❌ Although you'll meet new NPCs pretty early, and the enemy variety is greater even near the beginning, there aren't a lot of new foes to face. ❌ The few places where you have to deal with cars can be annoying, as their timing might catch you off guard. 🔍 There's a shop in Crosstown that sells a smart watch accessory for $1,000. It lowers the prices for all other stores, so it'll pay for itself given enough time, but only if you get it early and remember to equip it. Also, check your accessories at the start of any game session or if you switch characters.🔍 Since enemies you recruit still drop money and give experience, there's no reason not to do so when given the chance. 🔍 Due to the hideout system, you can store quite a few healing items for later.  I came into RCG2 expecting the sequel to be rather similar to the previous game. To be fair, it's not exactly a night and day difference, with enemies, locations, and character portraits being recycled. However, several quality of life improvements were made, which creates a more enjoyable experience. Some changes seem kind of obvious, such as letting you know what an item does before you buy it, and the bus travel system has a much better map so you can more easily tell where you're going. These may only make minor differences, but it represents the extra polish this title received in contrast to the predecessor. Even though it'd be impractical to upgrade the first game with all the features of the sequel, a patch to rebalance enemies so its closer to RCG2 would be great. I would be more likely to play more of the game if it felt this smooth. Although you'd lose out on some context, due to being a much superior game, I'd suggest buying RCG2 instead of the original for a better beat-'em-up playthrough. It'd easily be worth the higher price.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, the game IS a bunch of fun, and the combo potential and fluidity that you can do compared to the first game is a big step up. But there are a few glaring issues that I personally cannot overlook, and WayForward has shown little to no transparency as of this review and instead have adopted the public stance of, "We have your money, we don't have to fix anything. Deal with it"After the first game, River City Girls 2 was "promised" to have actual online functionality, without being forced to play local or through Steam Remote Play, which is always a very laggy experience. But since quite literally the day of release, the game has run like complete trash online with friends. The FPS is both very poor, and sometimes spikes to a crawl, and in a BeatemUp game, having huge input delay becomes both deadly, and a huge buzzkill for your fun.While you can "sortof" deal with it, it feels painful after awhile to even simply move around. They announced there was a framerate fix incoming, but it has been almost 2 months now with no updates anywhere, unless you specifically join their discord and dig around for it, which isn't acceptable when you're selling a game on multiple storefronts.Other issues in the game include the usual bugs and glitches, like being animation-locked in a jumping pose, so you lose the ability to literally fight unless you restart the game. Or how the game was designed to have not only a huge amount of tedious Collectible Side Quests, involving mundane things like, "break every single destructible object in an area to get a Purple Card drop" to far more unforgiveable ones where there are completely hidden doors with no icons or visual cues, while also being COMPLETELY off the map or in areas no one would normally even think you could access, such as specifically walljumping on a high ledge to bounce onto a powerline cable, and walking over to a background door. Another example being, jump on multiple rock platforms completely behind a waterfall, completely blind to not only where any of these jumps or ledges are, but theres also a hidden door at the very top left, again with no icon or prompts that theres something.WayForward has been like this with the Shantae games too, where its very poorly taken care of and seemingly given no love, but im not changing this review until they deliver a fully finished game with all the promised and announced features in actual working condition. Players should never feel like they were scammed out of something as purchase-defining as Online Co-Op to play with friends.*********************************************************Update as of 5/1/2023:It has now been over 5 months since the game released, and despite what that dev response was, theres still no updates or fixes or anything for the online functionality that again was promised. If a major selling point of one of your games has been broken for nearing "half a year" then you shouldn't release it.  The beta patch is entirely only for solo offline play, which is for most people, the only way to play it in the first place. Otherwise a lot more people would've just demanded refunds than there were.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a mixed bag, but been having fun overall.Pros:1. The game is pretty fun. Combat is enjoyable.2. The writing is irreverant and silly. This lands significantly more often than it misses, though you do miss some stuff you didn't play the first game (and more if you don't know anything about Double Dragon).3. The soundtrack is pretty good for this kind of game.4. Coop works pretty well once you get connected and understand that save progress is basically host only.Cons:1. We've had a lot of time getting coop to connect, with immediate "host disconnected" errors being a thing. Sometimes it takes us 10 minutes to actually get going.2. Only the host's save file progresses. That locks the other player out of some rewards and such as you have to then do them with you as the host (or single player) to get them. Your levels and money and such do progress, but it's a nuisance that doesn't have to exist.3.
