_childDocuments_.review: River City Girls continues to be a franchise which aggressively refuses to let me love it. I have never seen an art asset and music team let down by everyone else on a project so hard since... well, the first installment.This series seems tailor made for me. I have been fans of WayForward and Arc System Works since the original Shantae and GGX2 respectively. I love good spritework, and Double Dragon: Neon may very well be my most fondly remembered beat 'em up ever. I have a friend who adores the world and artstyle, and is always eager to co-op through this. The revamp of Marian couldn't have been more up my alley if they sent me design docs through the mail for personal review and approval.Yet, somehow, they managed to ♥♥♥♥ it all up. Again.Someone needs to sit the devs of this series down and let them know they haven't made an engine for platforming. It's astounding how such a glaring weakness is not only ignored but shoved into the player's face throughout the entire game. Those in the back with the scars, remember the DDR boss from the first River City Girls? The one that required precision jumps to not get murdered by descending "Notes" on a Guitar Hero track, but didn't take into account the travel time to make said jumps; Meaning that even if you were perfect there simply wasn't a long enough window to jump from safe area to safe area and being mowed down wasn't an "If" but a "When"? Hope you enjoy every boss doing that. Apparently this team thinks you want to precision platform in their engine SO MUCH that bosses will stop everything to put you through long and elaborate platform challenges before you can get back to the fight proper. Some are merciful and will only hurt you a little bit for failing these challenges. Others, like Marian, will cause cascades of fails leading into more fails because of a lack of mercy invulnerability so that a single mistake in them will bring you from full health to dead.Marian stops the fight to do this four times, by the way. Each time about a minute long. Because ♥♥♥♥ you.While we're talking about the bosses? Let me summarize how boss fights go if you put aside the platforming.Imagine two traffic lights, cycling at typical traffic light speeds. If both lights are green, you can hit the boss. If both lights are red, the stage hazards line up in such a way that you will get hit no matter what you do. In any other situation, hitting the boss will get you damaged by something else going on as well.Gradually, throughout the fight, add more traffic lights. By the last fourth of the healthbar you should have roughly seven traffic lights. Seven traffic lights you are waiting to line up to green at all the same time. Seven traffic lights wearing you down with unavoidable reds the whole while. Riveting.But hey, boss fights are but a portion of a game's appeal. How about that story, eh? WayForward is great at silly, character driven dialogue. In-between the trash fires of bosses, at least you can enjoy the antics of characters such as Marian and Provie, right?Get a load of this. I still have trouble believing it myself.Kiyoko and Misako are the only characters with lines. In the dumbest way possible. You see, every other character takes on the ROLE of Kyoko or Misako if used, saying exactly what Kyoko or Misako would say word for word. Even if it makes no sense, like Marian talking about herself in the third person to the guy who kidnapped her in Neon.Not *too* bad a concession, right? It's a decent saving on resources, especially with the cutting down on voicework.But it isn't. The voices are still there. Every character besides Misako and Kyoko have fully voiced lines for everything Kyoko says in the game AND everything Misako says in the game. The voiceactors for every secondary character has put in the work of both main characters COMBINED so they can be slotted into either "Role" on the fly. Shoddily, since there are no script tweaks despite the unnecessary resources spent. Easily the most lazy AND the most wasteful thing I have seen in ages.The worst part? Normal gameplay is alright. Fun with a friend, even. Granted, dying of colon cancer can be fun with a friend, but the point I'm getting at here is that there was potential. But it's buried under so many actively infuriating decisions that you could reasonably assume them to be deliberate acts of spite.I don't know what I did, River City Girls. I'm sorry. Please, *please* stop hurting yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: "Everyone knows that sequels are always better!" - Kyoko 15min into the game. I've been stoked waiting for this game for ages, so it stinks that it's launch has been a bit rough around the edges. 10min after launch was painful, the game ran at maybe 30fps + stutters (i9 10850k, 16gb RAM, 3070Ti, SSD). Switch release feels like 20fps max but that's another can of worms. The beta *significantly* improves performance, to the point where I wish that was the version that released first.River City Girls 2 is excellent so far. Story starts immediately after the events in that first game. Combat is familiar but butter smooth. New movement options and less ending lag across moves make combos more fluid and fun. Enemy and weapon types are more varied, certain moves and weapons can attack grounded enemies, you can actually get 3x curb stomps in at a time, and controls feel tighter overall. Things that make a brawler a good brawler are here and improved extensively over the first game. Well done WayForward.Missions kinda fly at you as you discover them, which is fine but can lead to a few disjointed story beats or commentary. Nothing breaking or impossible to follow however. The world interacts more with the player and your enemies: breakable objects and structures, more surfaces to pound bodies against. It all adds up to being a more satisfying experience and a fun romp. Areas from the previous title are revisited, but have marks left by your characters from before, which is great to see. Artwork is great as always, even the reused shops have a little extra flair based on your character choice. After hearing the new soundtrack before playing, I'm glad that it is intertwined with music from the first game. They work well together.If you liked the first game (River City Girls), this is an improvement across all fronts. Just make sure to sign up for the beta (as of writing). Happy Dragon Foot - Curb Stomp - German Suplexing your fellow neighbors!

_childDocuments_.review: Recommendable just barely because WOW what a mixed bag this game was on release. I hope a lot of these issues are patched out later or improved on in a 3rd game.The game still oozes style which is it's strongest area, however the spritework could do with a resolution upgrade on the characters if we ever get a 3rd game. The music mostly hits the mark of what they're aiming for with some of the sound design being so layered I was starting to get some GTA world building vibes. So it's a shame that sometimes you'll be stuck with the same song for ages and then the other extreme by the end of the game when you'll be moving so fast you'll rarely hear past the first minute of a piece of music. An unlockable radio you could bring with you might solve this?There's countless references to the River City Ransom games, Double Dragon, wayforward, and even some other cameos from other games and even internet personalities. My only complaint about the storytelling is all the key/famous male characters except the playable ones seem to be betrayed as sometimes Homer levels of incompetent on some level. Game 3 should have some sort of side story where the Double Dragon cast try to resolve some unsolved issues but that's just imo.The size of the game is more than doubled over the original, but a lot of the fetch quests which pad that out are an exercise in patience. This is especially bad with online play with the strangely long load screens between each map change (and you will be doing that A LOT) as if the game is fixing the connection every time. It's a great achievement this game even has cross play, but it's made less impressive by the load times and probably the biggest black mark it has of all.I'll be blunt and just go ahead and say it, despite this being advertised as a 4 player game, unless you play locally and have to share one visually crowded screen, ONLY player 1's (the host player) progress is saved! You can level up characters and buy moves and items, but ALL other game progress is only memorised on whoever the host player is, NOT EVEN character unlocks, item rewards on quests HELL even some story required minigames are single player only. This just seems like a baffling choice designed to make the game last longer for a generation of gamers who don't touch games anymore once they've unlocked everything. On the plus side? some content shifts depending on the characters being used, the banter between characters changes and even the pictures on the selfie quest. A lot of games would take the easy way out and not change this so the extra detail is appreciated.Speaking of Selfies, using a characters phone for the map, game progress and the majority of the menus ingame and features was a genius idea! I just wish I didn't feel I was putting my life in danger any time I checked it in online play. The enemies will show you zero mercy, creating frustrating LET ME JUST CHECK SOMETHING! Moments where you end up trying to find places to hide.Last we have the combat which I feel has gone a bit sideways. Why did wayforward ever think a 30fps fighting game was acceptable? Thankfully this is being patched but still. Being an rpg beatemup that means you can just muscle your way through most fights by having higher stats than whoever you're fighting, basically extrinsic progress over intrinsic as a player. The River City games have always been like this, but it has the bad effect of making the game hard at first and then a cakewalk later. I'm still underwhelmed by the characters combo potential so far (partly because by the end you can ko most things in a few hits), but I might just need to experiment more with it in the new dummy training room which is a great new feature. The ability to bring enemies you beat as a tag fighting style game assist character has been improved, with you now able to bring more than one and keep the ones you find. If only it was a bit easier to catch them in the first place since you have to weaken them pokemon style and pray no other enemies or players get in the way and you end up finishing them off.The bosses were pretty weak too, with an over-reliance on super armour, iframes and  "wait for their attacks to finish before you're allowed to do anything" If you remember the Noize boss fight from the first game it's basically that problem (though just to clarify Noize is NOT a bad character I just think the boss fight needed more work).Confusing review? _childDocuments_.review: I am a  main in the prior game and I can say this sequel is a definite improvement with the combat and move progression. I am not sure which variables were changed but I was able to juggle the enemy longer and more consistently which just feels so good. However, I feel the game still suffers from its previous issues such as the story, dialogue, backtracking and bosses that I still feel disappointed after finishing it despite its improvements. While I do recommend this game as a beginner couch/coop brawler, I suggest looking into other entries such as  for a better straightforward experience and gameplay. To reiterate, the game has many surface improvements but one (or two) is worth mentioning. One prior issue is the economy of money used in unlocking moves or buying healing items where death was too severe to encourage experimentation and healing too weak and expensive to make grinding profitable. Thankfully, losing money on death is less severe and healing items restore more making grinding viable and acquiring new moves beside boss rewards. At the very least, this makes exploring the town and engaging in random fights a pleasant experience.As much as I appreciate the improvements, it does not address the core issues of the game.Even if the dialogue and meta humor is not for me, I feel it does not elevate the game or is at best serviceable and at worst annoying. I was not personally invested or motivated in any of the characters (even my main) and the story for both games where I simply powered through it. Although the sidequests have improved and some minigames to add variety, I have no interest in replaying the game (aside for research) despite the new characters and improved combat because the whole experience feels underwhelming.Another issue is the mandatory backtracking which feels tedious and tiring alongside the longer load times. The level formula seems to be exploring an area first, then encountering a road block that requires going to several points, then going all the way back to the block and finally fighting the boss. It still feels like padding without any changes or challenges. Perhaps roaming NPCs or a persistent slow yet strong enemy chasing throughout the level would actually make use of the area for routing and planning. Regardless, I think a linear map design would be better and replayable specially for multiplayer than trying to be an underwhelming metroidvania.Bosses are less exciting and more unfair in this game specially the ones that includes platforming and throwing items. They also now breakout of long combos to prevent too much damage. Perhaps doing less damage the longer the combo would be a better alternative to reward juggle skill while maintaining balance. Nonetheless, some bosses can't be juggled which reduces potential damage and somewhat feels bad as a counterbalance. They tend to have longer attack phases without opportunities to be more proactive. Even if some bosses were bad in the prior game, at least the player could lay the smackdown just as well which I enjoy more.Lastly, the game introduced a new problem: too much healing. While I consider this a general improvement, healing items can now be stored (up to 10) and used later which breaks the late game difficulty by overstocking for boss fights. Perhaps a 2 or 3 item limit instead of 10 would not break the economy or difficulty while allowing for mistakes. When I came to the last boss with max heals, I was not afraid or taking it seriously which feels bad.

_childDocuments_.review: You can only play Story Mode twice per save slot unlike the first game.The original River City Girls allowed you to choose a New Game Plus option after every playthrough.River City Girls 2 only allows you to select New Game Plus once per save slot and after that you cannot play through the story a 3rd time or more.I played through the game twice.I got 100% completion and all the achievements.I might want to play a third time without grinding and collecting all those different enemy colors again, but that option was removed since the first game for some reason.Thankfully, a kind individual already released a mod to restore the unlimited New Game Plus functionality that was removed since the first game.I have not tested the mod yet, but I might consider it if the developers don't bother to restore functionality removed from the first game.Unfortunately, this mod will not help those who can't or won't use mods, including those who purchased River City Girls 2 on other platforms.I actually purchased River City Girls 2 on both Steam and Switch, and I guess my Switch version is out of luck if the developers don't restore the functionality.I know an owner of the PS5 version who is also disappointed by the lack of an unlimited New Game Plus option.There are not any other Game Modes besides Story Mode at this time, so only allowing 2 Story Mode plays per save slot seems to limit replayability.As for the rest of the game, I generally prefer River City Girls 2 over the first game (which is why I might want to play 3 or more times).I like that there are safe hideouts unlike the first game.I like that you can change your characters in hideouts without quitting the game.I like item storage and the ability to resummon any previously captured enemy colors in the hideouts.I like that your chosen characters actually speak throughout most of the game and appear in stores. (In the first game, it was always just Misako and Kyoko)I really like the new areas and enemy types.I also like the larger map.I like a number of the new bosses gimmicks, but one of the bosses seemed mostly like a repeat of a previous boss to me, and I think I preferred the final bosses in the original game.I think I like the music better in River City Girls 2 than in the first game.In the original game, the phone menu allowed you to see which enemy colors you had already recruited. In RCG 2, you have to go back to a hideout to check your enemy list, because it was removed from the phone menu for some reason.I thought it was annoying that we could not sort the accessories in the first game. Unfortunately we can still not sort them in River City Girls 2, but they are automatically sorted alphabetically. It's debatable whether or not this is actually an improvement.Overall I preferred River City Girls 2 to the first game.But it should not have removed the ability to replay Story Mode unlimited times.

Combos can go on and on and on even after you kill your enemy, and their are so many different typed of combo-leads after a complete normal combo. Bosses are different now slightly. Not even aerial combos change that, but by the time you get a launcher move and a full aerial combo that's already and infinite right next to a wall waiting to happen.Regular enemies are all here from the first with a 6 new groups. If they hit you with their special ranged attack. You might as well say goodbye to 1/4 of your cash and any recruits you claimed or purchased in that moment.I don't have much to say about the music besides that they are reused for areas from the first RCG and that they have a amazing new track's in place like the mall or the the Court in Downtown. I'm absolutely loving "River City Girls Anthem" (  ;link) right now. It's the only thing that completely held my mind since the Sonic Frontiers Bosses OST.I've only played as Misako and will be back for a replay of Kyoko, Riki, Kunio, Marian, and Provie after I finally beat this game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really engaging. The art and animation is very pretty, and the combo system is superb. Combos really are the core draw for this games combat imo. There's a great variety within a single characters combo routes as well interesting variety between characters. It has nice dynamic elements with the wall bounce mechanic, assists can further increase interest and variety. It truly is a fun and interesting game that drives you (or at least me personally) to clear out every screen of enemies before moving onto the next one just for the simple sake of engaging with the combo system even more. But this makes it all the more baffling as to why the bosses are so terribly designed.In a game where combos are king and combos are long, bosses universally tech out after hit 5. Why?? These should be the most fun and memorable and unique fights in the game, and while they achieved that to some extent, it's only because they are uniquely and memorably bad. Combat against bosses basically boil down to walking up to them, mashing out your light string, and then playing essentially a small mini game, rinse, repeat. Dreadful. if anything bosses shouldn't start taking damage *until* hit 5 so you're made to engage with the combo system that gives this game so much appeal.There's also something of an issue where all enemies by and large stand around waiting for their turn to have the ♥♥♥♥ kicked out of them in an 80 hit combo rather than being meaningful agents that pose some threat or challenge. This isn't really a problem with RCG2 specifically; Frankly all Beat em Ups seem to have this issue. I'm not sure how this could be solved, but combat largely boils down to showing off sick combos rather than a meaningful fight, so much so that enemies will usually die not even half way through your combo, but since combos are so much fun you'll continue to kick around their lifeless husks for another 40 hits just for the love of the game. (I will say though that the choice to make enemies continue to be combo-able after death was a fantastic choice and thank god they made it)Another comparatively small problem I have is that the game doesn't really incentivize you to fight enemies beyond how fun it is to do so. To be more precise: engaging with enemies and fighting them as you come across them, while easily the most fun way to play, is far far far from the most efficient way to play. Efficient play tends to involve just running past them. As stated before, combos are so fun that I chose to fight every enemy I saw regardless, but the fact that running past them is the most efficient way to play does slightly nag at you constantly. This problem seems to arise from the open world nature of the game. Where a more linear beat em up would just happily lock your screen in place until all enemies are dead, RCG2 is much more hestitant on this front, using screen locks much more sparingly and only for select story moment (and fair enough, constant random screen locks for no reason could prove kinda annoying). I'm not sure how this could be reconciled, but it is a bit of a problem imo nonetheless.The writing can also fall a bit flat to put it nicely, and there's way way waaay too much talking. tbf it is all skippable, though this comes at the risk of potentially missing out on context for what you're doing and missing some moments of genuinely fun characterization when it does happen.With all of that said, the game is so pretty, and the moment to moment gameplay is so enjoyable that this easily ranks as one of my favourite beat em up's. I pumped over a hundred hours into this game for a reason and would highly (HIGHLY) recommend it to anybody that'll listen. Big thumbs up to the devs, with just a few critical notes.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: well the performance update is out making the game actually playable which is great. so now I got no problem making this review positive. but that being said this isn't roses and gumdrop, cause:1) It REALLY shouldn't have taken this long for this update to come out2) Doesn't change the fact that wayforward knew the game was unplayable before launch but decided "f*ck it" and launched it and didn't acknowledge it till it got too controversial3) This performance update f*cked with some of the games logic where hit stun and physics were completely different than before, so a lot of combos aren't possible anymoreBut hey.. you know what.. THERE'S A BETA TOO (mostly) FIX THAT AGAIN!!Like god d*mmit Wayforward This game is f*cking great and with the beta branch it's the most playable this games ever been. are we gonna wait another 6 months for the games logic to function as it did before the performance update? and when it gets patched, is there gonna be another issue like the game overriding your computers BIOS or something?And once again, even with the beta branch, that's EXCLUSIVE to PC users. so if you got it on console you don't get the beta.Though I will be fair that the games performance is more vital than what combos are possible in the game, and even at it's most restrictive this game is still a great beat'em up. It's just super frustrating we're having this issue where after half a year when the games performance is FINALLY fixed, now the combos we practice are not possible unless you get the beta branch. and even THEN it's far stricter than it was before.I don't have much trouble recommending this game anymore since i do feel the game content does warrant the price, if not then on a sale. but I would still keep all of Wayforwards past actions and this current ongoing issue with the games Physics in mind when purchasing it.ORIGINAL REVIEW (5/12/2023):Having 100%'d this game shortly after it came out, I can say that I do very much enjoy the game and wouldn't have trouble recommending it at all for the actual qualities of the game.The caveat comes in when this game launched it was not only locked at 30FPS but it had baked in stuttering.but no problem, right? they provided a beta branch which helps performance significantly and makes the game [Mostly] playable!! and they've insisted that the patch is coming as well so surely the game should be completely playable in no time right? right?Well even with the beta branch it is FAR from perfect:1) There are still minor performance issues and hiccups in the game2) Online Multiplayer has actually been effectively unplayable ever since this game launched. so if you're like me who has friends that also play beat'em ups from across the world, you're pretty much SoL3) This is strictly assuming you are playing the PC Version. afaik the beta branch does not exist on the console versions. so again, get f*ckedand you know what, all of that would be forgivable if not for 1 extremely DAMNING thing... They announced the patch and insisted that it's coming but with no release date and somehow less communication than Team Cherry with Hollow Knight Silksong.On top of the team acting very defensively, banning people on their Public Discords for criticizing the unplayable nature of the game [and not even in a particularly harsh way either] and actively even DENYING that the game was unplayable when the game first launched until the following day where they said"Hey, here's a beta branch. :)"It is very disappointing that Wayforward continues to sit on their cloud, and just passively going "oh yeah, the update is coming.." especially when they knew ahead of time the glaring issues with the game since the Japanese release was also unplayable, and yet the Western Release has the exact same issues when it first released.While I can appreciate that updates can take time, I have to massively call into question if they are actually busting their *ss off with this update when the beta branch was released just a day after the game launched on steam, making the game SIGNIFICANTLY more playable.I am not necessarily gonna advocate for the boycott of Wayforward products from here on, but if this is how they are gonna act in the Foreseeable future, then I would be weary of being excited for any new Projects they announce.It's even more heartbreaking cause as I said, I think this game is Incredible and hell, when it gets fixed I have no issues Recommending it. but till then, I guess it's just gonna stay broke till Wayforward can finally be f*cked to fix it.Sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is good. If you liked the first game, you'll probably like this one.This game adds some quality of life improvements, like telling you which stats the food in shops will increase when you first eat them, and what they do before you buy them. There is no longer a money penalty for dying this time, you can retry from the last checkpoint or return to base.Story:The story isn't bad, but I think there was a little too much fourth-wall breaking for my taste. I don't mind a little, but to me the amount in this game was a little gratuitous.Music:Some of the music from the first game was re-used, but there is a decent amount of new music. I don't feel the new music is as good as what was in the first game.Gameplay:There are 2 new characters to unlock, but all of the characters seem to control more similarly in this game compared to the first game. I'm not sure why this change was made, but it feels like it doesn't matter much which character you use because they feel basically the same and have similar stats and moves. That said, it is much easier to juggle enemies in this one and rack up combos, which I do enjoy. This game also has a lot more mini-games to break up the fighting, which is good if you like that. Difficulty:This game is much easier that the previous entry. I was able to finish the game with very little trouble compared to the first one. Random mobs are a lot less dangerous and there seem to be less forced battles. I think I only died once, during a boss fight. It is longer than the first game though.Overall it's a fun game, with some pros and cons when compared to the previous game. It's worth playing if you like the genre and especially if you enjoyed the first game and want more.

_childDocuments_.review: Either to play for yourself or friends, it has many fun moments, good voice acting , great character design, entertaining gameplay with amazing combo mechanics, god tier music, very cool art/CG and there's just so much.While it's not in reality a long game if you don't plan to 100% all of it then you might not find as much worth in it, but it's still very good to entertain you and up to 3 other friends (in local at least), I've been using Parsec to play with other friends and it has been working great, I myself bought this game with the idea to 100% this game no matter if it was going to be solo or multiplayer.When I started playing these games I did not think I'd play such a "big" game, I expected the typical beat 'em up run one way until the end, defeat some boss, game over. The shock when I figured out we had a whole map to explore freely it was actually one of the best things, surrounded by Megan's McDuffe magnificent synth and singing, honestly the music is so good and so fitting, it'd be a loss to at least not give a chance to listen to some of the music even if you're not interested in the game. There are so many references around the game either in the enviorenment or in the conversations or characters you'll meet that's also nostalgic for some, and fun to see references from "culture" of the recent times as well, there's a lot of attention to design and writing at the very least for these parts.My only real issue with this game is that even in nightmare difficulty it's , I think there's only one particular boss that gave me a headache, you will still die though don't get me wrong, but if you're like me you'll powercreep easily without the secret items.The other issues is that there are a huge amount of weird bugs and issues regarding some maps, character movement, the strange 30fps lock issue as well and the game has been out for a month, at the time of this review, the latter can be dealt with if you enter the  for this game so it can run 60fps.While I can forgive some of the movement glitches and running out of the map or getting locked out (), the game has been quite stable for me without a single crash or freeze throughout my entire journey, however, there are other weird stuff I noticed:+ , it resets every now and then to the default one which kills a bit the purpose of buying the discs, but it's a minor inconvenience+  which you have to pay attention to put them again. (this is probably due to things being "set" per the character and not per "player")+ , neither does the Sauna, which kinda should but yeah minor inconvenience (kinda...)+  (Since last map entered)+ While the UI is now improved and we're allowed to use items without going through the menu, the first game had a "multiplayer" pause which would show at least two phones at the same time and players could set whatever they wanted, the issue with this was that if a player removed the pause then both would return to the game instantly, it was probably changed due to that and 4 player implementation, but it was a cool idea in the first game that sadly didn't carry on here and can make things a bit of a slog if you play multiplayer, then again, minor inconvenience and not really game breaking.+ Characters don't actually have many (if any?) unique voicelines in different combinations, each character will take an archetype of either "Kyoko" or "Misako" and then play their same voicelines but on a different voice acting, this is fine because there won't be any fear of missing dialogue due to choosing different characters but it is also a bit disappointing since the characters are so interesting to me. (Cutscenes do not include other voices than Kyoko or Misako (Or than the characters supposed to interact at this time of course). Keep in mind, for solo you can choose who your "Companion voice" is from pause menu > settings (This is applied per character if you do play multiple characters) which is a great setting, in multiplayer however, the voices will depend purely from "Player 1" (host) and "Player 2" (Based on which controller connected in order, and not which player joined the game...), whoever is considered Player 3 and Player 4 will have no interaction whatsoever during dialogues.+ Spanish text translation is a bit off (but this is clearly the normal for videogames no matter what if they don't have a native speaking working on it, I guess) but it still works nonetheless for those who may need it to understand the game better.The reason why some of these issues throw me off is mostly because it's stuff that in the first game didn't seem to happen at all and they were introduced in the sequel somehow, while I don't know nor really care much about the specifics, they were all things that caught me off guard, there are still a lot of improvements and a lot of enjoyment to get but be aware that in some situations you'll just encounter silly issues.I haven't tried online at all but I've read complaints about it being limited for 2 players...? Which is kinda strange and it isn't the only game that does that if it's true, since I remember Streets of Rage IV do the exact same thing, making 4 player multiplayer local-exclusive (which is terrible and I don't know (nor care) from a developer point of view but from my view there's no way that should be exclusive lol).While I think there's a lot of other things that could be added to make everything feel smoother, it's an outstanding game with a lot to give and I heavily encourage playing it, if you're not really sure about wanting to deal with a few issues or you don't think you'll play it as much it'd be perfect to wait for a sale as well. Hopefully in the future some of these issues will be addressed for people who might want to give this game a try so they may have a more enjoyable experience, or at the very least, a smoother one, it'd be a terrible that people were missing on this game over minor things.Honestly as I'm sitting here thinking what to say or what to add I just think that I write too much, and while I still listen to the OST after I just got the 100% completionist achievement, I can only think that I'm sad there's nothing else to be done other than just replay, but you know how it is sometimes... just ain't the same.tl;dr  it's ♥♥♥♥♥ great and the whole OST is a  I love it all.and PLEASE ADD A STEAM POINTS SHOP :boohoo:

Burnt out from repetitiveness and padding.  	• Combat system remains a key highlight from River City Girls 1 (RCG). Blends traditional beat-em-up combos with more advanced moves as you buy them from the shops but requires a lot of money grind.	• The ability to recruit enemies as allies doesn't feel as impactful.	• Multiplayer co-op mode offers drop-in/drop-out mechanics. Game is more fun when played with a friend.	• Many sections feel repetitive, padded out and backtrack-y, doubly so if you fight every enemy wherever you go as enemies constantly respawn.	• Character progression is satisfying, as players can unlock new abilities and power-ups throughout the game.	• Often can get lost due to map design and lack of mini-map or in-game marker. Will need to open up map every couple of instances.	• When in combat, vertical axis needs to be almost pixel perfect to do damage. Can often find yourself punching thin air.	• Most Boss battles are interesting and fun and require learning their mechanics to defeat them.  	• River City Girls overall gives the vibe of Scott Pilgrim vs the World.	• Narrative is light-hearted and filled with character, continuing from the River City Girls 1.	• The two protagonists, Misako and Kyoko, are likable, and their banter adds charm however can be annoying and grating to some.	• Beautiful pixel art with a modern flair. Animations are fluid, each environment is vibrant and filled with small details that make the world feel alive.	• Character designs are colourful and distinct.	• The vocals and music is stellar but as the vocals loop often, it can feel quite repetitive.	• If you didn’t play the first River City Girls, make sure to play that first before deciding if you're going to play\buy 2. The 2nd is double the length of the first and due to this both it's pro's and con's are also doubled. 	• Buy\eat at least one of each consumable at least once to gain a permanent buff stat on your character.	• Seek out Dojo's when you have the money to upgrade your characters abilities. _childDocuments_.review: While it took a long time, I can say the game is finally where it should have been at launch. You no longer need to use a beta build to achieve 60 FPS that only worked in single player.RCG2 reuses a lot of assets from the first game. Backgrounds, enemies, and attacks. While it looks and feels like the first game, I do feel like they changed enough.The biggest difference from the first game is cross-play with different platforms. I played with a friend who was on the Switch, and it ran great.The combat is way deeper and allows you to do some insane juggle combos. The most fun I had was just practicing combos to see how far I could go. If you have played Streets of Rage 4, then you know what I'm talking about.The new characters are also a nice addition. I personally do not like how they wrote Marian. Her story comes off more like cringe-worthy fan fiction. Which is super disappointing because she looks and plays amazing. She is hands-down the most fun character to play with and watch due to how flashy her attacks are. Which is why I'm so disappointed that they dropped the ball hard with her story.The main story is a step down from RCG1 at all levels. The story doesn't need to make "sense." The main issue with the story is that it lacks all the charm that the first game had. Compare both game intro levels.RCG1 school intro level had the "Puberty" slide show, and the end stage had you fight a female version of Abobo. The dialogue between the two leading ladies was great. It was so charming and always made me either smile or laugh.RCG2 has you go to school only to be kicked out a window, and then you stay at Kyoko's house to justify why they took all your moves away from you. While also trying to make meta-humor that falls really flat. The dialogue compared to RCG1 feels forced and lacks what made the first game so memorable.While the music also reuses the original OST, the new songs are just as good, if not better, than the RCG1. This is the one that stands out when you compare both games.Even though I am disappointed, I still think the game as a whole is good and worth playing. The game play really carries it on top of great music and crossplay. If you liked the first one, then you will more likely than not like the sequel. Just temper your expectations.As for the price, I purchased the game at launch for $40, and I'm mixed. I think the RCG1 was worth it, without question. RCG2, I'd suggest $20 as a fair and reasonable price.Original Review[Still no official 60 FPS patch after 6 months? It feels more like abandon and that really sucks. I loved the first one so much that not only did I tell everyone I knew, it replayed it 8 times with different people. I wish I could do that with this game. When you update the game is when I will change my review.]

_childDocuments_.review: River City Girls 2 is a thrilling continuation of the beloved beat 'em up franchise, delivering everything fans loved about the original and then some. Developed by WayForward, this sequel takes the already fantastic formula of its predecessor and elevates it to new heights, making for an electrifying gaming experience that will keep players hooked from start to finish.Gameplay:At its core, River City Girls 2 retains the addictive beat 'em up gameplay that made the original so enjoyable. Players once again step into the shoes of Misako and Kyoko, two fierce high school girls on a mission to rescue their kidnapped boyfriends. With a plethora of combos, special moves, and weapons at their disposal, combat feels fluid, fast-paced, and incredibly satisfying. Whether you're pummeling street thugs or taking on towering bosses, every punch and kick is packed with impact, making battles a joy to engage in.Story and Characters:One of the standout aspects of River City Girls 2 is its charming story and endearing characters. Misako and Kyoko return with their signature wit and spunk, but this time they're joined by a colorful cast of new allies and adversaries. From rival delinquents to eccentric shopkeepers, each character is brimming with personality, adding depth and humor to the narrative. The plot unfolds through vibrant cutscenes and hilarious dialogue, keeping players invested in the adventure from start to finish.Visuals and Sound:Visually, River City Girls 2 is a feast for the eyes. The hand-drawn art style is bursting with detail and personality, bringing the vibrant city of River City to life in stunning fashion. From bustling streets to neon-lit districts, each environment is beautifully crafted and teeming with personality. Complementing the gorgeous visuals is an energetic soundtrack that perfectly captures the game's frenetic pace. Catchy tunes and pulse-pounding beats accompany every brawl, enhancing the adrenaline-fueled experience.Replay Value:With multiple difficulty levels, unlockable characters, and secret areas to discover, "River City Girls 2" offers plenty of replay value. Whether you're tackling the story solo or teaming up with a friend in co-op mode, there's always something new to experience. Plus, the addictive combat system ensures that every playthrough feels fresh and exciting, encouraging players to come back for more.Final Verdict:River City Girls 2 is a triumphant sequel that surpasses its predecessor in every way. With its engaging gameplay, charming characters, stunning visuals, and infectious energy, it's a must-play for fans of the beat 'em up genre. WayForward has once again knocked it out of the park, delivering a game that is as fun as it is memorable. Whether you're a seasoned brawler or a newcomer to the series, River City Girls 2 is an experience that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why it has mixed recent reviews, long story short, the game is great.Elaborating a bit more, first part from personal opinion, I have more than 200 steam games, more than 100 PS games, I have had maybe other 300 games from all other consoles along my entire live, and if you had this many games as me, you know 80% of games out there are forgettable and something not worth finishing; this game is worth finishing, my wife who didn't like gaming changed her mind because of this game.Let's not forget it's a beat em up better played in coop, a genre from the 80 that was born partially out of creativity and a bit because of engine limitations of that time; you enter from the left, smash those couple of buttons a lot of times, you exit from the right, it is not chess exactly, difficulty can only spike by making mobs hit harder and have more life, is not like you can fit wave-runner races there or something like that, enter/smash/get-out, it is what it is.Why would I pick this game if I would not exactly pick an 80's game over late's AAA installments? It does great what a veteran gamer who has seen everything would demand from a game to make it good.>Tons of map exploration, it's not a metroidvania only because is not fully 2d really. The game rewards you heavily for exploring, you get rare weapons, base stats, equipment, companions, I haven't played other beat em ups, but I have played enough games to know quality is scarce, it doesn't take to neurons to realize this game is on the top of it's game regarding level design.>why not add that the pixel art is amazing, every single corner of this game has a lot of detail, cities feel lively, bad games often fail to bring life to their games, they make the model of a store and it's a bland cube sitting there with no purpose, here you see people doing rational things around these models, eating, dancing, taking a sun bath, there is no corner of this game where this part of the design was untouched; big IPs like YU-GI-OH or Pokemon fail to do this, recycle the same 4 models and make people just stand there iddle, to not notice how absurdly professional is the quality of t the background of this game is a newbe's mistake, it's not subjective nor up for debate really, just because of that you can not say this game is not something with quite a few bucks and great minds put into it.>The most important part, fighting, it has 6 different characters, each with quite a lot of moves, which can be linked together intuitively, you see a move, you can think of combos already, and they are satisfying to make, my wife who had never picked a game ended doing combos that started on the ground and ended in aereals, these moves were not auto-linked in any way, there was no tutorial or me telling her anything, she invented all those combos and she felt like she was good and loved that (which is objectively true tho, she became good at the game eventually)>Lastly, all the areas are different, they have their themed npc's and mobs, they have a boss with a unique personality and gameplay, no two areas or bosses feel the same.So you have it all really, as a half a k games veteran, I can tell you that we can objectively say that this game is good, it's not really that debatable, YOU COULD DEFINITELY NOT LIKE THIS GENRE, you could not like it's aesthetic theme, but the game is definitely not bad; it sounds like I'm in love with the game but I'm not, it's just a beat em up with cute girls, personally I normally enjoy more complex games, but if what you enjoy is the company, this might be one of the best co-op games out there to play with someone who is casual about gaming.This game is definitely best enjoy with someone else, but that doesn't mean is bad played alone of course, I play it in the hardest difficulty and it was a nice challenge until I became a god in it, and reaching that point was really satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: There's some good in this title, but right now I don't think it outweighs the cons. If there's a sequel I'd like them to work on the QoL, because I want this game to be good!I played about halfway through the story content on multiplayer co-op, I might update as I continue.The good:- Sprites and animation are the selling point. The game looks amazing.- Online connectivity feels good. I host the games and I don't notice any issues, I would like to see if it somehow feels different if I join someone else.- Mob combat feels good and fair. You generally know what you're supposed to be doing to succeed.- Bosses feel good when you understand the mechanics of the fight. There are some issues (more explained in "The bad")- Items are useful and the game rewards you for exploring shops.The mid:- Dialogue is whatever. Some NPCs are very grating when they appear and there's no charm. The game feels kinda schlocky on purpose but doesn't deliver on the camp well enough or the dialogue pacing hampers the delivery. The pacing during the Provie manga cutscene is pretty good actually, for example.The bad:- You should be able to put a marker on where you go, or have a minimap on the screen. I play the navigator in co-op sessions because finding the route to get to where you want to go feels like a chore.- It's pretty unsafe to check your map because you're expected to clear a map of enemies before checking your phone, adding to the tedium of navigating.- The z-axis/depth hitboxes of enemies are very thin. The social media boss is one of the worst offenders of this because of how deep the map for that boss and it's unclear when you can't land hits because you are at the wrong plane or just because the boss is phasing or otherwise invincible. There should be indicators for missing due to invuln or bad aiming somehow.- Not being able to skip individual lines during a cutscene. The dialogue is slow and eye-rolling, but there's always a hunk of important information at the end of it, so skipping a cutscene leaves you clueless sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: River City Girls 2 is a direct sequel to the original and ultimately more of the same with tons of new content. New areas in River City, new playable characters, new moves, new enemies and boss fights. And that is 100% what I wanted from the sequel, because the first game was a lot of fun. Sure, the combat sometimes feels a bit slow with long recovery times after getting beat down, but I got used to that pretty quickly. Just like the first game this is an open world brawler with RPG elements where the player can unlock new skills and permanent stat boosts by investing money. There is also a simple level up system that unlocks stat boosts for beating enemies and doing side quests. The game world is big and versatile, chopped into smaller screens that are connected to each other with a spectacular boss fight waiting at the end of each area. Unfortunately whenever you change the screen, there is a brief loading time. This can be especially annoying when the next quest marker is several screens away. The game also likes to do fetch quests where frequent running back and forth between locations is necessary. New areas are unlocked while proceeding through the story, so not every area is reachable from the get go. But all the areas are revisitable after they have been unlocked once. Fast travel is possible through bus stations. There are lots of enemy types that come with their own move sets and special attacks. A new gimmick is a small chance to recruit them after beating them. This way, they can be used as assist characters that enter the battle for a short time. The dialogues in the game are fully voiced and quite frequent. While the story is your usual Beat’em Up nonsense the presentation and characters are fun to listen to and the voice acting is good. There are also some nice comic-style cutscenes at the end of each chapter. The presentation in general is great. Colourful backgrounds, a vibrant art-style, well animated character sprites and gorgeous special attacks. Even better than the graphics are the superb soundtrack and the punchy sound effects. The game can be played alone where it is possible to switch between the six playable characters at the start of the game and in hideouts. Each character comes with his own moveset and has to be levelled up individually. With endless spawning enemies grinding is no issue, so the game invites you to try out all the characters. But it is also safe to play the game with only one character. There is both online and offline co-op for up to four players. The game runs mostly fine on the Steam Deck but comes with slowdowns here and there so I played it on my PC most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game and generally a top tier beat em up. There are a good number of moves and combos are both reasonably easy to pull of and quite satisfying. The narrative is amusing and the characters are generally enjoyable. The game is very similar to part 1, but there are a few welcome changes. The lowest difficulty is "normal", but it's actually pretty easy. That's a good thing. The previous game's normal mode was really hard. In the same vein, this game is a lot less punishing. If you die, you have the option of losing some of your money to stay in the same place or keep your money and be returned to your home base. Also, the money doesn't disappear so quickly. The game is still pretty stingy with money, but it's much easier to accumulate since you're not constantly losing it when you die.Other changes are the two boyfriend characters are unlocked from the start and you can unlock an additional two more characters. Each has a good number of moves to learn (though they are quite expensive to unlock), so there's a good deal of variety in terms of fighting styles. I don't really have any complaints about the game other than the price is bit a high (at $40) for my money considering there is a lot of overlap with the first game. If you haven't played the first game or are a big fan of the series or the game is on sale, then it's a non issue. All in all a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Played using the 60 FPS beta build from start to finish. Pretty much everything about this sequel is an upgrade from the first game. It's not without some flaws, but with only 2 games, it's already my favorite beat-em-up series.+ 6 playable characters. Each with their own playstyles, cancels, and combo routes.+ Deeper combat system. Less downtime and more ways to extend juggles with multiple enemies.+ Looks amazing. Seriously just look around at all the small details. From the sprites to the backgrounds, they are extremely colorful and expressive.+ Game was updated to support 4 players online and offline.+ Great variety of music- Needs an on-screen mini-map- Loading screens feel a little too long and you will change maps a lot- The last of the side collectible items (Gears) are not well implemented. I'm someone who likes to figure secrets out on their own, so trust me when I say this: Just look it up on the internet.I love this game. There are a lot less forced fights, yet I still felt the need to beat up everyone anyway. Even knowing the enemies have been defeated, I still kept the combos rolling. For me it was just pure fun. I played on Nightmare the whole way and the challenge felt just right, deadly, but doable. This is what modern beat-em-ups should feel like.We have assists, accessories, and on-the-fly item usage. The perfect foundation for a rogue-like/endless mode. WayForward plz.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this was one of the longest waits for a game release that I can recall in 2022. The Summer to Winter release window was unbearably long, and I constantly sought out any and all information about a potential release for this game. At the time, I thought it would be worth it. Instead, it was foreshadowing the long wait I'd have to endure to, then, play online with anybody and not suffer a 30 fps hardcap because, somehow, the game got released in a state that makes the promoted improved combo chains impossible to pull off and otherwise stagger through in what feels to be a completely unpolished state.I say this with regret, as I think the game is gorgeous and the music is robust and powerful, much like the first game. The story is hilarious, the replayability is there and worth running through multiple times. I'm just tired of being let down for what has now basically been 8 months of waiting, from a teased release window to where we're at now. I guess when I can finally see some progress with the frame rate fix in 2024, I'll update this.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game rules - needed to cool off from the first game a bit before diving into this one but it's frankly kind of just a mega-sized version of the first game, and I mean that in a really good way - you can now play it 4-player Co-Op, you have six characters to pick on, and you get remixed versions of every single area from the first game + 2 extra (rather hefty-sized) areas, and all of it in the same art style and quality of presentation as the first game (all the new tracks are still great - some were not as memorable as the first game's, but some of them ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rip).It's kind of a no-brainer really - if you liked RCG 1 you will love RCG 2. If I have any complaints there are relatively minor - there is some slight bugginess but it's nothing you didn't also probably see in the first game - Misako froze on me twice in the entirety of an extremely completionist playthrough on Nightmare difficulty due to the enemy she was grappling in mid-air or on the ground getting somehow dragged into another nearby player's combo. Same bug was in the first game and I assume it's just something inherent to the way combat interactions occur - more funny than annoying given that both times we were able to fix the situation without having to restart the game. We also accidentally knocked more dudes into weird places in the level geometry a handful of times, but it was also never a game ender.Play it, enjoy it, absolve River City of Yakuza using glorious abs of steel and unmitigated sukeban ADHD mayhem and laugh about the absurdity of it all with friends while you do it.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Despite the fact that my stats say I played this for less than an hour, I have finished it several times on my Steam Deck offline and that time is for some reason not reflected, which seems to be an issue with any game in general.I played the first RCG on PS4 a couple of years ago and I loved it. It was like playing the original River City Ransom but with more emphasis on the fight mechanics, and full of easter eggs and jokes about the various River City Ransom-related games, including the Double Dragon franchise by having characters Jimmy and Billy run the dojos where you learn new moves and Marian having her own shop, and even have Abobo as a boss.Well, this one is mostly more of the same but better, so to speak. More special moves, more characters to play and more jokes about what it's like to live in a video game beat 'em up world, especially the one where the River City and Double Dragon games take place, including a ton of easter eggs and references. The story picks up just after the end of the last game when Misako and Kyoko defeated a Yakuza boss thinking she had kidnapped their boyfriends Kunio and Rikki, the protagonists of the original River City Ransom game, just to find out they'd just gone to a spa to relax, so now the Yakuza's brother and father of course want revenge and set it off by getting Misako an Kyoko expelled from River City High (though Kyoko reminds us she doesn't even go to that school, like she said in the previous game). If you liked the first one, you'll probably like this one. I felt it was a bit less difficult, but that's fine by me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played River City Girls 2 for 5 hours now and I don't know if I want to finish it, and for me that's the main problem about this game.RCG2 is the sequel of River City Girls. It's a beat 'em up, where you can control 4 characters (+2 more characters that will join you later as you progress), in an open world and with a RPG progression like the one in Scott Pilgrim vs The World. In fact, for a beat 'em up, RCG2 is a pretty open game that offers a certain amount of freedom and customization to the player. For example, you can equip two items with passive effects or have two helpers which you can call at any time to help you in a pinch or to continue a combo. You can even unlock the two additional characters in the order of your choice. To be honest, RCG2 is a good enough game and if I were able to play it without having touched its predecessor, I would probably really like this game.Alas, RCG2 is extremely similar to the first game. In fact, it's so similar that you could even call it River City Girls 1.5. It has the same sprites, same environments, same enemies, same moves, same illustrations (when you're in a shop for example), same music but with more, more sprites, more environments, more enemis, more moves, more illustrations, more musics, more sidequests, more details, etc. It is a more polished RCG1. The combos are easier, enemies now bounce against the border of the screen, there are more aerial moves, the environments are slightly different, for a game with main characters called Misako and Kyoko there are now japanese voices, and there's a kind of day/night cycle. There are also some welcome quality of life additions that make the game more pleasing to play and less frustrating. For example, now you can change characters without having to restart the game or you can go into a dojo to practice your combos.However, that similarity is also what prevents me to have more fun with it. For all its qualities, there's a certain lack of discovery, or maybe a lack of sense of wonder, that make RCG2 pretty boring or maybe unappealing. True, this is something that only applies to someone like me, who has played the previous game. But as of now, I can't bring myself to play it more.RCG2 is far from being bad but some things that have bothered me are still here. One thing that the first lacked was special moves with i-frames and high priority to use in case of emergency. Strangely, even with all the additions made to the gameplay, the developpers at Wayforward still chose to not add that staple move of every beat 'em up. Enemies still have their auto-attack when they get-up. One more problem is the rather similar way all the characters are. For example, in Fight'n Rage, Gal is totally different from Ricardo. Here, all the characters have more or less the same moves, that have more or less the same use, and their combos are more or less similar.I should add that with all the additions made to the game, RCG2 can be overwhelming. At the beginning, it is easier to get lost and you'll have to rely on the map constantly to know where to go or what to do. One other problem is the readability of the environments; a lot of details were added to the old ones and it can make it hard to distinguish where you can go, where you shouldn't, where there's a trap and where there's none.Even though the first game was not a masterpiece, I still played it for 32 hours and finished it at least three times. So it came as a surprise to me when I stopped playing RCG2 after 5 hours. Like I said, it is indeed a good enough game and if I hadn't played the first one I would have probably liked this one more. But that's not the case. If I could go to the past, I would probably tell my old self to not buy this game, at least not right now and not at this price. Someone new might like it. All of its flaws are not irredeemable and are more annoyances than sins (except for the 30fps problem that's currently being worked on). That's why, after some time has passed, I would recommend it to new players and only give a maybe (not) to returning ones, me included.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Play River City Girls 1 before this. It's the better game. If you really enjoy part 1, maybe part 2 is something for you. It's just the same. I love RCG 1. I speedrun it for quite a while and was super excited about the second installment of the series. I'm not completely disappointed in what we got, but this games has some serious quality issues and lacks some attention to details.But the good things first:- This game is what most people want, the same as part 1, but more.- I enjoyed returning to River City, the overall reinterpretation of the city is nice.- The soundtrack is very good again (I love the basketball theme)- New characters, new move sets, fine-tuned fighting system. Everything perfect.- New enemies are ok.- Some minigames are fun.- Online Multiplayer (although not tested yet) is a nice addition.- Even more Crossover references to Double Dragon made me lough so hard.- I played on PC and Steamdeck and everything just works.--Here are the issues I have with the game. (Let's not talk about the FPS thing, because this will be fixed in the future):- The story started well, but fell flat at the end. I couldn't care less for the story and the ending at some point in the game.- Most of the side quest are just boring. Collect some 22 fluffy whatever here, collect 22 whatever there. Make some selfies.- All Boss Fights (except maybe the first one) are boring as hell (In really enjoyed the boss fights in RCG 1, as they are more creative and challenging) as in RCG 2). Here the fights aren't balanced at all, the enemies are missing funny or surprising attacks or any nice details. Except for "more bullets and faster" there isn't any real difference in the different phases during the fights. What also bothers me: The "opening VERSUS screens" are just a cheap quick and dirty work and missing the attention to detail which we got in part 1. This makes me just sad.- The lack of attention to detail in present all over the game. Of course, we get a hell lot of reused sprites in this game. I'm fine with it. But man, I really don't enjoy some of the super stupid color pallets some enemies have. - Revisiting the city is nice, but some changes to the city layout are strange. While exiting the Aquarium in Part 1 results in entering the hotel, now you end up on the beach at the weightlifting area? Why? Again, just some details got wrong.- Hell: The credits and the credit sequence are a complete mess. Ugly as hell, what even is the art style here? What are those fonts, why is everything so fast. You should celebrate yourself at this point.- I hate some of the new voices of existing characters. I'm too used to the original voices of part 1. (Sorry to you folks, still love you)- White subtitles during a black-and-white comic sequence are not readable! ;-)- Please fix those loading times. A game like this shouldn't have so many loading zones. This has to be improved. And man... these loading screen this the super huge text are just ugly. Please fix this (although I enjoy the loading-fighting-sprite thing)- The German localization is all over the place. At some places, the text just runs off the screen.In the end, for me, this game fells rushed for a release. Just one or two more rounds of QA and this game would be so much better. Most of my issues are solvable, but at this point I strongly recommend new player to start playing RCG1, if they have never played the game. Part 2 is just more of it, but in questionable quality.To those who love Part 1, enjoy part 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Me and my boyfriend have a lot of fun on this game, can’t put it down. Has minimal bugs that don’t hinder the core experience. Characters are funny and filled with personality, has 4 player coop local and online with full cross play. The world feels alive like you’re in it. Levels are larger and more expansive than the first game. Every character scales with the story progress instead of having to restart the story with the a new character everytime, although it does support multiple save files. Characters have their own unique fighting styles that you can buy more moves to extend your combos in dojo shops. Has secret areas, shops, and bosses and cutscenes. Combat has a nice flowing smooth combat system with an uncapped frame rate. Fully voice acted in game and in cutscenes. Has a new game plus with bonuses to offer. Probably one of the best 2D beat ‘em ups I’ve ever played, hope there’s a 3rd entry one day.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: The previous River City Girls was an excellent modernization of the classic and long-running River City/Kunio-Kun franchise that felt like the breath of fresh air the brawler genre needed, made by a developer who pretty consistently lands things. Three years later and they've given us another instalment. River City Girls 2 does improve on its predecessor, but not as much as you would think for a game in development this long and at this steep a price point.This series has always been greate at not taking itself seriously, and this one continues that with another ridiculous, goofy story that has some top-tier voice acting giving it personality. Beyond the two main heroines of the last game, you now have other characters you can play as, plus more that unlock throughout the campaign, all of which you can level up independently. There's also online play with crossplay functionality, though I was never able to find a game and several others have said that the netcode isn't great. The combat system has also been beefed up, with more moves to unlock, though I still really don't like the way blocking and parries are implemented.Beyond these things, the game recycles a lot of the same enemies, environments and progression ideas and doesn't bring as many new things to the table as I would have expected from a full-fledged sequel. It's still entertaining and if you like the first one, this is more and for many, that's plenty, especially if you want to level the characters or play in co-op.Unfortunately, in addition to the wonky multiplayer, the game has had a major "issue with the code" since launch that causes most of the action to run at 30fps. This can be mostly resolved on PC with a beta patch, but the patch causes issues with crossplay, is not yet out on the consoles and the PC beta patch hasn't been updated since the game's launch. WayForward told me they are still working on it, but have no ETA. Why the game launched with this issue when it runs on the same tech as the previous game which didn't have the issue I don't understand. The slow pace of updates and communication are frustrating though, especially given how expensive this is.I enjoyed my time with this game and do intend to finish it, but if I hadn't been given a review code, I likely would have waited for a sale, given the issues. It's nontheless a great new entry in a great series and it's keeping the brawler alive, which I'm happy to see.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a "Perhaps" reaction, this would be it. It's not a bad game per se, the FPS issue was fixed, but the thing is that this game is not a real sequel and more of a 1.5 or a side adventure. It reuses like 60% of the assets from the first one, only adding some new locations, bosses (and their songs) and two new characters. They didn't revamp much of the combat system, only added the Special Bar to make Kunio less broken as he was able to solo pretty much the entire game just by spamming the tornado special and also giving you two assists. You still need to recruit them, but once you do they can be re-equiped without limit.But that's it. Nothing new, nothing groundbreaking. The good parts of this game are thanks to the previous one and not because this game shines on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this saying I started playing RCG, found it very hard alone, but next time I could play with people there was four of us and since RCG2 offers 4 players local co-op, we went with that and... so I played RCG2 before 1. I didn't miss much in term of story, since you do get a general explanation of what happened and why things take place as they do here... but it's a silly and simple story that just works in its right. You don't need more than that. It's funny, at times witty, sometimes generic... but, as someone else said in their review, the writing lands more often than it doesn't. And while I missed many Double Dragon cameos and references until I looked it up (and my God there is so much about DD; I actually like some of the things I did with that for the RCG-verse), they still managed to make me laugh, along with friends.While we started with 4 players, most of the game ended up being completed by me and another friend. The biggest gripe is... damn, the map is so big it feels exhausting at times, especially with run backs for some mandatory side quests.Another "issue", but it seems to be a thing for the genre (I had the same "issue" with Scott Pilgrim versus the World The Videogame, and, as mentioned briefly, RCG1), is how tough the start is. If you're alone, you'll die a lot before you've leveled up and unlocked stronger moves. You're VERY limited initially and you will need to be damn good at the game to not die until you have an up to par arsenal to keep up with the game. Eventually, though, things become mostly fair and at times even very easy. Some bosses could be a bit easier, some could be a little harder, but they're overall okay and fun.I'm not great at reviews since I can't go in-depth, I'm no game expert (I play them, I have no clue how to make them, so no idea if something works as it should or not lmao I can't objectively comment on "this move is just right, tight as it should, this is too floaty, that is too weak", etc, sadly), but, to me, it was a good exprience, with its flaws. Definitely recommended, especially to play with friends.Art style is great, writing is funny 8.5 times out of 10, the game is goofy from start to end, once you unlock things by leveling up and buying new moves you become so damn strong (Riki's jacket is OP, praise be upon Riki's jacket) and it becomes even fun to bounce enemies and clash with them, playing co-op is plenty of fun and very enjoyable, the music is SO FRIGGING GOOD, the characters are very nice and the variety between them and their moveset is really nice, and I can't wait for the third one to come out, because they did say RCG3 should come... and I want it. Looking forward to that!

_childDocuments_.review: I replayed the first game from start to finish before starting on this one. I only have about 80 minutes into the second one, but from what I've played so far, I am impressed. Understandably, it's not the released version that was promised. The first time I booted up the game, I even had the "whoa what is this reaction" even after reading other reviews.River City Girls 2 has made quite a lot of improvements. Things like a day/night cycle, expanded maps that feel memorable but changed enough to feel like a new city, ambience sounds that reflect the environment, more enemies, more characters, combat is even better than the first. I didn't think that would be possible, since I loved the first game's fluidity and still more for me to discover.Combat feels a lot more accessible, more fluid or natural. As with all games, starting anew, it feels rigid but once you unlock your basic attacks, it becomes so much more fun very quickly. I really appreciate the interact-able environment, walking into debris has an effect that makes the world so much more alive. The day/night cycle, they didn't have to add it but it's there and I love it, exploration seems to play a part into it. I haven't gotten around much but I like that are new areas to access that weren't there before. The soundtrack is still bombastic, I wish I could purchase it as an extra DLC.It's not all sunshine and daisies though, right now, I'm not the biggest fan of the user interface. I feel they took a step backwards. A lot of the personality seems to have been stripped, going for a more safe/generic format. Some screens are just a generic table with ugly, maybe Arial, typeface. They had their own custom typeface and it's only used in certain sections and/or headings. Some QoL improvements were made in the UI, but I just feel bummed it's not the same. From one perspective, it could be said that this new UI makes things more accessible. Easier to read, clear understanding etc.I am certainly loving this game, I have no need to play this online. If you're looking to jam this online, just wait for the patch. If you're just looking to play this locally, join the beta. And if you liked the first one, and want more? You may enjoy this. As again, I've only experienced 80 minutes of it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like RCG, you'll enjoy this one. It's basically more of the same: more characters (they're fun btw), new moves, new NPCs, new music, bigger map that feels like an open-world sometimes because of the side-quests and all. I think social media aspect was a welcome addition. I think my biggest complaints are the dialogue (which is kinda cringe) and lack of new character panels. There's too much reused content, it feels more like RCG1.5. But that's okay for me 'cause the prequel was one of my gaming highlights of the year.What I find special about River City Girls is it's light-hearted atmosphere that doesn't take itself too seriously. I mean, you walk around the city as a teenage girl with your friend or boyfriend punching school kids in the face and kicking yakuza goons in the balls right in front of people minding their own business like if they are used to it. It's also refreshing to explore modern urban environment and talk to stylish-looking NPCs. Some boss fights are extremely original in their presentation like Primo or Tsuiko. We need more games with tone and atmosphere like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after patches: The frame rate issues have now been fixed and the game runs just as well as the original always did. At release this game run at 30fps with constant stuttering on all platforms including PC, despite the original supporting uncapped high frame rates without issue.Edit after beta patch a few days after release: It's great that Wayforward have responded to this issue so quickly after the western release; However I still can't ignore how insane it is that this wasn't caught by QA (Unless it was and just wasn't seen as a big deal which would be even worse...). The game also released in Japan 15 days earlier and people were definitely posting about the frame rate issues then. This game really shouldn't have released in this state; but once again I'm glad they're now working on a fix. The game itself appears to be an excellent refinement of the original, and I'm excited to play it now that jumping doesn't make me nauseous.Original Review on release: It's 2 because they divided the frame rate of the first game by 2.I'm really hoping they fix this, but until then I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a temporary fix for the 60FPS issue. See other reviews for that. Little bit whack that it requires a beta to fix but at least it's there.Story and art direction are fun so far. Single player is actually a pretty fun experience, but there was HORRIBLE lag during online play between a friend of mine and I (we are on opposite coasts of America). Which is a shame because co-op is often where this particular genre shines, and also baffling because other current beat-em-up games seem to have the online play figured out at a MUCH more playable state.I think the online lobby system could also do with some work. Trying to get a game in with my friend took a while to figure out how to connect with each other. It's not the most intuitive thing in the world.If you're planning on playing by yourself or doing local couch co-op with some buddies, this is an okay buy (albeit a bit steep at it's current $35/40 asking price), but if you are looking to do some online with a buddy and you guys are very far apart, I would consider holding off for now, as the experience might not be much better than just doing remote play or parsec.EDIT: I think there might be a chance that the online play felt really rough since the 60FPS fix doesn't apply to online yet, so any amount of online latency will feel much worse due to the game just running a lot slower. As it stands, it's still difficult for me to recommend the game outside of those who just want to play singleplayer or locally, but this may change if either the netcode gets fixed or if 60FPS online solves my current grievances.
