_childDocuments_.review: Much like real life, this game punishes you for being poorI like the game, but it is flawed and frustrating to play...much like real life.But why? Well...It is really hard to farm for money in this game to get the money you need, to buy the healing items you need to not die constantly in the game. And this is on normal difficulty. The enemies come at you in waves of around 5, and they can be walking bullet sponges that just won't die. But it sure is easy for them to kill you, especially because you can't block enemy attacks UNLESS you are quick enough to block the very first attack, because when they start combo hitting you, you just have to sit there and die.So, you lose a good chunk of money when you die. And this really sucks when you desperately need the healing items, but you can't get them because farming the enemies is really freaking hard and tedious and not fun.It does not help that the enemies DO NOT get weaker as you level up. Enemies in older areas will always be just as strong as the enemies in the later areas, due to the fact the AI as a whole scale/level up with you. And you know...that causes some problems that I think hurts the game. It really feels like you have made no progress in the game. Your character is not getting stronger in the way you'd hope they would.This has started to ruin the game for me personally. I don't feel excited to continue playing the game. It just feels like another daily chore you have to do. And that sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphically is amazing, I love the art. Also the game doesn't have glitches like crash or anything. The crossplay over the internet works good, not complaint on that regard. XP Grinding, issues with the controls while punching.That said, there is a lot of annoying stuff gameplay wise. As an example, if you are hitting the button rapidly, you can not turn around, this is key if there are enemies comming from behind and you want to stop their combo. This means that you can not punch left and right in a rapid succession, which create a feeling of unresponsiveness.Enemies have a short period of invulnerability, which means, let's say you cornered a group of enemies, if one fells while you keep punching other, there is no way you can avoid to get caught in a combo when this enemies stand from the floor. I understand this behavior in a boss fight, where you don't want the boss to be pin down in a corner, but for regular enemies this feature is annoying.The blocking button is useless.You need to navigate the map in order to grind and get XP, the game is not linear in that sense, like Final Fight let's say, you need to find your way to the bosses, and if you are playing with a friend this totally kills the mood of punching bad guys.Also, in order to navigate the map, you need to open your phone, and the bad guys can still punch you while you are checking your phone, so its super annoying to Tutorials are repetitive and intrusive, you have to read the equivalent to a tweet to understand what to do or to see something very obvious. And it shows you again if you die and have to restart the level. Like, the game stops until you accept the message, and this happens a lot. It feels so generic and dull now. It's so disappointing that a long anticipated sequel to what was a fantastic beat em up is riddled with performance issues." _childDocuments_.review: The control scheme is pretty stiff, animations have long recoveries that leave you vulnerable and are frustrating to deal with, enemies have frame advantage on recovery so the enemy AI has a 50/50 chance for free hits if your character is still standing next to them either due to slow controls or getting hitstunned by other enemies. It's just not even a decently-paced fighting system, it relies solely on beat'em-up nostalgia. This is all besides the stuttering and input lag that greatly interrupts the flow of fighting. The developers have a great idea here but I'd say it's maybe about 80% complete, they really need to go back and look into sprite movement and the speed/pacing of the literal selling point of their game: the fighting. Getting locked into combos, getting knocked down and having to wait while you mash buttons to get back up, having to wait for enemies to get back up, it's all too slow and just not fun waiting for the enemy to finish their combo, waiting for the character to recover from whiffed attack animations, etc. Maybe when they go back to the drawing board for RCG 3 they'll get it it right. But until then? The game's just not worth it for what little fun it provides. Considering they cooperated with Arc-System Works I would have expected better. I'm guessing Arc-Sys let them borrow the office a couple of times or something small like that. Production value on everything else is fine, it's just actual gameplay that feels like it fell flat.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: As of January 5th 2023 the game no longer has regional pricing in several countries. On release, I bought this for less than half the price it's going for at the moment. I'm willing to put the blame on ArcSys for this one, since they like to hike up the prices for anything related to Kunio-kun, but if the next WayForward title also tries to assblast me like this I might swear off buying their stuff for the foreseeable future.Okay, time for an actual review. I beat the game and it's...given me mixed feelings, honestly.  so far. (I haven't tried out the 3DS games or Three Kingdoms due to absurd regional pricing lol) Combat feels snappy and pulling off ground-to-air combos is very satisfying, plus having food items only give you stat bonuses on the first time you use them gives you more of an incentive to explore and browse all of the game's stores instead of minmaxing with the same handful of items. It's not insanely complex or anything, but that's perfectly fine for a 10~ hour game.Although, for all the praise I'm willing to give the gameplay, . River City Girls 2's dialogue tried to get a laugh out of me from start to finish and all it managed to do was make me want to dome myself whenever Kyoko opened her mouth. The game's humor tried to be "self-aware", do "let's run this joke to the ground" bits and occasionally try its hand at meta jokes, but ended up spreading itself too thin and not really getting me in any of those areas. (I did laugh at a small visual gag around the later half of the game though, short-lived as it was.)With that said, I'd hardly consider RCG2 a story-focused game, so I don't think it's fair to detract points from it just because I, personally, did not enjoy having my kick-ass gameplay interrupted by MCU-tier quips and unfunny jokes. I'm even willing to play devil's advocate for the writing team and guess that it's hard to make jokes at all with the source material, but if that's the case, then why go with this approach to River City lore at all? I dunno, man.Anyway: I think this game is tight. I had a lot of fun exploring the town and collecting recruits. If there's any criticism I'd offer towards the "game" part of RCG2, it's that I'd like to have a bit more freedom in exploring the town. I understand that sections of the map are blocked off so that you don't stray too far from your next story objective and end up getting curbstomped by stronger enemies, but I feel like a proper GPS function could do the same job while being less restrictive for players that do want to explore areas of the map out of their intended order. Also, having "examine" and "basic attack" on the same button is  fine, but really annoying for the one mission in the game where you're forced into an animation while examining things.That's it. That's the review. Down below are my complaints back when the game was initially locked to half the intended framerate.---------------------------------------------------------------Year of our Lord 2022 and there's a 2D Side-scrolling Beat 'em Up that runs at a fixed 30 FPS.It's even more insulting that things like menus, UI elements and  animate at 60.I'm not even that mad. I'm impressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, final edit: The long-heralded patch finally dropped, and it runs fine now. Took a long time with no communication on what was happening, but it's here. You can finally play online without horrible input lag and bad FPS.The gameplay is absolute combo porn and very fun, the writing is hilarious and the soundtrack slaps. The characters all play differently enough that it's fun mixing it up and mastering them all. I do wish the dialogue was a little more varied based on who's talking to who ─ there are basically 2 roles, the abrasive one and the dumb one, the VAs for the 6 characters all read the same lines and just slot into whatever role works based on the current party. The only time it changes is when it absolutely has to in order to make sense, like when playable Miriam encounters or is talking about boss Miriam, she'll mention "that other me," etc.Tons of sidequests and collectibles, it will take a good while to complete if you're looking to 100% it, and you're unlikely to get bored along the way. With the asterisk that I'm never buying a WayForward game AT RELEASE ever again(from now on I'm gonna wait a week, see if there are any glaring launch issues and wait until they get fixed to buy), I do recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: The fps-fixing OPENBETA game freezes every time I beat the first boss (right after the animation), I'm not sure whether it's a beta thing nor not.--------------------------------------------I don't even care that much about 30fps, the game itself is very lack of polish to say the least, many flaws combined to be a big mess.1. Being knocked down is a constant thing in beat'em-ups, WHY does it take FOREVER for the character to stand up again??? In most similar games' design, you push a button to recover quickly,  but in this game, you stay on the ground like  the character decides to take a nap, it breaks the whole fighting rhythm and thus irritating.(Since there are skill shops in the game, I assume there would eventually be a ''instant recovery'' skill or you can get it via leveling up, but that would also be a failure, quick stand-up SHOULD ALWAYS BE a basic thing.)2. Classic issue, you are easily in the different line with your enemies, so you need to relocate constantly to touch them. This happens in most horizontal scrolls, but in this game it stands out particularly. 3. The movement is clunky. When you are running and go straight up and own, you are back at walking. Walking is SLOW, and by double tapping up or down button you get a SMALL vertical jump, it's very hard to do any quick reflection in time. Also, it seems that my XBOX1 controller experiences input lagging (same issue not found in other games) , there's like a 20% chance to get no or late response, especially when I try to change facing directions while being surrounded.4. The command list is more of a puzzle than an actual guide, what exactly does it mean by "(X), rapidly"? Should I mash the button? And why are there several same commands?5. The animation of the boss replays even if you choose to load at a checkpoint. Though the animation can be skipped, when I decide to load a checkpoint, I want the fight to start as quickly as possible, why bother with the animation replay in the first place?The list can keep going, but I'll pause for now. I sincerely don't understand why the game makes me feel that the devs are deliberately trying to make inconveniences for the player.

_childDocuments_.review: I somehow went from liking this game to hating it in a period of about 2 hours, and I'm going to try hard to articulate why that happened.Firstly, like any WayForward game, RCG2 looks good. It has great sprite art and a fun soundtrack, all elements of presentation made to look like the game you're playing is way more fun than it actually is. If you're like me, and enjoy the coat of paint but could not care less about the characters or story, the amount of cutscene dialogue goes from mildly interesting to absolutely unbearable, to the extent that I skipped almost all of it after only a few hours of playing. No matter how interesting the characters could potentially be, I don't want to have to sit through three minutes of ambling meta-humor that basically says nothing other than "here's this character now fight them". The writing seemed initially a mix between cringe and actual humor, but it soon devolved into pure cringe and doesn't seem to understand how to make a joke funny enough to actually be worth telling. The characters just kind of say stuff over and over again and make little side quips that barely even amount to a blip on the humor scale, but sure don't mind taking up over half the actual conversations.Then there's the gameplay. For one thing, RCG2 plays very differently than most beat 'em ups for two reasons. The first is that all the encounters, outside of bosses and a very small handful of fight rooms, are semi-randomized. Certain areas have certain enemy types they can spawn, and these change a bit as the game goes on, but are never positioned in any pre-determined combination or layout. They're essentially trash mob spawns that pop up on every screen of the game, and this is because without this obligatory trash mob hassling you and giving you the potential for XP and money rewards, there would be literally no gameplay here of any kind.Initially this wasn't as problematic; the game has a lot to buy and unlock, and I'm a fiend for grinding currency, so beating up random bad guys over and over again was no problem. It's only once I finished unlocking all my moves at the dojo and purchased everything I wanted that I realized there was no actual game here--it's a series of annoying fetch-quests interspersed by trudges through 4 - 8 rooms of basically nothing besides garbage semi-random mobs. If you don't need XP or currency there's literally no reason to interact with them in any way, so the game devolves even further into walking mindlessly through effectively empty room after empty room to the next point in your fetch quest, hearing more annoying and poorly-written dialogue, then doing the same thing over and over again five hundred billion times.To be honest I don't know how I fell for this shallow of a gameplay model in the first place, and in retrospect I think it's almost entirely the presentation--it tricks you into thinking the game will have far more mechanical depth and even unlock content than it actually does. Even if I thought the moves you unlock were the coolest thing ever and I was intent on buying every single item in the game, the combat itself isn't actually fun, and that's the second main problem with this game.In a normal beat 'em up, enemy interactivity is in a weird place--you don't want them to be TOO active, because then they become annoying hazards that stop the pace of your run. Conversely, you also don't want enemies to be too easy, because then it just feels like you're lining up and punching bags of sand repeatedly. The way RCG2 attempts to solve this is by giving every single enemy in the game a sort of invincible wake-up attack--when you knock an enemy down, after an agonizingly long time, they will eventually get up, and if you are standing immediately adjacent to them, they will do some kind of wake-up counterattack that is meant to stop you from consistent pressuring and lockdowns.The problem is that this doesn't work in any beat 'em up, and the reason is that all you have to do is space yourself slightly outside the range of the wake-up detection, let the enemy get up, and then walk slightly forward and do the same thing you were already going to do. The enemies in this game do all have unique attacks, animations, sprites, etc., though some are just palette swaps, but the point is that there's no reason to actually let them hit you in optimal play, and when they do hit you, it's such a minor stakes scenario that it doesn't really matter. You can always just run back home, respawn there with no penalty if you die... and for what? So you can rush outside to more bland and semi-random encounters where you're effectively doing the same 'line them up and air combo then wait 5 seconds and repeat' bs every time, unless you feel like carrying a weapon or wall-comboing them? And again, as is the case with any fully optimal beat 'em up, if you are playing well, you are not letting the enemy do anything, so you ARE in effect just farming bags of sand over and over again for coins and experience... only so you can farm those same bags of sand slightly faster.Boss encounters in this game are a joke--they're laughably easy and annoying at the same time, as you can pad your way through damage infinitely with food items, which seems almost intended. The controls are stiff in this game in a weird way that makes platform jumping complete ass, yet many bosses will require it, and include ridiculous extended waiting period attacks you have to dodge multiple times before you can hit them again. I hate this type of partitioned waiting in boss design, and any attack which makes me stand around for upwards of 20 seconds before I can fight again is absolute garbage. This is the core element that made me realize WayForward may genuinely have no idea what they're doing when it comes to fun encounter design, and might just be really good at making it LOOK like they know what they're doing from the outside. I mean, look at this game's reviews. Look at my initial experience with it.It feels like I could rant about this game literally forever given how bland it is, and how therefore offensive basic QoL missteps become. The inventory in this game is worse than Earthbound on the SNES, where you move items one at a time. This is a game where you have stats and a level and you can't even SEE those stats or level by default on the pause screen, nor can you see the stat buffs food items give you while in your inventory or storage. Holy cow. That's just egregious lack of Q&A, and it pokes a hole in the entire presentation bubble for me.There's a huge potential this game could still be mindless fun if you don't mind farming mobs or just want to press buttons while hanging with a friend... but as an actual gameplay experience, especially single player, this feels hollow to the extent that it's almost fraudulent, and given my recent experience with other WayForward titles, it has me placing serious doubt on their pedigree as a developer overall.Don't buy this piece of ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game it is better than the first in terms of gameplay and combat. I played this for almost 42 hours single player, 40+ more hours on Parsec with a friend on their save, and got all the achievements on my save. This is one of my favorite beat em up games to date. The gameplay of just beating and juggling enemies is just very satisfying to summarize and simply put. The pixel art is an upgrade and evolution from the 16-bit of the original River City Ransom. If there were ever a remake of the original games from the Kunio series, WayForward should do it in this new pixel art. The characters are all fun to play and have their own playstyle, even if overlap a bit with the same combo press to everyone else. They fixed and improved the support/recruit system by adding another one and some of color palette swaps of the same recruits do different support move. Not only that but they fixed the support button not working for the whole game from the previous game. They reused most of the maps but added a more or expand them. The whole game map as a whole feels twice or thrice the previous's. The keyboard and mouse configuration menu is added that weren't present in the previous game, making it more comfortable playing with KBM. New accessories added and old accessories reworked. But accessories are more useful now. When game over, you have the choice now of respawning at the previous hideout and keep all your money instead of losing some of your cash to continue in that area. Enemies can finally be hit while on the ground instead of waiting for them to get back up. There are some really weird dialogues not aligning with what's going on like the boss fight at the school rooftop and saving your captured "friends". There are other gripes I have with the game like you can't use recruit/support while airborne, picking up light/heavy weapons overlap with the light attack button, air grabs being inconsistent due to lack of its own dedicated button and range feels short, block and parry feel very niche, just to name a few. The game lacks more game mode like a boss rush/gauntlet, survival, and a way to replay the minigames with higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: Ayy, it's River City Girls 2 and, no surprise, it's a mediocre to horrible game!A friend let me steam play this and I'm not going to put a lot of emphasis on this game's poor coding/performance.  That's known, there are fixes on the way but as of this current interview you have to stream the game to a friend if you want to use the 60fps patch.River City Girls 2 is a game by artistic hacks.  This game is a bastardization of, once again, most Technos properties, which it uses and/or reference to create a sense of importance in the story based on authority rather than writing in anything that resembles stakes that matter.Which is a shame, because if you wrote this for, for instance, "young people" I think it's important to make a list of things that they're not getting from River City Girls 2:1. A story worth paying attention to2. A depiction of Japan that resembles anything based in reality3. A game that might have, instead, use the actual "River City" setting instead of trying to get clout by claiming to be related to the settings of Downtown Nekketsu or Renegade Kunio.Characters are fetishes first and nothing else.  Marian's abs and Provie's fan fiction celebrity, used to legitimize the wet turd that is River City Ransom Underground, are what matter about those characters in this game's writing.  The dialogue doesn't even reflect one character's place in the story.  Why would Marian get lost "attending school" if she's an adult????  Don't get me wrong, picking the strategic realism of any story can get petty, but this game absolutely does not give a crap about those details.So what about the fighting?  It's pretty bland, you basically do what you did in the first game and turn enemies into hackeysacks.  That will get old very fast, and enemies just force the player to surrender their turn rather than there being anything resembling evasive or defensive mechanics that the player can use to keep the action swift and snappy.In terms of fighting, this game is functional but it's not very mentally stimulating.  In terms of the "RPG" half of the Action RPG, this game isn't very good either.  You can think of the scenario as being a series of scavenger hunts, which isn't necessarily bad unless we're talking about this game.  In order to drive the action forward, you are treated to a whitewashed version of Japan with hack writing straight out of an early 2000s web-comic.Much of the game is reused, which isn't necessarily a crime, but what is new is just a nerd's depiction of Japan.  Which is a failure for creators who are supposedly so in love with Japan.  This game better represents the boring, cynical nature of the internet than anything resembling materially reality.  It can look like someone's YouTube or Twitter feed, but it cannot represent Japan or its supposed setting with any respect.  If I wanted to YouTube then I would go watch videos and read a comment section.While this game likely appeals to weebs/anime nerds of the present moment, what's sad is that you can see anyone who likes this is cheating themselves out of anything representing Japan proper which means that their "love" isn't really love at all.  Anime nerds don't really like Japan.  Japan is what was fun and interesting about the Japanese Kunio games as a non-Japanese person.  Just the way characters fought was a reflection of the interests of a different culture, and those settings by extension at least were comedic or had stakes that were more than just using Technos properties as tent poles.  River City Girls 2 is more interested in making superficial cameos and character references than making a story that is good on its own merits.What you will see are references to the 90s, things akin to Generation X... but using the Red Herring of a setting like Japan in such a cowardly way.  I assure you, the road system, transport and city system of Japan wouldn't have things like "Capital Avenue."  But that's what makes this such a cynical, joyless effort.  I could see a snarky person really enjoying this game while trying to play off its many shortcomings, yet that's just not a fair standard to hold.  I've seen games sacked for worse.  The Callisto Protocol may run terribly, but at least it isn't artistically bankrupt.  What redeeming qualities does River City Girls 2 have other than paying sites to do promotional puff pieces? The music should be good and has some decent tracks, mostly from the first game, but it's so invested in communicating the aggressive cynicism and obnoxiousness of the plot and game design that I challenge anyone to like "I'm Better Than You" or "Get Off My Lawn" without revealing how much of a dork they are.  I think what's cathartic is just being able to call out this stuff here.What does this game even do well?  When you reach an area like the forest you're treated to some of the most tedious, dull platforming this side of River City Ransom Underground's milk transporting quest.  There's nothing dramatic or exciting about it... the combat is decidedly about feeding your brain dopamine hits for what are, for most characters, relatively easy infinites.  A good way to play this game is to pick Misako and buy Nut Cracker and just juggle everything to death.  Which is fine... but, again, just like River City Girls 1, the game just cannot execute any sort of competent boss battle design that meaningfully uses its core mechanics, the game instead chooses to turn the game into a Beat Em Shmup where players dodge projectiles and bosses stall because the designers cannot conceptualize how a game with PARRIES or dodges might operate.  It's afraid to let the player actually live the little power fantasy it teases the characters as being representative of.  River City Girls 2 just cannot utilize modern action mechanics for anything other than brain numbing grinding.You could try to say this about the NES River City Ransom game... but that is a blissfully brief experience that at least has an interesting premise.  Seeing the writing and scenario design of people who need to log off the internet is just sad.  I think Alan Moore gave pretty good advice however, you should experience certain things to know what NOT to do, to recognize what things are good.I would gladly go into the myriad of things that are awful with this game in a place that is a little robust, for the time being, here is why I think players should avoid this game in summary:1.  A Story that mocks you for investing any mental energy into it is not a story worth experiencing2. Sub-par combat balanced to punish players who are good at action games while tricking new players into thinking action games are tedious affairs that use input reading with little counter play potential and lots of "dodging/taking turn" call and response patterns.  It is a dull, boring action game unless you like kicking enemies as rocks from screen to screen.  3.  Strategy guide bait design for the various puzzles that are usually tedious and pad out an equally uninspired game.Play a real Kunio-kun game, play Double Dragon, hell, play a game inspired by it... but do not play River City Ransom Underground, River City Girls and River City Girls 2 unless you want to experience the joyless, artless philistine interpretation of much better source material.  This game isn't even good at being bad, it's just mediocre.  A bad game might have shot for the stars and not reached something, this game is just bland and sad. A game like this really just exists to show how to make joyless video games while running a pretty sweet promotional campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a power outage from a storm and it must have happened during an autosave. The data was corrupted. I had to delete the save data in the LocalLow and disable Steam cloud b/c it kept restoring the corrupted save. It really sucks because I was more than halfway through and lost all my progress. I was enjoying the everything and loved the first River City Girls, but because this could possibly happen again, it ruins the game for me.  Even though the game has multiple save slots, there is no manual save, just auto saves.  So there would be no way to disable this feature and because of the potential to lose everything again, I just can't recommend.  I'm really bummed and I don't feel like starting all over right now.In response to comment - I'm not the only person who has run into this issue where their save game was corrupted.  This was just the situation that happened to me.  The issue to me is that it happened and I'm not the only person who had to figure out how to restore their game to even work properly, let alone lose their data.  I've had minor freezes after boss fights and a soft lock where cut scenes failed to play - but losing all my progress is the final nail for me to say, yes the potential for the game to fail and require all data to be lost does ruin it and make me not recommend a game

I am glad I did...the first was cringy bad. The second...well....It fixes some things, but makes others worse. Far worse.First off, even as solo play, the Kunio series tend to be fun to play. The RC Girls games....aren't. The first one was a little more fun solo...but if you have no one to play with, then DON'T get this. Even with more character options than the first...its just boring.Second...once again I am probably not the right target age for this game. If i was still a high schooler that is into Twitter and Instagram and so forth..I might care. But I'm not, and i seriously don't want a game that mimics cell phones and social media. _childDocuments_.review: Summary:River City Girls 2 is a open-world beat'em'up, part of the Kunio-kun series. The series introduced a lot of new concepts to the beat'em'up genre:It was based on Kunio-tachi no Banka (localized to English as River City Girls Zero) but the whole theme and story are very different. The original game theme is a Japanese gang drama story, and you play with all the 4 characters, Kunio, Riki, Misako and Kyoko. In River City Girls 2 you can play with the same cast, but it's the main characters are Misako and Kyoko, instead of Kunio and Riki. The whole story is more girl themed, and more of an American region.Since it's more of an American region we do see a lot more diverse characters. The art style is a mix of American and Japanese and it doesn't always look good depending on the character. Some characters look very nice but others look totally ridiculous. In fact the whole theme is like that, hit or miss, including comedy, story, music, and voice acting. It's too varied and ends up feeling weird and unfocused.River City games give a lot of freedom to do what you want. You can pick any character inside the game, kick and punch, use several specials, pick and use weapons, pick objects like trash cans, sofas, and even enemies. There are side-quests scattered in the map, so while you're doing the main mission you might do those at the same time. You can also hire friends, or make enemies help you. It's fun to play with a friend, with friendly attack on, of course (can be disabled but no fun in that).I found the bosses to be tedious. They don't have enough personality, background story, and the fight itself is remembering patterns. It takes time and ends up being more of a chore than anything else. The good part is that you never really lose, so you can repeat as many times as you like. The other tedious part is loading times. The loading is fast but every time you change a place you get a loading, and you do have to travel a lot.Another problem is the story is not very well designed. It doesn't feel like it follows any direction, being very random. You are basically chasing characters but they don't look related to each other and have no clear background story. At least to me what ended up happening is not caring about the story at all. I don't even remember that well what it was about.In conclusion, personally I'm not a fan of the mixed art style, the too girly theme, story, and many of the characters. Even so, it's a fun game if you want to kill time, but I wouldn't say it's an excellent game. This is the kind of game you can play with anyone so it's a nice pick for friends and family, including younger kids, boys or girls.This section contains spoilers. These are more specific details of the game that are still relevant to the review. If you don't want to be spoiled, skip this section.You will eventually find Marian from Double Dragon. Unfortunately none of the story makes sense. She tells she is very close to Billy and Jimmy as a joke, but in the original game she was Billy's girlfriend. She is also shown with white hair, but she was blonde in most games. The logic and jokes look forced, just to have another woman character.Another odd character is Provie, who first showed up in River City Ransom: Underground, a spin-off of the original series. The problem is Provie is almost zero background story in the game so it feels completely shoved in just to have the spin-off character. You can play with Provie, but there's no real added value.You can also play Kunio and Riki, the main characters of the original River City Ransom. It's nice that you can but the developers don't seem to have understood their original personalities and how they're supposed to look. Either that or they wanted to make them a lot less delinquent and more westernized. They're okay for the most part, but feel nothing like the original series.I like the two main characters, Misako and Kyoko, but the others feel like pointless side-characters. While Misako and Kyoko are also re-imagined, there's was a lot more effort put into them. The personalities were kept more or less the same, but with some adjustments to be more distinct, and to not be as delinquent.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked RCG, this is more in pretty much every way. More characters, more meta referential humor, more enemy types and locations, and a whoooole lot more bugs. On the whole this one is quite a bit easier than RCG. I started one step up in difficulty - the main thing I noticed was more enemy spawns at once, usually 4-5. Money comes in faster but it felt like I was taking less damage than the first game, at least most of the time. There are a few quality of life improvements as well. The main one is experience sharing. You get 100% experience for your active character, but all the other characters, who you can swap between in safehouses, earn about half or so of both XP and money. This means you can generally swap in whoever you want, maybe being underleveled and underdeveloped, but not starting at level 1. You do need to buy food items for everyone individually, but it's usually not a big deal mid-game. Busses are typically near the stores, so you can gather most of your food within four screens of a bus stop. You also have equipment shared between all characters, so you buy it once and you're set. For example of how this goes, after I beat the game I figured "Eh, lemme see what Kunio does while I loiter". He had a wallet of about 6700 bucks and was level 15, I guess because I got the two main girls up to 29ish and Marion up to about 24. I popped out to the mall bus stop, grabbed all four restaurants' whole menu, went left to the dojo and bought his entire moveset, bought the other two Midtown restaurants' stuff.  Ran back the couple screens, hit the bus to Downtown, etc. Every enemy you've friended is also hanging out in your safehouses, so you can always go back and get effective buddies once you'd found em. Main gameplay is fairly normal combo beat-em up stuff. Maximize combos, do crowd controls. Enemies provide decent variety and are spawned randomly from those you've seen after predetermined entry points, it seems - you see LARPers and zombies after the woods, you get catgirls after Technos. This means you start with a fairly small pool of things to watch for, like cop gas grenades or Linda's air whip, and gradually move to watching for the zombie going into shadows or cat lasers. In the end you mostly do the same thing, kiting them into a group and wailing on em all at once. Some enemies wake up slower, though, so combined with wakeup danger it does slightly force more movement. You can equip two buddies instead of one now, and get some more powerful paid ones, and they also act as your combo break usually; they take the hit and you roll back, but some enemies like the kung fu guy can catch your buddy and you on stand-up.Anyway, just like the previous game, two dojos, lots of shops to increase your stats plus an XP level gain, fight through a series of gradually unlocked areas and complete side quests as you wish for more XP, money, and usually a bonus item. Bosses have three health bars to start, new attacks opened with each one, and have a super that usually kicks at the end of each bar, and sometimes in the middle.  You start with four character unlocked (the girls and their boyfriends), and unlock two more during play. Each has more or less the same number of moves, though Marion (unlockable) can get one more. Everyone can buy the knockup, diagonal knockback, standing knockback heavies and start with a pretty terrible basic knockdown. Normals are just combo extenders on the front - your endgame "bread and butter" is normal X 5 until knockdown starts, down heavy (knockup), normal X 3-4 (more if you got deeper while they're airborn), and up heavy (diagonal knockback). This takes awhile, and you might be better served with the normal launcher (jump after any normal hit) and aerial normals with a special finisher, or an air grab, which does huge impact damage to them and anything on the ground below. Walls bounce them on anything but a throw. so you can recapture really easily. Since most all characters have the same basic normal/heavy strings their special moves are the most different thing between them. Misako's air grab is a piledriver that takes her to the ground, while Kyoko does a volleyboll spike that seems to do less damage but keeps her a little safer. Marion is probably the most brutal character, since she can actively grab with her forward and down specials, create a 360 damage area or head smashing/arm lariat for the other and generally has more options, while Riki is the most finesse-like, using stuff like a weird energy ball he can move into position and knock enemies into it.  And... the bugs. It's 2024, a good long while past the FPS fix patch, and I had serious framerate issues on my dual-screen setup. It would be hanging at a very erratic 15-20FPS on my QHD monitor, and 60 on my FHD. Once I settled on using the FHD I found plenty of in-game bugs, mostly not affecting gameplay... but sometimes there's some weird geometry stuff going on (dudes on your plane that are actually up and to the left as far as hitting/being hit goes), plenty of minor visual glitches (transparency panels bugging out), some occasional unresponsiveness to Heavy inputs (kept giving me headbutt instead of knockup for one session). Lots of little things like this that make it seem less polished than the original. And my totally negligible gripe is they seemed a little more "heroic" in this game. My headcanon with the first was they were basically spoiled punk chicks out to fetch their boyfriends. This, they get kicked out of school, but then it's all about saving the city and getting back to school and videogames.  Anyway. Still a good game. Still not as good as Fight'n Rage, but it's pretty high grade, and the music is stuck in my head here and there. Lots of rehashed stuff but nothing really taken out, and more added. If you liked the original, you'll probably like this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is, mostly, "more of the first one". But there are quite a few welcome improvements that justify its existence and make it a much better game than its predecessor.The addition of launchers and air combos in particular is awazing, as it makes all combats much more dynamic and even puts a little bit of Marvel VS Capcom inside your 2D beat-them-up! And the 2 new characters movesets feel great and different to play from the others too!I will not explain all the changes, as pretty much everything was improved from RCG1. But the 2 changes mentioned above are those that contribute the most to making this sequel feel like a big upgrade.In many ways, River City Girls 2 is the polished, refined version of what the first episode was. So if you don't have the first game and want to give a shot to the series, you might as well get this one directly. This is mostly the same experience, but better in every way : more subquests, longer, depper mechanics, etc... Everything is basically better. And despite many recycled graphics and music tracks, it truly feels like a new game when it comes to the combos and minute-to-minute gameplay.The first game was fun, but a lot of that came from its humorous dialogue, constant winks to other Arcsys gales, and great pixel art. Because while the gameplay of 1 was functional, it was a bit too limited and (relatively) quickly became repetitive. But now that episode 2 has multiplied the combo routes, it is possible to fight more creatively and vary up your engaements, avoiding the feeling of repetition for a mch longer time than before.Recommended. But with a little warning : I liked 1 despite its flaws and am a big fan of Arcsys games. So I am biased and kind of the core audience for this game, which clearly skews my feedback. XDI am also aware RCG2 is sightly expensive compared to its competition. So it's one of those "the game has to satisfy at least one of your biases and you'll like it" kind of deals.But if you happen to enjoy classic beat them ups, kickass aime girls, pixel art or working on your combos. I'm pretty dang sure you'll have some fun beating up all the yakuza gangs of the infamous river City, and have a few laughs at the dialogue while you're at it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: I love muscle punch girls who use wrestling moves.Long review: River City Girls 2 is a lot of fun, albeit a little slow to start. During the first hour or so, your moves are limited and your cash is in short supply as well. But once you unlock the launcher combo for your chosen character, things really start to open up and allow for lots of creativity in the combat. Groups of enemies are no longer threatening, but allow for longer combos and more stylish setups. Truly reminds me of a 2D Devil May Cry 3.The story does really rely on previous knowledge of the series, however the characters usually give a one or two sentence breakdown on a characters motivation from the last game so theres no real issue there. It is better with that previous knowledge though.As far as difficulty, it truly does just scale with time played, but getting easier as far as ive noticed. Marian is maxed out at level 30 for me and the common enemies are no more than combo fodder for me at this point, but thats not to say that the combat is boring now. Figuring out new combo paths or utilizing each of the varied environments to keep the combos going is always engaging. And im assuming its easier with friends in co-op.Rarely nowadays does a game make me want to 100% it, but River City Girls 2 keeps things simple with its objectives and clearly showing them on the map (which you will be opening very often). This game rocks, its OST rocks, and I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be straight with you- no matter how much of a fan you were of the first, this game with the wealth of more in-depth beat-em-ups that have arrived on the market to quench that nostalgia vibe, most certainly doesn't warrant a $40 price tag. Buy at under $30 for sure- There's maybe 15-20 hours of content here max depending on how slow you play (and I played this very, very slowly because I enjoyed the crap out of the combat and wanted to savor it). The indie market and a resurgence of these things- all for cheaper price tags than this one, save Streets of Rage 4, mean that you have a ton of options (including one from the Kunio franchise that. now heavily patched, isn't half bad) all cheaper than this one, many that are very solid outings in and of themselves. Would I still recommend on even a reasonably small sale? 100% yes. This game, provided you can stand the rather obnoxious and meta dialogue, is worth your money on the combat and environments.Plot: Literally off the heels of the first, then an inexplicably stupid explanation to a six month time skip after a brief intro. The Yakuza are your adversaries. Plot is as simple as could be- beat the bad guys, progress from area to area like in the first, this time with seven areas instead of five, all a bit more expanded. Setting: No, before you ask, RCG Zero, AKA the first SNES Kunio spinoff, and not part of the original 13 Kunio games, is not *mandatory* to understand the plot whatsoever, but a lot of the game's humor and setting  makes some fairly appreciated references from it and it's not half bad. If you don't feel like shelling out the $15 to get that one you're really not missing a ton (save for a basic port, solid game, and mediocre-at-best translation designed to fit the RCG lingo more than respect the source material) , though I will note a lot of the game's setting is inspired by that one and the attention to detail is where this game really shines. There are SO many missable details all over and it's clear that the art here is a very impressive 9/10 for execution. The pixels crunch, the combos are animated smoothly, and it all just feels right on the graphical side, even moreso than the first game. I could not praise the game enough in this department. There's a ton of detail on every screen, and less than 30% of any part of the first game has actually been recycled here without a graphical overhaul, by what I saw- and when it was it always has new elements lovingly created to suit the idea that six months have passed (which they have taken great liberty to change the world with and add new areas for, to its credit). There's two entirely new areas and the rest is familiar but expanded. If you loved the first game's art style you're in for an absolute feast. They've barely removed, they've mostly added and modified.Flow and systems: In addition to the first game's mechanics, the hired heavies don't really add much. They deal slightly more damage for that extra combo power if you feel like using them, some of them have fairly unique attack ranges, that's about it. Upside is, they're cheap. The combat flow with the main four characters, as in this game's almost obssessive nature to acknowledge continuity (which I adore) you unlock Kunio and Riki from the start and will unlock two more playable characters through the natural course of the game, All four play with many of their signature moves from the last game, which you again have to unlock (their excuse is literally the six month time skip gag). The game's meta humor (granted it's almost an improvement compared to the first game's humor, which was just a tad on the childish side) is prevalent throughout. There are some rather interesting locations that get added to flesh out the existing five zones from the first game, and quests are more plentiful, rewarding, and varied this time. You will almost certainly be max level before reaching the end unless you really rush through everything and only do as many fights as are mandatory. The VO: The game is *heavy* on this department. I don't hate where most of the dialog's heart's at at the very least (though I do find some specific sections and characters rather annoying), but the game will often lock you into a room you enter while dialog is happening (this is ~50% of the barred 'cutscene' dialog, though you can beat things up while it's happening). As for dialog, player 1 has lines and player 2 has lines. If you're playing solo, the game defaults the second character to be the other's boyfriend/girlfriend, or in the case of the unlockables, just defaults to Misako. The game has no interest in adding anything from the characters you're not playing outside of a few instances- from what I've seen of others' playthroughs it's mostly the same lines voiced by everyone with maybe a tiny bit of variation and maybe the extra reference or two for boss dialogue, though everyone says their bit in the style of their character. Ergo you get a very different tone in delivery from Kyoko, Kunio, Misako, Riki and the two unlockables.  It's unfortunate that there isn't a bit more personality to the writing as the delivery is fine but a disproportionate amount of the lines are 'that's lame' or the like, and you will hear the same few things often. It serves as a disservice for what little story exists beyond shuffling you off to the next area (usually through a quest). What you won't find?The verdict: Despite this game's many shortcomings, it gets a hearty set of thumbs up from me. It's more of what I adored from the first game, and iterated on wonderfully, something WayForward has proven they're fantastic at with the Shantae games, and that's exactly what I wanted and was really expecting from it. A fun beat-em-up in a genre that has seen a recent resurgence of them in the past five or so years- this was absolutely the right time to strike with this, even if the price is a tad steep.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like its predecessor, there's a ton of heart and fun and sheer enjoyment in this sequel. It's a whole lot of more--more depth, more to do, a longer game, more fanservice and humor, all while juggling all of it in a tight and satisfying experience.While I still recommend it to anyone into beat 'em ups, there are still things that bugged me throughout my playthroughs, mostly minor gameplay things like too much cc and loss of control from eating a combo or knockdown, and very annoying UX things like being unable to skip cutscenes line by line (rather than the whole sequence) and just the general shorter maps and room that end up producing a lot of time-killing loading screens. I realize this is par for the course for a Kunio-kun game, but playing longer sequences like in SoR 4 and TMNT: SR really makes the effect more glaring.There was also the nagging feeling that the "more" here may not all have been good, like how grindy and tedious some of the side activities were, or how the moveset felt a bit more bloated than necessary, but I appreciate that all of this is in service to providing a more thorough brawler experience you'd want to keep coming back to, rather than the quick and done few hours' worth of the original.But at the end of the day, this is a great and super-fun sequel I enjoyed more than I expected, and still gets my Marian Legendary Abs Seal of Approval.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun from beginning to end. The plot isn't exactly nuanced, but the game has a ton of personality to it. The characters start at level 1 because they've been eating junk food and playing video games for two months straight. Everyone is on their phones constantly, Your quest list comes via "honkr". That kind of thing.The highlight for me is the same as it was in the first game: Megan McDuffee's soundtrack. It's a perfect fit for the game's atmosphere and is largely responsible for making this game memorable. Even the handful of tracks that I wouldn't find catchy on their own worm their way into my mind because they just feel so right in the game. I found myself actively seeking out paths that her lyrical songs play on, and her music is the reason I sometimes chose to backtrack through the levels instead of taking the fast-travel buses. Absolutely fantastic work on her part.Combat is enjoyable and full of combos. It feels more alive than the first game did. The stores are massively improved and give you a reason to check them all out. Multiplayer is quite chaotic but in a fun way.The only downsides I can think of are some bugs, some INCREDIBLY hard to find secrets that feel unfair, and the dialogue of the main characters feeling generic. I assume this is to compensate for the multiple characters that can be selected. Regardless, it was a noticeable step down from Kyoko and Misako's banter in the first game. I played through RCG2 two player with Kyoko and Riki. In the first game, Kyoko was obsessed with getting her Riki-poo back. In this one, they just seem like generic friends.All n all, highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this back to back with the first game, which I also enjoyed. I think there are a lot of improvements in this game, most notably being able to use consumables without pausing the game, extended hitstun that makes combos much easier and allowing more creativity in chaining moves together, and more content overall (side missions, minigames, etc.) There were some downsides, I didn't really enjoy having to mash to get up when knocked down, and there is a lot of backtracking involved for the main missions. The latter is more of a personal taste issue, but is a small complaint for what is otherwise a great game! It is packed to the brim with easter eggs from a stunning array of other games, movies, and tv shows that aren't obnoxiously shoved in your face but are quick nods for anyone who notices. The writing is very entertaining and funny in my opinion (much like the first game), I wasn't cracking up at every joke but it was always fun to hear the characters talk and interact. This game is clearly very similar both from a visual and gameplay standpoint to the first game, which some might complain about but I thought both games look great, and the second one provides a bit more in the way of visual effects. I could talk more about the game, but honestly it's best you just play it for yourself. If you're new to beat 'em ups, it's a great intro to the genre for sure, and I think it has something for everyone. I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I mean, what do I say? It's more River City Girls. The combat has been improved, adding more options for combos and strings of attacks. There's more playable characters, so not only can you play 4 player this time around, but you can ALSO play as 6 characters total! Including Legendary Abs. 🤤A few Quality of Life improvements have been made as well, specifically in co-op mode. Now only ONE player needs to purchase an accessory, and it's available to everyone (well, at least in couch co-op). It's great not having to wait and grind so both of us can have an item we want, IO can only see this issue getting exacerbated in 4 player. But NO LONGER! Now, you want an accessory? Only one player needs to purchase it, then everyone can use it simultaneously.One thing I'll note though that might have been an oversight. The ability for both players to open their phone menu at the same time is gone. Now only one player at a time can open their phone to equip accessories/check objectives, and that's a bit annoying.Also, platforming. Holy cow. it sucks. Like, this game is not a platformer, but there's a lot of painful platforming segments. The controls are clunky for precise movements like that, so I think they need to come up with a better system for the 3rd installment.Overall, a big improvement on the first game in a lot of ways. It's not perfect, but they've got a lot of content here, and it's such a unique experience, you can tell everyone involved put their heart into it. Love it. Nothing beats the atmosphere and the music either! Big Recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: River city girls 2 expands on what made the first one good with voiced tracks, 6 characters with unique movesets, a large map and some mini games and multiplayer with up to 4 players at once (Local co op). There are difficulty settings. I had a bit more trouble with river city girls 1 so maybe 2 is a bit easier. If you think it's too easy, try a harder difficulty.Essentially, the gameplay involves locating bosses, doing side missions for exp and money and eating food for stat bonuses. What's nice about missions is that they give exp and money to all your characters. Normally, each character levels up individually when used and they all have separate pools of money. The last enemy on the screen typically begs for mercy. If you accept it, you get summons that you can use in battle. Some summons must be paid for. You can always go back to your base and get old summons as well as put items in a shared box so you could transfer items from one character to the other. The game also includes accessories that are shared between all characters to add certain effects to your fighters such as having weapons explode when thrown. Pretty fun old school like game. Would probably be more fun multiplayer but unfortunately I had to play single player. The multiplayer includes online play where you can choose to go by region (or not) or you can have someone on your friend list play with you with a single copy of the game. Overall, I quite enjoyed the throwback like when played double dragons with my brother. If you would like more Japanese games, check out

_childDocuments_.review: Did you spend your childhood huddled over a keyboard with your best friend, with one using WASD/JKL and the other on arrow keys and 123 on the numpad, beating up all sorts of unfortunate enemies? Do you want to go back to those easy, simple days of mindless button-mashing? Do you also want to retain modern gaming conventions that you've come to take for granted in the recent years? RCG2 is basically RCG1 but with more content and new content. Gorgeous visuals, great gameplay. I am probably praising the game more than it really deserves because it hit my personal weak spots just about perfectly, but if you want a modern take on good old PvE gameplay, RCG2 is a gift that keeps on giving.Do you know what's amazing? The player character voice actors did each side of every conversation, so that you can play the game with any combination of characters and still get original dialogue!Honestly, it will be easier to write the negatives: 4-player coop is only available on couch, 2-player online. Some boss fights can be obnoxious. Your co-op friend won't have story progress for playing with you. Rollback can sometimes become jarring if someone has an unstable connection. No real modding support. It doesn't make you a sandwich.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally had a decent time with the game. But it does have some faults which I believe were quite harmful for my experience.There are several major improvements from the first game. The main one is that the combo system feels much better, it is way more natural to connect various moves between eachother, and launching enemies into the air to follow up with a strong air combo feels really good and reliable. It straight up feels like I'm playing a normal arcsys fighting game when I'm comboing enemies, and that's an extremely good thing. Combat is also much more fluid because enemies don't feel way too durable near the end of the game, which was an issue made the first game feel like a huge slog.The other improvements are quality of life changes, such as the hub that lets you manage your inventory, characters, and assists in a straightforward manner. There's also online co-op, which worked pretty well between me and a friend from an adjacent country (though at the time of writing this review it still ran at 30 fps, even with the 60 fps patch applied). And finally, the most important improvement for me was the proper keybinding support.However, I think the game suffers from some pretty bad game design choices that actively worsen the experience. There's way too many parts where in order to progress you have to move forward, talk to a character, go back and fetch something, and then go back again to where that character was. That back and forth formula really hurts the pace of the game. The boss designs are also pretty poor, most of them just consist of waiting around dodging a bullet hell or stage hazard waiting for them to be vulnerable, which ends up making them pretty tedious. And finally, the characters you're not currently playing as only get a small portion of the EXP and money your main character gets. This makes them fall behind in stats really quickly, which discourages switching to them if you want to keep progressing through the game.Finally, I think the writing takes itself waaay too unseriously, to the point where it actively removes the charm of the game. I have no problem with lighthearted writing, but the characters don't have any unique interactions with eachother, and don't really keep an identity of their own. This is especially noticeable when you unlock additional characters and select them as dialogue partners. They just have the exact same dialogue as any other character, to the point where if they are brought up in a conversation, the selected characters start talking in third person like they were clones, even in situations where they should DEFINITELY have a reaction to specific characters. Their personalities also change depending on who you're playing as, further demotivating you from changing up your characters, and making it very difficult to get attached to any of them.Finally, there's not much enemy variety compared to the first game, which is odd given that the game reutilizes a ton of assets from it. The boss intro animations are also simplified this time, and the sound mixing during cutscenes made them sound very low from the rest of the game for some reason. I beat the game at 53% completion rate. but I'm pretty sure the progress I'm missing just consists of collecting items and doing fetch quests. I may go back and do them at some point, but the dialogue and rewards feel pretty underwhelming to warrant doing them. After reading the credits, it feels like there were way too many resources dropped on having a billion voice actor cameos instead of adding enough gameplay content to separate it from the first game.The game is fine, mediocre at worst. But it constantly feels like it could've been so much better if just a little bit of polish was added and if there were a couple of better game design choices. This feeling is stronger if you consider that this sequel is not built from scratch and it uses a lot of resources from the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another review from one of my favorite indie developers Wayforward. And this time it is of one of my favorite properties they have acquired in the past few years to work on. River City Girls. As many of you already know I loved the first RCG. I have the soundtrack, bought merchandise of the series from limited run. And have completed speed runs. It was hard to imagine how they could begin to make a sequel or how they could top the first games charm. But let me say so far they have exceed all expectations. The game takes place right after the events of 2 with the fallout of the events there kickstarting this adventure. The girls have caused the entire city to fall under yakuza control and its up to you to take it back. I will do my best to avoid spoiling the story in the review but the comedy is just as golden here as it was in the first. You will walk away with a love of abs. No seriously…you will. Combat is basically the same from the first game with your standard quick and heavy attacks mixed in with a bevy of special moves you can use to combo enemies around. You can also parry some attacks with good timing though it is a small window. But with the choice of 4 characters at the start and 2 extras early on in the game there is a lot of variety to how each operates. Some new enemies make it into this game and a lot of familiar faces both bad and good carry over here. With many old foes now either friends or just taking a backseat to the action as new enemies raise to fill their roles. The map is also several times larger than the previous game. Where originally it was pretty simple running from one end to the end of each area. But now it is so large many times. I had to pull out the gps to find out where I was several times as I got confused and lost. But never did it feel bad to be lost just the sheer size the added onto previous areas was great. Speaking of previous the game does like its enemies reuse a lot of past areas from the first game and the same for the soundtrack. That said though do not think its just a rinse and repeat, they added on so many areas to past locations that while I recognized some of the locations like the mall or downtown in the scrapyard the additions complete changed how I knew of the area.  And the soundtrack was amazing. With work done by both Cristina Vee and Megan McDuffee. Past tracks still sound great but the new ones had me scrambling to download the soundtrack from bandcamp already. One small thing about the enemies though that also carries over for better or worse is the fact that once an enemy starts their attack if you happen to be caught in it you can not get out. There have been many times I get caught at the start of an attack trying to parry the later moves but you just have to take all hits. Also, the game has a pretty cruel method of you taking damage from multiple sources if struck before hitting the ground. One early boss was quite rng with a certain phase of their fight. And if you were struck by their projectile and also hit the toxic water, they poured into the arena you take damage from both. But when it works for you, it makes you feel good for all those times you yourself were bounced against objects. Another small issue WHICH let me state does not affect how great a game this is, is the fact WF added in a addition to the last game which carries over in which to transition to each section of the map you have to hold down the x button for a second or two. Originally you simply could rush each section which GREATLY benefited in speed runs or avoiding a area. Now sometimes you have to run to the end of the map and hold x and repeat this for each section. Granted it hurts speed runs but its more just a personal take on that one bit. If you were a fan of the first game, or have that itch of a side scrolling beat em up akin to callbacks of streets of rage this is a great if not near perfect sequel to the first game. With so much added to it you will definitely spend much more time on this title than the first. Aside from my very small minor gripes this game is easily one of WF best new titles they have released. A 10 out of 10 for me. Now excuse me as I go download the soundtrack.Id like to thank the good friends and team at WF as always for allowing me to review this game. Now please go download this game and have a great time

_childDocuments_.review: (Update: They added a beta patch that fixes the framerate for PC! Definitely will put it further into recommend especially if you enjoyed the first game!)My morbid curiosity led me to buy River City Girls 2 for Steam Deck use because everyone was complaining about the current issues. I was a big fan of the first game despite all its issues and Wayforward overall. First issue I ran into involved cutscenes not loading properly so I just forced Steam Deck to use the latest Proton firmware. After that, I started playing the game and noticed that it was running slower than River City Girls 1. However, I would still say that I enjoyed my current time playing this game due to its charm level. As a gamer, I tend to prioritize if the game's charm can overcome its technical deficiencies. In this case, I would have enjoyed shorter loading times and 60 frames per second. However, even with the current launch version, I found myself sucked into beating up randoms and hitting convenience stores without worrying about the technical issues. It's clearly a charming good game at its core with some unfortunate technical issues at the moment. I don't regret paying the price at the moment because I think Wayforward will address these issues and I am having a good time so far. However, if you can't tolerate the frame rate or can't adjust your muscle memory to that issue, I would wait for sure to see when the developer fixes it. I ended up sucking it up and just having a good time though. The core gameplay is still great alongside the charm factor.

name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition
detailed_description: The Outer Worlds: Spacer’s Choice Edition is the ultimate way to play the award-winning RPG from Obsidian Entertainment and Private Division. Players who already have The Outer Worlds and its associated DLC, Murder on Eridanos and Peril on Gorgon, on Steam can upgrade to The Outer Worlds: Spacer’s Choice Edition for a reduced purchase price.* To enable the upgrade purchasing option, players must be signed into the same Steam Account they used to purchase the base game and its associated DLC and select the “Complete the Bundle” purchasing option. You’ve tried the rest, now come back for the best! The Outer Worlds: Spacer’s Choice Edition includes the base game and all add-on content as the definitive way to play the beloved RPG from Obsidian Entertainment. This remastered masterpiece is optimized to be the absolute best version of The Outer Worlds… even if you choose to play this critically acclaimed RPG as the absolute worst version of your character. Lost in transit while on a colonist ship bound for the edge of the galaxy, you awake decades later only to find yourself in the midst of a deep conspiracy threatening to destroy the colony. Explore the various planets and locations of Halcyon, including the mysterious Gorgon Asteroid and delightful distilleries of Eridanos. As you encounter various factions, all vying for power, the character you decide to become will determine how this player-driven story unfolds. In the corporate equation for the colony, you are the unplanned variable. Key Features: • It’s The Outer Worlds you love, but even better: 2019’s hit RPG has been remastered with better graphics, improved performance, additional animations, higher-res environments, and more. • Increased level cap: A higher level cap means even more ways to build your character from the seven branches of the skill tree. • The player-driven story RPG: In keeping with the Obsidian tradition, how you approach The Outer Worlds is up to you. Your choices affect not only the way the story develops, they also affect your character build, companion stories, and end game scenarios. • Lead your companions: During your journey through the furthest colony, you will meet a host of characters who will want to join your crew. Armed with unique abilities, these companions all have their own missions, motivations, and ideals. It's up to you to help them achieve their goals, or exploit them to your own ends. • Explore the corporate colony: Halcyon is a colony at the edge of the galaxy owned and operated by a corporate board. They control everything... except for the alien monsters left behind when the terraforming of the colony’s two planets didn’t exactly go according to plan. Find your ship, build your crew, and explore the settlements, space stations, and other intriguing locations throughout Halcyon. *Based on Private Division’s suggested retail price for The Outer Worlds: Spacer’s Choice Edition on PC. Limit of one upgrade per account.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds Plays In Tandem To Fallout And Has Similar Gameplay Mechanics And Functionality As Well As it's Own Unique (Storyline, Side Quests, Dialogues, Companions, Colonies, Collectables, Characters, Enemy types, Locations/Planets, Fast Travelling Abilities, Weapons, Perks) And Other Core Features Such As; (Character And Weapon Modifications As Well As A Crafting System) That Yet Again Works Similar To Fallouts Scheme And Has A Consequential/Karma Progression System For Each Of The Colony Group[s] You Join along Your Travels Across the Cosmos And Throughout The Game Making Your Decisions Determine What Playstyle Your Playthrough/Or Experiences Will Be. On Which Can Either; (Postively impact Or Negatively impact Relationships With Your Colony And Companions Thus Altering You're Players Stigma And Overall Percentage of Trust, Valor And Communications with them later On Down The Road Leading To Different (Dialogue Options, Responses, Outcomes, Paths and Endings) All Tailored Around How You Play And Yet Again Boils Down To What Choices You Make Aswell As The Colony You Decide To Favour Over The Others Aswell As A Vast Array Of Difficultly Options To Choose From,  Stemming from: Very Easy to Hardcore ( Which Are Either Selected Upon Selection of Your Savefile, Or You Can Choose To Change and Tweak The Difficulty At Any Point Throughout your Playthrough, But  , So Be Aware Of That before Proceeding To Do So And Be Sure To Manually Save At Every Given Opportunity) Especially On SuperNova Difficulty, A Mode that is Considered Hardcore And Will Hinder Many Core Mechanics Such As; The Ability To Fast Travel Anywhere (In SuperNova Mode You Will Be Faced With Many Limitations And One Noteable Limitation Is That You Are Only Prohibited To Fast Travel And Manually Save On Your Ship And No Where Else On The Map, Aswell As Always Making Sure To Eat And Drink (Similar To Fallout New Vegas Hardcore Mode) Keeping Hydration And Hunger levels to Maximum Capacity At All Times, Aswell As Avoiding Any Additictions As You Are Also Limited To certain Perks And Become More Prone To Substances And Other Symptoms Such As; (Additiction to Caffeine, Drugs And/Or Alcohol Abuse) Just To Mention A Few That Will Drastically Change You're Characters Inability To Function Properly.Companions Are More Susceptible To Dying And You Will Not Be Able To Revive Them If They Die And Will Be Dead Forever With No Chances of Bringing Them back, Unless you Have Save Files to Fall Back On incase Of Such Events. (Pro tip: Best to leave them on The Ship, Unless Your Doing Companion Side Quests On Which I Heavily Advise Decking Them Out With The Best Armour And Weapons You Own in You're Inventory As Well As Setting Their Passive to Far To Avoid Any Unnecessary Deaths If Venturing Out, And yet again Remembering To save Frequently When You can)Armour And Weapons Break More Quickly, Ammo Becomes Less Easier To Obtain (Thus either relying on Vendors or Looting are The Only Feasible Options) Enemies Deal More Damage And Can inflict Certain Elemental Damage As Well As Making You Crippled Or Too Staggered To Move, These Are Just A Few Hindrances You Will Come Across on SuperNova Difficulty, And That's What Makes The Game More Thrilling And Exciting to Play, Perhaps On You're First Or Second Playthrough, Personally I Started Off On SuperNova difficulty from The Very Beginning, Going In As Blind As I Possibly Could And Did One Full Playthrough To Get The Best Overall Experience, And Boy Was I Not Disappointed!Would I Say This is Better Than Fallout?  No, But The Game itself Deserves it's Own Distinctional Merits and Praises, Other Than Being Labled As A Mimic imitation Of Fallout, And I Do Truly Believe This Game Deserves A Sequal. DLC Adds An Additional 20-30hrs of Content (Which is Not Too Bad Considering The Main game is about 50-60hrs in length Depending On How Good You Are) Also The DLC is Ram Packed With Fresh New Quests, Weapons, Character Items And Cosmetics, Also An increase in The Player Level Cap And More Unique Perks to Unlock And New Planets/Locations To Explore And Colonies to Discover.On The Whole The Game Runs Smooth And Is  (Story Rich, Has Stunning Visuals & Graphics, And Most Importantly You Can Play it On The SteamDeck Under The Lastest Proton Compatability Tool) I had An Absolute Blast Playing This Game From Start To Finsh And Would Highly Recommend it To All if You Can Pick it Up For A Decent Price, And It's Essentially Fallout In space!What's Not To Love?

Best played by finding the cool stuff on your own while on your way through the main quest, otherwise might be better suited towards more playthroughs vs. getting a bunch of side quests done in one go.- No way to SORT ITEMS when storing them in lockers on your ship. The storing UI is all sorts of weird. Normally if you try to break down an item in your inventory, you'll get a prompt that asks if you're sure you want to perform the action. If you do that while trying to store items between inventory -> container, the breaking down is instant. It's also kind of too easy to Take All from a container if you're not careful.- Not a huge variety in loot. Maybe there are more sidequests to get science weapons (I found ~5 on my first playthrough), but those are basically the only unique weapons you'll find,  also not necessarily the best weapons if you don't spec specifically to use them.- UNBEARABLY dark whenever it's night.
