_childDocuments_.review: MY FULL LONG-WINDED REVIEW IS OVER HERE:-> It's way too long to post here, so I'll chop this Review up a bit.COMBINED INTRO - UPDATED on 07-15-2023:So, in case you missed it - The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition (PC version for Steam) is in the current July 2023 Humble Bundle with a handful or so of other games for $12...and still is, right now. I loved this game (The Outer Worlds) on PC Game Pass, in its OG Version - and well, I think I'm gonna like this version too (Spacer's Choice Edition). Can't wait to check the DLC's too.  So, on my RTX 3070 8gb VRAM desktop PC - which also has 10700KF, 16GB RAM, Multiple HDD's & SSD's, W10, BTW - I can run this at 1080p with 55-60fps. So, I can max-out The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice no problem. For some reason - probably b/c not everybody has high-end GPU's, I'd guess - the game is set to Medium by default. Game runs no problem at 60fps when locked there, So, yeah - it's running really well, since it's been patched-up (namely since version 1.3, according to many online). Just be aware, this game can utilize 6-7GB VRAM no problem at these Ultra maxed-out settings. So far, so good on that rig. [SNIP] ADDENDUM - MORE ON PERFORMANCE = 07-08-2023:Performance update on my Gigabyte laptop (R5 5600H, 16 GB RAM, 6gb RTX 3060, 1 TB SSD, W11). So, it runs really good even on my 6gb RTX 3060 laptop. Eats around 5-6gb VRAM on laptop on the regular. Still, most of the time - it's 1080p60fps Ultra settings with FSR On. Sometimes take hits when saving and/or transition to new areas for the 1st time - but eh, this ain't often. Turning off FSR - yeah, performance at Ultra goes to crap with bouncing all over the place b/t 25-60fps; FSR saves it at Ultra & keeps it stable. TOW: SC is a blast & I'm still going here, some say 20+ hours in.[SNIP]ADDENDUM #5 = COMPLETED - 07-13-2023.So, I have finished also the base-game. Took around 59.8 hours in total overall after everything, with all the DLC's finished & the base-game. Yes, you should do the DLC's before you hit the "Point Of No Return" final mission(s) & that sequence of stuff - as the game does incorporate decisions you've made from DLC's into the base-game's ending, at the very end in the Epilogue/Credits sections. Regardless, my point still stands from the TOW OG version of the base-game: a lot of what happens at the end does, in many ways, feel a bit rushed & also is setting up for inevitable The Outer Worlds 2 (which I so can't wait for!) for part of the ending(s). Also, at least w/ my decisions in this playthrough, it didn't really feel like there was a big-bad as a face to really be say a Final Boss/Encounter to - unlike say the awesome Eridanos DLC (in which that DLC also has the best boss fight in the game). Despite that w/ the base-game & its few missteps, that's all still very minor.Many of the other end-stuff w/ the final permutations & ending(s) all is still very satisfying b/c it wraps up a lot of the story for your companions, factions, certain specific characters & any locations you made decisions about in particular in this game, in a fashion with a slide-show & narration like many other legendary RPG's have done - think like Fallout 1, 2 & NV; Arcanum; NWN: Hordes; DA: Inquisition's Trespasser DLC; and I'm sure there's many more if I could think of them. Let me add this: the base-game's content is still great for the most part here. If you want that Fallout 3/4/NV type of gameplay & combat (and much more refined & contained, I might add), Mass Effect style galaxy-travelling, and satire & comedy galore - TOW: Spacer's Choice certainly delivers a great game in that style & vein, which I'm sure many were looking for after Fallout 76 (ouch).And let me mention this, while I'm at it: the DLC's are at the very least really good. In particular, Gorgon DLC is the most action-packed type of Fallout 3/4/NV type of gameplay & has a good story with some twists - so if you want more TOW, that's here; and it's pretty good. Eridanos DLC goes in the other direction and focuses more on investigation, story, Lore, Choice, making Deductions (on who did the murder & why) - and is easily, IMHO, the best DLC of the two by a mile & is quite special; it feels much more unique & the investigation stuff adds an excellent element & variation to the game. Regardless, all of the DLC's are packaged here in Spacer's Choice right out-the-gate, which is awesome.Regardless, provided you have the hardware to handle this version here - TOW: Spacer's Choice is an excellent open-galaxy & open-world shooter-RPG in the style of games like Fallout 3/4/NV, Mass Effect Trilogy/Legendary, and many others of that sort. The gameplay's great (and feels much better than say Fallout 3/4/NV); the story & character stuff for the most part's great; the DLC's are at least really good - and yes, Eridanos is out-standing.In the end, after almost 60 hours of gameplay, my verdict is in: this is a "Must Play" shooter-RPG that fans of these type of games (Fallout 3, 4, NV & ME: Trilogy/Legendary) have to play & is also an excellent place for many that never played this type of game to get into, since a lot of this is executed in a much more streamlined & extremely well executed type of fashion.

_childDocuments_.review: "It's not the best choice, it's Spacer's Choice!"  That little slogan will forever be burned into my brain thanks to this game.  Whoever came up with that jingle is a musical genius.  Definitely has the old 40's style radio commercial feel to it, but someone fits into this universe flawlessly.This game is an example of how to pose a choice between corporations and people.  On the one hand, corporations provide people with reliable jobs, and there were some of them that seemed legitimate in trying to do the best with what they had.  Obsidian is made up of the team that created the fallout franchise, and the design clearly shows here, but it's incredibly polished in its presentation.Narrative choices seem to have weight, and if you were able to stack enough points into various attributes, you could find more than one way out of a situation if you wanted.  Only thing I found a bit lacking was the gear choice, which may have been a blessing in disguise.  There are only a handful of weapons you can get, and fewer of those had variations for you to worry about.  It was somewhat nice to be able to find a loadout that you are comfortable with and not have to worry about every single weapon you pick up be slightly better than what you currently have but with tradeoffs.I skipped some of the side missions here because I was lazy, but the main story is compelling enough.  I'd wait until a sale comes along, and you can have a ton of game time for a good value.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Obsidian had the budget that was devoted to that craptastic abortion called Starfield? Id love to see it, but this is already leagues above Starfield its not even funny. Setting: Its new IP which is hard to break into, it comes over as goofy and alien at first, but on a little digging there is depth here. A key callout is the conversations with NPCs, very little looping in the dialogue, the 'smart arse' and 'idiot' responses are actually funny and are responded to appropriately. It does a little more than borrow from Firefly, its more of a homage to that great series. The ship, companions, scenes, easter eggs are all direct interpretations of the Serenity and its missions. A big plus in my book. Gunplay:It feels ok - the weapons do lack a bit of punch and I found myself ignoring the scissor, paper, rock resistance system and just brute-forcing enemies down. I have to say that the weapon degradation is a bit of a miss in my opinion, I dont want to have to repair my weapon after each encounter, which is the case as degradation seems to be based on weapon damage. Companions: Good companions, they interact with the choices the player makes and contribute (either meaningfully or whimsically) to quests and conversations with NPCs. It does feel like some are more fleshed out than others (Im looking at you Felix and Nyoko), but all their skills are useful. Performance:I see lots of complaints - I didnt have one technical issue. THe game does stutter on the title screen for 1-2 second on initial load, but thats it. Not one crash, not one framerate drop. For reference I was running the HD packs etc. I think sometimes people equate their lack of tech with technical issues - you cannot expect optimisation to counter the fact you are trying to run this on a potato. Quests:Some did seem to overstay their welcome, namely Eridanos DLC, but I didnt feel like I was participating in a random generic quest generator. I felt every quest had at least a reasonable context and outcome, very few felt menial. If you like FIrefly, wanted more (or something?) from Starfield and want NV in space - dont pass up this gem. 8/10

Not the best or the most polished one, but it's got a proverbial twinkle in the corner of its proverbial eye, amusing characters, and a variety more and less nice places to stick one's nose into. And it's even got a courtesy to have an ending (probably endings in plural, to be fair) that wasn't me just getting bored a deciding to do something else. I appreciate that when it comes to my games, I really do.So... looking for a single player first-person RPG with an engaging world to get lost in? This might be it. If you like Bethesda's Fallout-series, this definitely might be it. And now I'm just rambling. Have a nice day... or night... or whatever time it happens to be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for July 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before August 1st, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Not Obsidian’s best.The Outer Worlds came out four years ago and then released an improved edition earlier this year called the Spacer’s Choice that comes with all the DLC and improved graphics.  We have what should be an Obsidian-tier story, with combat and speech crafting that fans of the Fallout or Elder Scroll series should recognize and enjoy.  That’s the idea of the game.But the result is weaker.  The Outer Worlds has a great first planet to explore, and then feels like it copies and pastes that conflict to a bunch of other levels that feel uninspired.  The environments are weaker, and the writing seems to fall off a cliff, and that’s while hammering a really weak message over and over for most of the game.  The locations are also tiny, and there’s nothing to discover or explore.  It’s a little depressing because this was Obsidian's big chance and it stumbles.Pick this up if you want an OK Bethesda-type game.  It doesn’t have the size of other titles, and most of Obsidian’s other titles are better written. This got a lot of credit when it came out because it wasn’t as big a mess as Fallout 76 was at the launch, which came out at the same time, but if we take away the comparison Outer Worlds is average.  Not bad, but not as good as people made it out to be.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of good and bad going on with The Outer Worlds.  The game feels like it has huge potential to have a living world the rewards exploration and leads you to meet interesting people.Straight from the get go the game sets the tone of the universe.  It doesn't take itself seriously.  It is an incredibly silly collections of corporate dystopias.  The main focus of the game is the dialog interactions with the NPCs.  Nearly every line of dialog in this game is comedic or sarcastic.  Sadly, I am not a fan of this style.  It is reminiscent of the saying 'throw enough mud at a wall, some of it will stick'.  I know this is a major point in the game but there is too much dialog and fluff.  What can be answered in a sentence is answered with a paragraph.  This isn't a few here and there situations it is every time to talk with anybody.  You will probably spend more time in a town chatting with the few NPCs you can talk to than you will going out and doing the task they are asking of you unless you just skip all the dialog.The game play outside of the dialog is actually pretty pleasing.  There is stuff to loot and things to shoot.  You'll probably have a bunch of extra junk you don't need taking all your weight.  Terminals that will reveal that pretty much everyone in this game is either a piece of ♥♥♥♥ or being manipulated.  The areas you will explore have good level design.  Maybe I'd like a pathway here or a ladder there but overall I like the zones and actually go out of my way to check the little corners and behind the buildings.Like I said there is a lot to like and dislike.  There are no moments where I felt in awe.  I like only a handful of NPCs and find the rest to be annoying. The worlds are just okay.  Wish that people were actually out and about going about all this business that is supposedly happening.If someone asked me if they should pick this game up I'd suggest watching someone else play the game on twitch or YouTube then if you want to get it to wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea behind this game was quite clear: make a better new Fallout game than Bethesda, which after troubled Fallout 4 and Fallout 76 releases didn't seem like an impossible task, particularly since it's the same studio that created Fallout: New Vegas, widely regarded as the best 3D Fallout game. Unfortunately, while Outer Worlds is not a bad game per se, it is fairly boring - mostly due to bland combat and unimaginative level design. As it is now, the game is only really interesting for the first 1-2h at most, and quickly becomes a chore to play through as it doesn't introduce any additional noteworthy new features or ideas.Good stuff:+ Writing is pretty decent and a lot of NPC lines are genuinely funny+ Quite polished, very few bugs - in stark contrast to Fallout games+ There's nothing particularly painful or frustrating about this game - it's just an inoffensive and unimaginative take on the Fallout recipe.Bad stuff:- The combat is extremely basic and there's only a handful enemy types (mostly various variations of bandits, robots, lizards and monkeys - that's like 90% of the roster - and they're shared across different planets and other locations). As a result it gets boring really quickly which is definitely not a good thing in an action RPG. Moreover, the vast majority of weapons does not feel satisfying to use and lacks character, making for an off-putting action experience.- The locations look ok visually but are fairly small and mostly lifeless (apart from scattered groups of enemies from one of the 4 above categories). There's also entirely too much loot scattered around, so very quickly you'll be overflowing with ammo, meds and other items. instead of asking yourself "which supplies can I spend to get through the next fight?" you'll be constantly deciding which items to sell/break down because you're at the weight limit (even with the limit-increasing perks)- The main plot is not terrible but it's presented in a way that makes it seem like there's no urgency and the whole thing is pretty inconsequential, like the main character is going for a sunday stroll and they may or may not kill some enemies along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: So while this is a similar style game to Obsidians previous masterpiece Fallout New Vegas, Outer Worlds mostly fails to live up to that high standard and it got a lot of flack for that. However I went in with my expectations lowered and found it to still be an ok game.It does have a lot of weaknesses. The setting, main story and most of the characters are bland. Combat is mostly boring and you fight the same types of enemies throughout the game. Unlike New Vegas there is no real motivation to explore as most of the points of interest in each map are usually tied into a quest so there arent any interesting, off the beaten track type areas. The whole corporatism on steroids in a space colony could have made for an interesting theme but instead the game just beats you over the head with "haha look how bad corporatism is".That said there are some things that are done well. The role playing elements are pretty good and levelling certain stats can open up dialogue options or give you a alternative way to complete a quest. In fact many quests have alternative ways to complete them or at least some parts of them.While the main quest line wasn't that good the DLC's are quite a big step up in quality and I really enjoyed Murder on Eridanos in particular as it has an interesting setting and story. If the standard of the DLCs can be carried over into the sequel, hopefully it will be a big improvement.Also I know the Spacers Choice Edition got a lot of criticism for having problems but in my experience they at least seem to be resolved. My system is closer to the minimum specs required but I was able to run the game on a mix of medium/low settings and didnt encounter any crashes or bugs.Overall if you are going into this game expecting another Fallout New Vegas quality game, you will just be disappointed. But there is still some enjoyment to be had if you lower your expectations. I got this game really cheap on a discounted Humble Choice which meant I was generally happy considering that I didnt pay much for it. I probably would have felt more aggrieved if I'd paid full price, so I'd definitely recommend waiting for a good sale discount if you are interested in picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: After all the (mostly) justified criticism of this Spacer's Choice Edition, I feel it's necessary to set the record straight on this game. Having played several games on the original version, and having spent some ten hours on this "next-gen upgrade", it seems obvious to me that the latter is not only worthy of interest, but also the best entry point for anyone wishing to discover this RPG.Firstly, The Outer Worlds is an extremely underrated game, which is in my opinion Obsidian's best work and my favorite RPG from this studio. The adventure is very well written, the art direction is original and charming, and the gameplay is almost identical to that of a CRPG à la Fallout New Vegas: skills are numerous and useful, character development is well thought-out, quests offer multiple approaches and solutions, and the extraterrestrial universe, which mixes spaghetti western and traditional science fiction, offers a real retro-futuristic touch where capitalism and communism clash, and is extremely well exploited, from start to finish. The adventure is funny, moving, rich in choices that count, and perpetually invites exploration in very well-designed environments. For me, The Outer Worlds is nothing more than a refined version of Fallout New Vegas, with less fat and more substance. Honestly, that's all you need to know to get into this game.The Spacer's Choice Edition got off to a poor start on PC, but at the time of this review (July 2023), for me the game performs identically to the original version, but with undeniably enhanced graphics, particularly in terms of character modeling, which is far more polished and offers incomparably livelier dialogue. Given that we spend a lot of time chatting, it's very pleasing to note the effort put into facial expressions and the expressiveness of the companions, in particular.Another advantage of this Spacer's Choice Edition is that it comes with the two expansions to the original game. These expansions are really great, and considerably enrich the game's lifespan by offering new, perfectly realized locations and quests.In my opinion, The Outer Worlds is one of the best role-playing games of the last 10 years; this Spacer's Choice, while not absolutely essential for owners of the original, has brought me enough improvements to satisfy me, and represents an opportunity to further support developers who are proving to be among the most talented RPG developers around.If you're a fan of the genre and of Obsidian in general, I urge you to jump on this game regardless of its reviews: you could well discover one of your new favourite RPGs."You've tried the best, now try the rest!"

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically New Vega's prettier, but more boring sibling. The colourful and dystopian setting is engaging and doesn't take itself too seriously, which I personally quite like. However, the game lacks depth with regards to general gameplay, mechanics, systems etc. The included RPG elements are too few  and too simplistic to add anything of value to the experience: Adding skill points makes numbers go up (exciting!) and any "progression" with perks barely registers. The gunplay is average, i.e., it's not noticeably terrible while also being nothing to write home about. The companions are well written and interesting and do all the combat for you so that you actually don't want to take them with you. Did I mention that there is basically no variety in play styles because of the lacklustre implementation of RPG elements? To make matters worse, the inventory management is an atrocity because there is very little in the sense of management. Obviously, I want to compare Outer Worlds to Fallout 4 as well. They both play pretty much the same, but I did find OW’s story and pacing much more enjoyable while playing. It’s also a more condensed game and, as such, less sprawling and thus mercifully devoid of useless fluff content. Conclusion: If you’ve never played Fallout 4, but really want to, play this instead. You could also just skip this game completely and your life would still be the same.

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of mediocre. It's not bad, but it's not as good as any of the first-person Fallout games (Fallout 3 / Fallout 4 / Fallout New Vegas).I've played through all those games multiple times. After completing the main game and the DLCs included in the Spacer's Choice Edition, I have no real interest in playing it again. That's still a bit over 70 hours of play, so I feel I got my money's worth.It's a variety of things. Combat is OK, but not great. Balance is generally off - there are a lot of unique or special weapons that are strictly inferior to the standard weapons you can buy anywhere. The writing is  decent, but not memorable. The theme of the game is evil, incompetent corporations. That's funny for a while, but it gets old after a while. It's basically the same joke in the various computer log entries, told over and over.The RPG elements seem underdeveloped compared to similar games. Skills matter some, but it feels like pretty much any character build is going to play the same. All too often there are dialog skill checks that don't really matter - you get to the same place whether you have sufficient Persuade or whatever regardless, you just gain a tiny amount of XP for passing a skill check.Still, I can't really give it a thumbs down. It's not like it's actually bad, just not what I'd hope for.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was an option somewhere in between "recommend" and "do not recommend", I'd probably have chosen that... but I also only paid $10 for this thing, so maybe I'm more inclined to go easy on it. It's absolutely not worth the full price, and I'm kind of on the fence as to whether or not it's even worth the $10. THE GOOD:- The updated graphics look very nice for the most part, and make the environments feel more vibrant. While the visuals in the original are perfectly fine, I did often find myself wishing they had a little more "oomph", which this version provides. I've seen people complain that it's over-saturated, but personally I prefer the richer, more dramatic colors and lighting. - There are also small changes to the environments themselves beyond just visual effects- there's more foliage, some of the structures (rocks, buildings, etc) have been tweaked, and there are added objects in the environment to make the world feel a bit more immersive, like piles of firewood stacked at the edge of campsites or red algae growing on the wreckage of a crashed spaceship.- The level cap has been raised to 99, which is a bit much considering the game was originally meant to be beat at level 30-36, but it does eliminate a somewhat frustrating aspect of the original where certain skill checks (particularly the ones required to get the "best" endings of each DLC) were so high that you'd either have to pour a bunch of points into those specific skills in preparation for only a handful of late-game skill checks (while 90% of the other checks in the game could be cleared at much lower skill levels) or pay a hefty fee to re-spec your character. It also makes it easier to become overpowered, sure, but that happened anyway even back when the level cap was 30 because it was never a particularly challenging game to begin with. THE BAD:- Performance, performance, performance. While my copy isn't suffering quite as badly from performance issues as some others (possibly because I got it after the patch) when I first booted up the game there was serious stuttering, lag and other performance issues. It got a bit better after I exited and re-opened the game, but there's still some noticeable stuttering, flickering, minor visual glitches and texture pop-in when reloading saves. Load times are also noticeably longer than they were in the original, where I can run all settings at max with zero issues. Also worth noting that I haven't gotten past the starting area yet, and I've seen people say that the performance issues get worse in later areas, so it's possible that the relatively minor issues I'm currently experiencing are just the beginning. - While I prefer the new graphics overall, the lighting in interior zones (towns, buildings, etc that require a load screen to enter) seems a lot darker than the original for no apparent reason. This is especially obvious with NPCs- some of the characters whose faces were previously illuminated by the warm orange glow of whatever light source they were standing near are now cast in shadow, as if the light bulbs in their shops and homes are no more luminescent than those glow-in-the-dark stars you put on the ceiling of a kid's bedroom. - Despite the player's level cap being raised to 99, enemies and items appear to still be capped at around 30. EXP gain also appears to be unchanged, meaning the average player will likely only get a handful of extra levels higher than the previous cap by the endgame, unless they mindlessly grind for dozens of hours. In summary, this is NOT a complete trash fire with zero redeeming qualities, at least after the patch. If you've got the original game and its DLCs and are curious about the remaster, ten bucks isn't bad- especially since the issues become apparent very early on, so if you're unable or unwilling to tolerate them you'll probably know before you've exceeded the time limit for refunds. Otherwise, though, just play the original or wait to see if they release another patch that properly fixes this thing, because it's certainly not worth $40+.

I was crashing to desktop every time I got the thomas dialogue from Parvita very early on, but verifying integrity fixed it completely. I've had no problems 24 hours of game time later. I think it would be pedantic to blame that on the game anyway.I think many people who are giving ♥♥♥♥ reviews, with less than an hour game time, have possibly written the game off before trying it much like I did before. _childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the RPG genre, I was excited to play The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition. While the game has received praise for its unique setting and engaging narrative, I found myself disappointed with a number of aspects that prevented me from fully enjoying the experience.One of the biggest issues I encountered was the game's lack of depth and variety in gameplay mechanics. The combat felt clunky and unresponsive at times, and the character progression system was shallow and uninspired. The dialogue options, while well-written, often felt limited in scope and failed to truly impact the story in a meaningful way.Additionally, I found the game world to be surprisingly empty and lifeless. Despite the promise of exploration and discovery, I often found myself wandering through seemingly endless stretches of generic environments with little to no interesting interactions or side quests to break up the monotony.Another concern I had was with the game's technical performance. I experienced frequent frame rate drops and texture pop-ins, which detracted from the overall immersion and enjoyment of the game.Overall, while The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition has its strengths, such as its witty writing and vibrant art style, it falls short in terms of gameplay depth, world-building, and technical polish. I would recommend this game to fans of the RPG genre who are willing to overlook these shortcomings in favor of a compelling narrative, but for those seeking a more comprehensive and well-rounded gaming experience, I would suggest looking elsewhere.

Even in the dlcs you are still fighting the same sh*t just reskinned.If you can't handle how old they look, i guess you could play fallout 4(worst of the main line fallout games but i would rather play that than this.) or you could get star field on gamepass(no idea on it's quality i really don't care about it)Pros1.The voice acting is overall decent.2.Overall decent art style.3.The graphics are fine.4.The facial animations are decent, i rarely cared about this until i played bg3 & especially as a dragon born, i was so used to talking to & looking at dead clay faced npcs.5.The gun play is overall fineCons1.There is no vaulting/climbing on terrain. Which i find utterly stupid for any game not to have it,the game didn't come out in the 2000s & this should of been a very basic feature to add.Why is this a issue? because to lose access to vantage points & makes traversing more annoying.2.It changing your skin tone to a darker one just because. I like to pick the whitest one out there & make it a melee juggernaut to fit one of my characters but for w/e reason i can't be that character in this game."it doesn't matter, it's a 1st person game" if it didn't matter then why did they let us customize them at all? My characters look amazing regardless but they ruined him. so now i go with my sniper.3.I hate that you can't loot everything off a corpse & it's reliant on rng. Doesn't matter which game does this, it's a sh*t mechanic that the devs were too lazy to balance around.4.Npcs do not react what so ever to you shooting near them but if they see a rat, they'll lose their sh*t.5.The hardest thing about supernova difficulty is making sure you're companions don't get knocked down because they will not get back up & you'll have to reload to revive them until you hit lvl18 so you can get the right perk to get them back up,Doesn't always work.6.The base game runs out of new enemy types reeeeeal quick.7.The companions aren't great what so ever, they are bland & will never leave you unless you tell them to get the f*ck off your ship. They do give you passive bonuses to skill checks but that would be the only reason you bring them along due to that & perks you can pick up that increases those bonuses from them.8.I know i bought this game to waste time to hold me until lords but i expected to get some joy out of the game but no i'm forcing myself not to rush through it to kill as much time as i can.9.They give you a robot companion & went "have fun" Maybe i could if i was allowed to upgrade or customize him in anyway, No he is just another bland robot companion in gaming.10.Known bugs that break quest that have existed for years. Example The "Electric Fling quest" where the robot is stuck in the waiting cycle.11.The majority of enemies scale to you're level, which is always an annoyance due to it ruining the power fantasy. I feel no different than i did when i first started the game.12.The character progression is sh*t,There aren't any abilities to work for, it's all worthless perks that make you take/deal more damage from/to specific enemies.13.You can't mod science weapons, They are just gimmicks.Peril on gorgon dlc 1/5Overall a waste of time that you'll figure out the whole plot in a matter of mins while adding in no new enemy types, just reskinned things you have already fought all game with a added feature on them.Murder on Eridanos DLC 3/5Actually for a "who done it" it's not that bad & reuses the assets from the base game better than the peril dlc which was just bland all around but this dlc has it's interesting moments & the best weapon in the game imo, shame i put it off until end game. figured it was going to be out right trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a decently fun game that shows Obsidian still knows how to make a good action/RPG game. While there are some unique elements, I could not help but notice a great many things borrowed from other big titles, namely Fallout and Borderlands for the most part. The gameplay, while fun, felt a little one-dimensional and could use more variety in terms of mission types and enemies. Most of the missions involve travelling to an location, fetching certain items, and killing some baddies in the process, which became repetitive and boring rather quickly. Story wise, I liked the amount of companion interactions and the overall vibe of the story line. However, not every other decision has to be intentionally constructed as a moral dilemma, which I think put a dent in the overall experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Its pretty good. The Outer Worlds plays into the good old Fallout humour, but in space. It is kinda fun, the story is pretty interesting. It starts slow, the middle parts are pretty much the best part. The DLCs are really good. The ending just lacks impact. I'd definitely recommend it on a sale. The characters are great, especially your ship.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I heard a lot of good about the game. It's good, but not as great like many people present it to be. The Outer Worlds is giving me this vibe of Borderlands, mixed with Bioshock's madness with a dash of Fallout: New Vegas. You can clearly see there was a lot of ambition and work put into this game. It seems the only lacking there was, was the time and money during the development.PROS:-Characters design is great, very interesting interactions.-World design is very well done, especially the stations. You can see how nothing works the way it should and age is taking a toll on them. -Very interesting idea for character's skill progression. CONS:-Side quests are boring and make you either go fetch an item or kill a unit.-Guns feel very boring, science guns are the only ones that  bring something extra to the table but I feel they are still very under powered.-You kill over and over again the same type of enemies. For the amount of enemies you reap through, a bigger variety would help the game a lot. I give it 7/10 - Get it at full price if you have nothing to do with the money or wait for a good sale.If only Obsidian was the studio behind Fallout 4, we wouldn't get the crap served by Todd Howards. I am looking forward to see if The Outer Worlds 2 will fix the issue and have more to offer than this part. Hopefully Bethesda/Microsoft will not be forcing Obsidian to do stupid stuff that will ruin the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Played the original version a while back and loved it but I never had the dlc, so I figured it'd be nice to get the full upgrade. I was hoping the upgrade would truly be an upgrade, but as of right now it's the exact opposite. The first patch to come out didn't do a thing for the stuttering and constant frame rate dropping for me. I wouldn't waste your money until an actual fix comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I've played and have beaten The Outer Worlds three times now. This version (Spacer's Choice) I beat the game relatively fast by being a solo psychopath, melee, and handgun only build and beat it within 4 1/2 hours. Which is definitely one of the fastest ways you can play this game and 2 out of my 3 playthroughs have been psychopath (Which is more enjoyable in my opinion).I do like the aesthetic and graphical design but a lot of the gameplay just seems like a butchered down New Vegas, which Obsidian was also behind. Don't get me wrong, it's a good game and I'm sure The Outer Worlds 2 will be much better and more polished. Do I think it's worth $60? No, This version comes with all the DLC which I have yet to experience fully. I've only dabbled in Peril on Gorgon, and Murder on Eridanos just a tad bit. They just didn't seem appealing to me. I would highly suggest getting the other version of The Outer Worlds. It's half the price normally, and when it goes on sale you can get it cheaper. I only got this version because it was apart of the Humble Bundle monthly games. So would I recommend it? Yes, but only if it's on SALE.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast! What a fun game. I had no technical issues, so I suppose that any bugs people had in the past are now fixed. I was hesitant to play it due some mixed reviews, but I'm so glad I did. Full playthrough with all quests and DLC took me 70 hours. Speaking of DLC, Murder on Eridanos was the best DLC I ever played and maybe even my favorite part of Outer Worlds. All in all, awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game is entertaining, it suffers greatly from the typical "anarchist v. reformist" trope so oft-presented in fiction, be it video games, film, or literature.  It's boilerplate, unrealistic, and is a tepid, false reflection of complex social conditions.  Where is the nuance?  Where is the option to support the workers that divorced themselves from the corporations and those that work for the corporations?  The game is rife with middle-class politics and exudes a sophomoric and politically vapid approach to politics.Notwithstanding these major flaws, the game's role-playing mechanics are fun and I am more or less enjoying the gameplay and quests.  Oft-compared to Fallout: New Vegas, though a pale imitation, it's leagues ahead of Fallout's 3, 4, and 76.  Play the game - it's fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition

_childDocuments_.review: People are not being hyperbolic. I loved The Outer Worlds, but these upgrades aren't doing it. Ran the original from start to finish at 1440, at a crispy 60 on Ultra, this one's barely hitting 60 on low, it's not just a hardware issue. There's some severe optimisation that needs to happen. If you're gonna buy it, buy the original, this is a mess. I'll update it if it's ever given any optimisation patches, but things are looking bleak at Private Division, and I'm not holding my breath.Update: As of 14 June 2023, the game has received several patches, and I am having no problems hitting 60FPS, the major stutter is gone, and everything appears to be fine so far. I've only replayed for a bit, but I do think the devs have made enough headway that this is worth grabbing at some point if you have never experienced the game, or want to see the new graphics, and enhanced level cap. I dunno about full price, but they more or less fixed the game as far as my computer is concerned.

_childDocuments_.review: Humble Bundled! This is your bog standard Obsidian rpg as far as i can tell, and it's worth playing as of date stamp.  game obviously is set up for multiple playthroughs, because there are perks for playing solo and you don't get perks before you hire your first person in most cases, so... If you're not obsessively completing every task like I am game probably holds up to a couple/multiple playthroughs.  Naught else to add, really.  Most of the choices aren't tricks, I re-did some things just because games like this train you to assume normal answer = bad, but you don't get much of that here.  Most of the times, I reloaded, checked, and then reloaded and did what I originally wanted.  They sneak one or two things in but it's more not-obvious-solutions if you haven't done enough work.  Still got the DLC and Tartarus to chug through, so we'll see if I have anything to add.  Doubt it, though.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the best choice its Spacers Choice.I keep wondering if this product that carries the Spacers Choice brand name was actually created at the Spacers Choice R&D Gaming Labs. Does strapping on a Spacers Choice logo automatically make your product a large pile of canid poop or is it the shoddy world of corporate greed that ultimately makes it so. I'd like to think that this was just a big "April fools" joke for the company like some one said " Hey you know Spacers Choice products are s*** right? So what if we put Spacers Choice on our game and f*** it up! That would be hilarious!" I mean the marketing actually does itself at that point.I've experienced stuttering which I can only assume are helpful attempts at making sure we concentrate on work and not take in the scenery. Because as a member of the Spacers Choice family being more productive is better than touching grass. I also have noticed that in my playthru I can only see the name and stats for one weapon, the Spacers Choice starting pistol. Ammo count and any other info on any other weapon are simply shown as stats for that pistol and when i put a different weapon in the rotation it will only have ammo for the clip that comes with it and when I buy more ammo the only weapon that registers is the starting pistol. Talk about brand loyalty and promotion. Even in the vending machines I can only see the stats for one product. No matter what I hover over or click there's always only one product that shows stats. After accepting the fact that I was stuck with the starting pistol for the rest of what would be my short life I decided to take a walk and came across 3 marauders. 2 I killed and the third shot at me twice, then approached me and then apparently forgot I was there because he then started looking for me. I was standing in the middle of the road with no cover around. Maybe those rounds he fired at me were to get my attention to see if I had any quality Spacers Choice products for sale?Most people are on about the stuttering and I'll agree that sux bad but there are a great many more things going on with this "remake" that people are experiencing. This truly deserves the Spacers Choice label.You've tried the rest now try the best-Spacers Choice!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Dishonored and Borderlands I really liked this game and it manages to be it's own thing. The setting is interesting, the characters are nice and the story (DLCs included) is pretty good. I have seen complaints related to performance and writing and I must partially agree. Nonetheless, the game is beautiful and I recommend it to at least give it a try.The performance issues didn't affect me that much and they're definitely not game breaking, but overall it could've used a little more polishing.The story (and the dialogue), while at times may seem written by that chick from Hellsing Abridged  - link related), is alright. I really enjoyed playing through it and I'm content with the choices I've made. The game doesn't take itself too seriously and once you get past the fact that you're doing a lot of fetch quests and most of the dialogue options (not all of them, some choices matter) are there just as filler content to get key items or get new objectives, you can focus on the story and your decisions.All in all, it may not be the best choice... but it's Spacer's Choice. I am looking forward to the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is mostly just fine. There's nothing egregiously bad about it, but it's also not particularly memorable either.It starts out well enough, but eventually you notice the theme is just the same joke stretched over 20-25 hours. It gets to the point where it makes it hard to care about what happens to anyone in the story, and almost everyone comes off as so incompetent that it makes you wonder how does their society even exists.You do get several options for how to resolve quests, and some of the companions have their moments, but the fact I mostly remember the cleaning robot that shouts slogans while fighting might tell you something about their lasting impact.Still, if you're looking for a relatively basic RPG and you do enjoy its brand of humor, you might end up having more fun with it than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much enjoyed this game. The setting is fun, there were some good stories and well-written dialogue, companions were interesting, and I even mostly enjoyed the combat. Took me about 50hrs to play through the main story and both DLCs on my Steamdeck. The game ran great, looked great, and I only had one crash.My main gripe with the game is the tinkering mechanic, which made me ridiculously overpowered at the end, even playing on hard, and I am generally not good at action games. This also meant that the many consumables cluttering the environment were completely useless and I ended the game with enough ammo to wage a minor war. I also didn't use any of the science weapons since they seemed puny compared to a tinkered out standard weapon. This made the game way too easy at the end and took most suspense out of firefights. Overall, I still had a very good time, though.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a brilliant  10/10 RPG, but a good RPG with silly humour in a dystopian worldYou can tell that this game was made by the New Vegas developers. It also reminds me a little of Mass Effect 1.Speaking of its flaws: - Performance is fine with (!) FSR2 set to quality. I did not notice any visual artifacts when using it.- What bothers me is the lack of a flashlight. The Spacers Choice edition has improved the game's lighting. It looks fantastic, but some areas are just too dimly lit, making it difficult to see.- The variety seems a little low: armour, weapons and enemies, but to be fair, I'm still enjoying it.Quests, companions and exploration are carrying this game for me.It's not the best choice, it's spacer's choice!While the game offers a lot of settings for HUD, conversations and other things, thanks to the Unreal Engine you can adjust even more with the ini. file, such as:- better AA- less texture pop-in- HUD customization- Ultrawide support (with corrected FOV)

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game to be amazing. From the reviews I see not everyone did.The Spacer's Choice Edition takes much beefier hardware to run. I didn't have much problem with it--a couple lags here and there--but it seems to be a big complaint. If your system struggled with the original Outer Worlds, it won't run Spacer's Choice.Having said that, the story and game play is fantastic. I've been through it twice in two weeks and will start a 3rd tomorrow. If you like character driven stories, you'll like Spacer's Choice.  If you're a sweaty, shoot-em-up who just wants to skip everything...might want to move on. This game has a lot of dialogue, and a lot of reading...most of which actually provides clues to what you're doing. It's in your best interest to form the relationships with your crew and to read logs and email messages. Many of the scenarios have multiple outcomes, it's up to you to find the best one.IMHO better than the Bioshock franchise...and I never thought I'd say that about anything. P.S. Parvati is absolutely adorable. Listen to her, she's right every time.

_childDocuments_.review: They fixed the performance issues with the Spacer's Choice version. PROS: The game is heavy into choices and consequences, even if the consequences are minor. There's a lot of attention to detail in what you've done, who you've spoken with, who's in your party during dialogue, so your experience will feel very "you". Dialogue options are great. Not only do you use the standard skill checks of Persuade, Lie, and Intimidate, but you also get dialogue options based off other skills, such as Perception, Intelligence, Medicine, Engineering, etc... How you handle problems is done well. One example: MINOR SPOILERS: I was asked to collect a bounty on a criminal, as a side quest. I picked up another side quest asking me to fix the radiators on a ship. It just so happened that the parts were being guarded by the guy with the bounty. Normally that would be a shoot out, but I was built for dialogue, meaning I first persuaded him to roam around his guarded area freely, then, to get the parts, I lied and said they were leaking toxins. Overall, the guy was a bit crazy, but also kind of endearing, so I felt weird about finishing the bounty on him. But I talked to him about it anyway, and was able to negotiate a deal that basically faked his death. Not only that, my perception came in handy, and I found out the person who put out the bounty was potentially an ex girlfriend (depending on who you believe). The characters are really well done up. Ashly Burch is her usual stellar self, and the rest of the actors do a great job. They all have something going on with their backstory as well, and it does take some time to figure out their motivation. They don't just open up immediately, or by pestering them, the game takes its time letting you get to know your crew. Your hub is you ship, akin to Mass Effect. However, the crew is more lively around your ship. You'll see them going about their business, doing what they prefer to do. Whether it's working on the ship, studying in their room, or hanging out in the galley talking about space operas, or debating religion. That same interaction happens during exploration, with the characters reacting to each other in many ways. CONS: I haven't played the DLC yet, but the base game is smaller than most other games of its type. Not by a lot, but the ending came up sooner than I anticipated. Even at my leisurely pace, it took me around 40 hours. BUT, with the DLC, it sounds like it will now be between 60-70. The exploration areas are small, but packed. The combat is lukewarm. Some gunplay feels great, some not so much. There are elemental effects like plasma and electricity, that are great for finding weaknesses. I will say, it's incredibly satisfying to take out a robot using a shock cannon. Also, the AI seems to have improved in the Spacer's Choice edition. You can also set the AI of your crew, so they don't go charging in and getting shot up. VERDICT: Anyone into ARPGs should pick this up. Obsidian always does well with making you feel like your choices really change the course of the game, and this is a prime example. The story itself is decent, but how it's delivered is great. So many NPCs will stand out, and there's a lot going on to uncover. SPACER'S CHOICE UPGRADE?I owned the game and all DLC, so I got it on sale for $8.50, which I have found to be WELL worth it. If you already have everything, and just need the upgrade, I would say it's worth it. The lighting overhaul is really noticeable, and the graphics mostly look better. This version actually runs smoother on my PC than the original game. If you don't own the game at all, the Spacer's Choice version is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this is a review of The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition, it should be noted that this was my first experience with the game, so this review encompasses my whole experience, not just things specifically added and/or improved in the Spacer's Choice Edition.During the period of roughly four years between the game’s initial release and my first playthrough, I’ve heard a lot of negative and disappointed opinions on this game. It ranges from being just a pale imitation of Fallout New Vegas to being outright bad and boring. Honestly, I can see where these people are coming from. However, I can personally say that I had a perfectly fun time with The Outer Worlds. Don’t get me wrong; it has a lot of shortcomings and missed opportunities, but we will get to that. However, as an overall experience, it is a perfect example of your typical 8/10 Obsidian AA game.- This is a well-crafted universe whose creation was guided by a clear vision and idea of what it should be. You may like it or not, but the universe is consistent in its overarching lore and foundations.- Perfect over-the-top humour. This is a parody of your typical cyberpunk settings, which revolve around overly exaggerated corporate greed and soullessness. I had my fair share of chuckles. Although this is highly subjective, I have seen many people find this type of humour boring and lazy. If it clicks with you, you will have a good time. - An excellent roster of companions with their unique personalities and worldviews. Some are better written than others, but none of them feels bland or generic. I had a fun time talking with them and learning about their personalities and worldviews.- The designs of the worlds you will be visiting are colourful and diverse. Although there are some repetitive elements, you will nonetheless have a lot of fun exploring them. Each location feels unique and exciting, and you will learn about its history, as well as its current problems and secrets.- The game is rich with content and various side quests, ranging from fetch quests to massive mysteries spanning multiple worlds and connecting significant characters. All of the side content is intriguing, and in terms of gameplay, it allows multiple approaches to solving them.- The music is absolutely fantastic, especially the main theme. Obsidian never disappoints with its soundtracks, and the same goes for the voice acting. The soundtrack evokes feelings of space mystery but also epic adventure.- Both DLCs are absolutely outstanding in terms of locations, stories, new lore, and new items. -  Staying true to tradition, facial animations are rather bad, especially so for a game where you will spend a lot of time having face-to-face dialogues. Characters barely show any emotions through facial expressions and mostly just stare blankly at you.- In terms of gameplay, the game fails to properly develop your companions' specific roles. I’ve played the game on hard settings and have been picking which companions to bring on a mission based on role-playing, not their skill set. It always feels like anyone would do the trick; I've never felt like I need to carefully choose which ones to bring for the task at hand.- While companions are mostly fun, it seems that their personal stories were not adequately fleshed out. Their companion quests are more like some smaller side missions rather than full sub-plots with broader implications. They are not particularly dull per se, but they could have been better and more significant. Nevertheless, they are still fun little stories that add to their personalities and backstories.- Combat is definitely a mixed bag. While I didn’t find it bad, it can sometimes feel outdated. There’s also a problem of balance. I played the game on Hard difficulty, and it never felt particularly challenging.- The world-building and side missions were much more enjoyable compared to the main story. It starts off strong with an intriguing premise and with a lot of things going on, but then it kinda loses its momentum and fails to answer many questions at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had the opportunity to be a really satisfying game with solid storytelling, but it's immediately bumbled face first into the sort of problem that plagues games like this. In the conflict between a corporate monolith and workers trying to be independent and live their lives, the moral decisions should come down to Morality vs. Practicality. How much do you believe people can get by without overbearing corporate presence providing a flood of convenient consumerism. But like so many other games, Outer Worlds wants there to not be a flatly correct moral answer. So you'll find a quest where the spacers choice corporation is being as casually cruel and back-breaking as a corporation is wont to do, but then they'll add some arbitrary and unconnected moral wrinkles to the worker's side of the issue to make it seem like a real moral debate. In the interest of evening out the moral debate, they have some important figure on the side of the workers just have some sort of crude moral failing that just makes the entire decision frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: While I can still wholeheartedly recommend this game, it should come with several asterisks. This game is a series of incredibly missed opportunities. If one were to describe this game in its entirety, the statement, "It's a playable three-way between the TV show Firefly, and the games Fallout: New Vegas and Mass Effect, but doesn't manage to get any of those things perfectly right". It attempts to strike that balance decently in a lot of ways, but it is held back, by its total lack of innovation in any real capacity. The game's Traits & Perks are terrible. None of them are notable or interesting in any way and it makes the process of leveling up feel completely lateral and unrewarding.The game has some great writing and can really strike a chord for anyone who's ever had a job that they hated, but that great writing doesn't support the game's lackluster overall story. I can genuinely say that this game's plot is so completely uncompelling that I do not think the main campaign is worth completing a second time. The game's companion quests, faction missions, odd jobs and side-quests, however, are typically quite engaging and I do enjoy many of them. There are systems in the game that are clearly only in it because 'that is the way it was done in a previous game'. Genuinely, the systems for item weight, item condition, crafting and leveled loot are completely meaningless and utterly at odds with one another, when experienced as a full package. There are other games that manage to successfully balance some of these systems, but The Outer Worlds cannot meet that standard. Tactical Time Dilation is complete garbage. Games like this will typically be lifted up by their "This ability makes me special" button and TTD is absolutely the least interesting, least worth using "unique ability" I've ever touched. Compared to V.A.T.S or Shouts or Tech/Biotic abilities or The Darkness or even that whip from Bulletstorm, TTD is the absolute bottom of the barrel when it comes to the super ability button.The area designs go from being "charming and thought provoking" Edgewater to, "I have seen this same building many, many times" Monarch. There are no locations as fascinating as Omega/Illium or the Citadel from Mass Effect or with as much visual personality as Boston from Fallout 4. By the time I got to Byzantium, I was over all of it.The characters and core combat loop are the big saving grace for the game. Again, the writing shines through in the form of companions and NPCs and shooting enemies is a fun time, but this needed way more than that to stand on. The DLC locations are markedly better than the base game's and they are very weighty expansions of the initial experience.In conclusion: While I recommend it, this had so much more potential and I hope to see it shine in the sequel. Also, as stated in my initial impression below, I have had no performance issues, but have experienced a couple of bugs that required me to reload saves, including doors that should not be locked or NPCs not activating when they are the next step of the quest.Initial Impression: Diving back into The Outer Worlds, having played the initial release, I was unsure of what changes to expect for this updated version. So far, it has exceeded my expectations on all fronts. I have experienced no issues with performance on my rig. The gameplay is smooth and it is a joy to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: is a remaster of the base game  that includes all of its DLCs with visual overhauls. When the Spacer's Choice version first launched, it was a horrible mess as I've heard and seen. At that time I didn't play it, however in the July 2023 Humble Choice, this version of The Outer Worlds was among the listed games and I didn't even hesitate to pick it up. It was an amazing deal.The Outer Worlds was developed by Obsidian Entertainment, the same people who made Fallout New Vegas, so they had knowledge on how to make their own RPG Shooter. - Character creation as in every RPG.- Leveling up in this game is kind of unique, with each level up you get skill points, pretty basic stuff, and at every 2 levels you get a perk point to unlock various perks. What makes it unique is the introduction of flaws, as you progress in the game, lots of stuff will happen to you and you will get pop up windows that says whether you want to accept a flaw and for that you get a perk point. For example your character might get a flaw that makes them more vulnerable to physical attacks, either you accept it or reject it. It is totally up to you, but if you do accept it, it is permanent.- This version of the game is gorgeous and it runs perfectly well as of now. I haven't played the earlier versions where the game suppossedly ran terribly and stuttered.- The story and the world-building of the game is actually really intriguing and also comedic in a way.- Companions are pretty great, my personal favorites were of course Parvati and Max. (You can take 2 companions at a time) Your companions can aid you with their unique skills in combat, interactions and even in dialogue they always have something to say and differs from each companion you take with yourself. Oh and they also have their own companion quests. I find these pretty neat.- The combat itself is great, various weapons are to be found and bought which you can upgrade with modifications or tinker with them to up its stats.- Reputation system that further elevates the RPG feel and makes you feel a bit more thoughtful as to what you'll do with various factions as they'll remember your doings.- Various outcomes in side missions and even in the main quests I believe.- Your character has their own unique ability, 'Tactical Time Dilation' that slows down time, yeah that's it. It can be helpful at times and can be improved with perks so that it lasts longer and actions don't drain it as much.- Locations are all unique and always have something new to explore and discover.- The 2 major DLCs,  and  are pretty good and worth checking out. They both offer up to 6-8 hours of plus gameplay with interesting storylines that further expand upon the lore of The Outer Worlds and its world.- The game is not fully 'Open-World', it is 'Semi-Open-Worlds'. All locations are just bigger maps with smaller maps inside of them (Buildings and such)- You yourself cannot pilot the Unreliable (Your Spaceship), but I don't find it a con as the game doesn't focus on it. It's just a hub for yourself and your companions.- The game is quite dialogue and text heavy (In the case of terminals), which can be a let-down for some.- I played the entire game on Supernova difficulty, which is basically 'Very Hard' and also introduces hunger, thirst and a sleep meter. These are actually great to even further elevate RPG mechanics, BUT you cannot make manual saves on this setting. It is absolutely awful that you cannot, the only way your game saves is whenever you enter another area, because that's when the game makes an autosave. If not, autosaves are extremely rare occurences. It is something for something.- There is a mission in the Peril of Gorgon DLC that I couldn't finish as it was bugged completely and halted my progress on that side mission, but other than that, there wasn't anything game breaking or any bug that would have prevented me from enjoying the game. The Outer Worlds is actually a pretty good game. I found it really enjoyable and I was intrigued by the World.. or Universe? it was presenting to me and I'm actually eager to see more of it in The Outer Worlds 2! I can recommend it during a heavier sale as this version is quite expensive on its own.I made a video to showcase the atmosphere and scenery of The Outer Worlds. Hope you like it!

There are a couple of issues with the intractable objects still emitting that blue outline for a second after you pick it up, but other than that the graphics are a much needed improvement of the original.But I'm only 7 hours in, so I can't attest for how the upgraded level system is or how the rest of the game looks, especially on the DLC. But I can say, if you're contemplating getting this version or the original + DLC, get this version.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I did get the game from the Humble Bundle, so the price I paid for it was aproximately USD 1.50I will try my best at not spoiling any twists or outcomes.I'm writing this Review immediately after finishing my first playthrough of the game and it's DLCs. I will give separate Reviews for the DLCs below. At this moment, my play time is 43.1 hours.First of all, this is not a "hard" sci-fi game, It's a space opera. Technology works, just "because". People a weird (just like in real life), but so is the universe and everything in it. The graphics are gorgeous. I played the game on my 8 year old rig (buy once but buy quality and take care of it, it will never let you down!), and apart from the "Peril on Gorgon" DLC, I had no issues with framerates or graphics (on Ultra settings, my PC started slightly heating up after an hour or so)The Main Game:The story has a nice twist on usual sci-fi settings, Corporations are in charge of practically everything, but there's no "free thought" allowed, so their slogans and programs increased to truely ridiculous levels, their staff are mere "Huminerals", and  it lead to hilarious slogans like "It's not the best choice, it's "SPACER's CHOICE!" among many others.The areas mostly feel huge when they need to, and cramped when they have to. I spend around 8 to 10 hours in the starting area alone because there is so incredibly much to discover, admire and run away from.Character creation, especially without any hints, is a bit of a gamble, I chose to play an Elevator-Attendent, Very high intelligence, high perception and stealth, and it generally worked out fine for most encounters. I only respec'd once during the whole game, after I was done with the starting area, because I spend a lot of points on combat skills that weren't neccessary.The quest in this main story line are often fetch quests, but the fact that the world is so well designed and full of flavor (lots of notes to read) makes it bearable. The level of encountered enemies was well fitted to the progess, so even when I messed up otherwise the game did not punish me overly for it. There are quests in game that will decide the ending, which is a slideshow with a bit of narration, but you usually are warned by companions that your decision "will have consequences". In game, those consequences often only influence your standing with different factions in game, and are quite forseable. You probably will not be able to be friends with everybody, but you also don't have to. You can also "murder-hobo" your way through Halcyon, leaving only death and destruction in your wake. But often, letting people live is more fun.If you ignore the DLCs (which you are free to do without consequences), you should be able to reach level 30 when the game is going into the final encounter (again, you will be warned explicitly), which is more then enough to build a character able to finish the game if you don't try to spead out too much. The game is a loot orgy, there's incredible amounts of stuff from trash to consumables to weapons lying around, and some might even be taken without stealing it. There are some (but not many) instances where loot is locked in an skill 150 lvl box, but I did not make an effort to go back to loot those, since my ship was already bursting from all the stuff I "liberated""Murder on Eridanos" DLC:This was the most fun and at the same time most disturbing (at least to me personally) DLC i've played in years. The Location is unique, the events you become involved in are weird, the Murder is mysterious and you get a gimmick weapon that talks to you and helps you find clues. The humor of the base game continues seamlessly into the DLC, I laughed a lot (when not totally freaked out) whilst on Eridanos.I decided to play the DLCs after finishing the main story line until the "point of no return", so most of the enemies were pretty easy to deal with. That became even more true after I "liberated" the science-gatling gun, which continued to be my most favorite gun until the very end of the game.THERE IS BODY HORROR in this DLC, i'll not spoil anything but it really made me uncomfortable, and it worked amazingly well.As for the story, I personally found it a bit shallow, but as I mentioned before, this game is a space opera, so it wasn't annoyingly obvious. There was one twist I didn't see comming, because there weren't any hints to it (and it's called "the best keept secret in Halcyon" later in the story), but the main twist was so obvious, one must be blind, deaf and slow not to get it ahead of time, there were moments, when I wanted to scream the solution in peoples faces, but the story didn't allow it. It was very much fun though.As with the base game, the graphics were amazing, and often there were moments when I simply stopped to smell the roses. (until the roses tried to eat me)There was one quest I actually finished, yet it stayed as unfinished in my quest log; the only bug I encountered so far, and It was a really minor one."Peril on Gorgon" DLCUnfortunately, this DLC did not live up to my expectations. First of all, the tone of the game changes drastically, it suddenly becomes much less humorous and a lot darker then before. No Body Horror as in "Murder on Eridanos", but sudden serious drama and moral issues. Also, this was the first time I encountered serious framerate issue, to the point where I seriously considered simply skipping the DLC and finishing the game without it being done. It got better later on, but especially in the outside areas of Gorgon, there were hard skips that often got me killed, even though I was so far above the enemy I hardly made an effort anymore (shoting them with my sniper rifle from the hip, not going for stealth headshots anymore, or not going for stealth at all), As for the story, I did also not really care, It felt very stilted and shallow to me, as was the whole planet Gorgon. Ways were artificially elongated and sprinkled with enemies to make it longer, but as I said before, combat was only an Issue when the frame rate dropped suddenly. I said before that even fetch quests were fun in the main game and "Murder on Eridanos" but in this DLC, I got so bored that I even ignored side quests intentionally. It was simply too uninspiring for me to care. And even the main plot of the DLC has multiple fetch quests leading you to places that are clearly just rehashes of older areas, to the point that I found the same "secret" passages leading to the same side areas.As for the story, again the main Twist was not forseable, but I was not that far of with my suspicion anyways. I have to admit that at this point, I only wanted to get it over and sleepwalked through everything. Quite the disappointment in my opinion.Conclusion:It's a fun game, not worth the 60$ price tag, but if you can get it for 20$ by all means you should give it a try. Apart from what I mentioned on the "Peril on Gorgon" DLC, I did not encounter any performance issues, serious bugs or soft-locks in the game, and it's story and world building are on the level of the original Fallout 1 and 2. It will take some time for me not to hum the corporate jingles when standing in line at the store, and overall I consider this game a very nice experience.I probably will put it away for some time now to give it a rest, but chances are that in a couple of months or so I might just get back to it and try a different approach character wise.10/10 - Definately worth the time, and a candidate for another playthrough later on...

_childDocuments_.review: Just about everything about this game is mediocre. I don't think anything about it is bad, at all really, but the game is something that is arguably worse: BORING. Too many quests are fetch-quests without much (if any) combat, meaningful exploration, or decision making.Companion quests are boring, requiring tedious back-and-forth fast travel for character development in a VERY mixed bag of companions. _childDocuments_.review: If games had a definition for mediocre and average Outer Worlds would have been used as an example. The game manages to do everything right while being complete devout of spirit. It’s a soulless Fallout clone in space. If you like that type of games – perhaps you may enjoy it. I didn’t.  - AverageLike the rest of the game the story is as generic as you can imagine. It is set in Halycon – an Earth colony far in the future where corporations rule and profit is everything. The theme is not that bad but the execution is. The “we are fighting the corporate patriarchy” can be felt throughout the whole story. I don’t want to spoil the story but as I said absolutely nothing is worth remembering from it. If you expect it will happen it will happen. Companions are worth mentioning. Mostly with the fact that you will not remember any of them 3 days after you have stopped playing the game.  - AverageOuter Worlds is a first person RPG similar to Fallout 4. You have your main stats which contribute to you secondary skills to which you assign skill points (10 per level). And you have perks. Did I mention it is a Fallout clone? I think I did. Than you go around killing stuff and looting everything which is not nailed down only to realize the inventory menu is awful and it will take you ages to sell and that you will not need almost any of that stuff. There isn’t much variety of enemies, there isnt’t much variety of weapons, there is a huge variety of armors (mostly useless). The game also have it’s own alternative to V.A.T.S where you slow down time and hit critical spots. Again absolutely nothing original.  - Very HighThe whole theme of the game is “Lets fight the corporate patriarchy” and it shows. About 95% of the “leaders” in the game are females – whether they will be a Faction leader, a warehouse foreman, a security chief or a head doctor. There will also be an underling around whose whole dialog will be to point you towards “The BOSS”. The other 5% of who are males the game strongly encourage you to displace for the “good” endings. The game also deliberately doesn’t have different hairstyles for males and female models. And for some reason the most common generic long hair is missing as an option.  - GoodNo problems here. Games runs smoothly, everything is voiced over. The game is ugly as hell though and many of the colors are deliberately muted. When they have copied Fallout they also copied the awful Bethesda character models and facial animations I guess… – Great DealThere are two DLC’s for the game which both come with the Spacer’s Choice edition of the game. Both DLC’s are long enough and worth playing. Game was on Humble Bundle and even Free on Epic so it will goes on regular sales from now on if you want to buy it. Definitely not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Visually fantastic, solid sound and music, good UI with the exception of item stats being very unreliable, mostly bland story with some humor, combat is oddly boring even at highest difficulty. Game would have been great if the story wasn't so bland, and the combat was engaging. But the story is mostly written for kids with a few exceptions. The combat is usually just you fighting maybe 3-5 units at a time, which takes little-to-no effort; it's almost like there is no combat. A shame to see such a visually stunning world wasted on childish writers and mechanics. Honestly, it reeks of a female-run project.
