_childDocuments_.review: After $elling out to Epic, Ob$idian finally allow$ u$ $team-pea$ant$ to $pend our money on their game with a 1-year delay.I'm going to be hone$t: that annoyed me $o much that I wa$ glad to $ee negative review after negative review appearing for thi$ game. And I had my mind $et on tra$hing the game a$ well, $pewing bile with glee.The truth i$, once I got to play the game I actually enjoyed it ju$t enough to leave a po$itive review.(I'll stop with the $-signs now. That will made the text better readible and I believe my point has been made.)---Outer Worlds is usually described as "Fallout in space" and that is honestly the best description you can get. It is Fallout 4 ... set in space! As if Fallout and Mass Effect had a baby. An ugly and slightly retarded baby for sure, but a baby nonetheless.The post-apocalyptic setting of Fallout has been replaced by a space colony that is falling apart, ripe with corruption, where nothing works and competing factions rule the lands. It's almost like being in Russia. But other than that: the dialog-system, the combat, the options to build your toon and even the feel of everything are "almost" as you'd expect from Fallout. The biggest difference: it is never on the same level as Fallout is, it's always "almost there". Just not interesting enough, just too bland, just too forgetful etc.The largest difference is probably the inventory system. At its hearth, Outer Worlds is a looter-shooter. Loot drops in abundant quantities and you're constantly on the lookout for an upgrade. Unfortunately the inventory lacks a decent filter-system so you have to sort through your MASSIVE inventory manually. I found this so annoying that I stopped bothering after a while. seriously: go grab a mod to increase your carry-weight to 1 million or so and forget about it. You'll come to enjoy the game a lot more.Another large and unfortunately lacking difference is the writing: its very one-dimensional and that is a problem in a supposed-RPG. The game grabs every opportunity to tell you how evil corporations are. Not exaggerating: in about every dialogue a mention will be made of the greed of "the board", or how companies are a bad thing, how bureaucrats ruined something and how glorious small groups of independent labourers are.When the game is not spouting its communist propaganda, it shows off a rather weird sense of humour. That in itself would be a positive thing, were it not that the humour is present in everything. Nothing is taking seriously, everything is made fun of. A guy just died? someone'll laugh about it. Community dying of hunger? They'll joke about it. someone beliefs have just been trashed? Oh L0L, 1'm s0 rand0m!!To quote a famous clown: it's "only funny when the sap's got dignity". There is no dignity to be found in Outer Worlds, I'm convinced that Obsidian doesn't even know that word. When there's no drama to set off against, humour stops working. There are 2 or 3 moments in the game where you'll laugh, but all the rest of the time the quips fall flat and the jokes and "why so serious" attitude come across as grating and childish rather than funny.A final point to mention is that the game appears to give you a lot of choice, but in the end there are no real choices. Choices don't matter: picking party X over party Y will not impact you. As a matter of fact there's only 1 choice in the entire game that really will make a difference, because you'll get slightly different quests. But other than that: the slideshow at the end of the game (that you'll probably not even pay attention to because it is so boring) may differ a tiny bit, but that's all. I really was expecting better from Obsidian.---The version you’re looking at here is the "spacer's Choice" edition. It's the original Outer Worlds + all DLC + performance improvements and reshading. The reshading is the biggst point of difference and something you'll love or hate, since it makes everything look very colourful.I never encountered performance issues, but it does appear that the spacer's Choice edition has in effect higher requirements that the base game so if you only barely meet those requirements it's something to look out for.---Summary: an OK game, but not one you'll remember. I hope the sequel will be better.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Outer Worlds" is a remarkable game. I LOVE it  so far!!!!!!Story so far is great also. "The game is set in an alternate future where mega-corporations have colonized space.Me, the player, i was revived from cryosleep by a scientist named Phineas Welles, who is on a mission to save the colonists of the Halcyon colony from corporate tyranny and the effects of a devastating chemical called Adrena-Time. It allows for various playstyles, whether you prefer a stealthy approach, diplomacy, or all-out combat.The game also has a unique sense of humor. The game dose not take it self to seriously all the time, and i love that. Great music and soundtracks. incredible graphics and style, especially at day. "The Outer Worlds" excels in its retro-futuristic art style. It blends elements of 1950s Americana with futuristic technology, creating a unique and visually striking world. I do see the *hate* for this game. but i did not play older version, ppl say this like remastered one runs horrible, i dont know maybe its fix. I have 0 problems so far. Playing the max on ULTRA 1080p 60fps, runs great.  In summary, "The Outer Worlds" is a fantastic action/RPG, Its unique setting, humor, gameplay, make it a MUST-play for fans of the genre and fans of Fallout games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a rethemed version of Fallout (the 1st person versions). There are some gameplay difference - e.g., a time-dilation system replaces VATS, and the lack of VATS makes the combat more real-time than in Fallout 3 or 4 - and the setting is more sc-ifi (but still post-apocalyptic) but the gameplay, setting (despite the retheme) storytelling are overall *very* similar. I really enjoyed all of the Fallout games, and I am enjoying this as well. I don't think it brings anything novel to the series, and the need to travel among worlds is more of a minor annoyance than a nice new addition, but overall this has been a good experience well worth my time as a fan of the Fallout games.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game through Humble Monthly. Always wanted to play it, so I'm excited.Start the game. Medium high settings.Runs "OK-ish" with frame stutters, opening cutscene audo/video is completely out of sync, then the game crashes soon after character creation due to running out of video memory, after just a few minutes of gameplay.Ok... Reduce settings, try again. Looks significantly worse. Runs at a resolution reduced from 1080. FSR in "balanced".Still only runs "OK-ish" with frame stutters. After a few minutes crashes with video memory error again.Oh.... Kaaayyy......... Set everything down to the lowest setting. Game looks AWFUL! Unplayably awful, almost.Performance hardly improves at all, and after a few minutes the game crashes with the same video memory error.Tried for hours to get this game to work properly, but never even got that far past the tutorial missions.I could play Cyberpunk 2077 reasonably well.What the hell is wrong with this game?

_childDocuments_.review:
The Outer Worlds: Spacer’s Choice Edition includes the base game and all add-on content as the definitive way to play the beloved RPG from Obsidian Entertainment. This remastered masterpiece is optimized to be the absolute best version of The Outer Worlds… even if you choose to play this critically acclaimed RPG as the absolute worst version of your character. Lost in transit while on a colonist ship bound for the edge of the galaxy, you awake decades later only to find yourself in the midst of a deep conspiracy threatening to destroy the colony. Explore the various planets and locations of Halcyon, including the mysterious Gorgon Asteroid and delightful distilleries of Eridanos. As you encounter various factions, all vying for power, the character you decide to become will determine how this player-driven story unfolds.
In the corporate equation for the colony, you are the unplanned variable.

name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical
detailed_description: ORPHEUS DLC OUT NOW About the Game In a modern fantasy world, college dropout Grace is granted the power of a Muse - power she’ll need to find out the truth behind her predecessor’s death before time runs out. You’ll decide who Grace allies with, who she can trust, and who may betray her in this beautifully hand-illustrated roleplaying musical. Written by David Gaider comes Stray Gods - an urban fantasy tale of finding your place, taking charge of your fate, and discovering answers. Your choices will change the endings, as well as the path you take to get there. A compelling story of hope, self-discovery, and forging your path. Adventure, love, and songs await! Charm, negotiate, or strong-arm your way through their world as Grace, playing through original, fully interactive musical numbers composed by Grammy-nominated composer Austin Wintory, Tripod (musicians Scott Edgar, Steven Gates, and Simon Hall) and Eurovision Australia’s own Montaigne (Jess Cerro). Fully orchestrated and performed by an all-star cast, you’ll feel as though you’re right there on the stage. With thousands of potential variations based on your choices, you’ll craft the soundtrack to your own one of a kind musical experience. Choice and consequence built from the DNA of RPGs - no two playthroughs are the same. Delve into a hidden world of mythic Greek gods and monsters as you get to know a cast of hilarious, enigmatic, and compelling characters. Forget what you know about these mythological beings - in Stray Gods you’ll forge friendships and find foes with many familiar names, but not so familiar stories. Play as star and stagehand as you determine the story you want to tell through conversation and song. Find friendship, love, or yourself. Build friendships with mortals and Gods alike. Stoke the fires of romance if you so choose - explore, pursue, and confess your love with four potential paramours. Decide who you want to be through every choice. David Gaider’s storytelling and characters come to life with performances by an all-star cast, with the likes of Laura Bailey, Mary Elizabeth McGlynn and more cast members across video games, television, and Broadway. A musical for video game lovers, and a video game for musical lovers. With all the comedy and tragedy of your favorite stage shows, Stray Gods is a tongue-in-cheek and heartfelt reconception of Greek mythology combining what we love about contemporary musical theater with video games where character and story take center stage. Collaborating with some of the best in music, broadway, television, and games - Stray Gods is a debut not to be missed. FOLLOW US ON STEAM Want to be in the room where it happens? Follow us on Steam to stay up-to-date on our development journey and don’t forget to wishlist us.

_childDocuments_.review: Decently good game. I don't believe this is actually a roleplaying musical though. It is a basic visual novel with slightly more animated scenes and some musical numbers. The music wasn't my favorite part of the whole thing, it does feel like more of an after thought instead of the primary focus of the "musical". I did enjoy the story and am excited to get all of the achievements but I would not recommend spending anything over $15 for this enhanced visual novel.Edit: If you plan on doing the achievements then I would say this game was worth $20. The alternative songs are high key impressive. I am glad this game exists and it was worth the time I spent getting the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Stray Gods, which I bought on a whim as I like narrative games and musicals, so this seemed like an interesting prospect that (as far as I'm aware) hasn't been done before. I'm going to get the negatives out of the way first, as they are few and some a bit nit-picky. Firstly, I thought the game would be animated, but it is a series of still frames that occasionally change as characters speak or move, which kind of disappointed me and sometimes looked weird when they were singing, but I was happy with the quality of the artwork so I can live with it. Secondly, the flow of the songs was sometimes jarring and I could on the spot think of better lyrics they could have used in certain situations; few songs had that 'punch' that I would expect out of a musical production (bearing in mind this is what the game is relying on), especially when compared to shows I love like The Greatest Showman, Les Miserables, Hello, Dolly!, etc. I honestly think something like Stray Gods would work wonderfully well on the stage, but they would need to provide more solid music throughout. That being said, they did have player choice to consider. The character you play, Grace, can work with one of three personalities (Charming, Kickass, and Clever), which affects the dialogue and flow of the songs depending on what you choose. This adds to replayability, but it can leave the songs feeling muddled sometimes. I really think it is a subjective matter however, so whereas I felt some of the songs were lackluster, others might find them to be really good. Don't let my opinion put you off!Now, the phenomenal: the voice actors put their heart and soul into this game, and it really, really shows. The singing is flawless and the emotion put into the characters is as good as you can get in a game of this type. Think back to Telltale's Walking Dead series and you get the same if not better quality. The only thing that could have made this better would have been animation over still frames but I'm aware the developer probably had a budget and this wasn't considered to be as vital as everything else. When you get the likes of Laura Bailey, Ashley Johnson and Troy Baker among many others to do the voices, you can see where the budget went, and it works for that reason. The story is decent and keeps you guessing right until the end; I am on my third playthrough right now as there are four characters to romance and paths I haven't taken yet in the story, so you can be sure that you will get your money's worth here. Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend if you like narrative games and musicals, as Stray Gods truly brings something unique to the table that can only get better in future if it has the support it needs!

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm.I wouldn't describe this as a "role-playing game".  At all.  It's basically a comic book visual novel, balls to bones.  There are branch paths and the like.  But there's no real "game" to this.I'll say "recommended" only because it's a decently good story and the execution is fairly well done.  But this should have been a FMV game.  Voice acting is decently good - the females are all standouts, the males...eh, Pan is the only real true standout.  Apollo isn't bad, but he's written poorly.  I did everything I could to pair Grace with Pan because Pan was just THAT convincing.Aphrodite was a complete let-down.  Maybe there's more with the branches, but the "good" branch was disappointing.The songs are...well, unique.  Minotaur had me dying laughing though.So what was bad?  Well...some of the branching was not fulfilling.  There's are multiple branches where you turn your back on an ally, but they're still forced on you later on instead of properly avoiding you or being negative.  This is because all three characters are basically foundational to the story flow - so the illusion of choice is lost when this happens.  You realize that your choices only matter for achievements and not true story branching.I'm also never a fan of girls dressing like dudes.  Kills the immersion.  Persephonie can be excused for...obvious reasons, but yeah.So...as long as you don't approach this thinking it's a role-playing game, and recognize it's nothing more than a comic book visual novel that tells a story, it's worth the playthrough.  But don't expect anything beyond that.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this game is quite short (I started it on a Friday night and finished it before the end of the same weekend), I still highly recommend it for anyone looking for a good, interactive "urban fantasy" story without having to slog through combat . The story was a fun, modern take on Greek mythology, while dealing with some serious concepts in a thoughtful manner. I appreciated that it aimed for a mature story that could be appealing to people looking for something a bit more in-depth than you might expect from a game based on mythology.  I love mythology, by the way, but I also appreciate thoughtful stories. Stray Gods calls itself a role-playing musical, and you do play a role, but you don't get to create your own character. You do get to control what type of person the main character is, however, by choosing different dialogue options and different approaches to situations. Even though the game is pretty much all dialogue (no walking around, extremely limited interaction with objects, no environmental puzzles, etc.) and some singing, it still feels very interactive. You are not just watching the story unfold passively. There are "dialogue puzzles" where you have to use your character skills and your own observational skills to read the situation and pick the best response to get the result you want (or you can role-play to the hilt and pick the option based on how you are playing the character). The graphic novel visual style works well for the game, but I was surprised at first that it was not fully animated. It was more like frames of a graphic novel that moved slightly. Once I got used to it, it didn't detract from my enjoyment of the game, and it probably meant it played better on my older machine. The voice acting and dialogue were good as well, which helped keep it engaging. There were a few game play features I really appreciated: you can pause the game at any time (and adjust settings), you can skip lines of dialogue if you are replaying a scene, and you can turn off the dialogue timers. A few things about game play I didn't like were: you can't save whenever you want (although the pause feature almost makes up for that) and you can't skip songs if you are replaying a scene. So if you are looking for a highly interactive, mature story with multiple paths through an urban mythology setting, then this is a good match. I found it a really enjoyable change of pace and very worth playing. It really goes way back to the concept of "interactive fiction."

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this on the store and went 'a musical rpg? what does that even look like?' and I watched the trailers to see what the game was about and as it says on the tin, the game sure is a musical with a huge list of big actor names both in and out of the voice acting field. As a fan of choice based games and an enjoyer of musicals, I decided to pick it up.I played through the story for the first time in one sitting with I think going for what I'd say was the best endings for the characters involved or at least some of the more positive endings as it looks like there are many ways paths can deviate base on choices (the story will still get you to the end regardless of what is picked). I also played it while a friend watched and she was also very happy about the whole experience as the story is one of the strongest bits about the game with a fun way to reimagine how Greek Gods would fit in a modern society and the struggles they go through with living thousands upon thousands of years. As the plot involves a murder-mystery I won't get too more in depth about the story but it sure was a highlight.The other major highlight is, of course, the voice acting. With the likes of Laura Bailey and Troy Baker taking up the main protagonist and a central character respectively, you are in for a treat of the years. Each of the characters are voiced so well that it feels like you're watching a television show which the only real downside to both the spoken and sung portions of work is sometimes the audio mixing is a bit weird? Sometimes characters sound like they're talking in another room one line before their volume normalizes again and it sounds crystal clear. Some highlights of voice work for me were Grace, Apollo, Persephone, Pan, Athena, Freddie and Hecate.The other major point of enjoyment is of course the musical aspect. The main character, Grace, becomes a Muse and her power is to make other people sing what's in their hearts and the most major choices happen during these song segments, which depending on the lines you pick can change the song's lyrics and vibe and what a character will decide to do at the end of it. While not all of the songs are totally memorable, a good portion of them are really catchy.While I recommend this game because I am of the target audience for such a game (an enjoyer of choice based story games with a emphasis on story and characters who also happens to like musicals) it is still a rather niche game that won't be everyone's cup of tea at the full $30 price point. If you are a fan of these sorts of games and want to support the idea of maybe getting more unique games like this from the devs, buy at full price. If you still like the genre but don't want to commit to the full price or you're curious about the premise, buying on a sale would be best. But if you're someone who doesn't like choice-based games, musicals, or a combo of a two... I doubt this game will make you a believer.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is is a successful prototype, even if the odd cog goes twang now and thenStray Gods bills itself as a role playing musical. This might be a bit misleading to the more avid gamer. It is a musical, of that there can be no doubt, but some of us have a very specific collection of gameplay systems and tropes in mind when they hear the word role playing, and Stray Gods doesn’t quite manage to meet these expectations.You do play a role, that’s for sure, specifically the role of Grace, a charming college dropout and singing talent, who feels a bit lost at the moment, but will be pushed into a world of hidden gods, intrigue and music about 15 minutes in. The problem with the role play tag is that you don’t really get to tell the game who Grace is, it’s more like you can mix a certain flavor of protagonist into her, and then you make about 5 crucial decisions during the course of the story, and that’s it.Here’s how this works: During the many musical numbers (this is a musical, remember), occasionally the Bioware Dialogue Wheel(TM) pops up and allows you to choose the emotional direction the song will take. Unfortunately, at quite a few junctions the label and the color of the choice do a poor job telegraphing the consequences of the choice. Most paths through the game are worth taking, so the damage from unintended consequences is small, but still irksome at times.That is all the gameplay there is. Sure, there are a few dialog trees to climb, and a few choices outside of the songs exist as well, but at its core Stray Gods is interactive fiction, which means it mostly has to rely on the art and the story to mine engagement from the player.The art is strong. The character designs are very charming, nary a dud among them. Grace especially leaps from the still images, charisma and energy dripping from every crease of her leather jacket. The environments, though, are nothing to write home about: Sparse on details and color, they evoke the feeling of a set without committing fully to that vibe. But of most importance for a musical must surely be the cast, and here Stray Gods scores quite a few points. The main cast performs admirably. Honorable mentions go to Troy Baker and Mary Elizabeth McGlynn, but for me, Stray Gods is the Laura Bailey show. She carries the game with so much warmth and spunk and verve that the occasional bit player with less than great voice work is completely eclipsed.The story, unfortunately, wobbles a bit at times. It starts strong and finds a satisfying ending, but a few parts in the middle sag a bit, a few story beats loose with twists I can’t quite relate to and setups that can’t quite land the pay-off. As for the script: The dialog is sharp and witty, and all songs are at least inoffensive, with a few absolute bangers strewn in-between. Fortunately I was so invested in Grace’s story that the occasional story weakness failed to stop me.Stray Gods is a fascinating prototype for a new genre: It has quite a few warts and falls short of its full potential, but it is something new and fresh, unique and captivating. Fans of musical theater should not miss this, everybody else still can probably have fun with this game.TLDR: If the tag line “The first interactive musical” sounds intriguing to you, you will have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of how David Gaider writes characters from early Dragon Age days, so I followed him into Stray Gods knowing my emotions were gonna be absolutely wrecked. I didn't expect that to happen so early in my game experience, which just goes to show I forgot how impactful the stories and characters he writes are from the very beginning. This is a unique experience - it's a visual novel style RPG mixed with ROLEPLAYING MUSICAL. I'm still in awe at how the music has a life of its own, how it changes and creates a song and a story that's based on your choices. It's an indie game, so there's a few rough edges here and there, such as inconsistent sound design in some of the character's spoken voice lines (some are too quiet, others are suddenly too loud, and the reverb/echo effects added to the voices are sometimes too noticeable), some little stutters between different characters speaking, that kind of thing. Honestly, none of this mattered to me. Sure, I noticed it, but I was also extremely engrossed in the story and kept asking myself existential questions about what I would do if I were in Grace's situation, or even the other characters'.If you love RPGs for the story and characters, if you love musicals, if you love experimental stuff that's never been seen before, try it. I can't account for people's tastes, but a lot of skill and effort went into making something new and ambitious, and for me it hits exactly right.EDIT: for people talking about bugs, it's an indie game that literally just came out. There's bound to be bugs. I personally did not have any issue with the save files, but that's because I had played the demo during the summer fest and the save file from back then was kept, so when I started my game I started it on the second slot. That must have been an inadvertent fix for a bug I had no idea existed until I read reviews today. Before the game's saves are fixed, I'd recommend starting the game, creating a new game on one save file, then exiting and creating another new game on a different save file and you should be fine. Devs are working on the fix anyway, so it'll come out soon, but if you're impatient this is the thing to try.

_childDocuments_.review: "They tortured her. Nothing too extreme . . ."Unfortunately the writing is terrible. This would have been so much better if it was simply a story about real people with relatable lives. The flimsy Greek god ... theme is weirdly incomprehensible. Who did what to who now? When and mostly why? Things happen to the characters that seem important and profound but it's almost impossible to understand why. Why are they so sad and upset and dramatic? Because someone doesn't want to get reincarnated? Again? I think. The music is also flatly forgettable and the cues you get for choosing where the lyrics will go next are vague and unhelpful.And how do 2D images manage to stutter?Why is the main character played by Kristen Stewart? Why is Eros doing ASMR? Can Apollo just button his shirt? Is Freddie based on Heather from Crazy Ex-Girlfriend?I don't have a problem  with the diversity of the project in itself, but the story suffers for it. How would a paralysed person feel if they meet a god who doesn't even offer to make them walk again. Or do I misunderstand their godliness? I do, don't I? Another day, another god.I'm disappointed.For future games, it would help if the developers build a soundscape for each setting, just a distinct set of background noises to help with a little immersion. Might be a good idea to have the mouse pointer disappear during dialogue. And the interface could generally be better if you always consistently had to click just once to make a choice.Ultimately, if you like musicals and you like RPGs, this is not the game you were looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed the game, but it was not without several flaws. Here’s what was good:- inclusive and diverse reimagining of Greek characters in a BIPOC / LGBT+ lens- pretty artwork and character designs - appreciated the innovative part of making an interactive musical with a huge number of decisions that need to be made, much in the vein of Life Is Strange- being a fan of Greek mythology, I enjoyed the interpretation of these Gods However, I found a lot of the plot to be poorly written at times, a bit simplistic and predictable, which really makes the game not that compelling. It had a fun sense of humour but I found the story beats to not match up very well, and some of the songs were not very memorable. The animation is not constant, ie the characters move around like a slideshow. If you want to experience a queer silly visual novel with musical elements, this might be for you! Would be good to support it to encourage more games like this to exist.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Love the premise of the game, and the writing is phenomenal. Very fun and interesting story that I simply could not put down in my first run. As many people have said before, if this sounds like your game, it definitely is a game for you. My only critiques would be that some plot points aren’t explained very well, and from what I’ve read this is because some dialogue choices do a better job at explaining the topic, but they treat it as if you’ve heard that explanation. After finishing this game, I do have a few questions on the wrap up.Second, I would say some of the musical verses can be weak. I believe this goes down to your subjective taste. Personally, I liked a lot of that flavor as some of the characters who sing are portrayed as being “non-singers” roped in to the musical, and the lines are very off the cuff. I can get behind that, and I think it really adds to the story of the game. However, some songs, especially the romance songs, I felt could have been improved in their composition. It’s hard to describe without spoiling anything, but some central songs really stand out as phenomenally done with beautiful and unique compositions. However, many of the smaller songs, like those locked behind roleplay and romance routes, don’t seem as strong in comparison. Even so, this is an incredible game that i highly recommend. A lot of these issues I’ve pointed out can be overlooked as the rest of the game is a brilliantly fun time with many emotional moments.

_childDocuments_.review: This review may be a little controversial, but let me cook. I will also mention a few negative points despite giving the game a thumbs up. I think it is more important to tell you what is bad so you are not disappointed when something really bothers you.The game tries to be a musical, and it is - a bad one. Don't get me wrong: The story is fine, the singers are fine, the characters are fine, but the songs are just ... meh. Nothing sticks, nothing leaves a lasting expression except for fragments here and there. As soon as any song ends, it's gone from my head. After you hear "Loathing" from "Wicked" or "Let it Go" from "Frozen" for the first time, you can at least partially sing along the next time (okay, I just outed myself as an Idina Menzel fan). Here? Nothing. The mechanic of making the songs the "battle/argumentation system" works well, they just are not memorable at all. Not to mention the constant style changes mid-song when you change the "color" of your reply.So, here is the controversial part: Another reviewer called it a "woke-washing-inclusion-pandering-rainbow-diversity-cast", and honestly, she's not wrong. You can tick off the list: Asian character? Check. Indian? Check. Black? Multi-check. Overweight? Check. Disabled? Check. Gay? Check. Trans with "they" as pronoun? Check. Most of them even in combination. Usually, this would destroy my immersion as this conglomerate seems FAR TOO FORCED and unlikely, but here it works. Why? Because we are talking about gods who CHOOSE their heirs, and it is understandable that they would choose non-average people who catch their attention. This is a group of people that per definition consists of snowflakes, so let them be special. The fact that this spills over to the mortals you meet does not really stop me from enjoying the game, as they are few and mostly just decoration. Also, Freddie (whatever female name that is supposed to be short for, her full/real name is never mentioned) is a great sidekick and I loved having her around.Although I think with Hermes (VERY MINOR spoiler) Talking of spoilers: There are trigger warnings that you can choose to display by theme for more detail, and while I prefer this over shoving all these keyword spoilers in my face, I'd prefer it even more if they had included a few "red herring" themes in there (that then tell you "nothing of that sort in the game") so I am not instantly aware of every controversial subject that will arise.While the story does not have any gaping plot holes, let's say many characters act unnecessarily ambiguous and withhold information that could have saved you half the game, for reasons that I can only call stupid. Still, there were no characters that I hated (even though a certain lovestruck simpleton added a little too much awkwardness for me to enjoy). The characters achieved what the music missed: They are REMEMBERABLE! Every single character you meet fulfills a purpose and leaves an impression, be it good, bad or ugly. Even the characters that are only mentioned in passing are given interesting background information and made part of the whole. You can tell the writers loved building their world.It is a little short, coming to a total of around 5-6 hours for the first playthrough, but for me this is just the right length. I got it at the November sale after it had caught my attention before, and if you are interested but unsure, I'd say get it at the next sale. Just be aware that this is a story game and all your interactions are dialogues, spoken and sung. That's the gameplay. It's really more of an interactive, animated comic book.The whole "secret society of supernaturals" hit me with a strong World of Darkness vibe, and anybody who ever played Vampire: The Masquerade or even more, Changeling: The Dreaming, will feel right at home. I enjoyed this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow. I never expected to be so captured by this game as I was. For those people out there who just want the TLDR: This game is great, totally worth your money and your time. Just be aware that the title says "roleplaying MUSICAL". Because I certainly skipped that.You play as Grace, a young woman who lives from one day to the next and looks for her place in the world. She lives with her best friend Freddie, spends her days practicing with her band, and is an all around normal girl. That is, until she is accused by greek gods for a murder she did not commit on one of their own. Now imbued with the powers of the last muse, she has to clear her name and solve this murder with nothing but her wits and the power of music on her side!Oh man, where to start...? First of all, this games writing is great. The dialogue between characters seems natural, sometimes witty, and even the necessary exposition does not feel forced.Of course the amazing voice acting does help. When the credits at the end revealed just how many big names worked on this, I was not surprised - these people brought their A-game.Which brings me to the characters: We have a diverse cast of romanceable humans and gods, or "Idols" as they are called here. You can and will interact with them at numerous occasions, and how you handle and respond to them in dialogue will not only change change how they see you, but also the outcome of the game.Lastly, this game does not overstay its welcome. The pacing is perfect! I would not add or take away anything! Which is great, since this game could (and should) at least be played twice to see the different outcomes of your decisions. Were it any longer it would become tedious.Ok, this may sound strange, but let me explain: I do not like the music.I know, I know, not liking the music in a musical? But I can't help it. You know, in long running TV-series, where they put in a token musical episode? This feels like that. Whenever you have the option to confront a character, your muse-power comes on and forces you and your opponent in a musical argument. And it changes according to your mood (thoughtful, compassionate or aggressive), sometimes multiple times in the same song. And these just do not fit together.But then again, I don't know much about music, so who knows.Now, some would think that since I don't like the music, I would not like the game. But I love it!The characters are great, the story is great, the writing is great, and the pacing is top notch perfect!And honestly, I believe if it did not have the musical numbers it would lose part of itself. Part of it soul. I wish I could experience this game as someone who enjoys this type of music, because then it probably would be in my Top 10 games of all time.Do give it a chance if you have not already.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute work of genius, and I do not use that word lightly. The gameplay itself might be simple, as mechanically, it's just the dialogue wheel from a Bioware game. But the story and the music elevates it far beyond its simple mechanics. An engaging story with vibrant characters, with a unique take on greek myth-inspired urban fantasy. And through it all, a brilliant soundtrack that forms the core of what makes this a work of genius. Each song has its own unique paths through, affected by the player's choices, and it all comes together seamlessly. A work of art that pushes musicals to a new level and creates a new genre of interactive media.

_childDocuments_.review: This unique game is a wonderful debut for Summerfall Studios. The  assembled industry veterans skills are definitely on display here with a bold experiment going farther than Telltale, Beammdog or even Bioware or Ubisoft as a studio. The first interactive musical game blends the genres of musical theater, role-playing, and visual novels to tell a tale of hidden gods in modern times, like Neil Gaiman's American Gods if it met with Wicked or Into the Woods. The characters are all recognizable from myths; however there are often twists from what you might expect because each is fleshed out as a person with their own goals and perspectives and a history that goes to modern day, not merely the ancient past. The branching storytelling would be impressive on its own but when you consider it allows you to remix the songs through the whole game it is really amazing. The permutations and branching variables are really complex and it builds from early game choices being referenced far into the last act. Your protagonist Grace is a young woman of talent that lacks direction, when she meets the literal Last Muse and they make a beautiful song together, then the muse is murdered, and Grace must prove she didn't do it or be executed. The story moves at a good pace, but does give you the chance to explore the world, its characters, romance one if you wish, and sing your songs as Grace grows into the muse you guide her to become. For my first play through it took roughly eight hours. The launch issues seem almost all patched out. I had one crash in the epilogue, but other than that no issues on my second or third play-through. If you like Greek Gods, modern fantasy, musical theater and branching storytelling, then I think this is a game you shouldn't miss. Well done Summerfall! I can't wait to follow your next project.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: There is no sign of this being the "roleplaying game" that the title implied to me; I feel pretty sorely deceived. There's so much exposition dump I have to assume the writers & worldbuilders aren't confident in their skills.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Fantastic voice acting, and the story was really interesting. Kind of hard to quantify the musical side of things with taste in music being very subjective, but I found myself enjoying most of the songs, and it was interesting that you made choices during the song that would effect who sang, the lyrics, and things like that. Based on the achievements, it looks like there are some different songs depending on choices to it looks like, which is kind of cool.Looking more to the negative side, the audio mixing seemed a little all over the place. Some characters were too quiet at times, while others were MUCH too loud more often than not (Pan in particular seemed to be turned up quite a bit higher than other characters a lot of the time). I'm also not sure how I feel about picking from the 3 "personality" types near the beginning as it didn't seem to have a whole lot of meaning, but that's hard to gauge without subsequent playthroughs to determine how much events can differ.Overall, it left me WANTING to play it again, so that's a good start. If it holds up to multiple play through will be the true test I suppose, but I haven't had a chance to do that just yet. It's a charming and interesting game regardless of how that turns out though, so I don't regret my purchase even should it not be able to follow through.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game! First of all, if you're not into creative stories and musicals, this game isn't for you. No, there is nothing to collect, no fighting, and no actual game play of any kind. This game runs closer to a choose your own adventure book than a hack and slash or point and click game. If you'd like an easy, song-filled, mystery movie, full of branching choices, and some optional LGBT+ inclusive romance sprinkled in, then you HAVE  to try Stray Dogs right now!For me, the highlights of this unique game were the songs. I can't wait to go back and re-do the songs  to see how my choices affect the lyrics, instruments, and flow. I already have a few favorite songs and I'm excited to hear the many different versions the game allows. Another highlight was the romance. It was weaved in really well with the story and didn't feel over or under used. I also liked that it was optional and never felt forced upon you.If you are even a little interested, buy this game! You will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in two days, it was great. The story was nice and the twists didn't feel outlandish at all. I'm not usually a fan of the mystery genre so I can't speak for that, but I do think the game did brilliantly giving us some information and concealing others, just enough that I was able to predict several twists but was surprised by others. Certain characters deceive you and when they reveal it I thought it made sense. Some of the songs, however, sounded off. The game does not expect you to change the color choices in the middle of the song despite how the previous dialogue may change your approach. Certain songs where characters were singing at the same time sounded oddly out of tune. However, the story beats were good and the songs were dramatic with plot/character purpose that I never felt irritated by a song popping up. I do think some singing voices sounded too similar though. Overall, it was a very lovely game where I played therapist to a bunch of sad gods. Probably a 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I am on the fence about recommending this game. Ultimately, I gave it a thumbs up because I loved the creativity that went into making it and I don't regret finishing it. Everything that had to do with the story, art, and voice acting was impressive, but the mechanics of playing the game, choices in the animation style, and mediocre music just made the pacing so much worse than it already was. I struggled with motivation to play and finish Stray Gods, even though on paper it was everything I wanted in a game. Blending a musical with a new style of story-based decision-making gameplay sounded amazing and I loved the inclusive character designs that I identified with - it was such a refreshing universe. But for other players out there thinking of getting it, know that it's probably worth your time, but might be hard to get through. Also - shout out to the highly appreciated land acknowledgement for stolen lands, which every game development studio should be doing. Thank you for making space for that in your game.Pros-Unique gameplay -Beautiful character design-Amazing voice acting-Fun and flirty storyCons-Slow pacing-Intentionally staggered animation -Not enough time to read and make decisions-Songs weren't memorable and sometimes not enjoyable to listen to
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Gosh, I never thought I'd see what is so literally an interactive musical. Interactive fiction leaves so much room for creativity, and this certainly does not disappoint! Beautiful art, musical numbers I found myself humming even when not playing, a diverse and fully voice-acted cast (including a visibly disabled character and a nonbinary character played by a genderfluid VA!), and lyrics influenced by your decisions... this delivered on everything I was hoping for when I first heard & read about it. I've been showing it to my housemates, watching live performances of the music, playing and replaying it -- I certainly give this game a big thumbs up. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this marvel to come out the moment I saw the announcements and realized who'd be voice acting, but I have to admit - the game has exceeded all my expectations. It is beautifully made, with gorgeous art and wonderful design work, the story is gripping, intense, even real and painful at times, and it sinks its claws into you and doesn't let go until the end credits. And the music - oh my god the music! As a musician, I was thoroughly enjoying every sound aspect of the game (minus the small volume discrepancies which are genuinely so minor), but the songs and the voice acting were exquisite and absolutely splendid. Laura Bailey is a queen, we're all aware of this already, but oh my god what a performance! Certain moments had me in awe, the raw emotion in her voice for some dialogue choices really cuts you and it's hard to keep those emotions from not flooding you. Every VA gave such an amazing performance, and the dialogues are so well written, it's really hard to find any fault in them at all. The characters are engaging, fun, annoying, suave - everything you'd expect from Greek mythology and so, SO MUCH MORE. And the songs are insanely catchy and you'll definitely find yourself singing along in your 2nd, 3rd, 77th playt-through (I'm about to start my 2nd of many, many more). A game that is definitely for you if you're into role-playing games, visual novels, musicals and amazing story-telling. This game has it all and so much more and it'll have you laughing, cackling, groaning, sobbing like a little baby, screaming, pacing the room, fuming and basically every other emotion on the spectrum. 100000/10, will play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: This moving story is brought to life by the amazing performance of the voice cast, the beautiful music, an immersive experience, and moments that would bring to tears even the most hardened hearts...Congratulation to the team for creating this musical, and yes, I do recommend this game if you are there for a story.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is like nothing you've ever experienced before. It's a mind-blowing mix of modern fantasy, interactive storytelling, and incredible music that'll leave you speechless. The story unfolds in a way that's completely up to you, shaping your own destiny and drawing you deeper into its captivating tale. But it's not just the story that'll grab you - the visuals in this game are unbelievable. Each character and setting is brought to life through stunning hand-illustrations that'll make you feel like you're really there. And get this - even the choices you make during the game's musical numbers have a real impact. It's an incredible example of how video games and musicals can come together and make each other even better. Stray Gods is truly a one-of-a-kind experience that you won't want to miss.Obviously, I've nominated this game for the Best Soundtrack Steam Awards :)

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a 9/10 (my opinion) or a 3/10 (my best friend's opinion)? Di you love the musical episodes of Buffy, Psych, and Strange New Worlds? Do you know every word of Rent and Chorus Line by heart? You will probably adore this. If not, maybe not so much. This is about as niche as a niche game gets, for me it succeeds almost brilliantly.It's a choice-driven musical, it's a singing dancing visual novel, and if you are theater geek, this is a must. It's not, however, really a role-playing game, except in the broadest sense. Now to the specifics:Ambition and Aim: A+This is one of the most wildly ambitious and original games in years. Full props for swinging for the fences.Story and writing: A-Visual novels live or die on the strength of the writing. Musicals live and die by the strength of "the book" and the score. Good marks here, the story is fresh, the writing is smart. It loses half a point because some of the lyrics are a bit generic. It's a trap only the greatest musicals manage to avoid.Voice acting/vocal performance: A++Absolutely smacked it. Almost every one of the performers brought depth and nuance to their roles, every one would be welcome as a Broadway cast member.Art/Visual style: AThe art is simple, bold, and effective. Think "Phoenix Wright" or 90's anime and you're in the ballpark. It works really, really well.Value/replayability: BIt's fairly short, at about 4 hours for a playthrough. Because it's replicating a musical, that's about right. There are at least three playthroughs to get all the musical choices and ending options. So, about 12 hours to complete? For a $30 game, that's not great value, but not the worst either.Spit and polish: C+This is where I really ding the game. The audio balance is all over the map, sometimes vocals are muddy and washed out. For a game that's all about the music, they really dropped the ball on sound engineering. Hopefully that won't be a difficult patch.Overall experience: For me, it's A+++ I don't remember the last time I felt this much joy booting up a new game. Kudos, props, and a tip o' the top-hat to the entire team behind this gem. Love, love, LOVE it!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game is so reactive to your choices in musical format is impressive. It's novel, it's new, it understands the mythology it's drawing from, and it straight up made me cry. It's not perfect (specifically, the audio mixing leaves the instrumental track too quiet and a few of the singers are too quiet in certain songs) but it's novel and interesting and it's just a joy to play through and play through again to see the other choices. I'm not even a fan of visual novels, but I liked this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, this game has a bit of cheese to it- but it works.The premise of the game is a pretty overdone trope, honestly. The whole 'misunderstood, lonely person is suddenly *special*. And for a moment I was getting quickly turned off to the narrative- but then came the choices you get to make for your character. You can be gritty, witty, or as sugary as southern sweet tea. The stories and dynamic between the idols are phenomenal, and by the end of the story you might "know" what is going to happen and yet you still find yourself jaw-dropped when the shoe finally drops.I'd get it. The music is beautiful, the story rocks, etc. The music is good enough to keep you hooked, and the story is charming enough to make you smile.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Less of a musical, more of a visual novel with lots of singing. An opera perhaps.The story was neat, the characters were interesting, it was an overall successful modern story of Greek myth. The visuals were compelling. I liked the dialogue options and how you could be your own type of Grace.I think it was really cool how the tracks were stitched together and the songs were in a sense customize-able.I was generally not bothered by the way it was less fully animated, more like a high fidelity storyboard. It gave it a comic book feel that was pretty interesting and workable.My overall complaint is that after 6 hours, not a single song is echoing in my head. I remember there being some clever lyrics in the moment, but I've got nothing. For me the best part of a musical is how the songs stick with you. Non-diegetic pageantry. And a song or two that blows your mind when you first hear them and has you listening to the whole soundtrack on repeat until you eventually just love most of if not all of it.If you are looking for something with amazing numbers that you'll want to listen to more than once, this just isn't it. If you're curious about seeing this interesting concept play out and have cash to burn, go for it. I don't regret my purchase and it wasn't a bad experience at all, it just didn't *feel* like a musical in the ways that I enjoy musicals.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I think I've fallen in love a bit with this game.The opening number is a great melancholic piece, and made me warm to Laura Bailey's Grace immediately, who has a fantastic voice. The rest of the cast I've encountered so far have been great, with a real highlight being the first "duet" with PersephoneI think the conversation system in songs where you can pick the tone of the verse in response is interesting, though at times can make the songs feel a little discordant if you pick varying options.It's more Telltale than a Baldur's gate kind of RPG, sitting much more in the lines of interactive visual novels. _childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a unique game, and clearly a lot of talent and energy went into its creation. For those reasons alone, it's worth a look. The voice cast is excellent, the comic-style art is expressive and stylish, and the story is interesting enough to keep you engaged for the relatively short length of the game.That being said, it's certainly not perfect. In spite of the title, i wouldn't really call it an RPG; the only game mechanic is making choices, so it feels like a visual novel through and through, albeit one with a full voice cast and interactive songs. There's nothing wrong with that, but I the title led me to expect more systems and complexity. I also found that (on my admittedly rather old laptop) the load times were long and the interface surprisingly laggy given the technical simplicity of the actual game. I also found the game's occasional attempts at animation distracting, making it feel like an unfinished storyboard; I would actually have preferred more static visuals in some places given that full animation was obviously beyond budgetary possibility here... though a fully animated remaster in future would be welcome if it ever became feasible.Bottom line: I enjoyed playing this, but because of the technical issues, I don't think I have the energy to sit through it again to see the other possibilities and collect more achievements. Maybe in the future, on better hardware!

_childDocuments_.review: It was the best of musical games.  It was the worst of musical games.  It was the *first* of musical games, and no matter what else, the very creation of something so novel by an indie studio on a shoestring budget is a staggering artistic achievement.But is it good?In a word, yes.You're solving the mystery of the murder of the last Muse, who passed her powers to you in her dying moments.  Like many storytelling games, many (not all) main points of the plot remain constant regardless of your choices.  But Stray Gods isn't so much about solving the crime as it is about relationships and emotions among the gods--some of whom will be your judges and all of whom are suspects.  The ending I reached had everything to do with the particular relationships I had (or hadn't) cultivated.  Subsequent plays ended in meaningfully different relationships, even if I would have appreciated if the plot points could have diverged more.The game primarily tests your emotional intelligence in intuiting quickly which direction a scene or song needs to move to reach the outcome your character needs.  The central characters are all interesting and complex enough to make this a challenge, and you have enough social cues that you can navigate these songscapes without an urge to reload saves.Not just your lyrics but the entirely musical style of a song can change with your choices.  If your choices make no story sense, then the musical would sound all over the place, whereas with the ways that I keyed into characters, each song told story both verbally and musically.  There was a character with whom I battled musically, then cooled down to empathy once she showed a crack in her exterior, or conversely another with whose feelings I sat gently until a finale of confrontation over her course of action.Stray Gods is brilliant, and there's nothing else quite like it.Most ways to improve it would have called for a much higher budget: several emotional moments felt as if they should have had songs but didn't, and fully animated visuals would've been engaging--though in some ways the animatic/graphic novel style is exceptionally well-suited to musicals.Several pieces of low-hanging fruit should have been in budget, though.  There are stretches with no music at all, for example the epilogue with lots of speech over still frames with no background music feels as if they ran out of money.  Also, particularly toward the end of the game, they didn't normalize the volume on their different voice actors' recordings, so some characters are much quieter than others in a shockingly rookie mistake on an otherwise so sophisticated product.  [EDIT: This got fixed with the first patch.] Finally, I was a Fig backer and couldn't find my name in the Fig backer credits.  What a grave oversight!!!Here's the thing: this is the first crowdfunded project where I've *looked* for my name, because despite how much I've loved many of the projects I've backed, this is the first one where, after finishing it, I felt as if I'd participated in a small bit of gaming history.  I very much hope we have other musical games ahead.  This first attempt, with no precedent or roadmap, was worth the time and wait.  I only wonder where the genre can go from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: The game's only issues on launch day are entirely technical: there's a glitch corrupting some peoples' save files (not an issue for me personally, though), voice line volume not being the same between characters in some scenes, there's one song where the captions are way faster than the singing, and there's a litany of little graphical glitches here and there that made characters that should've been in focus blurry or made the scaling of their portraits glitch so they oscillated between a little bit bigger than they should've been and the size they were actually supposed to be during a scene near one of the ends of the game.But all of that means literally nothing to me. This game kicks ass if you're in the mood for a witty, moving, emotionally intelligent romp through an alternate world where gods secretly live among us and almost all of them are lying to you constantly.I've never played a 'choices matter' game where the choices are this well articulated; there was never a moment where I clicked on a vague option and my character said something I didn't mean. Also, the fact you get to make multiple choices within each song the cast performs which changes the lyrics and how the other singer(s) react means there's a surprising amount of nuance to how you try and deal with everyone. All of the dialog options, alternate scenes, different song lyrics, and different endings makes me want to replay it again soon.The highest praise I can give it is this, though: I haven't been able to focus on a game for more than an hour or two at a time for weeks, but I sat and played Stray Gods for seven hours straight until I beat my first playthrough and I don't regret it at all, even though I'm typing this review at 3 a.m. already half-asleep!If the premise of the game, the visual novel genre, or musicals appeal to you, I think you'll enjoy it, because it delivers extremely well in all of those areas.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is worth your time because it's genuinely innovative. I've never seen a game (or anything else) tell a story in this way and it uses the music as a narrative device in a way I've not seen before but one that works incredibly well and elevates the rest of the game. As a game about its characters and story, it achieves its goals very well and is aided greatly by excellent performances. The only real downside is that the music itself isn't great. Allowing you to make genuine choices and guide the songs sacrifices the writers ability to write songs which can be listened to, are memorable, or really have anything interesting going on at all. I'd like to remember some music from a musical but I can barely pull up a couple of lines and I've only just finished the game. The music serves its purpose in the game well, just don't expect to take anything you'll want to listen to afterwards from it.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Stray gods offers the most unique experience I've had in a really long time. I'm obsessed with musicals and with visual novels, and I can say without any hesitation this game is a jaw dropping success in both categories. The music is phenomenal - though I won't lie, it does have a couple of clunky spots where the game has to figure out how to fit your dialogue choice into the song, as a fan of musical theater and improv I see that as a feature not a bug. To me, that little bit of clunkyness really sells that this is happening in real time for me and the characters, so there's going to be a little bit of awkward fits from one improved line to another. The characters and art is beautiful in every frame. I need elaborate no further, just look at the screenshots, it looks that good and distinct throughout. The voice actors for the characters are also absolutely spectacular, it's really star filled, and if you're like me - you'll spot some Broadway stars voices a mile away, and if you think it's them - it probably is. If you're a musical fan, a visual novel fan, or both and at all on the fence about buying this game - the game absolutely aces both categories, so trust me and go ahead and take plunge

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I loved so much of this game. Its heart shone through in utterly everything it did, and nobody felt like a caricature or like they hadn't been fleshed out, with plenty of good traits as well as flaws to go around in these complex, heartsoar, often love-laden situations between folks. The story has some really nuanced points that make you think, feel and consider on a heart level, which is my favorite thing ever. Yes, occasionally I'd find a song a little choppy/disjointed in its execution, or feel that a line or two in a song needed to be retried, especially with Grace. But I also had many songs that have stuck firmly in my head, or a moment I found myself exclaiming in happiness over the way something panned out, moments when music and message and performance came together absolutely perfectly with the through line I was following, and those moments? They're absolute magic. If you're looking for quick action, or absolute perfection, you won't find it here. But you'll find, in every sense of the word, a good story, told with passion and skill, in spite of or perhaps because of a few flaws. If you choose to play, may Stray Gods leave you a bit less adrift than when you began, even if only in some small way.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: There are three metrics by which I measure a good story game. First, do the songs play through my head at night as I try to fall asleep? Check. Do the characters feel alive and well-written, to the point that I still want to learn more about them when the credits roll? Check. And, most nerdily, do I want to create a tabletop RPG based on the game so I can keep living in the world? Check again. Everything about the setting, the story, and the music drew me in, and the more that I learned about the Idols and their existence, the more I wanted to peel back the layers of mystery surrounding these characters and the world they inhabit. Even characters only mentioned have emotional depth to them, as the lived tragedy of the idols slowly unfolds through each dialogue choice.As has been said, this is more of a visual novel type game, though really that's more of a shell for building around some stellar performances by a talented voice cast. There wasn't a single voice that felt miscast; they all embodied their characters perfectly, and if there's anything to be regretted, it's that there's only so many songs and so many characters to be featured in them. The songs are incredibly rich and varied, just between the branching choices; for most of the songs, it's an entirely different melody depending on which paths you choose, complete with alternate choruses and themes. Even just the song from the demo shows this with Pan's song varying between "My Time to Shine" for the rocker path, "Lost Girls" for the charmer path, and "Morning Fades" for the clever path.The story itself has some fixed points, and several of the songs, especially the Act 1 songs, don't have a heavy impact on the plot later on. It's really in Act 2 where the choice system shines, and Aphrodite's song still lives in my head as one of the most haunting and impactful gaming experiences I've ever had. Act 3 doesn't have as much narrative branching as you think, and the ending is a little weaker in that it relies on a narrated epilogue to reveal the lasting consequences of your choices; but, to be fair, this was what we had to whine and complain to get for Mass Effect 3, and it's still more than we got for Life is Strange, with its binary "render all of your choices meaningless" or "undo every choice you've ever made" ending. Also, I'll admit I haven't strayed far in my approach on subsequent playthroughs, so perhaps I'll discover more rich variation than I thought.There are some bugs, yes; the save file bug has already been squashed, and the most egregious ones, such as uneven volume levels between dialogues, are sure to be addressed by the devs quickly. For a game developed by a small studio, it still remains an impressive technical achievement, and goes well beyond being a proof of concept for a new form of narrative choice-based game. If this game didn't wrap up so neatly, I would hope there would be potential for a Stray Gods 2; of course, there's always room for doing one set in another pantheon. Choice-based metal musical set around the Norse gods, perhaps? There are some legitimate complaints about the way the interface was set up, with exploration scenes being especially egregious; choosing an option to explore, and then having to select a separate button to continue, is a bit arduous and breaks the flow, and the settings menu is similarly obtuse, with all of your choices undone unless you scroll down to hit 'confirm'. Honestly, though, the game more than makes up for these small gripes, and is well worth playing. Now that the mold has been broken, hopefully we'll see other studios experiment with this new form of storytelling, and get a rich line of successor games featuring evolving, varied musical numbers.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited 25 years for someone to make a game exactly like this kind of concept to come true. And it is every seconds worth the wait. It's like a Broadway musical that you are in control. And many of the songs are beautifully written. Several of the songs were very moving and I actually cried. Especially the song Lost In A Moment. Storywise it's a bit similar to The Wolf Among Us, you can almost think of it as a Wolf Among Us Musical. And there  certainly were a bunch of plot twists I did not expect.Absolutely 200% recommended to any musical lovers, and for someone who wants to play a brand new genre that has basically never been done before in gaming history. I was going to play just an hour of it today, but I ended up spending almost 7 hours to finish it all in one go, you just keep wanting to see the story unfold. A shiny 10 out 10 game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

I laughed, I cried (literally). I'm kind of sad it's over. But it's not really, is it? I can't wait to start over and begin using different choices.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I love Urban Fantasy. I love Musicals. I enjoy Murder Mysteries. This game offers all of that plus some of the best romance I've ever seen in a game. The mystery is really good. The worldbuilding is so well thought out and grounded. The characters are all distinct and engaging (Especially Persephone) and the fact that the songs in this game has DIALOGUE TREES shows a level of craft and care I've never before seen in a musical. I knew Stray Gods was going to be good when I saw the Bioware alumni behind it. A fantastic first game for Summerfall Studios and I hope it's just the first of many.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I have to say that I wish we had more games like these - Roleplaying Musicals where you have choices done (mostly) in form of song instead of dialogue.The story is not too bad either. Quite refreshing to hear some different kind of greeks myths, to a part.Though it's not all wine and roses. The game is definetely in desperate need of some patches, especially for the volume of the voices (sometimes in a normal conversation or even important plot points one person nearly whispers while the other one shouts). Also one dialogue after visiting the lair of a certain spymaster repeated twice at different locations (I think only one line or so was different). Not every chosen songline was matching well either. So, yeah, there is definetely some space for patches and improvements.I'd also love to see some message in the beginning telling you that your choices might have undesireable consequences or might not lead to solving the puzzle (even if that is only done for the same reasons like Hellblade).Still I think this game is brilliant and very enjoyable. You should give it a try, escpecially if you went out of your way to read this. The characters are very lovely, characteristic and distinct - great voice acting, by the way! - and if the game gets popular enough we most likely could expect more games like these, with better polishing, probably more songs and longer playtime; in other words: the devs will improve themselves next time. Experience grants mastery. (A good case for that is Larian studios atm)

_childDocuments_.review: What a breath of fresh air this game is! It is magical to be seen through inclusive and diverse characters with rich stories that are bursting with life. This game is more than just a who-dunnit roleplaying musical - it is therapy for the soul. You can choose to be kind, to be pissed off, to be thought-provoking. You can forgive and be forgiven. Your choices reflect you as a person and, most importantly, how you treat yourself. This is a love story to those seeking justice who are trying to find their voice in a world insistent on drowning everything else out under cries of pain and hurting. My play-through only took 5 hours but wow, I cried and I sang and I laughed and I hurt and I forgave myself. This game asks us that - are we capable of forgiving ourselves and moving forward, of being kind in a world that hurts us? Sure, the game has little glitches here and there, and sometimes things might not fully align, but that is forgotten almost instantly because the vibrancy of the visual and narrative designs are so vivid, you forgive these moments too. I am shocked that this game hasn't been talked about more, played more - there is so much here to unpack and revel in. This game is truly something very, very special <3
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of story rich games, this game was a huge pleasure. The voice actors were absolutely amazing, and the writing was quite well-done too. I'd love to see more games in this series or a continuation in visual novel or novel format. I'd like to revisit the Idol universe and delve into its lore more in depth. .Some of the song lines were a bit shaky at times or due to the choice based nature didn't blend or flow well. But there are definitely a few songs I'll end up listening to long from now. It was fun seeking out little bits of dialogue that you missed before, and going back to pick options that might give you easter eggs or amusing dialogue. I laughed a lot while doing this, searching for funny lines or combinations and even after many hours I kept finding new lines.When it comes to the DLC, it was okay. I did like Orpheus's designs and songs in the original. I wish the DLC had more of a plot though, it was so short and didn't really have any real substance. I was hoping for more worldbuilding, but I don't regret playing the DLC.Overall, I very highly recommend Stray Gods. It's especially fun if you play with friends or someone you can discuss your choices with or theorize with over the plot or your feelings/suspicions about specific characters.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend got me this game because we both love musicals and he wanted to have someone he could talk about the plot with. I know a lot of people are saying this game is amazing but it's not. I feel a bit bad my friend paid full price for this though, because it's not worth it in my opinion. The musical portion of it is just the VAs talking with music in the background for most of the songs, the music doesn't go with the "songs" being sung, and I've run into  a bug where the songs and voice lines will cutoff completely for a section of the game which already put a damper on my interest. Not to mention I've already figured out the who in how events transpired less than 4 hours in. I don't know why people think this is worth $30, but it's your money to burn, I just wish more effort was put into the actual music portion of the Musical game. Sure, it does decent with mythology and lore tinkering changing bits, but with how unrefined this game plays, its not worth it to buy it yourself, not full price at the very least. You're better off just watching a let's play online in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: For lovers of musicals and/or Greek mythology, This is an amazing experience. As a fan of the latter I really liked how they gave a new twist on how to see the myths and legends of old. The almost endless variations of most songs Is blowing my mind, and it has a lot of replay value because of that. _childDocuments_.review: I can't think of any other game quite like this, and that's a really hard thing to say, but it's true - this one absolutely breaks the mold. Sure, it's a narrative adventure - sure it's a musical - but it's both and not slavish to either. The flow of choices and how they impact songs is kind of staggering: do yourselves a favor and hop back to the start of a song just after you've played it so it's fresh in your head, make a different choice early on, and see how things pivot! There is a deeply embroidered complexity to this game and all the characters in it, things that will make you grin and get teary-eyed. The gameplay flows smoothly, the songs are incredibly catchy, the writing solid and engaging, the visuals unique, the performances solid - the only quibble I have is that the sound mixing is kind of all over the place (keep a hand on the volume knob, it can get weird, especially Pan being loud) - but that's early patch fix material for sure. All in all, this game is a must-buy: great fun, there's nothing like it, and hopefully it's an inspiration for much more to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like the animated version of The Wicked + The Divine with a splash of American Gods mixed in. Dialogues are very well written and  the voice acting is just phenomenal. Even the songs and musical elements of it work wonders, flawlessly blending into regular scenes with choices made in the game influencing the outcome and tone of the songs. Sure, it's a bit melodramatic but it's a musical, what did you expect? It's good for those who know about Greek mythology but even without it's very easy to catch up on the basics of the ancient lore. The quick time events are easy enough, but don't expect a massive amount of interaction. It's like a movie with interactive elements. Not bad in my opinion, since the artwork is absolutely stunning, from character design to environments, so just watching is a treat in and of itself. Style-wise it really made me think back to The Wolf Among Us (also one of my all time favs), although Stray Gods isn't as fluent as that. Had more of a comic book feel to it in animation as well, which my computer didn't always agree with. Make sure your hardware is up to par and you'll have an absolute blast if you enjoy story and character driven epics with a splash of music and drama.Verdict: 4,5 lightning bolts out of 5.
