_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game. So much so that I went back and played it again... And again... And again. One of the few games I actively went after 100% completion for because I loved so much about it. Tl;Dr at the bottom!The game has a few negatives. It's a bit buggy, with one song in particular sometimes freezing up at the start and requiring a restart of the game to make sure audio is synced properly - but because it autosaves at the start of the song, it's not a huge issue. Rarely, a character will vanish from the scene and reappear a few moments later. The audio mixing for the dialogue is hit or miss, with it usually being fine but a few are just too quiet - one in particular is far too quiet near the end of the game.But beyond that, the game is just so great. Most of the songs have tons of variations to them, even beyond the ones required for the achievements - despite 100%ing the game, I was able to find combinations I hadn't tried before on YouTube and see the lyrics totally change. Speaking of which, I adored those songs. I've been listening to them on YouTube a lot in the background. The characters are well-written, and I ended up liking all of the characterization for them. The story isn't incredibly deep, but it is interesting with some heartfelt moments and some fantastically emotional highs. The art is well made, with almost every scene being very pleasing to the eyes.Tl;Dr: A bit buggy, and the audio mixing for dialogue could use some work, but with an incredible cast of characters and some fantastic music, I have to recommend this game. Easily one of my top games of 2023 so far!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buy ASAP if you like musicals, or VNs. Surprising amount of song variety ,even within the same song. I laughed, I got teary eyed, I cheered, had a totally enjoyable experience!Obviously game is made with ehm "modern sensibilities"** BUT they don't overshadow the game, music and narrative (which is an amazing feat in 2023). You'll almost never want to push your fingers into your eyes (or ears) while playing/listening/watching this! Story is pretty much on rails but the songs manage to carry the game, makes you wanna try multiple playthroughs. You'll be surprised how much you'll like & sympathize with the cast. Characters have personality, and only their looks are exaggerated like it's a stage play. The art is great, has that comic book feeling, everyone looks gorgeous. (which is also an amazing feat in 2023) Oh did I mention how much I enjoyed the songs and how you can choose your little path during listening them? Like you can add a little aggressive outburst moment into an emotional slow song? I want to live in a world where this kind of game succeeds so we get more this! (Just imagine a Brütal Legend sequel done in this way!)** Look this is not a "woke" game with gender/race bingo to fill out the cast, even though the trailers kinda make it look like that. Strangely enough this is a game with just a diverse cast. Game never slows down to deliver "the message" or scolds the player. Except for one screen outside the story but they just say it and move on. Maybe the most unexpected part of this game is how much it only cares about telling it's story and have fun & look cool while doing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is pretty much a Telltale game minus the exploration part. The main gameplay mostly revolves around just  choosing which dialogue you think fits the situation. You could say that it's an interactive movie at most.What sets this one apart from other Telltale games aside from what I mentioned earlier is the musical set pieces. The choices you make doesn't just affect the relationships around you but it also changes how the song flows. The musical can start as a jazzy song but can suddenly be reverted into punk rock depending on the choices you make during the song. It's really fun exploring different options because of the amount of variation of songs you can experience with each choice. In my first run, I went with the charming style and even though most of the choices that I wanted was unlocked via that style, I really did miss out on the good songs that were made available when I chose the clever style on my 2nd run. Most of the choices doesn't really affect the initial ending, your choices however affects your journey towards that ending and replaying it multiple times is really worth it especially if you're a big fan of musicals.Overall, I really enjoyed Stray Gods in its entirety, from it's story down to every musical number it had to offer. I recommend Stray Gods if you really love musicals and just want a pretty chill experience. If you think the gameplay just ain't enough for the price then waiting for a sale is your more likely option or just skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Great cast (seriously... excellent cast), dope acting, fun choices with noticeable variance, engaging story (albeit slightly predictable imo, but it's about the journey, not the destination!), some really catchy songs that I found myself humming/singing at work the day after I played my first playthrough. Also has pretty diverse representation, which I felt wasn't unnecessary or out of place and actually attached the setting of the world to something more real and modern. The stakes felt important, the payoff/resolution felt satisfying. Cons: Volume levels of voice lines can be inconsistent (not during actual songs though, for the vast majority of the game)A few specific songs sounded very muddy, almost like there are too many voices or there was an additional, incorrect audio track playing (it literally might've been a bug in that playthrough, idk), and I didn't agree with the choices in musical composition for another song or two (Keep your talent in their appropriate ranges for impactful moments in songs, folks). None of the cons were that big of a deal to me overall. I loved playing through this once, I will love playing through it several more times to see all the different variations. None of the pros were enough to make me rant and rave about the game either. It's a solid, enjoyable experience that is unique, refreshing, and delightful. If I had to assign it a numerical score, I'd say 8.5/10. Good B-grade game. Not a B+, not a B-, just a good ol' solid B. Would be a 9/10 if they cleaned up the audio. Would've been a 10 if it was fully animated like the first part of the launch trailer instead :)

_childDocuments_.review: Stray gods is interesting concept, which for the most part is well executed but has some noticeable flaws. The worldbuilding is sublime, the characters are pitch perfect, however the musical numbers aren’t always strong, casting is either brilliant or average and the plot isn’t as strong as the genre requires. I’d rate a 7/10.Starting without the spoilers, the characters are a high point of this game, every single one is incredibly interesting, but an impressive part of these game’s writing is how they play on the myths of the Greek gods and how that impacts the personality of the characters. Apollo being a haunted figure because of his powers is perhaps one of the best examples of this. Grace is a protagonist you’ll immediately connect with, she passes the vibe of someone placed in a impossible situation and having to deal with it, with quite a range for the player to decide how you’ll react to the situation. A lot of Grace’s charm comes from Laura’s brilliant performance. This brings us to casting which falls on three categories: you have characters that are well cast both in the talking and the musical numbers, examples of this come with Laura Bailey as Grace and Ashley Jonhson as Calliope, the first musical number is arguably the best one in the game. The second is casting that is just boring on both counts, Felicia's Athena falls into this, you don’t get the vibe of the goddess of wisdom. Finally, the more interesting are the characters that work well when you’re in dialog but not in the musical numbers. Troy Baker’s Apollo falls into this, most songs felt like the notes weren’t quite right. Calling this game a musical is a bit of a misnomer; this is an epic poem. Most songs are story in rhyme first, songs second. The idea is having the player influence the song with the tried and tested dialog wheel, leading the song into different genres according to the “charm, Badass, clever” system. This is a fascinating idea, and for the most part it works, but the few moments it doesn’t presents the issues that this game finds.Here we enter the small spoiler’s territory. There are two issues, for some reason, the writters thought it was a good idea to have two or more actors singing on top of each other with different lyrics. As a non-native speaker, this makes following the song, difficult. I get the creative decision of making it an argument between the characters, but often times clear communication is more important than realism. The second issue is the shift in musical genres that don’t fit sometimes. For example, in the “battle” against Persephone, the blue option leads you to a song closer to Blues and the red option starts a Hip-Hop battle. There’s a gigantic disconnect between the two musical styles and it’s a jarring shift. Ultimately, the songs will work better if you maintain one option but that removes a bit of the roleplaying aspect. This leads us to the hidden approval system. Early on the system is quite punishing, I found myself locked out of dialog options because I chose the blue option in the song with Calliope. This game feels like it was built around the idea of sticking to one path rather than mixing the three choices, and some points of divergence that almost seem purposefully build to make the player have to play the game multiple times, but not necessarily sells why should one replay it. The worldbuilding here is sublime. Stray Gods has to be one of the best “gods among us” type narrative. Form the idols repassing their soul to chosen mortals, to the idea of how the memories merge and become one is fascinating. Although I doubt this game will have a sequel, this world certainly could support one. I cannot make this game take on Greek mythology justice, please watch the Overly Sacastic productions video.*Spoiler alert, will be discussing the plot* ***Conclusion***There’s one comparison that is quite fitting for Stray Gods, Dragon Age 2: an interesting concept, with mostly good execution but with noticeable rough spots. I’m not sure about the asking price. I understand it, due to the amount of voice actors getting paid, and the fact that you had to hire an orchestra; but you’re still charging half of BG3 does, not to mention that you can get older games for the price, ironically, the Dragon Age Trilogy is constantly at sale for this exact price. And while the comparison is unfair, I am not the one selling myself “the roleplaying musical”. Visual novels often sell themselves at a cheaper price, you can get the entire run of Telltale’s Batman for the asking price here. Thus, it’s hard to make a financial argument for this game, but artistically is an interesting experience that I honestly hope gets polished and, hopefully, a sequel. The fact that I’m not into musical or graphic novels and enjoyed my time in this game, is a testament that it did plenty right, it just didn’t blow my mind away.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game and give it an honest shot by completing it before writing a review, but after several weeks where I can't even bring myself to launch it again, I figured it was time to just be done with it. First some context: I am personally not that into musicals, but I did play Stray Gods together with my girlfriend who is. I have however played a lot of visual novel games.After our first session with the game we both agreed on a couple of things: The artstyle is wonderful and the voice actors do a phenomenal job with what they are given. But that's where the positives stop, as the songs, the main draw of the game, mostly sound like dialouge written for a B-movie which is then read out with some background music. The dynamic song mechanic is also just a novelty when the songs they are built around aren't interesting. I get that it is really impressive from a composition perspective to have so many branching pathways in a song, but it isn't really intersting for me as a player. Add to this that every other scene is just silence with the voice actors talking, and the animation style is stop motion-ish rather than constantly animated sprites makes it feel really flat at all times. As a visual novel, I can't help but compare it to The Wolf Among Us, which does the whole mythological creatures living in the real world trope better, and is in general a way better graphical novel. So I got bored, and couldn't be bothered to continue after getting a bit more than halfway into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me feeling conflicted, as I did enjoy playing it and would consider it a GOOD game there are several things barring me from saying it is a GREAT game. For the positives, the voice acting is amazing (the cast is stacked so I would sure hope so) and I overall enjoyed the story. I also really liked the general art style and look of the game. The overall concept of what they were going for is cool - adding musical elements to a visual novel is an interesting idea. The music, however, is where the game starts so fall short for me, as the songs are very hit or miss. The songs that work, REALLY work and added to the story. The songs that didn't work for me (which were more frequent) were harder to get through. I think it's a mix of poor lyric writing (trying to shoehorn in plot or character development without it flowing musically) and poor orchestration/mixing of the back track. There were definitely times that the singers sounded off key, which could be due to voice actors with less singing experience struggling. However, I think it is more due to the orchestration not meshing well with the vocal line and poor production. My one reason for thinking this is there were times that even Orpheus felt off key, and his VA Anthony Rapp is a Broadway titan. If they managed to make him sound bad, I hardly think it's the singers fault. My other complaints are more QOL. I wish there was a log of recent dialogue spoken as there were a few things I missed the first time. The skip button also seemed to skip to the next dialogue choice and not just the current voice line which also bugged me.I have a lot of complaints but overall I did enjoy myself. I am a lover of both musical and visual novels, so it was fun to see them combined. I only completed one play through, but I enjoyed the branching paths and the one romance I was able to pursue. I also like the mystery aspect of the story, even if it wasn't too hard to figure out on my own. At the end of the day, if this game seems up your alley and you're really excited about it, I would recommend you give it a try. However, at $30 I wouldn't recommend it to just anyone. I understand with the caliber of people working on this project that price is probably justified, but there are just so many other exceptional visual novels (and other cozy games) that are of way better value for a much better price. So good game, just not for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished the game and I have thoughts. I will flat out say I liked it. It’s not without flaws, it’s certainly not for everyone, but I liked it. The music was mostly good and mostly worked which for a thing of this nature that came together in this way is commendable. The art is just gorgeous. I’m something of a comic geek and this is like top tier comic art for the most part. Is it all the very best? No, like all comics, it’s going to have a wanky panel here or there. But overall, the art is the strongest part. My biggest critique is that it does get a little samy by the end. Starts to lose it’s luster by the end. And with music, that could be a project to really get value for money out of this game, you could try to work out all the combinations of paths in the songs and come up with the best version of every song. Have fun with that. Moving along though, one knock against it, I feel like it should have been longer. For the price point, I kind of feel like there should have been a bit more to it. Don’t get me wrong, I understand, they had a lot of moving parts. I get it already had to be a pretty tight budget to get full voice acting and to pay them to sing as well. And the artists and the people working on in the background and with the coding. Yeah, I get that every big is an expensive ask. And yet, I still feel like it should have been a little longer, flushed everything out just a bit more a bit better. As enjoyable as it was, it did feel a little rushed in parts. My playthrough was 6 and a half hours, for $30, I want a few more hours out of it. Which to be fair there are many more if you want to unlock all the achievements, but I mean in a campaign. Now what for many will be kind of a deal breaker. This game is essentially an interactive movie. It is not wrong to think of it that way. In my own mind, it has just enough elements of game play that to me it is actually a game. You do make choices that do affect the outcome. You are on a timer to make those choices. Though, you can remove the timer if you want to, but I’d see it as a mistake just for the flow of the songs, but it’s cool it’s there. I’m also unsure if there are actually any fail states or not. But I’m not 100% sure I agree a game needs fail states. Either way, that’s going to be the biggest draw back for some, but it’s not for us all, and certainly not for me. I was put on the wrong foot because of the notice of stolen land stuff and I was looking for woke nonsense in the game because of it, well… Looking for it is not correct. I was expecting it. However, if I’m totally fair, naw, not really. Oh sure, there are plenty of things that are there that woke culture rallies around, but they are not really focused on or pointed out. Not in a way that screamed to me they were letting agenda get in the way of good story and art. I mean, if the mere existence of things the cult of woke would love is something that would turn you off and make you hate the experience, then sure it’s there this one is not for you. But I try not to be Mr. Reactionary guy. At least not kneejerk reactionary. None of the characters are totally defined by any woke quotient they may fill. I don’t know, I just never felt like anything here was there to pander or to “educate” people. It all felt like it was just there, flavor for the story, seasonings they chose to use. Is there a cringe line here or there? Absolutely. But nothing about it bothered me and In went in on high alert. So, take that for what it’s worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is an interactive visual novel that seamlessly blends Greek mythological themes and musicals together, graced by enchanting visuals, an extraordinary ever-changing soundtrack, and stellar vocal performances. It is both an ambitious and innovative game, offering a refreshingly pleasant journey with ample replayability. You play as Grace, a young woman who gets framed for the murder of a muse. In order to clear your name, you must gather evidence and absolve yourself within a week. You discover a unique power that allows you to make people sing the truth. With this newfound ability, you collaborate with Greek deities, residing in human guise within the contemporary world. Along the way, you will uncover secrets, face dangers, and maybe even experience love.Your journey's outcome rests on your choices, shaping the narrative. The story captivates with its unique and modern take on Greek mythology, filled with enough twists and turns to prevent it from going stale, albeit predictable, but nonetheless thrilling to see play out.  From a mechanical standpoint, Stray Gods is an intriguing interactive visual novel game infused with a hint of RPG elements. At its core, the experience revolves around decision-making, intertwining threads of choices, harmonious musical interludes, relationship dynamics, and an enthralling murder mystery that awaits unraveling.  At the start of the game, you get a pivotal decision – the selection of one among three defining traits: "Charming," "Kickass," and "Clever." These traits serve as the compass for your interactions, shaping not only your path but also influencing the fates of those around you. Each unique quality unlocks specific dialogue options, granting access only accessible if you have the corresponding trait. For instance, with the "Kickass" trait, you can say something imposing and force your way through a situation, whereas with "Clever," you would use your intellect to navigate it. All the traits serve as pivotal junctions that help shape the trajectory of your narrative adventure, leading to noticeable variances in dialogue and outcomes. Witnessing their effects on the story is always entertaining and fascinating, even when it does not go as planned.Much like conversations, the musical sections are interactive and branching, but now with a unique twist – the ability to reshape lyrics and melodies according to your choices.  The musical acts undeniably take center stage, consistently delivering moments of sheer delight and profound narrative depth. They seamlessly intertwine entertainment with storytelling, ensuring an experience that is not only enjoyable but also enriched with layers of meaning. I even found myself humming along and, at times, could not resist the urge to mumble along, attempting to sing along with the piece. As you engage in noteworthy interactions, you forge relationships through your choices, ultimately influencing how the characters perceive and interact with you. They might offer invaluable assistance, become a reliable ally, or present unanticipated challenges that may either aid or hinder your progress in searching for clues. You will also occasionally get the opportunity to flirt and build romantic connections. These choices are always cherished, offering a delightful pause from the overarching story.  The visuals feature a captivating blend of cel-shading and cartoony graphics with various visual styles such as cross-hatching, halftone dots, and more creating a distinctive fusion of visual styles that breathe more life into the already vibrant and colorful 3D-modelled environments. In contrast, the characters exude charisma through their 2D hand-illustrated designs, adding an intriguing visual dimension to the storytelling.The character designs hold a distinctiveness, reimagining the Greek gods within a contemporary setting that challenges conventional tales and depictions of them.  In terms of movement, Summerfall Studios embraced a minimalist animation style. Everything remains mostly still, conveying only the necessary expressions and emotions while allowing the cinematography to do most of the work, which generally works fine. However, some scenes could have benefitted from just a touch more liveliness.Audibly, it sounds great; the voice-acting performances stand out as nothing short of spectacular, establishing a profound connection to each god's emotions and actions, which is hardly surprising given the ensemble's remarkable talent in this game. From Laura Bailey and Khary Payton to Troy Baker and an array of other immensely skilled voice actors, every individual consistently exceeds expectations. It is particularly apparent in their ability to perfectly convey inner struggles during subdued moments and casual conversations, transitioning seamlessly into the musical segments.Given its nature as a visual novel, while the presence of sound effects might not be abundant, the ones incorporated hold significant importance. These auditory elements contribute to the various scenarios, whether through subtle audio cues or the depiction of characters' movements. However, sporadic audio mixing issues did occur, impacting the experience and making some moments feel less impactful than they would have otherwise.The soundtrack by Austin Wintory truly is exceptional, not just because of its remarkable quality but also because of the quantity of potential variations. Depending on your choices, you will curate the soundtrack, creating a unique and personalized musical journey. Choices will significantly impact the song's mood and eventual outcome, but what is truly impressive is how seamlessly it blends and switches between these various moods while sounding incredible. The dedication invested in the OST is genuinely awe-inspiring – not one, but four soundtracks were meticulously crafted for Stray's God, each masterfully evoking a spectrum of emotions and contributing to an unceasingly enthralling and delightfully unparalleled experience with every musical act. The songs adhere to the typical musical pattern – with some exceptional works that leave a lasting impression for days, while others may not reach the same heights. Nevertheless, even at their least impressive, they remain enjoyable and remarkably suited to the narrative at hand.PC: i7-9700K, 24GB of RAM, and a RTX 2080 Ti. SD: 800p, 60 FPS, ~1.5-2 hours battery, ~20W,  65-72 C. My save file on PC was deleted due to a bug during Act 2, forcing me to start over. Fortunately, the issue has since been resolved. Additionally, the team has addressed the audio issues and is working to fix them with an upcoming patch.Stray Gods exceeded my expectations, providing an incredibly entertaining and refreshing experience filled with charm, joy, and evident love and care put into every aspect of the game. From the outstanding voice acting and soundtrack to the compelling story and stunning visuals, it all comes together to create an astonishing package.

_childDocuments_.review: I like story based games, I like good murder mystery, and I like musicals. I don't think I've ever played a musical game before. This game was so close to getting a recommendation for me, but it failed at being a musical.First of - the presentation is very good, but it might not be to everyones liking. For the most of the time you're presented still images with very little animations. It creates comic book vibe, and I'm fine with that. I found it generally very well done and pretty. I like the art style they went for as well.The mystery is... pretty bad. The obvious criminal is the real criminal, no twist, no mystery. The "how did it" is pretty lame as well... and "why did it" is even worse. Overall this fails as mystery. The murder mystery is only the background, really, for all the personal issues everyone has in this game. This is character-focused game, where story doesn't really matter.On the other hand I liked the premise of gods living in America under new lives, and the world created. There were some really interesting ideas, and it allowed for some room to explore interesting concepts, and lives of those kind-of-immortal beings. Everyone you meet is broken in some way, and you're there to fix them (or not). This could have been great, but I found most of the problems faced by the characters to be resolved in terrible ways. Because they are all solved by the power of songs. I'll get back to it.In general, in every chapter you first spend an 30-40 minutes talking with some relevant characters, and those dialogues are written in such a dry manner I had hard time staying asleep. In general they will complain how they face some "unsolvable" personal issue, and you can gather some more input on those topics from 3 people (usually that's how many you can talk with). Then the main person tries to do a thing, and you sing with them for 1-2 minutes, and in most non-convincing way magically convince the person to whatever you want them to. The game explains, that the songs you sing have power to lead people into directions they already can take, so in theory you just push them a bit over an edge. So the songs don't have to be convincing, good, or in any way coherent to get the person to do what they want. Usually the very last choice you make during a song is the choice of what will happen. It leads to unfulfilling finish in every sub-story.Furthermore, not how little time is spent on songs, and how much on regular boring talking. This game would have been much better if they cut off 90% of that fluff and had 1-2 hour runtime, mostly focused on being a musical. Right now it doesn't feel like one. But, I also didn't like the songs. They work like this - the opponent sings a bit, then you choose one of 3 options, related, and color coded to one of your main aspects(charming, clever, or kickass). You get such choice a few times during the songs... But unless you always select the same aspect the songs ends up as total mess. And you end up with the same choices anyway (I think, I didn't experiment with it fully, I think final songs might have more nuance to them). And the choices come out of nowhere, and have really not much to do with any convincing that went on. After each song I had this feeling of "this doesn't feel right", and like there was something missing. Near the start of the game you are made to choose an aspect, and this will lock you out of some options in dialogues later on. This reduces the ability to roleplay, as there was no way to stray too much out of the singular option selected at start. Somewhere mid-game you for some reason get another aspect, so it locks you only out of 1 option later on. I don't think it added much, if anything to the game, except for trying to add artificial replay value.Obviously a lot of work went into making basically 3 versions of each song, and making sure it kind of makes sense no matter what you choose... But it ends up underwhelming. It feels like the same effort would have been better spent on making the songs better, more songs, or longer songs.Some people complain that songs are badly written, but I would say, the ones I've heard (I've seen there are achievements for songs I didn't see) were just fine. The spread of styles of music and genres was pretty good. I've heard there's also rap song, but I didn't get it. The issue is, they are just not meaningful enough story-wise. And forcing nearly all major decisions into songs is double-edged sword. And in most cases it mostly hurt overall experience.There were also, some inconsistencies in stories. For example Faun character, when I last met him, we left in generally fine terms, but I didn't go into romance path. Next time I met him, he, and the MC, acted as if last time we went into worst argument ever. That was the biggest inconsistency, but there were also some tiny ones. I also, apparently, ordered a character to kill another by choosing "Do something about them", by which I though I meant . But fortunately all it did was leave an achievement, but no character was harmed.Also, I didn't buy the problems all the gods we met had. They struggled with them for hundreds of years, or thousands of years, and one or two songs fix them... Well, first of all, some of those problems are very implausible to be held for so long... For which I summoned suspension of disbelief to the best of my ability. Second of all, if the very unconvincing songs MC sings are enough to "fix those people" then .This game has pretty modern sensibilities. It has very inclusive cast, you have people of color, different body types, a person in wheelchair, non-binary person. Also, first time I've seen, trigger warnings in main menu (although they would fit better on store page, once the game is bought it it's a bit too late). It also has a launch screen about being made on stolen ground.One thing I didn't really care about was "time limit" of 7 days, but the writers didn't do anything with it. Really, only enough events happen for it to be 24 hours time limit. Most of the 7 days is just skipped over, and things continue that you wouldn't even notice time skip, if the day number wasn't written on the screen. So, this game is mostly a Telltale game, with a bit of songs thrown in. The roleplaying part is just limited to choices, and the choices are meh. Maybe, in the parts of the game I didn't see, things were more interesting, but I had no interest in replaying the game once finished to explore different possibilities. So judging from what I experienced in my playthrought - unfortunately I can't give this thumbs up. But there is potential, and while I'll be skipping the DLC, I'll be looking at developer's next game. Hopefully they learned a lot from this one, and only can get up.

_childDocuments_.review: A spoiler free review by a Hellenic Polytheist with some general notes at the end.The Bad- If you're hoping they didn't do the thing that pretty much all modern story's do you will be disappointed Ares, Zeus and Hades got the very typical "Bad guy" portrayal. Though none of them are actually in the game only mentioned by others.  - Zeus, A couple throwaway lines you might be able to play the game without ever coming across.  - Ares, Pretty big in Aphrodite's story not really avoidable, He is of course portrayed as a war obsessed betrayer with (I believe) the implication that he sided with the Nazi's in WW2.   - Hades, Very big in Persephone's story very unavoidable, He's portrayed as being a tyrant ruler, abuser, etc. pretty much what you'd expect.- Aphrodite, My interpretation is they made Her very much "The Victim" also no acknowledgment to her war aspects. I personally really didn't like Her overall portrayal, But I can see other interpretations.- They equate The Underworld to hell a couple times. One of the times was more of a metaphor.- Persephone, Personal preference I did not like anything about Her portrayal/story except how bad-ass She is. But as a character she's cool.The Neutral- They used the Latin spelling. The Good- Aphrodite, I like that they showed that beauty is not just a thin white woman. I also liked how (depending on how the song goes) Aphrodite's story shows how important it is to have love and support which I personally connect with Her.- They made a couple references to Kore and the connection to Persephone, I enjoyed that. There are a few other "easter eggs" too like the golden apple, reference to the Eleusinian Mysteries, etc it's all fun. - Orpheus' portrayal was amazing. No notes, 10/10.- I thought any other portrayals not mentioned were alright and/or fun, I really liked Eros' portrayal in particular.General Notes- The music is amazing! I didn't love every song immediately but by the end I did, though I like some versions better than others.- The art and character design are awesome!- Pan is the best romance. But I liked all except Freddie's but that's just because in order to romance her you have to not respect her wishes at a certain point. - The voice actor's are all super amazing but the ones that stood out a little more to me are Laura Bailey(Grace), Khary Payton(Pan) and Anjali Bhimani(Medusa).- The premise of the Idols and eidolons is very fun for a modern story.- Mostly a positive I thought it was pretty obvious who done it, but really how and why are almost always more important to me and while how is not explained to my liking why works for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I had only heard about this game on accident. I had previously backed a similar game (Karmaflow, a rock opera (really metal) video game) and had always wanted another game similar to it in concept. You have a song that changes based on your choices.  I was not only surprised by the depth of the choices, but the writing behind the characters. Being completely transparent, this game is NOT for everyone. You're going on a narrative journey from scene to scene and your choices are only in dialogue or musical sequences. There is very little interaction outside of this aspect. It is entirely voiced but does have issues with volume between lines, especially in act III. However, this does not ruin the experience. I have played through this game only twice and both playthroughs have similar narrative beats and ultimately culminates in a similar ending. However, who is with you along the way, what their story is after it "ends," and the songs you create can be drastically different. If you are a music nerd like me, like visual novel-lite gameplay elements, and geek out around the aspect that your musical numbers (for lack of a better term) can have dozens, if not hundreds of variations based on your choices, definitely get this game. Regarding the various soundtracks for purchase - I personally don't like them. This is due to my experiences not being reflected in the released soundtracks. I may have to record "my version" from my PC for my listening pleasure based on what I feel is the cannon based on my choices. A small gripe, for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for Stray Gods since the first moment I've heard about it and now that I have 4 runs of it under my belt I feel ready for a review.First off a few things that might be misleading from the trailers and should be cleared up:- It's not what most people (myself included) would call an "RPG". "RPG" evokes skill trees and levelling up, strategic battles and exploration. There's none of that here. It is TECHNICALLY a Roleplay as you will interpret the protagonist, Grace, in the way you best see fit, but there are no RPG mechanics. It's a Visual Novel, through and through.- It's not an actual murder mystery. Some games that revolve around murder mystery solving will have you actively look for clues and ask the players to find the murderer, possibly getting the wrong one or leaving the case unsolved. This is not the case here, the story will evolve regardless and the case will be solved. So... no need to take notes or wrack your brain, this isn't what the game is about.With this in mind, Stray Gods may be defined as less of a "game" and more of an "interactive graphic novel". You'll have plenty of choices that will affect HOW things develop but not WHAT the events are. The conversations that you'll have may be quite different, the events may change, but you'll still go from point A to point B in the same way regardless of your choices.Having said that, I wouldn't say that the choices don't matter, because they will affect the epilogue of basically each and every character in the story: you can't change the course of the story, but you can change the ending of specific character arcs. While that may not seem like much, I can almost guarantee that you're going to care because the characters are all well-written and easy to like, helped by the stellar voice acting that is the core of the game (even if sound balancing of some lines is all over the place). I may be biased as Laura Bailey and Troy Baker are my favourite VAs in general, but this game is just packed with the best, and even characters that have very little space in the story end up being memorable thanks to good lines delivered perfectly (e.g. Medusa). Still on the characters, being a VN it does feature the mandatory romance options: there are 4 in this case, and I found that all of them were very good options. So... have fun and explore them.Before moving to the juicy part of the game, which is the music, a mention of the graphics side: the graphical presentation of the game gives it a very "graphic novel/comic book" style, also because it uses mostly still images, there are no animations. The colors are bright and vibrant, there are lots of nice details on the art, and each character design is very well-defined and diverse... but during the conversations it can get a bit repetitive to see the same character artworks in the same poses over and over. During the song acts, instead, there's a lot more to see and it's much more interesting.So, the song acts... there are plenty and with lots of possible outcomes to them. As shown in the trailers, you'll have up to 3 choices at certain points of the songs, and your choices will affect the "mood" of the song, and possibly its overall outcome. What is important to know is that in some cases EARLIER choices affect this too: it's not just that every segment of a song has 3 possible variations, there are MANY more that you can discover by playing out the whole song differently. I also bought the 4 soundtracks to the game, and some sections that I played out by picking different choices are not found in any of those. The variation you can have is just that massive. This definitely took a lot of work and is played out wonderfully in game, making the song sections very interesting. The songs themselves are, like in every musical, not always the best: some are true masterworks that will remain in the back of your head for days, others not so much, but even at their worst they are a good listen and very appropriate for the narrative... maybe just not that catchy or memorable.In a bottom line comment Stray Gods features an interesting art style, a wonderful cast of characters brought to life by a wonderful cast of voice actors, a story that works, and some great musical pieces. I found myself wanting to explore all the choices and outcomes, and I think that many others might want to do the same. If it sounds like something you might enjoy, go for it.There are a few things that I found to be missing, though. Not flaws in and of themselves, but features that would have been welcome in my opinion:- More save slots and the ability to manually save the game. As things are, you cannot just save before a splitting point to have an easier time getting all the endings and exploring choices. As it takes a minimum of 5 runs to get all endings, and a run is around 5 hours long... I would have liked being able to get a few shortcuts.- A gallery feature where one can access the artworks, see journal entries, and replay songs without having to go through 4+ hours of gameplay maybe just to try a new variation on a specific song.

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole: one of the more solid VNs I've played. The voice acting is great across the board, the art style's clean and clear and despite never exactly being animated has enough reframing and camera movement to keep scenes feeling a lot more dynamic than the average "two character images stand side by side above a text box" structure of this kind of game. The sense of motion alone holds attention so much better for that reason, and that's before getting into the wide variety of moods and atmospheres created in the song events.The songs themselves may be fairly basic in structure, but given the context I'd say that makes sense. It's not turning everyone into complex poets; it's spilling their motives and feelings into the open in their own words, more or less.I think the only real drawback to the game's design is skipping: you can't just skip line by line, it jumps entire chunks of scenes if it's all text you've seen on a previous playthrough, often jumping right to the next decision point in the scene without providing much context for the answers you're offered if you don't remember exactly what's asked before that point, and I didn't see a transcript to review dialogue. On the other hand, you can't skip the songs at all, and since there's just one save slot per playthrough you can't easily branch off to try multiple outcomes from a decision point. It's not that the game isn't worth sitting through a second/third/fourth time to try an entirely different route, but it's a bit much when all you want to do is change one line in a song, or decide you don't want to flirt with X character after all, or etc.That only matters for completionism though, really. For the first playthrough? Fully recommended. And also fully recommended for the second playthrough to try desperately fixing what you messed up on your first.After that... *wobbles hand* YMMV

_childDocuments_.review: ❤️❤️🤍🤍🤍This is quite a unique visual novel crossed with a musical. It has a very light role-playing element to it based on three different traits you can express through dialogue and in song. You can use charm, be clever and witty, or approach the game with the firey passion of a rocker girl. The thing I loved the most about the game was the choice of voice actors, across the board. It made me especially happy to hear some of the Critical Role gang & guests sing. I didn't find the writing to be that great, but it was fine in the context of also attempting to be a musical. The songs themselves would have needed some more time to cook in order to become true bangers. They’re serviceable, if only for the novelty of it all, but if this studio or another tries to make a game like this in the future, the song writing will need to be at a much higher level for me to remain interested.  I’m not a fan of the art direction. Many of the character designs weren’t visually appealing to me at all. I also especially disliked how the artist exaggerates masculine features on female characters in some angles.Scene transitions also felt a bit jittery. Characters have a very limited range of expression as it’s all stills and paper dolls. Normally, this wouldn’t bother me, and it’s not that it feels cheap. I just think the presentation is held back by the tech. For example, I would really like to see what this studio could do with a game engine like the one used for The Wolf Among Us. All in all, it’s an okay game that I recommend if you’re looking for something different than what you’re used to.

_childDocuments_.review: "Stray Gods: the roleplaying musical " has truly captivated my heart and mind in a way I never anticipated. From the moment I stepped into this enchanting world, I felt an overwhelming wave of emotion, a connection to the characters and their stories that has left a profound impact on me. It’s rare for a game to resonate on such a deep level, and yet here I am, five playthroughs in, still discovering new layers and meanings within its beautifully crafted narrative.The premise of "Stray Gods" is engaging, to say the least. It beautifully intertwines music and storytelling, allowing players to explore themes of identity, belonging, and the notion that everything happens for a reason. As someone who has often felt lost in life, the game provided a kind of solace. It was as if the story was speaking directly to me, helping me to realize that my struggles and uncertainties are part of a larger journey. Each decision I made felt significant, impacting not just the characters’ paths but also my own introspection. This compelling sense of agency is enhanced by the multitude of choices offered throughout the game, resulting in a richly layered narrative that encourages replayability. The music is another highlight. Each song is crafted with care, enhancing the emotional stakes and drawing players deeper into the narrative. It’s astonishing how the soundtrack complements the gameplay, making every choice resonate even more. I found myself humming the tunes long after I had put down the controller, a testament to their catchiness and emotional weight.Moreover, the vibrant art style and character design create an immersive experience. The creators clearly dedicated time and effort to develop each character, giving them depth and complexity that make their arcs feel real and relatable. I became genuinely invested in their journeys, finding comfort and companionship in their stories.Overall, "Stray Gods" is more than just a game; it’s an emotional exploration of the human experience. Each playthrough reveals something new, reshaping my understanding of the narrative and, ultimately, myself. I am grateful to this game for helping me navigate my own feelings of belonging and purpose. It’s been a journey worth taking, and I am likely to replay it many more times in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is a breath of fresh air, even if I felt disappointed at the end of it.This game has a really great, unique concept--you play as a young woman suddenly gifted the powers of the Last Muse, and has seven days to prove her innocence in the murder of said muse. To do so, you need to help the last of the Greek gods confront their pasts and emotional blockages, and you do it by making them burst into song. It's equal parts silly and serious, and pretty engaging, with a wonderful cast of characters and enticing lore.My problems lie in how unfinished the game feels. For starters, the actual songs just... aren't very good. Part of this is due to the gameplay mechanic where you control the progression of the song--if you want to intervene, or let the other characters sing it out solo, and how intense or emotionally sensitive you want to be. These changes in direction can make each musical number feel like three separate songs smashed together. They don't flow. The lyrics themselves felt poorly written as well. I'm not a musician by any means, but it felt like the lyrics didn't meet the tempo and often went off beat, and were pretty cheesy.I also finished the game with lots of unfinished questions, and the resolution left a lot to be desired. It was also very short. I completed the game in about seven hours. It does have some branching paths, but they're pretty inconsequential to the outcome and didn't really feel worth it to me to replay for.Overall, I enjoyed this game, and would recommend others play it, but not for the $30 price tag it boasts. Especially given it is not animated, for $30 I would expect a much longer game, with a deeper story, and better musical pieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: idk if there's ever been a game more tailor made to my interests. Greek mythology, musicals, and choice-based RPGs? Sign me up! Too ADHD, things lose my attention, 100%ing stuff usually involves grinding out tedious achievements and I get bored. _childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is clearly a labor of love and is a great visual novel. It didn't feel like playing a game, and more-so like listening to a story; however, I think that's one of its strong suits, albeit one not well advertised. That genre choice allowed the music and the awesome voice acting to shine. There's very few games I finish this quickly, and it's for good reason. This isn't to say this game isn't without flaw--the very same indie aspects that allow it to shine also put blemishes on its surface. Some of the 3D graphics come off pixelated and under-finished at times when compared to the beautiful 2D art of the characters, and, as many people mention, the audio balancing is often an issue as it fluctuates from really quiet to uncalled-for yelling. In the end, the plot left me excited to pick up the "notes left unsung", as it were--there's plenty of opportunity for choice within the confines of the overall plot, and even the little achievements that pop up make you wonder what else is just behind the other doors. Each character feels like they're left a teeny bit underdeveloped after the first play through, but that's something I feel might be resolved as I play through it again. Definitely pick up this title and give it a chance--it's a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: It was an absolute amazing experience!The characters were real and grounded with their own well thought out motivations. The musical numbers were fantastic and I found that there were huge variations depending on your choices; the accompaniment and the backing changed drastically to fit within these choices and led to different songs too!The direction was phenomenal and all of the characters really embody the tone and atmosphere the work is trying to create: character design, art direction, background elements, voice acting, etc. These elements really blend well together into a kind of pot that--at least in my play-through--never felt out of place. Everyone who worked on this game did a great job bringing it all together!Although I did experience some minor graphical glitches and the some lines of dialogue would be too quiet compared to other characters within the scene. Additionally, there are some aspects of the ui/ux that feel very renpy adjacent and strange to navigate--for lack of a better word--though this doesn't detract from the experience in terms of the core musical game play.Overall, a fantastic musical that felt like it was just for me; getting to know all of the characters and getting to know them personally and on my own terms. This game really makes you feel like you're making an impact with all of the bigger choices. Not so much a traditional role-playing game in the strictest of definitions, but a game I feel stretches beyond into a different territory of gaming that I wished was more prevalent.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Stray Gods is a good game, buy it.Slightly longer version. Stray gods has a lot of heart and its characters are interesting and varied, not only that they can surprise you. I went into my first playthrough with the idea of being a fiery ass kicker who was gonna romance Persephone. But the story and the way the game introduced the plot elements I found myself suddenly more inclined towards a softer and earnest MC, I found myself mostly picking caring and forgiving choices and along the way despite having the options to, I found myself rooting for the MC's best friend and I simply had to go with that romance route.I was super pleased that my choices paid off, I befriended everyone and got my happy ever after. Nowadays many games require you to jump through hoops and select specific choices to get the best possible outcome but here I just felt it flowed naturally and I was rewarded for my less bleak outlook. Its hard to say much in detail as it would take away from the experience but I found myself sniffling more than once as the moments got to me.Its not perfect mind you, while I can't find much issue with the story, the game suffers from some audio imbalance(A massive no no in a game like this) and for a visual novel style game, its frankly silly the game automatically tries to run you at max frames. With no actual in-game frame limiter I have to deduct some points as my GPU was cooking. Still, I was able to set an FPS limit with my AMD software and the game ran pretty smoothly, I only encountered one time I was forced to restart the game as sound cut out.Overall I'd say once the stability issues and audio gets smoothed out I can't really find anything bad to say about the game.Okay maybe the whole joke about a cat dying felt a bit out of place.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some technical hiccups, a labor of love worth experiencing for anyone who enjoys a good fantasy storyline.Stray Gods is a narrative adventure musical that tells the tale of Grace as she transitions from being a mortal to an Idol- Greek gods who have lived amongst us in the shadows all this time- and is set to investigating the circumstances that lead to her change. Perhaps the genre of game this could be most likened to would be a visual novel, but calling it a visual novel would be doing it a  disservice.Whereas visual novels are usually a number of static images used over and over again, Stray Gods features a TON of animation, from detailed and expressive stills of the characters, to 3D-rendered environments that the camera swivels and pans and explores throughout the tale, especially during the musical sequences. One of the main mechanics of the game is definitely dialogue choices, but even these feel fresh during the musical sequences as your choices change the tone of the music in real time, and your duet partners will respond in kind.The game has a solid and engaging narrative throughout, with new plot mechanics and twists and turns that keeps you wondering what comes next. The writing is solid- playful when it's meant to be, and serious and believable when the situation calls for it. The time taken to develop the world and the characters actually surprised me- if you take the time to visit characters between main objectives they have A LOT to say about the world, the story and even their personal histories, that really help add depth to the events and the world of the game, as well as the characters themselves.The voice acting is often top notch, and there's some real great singers on board (Persephone and Pan especially stand out), and the amount of love that went into the animation of these characters and the cinematography of sequences is really quite impressive. And fortunately, there are a couple of memorable songs along the way- one that occurs at a party almost had me in tears.It's also worth mentioning that the game has both  as well as  Both of these add a lot of replayability incentive to the game, and with a run-through play time of about 6 hours, this feels a lot more doable than something like restarting The Witcher for another playthrough.Interestingly, for being a musical game, one of the biggest drawbacks of the game is the audio. The game desperately needs someone to go through and normalize all the voice acting- lines between characters in the same scenes can jump between being inaudible one line to blowing your ears out the next- and this isn't even necessarily between two different characters, this can happen between lines on the same character. At one point especially it was good that subtitles are on by default because I couldn't even hear that Calliope talking, while all the other characters in the scene were perfectly audible.I also hesitate to say this, because it may be entirely subjective, but a lot of the music was a miss for me. There's a lot really good passages of music inside of the songs, and some fun execution of ideas , but generally the background music feels 'OK' at best, and a lot of the lyrics don't feel... lyrical. Much more like they were written as script and then crammed in on top of existing music, which leads to a lot of crammed words, awkward melodies, non-pitched recitation and a lack of rhyming. As a person who's big into music this was disappointing for me- but it should also be noted that I'm not a big  person, so I might just not be the audience for the style of writing. That being said, the narrative of the story and the visuals was enough to carry me through these sequences without much discomfort, and there's at least one truly good song, and one that is at least interesting in its execution  There's also some issues with continuity in the current build, but hopefully that's something the developers can correct with time- I'll write up my experience in the forums rather than here, so hopefully it will be corrected for later players.This game is well worth picking up. A great story, great art, great animations, great voice acting, interesting characters and world, and strong replayability incentive make it worth every penny. There's some technical issues that hopefully the developer can correct with some time, and the music may not be to everyone's taste, but there's so much GOOD here that it's well worth experiencing for anyone who likes a good story.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have the power to change your fate? Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical follows Grace, a young woman feeling lost and alone, as she discovers the world of Greek Gods who have been hiding among the mortals. She encounters Calliope, the last existing Muse, who suddenly dies in Grace’s arms. In her final moments, Calliope gives Grace her powers. With little understanding of the world she has just found herself, Grace will have to prove her innocence by charming, negotiating, or strong-arming the individuals you come across. If you’ve been following my reviews, you’ll know visual novels get the strongest critiques. Stray Gods, however, fully captivated me. I actually wanted to take my time and listen to all of the dialogue options - which is incredibly rare. I also actively tried to figure out the mystery, I didn’t just wait to see what would happen. It’s good enough that I might even go back and play through to get all of the achievements and see what else could happen. The voice acting was absolutely phenomenal, which made up for the lack of drawn character emotion on a lot of lines, and I really loved the art style.   Now, I heard a lot about this game last year and it did win a few awards in 2023. But…in my personal opinion - the songs were not great. They felt like they were written by someone with very basic knowledge of how to write a song, with very basic rhyming. I absolutely love musicals, and I know there are some cheesy show tunes, but I wouldn’t even call these songs cheesy. Just poorly written and maybe not sung by the right person, despite the stellar voice acting cast. It was a really cool mechanic to decide which direction the song was taking, and it was one of the core game mechanics I loved about the game. But I think having so many options might have led to the poor quality of the overall song. Again, as with any review, this is just my opinion.The only other critique I had with the game was the dialogue. In certain spots of the game, the voice acting would just cut off. You were able to read the entire text with the subtitles so you didn’t miss anything, but it was just a little weird. It also didn’t happen just once or twice, it was pretty often, and was mostly with Apollo’s lines. I’m not sure if this was just a glitch or if this was an editing issue. I know those seem like pretty big critiques that would make me give it a poor rating. But there was just something about it that still has me wanting to pick it right back up. It might have been the voice acting (I’m a sucker for good voice acting) or it might have been the character growth, or the character relationships, or the overall gameplay. Take your pick, I’m still going to recommend it and can’t wait for the Orpheus DLC!

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting to settle down for a few hours of cheese, but actually the game holds up really well.The written dialogue and voice acting is almost universally fantastic, the songs are catchy and engaging in the musical theatre style you would expect, and the art is exceptionally easy on the eye.Despite being a pretty standard on-rails visual novel there was enough in the choices to give me a sense of agency.For the first couple of hours I was genuinely blown away, and I still have the songs stuck in my head.The second half falls off a bit, as I find is typical when a developer’s ambition exceeds their budget, but it’s a minor quibble.Slightly more jarring is how hard the game tries to get you to romance the main characters. Everyone is a love interest, and the interactions come across as forced and inauthentic. I mean, really, centuries old Greek gods swooning for a human after only a couple of days interaction is more than a little bit creepy.One wonders what could have been, had the developers invested a little more time into strengthening the main story arc instead of fragmenting it with distracting and unnecessary relationship drama.Which also leans into my main criticism, which is that the protagonist is a classic Mary Sue. Honestly, the game is far better in the first half where the protagonist is being swept up into a drama far greater than herself, compared to the second half which inexplicably flips to her more or less leading the whole shebang. It’s ultimately a lazy and uninspired story arc that leaves you with a touch of whiplash.The game also treats murder and death far too glibly for my taste. If nothing else, the main protagonist’s reactions are implausibly comfortable with circumstances that would be traumatic for anyone who isn’t an actual sociopath. Sure, it's a game, but it's a game that leans heavily into emotional authenticity, and mostly does so very well, so it feels particularly jarring in that context.As a result, I had to struggle through the second half of the game, and I have no particular interest in revisiting this world to see the missed content, or to buy the DLC, which is a shame.Still, I can happily recommend the game for what it is, and parts continue to linger, which is more than I can say for 99% of the games in my library.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to Stray Gods on the strength of some of the voice actors and several recommendations.  This kind of 'interactive graphic novel' format is largely not my jam - I want a little more game in my games, y'know?  But if you come to it expecting an interactive, musical graphic novel, there's a lot here to like: very many alternate paths, with very many alternate results; excellent music with many excellent vocal performances; characters that you can empathize with, who are really carried on the strength of the voices.  No speakers/headphones?  Don't bother.  But whoever can lend it an ear should appreciate the powerful performances put forth by the voice cast in this excellent piece of interactive fiction.

_childDocuments_.review: This game won't be for everyone and I'd rather people who are the target audience find it than those who aren't. This is for people who love musicals and interactive stories. There are some game elements in it, but so far it seems they are mainly directing the flow of the story and which characters are more involved. However, I have not yet finished it so I can't say yet how much "gaming" is involved. I hope people will let go of preconceived notions, and just enjoy something new and different. This isn't a traditional game, it never claimed to be. It will resonate with people who enjoy the voice cast. It will bore some people who want action and aren't that big into storytelling or don't like musical theater much. I personally am enjoying listening to the characters and story being brought to life with such passion and joy. But I do love musicals, so being able to direct the flow of this one and be in the middle of it resonates with me. I just hope people who aren't the target audience can just accept that fact, and not try to squish something new because it chose to color outside the lines.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute work of art, and the implementation of Mass Effect 2 - style conversation blockouts pulled me out of it terribly over and over and almost ruined it for me.The art is gorgeous. The music is fantastic. Your control over the music, is phenomenal. The setting is clever and scintillating and I want to live in this world forever. And the characters feel so real,  The voice acting is stellar, and the story is gripping and amazing.But holy crap, I hate games like this, like Mass Effect 2, where I'm actively penalized for making varied and interesting dialogue decisions instead of being a one-note character. I've had dialogues where all of my options but one were disabled because I didn't have enough Charming points to say "it's awful that that happened to you," or enough Kickass points to say "I'm angry right now!"If that doesn't turn you off, and it genuinely came close a few times for me, this game is a must-play.  It goes in my list of games to show off to people who don't believe that games can be art, because this is nothing less.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, I really loved this one! Big recommend for anyone who likes story-focused games (with a few caveats). Stray Gods describes itself as a "roleplaying musical," and it is; but I think looking at it more as "a cool visual novel with musical elements" will probably give you a better expectation. It's presented mostly in still images, with maybe just a bit animation thrown in (the characters do get to make lots of very expressive faces though!), and all your interactions happen via a Mass Effect-style dialogue wheel. The twist is that (for reasons that actually do factor into the plot) characters will periodically burst into song, and your dialogue choices can also happen *within* songs, sending them down alternate paths, and even changing the genre a bit in some cases. You also get to pick a trait at the beginning (clever, compassionate, or aggressive), which will unlock new dialogue options throughout the game.Now, while the way they pull this all off is a technical marvel, I don't think it's actually that great as a musical. Sometimes the orchestration can be awkward; sometimes they try to cram too much plot into the lyrics; sometimes the mixing quality just seems off. The dialogue itself is at least as engaging as the average story-based game, and often more so, but I think the songs end up being more a novel way to deliver dialogue rather than something you'll be humming afterwards. Similarly, while the plot is set up as a mystery, that's not really the hook either (don't expect much, or frankly anything at all, in the way of deduction). The real heart of the game is in the characters, and in the way it keeps coming up with weird, unexpected ways to portray modern interpretations of the Greek gods.  in particular is such a bonkers curve ball, but I was really impressed by how different it kept being from anything I was expecting. And I really, really fell for the characters (voiced by a murderers' row of talent--special shoutouts to Laura Bailey and Janina Gavankar, but they're all incredible). So much so in fact that now, having finished the story, I now just want to go back to make different choices, because oh man is there some stuff I wish I'd done differently. TL;DR: The songs are just okay, but the writing and the voice acting are excellent. If a six-to-seven hour story-based game sounds good to you, you'll probably enjoy this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Stick with me, because I loved this game but seem incapable of starting with the good when recounting or reviewing anything.The title's a misnomer - there's almost no gameplay to speak of and no more role playing than your average visual novel, which is more or less what it is. Any given screenshot - the promotional image isn't pulled directly from the game, but might as well be - looks great, but that's because the visuals are largely fully voiced storyboards, their limited movements having more in common with motion comics than other video games or animated films. The voice acting, too, despite its eye-popping cast (Troy Baker, who also served as voice director! Laura Bailey! Ashley Johnson! Merle Dandridge! Several other well-known folks NOT from the Last of Us!) feels more like an audio book than a video game, with characters more often talking at than to each other. And the songs are... functional, and sound like they were a nightmare to write (more on that in a moment), but I can't imagine myself listening to them outside of the game.I write the above not to condemn Stray Gods, but to temper expectations, because at its best it's like nothing I've played, using familiar mechanics - mainly a dialogue wheel - to tell a familiar type of story - a murder mystery - with some really eye-catching new coats of paint. David Gaider (a BioWare veteran who contributed to Neverwinter Nights and Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic before becoming the lead writer of the first three Dragon Age titles) is a talented, talented man, and he's firing on all cylinders here:- The world he's created feels well thought out, its depiction of the Greek gods feeling genuinely fresh (none of the six rulers have survived, for example) and its rules parcelled out in bits and pieces in a way that feels organic and delightful rather than overwhelming and underbaked;- His central mystery, involving the death of the muse Calliope, is engaging, with a solution holds water; - His plot is incredibly well-structured - framed for Calliope's death, Grace meets about ten gods or god-adjacent beings over the course of her journey, and your choices basically decide whether she'll have their support when she stands trial or alienate them along the way; and- His heroine's an all-timer.There's also the music, which may not be memorable on its own but has a surprisingly credible in-world explanation and literally sings in gameplay terms. The gods, you see, have always been susceptible to death in one form or another, and sometimes when one of them passes a mortal takes their place. For Calliope that mortal turns out to be Grace, who's seen fronting a rock band when the story begins and can use her new muse powers to make whoever she's confronting sing their hearts out - *and you, the player, get to choose which direction Grace pushes others to sing*.I do not envy the task the songwriters set for themselves with the soundtrack. Grace is so disaffected she needs the jolt of energy being blamed for a god's death can deliver, yet possesses enough warmth and latent anger that regardless of how you play her - and her mood can swing quite widely if you let it, and the songs along with it - she remains credibly herself. She's given multiple opportunities during every number to influence what her challengers are singing and the genre they're singing it in, and while more than a few individual lines made me cringe, the overall effect is powerful.I'm proud to have helped backed this game on Kickstarter and would do so again. If you have a spare weekend I highly recommend spending time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it because the idea sounded very promising: a playable musical. Could be fun. The story was interesting and it was cool to see what could happen if greek gods really existed and how they would live today. But unfortunately it was oh so bad in a lot of areas.That it's a VN was not the problem for once, but the character writing, depiction/artwork, and songs were. Most of the characters were almost unbearable, Freddy, Asterion and Venus above all.The characters look and act like the worst, most cringeworthy fan-fiction you've ever read.And it didn't help that the voice actors were pretty bad as well ( Except for Pan and Grace maybe ).As for the music: Sometimes the songs had a nice melody and it really felt like a musical.But the songs weren't really songs, more like speech but with melodic accentuation. More experiments like this are needed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a veeeeery qualified recommendation. IMO the game is good for one playthrough only, even though the gameplay is all about choices and consequences.The overall story and characters are great, the choose your own adventure mechanics fun and well developed. The voice acting is top notch. I never, and I mean never, listen to the full narration in games and always click to advance lines, but I wasn't moved to do that here at all because I wanted to listen to the actors. The art style is lovely.The problem is the songs. They're really not that good. They're clunky musically and weirdly emotionally flat. They all stay in a mopey, I'm-so-sad register without ever turning epic, even when the characters are singing about world-shattering confrontations. It's not clear to me whether that's due to a lack of singing skill on the part of the otherwise fantastic voice actors, or if the songs are just badly written, but they get so repetitive and so boring so quickly. Disclaimer though: I'm a professional classical singer so I have Opinions about songs and singing, haha.This is all okay for the first playthrough because the rest of the game is so good, but for me the songs really hinder replayability. I really don't want to listen to them again, and unlike the dialogue they are not skippable. It would be great if the devs could consider adding that as a feature!

_childDocuments_.review: The writing here is fantastic.I've played through it twice already, just to see how much minor changes affect the story.There have been cases where I was not entirely sure what a dialogue choice meant, but the game always gives you the option of going back to any earlier point in the story and replay from there if you're not happy with your choices.The characters and the voice acting are amazing. They really sell their lines.Arguably the most important part of this game.The songs vary in quality, although none of them ever go into the mediocre territory.They go from alright to absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bangers and to be honest most of them sit around in the upper end of that spectrum.The song audio is fantastic. I'm a bit of an audiophile and was listening mostly through my studio headphones.How a song should be mixed is always a subjective choice. Most songs in this game hit very close to orchestral and live performance audio, which for me was perfect.Again, subjective, but whenever the drums hit as well as they did I was having a blast.The vocals are very close to what you'd hear in a live stage performance, which fits the theme well I'd say.I encountered the 'deleted save file' bug on my first playthrough. Supposedly it is fixed now, but maybe exit the game after the first save icon appears, just to be sure. It only lost me like half an hour of gameplay, but some people seemed to have it a lot worse.Then there's the issue with the dialogue audio being in different volumes constantly.This is not something that happens during songs, however.Just be aware that you should turn down the volume to mediocre levels between songs, unless you like to flinch at someone whispering obnoxiously loud.It's so good.Honestly, the people behind this game have their heart in the right place and put that into their game as well.Be aware of the issues when you play it and you will have a great time, guaranteed.I highly recommend it and I'd love to see what else the creators can come up with.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is a musical experience. It's relatively short at about 5 hours and is essentially a musical production that you direct. The main plot doesn't change yet the choices made impact the lives of the characters you interact with in the story. There are pros and cons and on first play through it's a rare and amazing experience. The arrangement of the music is amazing. It's not perfect per say but it has a few tricks that make it astounding at times. Choices in the early part of the song can set the chorus which persist through a song or change the song format from ballad to rap.  Sometimes it feels organic and other times it can be jarring. The cons appear around the third play through when it starts to become apparent that player choices have weight but no consequence. That is to say the story will end relatively the same regardless of choice yet it has weight in the growth of the npc characters through their interaction with you and who will be with you in the end. Yet in a way this is not a weakness. Songs can get old after constant repetition if the player can actually take a wrong turn and end the story prematurely. Playing Stray Gods is like directing a musical with alternate approaches. The choices themselves are neither good or bad. Perhaps the story is better with tragic events of loss and lost love or perhaps it's a wondrous tale of adventure with new found friends or paving the road to new heights. The many facets give birth to new details in the story that can be surprising even after the sixth play through. In short Stray Gods is a marvelous experience well worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the game is not perfect.
