BUT, the music also has some pretty high highs and the positively stacked voice cast carries every line gracefully even when the words themselves can be, in my opinion, a little grating. I never found myself pulled out of the experience by a character's attempt at smartassery, it's just that it happened enough for me to feel the need to comment on. The story as a whole is great albeit a bit predictable (you'll guess the villain long before the game confirms it) but the story beats and world building are really clever and spark the imagination of the player and characters alike which should be commended. I never found myself wanting it to end or skipping over dialogue because the characters and the mechanics of their stories are genuinely fascinating in a way few media I've engaged with recently have been.Overall I would definitely recommend this game, it's a little rough around the edges but it offers an exceptional experience to those willing to cut loose and enjoy it's whimsy.

_childDocuments_.review: "Probably one of the most Disney-esque musicals to not be made by Disney." That's the comparison I gave my friend, but it doesn't quite do the game justice. That's just kind of the vibe I get. I played the entirety of Stray Gods, and it feels like what would happen if Disney and Telltale Games had a baby game. Cute and charming, but with abrupt moodswings towards dark intrigues and conflicts.When you hear "Role-Playing Musical," your immediate thought is going to be, "This is going to be really good or really cringe," but surprisingly its the former rather than the latter. Not all the musical numbers stick the landing, but what I like is that they serve the purpose of genuinely progressing the plot or character arc progression rather than just kinda interrupting everything for a two minute diversion. The songs are actual extensions of the characters and what's going on, thanks to the protagonists' Muse powers.The writing is solid. I somehow ended up liking even characters I kinda hated, because everyone has a story and their own personal damage, so after a few conversations, you start to get why they're so bitter or withdrawn, and set to work helping them grow as a person and heal. And despite this angst, some of the characters actually come across as fun and interesting. The world's beaten them down, but they haven't lost their wit or empathy. You know a game has good writing if you can name a point that made you "ugly cry," while also having a sense of humor to balance out the tragedies. And thank God it did, otherwise I might have stopped playing together and gone to bed wide-eyed and mind racing with alternative scenarios I wish had happened. The mystery was...eh. It loses its mystique as the game progresses and the suspect pool is whittled down. You kinda start drawing the obvious conclusion.This is the pettiest of peeves, but I do wish the "Skip" button would decide whether it skips an entire cutscene or just a line of dialogue, because it's irritating when I can't figure out how much I'm losing when I skip over dialogue I already played. SLIGHTLY irritating. Like I said, "the pettiest of peeves."Overall, Stray Gods was just a good time. Decent voice casting, a few memorable music numbers, and writing that kept me engaged rather than nodding off.Not gonna lie. I can't play any of my other games now; because this one is still stuck in my mind, making me replay over and over until it runs its course and I can stop humming the chorus line for The Ritual's red edition.EDIT: After coming back from Remnant 2 and Cyberpunk 2077's Phantom Liberty expansion, I think I can finally pin down why I obsessed over this game: It leaves me feeling HAPPY by the end. It doesn't yank my chain around, doesn't make me grind through the story toward a depressing ending, and it leaves me smiling, happy for characters I genuinely like. Most mainstream games nowadays have to end on some sad, tragic, or other depressing lamentation on the meaning of sacrifice and justice etc etc. or otherwise ends anticlimactically with "Teehee! You died anyway," or in a way that makes what you accomplished thus far feel moot. Stray Gods, an indie game, doesn't do that. And it was such a change of pace that it stuck in my mind for weeks after playing.So my 9/10 abruptly bumps up to 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for June 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 2nd, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.American Gods the Musical. Stray Gods does feel like a different take on American Gods, that’s not necessarily a bad thing, but it’s hard not to feel that this is a lighter version of American Gods, that doesn’t push the concept as far as it should have.  The main idea is that the Greek Gods are now in America and have been in hiding.  Grace, our main character, inherits the soul of a god but now needs to find out who killed the god to show she’s not a threat.  The entire game is done as a visual novel with a lot of musical numbers, using many of those musical numbers as the points where players make choices.  The choices usually seem to be about who you will side with but are done in a somewhat entertaining and clever way.  There’s a decent amount of music in this game as well. Which, I’m not a huge fan of.  I do like musicals, but I’m very picky and while the singing is good at times, it’s a very passive experience.  It is a visual novel, but the experience isn’t great.  The animation feels a touch cheap, at times, with it just moving between still images, and if anyone wants to see everything in the game you’ll have to play through it multiple times or just Youtube it. Pick this up if you are interested, or like what you see.  There are a lot of clever moments in the first hour, the songs aren’t terrible, and I’m just being picky as hell when I say I don’t like the music.  It’s a me thing, and the game as it is will be enjoyable.  I just have a bit of a high bar when it comes to music and this doesn’t reach it. _childDocuments_.review: A Greek mythology musical murder mystery? I mean, of course I had to give that a try. I helped kickstart this game years ago and it's crazy to finally see it come out. Is it a little cheesy/ridiculous at times? Yes. Is it absolutely wonderful? You bet. You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll rap battle the gods. It's amazing! Every character brings so much personality whether they are part of the main cast or in a supporting role. All kinds of representation is present without feeling like it was gratuitously and awkwardly thrown in. You can tell the developers put a lot of love into these characters, and they really bring the narrative to life. The gameplay is like a simplified TellTale game. It's purely conversations, so don't expect any other kind of running around or exploring. It's a shorthand version of what you're going to say (or sing) on a conversation wheel, so there are times when you might pick an option you misinterpreted, but I would say most of the time it's very straightforward, and in the songs especially it's very spelled out what direction the song will take. Much like TellTale games, it has auto-saves, so going back on a decision is not easy. You'll have to catch it before the next auto-save and then replay a good chunk to re-do the part you want. There are decisions to make as well. They didn't feel super weighty to me for the most part, it's more of two different ways to get to the same result, but there are some big ones that make you wonder how it would be different if you played through again. So there is a replay-ability factor (other than hearing the different versions of the songs of course!). I do also love that you can change the tone during the song and you're not just locked into your first choice. I'm sure that made things infinitely more complicated for the composers and the devs, and as someone who loves to play more neutral choices in RPGS, I cannot thank you enough for allowing that. Much love to the team for going the extra mile on that one.I'm not necessarily a big musical fan myself, but I thought the concept was intriguing, and they had an excellent narrative reason for why it makes perfect sense. In a lot of ways it feels almost like a classic Disney movie, singing as you reach main points of your adventure and introducing new characters. The performances are really well done. The songs themselves are not bad by any means, the composers did an awesome job, and I was moved to tears a few times, but I wouldn't exactly call them super catchy. The price of interchangeability, I imagine. It took me about six hours to play through the story, and I enjoyed it so that's too short! But for the narrative, it does feel appropriate. It's enough time to get to know the characters and their stories without going on for too long. I know narrative games will never reach the profit levels of all the free to play shooters, but I'm so happy studios are wiling to make them. Stories like this reach out and touch you and they remind us that video games can be such a beautiful art form. Looking forward to more games from Summerfall and will be especially praying for a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Free or Paid? Received FreeGeneral Rating? GoodPros:Decisions Matter (little details like music composition are affected)Multiple romance optionsEngaging storyline and charactersLong play time (about 6-7 hours for one run-through)Replayability value (not sure if the full story is subject to change but details can be)Cons: (many are subjective)Musical (this is subjective, I enjoy the musical aspect but most people I know wouldn’t)Greek myth retelling (this is subjective, I enjoy this but it is also currently a popular topic that could affect the game’s popularity negatively or positively in the future) Still images, not animated (some cool animated character scenes would have been awesome to watch, again this is subjective)No quick-time button events (there is quick-time dialogue but there is no other forms of playing other than choosing dialogue, the game could have minigames where you play instruments or something. CONS:The game leans on D.E.I. themes (Idols with changed ethnicity, “they” pronouns, and many more). Forced “diversity” because it has no connection to the story/has no other reason to be there than to promote an Agenda.What also stood out to me is the high piercing-to-person ratio. Everyone seems to have one.For this gamer at least, I cannot recommend the game.

Best to have subtitles on to catch it all.- I enjoyed the art and how it didn't pull too much away from the characters and story. In my perspective, it adds to the story and the characters more than hindering it.- I enjoyed the retelling of the Greek myths. I'd love to read more and what happened to the other idols. -Tagging on the previous point, I loved the idea of the idols being able to pass on their "essence" to another and would LOVE to see more of that.- Lastly, I adored the voice actors with their portrayal of the characters in the dialogue and the musical pieces. _childDocuments_.review: This game was such a pleasure!As a big fan of mythologies, History and musicals, this game was so fun to play, which seems rare in the video game sphere these days, a fun little game complete and done to enjoy from day one!You play as Grace, lost and astray, who ends up becoming... the last new muse when Calliope dies in your arms. Except you are left with only a week to discover what happens before you are judged for her murder! While you do so, you will encounter and battle many gods, goddesses, creatures and people from the Ancient World! And since you’re a muse, you’re gifting them and convincing them to help with songs!The art is very nice, the casting is amazing (Anthony Rapp, Felicia Day, Rahul Kohli, Troy Baker, Laura Bailey, Ashely Johnson, and all the others, I mean, how does that not convince you to play the game?!), the songs are great and I hummed some of them days later and the concept of playing and “fighting” with songs is pretty fun!The story was well written enough, the culprit easy to guess but it ties everything nicely and it’s the journey that matters, not the destination, you know. And the journey was amazing, thanks for the fun hours I had while playing the game!As I’m writing this review, some issues are ongoing, but the game isn’t even a week hold and they will probably be fixed: some dialogues are loud enough but some very low so they are hard to hear, but sure to put some subtitles on. As far as I know, the issue with the saves erasing themselves is gone, I didn’t have it.If you like quick, nice, fun games with mythologies in it and music, you'll surely enjoy this one between two AAA games!Thanks to the whole team for a wonderful experience! :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game, which is all about art and music, was delivered with little consideration for either.Firstly, let's discuss the graphic art. It appears to be concept art that's been roughly pencilled over and colored in. Furthermore, it's of low resolution, and playing the game on a high-resolution screen makes the pixelation painfully apparent. The lack of attention to detail is also evident. For instance, when a character grips her hair tightly with blood-stained hands, why is there no blood on her hair afterward? This kind of oversight suggests a disregard for detail that you wouldn't expect from a passion project. Though the simplistic drawings could be an artistic choice, the pixelation and lack of consistency certainly are not.Next, we have the sound. The lack of audio balance is a significant issue. I spent most of my time adjusting the volume to avoid either straining to hear or going deaf. The volume fluctuated greatly from one line of dialogue to another. For a game centered around sound, this is disappointing.The game's dialogue system is another drawback. Selecting dialogue with the mouse is frustrating, and annoyingly, there are no key binds for alternative responses. Although this system worked well in the Mass Effect series, here it seems unresponsive. This might relate to playing the game on an ultra-wide screen, but it generally doesn't respond in the way I expected.There are also basic user experience issues. For example, none of the options in the settings are explained. It merely assumes people will understand terms such as "night mode". And why can't players specify what type of audio device they want to use? Surely the game would require different settings for a 2.1 sound bar versus 7.1 headphones— yet it doesn't seem to.On a positive note, the game features Felicia Day, which is a blast of the past for me. The storyline seems intriguing, but it's challenging to become immersed due to these problematic and distracting issues.As a backer of this game, I question where the funding and time were invested. The final product is unequivocally not worth the advertised price. I anticipated a much higher-quality product with superior artistry and passion reflected in every detail. Yet it seems apparent corners were cut. Sadly, the numerous delays and subsequent excuses did not yield the fantastic product we expected.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I was intrigued by the comic book art style and the idea of interacting with Greek gods trying to make do in the modern world. As a huge fan of Neil Gaiman's The Sandman series of comics, I was hooked pretty easily. But the main story with its myriad twists and turns, well developed characters, mature themes, beautiful art (barring the occasional low res texture) and BANGING soundtrack really sealed the deal for me. I'd criticize just two things: the lack of a manual save button (I genuinely wish modern games, especially those in the vein of a visual novel, would just make it industry standard to have manual saves) and the lack of truly meaningful choices. Sure, there are choices relating to HOW you get from Point A to Point B and WHO you'll romance on the way but ultimately, the game is very much on a linear track and two players with very distinct personalities can still find themselves going through more or less the same journey. This is not an issue unique to Stray Gods and has basically plagued modern adventure gaming (think Telltale) for a decade now. However, it's disappointing that this game doesn't have much in the way of replayability. And no, the "personalities" don't really count as they're mostly gimmicks or just ways to sing the musical numbers differently. But this isn't a deal breaker by any means and I'd happily recommend Stray Gods to people who enjoy comics, Greek mythology, musicals and a good old fashioned hero's journey. I'm hoping this can serve as a proof of concept to David Gaider (the fantastic and very talented writer of the game) and the devs and I hope they can follow it up with something even bigger and badder.PS: I voted for this game for this year's Best OST!

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. This was what I'd call an Audio Visual Novel. Inasmuch as it's a VN, but with a definite focus on music and voice acting. I didn't love this game, but I did like and enjoy it quite a bit, and it made me laugh repeatedly throughout.Visually, this game is quite striking with very lush colors and a very modern cartoon-ey look. I thought the ability to convey emotion based on the looks on the character's faces was quite exceptional. The characters themselves all looked great. And the backdrops for each scene ranged from really nice looking to exceptional. The voice acting was about as good as it gets. Which comes as no surprise when you look at the all-star cast featuring Laura Bailey, Troy Baker, Khary Payton, Felicia Day, Ashley Johnson, and so on. There were a couple moments where the actors would skip a word in the dialogue, but that wasn't really an issue, and they all breathed real life into their characters. Every line in the game was voice acted, so this was an important element to the story telling, and the cast did an amazing job. The music was also super cool with a lot of variety but managing to stay in the moment. The singing OTOH, while all fundamentally excellent, didn't hit quite as well. Why? I think it was sort of intentional because an aspect of this game was having, under certain circumstances, conversations and normal sentences sung rather than spoken. Which was a big part of the story itself, and while it made total sense, it could be jarring or weird at times. At other times though, it was brilliant. So, a bit of a mixed bag. Albeit an often hilarious one.The story itself centers around a singer (Grace) who unknowingly meets one of the Three Muses (from Greek mythology) and ends up absorbing her Eidolon after a certain event, thus becoming the Muse herself. Which leads to what ends up being a murder investigation and adventure involving Grace, her best friend Freddie, and the various Greek gods, now knows as Idols, who are just trying to get by in the modern world while maintaining secrecy regarding their immortality. Which was a cool concept. I really enjoyed the story. Which makes sense since David Gaider is one of the premier writers when it comes to video games with branching paths and a morality system.Gameplay is strictly VN style, where you make dialogue and morality decisions, examine some items, and so on. It's kind of slow paced and certain sequences, due to the focus on lengthy dialogue, can drag on a bit. And I think this, combined with some of the more awkward singing moments, keep this game from being in the absolute top tier of VNs despite having so many amazing qualities working for it. Plus, you can't really skip through dialogue even though you might not want to anyway since it is all voice acted. Just needed a bit better pacing IMO.It only took about seven hours to complete one of the story arcs and you could probably speed things up in future playthroughs if you would like to see all the branching path impacted by your decisions within the game. I am confident I got what would be considered the "good" ending since everything worked out alright in the end. This game is featured in the current Humble Choice (as of the time of this writing), so a lot of people probably now own the game. I'd suggest firing it up and seeing if it's for you or not. As far as it's actual pricing goes, the $29.99 price tag makes sense given the cast and quality of the game, but I think I'd feel more comfortable with it being about half that at this point. Anyway, I enjoyed my time with it, and I do intend to play the Orpheus DLC here in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is a charming story-based game with the conceit that the Greek gods are here today but hidden. When Grace inherits the role of Calliope, the last Muse, she is accused of murder and must prove her innocence.The story is told in three acts: the first is introductory, the second revs up the story with a shocking ending (based on my choices), and a satisfactory third act that wraps everything up. Even someone who doesn't have a background in Greek mythology can understand the relationships and place names. The writing is great, and the character choices among the large Greek pantheon worked well together. The songs feel organic and range in tone from a bit of rap to a lovely Celtic-tinged duet at the end (my Grace romanced Apollo in this run). The voice actors were great and some of the best-known in the business. And they can sing! I was delighted to hear Anthony Rapp as Orpheus (I'm a big fan of Rent). Laura Bailey, Troy Baker, Ashley Johnson, and others have singing voices I would pay to hear on Broadway. I can't wait to replay with other choices and see how the story and music play out. It's a great game.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: The way this game makes the music seems to be love or hate in the reviews. I think it's because it's like a dialogue, and you have lots of choices in the musical numbers and that creates variations in the songs. I think it's pretty cool. I've played it 4 times and I do have parts of the songs stuck in my head, but I agree with some reviews about not having them stuck the first time.About replayability, this game is all about replaying. You really cannot see it's full potential of you play it only once. The second time will be much faster since you can skip dialogue (but you cannot skip songs part).The game has a dark undernote of depression, and boy, in my first playthrough I was tempted to go for the friendship route because I had trouble shallowing all that sadness, but I ended rather liking it in the next one when I understood why each one felt the way they felt. And knowing all that I felt it was rather lacking a poly option.Your choices outside songs don't make much change in the story but yes about the information you get, the choices in songs shape the story.I really think the game deserves a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I'm close to the end of my first playthrough. Overall, I'm extremely impressed.This truly a story-driven game with actual narrative stakes. The visual design is fantastic and matches the tone perfectly. True, not all the songs are great, and not all the singing voices are perfect, but that's really nitpicking. Getting a few more or less right would have been a huge achievement already, and Stray Gods goes well beyond that point.The way the story unfolds, the player has excellent incentive to start over and make different choices. I thought that the solution to the main mystery was pretty obvious, but the underlining story was not what I expected.Two things in which I think the game does not succeed as well as the rest: First, the icons in the dialogue options are not clear. I had to look up what they meant. Also, the dialogue options that allow Grace (the player character) to flirt are extremely cheesy. I don't think the characters she's talking to would respond to her being that direct.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many things weird about this one. For one, these are some VERY liberal takes on the greek pantheon. I understand the desire to do your own thing and such but to deviate THIS much then why even bother doing the pantheon in the first place? Like, why make Athena, the goddess of wisdom, a dumb and rash character who jumps to conclusions?Next is the musical bits. As a theatre kid, I dont think this dev team knows what a musical is. You can't just slot songs into a story and call it a musical. The visuals matter just as much as the audio and their slide show method of animation leaves so much out of the delivery. There is no energy in the stills. In addition, why would you include a line asking if its weird to be singing in the middle of the song? Lampshading in this manor shows that the team has no confidence in the narrative they are trying to deliver. That one line did more damage to my immersion and enjoyment than any historical inaccuracies or stilted musical numbers.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★A beautiful musical and mythical experience. I thoroughly enjoyed this game and highly recommend this to anyone looking for a great story-driven game. The voice-acting in this game is impeccable, and it immensely supports the excellent dialogues. Characters are memorable and mesmerizing, and the art is stylistic yet simple; everything looks and sounds gorgeous. The choices you make lead to different outcomes, so there's a good reason to replay and try other options.*The first play-through is obviously the best, especially if you're playing this without any prior knowledge since everything is new and the decisions you make have meaning behind them.In conclusion, this is an awesome game that is enjoyable from start to finish and like the game's description says, you'll surely find it to be *If you decide to replay the game and experience the other choices in the game that you could make, there is no way to reload to a specific part or skip the songs. It feels unnecessary and uninteresting to play through the parts of the game you've already seen. Perhaps, this is only an issue if you're impatient like me. However, there is a good value in replaying to see how differently the story can unfold. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: My review is somewhat neutral. I absolutely love the concept and the intro, its a beautiful way to start the game. But past the first act Stray Gods, well, strays. The sound mixing between characters voices is upsetting at best and grating at worst. You may want to have a preset high and low volume buttons to press in-between character lines. The art quality also degrades fast and furious, after intros to the main four, everyone else is extraordinarily flat and while I can feel the love for the character it doesn't show as well as it could have. The musicality is everywhere all at once, I wanted to feel at least a connecting line through the songs but there wasn't any thing to catch and hook onto. Everything else could be forgiven if not for the game's lack of vision, it feels like the story is pulling at the player in all directions like its plot was fully handed over to a new person over and over in development and wanting to ignore the past story progression and just do what they want. It presents itself as a roleplaying musical but actually plays akin to a visual novel/ comic book choose your own adventure, not a bad thing, just not what it says on the tin.In all I do recommend this game, hard to get through at parts but the meat of the fun and silliness you feel when singing with greek gods is still fun whatever form it came in. If possible it'd be better to grab it on sale. (Persephone is the only real option smh)
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Vocal millennial shows boomers the true meaning of life through song and the power of friendship.Eh, its the very definition of "Steam needs a button between thumbs up and thumbs down." There were some sweet moments and there is at least one song I will be humming for awhile, but a lot of the musical pieces felt uncomfortably squeezed into the dialogue and didn't land all that well. I will give it a tentative thumbs up because I appreciate games that try new things, but wait for a sale if you are on the fence. _childDocuments_.review: If you like musical theater, you'll probably like this -- it's suitably emotional and melodramatic, with some killer songs. Because of the choice you have during the songs, it's possible to zig-zag through them in a way that doesn't really come together, but there are also some bangers and earworms. And visually, the art style is gorgeous.There is an issue with the sound leveling during dialog (not during songs) where some lines can be very quiet and others come in very loud. _childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods caught my attention on setting, voice cast, and most of all being an interactive musical; to say I was happy with my experience is an understatement. It could be the time of my life that I am playing this game, but the themes were well executed and hard hitting. As purely a choose-your-own-adventure visual novel, Stray Gods gripped me fast and hard, beginning to end. I very much enjoyed how the story was told through interactive songs. While the visuals overall were pleasing and enjoyable, I would have liked to see more character expression, especially during the musical numbers. If you are looking for a fun, kind-of emotional, short experience, I highly recommend giving Stray Gods a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game a lot. To get some negatives out of the way first, the visuals sometimes felt off, like some key frames were missing, and the pauses between changes too big. Some pauses in the songs between multiple branches also were noticable. On the other hand, the story, characters and musical numbers were very emotional, heartfelt and enjoyable. Without spoilers, I went in wanting to fight all of the characters but never did because it just felt too wrong once you knew a little more about them. The voice cast is absolutely stacked. The music works very well in my opinion with only slight hickups sometimes. The relationships to and between the characters felt very impactful. Very LGBT+ friendly with tons of representation. Replayability doesn't feel very high, but I feel like the game is still very worth the money for the emotional journey it takes you on.

_childDocuments_.review: What an emotional journey! Stray Gods is a perfect mix of mystery, romance, and musical genres. It's a little bit short, but I think narrative-focused games, such as Stray Gods, shouldn't be too long, or else they're likely to bore you after a while. (You can find tl;dr in the end.)	Besides the amazing soundtrack (it's a musical game, of course it'll be amazing, duh!), one thing I want to point out is the excellent choice of visual art style. Hand-drawn styled graphics and still animations allow the player to easily follow both the songs/lyrics and the things happening on the screen without missing anything.I also really liked how the abruptly starting singing sections that we usually see in musicals are explained in a way that's very fitting to the story. To be fair, I'm definitely not a musical play or movie gourmet or anything. I rarely watch musicals, though I've always found it a bit weird that in musicals, characters speaking with each other in a scene suddenly switch to singing for no logical or realistic reason. I know the emotional or romantic scenes are usually reflected with music in this genre, but still, I can't help but find this sudden change of pace a bit odd. However, Stray Gods, thanks to its fantasy-heavy plot, offers a reasonable excuse for this trope Tl;dr if you like Telltale-like games that offers interactive stories, or you love musicals and want to try the genre as a video game, definitely give Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: Ye Gods, this is GOOD!It's a different experience to anything I've ever had in games, and it's a positive experience, and that's about the highest praise I can give to any game, as far as I'm concerned.Interestingly, the experience felt somewhat more passive than many games - not in a bad way, if you're in the right mood, it's perfect - like it felt a little bit BETWEEN watching and playing. This is weird, because it's not like the game lacks choice or interactivity, it just feels like you're nudging this other entity that has its own momentum. All games which have a story that you can influence are like that, but Stray Gods FEELS like it - perhaps because the songs feel like they have an energy and dynamism to them and your role is to (re)direct it?Anyway, if you've read this far, stop wondering and buy it, it's an experience well worth having.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:// After playing the game a second time and sleeping on it, oh my god the songs are absolutely stuck in my head!! You and I is SO GOOD, definitely my favourite. I take back it all, the songs are wickedly good and the genre changes wildly depending on your choices, if you dislike a song check out other versions of it!----I was really humming and hawing about whether to get this game or not, and the reviews left below were a big factor. I had heard such great things about the game and it was highly recommended to me by people who shared similar interests, so I was very interested until I saw all the negative reviews left below. I bought the game anyway (and I highly enjoyed it!) and I'd like to address some of the negative points left by other reviewers.This game is not so much a role-playing game, it is instead a visual novel perhaps similar to Edith Finch if you've played it. A movie in which you get dialogue options, and the dialogue options do seem to matter quite a bit in deciding plot points (your choices actually matter! yay!)Someone also said the songs were lacking, and I guess I can see where they're coming from?? _childDocuments_.review: Musicals. Are. Amazing. They convey messages and meanings through song and poetry. It explores the depths of a character or tells a story while providing an entertaining outlet of which many of us are happy to listen to, music. And Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical is no exception to that rule.Here's a rough guide without going in to spoiler-y territory. You place as Grace, a singer turned muse when the supposed last muse died on your doorstep, giving you powers. That's right, the Greek Gods are real, baby! But who murdered the last muse? Everyone suspects it was you, so it's up to you to prove your innocence. Explore famous Greek Gods and characters from the stories, namely Apollo, Persephone, and surprisingly, Pan. While you're doing so, buddy up with your best friend Freddie as you explore the old mixed with the new. This game is choice based, where decisions are important and choices have outcomes, as choices normally do. In the beginning of the game, you'll get to pick 1 of 3 traits your character will have. The trait will affect some choices your character can make. As you reach the halfway mark, you'll unlock your 2nd and only trait left, which means you should choose wisely on which trait you should use. Of course, what is this game without glancing over the main premise of this game: MUSIC! Fantastically produced, the music brings about emotion, be it sadness, or anger, or joy. And it does so so excellently. You'll also get to orchestrate how the music goes about, so choose wisely on what direction it takes. You'll also get to romance 1 of 4 characters, as mentioned earlier, Apollo, Pan, Persephone or Freddie. Artstyle of this game is phenomenal as well. I just hope for something similar in the future.So, bring along your best friend, some headphones, and a mic, as you partake in a tale worth 6 hours long, that is... Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been interested in what this game would prove to be since its announcement. A musical video game? The concept is genuinely innovative and this game will define the genre until more are released - IF more are released anyway.Essentially this game is a visual novel. You watch the scenes play out and are given time-sensitive prompts to have input in the moment. I'm going to level with you here, dear reader, don't worry about whether you are doing the 'right response' or not, there doesn't seem to be one. Your actions will have consequences but no consequence appears to change the overall trajectory of the story - so just choose the option you think is accurate to how you are playing, and enjoy the show!The music and songs are decent on the whole, each character you meet has their problems which are revealed through a duet (usually). The ones that work the best are the ones that have some level of tension and force you to pick sides. The music itself is well-done, motifs are used for different characters and repeat across the "show" much as they would in a live musical. Everyone given a song can sing, which is a relief. Your input genuinely shakes things up and can cause songs to completely alter in tempo, style and intensity, and the musical interactions are easily the best part of the game - WHEN you have input.I'm unclear as to how much replay value this game will have as the overall plot doesn't appear to change. You cannot re-do specific songs or scenes without re-doing the entire game...and I'm not convinced I have the patience to sit through all the dialogue again. If there was a way of replaying specific moments/songs after completing the game then I would be more excited to try different options.I'd recommend the game to anyone with an interest in the concept, the lore of Greek myths and legends, and to any musical theatre or RP fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Fellow musical theater fanatic and greek mythology enthusiast here! This game is definitely up your alley if you enjoy Telltale games (especially the Wolf Among Us), the Percy Jackson & the Olympians series, and/or the musical Hadestown. Since I'm also a huge TTRPG nerd, I also recommend this game to anyone who enjoys Scion or City of Mist. If you're curious about the quality and quantity of the songs, I highly recommend listening to the Pantheon Edition of the soundtrack on Spotify. After having the playlist on repeat a couple times, I took the plunge and never looked back after. Initially, I thought the price was steep for a game that is essentially a visual novel. However, it's way more worth it when you compare it to buying a ticket from any musical. Consider this as a one-time purchase to a musical that you can come back to over and over again. The replayability with the different choices (and thus different songs) really is the cherry on top!I was also hesitant to purchase the games because the reviews at launch mentioned a few bugs. One notable bug was that exiting out of your game would cause you to lose your save file. However, the developers resolved the issue with a recent hotfix. After seeing that update, I bought the game, and everything has worked perfectly for me.As for the actual gameplay, the game is less of an RPG and more of an interactive novel with a musical score. The audio levels are definitely wonky a couple of times because some characters get really quiet during more serious and solemn moments. Thank goodness for captions though. It was a pain to go into the menu and adjust the volume settings each time this occurred. The songs were not as obvious in having sound issues, except for when singers would clash with each other. One tended to drown out the other, especially if they had softer vocals. I quite enjoy the art style. It gives off neo-noir and urban fantasy vibes, which fit the setting and premise of the story. There were a lot of complaints about not full committing to either stills or animated graphics. I was fine with the half-measure because that was never the biggest appeal of the game for me. Speaking of which, I also really liked the plot, which followed a three-act structure. Without giving away any spoilers, here's my brief synopsis. Act I - Setup: The main character Grace is accused of murdering a Greek god of artistic inspiration known as a Muse. Act II - Confrontation: After inheriting the powers of the Last Muse, Grace must navigate the turbulent world of the Greek pantheon in a modern city setting. Act III - Resolution: Grace attempts to prove her innocence with the evidence that she's gathered and deals with the aftermath of her choices.I adore the characters because their stories were well-written and each felt complex in their own unique way. My only disappointment is that we didn't get to explore everyone's backstories further. Here's to hoping that there will be more games in the same universe/setting. The voice actors were fantastic and truly enhanced each character. Laura Bailey needs to stop captivating me with each role she takes on. Not all of the cast were phenomenal singers, but they gave their all into showcasing the character's personality through song.According to the Steam achievement, there are a total of 23 different songs in the game. Each "run" takes about 6 hours to complete, but the time passes by so quickly that you don't even notice how far along you are! The game needs to be refined in some aspects, but for an indie studio's first game, this is to be expected. Overall, I'm very happy with my purchase and definitely recommend this to anyone who thoroughly enjoys musicals. Otherwise, wait for the game to go on sale or watch some playthroughs to see if you would enjoy the game. I immediately hopped into another save after finishing the whole story once because I'm so excited to hear all the other storylines and songs!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty fun. The songs are good, well written, and performed incredibly. With only a few exceptions. The story is also quite interesting. I loved the alternative spin on Greek mythology. I also quite liked the art. Really nice environments and character designs.It felt more like a movie than other visual novels I've played, such as Vampire the Masquerade Coteries of New York. The animations were sometimes somewhat jarring, with characters jumping from one spot to another.The biggest issue I have is the audio balancing. For some reason, some characters voices are a lot quieter than others in particular scenes. It didn't happen that often, but when it did, it was quite annoying.And as for bugs, I encountered very few. The only thing I noticed was that sometimes characters would be transparent, or when swapping sprites, disappearing for a split second.I absolutely recommend this game to anyone interested in a very movie like visual novel. And I am glad that I backed it!

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've seen, this game is very much a matter of taste, but thankfully, it fits mine perfectly.Whether you'll like it will very much depend on your priorities and expectations going into it.As advertised, Stray Gods is a playable musical. The focus lies squarely on the characters, their relationships and the musical numbers and that is what the "roleplaying" part of this game is all about. While the general story structure always stays the same, your choices influence the characters and the songs they sing in quite innovative ways. The main character is included in that and I liked how different her personality can be depending on the player's choices.Aside from that, the worldbuilding is quite interesting, but in big part relegated to optional conversations, so as to not mess up the flow for players who only want to see the main story. The basic plot & mystery are both quite simple, but do a fine job of propping up the main attractions. The comic-like visuals are pretty, but might take some getting used to for people who are used to fully animated games. And the music can vary widely in quality depending on your choices, but has some real bops, in my opinion. The trailer includes parts from a couple of those, if you want to make sure it's to your taste.If all of that sounds appealing to you, I'd highly recommend checking this game out. It's very much one of my favorite indie titles this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: POSITIVES : Great character writing. I was surprised (pleasantly) to find that most if not all of the characters were written with much care and consideration. As the game progressed I felt increasingly compelled to know more about their backstories.Very witty lyrics that are complemented by a plethora of music genres. I was constantly kept on my toes anticipating the next song and the next song; wondering what kind of style they'd go for next. Amazing art and artstyle, fashion very slayful and fit the characters really nicely. A very diverse, inclusive, and colourful cast of characters.NEGATIVES : As a professional in the music industry, I think that the audio needed quite a bit more love and care. As it is a musical game, I had high expectations regarding the mix and sound design. Dialogue audio needed a bit of cleanup and it could've done with a bit of production based on the characters' locations as most of the time it just sounded like everyone was speaking in a dead room. It probably could've helped a little more with immersion. But I'm just being nitpicky.OVERVIEW:I would still recommend and have been recommending this game to the people around me. I think that the team at Summerfall did a stellar job at delivering a solid and well thought out game. And because there are so many different paths to take that result in different song outcomes, there is much replay value. I think this game opens doors to a future of more games with music as its main driving force. Well done!

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is just Ok. It's coherent which sets it a good measure above the majority of "pick option for cutscene" games out there; however, it's not good enough to compare to the better echelon of visual novels or actually good western story-related games. The art and animation are what they are - a stringed together slideshow of stills. As for the music in the musical.... Well, I liked it, and it worked for me. But I don't think I'm that cultured to make anymore of a judgment of it. Since I won't be playing it multiple times through, I do not think I'll be able to make comments on the intersection of different musical styles (which is a shame since I really want to try out the headstrong red trait and find out if it's more of a punk rock style as suggested.) Then why exactly am I recommending this game if all of its parts are at best just OK? It would be because the sum of these elements are brought together by an artistic vision that is carried out to completion. It may not be a revolutionary artistic vision - the commentary on fate through the linearity of the medium is nothing new and then throw in a dash of bringing about change to an outdated old system. Yet, it is sincere in the story it tells. For the characters that do appear, a level of care and empathy is always given to their character writing. Even if certain characters feel under-utilized (such as Eros and Orpheus, the latter of whom I really enjoyed and found his appearance a bit too short unfortunately speaking), they are never intentionally slighted or treated as simple tools.Even the "politically correct" elements (the game includes transgender characters and characters that fall out of binary norm and quite diverse representations), but for the game, the elements of modern society are not thrown in to cynically appeal to a demographic or to simply virtue signal as substitute for its quality. They clearly come from a sincere place that falls in line with those values.I can always respect an artistic vision that is seen through and completed.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made with love, and a lot of it.If you like choose your own adventure games I can almost guarantee you will enjoy this game too.A lot of the comments make this game sound like some weird mystical eldritch entity half game, it really isn't, its just like a telltale game. But unlike the competitors in this genre, Stray Gods shows care to the idea of choosing your own adventure.It does have those unavoidable fluff dialogue choices but it also actually lets you change the story completely. On top of that if you put yourself in the main characters shoes (hence: roleplaying musical) the world of the game and the connections between the characters can be completely different based on how you talk and what you do first.This attention to detail with giving the player actual choices shines a lot during the songs. It really blew me away, even moreso on my second playthrough (my playtime doesn't reflect two playthroughs I skipped all the dialogue because I wanted to hear the songs). Initially its just cool to fill in the words of the songs, but it gets even better when you realize how much the songs can change from the dialogue options. I'm talking entire scenes, entire branches of dialogues, entire sides to characters that are hidden all over the songs to give more value to the choices you make. I can't stress it enough, this is a game in the choose your own adventure genre... that ACTUALLY lets you choose your own adventure.This game is special, the songs are special, I highly, highly recommend it.apollo song made me cry, medusa song made me ♥♥♥♥ my pants, the duality of man is on full display here whats not to like?

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed the game and finished it, I wouldn't recommend buying this game right now. I think it could use some volume adjusting at the very least--for a game that relies so heavily on the voice acting, there sure was a lot of unbalanced voice lines in terms of the volume of the voice lines within an exchange. My overall opinion is that if you are a big fan of musicals, and this game ever goes on sale, then I would recommend it. But only if it's under $20Again, I enjoyed playing this game, but $30 for a visual novel (this is not an RPG like I've seen it tagged ) is steep for me. I didn't realize there was going to be next to no animation, and the longer I spent playing the game, the more that bothered me. There were also a weird amount of visual bugs for a game that has very little animation. And I would also say "full controller support" is a stretch because sometimes it glitches out and doesn't highlight choices properly when using a controller. Calling it a "Roleplaying Musical" feels like a stretch, because while it is interactive, in my opinion the game lacks core tenants of RPGs.But to bring it back around to the positives, I think it is an interesting concept, I just wish more polish and animation went into it. _childDocuments_.review: 'Stray Gods - The Roleplaying Musical' is EXACTLY what you'd expect it to be.Throughout my run through the game, I never once felt stifled by a lack of choice that Grace, the player character, can make - for anyone who plays choice-based story-heavy games, this is a known thing.Every single time I wanted to take an option, that option was available - given that this is a game with effectively 3 choices to choose from at any given point, sometimes even less, it's really clever writing.In addition, I was pleasantly surprised that you get to pick an additional character trait in the last third of of the story at an appropriately dramatic time, allowing more options - doesn't hurt replay value and provides a feel-good moment.Its only real demerit is that, if you go for options that let other characters make choices, they tend to gravitate towards the self-destructive ones, which is annoying.The songs are alright, if a bit understated with instrumentals, but that might have just been bad mixing on my end - it's no Broadway, but then again, it doesn't need to be. The VA's are all quite competent, and if there's off-key singing, it's very intentional.A bit of a cop-out on the main mystery, and some plot holes are left at the end (how the killer gained access to the murder 'weapon', for example), but overall it's a coherent and solid story with likable characters - even the fact that it's all a racially and ethnically diverse LGBTQ+ cast didn't feel harsh and forced the way it tends to in some other story-based games... the focus was very much on the experience rather than the agenda.Overall a great experience and a full recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re remotely into musicals, let’s just say this isn’t Broadway ready. The “songs” are more talk-singing than the sorta bangers Disney films raised us to expect. The problem is that this game feels cast-forward, art second, script a distant third, and gameplay forgotten in the shuffle. You just pick from three or four options in a text tree. That’s the game. As a visual novel, it’s fine. It’s just vastly inferior to its peers in adjacent media.So, the gods are real and you’re now one of them. That’s a cool premise, but I have Neil Gaiman’s Sandman, American Gods, and Fables’ Wolf Among Us to compare this game’s script to. Hell, even Percy Jackson. But since Sandman dealt directly with Calliope and Orpheus in far more tragic (and artful) terms, Stray Gods pales in comparison. The script wasn’t terrible, but it lacked heartfelt magic apart from that first auditorium scene.The same goes for this soundtrack. Like seriously, way to phone it in, Austin Wintory. Maybe he had his hands tied by the script and the executive direction on this game, but jeez. By any standard, the music isn’t harmonically cohesive or catchy. And Laura Bailey seems like the only one trying, with nobody else keeping up. The first song, Adrift, captures some of the same magic of Kentucky Route Zero's Act III musical moment, Too Late to Love You Now. In similar fashion, the roof comes off and you’re transported to this other world of music where you select the tone of the next verse. But too many songs in Stray Gods just fail to get back to the moments established in that first song. Most of the songs just kinda flounder in talk-singing. This would be unbearable on-stage, live.The sense of player agency in this game feels incredibly lacking, too, and it's not just because you never have any direct control of Grace in any scene. I really wish this game just had a sense of presence and atmosphere with stronger ambient sound. There's a huge absence of sounds in places that should be highly atmospheric, like Aphrodite's party or Hecate's reliquary. Instead there's no sound, no player control, and as a result: a total lack of immersion. This also gets inflated when the options presented in-game felt like they only covered how I wanted to respond about half the time. If the whole game is just picking text options, I want to be able to pick the ones I'm actually feeling. All-in-all, I really wanted to like this game. I do think the character art looks great, even if it's the game's core strength. It's just that my expectations were too high. So if you played the game and you're reading this review — feeling like I'm being too hard on the game, I have some recommended additional reading. Please go listen to the American Gods full-cast  audiobook, read volume three of Sandman (Dream Country), or watch a musical. Any musical. Live or recorded. I appreciate that Summerfall tried here, but I'd probably be fine if they didn't add the "Roleplaying Musical" to the title. It's a decent visual novel that's a bit of a vanity project for its voice talent. As such... okay, let's be honest, I'd still have issues with the script and music. But it's decent.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was one of the backers on their Fig campaign. This review is largely coming from the perspective of being heavily involved in the theatre and performing arts industries in Melbourne, where this game was primarily made. My exposure to musical theatre specifically is limited, but there is a lot of crossover.I think there was a ton of missed potential in engaging the Australian performing arts scene, especially Australian musical theatre, in the production of this game.Montaigne (who is Melbourne-based) is part of the songwriting crew, which is great! But it seems they prioritised getting Famous Voice Actors in, mostly from outside Australia, and who didn't necessarily have experience in musical theatre - perhaps because it felt like that was the main way to get people to get this game ("look! we have This Recognisable Person here!").These VAs definitely have skills. However, for a game that was centered around being a _musical_ - one of the first of its kind to boot - those choices of VAs missed the mark. Musical theatre demands a particular power and energy in its performances, which the songs here didn't quite have. The songs are OK - though, like some reviewers have said, not particularly memorable (especially since the audio mixing made the songs oddly quiet, and in one scene disappear completely). Part of that is the song composition, and another large part is the performance itself. I tried picturing this game on stage - and it felt like chunks of it would need a rewrite to make it compelling enough. Everything just seemed too **sublte** - there's no subtlety in musical theatre!!!There were so many talented performers (musical theatre or otherwise) right in the city this game was made in that could have been cast for these roles. Even local legends like jazz cabaret chanteuse Mama Alto (she would have been an amazing Aphrodite!). If their chosen VAs did have musical theatre experience, it seems to be underutilized - but again, that doesn't resolve the local talent issue.I'll also echo some other comments here about the game not being as interactive as it could be (not really much role-playing happening) and how the detective/investigative parts seems a bit tacked on. I was pleasantly surprised at first by the story being a murder mystery (I love such games) but it felt much like I was being put on rails.This game has a lot of potential. I just don't think it really realised it. The focus on Recognisable VAs, I believe, took away from making this a true musical experience - especially one that could have highlighted and platformed a thriving local performing arts scene, one of the biggest in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical is a true gem that shines in a unique way in the gaming universe, bringing a fascinating proposal that masterfully blends RPG with musical elements. The game achieves something remarkable by transforming Greek mythology into a modern and captivating narrative, where every musical note and dialogue has been meticulously planned to create a memorable experience.The soundtrack is simply exceptional. The compositions not only delight the ears, but also adapt fluidly to the player's choices, creating unique and personal musical moments. The duets and group numbers are particularly impressive, with complex harmonies that intertwine perfectly with the development of the story. It is admirable how each song manages to advance the narrative while maintaining its musical quality, something rare even in larger productions of the genre.The narrative and dialogues stand out for their intelligent and humorous writing, without losing moments of emotional depth. The game manages to naturally alternate between speech and music, maintaining an engaging rhythm that holds the player's attention from beginning to end. The choices available throughout the game have real weight, affecting not only the course of the story, but also how the songs unfold and how the relationships between the characters evolve.Speaking of characters, Grace, the protagonist, is a true triumph in terms of character development. Her journey of self-discovery is captivating and allows players to truly connect with her story. The supporting cast is equally memorable, with distinct personalities and rich backstories that unfold naturally throughout the adventure. The chemistry between the characters is palpable, and their interactions are always interesting, whether in dramatic moments or in lighter, more humorous situations.The choice system during musical performances is particularly innovative, allowing players to shape not only the course of the story, but also the style and tone of the songs. This adds an extra layer of customization to the experience, making each playthrough unique and personal. Replayability is naturally high, as different choices lead to significant variations in both the narrative and the musical performances.Visually, the game adopts a distinct artistic style that perfectly complements its musical proposition. The animations during the performances are fluid and expressive, while the art direction manages to capture both the modern essence and the mythological elements of the story. The interface is intuitive and well-designed, allowing players to focus on the story and the songs without unnecessary distractions.Stray Gods is clear proof that there is still room for innovation in the gaming industry. It is a title that not only sets new standards for interactive musical narratives, but also demonstrates how different art forms can come together to create something truly special. It is an experience that remains in the memory long after the final credits, whether for the quality of the music, the depth of the narrative or the charisma of the characters. For anyone interested in games that dare to be different and offer a truly unique experience, Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical is a must-have.

_childDocuments_.review: A single playthrough of the game is not very long - I've finished two playthroughs in my 16 hours so far - but I've been enjoying Stray Gods very much.  The voice acting and singing is great, and the dialogue and characters are fun.The interactive songs are also really well done.  An early choice will tend to set a particular musical and/or lyrical theme which will then recur through the rest of the piece, coming back in response to later choices. It results in songs which feels coherent and satisfying even if you jump around between the different approaches the game offers (charming/green, kickass/red and clever/blue).I don't know if there are ways to fail, so this is more of an experience than a winning/losing "game".  For example, the central murder mystery is not something you solve directly, in that there's no "now the player must pick whodunnit" moment.  It's more about exploring the world, following Grace's search for clues to solve the mystery, and enjoying the music and story.  That said, there are definitely consequences for the epilogues of various characters depending on what you choose.I also really like the way they've built the conversation side of the game.  It's a fairly traditional node-based conversation graph with you being told or asked something, and then you respond by choosing one of up to four options.  However, the options are flagged with a variety of icons which I found very intuitive.* Question marks indicate options which ask questions/get information without leaving this "node" of the conversation, meaning you can safely exhaust all such options without unexpectedly moving on and missing out on things you wanted to ask.* One of the three trait icons (charming/green, kickass/red and clever/blue) indicate that you need that trait in order to chose the option, and it will be greyed out if you don't/can't.  This makes it clear why you can't choose an option, and encourages you to replay with different traits.* A heart icon flags responses which attempt to romance the person you're talking with.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game when it was crowdfunded 3-4 years ago, and am admittedly a bit disappointed. I'm still going to play through and finish it because I've waited this long, but man. The biggest disappointment is the lack of attention to the audio. Some voicelines are MUCH louder than the others, and I needed to keep adjusting my volume so i didn't blow my ears out. For some reason, there are no sound effects? I'm not sure if this is an intentional choice, but its weird. It takes away from the experience because there is only voicelines and BGM. I feel like the voices aren't mixed very well either, and sometimes are much louder than the BGM. It was really strange because there was a dramatic moment where lightning flashed, and there was no cool thunder sound to back it up. Just one example. Things like doors slamming / heavy footsteps seem like just very basic things that weren't included. Also... the singing isn't very... good. It's alright. I wish they processed the singing more, because it feels very raw and unprocessed to me. Which is fine in a live setting, but with headphones on? Again a very weird decision, because there are scenes where the characters like sing in a microphone, but theres not even a microphone effect. I felt like it could've benefited from just a little reverb, but the singing voices are just so under processed. It felt like a lack of connection from the musical aspect to what was happening in the game. For a musical, none of the songs so far are really catchy / have stuck in my head. The lyrics aren't very catchy and have a weird tempo. I feel like it could've benefited from more polish in the right places. The art is really really good and I love the style, but its almost like they focused on the art... too much. This is a roleplaying MUSICAL, i went into this expecting an audio experience, and came away disappointed. They are pioneering this genre, which is really impressive, but the lack of understanding about what is needed for this genre is really apparent. In this game, they seemed to focus on the art experience, but have forgotten the holistic experience because things just play out in front of you like a slideshow -- one picture after another. Even in comics, there are things like written sound effects that tell the story. This game seems to have relied too much on their 'star cast' (who I don't really care for, so the magic is gone) to carry the delivery, and it's not enough. I hope the studio learns from this and continues to make more games with a better experience.--------------------------------------------Edit: I've played through more of the game, and I'm really shocked and appalled by the quality of it!!! I'm actually quite disappointed right now, and wish I could get a refund, but I backed it on Fig years ago. I will admit that my original review is slightly inaccurate. There ARE SOME sound effects, but it sincerely isn't enough. A character will straight up be performing magic in front of you, and it just plays out in a silent slideshow without any sound effects. I also encountered bugs where the singing lines and/or the character sprites just. Disappeared. The camera will just be panning over nothing silently. I followed development of this game closely and watched the livestream, and a really major red flag that stuck out to me was the devs said something along the lines of "we toned down the music / mixing in order to let the voice actor's talent shine through" and it gave me kind of.. purist vibes. This philosophy has made itself very apparent in the game, and not in a good way. I genuinely cringed and was very upset to hear that CHARACTERS WOULD SING NOTES OFF KEY!!! Why was this take in the final product?? The only character that has this excuse is Rahul Kohli's character, who canonically cannot sing. However, the song that featured him has 4 participants -- and every one of them had an off key note!! A little bit of autotune is not your enemy!! I honestly feel like the director has done a disservice to the voice talent by not processing their voices enough. A player also cannot skip dialogue, which is such an odd choice, one I can only believe was justified by the devs wanting to milk their voice talents content as much as possible. My save file was deleted with the bug everyone experienced, and I had to just grind through the beginning sections again with no way to skip / chose chapters. I genuinely believe this game would've been much better if the scope was reduced. I honestly feel like this game shouldn't be voice acted AT ALL apart from the musical sections. If the gameplay was text based, there could also have been more RPG elements because like other reviewers have said, this game is NOT an RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. The writing is top-notch, the characters are fantastic and have some actual depth to them--the trauma revealed for some of them is a lot heavier than I was expecting in a game like this, but it made the interactions so much better for it.This was a practically perfect bit of entertainment if you want what is essentially an interactive musical mini-series. There's very little to no gameplay, outside of timed choices during musical numbers (which you can turn the timed element off), but the fact that it is 100% voiced and done in the style of an animatic/story board rather than a typical Visual Novel style really helps make it sing. (Not sorry.) And the choices you do get to make feel like they can have some decent, actually interesting ripple effects on the ending.The art-style is amazing in its simplicity, and the feeling that this is a musical, motion comic works incredibly well. Would I have loved to see it fluidly animated? Sure. But I'm also aware of how much work that would be to hand animate what would essentially be an 8-hour movie (if counting the alternate scenes I didn't get to see in my 6-hour-ish playthrough). That's definitely not realistic. But what they did was waaaay more engaging than completely still portraits over dialogue boxes that you'd normally get in a VN.Over all, if you like musical episodes of your favorite shows and enjoy highly narrative choose your own adventure games or visual novels, I can't imagine you not having a good time with Stray Gods.

_childDocuments_.review: I am playing Stray Gods and this feels like a great experience. Somewhat of an ineractive movie and a cRPG, mixed with decision and some doubts... and these are good! Because that means you actually care about what option you're picking or which path you're going to follow. If I were to say what the style reminds me of, I would say it's a mix of Hadestown's artistic approach to mythology, City of Mist's play on contemporary depiction of legends, all packed in accessibility of visual novels or "choose your path" kind of games (As Dusk Falls, Life is Strange, Tell Me Why).Visually, it's like a well designed comic book, with saturated colors and nice character design. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: If you aren't a fan of musical, visual novels and indie games, obviously--you wouldn't get your fun. Also, musical style is subjective. Do keep that in mind. Overall, engaging musical thriller with lively characters.--I was enamoured with the visuals when they first announced it. I thought Grace had a familiar voice. Then I read "lead writer of Dragon Age" and Laura Bailey's name in the cast list. Say no more; take my money!Haven't been this engaged with a new game in a while. A nice change of pace compared to a lot of uninspired new productions that saturates the store page. Sometimes, you have good voice cast with mediocre writing. Sometimes, it's the other way around. Sometimes AAA titles fails to deliver in everything but the stellar visuals and the promise of branding. Sometimes you get games with very engaging games mechanics that...barely has anything resembling a story-line.Calling it a "musical RPG" is cute. It is essentially a visual novel, styled as a musical with multiple choices and perhaps the choice matters. I will only know as I continue to play the game. NGL, the visuals are superb. The visual arts team of this game deserves praise. Sure, it's in a style of animatic, however the dynamic angle, the movement, the expressions--wonderfully done. Is it the "first of its kind"? Far from it. Once upon a time on Steam, there was a game called "Of Bird and Cage". It was also a musical...um...interactive story. The musical cast had some well known musicians and bands. I never felt engage in that game as opposed to Stray Gods. The decisions to make it in 2D with live 2D elements is a sound decision. Keeping the game-play simple yet demanding a level of attention is also a very sound decision.It's a musical thriller with supernatural elements. Would I actively seek out this kind of music for myself? Most likely no. By no means the music is subpar. But art is subjective. If you like this very theatrical, old school Disney-like musical exchange, then you're gonna love it.For me, it is a visual and auditory treat, and a wonderful journey alongside our protagonist. For me, this beats going to the movies. Give it a try, unless you really hate musical with a passion.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely ever play choose your own adventure games or visual novels, but this game was a treat! If you want interesting characters, fun story telling, and really satisfying musical pieces that play very differently each time, this is that game. I am a fan of Greek mythology and this plays it's own variation on the tales. It spins into a murder mystery that has kept me interested even after I played it more than once! The Animatic way of telling the story actually works far better than I had imagined thanks to the powerful voice acting talent behind it and the incredible efforts of Austin Wintory and his colleagues. I found the story really gripping and fun though not for all audiences with brief mentions of PTSD, Suicide, Murder, and Alcohol. All the same, there are plenty of light-hearted comical moments, and the writing is quite talented. Small bug in that dialogue isn't currently normalized as well as it should be but they are aware and working the issue. I can't wait to play through another time and try out different choices, different songs, but all with such heart.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has everything. Trauma, gods, gays, crime, loads of romance options, great replayability. A fairly compelling game if you love choices matter and musicals. A great cast that was picked out with clear purpose and executed the game superbly. The story is amazing, the dialogue fun and witty, and you can clearly see that everyone had fun.ISSUES!Some of the audio isn't mixed well for several parts. Eros has some lines that sound echoed, as does Asterion, Persephone, and others dotted in and around the game. Once you hear the audio, you can't unhear the problem. There's also the trouble of balance mixing. This comes into the fore during the song Everybody, where the balance is clearly off instead of harmonious in any regard, which isn't great. The song is still absolutely amazing, but the audio balance is a bit odd. THANKFULLY, this can (and will hopefully) be fixed later on through a polish patch if they can remaster those parts.There is also an issue with desynced audio for a few songs, but this can be fixed with a reload of the last save point.All in all, if you can put the mixing aside, this game is absolutely something that musical and game lovers should at least check out. I'm hoping for DLC based sequels that can continue from the original "end" to keep those choices mattering into the future. It left so many tasty nuggets that can lead to future stories, and I for one will be buying them.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this one up as part of the June 2024 Humble Bundle and did enjoy it, although I would never have bought it on it's own.Contrary to what is advertised, though, this is NOT an RPG. It's a nice little story game where choices are made during musical sequences, which is rather refreshing (think the inevitable musical episode in your favourite show). Those choices are somewhat impactful, so it does feel as if there could have been much more to the game - as it is it's story mode, with classical RPG elements removed completely.Still a thumbs up, as I liked the story and characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I was blown away by how much I enjoyed Stray Gods. The concept of a roleplaying musical is genius, and the game really delivers. The story is immersive and full of meaningful choices that impact how everything unfolds. But what truly stands out is the music! The songs are catchy, emotional, and beautifully integrated into the gameplay. The characters are vibrant, and I loved how each one had a different role to play in the musical narrative. Whether you’re into RPGs or musicals (or both), this game is something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game with a fun mystery to unravel and an AMAZING OST. Each song was a delight to listen to, and I love how the way you decide to play Grace affects how each song goes down ("Challenging a Queen" is my favourite). As someone who had a past interest in greek mythology growing up too, this game was made even better. If you like musicals, you'll probably like this game. It's so unique and deserves all the praise it gets.

_childDocuments_.review: i didn't enjoy this game very much despite having high hopes, unfortunately!PROS:+ amazing performances -- Laura Bailey in particular is a star + very cool concept + complex and likable characters+ cool designsCONS:- in a musical game, the focus shouldn’t have been hiring good Game People. the voice actors and composer are good, but most of the actors aren’t suited for a musical. they should have hired people experienced in musical theater, because the songs, composed by an instrumentalist, aren’t memorable as musical numbers. some are downright deeply unpleasant to hear because the singing talent wasn’t there- it’s a visual novel, but it creates different expectations by advertising itself as something different. role-playing aspect is very limited — it’s more visual novel than life is strange or telltale - wondering why you get romance options, as i felt mine was pretty invalidated by the end! big bummer in a game that advertises itself as letting you romance others. would've preferred a game that follows the romance between grace and one specific central character, and does it well, than a game that offers me various choices but doesn't do right by them.- in a game about sound, audio mixing is VERY inconsistent to a distracting degree- feels very linear whereas I expected more choices and consequences - mystery is very easy to solve early on- not sure why you're walled off from picking dialogue choices that don't correspond with the personality you chose at the beginning -- and then you get a choice mid-way through to pick another personality than the one you identified with? very odd design choicethe concept for this game is lovely, but the execution leaves a lot to be desired.
