_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is a choice based interactive musical.Due to the subjective nature of musical taste it's hard to tell if someone will enjoy this or not, but the trailers offer a good sample of what the music is like. The lyrics will often not rhyme and sometimes one line will be longer than you expect in order to accommodate dialogue. Some of the music is intentionally discordant. If you like jazz you'll probably find a lot to love here. As someone who listens to music not too dissimilar to this, I enjoyed it.Story is well told, a mystery with a very obvious answer. Choices are more interesting than most Interactive fiction and seem to have more impact on the story, including changing the songs, but I suspect no matter what you do, you will find the answers you need. Still worth a replay to see the different outcomes and what people make of a different version of Grace.I really enjoyed this and it seemed like they were hinting at more stories to be told within this world, so hopefully we'll get more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty unique game.  Kind of a tell-tale like visual novel where you make choices as to where the story is heading and also make choices that help shape the songs.  Characters are likeable (particularly Fred!), story ok, some decent humour at points (gotta like Asterion!) though it ends a bit abruptly.  Music is okay to good.  The singer for protagonist Grace is particularly enjoyable as is Medusa.  I didn't feel Athena was very well done though, as a character or in the singing displayed.The game is pretty short, maybe six to eight hours, so you are mainly playing it for the fact that user-guided musicals don't otherwise exist that I know of!  DLC for Orpheus is very short and songs not as good (but Speed Dating one is pretty amusing), but worth buying if you want to support this sort of game!  Also...  Not sure why everyone is singing around Orpheus.  Grace is a god - a Muse - and her schtick is to turn stuff into a musical with her divine powers, but Orpheus is just a legendary bard and reborn mortal.  Folk around him would not be magically made to sing even though he himself would certainly be inclined to do so.  I chalk it up to Grace's influence being strong in the world at that point, at least from the decisions in my game :)

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this. I really did. But I can't recommend it to anyone. The story/plot is great. Probably an 8/10. Most of the songs are about the same. I actually was relieved when they started singing because other than that one song, they were good!One thing I noticed about the dialogue... it was at its worst when the mood of the scene was happy. _childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed opinions and feelings about this game but ultimately I had a good time playing it so it deserves a positive review.This review is spoiler-free for the story and characters.Thematically, the game is right up my alley; I love musical theater and I was a Percy Jackson & greek mythology nerd.For me the game succeeds in the mythology department. I love modern depictions of greek gods and myths and Stray Gods does this fantastically and also explains its own spin on it. It all makes sense to me.There are many moments where a mythology nerd would be like "uhmm, actually...", but I like how the game handles that, it's refreshing and modern.Every little detail in these mythology stories is usually heavily debated, which source is right, what or who came first, etc. It's always been very tiring and I personally don't care if it's not accurate to what I know because the in-game universe is coherent and consistent and still stays true to the "real" greek mythos without just doing the same thing over and over again.In my book this game is another win in modern mythology based media, and if you were anything like me in middle school you will like the characters and the world.Now on to the second main theme of the game: a MusicalI have to say I'm pretty disappointed when it comes to the songs, I didn't like the first ones and hoped maybe it would get better. Some songs did have their moments and none of them are bad by any means. It's just not typical musical tunes, sure, it's dramatic and the choice based shift in the songs is something I have never seen before. None of them stick out to me in any way, all of them are very slow and often too literal. Most Musicals I know have at least one song or one part I catch myself singing randomly. This doesn't exist here, it's not memorable.Also, the voices don't give me musical theater at all. None of the voices are bad, don't get me wrong, the voice acting in this game is great, the singing itself is great. They just don't sell the whole "Musical" aspect to me.The best part about this theme to me is that the characters acknowledge they are randomly breaking out into song and the story actually explains why this is a musical. Love that.I applaud the creators of this game for the novelty of the whole "choice-based musical" concept, I just wish it was executed a bit better. Sometimes the actual part that gets sung doesn't align with the choice you picked. In hindsight some choices are slightly misleading on what the characters will actually say/sing afterwards.Now on to a rather annoying part, I wish I didn't have to add this but it is a part of the game AS OF NOW.Glitches. Many.The glitches in this game are nothing game breaking, for me the game has been perfectly playable during my 3 runs.They are just really annoying; character sprites flickering or just becoming translucent during cutscenes, sometimes even disappearing for a moment. Many sound bugs or -which I hope is not the case- badly recorded or edited parts in the voice acting during dialogue, I feared my headphones were broken due to frequent weird cutoffs during dialogue scenes. Figured out it was the game.The mixing in most songs can also be kind of weird, some parts are quieter than others or a song is just quieter in general.Like I said, nothing game breaking, just annoying.I hope these issues can get resolved and patched.

_childDocuments_.review: A murder mystery musical involving Greek gods in our modern world. Beautiful songs that allow the player to direct it with their choices. So many charming characters voiced by a fantastic cast. You've even got romance options. I am currently in Act 2 and loving every second of it.Update: I have finished the game four times now. Romanced each of the characters. Freddie is my favorite, but they’re all fantastic. Plenty of unique songs and variations to hear on repeat playthroughs. One of the complaints I’ve heard is that this game is called a Roleplaying Musical. I understand why that confuses some people. Thinking it might be a classic leveling rpg when it’s not. The way I look at it, is that it’s something entirely new, a RPM (Roleplaying Musical). It’s all about the music and the literal hundreds of variations in the songs. That alone makes this game worth it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I've just finished my first playthrough and write the review based on that experience.Today is launch-day for Stray Gods and I've decided to dive right in. I've been looking forward to this since about a year by now, I think, when I first read about the basics of this game. Greek Mythology, but set in the modern day and with/as a musical? Yeah, count me in! I've played the demo when it was around and thought to myself that it's odd how the characters aren't *animated* but rather moved like maybe comic panels transitioning from one panel to the next and thought back then that maybe that was just a concept.It is launch day. That wasn't a concept. That is the chosen art style. And while at first I found it a little odd, after a few scenes you're quite grooved in on it. It works great with the characters' art styles, since the shading and setting and everything also feels very comicbookish. The details on the characters are quite nice, everyone is fairly easy to recognize if you have some idea of Greek Mythology and some are pleasant surprises as they break with the stereotype you might have of them in your head from stories you consumed so far in whatever shape they might have taken.The music itself is beautiful. I can't say I loved every song. There was at least one that I didn't really like. But they are all entertaining. The songtexts feel well written despite you being able to change the tone in the middle of the songs by the choices you make. It never felt out of place or like a weird transition. Some of the songs stay in your ear for a bit and I personally am not mad about it at all. I like the recurring themes as well. The choices you can make feel like you can build up to things and while I didn't feel like I had no idea where something was going, I also didn't think I already had it all figured out either just by reading my options. There is definitely replay-value. At the very least you can get two very different stories out of this, I'm sure, depending on who you side with. The story itself I found very intriguing as well. The way the Mythology was integrated into our modern age was well thought through and executed. I loved it. There were quite some points, too, that are still unresolved and inspire me to try and fill out the blanks the game's narration left open after my first playthrough. It encourages discussions and I loved that. Now so much for the good parts, here are the bad parts:Some voice lines were very, very quiet. As in I could barely at all hear them and was forced to use subtitles to read them. Now I have those on anyway, but I still found it annoying that in a full release they hadn't managed to fix the sound levels to find consistency between those. Grace is often at what I perceived as a 'normal' volume while e.g. Persephone was fairly quiet compared to her. I was also a little miffed about one of the songs near the end feeling like I couldn't pick choices that went in a direction I wanted them to go - but that was personal taste, I guess. Another thing that I noticed was that a lot of the songs felt like ballads while I wished there would have been a bit more different styles mixed in there. That might have been partly influenced by choices made though, so that's to be taken with a grain of salt.The visuals sometimes felt downgraded when there were character closeups. Not that of the characters, mind you, but the backgrounds. Sometimes there were the pixels clearly visible and almost distractingly so, other times the lines just felt like they got quite blurry, sometimes there was flickering between two lines that intersected, too. But those were mostly minor things and they don't distract enough to not enjoy the songs or the story.Altogether I'd recommend Stray Gods. I wouldn't say it's a must-play, but it was definitely a very enjoyable experience. For one playthrough, if you pause in between like I did, I guess you'd take something between 5 and 8 hours and they feel well invested. Playing it once definitely leaves you wondering what other endings you might discover. I'd give it a 8 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no doubt that Stray Gods is a niche game.  A narrative musical?  This game is a vision for a future of this type of game and it sets a bar for anyone who follows it and I really hope they do.  It's not a long game, but it doesn't need to be.  The teasing of different song results based on choices you make throughout urge you, and make you want, to play through it again.  What if I made that choice there?  That would change how that event happened completely!  You get to peek a little into the lives of Greek gods struggling to live in a forever changing world and get caught up in all the drama, history, trauma and neediness of some of them!It's like a beautiful choose your own adventure musical where you get to meet characters, change outcomes, get attached and maybe even fall in love.If you think maybe you'd like this game, it's worth the punt.  This is an original idea/dream brought to life by people very passionate about it being as good as it can be and doing something completely different in the gaming world.  It should be encouraged, it should be supported if you believe it's something we need more of. _childDocuments_.review: A wonderful adventure game with an interesting spin on the Greek gods. This is both a visual novel and a musical, meaning the choices that you make during the singing scenes also affect the direction that the music takes. It's a fascinating concept that is greatly enhanced by the acting and singing talents of many of the voice acting industry's heavy-hitters. My biggest gripe is that I wish the sound design had a little more time to cook in the oven because a lot of the audio sounded pretty raw. Some scenes just felt empty or otherwise not as emotionally impactful as they were supposed to be because sound effects were either sparse or altogether absent. All in all though, the narrative was compelling, the characters were endearing, and the VO performances were moving which made the experience as a whole worth it.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with a few caveats It's something I was interested in for a long time ever since I first saw it was announced a few years back, so I suppose my expectations also played a part in why I think it could've been a better experience overall. I think the game is definitely at least worth a sale purchase if you're into the visual novel genre, but it's probably floating somewhere around a 6 - 7/10 for me.I don't know if I'd say any aspects of the game are particularly -bad- exactly, but from what I've gained in one play through (picking charming/reckless options) there's definitely a couple of great things, with quite a lot of mixed.First off with the good:Grace, the player character is great. I love her VA, singing, personality and overall design.She's relatable from the very first scene imo. There's also a few other standout characters like Freddie, Pan and Hecate.Art direction was also really nice. I've seen a few people complain about it but I suppose this is subjective, I thought mostly every frame had something to offer!It handles sensitive subjects such as drug use, abuse and suicide in a very respectful mature way, something I think the writers and devs should be proud of themselves for. The Lgbtq+ characters are also portrayed well and I really appreciated that in particular.Okay so now with the mixed:Like a lot of reviews are saying on here, the direction the plot takes is about as predictable as it gets to the point where I'd guessed the mystery less than an hour into a 5 hour play through, this isn't awful because I think the explanation given was sufficient enough, but the game very much came off as a 'whodunit' and could've done a better job at not being so obvious in that regard.The audio - Take into account that the songs can change depending on your choices with instrumental change ups and completely different lyrics so your mileage may very, however I think musically the game starts off amazingly with the song 'Adrift' and quickly falls off a cliff not long after, and I mostly found myself underwhelmed through most of the musical numbers with only a small handful of tracks being standout enough to me, those being 'I can teach you' and 'The Ritual' (Specifically the angry/reckless versions).I think for a game specifically built around the fact that its a musical, the lyricism and song quality could've been much better with many of the songs coming off as regular spoken words shoved into a musical format, not to mention what everyone else is saying - the audio levels are completely out of whack at certain points and really just need looking at by a sound engineer, on top of that it may have been a bug on my end but in the latter half of the game the lyrics were completely out of sync with the songs.It's one of those games that makes me wish there was a "maybe" option on reviews. If you're a fan of the genre, you'll be entertained for 15 ish hours if you decide to do three playthroughs, but if you're coming in expecting a grand musical akin to your favourite disney movies then I think you're probably going to end up mostly disappointed.tl;dr: characters and representation are great with a bit of a lackluster mystery and a slightly disappointing musical aspect which doesn't live up to expectations but okay enough to not be called 'bad', maybe wait for sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished my first play-through, and holy Hades, what a ride!For me, everything from the characters to the music to the art style just works and syncs so so well together. _childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is a visual novel with unpleasantly chaotic musical. Voice acting, worldbuilding and art style are the strongest points of this game. Unfortunately choices presented have no real repercussions and lead to no new information making multiple playthroughs pointless.The game is presented in a form of slide-show of 2D characters and 3D backgrounds with animations restricted to objects such as opening doors or burning fire. The comic -esque art style is nice but it gets stale with limited amount of illustrations being recycled throughout the game multiple times. There are a couple of times when low-res textures are seen in the background too.Voice actors did an amazing job at dialogs however singing leaves a lot to be desired. The main selling point of this game, the musical is hard to complement. Most songs feel like a bunch of samples from various genres unintelligently glued together. It sounds as if VAs were improvising lyrics with akwardly prolonged words to match the melody.The story revolves around ancient greek dieties in modern day. I really enjoyed the worldbuilding aspect where all characters bring their own baggage to the table. Characters that usually take the main stage in this kind of story are actually missing which allows lesser known dieties like Eros or Hecate to make their case. Unfortunately the plot of murder-mystery is predictible and not much is there to be found on subsequent playthroughs. What needs to be mentioned, this game is one of those 'politically progressive' with every color of rainbow represented.Honestly this whole game could be an animated story rather than wasting our time on pointless choices in a visual novel. None of the choices lead to a different meaningfull outcome. You might get some variation of what characters say but you find the full context of the story in a single playthorugh. We have four love interests which give two songs to hear each. At the end of the day the story reaches its climax on a happy note no matter what you do.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, if the developers read this, I really hope they don't take my critique poorly. This game definitely gets a recommendation from me for the characters and story alone. It was very engaging and I had to keep playing to find out what would happen next! However... If you're looking for a good musical, this just isn't it. The songwriting is simply not very good. It serves its purpose for the sake of carrying the plot forward, but the lyric writing is incredibly sloppy and a lot of the music feels too samey going from song to song. However, I like I said, the devs made a really well told story overall and I hope to see what they make in the future with the lessons they learned here! It can't be easy to figure out how to make a video game into a musical and I think this was a really solid start to figuring that out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fantastic game, in so many ways. It's, fundamentally, a visual novel/choose your own adventure novel with music, except you can make choices in song that actually can have fairly important consequences, but also change lyrics and some of the music in the song itself.The story is well told, and very interesting. It's a very good urban fantasy take on Greek Mythology that definitely leans heavily on the Roman poet Ovid's tradition, but also makes its own changes, especially to bring it into the modern era in a way that is compelling and effectively allows for the main cast to be what it is. For anyone with interest in the classics, this will feel rewarding in its own way, while at the same time providing a rather fresh take on the topic, not just in how it's told, but simply of what is told.It is most definitely a David Gaider story and I mean that in the best way. I feel like his true excellence lies in the world building, and in letting the world building itself and the gameplay inform the story very well. The performances are strictly diegetic, and it's through what the main character, Grace, is able to do with her powers. That is the most obvious and present example, and is very well used. However, all of the unique ideas seem to be well thought out, and play their role very well to both craft the world and the story, as well as how the story goes.The plot itself is a touch simpler than the more elaborate world around it, but it doesn't need to be more complex. It's a good story, well told. It foreshadows things well, and the turns in the story are set up well, and both minor and major moments feel like they consistently lead you to exactly where you think they are. It doesn't rely on surprises, and even the sense of suspense is more related to specific interactions and being able to get an outcome you want. It builds, however, good anticipation. I always felt like I wanted to see/hear the next song, the next piece of the puzzle, the next conversation.The game isn't perfect and it could really use some more cooking. I didn't run into bugs or the like, but the audio mixing could use some help, particularly in the back half of the game. Some character voices are too quiet, while others are very loud, and the music, both background and the songs, has a habit of being all over the place in terms of volume. There are perhaps a couple of numbers (there are many in total) that were...less than exceptional, but I think that comes down more to genre choice than performances.The voice acting is superb. Honestly, I found dimensions to voice actors I've been hearing for 15+ years that I didn't know were there (plus the singing of course). The format, being a series of stills in relatively rapid sequence, more akin to a comic (although without the panel format) instead of animation, I think allowed and demanded of each voice actor to really unfurl their wings much more. Each character comes across impeccably in their voices, and there is never a moment where I hear anyone other than the character being portrayed. There are some characters I wish we could have spent more time with, but that is out of personal preference.Overall, a great game and a great concept. It could use a few updates and patches here and there, but this is a very good product, and a very good deal I would say even for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you're looking for likeable characters and a fun time. _childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: If you like visual novels and urban fantasy in a similar vein to American Gods or The Dresden Files, you'll probably enjoy this. It's a fairly straightforward, but solid, urban fantasy murder mystery story. The downside is it's pretty clear their budget went to getting it fully voice acted, and not to the art, UI, bug testing, optimization, or really any other aspect, all of which feel rough and unpolished.The messy art seems to be largely a stylistic choice, but I would be more inclined to buy into that if the art style was more consistent. Instead, most characters and backgrounds stick to simple flat tones with no lighting whatsoever and very loose, bold linework, but other art includes a lot more shading, gradients, and more detailed linework. Which is mostly fine, it's not too noticeable as long as there's a scene change, but there were a couple spots where this art was mixed together and it looked a bit amateurish. In addition, while most of the art appears sharp, some textures and shadows are inexplicably low-res and badly pixelated.The UI is pretty simple and standard for a decision-driven game like this. You can choose decisions with the keyboard, which is a nice option (not to mention necessary for accessibility)... except when you can't, so a mouse seems to be required anyway. And then there are certain points in the game when it switches to a long menu of options that require you to click an option, then click a confirm button. That may not sound bad, but consider that (as far as I can tell) in these sections you're generally going to work your way through all the options and it does not seem to matter what order you do them in. So requiring an extra click to confirm feels like a needlessly clunky design choice, which is exacerbated into being mildly annoying by the fact that when you click an option, the mouse glitches to the furthest corner of the screen from where the confirm button is located.Also, I couldn't help but notice that, despite this being a visual novel using sprites in low-poly 3D environments with virtually no animations, it still stuttered at times on a PC that can run most games with their settings turned up to ultra. How does something this lo-fi manage to get that badly optimized?Ok, finally, with this game's big claim to fame being that it's an interactive musical, I'd be remiss if I didn't comment on the songs. So the songs are... fine. They were certainly not written by the next Lin-Manuel Miranda – there's more sing-talk than full singing and they vary between leaning on the most simplistic and obvious rhymes possible, or not bothering to rhyme at all, and poor mixing combined with over-reliance on multiple characters singing over each other make some of the songs muddy and hard to follow. But a couple of the musical numbers are kinda cool and most of them at least manage to be serviceable at moving the plot forward. There's a thematic in-world lore reason for the singing, so it does need to be there, but it's really not good enough to be a reason to buy the game by itself.The bottom line though is that, as much as there is to complain about, none of those things are more than nuisances. Fundamentally this is a solid interactive story, and everything else does manage to do the bare minimum necessary to let you enjoy that story.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I've been following for a long time has finally arrived and I finished my first run in about 6 hours. No regrets. Reminder that it's a visual novel style kind of game so there's far more talking than there is a sense of gameplay but by allowing players to make their choice during songs, it gives it all a more unique spin and makes you feel more in control of the outcome. The music is the major selling point. It's beautifully written and every actor involved was clearly chosen based on their skill. tldr; If you like choose your own adventures, Greek Myth, and musicals, you're going to love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A game for a particular kind of player. _childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Really solid story, can be a little predictable if you're aware of tropes and Greek Myth 101 but still have enough whimsy in your heart to enjoy things for what they are. Still tugged at the heartstrings a few times, and made me glad that I took a moment to read the content warnings before playing. Still got devastated otherwise, but the warnings are always nice. I did play this in one full sitting, so I've not run into the bug a few negative reviews mentioned, but I do know if I ran into it, I'd have just dropped the game for a few months (or until they fixed it). I most likely won't do a new save til this happens, but already anticipating ways I could change things up and see how alternate scenarios play out (considering what I did do, options I missed out on, and guessing from locked achievement descriptions).From the trailers and hype about the game, it really is obvious the love and care was heavily put into the voice talent, and it IS well deserved, I never hated anyone's singing lines by any means and my ears didn't bleed during dialogue, so we got a win in that department. The art direction did feel a little janked at first, with the mix of 3D background with "wiggly outlining to appear 2D" and 2D character models with heavy black shading, but after a few hours of letting my eyes glaze over and get used to it, it just melded together and I had more time to appreciate how hot/adorable/charming the NPCs and Grace are. Would rate this an 8/10 from just my play experience as of day-after playing on release day. I wouldn't say everyone ABSOLUTELY HAS to get it at full price and you're completely valid if you just wanna wait til it goes on sale. Or hope a friend sees it on your wishlist and gifts it on your birthday/gift giving holiday/when you're a lil sad and they have 30 dollars to spare.Overall: it's a fun experience! I was charmed, saw hot interpretations of Gods, and listened to fun tunes. What I wanted when I bought the game, got it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game for the 1st time and I can say with certainty that this was one of the best story-driven games I have ever played. Incredibly complex? No. Perfectly executed? No.Did my save file poof the 1st time? Yes.But I cannot and will not deny that this game was deeply interesting and incredibly emotional and amazingly well voiced by some of the greatest in the industry today. The choices feel like they mean something, the progression makes sense, and you feel like you grew for having gone through the experience. The minor graphical bugs and save file issues will be patched soon, and then all that will remain is a beautiful story that will whisk you away again and again.And while I do think that $30 is a little steep for a 6 hour game, I know that the sheer amount of replayablility makes this more than worth the purchase.Buy it. Full Price, Half Price, Double Price, doesn't matter. It'll be worth it at any cost.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like musicals - and do not shy away from a bit of sillyness - play it.If you like greek mythology and enjoy modern interpretation with lots of clever twists - play it.If you like great characters (and voice acting) - play it.Comes of as charming mix, over the top at a lot of times. But ends on so many emotions, you'll shed a tear.Big thumbs up: If you happen to let this unique mix sink in.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Musicals in video games are probably rarest beast of them all. Even in movies that's a specific niche for a certain crowd. Stray Gods is what happens when you combine the musical part with Greek mythology, it sounds like a mess right? And it is. Murder mystery is very easy to solve, even in a couple of first scenes you will understand who is behind it. I thought that they would play more with intricacies and various theatrics from the mythology but the scope was very modest.Also it doesn't help that the animation isn't that fluid, and most of the design of the characters is "modern", would loved to see it be more expansive and connected to the initial lore, but hey, if you write this in a way for modern kids, then it might be your cup of tea in the end. Music is probably the best part, some arrangements are quite catchy, but the voices for the signing and the voice actors, that is something that fluctuates a lot throughout the whole game. Plus some of the lyrics seem to be there since they couldn't appropriate better words so it sounds clumsy at times.It's a very short game, somewhere around 5 to 6 hours, there are other pathways, but in terms of re-playing it again, I don't see that I will explore it since it won't be providing a Role Playing experience that i was hoping to get out of it.Full price skip it, but if it's a sale, and you don't mind the shallow gaming experience, then go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

Worth a buy if you just want to make choices with a cup of tea and relax into story telling and song :) x

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I found it a little hard to get into at the start, but by the time Pan's song was done I was fully invested (it's a great song, with a great many variations to it which showcases nicely what this game can do as an interactive musical, loved it!).I was always going to get this game because I adore the idea of it, and I'm happy to say that I loved my time with this team's result of that idea too!The performances were grand, there were several songs in it that I really really enjoyed, the world-writing was great fun to dive into (particularly dug how they tied the mythology fiction into bits of more mordern historical), and Freddie and Hecate are the best and I love them.Also worth mentioning that I love what they've done with Muses! It's such an inspired and perfect way to not only turn your story into a musical, but also get to have those heart to heart battles usually only reserved for card games, ballads, and anime characters punching each other.That's not to say all of the writing was perfect however, as there were a few scenes where it kind of felt like some writing should've been there that wasn't, like the connective tissue between the scenes had been snipped away, and that made said small handful of scenes a little more awkward than they should've been I feel.And then there was one point in Act 3 where a character was reacting to something a certain way and I couldn't help but feel the game wasn't addressing the points I felt should be brought up about that situation, that bit sadly rubbed me the wrong way a bit and made me feel kinda upset when it was happening.Happy to say that was only one moment in the story though! And that the overall ending and direction it took before and after that moment were good enough that I ended the game feeling happy when reflecting on my time with it and the story it told.Will definitely be happy to come back to this game again in the future, not just to check out the narrative path differences but to make different songs too! It was a fun experience and got a couple tears out of me along the way as all good musicals should.So yeah!Overall Thoughts: A solid 8/10 I think! Room for improvement but definitely something special that I'd love to see more of!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a mythology geek like me, you will not find this game very accurate to the Ancient Greek Mythology but the story is still great and the music is awesome. I experienced a few plot holes and a couple of bugs (like Freddie appearing on 1 slide out of nowhere when she wasn't there for the whole scene), but overall I enjoyed the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful experience, the world was engaging and the characters interesting, I remained guessing and putting clues together for much of it but the reveal wasn't frustrating. Of course now this brings the music and songs which are beautiful and I am extremely impressed by how layered they are. Each song has multiple ways it can go adding and layering different characters depending on choices, even the in universe explanation for the songs was solid and watching characters react to sudden music was good fun. All in all a game I greatly enjoyed and will be playing through again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended if you like visual novels or are open to trying one out. Astounding voice acting cast and I had so many of the songs stuck in my head after playing (and have been listening to the soundtrack at work). One playthrough is relatively short (I took 10 hours but definitely read and talked to everyone possible) but has lots of replay value. I love that the tone / style / even sometimes outcome of the songs change depending on your choices. I will definitely be playing through it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. I've played through one run of the game so far, didn't put the game down for even a second or want to, for that matter. You might look at my playtime and think 'damn, short game' - but if you think of it as a musical, which is essentially is, it's a pretty long musical. A long musical where your choices matter significantly, and even change the music! In terms of significant bugs, the only one I experienced was a song verse that didn't play the audio at all in Act III, which was a shame because the music was really kicking into gear right before that point, but it resolved once I moved into the next verse, which didn't take too long at all.Overall, absolutely worth the money I spent, looking forward to stepping back in and trying a different path through it again in future.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: So, I was sold when I saw the Morning Fades song on YouTube and I knew then that I have to buy this game to woo Pan. I was not disappointed. I DON'T THINK I CAN DO ROMANCE ANYMORE AFTER HIM. Khary Payton did such a fine job with this. Every main casts got great VA. I could write an essay of why Pan is such a delight character to befriend with, I'm always a sucker for characters that are like 'villain' of the story (his I Can Teach You will definitely send me running in reality, but since this is a fantasy world I get to take risks and be surprised he wasn't a scumbag) or the character that are so resourceful. He's a combination of both. There are still some transition issues and voice level inconsistency. There are songs I like and songs I find them nah, but the songs that really hit you? I'd pay $30 for that song alone, let alone getting to play the game AND have a couples of really, really great songs. One song made me got all swooning (which is yes, it was from Pan's Morning Fades.) And one song that was really, really sad that made me thought to myself I might play that song at a grieving event.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: As a musicals-obsessed, pagan, bisexual, millennial, who grew up with a tumblr and loves RPGs and Visual Novels, Stray Gods hits just about every box you can think it would hit.Stray Gods' feels like if the CW aired something good for the first time in 20 years with music that would become the cult darling of the nerdy girl in the high school drama club. If you understood either of those, you probably already bought this game and if you haven't, you should.Compelling mystery and story and characters, great songs and singing that blend near seamlessly with your choices. Just get the game if you're even thinking about it. It's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Good things I can say about this: Great voice performances, cool art style and I never found myself choosing a dialogue option where the character was not as tactful as I thought she'd be. You know how sometimes in visual novels and RPGs you click [Refuse.] and your character does the [Have an absolute meltdown.] instead? They managed to always avoid that, and it's their first game. Kudos.This is more of a visual novel than a roleplaying game, and not even a great one at that. Unless you're really interested in how this studio specifically approached making a game around voice talent, or you're invested in the performers starring in this, I doubt you'll find it worth your while.In a very short window (I played for about 5 hours), they tried setting up a murder mystery, a relatable/interesting main character with their own life and things they cared about before all this, a bunch of worldbuilding with their own take on how old-timey gods could be walking among us, and some "romancing" opportunities. None of these elements are very exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Gods is exactly what it says in the title, and it executes its premise incredibly well. The music is varied, responsive to your choices and a delight to listen to. Some songs made me laugh out loud, some still make me cry when I listen to them.Anyone who is interested enough in this game to read the reviews will probably enjoy it, so I wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: The worst part of the game is that I want a lot more of it. But after playing through, and then looking into the song variations I have to say its impressive how they weave the narrative into the music. It makes for a very unique experience, that is a fresh take on the story driven genre. Fun characters, neat plot, 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in one sitting and it was a pure blast. I really enjoyed myself. _childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Very happy I got this game for free. It is a rip off at full price. Even 5 euros is too much. It's a visual novel with small amount of interaction and your choices don't really matter. The music is banal and boring. The dialogue is cringe, the art style is minimal but doesn't work. I guess they spent most of the budget on the VAs and couldn't do any animation. Story wise the premise is interesting the characters are mostly lame, cringe and likely to cause eye turning due to aforementioned lameness and cringe worthiness. A musical lives and dies by its songs. The songs in this game are mediocre at best. Also the developers would do well to keep politics out of the game. The disclaimer at the start of the game that "this game was built on stolen lands" made me cringe so hard I almost went to the hospital. Pride flags in the backgrounds etc. Totally unnecessary virtue signalling. Maybe for the sequel they should add that the computers the game was developed on were made from slave labour by kids mining the lithium batteries in africa. Or that the clothes worn during the making of the game were made by children in a sweat factory in Asia. You see how cringe it gets once you follow the self-flogging woke nonesense. If you want a truly better visual novel that is well written and more interactive I would recommend you try Slay the Princess or even Hungry Lamb: Travelling in the Late Ming Dynasty. TL/DR: ♥♥♥♥ writing and music, unnecessary wokeness. Good VA. Pirate this game. It's not worth the price of coffee in your country.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, what to say about this game other than it seems to be tailor made to my specific interests.Its a choose your own adventure game musical where choices matter, there are romance options and it all has a spritz of greek mythology on top.Lets start with my favorite part of this game, the Music.  Gods the music.  I actually went back into steam in order to buy the albums because I'm so obsessed.   I dont think the music can be praised enough truly.  The lyrics are charming and the music flows so well together no matter what choice you make.  Every choice you make adds or subtracts specific sounds from the overall track, ending in a different sound every time.  (I'll get that achievement someday i swear).  The voice actors are fantastically talented and wonderful, even when one of them was supposed to be a 'terrible singer' i found myself grinning the entire time.Continuing on from the music, lets go to the visuals.  This game has a very interesting style.  i'd describe its visuals as having very limited animation if any.  However, when the animation is used its done so in a very effective way, usually coupled with the music to make a scene feel more intense or beautiful.  This is definitely more of a visual novel than anything else.  Despite the limited animation style, the art is done so beautifully that every movement and 'panel' feels fresh and intriguing.  Some of the imagery in this game will forever be ingrained  in my mind.Next i'd like to go over the characters themselves.  Every single one of them has a style and personality which makes them stick out.  They are all distinct, and given exactly enough time for you as a player to understand who they are and what makes them tick.  Romance characters get even more development than the side characters, and even get their own love songs involving Grace (which makes me kick my feet every time shh).  Even through all of this and the wonderful romances with complex characters who actively change during the game, my actual favorite character in the entire game is Medua (let me romance the snake lady you cowards AGH).Going over the Gameplay, this is a choose your own adventure game, and as you can imagine, you choose your path.  THis means you can select one of the options presented and steer the story down another pathway.  Now, this story always follows several beats, but you can affect what happens during those beats and the consequences thereof.  Replaying is also just as good, because you can press a little button to skip over he dialog (which is fully voice acted by the way).  This makes it easier to see how things change when you play through.  I will warn prospective players though, you can't use the button to skip through any musical numbers (though why would you want to, the voices are *Chefs kiss*)The story I will say was a bit predictable.  That could be because I'm a casual writer myself or  because I'm a DM  but I immediately guessed 'whodunnit'.  That being said, the ride of the story was still so interesting I couldn't recommend it more, and there was one part in the story that I wasn't expecting at all.Over all, this game was wonderfully beautiful and glorious. And the DLC was equally funny and Charming with Orpheus.  I honestly hope that this game gets popular enough for them to consider making another in the future.  Even if it doesn't involve Grace or the others from this game, I would love to see this studio make more games like this wholly unique masterpiece.  If you are even considering buying this, i promise its worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I found this game very enjoyable. The story was intriguing and I loved the musical twist on an rpg type game. The lore and world building was very thoroughly done and incredibly interesting. I also did very much appreciate the content warnings and the fact that you could reread them as necessary, helpful since I didn't complete the game in one sitting. I also did significantly enjoy the portrayals of each god and how they were given twists on the personalities they often have in the myths. Each of the gods' designs were extremely unique and intriguingI did, however, have a few issues. I don't know if the common pronunciations of the names are wrong and the game tried to correct that, but Demeter and Charon's names being pronounced differently than I'm used to was admittedly a bit jarring. Additionally, as someone who's favourite goddess is Hecate and also is a self-proclaimed witch, I did not enjoy the fact that she was declared "the idol of dark magic". That feels like a pretty poor representation of her and of witches in general. I understand watering down each god to one major aspect for the game, but Hecate is simply the goddess of magick, neither dark nor light. And the concept of dark magick is also an iffy one depending on who you're talking to.I do wish this game had an option to lower graphics as I think that would've made gameplay a bit smoother for someone like myself with an older pc. Another issue I had was while screensharing my playthrough through discord, the music and dialogue would sometimes cut out. I don't know if that's a game issue, discord issue, or computer issue, but it was an issue nonethelessAnother thing I wish this game had was an option where you could declare if you are knowledgeable about greek mythology or not. I understand trying to cater to a wider audience and also the need to world build, but as someone with an arguably decent knowledge of greek mythology, it was annoying to have a protagonist who knows nothing and also have to go through all the question options to get the achievement, though I do understand how that was an active choice by the completion-ist in meRegardless of my nitpicking of certain things, overall, my experience with this game was a remarkably pleasant one and I would definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes rpgs, musicals, and/or greek mythology
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the most unique games of the year. The developers really took a risk and that alone is worthy of praise.Sadly, Stray Gods just doesn't work.One, the music is terrible. None of the songs are memorable and most of the performances aren't great either.The murder mystery is not much of a mystery. I figured out who the killer was within the first two hours.Lastly, the role playing is pretty shallow. Your choices not mattering is not surprising, but the lack of impact in the moment to moment gameplay is really disappointing.The character writing and voice acting is solid though. And the animations are nice. So its not all bad.But its tough to recommend a "Musical RPG" when the music is the weakest part of the experience and the RPG parts aren't much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like it, but in the end it was just meh. I'm a big fan of musicals, so I came in with big expectations. In the end I was left feeling indifferent. Would've given it a middle thumb if it were possible. I don't regret playing through the game, but it's not an experience I will remember for a long time, nor one I'm interested in revisiting., nothing is catchy or memorable, neither the melodies nor the lyrics. In fact the lyrics feel very forced, it sounds like the melodies were written first and then they tried to force into them lyrics relevant to the scene. Nothing is outright terrible, but everything sounds like the filler songs you'd skip on a musical cd recording., and despite presenting itself as a detective-type mystery, you don't do any detecting yourself. In fact the game teases investigative elements at the very beginning by letting you inspect every single item in one of the first locations, only to have none of them matter and never to repeat that mechanic ever again. The story drags your character from place to place, where for 90% of the game you just learn about the world and the characters, and at the very end you're just given the solution to the entire mystery all at once. Again, neither the world nor the mystery are terrible, but the pacing feels off and player's role in solving the case is purely as a passive observer. The dialogue options might change some character interactions, but it didn't feel like anything could change any major story event. I would wager that the game's ending is chosen mainly, if not exclusively, through the final song.. Gamepad controls in the menus felt broken. Joystick was unresponsive and seemed to sometimes deselect anything and not be able to select any options again. D-pad was more consistent, but even then in the map screen I was never sure which direction I should press to select what I wanted. There are also a lot of audio issues, especially towards the end of the game. The volume would be all over the place, some characters being barely audible while others were too loud, all during the same conversation. A few dialogue lines would cut off halfway too, and during one of the songs the subtitles were off by at least a full second. After one of the scenes I had a conversation which was repeated a scene later in a different location - I assume my choices somehow triggered two versions of the same interaction, though the dialogue was exactly the same, safe for one missing response selection. Also, despite playing on a decent rig, the game would stutter slightly whenever a song was about to begin, if not midway through one.All of those issues can hopefully be patched though. Also, despite the game quite overtly wanting to be 'progressive' for lack of better term (which, by the way, if that puts you off - don't bother), most characters end up feeling tokenized if not stereotypical. To give some examples (minor spoilers):  And it's a shame, because the characters do actually have some depth and somewhat interesting backstories to them, so all that feels very forced, especially in light of the game's lore.Overall it's an interesting concept that I'd like to see expanded upon and improved in the future. As it is though, it doesn't live up to the 'role-playing musical' name. It's just a visual novel where some of the interactions happen through mediocre, in my opinion, songs.

_childDocuments_.review: This is really good. With some caveats:As a virtual novel, it is excellent. Great voice acting, multiple paths to follow, great character development. And as far as the songs go? They are great, too... except?They don't quite nail it in terms of "this is a musical." A musical has anthems that can become pop culture, divorced from the play they're attached to. Think "Camelot" or "Chorus Line" or "Singing in the Rain." There's nothing you will take away from here and be singing to yourself the next day.Not saying the music is bad; it's not, and I loved it. But it's not anthemic and catchy you can't deny it; a lost opportunity.Despite that, the story involving the Greek gods is involving; the character connections are emotionally impactful. This is unquestionably a good, narrative VN-style game and my quibble about they're not totally nailing the "musical" element is merely that: a quibble.You will likely enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: If you ask me about musicals, I would normally tell you " No, thank you, but no ".I listen to music all the time, and especially soundtracks... so how is it that I don't like musicals? Could it be that maybe I just don't like the musicals that were made recently (of the last 55 years basically) but in truth I do like a musical if It's done... different?It’s fair to say that I was very curious on seeing this play out, and test the first " RPG Musical " game.When I first started playing Stray Gods I was at ease with the voice actors for all the characters. It should be not surprise if you check some of the names that are part of this game and you know them from previous work. They are all absolutely great. One thing that I liked better about Stray Gods, is that, regardless of being a "musical" it's not just songs one after another. There is in fact a real story, a mystery to solve, and plenty of lines of dialogue. The songs are there, and they are the beating heart of this game (it sounds and flows everywhere you go) but I would say that the story, the mystery to solve and the characters conversations are the skeleton that holds everything together. If the story didn't make any sense, the songs wouldn't hold up so well...Then the songs... I did like them. A thing that shocked me and surprised me, was that I was paying attention to the lyrics of the songs, and finding some of the things being said amusing. One thing I appreciate is that there were very different styles of songs, (according to each character you meet) So they felt more alive, and poignant to the story. These songs made me feel like I was standing in a theater and watching a play, there was some kind of joy and exaggerated expression of these characters that worked really well. The visual style of a graphic novel also went well. It struck that balance between real and fantasy. You could say, it feels like a "representation of real" like watching a theater play.One negative thing I could say about the experience, is that, the choices you get to make within the songs sometimes are not very clear (the songs will change in style according to your choices, and also the story) Also it was impossible for me to have timed choices active since I am a freak of overthinking every choice I make so there was no way I was making 10 seconds quicktime events! (luckily, there’s an accessibility option to disable that) All in all, I would say this was a great experience and the first time I enjoyed a musical since I was a kid, and I was watching a very very old movie in my mother's house, called "The Sound of music" and singing along "Do re mi".I still don't like musicals, but I now understand, that It's just some of the musicals done today that I don't like (most of them). But if it’s done right (and especially if it’s a role playing musical) I may be tempted to play more of them, many more times.

_childDocuments_.review: This game I found it to be positively charming! Is it for everyone? No. But I really do implore people to give it a shot.  Playing this game for me actually surprised me to an extent because your choices really do affect how your character both reacts and how they will be reacted to which was kind of refreshing.  I also loved the fact that I was in control of how the songs played out and I wasn't bound to one particular path song-wise I could combine the different choices and make an entirely new song.  That being said I do have some things about this game that I wasn't entirely happy about.  The character designs are gorgeous but I would have loved to have seen more facial expressions for one and some different outfits.  The romance options aren't bad but I would have loved to see the romance developed a bit more and I was a bit disappointed with some of the romantic scenes that were shown they were often recurring instead of something new. Which can be kind of boring.  I thought the voice acting was really good but the singing for certain characters wasn't the best. As a whole, I plan to go back and replay Stray Gods it is an excellent game.  So much so that I hope they either plan to continue to story in a second game or make a DLC either way Stray Gods is one of those hidden gems that has its kinks but it is a lot of fun to play. I didn't mind paying Full Price for the game but for those who might not want to pay 30.00$ dollars for a 5ish Hour game, I would definitely wait till it goes on sale. Also, I played this game in offline mode so Steam didn't track my hours.  So for those looking at my time and wondering why I am making a review you now have your reason.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m really not the kind to post reviews, more the kind to silently enjoy games but I’m making an exception for Stray Gods.What can I say, it’s a prefect mix with everything I like.I can start by saying that the lore, the characters and basically the story is awesome : the fact that we follow Grace, completely lost in the world of idols is such a nice idea. With that we can understand how these idols survived and if the myths can be true or not.The main stuff now : the songs : I’ve actually never, during my different playthrough, had the same songs. So many details, so many changes that I’m really wondering how that works in fact-Yep. If you love greek mythology in a modern setting with musical show with endless possibilities then this game is for you :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game aims for a highly unique and very experimental concept, basically placing it in a genre all its own. I thoroughly enjoyed it, but it is unfortunate that the execution of the concept, while charming at times, is also inconsistent and rocky. For me, it's an 8/10 riding mainly on it's ambitious premise, and given that the issues below are fixed.It desperately needs polish. In the talking scenes there's a lot of differing volumes between speakers, and this is an issue from the first office scene throughout the game until the very end. It seems because the lines were recorded in VA's own booths. I empathize with the challenges of recording lines remotely, but this amount of inconsistency is unfortunately very distracting and should have been fixed before release, especially given that this was a critique I've seen multiple people give on the demo version as well. Needing to fiddle with audio sliders constantly during the game is not fun.The hand-drawn 2D art is gorgeous and evocative, yet makes the 3D art stick out like a sore thumb, with textures that leave you wondering if that's intended art style or somebody accidentally over-compressed all textures leaving an aliased and pixelated blur. In this type of game, it's obviously not a big deal. The focus is not on graphics, but like the audio volume issues, both are annoyances that distract players from the experience.I hope this game is gets out there (and is profitable) enough to inspire another one of it's unique genre, yet I also hope that the next game turns out more polished with the experience gained during this game's development.EDIT: Nominated it for Most Innovative Gameplay and Best Soundtrack on the Steam awards.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. I was expecting a campy, silly fun time, and don't get me wrong, there is plenty of that to be had depending on your choices. But this game is so *heartfelt*. The production behind it, for what it is, is genuinely mind blowing. The VAs have done a phenomenal job, but when you realise who they are, that's hardly a surprise, is it? The artwork is insane. Next level. The music composition, for it to fit the way it does regardless of which choices you make within the songs, is so clever and well done and somebody who does maths should work out how many different versions of each song there are because yeeeesh. wow. Is it perfect? Absolutely not. The only negative reviews I've seen here are about two things: 1. The dialogue volume is inconsistent; 2. There's no manual save feature. The dialogue thing is a little jarring, but seems like it should be possible to fix later down the line. I almost didn't even mention it, though, because it hasn't affected my playthrough even a little bit. This b loves a subtitle. The manual save thing made me play certain parts for way longer than I intended to, and had me replaying the first three and a half hours or so of gameplay because I made a Wrong Choice somewhere and had to fix it. It would be really nice to just nip back twenty minutes and fix it, however I realised on my second go that I'd missed a whole lot of dialogue by moving through it too quickly, so it more than worked out in the end.Overall, yea, can't recommend enough. If you like musicals, Greek mythology, and loveable (occasionally morally ambiguous) hotties, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be sappy, but bear with me. First of all, this game is amazing: when I first heard of it a few days after the trailer was released, I decided that I would keep my eye on it. I'm glad I did. This game literally had me in tears, and even after months of listening to some of the songs on repeat, I still managed to find myself surprised. I thought I would make some completely different choices, I can tell you that! Accidentally romanced Persephone and oh am I not disappointed. I found this to be such a refreshing interpretation of her, and her final song hit me in all the right places.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Gods: The Roleplaying Musical

_childDocuments_.review: With only a couple of notable exceptions I can't stand musicals and the same goes for visual novels. It is a testament to how good this is that I have enjoyed it enough to buy the DLC story. This is the beauty of Humble Choice - often you will be surprised by great games that you would never have bought otherwise. This said, Make no mistake that this particular game is all about the music and how you can present that music in different ways.Visual novels are, for me, NOT games but rather interactive stories. Sure all games are interactive stories but most have multiple layers beyond that. What makes this one different is that it is more like going to a show with audience participation. It remains problematic that I don't see these forms as games in the traditional sense but as anyone who has gone to a good production of The Rocky Horror Show can attest; a show with audience participation can be a wonderful thing. Ultimately Stray Gods succeeds brilliantly at what its makers set out to achieve.

name: #BLUD
detailed_description: Save your friends, fight off the vampire apocalypse, and survive the horrors of freshman field hockey practice in #BLUD, a delightfully zany animated dungeon crawler that blurs the line between action RPGs and hyperkinetic 90s cartoons. Slaying the undead is just another day at high school for Becky Brewster, new kid in town and latest in an ancient bloodline of spellcasting vampire hunters. Root out demonic infestations through the town’s buzzing social media, and take selfies with demonic forces to analyze their weaknesses. Power up your trusty fiend-thwacking field hockey stick, and level up your latent magic skills through grimoires and school supplies. Master the slaying game with the help of an eclectic cast of hilarious characters, and teach the vampires a thing or two about messing with Carpentersville High! Slay the vampiric legions Take on a delightfully macabre menagerie of outrageously mutated animals and vampirically possessed townsfolk. Engage in epic, energetic boss battles as you defend your hometown. Small-town dungeon crawl Hunt the forces of evil in high school halls, convenience store aisles, and shopping malls. Discover and accept missions from the town’s social media, and track down evil (and other after-school plans) with modern tech. In a class of your own Freshman life is ultrafast-paced—even more so when you’re the vampire-hunting new kid. Assist and befriend and assist a comic cast of quirky and memorable classmates as you find your place as a teenager in the world of #BLUD. Upgrade your field arsenal Discover and earn upgrades for Becky’s trusty vampire-slaying field hockey stick to face the mounting challenges, including handy attachments like a grappling hook, shovel, and umbrella shield. Uncover fiendish mysteries Research the demonic legions through means archaic and new. Translate your family’s mystic grimoire, and snap selfies with monsters to tag their strengths and weaknesses (just don't let them bite you!). Lively undead animated adventure #BLUD is brought to life by Exit 73 Studios, a team of creators with a passion for traditional hand-drawn 2D illustration and animation, the joyous and jubilant cartoons of the modern era, and game development.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are some quick points that I like and dislike of #BludPros:1. Beautiful hand-drawn animation2. Awesome soundtrack (some great ear worms)3. Fun and charming characters4. Intriguing, amusing, and enjoyable writing/story5. Some fun game-play elementsCons:1. Awkward hit boxes (For example, falling through a floor near a pit due to the hit box not being accurate to the animation itself)2. Slightly awkward combat (It gets better with practice, but the hit boxes are just slightly off)Overall, I recommend it, especially if you enjoy 90s Cartoon Network animation. Just approach with caution that the gameplay is not as highly enjoyable as all the other elements.Final Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Depending on what you're looking for, this may not be the right choice for you.You're probably considering buying it based on the visuals. This is by far its biggest strength, the animation is superb throughout and there's a lot of it! The dialogue is also well-written, it doesn't take itself too seriously, but still has room for some high-stakes moments. A lot of it is witty banter and one-liners, a lot of Dad jokes and frequent jabs at Gen Z. This was definitely made for millennials.The gameplay aspect, however, is much more disappointing. It could be that the presentation set my expectations too high, but currently most gameplay elements are either under-baked or have severe problems.1) The combat is awkward, with spotty hit-detection. The weapon only attacks directly in front of you, so you will often either miss and get hit, or get animation locked while attacking and be hit by something else coming from a different angle.  Boss difficulty is also inconsistent, with some feeling very unfair and with poorly telegraphed attacks. Enemies also give nothing upon defeat, so there is zero incentive to actually fight and just walk by everything (and you walk so damn slow it makes progression a chore).2) Stuff is poorly explained, especially the Grimoire. You unlock entries in this book like recipes, spells and such, but I have no idea what (if anything) they're supposed to do. I am going under the assumption that these are just non-functional collectables laid out in such a way as to make you think it's going to be "something" when it's actually not. Like trying to subvert my expectations but doing a bad job at it.3) The weapon has rune slots, but as far as I can tell all they do is change the animation of the attacks sometimes. Not sure, as it's never explained what these do.4) There's a ton of sequence breaking you can do by going to areas it doesn't want you to be in yet. For example, entering a specific area from one direction will have an NPC tell you that you can't leave during the tutorial, but you already did that tutorial ages ago and they just didn't remove the trigger.5) Bugs galore! Plenty of places to get stuck. Nothing more annoying than solving a puzzle and collecting the item at the end of it, only to realise they meant for you to use your hookshot to grab the item and you're now stuck. Or when you use the blood machine after already doing that particular part of the story, you just get locked in place. Some enemy types transform into bigger ones. When I'd beaten one (and it should turn into a big spiky flesh abomination on defeat) I went into a door while it was transforming, and when I came back the enemy was still there but invisible. Also stuff like enemies not coming through the portals and they just hang there indefinitely, soft-locked myself in the hospital because I did the bridge puzzle in a way it wasn't expecting and locked myself on the wrong side.Essentially, the disappointments mount the further in you get."Oh! Are they going to {insert cool thing from adventure games here}""Nope, actually it's something less cool."Everything about the gameplay just feels so half-arsed. I've seen people say its setting gives Earthbound vibes, but it lacks the scale of a world for it to have the same impact. I've seen it compared to games like Tunic, but the combat is just too clunky and dull. There's areas you can only access after certain abilities or items have been unlocked like in Zelda, but they're so few and do not yield anything interesting.You're basically slogging through, hoping and expecting something new to be introduced that shakes things up and besides getting a shield (way too late in, in my opinion) there's just nothing. It feels so barebones. It makes you fondly remember the games it's taking its mechanics from while simultaneously not delivering anything but the bare minimum on any of them. The abilities are boring, the "dungeons" are boring, and after shuffling from place to place over and over to make sure not to miss the MISSABLE QUESTS the town also became boring.So it was a really hard choice but I had to give it a thumbs down. The ending really cemented that for me, it just ends so abruptly and gives you nothing else to do. The presentation elevates it somewhat to make it a not-awful experience, but the tedious gameplay, lack of satisfying rewards and laundry list of glitches make it more frustrating than fun.I'm genuinely shocked I was able to finish the game at all with all the possible ways it could have glitched out and softlocked my progress, something other unfortunate players seem to have experienced.And the menu UI is a nightmare to navigate too.

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding art and animation, fun and simple gameplay, clever writing.Even though this is probably the last thing the devs want to hear just after having released their baby, I have some feedback for them so I'll just dump it here. I think it'll help with the problems people seem to be having with the gamefeel and combat:- FIXED [Adding invicibility frames to the dodge roll would be a huge plus without really changing anything to the balancing or pacing of combat. It's probably very easy to implement as well. I understand the idea that you should be wary of the direction in which you dodge roll but I don't think it works too well without i-frames.]- Attacks should be cancelable by the dodge roll at any point during their animation, even the finishers. I get the idea that you wanted us to commit to attacks at the risk of getting hit by other enemies, but it slows down the pace of combat a lot as well as being frustrating. I don't think managing distance in combat suits the game: It'd be more pleasant to leap from one enemy to the other, killing everything as fast as possible.-The umbrella shield sometimes gets locked in a specific direction, I'm not sure if it's a bug but either way, you should be able to orient the umbrella in all 8 directions while holding it instead of release the button and deploying it again in another direction.-Pencils are FUN. But there's SO few of them scattered here and there. Plus they're pretty weak, so it'd be nice if they replenished over time? Anything to be able to use them more often.-The shovel digging animation is a bit slow. This is a minor complaint but it'd feel better to use if it didn't lock you in place for so long (I know, that's 0.5 seconds but it adds up to a lot for my ADHD brain).-It's been said before in reviews, but a Sprint button would be amazing. Currently, spamming dodge rolls is the only way to go a bit faster, so you spend your time rolling through Carpentersville which looks a bit silly and feels a bit exploity. Why not re-use the walk animation and speed it up a bit, coupled with a faster walk speed? Boom, you've got a sprint. Maybe while keeping the B button pressed?EDIT 1 - - --Some enemy attacks lack telegraphs. For example, the small black vampire heads instantly deploy their "spiky tongue" attack when at range, leaving no choice to the player but to roll away based on their estimation of when the enemy is going to be at range BEFORE it attacks. This creates frustration because you're expected to react based on unclear metrics (Range of attack is not displayed and attack is instantaneous). Either the attack is slow and there's no need to telegraph it too much, or it's instantaneous and absolutely requires a long telegraph.EDIT 2 - - -The first patch adds invicibility to the roll and a much needed auto-target/lock to finishers, this feels much better this way! I'm still praying for a sprint button like mentionned above, it's frustrating to spam the dodge roll with its recovery animation in between breaking the momentum. I know this feels like a to-do list coming from a self-entitled stranger, but I swear it's not, thank you for this first patch.- - -I think BLUD is a good game, but with a few tweaks it could be great.I will update the review if I find more things.

_childDocuments_.review: #BLUD is a game I like, but it's a game I wanted to LOVE and it's not quite there for me. This may not surprise you, but this game was originally a pilot for a cartoon before the devs decided to make a video game instead. And while the the animation work is stellar, the video game portion of this video game leaves a lot to be desired.This game can be very dull, there are parts that feel heavily padded, combat has no room for experimentation or self expression and before an update added I-frames to the dodge roll it could be very punishing. Not that it was ever difficult, considering you can carry 35+ full heals and use them from the pause menu. This game might not be getting patched again since Humble Games exploded and fired all it's staff. And even though it's likely to remain in this rather raw state forever, I would still recommend this game to a certain type of person.Hey buddy. Yeah, you. Do love cartoons? Do you REALLY love cartoons? Than this is the game for you pal. There is SO MUCH amazing, stylish animation in this game. For every attack, with every weapon attachment, in eight different directions plus roll attacks! And for every character and all of the bosses and enemies to! There are parts of this game without static backgrounds, where the animation is taking place in front of more animation! There's even a reference to animation pioneer Windsor McKay and his character Gertie the dinosaur.This game can be raw, but it is never lacking for charm or personality. It's a janky Zelda clone under that hood, but it looks like nothing else.
