_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Well ♥♥♥♥, they actually came back to fix a lot of complaints I and others had, so I'll bite the bullet and say I was wrong about them dropping the game. Though no matter what, unless they change the entire game, a lot of my complaints stem from how the dull the combat is, how annoying the quests are, and how empty the ending of the game felt. So, while I still probably wouldn't recommend it at full price, maybe, if you see it on sale for less than $20 if I'm being nice, $15 if I'm being real, it might be worth buying. Just keep your expectations low.I really hate to add to this game's negative scoring but it really needs to be known, this game is all style and nothing else. It's a bad zelda clone, it's a bad rpg, It's just plain bad. I'm not going to continue to inflate the ego of the devs by talking about how nice it looks because this game feels rushed in every way and I'm sick of seeing positive reviews that, despite being filled with negative points, still give it a positive just because a game looks pretty. I'm just gonna list out the multiple problems I came across in this game.- It's a buggy mess where you can get softlocked, enemies can become invincible but still hurt you, items will just disappear from the world but still be there, sound clips will play even when the action itself isn't happening, characters will be talking about tasks that you've already completed 2 chapters ago because the programmers didn't think you'd ever go back to an old place when you absolutely would because of all of the fetch quests you have to do.- The game is overloaded with a bunch of side quests that are just fetch quests. They're not even interwoven into the main story plots so you can't just do them along the way, you have to go out of your way to complete them. And some of these can be missed like, halfway through the game, you pretty much stop going to school. So I hope, if you're a completionist, that you didn't forget to finish any quests while you were there, because you will never get the chance to finish them again. - Those beautiful animations take way too long to finish. I saw a bunch of people complaining about the finishers and I never really had a problem with those because I just thought that it was part of the gameplay to just be careful where you're fighting and I've had times where finishers on one enemy, insta-killed another. So I thought it was actually cool and apart of the gameplay (I love the big boot kick) but, with the amount of times I went to pick up a pile of pencils and got stuck in the 'got item' animation while enemies were attacking me is making me second guess that. Same goes for the fire/electrocuted animations, it was funny ONE TIME and then REALLLLYYYY ANNOYING every other time.- Combat is lackluster. Zelda games are more than just throwing bombs and swinging your sword around! There's boomerangs and hammers and element rods and bows and arrows! All with different combat AND puzzle solving features. Yet, in this game, there is 1 enemy to use the shovel on otherwise it is not worth having out because you'll just get stuck in the 'you can't dig here' animation if you use it in the wrong place. There's also only one enemy that you have to use the umbrella on BUT the umbrella is best item in the game! The hookshot is too difficult to aim at enemies so it's also no good (you already have pencils anyway).- There's no point in fighting the enemies. Enemies will not drop anything, they don't drop money, they don't items, they don't drop health. So there's no point in fighting them because combat is trash... except for the final couple of chapters where enemies become overwhelming in numbers.- Spoilers for story of the game though it's pretty simple and you can probably guess all of the beats:  This game is mediocre and that's the worst thing you could say about a game. Its animations and art style are amazing but it is extremely boring and frustrating to play. It's not worthy of praise for its art alone because this is a game, not a cartoon. If your gameplay is bad then your game is bad, no excuses. It's not even bad enough to be offensive. This game will be forgotten. Nobody will play it again and nobody will care about it in a year or two. Even if you think I'm being too harsh, only 7% of people have actually beaten the game, and that's just sadI'd gladly change my review if they were to patch the game and fix a lot of bugs at least, but it's been almost three weeks and there's been no word of a patch, so I'm just saying this game has been abandoned.  (tl;dr: They're working on fixing it, though it's still at most going to end up a 5/10 experience)4/10 - go spend your money on something worth playing

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I just finished the game. Everything I said in my original review still stands. But despite game having many cons, I'm still glad I've played it. It has a special charm to it and the ending is good.Original review:This is such a strange game to review.It does so much right, but then again, it also does so much wrong.First of all, yes graphics and animations are great, Perch social network mechanic is a stroke of pure genius, dialogues are fun and the story, while nothing to write home about, nice to follow.But then you have a gameplay that never feels quite right. It mostly feels like everything you do has a slight latency to it. The running is just a bit too slow and rolling has just a bit too much downtime before you can do it again, to feel annoying.And then you get special gadget, like grappling arrow... surely you'll be able to shoot it to the nearest objects and zip through the world like this, right? Nope. You can only do it at specific targets, for environmental puzzles sake.And the world... it's gorgeously designed and should be fun to explore. Well, ok, it's still fun to explore, just much less than I expected. It seems like there's no real reason to explore it outside the story missions. Such a wasted opportunity.Don't get me wrong, I'm still enjoying the game for what it is (I'm nearing the end), it's just too bad devs didn't do more polishing of gameplay mechanics. With some tweaks (smoother combat, faster running, less latency between actions), it could become a real gem.As it is: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: #Blud is an awesome game, with some flaws. The story is cool and the artwork is top-notch. However, as an achievement hunter, the game is quite a nightmare and the combat might benefit from some tweaking.  20h 3/10 1 Not yet a full guide, but  list a lot of the information needed. No YES, a lot of achievements are missable No No No No No No difficulty option No#BLUD is awesome. The artwork and humor are great and remind me so much of the old cartoons like Dexter and The Power Puff Girls. I did enjoy the story a lot. You play as this young girl who just moved and this is your first day at school. However, you're not a normal girl and this little town isn't a normal town...  I found it nice how you being new fitted the gameplay where you at first also don't know your way around. For me, the highlight of this game is how different the boss fights are. In some, you'll walk and dodge around and hit the boss with your hockey stick, but in others, you are on vehicles and fight them in a different way. Sometimes it took a bit of trial and error to figure out how to damage a boss. Most of the time when I struggled at the start was in fights where you couldn't use brute force, but had to defend for a little to create an opening to attack. That is all on me, I'm more the kind of girl who keeps attacking in games and doesn't defend. Sadly combat is one of the more raw edges of #Blud. It felt clumsy and challenging, but not in the way that you expect. Your roll doesn't have any invisibility frames, so you can still get hit when rolling away. Also during your finisher move you can still get hit, as the enemies will keep going while you show off an awesome move for a second or so. Maybe even harder is that when you get hit your character is stunned for a second or so, but again the enemies still can hit you.. that means that if you're surrounded by enemies there is a high chance that they keep hitting you while you don't have a way out. I got better in combat just by playing more and getting used to it, but this takes some time to get adjusted to. I did enjoy how the different enemies need different attacks to get killed, but that can also be overly complicated when dealing with different enemies at the same time. And let's not talk about the last phase of the last boss, that was so frustrating that I almost quit, but I didn't want to give up at the end. I want to highlight how important it is to start looking for the health upgrades as soon as you can because the combat is so challenging that you won't stay at 5 hearts if you don't have to and I think that the later bosses are a real nightmare if you don't get those health upgrades. Check out the topic linked above to know where to find them. About the achievements in #BLUD, I don't think I recommend hunting them down at all. I expected missable achievements when starting this game on the release day, but there were no guides yet.  There are achievements for taking a photo of every person but also every enemy. So I started with the first hour not going to my objective but trying to find everybody in all the other locations in the hopes of not missing out on somebody but in the end, I still did miss out on people. This first hour was boring because you don't interact with the story at all this way and you get too much of the same humor all at once which makes it less funny also. so I don't recommend doing this at all. And while I did do my best to get everything, there were so many achievements I still missed some things in the end without a way to still get them. So in order to get all the achievements, you really have to work with checklists or a guide that tells you step by step what to do and in which way to not miss out on a single item, which sucks out all the fun of playing a game. So just don't try to complete #BLUD and maybe only try to go for them in a second playthrough if you really did enjoy the game. I give #BLUD 3 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game for the most part but I would not recommend it to anyone.ProsWitty dialogue and silly jokes that kept me entertainedDiverse cast of entertaining characters Hand drawn animation on par with the likes of cup headEnjoyable vampire hunter story in the vain of Buffy the vampire slayer, though it is a pretty simple premiseAtmospheric soundtrack that through the use of selfies.ConsThe throwing pencils which act as stakes in the game are difficult to aim and sometimes would not throw when I needed them to.The umbrella shield upgrade for your weapon would often block in a different direction from where I was aiming.The cherry bomb’s have a tiny blast radius making them kind of useless for clearing mobs unless you can get them all tightly bunched togetherEnemies have inconsistent contact damage as sometimes you may roll into an enemy and lose health but other times you could make contact and nothing happens.There is no dedicated sprint/run button so the only way of getting around quickly is spamming the dodge roll.There are no  invincibility frames for when you dodge and when you take damage the game gives you no chance to recover as you can be repeatedly hit until you die.The chain upgrade for your weapon proves to be just about completely useless in combat and only hits things about 50% of the time.There is no way of canceling out of throwing a cherry bomb that I know of.It’s hard to know how close you can stand next to the edge of a platform because you’ll often fall off without being close enough to the edge.You can still be hit while the game is making you interact with something like picking up an object.Enemies still wait for you when you come back through a door and can attack you just as you are coming enemies in general being the barbed hatchlings that hits you instantly with tracking that is only effectively countered by blocking.The two most annoying bosses in the game were the demonic goat and _childDocuments_.review: An incredible artstyle and interesting concept overall brought down by irritating combat, tedious backtracking and tiresome quest designing.As was said in another review, to paraphrase: "A game with a great artstyle and animation but with bad gameplay is a bad game. There is no excuse".I will try to go through and list the pros and cons part by part to give you the best idea I can.PROS:- Artstyle and animation clearly has time and effort and love put into it (however I imagine due to this, attention was neglected on the actual game design itself).- A few of the puzzles past the halfway point of the game did have me enjoying small brainteasers and item usage.- The bosses, at least, most of them, have good designs and mostly feel fair (as for the bad ones, I will get to that shortly).- Dialogue and characters are mostly charming and I found myself chuckling on a few occasions. - The Hockey Stick powerups you acquire later on in the game do help with exploration and combat (mostly). It would have been nice to see this better explored than what we had.CONS:- Enemy design is frustrating. Some of the more dangerous ones have NO windup animations to provide the player a fair window to avoid damage, so you are forced to make a guesstimate on when to duck away to MAYBE avoid taking damage and then thus hit the enemy. -You are offered no invincibility frames when rolling, which can leave you open for other enemy attacks.-Player's attack animations and 'execution' animations also leave the player open for more damage.-Most of the quests are, sadly, the ever-present "Fetch Quests" which offer no enjoyment nor new environment exploration and serves as needless busywork. What makes this all the more negative is the game itself -- through a character interaction -- acknowledges this issue, which offers no humor or excuses.-A few of the bosses (Namely the final boss, which I will get to next) are simply irritating to fight against since they too lack proper wind up animations to give the player a chance to avoid damage. Particularly one of the late game bosses, Dragur's Second Lieutenant, has a second phase that completely lacks proper attack windows and I found myself dying there frequently.SPOILER ENDGAME REVIEWS:I Do want to preface this part saying I cannot recall all of the spoilers nor do I wish to attempt to recall them. This game has drained me enough.-The final boss against Dragur is an utter slog. Near instant attacks with little to no tell. A gauntlet of enemies you have to run through or risk taking even more damage before reaching him again. If you die at ANY point during this fight, you must do it all over again. What's worse is this is an exact repeat of an earlier match against Dragur in an earlier chapter (minus the gauntlet and endgame cutscenes).-The story's end cutscenes and wrap up feel oddly rushed. Again I apologize for not trying to recount more of  this particular part, however I do not wish to spend more energy than I already have.It's just not worth it at full price. I recommend you spend your money on another game or wait for this to go on a good discount if you truly find yourself curious.

_childDocuments_.review: God does it hurt to give this game a negative review.It goes without saying that the art of the game just oozes with charm and love. For the first 2 hours of the game I quickly noticed that the gameplay wasn't anything amazing and a little clunky, the music was so forgettable that I didn't even notice that there was music until a friend pointed it out, the dialouge is servicable but I didn't mind all those things too much because the first rat boss and the overall charm of the game would have been easily enough to still make it a fun time...and then I got to that stupid goat. Honestly after only 4 attempts I just closed the game and knew that I am not gonna touch it until some serious fixes are done.For starters: the combat overall feels a bit clunky mostly due to how long you get locked into an animation especially during a finisher move that as far as I am aware you have no control over and just triggers when you attack a low health enemy. You can't even pause your combo to avoid it or anything so you sometimes will be aiming for one enemy to get a few hits in and dodge out only for a literal germlin to run in, triggering your big smack finisher and holding you in place as you just have to watch a snot ball from a fly come towards you, unable to dodge out or anything. It just breaks the flow so much and sometimes makes it feel out of your control if you get hit or not when fighting groups of fodder enemies.The reason why the goat boss in particular made me give up almost instantly tho was the fact that while the order of his attacks are fixed, the transitions between attacks are near instantly without any time to actually react. you just need to know where the hitboxes will just spawn resulting in a ton of cheap and frustrating hits. This is already bad but would be bearable if it wasn't for the real AIDS that is "Getting stuck in hitboxes". So on my first fight I got absolutely folded by the goat due to just taking a few normal hits due to not knowing the attacks yet which is fine while also basically passively taking damage whenever a new phase started thanks to the instant hitboxes mentioned before... but on my second try I got about half way through without taking any damage. I was actually feeling pretty confident until boom next phase starts, I get hit by one  of the limbs, try to dodge out but since dodging sends you forward in a straight line witout any way to cancel or shorten the length of the roll I just ended up inside the next body part/lingering hitbox, literally going from full health to half a heart and dying shortly after as I finally manage to roll out of the hitbox directly into a attack.I was already baffled at that point but thought it was just a bug or bad luck but pretty much the same thing happend in the next 2 runs. First few phases go by just fine with either not getting hit at all or taking a cheap shot during a transition and then boom just in the wrong place as the next phase starts without any tell or warning and just getting all health drained as a result of one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hit.Its not even that the fight is too hard. I am certain that I could probably beat it in less than 10 minutes if I simply memorized where the hitboxes will be showing up during the phase transitions but I really just... did not want to after that. This was just the second boss and if this would be the trend going forward I rather just play something else until they clean up the combat. I don't know HOW something this just bad of a game design ended up in such a visually well designed game. How does something like this not come up in playtesting. Don't get me wrong I don't want to sound like some entitled idiot who says "Revamp the combat" like thats an easy thing to do. I wouldn't mind the flawed combat that much but holy moly at least add a pushforce or something that moves you away from the hitbox   or extend the invincibility kinda like in cuphead where you get a moment to reset after getting hit. If that makes the game too easy just lower the health or only have it apply to bossfights but as it is right now, the fact that I just said "yea no this isn't worth it" after only 4 tries just kinda says it all. Again it doesn't even feel like its hard... just insanely clunky and nearly broken at times.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't help but notice how much this game resembles classic cartoons like Billy & Mandy, Dexters Laboratory, and My Teenage Robot Life, with all of their graphic styles and comedy elements. I feel like that is what initially drew me into sitting down and playing through it to see what it's all about before ultimately just having to put it down out of frustration.Combat is tedious and clunky. You have little control over your character after a combo because you're kind of just stuck there for a moment even if you try to dodge, especially while avoiding, because you're hit automatically if you finish the roll near a Vampyr or insect due to the lack of invincibility frames and how quickly they strike as many others have stated. Not that it's difficult or anything it's just this one singular feature makes it frustrating because you can't avoid damage due to it. It's just annoying when you know you shouldn't have received damage but did anyway because of the lack of polish there.You'll be moving around doing task through social media, connecting with selfies for said social media, which can include you in specific quests, while also acting like your own personal journal rather than an actual log of your quests, giving it a unique vibe compared to most every other game. There is a lot of discussion between characters, a few fetch quests, and interesting monsters, fun mini-games and stories but it all falls apart since you can't dodge effectively ruining the fundamental game play. A simple look into making it more responsive to what we all want would greatly improve it. The game is humorous, witty, and generally interesting because of how it looks and how it expresses a lot of emotion, but it is quite annoying. I also got a little headache from listening to the same looping songs playing in specified locations like school and so on because they weren't very catchy and were overly irritating to listen to for extended periods of time.Fix the dodge issue for combat, then I could suggest it for sure, but as of right now. Anything to be able to use them more often.-The shovel digging animation is a bit slow. Currently, spamming dodge rolls is the only way to go a bit faster, so you spend your time rolling through Carpentersville which looks a bit silly and feels a bit exploity. _childDocuments_.review: Before we begin, I want to address something first. When I first saw the trailer for #BLUD, I was really excited for this game, and I was impatient to wait for this game to come out because the trailers looked really promising. When the game finally released and I checked the reviews on Steam, I saw the “Recent Reviews” go from “Mostly Positive” to “Mixed,” which had me worried. So, now that I got the game on sale and played till completing the campaign, I want to give my own thoughts. So, hopefully this review doesn’t come across as me blindly praising this game.Presentation	Starting off, this game looks GORGEOUS. The reason I say gorgeous is solely because of the smooth, snappy, and whacky animation, which makes sense since the game’s developer, Exit 73 Studios, is very skilled in animation, as evidenced by their YouTube channel. Now I could provide a link to their channel if I could, but I would risk this review being taken down by VALVe/Steam. So, please go type “Exit 73 Studios” into the YouTube search bar and go check out their YouTube channel. They have some really fun and inspiring animations. Also, I really appreciate the choice to use phone garbles instead of voice-acting. Not only is Becky herself animated nicely, but so are the non-playable characters and even Becky’s HUD icon. THAT’S how much you know was put into making this game look awesome. Going off topic here, from what I watched on one of E73S’s YouTube shorts, and from what I could understand, #BLUD was meant to be a pitch for T.V. but sadly never got picked up. Honestly, that sounds really awesome. I mean, now that I’m an adult, I would have loved to see #BLUD as a T.V. or even web series since I am now getting into the “Horror” genre with games like TCoAnL and DDLC. Before I end this section I want to say that this game not only reminds me of old-school CN and Boomerang, but also classic Nick shows like SpongeBob Seasons 1-3, Rugrats, and even the pilot episodes of The Fairly Oddparents. Also, Becky’s front teeth somewhat remind me of Timmy Turner. Also, no, I do not want to talk about You Know Who.Presentation: 10/10Gameplay	The gameplay in this game is kind of... weird. Sure it has flaws, but I didn’t find the combat to be too frustrating at least until the final boss where you face 3-4 boss phases and make your way through an enemy gauntlet. The combat is not awful in my opinion but one issue I found with it is that you could get stuck in the finisher animation for a couple of seconds before you can dodge out of the way. Also, PLEASE do what Corey says and abuse the dodge-attack combo as that will finish the unguardable enemies off in an instant. Although the big vampyres will take two of the dodge-attacks. Not only will you be fighting enemies on your journey, but you will also take selfies with them including the background character. Becky’s selfie animations are funny to watch. Also, doesn’t Perch remind you of Twitter? Yes, I’m still calling it Twitter, not X.However, aside from the main campaign, you also have the option to do side quests. I was pretty mixed on these. They sometimes ranged from fun to cryptic. For example, I had to collect like four, five, or six flamingos for the goth group in the mall. The reason I was able to collect them was by walking out of the mall and buying the extra one (although that might be a bug or something). There are some upgrades you can find for your hockey stick but for the majority of my playthrough, I didn’t bother finding them and just focused on getting an extra heart to get through the game without too much trouble. BTW, to get health back, you will need to pick up energy bars, soda cans, and even use the first aid kits in your inventory. Also, you can throw No. 2 Pencils at enemies and use cherry bombs to burn enemies to a crisp.There are other gameplay scenarios though. In the school bus section, Corey takes control of the bus and Becky is tasked with throwing cherry bombs at the boss while their guard is down. When you face the main antagonist in the graveyard, there is a QTE section which I feel doesn’t really have a place in the game. Yes, you could argue that #BLUD is poking fun at QTEs being the norm in the gaming industry, but this could catch players off guard and turn them off. I mean I was caught off guard when I first played this. Also, get this you get to play Robot Punch-Out!! with Corey! My goodness this game has variety! Overall, the gameplay, while not perfect, I believe has some potential if given the proper updates and content it deserves. In my opinion, I believe this is a framework but in a good way.Gameplay: 7/10Performance	Now unless my memory is wrong, the Steam page for this game said this game was playable on the Steam Deck. However, right now, #BLUD is Steam Deck verified. When I played it on the Steam Deck, the performance was amazing. No framerate drops whatsoever. If you have a computer that works like a dream, feel free to test this game out if it interests you.Performance: 10/10Story	Now I thought about taking the story out of this review, but I decided not to. The story of this game is mainly conveyed through animations, garbled speeches, and sound effects. Personally, I really like this approach. It reminds me of the phrase, “Show, don’t Tell.” However, one issue I had with the story is its pacing. However, that issue is so minimal that I am not going to give this section too much flak over. The story is light-hearted and has some funny moments, but also has some heartful and dark moments. That I respect. I know this is unrelated to the topic, but it reminds me of what Always Nerdy on YouTube said in his Sam Raimi’s Spider-Man 2 Video Game Retrospective. He said Peter Parker doesn’t have to quit being himself or Spider-Man; he needs to find the right balance. That to me sounds really inspiring whenever I am learning to make my own projects. To me, a story doesn’t have to be strictly for kids, or dark, serious, and sad; we need to find a way to balance these two aspects. I’m reminded of my favorite show Avatar: The Last Airbender, which balanced both light-hearted and heartfelt moments in its story. Sorry for that tangent, let’s end this review now before I start rambling.Story: 9/10Final Verdict	I really enjoyed my time with #BLUD. I would even go so far as to say that it’s now one of my favorite indie games to look back on. Now I did mention that this game has some bugs that need to be ironed out, but I want to address this. Exit 73, if you happen to come across this review by any chance, I want you to know that you are now one of my inspirations for animation, right next to Studio MDHR. You guys are the reason why I love animation in video games and why I love doing art and animation in the first place. However, I feel like this game is a framework for what is a good game in my eyes. I have faith that you guys have the potential to do something amazing. I would even love for #BLUD to be its own series on YouTube. If it doesn’t then I’m okay with that, I’d much rather have a series have its legacy unharmed than milked dry. So, thank you all for reading and stay safe out there guys.Verdict: 36/40

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for a while now, and I think I may have over hyped it  a bit in my mind.like most people have said, this game is a visual gourmet feast for the eyes. Some animations don't seem finished and or are choppy. your item pick up animation is so long that enemy's can just walk up and hit you during it. That being said I do want to stress this game IS fun and if it's art style is at all appealing to you then please play it, you wont regret it. _childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, it's just not a great game. Pros:- Visually the game is a FEAST. They absolutely killed the mid 2000s Cartoon Network look, I love it. The cutscenes feel like a genuine reward for progression and was honestly the main driving force for me to continue.- While there is a LOT of dialogue, it's actually pretty funny. There was plenty of times throughout the game where the game gave me a genuine chuckle, and I grew to appreciate a good chunk of the characters (namely Kristofferson and Becky).- The boss fights spice the monotony of combat in a refreshing way. Outside of the animation, the boss fights were definitely the highlight of this game for me. Most of them anyway (the goat and the final boss needed some work.)- Not a super long game. Some may see this as a con considering the price tag, but I don't feel like I wasted my money. Cons:-The combat is VERY wonky. This is my major complaint of the game, and if you're only getting the game for the combat you will be left wanting.  The hitboxes on both your and the enemies moves are not consistent in the slightest. The game teaches you about a roll attack early on that I stopped using in the first third of the game because the hitbox felt nonexistent and I ended up taking more damage than I could dish out. Also major criticism, the roll not having any invincibility frames whatsoever absolutely KILLS the combat for this game. It turns a lot of what should be easy encounters into frustrating slogs where you're taking damage for no reason and you're afraid of taking any risks outside of just mashing your normal attack. Your finishers also don't have invincibility so you'll do a super long killing animation while the other enemies swarm you and attack you and you can't do anything to stop it. This also applies to picking up items for some reason? You do an animation every time you pick up an item but you can still be hit, making you take unnecessary damage when they play pencils or keys or what have you in combat areas. A little invincibility would go a long way for this game.-Final fight was a huge let down. It was just a copy and paste of a previous encounter but now you're running through a hallway filled with enemies in between the fight itself. The cutscenes were sick as hell though.-There's no run button, so if you're trying to get around an area as fast as possible you just have to mash your roll button which doesn't feel great. The different areas also feel really large so exploring for any secrets or fetch quests can admittedly get tiring of frustrating.-Wasn't a huge fan of some of the crystal puzzles. They usually give you a clue in the locale but some of the clues just didn't apply to the corresponding puzzles, so I was just left guessing. This is likely more of a skill issue on my part though.Minor things:- Little bit of pop-in with props (mostly trees) as you're exploring. Minor nitpick but it's just something I noticed while exploring.- Music is just fine.- Whoever thought of having title cards for every chapter was a genius.-Few softlocks here and there (mostly attributed to the clamper bots in Perch HQ).If you're considering the game for the presentation, get it, maybe considering getting it on sale but definitely get it they did NOT disappoint. If you're considering it for the gameplay, you might want to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an intense mixed bagPros- the aesthetic and writing are great, more than enough to buoy a game-Characters directly related to the plot are all engaging and unique, even if we spend way to little time with them Cons- Combat is finicky, hitboxes are wonky in general both in combat and in puzzles -the game feels ... cut down? I've read this was meant to be an animated series before pivoting to a game and that makes a lot of sense with how choppy and rushed the pacing is, with several plot points and character beats (Becky playing field hocky, her training with Kristopherson, Becky quitting vampire hunting) Extremely rushed.- Side Quests you just kinda have to talk to everyone, theres not really any indication of where your supposed to go to do several of them -Several out of the box mechanics ( a certain late game boss fight comes to mind) your just thrown into with no controls or explinaiton-The dodge roll is near entirely useless, and several boss attacks are almost undodgeable unless you already know from previous attempts they are comingNow, this appears to be the Studio's first game, and as a first game its not a bad effort. I really hope this game does well enough to justify more because there are a lot of good ideas in the world and story, and most of these issues are those that will be ironed out with experience, but this will be a rough time for some

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Looking GameVisually Stunning, Character Designs are Neat and the Writing is Superb.Gameplay is Decent at BestThe Overall Experience does not Disappoint but I do however want to share my nitpicks when it comes to how the game functioned and my Critiques of what should be fixed and polished.For Gameplay I do feel the combat could be fleshed out more, I've put in almost 5 hours of playtime and so far while it isn't an overall bad thing. I do think it can more in depth and interesting rather than just it being the same animations. I could be wrong. but that's going in within most of my time playing it.The dodging mechanic needs to be addressed somehow. My suggestion is to add in a counter button whenever an enemy is close to hitting you. However, when I dodge away from an enemy or a boss's hitbox. it registers me being hit and I don't have a quick enough response. So in a way it felt unfair dying so easily when it isn't the players fault.Also implementing a Sprint Button would help alot since Becky is VERY slow. the way out of it is by rolling but can be tedious.For controller, I don't know if anyone has had this issue. but for me when I first tried to play it on an Xbox Controller. The input has a terrible delay. and always goes down for some reason. Hopefully this will be patched in. Which is why I went ahead and played on Keyboard and Mouse.While I never encountered many bugs during my playthrough, whenever I rolled through an opening gap on the ground moments before the animation frames went back to being opened it somehow counted as me falling down.And last but not least, while I believe many will find this to be a silly thing to point out. But it would be nice if in the near future there will be voice acting added on. While I don't mind the sound bytes used for when characters are talking and interacting with each other. It would be more lively to have characters actually speak than just sound effects in place.With that being said, this is still a great game and I am having a fun time with it. The wait did not let me down despite what I've said here in my review. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great looking game, decently funny with a lot of personality... but horribly rough and untested gameplay.All the bosses have several phases and do NOT drop you back into whatever phase you got to on death, and healthkits are EXTREMELY limited, so you end up either having to do them perfectly... With no warning as to what attack is coming next, what add they're going to spawn, where they're going to spawn it, nor what to actually do to defeat said bosses. Yes. Trial and Error and bs attacks, in the year 2024. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.This extends out into the normal combat, where enemies WILL do attacks within .1 second if you happen to be in the wrong position or get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ by how THEY're positioned, which wouldn't be a problem if the enemies weren't spammed and didn't each require a specific gimmick to defeat, but, here we are. Three instaattacking umbrella-guardables right next to eachother and they attack so fast with enough delays on each that you HAVE to take damage to damage them back. Yippie. That, or the flies are put offscreen so that when you walk down, you get instantly hit with no warning, or several enemies requiring different gimmicks are put right next to eachother or close enough together that you have to hotswap in order to defeat them, but the .1 second attacks mean you will ALWAYS take damage... Did I mention that they do contact damage too, and that rolling into them can stunlock you, especially with hordes? What's hilarious is that the thing you get taught at the start of the game, the roll-attack, is literally never usable, either because the area is small (which is almost always), or there's enough other enemies around that trying to would just get you contact-damaged multiple times unnecessarially.That's not all, though. A lot of the zelda-esque puzzles are *fine*, but this dev is cruel and evil, and spawns enemies with ranged attacks directly in your path while you're trying to do timing puzzles that REALLY demand you do them near-perfectly to progress.If all that's not enough, there's a 4-phase boss in the forest that you have to do all in one with about 1 or no medkits, the first two phases are fine, very rng, but the third and fourth take place in a TINY space with slam attacks happening at random in random configurations with random spawns, one of which you need to hookshot for the fourth phase, but if you're standing in the center, you get stunlocked by a laser and comboed by one of the slams. Do you get it now?

_childDocuments_.review: Pros*Amazing animation*Really great writing even if a bit cliche at times*Enemy design is really unique and makes each one different from the others. Good amount too!*Most if not all the music is fantastic*Cool fast travel system*Charming atmosphere, characters and world in general*The whole selfie and in game social media system is fun!*At times combat feels really fast and fluidCons*Very awkward hitboxes on just about everything*Some puzzles are very tedious*Takes forever to move from point A to point B*Upgrades aside from main story one's are a bit pointless*Lots of instances where there felt like missing sound effects even if it might have been intentional*Most bosses are good but can suffer from bad telegraphing or awkward ways to hit them*Awkward timing for dialogue, coming out of cutscenes, some of the cutscenes themselves, certain animations playing*Very easy to do side quest or selfie actions out of order than the game was expecting leading to weird interactions*The game is a good length but the characters and the world don't get enough time to shine*Lack of direction as to where to go next in many areas*Major lag in some bigger areas when playing in full screen mode*Decent number of minor bugs*Why does every enemy still do contact damage even if they're stunned?To me this felt like a passion project from people with a lot of animation and writing experience but not a ton of experience with games. _childDocuments_.review: #BLUD FOR THE BLUD GODAfter my first stream here's what I have to say:  Blud is an absolute visual delight, the characters are sweet, funny, and everything looks so good.  The story is corny but by design, v saturday morning cartoon or 'D&D in highschool'.  The combat is pretty solid as well but can feel very floaty.I only have a few 'complaints' and these are more just things that are standard in the genre for a reason that seem to have been left out.First is enemies lack wind up.  As in very *very* few enemy attacks have any wind up or delay to animation interaction.  Which makes them each a single frame interaction to avoid.  The only creatures with wind up are some boss stuff and the flies of all things.  Even those the animations while very pretty lack some clarity, sometimes.Two dodge roll is... not a dodge roll.  As in there's not a single iframe on it, coupled with enemies lacking wind up if you're used to dodging into or around enemy attack ranges to bait attacks you *will* take hits, because you'll dodge into range, the enemy attack will trigger and you'll be knocked out of your animation, stopping your dodge and getting hurt.Speaking of animations, there is animation cancelling!For the enemies.As in a portion of enemy animations you would think are made to give windows for approaching, will be cancelled into attacks if you reach attack range.  Whereas you, the player, lack animation cancelling through the move roll (because remember it's not a dodge) or through attacks.  This isn't a huge issue except in two circumstances.  Dodge attacks, where it's actually fine as that's the commitment you make when choosing to do that, and Finishers.  Finishers wouldn't be an issue, if it was a choice of your own but it's not.  I haven't checked to see if you can disable an upgrade yet, if I can I will be disabling finishers, because the nearly two second hang time after a finisher, which triggers on all but the first attack in a chain if that attack would normally kill a mob, often results in other enemies in crowded encounters walking up and just wacking you.Though the finisher is crazy powerful as it seems to one shot anything it hits and is a larger range attack then the basic combo attacks.  When you can use it really well you can kill dangerous enemies by using finishers on smaller enemies that catch the big one.  Very nice.Altogether if you like the art style and don't mind taking a few hits that feel... irritating, it is an exceptionally fun game in it's genre and definitely worth playing if you're a fan of these.  It's genuinely very good minus the issues I explain above, and those are easily problems that can be played around if you go in aware of them, or do as I did and learn to work around them.  Absolutely recommend giving it a shot if you've go the money and like the art.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so disclaimer, I have not finished the game. But I have some things to say, especially seeing as i am stuck on the goat boss. ngl, despite the games many flaws i am enjoying it so far, even so i cannot recommend it to anyone, at least until they fix some of the glaring issues with it. Weird hitboxes, no I-frames when you get hit, the goat boss itself is has this in spades. Not to mention the lack of space, meaning that you can easily take multiple hits in a matter of seconds. While rolling under the bosses weird intestine wall things, your roll can get you stuck underneath them and since every part of the boss gives you contact damage, for some odd reason, you will be completely punished if your roll sends you just a bit too far.outside of that boss, you have enemies that can attack you mid pause and selfie animation, either make it so that doesn't happen, or give the player I-frames so that you can't get hit every single time you want to take a picture of an enemy. especially since some of them are faster than you. _childDocuments_.review: Only a short ways into the game and loving most of it so far! I’m gonna recommend this game, but I do feel there are some small changes that I think it could really do with. Slight spoilers ahead:The dodge roll doesn’t feel great to use. It kills your momentum and makes it feel like I’m having to somewhat fight the dodge as much as the enemies on screen. Not every game needs i-frames, but the lack of them here feels kind of bad. During the goat boss fight in particular you have to dodge under its (tentacles? Tendrils?) but if you hit a goat head you’ll take damage, stop in your tracks, then have to wait a split second before you can move again, but since you were stopped right where it’s tendrils are you take damage again before being able to get out of the way. Then if it’s not the goat heads you ran into it’s that you started your dodge a little too far away, and you take damage from your dodge ending right where an arm is. _childDocuments_.review: A charming game with great writing and solid gameplay, it's really going to boil down to how much you enjoy the overall gimmick.  If you would even remotely enjoy the setup, there's no excuse to miss this.The elephant in the room is that it's a surprisingly challenging game.  Not mindlessly punishing, but anyone expecting a cakewalk will be in for a rude awakening.  Combat rewards patience, as enemies punish reckless behavior.  Enemies have their different patterns and forms, and you just have to experiment to see what works.  And it doesn't help you don't get the ability to block immediately, nor any weapons, but if you're willing to work through the first couple of chapters, things ease up.  Puzzles are surprisingly cheeky and clever, but I can see how some could be stuck if they missed a detail.  When not in a dungeon, it's an open world, and there are plenty of side quests and hidden goodies to get.  Not terribly punished for not exploring, but definitely rewarded if you do.  The overall gameplay is enjoyable, but it's not the strong point of this game.  There are some bugs, but nothing game breaking (at least on PC), but it will lead to a few unfair deaths.The artwork and writing is what shines, though.  The animation is fun, the art style adorable, the characters are written well, and the dialogue is smart, believable, surprisingly mature, and consistently funny.  There's a lot of inspiration and references, but it's clearly doing its own thing.  It has its own flow and its own vibe, and if you click with it, it sucks you in.  This will be the reason why you'll keep coming back to finish this game.It's a charming romp that takes inspiration from various things, though ultimately being its own thing.  A good game overall, just be a little patient and you'll avoid most of the frustrations.

_childDocuments_.review: What I Love: First and foremost, the game is beautifully animated. Seriously, it's like Cuphead quality. I also found the writing to be pretty funny. I also found the story to be pretty strong, if a bit cliche. If anyone's looking for a classic Zelda-like game, I would strongly recommend it.However, I would be remiss to not mention the few issues I have with the game:- Lack of a chapter select/ a notable amount of permanently missable content. For example, I didn't do the Eraser-collecting story when it came up because I thought I would have another opportunity to get them, however I was wrong. Similarly, I missed taking a selfie with the mother vampire because it was cumbersome and there are only 4 opportunities in the entire game. Because the game lacks a chapter select, I am now locked out of 100% completion on my initial file, which disappoints me as a completionist.- The selfie-with-enemies mechanic is cumbersome. It's hard to pull of due to taking a while to open the camera and not being able to select which enemy to photograph. It's cute, but not worth the effort for the diminishing returns.- Most bosses lack proper telegraphs, for instance the belltower boss gives no indication it will follow one window attack by coming out of a window on the OPPOSITE side, and the final phase of the 2nd lieutenant has attacks coming from all sides with little warning. The only bosses to avoid this problem are the early ones and the Punch-Out style boss.It may seem odd that this "Recommended' review has a larger negatives section than positives, but that's because the game is overall excellent but has a few issues preventing me from fully loving it. Steam doesn't have number scores but I'd put it at a 7/10 in it's current state.

If you do all the side quests and achievement hunt you can also put a lot of time into this game. If you just do the main story I think you could beat this in a day.My only gripes are very minor ones:I've had a few bugs were scripted encounters didn't trigger or a monster didn't spawn that I needed to beat. The game saves so often you can just reload and it'll work fine. I also had one bug were an invincible rat chased me around until I left the room I was in.My only other gripe is that once you get to certain points in the game some quests aren't possible to complete. I accidentally progressed too far so all the quests I got on Day 1 weren't accessible. This is my own fault and there might have been a text box I missed warning me about this, I know there is one that warns you before the final boss. I also wish I could reload certain chapters so I could continue achievement hunting on my current save. Maybe you can and I haven't found it yet, after all I'm writing this immediately after watching the credits roll. For now, I think I'll take a break and I definitely think I'll be returning to this to replay it, which I rarely do anymore as an adult. There is also room for potential DLC or a sequel left in the game and I really hope we do get more eventually. What this game might lack in super deep game play it makes up for in charm and honestly just being a lot of good fun without any classic video game tropes bogging it down. 10/10, give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I figured I should come back to this review after doing absolutely everything the game had to offer. Every last achievement. IDK if anyone will read this but I feel like the game deserves my time to leave a review after the 20 hrs I put into it.Let's start with the positive:Genuinely, I think it's a really whimsical time. The environments are all wonderful and the major characters are very colorful and unique. Each of them gets their own individual time to mingle with Becky (the player's character) and it feels like every corner of the world you explore is filled with significant detail. The world building is glorious and I can't help but eat it up. It makes me wish that this did get greenlit to be a cartoon back then. The synth-y music also really helps the feeling of the environment, even if it can be repetitive at times. You'll have a wonderful time playing through the game's story and seeing every kooky detail it has to offer.As for the negative:Everyone's said it by this point but yes the combat can be clunky. It can be fun to fight a new type of vampire for the first time, figuring out what their weakness is and how to exploit it but doing it 100 times over can get repetitive. That being said, using pencils like miniature projectile stakes is a GENIUS IDEA. It helps they're probably the most satisfying weapon in the game to use aside from your primary attack. But when you're just trying to go from point A to point B certain vampire types can just get in the way sometimes and that can be very annoying. Which brings me to my next point, something I mentioned in the initial review: You'll want to finish the game, but not go out of your way to complete it. Do any side quests you run into, they're great, funny, and well thought-out, but you're not gonna want to go out of your way to achieve 100%. Many of the game's collectibles are locked to areas and dungeons you can only visit ONCE. They're all extremely missable if you aren't careful. You'll be pulling your hair out trying to find a collectible only to realize it's from a side quest or area you can't access anymore and you'll need to do another playthrough. Final Words:I've been following the development of this game on and off and I do really think that Exit 73 delivered a great game for 2000's cartoon and 2d zelda enjoyers alike. You shouldn't expect mind-blowing combat, but you can expect a well-written and charming story with likeable characters, interesting environments, and innovative ideas you don't normally see in this medium.I think number scores are arbitrary and shallow but if you want one I give it an 8/10.I hope that my words convince you to buy the game and support the developers so they keep making great content like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I had enough time to really sit and think about my experience with the game and overall I liked it.For starters, the visual presentation is its strongest point. You can really tell at one point it was pitched as a cartoon before turning into a game. That mid-to-late 90s cartoon feel is here in spades, it's DELIGHTFULLY animated in pretty much every way. The characters, the enemies, attacking animations, damage animations, everything is expressive and lively and the game clearly wants you to look at it (for better AND for worse which I'll get to into a bit).Sound wise this does leave a bit to be desired. The music is pretty much what I would describe as background cartoon music. You don't notice it and it's repetitive, but it's harmless. Sound effects are largely stock cartoon sounds which is very fitting with the game so no complaints there. This also leads into..."voice acting". While playing, Becky has usual attack and damage grunts and barks, but when speaking she (and every other character) speaks with those stock cartoon phone chatter effects which is amusing but might annoy some people who don't get the audio references or just plain aren't into the blabber.The story is largely fine and fairly engaging, but I can't help but feel like it was rushed in parts. There's a very interesting story bit you can uncover which goes nowhere (unless it's left on the stove for a possible sequel) and there's some events that end VERY abruptly. I do like that each chapter is presented like an episode in a cartoon complete with a title card, but the ends of the chapters don't feel like an episode ending, it's just *poof* onto the next one! It also somewhat feels like more time would be spent with the various characters but even that feels abrupt.And now the gameplay which certainly has some peaks and valleys. For the most part it plays fairly Zelda-ish. Combat is simple, you have your dungeon areas, there's a few tools you get, there's a projectile and there's bombs, there's puzzles to solve and even heart pieces to find. The troublesome part is that there is a level of jank that bothers me more times than I'd like. As I mentioned before the game loves its animations and I do too! But this results in a bunch of animation lock which can sometimes cause you to take damage when you don't want to because there isn't enough iframes after some animations where there is a window of delay before you can control Becky again. In isolated cases it's not a bad thing, if an enemy hits you and there's an elaborate animation for it there's some time before they attack again, but this isn't the case when there's multiple enemies or bosses with extra parts (or minions) that attack separately from other parts as well. This results in some annoying cases of mini stunlocks that deprives you of control for a few seconds and it can be quite aggravating. This can be bothersome on the offensive when there's a bunch of enemies as well, as once you unlock finishing attacks, you get a cool final hit on an enemy, but you're frozen while the animation plays out which can cause you to be lined up into an enemy attack immediately before you can act again.Then we have the dodge roll. The dodge roll is not good. The only purpose it serves is the fastest form of movement and to use an attack locked behind it for the few times you need it. There is NO invincibility on it which makes it seem very counter-intuitive compared to....well....every other game with a dodge roll. You're meant to treat it as a "dodge out of the way" roll rather than a "dodge through attacks" roll, which would be fine if the distance wasn't so short with a slight pause at the end. And when it comes to that attack locked behind it? Better learn how to space that thing or you'll also take another round of accidental damage!Hit and hurtboxes also have a tendency to be strange, you'll whiff attacks where you feel like you shouldn't, you'll take damage/hit a trap or hazard when you feel like you shouldn't. And sometimes there's some random bits of delay/detection.But despite the jank getting on my nerves, I had a good time for the most part, and I can certainly recommend it if the game seems appealing to you in anyway. I like what Exit 73 brought to the table here and all I could wish for is more polish and fleshing out. But maybe catch it on a sale if you're on the fence. Thumbs up.

name: Between Horizons
detailed_description: ABOUT THE GAME Between Horizons is set aboard the Zephyr, humanity's first generation ship en route to another star. You assume the role of Stella, who was born on the ship 24 years ago and recently inherited her father's post as Chief of Security. Dive into the conspiracy behind the incident that threatens to disrupt the Zephyr's social order and foil its mission. Between Horizons is a modern 2.5D pixel art adventure that brings a branching narrative into a semi-open world. The team at DigiTales has applied numerous lessons from their first game Lacuna and proven solutions to detective game design problems to maximize player agency in the investigation process – all the while maintaining the tight pacing of a meaningful story that will ask you to reevaluate your moral compass and make increasingly tough decisions as the situation aboard the ship spirals out of control. FEATURES An Unusual Adventure: Between Horizons merges investigation gameplay with a branching sci-fi story in an ever-expanding Metroidvania-style environment. Think For Yourself: The flexible evidence system lets you assign clues to cases, confront ship denizens about them, and solve any case with at any point in time. Everything you find on the ship may or may not be connected to the mystery at hand. Failure is Very Much an Option: There are no second chances — submitting a wrong solution means the story will go with all the consequences. A new and improved auto-save system will make sure there is no going back, as the story branches and ends based on your decisions. Set Your Course: Underneath the game's exciting and plausible sci-fi plot lies a number of thought-provoking problems inviting you to weigh intergenerational responsibility against personal freedom. A New Dimension: Timeless pixel art merge with 3D environments and modern visual effects to create a unique visual style.

Can you find the culprit before it's too late? Experience an enthralling story set in a semi-open world that branches and ends based on your choices.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are just interested in point and click adventures go here: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but its a nice sci-fi detective adventure. The Zephyr - a spaceship with 1,300 people on board - has been on its way to a planet many light years away for many years. The survival of the human race is at stake - things don't seem to be going so well on Earth. However, the expected arrival on the new planet is not for another three generations, which means that the current crew will never see the new planet and will have to spend their entire lives on board the ship. I hope there are enough children on board. We play Stella, the depressed daughter of the current head of security, who lies around in her cabin with her strange pet. Our job is deputy head of security... apparently on the ship, jobs are passed down in the family. Anyway, it's strange to be in such a position as a young woman in her mid-20s. We can no longer remember our mother. She has stayed behind on Earth due to health problems, but we sometimes receive messages from her - with a delay of around a year due to the distance.Soon there is a security incident on the ship and we have to solve our first case. At the core of our job, we are a detective. Our first "case" consists of looking at network logs to perhaps discover an irregularity. The second case, however, is much more complex, with several questions to solve. Who did what, when and why - the usual challenge faced by detectives and investigating authorities.On the one hand, the gameplay mainly consists of moving around the spaceship, with more and more parts becoming accessible as the game progresses. If walking is too slow for you, you can also run. For better orientation, we can call up a map at any time, on which fast travel to many rooms is also possible. On the other hand, we must always keep our eyes open and investigate hotspots. Every clue we find is automatically stored on our PDA. We can talk to other people (often with several possible answers under time pressure) or talk to them about specific clues (which are stored on our PDA). All our dialogs are also saved so that we can look at them again later at our leisure. To solve a case, we have to upload the correct clue to the police computer. This automatically closes the case, regardless of whether our investigation was right or wrong.There is no way back - neither for the Zephyr nor for us. Saving is automatic, and no manual saves can be made. The game is designed in such a way that you have to play through it, and once you have made your decisions, they are final. The only way to change your mind is to start a new game.The background graphics are quite nice, but of course not particularly eye-catching. Between Horizons is basically a side-scrolling game, but our character can also move forwards or backwards in the picture in some places. However, I would like to know what the developers had in mind when it came to the graphic design of the characters, especially Stella. Stella looks horrible up close - she is completely pixelated. The closer she is in the foreground, the more pixelated. This is an extreme contrast to the background graphics and a complete break in style. What is a pixelated player character doing in a game with high-resolution background graphics?The game can be controlled entirely with the keyboard, but it plays really well with the gamepad. Voice output is very limited. Instructions, descriptions or conversations are not voiced. At certain points in the game, however, we can hear Stella's inner monologue. Saves are stored in the cloud. The plot is branched, which can be a motivation to play through the game several times.Typical narrative adventure game - we talk to other people, investigate things and explore the surroundings. The special feature is the detective work - we have to use our brains to uncover connections in order to solve a threatening situation on board a spaceship in the depths of space. The story continues in any case, even if you are as stupid as Louis de Funès in "The Gendarme of St. Tropez" - but the end of the story may not be a happy ending. All in all, a great indie adventure game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game.  I think few minor UI tweaks would make this game very good, but those missing pieces let it down. The puzzles are hard but do-able!The bad: these will sound like nitpicks and they /are/, which is why it's so sad they let this game down so far.- You have many conversation options that change the course of the game permanently, which is great.  The problem is if you're clicking through the dialogue to read it, you just... click the first dialogue option.  Every time.  You don't get warning when you're about to make a dialogue choice, so you either plod through all dialogue or skip most choices.  I made exactly two dialogue choices on my playthrough: I drew my gun on the intruder in my room and I demanded the Captain tell me what was going on. Every other dialogue choice (including vote/decide etc) I made by accidental clicking.  : apparently the end options are meant to be influenced by your earlier choices?  I think this needs more telegraphing too, like a voiceover saying "Should I call a vote?  I thought back to the mob in the cafeteria [flashback].  No, this was no time to let an angry population choose its own destiny."- The eventual reveal was kind of confusing .  It needed more telegraphing that the things that were going wrong weren't coherent.- the  didn't really make much sense to me.  The entire , absolutely you would interrupt .  It you want stakes, ?What could be better:- Dialogue choices _need_ to be default-highlighted onto an unclickable button with text like like "You must choose" so you can't accidentally click through all of the choices.  - Warp straight to location.  The train stations are a nice idea but running up and down steps to L3C and R2D got old.- The ability to type in names to search your ID cards, and their usual locations e.g. home, workplace, favourite activity be highlighted on the map.  I picked Erik for one case because I couldn't _find_ Erik anywhere.- More interaction with the two main characters.- I would like to give the bonsai to the lady who likes bonsai.  Stella is not going to take care of it.The weird:- In the end section of the game, I asked the Navigator about his argument with the Captain and he brushed me off.  I have no idea who I was supposed to talk to here. _childDocuments_.review: # I have never seen a game hampered so much by such a small decision.I like this game. I should love it. It is exactly my cup of tea genre-wise, and the writing and art are excellent. Most of the mechanics and controls are great. There is just one tiny exception. Whenever you interact with a clue, it goes straight into the "evidence" section of your PDA. You never look at the object directly. There's just a little pop-up at the top of the screen: "Evidence Collected: Strange Letter" or whatever. Then if you want to read the letter—and of course you do!—you have to open your PDA, tab over to "Evidence," and manually select the new item.It's a bit frustrating. More importantly, it's immersion-breaking. It doesn't feel like you're actually examining your surroundings to figure out what happened. It feels like you're collecting Clue Points and once you get enough Clue Points you can progress in the game.That's a shame, because everything else about the game is really excellent so far.

_childDocuments_.review: The dim glow of the computer screen illuminated the otherwise dark room as I delved into the depths of the virtual world of Between Horizons. A creation of the clever minds at DigiTales Interactive, this game was not for the faint of heart.In this digital labyrinth, I took on the role of security chief Stella, a character tasked with unraveling the secrets aboard the colony ship Zephyr after its arduous 33-year journey through the vastness of space. The echoes of classic detective stories echoed in the pixelated corridors, reminiscent of “Murder on the Mississippi” from years past.But make no mistake, dear reader, for this was no easy walk through the annals of mystery. No, it was a labyrinthine puzzle, a puzzle wrapped in a puzzle. The first steps were deceptively simple, the introduction gentle and the hints sparse. But with every moment the web of possibilities expanded, threatening to captivate the unwary.The initially sparse collection of clues turned out to be the linchpin of the investigation. Every bit of information is carefully preserved and ready to be used in interrogation. But as the list of questions lengthened, so did the complexity of the task at hand. The pool of suspects, once small and manageable, grew into a cacophony of voices, each whispering half-truths and hidden agendas.Amid this tangled web there was confusion. Missteps once made can spell disaster. The consequences of erroneous conclusions affected the entire ship and were reflected in damaged ships and damaged systems. Explosives ravaged the ship and saboteurs lurked in the shadows, their nefarious deeds leaving a trail of chaos in their wake.Despite the danger of the journey, however, the challenge had an undeniable appeal. For those who enjoy the thrill of the hunt and appreciate the intricacies of deduction, Between Horizons offers a tantalizing prospect. A realm where every decision had weight and every conclusion had consequences.In conclusion, dear reader, Between Horizons is a testament to the artistry of the detective genre. A realm where the line between truth and deception is blurred and where the intrepid explorer must navigate with caution. So if you dare to go where others fail, if you crave the thrill of the hunt, then you are entering the unknown. But be careful, because in this world of shadows and deception, not everything is as it seems.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no game I like better than a good investigation game, and  is a damn near perfect example of what the form is capable of.  I'll try to be brief.Most importantly, the investigations themselves are  thoughtfully balanced.  Most of the 10 cases start wide open, overwhelming you with too many possibilities; then as you gather clues one by one, suspects are eliminated until you are left with just a few likely alternatives.  At that point you  need to pay attention and review your evidence carefully.  Sometimes damning evidence will clearly point to a single person, but usually you have to get as close as you can.  Also, not all cases are about apprehending a suspect; some require you to figure out where something is hidden, what time something took place, or other variations, which gives a nice variety.More than once, I ended a play session completely stumped, slept on it, and came back the next day with a fresh perspective that helped me intuit a new line of investigation.Despite dialogue about how the characters are in a big hurry to solve everything, there are no timers and you can take as long as you like to read and reread your dialogue history, review your evidence, and explore the map looking for one more clue you might have missed, before submitting your solution.Some of the cases are .  I felt good about my answers to most of them but was really not sure about a lot of my answers, even after being doggedly persistent in trying to uncover every clue.  I guarantee this game will stretch your brain if you promise not to look up any spoilers.Wonderfully, there is a great deal of reactivity as well, and "failing forward" is hardcoded into the design.  You play through from beginning to end with no reloads, no do-overs, and no second chances.  This makes every case solution nail-bitingly tense and all the more satisfying when you get it right.  Often you can see the results of not only your case solutions but other decisions as well.  A character might refuse forever to give you information if you make a choice they don't like.  Another character might be found in a different area and have different dialogue depending on decisions you made about them earlier.  And naturally at the end there is a big roundup of how everything turned out, with short vignettes about the fates of several major characters and situations.A quick word about presentation: I found the pixel art style very charming and atmospheric, with natural, readable animations.  Once again Julian Colbus has come through with a wonderful soundtrack that I am purchasing to put on my phone right now.The story is excellent as well, in my opinion, boasting a large cast of distinct and memorable characters with understandable motivations.  I found it delightful to meet some of the cast casually in passing, only to see them return later as important witnesses ... or antagonists.  The plot, like the investigations, is nicely balanced - complicated enough to need some unraveling, but not so overboard as to smother you in a million twists and turns.  I quickly invested in the main character's story, and the many stories of the ship's other inhabitants.I can't say enough good things about  but it's time for me to stop.  I paid full price $16 and bought the soundtrack too.  The game lasted me almost exactly 10 hours, much longer than average apparently, I guess because I really had to think hard about a lot of the cases.  Definitely spent plenty of time rereading my conversations or just staring at the screen trying to put it all together.  Even if your playthrough takes less time than mine, I unreservedly recommend this at full price.I think you'll pick up the full game right away after that.Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the storyline and characters, but the gameplay, mystery logic and game world are really unpolished. It is obvious that the inventory system was a struggle for the developers, it is an unorganized mess and a bit of a headache to find what you need. If you decide to play this, grab a notepad, or remap the PDA to another key so you can use steam overlay's notepad without opening and closing the PDA.The game world is not very interactive other than what is barely needed to push the story along, and most of the investigation process is fumbling around between the huge pile of evidence and your case notes to write down the nibbles of data and eventually deduce the answer. Towards the end I really did not feel like mucking with it and just guessed at the cases to move it along. I suspect that on a replay you could just solve the cases immediately after getting the evidence chunk that you can use to solve the case (who or what was important)... since it accepted my guesses without having any real backing to the evidence (just talked to the suspect and got their name in the evidence). That feels a bit off.Overall though the storywriting was solid, I hope the devs cook up another one but take some notes from Shadows of Doubt - a freeform evidence handler and allow the user to assign their own cases to drop evidence into and draw their own conclusions, and post more than one evidence to tie their case together - who, what, when, where, how, why, etc. The game really fell apart for me when I didn't have an active case and just wandered around wondering what I needed to do to make it progress... it was hiding in the "not a case" case notes. I would rather fail that side mission for having too much time go by than to have time frozen and all progress halt because there was a single mention of the next thing to do that was scrolled by other interactions.
