_childDocuments_.review: This is a narrative-driven detective game that focuses on gathering clues through dialogue and exploration in an interesting sci-fi setting. If you are looking for classic point-and-click with gathering and combining objects, I can tell you: it's not included in this game, look no further if this mechanic is vital for you.The story and atmosphere are gripping and I had fun trying to find out what everything is about. You can shape the protagonist's personality to a certain extent depending on your dialogue choices and also the endings (I liked mine) have some moral ambiguity to them which is a nice touch. I wish some of the more important characters would've been fleshed out more, also the protagonist's relationship with them to give them more emotional depth and meaning - this is definitely a point that could be improved in the developer's next game. There is the potential to come to wrong conclusions and miss information (which is great, because you really need to use your head), but if you really take your time and explore everything and talk to everybody, it is possible to solve most cases without a guide (there was only 1 puzzle I didn't like and had problems to understand, the one involving a ping signal). If you turn it off in the settings, there is no timer while picking your dialogue choices, so you can take your time gathering all of the information and evidence needed to solve the cases. There is only one auto-save, so if you want to save manually and try out different things, this is sadly not possible. There is also no way to start from a later chapter. I don't like it when games take away your freedom to save whenever you like, even if I understand the reason behind it (they want you to really think about your choices and live with them even if they were wrong). If you already know the correct solution of your cases, you can skip a lot of the game in your next playthrough by immediately submitting the correct solution once you get the case which at least saves some time (manual savegames and the possibility to start from a certain chapter would've been better still, I think).I can definitely recommend the game if you like detective games and sci-fi!Edit after playing Lacuna (the game they made before Between Horizons):The mechanic to highlight objects you can interact with (spamming the corresponding button instead of toggling a button like in Lacuna) was kind of annoying. I hope the developers will return to the toggle mechanic they used in Lacuna. :)The cases and puzzles were more difficult in a positive way compared to Lacuna. You really need to think more and cross-reference all of your information which I really, really liked! So please keep this level of difficulty in your next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Really well put together branching narrative sci-fi tale. It takes a lot of inspiration in style and dialogue from classic 2d point-and-click adventures, but instead of lots of item manipulation and deep dialogue trees, you're given cases to solve which are mainly revolve around a central math/IQ puzzle with the hints scattered across dialogue trees and exploration. They don't  like puzzles because of all the storytelling wrapped around each one, but that's essentially what they are. There is detective work to be done a la the modern Sherlock games (select who you believe is the culprit) with varying degrees of ambiguity, and there are in/correct answers which you will find out along the way if not definitively at the end. I enjoyed how everything tied together storywise, and the choices the developers that both respect your time (e.g. fast travel, conversation history) and provide small additional challenges (e.g. time-sensitive dialogue - which you can opt out of - and the optional encounters and 'side' case you can pursue).A couple of puzzles were very opaque and frustrating but I have no doubt the developers will improve this. They're very responsive, helpful -- head to the discussions or their discord if you wish to see for yourself.Overall, I recommend it for those who enjoy these kinds of games -- it's a slightly different formula to most of the common genres you'd label this as, and if you're not one of those choices and consequences weirdos who wants the game to become either a bullet hell shooter or rhythm platformer in the 2nd act based on whether you pet the optional zebra in the opening sequence, then I think you'll enjoy the story. p.s. If you want the CRPG version of this game then I recommend playing Colony Ship.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a good detective game that takes place on a compelling generation spaceship. The story has enough intrigue, as players uncover more secrets and slowly identify members of a dissident group. Cases feature logical deductions and mathematical solutions, with most having enough proof to satisfy even the most doubtful. It is also great that players can submit answers without going through all the steps, and face the consequences of any mistakes. Some cases needed a bit more fine tuning, with more clues and deeper investigations. But despite this, there is a solid 5-6 hours of investigative work here, and for fans of detective games, it puts forward a strong case.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is great, but it needed more time in the oven. In no particular order, here are my gripes:The start of the game has pacing issues, and feels rushed. You are constantly interrupted with tutorial pop-ups grinding things to a halt. At the same time, the initial plot is going at mach 5. The character you play as comes across as emotionally stunted, given how little time they get to express anything - at the end of the intro, it was almost comedic how quickly things went from 'a chase' to 'guy stuck in door' to 'oh we're at a funer-' to 'oh we're in bed again'. It's certainly hitting story beats, but ends up feeling like more of a character motivation checkbox exercise.Let's talk about the graphics. While clearly a step up from Lacuna in terms of dimensions, it comes with some new problems. Foreground objects often obscure the screen, sometimes even during mandatory dialogue (e.g. Hospital). The lighting on most of the ship is... really dim? I thought it was a temporal thing to simulate night time on the ship, but no, and there's no in-universe explanation either. It probably added a lot of development time that could have been spent on the core systems.From the opening you might assume that there's a fair bit of exploration around the ship, where you're let off the training wheels and can discover cases naturally. In reality, only a select few locations are accessible or non-empty at a time, and any characters that aren't immediately plot relevant will only utter a few lines of dialogue before shutting up for good. You can present evidence to them, but will get only 1 of 3 possible responses: 'I don't know what that is', "That's me", when you show them their own evidence file, or '[this is classified information, I shouldn't...]', which is shown even when you're presenting it to the character who gave it to you!Fast travel is an option, but only cuts out about half the travel time, travel time that really shouldn't be so high with such a small number of points of interest. Things just feel a bit empty, honestly. A few characters which are integral to the plot, such as the rebel leader, and the person who is literally behind the final case, have almost no dialogue.When you discover a new location, character, or piece of information, it's added to your evidence tab, in the order you found it. Nothing is ever removed or re-ordered from this tab. There are no sub-tabs or sorting options, so by late-game it's an absolute mess and 95% of it clearly isn't relevant at all. Why?At time of writing, there's also a loud audio bug when selecting an answer for a case and scrolling above the top of the list.With all that said, it's an overall good experience. But pick up and play Lacuna first.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright.The premise is interesting, but hamstrung by poor design.You're basically a detective in a sci-fi Ark ship on the way to colonise a planet, though you'll never see it yourself cos, lol, it's a long time away, but your kids might.Stuff goes wrong, you have to investigate and solve cases, whatever you submit is final, whether you get it right or wrong, the game cracks on regardless. It is ironman mode all the way through, no manual saving, so you're in for the long haul.You scan for objects to collect evidence, go through witness testimony and so on, all the basics basically, and then come to your own conclusions. Where it fails? The UI is a complete mess. Evidence collects in a panel that, although you can sort by 'type'; so physical evidence/person/location lists, it is still one giant jumble of crap that is tedious to scour through when you're trying to find 'Steve the Hick' that you met two chapters back and he's all the way down the bottom, except you can't remember what this pillock even looks like. There's a UI bug as well where evidence won't scroll correctly if you go too far down the list, so although you'll highlight the correct evidence, it'll show the text for some other evidence instead, and if you present said evidence to someone, it'll present the text version and not what is actually selected on the evidence tab.The lack of an ability to collate/compare two pieces of evidence side by side also hurts the game, as does the lack of being able to sift through statements side-by-side. You'd better have a notepad available to take notes, and to be happy to switch between pages and pages of evidence just to work out the puzzles in here; and they're mostly mathematical, or 'logic' tests, nothing that really stretches the imagination.The core story presents moral dilemmas that don't really work for several reasons;1. The story goes far too fast, I don't really have any connection to the crew, outside of my 'case-work'.2. You never actually socialise prior to your job, so there's not really any relationships to speak of for the player (not necessarily for the NPCs themselves).3. If you're a pragmatic person, the 'moral dilemma' isn't really that difficult to consider IMO and nothing was really done by the writing team to hammer home the conflict points and severity of the dilemma ~ in black and white terms it was a fairly easy, binary choice to make.And to tie into that, when you have this big dilemma to deal with, you can more or less talk people down with far too much ease. That was immersion breaking, for me anyway, people aren't rational in high pressure situations when things unfold, so to basically go 'lol no' to the binary choice at the end and suffer absolutely zero consequences is a bit of a damp squib (I'm aware it can go sideways if you go the other way, but even so, squib...)I only recommend it for those that really need a sci-fi game and a bit of an open and shut investigation case to deal with. It isn't going to set the stars alight, unfortunately, not for me anyway, it was alright and that's fine, but it definitely wasn't anything to write home about.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of surprised Steam says I spent nearly 6 hours on this game, because it certainly didn't feel that long. Between Horizons is really well-paced and I was constantly looking forward to finding the next clue to solve whichever case(s) I was working on at the time, but let me start by explaining the game a little.You play as the chief of security on a generation ship sent to a distant planet with all the necessities on board to keep the ship running for 130 years and then terraform the planet after landing. The game contains no combat and consists of walking around, talking to characters, confronting them with evidence, finding clues and solving cases. Interestingly, the game will let you pick the wrong solution to a puzzle and won't tell you whether you got it right until later. There are no manual saves and the idea is that you have to deal with the consequences of your choices and how you resolved each case.I want to be very clear about this: every case can be solved correctly with the evidence available. There are no "guess what the devs were thinking" type puzzles here and thank God for that. This is honestly a large part of why I liked the game, because I can't stand puzzle games where the solutions are nonsensical or aren't necessarily true based on the evidence. Follow the clues, ask the right questions and use logical deduction. You'll get to the correct solution every time. Or, you know, just randomly pick something from the possible list and see what happens in a disaster run where you roleplay as the single most irresponsible person on the ship. Your call, really.I don't know how the story would change, if you completely mess it up, but it was interesting when played correctly. Without giving anything away, the story uses the setting well and it becomes clear later on why they chose to have it take place specifically on a generational terraforming ship, beyond the seemingly obvious 'bottle' nature. Like a lot of good sci-fi, it introduces a futuristic situation and then explores how human nature would react to that setting, starting with how the player will choose to perform their job as chief of security.I enjoyed solving the cases, putting together the pieces of the story, the later plot twists and the choices available to the player. In a longer game, I would've liked to see more character development from a lot of the side characters, but the game's focus is clearly more on the mystery rather than the characters. The characters were fleshed out enough to feel distinct, but getting little more than "we used to date" as character background when the people on this ship have been dealing with each other for 30 years felt a bit lacking, but I'm honestly nit picking at this point.Overall, a very enjoyable experience and a well-made puzzle/detective game.

_childDocuments_.review: Earth is dying, and they send a ship with thousands of people to a habitable planet. The ship was sent 33 years ago, and you've grown up on that ship, knowing that you'll die in it because it will take another 100 years to reach its destination. The game starts with reports of a dissident group who are trying to jeopardize the ship's mission to reach its destination. Your task is to find out who and why.   There are 10 cases in the game, each with different challenges and fairly difficult. If a case is too difficult for you, you can even pick a random conclusion to end it, so you can't get stuck. But the difficulty is fair, and I only stumbled in one case but managed to solve it with a simple hint from the community. The case and evidence UI are not the best, but they are manageable and work.    The story is good, the mystery unraveling knot by knot, and the pacing is on point. There are lots of choices, and theyt affect the ending. How successful you are with the cases also affects the ending. I can't compare it with Lacuna (the developer's first game) since I only played it for a few hours, but this is a pretty good detective game, and I want to finish Lacuna next.    I was expecting bugs since it's a new release from an indie dev, yet I only came across one, but it was not game-breaking since I managed to get out with fast traveling, and I think it has already been fixed with the first patch.I hope that we can see another game from the developer in the future. They have their own flavor in their games, and it's pretty damn good.Make sure to try the demo if you're on the verge. It gives a good sense of what the gameplay loop is about.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished playing the game and thoroughly enjoyed it. After playing Lacuna, I was excited to see another game recently released by the developer and decided to give it a go. Unlike Lacuna, I had to get a pen and paper out to parse through the challenging though not too difficult puzzles. That said, there were definitely some interface decisions I did not enjoy, such as putting all the people (of which the game touts 40 of them) in the same tab as the clues, leading to a confusing mixture of evidence and characters. Had these been separated, I would have been much happier. The game also did not actively encourage exploring as much as I would have hoped and I think I missed some encounters with other characters. This might be intentional to let people replay the game to try and find them, and maybe I will give it a go again sometime. Overall, a great game with challenging enough clues and an enjoyable narrative. Hoping to see more from DigiTales in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing Lacuna, I felt bad about having bought it for literal pennies. That's why I decided to buy the next game by DigiTales day 1, even though I normally don't do that. "Even if it's bad", I thought, "I'll consider it a delayed payment for Lacuna. At least my debt will be paid off."Just like Lacuna, Between Horizons is a detective story. This time the main character is a young woman rather than a middle aged man, the story takes place on a spaceship and the game itself is less linear. These would be the main differences, the rest works basically the same.On screenshots Lacuna didn't look like much, but in motion - due to animations together with art direction - was extremely climactic. Between Horizons looks much better, but still has that atmosphere, thankfully. Enhanced by very nice and fitting music, too. Again, only the protagonist's monologues are voiced.The story is interesting and, much like in the previous game, escalates quickly. Dialogues are well written, characters may be somewhat less deep than in Lacuna, but that's because there are many more of them involved in the story, so you spend less time with each of them.Now, for the gameplay. Investigations are still fundamentally the same, but as the world is more open, we get many more clues and characters to talk to. This means the player is even more than before forced - or perhaps I should say "allowed" - to think by themselves. You need to choose characters important to your current case and ask them about the right clues. Of course, you can try talking to everyone about everything in each case, but that would be a massive waste of time. Therefore, thinking is the preferred method of solving cases here, as opposed to clicking. Like in Lacuna, you're provided with raw clues, but dialogues and cutscenes don't process them, explain their meanings and draw conclusions for you. You're the one who decides which clue is important and whether to trust a testimony or not.Of course, the game has a number of small flaws and bugs, some of them already fixed, some probably soon. A few typos, interface and menu navigation still not perfect (although better than in Lacuna) and so on.The game could do a better job at telling you what to do next as well. I'm not talking about some unnecessary "hand-holding". Sometimes characters talk about something you're supposed to do, but if you try, it turns out that you can't. You may feel like you're stuck, but that only means you have to do something else first. This wouldn't be a problem if the game indicated this somehow, for example Stella could say to herself "Later, I need take care of X first".Those are really small things that didn't affect my enjoyment in the least. One problem that is bigger for me personally, however, is that there are times when you need to provide an answer to a case based not on solid evidence, but solely on testimonies whose credibility you can't confirm. The correct answer may be obvious, it may make sense, but you still can't be 100% sure. I realize such are the circumstances and that Stella has to work with what she got, but I guess it's just not my style.To summarize, despite some small flaws/bugs and subjective problems, Between Horizon is an amazing game, a very fun to follow story and just a pleasant experience. Another step towards the perfect model of detective games where the player does the thinking. And I believe we're getting close.Unfortunately, it seems I still owe the devs for Lacuna. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ Your name is Stella.  You’re the security assistant on the Zephyr spaceship, which is on its way to the star Eurus-d, a suitable planet for humans located four lightyears away from Earth. Its mission is to settle the planet for the survival of humankind. Thirty three years into its mission, a chain of events puts the success of the ship's mission and its 1,300 cohabitants in danger. Now promoted to the chief of security, it is up to you to investigate these events and save the mission in Between Horizons.Between Horizons is a sci-fi point-and-click pixelated adventure game developed by DigiTales Interactive and published by Assemble Entertainment on the 26th of March 2024 on the Steam platform.The game is presented as a side-scroller and consists of a very well-structured story with ten cases to solve. Most cases are average in difficulty, while a couple might take some time and deduction to complete. The game offers a couple of endings. Playtime is around 10 hours, which is pretty good for that genre of games.The story takes place on the spaceship, Zephyr, and has seven different areas to explore, with many NPCs that Stella will need to talk to to gather information for her cases. She will also have a scanner on her suit that can be activated by pressing the space key on your keyboard, allowing her to collect evidence within the rooms. At the start of the game, only a few areas will be accessible, but more will unlock as Stella successfully resolves cases. It might take some time to run from one part of the ship to another, but you can also use the fast travel option on the map by clicking on a specific room. Then, Stella will appear out of the transport station that’s nearest your selected room, and will walk the distance to get to the room. This option will be helpful later on in the game. Stella’s PDA can be accessed at any time by pressing the TAB key. A few options will be available: the cases, the evidence, the comms and the map tabs. The cases tab will display the current cases you are working on. The evidence tabs will display items, people, and devices Stella has come across during cases, and the comms tabs will show all the discussions she’s had with the relevant people in those cases. To resolve cases, you will have to choose a character, a room, or a device. I strongly recommend revisiting Stella's communications before making a choice on a character. As mentioned, you might need to create a schematic to figure out a couple of cases. I made a bad choice in one case by not talking to a specific character.  The result was that Stella shot a suspect dead. Unbeknownst to me until the next scene, this suspect held the remaining numbers of the server code that I needed. Thank god it was only two letters, and as a result, it was a guessing game for a while, but as I had the first and last number of the code, it was too long to resolve the puzzle. And, of course, at the end of the game, Stella and I needed to make the last decision for one specific ending.The developers have done a sterling job with Between Horizons, and it is as good as their first game Lacuna. The tutorial is brilliant. Once in a while, when you find new things a pop-up will appear and explain how to use them. Great pixel graphics, and the soundtrack is excellent. There are some scenes with voice-overs, which are well executed. I didn’t encounter any issues throughout my gameplay. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Great Pixel artwork+	Well-written and well-structured story+	Good soundtrack and voice-over on selecting scenes+	10 cases to resolve and a couple of endings+	Easy to play+	AchievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	No trading cards as yet-	It would have been nice if the cases were a little bit more difficult to resolveBetween Horizons has a well-written and well-structured story and provides interesting cases to solve. A game not to miss for fans of the genre.  8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting story based game where choices actually make a difference, and plenty of lore to keep you occupied for 10 good hours. Not usually my type of game as i'm not patient enough to sit and read through dialogue for the most part but I have to say I actually enjoyed this, so if it appeals to me it will appeal to those that like a good book to read. Graphics are great with that 2.5D retro style and whilst it has the odd typo and bug, it's a pretty well polished game overall. Not to mention the devs are pretty solid when it comes to fixing things, so far. It also runs as smooth as butter so I can't complain about performance.The negative side isn't much really. I think it could be much longer, bigger ship, more to explore but who knows, there could be DLC further along. The biggest gripe would be the no voice acting, other than the main character during cutscenes. I prefer to listen rather than have to read, but that's just my own personal preference, I think the old school gamers might actually appreciate the non voice acting like back in the day. Again, for those lore hunters you're looking at a good >10hrs but you can speed through it in around 2hrs if that's your jam, including the achievements (check out my guide) and a fairly easy one to 100%. Price i'd say is reasonable for what it is but it's always going to be on sale at some point so that should solve any problems if you're on the fence.Overall a thoroughly enjoyable game and whilst short, the story is enough to keep you engrossed throughout. Polished and playable. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of sci-fi, detective stories, narrative-driven games and pixel art, this is the game for you. I played the team's first game, Lacuna, on Nintendo Switch a few months ago, and there are some interesting tweaks to the gameplay formula that make this new game worthwhile. The 2D/3D mix can be a little jarring at times, as can the UI design in my opinion, but nothing that takes away from the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed this game, I can now give it a whole-hearted recommendation.You play Stella, the newly-promoted chief of security on a colony ship sent on a mission to establish humanity on a distant planet. So distant in fact that the journey will last multiple generations, and nobody currently alive will see its conclusion.As settings go, it's a perfect fit for the two main defining features genres of this game: detective, and choices-matter. The ship is a self-contained world which you can traverse and get to know as you progress through unravelling the plot's central mysteries. It also presents some genuinely interesting moral quandries: the ship's mission is of the upmost importance to Earth, and so society exists in an uneasy state in between normal civilian life and military hierarchy. Decisions are made in an authoritarian manner, jobs roles are inherited rather than chosen, and as people are born on the ship a generation is coming of age who never chose to be there or make those sacrifices.Against this backdrop is an engaging, pacy thriller type plot of conspiracy and sabotage.The gameplay is primarily about solving cases. There's usually two elements to this: investigation-style gameplay where you gather information, often involving working out who to ask about what, and deduction gameplay where you put clues together to answer specific questions.Don't expect a Return of the Obra Dinn or Case of the Golden Idol style of puzzle here in which you are deluged with information and need to construct a narriative out of it. Once you have gathered all the relevant information, the deduction aspect is more like traditional point-and-click puzzles. I never found these too taxing, but they hit a good level of challenge where solving each one was rewarding.The game has a nice style to it. Visually, it's a 2.5-D style which does a good job of blending a retro pixel into a quasi-3D environment. The music does a great job of capturing both the sci-fi and mystery moods of the game, and provides a good ambience while usually not being too attention-grabbing. Voice acting is limited but is high quality when it appears.As you can probably guess from the above, my review is very positive. The one area that could have been improved is that it would have been nice to have a more conversation options, to help make the characters a little more fleshed out and give the world more of a lived-in feeling. However, I highly doubt this is going to really negatively impact anyone's experience of the game. Overall, story, setting, visuals, music, voice acting and well-designed puzzles combine to make a really engaging sci-fi thriller.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game.  Your choices matter, even if you don't realize you are making them.  The puzzles also track several logic bends, such as breaking down timelines or attributes to arrive at a conclusion, visual puzzles, math puzzles, and others.  The game does a bit of hand-holding, with the character commenting if you approach a loose thread that leads to clues for the current puzzle, but if you've been thorough you're already thinking her commentary as an internal monologue.  While playing I had a note sheet open, which was good fun in keeping suspects aligned and allowing me to eliminate them one by one until I had the correct solution left.  Voice acting is good, and the soundtrack is an excellent tonal fit to the story, and the pixel graphics give it the retro feel of classic point and click games.  Highly recommended.Suggestion to the Developer:  While there are multiple endings and dialogue branches to encourage replay, the puzzle solutions are always the same, due to the solutions tying directly to the plot.  It would be good to see this model expanded upon, not necessarily in a fully-procedural way which would deprive the solutions of all logical impact and cohesion, but more in line with the movie Clue where a few solution 'sets' are available, and the player may get any of them upon starting a playthrough.  Although such an expansion of the scrip and puzzle set may be a bit too ambitious, know I only mean to compliment the game in that I wish there was more of it to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a fun point & click style detective adventure game. There are 10 official cases that need solving, however you are in an open world and some detectiving can be done outside of the official cases to find out additional things about the story.The story is pretty good, which unfolds while you solve the cases. Based on your deductions, the story and ending changes. This allows the game to be replayed once or twice for different results.The difficulty of the detective cases range from "as easy as taking candy from a baby" to "Sherlock Holmes worthy" level difficulty in my opinion. However, getting a case wrong is not directly punished and the (altered) story continues based on your false deductions.The UI is a bit clunky at times, especially when wanting to review collected evidence and having to go through lots of items to find the one you are looking for, but the game is relatively short (about 5-6 hours) which keeps the clunkyness within acceptable limits for me.Overall I would rate this an 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: This definitely improves on Lacuna. Art and music style is really great. There's a lot of stuff to explore on the ship though it is a little disappointing that sections are intentionally closed off even if it probably is a better experience across the board.Similar to Lacuna, the cases aren't super complicated but you do need to put in the investigation effort. There's a lot more to explore here and it really makes the cases rewarding. I wish there was more red herring paths but I'm sure they didn't playtest as well.I wish there was a bit more interaction with the crew. I get that time is of the essence in the story but it would have been nicer to build more of a rapport with folks. Perhaps it would have been nice as part of the tutorial/first case to build more of a vibe of how life is on the ship for the first generation born on board.While I think it's definitely a pro that there's no longer eight different endings and an achievement to go along with it, I also think this ending where there's some random number with a summary of things is kind of confusing. It's not bad but I feel like it's harder to figure out some of the variables you might change between runs.I think this is definitely a fun game and builds more on the style of DigiTales Interactive. Curious to see what's next!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: A fun detective game about the potential dilemmas around human space colonization and generation ships. Asks some interesting moral questions, and leaves it up to you to decide.If you like solving puzzle and deducing whodonit - as well as space travel and moral quandaries, this game may be for you.The game is a bit on the short side - could likely be completed in 5-6 hours depending on how through you want to be with your investigations, and how quickly you solve them.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Between Horizons. To talk much about the plot of the game is to already tell too much. And to just repeat the setting that's already lined out here on the store page is pointless, so I'll just refrain from that.Its story plays off of some very interesting societal dilemmas which we are facing in the real world right now as well. It does a very good job of conveying what it means to be born, live and die on a Generation-Ship, knowing full well that you will never set foot on a planet - that the ship and the emptyness of interstellar space are the only world you will ever get to know. While it is in essence a SciFi story, it encorporates some real-life physics as a basis to make the setting more belieavable.The cases you're solving in your work as detective are very compelling and, while not brutally hard, require quite some deduction to crack at times. I managed to get every solution correct in my playthrough with the help of a piece of paper for quick notes and visualization aid.That being said, if you get a case wrong the story will continue regardless and the real culprit may walk free, influencing the direction of story down the line.While I only made a single playthrough my decisions felt quite impactful. The game did an excellent job of indicating the consequences of my actions, without spelling them out in minute detail and the Ending I arrived at felt very satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Completed  Between Horizons for the first time.One of the best adventure game ever. Art, sound, characters, atmosphere -- all great.You play as an assistant chief of security on a generations ship traveling to a distant star. You are due to arrive in a hundred years. But. Life on the ship is about to change.Keep in mind this is not your usual quest. It's more of a detective story. You need to gather clues, talk to people, connect the dots and make a conclusion. If you are right the game continues. If you are wrong THE GAME CONTINUES. You form the story as you go.All executed brilliantly. An amazing experience. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: It was a neat little story, but I was bogged down by the interface, and lack of quest pointers.  I ended up having to check every location to find certain people, if I didn't randomly find them.  That lead me to finally looking up the answers in an attempt to see the story, and not feel drudgery.  Ultimately, it was worth the purchase, and the few hours of time to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the money.Not great at writing so here's few points:One thing I was not so huge on was the setting (big part of the story would in may ways be better if it was a bunker IMO). However the story over all turned out great in the end.  You might need a pen and paper as I did since the evidence/case view is good but not great.Overall a great game with good writing and solid art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I played Lacuna right when it came out, and have been waiting impatiently for a follow-up. I'm happy to report that Between Horizons was well-worth the wait. DigiTales creates these fantastically atmospheric pixel sci-fi worlds that are an absolute pleasure to play in. If I had a wish, it's that the beginning spent a little more time setting the stage and introducing its characters before launching into the meat of its story, though of course that's also me selfishly wishing for more to play. All in all, the game is what I wanted so now I'm impatiently waiting for what comes next! Need one more like this to round out the thematic trilogy they've got going here. :-)(And will happily play more than three of these kinds of games!)
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I liked "Lacuna", and I liked "Between Horizons" even more. Good stuff. The game is more about enjoying the story than solving puzzles, just so you know, and it hit the perfect spot for me: the locked down ship on its endless space odyssey, the society built around the concept of a Mission with a capital "M", the intrigue, the characters acting on what little knowledge they have about the bigger picture. I believe that this game is one of the two (The second one being "Primordia". ) that can compete with the books of the science fiction genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: The visual style, music, and especially story really carry this game. The detective gameplay is fun and with the hardcore mode of choices matter (no manual saves) it really feels like your decisions have weight. Some quality of life things could have been better (there’s so much elevator usage, trying to find specific NPCs is hard as you have to remember where they are located on this massive ship etc.). The Painkillers Case was so easy to miss, really only figured out something was missing way deeper into another case where I hit a wall and one of my chatters told me to revisit and scan an area. The biggest gripe was the extremely confusing ping puzzle, god I was stuck on trying to understand it for more than an hour and then the solution was super easy to find out by sidestepping the puzzle entirely -.- Basically with some caveats, this is a good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game for its gameplay. Given its price, it's a nice way to spend a day off. You really are solving the cases yourself, so in that sense, you do feel like the security officer. I also like the setting: the ship and the way it is structured (both spatially, and socially) have clearly been well thought out, and it works well. I do think the game has less of that detective/noir style that Lacuna excelled in, and also in terms of its main conflict, I found it lacking. While it's clear enough what the conflict is and what the sides to it are, I feel like the game ultimately fails to get you to empathize strongly with either side. I think the game would have profited either from a longer run (it's about 6 hours for a single play-through) or a smaller scope. Some of the characters are introduced but you don't connect to them much, until you're in the final act, and you realise you're supposed to feel some type of way about them, when you've barely interacted with them throughout the game. The characters that I did care about where all characters that you interacted with multiple times throughout the different acts for more than one conversation.I think the story elements were interesting and with a longer play time and more fleshed out characters (more insight into their lives), I could have come to care about it enough to make the final choice of the game impactful. As it was, for me, the game started out strong but did not improve over the acts. Final verdict: recommend for the gameplay and the world-building, do not recommend for its story and its ability to take you along in that story.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Taken on its own merits this is a good game. I like deduction-detective mystery games and this is a good one. The cases are varied and require you to both explore and think through things. Overall they were very good. As for the narrative, that was less interesting. It's perfectly serviceable as a vehicle for the deduction stuff, but not enough to stand on its own merits. As a sequel to Lacuna however the game does less well. Lacuna had a great narrative, which this one lacks. And while the cases in this case were grander requiring legwork across different areas of the map whereas Lacuna's were mostly based in a single room - I thought the cases in Lacuna were better. This is not a game that will stand up the the previous game in my mind. However, that doesn't stop me from being able to appreciate this as a good deduction-detective mystery game and we are not exactly spoiled with a lot of those. So going in with this in mind, I recommend the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I had an incredible time with Between Horizons. The characters and the story were very fleshed out, and I love the decisions I got to make and how they affected the story. The game is visually stunning even though I generally don't care for pixelated art styles. The puzzles throughout the game were all really intriguing but there was one in particular that was far too difficult for me personally. The map, while visually appealing, was difficult at times to parse. There is a journal to help keep track of all of your tasks and information which was so helpful when taking a short break between sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: A great game (who doesn't love a detective game?), but the wheels came off in the final act.  Quest lines got broken.  Maybe I solved the cases out of order?  Either way, I was forced to guess the solution for the final case.  Fortunately, I'm basically 2% genius and got it right  B)  Look forward to the next game.  Maybe skip the branching and focus more on nailing the ending.  Oh, and needs more furry characters OwO
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a smart and fun detective game that establishes a really rich cast and setting and then lets you solve cases in a relatively freeform way - you can accuse anyone of anything in your case work, and the story continues. It has the basic good stuff a game like this has, like puzzles and logic deductions and stuff, but it also has richer bonus things you can figure out that make you feel smart and let you pursue hunches. The devs' other game, Lacuna, was also excellent, they're going from strength to strength in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: If you wanted a spiritual successor to Lacuna like I did, this will greatly disappoint you. The characters feel shallow and some feel unnecessary, your relationships with them only ever going a few lines and a codex description. There's alot less outcome variation here, about 5 things that can be changed from what I saw in the ending screen. This isn't a gritty detective-noir story, but more of a generic conspiracy-mystery.The ending doesn't give you a chance for last-minute choices, and more plays out like a cutscene before the actual ending cutscene. It seems like it's based on your previous actions which, while it does make sense, makes me feel like I have no controll over the actions that transpire in the ending. At least give me some dialogue options!Plus there just alot of small things, like the inner monologue text system feeling alot less cinematic, making the game blink for a second and even failing to appear at times, both of which take you out of the immersion immediately. When you show things to people and they spit out the generic "I dont have anything to say about that" even though they should atleast have some sort of flavor text. Theres alot of talk about the ethics commitee but you never meet them (unless the committee is made up of normal people on the ship that you do meet. In that case you should have made that clearer.)This game does have it's merits though. The 3d combined with 2d art style perhaps being it's greatest. But I cannot reccomend this over something like Lacuna, which this studio has shown it is completley capable of doing since they are the ones who made lacuna.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I was given a free copy to play on stream for my community. Thank you for giving me this wonderful opportunity devs. While this is not the usual type of game I play, I thoroughly enjoyed it. The mystery was very intriguing. I just needed to know more and more, I didn't want to stop playing. And while I ended up getting 7/10 of the cases I worked on correct, I managed to be happy about the ending. The writing is really engaging. It had a hold of me from the beginning. There is only one important question I still have that's unanswered, though.What kind of creature is Chichi? xD
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles/cases in it's predecessor Lacuna were really well made with a bunch of clues and a nice challenge.The puzzles/cases here give you so few clues that it feels like the world is just empty except two clues and from that point on you just have to guess. I shamelessly used the walkthrough.The graphics, the scenario, the music and the the overall atmosphere and feeling are nice. But in a game which mostly lives by it's puzzles it is crucial that these puzzles are fun and solveable. These are too often frustrating and sometimes even just confusing. I am sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a mystery game that mildly resembles Lacuna in many ways, despite its story taking place on a colony ship in space. Overall I enjoyed this game and would recommend it for anyone looking for some casual mystery and light story.PROS+ Lovely pixel art style+ Variety of spaces to explore on the ship+ Challenging mysteries that you solve while threading the storyline+ Myriad characters to engage with+ A compelling story on the surface (see cons)+ Fast travel is a boon for needing to run around+ Rewarding ending (at least on your first playthrough)+ The developer made it easy to try out other endings without needing to slog through the entire game.+ Choices will impact downstream results (to a degree).NEUTRAL= The soundtrack is nice, but it did get a bit repetitive at times= The endings felt similar rather than uniqueCONS- Despite the fact that your choices can somewhat impact the ending, the story felt linear.- Lots of running around to disparate part of the ship (fast travel helps)- Despite being a compelling story, at times it simply lacks the depth that it could have gone into. The potential was there, but it simply wasn't explored further.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than Lacuna. The story is way more interesting and better written, and the graphics are a huge step up. Each playthrough is a little different and adapts based on your successes and failures. There are also a couple different possible endings, but those seem to be mainly based on a couple decisions you make at the very end of the game (at least I think so; I've only played through once in my ~7 hours of playtime). If you like point-and-click mystery games, this is possibly the best one there is.My only complaint is that I feel like the developers stopped short of some very low-hanging fruit. For example, suppose the developers had continued working on the game for just another 2 weeks to add unique dialogue for each piece of "evidence" that you can show to NPCs. It wouldn't have even required coding any new features, yet the payoff would've been massive and would've made the game feel much more immersive.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I can't imagine a more annoying start. It seems to be a book disguised as a game. First you are bombarded with a crap load of tutorial messages, and barely know what the game itself is about. And then you get to read a bunch of dialogue, combined with a timeout whenever you get to choose a reply to something. It just adds stress and nothing else.The first objective - walk up to  your father and have a chat - should have been part of the intro instead, and not part of the gameplay. My patience ended there, already. So I go 8 minutes of total gameplay. But on the other hand, I found the game for almost nothing, so no loss there.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: If detective games are your genre, check this out. It is not a dumb point and click where a solution is to use a duck to make a loud noise to startle a guard to drop a key you need.It would have been nice to have a guide at the end to explain solutions like  I guess I will never know, unless someone comments.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I think there's an experience common to playing most games, where, knowing the conventions of the genre, and perhaps the limitations of game development, you act in ways designed to maximize success in the video game world that you surely wouldn't do in anything approaching actual reality. What was remarkable about this game, apart from the inability to save--which really does heighten the experience--and the oh-so-difficult-to-achieve 'choices matter', especially where those choices aren't between being Evil or Good (which is what it almost always is in most games), was that there were two or three moments where I felt BETRAYED by the game, not because it was unfair, but because it subverted some gaming conventions that had me thinking, "I should be treating these detective cases a little bit more like I would if this were real life." That's pretty awesome, if you ask me. Spoilers:1) 2) 3)
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the devs read my  and took it to heart.Between horizons is short and rich and satisfying. Like an upscale restaurant portion of a decadent cake. A rich, compact, memorable, elegantly drawn cake. Where how you eat it meaningfully impacts how it goes down.I'm on board with what these devs are doing, and I'm excited to see what they release next.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot Praise this game highly enough. It was an experience I will not soon forget. the logic puzzles really made me thing, i even needed to pull out a notepad to jot down notes. Interacting with the character aboard the zephyr and rooting out dissidents really was a one in a million experience. after playing their first game Lacuna i was super excited to play this, and let me just say- it was worth the wait. what a wonderful little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an interesting world for a game, i love sci-fi stuff like this with moral judgements at it's core. It's very cleverly written and leaves a lot of stuff up to you to decide what you think is the right/wrong decision. Gameplay is mostly detective work, spruced in with choices you have to make about the mission and the lives of everyone aboard Zephyr. It's has a really unique 2.5D artstyle i haven't seen much before, and the art direction is just fantastic everything feels so personable and alive. Most of the cases were quite challenging but manageable. And the game really allows you to explore and figure out on your own with tips and clues to help you along.The biggest issues i have is probably the music feeling very samey and looping over and over again, and not having more options for chapter selection to try out the different endings/choices. Overall fantastic experience and I hope to see more like it in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice story, if it took a bit of time to get going. Puzzles were good, not as constrained as the designers' previous game, and more open-ended. The fact you can't reload previous saves if you get something wrong is interesting - good, I think, as it adds a bit of pressure as you have to live with your choices and your mistakes. The control system is a bit clunky - you can reassign keys, but really several functions should be possible using one key.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I'm usually very critical and found this game pretty good!The writing / story is engaging and everything eventually comes together beautifully. The only critique I have is that1) it becomes pretty annoying to run back and forth so many times. Citizen Sleeper has shown that this is not necessary for immersion.2) the system of scanning for objects to interact with is superfluous and annoying, because you will be spamming that button like a madman and still sometimes miss clues, because they're not highlighted well. Not a fun mechanic and not what the game is about, just highlight the items or find a solution that lets us actually look at the beautiful backgrounds.3) While some of the puzzles are brilliant, especially at making you feel smart, some solutions felt pretty far-fetched. You will be accusing people of crimes when they are clearly not guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. I still got them all, because I understood what the game was hinting at, but there were often other ways things could have happened.However, the game had a good length for what it is and had intriguing, round characters that are fleshed out really well for the short amount of time that it had. Nobody's just a bad or good person, everyone has their motivations and they're almost always very relatable and believable. The best thing: the game doesn't need walls of text to bring these personalities to life. Hats off for that, not even triple A games manage this. The themes are pretty philosophical and really make you think, especially about the whole idea of a multi-generational ship and what it would feel like to be born on one. Some moments in the game made me emotional and there were great Aha!-moments. A lot of love has clearly gone into this project and it shows. Will be keeping my eyes open for future releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Point-and-Click detective game with an interesting bit of storyline to back it up. You play as the newly-promoted Chief of Security on the , a generation ship 30 years into it's 130 year mission. While questions on the ethical viability of generation ships aren't exactly new to SF, I thought this game's approach was well done. Despite a lot of running around and a slightly clunky inventory/evidence system, I enjoyed my playthrough, clocking in at just shy of 7 hours.Completionists will want to note that the game has a vigorous autosave with no reload option or chapter select.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is an excellent game, and an excellent story, that speaks to what "justice" or "ethics" mean in small, remote communities. At times it can be a little confusing, and I found myself frustrated a couple of times before realising that I had all the clues I needed, they were just presented in a way that wasn't immediately obvious, but it gives you those "aha!" moments that matter. I'd wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with my first DigiTales game. The characters were great and the case system was beautifully designed. I'm glad I kept the timed response system on, despite being an overthinker, as it helped a lot with immersion. The music was repetitive and traversal was janky, but overall bearable.Overall, I would  again.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a good game, very enjoyable, with a lot of effort shown on behave of the devs. Enjoyed it a fair bit. It was shorter than I was expecting (1st play through took about 9 hours with a decent share of that being over-exploring), but even so, it's an experience worth the time. Aside from the main character, you don't interact on a personal level with many character, so it's hard to say they really hook you in, but they were all solid as they were for what was needed of each of them. The main character was enjoyable to play as, so that was good.Overall, solid and sweet. Would love to play more in this series, solve more stories on the Zypher and beyond.--- For the Devs---Good game, would like more. If there are any, an Auto and a Skip text function would be really helpful for replays. Tried for alt endings half a dozen times because in trying to skip through the texts at times I'd by accident hit a choice by mistake. Not a happy thing when there's no saves to reload, you know?Also, just so y'all know. Played the demo during the Steam Next Fest, first time I'd heard of the game, got it in the Summer Sale when it came out.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to love about this game, but there are still some rough edges. Some of the puzzles require you to just run around to locate people you need to speak with. You already know who you're looking for, but there aren't dialogue options where you can ask about said person, or if you do ask about this person, you'll be given a dismissive line. The atmosphere, graphics, music and everything else are great. It just fell short of being a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little investigation game where the choices you are able to make often depend on what you can find out. Some of the puzzles are a little vague, and there was once or twice i had to look up information, not the solutions, but where to actually find information I was supposed to have from past choices (check comms for interrogations in the future). Despite these hiccups, I enjoyed the story and the world it was made in. Not much there for replays unless you wanna see what happens if you get certain cases right or wrong, but a decent 6-7 hour game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of Between Horizons ticks all the right boxes for me: a science fiction story on a space ship, a non-action detective and mystery story, believable characters with individual motivations and a game progression that rewards exploration, thoroughness and making sensible choices. The player character is not a blank slate, but very easy to get into and make your own.Overall, the game is close to perfect for anyone who is intrigued by the premise I mentioned above. However, there are minor technical quirks, like a somewhat clunky interface and a graphics style that feels uneven (characters deserve more pixels, the environment could do with less, so that it feels more akin to pixel art adventure games instead of Octopath Traveler -- but maybe that's just me, as I do not like the mixed style much). The music is fine, but entirely forgettable. There is a fast travel system that fails to feel like one, as it often still requires you to use elevators, stairs or doors to get to where you actually want to go. It reduces the time, but not by much, so feels pointless: either the player wants to travel on foot to discover new things or they want to go somewhere specific, in which case a "move to room" travel system would have been far less tedious.With the negativity out of the way, everything about the gameplay and the plot, i.e. the 90% what drives games like this, is excellent. There are only a handful of cases, but I rarely felt as much satisfaction solving the mysteries in other games. The clues are always there, but the game does not focus on them or mark them with a blinking icon like in so many other games. But thankfully, they are also fair and logical and relatively easy to obtain as there is usually no time pressure or restriction on using an environment scanner function, thus careful exploration and reading the various items in the inventory or questlog gets you most of the way to the solution. Despite considering myself not a great detective by any means, I managed to get all the solutions right on my first playthrough (there is a mechanic that allows you to fail and thus change the story, but I didn't experience it) and achieved an ending that felt logical for my character, satisfying for the story and overall realistic in the context of the game's universe.In summary, I thoroughly enjoyed the ~5 hours I spend on the Zephyr. There is not much reason to replay (for me anyway, since I got everything correct luckily), but I will fondly look back on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A good game although not without a few bugs and sadly not as good as Lacuna the developers previous entry.Positives-Graphics are great the devs have really figured out a very beautiful pixelated style not a huge suprise since Lacuna had great pixel art as well but worth mentioning nonetheless.-The story and choices are interesting some of the antagonist motivations are in my view dumb but I'm sure that someone with a different perspective would come away with a very different opinion.Stuff that I found annoying-The ultimate difference between the two games is that Lacuna was a lot more linear and controlled in terms of where the player was going and what they were doing. Between Horizons opens this up a bit with a semi-open generation ship the player can wander around and explore in the course of solving their cases. Unfortunately this proves to be more of a negative than a positive as the player constantly has to backtrack from one end of the ship to the other trying to figure out who they need to talk to or what evidence they need to present to someone to get the next bit of information to solve there cases. This sounds great in theory but Between Horizons tends to cross the streams in terms of what evidence is important for what case which means you end up with every piece of evidence you've ever collected staring at you any time you go to provide it to POI's in the world. In theory it isn't too much of a problem since some of the cases are small enough that you won't really be struggling to figure out what's important and what's not but some of the later cases especially the last case take an all of the above approach to whats important so much so that I was genuinely struggling to even come up with a guess as to whodunnit.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Very recommend! Fascinating setting and story with several surprising twists. Very good detective gameplay that strikes a good between being managable and making you feel like an actual detective.Shares a lot of qualities with Lacuna, but the more open nature adds a level of exploration and makes some the detective gameplay even more engaging. Plus, the setting feels more unique.Some things I didn't like though:- Some of the texts (like those parallel to the voice-acted thoughts of the main character) were difficult to read.- Finding clues will just quickly pop up a message and you first need to go into the menu to read what it is all about, making the whole experience a bit less "streamlined"- Some of the more dramatic scenes are sometimes paced a bit too quickly with a lack of pauses between consecutive scenes.- Didn't like that statue for some reason
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a sci-fi detective adventure about a ring ship known as the Zephyr, it doesn't take long for things to go wrong and the player is thrown into the thick of it to find out what it going on.Pros:- 10 cases to work your way through, be thorough and the solution will present itself to the player.- Beautiful 2.5D aethetic.- Interesting story with plenty of mystery trying to find out who is sabotaging things on the ship and for what reason.- Nice accessibility options to tailor the experience to the player.- While it's minimal and one occurs during major events/revelations, the voice acting was very good.Cons:- Fast travel system was a little awkward to get used to.- The last case didn't have any obvious clues as to the answer, was mostly a guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: You're Stella, raised on the Zephyr, a spaceship with the long-time mission to bring human life to an alternate Earth. The society on the ship initially seems well organized and guided, but soon you realize that not everyone on the ship might be happy with the fate of being an in-between generation without any free will regarding important life choices.  As the Chief of Security you are soon confronted with intrigues, conspiracies and betrayal. Just as in Lacuna you have to read carefully and be observant - and of course again your choices matter and affect the outcome of the game. Another excellent crime story by DigiTales Interactive!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Agree with others that it's a step down from Lacuna, but that's not to say it's bad. Both games are pretty good, I just think Lacuna has better pacing and higher stakes. Maybe it's just me but I didn't feel as emotionally involved with the outcome of the game other than getting the ending that I think was the good one (which I think I did).Which brings me to the next issue: like Lacuna, it's pretty hard to explore multiple endings unless I'm missing something. Once you complete the game for the first time it should just let you backtrack as needed to explore the alternate endings.Game suffers from some issues with backtracking in general and the next steps not being immediately clear, but I don't think this is necessarily an issue. Take some time to stop and review clues and most of the puzzles are able to be deduced. I think the non-linearity of the game is a step up from Lacuna and makes it feel a bit more immersive.None of the puzzles seem all that contrived or too difficult. I managed 9/10 and some other people mention the one I didn't solve and unless we're all missing something I think the Paper Trail puzzle is a bit strange, in that the logical answer isn't the correct one. Again, could be a skill issue, but whatever.Overall would give this one a 8/10. Great title from a developer who I hope keeps making these awesome story games. Can't wait to see what they implement in the next one (hopefully there will be a next one).
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Overall quality of everything is quite high. - Plot is captivating.- Puzzles are solvable, but interesting.Cons:- Museum case is very similar to the one from Lacuna. If you played it, you will understand. Moreover, it is simpler.- Final case feels a little underwhelming. Overall, very good. Finished the game in two evenings and had a good time. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons was an absolute delight to play! I wasn’t expecting for the story to move me and be as well written as it was. The characters each had a distinct personality, even though there were a lot of them to keep track of. The mystery solving aspect of the game kept me engaged with the story line and was very fun to solve. The only gripe I had overall was the lack of guidance in some aspects of the cases. There were times when I needed to give the right piece of evidence to the right person in order to figure out a clue but it wasn’t always clear what evidence or what person. There was also one case where the game basically tells you that you’ll figure out a mechanic as you go along which was very confusing to me. Outside of those few things (which could very easily be user error) I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun challenge and a riveting, detective style experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In this episode I'm checking out a new Sci-Fi detective RPG called Between Horizons.This game was developed by DigiTales Interactive, who also worked on the excellent Detective RPG Lacuna, which ive also reviewed, and was published by Assemble Entertainment who released the Post Apocalyptic Side Scroller Far - Lone Sails. Between Horizons takes place in the far future, following the colony ship called the Zephyr, which is seeking to settle on a new planet called Europa. The story follows Stella, a security officer on the ship, who is investigating a criminal trying to access the ships network. A routine case goes horribly wrong when Stellas father is killed by the criminal they are pursuing. Stepping into her fathers role as the chief of security, she is thrust into a plot to prevent the Zephyr from reaching its destination along with threatening the lives of everyone on board.Players will take control of Stella, as she tackles several high profile cases accross the Zephyr, using her detective skills, knowledge of the ship and her high tech tools to gather evidence, interview suspects and apprehend the criminals. Stella will also navigate the complex politics of the key factions of the crew as well as deal with the challenges of surviving deep space. DigiTales has taken everything they have learned from working on Lacuna to create a vastly improved experience with Between Horizons, whilst keeping their accessible gameplay and signature mixed 2D/3D graphics style. Between Horizons also boasts a similar narrative style to Lacuna, where decisions permanently alter the direction of the campaign and determine which one of the games multiple endings that you will recieve.This game is an worthy successor to Lacuna and showcases the developers growth in the indie gaming market. I highly recommend this game to fans of DigiTales games or player who enjoy Detective stylegames.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. _childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: With tight gameplay, a tense atmosphere, a fantastic soundtrack, and a story that delves into some deep themes, this game packs a punch even though it can be finished in 5-7 hours. The generation ship setting is ripe with intrigue and moral dilemmas, and Between Horizons really makes the most of this. I have not played a game quite like this before, with no combat, platforming, just investigation and deduction, but I'm glad I did. Give it a try if you like sci fi, mysteries, or just great storytelling.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: While the user interface takes some getting used to, and the script could have used a little more polish, the story and investigative gameplay of Between Horizons are highly entertaining. I really enjoyed playing as Stella, molding both her character and the story’s ultimate outcome with my dialogue choices and efficiency as the Zephyr’s chief of security. I loved roaming around the spaceship looking for clues and talking to other characters, each with their own unique personality and background, with not one but ten different mysteries to investigate. And there’s a great amount of detailed worldbuilding, both visually and narratively found in this game. It’s a shame that trying for a different outcome demands another complete playthrough, but I was very satisfied with the ending I got, despite only finding the right solution for eight out of ten cases. Even if you’re like me and generally have no real affinity for science fiction, this intriguing detective/sci-fi story aims for the stars, and as far as I’m concerned it’s mission successful!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons promises a detective adventure, and delivers it accordingly.- Lore: human inhabitants of a spaceship are on "The Mission": traveling to a far away destination, an inhabitable planet that will serve as humanity's colony. Unfortunately, due to the distance between Earth and this planet, a few generations are expected to live and die inside this spaceship before it can arrive at its destination. Albeit simple, this is the main point of Between Horizons' lore and the center of the story.- Art: 2.5D graphics that have upgraded visuals from the developer's previous game, Lacuna.- Music: the soundtracks are similar throughout the game's stages and resemble previous scores included in Lacuna.- Gameplay: a classic detective UI, which has several tabs that can be scrolled through. Traveling around the map is simple and interacting with objects of interest follows a classic pattern in the genre. There are very few issues, notably with text placement displayed during narrative bits.   - Story: the inhabitants of the starship are submitted to a rigid social structure, which forms the basis of the conflict. Story progression involves secrets about The Mission, a murder investigation, turmoil caused by an elusive, dissident group, and actions taken by a mysterious hacker. These cases are investigated following each act of the story, until a conclusion for them (or lack of it) is reached.Between Horizons lives up to the promises and intentions of its developer. As is the case with Lacuna, it is a short, but effective narrative, very suitable for a few hours of your leisure time.82/100
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: So let me say first off, that I like this game. I really enjoyed the story and most of the cases and really recommend it. It was a fun few hours playing and then trying different endings and I really recommend it for anyone who likes point and clicks, mysteries or enjoyed the excellent Lacuna.I'd rate the cases as being on the easy side (maybe even easier than Lacuna) but sometimes I'm in the mood for easier cases and sometimes I'm in the mood for harder puzzles.I do have a few nitpicks though. First, there's a lot of QOL elements that would make the game nicer (I know that they're being worked on):- Evidence should really be sorted, it's really annoying trying to find someone you met in the list when they're not organized alphabetically. I somehow always remember the names rather than their face so I keep clicking on a few faces to see if it's the correct person. - I wish it was possible to toggle running, pressing shift with wasd hurts my hands for no reason. There's never a reason in this game to walk instead of running so why not allow me to toggle running all the time?- It would be great to be able to skip the monologues. When trying to test different endings, it's rather annoying to have to wait for a monologue to finish when you've already read it multiple times. - Related but a way to fast skip previously read dialogue (like some visual novels) would also be great- Like Lacuna, I wish after finishing the game it was possible to go back in time and try different things. Right now you can only replay since the last save just before you submit the last evidence. I don't want to give explicit spoilers but there are some decisions that I would have liked to explore the consequences of.  For example, the impact of not helping a person earlier in the game. Or, to see what happens if you decide not to forgive someone. - I would love a way to locate where crew members are, I spent so much time just walking around trying to find one specific character. Lastly we come to the main criticisms I have:1. Overall, I feel that the game would have been better with more writing and more dialogues. Right now, the discussions with most characters is very limited, after a single time talking to them the only remaining interactions are through showing them evidence. They often don't even react to the evidence you show even though they should. I expected rose to have something to say about fertilizers even if it's not relevant to the case. I expected Eric's son to have something to say about his father and vice versa... Because of this, the world doesn't feel as alive as it should. Even the feeling of betrayal that the main character feels towards some people is muted because there's very little interactions between them. We get to know that they are friends but there are barely any casual interactions.  2. Similarly, when you walk around, you never hear other people's conversations. This is a bit of a wasted opportunity because it would have made the world feel more alive while at the same time showing the growing discontent. 3. The intro's pacing is too fast, I think having some slice of life elements after the funeral would have helped with character development.  4. Lacuna had more relaxing moments dedicated to introspection when smoking, when talking to his wife or relaxing on the sofa. Neil felt more real thanks to them. Again, while this might sound like a lot of criticisms, I genuinely like this game and think it's very good. It's just that it could have been amazing if not for those faults.
