_childDocuments_.review: I played Lacuna and this game seemed like a great way to continue the fun. This was an entertaining little detective story game with a satisfying ending, and I definitely recommend it to point-and-click detective game fans.However, there were some silly issues that should have been fixed which made it pointlessly annoying in some places. I hope the dev considers these improvements!:1. A high number of typos in the dialogue. Anyone who simply sat down and played this game through once should have easily many of caught these.2. The fast travel was a pain, as was navigating the map with the keyboard. Specifically, picking the navigation room on the map was a huge pain to do with the keyboard, as other options around it kept getting jumped to instead.3. Finding solutions to certain cases was so easy that I thought it must have been a trick. I discovered who  was almost immediately after I began collecting clues for it from , but had to wait until the end to actually point the finger.  It was very odd to allow us to solve it so quickly and yet not be able to say anything. More bizarre was that I still had to sit around and collect more clues from  to confirm what I already knew.  quest should have only partially revealed the truth to avoid this, not fully revealed it.4. Frustratingly, the clues I collected for the main dissident did not compile into the case once it finally opened. I had to comb back through the "general" section to read through all of them.5. Finding the damn Activities Room keeper was incredibly annoying at the beginning. There was no indication of where he would be and he appeared to basically be in a random area of the map. Running around blindly hoping to stumble across someone is NOT fun gameplay. It felt like I was doing this several times throughout the game, such as when trying to find the Teacher. There should have been some way to quickly locate or ask around about people's location if they are not in their workplace.6. It was extremely disappointing that I could not talk about  to Luis, nor visit the brig for the last several acts of the game. I thought the interrogation room was going to be seen in action at least once. It felt very sketchy and weird that my character, the chief of Security, was not allowed to see her cronies (one of whom is described as a creep) interrogate people. This is never brought up again, so it left a bad taste in my mouth--as if my character was responsible for torture of those interrogated. I wish there was more interesting flavor text in general in this game beyond the bare minimum. It would have gone a long way toward making our actions feel more weighty in the moment as opposed to the text dump at the very end.7. The leader of the uprising being
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Lacuna, you will enjoy Between Horizons. The core elements have been improved, the new setting is fitting and the story has enough branches to make it worth at least two or three replays. There are two or three minor points where I would have loved to have more input in certain decisions (spoilers!) but overall this is more than a worthy successor to Lacuna.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, and I'm in awe!The visual style, music, soundscape and ambience is great and just sucks you right in! The setting and story are very grounded and believable sci-fi which I really appreciate. It is so tempting to explain things away with sci-fi tech, but everything relevant to the story makes sense and is reasonable!I was one of the playtesters of an early version, but they only covered the first 2 acts and was focused on bugs and general gameplay. So experiencing the whole story now gave me a new picture of the game!I love the system of collecting evidence and filling out the form yourselves, leaving room for failure while the story kept going. It gives great replay value and discussions with friends! Something their previous game, Lacuna, also did really well.The 10 hours of gameplay feel almost perfect, the pace is overall really well done with a few scenes feeling rushed. But that doesn't take anything away. Every hobby detective out there should give this game a chance, it's definitely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Lacuna, and if you did as well, this is a solid game with great ideas.  I will say, it's quite buggy, with a lot of branching dialogue issues at the moment (a few days after release) so I might wait a couple of weeks for things to get ironed out, but the concept and puzzle system of the game are well done, and it is graphically beautiful.  Very reminiscent of the TV series SILO in fact.  But for $15 bucks, its an easy buy to play a clever and pretty indie like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: More similar to Lacuna than it initially appears, it's basically a narrative-focused adventure game with a few puzzles and branching story points.  The plot, visuals, and sounds are excellent.  Backtracking through the same corridors or trying to intuit where the game wants you to go next can drag the pace down a bit.  Also, prior to the third act, most of the choices you make are simply whether you get a case right or wrong.Overall length was about 4 hours for me.  I doubt the content would be drastically different on replay, though there would be a few different things to experience.  I quite enjoyed my time with Between Horizons, and will probably play it again at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to play games that are more action packed, however I've been trying to expand my horizons (see what I did there?) and I'm so glad I gave this game chance! For a game that's dialogue heavy, I had a blast, I enjoyed interogat- I mean talking with the various characters to piece together the truth.Going through each case, determining whether my info was correct, solving puzzles, all of it was entertaining! The fact that you can give a wrong answer and it affects the story really makes you be thorough with your investigation! There's multiple endings as well and while I COULD have done a bit better I think overall I got a good ending! The story has it's twists and turns but how things end up hinge on your skills as a detective and the choices you make...You can rush through the game or take your time to discover clues, the game will take you around 7hrs give or take depending on how indecisive you are lolDefinitely give this game a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Great atmosphere, enjoyable characters, challenging cases to solve, and multiple endings for story satisfaction and replay-ability. Stella and her character arc is very relatable for my age group. Being able to control everything with one hand on the keyboard was super convenient, and hopefully adds some accessibility for other people who may need that. Only complaints: 1. the game still has some minor bugs, but nothing that breaks the game, 2. would have preferred a save system opposed to auto saves alone so that the player could go back and fix case solution mistakes at their leisure, and 3. would have liked to have a filter on the evidence so that it could be easier to sort and look through, making it easier to look at what evidence the player has of every category, and saving time having to scroll through the evidence list once the player gets further into the game. 10/10 enjoyed this experience, looking forward to trying out Lacuna next.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended. It's not overly long and failure indeed is an option. Unexpectedly, I enjoyed the puzzles too, which often require pen and paper and sometimes elementary algebra (but can be solved at a glance as well). I wouldn't pretend to *know* but I did feel like a detective piecing together the evidence.Totally unexpectedly for a quest, I might want to replay this one. I haven't quite solved everything, and I'm interested to see more dialogue and endings.Oh, graphics and soundtrack are very nice. Overall atmosphere is top-notch. Characters are not super-deep, but not entirely shallow either.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked Lacuna by the same devs and was looking forward for more games like it. Between Horizons does not disappoint. The story and the soundtrack are very solid. One of the plot twists was quite cool: I haven't seen it in any other media dealing with interstellar travel (not going to spoil what it is).There are some bugs in the game, but I am sure that the devs will fix it eventually (I played the game literally on the release day and there were no game breaking ones). My only real problem is somewhat clunky evidence tab, I hope they'll add an option to sort items or group them by type (e.g people, locations etc).P.S. There is a space cat that you can pet.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! I played it for a little more than two hours and everything about this game just feels right. I really like detective games and this does not disappoint as such. Above all the game got me with its world, that feels alive and meaningful but not staged. Looking forward to enjoy the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Really good detective adventure set on a generational ship.The puzzles aren't too difficult and they all are logical. I was able to solve them all except for one where I needed help. You can solve cases by collecting clues, talking to people and showing clues to people. It's an interesting system that turns out well.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little detective game. It especially shines in the story department, telling a compelling and gripping story over the course of 5 to 7 hours for your first playthrough. There are a lot of different choices one can take, meaning there is a reasonable amount of replayability, even if its not a Baldurs Gate 3 when it comes to choiches and consequence. The artstyle is well executed for the most part, even if its not a visual masterpiece. I encountered no bugs or visual glitches, the game ran well and was on a tip top technical state. Any gripes i might have with the game are small blemishes that are quickly forgotten in the excellent storytelling. Definitely recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time with this game. On the first screen it warns you that it's autosaves only, you can't make saves whenever you want. This combined with the fact that you can make the wrong conclusions in investigations led me to a bit of analysis paralysis. It turns out that wasn't a big deal, restarting and immediately giving the conclusions to the investigations you know the correct answer to was quick. I did a few playthroughs back to back. My first one I very thoroughly scoured for clues (and had a great time!), the next ones I zoomed through.Loved the setting and theme and art and puzzles. Easy recommend from me.PS: There's one place where you can get stuck in the geometry. In the discord they mention a fix is done but hasn't been uploaded to steam as of this writing. The workaround is to unstuck yourself using the fast travel system. [EDIT: The bug was fixed in version 1.0.5, new buyers shouldn't run into it.]
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable sidescroller game - and one that doesn't hold your hand, it genuinely makes you think! Some early bugs were very quickly squashed by the devs (responsive in the steam forum, quickly putting out patches and explaining things)Will be replaying this to try different options/decisions! Overall 9/10 for the game, 10/10 for dev responsiveness.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: If you were a fan of Lacuna you will love Between Horizons! I tried out the demo and it hooked me into buying the whole game. Truly a fantastic detective game with a great story that can be uncovered. My first playthrough was enjoyable and I liked figuring out the answers to cases through my own investigation of the clues/testimony. I messed up a lot on the right answers for the last few cases which I corrected my second playthrough and I ended up with a totally different ending (the best one imo). Lots of investigation can happen (or not) that can totally change how the story plays out. All in all, Between Horizons is a great game, and I can tell a lot of love was put into it! Thanks Digitales!
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review: Between Horizons is a gorgeous game, discussing an interesting setting and its implications to society. I espacially liked the plausibility of all characters. Nothing is absolutly black and white, and I could understand every characters motivation and why they choose their respective course of action.Everyone who likes a short but intensive storytelling experiences with a huge bunch of brain fodder to think about, will love this game as much as I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Between Horizons

_childDocuments_.review:
Between Horizons is set aboard the Zephyr, humanity's first generation ship en route to another star. You assume the role of Stella, who was born on the ship 24 years ago and recently inherited her father's post as Chief of Security.

Dive into the conspiracy behind the incident that threatens to disrupt the Zephyr's social order and foil its mission.

name: TT Isle Of Man: Ride on the Edge 3
detailed_description: The Isle of Man Tourist Trophy is the most epic, most dangerous and most spectacular race in the world. It is a course of over 60 kms on the roads of the Isle of Man, includes 264 bends, and requires high-powered bikes specially prepared for the race. The riders who compete in it train their whole lives for the chance to win the ultimate accolade: being crowned champion of the Isle of Man TT. The game includes all the official content of the latest TT (riders, bikes, teams, course) for a unique and true-to-life experience. You are plunged into the middle of the TT as if you were there. And you will feel all the passion and tension this race generates. Whether you compete in the Supersport or Superbike class, you can ride on 32 different circuits and over 200 kms of roads. Simply choose one of the 38 official riders available: 21 in Superbike and 17 in Supersport. The game features easy-to-learn and intuitive riding with ultra-realistic and cutting-edge physics for the ultimate immersion and simulation quality. Many professional riders even use the game to train and learn the circuit. The major new feature in this edition is an open world that can be used to freely ride around the roads of the Isle of Man to find different game modes and a wide range of challenges: - Quick Race - Career Mode - Online Multiplayer - Weekly and monthly races

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: All in all an ok game.  There is a lot of things that need some work, but it is playable and does not crash.  Some things are missing from TTIOM2, a number of things are better than TTIOM2, and some things are worse than TTIOM2.  I give it a 5/10 and cautiously recommend buying the game as long as the devs offer some fixes for the issues.  I will update my review depending on what gets fixed or not.  I wish steam offered a middle review as I don't think this game is a full thumbs down.Positives:The bike wheeling is much improved over TTIOM2, you can actually do proper wheelies now and through multiple gears.Bike handles jumps much better and you can get a wobble just like in real life if you don't perfectly nail the landing.Slow speed handling actually exists now unlike TTIOM2 and the bike behaves and is animated correctly for a racing bike.The TT and other circuits are well modeled, if a tiny bit more bumpy than the real track (still better than TTIOM2 which sometimes felt like I was riding on broken pavement due to how rough it was).Graphics are quite good for a sim game, The sun and the shade and your vision are modeled realistically The super sport bikes are, in general, handling really well, and only need some slight tweaking.Most of the animations are correct to the real world.Note: before I get to the issues, I have tested both types of bikes with stock and gold parts, tuned and untuned, and my controller is configured properly.  While some of these issues can be lessened slightly with tuning and parts, they are still issuesMajor Issues:Bikes do not corner right, it impossible to make high speed turns in game at the same speeds as in real life such as Ballagarey.  Bikes feel like they are under-steering a fair bit more than they should be vs their real life counterparts, especially with all gold parts.Sport bikes are a little too stiff at high speed, making hard to get turned in at corners like Ballagarey in time making just barely possible to do at real world speed. Superbikes are considerably worse off.  The corner at Ballagarey is impossible to take full tilt like you can in real life on a super bike, because you can't get the bike over in time due to how stiff the handling gets at high speed.The handling characteristics of super bikes are much closer to sport bikes than portrayed in the game, aside from the power difference, the weight is only around 10% higher, the wheels and tires are largely the same (with the same centrifugal forces).  The only other difference is the engine centrifugal force is slightly higher due to the increased engine mass.  Which is why superbikes are a just a bit slower to shift left to right vs a super sport bike.  That mass and centrifugal force difference also makes super bikes a bit more stable on rough patchesSuper bikes tend to be a bit more stable due to their slightly higher weight and higher engine centrifugal force. But in game they feel less stable.Super bikes still have this nasty tendency to suddenly snap over 45-90 degrees (almost always to the left) while racing with the bike upright (10% or less lean angle).  I've had this happen just before jumps, and particularly the corner going into bray hill and also going down bray hill.  This almost never happens to the super sport bikesReal world motorcycles tend to get the shakes not when wheeling over a jump and the rear lands, but when the front tire lands, particularly the front wheel is not perfectly straightThe rider head position is incorrect in all the views.  In helmet and the other two first person on motorcycle views, the rider's head is about 5 inches too low (it is currently set where a chin camera would be, not the rider's eyes).  In 3rd person the rider's head clips into the windshield when starting, and then his chin is clipped inside the tank when fully tucked.  Generally real world riders tend to either look through the top part of the windscreen or just over top of the windscreen.High speed wheelies are more stable in real life, and are not prone to shaking back and forth as in game.Moderate Issues:Soundscape is very muddy and muted particularly in 3rd person.  It is fine for the helmet view as racers wear ear plugs, and the helmet also mutes the soundIt does not feel like the rider is shifting his weight back and forth, appropriately for keeping the wheel down when accelerating, and particularly for braking.  One tends to lean over the handlebars when accelerating, and push back and up when braking (some riders even stand up slightly while braking).  Also when taking a jump riders will stand up on the pegs a bit so their legs absorb the shock of landing.I would like to have options to turn individual HUD elements on or off (such as the mini-map, the right side display with revs gear etc, and any other ones.Why were the names of the different parts of the track removed from the HUD?Please remember my settings for all bikes when it comes to ABS, TCS etc, or at least let me set them before the race starts.The game has 8 circuits not 34.  The 34 figure includes the 8 full circuits, and all the sections you can break the 8 into.What happened to practice against the clock mode where I can just practice as long as I want?It would be nice if I could feel better when the bike is about to lose grip through controller vibration better, also why no trigger vibrations for Xbox controller?Minor Annoyances:It would be nice if I could set the brake pressure I want for the rear brake when using a button, as that sudden full rear brake can destabilizes the bikeI personally do not care about bug splats, but they should be optional if added.I don't care for the damage skins and would like to disable them.  The idea I can pick up a bike after a 150mph crash, and the bike (and rider) just being a bit scuffed & muddied up with some dents and scrapes is kind of silly.I also would like to get rid of that invulnerability glow when you get back on your bike after a crash.That sharp bang sound when you come off the bike is kind of dumb, particularly for a low side or slow speed fall where there isn't much of an impact.Would be nice if I could teleport around in free roamReal world racing bikes all have quick shifters, the only time you need to use the clutch is going from neutral to first gear while launching, after that it is just left foot click up/down (and very quick to shift)Most riders tend to keep the right foot down and the left foot on the peg when stopped (so you can shift from neutral to first).  Only utter novices push off with their feet (especially both feet), and you move your foot up on the peg when you hit the clutch friction zone and the bike starts moving.I am a bit confused why the people working on the bikes in your paddock are in full flame retardant gear. That clothing is appropriate when in the pits working with hot bikes and fuel, not in the paddock on a cold unfueled bike. Also no sane rider will keep his helmet on or the racing suit & armor in the middle of summer, while the techs work on the bike.About me:I’ve been riding for about 40 years now, raced in lower divisions at full racing speeds (mostly racing tracks though, I'm not quite crazy enough to go full tilt on road courses, but I was on the TT once as a closed circuit for a lap), and have raced a few of the racing spec bikes that are in the game (though not the same years) including the Kawasaki ZX-6R, Honda CBR1000RR SP, and BMW S1000RR. I still do track days with my own bikes, but I don't race any more.

_childDocuments_.review: So after gathering my thoughts I would like to say what I think about Ride on The Edge 3.Let's start from BAD:- CAREER (if you can call it like that)Totally unrelated to the reality of road racing. First and second game done it way better with building founds and fame to get better bikes, sponsored races and eventually qualifying for TT. All that gave sense of progress. In number three its just collection of random events one discovers in free roam mode but that's due to the fact that ALL of the racing happens on the Isle of Man.No character creation, just selection of TT riders and teams. Also rider models all look the same, and lets be honest John McGuinnes was never that slim... xD- BIKE UPGRADES ( if You can call it like that)So this idea is reused from second game. In my opinion totally unnecessary. Why? You earn upgrade points by completing events on the map. No visual change to the bike, just slight spec boost.  And to begin with you start on a fully upgraded (visually) race bike in either Supersport or Superbike category. - RAIN ( not just any rain but rainstorm)And as much as Weather goes I'm sure that Isle Of Man gets tons of rain in reality but lets be hones, during TT normally in JUNE any rain will postpone or cancel racing / qualifying. So I don't really get why we need it in this game.... ?- LONG SECTIONSThis relates to number of sections tracks are divided. Most of tacks in the game are long with the TT cousre being 37,73 miles long being the longest. its divided to 6 sections. Previous games had it divided to 12, and in my opinion that made it easier to learn. Other tracks in the game suffer from same problem. I can see this being one of the reasons why it puts people off, it took my 78h in the first game to learn the track.  Now to NEUTRAL:- FREE ROAMFirst on the list is free roam. It's fun initially but apart from discovering events on the map there in no practical reason to do much of it.- GRAPHICSGood enough. - BIKE SELECTIONAs the game is based on the recent 2022 season (and since November, 2023 season as well) in two categories SUPERSPORT and SUPERBIKE class. No Classics No Supertwins.Also I wish that rider selection would represent different riding styles.And finally GOOD: - PHYSICSAs far as my personal experience goes best out of all three games. Similar to RIMS RACING, bit more stiff with three levels of realism. Pro Tip:Go to control settings and change sensitivity on steering, throttle and brake to at least 0.To do this you need to go to change it manually to every button in the controls menu. When you pres on say steer left button menu will pop up and sensitivity setting will be there.... ;D    - CAMERAS AND SENSE OF SPEED Helmet camera is great, very rewarding if you'll master it ( I haven't yet.. xD ). 3rd person is my favourite. Sense of speed suffers but still challenging and satisfying enough.- SOUND OF THE BIKES- TT TRACKVery well represented as far as comparison to videos and on board footage of race goes.- MUCH INFOIf want learn more about the history of the race and the Isle Of Man this game has got section where you can learn about interesting stuff. FINAL WORD:I'm a big fun of RIMS RACING (made by same devs) and IOM TT Ride on The Edge games so for me it was must have. Its a solid motorcycle racing game but sadly not great. Definitely not for everyone due to very in my opinion steep learning curve. I hope next time we'll get better career mode. Grab it on offer if unsure skip if you come from RIDE 4/5 background... ;DBut for all TT heads its big YES!

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to preface my review by saying, I am a motorcycle rider, and while I have never done extreme track time on a ultra-high performance motorcycle, I have ridden some supersports as well as scooters and everything in between, as well as some high performance driving and track time in cars.I'll start with what I liked about TT Isle of Man 3- visuals are nice, audio is quite good and the bikes sound pretty close to their real-world counterparts.  Game ran really well on my gaming laptop, seems well optimized.  I was surprised to see all the different track layouts and not just the big main mountain course.  Sense of speed is good and it is utterly terrifying at high speed going through the tight course.There are a lot of things I don't like, some I could live with, but ultimately the reason why I refunded was due to the physics.  I get it, there is a steep learning curve to this game.  I tweaked controller settings according to what everyone recommended.  But after 2 hours of practicing and not feeling like I was getting anywhere at all?  I gotta pass.  It would be different if I knew it was my fault.  But there were many instances where my intuition and experience told me to do something, and the bike didn't react at all the way it would have in real life.  I'll try to list some  examples.1. I noticed zero difference from beginner physics to experienced physics. 2. Transition from one lean angle to the opposite side.  Even on the supersport bikes, it seems to take forever, and taking some of the back and fourth turns at what the racing line says is a good speed, the bike simply will not transition fast enough, causing a crash.  Watching real-live footage of the TT in the same sections where this happens, the real life riders are capable of doing it much faster than it happens in-game.3. The racing line in general seems a little too enthusiastic at times, I dip into a corner and the racing line is green, maintaining speed, but the bike understeers, I am full-lean and continuing to understeer, racing line is still green, then crash- i'm into the wall.4. You can be at full lean, all assists off, and pin the throttle, and the bike stays on course.  Likewise, you can aggressively downshift expecting the rear tire to skid out, nothing happens.5. Sometimes, leaning hard into a turn, it requires an extreme amount of counter-steering to straighten the bike back up.  Other times, it stands back up immediately and since you are used to counter-steering, you go to far and crash into the other side of the track.Other things that bothered me but aren't as bad as the physics-The UI is terrible.  Some screens, you can mouse click on the buttons, others you can't, and have to use a controller button, which isn't always obvious.  Too much menuing.The open-world concept is really poorly done.  Just let me select free ride, or time trial, or practice, or season... don't just dump me in to an open world without any clear instructions, and require me to go back into a menu system to actually select what I want to do.  The open world concept adds literally nothing to the game at all.And some suggestions that I think would really improve the overall experience.  Outside of correcting the physics.- Have a fictional "practice" track, that is a simple, fairly short and easy to memorize road course, with a wide track surface, run off areas, etc.. so you can really learn the flow of the bikes better.  Even the shortest layout in TT is much longer than most circuit tracks and there is still very little room for error.  - Have a "follow me" mode, where an AI bike will ride ahead and you follow, and have the pace increase slowly as you get better and learn the course. (this would work well with the fictional practice track too)- More bikes to choose would also be awesome.  Some of the classic bikes as well as the "super twins" class.  A slower bike would also really help improve the learning curve some, and an old bike on 18" spoked wheels with bias-ply tires would be a whole lot of fun!I really wanted to like this game enough to keep it, and maybe if more things were corrected I would consider purchasing it again, but for now, it's too frustrating of an experience, and it contradicts a lot of what I already know and have learned about riding, to continue to fight with.  I feel like the TT is one of the most incredible motorsport events of our time and it should be done right.

_childDocuments_.review: EDITS:I have spent a bit more time on the game, and Upgraded the bikes a bit more. The upgraded bikes are an improvement in handling to the Standard bikes (as perhaps they should be), but to me it feels like they're simply better suited to the behaviour coding of the game, rather than actual bike upgrades. There have been some patches, amending slipstream, and statistics of the bikes, as well as more developer interaction already since the first 2 (the reply here was a pleasant surprise for me props for that one).That being said the patches seem to have introduced some bugs.The first being that after about 1.5 hours of playing I lose sound. Not entirely sure why that is but its only happened recently since the latest update. The second and equally game braking, is that the grass has started entering the track again, really badly this time.Overall the patches are improving, and I do enjoy playing, but it is still not where it needs to be for me honestly.Original review:The game overall has a bit more "polish" than TT2. The models are done this time. and the sounds are a little bit better, although there is a "Desync" bug at the time of writing.That, really is it. The handling is really not good. It still handles like a car. Just with some more animations. RiMS was the same, but even that "covered" the poor physics up better.The previous TT games had more content. There really is no reason to remove the content from the game, as its unlicensed anyway, and while fictional, they were unique and of a decent quality.There are new bikes, but most are reskins of previous bikes, with some upgrades to things like dashboards etc. But it is still Supersport and Superbike. No Supertwins, Lightweights, or Sidecars.There is a free roam feature, but that is a poor feature in itself, as there are no new roads. Just bits of other courses that are available. And for a game set now purely on the IoM (with no Irish or British tracks), the lack of inclusion of at least the S100 and Jurby Airfield is really, really poor.Multiplayer is shocking. The servers make the game almost unplayable, with bikes warping all over the road, tracks not loading while riding on them, basically all the same bugs as the previous games.Career mode is poor. As there isn't one. It is now known as "seasons" mode, which you pick a rider and ride a season as that rider. There is no custom rider, no signatures to enter the TT, no managing a schedule, no nothing of what made the previous games even remotely enjoyable.This game is purely a learning tool for the TT course, and a pretty p**s poor one at that. The challenge of the TT course is still there, and the leader-board hunting of the previous games is entire reason to play this game. Ah well, back to PCSX2 and Jester for me. Better handling, better representation of riding the TT course, and its free as well.TLDR: Same broken game as previous, less content, and overall brings nothing to the table but bits people didn't ask for.

_childDocuments_.review: Again I can only wonder why Milestone wasn't approached to make this considering they have at the very least a proven track record in making motorbike games. Instead RaceWard who made RiMS Racing was asked..., who have made ONE bike racing game which received very mixed reviews. I honestly don't know who sits the development and marketing boards of these games and makes these decisions but they need to be sacked. If you're not familiar with RiMS ... terrible menus systems, lacklustre graphics (especially for the 2nd quarter of 2023), if Ride's bikes physics are a 5/10, then RiMS and OIMTT 3 are only a 6.5/10 at best (yes I ride motorbikes irl).This game at the price point is disappointing at best and daylight robbery at worst.Menus . . the game basically dumps you on the Isle of Man to ride around Forza Horizon style. Except with none of the fun of FH. And you have to press pause to access the game menus and then you have to go into the map to find any events or time trials to see how you actually do on the Mountain Course you have to go to markers on the map and hold X ot whatever to access your event/garage. Why they went this way with the interface is beyond me. It's fronking awfulThe bike selection is all the official riders as you'd expect, with all the official bikes from the Superbike and Super-sport class. But nothing else, no classics like in IOMTT 2, not other road courses at all. Its the Mountain course or made up sections from the Isle of Man. I don't mind that really but it would be nice to see some of the other road courses from the road racing series which leads up to the IOMTT. On the upside, the moutain course at least looks pretty nice and weather effects are alright. I expected to essentially have the option to enter the IOMTT as a privateer (which is a real thing) and work up from there, but this doesn't exist in game either. You pick an offical rider, that's it. Even in the MotoGP games you could essentially start as a privateer. Its almost as if the game is made by people who have only heard of the IOMTT in passing but have not a single funking clue about it. The bike 'upgrades' are generic as flock and essentially the usual nonsensical tier method where teir 2 brakes give you some RNG bonus over tier 1 and you need each previous tier to unlock the rest. What?? I mean WHAT? You're already on a fully race prepped superbike for crying out loud? What even is this? *VISIBLE CONFUSION*Talking of that, the models seem ripped right out of RiMS because even though they're fully prepped race bikes they still have all the road switch gear on them which is stupid as hell. Its a total lack of effort and attention to detail.The riding is... alright.The physics and feel is massively improved over the last iteration no doubt about it but that's not saying much in all honestly. The bikes are still FAR too twitchy, especially at speed and have no real sense of mass in many scenarios. And are a long way from as manoeuvrable as they ought to be for race bikes. You get these weird snap wheelies out of nowhere every-time you mount a crest in the road and I can tell you that doesn't happen irl. The bike will come up don't get me wrong and a 1000cc has no issue lifting the front, but its progressive. The braking feels....lifeless. Its like the braking force is necked by the game somehow, the stoppers on race bikes are uncommonly good. In IOMTT 3 they're about passable. The rear brake does literally nothing. Trail braking is perilous as hell with the game seemingly RNG'ing if you're gonna tuck the front or not, this was a complaint in the previous iteration as well, trial braking is a thing RaceWard, you managed to get it mostly right in RiMS. wtf. The onboard assists are lack lustre as well, more intrusive than intuitive, ride without ABS/TCS it literally makes no difference. The game will still lowside you into a corner even with it on. or highside you on the way out - or neither, I've had the rear spinning up in 2nd on corner exit with TCS on (?? what the actual farm ??) and with it off and not highsided. Anti wheelie (or lift control) is intrusive (it isn't irl btw), and basically works as a throttle cut which then unbalances the bike at corner exit causing stupid crashes but leave it off and the thing will jump into the air if you so much as look at the throttle. Again, this isn't fracking realistic! I ride a CBR1000RR, yeah it'll pick the front up with ease, but not like the game implies at all. Its progressive and controllable on the rear brake (which does frank all in the game as I've said)IOMTT3 is better than the previous iterations and so the fronking hell it should be quite frankly. However it is disgustingly bad for the triple A price-tagged game for something that feels and looks this mediocre. If you like the IOMTT and hated the other games this is better to ride without a doubt, but thats about it. Do I recommend? In a sale.. like a 75% off sale, sure. Full price? Hell fronking no.

_childDocuments_.review: I will write the review again to make it shorter.I absolutely love the game. Physics are a nice balance of arcadish behaviour (stability of bikes, rear brake not locking the rear wheel, excessive edge grip, no crash if you hit the curb in many situations) and simulation (tire wear, lateral front tire grip if you brake, wheelies, stoppies). Game allows to change bike set up like tires pressure, suspension, gear ratio what has impact on bike behaviour. Physics is the biggest improvement comparing to TT2 and what makes the game enjoyable. Some may complain about slow direction change (fast left roght corners) in chicanes, but it can be slightly improved by increasing controler sensitivity in settings. Although it is not very realistic, it is not that irritating. On full, realistic settings bike feel alive and you really can feel the bumps thanks to a great interaction with track.Graphics are quite decent. It is inprovement comparing to RiMS but objects suddenly showing up in close distance and some misaligned models (like hands on handlebars or rider disappearing inside bike model) are not nice. There are some immersion elements that I really miss: watersprays when racing in wet look poor, lack of bugs on visor and bike also were removed - what is big shame. The biggest negative of TT3 is lack of content and customisation. You can choose from few existing real life riders from Superbike and Supersport classes. It is impossible to make your own custom bike and rider, or change riding style that may fit your preferences. Addition of Supertwins and Historic iconic bikes would be a big positive. Addition of more roads on the IoM would be even better. At first Isle of Man replica may overwhelm you, because there are lots of road to ride on. But shortly after I started to play I realised that it is not enough to keep me entertained for longer time. I miss especially northern and southern roads to visit Point of Ayre, Castletown or have it possible to ride on Billown Circuit (Southern 100). Multiplayer is simple but entertaining. Sometimes other players were jumping from sode to side, however I blame worse connection for it. Big shame there is no multiplayer freeroam on the Isle as this would be fantastic addition.In general. Game is big step forward. Very nice physics compensate lack of content and customisation, however some may feel disappointed. Less experienced players will feel frustrated at first because the entertainment comes after learning the tracks and understanding that motorbikes are not cars and you can not do some things. I hope developers will add more tracks and bikes in future and fix those few bugs (but non game braking) that exist.

_childDocuments_.review: I held off from buying this as it's never on sale. Finally found it for 1/3 of it's full price. Glad I waited.Impressions from my first hour: Animations are stiff. Rider moves like he is having seizures and the bike has no suspension. He vibrates like on a go-kart.Visuals are poor. You either get muddy textures with TAA or disable it and get PS2 graphics. Mind you I play on 2K...Optimization is lacking. Low FPS and stutters on all kind of powerful systems. Texture pop-in and poor LOD in the distance. On some roads the markings on the pavement load just 30 meters in front of you.Physics are questionable, at best. My man leans the 600cc sportbikes like he is on a Busa...Changing direction is the slowest of any bike game. My impression is that this is done to artificially increase the difficulty, since there is almost no physics engine to speak of. 100% of the difficulty in this game comes from knowing the track. You can slam the throttle at corner exit at full lean and get ZERO rear wheel spin. There is no possible way to highside the bike. It's so bad that you can't even do a donut. Almost impossible to lock the brakes either. Electronics seem to do nothing. It's a mess.Gameplay loop is poorly designed. You enter a challenge that takes 25 minutes of pretty hard riding. You fail it at the end = get no rewards AT ALL. On top of that you have no rewind option.Manual gears? Good luck launching because the game gives you no way of modulating the clutch input. It's either on/off so it's always a wheelie.You dialed-in your electronics? The game randomizes them after every event or booting the game. In Ride4 the game even remembers your electronics PER BIKE. GET A GRIP!It's a shame that Ride4 doesn't have more Isle of Man content otherwise there would be no need for this game to exist.Fingers crossed for Ride5 to have it as DLCs.Worst of all, similar to another KT Engine game I own (WRC Generations), it's getting no updates already just shortly after release. I will be on the lookout for a big patch that addresses some or all of those points. _childDocuments_.review: Title: A solid racing game with room for improvementTT Isle of Man - Ride on the Edge 3 is a solid racing game that delivers a satisfying experience for fans of motorcycle racing. Here are my thoughts on some of the key aspects of the game:Physics: The handling in this game is amazing. The motorcycles feel planted on the ground and I can really feel their mass, especially at the highest difficulty settings, which I think are the best. The realistic physics make the game challenging but also rewarding when you finally master the controls.Graphics: While some of the shots in the game are great, others are a bit lackluster, especially in the mountain part. The model bikes are amazing and top-level, but some of their damaged textures have poor resolution. Overall, the graphics could use some improvement in certain areas.Game Modes and Career: The game offers basic content for a standard gameplay experience, but I think it falls short in terms of game modes and career options. Creating my own rider and team is a must-have for any racing game in this era, and I wish that was included in this game. However, the standard game modes are still enjoyable and provide a good challenge.Overall, TT3 is a solid racing game with room for improvement. The physic is fantastic, the graphics could use some work, and the game modes and career options could be more expansive. If you're a pure fan of motorcycle racing, you'll likely enjoy this game sinche the simulation model is the best out there!

_childDocuments_.review: TT3 Takes the great simulation from Rims Racing and combines it with an immersive open world set on the Isle of Man itself. Having the open world on the Isle of Man is absolutely awesome, and is much preferred to previous games open world on made up roads in Ireland. I want to point out that contrary to what T_balls implies in his review, the open world feature is not a time waster. Races and challenges are in different locations on the map, but you are not required to ride to the location to start a race. You can simply open the map and start the race from there. The simulation is much improved from the last game to be more realistic and challenging, well also being more predictable. In the previous game you might fly off your bike instantly while going straight over a small bump. TT2 also gave your tires infinite grip and would not allow you to lean too far. Though that might make the game easier if you want a more realistic simulation of a motorcycle than TT3 is the right game for you. However if you want to just chill out and go fast around a beautiful course, then you can simply turn down the simulation and it becomes much more difficult to lose control of the bike. A few people have been whining about not being able to flip the bike side to side in a split second. Besides the fact that they are exaggerating how much slower the transition is compared to other games, there are settings that you can change to make it more sensitive. You can also improve the way you enter a corner by trail braking more, as a bike will turn in better when the front is loaded. If you going though a fast corner that doesn't require braking you can let off slightly as you initial the lean. The upgrading process is much more convenient and easy to use than the previous game. All you need to do is get upgrade points from racing, then spend them on upgrades. There is no requirement to complete other things to unlock access to high level upgrades before you can buy them.  There are a couple bugs I have found as per our usual arrangement with new games I guess. One bug involves not being able to shift gears when you start a race or challenge. This seems to only happen occasionally, and when it does you can fix it by exiting the race, shifting gear in the open world (you are always in the open world if not in a race or challenge), then restart the race. You do not need to restart the game. I have also experienced an audio bug where after riding around for about 30 minutes sometimes the engine sound at low RPM will be distorted and shifting sounds slower. However no one else seems to have had that issue. Overall I recommend this game to any racing fan, and especially any motorcycle racing fan. The game is quite immersive and can also be a great teacher of all things TT related.

_childDocuments_.review: They did it! I didn't have to rebind my controls every time i restarted the game! Jokes aside, Raceward has proven that they really understand motorcycles and it's amazing to see. I played a lot of Rims and a lot of the other 2 tt games. Those were fun because you could go fast without consequences. They were cheesy but really fun. Rims though was the experience i was really looking for. Great first person camera, realistic rider movement and physics. It was a great game with a number of annoying flaws. This game is much better with fixing the annoyances that rims had, but it still has a few problems.I'll get the things I am sure people will bring up out of the way first. While you don't have to bind your controls every time you load the game, there is still no controller vibration. It's non existent on any controller besides the default xbox one controller.  I mainly play with the Elite 2 controller but I also tried the Dualsense and neither had vibration. Frame syncing does not work as intended. It's not a big deal to me to play at 60fps but the vsync doesn't work right. It doesn't allow tearing but it stutters and smears the image. Without it on and just using gsync, it is much worse. Those things aside. I immediately wanted to try testing bike setups, rain traction, AI races and of course the main TT course. Bike setup changes do have a better intended impact than they did in Rims, especially on the low level parts. Rain traction is good. It's easier in this game because you don't cook your tires like you do in Rims, but I still didn't have to be that cautious. I purposely got in the way of the AI and I didn't get thrown of the bike like Rims without even realizing what was really happening. So they seem to act better. Not sure yet about how fast they are on everything but they didn't seem to take crazy lines like they did on many of the tracks in Rims. I had to do the main track twice before writing this because it was just so good. With all the HUD off and music off. It's just so immersive to go around and to go fast. I do have the track memorized from years of rfactor and the other tt games, so that does help shorten the learning process, but it is so good. The audio, feeling of speed, dangerous turns, and of course the jump are all really exciting. So far this seems like another Raceward game I will spend a few hundred more hours in. I do really hope that controller issues get sorted out this time though, because sadly, it was never really fixed in Rims.

_childDocuments_.review: This is undoubtedly the best motorbike game out there (and probably the best of next years!). Finally, the TT series has received a boost in overall quality and, most importantly, in terms of the physics! The bike is extremely "physical", perfectly planted on the surface and with a completely revised weight system that significantly influences its leaning, which is now much more solid and structured than in the past. Now, each model requires a REAL different approach to driving, and I find it incredibly stimulating to have to learn the different motorbike models and understand their qualities and weaknesses to tackle the roads proposed by the game! The career is certainly long and complex to deal with, and perhaps some challenges are too demanding, but the open road feature is an interesting first approach for a change of direction in the world of motorbike games.On the technical side, the game is not perfect, it's true. Although graphically the game is superior to previous chapters, I expected a slightly different quality and, above all, greater precision in the rendering of some views of the island and the road sections. On the other hand, some areas of the Isle of Man are completely new and reproduced extremely faithfully, fantastic to ride at high speeds with your bikes, and this is a great added value!

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game too much though. 3 and a half stars. Sometimes it can go well, and be cool, and the sense of speed is very realistic. However, aside from the 'weighted' feel of cornering a bike at such speeds, the physics are abysmal. Sometimes, the bike will just randomly flip over and crash, as if somebody were to have sideswiped you. Even in a pretty straight line (such as bray hill, corner just before K trees, etc). The game does this frequently, and with the lack of a rewind option in the event a crash with no fault of your own happens, it gets annoying incredibly quickly having to respawn all the way back at Bray hill and start your lap completely over again. Not to mention all the riders have the same riding style, which is odd considering I dont remember Michael Rutter being an elbow down rider. The hit boxes can be extreme. Sometimes, ill get a corner perfect, such as Barragarow, and I wont visually see myself touch the cobble house, and my bike clearly hasn't hit it, yet my rider will just fly off as if hes been flicked off by a giant. In real life, riders get close and scrape their shoulders all the time (Macau for example), in this game, thats not possible. Its a shame, as I both really hate and really enjoy the game. The game has a very good sense of speed, and the bikes sound pretty good. But it just has so many ridiculous moments I find I struggle to enjoy it for a long amount of time.
_childDocuments_.name: TT Isle Of Man: Ride on the Edge 3

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say physics wise it's absolutely night and day once you get the controls dialled in for dead zones' and sensitivity to your controller it's brilliant. I refunded it twice before I figure that out I wanted to enjoy the game and couldn't until I stopped being an idiot and took the time to appreciate I can't just pick it up and attack it like the previous versions, I would say this is a successive title in name alone with comparison to the previous two titles owing to the massive discrepancy with the physics and approach in general.I have to say I would recommend the game for those tempted but caveat it with it will likely not be fun until taking the time to correct the inputs to the settings your controller needs not the game suggests! Also free ride is around the Isle of Man and that allows for exploration of the island without limiting yourself to specific sections or the whole circuit to have to learn, it will perfectly allow for you to take a section in one direction and then back allowing you to truly gain a feel of the track inside and out. I am disappointed by the lack of bike choice I know I know but it would be great to have some of the classic bikes and more obscure ones from over the years in an open category for multiplayer use perhaps? I mean a 500cc two stroke would be awesome as long as it's not that suter alone but some of the older ones like the YZR500 or the TZ.After some time in the game, one simply cannot complete a race without some AI taking them out randomly, even on the straights.... 100% AI are just beyond a joke.

_childDocuments_.review: I Have genuinely enjoyed  playing this game, but I will admit that if you can wait for a sale, I would definitely do that. $50 is a bit steep in my honest opinion. I don't think that this game will have much longevity to it.I began this game on realistic difficulty with all of the assists turned off, and although it's been very challenging, the learning process has actually been quite fun. This particular game requires so much concentration that I've found it to be incredibly easy to lose myself in it, and because of that I've found this to be very relaxing to just zone out to.Though I do recommend this game, there are two things I don't like about it. The scenery in this game kind of flickers as you go by and it can be incredibly distracting. I've adjusted my settings multiple times and have yet to mitigate this issue. There's also ZERO customization in this game, you have a list of professional racers to choose from and that's who you will play as throughout the season.Aside from the two things listed above, this game is solid. This is my first sportbike game in ages and it's been humbling to play. Find me on Twitch if you'd like to see me struggle to go fast. xD*Update: May 16, 2023*I got into a multiplayer lobby for the first time yesterday with a friend that I've convinced to purchase the game. I ran into a bug when I opened the map that caused my HUD to disappear and rendered all of my controls unresponsive. I tried tabbing out and tabbing back in and I pressed every button on my controller and my keyboard, but I ultimately had to restart my game to regain functionality. There also seems to be a large amount of desync in multiplayer. My buddy and I were sharing screens while we played online and found that there were multiple instances that we made contact during the race that didn't actually happen on our own screens. If the net coding could be improved, multiplayer could have much closer and enjoyable racing in the future.In regards to the customization, if we could get a personal character, a selection of gear, helmets, bikes, and liveries, I think that would go a long way for a lot of players.

_childDocuments_.review: It seems a lot of the problems from the previous 2 games have been fixed in this version, it is certainly the best of the 3 games so far. The 600's and the 1000's feel very planted to the road now and the game is very enjoyable to play. Complaints would be FPS issues when your monitor is not set at 60fps or 120fps, the game locks the fps at 60fps with vsync on so if your set at anything other than 60fps or 120fps you will get stutter. However, if you set 120fps on your monitor and run the game in borderless fullscreen mode with the game set to 60fps locked and the vsync on it forces the game to run at a smooth and fast 120fps, looks good on my machine with a 3070 gfx card. There isn't a great deal of content or extra things to do but there is enough to enable you to get your bike upgraded to full before you attempt the TT, it also allows novices to get used to the bike at slower speeds, on a level 1 engine for instance you get 140mph and with a level 5 your doing 198mph and getting there quicker so it helps with the learning curve of staying on the track. If your a TT fan though or a bike racing fan, you won't get a better bike game than this, it feels more playable now on both the 600 and 1000 and there are a good amount of difficulty settings in game now too allowing even a total novice to still feel like they have a chance of winning. Overall, very much like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It has the best feel of any motorcycle game I've played, predictable physics that allow for accurate cornering and corrections, I've even been able to save a tank slapper, so I'm really enjoying it, but there's some issues and strange game design decisions on the career mode that make it a mixed bag that will annoy some people:1. Framerate seems to be locked at 60fps and there can be some frame drops in busy areas2. You can't design your own rider, can only pick one of the existing real riders and bikes3. For the races, the qualifying sessions take place on a different course than the actual race, which makes no sense and makes the qualifying not be as useful for course familiarity as it should be4. Before you can enter the TT race, you first have to complete a career full of smaller course races to be eligible to enter the TT5. Even if you get those career feeder races complete and are in the final TT qualifier but somehow exit the qualifying session to take a phone call or something, then you fail qualifying for the TT race, and on reload the qualifier for it is no longer available, I had to restart the career at that pointOverall I'm really enjoying this title much more than I have the past IOM, Ride, MotoGP titles, but I hope they can sort out the strange career mode design decisions in updates, otherwise this will be a flawed game.

_childDocuments_.review: Racing down Glencrutchery road the first time, and every time is nothing short of spectacular. This game exceeded my expectations in many ways. The developers have captured the essence of riding a motorcycle to a fine tip. There hasn't been one single moment where I didn't deserved a crash, not once. You can easily feel and control the level of adhesion as you rocket down Kirk Micheal. You even get nervous when confronting important braking points. Or you have to check your speed as your bike compresses down the daunting Barregarrow drop. The AI also surprised me. No longer are they dumb obstacles. I've had fun back and forth battles. Their racing lines seem fine, and they overtake appropriately. The physics, the richness of the island, the bikes roaring engines and fierce pops and screams are a labour of love. I cannot wait, and I hope there is DLC available in the future. Cons:- The Suzuki and Kawasaki bikes are a level below the Honda, BMW and Yamaha bikes in their audio quality and overall likeness to their real life counterpart. To the point where I'd rather not even use them.- The time of day visuals in TT2 were more realistic and enjoyable. I feel like the only real usable time of day is Afternoon/Clear and rain. - No mixed weather during a race. In TT2 it was always fun running into overcast, or even fog. It adds to the sense of a journey, like chapters in a book. - There's an annoying filter that makes my computer screen appear dirty. I suppose it replicates a visor, but it's even present in 3rd person, and it cannot be removed. It's so bad, I dread the mountain part of the track where it's extra viable.  - I think there should be a semi-automatic option for for the tuck position as I do use the manual tuck, but do not like holding down a face button, or my analog stick forward for long periods of time. But when I use automatic tuck, the rider is often stuck in the tucked position and I cannot lean back (it's locked). The alternative tweak that should have been made is a throttle/tuck tandem. When there is no throttle applied, or lets say only 20-40% throttle the rider sits upright. It looks really funny when you aren't applying gas and your riders body position is fully tucked. - The riders on the Triumph bikes are not positioned correctly at all. Their chest sits about 10 inches off the tank, and they're barley reaching the handlebars like a 10 year old on a full sized motorcycle. It looks very odd. - The custom racing settings don't save, so I need constantly need to adjust settings I would never change, like AI difficulty. - You cannot lock the rear tire. The rear brake seems to do very little in general. - The Xbox one impulse triggers do not work (They worked in TT2)Overall, this is one of my favourite games of all time. If the issues above were fixed, it wouldn't be a contest. I can't even enjoy another motorcycle game now. The realism is off the charts in this title. I would highly recommend this game to any racing and motorcycle enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy playing this game. I don't understand why some people are negative about physics and handling in the game. From my point of view physics is on point what would you except from handling real bike. It surprises me that those comments are from people which are riding those machines, or they say they do, in real life.I have never played this game before, or any from the franchise. I have spend quiet some time playing RIDE and I can assume you that RIDE physics seems so off compared to this title. Riding those bikes in RIDE feels so easy, the bikes forgave you alot of things, even non player guy could handle theese with assists-off, which some people may like it, but I am not that kind of person.There were alot of comments about that leaning is so slow and its very difficult. Guys, what do you expect from the bike doing 200 kmph. At those speeds you have to have techniques and use momentum of the body and the bike to be able to lean more agile. You have to be set way before the turn to be able to get through the corner. You can't just start turning in the corner and expect to go through it. And this is the exact thing that this game allows you, to prepare for that turn, to play with that bike to be able to make that corner, little brake tap to help you lean from the one side to another, just play with it, like on the real machine. Yes, it is really difficult, but riding at those speeds in real life is so - Very important to say is that you have to setup controller setting to suit you. It will take some time but I guarantee you if you give it some time, you will find the exact point where it seems so on point. In this game, the bike does not forgive you any mistakes with assists-off. Great even that assists-on are not oversaturated. If you make mistake, the game will let you handle it for yourself and if you do it right, you will get out of it, if not, you are on the ground. The physics is so on point that you can use momentum of the bike, throttle power, braking power and leaning to play with it, which gives you the real feeling of the bike. That is the exact reason why I felt love with this game. The feeling of the speed, the bumps. It gives you the exact same or very close feelings from the bike handling as you would except from real machine. Of course there are few here and theres which can be improved, but from overal point of view it feels great and on point. Also the game offers you one of the best camera angles, which very contribute to the experience.There are some bugs and problems and improvements that could be done that I have found so far:- It seems that this game is mained to be played on controller. It have very bad keyboard support- At some places in the game the colliders of the game objects, mainly of walls, are missing or are way beyond the textures, which can cause you some frustration when you fall of the bike not even touching the wall because you collided with the missaligned collider. But there are only two spots on the map that I have found so far, so nothing crazy- Very iritating texture at the end of the course, at the secion of open plains, where backround textures of montains are not properly finished. It would be great if they had better details, as it gives you hard time to focus on the road, as textures in the backround are popping, missing and glitching- Graphically the game looks awesome, but implementation of FXAA and TAA is horrible. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly, the trailer doesn't do this game justice. Upon actually playing the game and removing the motion blur, bloom and vignette the graphics are an improvement over the previous versions by a long shot. The scenery looks more realistic with the buildings and streets off the main TT course being a good approximation of what you'd find in the Isle of Man in general.    The bike handling is improved from the last version too, like that game there is an option to 'Autotuck' and 'Sit up' when braking and in this game the rider actually does this. The controls are very sharp, there are options to increase deadzone for gamepads as just the slightest movement will input into the bikes direction. There's also an option to reduce the amount of travel you have to move the stick and if one game didn't need it it's this ! Infact it could do with adjusting the other way. Bear in mind this is with riding the bikes given to you at the start of the game and the tuning set ups by default so some adjustment could tune things to your liking better in that respect.  The bike handles the rises in a more predictable and realistic way, those spots where you could ride on one lap, do the exact same thing the following lap and find yourself sliding on your arse seem to of been solved ! At last !   The bike handles really well at speed and something I've noticed in this version is the fence posts whizz by selling that your travelling at a fair old pelt on.     It will take time to adapt to the new handling no doubt though. For one the engine sound feedback just seems off and difficult to dial in - in that your either going way too fast or too slow. There isn't that distinction from the audio somehow. The BIGGEST fault though is the slow / low speed handing it's all too easy with the merest input to find yourself veering right into the wall at the slightest touch. I've also noticed sometimes the bike will lowside when really it shouldn't be doing. It's like there's a certain speed range at the low end where you've got to be so careful. Get out of this range and your back to smooth handling again.  Once again the engine sounds do not help you judge, though once you get used to the game I suppose you'd adapt.  With this evil handling though comes kerbs that are more forgiving than they ever would be, sometimes that is, so that's a plus.        So in summary your buying this game purely for the TT isle of man circuit, there are other bits around the island that is done well graphically, which will be good for a blast around I guess.       The handling is much improved in the previous dodgy areas, but still suffers from low speed oversteer and appointment with the nearest dry stone wall / field or someones front garden of your choice.      Graphics are improved and the trailers do not do this justice at all. Plus they convey speed excellently      The engine sound has it's moments but is still dire **After spending more time with the game, have got used to the sound differences. It is actually very good though really shines in 3rd person the best - which is a view I don't play in. I found backing the difficulty down one from the highest made a massive difference re handling at low speeds. Definitely the best Motorbike sim/game out there.

_childDocuments_.review: "A wonderful blend of RiMS Racing and the most amazing race in the world."-Sprolly GEDIT after more play time:This game is not easy, but nor is the actual TT for motorcycle racers, taking an average of 2 souls (officially) each year. The "unofficial" death toll being higher, of course. If you want to compare this game to something like MotoGP or WorldSBK, go play MotoGP or WorldSBK, as you'll be happier. For the third release of the TT title games, it feels like the team who created this game actually read what we commented about TT2 and took that into consideration while making this game. If you liked RiMS, it sort of feels (to me) like a cleaned up version of that, but racing on the Isle of Man. I also haven't had to repair anything yet, like you do in RiMS, so that's nice too. I love that this game has actual Big Name TT racers, lets you freely roam around the roads, has information about the TT, and events leading up to the TT sprinkled in. Oh, I also enjoy seeing the IOMTT website on the starting posts where the last person to touch some of these racers is holding your shoulder before you launch. Something about little things like that really make the game pop for me. I bought the Racing Fan edition with the McGuinness Special Livery and Career Starter Pack, because, why not.I still think it would be cool if your after-race replay would take the highlights and coolest moments of your race and whip up a quick "youtube" video of your race with music, like we get each year on youtube in real life. Maybe showing a minute or two of passing and jumping or flying past points of interest at extreme speeds. It's rewarding to make some of these turns properly at high speeds and survive, so why not exploit that feeling with silly things to reward ourselves with a shot of serotonin.SIDECARS and side events throughout the fortweek:I'm not sure if sidecars will ever be a part of these games, but who knows?POINTS AND STARTER PACK:The Starter Pack gives you 380 points to upgrade your parts for each riders bike, each part upgrade ranging from costs of 10-31 (give or take). I don't think you can get to a garage to buy any upgrades at the start until you've finished your first race and made points, so I ended up getting a few more points on top of the 380 and was able to max-upgraded (Level 5 - Gold) the more important parts for Hickman's BMW before grinding out more points for the other parts. The best part is, it's a free pack. I like to try to tune my bikes, but you'll probably need to adjust the bike every time you upgrade parts. I find myself not making many points in the season races, as I'm a bit picky and try to get the race in 1 go without crashing so I keep restarting and restarting and...It will take a long time this way. I suppose we just have to suck it up and get what we get until the bike is fully upgraded and you can find the tuning sweet spot. Then, git gud.CONTROLLER:I'm playing with 'Realistic' settings using a PS4 controller (with a USB wire) that I must have "dropped" a long time ago when I had a "beverage" or two, but it's working well enough with Steam and the game. I had to reset the left and right turning inputs and then adjust the sensitivity and dead spots or the bike just turns right (and a couple times it only went to the left..I have no idea why the random change). I checked out the discussions and found other people had this issue. I ended up putting the sensitivity to 10 and the dead zone to 10 as well. I might bring the dead zones down a bit and test on the open roads between races to find the sweet spot.MULTIPLAYER:I've tried to play online several times, but I find no games. I have no input here, but at least there are races that you can put your time trial for the Tourist Trophy against other players.TAKEAWAY:I feel like you "hit the nail on the head" with this one for game play, but it may not be for everyone. The season is a bit smaller/slower than other titles and pits you against other peoples times every several hours (the race-time expiration depends on the race). Other than that, it's quite the challenge and gives your vision that crazy psychedelic wavy motion when you're done concentrating for 5-100+ minutes per race. The wall moves like water when I'm done with a race for a minute or two until my eyes and brain settle down.If anyone was curious:Dunlop for SuportsportHickman for SuperbikeI'm not worthy enough to play as John McGuinness #1.Slow is steady and steady is fast.

_childDocuments_.review: TT3 is a recent release that delivers an exciting motorbike racing experience. Below are my thoughts:The game's physics are truly impressive, providing an authentic sense of the road's bumpiness. It adds a level of realism that enhances the overall immersion, making every ride feel intense and thrilling.The sound design in this game is top-notch, with immersive and high-quality motorbike sounds. The roaring engines, screeching tires, and other audio effects contribute to the overall adrenaline-pumping experience.One standout feature is the variety of playable camera angles. While all cameras offer a satisfying perspective, the first-person view, in particular, is exceptional compared to other similar racing titles. It enhances the feeling of being on the bike, adding to the overall immersion.TT3 strikes a great balance with its difficulty modes. It caters to both beginners and seasoned racing players. It offers a welcoming experience for newcomers to the genre, while also providing a challenging and satisfying gameplay experience for hardcore motorbike racing enthusiasts.Overall, the game delivers an exhilarating motorbike racing experience with its impressive physics, immersive sound design, playable camera angles, and well-tuned difficulty modes. Whether you're a casual player or a hardcore racing fan, this game has something to offer, making it a worthwhile.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible open world motorcycle racing game!!  (needle scratches off the record...) BUT ONLY IN SINGLE PLAYER.  That's right, if you want multiplayer you have to pick a track. Thus making it nearly useless amongst all the other gaming options we have available to us, and most of them we already own. Devs, you have to enable multiplayer for the open world map. It's the most stupidly obvious thing in game design history.Updating after more time with the gameStill sorely missing the ability to ride in the open map with my friends. It makes it worse that it's such a beautiful game and feels so good to play. I've played a lot of MotoGP, since some of the earliest versions. I played all the Rides, Rims Racing, GP Bikes (erf) and so on. I ride in real life (S1000RR). I even have a teensy bit of track time (via California Superbike School L1-L4). This game feels really, really good. Don't get me wrong with my earlier review. It's fun to play. It's addictive, even. AND I'll concede that having a 35 mile track to ride in multiplayer isn't bad. But that said, missing the mark with open world/non-competitive meet-and-greet riding like one would see in Forza Horizons is a glaring omission and shoots me through the heart. The rest of it is SO good. Looks great, sounds are amazing, and feels great to play. Is it realistic?  Meh...but most probably don't want a truly realistic m/c sim. MotoGP is closer and so many walk away from the franchise because "it's too hard to play". TT3 strike a very, very nice balance between "this is how it's done in real life" and "this feels fun to play". Rider animations are a little...dramatic...at times. E.g., I don't know about you guys but shifting doesn't cause me to have a full-body spasm. I get the intention, but some of the movements are overdone. The points system and parts management...it's not my favorite but definitely a huge improvement over how Rims Racing approached gameplay. I think the problem is that it simply isn't very easy to navigate and use. As a UXD/R in real life, I think this part of the game needs the most rework in terms of usability. But, without the ability to just ride the island, and come across another rider, and challenge them to race or to invite friends to ride as a group and leverage those opportunities then you can expect the multiplayer component to be completely dead within a month. Just like in EVERY OTHER racing sim on the market EXCEPT Forza Horizons (and I'm not including iRacing in that statement because that's a whole other thing from this or Forza or Ride or even MotoGP). You are >< this close to the perfect motorcycle racing game, but also only halfway there. I have about a thousand more ideas of where this can go. Devs, you're off to a great start but just missing the opportunity to fill some critical gaps in the online sim racing arena. I really hope you stick with it.
