_childDocuments_.name: Lil' Guardsman

_childDocuments_.review:
In this deduction adventure, you play as Lil - an unlikely 12-year-old hero - covering your dad's shift at the guard shed and are tasked with deciding the fate of over 100 unique characters.

You will question humans, elves, goblins, cyclopses, and other fantasy creatures using your powers of deduction to determine who to admit or deny based on how they respond to your questions and your trusty tools. Sending visitors to jail, inadvertently zapping them to smithereens, or letting them go on their merry way are all part of the job. But be careful: who you let through the castle gates will determine the kingdom's fate.

name: Cookie Cutter
detailed_description: Cookie Cutter, which IGN calls a “GORY, GORGEOUS, AND BLOODY GOOD METROIDVANIA,” features lovingly crafted hand-drawn 2D visuals, challenging and satisfying combat, a wild dystopian world full of irreverent characters, buckets of violence, and underneath it all a sweet, beautiful story. The Void. The Matter. The Megastructure. A dystopian world with an egomaniac leader determined to unveil the secrets of the universe. INFONET promised a utopia built on the backs of tireless androids called Denzels. It was a lie. 200 years later the planet is decaying and the mysterious Red Seed has been stolen. Raz, a renegade mechanic, searches a hidden lab and discovers the Denzel Cherry, butchered and left for dead, clinging to life by sheer will alone. Her creator—and the love of her life, Doctor Shinji Fallon—has been taken by a demented sicko and Cherry intends to make him—and anybody or anything who gets in her way—pay. Fueled by love and powered by rage, join Cherry on a blood-soaked quest for revenge as she explores the massive Megastructure and eviscerates the armies of INFONET in an unforgettable over-the-top 2D platformer that breaks tropes and bones. Cookie Cutter is unabashedly irreverent, violent, and risqué. Become Cherry, a badass android on a rage-filled and love-driven quest. To save her beloved creator she’ll explore and fight her way through a unique illustrated sci-fi dystopian world as she chainsaw-murders anybody who stands in her way. Every frame of this immersive experience is drawn by hand with copious amounts of love. That means epic, fall-out-of-your-chair visuals. Grotesque bugs and menacing robots. Gargantuan bosses. Ridiculous weapons, special moves, and brutal gory finishers. All of it brought to life with benchmark 2D animation. Whether you’re ripping the wings off overgrown mosquitos, impaling mini-bosses, crushing robots on Cherry’s motorcycle, or kick-punch-uppercut-stomping waves of foes with complex combos, you won’t find a better fighting experience with responsiveness and all the flair you could ask for in a Metroidvania. Far future dystopia? Check. An android companion turned rage-filled killer? Check. Over-the-top characters and enemies? Check. Buckets of blood? Of course. Experience our bizarre tale, inspired by Japanese manga and Quentin Tarantino films, through 10 huge zones, each weirder than the next.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and animations are absolutely amazing, the gameplay/combat is servicable for the price. The story is intriguing but has some rough spots I think. Still a recommend overall easily.Edit after completion: the ending was poorly executed... that on top of the poor writing/dialogue, this is very close to a do not recommend. Consider this a neutral review where I would really only recommend the game if you love the genre and have played all of the best metroidvanias already.
_childDocuments_.name: Cookie Cutter

_childDocuments_.review: About 3/4 of the way through, a passable, combat-focused Metroidvania decides it wants to be a precision platformer instead by introducing cramped sections filled with spikes that kill you on impact, and checkpoint placements that make you waste several minutes between attempts. Cookie Cutter's controls simply are not tight enough to do this well. The first 3/4 of the game hides its crappy story and button masher combat behind enough stylistic flair that it didn't bother me, but when the game switches gears and decides to place the spotlight on its level design, it falls apart.
_childDocuments_.name: Cookie Cutter

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to say I cannot recommend this at this point. The art is delicious. The story is serviceable. I am smitten with the MC and am onboard for the rest. Cookie Cutter feels like a love letter to Tank Girl x Appleseed x Dead Cells x The Pro and it is low-brow candy for the soul. But there are so many other issues that have made my so far 2 hour play experience less and less fun. - Sound constantly drops, necessitating restart- Have had x2 animation glitches, necessitating restart- zero trophies have popped for me, and I have cleared at least a few at this point- the parry function is infuriating and inconsistent - enemy variety and population is sparse- voice acting is terrible, probably not needed at allI really really wanted to like this one and I do think there's a lot of good going on here. I am glad I got it on sale price, though, because for $20 there is much better out there, as others have said.Edit 12/21: I am stoked to see the big patch roll out because despite the issues I still really want CC to be successful (and I was looking forward to some holiday catharsis so I don't burn this whole thing down). That said, here's my big overarching gripe: I am tired of paying to be a play tester. Under very few other circumstances would it be acceptable for an entity to advertise a product, sell something broken to a bunch of people, and then expect for there to be no clap back, but for some reason this has become an acceptable practice in the gaming industry. Cookie Cutter was an impulsive first-day purchase and I still feel salty that I spent money I earned through my own labor + time I struggle to come up with and had an acutely un-fun experience because of technical issues. What is the expectation for the consumer at that point? Bend over and take it? I am refraining from writing an entire op-ed here but I guess my ultimate point is C.R.E.A.M. and I hope to see smaller devs in particular act smarter so that they can manage releases better so we can enjoy all this brilliant stuff they're creating. I am tired of feeling guilted into positive reviews just because something is a "labor of love" and has all the best intentions in the world. The whole thing gives me diarrhea.Edit 12/29: community reports ongoing issues despite patches. Refunded. I don't have time for multiple playthroughs to *maybe* get a complete experience. What a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=================A fantastic looking Metroidvania with tragic combat that knocks it down from "great buy" to "sale only"Good Stuff================- The in game animations look fantastic and everything in the world oozes style. From the characters to the world and background designs, everything looks and moves very smoothly and even the more outlandish "(and uhh....gross) designs blend together incredibly well.- Cherry controls very well with regard to her movements and navigating around the map is never a huge issue. She's just fast enough where world travel doesn't feel horrible until...Bad Stuff===================- Strap in folks, cause this game has some of the, bar-none, worst combat in a Metroidvania I've played recently. I really struggle to think of a worse entry on combat alone and I'll try to list all the ones I can remember:     - You take tremendous damage from most enemies with end game enemies sometimes doing up to half your base health in a single hit     - Everything juggles you when you get hit, and you juggle everything you hit. Enemies and you will fly around like ping-pong balls, bounding off everything ( especially stage hazards) when hit. This makes getting in combos a pain in the ass.     - Your basic attack, even fully upgraded with badges ( the games level up system) do garbage damage and enemies take forever to kill. This is offset by the weapons you get which do big hits but basically lock you in place for a long period of time.     - The parry timing is so tight it may as well be impossible, I don't think I used the mechanic a single time.     - Grit, a stat tied to parry, is equally useless, supposedly depleting it makes the enemy vulnerable for a few minutes.     - You have to execute enemies when they get low for health and void energy ( mana), however there is no uniform health for this just "low." Considering you are locked into attack animations, you will often kill enemies you mean to execute, getting no resources.     - Enemies are still completely functional during an execute, and in fact, all the time. So if you are doing an execute to get health back, but another enemy is next to you mid swing? Well guess what! You're getting hit and maybe even killed. Even more fun when surrounded by multiple enemies and you get hit 4-5 times ensuring death.     - No hit-stun. When you get hit you're getting juggled and quite possible right into something that's going to damage you further.     - Enemies will sometimes follow you between screens, especially flying enemies to whom the room borders are merely a suggestion. This is at its best when you run out of a room with an enemy just winding up to hit you. I promise if you walk back into the room from the same door, you're getting smacked.- After losing to the last boss I thought " Oh I can change my loadout and try him again." Well guess what? the last boss autosave room is PAST the last loadout station for the game, meaning your stuck with your build. This is a minor thing but oh my GOD is it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid for no reason.- There's an elevator in the last zone that takes like 3 minutes to get to the top as a "lol funny" joke. Too bad there are a few combat rooms after this and if you die? Back to the bottom to appreciate the hilarity of the joke again. Again, this is a minor thing but so damn unnecessary.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that feels like it should have been an animated short rather than a game.For how nice it looks, the game is severely lacking, combat has poor hit feedback, hitboxes are iffy, and some things are over-animated without any means of animation cancelling.What does this mean for the game? You get flash game tier "too light feeling for how well animated it is" in a game where any flow is often completely stifled by needing to watch an (admittedly very well done) animation before your next move will work. The most obvious of these is the parry, when you land on a platform you can't immediately parry, you have to wait for the landing animation to play out. Is this intended? Shrug. Is this fun? Naw lol.I noticed at the start that even though your character is all messed up and bleeding (fun to waggle the stick left and right here as there's no turning animation), the blood coming from your character doesn't even leave a smear on the floor. This wouldn't be a problem normally, but it turns out the rest of the game is like that too - bland environments that feel like both you and the enemies aren't there due to lack of decals, or any hint of interactivity that could possibly let you suspend your disbelief for 2 seconds.I think what this all boils down to is a lack of polish, enemies will sometimes teleport both you and themselves into random locations during the (well animated) finishers, your character will often run in front of objects that should clearly be in the background, it just... looks crappy.Again, despite the clear effort that's gone into the animations, where's that sort of love for the other artistic aspects? Ignoring the glaring flaws with the gameplay, it's just not very fun to look at, or attempt to interact with.

_childDocuments_.review: Souls-like fan? Give it a go. Otherwise, avoid or get in a bundle/sale - Humble Bundle is where I got it.Platforming: Poor.Game often tries to help you by letting you grab onto a ledge that you're near enough to hold on to. The problem is that it is inconsistent. Sometimes when you expect it to help and it doesn't you miss the jump, other times when you don't think it will, you climb onto a ledge that has spikes/fire/lightning in the way and take ~30 dmg for the assist. Jumping off the edge of a platform often ignores your jump input; not pleasant when the game is a platformer.Combat: Decent-ish, but with a caveat.The abilities have been fun to use for the most part, but I find that enemies just hit too hard (some doing 10-20 damage per hit, others hitting you for 30-50 per hit - you only have a base of 100 HP). I don't mind a hard fight, but for there to be a mob gang up on me, it's really a 2-3 hit system before you're back in the fight which is irritating. Respawning is fortunately quick; I hate games that force you to wait through a cutscene or make a comment at you before you can jump into the fray again. I still think that Astlibra Revision did the best at this; if you died at a boss it'd ask if you would like to restart the fight.Basic attacks suck. The game has an upgrade system to increase their power, but really they suck. The heavy attack weapons are fine, but often are underwhelming or get you stuck in an animation that you can't cancel out of and don't give you i-frames to block projectiles. Flying enemies and projectiles are the worst part of this game. You can parry enemy moves in melee, but ranged you have really no defense but a single dodge roll/dash that has a cooldown that's long enough to get you into trouble. When fighting the DH Shooter and Macer, I could take down the Macer repeatedly with Parry, but the Shooter was the one ending the fight and causing reloads (doing 20-40 damage per shot).Parrying is the second worst part of combat. The frame-perfect inputs for it to work are awful, and if you take the hit (being a fraction of a second early/late) you're punished severely. The window needs to be longer, and sometimes it felt as though it was ignoring my inputs.Finishing moves are epic, but the game relies on you doing them for ease of healing and void generation. That said, pressing the activation button if in the middle of a combo or swarm of enemies doesn't always activate them. Consistency is lacking. Some moments where you kill a boss by parrying perfectly feel damn good...other times it gets you killed for your efforts.Reward for Effort: Mostly good with a few exceptions.It was often pretty good at rewarding you with powers, add-ons, money, or energy cells when you found a treasure chest. There were times, however, that you'd complete a puzzle or kill an enemy then open a chest to get mundane parts that you could either kill an enemy for or buy with far less effort. Not as bad as the game Chasm (which had what felt like a complete unawareness of scaling), but I still don't like the feeling of wasting my time.Map: Big, labeled, and mostly useful; loading times atrociousThe map was helpful, except that you couldn't place your own markers or notes. There'd be a section that I hadn't been to, but with no way to say "wait until you have [insert power]" I'd sometimes make the trek back only to be disappointed and have to leave again. The labeling of NPCs, chests, and save locations was helpful - some secrets were also hinted at by the map, which I appreciated - I shouldn't have to bash in every blank wall hoping that there's a hidden passage. The biggest issue with the maps were the loading times when entering/warping to a zone. I am on steam deck, so that may have a bit to do with it, but it was a long several minute wait every time you changed zones. It often wasn't obvious you were entering a new zone (or entered one where you didn't yet have access), so you'd wait a few minutes to load the zone then immediately double back and have to wait several more minutes.Aesthetics: Good.The main character looks a little worse for wear, but that's kinda the point. The animations are fun if occasionally disturbing (wasn't bargaining on that opening cutscene where you're walking around mostly destroyed), but the game world/atmosphere/ambiance is well developed and looks great.Music: Forgettable.I've played for 10 hours, and I can't remember any of the tunes being a bop except the LED visor dude's music.Overall: Pass unless a souls-like enjoyer or if you can overlook some compound flawsGame needs tighter controls (platforming and combat), a better way of counterplaying/parrying against flying enemies and projectiles, for enemies to hit for less damage (or some kind of armor to mitigate it), and for loading zones to be sped way up. Game was occasionally fun for the time I played it, but I won't be finishing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is an excellent metroidvania with consistently satisfying moment to moment gameplay. They really nailed the game feel and there is a very nice flow to the general progression. Combat feels great and maps are a good size where exploration never feels overwhelming. The game is constantly introducing new mechanics, enemy types, and abilities so it continues to feel fresh. Artstyle is very unique and couples well with the edgy sci-fi setting. I do have a few complaints though:-The beginning of the game has full voice acting but then there's pretty much no more voice acting afterwards. Would be cool of they could add voice acting to the rest of the game. -Not enough warp points.-Maybe this is just a skill issue but I can't grasp the parry timing for the life of me. It feels inconsistent so far.-In some case the nearest checkpoint to a boss room is a bit too far away.-Some of the earlier bosses are rather underwhelming but they seem to be getting better. -Checkpionts don't recover health when I feel they should. -I've experienced some minor bugs such as occassional micro-freezing while auto-saving at checkpoints and audio not resuming to normal levels after checking the map. These issues happened very infrequently and I imagine they will be patched out shortly.Anyways, despite my issues I absolutely recommend this if you enjoy metroidvanias. This one seems rather underrated so far judging by the small number of Steam reviews. It deserves much more attention than that. Fantastic work Subcult Joint! Looking forward to whatever you decide to add to Cookie Cutter and your future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: It is 6.5/10 for me. Competent design but could use more polish and do with less enemy inconsistency.Good parts - level design is allright, animations are great, executions for every enemy and all different (not lazy like in Blasphemous 2), different weapons, responsive movement. Enemy variety is ok.So now, moving to the issues.There are enemies in this game that can just go through walls and even follow you from another screen and they are frustrating af. Like why would anyone implement bs like this? Also, there are some enemies that shoot through walls and similarly to the complaint I just made, annoying af. Why the inconsistencies? Who would find this fun? It's not even like well thought out placement or really any deep scheme to this. Just 2 types of enemies in this game are there purely to be d**ks.Speaking of d**ks, the whole humor and theme is heavily influenced by sex and genitalia. Your "sidekick" is called Regina and it is an AI. This AI though looks similar to a real "regina" if you catch my drift and is also situated in the protagonist's crotch area. The game is not woke or anything, it just has this kind of juvenile, crude humor.Controls are rebindable but the directional inputs are not the same for menus and character control so if you swap from arrows to WSAD then you will have to use arrows for menus anyway. It is janky af + they forgot to add a rebind for "zoom out" so for me it was forever stuck to A. A is also move left which means every time I moved map left it was zooming out. Defninitely could use more work.Also, only the very beginning of the game is voiced, like literally first 5 min (and the voiceover doesn't even match the text for some reason). It gives a really bad impression but the story is very simple so it's not like there is a deep lore to follow.In the later part of the game the devs keep relying heavily on instant death spikes. I know some ppl hate those a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the trend in recent metroidvanias that I love about. Aside from the usual mobility unlocks such as Double Jump, Wall Slide, and Air Dash, Cookie Cutter features weapons and skills as gating abilities. These unlockables not only help players get to places previously unavailable but also serve as combo options when it comes to battle. For example, The Educator is a chainsaw players can get from helping a certain NPC. It is a good combo finisher because of its multi-hit nature. Besides that, this weapon can cut through electro-titanium walls as well, which often hides new areas or new path to get around quicker. This is a wonderful design. Combining  tools and abilities with core gameplay instead of making them glorified keys to specific locks is the best way to make a metreoidvania. →Brutalization is quite brutal, and the animation is wild.→Characters' designs are nothing short of quirky, and wild.→Your lady's part talks back to you, like WTF!? This is wild.→A lot of hidden references throughout the game.→I like how the game is trying so hard to make Cherry un-sexy, but it just make her all the more attractive to me.→: Combat in Cookie Cutter burns slowly. It may feels lacking at first, but as you gradually unlock more tools, the thrill of pulling off combos will soon catch up. The basic of combat is a simple two-steps: first launching the enemies in the air, then you are free to do whatever you want. How you launch the enemies airborne is already an interesting thought process. You can of course just uppercut them with your fists and do some normal punches in the air. You can also uppercut them with The Gauntlet which deals more damage and lets you stay at the ground. You can use Void Hand to juggle them into walls or into another enemies as well. There are many options to keep the enemies in an uncounterable state, aka airborne. Now unto the second part, which varies because of players' preference. The combo potential is quite limitless. My favorite combo comprises dropping the Head Grenade first, hitting the enemies with an uppercut, swinging twice with The Stratoblaster, slamming them back down with the same weapon, and by the time the enemies are down on the floor the explosion from Head Grenade will send them upward again, allowing me to do another combo.→: This is not about the combat itself, but the way the game handles weapon switching mechanic. In order to switch weapons and abilities, you need to pull out the weapon wheel and move the left joystick to the weapon, left and right button on D-pad for abilities. This design to me feels awkward to use. I know it slows down time when the wheel is on the screen, but it interrupts the momentum I have for the combo. Why not assign the whole thing on the D-pad? You could assign the weapons on the right sequence and cycle them with left and right button. Abilities could also have the same treatment. Let the players choose whichever four abilities they want and assign them to RB and RB with additional directional inputs. Why is metroidvania so obsessed with putting a platforming section over an instant-kill trap, while a ranged enemy shooting nearby? This happens way more often than I imagine, and Cookie Cutter is no exception. There are so many platforming sections infested with ranged enemies. It is annoying that their projectiles can go through walls. It is more annoying that you can only roll through them, which is a really risky move during platforming. You can't block projectiles in this game. In fact, you can't even block in this game. There is only parry button, and you cannot parry projectile. It would be so much better if you can parry ranged attacks.Before I played this game, I heard a lot of complaints about parry. Most of them stated parry window was way too short, and the punishment for failing was way too harsh. So I purposefully waited a few months to see if the developers had made some changes. Now back to my post-game review. The parry still feels really hard to pull off. The animation and the indication lands faster than you can react. The risk of failing is harsh because some enemies have follow-up attack that ignores your recovery window when you are down, resulting in losing much of your health. I would even go further and say just forget about parry unless you are absolutely sure you can make it, and focus on doing combo and dodging.→The background design of each stage feels dull and kinda empty.→There is no voice acting beyond the first ten minutes.→For some reason my audio bugs out when I use the chainsaw too much. The chainsaw noise over lapses everything.中文小簡評→設計很狂的類銀河系惡魔城。→重要的技能不只能用來開通新的區域，也是戰鬥中連技的好選擇。→連技一開始會因為選項少很顯得乏味，但隨著武器及技能解鎖後就能玩出許多連擊。→處決動畫很狂很暴力。→角色設計很狂很浮誇，令人印象深刻。→主角的兩腿間有個會講話的AI夥伴，這設計夠狂了吧?→關卡背景藏有許多致敬其他遊戲的彩蛋。→這遊戲似乎不斷強調主角有多麼的粗俗多麼不正，但我反而覺得這樣很有魅力。→武器切換應該要改成指定指令而不是叫一個選單出來，至少這樣打連擊的時候不會因此而略失手感。→不能架招遠程攻擊真的很糟，特別是在跳臺的部分尤其明顯。→為什麼跳臺下一定要設計即死陷阱啊啊啊啊!!→架招的時間非常短，失敗的懲罰也很高，完全不建議使用。→背景設計有點空有點單調。→遊戲只有前十分鐘有配音而已。

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game the best chance I could and...yeah, it's okay, but it really flops the landing in a lot of places. Please note, this review is subjective to my opinions, a bisexual male who has pleeeenty of LGBT friends out there.The good:-Decently tight controls! Not Hollow Knight, but I have definitely seen/played worse.-The character animations are really something to see, though I am somewhat disquieted by how almost fetishistic it can really get with some of the kills. -Music's decent too. Not sure I'd get the soundtrack, even if it was available, but its far from bad.The bland: -This game has taken ideas/inspiration from a LOT of other games. Hollow Knight, Metroid Dread, and a bunch of other MVs, but I also see hints of Battletoads (of all things).-Map design isn't great. There's quite a few weird twists and turns and that last area can eff right off since it really looks like the designers weren't sure how to make the final level difficult or engaging beyond "Instant death spike traps everywhere".-The Story. It starts off strong but quickly loses steam (coincidentally alongside the voice acting disappearing altogether) and kind of just lands with a weak thud at the end. I feel no shame spoiling this: the ending is setting up for a sequel or a DLC to wrap things up and I honestly do not care enough to want to try. I am tired of this game. Bored and tired. The bad:-Bugs everywhere. Map pieces that were explored suddenly NOT being explored/revealed. Audio glitches happening (ride the nitro bunny bike from one zone to the next; hope you enjoy motorcycle engine revving permanently until you shut the game off!). Graphical errors (targeting overlay for various powers disappears at random times with no real reason present). This game is just...not quite finished yet.-The 'humor'. Look, this is a game some have said is irreverent, satire,  or is reveling in its debauchery. No, it really isn't. Satire stops the flow and points out when its doing trope-ish things. This game doesn't do that. It both tries and tries not to take itself seriously and we, the player, end up with severe tonal whiplash constantly. The constant raging lesbian jokes, the horrendous hidden Chozo statue that has a limp phallus for a head, the inexplicable pastiche cameo of Toby Fox that makes him look like an utterly moronic idiot, it's all so mean-spirited and smacks of someone trying way way WAY too hard to make us laugh. I never once laughed in this game. I snorted with disdain a lot. Because the humor is that f***ing bad. It reeks of highschoolers who find out more swear words than they knew before upon their first freshman day and thus go around swearing constantly. Penis and boob drawings everywhere. Your sidekick being your literal crotch. This game does not empower LGBT culture. I don't know if I can say that it belittles it, but it is certainly not an empowerment of it. Look, Subcult Joint, if you're reading this? Please. Stop and reflect for a moment. You have made a competent metroidvania and yes, it's pretty easy to see where and how you peeked off of your peers' test sheets. That's fine! But for the love of Samus, stop it with the lameassed humor. It just isn't funny. Rethink your strategy, decide if you want to play it legit or to ham it up. Don't try to do both. You aren't making lesbians look stronger here by slapping a talking vagina onto the main character. You really aren't making her look strong by having her never get any better or change her overall raging b***ch persona. You REALLY aren't making us laugh with the d*ck and vagina jokes. Grow up. Be better than this. I would love to see another game from you with more focus, more maturity. As it is, I cannot recommend this game. Not at full price, not even at half. I'm sorry, Subcult Joint, but you flopped it hard at the end. I do not want to play this game again, I do not want to play its DLC/sequel. Not unless you all have a serious talk about what mature humor really means. Until you grow up, I won't play it anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is a side-scrolling action platformer in the vein of metroidvanias. I like metroidvanias, and combat, and platforming, so why then do I not like this?As a genre it can be broken down into 4 elements: the presentation (be that the graphical quality, or being rich in atmosphere, or having excellent music), the story, the combat, and the exploration. In those regards Cookie Cutter only gets two out of the four right, albeit with both of them still being a bit dubious.I don't like the art-style, but it does look pleasant enough graphically, with crisp, vibrant colours and smooth expressive animation. Though often it's far too eager throwing this in your face, and come the point that the action sequences start ramping up, it becomes a mess of flashy effects for your attacks and flashy effects for your enemies, and its easy to be unable to see yourself on-screen.Combat is the other decent thing that it has, with responsive controls and a varied selection for your attacks. Mechanically its quite slick, and to an extent fairly enjoyable, but it undoes this partly through the visual overload, and the rest is undermined by clumsy design.As an example: When facing a ranged enemy it becomes awkward that they are deliberately allowed to shoot through the floor and other obstacles, which doesn't feel right to me. Nor the fact that, midway through you battering them in a combo, they can just suddenly fire off a really quick energy blast at point-blank range that you can't even block, because there is no block function in the first place.There's only parrying and (a) it doesn't work on their attack, and (b) it doesn't work for me 90% of the time either. That's another area where they sabotage the games appeal: The wind-up for enemy attacks is so slow, but then the actual attack is so insanely quick that I could rarely time it right. Which then makes it even trickier, as parrying stuns enemies, whereas your other general attacks hardly do anything by comparison.For all that there are slick combos and aerial juggles, ground-pounds and special attacks, it often devolved into simply walloping enemies over and over again with a special attack. As the design made encounters somewhat clumsy and messy affairs: here's four melee enemy with their ridiculous windows for attacks and parrying, here's another three ranged enemy going to shoot you with an unblockable, un-parryable attack, that also goes through the platforms you're trying to get onto as you escape the others.Being unable to parry the melee types left me spamming a move that instantly slammed most enemy types to the floor, and that actually interrupted their attacks, which your other moves don't. Despite having a lot of potential, I just didn't find the end result to be enjoyable, and all that eye-candy whizz-bang can't distract me from the thought it's all a bit mediocre.     And those are the relatively good points, I still haven't gotten around to the bad points. So here goes....Is there anything truly awful about it? I wouldn't say so, but the remaining two elements (story / exploration) are rather underwhelming.The story is pish. It's not badly written, or poorly translated, but its pretty typical guff. Sure, I guess playing as a chunky blood-thirsty bow-legged lesbian robot who walks around like she has ricketts, is a fairly unique proposition. On the other hand: this is saturday morning cartoons / 1990's JRPG's levels of drama and writing that I just don't find compelling or engaging.Whilst I doubt this would change my opinion of it, it surely would be less boring overall if the music wasn't utterly bland lounge tunes that plod along. When the action is plodding (which it does for the first hour or so) and the music is so wishy-washy that even basic background ambience would have more life to it, then it becomes a slog exploring.There's no atmosphere, just this wanky, slow, chill-out music that bored the sh*t out of me 25+ years ago as a genre, and that hasn't changed since. When fighting starts it does get more up-tempo and rawk-y, but it's at odds with the generally dull main track you'll hear the rest of the time.  Add all of these things together and it amounts to a game that's somewhat disappointing on the game-play front, somewhat minging to my eyes in terms of its design, but technically kind of nice to look at, but also a bit too over the top to remain readable during the action. The musics sh*t and the plot is mediocre tweenage guff that thinks its adult simply because the protagonist swears a lot and has a nonchalent approach to committing acts of extreme violence.That only works for me if there's a reasonable level of drama behind it, or at least a ridiculously exciting style of choreography to the brutality. This is like Wolfenstein Youngblood with a protagonist spouting such sophisticated dialogue as "f**k yeah dude! I am going to f**k up some evil f**kers face, whoo! yeah!...whoo!!"*coughs* It's not exactly God Of War.....but, hey! You do get to play as a chunky bow-legged blood-thirsty lesbian robot with ricketts, so that, at least, is..uh..something, right?It cost me £3 and I still regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: In an effort to not spend paragraphs explaining it when I don't need to, in summary, this game lacks the polish that its art direction deserves. Could've used more development time in order to properly use assets without making background/foreground elements low-res and polish combat to make it a bit more satisfying. That being said, this is quite the impressive debut for an indie studio, so it's certainly worth playing if you are interested in the game's art style or story.
_childDocuments_.name: Cookie Cutter

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter impresses visually with its high-quality animations, detailed enemy death sequences, and brutal finishing moves. It’s clear that a significant portion of the development effort went into the game’s presentation, which is undeniably a highlight.Unfortunately, the gameplay doesn’t live up to the same standard. Combat quickly becomes monotonous due to limited enemy variety—each area features around three enemy types, which isn’t enough to maintain engagement, especially given their large health pools. This design choice makes battles drag on unnecessarily, exacerbating the lack of diversity.The combat system itself is simple but flawed. Players use light attacks to generate grit and weapon attacks to consume it, with the latter being so overpowered that spamming them trivializes most encounters. The flow of combat rarely changes: light attacks for grit, weapon attacks for damage, brutalize weakened enemies to refill grit, and repeat. This lack of nuance makes fights feel stale after only a short time.Adding to the frustration is the parry mechanic. The parry window is exceptionally narrow, making it feel inconsistent and frustrating to rely on, even for experienced players. This further limits the player’s options and adds to the game’s mechanical shortcomings.While Cookie Cutter is a visual treat, its lackluster combat system and repetitive gameplay prevent it from being more than a surface-level experience. It’s a shame, as the game’s aesthetic deserves a more polished and engaging foundation to truly shine.

_childDocuments_.review: So I am a huge fan of indie games, but I cannot recommend this game and I will detail why. For starters, as soon as the game was released the developers wanted everyone to report bugs to them and started a Discussion tab for that. Please be aware that doing this for them gives them FREE QA work, that they should be paying for. They could have budgeted more for QA professionals and given them more work instead of dumping this work on consumers for free. We should not be play testers, especially not for a game that has been in production for 6 years and that has a 20USD price tag. If you are a developer and you are reading this, please tell me why we should be paying full price for a broken product and saying thank you? If this were any other profession you'd be fired, full stop. So the actual game: TLDR: THE GAME IS NOT FINISHED. There isn't an ending, there are locked doors with no way to get inside (I've checked....it's intentionally left open ended). Combat is slippery, unreadable and so fast that you don't know what is happening due to the visual noise. Humor is immature and instead of being a compelling LGBT story it resorts to making crude SA jokes and drawing genitalia on the walls/background. Achievements are bugged, audio is bugged, story cutscenes are locked behind bugs. Developers are asking for free QA support without releasing as early access. Pros: - voice acting for the first scene, but then they bait and switch and get rid of the voice acting for the rest of the game. I am assuming they ran out of budget, but this was not disclosed on the store page. - stunning animation style and animation work. The art is really saving the game and experience here. - Cool inspiration of execution style killings from games like Blasphemous, etc. Unfortunately you can be punished for executing an enemy because of the swarm mechanic leaving you vulnerable right after executing someone. Cool animations....just not well implemented into the gameplay. Cons: - Combat system shows you combos that end up not working on 80% of the enemies after the first biome(s). Most of the time you are left with hit-dodge-hit-dodge because your combos don't stagger enemies at all. - Void punch mechanic only stuns or moves certain enemies, and you find out the hard way that some elite enemies cannot be affected by this mechanic with zero warning or explanation from the game. - The parry system just does not work. Played the entire game without it, but it really is a shame. Completely broken imo. - The head grenade ability has literally ZERO implementation or use in the game whatsoever. I tried using it in multiple places and realized other things would work better and more effectively. - Upgrades always come well after they would have been helpful- Combat is visually noisy, in many arenas character gets completely buried underneath a mob of enemies and flashing lights and you can't find your character on the screen- The humor consists of SA jokes, genitalia drawn on the walls and more genitalia jokes. Clearly not QA checked by diversity/inclusion experts. The focus was not on the LGBT romance and more on tokenizing LGBT relationships. Problematic representation at best, but more likely it's just harmful. Seems like the developers were all cis men, would be shocked if it were not the case.- Game advertises 10 biomes, there are 7 (9 if you count overworlds that don't really have enemies in them, I don't)- Lacking in enemy design, many of the enemies are just different colored version of previous enemies. - Lots of death pits that would be less of a problem if the camera pan function wasn't bugged. - Camera pan function doesn't work and will cause the screen to glitch and shake. - Map is broken, world view map also poorly denotes which teleport goes to which area, i.e. the "Upper swamp" teleport highlights entirely the wrong area on the world map. - You are punished for finding any late game biomes by having to turn around and endure another loading screen. - At least 4 entrances to biomes after a 20 second loading screen force you to turn back and wait for the load screen again. Just lock us out of the entrance on the other side of the load screen so we don't have to suffer needlessly. - THIS IS A BIG ONE: Story is not finished, quite literally there are allusions to locked doors and biomes that are not in the game. This gives the impression more was planned than has been released, or that they are full of themselves and think they will be successful with a later DLC. The major conflict of the game is NOT RESOLVED or dealt with at all by the end of the game. It is left on a cliff hanger with no mention of a sequel, DLC, or any sort of resolution on the horizon. To me this smells like botched production management and greenlighting the release of a completely unpolished game. Huge letdown to fans of indie metroidvanias. DEVELOPERS : we cannot support you when you're wrong. If you want more play testing, pay for it. Don't expect money for a broken and unfinished product it's not ethical and it further alienates gamers from exploring other indie titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is a superb, hyperviolent metroidlike I had an absolute blast playing through. Platforming takes a moment to get used to, but you'll soon be double jumping and airdashing through everything with relative ease. That's not to say the game doesn't get challenging, cause it does, especially early on when you don't have any health upgrades and are still getting used to the combat. It can be a tough game, but there's dozens of tools at your disposal to mitigate some of the challenge. For instance, the parry is extremely satisfying to pull off, especially when chaining multiple against a boss. But the parry window is fairly strict and you have to pay attention to enemy attacks as there is no easy prompt telling you when to press the button, making it a high risk, high reward mechanic that you have as an option, but don't need to rely on if it's too hard. Enemies and bosses can be taken down through various other weapons, moves and dodges as well. Once you get a few more moves and learn to juggle enemies and dodge out of the way instead of just button mashing, it really opens up and proves very rewarding. I really loved how enemies and items would react to each other and the environment, so enemies could be punched into walls or each other, they would bounce off pads and take damage from hazards, just like you do. Larger fights got wonderfully chaotic as you were dodging back and forth, trying to find an opening to get a gauntlet smash in, launching an enemy to collide with a group, pushing one into a bounce pad, launching them into spikes in the ceiling, as you dodge another strike, and the attacker slips off the ledge into below sawblades. Then you uppercut a whole group into the air and combo them until the finisher indicators pop up and you get to collect some health and void meter back. It's so GOOD.The aesthetics, especially the detailed and wild animation, are obviously the main draw, but the game looks great elsewhere too with some subtle lighting and varied, atmospheric environments and background detail. The characters are expressive and the art all around has a wonderful punk and weird vibe going. Great music, awesome sounds, and as with the best metroidlikes, the new abilities you gain aren't just for opening a single type of locked door (well, one of them is), but can be used in various ways in combat and improving your movement options.Structurally this does what I like in metroidlikes, it will tell you where you should be heading next, but you are pretty free to explore where else can you get to at all times, and exploring and finding every hidden secret is really satisfying. It's a fairly big game too, I took a good 18 hours to get to the end, and I didn't find everything.EDIT: Yup, the latest patch fixed the one side quest that wasn't progressing for me. Achievements are also working fine now.Look at the screenshots and video clips of the game. Does that look cool? That's the game. It's a tough but fair melee focused metroidlike, with a ton of satisfying exploration, awesome fights and a cool world and characters I wouldn't mind seeing a sequel for.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 5/10Visuals: This is what you're here for if anything. The colorful hand drawn animations are good, particularly the finisher kills (though it's a shame those play so quickly that I can barely see what happens in them). The game is oozing with style in every scene. Some background details make references to other popular media, but very rarely do anything other than simply display an existing poster/cover/character. 8/10Gameplay: Cookie Cutter is right. Standard Metroidvania stock, except even some genre staple moves which games tend to begin with, such as air-dash and wall-jump, are gateway powerups here. The beat-em-up combat gets monotonous towards the middle of the game, then tapers off as you collect the remaining powerups until the endgame is easier than the beginning. Map glitches and inconsistencies in how secrets can be discovered, as well as the ongoing inability to actually reach 100% completion, make for an unsatisfying "roundup" stage. 4/10Music: None was really memorable to me, except for the fact that a single track near the very end actually did kind of shred, as an exception to define the rule. It's not a good look for a game with so much punk-rock inspiration. 3/10Story: There's some fun worldbuilding if you look through how much of the lore is just typical "bad megacorporation being bad". The characters are sometimes interesting, if a bit one-note. The main character's lesbian relationship is almost a bold move, but we see so little of her lover that it almost feels like queerbaiting. This would be a double standard when compared to how many games used to get away with "male hero saves princess", but this is a 2023 game and those would not be considered interesting stories now either.Every single story thread is left unresolved in order to hype up a sequel (or expansion?) we may never see at this solo developer's pace, so it feels like the credits roll at what ought to be the halfway point. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The art and animation are great but unfortunately everything else is a letdown.The load times are obnoxiously long for a 2d platformer. The game doesn't autosave on going to a different area, so if I died after fast travelling I would respawn in the first area and have to endure another 2 load screens to get back to where I was. The combat is extremely repetitive, after around the 3rd area I had the terrible realization that I was going to be doing this for the entire game. The window for parries is extremely small, I couldn't consistently nail it on the first few enemies so I forgot about it for the rest of the game. Sometimes I would be trapped with a large amount of enemies in a room, it was impossible to see where my character was and I would quickly be overwhelmed.Inexcusably buggy for a game that's been out for 5 months now. The screen will jitter unsettlingly when looking around with the right stick, this happens more often than not. Map markers for pickups sometimes don't disappear after collecting, leading to false positives. Many more minor bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I've tried and I've tried. The game looks so cool but it feel so clunky in execution across the board. It's so frustrating. The little checkpoint system is too few and far between for the systems in place (enemies can start there attack during your jump to them, so if they attack you on your way to jumping to their platform there is nothing you can do but fall) so you're often left with a couple minutes of clunky traversal between deaths at the hand of the parry system or enemies attacking through your attacks. Healing is super slow so there's no point trying to heal during the 1000 times you get ganked by enemies you can't parry ( 5 or  6 at a time) I've upgraded the base attack twice and its still terrible but i have to use it to use the strong attack which is the only viable attack but it power is the same source as the healing so it's either use your only viable attack or heal after getting ganked.Honestly baffling design choices here. Thank god they'll fool alot of people with the cool art style

_childDocuments_.review: Its been a bit since I've gotten invested into a game this much, I've been looking for a game to put hours into sine my play through of Elden Ring and Have a Nice Death, this game has hit that itch I've had. The art style and aesthetic of the really reminds me of an late night adult swim show from how it presents itself and that's one of the things that really captivates me. There are a few issues overall that do need some addressing, giving this is the first game of a small indie though, talk about a good entrance!As stated there are a few issues that do need some address, the two main issues I have overall is the parry mechanic and the time it takes to recover. At the beginning of the game you are told that when an enemy attack flashes blue then it can be parried, however the lighting is not synced with the attack itself which makes it really difficult to use any parry. I find myself not using parry for that reason, which even then from where I am at the parry mechanic is just an after thought due to the ease it is to kill enemies.My other issue has to be the time it takes to recover on getting attacked, it seems extremely inconsistent on any frames you do get, there are times where I have invincibility frames from either getting hit by a laser or a boss and then there are times where it just doesn't exist and I get hit back to back without any way to react. It can be frustrating and extremely unfair when you have no idea how the game is going to react to you getting hit and if you're doing to die off one hit.Those two issues are my only gripes, otherwise I love this game for what it is and I do think this is a good start for a new studio! Happy to have randomly found this!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an entertaining, 2D Metroidvania that feels like the spiritual mix of Earthworm Jim and Alien Hominid. The game's setting is decidedly cyberpunk, with an art style that leans heavily on off-colour humour. The main character is an robot named Cherry. Her sidekick is an artificial intelligence named Regina. Regina is shaped like a vulva and is grafted to Cherry's nethers in the same spot. All of that, is just the start. Developer Subcult has peppered each level with so much genitalia-themed art that it sometimes feels like a Georgia O'Keeffe gallery as seen through the eyes of H.R. Giger. This type of humour and atmosphere is right up my alley, but may turn off the more prudish. Along with the genital themes, the developers also showcased their love for punk and metal music. I spotted a few Tool album covers, along with Misfits, Slipknot, and a nod to Marilyn Manson in one of the main characters. Gameplay-wise, you will get the standard Metroidvania style of exploring the map and engaging with enemies in battle. Fights play out more like a beat-em up in that enemies always take a few hits before they die. Traversal mechanics incorporate timed jumps, dashes, and slides. Getting into battles is mostly fun, with the ever increasing move set (and power increase) encouraging you to try different moves with different enemy types. The only time fights get frustrating is in kill rooms where you need to take everyone out to progress. You will almost certainly die in at least a few of these rooms throughout the game. The issue is that the second everyone spawns in, you lose Cherry's location amidst the chaos. It's hard to jump away from a room full of  suddenly spawned-in enemies when you aren't even sure where you are anymore. That the camera is often panned way back (to fit everyone on screen) just makes it easier to get lost. Platforming can also get a bit frustrating, especially in the more challenging spike rooms. Cherry's jump mechanics are a bit floaty and the game will occasionally either forget to register a mid-air dash, or treat a single jump off a ledge as two jumps. During my playthrough of the game, I did incur a few game bugs that required workarounds to get past, and even full-on restarts to break out of. Some of the problems were text boxes not appearing in "cut scenes", requiring a full reset of the game to fix, or getting locked out of a kill room because I was punched through a wall. The most consistent bug I encountered was with the teleporters. The initial flash from entering the teleporter sometimes gets stuck, leaving me with a big, bright pink screen that won't leave. The teleport menu is still active at this point, but I can't see it. The only way to fix it is to use muscle memory to teleport to anywhere else in the game (causing the load screen to appear). All of these bugs can be fixed with subsequent patches, so your mileage will vary.  In summary, Cookie Cutter is a blast to play with fun combat and an interesting cyberpunk storyline. There are some slight bugs to the game, and the off-colour humour / art style may turn off the more prudish, but if you like metal / punk and enjoy a good Metroid-ish beat-em up, then by all means give this one a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following through socials the team developing this game and it's amazing to see the result of love and sweat put into it. I'm happy to see that so far it also plays and looks great! Story, animation, art style and music kick asses and are clearly the strong point of this gem. The combat feels rewarding and paced nicely with frequent upgrades, making (for me) irrelevant the not so accurate feeling of the parry or some of the minor issues reported in other reviews. Dodge roll, stun combos, knock-backs and powers give you tools even from early game to deal with encounters in multiple ways. Overall highly recommended if you are a fan of Metroidvanias and you find the art-style appealing.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game doesn't feel as good, combat wise, as similar type games on the market, it makes up for it with it's story, charm and humor. The main character in this game is unique and unlike any other I've seen. The dialog between the main character and other characters is a joy to read at times.The game was a lot of fun to play, but also a little boring here and there. As stated above, the combat and parry system doesn't feel as clean as similar games I've played. I hardly ever had to use the light kicking attack, making them game play mostly heavy punches and parrying. While there is nothing wrong with that, I never really got much joy or felt powerful while killing enemies.I'm not the best at these games, and some of the bosses were very easy to kill, even for me. Especially the final boss, which should technically be the hardest; forcing you to put everything you unlocked and learned to the test. I see a lot of comments about making a harder difficulty, and I can agree that the game needs that for the players looking for a challenge. If you are looking for just a chill game play experience like me, then the difficulty is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is a sicknasty metroidvania with a fantastic cyborg-punk aesthetic - which I love - and solid gameplay and storytelling. This indy game lacks some polish and has quite a few bugs, aswell as being a bit rough around the edges in terms of its attention to detail, but it makes up for that with heaps of style, energy, and beautiful hand drawn animation. It feels a lot like playing Bastion when it came out; I will watch these developers closely and see what they come up with in the future. I don't tend to get along too well with MV games but this was very approachable for me and I managed to complete it thanks to its generous checkpoints and consequence-free deaths balancing out the punishing difficulty in a tidy 17 hours. Better gamers will do it in less. I cant really speak to the quality of the design of this sort of game so I will focus on the story. The story is fairly solid: not cookie cutter atall but quite original. heh. I bet all the paid reviewers will be making that joke. Calling it now. Anyway, there's a cool lesbian romance and while there's a lot of humour to the design and aesthetic it really nails the drama and it plays it straight when it needs to and this really strengthens the whole. Seeing the Tank Girl influence here. The Corporation is a dull name for a great concept. Defeating death by putting human souls in machines bound to service is a fantastic concept, and you really feel that vibe especially in the game's first area. The characters are all very vibrant and really feel like they have a life outside of the game. Whats there in the interactions is fleshed out by text logs, but honestly the art design of the characters does more for me in telling their stories than a pile of audio logs ever could. There's voice acting at the very start, for the opening CS and a couple of the missions, which gives you a flavour of what the characters sound like, but it looks like the game doesn't have full VA, which is a real shame because it would rock if it did. That said, I didn't miss it. The character designs have so much personality that I feel like I know what they'd sound like just from their animations. Speaking of the animations, they're all fantastic. Watching cherry rip a robots organs out its mouth with a wicked little grin on her face is enough to stop me from wondering why the robots have organs. This game about robots manages to be on a similar level of gore to Gears of War, which is honestly great and I love it. Cover me in that viscera, Cookie Cutter. Should you buy this game? I think if you enjoy Hewlettesque Punk, Lesbians, old school 2D animation, gore, soul-cyborgs or (I assume) metroidvania, this game is for you, and I think this is definitely a developer to give some money to.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm super torn about this game to be honest, I have a bunch of gripes with the game but it managed to keep me engaged the entire time. I'm just going to do a list with pros and cons about what I personally disliked and liked. I cannot comment on the story since I did not pay that much attention, but it seemed well ordered and well written.Liked:- The level design: Map is pretty fun to explore and there are plenty of secrets.- Weapons: Weapon combat feels nice and the animations feel fluid and fun, more on this later.- Platforming: Ties in with level design, done very well.- Bosses: Boss enemies that do not get reused (most of them were unique), have fun move sets but I did find them overly tanky at times. This could be my fault since I forgot to level my weapon early and it led to some long fights. Disliked:- Combat: Combat feels too repetitive for how many combat encounters are present in the game. - Enemy Diversity: Enemies are reused far too much, especially in the early game. I probably fought 3 different variants of 3 separate enemies. For example green bug, blue bug, red bug. This happened A LOT early.- Character: So again just my opinion, but I was not a huge fan of the main characters design or personality. I liked her robot aspects, but I think her design is too "basic." Her personality also seemed like she was trying too hard to be edgy. I had mixed feelings about the execute system but I was unsure where to put it since I both liked and disliked it. _childDocuments_.review: Get it on a good sale if u like action focused metroidvania games (2 reasons why I reco only on sale, see below)+ Very nice graphics (unique hand drawn and fits the game very well)+ Story is ok+ First half of the game is great in terms of maps, progress, "powerups", enemies and combat- Second half was meh 2 me :/ felt a bit bored, maps weren't that interesting (and it almost felt like a chore to try getting all collectibles later on altho those are optional) and enemies got annoying and not fun to beat up.+ Combat is very nice (decent weapon variety)+- Guard/Block mechanic is there but mostly ignored, mby they should have done it better and it would have some (late game) enemy fights easier but more fun (might just be a personal thing where I didn't feel like bothering to master the block timings when I could just punch through or rush past enemies).+ Nice challenge rooms (some are optional)+ Amazing easter eggz across the whole game (from ps1 clasics like Tomba! and Castlevania SOTN through Ramona from Scott Pilgrim vs the World to Corey Taylor from Slipknot!)+ Very nice easter egg weapon (DMC fans will know once they see it ^^)+ Bosses are great and their difficulty is perfect (from early easy ones to mid-late game very challenging ones. Just like it should be)+- Semi bugged maps/pickups (game forgets some maps so after not playing for a while the maps for some areas reset and become blank till u go tru them again & some pickups reset as soon as u leave the room)+- Semi bugged 'Sweet Tooth' achiv (dw you can 100% the game still easily) -> My reco, try to 100% everything and just before you go to beat the final boss check out a guide to get this achiv. Basically u have to talk with an NPC, give her some items and then beat the finall boss and u get the achiv in the post final battle. Note if u gave her the items earlier dw, quit the game and reload and you will be able to do it again due to the bug)- Annoying farming achiv (upgrade all weapons = farming a lot for cash = boring)- There are ~3 doors that are never unlocked in the game, my guess they were for a secret finale/ending but got scrapped for reasons and that kinda sucks cos they could have at least removed those doors.. And the ending does tease a secret finale continuation w secret final boss that we never got so it kinda ruins the ending as well.. If they removed the doors and had this as a cliff ending that would have been totally fine..Overall a very nice but sadly flawed metroidvania (2nd half of the game & the ending cliff/3 leftover unopenable doors).Still recommended for action metrodivania fans on a good sale :)

_childDocuments_.review: Quite the personality on this Metroidvania ! If you like the art style and don't mind a combat that's a little simplistic, Cookie Cutter is an entertaining 10 to 15 hour adventure in a stylish, broken world.With great animations for characters, moves and executions, the visuals do a lot for Cookie Cutter, but that's not all the game has. The gameplay, whether it's the platforming or the fighting, feels responsive and enjoyable, especially once you unlock a few upgrades like the air dash. You use these new abilities and weapons to explore progressively more of a map that is quite big and offers diverse environments, home to many secrets and platforming challenges. Some of those can get tricky or even frustrating when enemies come into the mix, but there are checkpoints everywhere and dying is not penalized.Which is good, because encounters are pretty hectic and you'll find yourself getting comboed into traps or other enemies more than once, so death is just around the corner. But so is the checkpoint, crisis averted !There are several weapons, secondaries and powers to find and unlock that spice up the gameplay, but they're pretty clunky and costly to upgrade. This means you'll probably stick to the basic ones unless you're feeling fancy.The game chose to put a big focus on parrying, so most enemies and bosses can be dealt with that way. It's rewarding but also dangerous, as you're only invincible during the execution and enemies are constantly attacking. A high risk, stylish reward kind of situation.There are a few bugs to be aware of. The sound settings reset everytime you close the game, and some audio glitches exist. More annoying, the map doesn't always save as you explore it, which seems to happen when you teleport to different areas.And although technically not a bug, only the intro of the game is voiced, which is a little disappointing. Here's hoping they'll add the rest somewhere down the line.A few details that shouldn't deter you from trying out Cookie Cutter, as it's a really cool Metroidvania. Stylish and violent, it will leave you wanting more, at least to know the end of Cherry's story since the game ends on a cliffhanger.As is, I'll give Cookie Cutter a  because I had a brutal, bloody good time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes and no.The sheer volume of references throughout this game was fun. So many images immediately made me think, "f*** yeah! I love that too" etc.The  catalogue of influences that're on display throughout this title was awesome to see. Throughout the game I was constantly bombarded with imagery that reminded me of but not limited to Tank Girl, Judge Dredd, The Prodigy, Marilyn Manson & the Spooky Kids, QOTSA, Berserk in fact lots of manga (specifically Japanese manga), punk and the general mindset that says "I wasn't born with enough middle fingers".It's so clear and obvious, intentional or not, that the person/s that made this game wanted to splatter the hell outta it with everything they like. I appreciate that. I also appreciate the unapologetic attitude that's, again intentional or not, sewn into this title.Including this game, I only have three metroidvania games. It's a genre that isn't really for me. Literally the  reasons that I decided to buy this game was because I think the art/visual designs look great plus they're backed by thumping music that fit an aesthetic I've always liked. Going into Cookie Cutter with this mindset, I totally wanted the gameplay to standout and perhaps "whoa" me but instead - despite being unfamiliar with the genre - Cookie Cutters gameplay felt by the numbers and at times lacking.There's nothing inherently bad about the gameplay however that in and of itself makes me think "why then would I recommend it if I can also say there's nothing really that grabbed my attention" (gameplaywise).Definitely go for it if you're  into the metroidvania genre as well as the aesthetic and attitude on display within the trailers.If there's a sequel in the future, this is a hellava good jumping off point for the dev/s.

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a midnight dreary, while I pondered, weak and weary, Over many a quaint and curious volume of forgotten lore— I stumbled upon a game, Cookie Cutter by name, A metroidvania, drenched in blood and gore.In the depths of The Megastructure, Cherry’s quest did unfurl, A tale of vengeance, love, and a world in peril. With fists of fury and a heart of steel, She battled through biomes, her enemies to quell.The hand-drawn graphics, a feast for the eyes, Each stroke of color, a vivid surprise. Yet, amidst the beauty, frustration did creep, For the foes were many, and the challenges steep.But oh, the combat, a dance of death, With combos and parries, I held my breath. Each boss, a puzzle, each fight, a test, In this dark, twisted world, I gave my best.Though the journey was fraught with trials and pain, The allure of Cookie Cutter did remain. For in its heart, a story bold, Of love and loss, and a heroine’s soul.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like leaving negative reviews for indie games, but in this instance I have to bring attention to something. It's a frustration I have never felt in a video game before.Like a good metroidvania, the map is dense with collectibles, hidden areas and robot loot to be plundered. So consult the map to track where you need to go right?Here's the problem - the map moves incredibly slow. And I'm not exaggerating here. I thought my game was broken until a sense check in the forums confirming other users experienced the same.Up, down, left or right - even zooming in or out is slow. If you're just combing an area, you spend WAY too much time just in the map screen slowly waiting for the map to move or zoom out to where you want to focus on. It's the weirdest issue I've encountered in a metroidvania and it really makes navigating to unexplored areas a slog. Some unrelated issues that are dampening the experience...- Weird bug where hitting a teleport post will freeze the screen but I can still do things behind it- Jumping feels ridiculously floaty and hard to control your movements- Double jump seems to just trigger even when launching from the ground- The art for the game is fantastic but the MC does have a very strange design, I can get used to that if the other issues smoothed over.Again, I hate to leave a negative review and I will gladly revise if the map issue is remedied.

_childDocuments_.review: You know when you a trailer of a game and it just looks amazing to you. The art style, the moves, the animation, a large sprawling map, the attitude of the character. I was hyped for this game. And then it came out and the reviews were mixed and players and critics were - it has problems.But the vocal fans were like - Nah! It's just how it's suppose to be! Metroidvanias should have a lot of backtracking, the combat should be samey with spongey enemies how else are you going to learn the moves! Use the enviroment, bruh! Castlevania had insane knowback on each enemy attack, it good, it makes you THINK before you do something. Just get good at the gameplay. The parry should be very hard to do with enemies glowing blue BUT that's not the time to hit the parry you gotta look at their animation! Oh what there are a ton of enemies on the screen and you cannot see the animations? Pfff learn the telegraphs bro, be more attentive! Also yeah the back end of the game should be filled with one hit kill spikes! Member, Super Meat boy, that had one hit kills and it was goooooood. Just learn the level, dude! What the hit boxes of enemies, your weapons and the spikes are not aligned and either too small or too large??? Pfff, stop whinying mate. go and make a better game then!So I bough the game and I powered through to the Golden Tower and I was not having fun and then once I died for the N-th time to a cheap attack off-screen I stopped the game and I asked myself - "Why are you playing this? Just go watch Tank Girl and then play any of the other at least 10 metroidvanias that are better designed, play better and are as gorgeous as this one". So yeah, good reader go and do that - watch Tank Girl, Buckaroo Banzai, Dark City, etc. and play better designed games. Don't waste your time with this game until the devs decide to patch it to a place that is actually fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I somewhat enjoyed Cookie Cutter.  I explored 'pretty much' every last corner of each map, minus one bit that I think is bugged.  Steam achievements are bugged, you won't get any (Going to be addressed in an upcoming patch supposedly).There wasn't a lot of diversity in the biomes, so much so that discovering a new area/biome didn't feel like a new one. There was a couple of exceptions to this, but most areas just feel like the same factory/lab place.There's something about the fast animations, most irksome when the game zooms in a bit, like in a smaller room. If i zip my character across the screen, my eyes don't fully track all of the animations or something, not sure how to describe it. Jarring to look at.It feels similar to how in some other games you need to toggle vsync to make it look right. There's no graphics options to try anything like that though. I'm thinking it is possibly to do with some of the animations lacking frames though, such as turning left and right and running across the screen.  There are other animations which look great, such as mashing X to kick.  I recall a similar problem when i played Fearmonium.  Anyway, it's a lot less noticeable when the game is more zoomed out, which thankfully a lot of it is.  That's when I can enjoy the animations, rather than be distracted by this problem.If i want to walk off of the left side of a platform to drop down, then I immediately hug right to land somewhere in that direction, i will instead climb the ledge back onto the platform i was trying to drop off of.I've tried using parry about 10 times and never seen it work, so i just use dodge. It must have a very unclear and specific window to function.  I've heard that the devs intend to make this less finicky, hopefully that is true.I could've sworn I used my B attack to reflect a projectile at a boss one time, but then failed like 15 times in a row trying to replicate it, so i think that has a very tight/unclear timing window as well (Or I dreamt that i reflected it in the first place :)).I liked breaking stuff on each screen. I got kind of OCD with destroying every little thing on the screen.  Movement and combat felt good, though perhaps in part due to the difficulty of not using parry; things can get pretty annoying in places.  There are instant death spikes you will get knocked into by enemies, and when an enemy hits you, you get knocked back and can't do anything for a second.  Sometimes you are being attacked by so many things in a narrow space, and can only use your dodge once before a 1 second cooldown where the other attacks will hit you.  You can get gang banged very easily.The last area had a steep rise in the difficulty of the platforming, which started to get a bit closer to segments in Aeterna Noctis, but I like that they at least saved this bit toward the end.Cookie Cutters level design and fast movement made it pretty chill to play.
