_childDocuments_.review: Got this one in Humble's recent Metroidvania bundle, and I've gotta say, I was quite impressed overall. Here's my breakdown of the good and the bad:The Good:-Graphics and art design. Loved the fluid 2D animation, the cyberpunk aesthetic, the character designs, and just the overall look.-Sound. Decent music that keeps the mood, very punchy sound effects. Solid voice acting for an indy title.-Level design. This can make or break any platformer, especially Metroidvanias. Here it's solid, flows well, and while it has some challenging sections, it's nothing that will break genre veterans.-Combat. The focus on getting currencty from enemies to purchase upgrades incentivises fighting enemies when you're backtracking, the way weak combos charge up your resources to use stronger weapons encourages players to mix it up, and the weapons are all satisfying to use. It borrows Hollow Knight's resource economy, where the resource that governs your powers is also what you'll use for healing, but removes the Souls-like need to retrieve resources upon death, which is a welcome change and further encourages combat. Combos are simple enough to learn quickly, but deep enough to be engaging. Enemies require you to learn their tells and patterns so the game doesn't just become a mash-fest, but you do get a sense of power from fighting earlier enemies and being able to beat them more quickly with upgraded weapons.-Upgrades. The game makes smart use of the various powers and weapons you get, with most of them being usable for both combat and progression, rather than being exclusively for one or the other. Very welcome in a Metroidvania. Passive upgrades have to be equipped and can be swapped out for different builds within resource limits, making your character very customizable, and further encouraging exploration to find more energy cells to increase the number you can equip at once.-Length. You can easily rack up 15+ hours trying to get all the upgrades and collectibles, which is a good length for a game like this. It doesn't overstay its welcome, but it's meaty enough to be satisfying.The Bad:-Parrying. Despite me singing the praises of the combat, I was never able to get the hang of one of its core elements, parrying. Maybe it's just me needing to "git gud," but the timing required for parries is very finicky and seemed inconsistent to me, so I just ignored it entirely and focused on combos and dodging to defeat enemies, which works just fine. Judging from other reviews, I'm not the only one who had a problem with this, so maybe it's something the devs should consider tweaking down the line.-Ending. The story is serviceable and fine, and hits some good emotional beats, but the ending is seriously abrupt and leaves major chunks of the story unresolved. At first I thought I'd hit an Igavania-style "bad end," but no, apparently that's just the only ending to the game. Perhaps there's DLC coming to expand on the story, or a sequel in the works, but by and large, it left me feeling flat and a little unsatisfied after such a fun ride. Other players may not be as bothered by this sort of thing, though.On balance, though, the good far outweighs the bad here. If you like Metroidvanias, cyberpunk as a genre and Western-style animation, and you have a slightly warped sense of humor like me, then this'll be right up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with the game, the sprites look amazing in motion. The finishers on the enemies are varied and each enemy has their own finishing move by the protagonist with expanding limbs reminding me a bit of Battletoads. It's also true that the some enemies are recolors of existing enemies with some attack variant yet they got their own unique execution move to receive.The map is fine for the most part, while we don't get custom marks to put on the map, most of the important stuff is shown if you're near it (except for some little robots and secret passages). The fact they put a counter on every collectible on every map is a godsend to have an idea on what's left to search on each zone. That said, I was not a fan on arena rooms (enter in a room, get locked in and beat the enemies to leave) and have to say the last zone has quite a lot of instakill spikes you need to be careful moving around.You have a few side quests that may reward you a weapon or a npc that goes to your base of operations. The upgrade system for some weapons and habilities are ok, didn't like to roam around gathering materials from mobs hoping they give me the specific item given they can drop a few items of different rarities. If I'm honest I would preffered just using the currency to upgrade.To finish the review, I'll say it has been an enjoyable experience overall.

_childDocuments_.review: It takes a lot for me to pick up a game twice... I guess I'm just pickier than most people. Cookie Cutter makes the grade though. The character art style drew me in, and the animation is very fluid (gender fluid?). There's a big huge map that interconnects just like any other great Metroidvania, and unlockable powers to further explore as you progress, many of these worded as humorous double entendres. Also very importantly are secret rooms to find, which are an absolute necessity IMHO. Combat requires a lot of parrying. Normally this would make me assume the game is souls-like difficult which is a huge turn-off, but fortunately it's not difficult for people like me that suck at quick response times. It might be good for accessibility options to slow the parry time down a bit for handicapped or zen gamers, but if I can do it I think most can.  Tiny quibbles are the enemies can be a little stingy with the coins, and a little more variety with the enemies would be nice. Otherwise this is a super solid game and a bargain at the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm absolutely IN LOVE with this art style and voice acting, but that's about it. The protagonist feels too slippery when controlling her and I'm not a fan of the her design. The aesthetic absolutely drips with punk, but I've never been into these patchwork hairstyles. Reading other reviews that state the later 1/3 of the game becomes more platforming than welcome was the nail in the coffin.
_childDocuments_.name: Cookie Cutter

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing animations, great character and background art and enjoyable metroidvania exploration make Cookie Cutter an easy recommendation for anyone that is a fan of the genre or enjoys games with handdrawn animations.The animations are the first thing that really piqued my interest when seeing the first trailers for the game, especially all the smooth and gorey finisher moves you can use on low HP enemies are all around amazing.This also applies to Cherry's movement and normal attacks, it's all so beautifully animated that it is a joy to just watch them over and over.The soundtrack is great for building the atmosphere of each level, but there wasn't many tracks that really stuck out to me. Frankly, I expected something more intense and punk-y looking at the aesthetics of the game and especially the design of the main character.My one gripe with the game right now is, that the ending is a little abrupt.All in all the plot of the game is resolved by the end of it, but it feels like it's setting up for either a sequel or DLC, so it's still kind of left open ended.And while I would certainly look forward for a DLC to continue playing the game, in it's current state that leaves the ending feeling - not bad at all, but a little weak.Nevertheless, I highly recommend checking out Cookie Cutter!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game but I wish there was more story involved. The combat was responsive, fluid and addicting. However the countering system was trash. The art style and animation is superb and something to marvel at. The intro to the game is really the only exciting part of the story. I wish we could have got more of that through the game. Loved the power ups and puzzles. I am not a fan of Mertroidvania games but clearly with 40 hours under my belt I may start playing more of them. Maybe! For $20 this is a solid game that's fun, frustrating at times, and a bit cheesy with it's humor and innuendos. The game started at a 9 out of 10 and after I finished the game I'm going to say a 7.75 out of 10.I like ground work the devs have set up here and I look forward to trying out more games from them. Cookie Cutter is worth a play for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Metroidvania with a particularly nice focus on some pretty meaty combat. However, it is not without its flaws though - and some of them are very serious. Firstly, the parry function is utterly useless; it's in the game, but is so poorly implemented there is no point in using it. I don't know why it's been included as it's effectively a waste of everyone's time. Secondly, a lot of the areas kind of blend into one another aesthetically; while in something like Castlevania: SotN every part of the castle feels memorable and distinct, here, all the areas are... well, just kind of samey. Nothing really stands out, which makes backtracking kind of a pain - you can't remember where to go, you have to constantly be looking at your map. The game is also incredibly stingy with its levelling system - you're going to spend the first 70% of the game with almost no abilities, then the game will give you almost everything in the last hour. It's a weird choice, and kind of annoying.Finally, and most egregiously, there are a few areas with the dreaded Instant Death Spikes. If you like precision platforming, then this is obviously fine, but I don't at all. I was enjoying the beat 'em up fun, and then I ran into a brick wall of "Time this perfectly or repeat it again" platforming hell... which kind of sucked all the fun out of things - especially when those areas are followed up by some very cheap enemy placement which means that even if you manage to pull off the precise platforming, you're probably going to get knocked onto the spikes by said cheap enemies. Really left a foul taste in my mouth after nearly 17 hours of play to have this nonsense show up late game.Despite this, the rest of the game is really very enjoyable. The central gameplay loop is honestly a lot of fun and while this review might sound negative, I've had a good time with Cookie Cutter. I'm just a little irked that a few truly glaring flaws get in the way of preventing this game from being great.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is a game made by some people that really like games.It's very obvious, given the large number of references to other games throughout. From Metroid to Battletoads to Undertale. Most of these are simply background images but there's a few quests and lines of dialogue that underline this.But you can't make a game out of references, it takes more than some funny art to keep our attention and keep us traversing maps and fighting baddies.Cookie Cutter is a solid Metroidvania (ability-gated progression, a variety of weaponry) with a strong story (a cyberpunk tale of revenge, a revolution, and the friends you meet along the way), a fun combat system (multiple weapons, powers, upgrades, ect), and some truly spectacular finishers.In fact, the finishers are so good that every time I encountered a new enemy I HAD to see what kind of over-the-top mutilation was in store for them. These finishers combine the goofiness of Battletoads' morphing body parts with the gratuitous bloodshed of Blasphemous I+II. I can't think of a way to improve them other than adding more; maybe in the sequel we'll get different finishers based on how we stunned the enemy? Maybe have ones associated with the weapons we used?The art style really puts the punk in cyberpunk: We have a protagonist dressed like a Waffle House waitress with a reverse mullet. She kicks ass and takes names. She's got moxie and style, and a chainsaw, and she has a talking robot vagina. If I had to describe the animation, think about it as a cross between Ren & Stimpy, Graffiti, and tattoos. I think my only gripe is this: We're a punk character fighting a corrupt fascist bourgeois corporate entity; but the low-tier enemies all seem to be fellow victims of the system? Why are we fighting those we should be recruiting to our cause? When the revolution happens, why aren't there any fellow Denzels shoring up our numbers? Pick this game up if you enjoyed Blasphemous, or Axiom Verge, or want something a little different aesthetically. If you like beat-'em-ups. If you like to revel in violence and occasionally question the systems that keep the wealthy in power, this is a game you'd enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam could give a rating stating a recommendation with caveats. This is a fun metroidvania. The combat and aesthetic are both fun. That said, sometimes the "edgy" nature is a bit much and,..... The game doesn't have a concrete ending. Like, it ends but what is intended as a sequel hook takes much of the wind out of your sales on finishing the game. I 100% completed hoping there would be additional story to make it feel less like they are just leaving you hanging, but to no avail. Blast Brigade did the same thing and I wish creators would let a game have an ending that felt satisfying. That said, I still had a lot of fun with it and would be interested in a sequel based on gameplay and spending more time with that characters, just wish the story didn't feel unfinished.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the time I spent with Cookie Cutter and don't regret buying this game or supporting these devs in the slightest. As an animator I can feel the time and love and attention they spent on all of the animations in this game. The world is fun. The Villain is fun and highly punchable. (I personally got some catharsis in kicking the crap out of Legally Distinct Marilyn Manson) I enjoyed spending time with the main characters of Cherry and Gina. For what is likely a first game from an incredibly small team I would call this a success and the team should be proud of their accomplishment. But to call it flawless would be an outright lie.The ending sucks. It makes most of the game feel pointless and acts as a sequel bait that simultaneously goes on for far to long and says very little. An ending that tries to have its cake and eat it too but instead trips leaving the bakery and faceplants face first into it.Combat starts to feel very samey once you unlock a second primary weapon and realize that the best weapon in the game is the first one you are given. Save for a couple doors, I never switched off the default weapons. By the end I realized that since there is very little incentive to fight the baddies I began to just run through them and blitz through rooms with no real drawback. There is very little reward in exploring. 98% of secrets are either money (which I will get to later) or mob drops. It just feels bad to feel clever and notice a secret room and it be tiny with nothing but a band reference graffiti on the wall 200 gold that I don't need and some upgrade parts to a weapon I never needed to use.There is nothing to spend money on other than weapon upgrades and I never said "oh damn I wish I had more money so I could buy this upgrade" There is no sidequest that needs money. There is nothing to do with it other than hoard it until you remember to buy an upgrade.The glory kills happen way to much. The only thing you need to do is drop their health bar. There is no reason to every parry enemies. There is no real use for the force push. The subweapons are cool but slower than the default and do less damage. Its a lot of cool concepts that I can't wait to see the next iteration and attempt from this team.

_childDocuments_.review: A super slick and stylish looking Metroidvania that does well to stand on it's own with awesome visuals, solid gameplay and a simple, compelling story! Sadly I've bounced off the game but that's entirely a me thing and zero fault of the game. I do this a lot but I could easily come back to this one (and I hope I do) and keep at it. I really appreciated that the start is fast paced to get you into the gameplay but also used it's brief time to setup the world and the story quickly, efficently and with more heart than I anticipated. The visual style is strong and really makes the game stand out and pop. The gameplay is fun and pretty in-depth for a game of this type. Works wonderfully on the Steam Deck which is a must for me.  The only negative I have to say about the game so far is that sometimes there's a bit too much 'screen vomit' during action, especially a bunch of close quarters melee with a few enemies at the same time and it gets a little confusing as to exactly where you are and what is going on. But that's been by no means a deal breaker at all. The game is awesome and a great time even with that small negative in my view. Good and even great Metroidvania's are kinda all over the place these days, but if this one catches your eye I wouldn't pass it up, from what I've played so far it's easily worth getting and an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game despite some frustrating flaws.  It’s a Metroidvania that doesn’t reinvent the wheel.  It sticks with the tried and true formula, but it does it with a style and sense of adult humor sorely lacking in most games today.Let’s get the frustrating stuff out of the way first.  There is a pretty big difficulty curve that’s thrown at you almost right out of the gate.  As with every good Metroidvania, at the outset you are way underpowered.  Typically in these games, even the weakest enemies can be a little challenging.  When you’re locked into a room with many of these enemies at one time and have to defeat wave after wave until the doors unlock….well it can get VERY frustrating.  Especially so if you are a casual gamer and aren’t used to this type of game.   Compound that with the chaotic nature of the combat and the cartoon art style, and things on the screen can get very confusing fast.  There were multiple times in the game where my character was lost in the chaos and I couldn’t see exactly where she was on the screen.  It doesn’t help that these rooms zoom out and all the characters on screen are made very small.  I get that zooming out is necessary in order to show the whole room, but it would have been nice in these situations to have some way of keeping track of your character amidst all of the chaos.Sometimes the controls can feel a little “floaty”.  This isn’t a problem most of the time and is pretty much unnoticeable until you hit a section where precision platforming comes into play.  Having precise controls is essential in areas where one misstep is certain death (areas with spikes and spike-like crystals).  You have to navigate these areas using combinations of dashing, jumping, sliding and special abilities.  Constantly missing a jump onto a small ledge time and time again, is to say the least, frustrating.  Maybe I’m just used to the precise controls of Super Mario .Fast travel in a Metroidvania is essential given that you come across areas that are inaccessible until you get a new weapon or ability later in the game.  Without fast travel (warp room, teleporter, etc) the backtracking would be very tedious,  Cookie Cutter is no different, but it has a a small number of fast travel points compared with the best Metroidvanias I have played.   The different biomes (levels) in the game are sprawling mazes.  Which is awesome because it provides for a ton of exploration.  But most of the biomes have only two fast travel points.  Some only have one.  This makes backtracking tedious.  As with all good Metroidvanias, there are areas you’ll come across that you need a certain special ability or tool to access, and that ability or tool is gained later in the game - usually in a far off location - thus requiring the backtracking.  I spent a lot of time backtracking through an entire biome just to reach the area that I needed my weapon or ability to access.  Then I had to backtrack again all the way through the biome to reach the fast travel point.I also encountered some bugs in the game that, while not game breaking, are frustrating.  First is that there is an area where you have to get a big metal ball into a slot on the ceiling.  It’s a little challenging getting the ball to where you need it to be.  When I got the ball there, the receptor the ball goes into wouldn’t work.  I saw that the developers responded to a comment a person in the Steam community made about encountering the exact same issue.  What the devs suggested was to restart the game from the last saved checkpoint.  This solved the issue.  But it’s a bug they should have seen when testing the game.  It’s a pretty obvious bug and one experienced by multiple people.  The other issue is with the game crashing.  I experienced this three times.  I don’t recall what I was doing or what was happening in-game when the first two crashes occurred.  However, the third crash happened after I defeated the final boss and after the prologue.  The game’s load screen came up and the game just froze.  I had to completely reboot my Steam Deck.  After that, when I clicked the “continue” button to continue the game, my progress had only been saved from the last checkpoint before the boss.  I now have to defeat the boss again. Now that the frustrating things are out of the way, on to the good stuff!  The game is just dripping with style and humor:  it’s something that is sorely lacking in today’s video game landscape that is littered with souls-like and rouge-lite/like games.  The “kill” animations are big, bloody and hilarious.  The animation style, to me, is like Ren & Stimpy meet Loony Tunes.  It’s goofy and fun.  I just wish there was a special feature after completing the game where there is a video gallery showing all of the creative ways you can “kill” and enemy.  And it should be in slow-motion so you can see it in all its over the top, crazy, detail.  Some of the in-game animations happen so fast that it’s hard to take it all in.The exploration is great.  It’s what you’d expect from a good Metroidvania.  It doesn’t tread new ground or do anything innovative.  Which is a good thing.  The game seemed a little short when comparing to most other Metroidvania I’ve played, but each biome is huge.  Each biome also is host to several enemies that are unique to that biome, however  there are some re-appearing enemies, including some bosses that appear again  later in the game as as sort of “elite” enemies.  The bosses in each biome are also appropriate to that particular biome.  A gripe I’ve had with other Metroidvania games is that they put bosses in certain areas that seem kind of out of place. - like why are you fighting a giant bat in the middle of a castle’s foyer instead of the deep in the caves, or in the bellfrys that you discover later?The story, while not wholly original, is good.  It kept me engaged and caring about the outcome the whole time.  I was excited each time I unlocked a little more of the story.  The would and characters the developers created had me engaged from beginning to end.   I was a little surprised (pleasantly) with the direction the story went at the end.  But if definitely leaves it open for a sequel (please let there be a sequel).With all that said, the bottom line is whether this game is fun, engaging and worth your time (and money).  I definitely think it is.  I think it’s worth every nickel of its $20 price tag.  And compared to other, more expensive, Metroidvania out there it’s definitely a great value.  What the game lacks in terms of game length, it makes up for with its  fun gameplay, style and sense of humor.If I had to give this game a numerical rating on a scale of 1-10, I would put it at a 7.5.  If the flaws were fixed, it would bump it up a whole point.  The game doesn’t break new ground or innovate, but it’s a ton of fun to play despite its flaws.

Still worth playing.Cons: Several bugs; visual and audio bugs. If you leave it open for a while in the background you'll need to restart it. Countering is inconsistent/unreliable to the point of being unusable. It's worse than elden ring. Too many spike trap puzzle rooms (my opinion). I got really tired of them by the end.

_childDocuments_.review: This game opened the doors to my passion for Metroidvanias again. It has been a while that I found a game that was so detailed, filled with romance, pain and humor, the developers really put their love and passion into creating this game, the world and its characters. Cherry is not just your character, she became someone I could relate to and someone I was inspired by. She taught me to be a bad ass and to never give up. Cherry is you, she's me and everyone else who strives for someone they love. This game has a very similar combat to River City Girls and has very similar animation, making it very comic style but also maintaining originality. Attacking with Cherry can be with difficult to master since there's many variations but all are very rewarding. Exploration in this game is top notch and I loved opening up every area and finding secret walls and doors. The story itself is beautiful, and you have to understand that the romance between the main character and her lover is not for everyone. If you aren't open-minded, accept love in all shapes and colors, then this game is not for you. If you accept everyone for who they are then you will love the story between Cherry and her partner. I give this Metroidvania a 10/10, from the music, the environment, the smooth controls and gameplay. However, if you are sensitive, I would not recommend this game to you. There are many themes in this game that will turn you off and you will end up resenting a game that 2 developers put their love and soul into and ruining their reputation.

_childDocuments_.review: A good and unique metroidvania game, reminds me of that Battletoads game with hand drawn animations, even the finishers are almost similar, with the transforming and enlarging limbs. _childDocuments_.review: While Cherry’s primary function is to find Shinji, the player’s primary function is to get Cherry there. Cookie Cutter pushes the player to consistently change their play style when approaching new biomes, bosses, or fight rooms. Whether it’s providing you a new component to air dash that prevents Cherry from taking damage from enemy attacks or providing you regenerative Void Energy to evade bosses and strike just when the time is right, no two fights are quite the same.While fighting against strange creatures and mutations is satisfying, the visuals are where Cookie Cutter slashes through its competitors. Every second, every step, every pixel there’s something stunning that catches the player’s eye. The attention to detail for the environments, characters, and creature design constantly changes, encouraging the player to continue seeking out every nook and cranny. With art inspirations from rock bands and pop culture (thank you for that Ramona poster), it only solidifies the punk aesthetic that Cherry lives and breathes. Plus, finding those secret rooms – some themed or hosting strange phallic-like creatures – will never get old.While fights can grow to be frustrating, Cookie Cutter is superbly fun. Yes playing against the same boss over and over trying new abilities may seem irritating, but you always come back, ready to put up a fight. Players will never tire after watching Cherry’s aptly named Brutalities. The finishing moves will surely put a smile on your face and make you root for her as she saws her adversaries in half. Or quite literally rips them to shreds.While named Cookie Cutter, this game doesn’t fit into that mold. Like its protagonist, it’s loud, unapologetic, and at the end of the day, a bloody good time.Check out my full review on Downright Creepy:
_childDocuments_.name: Cookie Cutter

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy brutally gory cyberpunk ♥♥♥♥ and are in a borderline abusive relationship with Hollow Knight, you kinda owe it to yourself to play Cookie Cutter. There's a lot of jank here and a lot of things I think could be better, but none of those things are deal breakers. This game feels pretty tailor made for me, so I really want to emphasise how much I recommend you play it.We good? Expectations reasonably set? Awesome! now I can start my petty tirade of inconsequential gripes.Mechanically, Cookie Cutter feels like the love child of Hollow Knight, Blasphemous, and Haak, with The Dishwasher: Vampire Smile watching the action from the sidelines, rubbing one out. If the game feels like it doesn't have an identity of its own that's probably because the only unique trait it has is kleptomania.I jest, obviously. I am very much in favour of devs taking ideas that worked and putting their own twist on those ideas. I've seen people call Cookie Cutter derivative but honestly I don't give half a ♥♥♥♥ if it is. Art is regurgitation. Individuality isn't a lie, it's just not what they told you it was. Creativity is slight of hand, and to deride art for its influences is to demand a magician does the cup and balls with no cup and no balls to ensure authenticity.The controls need some serious polish, tho. If you heal and then try to move before you release the heal button, the game won't register your stick input. You have to return the stick to neutral and let go of heal before you can move at all. As gripes go, it sounds petty, but if something in a game kills me more than once, I'm at liberty to bring it up. Similarly, platforms can be finicky about when you grab them. Sometimes I snapped to ledges mid jump, but more often, I went sailing through them like Danny ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Phantom and into the whirring blades below.Coyote time feels a bit stingy too. You can tell that kind of thing isn't tuned right when you're having one-sided arguments with the physics engine or burning your double jump without realising.I have a few more little nits to pick before we can meander towards something like a conclusion, so I'mma just do them rapid fire:-Why don't checkpoints heal you?-Why doesn't hitting the back button exit out of the denzel station menu?-Hitstun feels a bit much... a lot much.-Am I an idiot or does the map not have a legend?-Why instant death spikes? I thought the industry realised yonks ago that they're a terrible experience both mechanically and existentially.The only thing that actually pissed me off, tho, was how long the game withholds basic movement mechanics. I didn't get wall jump until about an hour from the end of the game and that is insane. Give us at most an hour between each movement upgrade so we have time to learn them.While going through my list of gripes, it would be remiss of me not to mention the odd level of hyper sexualisation. It doesn't really bother me, I just question the necessity of making the helper bot look so... yonic, or sticking a pair of neon boobs on random walls. Most of the shopkeeper/upgrade NPCs make a pass a Cherry as well, and it just feels gross and weird.Anywho, robo-coochie aside, the enemy design is generally pretty stellar. Boss fights are fun to learn with patterns that make me feel smart for playing around them. However, late game fights get despicably damage spongy. They don't really evolve beyond the same basic attack pattern, you just have to wail on them for minutes of your life that you will not get back.Conclusion time: As I gazed at the end credits (unskipable, natch) I was mostly left with a profound sense of anticlimax. The story doesn't really conclude, this is more of an "end of act one" situation. given I'm as interested in story as I am in the daily goings on of the Swindon local council, this didn't really bother me. I can, however, imagine someone playing this game for the story and getting upset at the payoff being ruined for the sake of a sequel hook.Let me reiterate what I said earlier: I had a lot of fun with Cookie Cutter. It's rare these days that I finish such a long game and I'm definitely glad I did. Now if you'll excuse me, I'mma go play some Cat Quest. I have metroidvania fatigue.

_childDocuments_.review: In terms of gameplay, the combat and platforming is solid. _childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Cookie Cutter. I'm a big fan of metroidvanias, and I think this game checked most of the boxes for me. The exploration felt intuitive and most spots you need to backtrack to are marked on the map, save for some hidden rooms. I guess you could consider that a downside when you try to find everything, when you can't see what you missed. It's a shame, though, that when you backtrack, even though it's tempting to skip all the enemy hordes along the way, you still have to fight through them if you hope to upgrade everything fully. It's a bit more challenging than the average game I play, but the combat mechanics felt satisfying for the most part. Though to me, the timing windows seemed a bit harsh, when I don't have the reflexes that a lot of people have because of a visual disability. This made some deaths somewhat unfair in my impaired eyes, but I somehow managed to overcome this in the end. Some accessibility would be nice though, with all the flashy moves.There's just a few things that itch me like a rash; There's a few spots in the game where the map shows a tiny spot unexplored that you can't reach, even if you hug the walls. The other thing that kinda bothered me is the sexual puns in this game. I don't mind that they're there, but some of it is very in your face and unnecessary, like that co-cpu. I didn't dislike it, but it felt a bit cringey at times.The ending.... was unexpected. I understand the direction, but to me it felt unsatisfying, not to mention the open ended nature. I imagine there will be DLC in the future to wrap things up, but I think I'll still have mixed feelings about those events even after the story is nicely wrapped up. All that said, it was a solid game so far, even with the few bugs I encountered that I'm sure will be patched away in the future. I do hope to see the story wrapped up in future DLCs or a sequel, sooner rather than later with that unresolved ending. I have and will continue to recommend people to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cookie Cutter is one of the best Metroidvanias to release in the last several years, and if you're debating if you should buy it - even at full price - you should. Also it runs like a champ on the Steam Deck.Did you like Guacamelee? Cookie Cutter is like an R-Rated version of Guacamelee if it was made today after the onslaught of 'souls-born-whatever-we-call-it-now, you-know-games-where-you-have-to-dodge-and-parry-a-lot' games.There is a ton of fun combat and abilities to learn, excellent storytelling that far exceeds the majority of the genre, a huge map that's fun to explore, and just enough gore that happens fast enough where it doesn't bother my queasy-baby-usually-plays-nintendo-games sensibilities.Ask yourself this: Do you like Metroidvanias with good combat? Do you like sci-fi/cyberpunk stuff with sarcastic, witty humor? DO YOU LIKE GAMES THAT ARE FUN TO PLAY? Then pick up Cookie Cutter.

_childDocuments_.review: First off the game is a 10 out of 10. The game, art, and attitude is amazing. I loved this game.  I enjoyed the button mash combos, and the game even makes fun of that.  It's a game that doesn't take itself serious.  The story was cool so I don't know what people are on about expecting a complex story in a metroidvania.   I think the gameplay is great.  There is some tweaking that needs to happen with some of the abilities because i mostly stuck with the guitar.  So buff the other abilities.  Especially the start up frames.  I ran into a couple of bugs but not game breaking.  The parry has everyone crying. I will say the parry tutorial sucks but just stand in front of an enemy take a few tries to learn the parry timing because save points are literally everywhere,  and if you die there is no penalty.  This is exactly what I did and i quickly became a parry master.  The boss fights were amazing.  They had my heart pounding.  Cherry is a funny character and the whole talking vagina thing that had people feeling a type of way. Come on,   you had to expect this from the d*ckhead enemies and all the high school humor.  I get it if it's not your type of humor but it shouldn't be a knock against the game.  Overall, the game felt like a quacamelee game to me, which I also really loved, so this is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the visuals. The story was fun and compelling. Bits of lore stashed about the map fill in some blanks and provide an occasional chuckle. The combat abilities, weapons and finishers are over the top and well rendered. Enemies come in the form of cute weird little robots, or vile grotesque monsters, both leaking innards and viscera with every jab. I had great fun with it.And as much as I enjoyed it, it is a little buggy and the map looks a bit janky in places. Expect that shortcut you opened yesterday to be closed when you reload. Sometimes your camera will stutter as you try to look ahead. Save points won't automatically activate as you pass. Some of the late game abilities I'll never use after earning and trying them out. None of this diminished my enjoyment in the moment, but some spots feel unpolished. I hit 20 hours as I reached the BBEG and I'll probably give it another playthrough in a few weeks because the visuals and the jokes are that fun.

On the other hand the horde rooms become very frustrating when you have 4 different enemy types attacking you and so much stuff going on you just can't see everything or keep up. _childDocuments_.review: Stylish and fun Metroidvania with some little flaws.Technical: Framerate-Drops when to many enemies are on screen or from some environment effects, which is especially annoying in some of the later jump/skillbased sections with instant-kill spikes.Had one major bug which put me back about half an hour of progress, where i used the teleport and the whole screen slowly filled with a white flash of light. Had to quit out cause the effect was not fading away. _childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: There's a lot of metroidvanias out there now, so I'm always interested in ones that do something different or at least have a unique look to them. Cookie Cutter definitely has that. The edgy comic book style really stands out and brings life to the messed up dystopian world you're exploring. The story is that in this future, people have been given immortality by being turned into robots, but also have become enslaved to a mega corporation from it. Your creator is a scientist for that corporation who made you in secret and gets kidnapped for it, with you almost getting killed. Your driver is trying to get her back. Some of the core dialogue is voiced, but most of it isn't, which is kind of a bummer. I'd rather the game have no voice at all than only a small amount of it.You get a lot of game here for the money. As I write this, I'm 7 hours in and definitely still have a ways to go. The map is quite large, but your character also moves quickly so even though there's a lot of backtracking as you'd expect from this kind of game, it's never a slog to do.The powers and weapons you'll unlock are also rather unique and keep combat interesting. It reminds me a lot of Guacamelee or Devil May Cry, though there's no combo meter. It is fast and fluid and requires you to mix things up to manage large crowds. I only ran into a handful of boss level enemies, which were really just larger variants of standard enemies, but you will often hit combat challenge rooms with large groups of enemies that provide a similar challenge. There's a lot of enemy variety, both in looks and in their attacks and every new area brings several new ones.At least at the point I'm up to, I haven't found the game especially hard. I've definitely died a few times, but the only penalty is respawning at the last checkpoint and once you learn the patterns of enemies, it's usually easy enough to deal with them. I will say that even with the patch to make parrying less punishing, I still rarely use it because I find the timing requirements too strict. You'll also need to do a lot of exploring and backtracking to get all the powerups, but I also don't think the game is hard enough that you'll definitely need them to be able to finish it.This is a great metroidvania overall that for the price, offers a lot of hours, a great art style and a really cool world to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!  This game absolutely oozes with style that I love, it's like Tank Girl meets Blame! Very punk album cover/ indie comics sort of thing! Cherry feels right out of a 90's alternative comic, shaved head, tattoos, really a badass and a rebel. And the world is awesome, huge big maze with interconnecting pathways where you actually have to think about how to get to where you are going instead of just following a waypoint marker the entire time. Movement felt really snappy, running, jumping dashing, double jumping, punching, kicking, screaming.  Jumping to avoid a lazer or a burst of fire coming at ya, jumping onto the ledge and just making it. It felt fast without being uncontrollable. I haven't gotten the motorcycle yet, I don't know what that's gonna do for movement, but I'm looking forward to it!  Fighting felt really fluid, doing dodges and blocks and then getting in several weaker attacks or using some of the void to do a heavy hitting thing, getting the timing for parrying is tough, but so worth it to do those brutal visceral kills, also being able to toss enemies around and into environmental hazards is super satisfying! I highly recommend this game to anyone that's a fan of Metroidvanias or who is a fan of some extreme cartoon violence. 10 out of 10!

_childDocuments_.review: Wow!Let me just say, I was very pleasantly surprised by this game. I am by no means an expert when it comes to writing game reviews, but I felt really compelled to share just how great this game really is.Though I really enjoy Metroidvania style games, I've found over the years that my interest tends to wane in the final third of many of these--the exploration and combat tend to get repetitive, and I look to pick up something else as a result.I can tell you, Cookie Cutter kept me engaged throughout its entire runtime, and in the end, only left me wanting more. The visuals, combat, and exploration in this game are all top-notch, and it's the most fun I've had with a game in a long time. My playtime ran about 20 hours, though your mileage may vary.Overall, I give it a 9/10--I would have given it a 10, but there are still a few bugs I think need to be worked through before I could call it a fully polished experience. Definitely two thumbs up from me--check it out if you get a chance!

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. It has it's problems but if you're a fan of indie metroidvanias I would definitely give it a shot.Pros:*Great art style that's fairly unique in the videogaming space*Great combat, a lot of metroidvanias have mediocre/perfunctory/rote combat, but the combat here feels quite good*Good level design and exploration*The story isn't anything you haven't seen before, but it does a solid job of making you care about the charactersCons:*Some polish issues and bugs, no dealbreakers (I played after the first round of patches) but a few annoyances, including a camera bug that required me to restart the game.*Cliffhanger ending. You kill the main dude who has obviously been set up as the final boss since the opening, but then Cherry says "Sir, finishing this fight" *roll credits*. What the hell. It's not like the game is too short, but why end it like this?*Too much combat. I've heard some people complain about enemy variety, but I think they've misdiagnosed the problem. The variety is decent but there's just SO MUCH fighting the enemies kind of wear out their welcome. If they trimmed a third of the combat from the game I think the pacing would be better. Of course you could just run past stuff, which I was doing a lot in the final area.My cons section may have more words, but that's just due to my gripes being more specific. The good definitely outweighed the bad by quite a bit for me.Some other thoughts:*I'm not a fan of the "gore porn" genre so I thought I might not enjoy this, but the cartoony art style keeps it from feeling skeevy like, say, modern Mortal Kombat or Tomb Raider.*I'd estimate 15ish hours for a playthrough where you clear the whole map. It took me 8 to beat the game, but I clear games very quickly and also left a decent amount of the map unexplored. There where still several empty spots in the UI for weapons/upgrades I never found.*I could never get the hang of the parry mechanic. I've 100%ed Sekiro, cleared Dead Cells with parry builds, I could go on, so I feel like I should be able to do this. But after spending 5 minutes trying to get the timing down I just shrugged and moved on. Luckily it's totally optional.*One of my favorite protagonists of 2023

_childDocuments_.review: Cool, stylish metroidvania that's well worth your time. A lots been said about the character art/animations and for good reason, although the environment art does kinda pale in comparison. Combat is fluid and responsive (played with xbox controller) but I feel still needs some balancing to make it more interesting.  Fighting boils down to dodge and parry. Dodging is pretty OP with its very generous i-frames. Don't believe I died in combat more than a few times with hit and run tactics. Parrying is basically useless and can actually be pretty punishing if you miss the timing as enemies can chunk your health bar with just a few hits (but if you insist on learning the parry timing for each enemy the healing mechanic is extremely forgiving outside of boss fights). Air juggling is also pretty OP as it essentially perma stuns non elites, otherwise you'll just get hit right through normal ground attack combos. Sounds like I'm doing a lot of complaining but I highly recommend if you're looking for a super solid metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so, let's get a few things out of the way if they weren't obvious from glancing at the trailer or screenshots: this is metroidvania with excessive gore and some sexual fanservice. If that kind of stuff bothers you at all, this game ain't for you.Secondly, I'll address a few technical issues I had within the short time I've played so far. Now, this might just be because I'm on a potato PC, but the loading times are pretty bad. The first time I thought the game had actually froze so I closed, rebooted, and... yeah. Just had to wait a while longer. But they also happen like... every screen or so. Which might get a tad annoying over time lol. Had a random crash too, but I think it's because my stupid HD updated in the middle of playing. Though I did take a screenshot of the errors just in case the dev needs them. Those aside, there were a few inconsistencies between the spoken dialogue and the text (no biggie honestly, just a nitpick.) And the opening cutscene in particular had a lot of audio glitches (but again, probably just my potato.)Now with THAT out of the way: dude, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥' awesome. I don't think I've seen another metroidvania done in this style, it's so unique and breathtaking. The combat (at least at the very start) is pretty fairly balanced, I died but it was through my own fault of not learning how to DODGE lmao. The story also seems pretty interesting thus far, and the music? Beautiful backdrop to the whole thing. I think this is certainly worth picking up if you're at all interested in it.Edit: after a few more hours with it, it really is much more style over substance. I got bored of it already. _childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty fun although it does have some annoying bits which will hopefully be fixedThe art style and level designs are cool, has the usual upgrades to unlock new areas etc.Has some cool finishing moves which are really OTT.I really enjoyed the story line, lesbian robots FTWThings it falls down on....It runs like ass on steam deck despite being "verified", I played a large chunk of it on the deck and I lost count how many times I died due to it stuttering like a mofo.The parry system is still broken post patch, I played when first released and it was impossible to consistently parry, patch was released and still didn't seem right, ended up competing the game without parrying.Quite often key presses for instigating a finisher move aren't picked up (despite definitely being in range) and the character is instead doing special attacks  as uses the same button, I think thus may be because its trying to do a combo, the finisher should take precedence over this.A couple of bits I found annoying but not bugsInstadeath spikes not near a save point, there are a couple of these in the game, I feel there should be a save plonked next to any precise platform sections, especially when monsters respawn that you have to dodge past to get back to where you are.I think it might be handy to have a few invincible frames after the finisher, it's annoying performing a finisher on an enemy only to get twatted by someone without the chance to dodge out of their way.I'm still giving the game a positive review as it's still really cool and the devs should be congratulated (Hi devs if you are reading, Merry Christmas)

_childDocuments_.review: For ~$10 price in my region -- I can recommend it. But not for Steam Deck users, because on it this game suffers from huge stutters (Proton GE 8-25). On Asus Ally this problem persists as well, but it occurs much more rarely there, plus VRR smoothers it out very nicely (what VRR always does).Minor recommendations, if needed:* Don't save energy, spam Y as much as you like.* Don't forget about B skill, crowd control -- it's free and is actually useful.Pros:* Level design is alright-good (I've skipped just one or a few hardest endgame puzzles because wanted to finish the game already, but still, all the rest I've cleared, totally willingly).* Music is not great, and maybe not even always good, but most of the time it's good that's for sure.* Combat system is pleasing and fluid, despite maybe not being enriched with a lot of different combo chains. No, it's rather simple, but good, more than just "enough" and "fitting".* Visual style is cool! I'm, honestly, generally not into gore, dismembering and meat, but here it does look cool and to the point, yeah.* Respectively all these dialogs filled with "yo, wassup, wocha doin?" were at the absolutely right place, here, haha. Honestly, I've skipped all the terminals with all those boring texts, and all descypted logs too, that's not for me. Actually, most of the live conversations as well. But verbal style of what I've seen was nice, haha.* Game performance is good (except stutters!). Game could've had more settings though, or, I should say, at least some settings.* Impactful skills (not all) and weapon (not all) needed for puzzle solving. That's great, I like to use collected stuff, not just collect it. Same for skills, who likes +10% max HP, with conditions? +75% max HP -- now that's something. Same for movement, farming, other skills (no spoilers).* Surprisingly (for me, at least) the final boss was not some 999999999 HP turbo sniper, dropping AOE nukes every 10 seconds. But, instead, just active, fat, slightly complex, interesting normal boss. Thanks I guess!Cons:* As of now the game is highly NOT recommended to be played on the Steam Deck. At the beginning the game runs mostly good. The deeper you're into the game, the more stuttering you'll see. You can try limiting TDP to 5-6 W and iGPU frequency to ~400 MHz and fps cap to 30-60 fps, and that'll help at first. But in the Golden Tower (endgame area) you'll literally be seeing a slideshow, with drops of your regular 30-60-90 fps to 0 few times a second. No kidding, no exagerrating, literally.* The game may time to time skip your inputs, ignoring them completely. Not frequent problem if the game doesn't stutter on your machine and, instead, well, a very frequent if it does.* The game sometimes likes to ignore saves. You may discover the new teleport, but the next time you'll try to find it on the map to teleport to it -- it won't be there (I recommend pressing dpad UP on each newly found teleport to enter it, to make sure it's saved). You may discover the new respawn point (and even hit the dpad UP button to save progress), see the "saving..." message, die, and get respawned somewhere else, on the previous respawn, not the last one.* The game may rarely but "surprise" you with the closed gates, which you've definitely opened before (another progress save bug?). Or the not opened red floor door on the map, which actully will be opened when you return to it (because you've indeed opened it before, this is the map mark just being stuck).* Not all quest rooms, with red crates as the reward, are worth solving. I'd say around the half, maybe lesser half, aren't. Because at first you'll be rewarded with skills (cool!), later in the game -- with resources (which you can simply purchase, meh), and later -- with money (wut? you serious?). As you understand this is a straightforward game walkthrough time stratching mechanism (in the game of genre that already is all about the backtracking; devs add more unrewarding backtracking; cool... probably for someone).* The amount of special effects is too high. If you're trapped in large enemy room, where the camera zooms out, and a few enemies are attacking you -- all what left for you to be doing is only to keep hitting Y constantly to clear your way out. Because you'll see literally nothing there to be able to make any situative decisions, nothing, just a pile of textures.* Traps are in many if not most cases not synchronized (it is the more noticeable the deeper you're progressing in the game, obviously, because the more complex traps will be there). Example: if you need to jump on the platform when the laser is off, the repeat cycle of the laser will be 3 seconds, and 5 seconds for the platform; so if you miss the first awailable window, you'll have to wait for lcm(3, 5) = 15 seconds for the next attempt window. When in good game it'd be, for example, lcm(3, 6) = 6 seconds. Just 1 second difference changes a lot, do you see? They -- don't. At least didn't.* Okay, the first weapon, probably been shown even in the trailer, the iron hand, is cool, simple, useful and handy, alrighty (upgraded it to the max and didn't regret even for a moment). Two more are tied to the puzzles and progressing, that's great, I liked it! But the rest two, well... the moment I've gained them is the moment I've never used them again after. Usefulness somewhere on that level.* Parry system is unreliable, unpredicable, but, fortunatelly, unneeded as well. Good luck in attempts to master it, or you can just forget about it (I've personally finished the game, and haven't been using it).* Honestly, enemies, shooting through textures, through 1-2 floors below the player? Are you serious?

detailed_description: After ten years of peace...the evil Daimur has returned! Princess Arzette is the Kingdom of Faramore’s only hope to restore harmony to the land! In this brand new interactive action adventure game, you control the resourceful princess Arzette. Travel through multiple breathtaking locations filled with scum, villainy and secrets, speak with the locals to uncover mysteries and objectives, and take on the evil Daimur as Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore brings you the best interactive gaming experience since the invention of the CD-ROM! Featuring: Hand painted backgrounds and incredible sprite art. Fully voice-acted cartoon cinematics with a colorful cast of characters. A sprawling world with diverse locations and many secrets. Acquire powerful items and abilities by exploring and helping those in need. Veteran dev team including artist Rob Dunlavey, Digital Foundry's John Linneman and Audi Sorlie, voice talent Jeffrey Rath and Bonnie Jean Wilbur, and award winning composer Jake 'Button Masher' Silverman.

_childDocuments_.review: I've long held a belief that there should be more remakes of outright bad games, just to see if they could get it right the second time. Dopply, Arzette's lead developer, literally did that in 2020, when he released his unofficial remakes of Link: The Faces of Evil and Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon. I don't necessarily believe these remakes magically make those games good, but it certainly made them more playable, and arguably more importantly, accessible.Arzette then represents the actual redemption of the CD-i games. It retains the aspects people actually liked about those games, mainly the bizarre and humorous animated cutscenes and over the top voice acting, while building around the improved gameplay of the remakes. This results in a shockingly high quality experience, and, in my eyes anyway, proves that there was greater potential in the CD-i games than many would care to think about.

_childDocuments_.review: Word of caution: There will be spoilers, but they're tied to game mechanics mostly. This is a review from someone who's only played for two hours or so. That's $10 an hour. This is a nice price. It'l be more value as you play longer.  UPDATE: Just finished the game! Adding a new section to the comments to reflect this. It'l have spoilers, so I don't recommend reading it until you have gotten far into the game. Don't worry, if curiosity gnaws at you, the spoilers are mostly insignificant to the plot.Alright, so I've never ever posted a review fellas. Ever. I'm usually an introvert, and this game broke me. It's just that good.I was chilling on Discord and got sent the trailer for this by my best friend. As an avid YTP fan, I saw it reverently referencing it's source material; this game is based off of the classic CD-i Zelda games, and it's proud of that fact. It has no shame whatsoever. The intro screen when you boot up the game is drawn in crayon. The names and theming is blatant. If you know, you know. It is amazing.For those of you who are unfamiliar with the CD-i Zelda games; they're 2D platformers with notoriously difficult gameplay, entertaining cutscenes of inconsistent quality, secrets, instant death pits, areas you have to revisit with traps and danger, and other lovable junk that made those games so memorable. You are entering the splash zone. The game is DESIGNED to be this way, and it hits the mark. Turn off subtitles before starting the game. (unless you have a need for the accessibility due to health) You'll thank me later. It's the difference between a joke catching you out of left field and being spoilt before the characters tell it.It's the Zelda CD-i games, with all the bells and whistles. While the controls have been made more accessible, they're intentionally arbitrary. The hitbox of the enemies and your own weapons may float over or under them even if the sprite hits. Enemies will prepare to swing their weapon and before the animation finishes, you take the hit. Daring to touch a body of water will obliterate you. Some areas have bottomless kill pits ABOVE LOWER FLOORS OF THE AREA. The controls are simple, and there's a nice tutorial for them. The bomb arc is intentionally janky and you'll learn that the game relies on classic platforming tricks (like jumping in a way to clip past a platform to avoid landing on it) and death traps, all the juicy stuff. It's challenging, and it's very fun. This game is whooping me harder than Cuphead.There is "Casual Mode". It lets you find heart drops and this actually makes the game slightly harder, since enemies drop less rubies and ammo when you're grabbing hearts.If you die, you respawn at the start of a ROOM (not a level) or at a checkpoint flag or bonus area. This encourages you to poke your head into places and see what's inside, even if you can't explore it yet. There is a LOT of backtracking, and it's the classic kind that you're signing up for. When you consider what this game is aiming to be, it is absolutely perfect. The controls and sprites are smooth, you'll eventually figure out what's going on and have a good time. Or maybe you won't, I'm a random internet person, not your mother. (i hope you have fun anyways)There is a merit to making a game artistically bad. Like, intentionally drawing "bad" art but making it look amazing, such as fantastic spritework and MSpaint-style cutscenes, inconsistent anatomy, quirks and charm that made the source material shine. The backgrounds are gorgeous. The spritework is beautiful. The cutscenes are everything I could have ever wanted and more. While there are some design gaffes, they can be completely forgiven due to the game being what it is.The enemy design consists of the same kind of colorful cast you'd see the Angry Video Game Nerd complain about. Varied in design, accessible in theme. Anyone who has played a classic video game can recognize the feel they're going for, and like the rest of the spritework, they look great.  Some people will turn their noses at the cutscenes. "Cyan", they say. "This looks awful." That's the point. They're based off of the Zelda CD-i games and the artists are clearly more than capable of higher quality work. It's by design, it's lovely, and some of it is so cursed that I squint or avert my eyes for a moment. Moving on!Tony Trippi and William Havlicek, eat your hearts out. Jake Silverman, also known as Button Masher, has done an amazing job at capturing the feel and mood of the old games with a modern flair. It sounds like MIDIs mashed with classic game disk music, it's just glorious on the ears. It doesn't get in the way of the gameplay, and the other sound effects are inoffensive and nice. Hard hit means no, you can't damage that. Zap is zap. Boom is boom. It's easy to understand and enjoy.One big thing is that none of the stuff in the game has hurt my ears so far or made me feel a headache from playing. A lot of modern games can be disorienting due to their soundscapes and this one feels comfortable and fun. The voice acting is also inconsistent in quality. Some of it sounds like it was recorded by a professional, other bits of it sounds like they grabbed a random person to do lines and did it on the first take. While it is the point, I will say that there are good voiced cutscenes, and then there are cutscenes that could use more ENERGY in the voice acting! Some of the VAs just sound sleepy or like it was recorded on a 2000s webcam, or like The Guy's voice acting in I Wanna Be The Guy, or the AVGN's voice acting in the modern Screenwave era episodes. There's a fire and passion behind voices, tone or not, that can be felt. Some of it wasn't there, but I'll be nice and real; that's probably the point. I still enjoyed it!Not gonna tell ya, bud. Go in, enjoy it for yourself, and formulate your own opinion. Don't let my review dissuade you from playing it, because at the end of the day, you'll have your own experience and I won't steal it from you by spoiling the game. Just try to enjoy yourself without expectations. If you don't want something, then everything you do or enjoy is a treat.This is a really, really good video game so far. Like Palworld and how it inspires itself on Pokemon, this game lacks shame and is proudly inspired by the CD-i games. Potential for lawsuits aside, I think that it's a definite buy if you enjoy classic video games that challenge the player and make them stop to think or go "Where do I go now?" It encourages taking notes of spots to revisit, being patient, failing to learn to succeed, and a lot of the cornerstones of gaming from the before-times of the medium. It's really fun. Go play it! Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game 100%, and wanted to leave a positive review here to hopefully get this game to the "Overwhelmingly Postive" rating it deserves.Seedy Eye managed to capture the goofiness and gameplay of the original CD-i games without the messy controls or wonky level designs where you could never tell what was a platform or just a part of the foreground. It doesn't overstay its welcome while encouraging exploration and even leaves you with a couple fun extras when the adventure is all done and dusted, and the soundtrack is just excellent all around.There's some minor issues with the amount of backtracking you do, but the levels are thankfully short enough to where it doesn't feel like a chore (However, there's an item trade quest towards the end that sends you to one level, then to another, then back to the first level again), and some of the FMV video cutscenes don't look like they match the others in terms of quality (A few you can tell are just 3D models sometimes), but those are incredibly minor gripes in what is otherwise a fairly priced game that knows exactly how long it needs to be.If you feel the need to go back to the YTP days of yore but with a good game attached to it this time, I guess you better get going!

_childDocuments_.review: As a CERTIFIED PSYCHO whose only completed Zelda games to this date are the CD-i duo, I feel like I kinda have a finer appreciation for what Arzette does. As someone who really unironically likes the Zelda CD-i gameplay and its world, I'm glad  to say that this game does almost everything good that the games it is paying homage to do but even better.In general, the gamefeel is much better, movement is less tight, jumps are less strict, it's a vast improvement.The cutscenes are lovingly produced and voice acted perfectly. My only complaint is some of the characters later on lack cutscenes and just use un-voice acted dialogue boxes, although this IS understandable. The progression is MUCH better than the original. Almost all the items and upgrades you receive serve a purpose and it is a delight to feel your power slowly increasing.My only complaints is that the background art of the levels lacks the exact hand painted quality that the originals had, and that is something I miss. Only a few levels live up to the vibes of the originals. The music also, I wish every sub area of the levels had a slightly different track like is the case with the originals, again though, I understand this limitation.Needless to say I want to say thank you to the man behind this all for his passion relating to these two awkward pieces of gaming history and the culture surrounding them. I loved this game.Here's hoping for a sequel! Starring the Link lookalike and hopefully with some I.M. Meen references :))

_childDocuments_.review: Despite their infamous status in internet culture, the Zelda CD-I games (not counting Zelda's Adventure) were built off of a solid foundation that sadly wasn't complimented by the games' choppy framerate, unforgiving difficulty, and baffling control scheme. At their core, they are adventure games where you slowly uncover more of the map by completing objectives and obtaining useful items. In a sense, the world was one giant puzzle box that you had to solve piece by piece as is tradition for Zelda games around that time. After trying out the Zelda CD-I remasters created by Dopply years ago, I believe they had potential to be good if the hardware was capable of handling games of this scope.Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore is a continuation of the groundwork the Zelda CD-I duology laid out with the refinements of Dopply's prior work with the remasters. The end result is a great action/adventure sidescroller that succeeds its predecessors while also staying true to the tropes of the CD-I games. The gameplay is much more fast and frantic with some new combat tools and upgrades akin to a standard Metroidvania. The environments and music are pleasing to listen to and look at, everything checks out.Although the animated cutscenes in the CD-I games are infamous for their ridiculous quality and reputation as a Youtube Poop goldmine, you never really got a game with hand drawn animation at the time. They're not good, but I always admire the ambition despite the outcome. Arzette's cutscenes are in a similar vain, but each one is drawn in a different style with one being fully 3D animated. With how exuberant most of the characters you meet can be, the change in style adds a layer of depth to the cutscenes while also always being fun to watch.Arzette is just a good game all around, there's not really much I can dissect outside of how open the world can be on a replay. Like how you can get sword beams on your first visit in the forest which opens up so many pathways instead of backtracking to the cave, desert, and canyon for the first hour. I enjoyed my time with Arzette and if possible, a randomizer could add even further replayability given how open the game's structure really is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a simple action platforming Metroidvania title, at its heart - and that heart is in good working order.The appeal is in how it invokes the aesthetics of an infamous set of games using licensed Nintendo characters on a failed multimedia system (the CD-i from the early 1990s), so if you aren't familiar with Hotel Mario, the Faces of Evil, or the Wand of Gamelon... you might be left wondering what's so special about the intentionally silly low-resolution animations of intentionally hit-and-miss voice direction. The homages to characters animated by the long-defunct Animation Magic studio might fly over your head, but for those 'in the know' they're a treat to discover.Even so, it's a technically competent action game with simple design, gorgeous level design that is only rarely unclear on what is a platform, and the rare bit of aimless backtracking across replayed short levels when it's not clear where to go next. There are a few instances where one needs to make a blind descent which is the biggest level design issue by far, though the penalty for death is merely just resetting the room you fell in, so the annoyance rarely lasts long.General advice: always carry bombs, and if something looks cracked, throw a bomb at it. Hitboxes can be a bit deceptively large, but as your sword deflects virtually all projectiles the issue is usually mitigated. You can find a shielding item early on that lets you take projectile-heavy situations at your own pace usually, and enemies that only attack with projectiles tend not to deal damage by being directly touched (so if you encounter a shielded enemy you can't yet damage, typically you can just walk past them - and will need to do so at least once).With some better signposting this would be an even better game, but on a ~5 hour first time run this didn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of making a CD-i inspired pseudo-parody game like this is the kind of thing that I could've seen being pretty insufferable in the wrong hands. The legacy of these games largely boils down to its cutscenes and its "so bad its good" nature, but basing an entire game around this not only would've made for something that was barely a game, but also something profoundly annoying and submerged in tedious ironic humour. Arzette being developed by the same person who made the PC remasters of those games puts the game in a much more favourable position however, with a very clear understanding on the intricacies of the game as a whole being put on display, as well as coming across as a far more earnest tribute as opposed to pointing and laughing.Arzette understands the incongruencies of its inspirations well, but also digs further down to see the good that game had as well, expanding upon them to create versions of these concepts that are more palatable, rather than getting rid of them. In this regard, saying that this game is just "CD-i but good" misses out on analysing the way that the positive qualities here are largely lifted from them, with the positive aspects simply highlighted and some of the elements obscuring these qualities being lessened, wanting to craft a similar sense of identity. One of the biggest ways I see this working is how boss fights are handled in this, with all of them functioning in very similar ways to the CD-i titles, but tweaked to still feel more like actual boss fights. The strategies for all of these is extremely simple, with them all either being countered either by being in certain locations where they cannot reach you, or countering all of their attacks with a single item, but these fights still go on for a bit, requiring multiple hits and the like, even though it's always entirely trivial. This riffs nicely off of the idea of "the bosses in these games get hit with an item once and go poof", by keeping the spirit of this alive while making it feel just a tad less anticlimactic, still feeling like an actual confrontation to some degree.The other enjoyable aspects of the original games are also here in full force, with the gorgeous backgrounds and awesome, energetic music making the game an absolute treat presentation wise. It's also interesting to note that despite the backgrounds going for such a similar style, that there aren't any instances of it being hard to tell what is a platform and what isn't outside of a couple of instances that very clearly felt intentionally funny to me. The platforms themselves aren't highlighted or made overly visible or anything like that, it's just that the scenery is composed in such a way to make it feel immediately intuitive, making you feel fully immersed in traversing these painted landscapes.The cutscenes are also delightful as well of course, as while they're not quite as wild with the constant character distortions and expressiveness of the smallest of details, the vibe is close enough and falls quite comfortably into its own style that runs very closely parallel, rather than entirely mimicking everything. The writing contains a bit of meta-humour but also largely feels like a nice bit of camp that's elevated by the cutscene style rather than focusing solely on making everything seem intentionally awkward and "bad". Even the animation itself tends to go for slightly different quirks to focus on, the biggest of which being that Arzette herself never seems to look quite the same in any 2 cutscenes, always shifting between a variety of incredibly similar, yet nonetheless different styles.Really, really love what this game sets out to do and I think that it culminates in something that feels special in how earnest it is. I can't see many cases where this idea would've come to life in a satisfying way to me if basically anyone else had handled this project, but here it is, and it's an absolute blast :)8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the very definition of "understood the assignment." Every single aspect of this game PERFECTLY captures what made the Zelda CD-i games notable while simultaneously being actually fun to play.The animation captures the style exactly right, the voice acting is exquisitely amateur, and the gameplay is perfectly janky enough to capture the vibe without actually being frustrating. In fact, I'd say it's remarkably satisfying. Although the total playtime isn't *terribly* long, it's actually pretty content-dense, with tons of optional upgrades and sidequests. It is very apparent from beginning to end that this is a labor of love, and in a weird sort of way it gave me a new appreciation for the original games. I very much look forward to whatever Seedy Eye makes next.
