_childDocuments_.review: You know you're in for a treat when the developer is subtly named after the console they're parodying.In all my years of gaming, I thought nothing could surprise me now. So imagine my amazement when they first announced Arzette: The Jewel of Farramore. A game based on three of the worst games ever created, and yet it's actually good.(Take notes Shaq Fu the legend reborn, THIS is how you turn something bad into something awesome.)The game nails the look and feel of the infamous titles of the 90sDeceivingly beautiful backgrounds where it's not always clear what's a platform, Check!Awkwardly animated cutscenes with no background and cursed imagery, Check!Can only pick up items with your sword, Nope! That BS is now completely optional!Awful controls where you press up to jump and one button is assigned to too many different actions, Nope! Nobody wants that back. Controls are way more intuitive here. They even have button prompts for Nintendo Switch controllers.A Final Boss that dies in one hit, Check!I love it!This game takes the look of the dreaded games of old, but the experience is more akin to Half Genie Hero than the Wand of Gamelon.And it's all done in a campy tongue in cheek manner. With a comic relief who looks alarmingly familiar, and... a bonus minigame where you close doors? WOW! Who came up with this? This is peak gameplay right here! Seriously! Give the guy who came up with this Game of the Year! FOR ETERNITY! INCREDIBLE!They just saved us from bad gameplay! They won! I guess you know what they say, all toasters toast toast! Gee, it sure is boring around here now I'm done playing. Maybe I'll go play Hero mode. I can't wait to bomb some... bunny... golem things. Say, you're not afraid of horsemen are you? Just don't go into the pit! It burns!(This review will now be stopped as the reviewer cannot contain his laughter.)

_childDocuments_.review: This is... okay. I may need to give it more time but there's not enough to make me want to. The cutscenes are pretty boring. I feel like they probably give you information you want, but don't necessarily need. It's mostly just, get a new ability, retread every level you've already played in case there's one spot where that ability applies. The hitboxing is not great. For having so many platforming elements, it's far too often nonobvious where you can stand vs. where you cannot. Often times, standable platforms will appear to be part of the background, or non-standable platforms will appear standable. There's also no way to jump down through something you can jump up through, unless that's an ability you get later. That's been a solved problem in platformers since the 80s and 90s, I would expect to be able to descend through a platform like in, well, every other platforming game since. Enemies that throw things at you are incredibly annoying because the thrown objects are far too large given their trajectory. It makes you think you could jump over them, but you get hit every time. The only solution is to hit them with your sword. Also many of these enemies have way too much health, which means you sit there and just hit them over, and over, and over, with little fun to be had.The level design and powers are interesting, movement mechanics are okay (jumps are a bit too floaty), characters might be memorable if you can get through their dialogue. Overall it's an okay game. Still way better than most AAA trash out there right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I was debating on making this a negative review or not because this game existing as a whole is just amazing, there is very clearly a huge amount of talent behind it's development. I will make keep this a positive review but I will still lay out the main problem that I see with this game as I genuinely can't scratch off the feeling that this was supposed to be a fan sequel game to Zelda CDI instead of a spiritual successor but couldn't because of copyright concerns which sadly would be warranted if true with how litigious Nintendo is after all.The reason for the speculation is that this game isn't just a spiritual successor as instead of just having a few characters that are similar, there is about six and they are all integral to the story which isn't just limited to the hero's side as the lineup is indeed filled with incredibly familiar characters to The Faces of Evil but also even the villain is like Ganon down to the whole being defeated by a book thing and his right hand man is also heavily inspired by a character from The Wand of Gamelon.This makes enjoying the story incredibly hard as I keep getting reminded of the counterparts for these characters over and over again, that any progression in the narrative feels like I accidentally slipped into another universe and I'm seeing the events for a game after "Arzette: The Faces Of Evil" and "Arzette: The Wand Of Gamelon" which isn't something that I could say is a problem for Freedom Planet or A Hat in Time as those games don't rely on such incredibly similar characters to the things that they are being a spiritual successor of on top of feeling like they are after the events of one of those games although in a Bizarro Universe version of it.The worst part about this though is that the rest of the game does not have this problem, it's just the main cast who are stuck as strange off brand versions of characters that the main audience base would already know and care way more about.To end this large critique of the reliance on having a narrative that feels like a sequel but isn't is that Zelda CDI itself had this problem as well although to a lesser extent. The Wand of Gamelon both had a replacement character for the main guiding character and the shopkeeper which are anonymously less beloved than the ones that showed up in The Faces of Evil so it sucks that Arzette's main story cast fall into this same trap especially when the game built around them is so good.

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all, let's be clear here: There was clearly a lot of love put into this game, especially in recreating the feel of the CDi games - if you enjoyed this game, don't let me take that away from you.When I saw this pop up in Steam, however, my question was..."but why the Zelda CDi games?"Forgive me, I have never actually played the Zelda CDi games, but through cultural osmosis, I have only known them as janky unfun games where most of the enjoyment came from the memes.And...well...let's just say they hit the nail on the head with this game (sans the memes)Going forward, I'm approaching this game as basically someone completely new to Zelda CDi games. All I know about those games are the millions of YTP that have been made about the king and Link eating dodongos.The game is extremely old-skool, and I'd argue to the game's detriment. There's a lot just hateful game design built into it - as in the game hates you the player. Enemies positioned on platforms that basically guarantee you'll get hit, hit boxes that are large that basically making getting hit unavoidable, instant death traps and pits just out of screen of the camera requiring leaps of faith, platform design that's difficult to discern what's a background element and what's an element the player can jump on, and so on.It's all old-skool. I imagine that ***is*** the dev's intention, but I beg to ask "but why?". As an opportunity to prove there is something to love about the actual gameplay of the CDi games and that they aren't just great meme material, wouldn't you want to offer a more approachable experience?This hateful game design philosophy is consistent throughout the game's design as well, beyond just the moment-to-moment interactions.You will be expected to replay levels multiple times. Play through the forest level, get a quest, return to town and get quest item, play through the forest level, give quest item to complete it. Play next level, get new collectible, go back to the forest level, play through it, use new collectible to access a boss. Play next level, get new gadget to open new pathway, go back to the forest, open the new path way. I estimated you'd need to replay the forest level at least 7 times, and that's just the forest level. Each level is designed in a similar way. Holy game-padding batman.And here's the thing; there's no random elements. When you are replaying the level, it is exactly the same every time. They couldn't bother with changing enemy placements or adding a score attack/time attack to levels to at least give you an additional challenge when replaying the levels. It just feels like padding for the sake of padding.My verdict is; if you like these old skool games, warts and all, then yeah, you'll probably have a great time. Personally, nah, this just got on my nerves. I'd rather just look up the cutscenes on Youtube to get my fill (side note; main character comes off as a complete b/tch, some of her first pieces of dialogue are her complaining or making sarcastic jokes at people's expense)I picked up this game wondering "Why would anyone remake the CDi games?" and I have left asking the same question.

_childDocuments_.review: They tried to make a good version of the Zelda CD-I games, which apparently averages out to a mediocre action-platformer. The exploration is too simplified and clearly marked by massive color-coded roadblocks. The animated cut-scenes are verbose and excessively meme-heavy. The combat is so dead-simple you can button-mash through most of it, and you have an item which blocks/reflects all enemy projectiles on command. All the bosses are trivial, except the final one, and even that's just a basic platforming gauntlet.Basically, everything here has been done better elsewhere. It's not even a particularly good homage to the CD-I titles. I played those the same day I played this, and they're far funnier and more interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't live up to the hype. It looks at first like it has more effort put into it than a simple meme game retread, with all the artwork and music, but its really a shallow experience that repeats itself after the first few levels. The controls and responsiveness of the game are also spotty in ways that a brand new $20 game really shouldn't have issues with. There's just enough content to cheat you out of your $20 by making you go over the the 2 hour time limit, but then after that it becomes extremely samey and repetitive. There is also no character development at all, and the writing can't make up its mind if it wants to be funny or serious. Not worth what they're they're asking for it, play something else instead. I wish I could get my money back.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Game is not good, play Hollow Knight or GRIME instead.This game is like a 4/10 at best, for me anyway. Designed to be a 'good' version of the infamous CDI Zelda games, Arzette: Jewel of Faramore is a 2D action platformer with an item-based progression system, somewhat like a Metroidvania. However, playing the game, I largely found progression nonsensical and all over the place. At the beginning of the game, so many things are inaccessible, but by the time I unlocked more items, I found myself unable to remember what I could do with them: the flute, gauntlet and the different color magic. There's also this quest to make your sword stronger, but by the time I completed it, all could use it for was Daimur's lair. I more or less accidentally stumbled into all the game's bosses before.Speaking of bosses, I found them all extremely underwhelming - and this goes for the entire combat as well. Regular enemies are fine, but then you have enemies which take multiple hits, which are just annoying: especially the musquito hives. Either you use a bomb (which you may need for secrets/progression) or you wait a long time to slowly kill it with five hits plus I-frames. Not to mention the level design often makes it difficult if not impossible to avoid these enemies. It often includes leaps of faith, too, with no way to look down to see what's below, resulting in frequent deaths. Yes, respawning is generous, but it's still annoying.So what does this game have? Well, good controls, but considering how bad they were in the game's source of inspiration, that's not a high bar to clear. It also had a few good laughs here and there, and the sprite work is nice. At the end of the day, it seems this game was mostly made to recreate the laughs we all had when we discovered the CDI's terrible cutscenes back in the early days of YouTube Poop. But even that still doesn't always work with the game's inconsistent voice acting and its attempt to have actual drama in the story. They should have just gone full-on camp with this game, and the decision to not do that just baffles me.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A funny and quirky ""metroidvania"" that is on the shorter side. The cutscenes and aesthetics, as well as the level design, is refined versions of things that aren't made anymore; all which makes this a *very* unique experience.My only immediate complaint is the price point which is a bit high for how relatively short the game is. _childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful, five-hour-long ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in video game form. Imagine all the labor, the careful fine-tuning, the concerted effort of so many people that went into producing this tribute to some of the worst video games ever made. Every detail is perfect, from the low-res title screen with its enormous jagged pixels to the way the music cuts out when you initiate dialogue with an NPC (because of course the console has to read from a different track on the game disc now).Oh, and the game's singular unskippable cutscene: perfection.I finished the entire thing in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: There's a buttery smooth action game with a huge personality hidden under all the references to the funny Zelda meme game.You have to be familiar with the game's inspirations to fully appreciate both the skill and effort that went into reinterpreting this aesthetic. It's a jarring, funny looking, and amateurish style, but it's not random, and they found a way to make it their own and make it interesting. Getting to the next cutscene is another opportunity to see how they twist and bend these goofyass characters. You can tell this was made by people who know their stuff. Having autistic levels of appreciation for animation definitely adds to the experience. The CDi inspiration goes beyond the cutscenes. They even kept stuff like stabbing friendly npcs to talk to them, which has an in-universe explanation here, which is hilarious to me.I mentioned the look a lot, but there's a genuinely fun and competent metroidvania here. Replace everything with generic modern clean fantasy assets, and you still have a solid action game. Every character has a colorful personality, exploration and side quests are rewarding, and I found some parts to be genuinely clever and hilarious. Can't help but admire the work that's been accomplished here. Nice
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short, sweet, to the point, but a blast all the way through. It's a passion project, and if you like silly but charming then you'll find a lot out of this game. Only criticism I can think of is that rope feels a little useless, but that's not really a big deal. It's just kinda there. Bring a controller. Or buy the spoon shaped controller.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I owned this game for a while before playing. I bought it because I had seen it mentioned on a video about the Philips CD-i Zelda games and decided to try it out. The game play and controls (especially the controls!) are like a completely fixed verison of the old games I had so much admiration for in spite of their many, many flaws. But this game hits everything right all the way down to over the top, so bad it is amazing voice acting and cut-scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game way more than I thought I would. The humour in the cut-scenes is genuinely funny and doesn't take itself seriously. The gameplay itself although pretty short, is very fun and not overly difficult. Really enjoyed collecting stuff and returning to levels etc. By FAR, the most impressive thing for me was the soundtrack - it's so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: this game takes me back to stuff I played on the computer when I was growing up--it feels like it understands this era of adventure game beyond just the CDI games it's a blatant homage to. _childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Great game that is dedicated to its idea.While you might not have been alive or remember when the CDI games where on the market, or even when they dominated the youtube poop scene; here is a game that allows you to experience those games in a tidy package. Its suprising that we dont see more similarly to it, its so unique and should be experienced by anyone with an interest in games.And while the game is "short" and can be 100% in less than a day, that is not a reason not to play it. While it may not be in your budget, get it on sale if you're at least interested in the game.Gameplaywize, its a "level based metroidvania" (levels have secrets that need items to unlock that can be aquired from other levels) where you have to play some levels multiple times, and can get a bit repetative, but the art (yes there is art outside of the cutscenes) is realy good; and i cant tell if this is authentic to the CDI games, i have never played them.Fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette is a pretty good game. Worth buying if it's on sale for under $20, I'd say. The game isn't very complex or difficult, but the story and presentation are charming and enjoyable. One thing you'll notice is that this game is pretty short. I'd recommend going for 100% even if you're not the type of person to do that, because it only took me 6 hours to get 100% completion on my first playthrough without looking anything up. You could definitely blow though this game blind in 2-3 hours if you wanted to.Getting all steam achievements requires 3 separate playthroughs, but if you look up the any% speedrun record for this game and follow its route (while maybe taking detours to get some convenience items that don't mess up achievements), you can casually finish subsequent playthroughs of the game in a little over an hour each.  That gives you about 9 hours worth of content total.Overall, it's fun and doesn't overstay its welcome. Would definitely recommend giving it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: For as much as I've watched the old Zelda CDI ytp's, the cutscenes have really grown on me and I think some significant portion of the people who made this game feel the exact same way. Arzette's cutscenes are overacted and goofy in the exact right way and there are so many choice screenshots to be had. The levels are simple and I only got stuck a couple of times. The bosses don't offer much difficulty either so this game is really a short breeze and I'm so happy to have played it. 7/10 i kinda wish I could play this game again from a blank slate.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: When I first discovered Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore, I was intrigued, but also incredibly skeptical of its core premise. Obviously, this whole game is a huge love letter to the Zelda CDi games, with the creators even being responsible for the fan-made remasters of said games. As someone who never grew up with a Phillips CDi, nor someone who had any desire to play the Zelda CDi games due to their infamy, a game that takes heavy inspiration from arguably games with some of the worst reputations I know of, sounded like a recipe for disaster.After playing Arzette to completion (i.e., collecting every achievement the game has to offer) I can say with certainty this was one of the most charming games I've got to experience in recent years. While the general gameplay really isn't anything to special, the beautifully crafted environments and the animated cutscenes for almost all character interactions made this a joy to play through. It was surprisingly satisfying completing all the side quests you come across and seeing the overall progression among both the various NPCs as well as Arzette, with her gaining more and more useful tools to her arsenal.One aspect that really caught me off guard was the joy of replaying the game. Arzette is not a very long game to complete, and can be rather easily completed in just a few hours, even on a first playthrough. As I was going for all the achievements, multiple playthroughs were required for certain achievements as you unlock new difficulties for beating the game. Once you've played through the game the first time, you kind of get a sense of some more optimal routing choices you can make and it becomes a very fun game to speedrun, even as someone with little to no previous speedrun experience. For instance, you're able to get the Sword Beam upgrade in the first stage on your first visit once you discover an alternate method of getting into the cave its hiding in. Not only does this help speed take care of early game foes much more easily, but it grants you access to magic much earlier, which in turn, means you can collect even more collectibles/upgrades much earlier as well.TLDR; Don't be put off by the fact that Arzette is inspired by some rather notorious games, if you are even remotely a fan of 2D platformers or Metroidvanias, you will probably adore this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: It works as parody because it clearly very sincerely loves the source material and communicates what was unintentionally funny about it as well as what ideas in it actually worked. Genuinely a fun little side scroller and a delight for anyone who was around for classic YTP and still has an appreciation for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: While the characters aren't quite as iconic as the characters that inspired them, this game exceeds its inspirations in every single way. Somehow, it takes the formula from the Zelda CD-I games and actually makes it fun. It intentionally retains its fair share of clunkiness & cheesiness as a direct reference to its spiritual predecessor, but tightens up the controls and level design almost as comparatively well as Christian Whitehead & Taxman did for Sonic with Sonic Mania. They even pull a similar trick as Sonic Mania did with a Mean Bean Machine inspired boss fight by recycling the style of game play from Hotel Mario for some special stages, which is really freaking neat tbh.This is a indie platforming game I'd say deserves to be in the ranks with some of the greats like Shovel Knight, Shantae & maybe even Hollow Knight. While it isn't as groundbreaking it its genre as Hollow Knight, it still deserves a solid 9.0 both for being one of the most charming indie games of the 2024 and for taking inspiration from a game that sucked and making the formula a lot of fun for what feels like the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Shantae and the Pirate's Curse in the skin of something resembling Hotel Mario. The result is a fast-paced Metroidvania that isn't afraid to let you feel overpowered if you put in the work. It's also both the most loving tribute to a niche fandom possible, while also being one of the most elaborate and expensive $#*t-posts of all time.If your sense of humor was permanently annihilated by Youtube Poops as a child and you have a soft spot in your heart for those goofy, off-brand Zelda characters they often featured, chances are you'll get a kick out of this. If you're purely looking for yet another Metroidvania to tide you over until Silksong, maybe wait for a sale. But definitely buy it. Because when developers actually care about the art they make, you can always tell. These guys cared.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I have no firsthand memory of the Philips CD-i outside of gaming magazines, which referenced its bizarre (yet authorized) Zelda games for an occasional "fun fact" or punchline. As a kid, I found these anecdotes amusing, but also a little disappointing. In 1993, an action-adventure platformer with lush, illustrated backgrounds and animated cut scenes sounded . What a shame they were so terrible!Playing Arzette today, I felt taken by nostalgia. Not nostalgia for anything I've personally experienced, but nostalgia for what  have been. Because Arzette manages to successfully parody  redeem the core concept of its source material.The parody part I expected. I laughed aloud multiple times, especially during cut scenes: The animators clearly had a ball mimicking that distinctive CD-i style. (I later learned that some of the CD-i voice cast reprised their roles, which is incredible.)But I was surprised at how much I enjoyed the game for its own merits. Movement and combat is tight and predictable. Aside from a few faithfully awkward enemy designs, the character sprites and background layers are as lovely as my childhood self would want. The game's music has been stuck in my head all weekend.Some dislike the backtracking, but I enjoyed it: Levels are modest in length and well segmented. Plenty of hidden secrets warrant repeated exploration as you gain new abilities, and it's easy to save your haul and exit midway through a level. I did occasionally wonder what to do next, but revisiting a stage or two always revealed a path forward.The CD-i Zelda games are generally regarded as unmitigated failures. But just as Arzette  triumphs over evil by disregarding the buffoonery of her kingdom's forebears, Arzette  untangles the legacy of its influences by resolving the sins of their poor execution... an important lesson for game developers, and a glimpse into a better timeline for the CD-i.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette is a loving tribute to those Zelda games that were on the CD-I that I so badly wanted to play when I was a kid but then was pretty glad later in life we didn't waste money on that console. The big difference here though is Arzette is a game you want to play. I really like that instead of a big interconnected world there are small stages that you can come back to when you pick up new abilities. The characters and the cutscenes are all great and silly throughout. The game is a little on the short side, I was able to get 100% in just about 3 hours. But what is here is a must if you are a fan of metroidvanias or of the weird lore around the CD-i Zelda games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice send up to the CD-i Zelda games. Lots of lines and sound effects are references to the original, but this plays well and doesn't make your system out of a window.  It's a high 7/10 game if you're into the CD-i throwback, and the soundtrack is real great too. Doesn't overstay its welcome at 5 hrs clocked for a >95% clear. If you wanted you could probably finish it in 3 to 4 hours, it's pretty short but that's fine.I only got a few minor negatives. Gameplay wise, you unlock a lot of stuff/abilities very quick past the 3/4 mark or so. This does make some of the game very easy, but it's satisfying. Some of the abilities like the float jump just make me scratch my head, I never really needed to use it. Same with the backstep, it just didn't need to be in the game. Art-wise it could be a bit more cohesive, but whatever it's fun go check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Of all games to make me go "oh my god. I get it" at metroidvanias I didn't expect the funny cd-i homage game to be the one to do it but here we are. It's pretty fun and kind of short (anywhere between 4 to 6 hours, maybe less if you don't go for all collectibles.) The game absolutely nails the stylistic suck charm vibes that it wants to go for. It's a riot, and the secrets aren't too far fetched, as long as you explore enough you'll instantly be able to tell what item is meant for which NPC for stuff like fetch quests. While you will have to replay levels a lot to see what you miss and what you didn't, the levels themselves are so short, especially once you start getting more and more upgrades, that it really is not a huge deal. So yeah, really charming game. As for the story, it's fairly generic, about what you'd expect, though it is better than what you'd think given the inspiration for the game and what it is a homage to. The art style (outside of cutscenes) actually looks really good??? Like the hand-drawn backgrounds with more traditional sprites look good, you know? Speaking of art, the game's soundtrack is really really good too. I wasn't expecting that it'd be, but it is. Oh, in cutscenes, the game goes all in on stylistic suck, but at the same time it's not as bad as you'd think? Like. It's charming and looks better than you would have expected, yet it also nails what it's going for?? It's very praiseworthy.So yeah, good game. November approved metroidvania. Yippie!!they made count denny hot and i respect them for that
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly a gem.It is a short game & left me wanting more after the initial play-through. It is a fun & at times challenging platformer with a cool but simple story, good art, fun characters & side quests. It is simple & finding collectibles is rewarding. I really liked this game, so much so I 100% it in 2 days lol
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique metroidvania that's a spiritual successor of the old Zelda CD-I games. I never played the original CD-I games myself, but Arzette is a really fun game. Gameplay wise, since i never played a CD-I game myself, I could say it feels like a faster Shantae Risky's Revenge. Cutscenes are chock full of charm and the soundtrack is really well done. Overall, a really fun time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore is indeed a quirky game, but it also shows that good things can come in quirky packaging. Taking, as I like to say, the mold of games that there is almost a unanimous opinion that was not a good game, and then making a good game out of it is a kind of feat that I know I have a hard time putting completely words on. Had Seedy Eyes Software done too much or too little of this to recreate the feel of the Zelda CD-I games, I think the game would have definitely suffered. Here they manage to strike a perfect balance between paying tribute to those games for what they were, while at the same time making a better game than what those games ever were.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: CD-i Zelda modernized. It's doing its own thing, though, and it's great. The game play is pretty simple. It's very straightforward. You're not going to be perfect parrying or just frame dodging anything here, but it's got basic,  solid platforming. The story is whatever, BUT it has memorable characters, and its delivery is great as all the animated cinematics are beautiful. They really are the highlight of the game and everyone who worked to animate them deserves oodles of credit for adding so much to the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A great homage to Zelda CDI games, a love letter to what those games did well, and an improvement on what they did wrong.There is an intrinsic limitation in what type of game can get out from homaging garbage, so if you know the limitations of the games it is homaging, you also know what to expect: very one-dimensional combat and puzzle solving, you buy this game for the homage it is, and not for the gameplay.If you are a completionist, there are some end-game challenges that are very long and boring, like replaying the entire game multiple times, keep that in mind before engaging with this game if that's a problem for you
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I have been growing up with YouTube poop videos so I am very familiar with Zelda, Mario and other marvellous titles from Philips CDI. It is hard to believe that those games could have been good if enough polish would be put into them, as the Arzette game shows that it is possible.I have finished the game on normal mode with 100% completion. It was a fun time.Pros:- Philips CDI games animation style. It is just as wacky as old Mario, Zedla cutscenes. The only minus here I think back then it was not intentional to be funny, but here I think that it was the aim and those animations might never get the same level of fame as the classical ones.- Simple relaxing gameplay. Game never punishes you for your mistakes.- Nice sprites and backgrounds. Game looks very nice, just like good old Zelda CDI games.- Soundtrack is solid. It quite well resembles the soundtrack from Zelda CDI games but I doubt that I will spontaneously go back to listening to this game soundtrack.Cons:- Not all NPC conversations have CDI cutscenes. In late game when you are doing side quests a lot of characters start to have simple dialog boxes with text instead of cut scenes. I would love to see more cut scenes with those characters, wasted potential.In general I can recommend this game to those who also enjoyed youtube poops back in the early youtube era. It seems that there will be a sequel... I hope that this time we will be able to play as Dail. Arzette is fine but I would like to play as a goofball, someone similar to Link. Arzette sometimes is just too serious and uptight and Dale seems to have potential for hilarious cut-scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly solid for what it is.despite being a blatant successor of the CD-i zelda series it also reminds me of some of the off-brand 2D platformers that were everywhere on the GBA. controls are responsive and there's plenty of charm throughout.There isn't to much to say about it as ultimately doing a single run isn't that long, 5 hours was my time but that's playing blind and going out of my way for a number of side objectives.final verdict 8/10TLDR: its amazing for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I have been on the edge with this one before I bought it, but now I am completely sold.The "it is so bad it is good"-theme works quite well in this one. And not to confuse, I have not experienced any technical issues, so the eye-rolling "bad" vibe comes with the artwork, jokes and quest objectives which then again has its own charm if you give it a chance.The gameplay is good and quite non-linear. There are different difficulty modes, which you have to unlock. So unless you manipulate the game files and if you want 100% achievements, you are most likely going for three playthroughs or more.  Depending on the order how you collect things and what the difficulty level applies, the runs feel differently enough to spent another few hours. Can recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I would've loved to have been a voice actor in this game. I'm not a professional VA, but I made this video: ------The game is a great tribute to Zelda CDi overall. The artwork, animation, music, and gameplay are mostly solid.However, I have a complaint about the opening cutscene. The opening basically tells us that this story has already happened once before. I'm sure that these past events are meant to be a reference to the Zelda CDi games, but it's weird because it seems like you're trying to make the CDi games canon to this game while still keeping this game legally distinct. You can't have your cake and eat it too. Hearing about Arzette's first  adventure makes me wonder why you didn't just make this game about that adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Unironically, Arzette is my favorite game released in 2024 so far. I saw the trailer and the basic concept of the game made me instantly buy it. They actually did it, they took the basic framework of the Zelda CD-i games and actually made them really fun and good. The story is really simple but it works for what the game is going for, and has some funny moments. The cutscenes in the style of the CD-i games is really charming. And the gameplay is fun. You start off with just a basic sword attack but as the game goes on you get more and more abilities, from magic attacks that open new areas to sword beams to a double jump. The game is short especially if you don't go for 100%, which some might consider a downside, but I like that it doesn't overstay its welcome. I hope Arzette gets a sequel one day
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: My boy, this peace is what all true warriors strive for!For a game that I beat in 4 1/2 hours on the first playthrough, I would be more than happy to play it again.  So, I'm sure I'm not the only one tired of seeing Link: The Faces of Evil or Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon memes on here, but let me assure you; there is no Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore without either.  Watching through the cutscenes, there are deliberate references to each one.  If you haven't seen the cutscenes of either, I would recommend watching both on YouTube as an accompaniment to this game.  It definitely enhances an already fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Nails the CD-i Zelda vibes, perhaps a bit too much in some cases. There is a lot of back tracking through areas you've been through several times and a lot of guessing about where you're supposed to be going next, but even on normal the game is extremely casual so it doesn't really result in frustration. Some of the voice acting is a bit rough, and sadly the animations aren't quite as wild as their inspiration.Over all though, I found it thoroughly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Here at the CDi Trauma Recovery Institute, we strive to help those who suffered from the trauma of Gamelonitis and Evil Face Syndrome alongside other similar maladies.  That is why we are proud to endorse Arzette.  Purposefully made to resemble those old games, but actually being fun, we are able to prove that there is hope.  There is recovery, and you can actually like video games.  And as an extra bit of spice, Arzette has no qualms about letting you eventually become OP without having to resort to cheat codes or game mods.  Ask your therapist if Arzette is right for you.Side effects include laughing at horses, "Just Five More Minutes" Syndrome, wanting to play more games, becoming a fan of Metroidvanias, and an inexplicable desire to look up "Arachibutyrophobia."
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A wacky platformer based on the infamous Zelda CD-i games. It has all the memeability of those games, but the parts between the cutscenes are actually worth playing. It's even got some built-in shortcuts and sequence breaks for speedrunning shennanagans; I'm not usually one to actively speedrun, but I couldn't help but see how low I could push that clear timer.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and breezy platformer that nails the Zelda CDI aesthetic. If you have any nostalgia for those games, have seen playthroughs, or watched early youtube poop, you'll have a great time with this. The gameplay is light and simple, but the environments are nice and it's mildly fun to build out your kit over the course of the game. You're overpowered from the jump and every boss encounter is easier than the last. That said, I think this game gets away with how little it has going on and how little it asks of you because it doesn't overstay it's welcome and even just as a aesthetic piece it more than succeeds. It's a chill time and the art, voice acting, music, and environments are well worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore is a fun fantasy-action 2D game which contains a lot of references to the iconic CD-I games, which, due to their infamous cutscenes, literally constituted the main content of the early Youtube and beyond.The game system mimics the CD-I game system and therefore it is rather simplistic, at least on keyboard. The basic controls are quite easy to learn, and as the game progresses and new skills unlock, the controls are familiar enough for the player to perform advanced movements in levels.The story of Arzette is basically a generic fantasy story: a dark lord called Daimur, who was once sealed in a magic book, is released by one of his henchmen, and as he and his minions start causing havoc in Faramore, Princess Arzette has to take down Daimur and save the kingdom. Most of the existing characters in the game offer some humor and references to the classic CD-I games, and some of them offer you helpful rewards like tools and skills after completing specific sidequests. Personally, I think Arzette is more like a great tribute to the CD-I games; from the first cutscenes alone the game makes it openly clear where its sources of inspiration come from. Overall, the game is not that amazing or it doesn’t actually try to pretend being like that. It is a fun fantasy game which can be an enjoyable experience for new and older CD-I fans, and it offers decent challenges for regular gamers and 2D speedrunners. I recommend this game for average 2009 enjoyers.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for anyone who's ever wished the Zelda CD-i games were good.  Cutscenes are great with fantastic acting in that classic over-the-top style with the wild "camera angles" to match.  Base game is about 5 hours to 100% so it doesn't overstay its welcome, but multiple harder modes can be unlocked, so the replayability is there for those who want it.It seemed to be a little backtrack heavy, but levels weren't so long that it was tedious (once you get enough upgrades to be able to face-tank/jump over a couple enemies, each level only takes about 2-4 minutes), and it's possible there was a different order I could've unlocked the upgrades in that would've substantially lessened that so your mileage may vary, but if that's a turnoff for you, it's really the only negative I can think of.A game that's clearly had a lot of love poured into it, and a hearty recommend for anyone looking for a nice exploration-focused platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Scarily accurate to the source material that left me genuinely speechless, although the gimmick wore off pretty quickly to me; especially if you're not at least partially familiar to what its parodying. Outside of that, its a solid enough title that doesn't bite off more than it can chew with it's limited scope.+ Small levels and simple controls make for speedy pacing- Fetch-quest heavy progression that feels too meandering at times- Abrupt and wonky enemy behavior
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't here for the nostalgia or the YTP, I always liked those Zelda CD-i games crappy animations. They have these shifting angles, close-ups, grotesque facial expressions, inconsistent details, etc. that gave them a unique flavor that goes beyond "so bad it's good", it becomes a style in itself. And this game succeeds capturing that charm. On the gameplay side, it smartly replicates the flaws of the source material and avoids the frustrating edges by introducing QOL changes. By design it is a pretty light experience that takes a few hours to complete. TLDR, If you're looking a for a "gamer challenge" this is not the game for you. Otherwise, if you want an experience that moves between parody and homage of some very unique bad games, this one is really well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely something to check out if you are fond of the cdi zelda games - this is a delightfully earnest homage, with a fantastic soundtrack, inspired voice acting, and fun animation. the vibes are really perfect! and i love arzette. i appreciate not only how this updates the formula of the cdi games into something fun to play, but also how it's not afraid to be kind of obtuse sometimes (for example, hunting around for items is a bit annoying). for this reason, i'm not sure i'd recommend it to anyone who doesn't already have an interest in the cdi games, but it's also a great example of how sometimes jank in a game is important to the experience, especially if you're playing with friends. (i do hope any hypothetical sequels have more directional attacks, though!)
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with this as a fan of the cd-i Zelda games. I'd definitely recommend if you were into the memes back in the day (or hell, maybe you actually played the games), but otherwise, definitely look elsewhere considering that's the biggest appeal by far. Now while I do think the game is overall very good and fun to play, I also have a bunch of nitpicks that honestly keep this from being above a 7/10 for me.Let's talk about the cutscenes. They're definitely funny and one of the main highlights of the game, but they feel a little too in on the joke. Specifically Arzette - in a lot of cutscenes - reflects more what the viewer is probably feeling or thinking rather than playing along with the weird ♥♥♥♥ that happens like Link or Zelda would in the original CD-i games. Stuff like sarcastically responding to over the top characters, or just in general looking like she's done with people's blabbering is pretty commonplace. It's understandable they didn't want to make every cutscene an incoherent mess, but they undoubtedly have a different feel than the original games (which you may prefer, but still it's worth pointing out).On another a side note regarding the art, I also kind of wish you could unlock an option to digitize the level art similar to how they look in the original CD-i titles. the fact that they're in full resolution but the sprites are in the same style give the game a weirdly inconsistent look in a lot of spots imo.I think my only other main complaint is that they didn't go hard enough on Classic mode being an actually different experience to Hero mode. They're basically the exact same thing except you get three lives just like in CD-i, and you have to crouch to use the menu, but other than that I think it's literally just hero mode (I could have missed something but idk). It really isn't realistic to expect some of the stuff I'm complaining about to be in the game considering it seems like the budget was a little tight (I'm guessing anyways, there's quite a few occasions where it seems there should have been a cutscene and you get hit with a textbox instead), but I still can't help but wish it was better.Though no matter how much I pick apart the little details, I think they still did a fantastic job with this game. Nailed it on the sound design, music, game feel, and balance between CD-i and actually good. Also some secret tricks to master and sequence breaks and the like."Good." - Zelda, 1993
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Memes aside, this is a genuinely fun game that pays tribute to the unfortunate Zelda CDi games by being a spiritual successor that plays like it would if Philips CDi wasn't a terrible system and devs got enough time. _childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This review is spoiler-free.I never found the hardware to authentically play any of the CDi games, but this game makes me wish I put in the effort to. It polishes all of the mechanics of the old Zelda CDi games that I've heard were very clunky and unpleasant before.The combat is actually a lot more fun than I thought a game like this could achieve. Arzette has a sword that can easily cut down every normal enemy in the game, and she can pick up a bunch of items and power-ups that make combat and platforming much easier.The one thing about this game that I dislike is the backtracking. Each level has many secrets, with many of them requiring an item or ability to access, and some of these are put right in your face at the beginning of the game while you have no way to get them. I think it's fine you need to go back into older levels to get secrets that can only be gotten with later-game abilities, but why do I always need to replay the level from the beginning? When I've already gone through the level before and need to go through the whole thing just to get a secret or rare item closer to the end, it feels like a slog. I feel like this one issue could have been remedied by allowing the player to enter the level from any teleportation scroll they used before, but it's a small issue that really isn't that important in the grand scheme of things. Besides, this fix would have made Arzette even shorter while it is already a somewhat short experience.Other than that, I love how faithful this new game is to the old Zelda games. Some of the original staff members even contributed to it, and it shows. I haven't delved into any modes harder than normal after I've beaten it, but I look forward to playing the other modes and seeing the extra challenges that it presents.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette in a nutshell is what if the zelda CDI games were good. If that sounds like something you want, then you should get this game. I can't say as I don't exist in a universe where I never saw the CDI cutscenes and had that connection, but I do really feel that it can also stand on its own. The gameplay is very fun and responsive, albiet a tad simple. It's fun to explore the stages, though you will be backtracking and relooking for new items a lot so you got to be prepared for that. I think this game is good, but a bit flawed in some ways. But I am definitely glad I played (and 100%) it.

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette is basically a zelda CDI game where the gameplay isn't atrocious. The gameplay isn't all that crazy, it's a pretty standard retro action platform game. You basically explore level and collect upgrades. The goal is to defeat 5 bosses (wich are pretty anticlimactic tbh) to get the 5 pieces of the Jewel of Faramore.While the gameplay is pretty average, i absolutely love the Art Direction of the game, especially the cutscenes wich capture that Zelda CDI feeling extremely well. The music is fantastic too, I was excited when i heard Button Masher would do the soundtrack and it is such a banger ost.While the gameplay is pretty average, i still really enjoyed my time with Arzette, and discovering the characters and their cutscenes really kept me going through the game. The game isn't too long (about 3hrs for my 1rst playthrough) so it didn't have time to get boring. If you're looking for a fun little action platformer with crazy aesthetics then this game is a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore is worth your time and money, full price.It captures the charm of CDI games with none of the downsides.First and foremost the movement is solid, no fighting the game to land where you mean to.Explore levels and help NPCs to collect equipment that'll help you on your journey, ranging from upgrades to new abilities for both combat and exploration, everything feels useful.There are two starting difficulties:Dying isn't too punishing, the most you have to do is restart from the last checkpoint in the level.It's hard to overstate how well this game captures the charm of CDI games without anything that made them legitimately bad.Every character is entertaining and the art is fantastic both in and out of cutscenes.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this one! This is a simple platformer with some metroidvania elements thrown in. It plays real well. Soundtrack is really good. Love the artwork. Voice acting is amazing. Humor is spot on. It's a solid fun game all around.It's a standard story of, "Big bad threatens the kingdom again! Go get the stuff to beat the big bad and save the kingdom!" It's a short 3-5 hour game depending on how much time you spend finding everything. For those that are new to platformer games and metroidvanias, this is beginner level for those types of games so everyone should be able to finish it.You'll likely see a lot of comparisons of this game to the old Zelda CDi games and there are a lot of in game references to the old games, but this game stands on its own as a spiritual successor to those games. You'll need to dig up some Youtube videos if you want to know more about the old games and to get all the references here, but it's not needed to enjoy this game. The TL:DR is, the format of this game is similar to those games, but everything has been improved since then.Hoping for a sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a strange one: Designed as a tongue-in-cheek unofficial sequel to “Link: Faces of Evil” and “Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon” on the Phillips CDI system of the early 90s, but without the Nintendo branding anywhere in the game. Oh, and also unlike those other games, it’s *GOOD*.Snappy controls, plenty of secrets, and lots of power-up items make what could be a tedious game into something special. Beautiful painted backgrounds and sprites that aren’t quite modern, but nonetheless get the job done. The animated cutscenes evoke the goofy CDI videos while advancing the story. This accomplishes everything that the CDI games failed at, while creating its own identity.If I had one complaint (and it’s not really a complaint), it’s that the enemy variety is pretty limited. You’ll see the same enemies often and in different stages, but really it’s a minor gripe for what is a spectacular nostalgic experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette is a great love letter to those old CDI Zelda games that we all know and love to hate. Probably made famous by YouTubers like James Rolphe (AVGN) This game basically looks at those old games, and goes "What if this game didn't suck?" and you get this. Has a similar feel and sound to the old CDI games, and that's a GOOD thing. It's nostalgic in weird ways that doesn't make sense. But the gameplay is really fun, and simple to grasp. Character controls feel tight and responsive, levels don't seem too cryptic. There's a lot of Metroidvania aspects to the game, where you're constantly backtracking after getting new spells/abilities/items that unlock whole new areas and new monsters to fight. Highly recommend this game. Easily worth your $20. So much love and care went into this game, and you will NOT regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a spiritual successor to the CDi Zelda games from the 90s, and that's not a bad thing. It's got controls accurate enough for what you need them to do, and there are wonky hit boxes, just like the games its based on. And the cinematics use the same art style that the CDi Zelda games did. The story is goofy, the enemies are off the wall, and the color palette is perfect.But all done with the care of a modern indie developer. Built around a full modern controller instead of the many strange controllers for the CDi (just look up the CDi controllers to see what I'm talking about), it has access to many more buttons than the CDi ever did, and that's what makes the game incredibly playable. And that's the important part; playability.  The game is fun to play, and that's what matters most. With or without the CDi aesthetic, the game plays great, and what makes the difference.

_childDocuments_.review: The game achieves what it sets out to do - that is, being a recreation/reimagining of mid-90s B-grade 2D platformers, CD-I Zelda's most prominently. _childDocuments_.review: If you were to tell me that in 2024, we would be getting a brand new game inspired by the hysterically bad The Legend of Zelda games for the Philips CD-i, mainly Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon and Link: The Faces of Evil, I probably wouldn't have believed you.But, not only did we receive a new original game based off of those aforementioned titles, complete with hand-drawn environments and full-motion video cutscenes that are intentionally cheesy and ripe with potential for future YouTube Poops, but the game itself is actually unironically good. It's also incredibly polished for a game of its kind and the controls for it are excellent with the only real gripe I have is that the final boss is incredibly easy. Other than that, for $20, you're getting a solid Metroidvania that pays homage to a not-so-bright part of video game history that Nintendo would want you to forget, but ultimately had its own legacy carved as iconic sources for YTPs.If there truly is a sequel planned for this game, I'll be looking forward to it. Great work, Seedy Eye Software.Edit: I should also mention that there are a few noteworthy YouTubers that had a part in the making of this game, which I won't spoil as I would want you to experience for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by it's memey inspirations; this is a solid 2D platformer/metroidvania. _childDocuments_.review: It was ok. The Zelda CDI scenes were unsurprisingly the highlight with some being really funny, and the character designs were consistently fun too. The actual gameplay of platforming and fighting was not breaking any new ground but it was serviceably fun. The big problems were that the "Metroidvania" design was not done well at all. In order to 100% you need to tediously re-do each level many times, and the "blocks" that you need new items for are never interesting--like a cracked wall for using bombs is far more interesting than a bunch of white blocks you need to use your power fist move that is otherwise completely worthless to get through. Also for some reason two of the blocks are a very similar color--why not use like Yellow or something that wasn't used?. Many of the upgrades are nearly worthless in combat and just serve to "open" their associated blocks. You start the game with bombs but they're super underutilized as well. Many of the rewards you get are disappointing too like getting more bomb slots despite it being a useless item or more ammo (and eventually infinite ammo) for your gun but by that point your gun is already essentially useless compared to using the charged up sword beam. Even the ultimate weapon upgrade is kind of whatever since it doesn't increase the sword beam damage. The upgraded sword also can't kill enemies with red or blue shields with a normal slash either. The enemies that take more than one hit have really long i-frames so they're very tedious to fight--by the end I was mostly running through enemies and just taking the damage. Sometimes it is really unclear whether or not a hole will kill you or is somewhere you can go (especially in the cave level) but the punishment is pretty minor for dying. There's supposed to be a red "!" for areas where you have a quest turn-in but this often doesn't work, especially late in the "trading quest". The bosses were all really weak, multiple you could just use the spell reflect shield and sit there and the final boss was a joke. Overall, I still recommend in the sense that it is a s hitpost Zelda CDI game that has charm and is funny and is serviceably fun, but I don't recommend at full-price and I wouldn't say you should expect it to be all that much more fun than the Zelda CDI games themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette: The Jewel Of Faramore is an incredibly fun game that was inspired by the cheesy Zelda CDI games on the Philips CDI console that launched back in the early 90s. Those Zelda CDI games were memorable for being so bad that it was good (But that was only for the animated cut-scenes and awful one liners you'd hear in those games). People did not remember the Zelda CDI games for the gameplay. In fact, a lot of people have complained about those games being repetitive and tedious in terms of it's mechanics and flow of the games. So the question is? Why would happened if there was a game that improved  on the gameplay alongside having those cheesy Ms Paint cut-scenes. Well, You'd have Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore. Is this game a parody of the zelda cdi games? Yes. Everything about this game is almost exactly like the Zelda CDI games. The only difference is that the gameplay is actually GOOD.Your character Arzette is really likable and understanding. She is optimistic and hopeful, a bit like Zelda in Wand of Gamelon. Zelda was fierce and relentless towards her foes in that game Just like how Arzette is in this game. Most of the NPC characters are goofy, and my favorite character is Fleetus (A purple crocodile that likes to run really fast).There were some moments in this game that really made me laugh.Here is the thing about Arzette: the Jewel of Faramore. You can beat the game within 1-5 hours on your first play-through. Which is not great if you're someone that just plays a game and is done with it once you've completed. BUT, if you go for the achievements. That time will double or even triple the length of the game. Once you complete the game the first time you have extra difficulty mode. Normal mode, casual mode (so easy, and every dies in one hit). Then you have hero mode with the difficulty being cranked up a bit. Classic Mode was VERY interesting cause that mode is essentially a 1:1 on how to play the game exactly like zelda CDI games did back then. You'd have to crouch down on your knees to be able to open the item menu. I thought that was really cool, but essentially Classic is the HARDEST mode in the game. And lastly, you have Boss rush mode with different challenges. You can tackle boss rush mode with or WITHOUT items (I have perfected without items yet, cause thats crazy hard) Essentially what you're doing in this game for the most part is talking to Characters and noticing that they need something. When you get that particular something for that specific character you get a reward. So yes, this whole game has a lot to do with fetch quests and BACKTRACKING. I am not a fan of backtracking but this game isn't too harsh on it. Theres some level that you cannot do yet so you'd have to skip over it to the next one to get an item that allows you progress in that prior level. Mainly, You sword is powered up by different colored magic. Pink, Blue, and you get an Item that destroys a light green platform barrier. BUT, eventually once you get all the Jewels of Faramore. You go to the blacksmith and he crafts you a sword that can destorys all colored obstacles which makes life for you better in the game. You can now do all the side quests, and get all the items (IF you want to)The main goal of this game is to just the sword of faramore to get powered up to defeat the main antagonist Daimur. And thats why the game is short. When you finally power up your sword, you can go straight to Daimur and destroy him. There's nothing to stand in your way. But if you want to 100% this game. Then is more to do. Which is why My progress ended nearly close to 20 hours. I had to do about 5-6 playthroughs of this game to get all the achievements. So that can give you a better perspective. The items and abilities you get in this game are great, the ability to float across the air for a brief amount of time is awesome. You're gonna have to also visit the shop and buy A LOT of lamp oil. You need it to get through caves and dark places. There are some spots in certain levels that WON'T let you progress unless you bomb it. I've made that mistake about one time. You'll understand what is necessary to do once you dive into this game. I really feel like a lot of people will like this game. You don't even need to have knowledge of the prior Zelda CDI games. It's a fun game that can be beat in one night. Personally i wish this game was maybe like 15 dollars instead. Wait for a sale on it, if you're unsure. I think it gave me a good amount of hours for content. I liked it a lot! One of my favorites in 2024

_childDocuments_.review: EXTREMELY charming with a colorful cast of characters and a solid love letter to the CD-i games, but the main game loop is a bit simplistic, especially for $20. Very small selection of enemy types and little in the way of actual platforming gimmicks, however it moves along quick enough and the narrative is fun enough to not get grating.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This is the definition if a niche game. It is meant to be a tongue-in-cheek homage to the Phillips CD-I Zelda games, and it accomplishes that goal flawlessly! There are intentionally awful cutscenes that look like they were done completely in MS Paint and they are for the most part corny and fun. Gameplay is I believe intentionally clunky but very playable, this is where you need to understand what it is going for in order to be entertained. The CD-I games had weird hitboxes and very unforgiving player tracking when it came to flying objects. This game has the same thing going on but is clearly refined enough so that you get the joke but still have fun. There is a lot of backtracking and Metroidvania style secrets, but thankfully the upgrades you get and the easy on the ears soundtrack make repeated stages pretty painless to get through. You can even find shortcuts with your new tools as you progress. Solid 8/10 for me, and really for the genre and time period they were going for I think this is about the best you can do. Unfortunately the CD-I experience is inherently flawed so I cannot in good conscience give this a higher rating.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a nice homage to the CDI zelda games. Sort of like a "What if those games were actually good and fun to play?"I would say the game's right about the perfect length and I had to stop myself from finishing it on one sitting.Definitely enjoyed thinking about the places where secrets could be and how to get them as fast as possible on a new run. Which comes in handy if you want to try and get the achievements and do the tougher difficulty 'hero mode'. All and all it's not a 'long' game but definitely worth it, I'd say its strength is the sense of exploration, fun and progression you make and being shorter only makes for a better overall experience rather than feeling like a slog to get through.Now, some more personal opinion stuff.I absolutely love the silly humor and animations on the cutscenes, the voice acting and the little animations of the NPCs in the game. This might not be for everybody, but it definitely helped me get way into the world along with the painterly backgrounds. Love 'm or hate them, I think that the secrets are intuitive enough to find, and this might be one of those games that I will try to get 100% achievements on. (As I don't care for looking up how to do it with a guide.)I hope this game will do well and inspire teams to make their own, short, charming games that are a worthwhile experience without having to slaver over making 20+ hour games to be worth people's money.In my personal opinion, this is well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun and a faithful throwback to the infamous CD-i games. However, if you're not familiar with how those games played and their quirks, you might not enjoy the joke. It'll just come off as rough gameplay randomly with lots of strange choices. But if you're familiar with these games, you'll understand why the game plays the way it does. The game is very authentic, warts and all. It's not quite as tedious as real CD-i games, but it stays as true as possible while still trying to be fun. Though I shouldn't need to point out that the real selling point is the authentic CD-i quality cutscenes and absurd story. There's a lot of these and they're all top notch. They're worth the price of admission. But again, you have to be willing to accept the gameplay.I'm certainly enjoying the game so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: As part of this game's very niche demographic, I originally picked up this game out of obligation, having grown up with the CD-i Youtube Poops. I wasn't expecting to enjoy Arzette as much as I did. It's a little short at around 5-7 hours, but it's very charming with satisfying gameplay. The team really understands how to replicate the CD-i cutscenes, although some of them can differ in quality, (there's one scene in particular where you can tell the characters are 3D animated with a pixely filter thrown overtop of them.) Although hilariously, it's almost authentic, because looking back at the old CD-i cutscenes, they would sometimes have different artstyles for one scene as well.The gameplay reminded me a bit of Wario Land 3, in that you entered smaller levels, got an item, and then were able to access new areas in previous levels. There's a lot of trade quests, which is fine because it gives you an excuse to see all these charming cutscenes.The music and backgrounds were also very good. All in all, very very surprised at how solid this game was. At 6 hours, I don't know if it's worth $20, but I would definitely recommend wishlisting it and picking it up on sale. Now enough. My ship sails in the morning. I wonder what's for DINNER.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is alright, it clearly was made with a lot of love and it has a great start. However as the game dragged on, I came to realize a few things:- There were missing animations replaced dialogue boxes that took me right out of the immersion of the cdi-like it is supposed to be emulating. Although I can understand because animation is expensive and hard... though when your spiritual successor animated practically every interaction with major and minor npcs it just feels... unnerving. It gives a rushed and unpolished feature with a lack of closure on some punchlines set up at the start of the game.- The first level looked awful. It was a really bad first impression. The rest of the game is beautiful by comparison, and that is really a shame.- The game's pacing is all over the place. It was really well done for the first ... 4 levels? Then it just hit a wall, and then sprinted to the end.However, despite this the characters were really nice and the ending was expectantly unexpected. I would recommend this game if you are enough of a fan of the CDI games to appreciate all the subtle call backs and references this game is filled with. If not, this might not be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The level design is smart and makes for quick decision making and simple navigation. However, your character moves very quickly and there are no load times between areas, where platforms and enemies are fun to run through. So it's fine.Arzette isn't just a parody or a direct recreation of the CD-I games. _childDocuments_.review: Some folks wonder what's for dinner. I on the other hand wonder how emotionally broken little Zhazi will be upon hearing of Daimur's defeat!Arzette - The Jewel of Faramore is a meme game done right, as in it's a very pleasant, well-designed Metroidvania first and a collection of jokes and references second. Often, it's timeless classics that inspire retro-style games like these. That Seedy Eye Software would look towards the infamous Zelda CD-I games was pretty bold. You'd think this would have to be a bad idea that dooms a game. But it's quite the opposite!What was awful about Faces of Evil / Wand of Gamelon was properly fixed. The little that was decent was significantly improved upon and modernized. Finally, the intrusive cutscenes and odd charm was doubled down on. What amuses me most is how many of the NPCs seem to not just invade the personal space of heroine Arzette, but yours as the player...Really makes it feel like you're the only sane person in a world of cartoony nutcases.Anyway, the result is that Arzette turned out really fresh, recognizable and not more stellar than it was allowed to be. As in, it's quality at its core, but still poopy enough to feel authentic to the CD-I.On anything but the highest difficulty, the game is pretty easy and forgiving. Said difficulty can't be unlocked before beating the game twice, so there's little danger of overestimating yourself. Making you play it multiple times is alright, as it is a very brief playthrough, with potential to play it very efficiently. One of the Steam achievements forces you to sequence break, so you can bet a lot of thought went into the level design.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Faithful homage to the CD-based era of gaming, especially the CD-i which takes heavy inspiration of the two infamous Zelda game alongside the YTP that it brought along. It's structure as a light "metroidvania" game with some cool sequence breaking, has fantastic controls, phenomenal soundtrack by Jake "Button Masher" Silverman, and hilarious cutscenes.I just wish it was a bit more challenging, even with all the difficulty you can unlock. Can't wait to play more of this franchise!

_childDocuments_.review: This game rules. Highlight of my week. The game presents a really fun zelda-style puzzle box of power-ups and trading sequences. I hope that promised sequel is for real!
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not entirely sure why anyone would want to make a tribute to the CD-i Zelda titles (the first two, anyway), considering those games aren't good and the cutscenes are infamous because they also aren't good, but in an intriguing yet also amusing kind of way, but I'm so glad Seedy Eye Software made this game. Not only are the cutscenes as endearingly cheesy and uncanny like the original two games, the gameplay itself zeroes in on what the developers of those to games were going for and improved upon it to the point of actually making it playable. I find this fascinating, since it would have been easy to just completely redo the gameplay and just keep the weird cutscenes, but there's a deep level of understanding what made the CD-i games tick, and that level of knowledge and appreciation shows in every aspect of this game, from the art direction, to the level design, to the music, all of it! There was clearly a lot of love and passion put into this game and it shows. I sincerely hope they make more games of this ilk in the future!
