_childDocuments_.review: I almost never post reviews on Steam games because Uhhh who gives a ♥♥♥♥, but this game is more personally important to the type of human I am, so I figure I'd play it and then give my thoughts. For some background on myself, I know the guy who developed the game from our time in a mutual online community, so I've been aware of his desire/passion project to recreate "good" Zelda CD-i games for years. He was always very enthusiastic about how the games "Could be good" if you just "Fixed" them, and honestly whenever I saw him talking like that I'd always sort of stretch my mouth thin and give a few awkward nods, backing away slowly. This is because the Zelda CD-i games are (big shock): Really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad. Like, really really bad. There's nothing I can say about them that hasn't been said before, but their infamously bad reputation is well earned, so to "Fix" them, I always thought, would really need to involve more or less making them entirely new games (as they'd be almost unrecognizable as "fixed" versions of the old CD-i games by the time you made them actually good games).And, honestly, Arzette doesn't go the distance to remake the CD-i games into genuinely great video games. Arzette is exactly what it was billed as: a "Fixed" version of the old Zelda CD-i games, and as some negative reviews have pointed out, it frankly doesn't do much to really improve the core game play, it just makes it bearable. So does that mean the game is actually bad? No, absolutely not. I do feel there could've been more done to make the combat feel more fun (I have not yet completed the game myself but I have watched playthroughs of it so I'm aware of how even late game gameplay feels), and as a Metroidvania I think it's so-so (take this with a grain of salt, I don't like Metroidvanias in general very much).But as a game itself, Arzette is decent and merits its own existence. If this weren't a remake of a classically despised and mocked Zelda game, I would say it's still an okay game from a first time developer. It has good music, different-but-charming cutscenes and art style and the base game play is definitely "good enough". But because it IS a remake of a classically despised and mocked Zelda game, there's a certain level of meta charm coming from the fact that the game is a soft remake of some of history's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ games, and obviously that plays into Arzette's amusement and novelty factor.As a more specific review, I liked level layout. Like most things, it was standard but good. The hand painted backgrounds are cool, and while I don't think they're as cool looking as the original CD-i games, they're also much better designed and way more readable (in the CD-i games, nothing in the background of stages stood out. A ladder in the background would look like mere scene dressing, yet you could actually climb it, which made navigating the terrible levels all the more painful).If I had to get super critical about something, I think the 1.0 launch lacks technical options. There aren't many settings for screen size, for instance, and I am a BIG MAN who plays with BIG SCREENS and on my larger screens, the pixel art of the cut scenes (as it wasn't made pixel perfect) stretches and skews really badly, making cut scenes look ugly in a way that was unintentional from the artists.I think overall just the fact this game exists is sort of amazing. I followed a couple interviews the developers did prior to release and it's a very interesting and funny story how the game was picked up by Limited Run. It's the end result of a web community that elevated some bad but otherwise mostly unremarkable video games to an enduring piece of internet culture through YouTube Poop, and considering where its roots are it's pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious and awesome that this actually exists. And not as some fan game or random indie project made by one deranged man, but a published game with production value and talent behind it. It's almost surreal.The game is primarily a send up of the CD-i games, but I do appreciate that there's originality in character designs. Though the fat, bomb-selling CD-i shopkeeper Morshu is essentially just reskinned to be a fat elvis-haired man in this game, I think the blatant "rip offing" is fine, as it plays into the familiarity and homage of the games Arzette is based on. I appreciated more the subtle references to poses and expressions, where the king might make the memorable "Hmmm" face, but in a unique context and only as a passing blink-and-you-miss-it nod to the original.I think it's worth owning and playing if only for the novelty of what the game is and where it came from, but it's also a bit more than the sum of its parts, and decent enough to stand on its own, even if it realistically could have done more to make movement and combat more fun/interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played and own all the CDI versions of Zelda, and this is WAY better as far as controls and game play.It has the same fun animations only instead of trying to be "good" they are mimicking the original style and doing it VERY well. The animations are fun, and actually add more to the story than you'd expect.The game has GREAT replayability, and is actually quite addictive.I expected this to be kind of a crappy game, having played the originals.I was wrong. VERY wrong.There are so many side quests, fun and interesting characters, as well as great controls and hidden jokes and humor that spans the old versions as well as other NES games.It's a great hat tip to the originals, and feels very satire to them as well as legit trying to recoup the game's story.The "non copyright infringing" but familiar characters are hilarious, and I love it.I have to go back and get all the side quests because I accidentally finished the game before doing so, but you can just keep playing after you beat it, without starting a new game yet.So you can go back and grind those achievements and side quests.As far as game play, the controls are AWESOME with an xbox controller this game is intuitive to play and feels great, unlike the OGs.The fact that you continue in a decent spot after dying instead of starting everything over is great, you just start at the last entry point to the small areas.It's player friendly, in that you can save and exit to the map whenever you want.So, weather you want to grind the game or just play casually here and there, it remains fun and an easy play.I could go back and play though this a bunch of times without getting bored.The backgrounds being "hand painted" look amazing, and there is great attention to detail, there is one spot where you just go below deck on a random boat, and the attention to detail with objects and background stuff is REALLY good, like, it didn't have to look so good but they put that effort into it.I seriously hope they make more games... Seedy Eye... I like what they did wit the name of their little company, it's great.So, TL;DR:It's a great game, fun to play casually or to grind.Has awesome backgrounds and good music as well as decent voice acting.A good hat tip to the OG versions but with GREAT controlls.Overall, this is a really awesome game, and weather you liked or hated the originals, this makes up for it ten fold, with fun story lines, good humor, and an honestly good redux of the games.VERY good highly recommend this one.It seems to very much under-rate itself, it's just damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game.The memes about it's existence are obvious, but the reason the game exists is sound: its creator felt the old horrendous CDI games we clowned on for decades had real potential under their botched execution.  And they did.  It's here that potential is tapped to a degree that exceeds expectations.    Gameplay wise - it plays like a disjointed OG Castlevania or Mega-Man game.  It presents levels whose completion order is up to you, and most have a hidden item to collect, like Metroid level powerups (i.e. a projectile shield, etc).  There's definitely a recommended path in the levels to do first, but I won't say which order.  I feel that was part of the fun for me.  Within the levels and the town also exist some very basic side quests to do, all of them a fetch quest with something you'll get from someone or somewhere in a different level.  On combat, it's just slashing at bad guys like a Belmont with a boss (which are actually super fun for how simple each fight is) in a few of the levels.  And yes, every NPC you see has a super clunky-looking "cutscene" that perfectly replicates that signature stinky look of those from the Phillips CDI.  They are all hilarious.On negatives, the gameplay itself had nothing major.  Someone may get annoyed that you can't jump down off a platform (as in through it rather than walking off of it), or some of the projectile hurtboxes are a bit fat and deceptive, but that's petty poop.  Just a bit lackluster in the options department for a PC game, though.  I didn't expect to be able to manipulate graphical options, since the game was designed to emulate the crusty early 90s digital look, but I would have at least liked a volume slider.  But if the game's loud af, at least you get to clearly hear the return of the legendary Jeff Rath and Bonnie Wilbur (Link and Zelda's voice actors respectively from the old games.  Their participation and the dev's dedication in offering them the chance to play along was amazing, brief though their parts may be).This is an enjoyable, humorous, palatable experience that I needed to play not only to give praise to another innovative indie "jewel", but also as a respectful throwback to a special era in my life.  Those old YTP videos helped shaped several core pillars of my sense of humor and even my personality (cringe if you want, it's true), so to partake in an homage that plays like the best of something that would have come from the actual console was a worthwhile use of $20. I implore you to give it a try.  I had a giant smile plastered on my face the whole time - not because of the absurdity, but because the game was genuinely that fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: It may seem crude and barebones by today's standards, but this game was made with love. Love for an odd chapter in video game history, a time of ambition shaped by limitation. And the time not long after that, where such oddities took on a new life in internet counterculture.But most importantly, it's fun. The game nails that CD-ROM look and feel with wacky characters and a rockin' soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much more than the YouTube Poop material that a lot of people might think it as going in! The game-play loop is addicting, the controls are fluid and responsive, the levels are cohesive, interesting, and overall beautiful, the characters are wonderful and iconic (Rudy my beloved).Cannot recommend this game enough, 11/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Fortunately not just a meme game with wacky cutscenes.  I have never played Zelda: Wand of Gamelon, but this is totally solid adventure that reminds me of games like Monster World and Shantae.  Worth playing if you're curious at all.  Fairly short if you're just mainlining it, but to me that just means it doesn't overstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect, but I had a great time with it.+ Fantastic presentation, both visually and musically.+ Controls well.+ Fun characters, world, and story.+ Perfect recreation and fine-tuning of the Zelda CD-i style.- Similar to the Zelda CD-i games, the hand-painted backgrounds can make it difficult to distinguish solid platforms from background details.- The scaling in the cutscenes loses some sharpness here and there. Additionally, some character voices were noticeably louder than others in certain cutscenes.- The bosses are disappointingly short and easy.- There's not much variety in enemy behavior.I believe that if the team learns from the flaws of this game and creates a sequel that addresses them, we could have a truly fantastic game. As it stands, Arzette is really good but not outstanding.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: We all know what this game is supposed to be and it surpasses the bar of what it's based off of further than it really should have. controls are tight and responsive, there's plenty of things to do (albeit a little cryptic if you don't have a sharp eye for side quests), and the music and graphics are fantastic.whether it's of genuine interest as a zelda fan and it's muddled history with third party developers or for the lols, i  recommend buying this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Arzette transports you back to the era of vintage animated adventure games, complete with sprite art, hand-painted backdrops, and vocal sequences. For lovers of the genre, it is a lovely journey down memory lane.Arzette provides a fun and varied gaming experience, ranging from defeating enemies to resolving puzzles and assisting oddball characters. The level of difficulty is just right—it's approachable for beginners while providing experienced players with an enjoyable challenge.The game's controls allow you to play with a keyboard, Xbox Controller, or DualShock. I used a DualShock controller and, despite the fact that it recommended using USB, I played without it and connected via Bluetooth because using USB caused the controls to seem rigid.If you appreciate old school vintage style games, I definitely recommend playing Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore; everything is a touch over the top, especially in the cutscenes, but I enjoyed it, and I believe they captured old CDi feel very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very sweet and hilarious loveletter to the CD-i Zelda games.In a way it's funny in that revisiting that old janky game design philosophy in turn makes Arzette feel surprisingly unique and engaging amidst the countless rougelikes, Metroidvanias, and 2D puzzle platformers that dominate the indie scene, giving us something that plays very distinct from all of them.The game is an extended homage and throwback to the Faces of Evil and Wand of Gamelon, with the same kind of deranged animation to boot.  It is incredibly difficult to intentionally replicate the hilarity that the old CD-i Zelda games achieved by accident, but Arzette does a very good job capturing the spirit, just with having our heroine play a still-comical straight woman to the hilarity and bizareness around her.Controls are smooth, and though projectile hitboxes are kinda jank, the game throws you a forcefield you can acquire to deal with that problem.  Dying (at least on the normal difficulty) just spits you back out at the start of the screen you were on too, so you can quickly recover your progress.Speaking of game progression, things are somewhat nonlinear.  Additional areas in the game world are unlocked by finding and activating five magical beacons, and you must also find and defeat the five henchmen of Daimur (aka not-Ganon) in order to fight him and complete the game.  There are additional obstacles as well for you to get through, and the game doesn't actually tell you where to progress other than telling you wehere to go to complete a sidequest once you acquire the corresponding items.  You can also tell that many of the purely optional sidequests were incorporated near the end of development, as they lack the animated sequences that make up most of the game's dialogue.All in all it was a very fun romp for a few hours, and it was endearing to see some bad games with an adoring fandom get a successor title that was made into something as much fun to play as it was to watch.Here's to a decade of Arzette youtube poops!
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way better than initially expected.It has a familiar aesthetic and charm to the zelda cdi games, but with far superior gameplay.The gameplay loop is sorta like "Shantae and the Pirates Curse" with how you have multiple linear stages. You will find roadblocks and collectibles that requires you to revisit past stages to progress. It was surprisingly fun learning to optimize running through the stages and incorporating the new mechanics I found along the way. Oh yea also the soundtrack is soooo good, im definitely picking that up.Id very much recommend the game!!!The only critiques i would mainly say about the game are...1) There is this switch near the end of the game where suddenly the town NPCs stop having short cutscenes tied to their dialogue which ended up being very jarring and feeling very cheap. I get it is expensive and time consuming to create stuff like that, but that's just the impression it left me with.2) A couple of the cutscenes looked way off compared to the others. I only really noticed it in the second cutscene with the king and in the cutscenes where you activate the beacons, but it was like arzette was traced over a 3D model and stylistically changed from how she appeared in the rest of the game so im not sure what was happening there.3) Some of the hidden collectibles were so hidden that a little tiny spec of light was all you got to tell they were there. I dont think i could have found them without a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Idk who would ever think to themselves "What if I made a CD-i style game...but good". And honestly, I'm glad someone did think of it.This $20 dollar game is short, sweet, and full of love for something that has basically only been enjoyed ironically. It is basically a 4th Zelda CD-i game, but with none of the things that make those games terrible. And the one thing that they are most well known for (the cutscenes), this game has those in force, and they are plenty charming.Consider checking this out. Its a sweet little treat that all warriors should strive to play
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun little experience that's very faithful to the charming camp of the Zelda CDI game's animations and voice acting, but with improved gameplay and QOL features that make it infinitely more enjoyable than it's inspiration.Highly recommended to anybody who enjoys 2D platformers, even without a fondness for the meme status of all the zelda CDI cutscenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A super charming, genuine love letter to its inspirations. I feel like there's a number of useful missing options like volume sliders, but hopefully such things can be added in without much difficulty.As far as Metroidvanias go, it's very good at pointing out where you oughta go and what to do! There's definitely some hiccups in the pacing by its nature, but also maybe that's just how approach these types of games sometimes. Oops.The soundtrack is all around fantastic! Hope to pick it up when it's available.The art throughout the game is gorgeous--the cutscenes are very charming too. Lots of fun voicework throughout!Kudos to Seth and all else involved, you've created a genuine delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. The music is great, the art captures what it's trying to emulate very well. There are a few suggestions I have for post launch updates.-The Slide/back dash is kind of lacking. I didn't find myself using it much at all, if it covered more distance then it could be used better to avoid enemy attacks.-It'd be pretty neat to have alternate costumes (like a Gold dress for all coins collected, a blue-ish/purple-ish dress for all candles, etc...), only in gameplay cause I imagine that having to animate all the cutscenes with the alternate colors would be quite time consuming.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A true love letter to those cheesey animation magic Phillips cdi  games ,Hotel Mario, Link the faces of evil, zelda wand of gamelon, and their pc game I.M. Mean. If you were on YouTube in the mid 2000's you know how infamous these games were with there cutscenes being the most notable part being turned into some of the first YouTube poops. So in a world of triple A games  failing to deliver its really refreshing to see a dev so dedicated to making a game in the vein of those infamous zelda cdi games, down to the music , the cutscenes, art style and gameplay , and voice acting, they some how got the original voice of Link and zelda from the cdi games, which is dedication.  The dev even remastered the original cdi zelda games so he knows tons about  how they should look and feel, i think thats  what makes it so authentic.As for gameplay it plays like the zelda cdi games but even better smooth controls and it's actually fun to explore Faramore thanks to the metroidvania esque progression and the bopping tunes. I honestly give this game a 8/10 and it's a must play for anyone who grew up watching  YouTube poops of old. DINNER.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is an homage to the old Zelda CD-I games in the best of ways.  Gonna be a bit thorough here, but tl;dr: if you like retro 2d platformers, enjoy the absurd silliness of the Zelda CD-I cutscenes, or both, play this.  I promise it's worth it.Graphics: The backgrounds are super well done, with very little ambiguity on what is and it not possible to stand on.  As someone with not great eyesight, this was was biggest worry going in, and I was very pleased with how clear things were.  The sprite art is very good, and the gameplay animations are great.  Were it not for the cutscenes, you'd think this was a Shantae homage.Sound: the sound effects are clean, and many are direct tributes to the old CD-I games.  The soundtrack is just wonderful.  Basically every track is both fitting and fun to listen to.Gameplay:  Exploration heavy, with mild puzzles and a lot of 2d action platforming.  You'll revisit areas several times as you gain upgrades to clear obstacles or reach previously unreachable areas.  The combat and platforming work very well.  Jumping takes a little getting used to, but once you get a feel for how Arzette moves in the air, it's generally very good.  The movement related upgrades are a huge help and make the game flow much faster, which makes revisits feel much, much less annoying than they otherwise would have.The inventory management aspect of the game feels a little unnecessary in the overall scheme of the game, and was honestly the thing that felt most like it was just there because of the CD-I games.  I never got close to running out of supplies and didn't farm outside of just the extra kills while searching for hidden goodies at the endgame, where I had 99 of everything except for canteen.  Still, it did make finding rubies feel worthwhile, so there's that.Nearly all of the hidden goodies had hints to help you find them, which was greatly appreciated, though I tended to miss them anyway.  Not all of the candles or coins are required, so don't sweat it if you're not the super observant exploration type.  Story/cutscenes:  Oh boy, I can't wait to watch another cutscene!  Seriously, if you found the humor of the old CD-I cutscenes amusing, you'll likely find these hysterical.  There's a ton of references to those games, with plenty of their own humor too, and they did an amazing job emulating the feel of those old scenes and keeping the same kind of nonsense flowing.  I don't think I've giggled at a game this much in years, and I appreciate it.  Overall, the story is straightforward, does its job, and stays out of the way.  It has some emotional scenes, plenty of humor, and the progression of unlocking new areas feels great.  Sidequests feel in the same vein of nonsense as you'd see in a Shantae game, and the rewards are generally worth it.UI/Options:  The UI isn't too bad.  Very basic, does its job and generally stays out of the way.  The options menu feels like it could use a lot more, particularly sound settings, but a bit of fiddling in the volume mixer was a decent substitute.Overall/Closing Thoughts:  If you're looking at the game and thinking about picking it up, do it.  It's a short game (even with some idle time and exploring extra for 100%, I took about 6 hours) and it's a blast of an experience.  If you, like me, spent a lot of time like 10-15 years ago laughing at the CD-I cutscenes and edits of them, this is 100% worth getting.  This game was a labor of love, and I was shocked to see how many people worked on it, because I'm used to tribute games that are this full of personality being from tiny teams or single developers.  If you're concerned that the game is just a tribute, don't be; it's a solid 2d platformer in its own right.The devs should be proud.  I bought this on a whim, worried that $20 may have been too much for a game like this, and I'm left feeling like I got a wonderful bargain.  I just want more now.  All I can say is thank you, I desperately needed a laugh and this game delivered far more than I ever expected.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried this game might be too stuck on its inspiration's roots.  Fortunately, Arzette kept all the charming stuff about the old CDi games (the painted stages, the infamous animation, etc) and was absolutely willing to rework all the stuff that sucked (controls, stage readability and design).  The result is actually just a very solid, fun little adventure I enjoyed and will be coming back to.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, and quick little 2D experience. It's very silly and fun with some real talent and work behind it. The game nails the YTP type feel while having some good level design, some well placed secrets and some good animations along the way. It overall feels like a mix between the 3 prominent CD-I games (Wand of Gamelon, Faces of Evil and a bit of Hotel Mario in there) as well as some Rayman 1 and Shantae as well. As far as criticisms go, it's got a lot of backtracking, so if that's something you despise, that might hurt the experience for you. But I really think it's the perfect length for a game like this. The only thing that I would personally add would be a song and animation viewer after the game is over. Other than that, this is a really fun game and I highly recommend giving it a play if you enjoy a good, short 2D platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: So I've never played the Zelda CD-I games, but I've watched gameplay videos, am familiar with the memes and the AVGN reviews. I accidentally saw this game in the shop. I didn't knew someone was making such a game, otherwise I would've wishlisted it. I was very surprised that someone made such a game. And of course, at the moment I saw it, I quickly bought it. Turns out these are well spent 20 rupees because this game is fantastic!Now, I know this isn't everyone's cup of tea, but if you like Shantae, this is a lot like it. This game is completely new, but it's also a spiritual successor to the Zelda CD-I games. It's borrowing only the good from them without the flaws. The gameplay is actually good and the game is bigger that I expected. There are plenty of quests and side-quests and you constantly unlock new locations or areas you were not able to access before. The cut scenes and animations are always entertaining and very well done. The environments, world map and backgrounds are very well drawn as well, and somehow managing to capture the spirit of the originals. At first, I wasn't even sure if this is an old game released now or if it's a new game. It's not very often when you can see such thing happen. I can see that a lot of work went into making this.It's like what would Zelda for CD-I would've been, but if it was actually good.
_childDocuments_.name: Arzette: The Jewel of Faramore

_childDocuments_.review: A NEW interactive animated adventure! In this action-adventure game, Arzette must explore the Kingdom of Faramore, slay fearsome foes, acquire powerful items, discover secrets, assist colorful characters, and defeat the evil Daimur!

name: Kamiwaza: Way of the Thief
detailed_description: On the streets of Mikado, only the tough survive. For one man, a heist gone wrong would change his life forever. Set during the Edo period of Japan, Kamiwaza stars amateur thief Ebizo, who aspires to steal from the rich and give to the poor. During his first stint, however, he and his mentor, Ainosuke, witness their own men take the lives of innocent civilians. Disillusioned by the horrific display of violence, Ainosuke advises Ebizo to escape with the only survivor—a lone girl. A decade later, Ebizo has held fast to his morals, living an honest and fulfilling life with Suzuna, the young girl he took in as his own daughter. But the illusion of security is shattered once Suzuna falls ill. In order to buy the medicine she desperately needs, Ebizo is faced with a heavy financial burden. Conflicted, Ebizo is forced to return to the underbelly of Mikado, but vows only to steal for the sake of those less fortunate. Will you walk the path of honor, even as a thief? The choice is yours to make. Family First: What lengths would you go to for those you hold dear? Familial bonds will be put to the test in this uniquely heartwarming tale. History in the Making: Your decisions as a thief will determine your future with multiple branching storylines. Fancy Footwork: Avoid enemy detection with stealthy action gameplay and build your reputation as a thief!

_childDocuments_.review: During my first couple of hours with Kamiwaza, I had a blast. Stealing everything in sight while taking on missions in feudal Japan alongside the game's inventive, addicting stealth combos is insanely enjoyable at first. You have a cartwheel move that allows you to escape from an enemy as long as you use it in the allotted window. Stealing anything immediately after using this cartwheel gives you skill points and lets you chain together acts of theft. It's kind of brilliant. The world is well-designed and fun enough to get around as well. But the maps are also tiny. Within a few hours you'll have been everywhere and done most everything. After that, you'll mostly be going to the same few places and stealing the same few things.Kamiwaza was originally a PS2 game but, in a lot of ways, it looks more like it was a PSP game. Shinobido by the same developer had much better character models and art direction. Still, unlike Shinobido, Kamiwaza controls pretty well. Your steal move functions a lot like an attack, only it doesn't damage anything. Instead, the more you hit it, the closer you get to stealing it, as a bar appears above larger items. You'll level up your stealing ability the more you take too, which is fun. You can also pickpocket enemies. NPCs tend to have money on them and, if you pickpocket all of it, they faint from the shock. It's pretty amusing. Unfortunately, you can only pickpocket them from the front. Why? There's no reason given. It's just to force the player to use the cartwheel or fight off enemies desperately after getting spotted because I guess it'd be too easy if you could knock enemies out just by sneaking up behind them and pressing a button. You know, that thing that almost EVERY STEALTH GAME DOES.The problems don't stop there. There's no lock-on, so the pickpocket combat can be wonky (even though Shinobido had a lock-on.) Granted, the combat in Shinobido was some of the worst in the medium and Kamiwaza handles it much better aside from the lock-on. But the MC here isn't as mobile as in that game on account of not being a ninja. Your wanted level rises as you get spotted, resulting in wanted signs with your face on them going up around town. You can also donate things you steal to the people instead of exchanging for cash, which will result in people being friendly to you, destroying wanted signs to help you, and leaving items for you outside of your door. The main story beat has you buying medicine to give to your daughter and she'll get better the more medicine you give her. The game has multiple endings but I got a bad ending even though I mostly healed the daughter, had maximum affinity with the people, and had my wanted level down to nothing, I got the worst possible ending. When you beat the game, you can do a new game plus, but you lose all of moves you purchased with skill points, which is moronic. You can also buy licenses to unlock passives, but if you remove a license from your inventory, it's gone for good for that playthrough, which is another terrible decision. There just doesn't feel like there's a full game here, nor were a lot of the decisions well thought out. On top of that, it's 16 years old and $40. There is literally no good reason for this game to be more than $20 aside from pure greed. I like things about Kamiwaza and wish I could give a mixed rating, but between the price tag, the design oversights, and all the frustration, I can't recommend it, at least not at a AA price point.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna be real, $40 is definitely an insane asking price for an Unreal port of a PS2 game, (especially one with what seems like a couple graphics issues during extended play sessions like the fog/steam not loading, but that could be a funny linux gaming moment.) But I really don't regret it. I've loved Acquire's catalog since I was in high school with things like Way of The Samurai and Shinobido. This is just another great entry from them in the stealth genre with a wacky action twist. Should it be $20? Yeah, probably. Should you get it if you love old Acquire games? Yeah, probably.
_childDocuments_.name: Kamiwaza: Way of the Thief

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game about a noble thief from feudal Japan (or not so noble). Depending on your actions, your main character Ebizo can become either a petty thief, hero of the poor or just a desperate father who turned into thief to gain money to save his dying daughter. The story is pretty short, which is to be expected from a game made in 2006, but it's replayable to the extent of getting 4 different endings depending on who you side with. The only one ending is true. Kamiwaza is not to be mistaken for a realistic game; there are a lot of shenanigans most Japanese games have; for example, if you level up your skills enough, you can steal women's dresses or start blasting stolen goods on your enemies. It's a shame this game was kept Japan exclusive for so many years, and because of it, it lost its positive reception. It's still a pretty pricey game, but the fun is worth it. Grab it on sale and enjoy this hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Kamiwaza: Way of the Thief

However, the combination of pseudo-combat and katamari-esque item collection is addictive, especially when you get into the groove of chaining style moves.If you're a fan of Way of the Samurai, I couldn't recommend this enough.

name: Gargoyles Remastered
detailed_description: Gargoyles Remastered is an artfully crafted revival of the ‘90s classic 16-bit side-scrolling platform adventure. Relive the epic journey of Goliath and the Gargoyles featuring enhanced visuals, animations, and SFX, all inspired by the acclaimed animated series. The world of Gargoyles comes to life with a level of detail that will thrill fans of the animated series and retro gaming enthusiasts alike. Experience classic gameplay that stays authentic to its predecessor while including new features such as achievements, gameplay rewind, and more! Key Features • Play as Goliath, leader of the Gargoyles: Use stone-crushing strength, scale stone towers and buildings with razor-sharp claws, and glide through the air as you master mid-air attacks and hand-to-hand combat in non-stop action to save the world from destruction. • Immersive Graphics Experience: Seamlessly toggle in real-time between graphics inspired by the animated series and classic 16-bit mode true to the original game. • Authentic Gargoyles Experience: Relive the story of Goliath and the Gargoyles’ battle against the evil Eye of Odin with new animations and sound effects inspired by the Gargoyles animated series. • Customize Your Experience: tailor your gameplay with modern features including instant rewind, wide-screen presentation, and achievements! • Remastered Soundtrack: Experience the original soundtrack, remastered and optimized for a more immersive adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Played and beat Gargoyles Remastered not long after it was released, and I will say I love it with the exception of the load times between screens (but that's due to the speedrunner in me).(Slightly) Longer review:Gargoyles Remastered feels like a love letter to, in my very personal opinion, one of the greatest games on the Sega Genesis in the 90's, where the people behind the remastered said "if isn't broke, why fix it?". With that said the game is exactly the same, even allowing you to play the original version of the game in terms of look. I was initially worried about the look of the game having seen the original trailer and screenshots, but having played through it myself, I think they did a great job with the visuals. There was one section in the Forge level that I think could've used an update, but other than this, yeah, I was very impressed. I think the music has a symphonic aspect to it, where I think in some stages/areas, it really hits. In some areas, I feel like it misses some "oomph". But overall again, I enjoyed the music, which helped bring me back to my childhood and loving Gargoyles.The controls are exactly the same. For some people I've watched play and stream the original, they have a hard time getting over what they deem as "clunkiness". I look at it instead as "letting the animations complete their frames", because even the original had beautiful animations as Goliath ran, jumped, flapped his way through run down castles and soaring skyscrapers. So if you didn't quite enjoy that "clunkiness", it's still here.I have to cut this review short. But if I'm able, I'll edit it later. Again, only real downside for me personally are the load times that occur between sections. Other than this, I will definitely play more of this game. And I hope with the remaster, it will open up the wonderful game that's been with me for about 30+ years now.

_childDocuments_.review: In retrospect -  is not technically a sound game. Having come out at the tail-end of the true magical Disney platformer era, it's animations don't seem as cut-straight-from-the-cartoon (although this remaster does help), and the hitboxes/detection is barely present, at best.But it is one of those 90's-era media tie-ins that is serviceable due to the fact that barely little else for the series exists.There is no tale of kinship here, it's just Goliath going ham. There is no solid platforming here - you are a hulking, chunky gargoyle.What IS here is a solid remaster of a decent title based on a very good series for $15. + Gargoyles 'Nuff said.+One of my major gripes with the TRUE Disney platformers is that they are bundled together. Sure, it's great to get all that, but really, I didn't want  (as good as it is) or  - I just wanted . I like that this product is solely for  - perhaps because there is nothing else that best pairs with it? Not sure, but we're certainly all better off for it.+I sincerely like the graphics. I understand some of the gripes for it, but with the flick of RB, you can go right back to Genesis-goodness. I think it hews much closer to the cartoon without appearing too tacky like SoR4, and I would genuinely like to see the other Disney platformers released with this styling.+Listen - $15 is A STEAL. This was gifted to me  it is $15. So, for that price, if you are or have a Genesis or  fan in your Life, you pretty much can't go wrong.+Yup, 'nuff said.-It was already terrible on the Genesis, but I feel the hitboxes and detection with the lovely new graphics only made a pre-existing condition worse.For one, attacks do not feel weighty. But platforming sure does. I can't tell if my hit is registering, but I am doing the animation. Whilst the animation plays, the enemy is doing their animation, and my health is diminishing. Overtime, you learn it, but it doesn't not make it stop being terrible in foundation.Swapping to older graphics, and you can feel a lil' more whoosh, but not much.-I LOVE platforming! It's a chore and half here. The only time I truly feel like a gargoyle is trying to navigate the jumps, because jumping is slow-paced. Additionally, like the hitboxes on enemies, sometimes Goliath will grab the thing I intend, other times he will start and then stop. Other other times he will climb on top of the ceiling when I was intending to slide him down.Couple this with level-gimmicks that are there to say gimmicks are in place, and you are left with a product that functions, but is not actually very much fun for the majority of your duration with it.The first boss is a marriage of these two "features".With much respect, .-Look, I ain't expecting a mural to screenshot and wallpaper here, but I was quite aghast when the menu screen loaded up. Again, I know this is low-effort asset swap remaster, but even the text looked very "Add you flavor here" put right into the code. Just my opinion.They couldn't even bother to copy/pasta the logo from the title screen into the main menu. Looks like shareware almost.-Odd that the overall tactile charm of the remaster is lost during the level transitions. To me, the cutscenes, as they are, seem very amatuer-ish, as if a fan has released this to the web.While I may seem over down on , I must reiterate that I truly am not, as I love the series, and I think the price-point for what is on offer here is spot-on.I just want to make sure I am honest in my experience and view with this title so that those that may not be sure get a better idea. But, for $15, you can make worse decisions, I suppose!

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Gargoyles fan, I cannot recommend this game. It looks and feels like something that needed more QA passes before it shipped. I say this because:1.) The version number that appears when you pause the game is v0.6.5, not v1.0 or something similar.2.) The remastered assets are a mess. Some character sprites are larger than their original counterparts, obfuscating the sizes of the hit/hurt boxes; some level sprites aren't tiled properly, showing visible seams where there shouldn't be any (most noticeable in the Rookery levels); some background sprites are missing detail compared to their original counterparts (most noticeable in the Forge levels); some sprites do not display properly despite the originals displaying perfectly fine (most noticeable in the Subterranean levels); and in one case the remastered asset is just a blurry, stretched version of its original counterpart (seen in the Subterranean levels). The art itself is fine, and overall more legible than what's in the original given the Sega Genesis's small color palette, but the presentation feels inconsistent and incomplete.3.) While I did not encounter any crashes, I still experienced many strange bugs. One time the game stopped playing background music exclusively when using the remastered assets; sometimes music playing when using the remastered assets would not match what was playing when switching to the original assets; and like several others reported in the Discussions board, I could not get the "Variety Pack" achievement to trigger no matter how many robot enemies I defeated.4.) Gamepad button mapping options are limited to swapping what the Xbox X, A, and B buttons do. I played through this game using Retro-Bit's 2.4 Ghz wireless Sega Saturn Pro Controller, so not being able to remap actions off of Xbox X, A, and B or change the Rewind and Mode Switch buttons made controlling the game more awkward than I would have liked.All this has me wondering if this game should've received a remaster in the first place. What we got clearly needed more time in the oven, and even if it did receive all the time it needed, it would be tethered to the original's iffy collision detection, loose camera, and sluggish, stop-and-start movement. As such, I feel we would've been better off with a full-on remake that addresses those shortcomings. Given how little Disney seems to care for Gargoyles, though, I suppose we should be thankful we even got this.

_childDocuments_.review: >>If you are on the fence about this title Steam allows you to refund a game as long as you have 2 hours or less in it! Grab a copy and give it a go, you're going to make reasonable progress in two hours easily and be able to tell if its your cup of tea or not. It's also on Xbox~PC Game Pass for maybe 12USD a month? Check with Discord friends, they probably have free trials for Game Pass in their gift inventory on Discord.<<Honestly it's a pretty fun and cute little game. You lazy-harvest some resources, you quick spawn some units and buildings, you run around razing a bit of hell here and there. It's just enough action to be fun, just enough base building to be comfy, and just the right dash of Pikmin-like army logic to make you think.It's a Minecraft spinoff, it's aimed at the younger players more than the older players but the older players will have some fun here too I feel, I know I did and I've been happily enjoying Minecraft since 2009!Also Blackbird Interactive is the team behind the most recent Homeworld game (DoK) and the upcoming Homeworld 3, and I have complete faith in their ability to make a comfy child-friendly RTS-like game.Oh and before anyone panics about any concerns of it "being too easy" the game starts your first world off on the easiest difficulty "Fabled," swap to "Mythic" for a more common difficulty curve.I'll be editing as I go:The banter and characters are cute. Despite the bad scenario going down the world you're trying to save is basically Minecraft Peaceful but enemy mobs spawn and just want to exist. All interactions between the non-Piglins is pleasant and fun, lots of laughing and cheer with lots of comfy vibes.The controls are more than simple so I'm not really sure the complaining so far unless maybe someone has a rough time with the keyboard. You have your few keys to hit right next to each other for what building category you want to hit, you have two main buttons to hit to command or call your army to you, and everything else is easily hit even in the middle of a fight. This isn't ARMA levels of needing to know how to keybind in the slightest bit.The world is vast and pretty for campaign though it also supports coop so this would make sense. PVP worlds are quite a bit smaller for obvious reasons but campaign things take time to get between though there is a portal system that just speeds everything up from what I've been told.At this point I am experiencing no bugs to speak of. Sounds work, FPS is great, keys all working, mouse response is fine, everything doing what it visibly should be doing as far as I can tell, no visual glitches, alt-tabbing just fine, no disconnects, no audio popping, literally zero bugs at this time. I've seen some people clamoring "oh it's a half-bake launch, blah blah" but honestly I'm not experiencing a single problem like I've been seeing in reports. Please be sure to mention bugs found in the Steam forums though and I have no doubt that Microsoft will do their best to help out with getting them solved, but good chance they are more clientside than global bugs.Sounds are great, music is cozy, I think forty dollars is honestly a fair price.If anyone has personal questions feel free to put them in the comments and I'll do my best to answer.Possible final edit:Alright so I beat the campaign, took me about 13ish hours. I had a great time, sure it was a bit sloggish after a while as the gameplay is straightforward but I still had a great time all the same. Ending of course left just enough of a "what if" cliffhanger so I'm sure they'll try to do some more story stuff down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Janky, unoptimized, unpolished, and overpriced mess that overshadows the idea of it.Although the core idea of the game is one that I would enjoy, I simply cannot enjoy Minecraft Legends. Almost every part of the game has some amount of jankiness to it. It is an unpolished, unoptimized mess that does not deserve a recommendation, unless you buy it for less than $5. However, it costs a whopping $40, which is becoming quite common for AAA games, but at least most other AAA games are worth it. This, however, is not even worth the aforementioned $5. In addition  to being unpolished, unoptimized, and having a general jankiness to most aspects of this game, the online connection barely works. This is not an issue with my signal, but an issue of Mojang's servers. This becomes a very glaring issue, as the singleplayer campaign will not last the average person playing it over 10 hours (and a boring 10 hours it is), so the main game is basically the multiplayer part of it. Finally, this multiplayer gamemode is unbalanced and lacking many common features that would be quite useful to the players (I'm not listing them all).

So even if you have 3 friends on, and invite them all in, the lobby will configure itself to be 2 of you versus 2 other of you, and when you search, it'll add random players to the other four slots, two per team.No voice chat, no real ping system, YOUR TEAMMATES CAN UNBUILD YOUR UPGRADES.Maybe in a week or two there'll be a great patch to fix some of this stuff, but for now, don't buy if you are here for the PvP.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was abandoned after launch. I thought the game had an odd long tutorial but... Turns out that's just how the whole game is apparently. The game is truly very visually appealing, but there's a lot of issues with the game that do add up to a bad experience:- The game seems to be made to be played with a controller and as such as very odd keyboard and mouse controls that aren't common on a PC game but typical of consoles games.- The game relies a lot on having an army of allies for combat, but their AI is incredibly stupid and doesn't do the most basic thing you could probably even imagine it could do. Many times i had to "capture" them to select and send them again against a certain direction or else they wouldn't attack after going forward.- The game will require you to make bridges and stairs and it fails at that. Most of the times the game won't understand where you want to put your stairs and will simply say you can't build it that big or high, and, if because the game doesn't pause when construction, you might face quite some damage while trying to make your stairs happen. If this wasn't enough, enemies can pull you out of position, ruining entirely the very precise and careful attempt at placing stairs. Awful.- The main character is mostly useless. The game seems to be strategy oriented, so why the controls for the main character seem to divert from that? If damage needs to be done by the main character it's necessary to spam buttons, and i assure you there's not a single indicator of damage or HP on enemy structures. The main character is also very fragile and consequences are severe if you die in battle, unlike the allies that are expendable and renewable.I bought this on launch because i thought this would be incredible with all those trailers and announcements made at big events and conferences but it ended up being a big disappointment. Unfortunately, I had played this game for over 2 hours when i decided it was not good enough. This game is one of the worst i've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: As a guy who grew up playing Starcraft 1 & 2, this isn't the best RTS out there but it's trying... sortaThis game has its issues, like I feel like the campaign could use a little more variety in some things like random events of some sort to spice it up other then, Siege a base and Defend a village.The unit variety is fine but could use some more stuff like maybe they could bring in the Iron Golem for some sort of Heavy Infantry like unit or add the spiders. Small thing but it can be better.I wish the player character had more upgrades for them specifically, like your gonna be in the heat of battle most of the time so why not add an unlock-able ranged attack option or the ability to repair buildings with an upgrade. small things to let the player interact with their base and world more ya know? of course I understand that some of those mechanics might get delegated to campaign only but hey, can make campaign more interesting atleast.Multiplayer has some Desync issues here and there but its not the worst and happens rarely for me.I do see the problem and dislike for the Cosmetic store and I do agree its not a great thing but in the long term its not the worst thing here, its all optional cosmetics and can be ignored if you wish.The worse thing with the game imo is the fact the game has too little content for it to be worth 40$. The campaign is not super long and pretty repetitive. I feel like they ride on the fact its a randomly generated world on each new save a bit much, while that adds some replayability, its not a great value with the campaign in its current state.As for the PvP, I haven't done that yet so I wont leave an opinion here as it wouldn't be right.But despite its problems, its still pretty damn fun for me as a casual. Its far from perfect but the Campaign being co-op is really fun and I enjoy coordinating sieges with my friends.Though are if you want to buy it, wait until its on sale imo. 15-20$ I feel is what its proper price should be with its current content. Overtime I'm sure they will add more things but if those are required to make the game feel worth the 40$, the game shoulda been delayed a bit.Overall not the worst RTS game but not the best either, kinda middle of the road and I feel the current Mixed Ratings is correct.Oh and the game is cross platform so there is that, def was a selling point for me since I have some friends who only have PC and others that only of an Xbox, PS, or a Switch. So this was added to the small pile of games where my friend group can all hang out together.P.S. I do recommend reading other reviews, you were probably already gonna do that but I just want to ensure you get informed of any other pros and cons the game has.

_childDocuments_.review: It's graphically charming the game functions for the most part, but it feels very hollow. It feels like an RTS in name only. The outposts you build are usually just going to be for fast travel purposes. The villages already make resources for you. Due to how enemy mobilizes (or rather, how they don't mobilize) their armies in this game, you don't have to really think about building outposts to hold off the enemy from occupying a space or to cut them off from resources. Besides the attack and occasional new base every night, the piglin army are just sitting there waiting for you.In terms of action and combat tactics the game also feels very limited. Defensively, the upgrades you can get to your building feel like they're just an afterthought when just spamming walls and arrow towers already suffices. Offensively, it's just a cycle of leading a bunch of stone golems to rush a few buildings in the enemy base, retreating to make more, and then bringing out your creepers to nuke the nether portal when the enemy's defenses are down. Where I think the game could've salvaged itself was to have a lot of interesting side content in the world and a good campaign. Sadly, I found that the game failed on both these fronts too. Besides some admittedly helpful mounts, you just find some resources laying around + some golems and towers that I really never got much use out of. The story feels like it's aimed strictly at an extremely young audience. Nearly all the cutscenes featuring the horde being the exact same joke of a commander Piglin bullying the smaller ones. Your allies has scripts written on wooden that hasn't been turned to paper yet, with only one of them even attempting to say even slightly amusing things and still fumbling at that.

_childDocuments_.review: My biggest problem right now is the structure limit. I know I'm not the only one. I don't think the game told me about it until I ran into the "Too many structures" error. The thing is, like some others, I made triple layers walls so that the enemies have a hard time getting through. Apparently each individual wall counts as a structure. So, if you triple layers walls, you'll only be able to do that for a smaller area because you'll eventually run into the "structure limit" and you won't be able to place any towers or other defenses. I found this out 10 hours into the game and now I can't get a refund because I've played for more than 2 hours. Also, this is just one out of multiple other problems I've had with this game but this "Too many structures" error just did it for me. Hopefully, this one little review out of thousands of others will contribute to the devs fixing the problems so many people are running into.

_childDocuments_.review: Some good ideas surrounded by a lot of badly done ones. Having to balance resources between defenses and troops is a great little thing. But then the finer details of trying to build an efficient defense is undermined by janky placement controls, and having camera locked to where your mouse cursor is at during build mode. You can't delete multiple buildings at the same time, there isnt a way to select multiple structures to delete them. You must individually delete structures that you built. This includes walls.What makes this worse is that walls are easily built. But then, each plank of the wall must be deleted individually. Not only that, you must approach the particular offending plank, and press and hold a delete button to remove the singular structure you want to remove. If you had to build some hastily made defense, fixing it up for the next potential attack is going to be a real pain. The game wants you to be efficient, but then lacks the finer controls to help you along in being more efficient. Its a real shame, because it can be really fun at times.For 40 dollars? Nope. Come back when its cheaper. Or even better, find a better game.For everyone else still playing, its a frustrating experience of always wishing it was better.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest review.Cons:The campaign on the recommended difficulty (2nd lowest) takes around 8-12 hours to complete. Higher difficulties just have more starting piglin bases and they only do slightly more damage. After you finish the campaign there is no reason to play your world anymore. You cannot build for style (only like 12 buildings for defensive and the rest are for upgrades). While there's plenty of units you can control most of them are passive mobs (wolves etc.) that cannot attack buildings. The 8 spawnable mobs and 4 legendary ones don't offer alot in the way of customizable armies. I found I was constantly just making armies of one or two units depending on what I was fighting. Every base you destroy feels super repetitive. PvP is more about making a base near you enemies right off the bat and then attacking as soon as your able. Massive lack of strategy in its current state.Pros: Game is light hearted and the graphics are beautiful and computer friendly. There are many pieces of minecraft lore spread around that gives depth to the minecraft timeline. The controls takes a while to get used to but once you learn them it becomes second nature. Super good filler game (for those times where you can't get a full online game in, except  PVP can last awhile depending on the teams understanding of the game). Cross platform play suggests that the companies are going to expand the pvp. So far its not pay to win. There are micro transactions for cosmetics for your character and mounts, but it would be nice if there were skins for buildings too. Overall I wouldn't say its isn't worth the $50 especially if you aren't interested in co-op or pvp. The single player aspect is lackluster  to say the least. While I enjoyed the experience, I can't help feeling disappointed in the game. I've sat in the menu and thought "what is there to do thats fun" and then closed the game multiple times. I would suggest waiting for more content for both single player and PVP.

_childDocuments_.review: It appears as if reviews for this game are mixed... Mixed as in split between people who came to it for the RTS side, and people who only came for the Minecraft side.This game is very much, an RTS game. it's convoluted nature is commonplace with alot of RTS out there, and due to the attempt at being toned down, It most likely won't be as bad as other RTS games. I'd say the co-developer 'Blackbird Interactive' are trustworthy, as they seem to have developed games such as Homeworld 3 and Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak.The main complaint is the lack of content, I saw someone saying that the campaign lasted for 2 hours, which is abnormal since it took me an hour and a half to even complete the tutorial? but the game does change from a storied linear pattern to a open world RTS where you defend against a 'Dynamic' enemy. so they might of thought that the game ended once the tutorial finished.In terms of outside the length of the campaign, it's a live service game. I'm gonna expect more stuff to come in the future. hopefully in the form of free updates, with income generated from the marketplace instead of DLC. but for now, it is slightly limiting on unit choices, with only 8 standard units, excluding 'Super' units. but as with all RTS games. units are for purpose, rather than just to exist. so there might be no need for other units, as most RTS game's basic spam units are basically the same amount, going for upgrades or stronger units later to add diversity. It's not something you should care about if you're going into this for an RTS game.I however have one issue with the game, that has the possibility of not being fixed, and that's the AI in this game. the AI is workable. but 'Stupid' you tell them to go attack a base across lava with a bridge beside you, they'll go into the lava unless the bridge is directly in front.There's no 'Call all troops to follow you' button though. which, I can't decide whether it's a positive or a negative. Singleplayer, it's tedious and annoying. Multiplayer however, it allows for both players to micromanage an army as the other player can control the army that's not following you. the recall button on a spawner seems to only recall those not following others though. so in the middle of an attack move, your guys may vanish.In summery, the game has a few faults. which are commonplace for RTS games, and will be manageable for those who actually play RTS games. So I'd totally recommend this game to those who do play RTS games.

name: Spirittea
detailed_description: Wait! Who the heck are you?! Can you see me? You CAN, can't you? You've drunk the Spirittea and now you can see me!! Look, we've got problems! This town is crawling with troublemaking spirits . They've become lost because humans have stopped worshipping, leaving offerings or even thinking about them anymore. This is- well... used to be a nice town, but there have been some strange goings-on lately! You're going to find the spirits causing mayhem and fix their problems so they can become paying customers , and get to know the townspeople and explore the mountain to its fullest! Here's the stuff you'll want to get involved in: Solving the spirit's problems - To remember themselves, they'll need anything from some spicy noodles to finding and digging up their lost treasures, so get your problem-solving hat on! Making friends with the locals - The townspeople all have their own schedules, likes, dislikes and hobbies to take part in - from bug catching to karaoke, there's something for everyone! Managing the bathhouse - You'll need to clean towels, chop wood to heat the baths and seat the spirits with their friends for the ultimate bathing experience. Upgrading and decorating - The local shops can make a whole lot of cool furniture and help you fix up your house. Make your new house your home! THE BATHHOUSE The bathhouse is an ancient spirit building hidden up in the mountain, and it's up to you to clean it up and fill it full of customers! Once the spirits are in the bathhouse, you'll need to clean towels, chop wood to heat the baths and seat the spirits with their friends for the ultimate bathing experience. Each spirit has their own preferences so you'll need to get to know them all and upgrade the bathhouse to become the best bathhouse keeper around. To keep your bathhouse running, you'll need to: Keep the bathhouse and towels clean - Grab your trusty broom to sweep away the cobwebs and collect up all your towels, you'll need to keep everything clean, dry and organised. Deliver a five-star service with food and scrubbing - Get ready to pamper your spirits with food straight from your kitchen and a give them a good scrub while they're relaxing! Make the water perfect for each spirit - Chop wood for the boilers to heat up the water to the perfect temperature and mix up various elixirs to make the water perfect for each spirit - they'll all have their preferences and favourite recipes! Sit friends together and enemies apart - Every spirit has others they like best, as well as some they don't enjoy spending time with at all! You'll have to plan carefully when you lead spirits to their baths - don't seat just anyone together! Unless, of course, you don't care about making money. Which I do. Very much so in-fact.

short_description: Hey human, we've got problems! This town is crawling with troublesome spirits, and you're the only one who can see them. You'd better get that old bathhouse up and running, maybe that'll help them chill out!

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly enchanting. One of the few games that I've reviewed before 100%'ing just because I'm enjoying it so much. It's charming and beautifully designed, from the character sprites down to audio. The story is captivating and intriguing, with a hint of craziness that I didn't expect and am thrilled to see. It's more Dave the Diver than Stardew valley, but the characters are already so vivid and unique to me, and the environments are nostalgic-feeling and incredibly detailed. Mechanically, the gameplay has a good dopamine loop without being tedious or too difficult, and you feel like you're making real progress as you play. Also appreciated the exhaustion system and the customisable sleep times - it's unique and I haven't seen it before, especially in a way that doesn't absolutely throttle your stamina bar. It's a minor complaint, but I wish the controls were better optimised with the keyboard; catching the spirits and using the inventory system are much easier on a controller and it felt a bit clunky with keyboard and mouse, which is a shame.Regardless, thoroughly enjoying myself. The comparison is beaten to death, but this might be the most impressed I've been with a casual life-sim since Stardew - truly. It feels like Roots of Pacha but more alive, with clearer goals and progress, and I'm a sucker for the setting. An author in a quiet japanese village tending a bathhouse for spirits? Sign me up. Told myself I'd only play 20 minutes and hours have somehow passed by.Edit for 11 additional hours: There's quite a few bugs, the spirit puzzles can be confusing and difficult and the mini-games including fishing are nightmarishly hard for no reason - and also add to frustration playing with keyboard. I've had to go to the official discord for the answers to some of the more frustrating spirits. Still enjoying it - but it's not perfect and a bumpy launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, but I just don't.It's not the visuals or the audio. They're nice. It's not the characters or the plot/premise - they're all serviceable for the genre (with the premise being a really nice hook).My issue is with the gameplay. It's rough and much of it is just not fun. The core gameplay loop of running the bathhouse and interacting with the townsfolk is straightforward enough. There is a good cadence. Unfortunately, the bathhouse is very shallow and feels more like a time-sink than an engaging mechanic.Likewise, increasing your relationships with the townsfolk is both shallow and outright frustrating . The minigames are simple, repetitive and in some cases (digging, bug catching, karaoke) poorly designed. The controls are clumsy and it doesn't feel like the developers put enough time into exploring how the game  to play.Then there's also the mechanics. So many aspects are either poorly explained a single time (no ability to revisit tutorial messages or a reference section) or just straight up not explained (tomes, seeds, treasure maps, stamina mechanics). Too much of the community discourse is being spent on answering simple questions that the game itself should be answering.If you're looking for a village/life sim and no other titles are catching your eye, then it's okay. There is definitely a charm to it that I've enjoyed - I just wish that I wasn't fighting the game itself to experience the charm and narrative. Hopefully with patches it will become a better experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played 30 minutes, but the impression this game has caused on me has made me say "I must leave a review"This is my second review on Steam. I hardly ever review games, so this is proof of how amazing this game is.First of all, I was so impressed by the pixelart. It looks beautiful, there's lots of diversity and it is all done in a very respectful way. The game has very heartwarming vibes.But what impressed me the most was how autism-friendly it is. I am autistic and I struggle with maps and knowing where to go. This is the first game that has somebody that guides you to meet the townfolk. You can select who you want to meet and that character guides you there.This game has everything I ever wanted: customisable character and house, cooking, cool minigames, diverse characters, good vibes, beautiful artwork... It reminds me so much of one of my favourite movies, Spirited Away. I bet there are many cool things for me to discover, but I was too excited and had to review it straight away.My boyfriend gifted me this game today, one of the best gifts ever. Can't wait to play more. Thanks for creating games that autistic people enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game works perfectly on steamdeck. I thought I had a bug because large gifts from villagers disappeared when they'd hand it over, but it wasn't a bug. The gifts were in the decor editor at my house.This game is really original. There's no debt to pay off, no deadline, no quotas to meet and no passing out at night. The focus is running the bathhouse and it's the main source of money, leveling up, and unlocking progress. There's a variety of activities and minigames to do in your off time, but there's no need to grind. It's a hobby, not a side hustle. You gain friendship with people by investing your time, not buying them off with gifts. That's kind of refreshing.I love the sleep/save in this game. You can sleep whenever you want for as long as you want. You can nap for an hour to save progress instead of having to end your day to save. You can sleep during the day and stay up all night without passing out. The game makes you get tired and lose stamina based on how long you've been awake after a long sleep, not what time of day it is. Finally my character can have as chaotic a sleep schedule as I do!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw this game pop up under Studio Ghibli recommendations in a blog I follow, I was ecstatic. I immediately went to steam for the demo. The demo is quick, and really does not dive into the depths of the game, well you think. I feel this game after playing it falls short. After buying and playing for hours I find myself wanting more than what the game gives, and not wanting to further it because it is lacking overall on things to do. - Friendships never lock in after being maxed out. You consistently have to talk, play mini games with them to maintain them. You cannot gift them anything, however every level you make with them, they do give you gifts. - This is very hard to control on a keyboard, and I feel it should of been adjusted more to fit a computer player versus a console player, why make a game for PC and console if you will not accommodate it to the people you are selling it too. - The mini games, especially the karaoke is hard, trying to manage hitting the keys, at the right moment, plus multiple ones coming in at the same time on a keyboard, and the choices of songs is slim. - No romance in this game, no upgrading your house, no changing your spa not really many choices to creativity or making the space/game your own which is what I was hoping was to design my spa different, to my own likes and desires. Sure you can move furniture. You do not even get the chance to upgrade the town, grow with the town, any town events. JUST NEEDS SOMETHING. - This game is very repetitive. Grinding in a way. I feel like it lacks in the story, you are trying to help the spirits in the town regain themselves, and have a safe space. Okay, awesome. But that is pretty much it, then you run the spa. - Cannot Farm, Garden any of the ingredients for the spirits that they need, basically buy it all then cook it for them to give it to them.  *However you can pet the dogs, and cats, build a friendship with them. The bantering between Wonyan and the spirits is adorable. * This game to me I thought was going to be my game of the year, I was like YES Spirited Away, mixed with Stardew. SOLD. But it is lacking. I even went on vacation for 10 days, and came back bought it to be played immediately. I think as it stands right now, it is a cute game, unique in what they want to achieve, the environment in it is nice, cozy, relaxing, has the vibes of a studio ghibli meets stardew with potential but for me as it is, I cannot recommend it, or continue playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: First all I want to preface this by saying that overall, I do enjoy this game quite a bit!But I feel I have to comment on some of the misgivings of this game:1. The lack of visual indicators is quite simply appalling!I've pumped say about 24 hrs into this game, and only now have I realised there are brooms in your towel room that are there to clean the place up. There are no object/item highlights, nothing to tell one whatsoever that something might be interactable and therefore used. (I bet there are already a number of items in the game that I could be using that I've simply missed out purely because of this)2. The way the game explains it's mechanics, ie fishing, stamina and overall tutorials is just not good enough. There is also no menu in the UI to go back to in case one needs a refresher of how something works... To me, this is something that really should be there at release...and is inexcusable.3. Interacting with townsfolk and the activities to increase friendship. Walk up to say Clarence,  select prompt that asks him to go for a drink with you... Go to Leigh's drink stand (with Leigh behind the bar), only for the minigame not to initiate. Whether this is a bug or deliberate, I'm not sure. But it sure is frustrating4. Being on your way trying to solve a quest only for the spirit cat to then constantly bombard you with a spicy noodles quest...It's just really really poor.5. The mechanics of your backpack and notebook system is just really average. Having to flip between the 2 is plainly annoying.6. It is so easy to accidentally drop an item out of your hand without realising it. I've done it a number of times with my shovel. No prompt nor visual indicator that you're removing an item. These might seem like really small nitpick things but they all add up.Overall+++++++++++The game has a solid foundation and the Devs clearly made this game with love. I am not doubting this at all!It's cute, it's fun when your not experiencing the frustrations listed above.Right now, this game shouldn't be listed as a full release. It's clearly lacking months and months of much needed polish. For me, it really should have been listed as an early access title and I feel a little cheated that it's not. I won't be refunding this game nor am I recommending not to buy the game either.There is a great game in here when it actually allows you to play it. I am merely writing this review because many of these mechanics have not been thought through enough and cause more frustrations than not...
