_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard review to do, because while I DO highly recommend this game to others for what it does right, I also recognize it could use some improvement.. or it just may not be suitable for those with certain limitations. Let me explain.What this game does right is.. well, mostly everything you see within the game. When you first boot it up, you'll be swept up quickly by the comforting soundtrack, daily task routine and rotation (want to focus on the bathhouse? Devote a day or two to it. Want to socialize? Devote days to that too!) and the charming graphics/color scheme. The game never makes you feel rushed.. there doesn't seem to be any timed goals or pressure on you, and you can go at your own pace. There's also at the same time an abundance of things to do, so if you suffer burnout from something in particular, you can take a break and enjoy everything else the game has to offer. There is however something glaring at me now that I've been playing for a decent span of time.This game doesn't play well with people who have limitations or physical disabilities. There is no toggle for the run.. so you have to keep your finger pressed down on the key/button the whole time. Maybe not that big an issue for controller players. but with a keyboard and mobility issues.. it's not pleasant. There's also the mini games.. on the surface, they're fun, but if you can't move your hands quickly or very precisely for whatever reason.. they become something you start to dread. They aren't really optional either, as there doesn't appear to be any other way to get things such as fish without them.So yes, I do recommend this game. For what it does right, but I hope that with time the devs are willing to maybe make it a bit more accessible to those of us lacking in reflexes or mobility. Until then, yes play this game, but go in knowing it may provide some struggles.Edit: I'd just like to say that the latest update seems to have fixed the fishing issues.. caught my first fish, a flounder! It's still a bit frustrating but totally doable now. The other mini games I still feel are a bit too complicated for what they are, but it's REALLY encouraging that the dev is listening to concerns about the fishing/mini games! So hands down, definitely recommending this game for sure!Edit AGAIN: So now the karaoke difficulty seems to be fixed! I really have high hopes for this game and each new update continues to impress and amaze me. :) I can honestly say I feel heard, and I feel like a lot of the concerns I had with the difficulty of the games were seen as valid.. and that in itself means a lot!! Thank you dev, for listening to the fans!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who watched 'Spirited Away' a lot, this game seemed to check out the box for theme, and it does. I love the story of a writer who gets mixed in with being a manager for a spirit spa who can recruit the help of the villagers to manage said spa, while also helping the lost spirits regain their memories and return as patreons.The quests that will trigger through the notice board or with you speaking to quest-related NPCs are pretty standard but fit well into the game, seeing as you have to investigate a lot of them by speaking with different people at times and some have puzzle elements to them, some harder than others.For all the things I love about the game, I really dislike a lot of the game mechanics.Worst is the crafting system! Crafting would be cooking or creating elixirs and in order to craft, you need to manually add each of the three ingredients, choose what method to use, and then start cooking which is a times event. BUT this is only if you cook from home, where the screen lets out choose your recipe cook, storage, inventory fridge and the cooking screen.If you want to cook from the spa you need to:This in itself is not fun, it's a hassle and it's really destroying the enjoyment of crafting, so much that I don't craft anything unless I know a Spirit Lord is gonna demand food (late game room). But getting ingredients is even worse since most of what you need is bought from the shop, where they rotate items, so there is no guarantee you can get your ingredients. This might be realistic, but it's a game about a spirit spa, realisme is already out the window. Just make it fun.The management of the spa is also something that has started to bother me after playing over 20 hours. It's nice that you can "hire" your friends in the two (I recommend doing the easy Karaoke option, it's boring but effective compared to many of the other options) but I do not understand why I can only have ONCE person washing the spirits!?!There are 27 NPCs but you can only have 4 of them hired at one time? Sure they also give you some collectables when you raise your relationship with them, but not being able to have more of the being active in the spa at one time seems like an oversight for me. One person cutting wood, one person picking up and one person delivering towels makes sense, but not serving the clients in the spa, which was a huge let down for me, and it gives the spa an empty feeling.Speaking of the spa, late game it feels like you are mostly just waiting to become exhausted and either pass out with a money penalty or close early and maybe get a money penalty? The reason I'm not sure if the spirits pay in full when you close early comes from the lack of information, there is no information about how the business is going, other than you get paid more if you have seated more spirits.A low-stakes game, where you can more or less shut off your brain and just enjoy it for what it is, and you have to love the theme if you're getting any enjoyment out of the game.Personally, I've gotten a bit bored with the repetitiveness after unlocking every room in the spa, and I feel like it's lacking in the business management department now. I would love to order produce and hire a cook to serve the client's food, but right now the crafting is so bad I more or less ignore it completely. And I shamely rely a lot on Reddit and wikis to get information about characters and creatures where the UI and UX are just a drag to mess around with.That's why it's a maybe.I don't regret paying for it or playing it, but I just wished it was a bit more fun to manage the spa.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good life sim but riddled with couple annoying bugs and some jankyness.The premise is pretty original and fun. It's not just running a bathhouse for spirits but also first finding the spirits and resolving the whatever trouble they are causing around town which is probably the most entertaining part. The bathhouse running itself is pretty deep and does not become annoying or boring quickly, the reward money you get for it is usually big enough to be able to afford an upgrade or an useful tool for your character that helps you do other activities around town which in turn makes pretty balanced experience that does not force you to just do one activity over and over again, you can just choose whatever you want so, it's pretty relaxing.The other activities are pretty standard, you have your bug catching, your fishing, your digging for treasure and they are all solid but require some online help as game provides little information about what kind of fish or bugs you can catch each season. Minigames you can do with NPCs for friendship points are alright but get rather bothersome when you try to max friendships with all characters.The town NPCs are pretty bland to be honest, there is a lot of them but each has like one or two personality traits and the friendships don't ever develop into anything meaningful so it's pretty meh. Also I gotta mention - for a small rural Asian (Japanese? Korean?) town there is some extreme racial and cultural diversity here which is pretty silly.The spirits itself are the main reason you play the game to just see what kind of shenanigans they will cause and how they look like, unfortunately there is almost no interaction with them after you discover them which is pretty sad. Game should have really dump most of the human NPCs and concentrate on fleshing out the youkai more.There are tons of weird design decisions that hamper the experience however. When you obtain an object (eg. a gift from an NPC) while holding another object you will drop the currently holding object so you can hold the new one, instead of stashing one or the other into a backpack. You think it's not a common occurrence but will actually happen constantly while doing activities with NPCs, and you'll realize 2 minutes after the fact that your shovel is no longer with you and have to go back look for it.Lack of object stacking especially in fridge or house chest is just bizarre, good luck scrolling though all your junk or ingredients. No way to sort them either so you'll eventually be stuck with huge gaps of nothing in your containers. Tracking of your collectables etc. is done through 2 different menus - one from pause and one from ingame object - and each provides different information. This all feels very archaic or and/or patched separately later instead of fixing original system. Also cooking is just the very definition of not worth the effort, aside from couple of things that are required for quests it's too slow and annoying and useless to be done regularly.I have to mention couple irritating bugs. Items will sometimes just disappear from your hands (eg. when NPC digs up a treasure your shovel will become invisible), 2 music tracks will sometimes play at top of each other, textboxes can layer at top of each other or at the top of other menus etc. Nothing gamebreaking, seems like a lot of them are gamemaker engine quirks but there they are here and they are annoying regardless.At the end I still liked it enough to 100% it. The life sim elements are entertaining, the moneymaking part is pretty good and the spirits are interesting enough to make you wanna see all of them. So it gets a recommendation, however I think the devs should still iron out the bugs and provide couple QOL improvements to combat previously mentioned annoying design quirks.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Stardew Valley. If you're coming here for the sake of comprehensive customization, or building close & meaningful relationships with the NPCs, you're probably in the wrong place.If you're here for exploration, discovery, solving little mysteries, getting a peek into the townsfolk's lives, and collecting things, then you're in the right place.  And I think the bath house memory / puzzle / placement game is pretty fun.There are still some occasional bugs, but devs are clearly proactively working them out and making improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Once you hit the start button, you can't stop playing it until the next day, asking about your name and time.It's a cute game, not too long or too hard to gain the most achievements. It's the perfect game for a lazy afternoon or weekend, under a blanket. The characters are nicely done and the spirits are all differents and kirky. I do think it can be replayable. The dev' is active about bugs or any suggestion to make it even better. I read a lot about the minigames, and I do confess that some can be tedious or pointeless (karaoke and barbecue, I'm looking at you), but the game is plenty eventfull without them so don't be afraid to let them on the side of the road. Do try it and even if you don't fall in love, it will be a nice game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Spirittea! Such great game play, so many main and side quests with varying difficulty. I love the friendship aspect of the game it comes in handy so much as you play more. The music and sounds (ex-rain and storms etc) are done so well. It gives me spirited away vibes 10000%. Can't wait to see and hear what others think of the game, it has come so far from the demo a year ago! The devs have been very on top of issues and bugs and correcting what was needed for release. if you enjoy the cozy game genre this is absolutely for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! Pros:-You can go to bed whenever, and wake up whenever it suits you and your goals. -The different spirits and the different ways you can catch them. Some of these spirits are really up to no good! It's great!-The different villagers each have something charming-Art style is *chefs kiss*-You have a reason to run the bathhouse. You have to to progress the game!Cons:-Keyboard play is clunky. Had to go in a reassign key binds to make it playable.-Had the game crash during a cut scene. I just had to try to start that cut scene at a different time of day, and it worked fine. But still..
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a massive Ghibli fan and a massive fan of Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, etc etc. I am basically the exact target audience for this game.And while i did enjoy it quite a bit at first, it grew very stale for me much more quickly than i would have liked. It becomes very monotonous in a relatively short amount of time, and it ultimately just feels like something is missing. The bathhouse itself, while fun initially, grows very repetitive and monotonous after a while, and really and truly begins to feel like work (not to mention the frequent periods spent just standing around waiting for a spot to open up, or a new customer to arrive). On the other hand, however, if you don't go to the bathhouse for the day, there is usually absolutely nothing of interest to do. You basically just wander around hoping/wishing to find something to do, and usually failing to do so, especially once the relationships have been maxed (which can be done very quickly, especially if they enjoy karaoke). And even before the relationships are maxed, you may still just end up spending the entire day just wandering aimlessly with nothing to do. You may find that the villagers you need/want to talk to are busy or the activities that they enjoy aren't available. There is no dungeon or mine you can visit like Stardew Valley (or any type of combat at all), there is so little "farming" as to not even be worth mentioning, the fishing is nowhere near as fun as some other games in the genre... there's just nothing to do or to occupy your time outside of the (again, very repetitive) bathhouse, day after day after day.On top of that, the townspeople themselves feel far more bland and shallow than they do in other games in the genre. I hate to keep bringing it back to Stardeww Valley, but even people who havent played the game in years remember the villagers, their names, their personalities. They were memorable. It's been less than a month since i last played this, and i honestly could not name a single villager. They are just not memorable or interesting.I feel bad giving it a thumbs down. It's not necessarily a BAD game. But it does become a very grindy, repetitive, and monotonous one after a fairly short amount of playtime.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I can see what the creators were trying to do with this game. They are going for a Spirited Away + Stardew feel. The bathouse mechanics are good overall, and it's pleasant when you figure it out, but many other mechanics are clunky. My chief complaints: Socialization with the other people is mainly to convince them to slave away in the bathouse for you. They aren't particularly interesting and the socializing minigames are not very good.The rate of customers is slow. Once you get all of the baths, the strategic challenge of placing the spirits, which adds a bit of spice to the cozy mechanics, is not really there anymore. Maybe they get faster later on, but I didn't feel motivated enough to do that.The bathouse is the only way to earn money. This is a matter of personal taste, but the cozy games that hyper-emphasize making money (Little-known Galaxy comes to mind) feel off somehow. The cat spirit can be greedy and money loving, that's his character and I love him for it, but the game really straps you for cash, and everything has to be bought. The time stamina mechanic makes the bathhouse awkward, too.Finally, one of the key ways that farming and life sims (like Animal Crossing) give you a sense of everyday life is by tying you to the seasons. Certain crops grow, certain bugs show up, and you are very aware of what you need to be doing. That isn't entirely there in Spiritea - there are season-tied mechanics, but - and this is key - no garden space. You can't grow a little garden to support and improve your bathhouse experience, and it's very easy to lose track of time... and not in a good way. If I lose track of time in a game like this, I want it to be "Oh, I spent hours playing this... ah, just one more day," and not "Oh. Spring passed in game without me noticing it because I was dedicated to that spirit bathhouse grind." It's very capitalist rat-race and it doesn't feel like it goes with the theme. Anyway, some of these might get patched, but that's my experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people have referred to this as Stardew Valley meets Spirited Away.I would caution against this specific analogy, because depending on what people really liked about Stardew, they may be disappointed.If you're expecting the farming, the really great character moments as you build friendships with the other townspeople, they aren't there.But if you enjoy mysteries, puzzles, and managementy things, this game is great! I've been quite enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the premise of this game. The bathhouse mechanics are fun. But the interaction with the townspeople is not intuitive. It took forever to figure out how to buy things (you have to speak to them twice in a row) or go on play dates (again, speak to them twice in a row). But it was the fishing minigame that made me rage quit... The instructions say use the joystick to point in the direction of the fish and repeatedly mash 'B'. The instructions made it seem that if I leaned the joystick in the correct direction (and the fish constantly changes position) I could zero in on the fish. But that's not how it works... you have to rotate the joystick to rotate your hook and it's so slow and clunky it impossible to even come close let alone catch anything! I can appreciate wanting to make a minigame a challenge, but the fishing game is an impossible to win mess and it makes me not want to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: While I really love this -- as in, it's all I did all weekend -- and expect it will continue to delight me, I do want to try and give a thorough review in case it's helpful. I absolutely LOVE the bathhouse mechanic, it's so satisfying and I love seating the little spirits and hurrying about with the towels. I even like the small little tasks you do to get ready and keep it going, and the upgrades for the bathhouse are really fun and attainable while still being a challenge to keep you engaged. As you can see, I've played 40 hours so I'm really into the game. I just have some suggestions for how it could be even BETTER. I like the town and the characters, and there's a lot about the game's letting you just...figure things out that I appreciate, but it's not quite intuitive enough to do that in its early state, I think. (It's confusing to know which plants/flowers you can pick and which you can't, what to do with some of the items, that sort of thing.) While I really like this game and am adoring how easily it plays on the Steam Deck, there are a few quality of life improvements that would help IMHO: 1. The tools (thinking about the shovel/net/fishing rod/brooms in the bathhouse)  can very easily be set down and left, since you have to equip it and use it and then put it back in the backpack, instead and you can't run with them, Having some kind of radial tool bar where it has a dedicated hotkey or something would really help, I think -- I've had to buy the shovel twice, because I put it down instead of back in my bag and ??? 2. The way you have to shift items from your hand/bag/storage/fridge is a little clunky. Also, devs, please let items stack and be ordered! 3. When the bathhouse upgrades are being done, there's....not a lot to do. Villagers are fun to talk to, but i find i go to sleep pretty early because i just don't have enough to do. Filling the shrines is great, but it's not super difficult and other than cooking there's not a lot of crafting to do. I wish there was more, and that you had more to *do* outside of the bathhouse (I feel like this will happen later). 4. The minigames -- while I love the idea and find it really fun to have them, some of them don't really make a lot of sense. Fishing is frustrating until you figure out the mechanics, and even then, the timing is really frustrating with the seaweed catching your hook and by the time you get it free, the timer is up and no fish for you. Also it took me a bit to figure out to hold down B on the Deck for a long cast, i couldn't figure out why I wasn't able to cast into the ocean. The cooking minigame with the lettuce wrap is fun but the perimeters weren't really explained and that's another thing I'll get to, lack of a quest journal or a tutorial to revisit. I think I get it, but the meter when you're with another person is ??? I haven't done the drinking one because it's locked to a quest i have to finish with Leigh, but the karaoke game is mystifying. I know I get a few of the notes at LEAST and still get an F. (Does it take points away if you miss one? Who knows) And the songs are WAY TOO LONG -- there's only a few of them so far and they're difficult, boring, and just far too long. Bug catching is fine but every time I try and bring a villager along, the bugs are nowhere to be found?? I've seen someone else mention that too. But the karaoke game is the one that gives me fits -- look, I don't mind if you have to practice to get good, but it needs to be a little smoother of a rhythm game. Digging is very....clunky, because you have to figure out where to go and access maps through the pause screen, which is annoying. 4. The game is in desperate need of a quest log/journal/one central location for spirit info, recipes, maps, etc. The resources are confusing when it comes to what can be gathered and what has to be bought, and there just needs to be a little more time and attention here toward gameplay as a player, as someone who hasn't lived and breathed the game map and assets for however long. I had no idea you could take grass from that one plant by the beach, just like I had no idea you could pick up the brooms from the bathhouse to clean it. I don't mind discovering things on my own, but it's frustrating to have sixteen websites open. And oh my god, PLEASE, the letters you get in the mail? Can they not have the sender's NAME AT THE BOTTOM, those little pictures are so small it's impossible to tell who sent them. There's no labels on the map, and no hours on the store signs, which I think would also be helpful. like you should have at least ONE of those -- either on the map, or on a sign -- or have it under villager information. The notebook and pamphlet is fine, but switching is confusing and also it seems vital info is weirdly spread between the pause screen and the pamphlet/notebook and I would think all of that could be in one place?? But yeah not having names/labels/hours on the map or the actual places is a little confusing. There's a couple other things -- the palette could be more vibrant, and it sure rains a lot -- but overall I really am enjoying this. I especially love the aspect of finding the lost ghosts and helping them, and the bathhouse is my favorite part (and I'm a fantasy novelist in real life, so that's fun!) and I know this is an indie game and i love that, i really enjoy playing this and even joined the discord. i think with some patches they'll be able to fix most of these issues, but please devs, that karaoke mini-game is giving me a rage blackout every time I play it, LOL. Also I know this might sound nit-picky but I swear it's only because I love the game and the idea of it so much that I'm leaving such a detailed review. So yes, I recommend this as a game that gives cozy without being a farming sim, and the bathhouse is really fun to manage -- with a couple tweaks/patches i can see me playing this for a few hundred hours. I really do recommend it but keep in mind it's a new game from a small team, so it's going to have growing pains -- for me, those aren't enough to keep me from playing but I did want to share them.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed this game and feel like it was worth the price paid. However, it does have some issues:1) Many of the interactions with NPCs are ultimately shallow, and I wish the limit on new dialogue hadn't come quite so quickly.2) The endgame comes on you pretty quickly if you do things a certain way (being vague to avoid spoilers), and there doesn't seem to be a way to avoid it aside from just.. not getting on the bus. I wish there was an in-game choice of taking the step/not taking the step instead. Wonyan pouted at me for no reason.3) I really don't like the fishing minigame, and you have to offer fish to the shrines to complete them (which I think lets you meet more spirits--not sure what else the shrines do, if anything). No doubt I'd like it better if I weren't playing it on PC, but I am; that's how I game. So fair warning: if you too are playing on PC, the fishing minigame is not designed for you. I find it pretty annoying and have yet to catch a single fish.4) You don't choose a gender. Everyone calls you by the pronouns they/them, but if you pick a short-haired character, at least one younger woman is pretty iffy about getting in the hot springs with you in a very gendered way that the guys are not. It's a small thing, but it struck me as odd. Either you're picking a gender or you're not. If I'm picking, I'd like to pick pronouns too. :D5) You can waste a lot of time trying to figure out how to resolve NPCs' problems based on their extremely vague and sparse clues. Maybe the latest update helped; now you can ask Wonyan for hints. That could be nice.The good:1) Catchy music.2) Fun spirit design.3) The main gameplay loop (the spirit sauna) is easy to immerse yourself in if you want to just chill for a while.4) Love the birds. Love bug-catching.5) Talking to the NPCs is fun until they run out of dialogue.6) It's a low-stakes game with a refreshingly different premise.

Currently, you have to open your backpack and then select the tool you want to use.- Descriptions for each item.- An instruction manual that you can access at any time (on how to use this and that).- A list of fish/bugs that you have already captured (not just how they look).- The collection of spirits should be in alphabetical order.

_childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy most of the game, and I think the idea is unique and different from a lot of the other "cozy" games out there, there are just still too many things that make the game just not worth completing. The game feels almost...unfinished in a way, and would definitley be in need of some polishing and fine tuning. I agree with a lot of the criticism you see in the other comments about how the developers did not really think of how the game feels the play, as things like the controls and mechanics make the game less enjoyable. For example, it's very annoying that some bugs/insects can ONLY be triggered by sprinting, but because sprinting and tool-use are THE SAME button and cannot be set seperately, this is an extremely annoying mechanic to deal with. It's also extremely annoying that anytime you are handed something, by an npc, or pick up something, you drop your tool. This really doesn't make sense and could have been avoided as well if there was more thought into the tool usage, which would be improved by having a proper toolbar. It's also a weird mechanic that I have to open my backpack, select my tool, then close my backpack, to switch between tools. Aside from the mechanics, while there is a lot to do, I am always feeling quite bored inbetween certain events in tasks. It feels like there is nothing to do at certain points, so the flow and balance between these different tasks and events is lacking. While the bathhouse is being fixed, you can fish, bug catch, etc. But a lot of the characters are always busy, and once you catch what you need to for your shrines or collections, there is not much motivation to keep fishing or bug catching (cannot sell at a good price, make things or cook with most of them), so what is the point of catching them beyond the first one?The game is also missing a lot of details that, while would not make the game "better" are things I would consider a minimum to not make the game worse. This includes things like: proper item descriptions (what does the different types of coffee do? how long do they last?), better notifications (when does an item wear off, I should still be able to see the friend meter go up even if they're not right next to me, such as after spending time at the hot springs), etc.It also feels a bit unfinished in a way through the characters. Based on some of the dialogue, it seems almost like romancing was an option at some point, but was maybe not included. I also feel like the characters are not really exciting to interact with as a whole. I think the idea of doing things with them to increase the friendship meter is a really nice idea, and that adds a lot to the game, but it still feels like there should be more hearts, more dialogue, gifts, or cutscenes to the characters. I'm not really invested in them at all, they're just slaves for my bathhouse.In conclusion, I really wanted to like this game,, the idea is good and unique, but it needs to be improved, somehow I lost my expensive bicycle in the ocean by getting off of it on the bridge out of town, so I wouldn't bother getting this game until they do so more bug patches and work on it. I hope the developers continue to fix it so it can be the game it has the potential to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with good vibes let down by pointless and frustrating mini-games and bad keyboard play defaultsI saw articles about this game before it was released and was instantly interested due to the cute pixel art graphics and the premise of the game being interacting with and helping spirits and running a bathhouse.Both of those aspects of the game are great. I love the little village, the character portraits are really nice and feel like realistic people, little things like the trees and little details like the mini shrines and decorations in rooms seem like they have been drawn and rendered with care. Running the bathhouse only ever felt grindy in a chill way for me (I quite like repetitive tasks like that but I get that it'd bore some people), and solving the mysteries of all of the spirits and discovering who they were was interesting and fun, as was getting to know all of the NPCs - honestly, I wish the game had just focused on all of that stuff more, maybe brought a little more folklore in.Unfortunately, there were several minigames that felt crowbarred in for the sake of giving the player more to do.These minigames were either needlessly complicated (fishing), pointless (the barbecue), or just not fun (karaoke) to the point that they were just irritating and I ended up not wanting to do any of them and kind of resenting their existence. Unfortunately, all of them are ways to increase friendship with the NPCs in the game, so while not compulsory (you can still increase friendship with everyone by talking to them all as much as possible each day, but of course that takes much longer), ignoring them makes the game more time-consuming.The default controls for the keyboard also make playing these minigames difficult at best and frustrating at worst (better make sure you have StickyKeys disabled for that fishing one, otherwise the notice pops up constantly as you try to reel in the fish, minimising the game every time it does so).The controls (left shift being 'use item' but also 'back', and interacting with people being E which is also the 'pick things up/put things down' button) felt counter-intuitive, and don't allow you to change them to what would feel most intuitive for me at least (left mouse button for use item/interact with people, right mouse button for back, cancel, etc.) as it doesn't let you use the mouse keys as inputs at all.The game also doesn't work with non-official Nintendo Switch controllers (I didn't even know mine was non-official until I played this game), and 'only partly works' with PS4 controllers, despite PS4 being one of the main consoles around?? I like many things about this game - the graphics, the music (not so much the karaoke songs), the sound giving it a realistic atmosphere, the cute little strutting squawking crows, the characters, the bathhouse...But I felt forced to play it with the controller to be able to play any of the minigames without my fingers locking up, and even after having an easier time playing the minigames with the controller, I still don't like them and would rather not have them in the game. It feels too much like the devs were trying so hard to make the minigames different to other games that they didn't really consider whether the minigames were actually necessary or not. I haven't even unlocked the hot spring for the human characters yet (as of this review I've only played through Spring) but it wouldn't surprise me if that was minigame-ified tooIf you can look past (or if you somehow end up enjoying) the minigames, then I'd recommend this game. Playing the game while ignoring the minigames, I still enjoy all of the other stuff enough.If you don't like repetitive tasks or taking time getting to know characters then this game may bore you as there isn't much else to do

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game! I backed the Kickstarter campaign three years ago and have no complaints about the wait. Whether you like exploring the town, talking to the townspeople and helping to solve their problems, or prefer to spend your time tending to the spirits at the bath house, this game provides so many unique game play features that I think anyone could find enjoyment out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems to be lovingly designed, but not very thoroughly programmed/tested. The concept is cute and cozy, but the small usability things constantly get in my way, like- I can only see if my character is carrying anything in their hands if they face me- I don't understand where the stamina bar is or how to interpret it- The 'use', 'back', and 'esc' buttons/controls seem to have no consistency across different surfaces of UI, e.g. sometimes I have to press 'use' to get out of some screen, other times it's 'back', and yet other times it's 'esc'- Showing all the other people locations on the map is convenient, but takes away the discovery- The bath repairs said will be done by say Monday, means I can actually use them only on Tuesday- It's very unclear from the visuals where the characters will get stuck when walking (tea plantation?), and where they would just walk all over (veggie fields?)- Altogether the movement is annoyingly stucky behind all kinds of things, which gets extremely irritating when you have to chase someone faster than youIf it was alpha version, all of that would be fine and good things to discover, but in the final release seems unpolished and is a pity.Not recommended in the current state, but happy to revisit that some time later.

_childDocuments_.review: As promised by the developer, it looks like a lot of the difficulties I was having before the recent update have been fixed. We tried it out on a friend's fresh install, and it's much more playable. Review has been changed to recommended. :)Original review [updates in brackets]:The core gameplay is great. I want to be able to recommend this game, but it had way too many annoying and sometimes game-breaking bugs.The good things:-The core gameplay is fun. The "repetitive" portion (running the bath house) is kind of like a puzzle, so it rarely gets boring.-The mini-games are fun.-The NPCs are mostly charming, even if a few are flat. -It's Spirited Away mixed with Stardew Valley in terms of flavor; yum. -Lots of things to discover.Game-breaking bugs:-Wonyan interrupted me for a tutorial while carrying a towel, which caused the towel to drop into an out-of-bounds area (into the middle of a bath, mysteriously). This crashed the game at the end of the day, forcing me to redo the entire day. [Fixed in the new update.]-Multiple times, the Towel Runner has dropped towels out of bounds when I close the bath house for the day. Most commonly, they'll drop them in the threshold of a doorway such that if I try to go near them to pick them up, the PC just walks into the next room. This makes the objects irretrievable. [Fixed in the new update.]-A certain character has, in theory, given me all 3 of their maps. However, the first one doesn't show as having been given to me--even though the 2nd and 3rd do. As a result, digging in that spot creates the "Eureka!" sound of having found an object, but does not actually give the object. This means that achievement is not receivable. [I'm still having this problem; friend has not gotten far enough to confirm if it's still happening. I'm not sure if the newly-added recovery shrine includes maps.]-The Sunset Moth is uncatchable in my game, as it "fades" out of existence the moment a net interacts with it--something that normally only happens after you chase a bug for a bit. This also prevents an achievement from being receivable. [We eventually caught this doing something counterintuitive.]Other bugs:-NPC animations and pathing breaks pretty regularly. NPCs can end up in out of bounds areas, or they move around but in a static position (most commonly seated). [This seems largely fixed, probably due to NPC animations being added.]-The game tells you to use a controller, so I plugged in a Playstation controller. It then proceeded to tell me that the game was not compatible with this controller. If you want a *specific* controller to be used, you need to tell players that. [Does seem to be something with Steam settings, as we didn't encounter this on friend's system.]-Playing with a controller forces me to actually load the game twice. The first time I load it after starting up my computer, the pause menu is inaccessible. Rebooting the game fixes it, but this is an annoying thing to have to do every time. [We did still encounter this issue on the fresh install, but it's a mild inconvenience.]Annoying, but not bugs:-Inventory management is terrible. You have to move objects 1 by 1 and there is no wraparound (like moving items from the far left to far right of the inventory by going left/off screen). [Fixed in the new update.]-You can't buy multiple of any item at a time, so you're forced to buy cooking ingredients 1 by 1.[Still applicable.]-You can't run with tools because the "use tool" and "run" buttons are the same button.[Still applicable.]-The game is DARK. I tried removing the blue filter on my PC, and it was still dark except during the brightest portions of the day. By the very nature of the game, you're going to end up playing at night quite a lot, and it's currently really awful to try to move around or explore almost anywhere past 10 PM. [Huge quality of life improvement in the new update, where this is fixed.]
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by saying this game is not done. It's VERY buggy, often in a game-breaking way. I've made it to mid-fall and largely without having to reference a walk-through. The story itself is very fun and relaxing while also being interesting. Some of the mini-games are a bit confusing (I still don't know how the cooking mini-game works exactly) and a little too challenging (the harder karaoke levels are a bit much at times). Certain bug-catching is honestly infuriating (the catching mechanics are too slow for a lot of them and you can't set the bug trap in time either). The fishing and drinking mini-games are pretty solid, though. My biggest issues are the lack of direction (you really have to seek out the story at times) and the buggy spirit and neighbor interactions. It's like the scripts for them just don't run sometimes. I had one neighbor stuck in an inaccessible part of the railroad for over a week even after closing and opening the game back up. Neighbors sometimes stack on top of each other and you can't interact with one or all of them. Spirits flea from you even though according to other players' accounts, they were meant to respond differently (and you can't tell at first because some spirits need you to do the same thing with the same result multiple times, which isn't very intuitive; it doesn't encourage further interaction from the player but you have to do it to proceed). A lot of the puzzles around the spirits are extremely vague. I didn't even realize one of the community posts was a mission because the neighbor it corresponds to never talks about it when you talk to him, but you're supposed to talk to him at a certain time. Aside from the actual bugs, the worst part is the diggable items. Maps are extremely pricey, and they're horrible. Even after looking through a guide, I couldn't see how the dig spots corresponded to the maps very well. Sometimes you can't even dig up an item because it's bugged as well.All this said, I do really love the game. I like the mechanics of the bathhouse and the spirits have a variety of charming and annoying personalities. I feel like there's a good story brewing in it. I love the neighbors' personalities and even the little bit of attitude some of them give you. The cultural mish-mash of everyone is pretty fun too. I enjoy recognizing pieces of each NPC's background in how they dress, food they eat, stories they tell, and things they care about. I hope the bugs will be fixed and maybe some of the mini-games will be worked on? I really love this game, but it's becoming difficult to play. I'd rather quit before hitting a wall. I look forward to updates on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: i really liked playing this game. but the bathhouse was always way to grindy even after you get all the helpers. half the time at the end of the night i would just sit there and wait for people to leave. also i ended up beating the game before i got all the spirits, i ended up sleeping for like 20 days to get to winter to get the last ones. there really isn't much to do after that
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: After over 17 hours in Spirittea, here is my TLDR:What I LIKE: - Solving mysteries & finding spirits - Managing the bathhouse (especially with helpers) - Booby-trapping houses with hermit crabs - Unexpected humor from NPCs - Prowling through villager homes (a kleptomaniac's dream) - TONS of content for $20 - Cozy Japanese aesthetic - No farming, just a life sim that thinks outside the curry noodle cup - Cloud save + works on Steam Deck - Kenzo is a hottieWhat could be BETTER: - Mini games are tough (though have been nerfed in updates) - Tutorials are a tad lacking at times - Minor pacing issues - Expect to be stumped and resort to Googling how to find the spiritSpirittea is such a surprising breath of fresh air and is well worth the 20 bucks.  Want help getting started?  Check out my beginner Spirittea tips video (and let's play series and YT shorts).  Disclaimer: I did NOT receive a free copy of this game or ANY compensation from the dev or publisher.  I just like the game, gosh darn it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This scratches an itch I've had for awhile.It's a fresh take on the relaxing Life Sim genre with the central loop being around a bathhouse for spirits à la Spirited Away. It manages to create a really interesting and altogether inviting atmosphere where things are kind of charming and kind of spooky. The spirits are all very unique and cute, with the main little cat dude hanging around you constantly being my favorite.There's some lulls in gameplay which offer up some time to explore and chat up the locals, in addition to gathering ingredients and seeds to use later in cooking. There's some mini games (e.g., Karaoke, Fishing) and the ability to furnish and re-arrange your home. The story has been compelling so far, and I've really enjoyed the pace of it.You'll be splitting your time between town activities and the bathhouse. Neither of which ever feel overwhelming, and you don't suffer any penalties for taking your time with things. If you manage to keep your spirits happy during their stay at your bathhouse, they'll give you a little extra. There's some problem solving involved as some spirits don't get along with others, so you'll have to experiment to find out which combination works best.So If you'd like to play a life sim with a different twist, I'd highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: --EDIT 06/24-- Bugs are fixed, the game is playable now!.I wish I could recommend this game right now. Atmosphere is great, game is cozy and relaxing without any stress but still enough things to work for. The world and quests are more expansive and whimsical than I expected and I urge everyone not to rely on guides but to try to discover things on their own. But I've encountered so many bugs - some of them are game-breaking, others frustrating. Feels as if it hasn't been playtested. This game should not be out as a full release, this is more of a beta. Hope to be able to recommend it in the future because the ideas and worldbuilding are solid.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: While the premise of Spirittea is interesting an innovative, this game feels like a chore. I've been playing for 4 hours and the only change to the gameplay was unlocking more spirits (which only makes catering to them harder since you're supposed to memorise who likes sitting next to who...).Spirittea lacks the charm of Stardew Valley. The NPCs look a little uncanny.The main game loop also doesn't look like it will have the depth of Stardew - I don't see you optimising your spa engine rolling in more and more rewards as you play it more. Sure, you might be getting some NPCs to help you out, you could be spending time cooking for your guests and rubbing them with a broom, but is that much better than what you are doing at the start of the game?I guess it would be nice if this game had some better feedback from your guests. Get some good meter of how well you did, let us know how much cash they paid, etc. Even some kind of summary at the end of the shift would be nice.So overall, I'd first recommend games like Stardew Valley or Graveyard Keeper before giving this one a go. Maybe with a good amount of love and polish it will get better over time, but so far it looks like a slow, okay game while I was expecting something better.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR "I like it more than it annoys me"It's secretive. Mysterious. It almost doesn't want to be played. Its controls are very rudimentary, sometimes even unintuitive. Barely anything is explained. Yet there's a depth of gameplay emerging here that could maybe rival Stardew Valley, and it's going to take me 30 more hours or longer to find out. So far though, I like it more than it annoys me. The minigames are garbage (worst karaoke ever) but I still feel compelled to grind through them to find out where this all goes. I originally gave this game a negative review because its writing is quite odd and it didn't land to begin with, but it's starting to add up more. This review will go right back to negative though if all this gameplay doesn't lead anywhere in the end!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Idea is good, execution is cool, programming is awful.Controls unexpectedly switch during the game, where critical commands become unaccesible. Other than that, the storyline is broken, with spirits disappearing, quests that can't be completed, and other nonsense. Wait for the bugs to be fixed before you buy.EDIT: one of the devs reached out, and asked which issues I am experiencing. Well:- Controls are weird and remapping does nothing- Controls suddenly change during the game, where spirit vision becomes unaccesible (and still; remapping does nothing)- The boat vandal quest has the spirit disappear in the tunnel; not 'run through', but 'disappear'. The spirit does not appear again after this --> quest brokenI find it weird that the dev asks this, since these issues are wel-known and the main source of negative reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Rating: 8/10TL/DR: This game has been worth every penny and it's one of the games I return to often when I need a break from something else. I will never regret this purchase. Story: The overall story is pretty amazing. You play as a city person whose moved to a small town and eventually you get dragged into opening up a bathhouse to make some spirits happy. Its very, Stardew Valley meets Spirited Away and I absolutely love this concept so so much.Gameplay: The overall gameplay is very user friendly. There's not long tutorial to learn or understand so you can just jump right into playing the game. There are also weird Easter Eggs here and there that I find pretty fun. There are both quests and fun mini games so I never feel lost or unsure of what my next step is. Its a very fun immersive experience.Graphics/Art: I'm a sucker for a good pixel art game, but there's still such a whimsical quality about it. This game has taken such a familir art style and added something so unfamiliar to it making it such an amazing blend of comfort and quality. Best/Worst Qualities: I don't have anything negative to say about the game. It has a fun little add in of certain things being choice based which is nice. I love the ability to collect smaller objects for shrines that unlock certain things. The personalities of the spirits are fun to learn and being able to have relationships with the NPC's instead of them just being fillers.Final Thoughts: This is a must have for any RPG players that appreciate smaller indie style games. Also, this discord community for this game is a must join. The people there are so friendly and willing to help with tips and tricks for a fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever thought you could do better than Chihiro did and you like your games a little on the cozy side, you've got Spirittea. You've just moved into town (like most cozy games) and you're eager to start on your new book. Turns out your teapot is haunted and the spirit hanging out in it implores you to open the neglected bathhouse to get rich quick and save the spirits that are lost in town. But mostly get rich.The devs are very active, hi devs, and are very happy to receive feedback. They squash bugs and give hints. They're awesome. They're amazing. So let's just get that out of the way.The game is very cozy coded but feels a little more time management. You can't do everything in one day, but there's also no rush. People leave their doors unlocked and while some spirits and your neighbors are on a timer, there's always tomorrow. Sure, some spirits only arrive during certain seasons but there's no timer. The game doesn't suddenly stop after three years. You go at your own pace and discover at your own pace. If and when that book gets done, it gets done. There's no rush and the land and spirits will heal.This is my kind of game. There's no threat looming over me that everyone will suffer, die, move away, etc... I'm just here to do my thing. This is what I really want out of a cozy game. That even when my actions are the same ones over and over, there's no looming deadline that someone will swoop in and buy up the town or I'll get docked invisible points for not being married after so many years.There is no marriage here. You just become best friends. The benefits of friendship is getting people to work in the bathhouse. That's right, friendship is about manipulating people! I mean, they become more in tune to nature around them? ...No it's about manipulation you don't have to feel guilty about.Honestly it's just a breath of fresh air. It's a game I've really been looking for among all these other titles and just really was happy to find it. Worth the wait.As of writing this, there's a few bugs and trying to fish is near impossible, but I have some faith. As mentioned, the devs have great communication. So, so far so good. If anything changes, this will be updated.Potential wrist cramps. You may want a controller for this game for comfort. Some sections are incredibly dark, even with brightness adjusted. Easy enough without a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game when it came out. Absolutely loved it from top to bottom, had no problems. When I hit around 50% completion, I suddenly encountered a game-halting bug that would NOT let me ever hit 100%, and it was a nasty one that messed with some story stuff too and made a few things a pain. I left the game for MONTHS because I was so upset (monitoring if it would ever pop up as something fixed, it hasn't). Decided to start a new run a few days ago, and I've already hit a completely different game-halting bug. I love this game but I don't think this game loves its players.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly everything I was looking for in terms of relaxing, management, and a sense of coziness. The town/map is fairly small, but it doesn't FEEL small which is nice. The story line is fun and so far I've progressed a little bit to open up the bathhouse to the first four baths and I'm about to open up the stairs in the main room. All in all this game is so sweet and comforting which ticks all the boxes I was hoping it would. I would agree that it's a mixture of Stardew Valley, of which I've played so much of, and Spirited Away, one of Myazaki's greatest films. If you like either of those things and enjoy a nice and cozy game then this is definitely one you should consider buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: this game is s charming. the humor is great and i really like the mechanics. running the bathhouse can feel overwhelming but they give you the option of making friends to help out which is really great. i feel like i havent even scratched the surface of what this game still has to offer. i have had to look a few things up but that happens for me in a lot of games. give it a try! you wont regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a delight if you enjoy life sims. Spirittea is a great game to pop on to relax to. The characters are cute, the spirits are quirky and silly, and the bath house is so much fun. This game was clearly made with love and while does have some bugs, work is constantly being done to improve it. I did encounter a bug and reached out on discord and was able to find it was just an error with my save, but was able to get it fixed nonetheless within the same day :) I do think it's easy to forget that small indie devs often don't have huge teams to help polish a game quickly. I think with a little time this game will be among the top recommendations in the life sim category constantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Every bone in my body WANTS to love this. Very few games of this ilk really feel like they have their own strongly defined identity while still keeping what makes "farming" games wonderful. Graveyard Keeper remains a standout for being so successful at that, and is the first similarity to come to mind when I play this.However: the UI in this is bad and unless that gets some major improvements or someone mods this thing to fix the most egregious flaws, I'm afraid I can't recommend this.The biggest problem I have with the UI is that there is no way to tell how tired your character is until you start getting warnings that you're about to collapse. The game allows you to sleep any number of hours, which is fantastic for allowing you to be in a place at the right time, but doesn't explain to you how tiredness works unless you are about to collapse. And there is absolutely nothing in the UI to allow you to monitor tiredness.But there are other things:- It took me three in-game days to figure out where the stamina bar is. The graphic they gave it so it looks like a bento box gradually growing empty is cute, but it needs a label.- The map is terribly unhelpful. It doesn't give you any way to see NPC names, or shop indicators, both of which would be really helpful before you get more familiar with the town and its people.- Mystery Maps make no sense.- I can't seem to place furniture in my house such that it's against the wall.- The game tells you that as you progress and serve more spirits, the special tree at the bathhouse will take care of making the place nicer. That made me think for days that it would take care of the dust and cobwebs. I picked up the broom on accident, finally, and found out the hard way that I should have been sweeping things the whole time.It's too bad that this has such rough UI and onboarding, because this could be an amazing game if those aspects were better. I'll check back again in 6 months or something and see how things look.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: so far, Spirittea has two great things going for it:- the atmosphere. this is the type of beautiful, atmospheric game i wish i could just keep on my second monitor as a relaxing background. maybe record walking around the world, turning it into a gif, and make it a background? idk, but its very calming- the bathhouse "mini" game. its very head empty, no thoughts, so ive enjoyed the bathhouse for when im waiting for something irl. the only issue is that there isnt AWAYS something to do there, except maybe if you start cooking, but i havent done that.if you want a game like Stardew, Spirittea is far from it. if you read other reviews, you'll find that befriending NPCs or figuring out what to do is quite a hassle. but managing the bathhouse is fun! so i recommend the game if you want a very simple and calming bathhouse simulator, basically. but thats really all its got going for it
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for that Spirited Away itch, you've found it. Its different from the typical run a farm mill type of game like Stardew just enough for you to latch on and not want to stop playing. The premise is simple, and the tutorial is very thorough. The spirit designs are unique, as well as the scenarios to getting more spirits, and who doesn't love a sassy cat spirit.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Studio Ghibli-esque world, Spirit tea, and a beautiful soundtrack? What else could you ask for? This cozy game has a wonderfully atmospheric world full of lost spirits that you have to assist in helping remember who they are. The "quests" to help the townspeople with their various scenarios are super cute, and I love the way that they help you learn more about the people who live in the town. I also really adore the various personalities of the spirits and solving their various issues. I played the demo of this game and was really looking forward to launch, and I am so impressed and pleased with the full version! My bathhouse needs a lot of work, but I'm looking forward to discovering new spirits and making lots of moolags!I definitely recommend this game if you like low stress, low-pressure cozy games!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: The game is generally meh and not downright bad, but also not good enough to be recommendable. The gameplay loop at the bathhouse is okay, although it can get pretty old and repetitive pretty fast. You will be told to befriend villagers to help you, but that would honestly just give me less to do and it takes a while. The tasks to unlock more spirit and help the villagers are most of the time either unclear or involve sensitive timing which made me stand around and waiting in places a lot. Since I love all things around legends, yokai and the likes that would have still not kept me from the game, however there's also many bugs. Sometimes a menu just won't close. Sometimes all sound will randomly stop. Also the game always starts up in a small window despite choosing fullscreen again and again. None of it is gamebreaking so far, but I'm done putting up with it. Just not my cup of tea you could say.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is close to being a good game. It ends up slow, repetitive, and frustrating.The initial frustration is from bugs - there are surprisingly many in the first 30 minutes of game play. For example, my controller only mostly works. Finding the spirits is okay but again frustrating because of the non-linear way you can get involved or how specific you need to be. I got a clue for a spirit, and spent quite a while trying to figure that out, only to finally figure out, somewhat inconsistently, an earlier clue needed to be acted on first.I shouldn't need to search the internet to figure out how to grow seeds.If you decide to take a day off from looking after the bathhouse, there is little to do whilst waiting for the right time to do a spirit quest. For example, once you've caught all the solo fish - maybe a few sessions of fishing for the month - you can't finish the team fish in the collection because everyone is busy and won't talk to you, or leaves in the middle of a fishing session. So you wander town hoping to find someone to fish with you, instead of fishing - that's just not fun.So it's cute, it's almost fun. I actually sank a fair bit of time into it. I got through most of fall, I'm not that excited to play through winter, and, while I might play a bit more, I definitely won't put stardew valley levels of time into this one. There are better games to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I initially bought this game on the switch and completed it. I absolutely love this game so much so I had to get it on steam to play again. I love Studio Ghibli, especially spirited away so this game feels like it was made for me. The story, characters, music, art style and game play are all so well done. I would recommend this game to anyone who appreciates cozy games. Also I had an issue with getting the game to run and my boyfriend reached out to the developer and they were so nice and responded so fast!! It ended up being an issue with my pc, not the game! They got it figured out and now I can enjoy this game all over again!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game with an interesting, unique concept and plenty to do! It is very creatively done, and it delivers on the "Spirited Away" feeling. There are plenty of secrets that I feel motivated to keep playing and unlock. There is a good mix of mechanics in the quests. Because the mechanics are varied, the quests do not feel repetitive and grindy. The bathhouse is the opposite, very repetitive and grindy (like many retail businesses IRL), but there are additional features to unlock that make running it much easier. The controls are a bit clunky at times, which can lead to difficulty in completing the quests, but I still enjoy myself.  I do wish relationships with townsfolk and spirits had more life to them. I adore the creativeness in the menu screen and collections screen. Through that, I can see the love put into this game. I'd like to see more games like this. Edit: I want to add that controls and objectives can be quite confusing at times, but the developer has been making consistent effort to improve QOL in that regard.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Yes, BUTThe game is fun. It's cute. It's engaging. It's also got bugs and doesn't explain a lot of things, so you'll want to look up guides/tips/wikia to learn what you need to know. I wouldn't pay full price for this, but I'm happy that I did buy it and I anticipate a lot of hours of fun to come.And checking the guides.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much charm to it, I love it. Whether you just like chill games and farming sims or if you're a fan of Ghibliesque type things, this game is for you. One thing that that is throwing me for a bit of a loop at the moment is simply how many things you can pick up without it being obvious to notice, but that also sort of adds to the charm so it's probably just a me thing.I'm also unsure if the bathhouse has a time that it will run to at the max, maybe it simply stays open as long as you want it to? You do get exhausted after spending too many hours up. I sort of wish there was a few more tutorials you could read in the beginning ( which is funny because I usually want less ). Such as, I had to go in the control menu to find out that I could use items with the run button. There would have been a perfect opportunity for Wonyan to explain that to me for sweeping the bathhouse. I figured as I upgraded it, then it would get more clean but you actually have to clean it with the broom and duster in the kitchen. Then I could apply it to fishing and bug catching myself but it took longer than I would have liked to get there, haha. ( I possibly just missed a text box? but I think I would have remembered that. ) My least favorite thing so far is the karaoke game. There are too many colors in the background and I can't focus on the directions. I think either make a complicated looking layout and make the songs easier, or make it simpler and make the songs harder. But my brain can't correlate the flying objects to certain buttons and the octopus is too easy to miss. The songs are super difficult so I don't think I'll ever get a perfect. And having to pay to play a song each time instead of paying a larger fee for a session of however many you want will hinder my desire to even try unfortunately. That and I get a headache from looking at that screen and the songs feeling like full length songs. ( which is sad because it actually seems based on rhythm unlike some mini games I've played recently and it seems like it would be fun! )I'll update this if anything changes how I feel about the game though!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are frustratingCentral gameplay loop is quite boringIn-game improvements must be purchased, time wasted on, and then understood.  The player is free to make as many mistakes as they want.  This leads to a lot of frustration waiting around for... maybe something good maybe something badObtuse goals, in-game map is clearly from an earlier build (shows incorrect information frequently), in-game clippy-esque character will literally respond "what?" if you ask too many questionson top of all these problems, it is *riddled* with bugs, ranging from "oops I accidentally deleted an important item better buy a new one.... next week when the shop keeper is home" all the way to "can I ... move now?  can I interact at all with this game?"Save your money, just get an exotic stardew valley mod.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but with the understanding that this game still has areas that could use improvement in my opinion.The Positive:-Running the bathhouse is extremely fun and engaging. I love running around serving all the different spirits. There's always something to do, even when you hire helpers (especially once you have a bunch of upgrades and thus introduce other things to take care of). I also love having to take into account what each spirit type is and experimenting to find out which spirits like sitting next to each other.-Wonyan's personality is super fun and very lively. The personalities of the spirits in their quests are also engaging. To some extent I would say the same for the NPCs (although I will go more in depth as to why I don't think the NPCs are quite as lively in the negative section).-Some people think the art style is ugly, but I actually like it for the most part (although the style of your avatar is a bit of an acquired taste in my opinion). I particularly love how the bathhouse looks in the game, and I also love how the house the player lives in looks a little like the house in My Neighbor Totoro.-I thought that the quest to introduce yourself to the NPCs was super adorable with [SPOILERS] having a dog lead you around. Usually you just have to run around and hope you run into NPCs. I loved having a dog companion sniff out the person you were looking for and lead the way. It saves the player lots of time while also giving you a furry friend to gush over!-I've never played the old fishing minigame, but I like the new fishing game well enough. It's simple, but I find that it still provides its own challenge.-The OST is very nice! I have some songs I prefer more than others but overall it's a great soundtrack. I also love that the bathhouse music changes from season to season (although my favorite track for the bathhouse is the spring one). I'm just to games never changing the interior music for certain places so I just thought that was a fun detail.-I like the fact that you can invite NPCs out to do things. It makes friendships with them feel a little more dynamic, especially because the friendship system in this game is rather simplistic. Being able to invite NPCs that you like out to do certain hobbies makes me feel like I'm hanging out with a friend, which just helps me to feel closer to those NPCs.-A lot of people have mentioned bugs in the game that have been game breaking or otherwise inconvenient. I was fortunate to not really run into any that I am aware of. I've seen that the devs have been working hard to patch these out so I believe some of the worst bugs are no longer present in the game!The Negative:-Bug catching feels almost impossible. I'm not exactly sure why I've found it so difficult in this game compared to other games where bug catching is an option, but I rarely have luck catching bugs in this game. I think it's because the bug catching animation takes too long, to where by the time it finishes, bugs have moved outside of your range most of the time. Because of this, I just don't like going out to catch bugs because there's no way to sneak up on them, and no way to really help your chances besides just getting really lucky.-Generally speaking, I don't find a lot of activities outside of running the bathhouse engaging. Sure, I can fish (I'm definitely not catching bugs), but there's not really anything I can do with the majority of the fish I catch. There's no clear place to sell the fish (I've heard there's a spot where you can do it, but even then that location is open very rarely and you don't get much money from it). Most of the fish you catch can't be used for any recipes. The fish that can be used for recipes I almost never catch. There's minigames, sure, but they aren't exactly core mechanics that I'm looking to use during my play time all the time. Mainly I like using them to build friendship with NPCs, but otherwise I don't usually like to engage with them. You could argue I could spend more time befriending NPCs, but that leads me to my next point.-The spirit quests range from tedious to just super frustrating. I acknowledge that the dev team has been working to streamline this process with having Wonyan and other NPCs give you hints. However, I've found that hints range in helpfulness. Sometimes, the hints tell me information that I already know but don't really give me more clues to help narrow down what I need to do for a certain quest. It doesn't help that sometimes Wonyan won't even recognize I have a certain quest active even though certain events in the quest have started, so I can't ask for hints if I get stuck. I've found myself frequently looking up information on certain quests, just because some quests are really difficult to know what to do. This was one of the main aspects that I would use to occupy my time outside of the bathhouse, but lately I've been running into some quests that have really frustrated me (looking at you Clarence) and I just lost all my motivation and steam to continue with that. This meant I was frequently sleeping through days and free time just so I could go back to running the bathhouse.The Neutral:-The NPCs do have distinct personalities and I like them, but I wish they had more dialogue and just a bit more life. I've found myself quickly running into the same dialogues all the time. Normally I wouldn't take as much of an issue with this, as in most games in the genre you usually have revamped dialogues for each season. However, from what I've seen the dialogues don't change all that much from season to season, which makes me seek out the NPCs less often.-I like the cooking system to some extent, but I do feel like the process is a little tedious. Having a separate menu to deposit items into your desired cooking utensil feels a little redundant when I then have to go into a different menu to start the cooking process. I also think that it would be easier to select a recipe from your recipe book that would automatically put the necessary ingredients into the cooking utensil you are interacting with. It's a small thing but I think it would make a world of difference.From my post it may sound like I don't like this game, but truly enjoy it a lot! I adored playing this and streaming it to my friends! However, I feel that while the core mechanics of this game are strong, there's some areas that could be improved when it comes to everything surrounding the bathhouse mechanic. I especially hope to see improvements when it comes to bug catching, so that it might be a little easier for players to do. I also would love to see more uses for a lot of the bugs and fish outside of donating them to the shrines (after all, there's a lot more bugs and fish than are actually required by the shrines).As is, though, I think the game is a lot of fun and I think it's worth the price point!

_childDocuments_.review: Clocked 7 hours since it's release yesterday. I love it, it's everything I wanted it to be. There's also a few challenging parts that I normally would have looked up to get through but it's too new for that! I did eventually make it through them and it felt rewarding! _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic management + life sim hybrid that doesn’t fall victim to the “jack of all trades, master of none” type gameplay and instead fleshes out considerable thought to all of the different ideas the game has. This game PACKS content and is surely one to be played over many, many hours. The more you play, the more you’ll pick up on just how much freedom this game allows you to have to go about strategizing your bath house business, to potentially stealing neighbor’s plants because you can pick up just about anything. The pacing is fantastic in teaching you how to go about the management mechanics. It feels very relaxed but with obvious signs that later on, you can crank up the micromanagement—however, it again allows freedom to its players in just how much “management” you want to do. Whether you want to continue playing things slow and casual, or you want to min-max coin efficiency, you’ll find the gameplay rewarding however you go about choosing to play it. Fantastic soundtrack. The graphics grew on me within an hour or so and I really like the art style now. The writing is great, funny in a way that isn’t over the top or trying too hard, and playing just feels fun. After so many recent, half-finished and disappointing game releases that have bloated the “cozy game” tag, SpiritTea is a fantastic addition to the simulation genre that ends this year on a high note.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. I have encountered one game-breaking bug which is now fixed, and a few times have had weird layering of music. Otherwise, the game works well.I think the game would benefit from having a place where you can mark down what season you have deduced a spirit to belong to, if you haven't yet found their spirit tome. Also, maybe an easier way to view the spirits without having to key across to each one individually, which makes it time consuming to view while you're running the bathhouse.The Cheese Master, love your work!

_childDocuments_.review: If you recommend the game to be played using a controller, add support for PlayStation controllers.I'm confused by this game. The font is kinda rough around the edges that is not pleasing to my eye; there's no option to change font type. I don't see any options to skip cut scenes. The customising space option is strange to me; I can pick up some objects but for others, I need to use a specific menu for it? I really don't like being unable to save outside of one specific spot- really difficult for someone who has tech issues or has to attend to other matters quickly (like a baby waking from her nap). The controls feel very strange- the use of "run" and "use item" as the same button is confusing. I don't like that I can't change WASD to the Arrows because they're more comfortable for me.
