_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute poetic kind of masterpiece when it comes to "Stardew valley" like design. The characters in the game feel very much alive- especially your feline companion, and the dialog is frequently quite hilarious, and occasionally touching or deeply mysterious. It does know how to get you intrigued. It's also refreshing to NOT have one of these be just another farming sim, the main gameplay loop feels refreshingly new because of that, and it's changes that come over the course of the game are unpredictable- making for a much more interesting journey.Some of the quests and what you need to do for side activities is a bit obtuse, though you can get some useful hints from your cat friend. Still, all else fails, there's already a very helpful wiki waiting for you.Totally recommend this title! It's quite slow paced, so if you enjoy things like that, kick back, relax, maybe listen to your favorite show in the background, and be prepared to have a very interesting time.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game with a high level of detail for the environment, characters, and backgrounds. Music is really nice too. It's basically a bathhouse management sim for spirits, and you get more spirits by completing quests for neighbors and you get more help for your bathhouse by maxing out friendship with neighbors.The core gameplay loop of managing the bathhouse is nice, and there's a lot of different minigames and objects to play around and interact with. Each neighbor has their own quest tied to them and you unlock a new spirit that can then visit your bathhouse and help you make more money. The more spirits you have, the more you progress with the overall plot, which is to finish writing a book about your experiences. There's only a few things that are a bit of a gripe for me. First of all, even though you get hints for how to complete some of the quests, sometimes those hints are still too vague for me to understand how to complete, and I still have to check online for the answer. Sometimes, quest events happen only once a week, and if you miss those, then you have to wait a whole week again or reload the save to try and catch it for the next time. There are times when an event will happen "in the middle of the night" but does not tell you what time it is, whether 1am or 4am, for example.Finally, I find it strange that so few buttons are used for the various menu items. Y opens your bag, but in that menu you can then press X to switch to a journal and progress completion tab, and then press Y again to close it. Perhaps either of the trigger buttons or other bumper could also be used instead?Overall, I find this game does scratch that farming itch in the terms of the consistent routine, slow progression through upgrading the bathhouse, communication with other villagers, and item gathering aspects. I enjoy playing it in my downtime. And it works perfectly on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: A little gem of a cozy game where you feel that it was made with a lot of love. I really enjoyed my playthrough. Is it perfect? No. Is it a lot of fun to play? Yes!The game doesn't always hold your hand which was kind of refreshing actually.e.g. digging for treasure is a mini-game where some maps are quite explicit showing a big "X" while others just give a general idea of the area where you should look. It didn't feel unfair to me though, just don't expect to find every treasure during your first trip. (unless you use the wiki)I did not encounter any game breaking bugs myself (90 hours played) but there are still some fixes to be done and I am looking forward to see future updates. Speaking of which: Updates are being pushed out quite quickly and the Developer is highly responsive as well - much more than I would have expected.Definitely worth a look!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on the edge about this game. The setting is nice, but the implementation is such a mixed bag: inconvenient inventory (sorting? no, never heard of it), fishing on the level of Stardew Valley without mods (fish that jumps every 5 seconds, and half the time into the damn seaweed!), grind to catch insects (leave area, enter area, leave area, rinse, repeat), grind minifigs (I guess it's just a money sink actually :)), ...  Cooking and elixirs are practically useless: you are already swimming in moolags, and the ingredients are difficult to get (some - randomly from the store, some - randomly found in the world, and some - grown from seeds that squirrels may drop). Plus a bunch bugs: twice I had to patch the game twice to fix random glitches. In general, it seems that to the simulator of something from the times of 90s - early 00s they added a village sim, and in the end it turned out to be something strange. Yes, Graveyard Keeper can also be called so, but there everything is glued together by a single and high-quality plot.Let's assume that I was just unlucky to come across both bugs, and those who will play now from scratch will not encounter them. And maybe the rest of the bugs will eventually fix the developer, and make cooking more convenient. But for now, that's what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Having had the chance to experience the demo, this game has only heightened my anticipation for it's full release. This game,  where charm meets captivating storytelling and beautifully crafted design. This delightful life-sim, reminiscent of Stardew Valley with its own unique flair, offers vibrant characters, nostalgic landscapes, and and immersive narrative that feels like Spirited Away and Natsume Yujinchou.The game's meticulous design, from lively character sprites to seamless audio, creates an irresistible atmosphere. While it strikes a perfect balance between satisfying gameplay and progression, one minor issue for me so far is the challenging fishing mechanics with a controller slightly detract from the experience. (but it could just be me since I'm not very good with any fishing controls like in Stardew Valley)Yet, the game remains a mesmerizing adventure, offering a delightful mix of magic and progress. Despite its flaws, it's a game that effortlessly pulls players in, inviting them to lose themselves in its captivating world.

_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Charming, and simultaneously down to earth and whimsical.  Theres lots to do such as genre staples like bug catching but also minigames for many different activities with the townsfolk, and without spoiling anything theres more than meets the eye too.  Spirittea is a refreshing take on the slice of life town sim, you can play at your own pace yet still challenge yourself if you so choose.  Not to mention being set in the japanese country side means theres lots of cool things to see, and the music really sets the mood.  whether its pleasant and calm running around talking to everyone or happy and upbeat in the bathhouse that would fit perfectly for a cleaning montage.  I will say the run button being the same as the held item action button can be confusing at times tho.  TLDR : Filled my house with frogs 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited to play this game and then... So disappointed. The premise is great, but actual gameplay is so grindy. It felt more like a mobile cooking game than a story-rich sim. The characters are shallow (including your own character), there is little time or ability to explore the world, just constantconstantconstant tasks. I was hoping there would be a bit more Stardew Valley feel, so if you are looking for that, be aware that this isn't it.Edit (SPOILERS Below):I went back to try this again and...after 30 hours of gameplay there really isn't much to show.I finished the book, but why? Nothing happens, nothing changes, no $$, no conversations about it with any of the NPCs, just some rude, resentful, ill-mannered comments from ghost cat.Maps for treasure and elixirs are really expensive and weird and need online videos just to figure a lot of them out (I am usually pretty good at these in most games, but like much else in this game, it isn't intuitive or user-friendly. After getting slammed with an overabundance of directions your first two days, much of the game is just "figure it out. Somehow.").The bug catching--ughughugh--Hate. It seems set up to make players fail. Some bugs are exceedingly easy, but others you can't even see unless you literally trip over them, then there isn't time to 1. Open your backpack 2. select the net 3. close the backpack 4. line up with the bug well enough to catch them. It's such a pain that I just stopped bug catching. Truly awful and definitely not Accessible for a lot of people with disabilities. Other games that have made bug catching challenging, but fun--Coral Island, Animal Crossing--would love some mechanics that make sense here.The fishing is okay once you understand what they want.Gaining friendship points is also a pain, and the activities are just not fun. What if you don't drink? Why would you want to play a drinking game? And why do you want to be friends with these one-dimensional people anyway? Why do you have to cook your own food at the restaurant instead of just going out for a meal? Taking a walk? Playing a video game? Maybe a movie theater or live theater in town could provide some activity to gain friendship.The "Your Spirituality has increased" message along with the "Midnight" message both interrupt gameplay and take you completely out of the experience. There are many ways to denote a new level without stopping the whole gameplay (a glow with a chime, something less intrusive anyway).The lighting is so, so bad. Yes, it is night and night is dark. That said,, I should be able to see what my character is doing on the screen.The cat spirit is both mean and annoying, both as a character and as something that gets in the way in the bathhouse. There is no reason for them to be there unless you are actively pursuing a spirit. They don't give hints or reminders about current missions, and I literally accidentally click on them while trying to grab something in the bathhouse at least 4-5 times/day., only for them to say, "What?" or "Nyat".ALSO there is a bug on the school horror game with Yumi where I can go in, but can't move at all or exit out of the minigame. I checked my controller, the connection, everything, and finally had to just close it and lost a whole (very busy) day.

_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a lot of potential, but just can't recommend it in its current state.My complaints are largely similar to many people's - the gameplay is clunky and there's virtually no quality of life mechanics. Items don't stack. Usable items blend in perfectly to the background - I spent a good while wondering when I was going to unlock the tools to clean the bathhouse, and I didn't even know I could pick fruit until I did it on accident. And, on that note, picking things up - and dropping things - on accident is way too easy. When I first started the game, I had to restart the day because when I went to go get that first tea leaf sample, I must have accidentally dropped it, didn't realize it until I was back at my house since there was no indicator i'd done so, and couldn't find it again.The maps are confusing. The inability to review gameplay tips is frustrating. The text is hard on the eyes. It's annoying to only be able to run around in spirit vision for a little while, desperately searching for dig spots, and then having to go all the way home to make tea with the clunky item use mechanics and then do it all over again. The bathhouse is strangely paced and I don't feel like anything i'm doing aside from cleaning towels is actually *accomplishing* anything. God help you if you seat bad guests next to each other, because they spend *so long* sitting in the bath, and you can do nothing about it. I can't seem to re-seat bathhouse guests, and have seen no indication of otherwise.And, one complaint I *haven't* seen, which is maybe the biggest one for me - in what i can only assume is an effort to take pressure off the players, to make the game Cozier™, there's very little structure in the game. When you're servicing spirits, they'll sit there and wait for you to take them to the bath for all of eternity. You can sleep and wake up whenever you like.  But, instead of taking pressure off, all this really seems to do is remove any sense of stakes - and thus, any sense of accomplishment - or make it easy for the days to blend together and make you lose your sense of time.I was genuinely surprised to find out this game was not an early access title. I hope updates continue for it - it has a lot of potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to Spirittea and can't help but feel a little let down. There's a lot of potential here and it could be an amazing game if they implemented more quality of life features. Pros:- The cat spirit is mean and bullies me--like my irl cat.  - You can pet the cats and dogs!- The socialization mini-games, like Korean barbecue and karaoke, are very creative- The main quest of finding spirits for your bathroom is engaging- Bathhouse management is straightforward and funCons:- Needs an in-game help menu, so you can look up mechanics that you've forgotten- Needs more hand-holding. They don't tell you a lot of important stuff, like where/how to plant your seedbags or how to scrub your spirits. I had to look it up online- Very little character customization. This isn't gamebreaking, but I wanna look cute if I have to look at my character all the time- Controls are so clunky. I play on keyboard and the keybinds are so unintuitive. Why would you not include mouse buttons? Gameplay would be smoother if I can just move and mouse and click on things, instead of needing to remember which key is "interact" and which key opens my backpack - UI needs more work. There’s no “interact” key that hovers over items and I think it’d vastly improve gameplay if you could see what is background and what is an interactable object - Map needs place names. As a new player, I get confused about which place is which. - The fishing minigame is ridiculously difficult- You need to spam the "interact" button for 30+ seconds for the cooking minigame, which is tiring and unnecessary.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't finished. I want to start by saying that. There are many places where you'll wish there was more flesh on the bones - hopefully, all of this is yet to come. But this game is made with love, and it shines through in every single way - from the carefully designed characters, to the humour, to the emotions. It's not easy and will not hold your hand, but it's not so hard you'll end up hating it (you may end up with the wiki constantly open, though)! It's a Stardew-alike, but it's not a clone. It feels like its own beast, and I for one eagerly await future updates to give this complete skeleton its flesh and feathers.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. The characters are quirky but down to earth, each NPC's problems are a fun and unique little side quest that are actually part of the main storyline (so it feels episodic instead of one looooooong main quest with little diversions to keep you engaged (*side eyes some more "popular" AAA games*)), and the game has you  feel like you're continually making progress through progress bars for relationships, quick visuals on the continue game screen, and even an in-game pamphlet that will let you know where you're at with your collectibles.As a few other reviewers have noted, Spirittea's main area of less than amazingness is it's controls. By the love of each seasonal king spirit, play this with a controller. Especially on the fishing minigame. The other three minigames can each be passibly played on M+K, but the fishing game is a nightmare with WASD, as it utilizes eight compass points around a circular node and trying to get keys to accurately replicate NW, NE, SW, and SE without releasing one key later than the others (and thus ending up with N,W, E, or S) is a frustrating experience. This game could really do with some key remaping.Speaking of, you really only use WASD, shift, and E for most in-game actions (with things like your map mapped to the obligatory M key), with no mouse at all. Not game-breaking, but I really do wish I had something to do with my right hand (MIND OUT OF THE GUTTER) while playing this.If anyone is wondering why there are a few friend-activities that are greyed out, the drinking minigame can only be done while Leigh is at his stall  (after dark! no day drinking!), and the hot springs don't open until you repair the bridge north of town.I'll say this, too, though it's more about the community than the game: If you want walkthroughs and need guides, go to the official discord, and not the steam guides. With the exception of an incredibly helpful seasonal spirit map, there's basically nothing for steam community posted guides. I hope this changes at some point (I guide for how rare all the collectibles are would be super nice!), but for now, it's sadly lacking.I just wish I could figure out how/when the game saves cause I've lost a few in-game days by closing the game when I THOUGHT it saved (when you sleep), but I seem to be mistaken?8/10 stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: If you are into comfy games then this is one to definitely put in your library. What a chill game to do after work, during a lazy day, or just need something that is fun not time sensitive and has a fun art style. There are a few things I found a bit aggravating though they are more user error I think so I won't go into into detail unless later issues arise. Safe to say while Stardew is still my favorite lazy day game to play I think this will become a favorite as well and may even stand equal to stardew in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and relaxing management sim, it was exactly what I was looking for. I really like the bathhouse game play and management. While the bathhouse is closed for upgrades there isn't much to do to fill the days once you've found most of the spirits so additional things to do would be nice, but it's not too bad since you can always sleep early to skip the day. The game is very enjoyable and worth a try if you like management/business sims! The dev team is very responsive to bugs and updates as well :) I'm super excited to see what new content they will be adding in 2024 and am so glad they plan to keep working on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Generally, if you like this genre of game -- move to some random village, get to know the town, forage and harvest, etc.-- you'll enjoy this game.If you are on the fence, the cons are more in line with quality and polish. There are bugs and glitches that require you to exit the game and restart from your last sleep-to-save point. The other aspect of quality in the UX of things. It's pretty easy to lose track of items (at least on the steam deck) because 1. picking up and dropping is the same button and because when you fish, dig, or otherwise use an item, it may automatically drops the item so you can pick up the found item and 2. there is no mechanism to recover critical items that you may discover early.A different kind of problem is navigation. So take the collection page for treasure maps. There *is* an order to them but you can't tell at first. Instead, it feels like madness trying to keep track and scroll through. I really like the visual attempt for delight in how it is presented, but it falls short of any sort of usability bar. The minigames have similar kind of ux problems but all of these things are ultimately doable.I still enjoyed the game and played it long enough to feel like I got my money's worth. I peeked into the discord and it seems like the devs are pretty responsive and are putting love into the game. That's why I recommend it overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Currently, and sadly, no.While they're smashing bugs as fast as they can, my issue is actually mechanics and accessibility:-There is no real keyboard+mouse support.-Every mechanic is 'hold the button down forever' option for controls.-Why is there no way to turn off the spinning background and constantly moving graphics?Backed this on Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoy this game. Chill, laid-back, collecting the spirits is fun.As some other reviewers have mentioned, it doesn't really explain some things which would be nice to have explained. For instance, the only way I knew how to plant seeds, or that they were even used for something, was by reading it in their discord server.And, as of writing this,  the game is quite buggy. Not enough to ruin my enjoyment of the game, though. But I also haven't had it crash on me after a full day of running the bathhouse.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed the game a lot so far, but I also think it could use some adjustments in certain areas. It's a nice cozy game with a pleasant soundtrack and enjoyable tasks. I love the spirit interactions, and the villagers feel like they all have unique personalities. There's a nice balance between building friendships, working in the bathhouse, and fun side activities.Some things that I think could use adjusting:- The "run" button is also the same as the "use item" button for most items, so you can't run while holding most things. This makes bug catching particularly tricky cause some of them are very fast. Also, holding left shift constantly gets tiring for your hand after a while. - The karaoke video game is overly complicated. Having to press the "C" key in addition to WASD is too much considering the notes don't feel like they coincide with the music. This makes the mini game a chore rather than an enjoyable way to build friendship with people in the village.- Time doesn't pause when your inventory is open, and items in your inventory don't stack. The not stacking is annoying since you have a pretty small inventory.Overall takeaway: I think it's a fun game with good bones, but I think it needs a few adjustments to make it more user friendly and to make it feel more polished. I think it's a good game worth playing if you like cozy games.

_childDocuments_.review: i have played about 4 hours, so far i like it but it does have its mix of pros and cons for me.pros: the music is great, the ambient sounds are basically perfect, the design of the environment is very nice (this being like nature, the buildings, lighting, and the backgrounds) the character portraits  are very good and the sprites of the spirits are very good and i love the studio ghibli inspiration is awesome.cons: the townsfolk sprites are not as detailed as they could be in my opinion, the beginning options for customisation are a bit limiting and disappointing (specifically not enough hair styles, not enough for clothing options/colors) and from my experience the towns folk interactions have been a small bit dry. but overall id say its pretty good and id recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: You REALLY can feel the love put into this game. I've personally held off on the demo so I could experience this game for the first time. The music speaks to me the most amongst many other things as I play! The game really makes you feel like you're *there* yourself. Every part of it is handcrafted to be as immersive as possible even in a Stardew Valley-esque format. There's so much detail put into the game, down to hearing the blacksmith working on the anvil even outside of the shop.Let's not forget our favorite spirit cat. Let's just say... it's the little things that happen that really elicit that chuckle.I've been eyeballing this game for two years now, and I have to say, it's worth the wait!Also. The flute is the only item you should be running around with :^)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: The world of Spirittea is such a relaxing place to be and I love everything about it, from the welcoming people who live there to the packed wildlife and the numerous mysteries to explore. Spirittea is a masterclass in what makes a game world somewhere you don't want to leave. The story its satisfying whilst not shackling you to do something right this moment and leaving enough freedom for you to make the story yours - whether that means going fishing with one of the villagers, eating some delicious BBQ or a very profitable shift at the bath house - you'll enjoy all this and much more in Spirittea.TLDR: Spirittea is a very cosy game filled with that "just one more" feeling and a charming world where you'll enjoy every minute spent. Get it now and thank me later
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played a couple of hours of this game, but I see a lot of potential for it. The writing is cute, I enjoy the art style, and I like the overall game play.That being said there are a few things which need to be fixed/adjusted. The first are the mini games, especially the fishing mini game which is nearly impossible with a controller. You have to aim the hook and press B, only you have to point the joy stick the opposite direction of where you would think you should point making it absolutely no fun and unbearable to do. I recommend either changing the mechanic for this mini game or allowing an 'easy mode' for these mini games. Especially for those of us who use controllers. The game overall is simple, relaxing, and stress free so including these stressful and overly difficult mini games makes no sense to me.Additionally, the game allows you to buy more than you can fit in your inventory but just leaves it on the ground. I( did not notice this and ended up dropping things off at home and buying a second shovel because I thought the game glitched. I also could not sell back anything to the shop owner so I essentially lost money in game for this. Not allowing purchases when your backpack is full would be the best solution.I enjoy the game, but I hope the devs work on adjusting some of the issues in the game play. Still for the price the game is well worth it and definitely worth keeping an eye on.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with great characters, engaging gameplay, challenging minigames, and a well rounded story. The only problem as of writing this is that it seems prematurely released, and still has a lot of game breaking bugs that need ironed out. Definitely worth picking up, but maybe give it a few more patches first.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a mixed review because I did enjoy the beginning and it's not terrible. My biggest problem is the mini games. There's a lot of them and most aren't fun, but they're required to befriend villagers and get all the spirits. Villagers only have two activities that they're willing to do, so you can't even pick a mini game you like. The drinking mini game wont even load for me half of the time. You get money by making spirits happy while in your bath house. You make them happy by feeding them and sitting them next to other spirits types they like. However, the only way to figure out what they like is doing treasure hunts. You get maps slowly and you probably wont unlock info on a spirit you currently have. This feels like information you should get as you unlock spirits.Also, the shop rotates out items everyday so you could be waiting days to be able to buy quests items or ingredients to make food.

However, I got some grindy experience at the end, where I just need to wait for 2 more spirits to appear, but it hasn't spoiled anything. Still 10\10 though. Spirits designs are very cool, Wonyan's interractions are my most fav. The dev is very responsive here and even helped me with the Demo issue.

_childDocuments_.review: i HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone who was a fan of the following: stardew valley, roots of pacha, travellers rest, sun haven- and really any life sim with farming/cooking aspects and a great questline. i would argue that the developers of this game have put a lot more effort into the personality of the NPCs, dialogue, and questline than most other games ive played. i really like that this game has a bit of customization, tons of decor options in the store, and several shops to go to. the design of the characters & spirits, minigames, differing hobbies of the NPCs has really elevated the gameplay. i truly hold this game close to my heart. i am emotionally attached, im really hoping romancing NPCs comes in the future! i will say that as of late january, this game is basically impossible to play without looking up online guides or using reddit (which has been my bff for this game). the quests are really time sensitive, and some of tem have to be completed before others in order for the other quests to spawn correctly- in my opinion it makes the game more challenging and requires the use of some critical thinking and deductive reasoning to play! there are several nods of cultural signifigance throughout the playthrough of the game, and theres already a ton to unlock. this is not a game you will get bored of halfway through the storyline. it seems simple, but there is a bunch of stuff hiding right underneath your nose!my last point is that the developers are phenomenal!! they have listened carefully to the feedback of the players and, get this: actually implemented a good chunk of it into the game!!! i love following games through pre-release until they are completed. kudos to the developers. if you're on the fence- get the darn game, i promise you if you like the games i listed above, you will adore this game as much as i do.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer that I am a Kickstarter (99$) for this gameI have been following this game for quite some time and was super excited to see the game reach it's funding goals in the last week after some worrying. This game oozes indie charm made by someone who really feels for the game they developed. Easily on the same level of Stardew Valley with the game feel and overall just wholesome good chill fun. I've put more hours into this than my time shows with the demos and testing and have really enjoyed the game. Do not let the graphics full you, this is a robust game with many mechanics and customization just waiting for you. There's lots of gameplay elements in this that I can assure you that you've never encountered before. Give it a shot if you vibe with the trailer

_childDocuments_.review: Would still recommend as this lover of cozy games is having fun for the price, but with some big caveats and things that need to be improved. (disclaimer: I haven't checked the latest update yet and I won't be able to for a while, but it looks like the update mostly addresses bugs and not the criticism written here). The style is very very cute and the gameplay loop is fine, I enjoy running the bathhouse (though I wish there were some more things to do besides taking care of towels and wood and scrubbing guests).  Many of the villagers are charming (not all lol some are obnoxious from the get go and I have zero interest in talking to them more) and the dialogues are generally interesting. The quests so far are varied enough. However, this game needs serious improvement, especially in terms of explanation and tutorials. It literally took me a day to figure out  the right KEY to do something because it was never explained in game and it is not explained in the controls page. Some basic things are explained only once briefly and there's no way to go back and consult instructions. Some things are never explained: for example, the minigames. I only tried one so far and there was zero explanation on what to do and how to win. I'm okay with games not holding your hand too much, but this game errs in the opposite direction of not explaining anything. Also, fishing is downright IMPOSSIBLE, makes no sense and I just gave up on it already.  Overall it's a nice little game but still has a long way to go if it wants to get anywhere near Stardew level of awesome (I know, not fair to compare, but we all are anyway).(edited for grammar)
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it just recently and I already have 59.5 hours played. I really enjoy the music and the art. I also love how you basically choose makeup or no make up for your character avatar. No NPC has really used any gendered language (one character says dude a lot, but I think that would be the same if I had picked make up). There is a pretty steep learning curve for the controls, but I was ecstatic when I caught my first aggressive (ie. It likes to surprise you and vanish)  bug. There are a fair few game bugs to look out for, most of them do not break the game, but some of them can be frustrating. Be very careful not to loose key items (I just assume everything is a key item unless Its a rotating food stock lol) because they are as of now impossible to recover using the game mechanics. Fortunately, the dev seems responsive to help with fixes. There are so many cute things to find. This game immediately went in my favorites folder. I think it is worth the 20 dollars and I have been really enjoying it. I'd also check out the community resources for Spirittea on steam (look for a message form the dev for more things, no spoilers lol).

_childDocuments_.review: The developers nailed the atmosphere and environment design. The ambient sound without unnecessary music is great. The sprites look simple and basic at glance, but very expressive in game for some reason. I love it! Definitely a game with great potential! It could become one of the best if the developers keep adding content and improving on quality of life. A few  things I've noticed in my short play time.1. Please add more save points. I can not save in the middle of 'introduce yourself to everyone' quest.  I am not allowed to sleep to save at all.2. Can we make the dog follow the character during this quest?3. It is a small town with older or unmarried people, but surely a lot of children in school... Whose kids are those and how come we cannot even talk to them?I love the game and can't wait for more updates.The past a few updates are awesome! Ducks and new vendors are so cute!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: While I do love this game and how cute the characters are, there is a lot of bugs I've noticed in the game. It's very fun and honestly addicting but I can't recommend it due to how incomplete it feels sometimes. A lot of the characters repeat the same lines each time they're talked to and only serve as much as workers once befriended and nothing else. There's not much story when it comes to character or spirit interaction, most is vague and leaves the game feeling kind of empty. I was pretty disappointed when I first found out that there's not many options beyond spending money on characters to befriend them through certain minigames or just bug catching/fishing. I sort of wish there were more variations and life given to the characters beyond their usefulness in a work aspect.A lot of the minigames and game mechanics aren't explained and are just left up to the person to try and figure it out. As much as I do love the variety of minigames, things like fishing or even finding how to use seeds were troublesome. Even now, I still am having trouble with figuring out how to properly handle the fishing minigame. I've been avoiding fishing or bug catching due to how unbalanced the minigames seem to be when it comes to keyboard players.It is fun, but some of the mechanics and features get slightly irritating over time. It is a sweet slow game and I honestly would love to see this game develop more than where it currently stands.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: its clunky, repetitive, and simple. The minigames are. . . meh. The work cycle is mind-numbing which can be fine but after a bit gets boring. The art is fine (....aside from the sterotyping), the sound work is nice, and the maps are pretty well done. But it feels unfinished, more a beta than a polished game. At times it reminds me of Chulip, a quirky mystery game I enjoy highly--but the part of Chulip I enjoy was the characters, not the obtuse riddles. There's mystery, and then there's making the player randomly talk to every townperson for every quest in hopes the notebook has a clue. Its. . . not well play-tested? Granted, even AAA titles can struggle with obtuse puzzles, but I've played games like Ace Attorney and had to rely on wikis far less often.

_childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm, I bought it right after it launched and I'll admit it was a little rough, after a week the developers came back with a few bug fixes and patches that have smoothed out the game play and really showed they were listening to the communities issues. I can't give enough praise to developers that engage with their community.The game itself is a management sim more than anything, you will run a spa for spirits, you will earn money and upgrade the spa to provide the spirits with a better time. You'll be given somewhat vague but mostly followable instructions on how to solve issues for the people around town, which are caused by spirits, who will visit your spa once they've been solved.There are a lot of minigames that help you build relationships with the townsfolks (, with recent updates, none of the games are 'hard' and karaoke's difficulty is trivial now), collectibles in the form of fish, bugs, and figurines from gacha capsules. Lots of stuff to do other than the spa.At the end of the day, I glad I picked this game up.Edit: Its so good I got a copy for my wife, she can't stop playing, so much so she bought a copy for the Switch too. So between the two of us we own three copies, that's how good it is.

The way the different objectives and how you can use your spirit-seeking experiences to write a book is super interesting. I enjoy the atmosphere, the music, the absolute bonkers and greedy cat spirit that gives you tip

_childDocuments_.review: While I really, really wanted to like this game-- I can't recommend a game set in Japan that gets everything wrong. The cars drive on the wrong side of the road, people's names don't make sense, there's a huge Buddha statue turning its back to the village in the middle of a shinto temple, and you keep your shoes inside the house. I find this lack of accuracy really disrespectful, both to Japanese culture and to non-Japanese players who think they are playing a "Japanese" game. Also, the graphics are really busy, which hurt my eyes a little, and the map has the buildings dancing to its music, which makes it quite hard to read.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game on my steamdeck only and controllwise everything worked really great! :)I think this game is sometimes really confusing since it explaines some parts really detailed and other parts not at all. So I think being a bit advanced in this type of games is a must. But also beeing used to games like stardew valley might be a trap, since some mechanics work totally different. (I really was wondering where to get wood and was waiting to buy a axe, but there is none :D I mean it is kind of obvious how to get wood thinking about it but yeas, my stardew brain couldn't do it haha.)The story and the characters are a real blast. Really there is such a great humor and love to detail in the character design and also int he story. Like I had a ghost quest where my heart nearly broke since I really wanted to solve it, and the reward was reasonable high for it, wich took me by surprice. But thats what I love. You will never know when Whonyan will slay with his comments about any character in the game. As I finished my book and left the town I was near tears, I really fell in love with thies world, the town, the characters, the ghosts... just everything. (But dont worry, you can continue playing after finishing the book, since there are more ghosts, bugs, fishes, treasures... to find).But I also have a really hard time catching bugs,fishing is okay for me, it is also so nice to do it with my friends in the town. :) But really, I guess I will never have all the bugs! :D I also think some of the ghost quests are really hard, like it is not getting harder if you progress, I think some of the early ghost quests were harder than the ones after, but this also makes it surprising and fun since no quest is the same.I think this is a great game, but dont expect a stardew valley clone, this game (luckily) is far away from that. It is a lovely game and also the translation in german is really good (especially compared to the sun haven translation... if you know you know.).
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game. I believed it was about tea making, my fault for not reading the description of the game.Easy controls and flexible gameplay. You can be a social butterfly or the grumpy proprietor of a bathhouse for spirits. The NPCs have an indispensable role for game progress - unlike other games where you can just go about your business without any NPC interaction. The stamina gauge is almost as harsh as the Harvest Moon Winds of Anthos where even a step costs stamina but can be supplemented by food and rest. And speaking of rest, you can choose how long you would sleep. Very nice. I can be up working at any time of the day and night.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is really one of the best cozy games I've played since Stardew Valley. Based on the graphics, number of reviews, small size of the community, and general lack of public fanfare r/t this game I've heard, I bought it on sale expecting it to be something I could play for a few hours before I got bored. Now, I really really look forward to playing this game. While it's small and some things are a bit limited, this game has a really charming atmosphere, tight art direction, and a cast of characters who are strangely compelling given their limited dialogue and lack of events. The minigames are absolutely godawful but it does nothing to take away from the atmosphere and compelling environment. There are a lot of these "cozy" games about in the wake of Stardew Valley that lack a heart and soul--this isn't one of them. This game is adorable and handcrafted. A real treat.I'm 19 hours of playtime in and still have quite a lot to discover -- and many more chapters to write.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit tea is a game I love and I’m glad to have supported on Kickstarter.Do you like the concept of farming games? The premise of existing in their worlds but you dislike how the farming mechanics control part of your day?Well in spirittea the bathhouse does not require such a commitment. You can focus your weekend on hanging out with the cast. And pick which days you want to work. Allowing much more choice in the in-game day to day.The spirits quests are humorous and memorable and will be the main thing you can occupy your time within the first year. My favourite being Onishi, I was stuck on them for awhile, and once you encounter them you'll know why that’s funny. You can take your time with most of them (others will feel more urgent) which I recommend doing as once fully completed the game feels finished. You will likely get the most out of the game in the first year and little into the second. This is a good amount of stuff to play through so do not let the fact the game should last one year discourage you.But, if you’re a completionist I’d suggest focusing on the bugs and fish as they change completely every season. Thus, if you miss one you must wait a year to try again. Which will feel tedious.AND ALSO you may want to consult guides in order to dig up the spirit elixirs as they are necessary for fully pleasing a lord spirit. Due to bad luck, I did not get them for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game when it first came out and played almost 6 hours before realizing that as charming and relaxing as the game -could- be, it just wasn't polished at that time enough for me to continue my playthrough. I am SO glad I gave the game a try again after some of the updates the dev has made. I've hit the same number of play hours in my 2nd playthrough and am double, if not triple, where I was the first time around thanks to quality of life updates and player guides online. The gameplay loop of the bathhouse is very relaxing while still giving enough activity/thought ordering to be a distraction and entertaining. The music is delightful (I totally listen to it at work), as are the characters as I'm slowly getting to know them. I was not the biggest fan of the sprite style at first, but the rest of the art quality makes up for it. Would highly recommend as a cozy, escape-the-day sort of game (just know that you might be looking up guides for obtaining spirits as some of the quests can be a little finicky). This game was made with lots of love and it shows.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This just doesn't quite hit the mark. The gameplay is overly simple but rather opaque leading to a steep learning curve with poor guidance. The visuals are nice enough but not a scratch on something like Stardew. The audio tracks are generally nice but there's an annoying beep whenever npcs talk that you can't get rid off without removing other ambient sounds that can impact gameplay (like the rooster crowing when you're out of power). Running the bathhouse is a little too simple but kind of relaxing, so I don't mind that as the main mechanic. The minigames are boring, and the karaoke is outright sickening. The quest to find the spirits is kind of fun but doesn't give enough of a clue half the time, so I ended up looking online anyway. Didn't finish it in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this on PC Gamepass for Xbox, however it was well behind on updates and quite glitchy and a little confusing at first. I really enjoyed the game regardless because it felt quite fresh. I much preferred this version as it had some QOL updates which made the quests less confusing.A lot like Stardew Valley but no farming involved so far. Running the bathhouse is quite fun. It feels like a puzzle game rather than a chore (you have to put certain spirits next to one another so that they are happy and pay more). I guess it can get a bit grindy in terms of washing towels and chopping logs. But I think it can be quite relaxing at the same time. I am not sure if this is already a thing, but unlocking a spirit who helps you wash towels / chop logs later in the game would be awesome and take away some of the grind.I love the characters, the townspeople and the spirits are a delight, the music is relaxing. I can really just hunker down and lose several hours in this game.Will edit my review if anything changes. So far, thumbs up! I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the type of cozy game I was looking for after a work week - nice artwork, pleasant soundtrack and no very demanding. So far getting my money's worth for sure!About 70 hours later, and still loving it! Like that townsfolk stores are not too long and come in different difficulties. Additionally, it is actually worth to do their stories. Just learned how treasure maps work - so that is a lot of new stuff to see through. Just finished my bathhouse and the monkeys are driving me a little bit insane. Trio of frogs are my absolute favorite spirits!!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super charming and adorable!While I'm not a big fan of how it controls at times, the game play and idea is unique and fun. It's like a mix of Stardew Valley and Spirited Away! There are a few things I would change when it comes to how the controls work, it was obviously designed with controllers in mind rather than keyboard and mouse, so playing keyboard is a little janky. It's really the only gripe I have with the game.I hope one day to see some content updates or maybe even a sequel to the game! Good job developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: There's been a boom in cozy games lately but Spirittea is the first one that really grabbed.With it's clear inspirations in japanese mythology, kami and yokai and some big Spirited Away vibes with it's bathhouse, Spirittea really drew me in.There's lots to do between managing and upgrading the old bathhouse to service all kinds of different spirits, each with gorgeous character designs and beautifully animated pixel art and hanging out with more than a dozen of the townsfolk.You've got your staple fishing and bug catching too, of course, but you can also dig up treasure with treasure maps and riddles, sing karaoke, go eat and drink with friends or visit the hotsprings together, most of which come in the form of minigames, which adds up for some nice variety.I especially like that your friends can actually help with catching bugs for example instead of just following you around.Like I already mentioned in regards to the spirits, the art is just really pretty, really elevating this little town and making it into a place you actually want to stay in.Add to that lots of cozy music for each of the seasons and different times of day and you really start enjyoing your time around the town.I highly recommend Spirittea to all that enjoy their cozy games and or like japanese mythology and Ghibli vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game not knowing what to expect, and honestly, I have been in love with it. I am a casual gamer, stardew/minecraft/dinkum/peglin type of girlie. Random little games too, and out of all of them, I would give this game an 9/10.I love all the characters, each little story along with them, the activities you get to do. It is a game I highly recommend, its super chill, and you can play at your own pace. You do need a controller to play, which, i honestly prefer because I can kick back and relax. I am still finding new things every time I play.People have been comparing it to Stardew, which, I have 500+ hours on, and I can understand why they would say it, but I find it to be very different, but equally as wholesome and cute as Stardew. There are so many little details in this game that I adore. I havent given it a 10/10 because I haven't gotten too far/still has a lot to do and explore, people to make friends with, things to collect; but overall, I have been a huge fan. I have even joined their discord!I personally found comfort in this game almost immediately, keeping me calm through a family member passing recently. I get so immersed in the game, it pulled me in and I appreciate that. So thank you to the creators! Super in love with this game! Single-player adventure, for the coziest of times, if you need comfort, gaining happiness from helping people and honestly a fun getaway. Please give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAME. I absolutely love the premise and it is just a joy to play! The quests are a little hard to figure out sometimes but I think that's what makes it just so so much fun! Anyways I am still at the beginning and can not wait to put in so many more hours.ALSO your cat companion is absolutely hilarious and likes to hit other spirits with its glowing coin! It is so so so sassy and you are bound to have a chuckle or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cozy game, with a bath house maintenance as it's biggest time consumer. Kinda like pappa's Pizzareia but less stress upfront. There's a ton of minigames, and the side quest of finding the ghosts is fun. I will say, it does lean more heavily toward finding and figuring out yourself, where everything is more clue-based than straight-up told to you. Not quite a puzzle, but almost.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: If you got bored of Stardew Valley, and feeling nostalgia for Spirited Away, then this is the game for you.!Set in a little cozy town, as a writer, where you happen upon the spirit world in your new residence, you quickly get wrapped up in helping the spirited that have long been lost. I’ve had this game for a couple of weeks and have already spent nearly 50 hours on it. This isn’t a game where you want to speedrun things not does it outright tell you what to do, or how to play, which adds to it’s charm an appeal. It’s a good thing to work through the game on your own and take it day at a time. Sure, things can be confusing, but if you find yourself getting fed up or frustrated, just pop on over to google or the discord for some helpful advice! Being as the game is very new, bugs are to be expected, and I haven’t had any big issues that break gameplay, so keep your expectations reasonable. All in all, I strongly recommend giving this game a try?Who doesn’t want to scrub spirits in exchange for coins?? 😁
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: amazing game, fairly new but still a wonderful game. The minigames are a big pain in my opinion the hardest being karaoke but its fine once you get the hang of it and can be really fun. the interactions with npcs in the town have been kinda dry so far but the best part of the game is the bathhouse and finding spirits whilst helping the townsfolk. the bathhouse is my favorite part! however it would be nice to have more immersive dialogue from the npcs. part of immersion is character customization there are barely any options for that you can however buy a wardrobe along with clothes at the shop but the face options and hair are very very limited. if you were hoping to find a lot of fun in dating npcs in this game i would say you would not get exactly what you paid for. wait for more updates before you purchase, but if you, like me are more interested in the bathhouse and spirits then get it now! its wonderful i am excited to see how this game grows. also if you buy this game make sure you have a controller
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a warm blanket. I really love the town and wish I could live there for real. The art and music are beautiful. A proper cozy game. But instead of farming you run a bathhouse for spirits. Running the bathhouse makes me think of Tetris but instead of placing blocks you are placing fantastically designed spirits into bathtubs -- it's super cute. After playing a year in-game, I've completed most of the content and lost a bit of my motivation to keep playing. While that bums me out, I really enjoyed the journey. I am hopeful and excited to see how this game grows and develops!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful and very Ghibli-esque experience. There is not much hand-holding in terms of quests which is to a certain extent refreshing, no quest markers, but only old-school hints. The bath house mechanics are really cool too and there are so many collectibles. It looks like the game is getting lots of love from the devs and is being updated to fix any issues that crop up. I am having lots of fun ♥
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I really do enjoy this game, I've been wanting a spirited away type game for ages and now there finally is one. BUT, some issues I do have with it, I wish there was more dynamic lighting and shading, Graveyard Keeper captures that really well. The same with the game music, don't get me wrong I really enjoy the music, but there are too many times where it's just eerily quiet. Somethings that should have sound effects don't as well. I wished the fishpond worked lol doesn't even look like there's water in it. I understand that the game is still fairly new and I really hope the devs keep working to improve the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying it very much so far, but it is extremely difficult to chase after spirits using the keyboard controls (I don't own a controller). I like building the relationship with the townsfolk, and running the bathhouse isn't too difficult but still has challenges which I appreciate, I am looking forward to engaging with this game further.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun and cozy.  I find the mini-games and the puzzles the games presents to you fun and challenging enough to make you think but not frustrating.  It does have some bugs, I haven't encountered anything game breaking and the devs are contently updating and improving the game.  I would highly recommend this to anyone who likes Stardew Valley or Dave the Diver.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Day 1: dog escorts you to all the villagers you need to meet, AND you can pet him for being a good boi. Day 5: discovered the broom, hyper-fixated on cleaning ALL THE THINGS in the bath house. Day 10: unlocked several spirits, obsessing over figuring out who likes who and who doesn't like who so I can maximize their placements perfectly; would die for any of them, they are perfect in every way. Ultimately so far, 9/10, feels like Spirited Away the game. Love that the tasks are meaningful and contribute to plot AND world-building, progression of tasks and skills so you can optimize with just right pacing. My only hiccups so far are the occasional instances where it's hard to tell if the game glitched or if I missed a step. EDIT: For example, figuring out how to trigger the ending of Bruce's Fix a Shrine quest or Wonyan's random dialogue box popping up saying "What's going on with that? Why does that keep happening?" Why does what keep happening?? I have to google these weird instances to figure them out. Also, the store owner stopped talking to me or letting me shop, but I could talk to other NPCs. Thought maybe the shop was closed (it was 9pm the first time this happened). Came back the next day at noon and she still wouldn't talk to me. Hard reset fixed whatever caused the NPC to not interact with me.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirittea has been both a lot of fun and very refreshing in terms of gameplay. The player can choose freely which quests to do from the notice board and there's no deadlines or rushing through the game. Also, there's tons of little surprises which don't advance the game/story but make for a very satisfying playing experience (my favorite must be the gachapon machine).From the artwork to the characters' personalities, there's a lot of lovely details that has been put into the game. You can pet all the dogs and the cat and befriend them that way :) The game feels really cohesive and makes for a great visual treat. Finally, the problem solving in the game really puts the icing on the cake for me. The little puzzles are fun and sometimes veer into the whimsical.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: It has it problems, but the game is overall really good. The devs are incredibly responsive and work really hard to address everything they can as promptly as possible. There's a lot of incredibly unique ideas and I think this game has a lot of potential, and the community is incredibly friendly, helpful and welcoming. I hope to be able to edit this in the future with a fully polished game review
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I have endless love for this game. The dev is attentive, and passionate. The game has continued to progress and improve over several patches that have been released promptly and successfully (no roll backs!).Spirittea has many mechanics that are new and unexplored in the life sim genre, such as the owning of one's own bathhouse. The main character has set out for the countryside in a bid to try and write a book and the little town of [insert town name here] (I named my town Oninote, you can name your town, it's pretty cute) certainly fit the bill. You are quickly whisked into a life sim that has familiar and unfamiliar elements.The town itself is a cute little Asian-esque inspired town ( Temple included) filled with a diverse cast of characters who I find charming, though some are definitely not so charming at first, they're sweet. Each of them has a story that you get to find out through getting to know them.Unlike many previous life sim iterations where you simply throw gifts at people or run up to them scream "HI" and then run off to do the same thing to the other 10 characters, this game encourages you to get to know the NPC's lives and find time to spend time with them (you've got karaoke, bug catching, fishing, going to the restaurant, and later on the game you can hang out at the hotsprings) and do so successfully so that you can build your relationships.I won't spoil the game too much, because I honestly think knowing very little about this game when I first played it was part of the magic, but there are wonderful theology inspired spirits throughout the game that I also find charming and I really appreciate the work that went into them. This is also the only game I've played in a while that doesn't automatically have a "well you passed out" point  at some point during the night. You're able to stay up quite a long time, but eventually it will take a toll on your health. Honestly, this game deserves your time if you're interested in it. Note for people who are reading this and planning to purchase on Xbox/Switch: The consoles are several patches behind due to the nature of their quality control process, and will remain several patches behind until they catch up to the Steam version at some later point when the game isn't being patched as often.Also, this game has a very friendly and charming discord server, the dev is active, also friendly, and very receptive to feedback. I suggest you join if you have interest in this game and want to know more!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Certainly, let's format your review for better readability:---**Firstly, a huge thank you to the Developers for their transparent approach to this game. Transparency is a significant part of my enjoyment and something every developer should strive for.****Now, onto the positives:**- **Story:** The game's story, though sparse initially, unfolds beautifully as you play. It's a refreshing change from games that force the narrative down your throat in the first 5 minutes.- **Mechanics:** Simple to pick up, hard to master. Provides replayability and is a haven for completionists with a plethora of side quests and more to come.- **Music:** The incredible music serves as a perfect background, enhancing the cozy vibe of the game.**Areas for Improvement:**- **Mini Games:** Some, like fishing and karaoke, can be quite challenging. While updates have addressed this, the choice of input (e.g., Steam Deck vs. keyboard/mouse) can affect the experience.- **Keyboard Controls:** Rebindable but default controls are a bit peculiar. For instance, 'F' as the open backpack key, 'Shift' for item interaction, and 'E' for general interaction. Worth considering before purchasing.- **Depth:** The game offers a staggering amount of depth, not all of which is explained in-game. The community and Wiki are invaluable resources, but be aware that some aspects may require extra exploration.**Overall Experience:**- **Community:** The developer community at No More Robots is among the best I've seen in terms of updates and transparency. Having been part of the alpha, I've witnessed substantial progress from alpha to the release game.- **Accessibility:** A wonderfully easy game to pick up and play for a casual experience, yet with enough depth for those seeking to invest time and effort.**Conclusion:**- **Recommendation:** A wonderful game with a fantastic community. Whether you're after a casual experience or a deep dive, this game has something for everyone. Excited to see what the developers come up with next. Hoping others find as much joy as I do every time I boot it up
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirit Tea is a fun and extremely cozy game! There are some aspects that I wish they'd go into a bit more detail about, such as where and when to use the shovel. Some kind of quest or task manager of sorts would be nice also, it's easy to get side tracked. _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I  really like this game. It's been a while since I've really been able to enjoy one of those cozy games and this one ticks all the boxes for me. Hopefully they'll keep releasing content for this game. I see this going a long way.My only negative is that sometimes I struggle to fill the day when I'm not working at the bathhouse.The problem is that sometimes to collect spirits, you need to wait for a certain day or time. _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I read had about Spirittea on an article about upcoming games around a year ago, and made a mental note to look out for it, and just hoped it'd be good because the premise sounded great.This game is CRIMINALLY underrated! _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super cozy game for anybody, casual or more advanced gamers. If you like anything Ghibli related, especially Spirited Away, this game will speak to you. Taking on the adventure of repairing the old bathhouse, meeting new spirits and solving mysteries for townsfolk, all a lot of fun. _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirittea is an amazing management sim game, I really enjoy the management aspect of it while talking to the villagers feels a little hollow and the only reason I speak to them is to get them hired at my bathhouse. There is many bugs with the game but they are regularly getting fixes and I don't run into them often. Overall it's a great game just play it for the management sim aspect not for any story or interacting with the villagers as I personally feel there isn't much substance to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: There are definitely some pros and cons to consider here, but I will say that the dev is doing a great job at being receptive to the audience. A lot of updates are in the works already, and I fully expect that there will be even more QoL updates coming. Firstly, I play on the steam deck, and it's a great experience. I think handheld is the best way to play if you are able. I do, however, wish that the run and interact buttons were separate. I also participated in the discord meta game which I highly recommend joining if you like the game even a little bit and are up for some shenanigans. But anyways....The premise is SO cute. The characters have so much personality, and Wonyan is SUCH a character. The spirits are also a fun little cast to meet. I like the rural, east asian vibes. I also like the whole bathhouse part of the game. Within the bathhouse, I think the gameplay is magnificent. Just enough going on to be fun, but not so much that it becomes a chore. I get to live out my fun dream of working a menial job and loving every second. Why is cleaning so fun??? (Can I open an in game maid service around town please?) I also like the clever little 4th wall breaks (Yes, I thought it was a glitch at first).What I don't love is the balance of the remaining gameplay. I think that the concepts are great for a lot of individual parts, but there are times where I would love to just fast forward a few in game days.  You can sleep a lot. But then the day night cycles get wonky bc you have to math out when and how long to sleep to be able to get a full night's rest before you start playing again. There are times where it feels like I'm just..... waiting for something new to do. Waiting for the spirit I need to show up. Waiting for Fae to finish the upgrade so I can go back to work. Waiting for the next day so I can start another shift. The world outside the bathhouse is only really interesting when there is an event tied to it or a goal to achieve, and I don't personally think the game guides you there intuitively. Relationship building isn't exceptionally fun to me, despite the fact that I do like the characters. I think there is just something missing. (QNo romance options if you're into that kind of thing). I also think the mini games need more feedback - it would be good to have a more clear signal that something was done right or wrong. And I think it would be nice to have a better menu for looking at collected items. Maybe even a map or helper to find certain ingredients without having to ask discord.So if you read that all, keep in mind that I do still recommend this game!! But make sure you know what you're getting into. Do you like puzzles (solving hauntings around town)? Do you like mini games + relationship building? Do you like search and find games (looking for shrine and recipe items)? Do you like cats (that boss you around but actually seem very wholesome for sticking around, even when you can't see him)? If you said yes to all this then good. Because there is a lot going on outside the bathhouse.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Here are a few of my opinions.Language is not done well, most of Wonyan or spirit cat's dialogs includes nya or something like that at the start of each and every of his sentences.  I know that the game was created overseas but wouldn't it be better if the characters in the game had English names if you chose to play in English?The backpack won't let you stack same items in one box like 2 peppers or other stuff🤦Fishing control buttons are exact opposite of where the fish is in circle, if it's on top you have to press down button to reel it in.Keyboard and mouse support can definitely be improvedThanks for the great game and can't wait to see more content
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Ya'll know what you are here to ask. Is it as good as Stardew Valley?No. But it will tide you over for a bit while Concerned Ape finishes up Haunted Chocolatier?For about 20 hours. More, if you don't read any guides. But that's going to mean a lot of pixel hunting, moon logic, and repetitive gameplay. If you use the handful of sketchy guides on 3rd tier web sites, you can barrel through, get a concentrated shot of charm and whimsy, and go on about your Stardew-less life.The problem is that the game does not have enough customization, story content, or economic incentive to keep it motivating for much longer than that concentrated shot. If you are efficient and make copious use of the run button, your bath house can generate enough cash to buy all the expensive upgrades and items by the third season. The rest is just hunting for obscure items and secrets on the map, which might be your jam. You can reach the "ending" of the game in half a year.The minigames are kinda trash. This guy made the Dark Souls of rhythm games, and the fishing is bizarre and frustrating. Stick to talking up the lads and ladies in the bath.But Spirittea is a beautiful little experience until you exhaust it. A good balance of characters with actual depth and motivation. Soothing wind and wave animations. Excellent art. Lots to collect and tick off your list if you like that kind of thing. The dialogue is witty and sweet with just a hint of aching ennui, especially in the hotspring confessional scenes. It's surprisingly subtle and adult in its presentation.

And make plenty of cash on the way!+Super relaxing gameplay.+Slowly building the bathhouse seems fun.+Plenty of funny and humorous dialogue from NPCS.+Plenty of things to do around town.+A great game to relax to after a stressful day.+Cute pixel graphics.+Some of the ways of finding spirits is hilarious.-Some of the mini games are really tedious, such as the fishing mini game.-Has a fair few bugsSpittea does a good job at what it does. Gives a relaxing, soothing experience as you solve the mysteries of spirits throughout town. This is the perfect game to play when you simply want to calm down after a long day and take a long bath.9/10 Great game!

_childDocuments_.review: Part Stardew Valley, part Spirited Away. I would definitely recommend. There's no combat (except with a bug net), no planting, and no rush to get things done in a certain time. _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Articles and pre-release reviews touted this game as "Spirited Away meets Stardew Valley", and whilst it may be a comfy game, and time/resource management game, the truth is so much bigger than that. I wouldn't even put it in the same basket as SV. Whilst SV has an almost 'sandbox' level of "choose your own adventure", Spirittea has a beautifully structured quest system, as you progress, and work towards completing and progressing through the absolutely amazing storyline.The graphics are everything you'd want them to be.The music is phenomenally created and suits every facet of the game perfectly. Even if you go to the karaoke bar and make a complete fool of yourself.The minigames are absolutely unique, refreshing, and exciting. Whilst some may go into it expecting SV, minigames involved, like fishing, are completely different and add a whole new dimension of gameplay.I was skeptical, I'll be honest, having sunken thousands of hours into SV, and being such a Ghibli fan, it was two of my favourite things being put together and used to describe this game.Is it like SV and Spirited Away? No.Is it a good game? UNQUESTIONABLY. It's fantastic. Absolutely fantastic.What's even more is the development team are caring, involved, and really genuinely care about the playerbase, and the game. This is NOT abandonware. They're there, hands on with the community, every single day, improving it, fixing any little bugs, and chasing after any naughty spirits that cause trouble. It's something you don't get to see often and put it all together with the absolutely excellent game and you've got a winner here.This game is worthy of the comfy game nomination, style, music, and more. Honestly one of the best releases of 2023, and the developers commitment to each and every little bug and issue the playerbase might come across, alongside a loving, caring, committed team makes it all the more wonderful.Play this game. Also, Radish is the best.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Overall worth the price, I actually bought it twice so I could play on Switch. The story, premise, and characters are charming and I like the portrait art.  The overall art though is a little off putting as the land seems odd and lacks the charm of pixel art games like SDV or Diver Dave.The opening mission to meet the people seems like a lot of people but takes like two minutes and there's a super helpful cute dog so complaints about that should be taken with a grain of salt.However, there are some legitimate issues users might want to be aware of.There are no item highlights so you basically have to guess if you should try to interact with something (I am old and do this out of habit because 80/90s games were like that) which in 2023 should not be a thing.The minigames are a bit fiddly and really need adjustable difficulty. The bathhouse could use some deepening to make it feel like your input really matters.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprittea emerges as a unique gaming experience that splendidly marries cultural depth with the engaging mechanics of a bathhouse simulation. The game's homage to cultural elements adds a layer of authenticity that enriches the overall experience, making it more than just a game—it's an exploration of tradition and folklore.While the controls present a slight learning curve, even for those using a controller, this minor hurdle does not detract from the game's enjoyment. Instead, it adds a layer of complexity that players may come to appreciate as they delve deeper into the gameplay. The limited inventory space, though a point of contention, could be seen as a strategic element that requires players to think critically about their resources and management skills.The puzzles are where Sprittea truly shines, offering a balanced level of difficulty that is neither too easy to solve nor frustratingly inscrutable. They manage to maintain a player's interest.In summary, Sprittea invites players into a world where the supernatural blends seamlessly with the mundane. Tasked with the rejuvenation of an old bathhouse, players will find themselves at the heart of a town teeming with spirits. The game cleverly uses this premise to challenge players to find harmony between the human and spirit realms. With its challenging puzzles and cultural richness, Sprittea is a game that promises to keep your fingers busy and your spirit intrigued.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried the demo when it released a couple of months back, and I already liked it then.Basically, this game is set in a very Japanese themed town (which you can name), and you are essentially a writer that moved there to work on your book, but ultimately ended up roped into running a bathhouse for the spirits that roam the town.
