_childDocuments_.review: SpiritTea is a great, original concept and fun but flawed.It takes a moment to get into, the intro designed to have you pretty comfortable getting your way around town. That's because the game itself relies on two elements:1. Obtain, run, and expand your bath house2. Explore and travel around town to progress with people and spiritsIt's very fun, especially when you start getting the first essential things to your bath house like towels and another pool is where it starts to feel really interesting. However, as expected, this also feels unfinished and like there can be more. Progressing a friend's affinity to max seems relatively easy with only taking a couple hang outs which makes the amount of their dialog seem short. It also feels meager when all people only want to do only two activities. Which normally seems to be Dig or X. I feel like I'm torn between some days feeling like I have so much or even too much to do and other days where there doesn't seem to be anything at all. Possibly because the game doesn't entirely hold your hand, rewarding you exploring and talking to people. It took awhile to figure out where to even go drinking with some of the NPCs. There's a lot to mention, but I think overall the game just needs "more" and the design like the lack of customization options with depth to other things that would seem promising to see means this will get necessary updates.Especially for bug fixes, which I'm glad they are doing first before anything.However, I hope the devs highly consider that their game is lovely and charming, but it needs slight improvement over time with more additional stuff to shine.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I do like and enjoy the game, but there's also some frustrating things to it.I didn't encounter gamebreaking bugs, but still bugs that are quite inconvenient. E.g. time stops running until I either go to sleep or do a time consuming activity or also my brooms are not working anymore to clean the bathhouse - which is really sad because I really enjoy cleaning in games :(Additionally, I have to say that the game is not explaining things very well. At first I totally misunderstood the karaoke minigame that you only have to do the cat-icons (it's also hard to know when to flip the food in the dinner minigame, because there's no indication (change of colour, smoke whatever) if it's ready to be flipped.)Or the game told me that I should talk to Fae to upgrade the bathhouse - which I did. 6 times at different times of the day/over days, and she never mentioned anything. Until the game fiiiiiiinally gave me the info that I have to interact with her ordering table and not talk to her as stated by the game before.Also, I didn't see the brooms the first time I went into the kitchen, and therefore thought that I have to unlock the brooms with my spirituality level.It's okay to leave the player to find out things by himself, but for me personally I found the lack of clearness on what I can do and how to do it, a bit frustrating and annoying.I do like the artstyle though and the game mechanics.The characters are a bit bland and lacking a bit of depth for my taste so far, but maybe this will change when I get to know them more. I do love the cat Woyan(? I think) though - he's really cheeky and made me chuckle a few times. :)All in all I do recommend the game as it's still fun and compelling, but I'm hoping for some bug fixing updates and maybe more/clearer explanations. :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you, like I was, are intrigued by the premise of an indie sim game that deviates from the usual farming aspect, Spirittea might be a worthy addition to your shelf.Overall, the variety of gameplay in different minigames alongside the main bathhouse management, details such as the sleep cycle, additional mechanics that alludes to more unlockable gameplay, the OST, and the general charm this solo dev project exudes make this game an enjoyable and "cozy" experience.There are some bugs as can be expected on release day, but developer/publisher/community responsiveness is quite high.Looking forward to seeing how the game opens up further along and any future additions/content!Edit: Editing to add that they've turned around the first patch with QoL updates and bug fixes, as well as transparently addressing and laying out the reason for the delay on consoles. _childDocuments_.review: This game is so amazing! I'v been playing for a few hours, and there is so much to do in the game. It never feels like a grind or overwhelming to play like some other games can be. It is charming, funny, sweet, calming, and beautiful. The overall design is so detailed and pretty, and the dialogue is great. If anyone is familiar with Nyanko-Sensei from the anime "Natsume and the Book of Friends", will especially love the cat spirit sidekick/character 'Wonyan'. If you have any hesitation with getting this game, don't, you will not be disappointed, you will absolutely adore this game like I do!

_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game! I enjoyed the demo a lot(played it 3 times) and was so impatient for the full game to release! _childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as Amelia said something about 'rice ball convenience store special' I was sold. While waiting for SDV 1.6, I started playing Moonstone Island. During my Moonstone playtime, I realized that depth of characters is a must for me in cozy games like this. As someone who doesn't primarily play games like this for the social aspect, I never thought it would have much of an impact on my overall experience, but playing Spirittea reinforced the fact that it does.While Spirittea's positive elements stand on their own without being compared to other games, a comparison is worthwhile in this case to explain what I mean by character depth and how it can really impact the overall experience in games like this. Stardew Valley, for example, is a shining example of characters with depth within the life sim format. Moonstone Island, in contrast, has cute characters that make you want to get to know them, but their minimal, redundant voice lines -- and the fact that after a voice line or two, you just click 'chat,' 'flirt,' etc. without knowing what is actually being said between your character and the NPC -- is a big let down. You already spend much of your time on the outer islands away from the NPCs, and the dialogue doesn't really give make you want to go back to the main island and interact with them further.Although I've only played Spirittea for a couple of hours outside of the demo, already my interactions with the characters have far exceeded those in Moonstone (and I really wanted to love Moonstone). From Wonyan's condescending yet endearing ♥♥♥♥ talking, to Miko's chattiness and warmth (and Quill's irritation with it), it's clear that these characters have well-developed, distinct personalities, and that makes me want to go out of my way to chat with them. In a game that already seems to have a lot to do, this rich social element is a massive bonus that adds to the appeal of the town and the sense that there's a lot of lore to be uncovered.There's a lot of other positive elements to this game (and more I'm yet to discover), but for now, I'm happy to just sing the praises of the NPCs and go back to playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful, relaxing game! I love the freedom you have to explore and discover things. So satisfying! Wonderful pixel art. I find myself really wanting to progress the bathhouse to see what interesting new spirits might come and also to make allllll the monies to buy cool things at the shops in town. So many things to do. I once decided to catch as many crabs as I could and then tried to store them in a room in my house but they all ESCAPED! lol
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: This is a work in progress review as I imagine I still need to play some minigames and get a bit further along, I've played enough to give my first impressions and offer some ideas for future quality of life things to be added later on. edit after more hours: game's still fun but I wanted to add that while I personally haven't encountered any game breaking bugs like others I've seen had a few and the quests for spirits can be rather obtuse sometimes and not offer much help when it comes to certain things (I've had to ask the nice people in the community discord for help many times) and some things are not as well explained as others. edit edit: I've added more things to the bottom of the review that I'd like to see added/explained better as the onboarding process for the game is rather rough but the game is still lovely and charming.Overall, I really like the game! I saw it on Steam a few months ago and waited for the launch, joining the discord community a few days prior to launch (lot of nice people over there and the devs are very active!) and bought it immediately when it launched. It has a charming art style, lovely music and a so far engaging gameplay loop of managing the bathhouse. One thing I enjoy about that part is you can pretty much work whenever you want timewise as long as you don't fatigue yourself which is helped by eating food and also sleeping a set amount of hours to stave off exhaustion. The townspeople are also charming, each having their own personalities and routines but one thing is there doesn't seem to be any 'events' outside of friends giving you gifts when you hit certain friendship thresholds, which is something I like from games like Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley to make the characters feel a bit more alive. Granted there may be more when I get full friendship with one of the humans (as of now I'm only best friends with the three animal villagers) so I'll edit once I have some actual people be my friends!Some nitpicks now as nothing can truly be perfect. While the game is on steam and can be played relatively comfortably with the keyboard, one of the minigames feels actually impossible to do and that's fishing. It feels like it was intended to be played with a controller as there are directions in the minigame that are not north, south, east, west that didn't feel very comfortable to try and reach when the fish got there. Nevermind the fact that the directions appear to be inverted (hitting w actually makes the cursor go south and hitting s makes it go north, similarly when hitting a and d) and can't be changed and the default accepting to do button is LShift which if pressed multiple times as the minigame commands you do will make sticky keys happen, which will pop you out of the game if in full screen. It's a shame since of the minigames I've played so far this one feels the worst to control as the rest of the game is pretty easy to handle on the keyboard. I also wish there was mouse support as some things would probably feel better if the mouse was an option but it isn't a deal breaker. It'd also be nice if there was a way to tell when you're picking up something in the world as when I do hit the button to do so I can randomly pick up things I didn't mean to (like people's furniture), a little text bubble popping up somewhere just to give feedback would be nice. Another thing would be the ability to rotate furniture but this isn't that big of a deal as it looks like all furniture looks pretty good the default way. Another minigame foible I have is that karaoke is fun but visually a lot is going on in the game that it'd be nice if there were difficulties displayed for the songs so you can get comfortable with the controls.Again, I really like the game and it'll be a fun little time sink to get lost in as I'm a fan of the genre and the vibe cozy games like this have but some little tweaks and fixes to some gameplay things would be heavenly.-Some kind of inverse control option for fishing (have w actually make it go to the top, etc)-Some kind of visual feedback that you have picked up something-Some kind of friendship events for characters hitting certain threshholds to learn more about them(if they don't already exist, will edit if this is the case)-Rotating furniture option-See a difficulty ranking for karaoke songs to get used to the controls.-Have the map be a bit clearer with the names of buildings.-Skip/shorten the animation for gaining spirituality.-Somewhere to check what the working times are for the shops, having it be a guessing game and stalking the NPCs to see when they work/don't work the shops isn't very fun.-A way to read back tutorials as the game explains things once when you encounter them and never again.-A clearer way to see the stamina, for a while after I started to play I thought I had infinite stamina and expected a bar or something to appear near me but it is infact the bento box in the right corner. No tutorial tells you this.-I saw someone mention this in another review but a clearer way to tell we're getting tired outside of text, like our character sags or gets a bit slower in movement.-Some kind of way to have items stack. A stack of 10 would go great lengths with food you can guy as each one takes up an inventory space, bit silly there isn't something like this.-a tool bar would do wonders instead of opening up the bag and picking them-a nitpick but why doesn't time stop when we open our bag/pamphlet/journal? would be nice if it did.Also join the discord! Lovely group of people.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: 1 hour in and I'm already fond of it. Maybe it's the Ghibli lover in me, but a bathhouse for spirits??! I'm not sure how deep the game gets yet as I'm still in the beginning, but so far the characters have been charming, there's so much detail in all the decor of every location, the writing is funny, and the buildings dance on the map. Why wouldn't you be happy??!I'm an hour in and already the game is hinting at future mysteries and unlockables (cooking for spirits?? a bike?! what's up with that one person's boat and the graffiti??) and having me interested in finding out has me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirittea is a delightfully cozy life sim with stunning pixel art and a beautiful soundtrack that feels like stepping into a Ghibli movie. I am having a blast running the bathhouse - there isn't a bunch of waiting around since there's always something to do from dealing with spirits to cleaning up the bathhouse. Each of the characters has a distinct personality that really feels fleshed out, adds to the overall vibe of the town, and makes befriending each a fun task. Finding them running around the town always gives me a laugh. Overall, I'm looking forward to continuing to explore the world!
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Spirittea is one of the most beautiful, intriguing and captivating games I have seen in recent years. Don't let the 30 minutes of play time fool you, or by the time you're reading this it might be 30 hours.I played countless hours of this game in the demo and watched countless people play. It is one of the most beautiful pixel style games I have ever seen, full of different vibes it feels like stardew valley, animal crossing and different anime fused into one game. The concept of running a bathhouse is one of the most enjoyable game concepts I've seen in a long time allowing me to feel like I've been thrown away straight into the storyline of spirited away. Even just walking around the map is visually  (and audibly) enough of a beautiful experience that I can't help but purchase the soundtrack too. I have no faults for this game. Beautiful map, concept, townsfolk and spirits with their own unique personalities, I wish there was an extra option ABOVE recommending the game. If you're considering it, buy it, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I had the pleasure of also playing the Alpha, and have clocked up several hours in Spirittea.This is a delightfully cozy game, with a really interesting story and interesting cast of Characters.The sound design is absolutely delightful with excellent music, and atmospheric nature noises which really lend depth to the gameplay.The bathhouse game play is well thought out, and the Dev was very responsive to tester feedback, and so the balance of the game is very good. It's not too grindy, but not too easy either.There's some very innovative quests and storylines to track down those customers (I mean pesky spirits!)This has been one of my favourite games of 2023, and I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: Please note I've split my game time between Xbox game pass and the steam versions.I've bought it on steam to support a wonderful developer and an awesome game.The game is a fun little jaunt into something I've waited for a long time to experience. Its something adjacent to the management genre that is a bit saturated that I really appreciate. I have no sense of direction and that puts me off some similar games of the genre, but this game makes me feel less intimidated, I also like the big fonts and easy readability. Being accessible from the get go is a big plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still very early in the game, but I'm incredibly impressed and happy at what the game is so far! I've been waiting for Spirittea for a while, but I have never played the demo; I like jumping into games blind, and every feature in the game was something that appealed to me anyway, so it wasn't a case of 'oh I want to try this before I buy it just in case I don't like it' - I already knew I'd adore it.I am extremely biased towards pixel art games, it is my favourite art style and I instantly gravitate towards any game with it. Spirittea's art style is pixel, but also unique in a way that it isn't overly cutesy or super saturated, and it almost follows a more 'realistic' style. This really fits the game's vision well, and will definitely help my eyes when it comes to long play sessions. The pause menu is also the most gorgeous pause menu I have ever seen, and I had to comment on it because it blew me away when I paused the game for the first time!Your first 'quest' is meeting everybody, much like it is in Stardew Valley, however this is 100% less frustrating than Stardew and I really enjoyed it; you're given a dog for this quest, Jan, to follow around, and you can ask him to hunt down specific NPCs, and it even gives you a list of everybody and which ones you have, and haven't, introduced yourself to. This is a huge plus for me, furthermore, no houses/areas are out-of-bounds, so you can easily find everyone and not have to worry if they've locked themselves inside their bedroom all day. Did i boot open the doors to everyone's bathrooms? Yeah. No-one was ever in them, but even little things like every bathroom being different really gives the impression that thought and care was put into every little detail in this game.I've only met three spirits total, including Wonyan, but the dialogue with them is already full of charm. Collecting things in games is something I love to do and do anyway, regardless of reward, but when the things you 'collect' are this uniquely interesting, it's even more rewarding and makes it so much more exciting!I can't wait to sink hours into this. I'll probably sink hours into the gacha machine alone once I have the moolags. The music is also lovely - I've been sat writing this with the ambient nature pause 'music' in the background, and it's very relaxing! Now I'm off to run my bathhouse...
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

_childDocuments_.review:
Inspired in equal measure by iconic life sim Stardew Valley, and classic spirit-focused anime and manga, Spirittea follows a writer who has escaped to the countryside in order to clear their head and find inspiration for their next novel. However, after accidentally drinking from an old mystical teapot, our protagonist begins to see the spirit world overlapping with their reality.

Spirittea is both a life sim, and management game, all in one. Players live day to day, finding local NPCs and spirits to help, and taking part in tons of different hobbies, ranging from bug catching to karaoke.
_childDocuments_.name: Spirittea

name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE
detailed_description: Welcome back recruit! MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE is a frantic VR FPS roguelite where players craft powerful hand-held weapons and struggle to survive — er defeat — the MOTHERGUNSHIP. Experience room scale movement*, dodging, limbo-ing and even relishing the satisfaction of literally punching through clouds of bullets, all while perfecting your weapon masterpiece. Survive the MOTHERGUNSHIP’s metal minions and earn gun parts to add to your weapon, easily picking them up and snapping them into place in VR. You’ll choose from a wild array of distinct gun parts and upgrades like chainguns, railguns, and pizza launchers (yes, explosive pizzas) to forge hell-ish combinations. Design your weapon, then destroy the MOTHERGUNSHIP fleet as alien machines, explosive traps, metal pests, and deadly bosses do everything they can to blast you and your weapon back to square one. *MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE includes accessibility modes to support all players. Seated-mode enables stationary gameplay, and free movement mode enables the player character to dodge with the controller. More accessibility information can be found in the game’s settings. *MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE supports Meta Quest 2, Valve Index, HTC Vive, and HP Reverb G2.

short_description: Craft. Shoot. Die. Repeat. Forge absurdly powerful guns and fight through the belly of a metal alien monstrosity in this VR FPS roguelite follow up to MOTHERGUNSHIP. Wanna build a rocket-firing-shotgun or a toxic spike-ball-launcher? Unleash your inner mad scientist, then take on the MOTHERGUNSHIP.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes.  God yes.  All of it.  The best 19.99 you can spend on a VR game right now, no question.  Wave shooters might not be everyone's bag but when it's as well done as this game (and you can create some genuinely absurd weapons), you're just simply missing out if you sleep on it.  The weapon building aspect of this game is really well done and the UI works beautifully.  This was the shot of magic my VR library currently needed.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: There's something incredibly satisfying about this gameplay loop. Attaching a new socket or buff to your already ridiculous looking weapon just doesn't get old. It's another wave shooter, which VR probably doesn't need more of - however, it's the one I'm going to keep coming back to for some time. Co-op is a blast.Don't sign up expecting a story or varied campaign experience.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Best wave shooter on the market that I've ever seen. The roguelike nature of it is very fun. Each run hits you with different challenges in building your weapons.Biggest critiques - 1. Achievements locked behind multiplayer in a dead game. God I hate when devs do this. It luckily lets you play through normal mode when queuing, but its still very annoying. The last achievement I needed was "get to wave 50 of multiplayer gauntlet mode". I've so far been able to play 2 games of multiplayer. One, my partner had no voice coms. Second, my partner started with extremely staticy voice coms and it cut out at about wave 5. We pushed through to wave 48. Aaaaaaaaaand network error. It took about an hour and a half to get that far just for the game to crash and lose it all. Devs, please stop hiding achievements behind multiplayer when you know full well your game won't have a huge online player base.2. You get TWO GUN ARMS! This is AMAZING AND AWESOME! Except for the fact that a ton of the attachments for your weapons affect every part on your gun. So by not just making one super mega death arm, you are effectively chopping your total strength into two parts. There are a few pieces that only give you buffs for "dual wielding" or having a firing barrel on each arm. But these are not very common, and the stats you get from them pale in comparison to just making a super gun on one arm and keeping the other arm clenched for punching enemies that get up to your face, or putting on a single melee weapon on the other hand for the same purpose. 3. The variety of guns is fun, but in the end it ends up turning into "hold the fire button, aim for enemies, walk in a circle to trick enemy aim as best as possible, and occasionally punch an enemy that gets to you". The biggest change to this system is getting either the rocket launcher or the Barrel Barrel which shoots massive barrels at the enemies. They have a very slow fire rate and do best when aiming the shots more precisely. But even then, with some weapons having a spooling time, and others outputting a hale of bullets, the best strategy is to just keep the trigger held 24/7 and strafe your aim from enemy to enemy.I really enjoyed my time with this game, but don't try to 100% it. The multiplayer achievement isn't worth it. Network is terrible. There's too much going on on screen when you have 2 players in the mix so crashing is likely. If I were the Completionist I would give this game a rating of Finish It. Play through the game with all the unique starting bonuses, all the difficulties. But stay away from multiplayer unless you have a friend to dedicate multiple hours to trying the gauntlet with.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: The best VR standing wave shooter, that plays a lot like mix of Space Pirate Trainer and Blasters of the Universe with much more variety and rogue-lite elements.I never expected to like the game of this genre in 2022, but it's just that well-made. Only visuals are not the best, but they allow to fill the whole screen with enemies, projectiles and explosives without any noticeable fps drops.Works on Reverb G2, but height adjustment is incorrect for it
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: AAAAAAAAAAAAThis game has sold me on VR entirely, I never wanna play a fps game in not-vr again. This just feels better. In every way. The gun customization mechanics are rad, the bullet dodging is rad, the music is rad, playing co-op with a friend is very fun.I do wish that there were more co-op modes where you could play more like the normal game, vote on bosses and hold out in different corners of the room between each room, and I wish there was a more free-roaming museum area where you could look at all of your guns from past runs, but even without those things the game is an absolute blast!
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Mothergunship: Forge is fantastic arcade fun. Super polished. Looks and sounds great. It's a roguelite wave shooter with: attitude; huge replayability; graphics are fun and make reasonable use of my PC; li'l bit roomscale movement (can play seated); great amount of stats to nerd out on; crazy weapons building system that just works; a sense of exploration and progression; randomness and much karnage. Great VR.edit: 99% percent complete in-game at 37.5 hours. Just those final five caps to find. And then some co-op action. Fantastic time had. Will be back.

_childDocuments_.review: Wave shooters obviously are what VR was made for, and it takes a good one to rise above the many that have already been churned out and MGSF is the best I've played, especially for its co-op functionality. The roguelike structure and different game modes prevent it from getting stale, and learning the nuances of how each part and game mode work especially in multiplayer are very satisfying. The end game where bullets are flying around and your synergy is fully online is the most fun. This is THE co op VR shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Was a bit turn off when I saw it was a stationary shooter, but the game is so fun I look past that and even began to enjoy the room scaling dodging mechanics (game can make you work up a sweat!).A must for anyone looking for a more intense arcade shooting experience. I cannot overstate how fun it is to build your weapons in VR, the crafting system works flawlessly and seemely without the need of menus or UIs getting in the way, props for the devs for how well the game integrates with VR controls.What I liked:- Varied enemies - Great VR controls- Gun crafting is addicting and allows for a lot of experimentation- Great BossesWhat I had trouble with:- Makes you wish you could run around the rooms like the original game!- The reduced FOV of most VR headsets makes it quite difficult to keep track of enemies that come from multiple directions. Some rooms require so much head movement that I tend to get sick.- When a room spawns with multiple shield pylons and a healer bot, it gets extremely frustrating if you have slow moving projectile weapons.Wishes:- More gun parts! (Maybe future DLC?)
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best roguelites I've played for sure. The thing I hate most about roguelikes/lites is when you're barricaded from progressing because the game refuses to help you out- but Mothergunship: Forge doesn't have that problem. Even with a Luck stat of 0, the game is very forgiving with the parts and rooms it offers you. The hitboxes are forgiving, too, and most of the time you get hit, it feels like it was your own fault for failing to dodge, rather than making you feel like you got scammed out of a health point. Overall, it's damn good. Highly recommended!Played on a HP Reverb G2.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Look at my name. Look at my thumbs up. Need I say more?Ok, i'll say more.The mechanics are fun. Modify the gun of you dreams with all sorts of crazy thingymajiggs.Sick of the usual +1 to damage upgrades and the +4 to ammo clip upgrades?Want more things like +1 to chain effect or bounce and things like chances of spawning LAVA MINES and other sorts of crazy things? Add to that the immersive VR mechanics of snapping all those parts on several types of barrels like rocket launchers or shotguns, rail guns and so on, well i think you are starting to get the picture of why this is a unique title.Now that you have made up your mind, stop reading this review and go have some fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello gamers,im wanting to place a review here on this game, something I have been following for some time now. In terms of the game: its good ; where you want to get nit picky with how it looks or how some of the AI runs, over all its a pretty great well made games.the pros: great VO lines between charactersthe gun-playthe customizationthe cons:the aiming system for guns the empty space for some bossesthe details on the good: I enjoy some good banter and when the characters of this game talk to both us and the other NPCs made it fun to hear. the writing stands on its own to where I can see greater work being done down the pipe line. the gunplay for this game is really fun , simply being able to adjust your literal gun wrist is wild. over all id make one gun lay out and half way through my game i take 10 mins to rearrange my whole rig so things either make sense for damage or it just looks better in my own eyse.now the sad part, the cons:if there are some things id have to complane about , its the aiming system. Ive got glasses , as does most of our gaming community BUT I will say its abit of a pain to try and look down the "sights". there is a very thin line that we could see possibly where our bullets will go to; its nice to make the game play abit more challenging but its also a headache to try to aim to find out im not aiming correctly when im either aiming with 1 hand or 2 depending on your gameplay,this last part is more of a personal downside:there alot of negative space left behind in some of the boss rooms , and if you are me , the empty space plus the boss fight will cause afew "worries" to appear and make you stressed.over all a great game and i recommend this game to everyone i know that is a fan of VR and a HUGE fan of rougelites.thank you , thank you for reading this and have a great day

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a blast! Easy to grasp hard to master. The roguelike elements create so much variety in every new run. Big recommendation for all action fans with huge replayability value! It doesn't matter that it's a waveshooter.edit:To add a few things I think are very cool or outstanding in this game, the very dynamic boss battles, creating contant ermergency state for the player is one thing. Getting randomized connector boxes with different shapes and number of slots, many different weapon types, ammunition types, amplifiers in different rarities and then sticking them interactively together in a very intuitive way, reconfiguring if necessary, upgrading them, that's a big fun factor here! The bigger the challenge the bigger the reward, there is always a choice. If you are low on health you maybe don't wanna die in a challenging room, but if you are well equipped then you go for the big rewards.There are even locked hidden rooms or rooms with a question mark where you can find cool and dangerous things. Every run is so different and fun. The game feels very polished, similar to Until You Fall, everything works as expected, smooth and fast.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite VR games, and possibly my favorite wave shooter ever. I love rogue-lite action games in general, and this is very satisfying example. Excellent use of the VR play space, great visuals and sounds, fun progression, and a number of options to keep gameplay interesting even after a lot of runs. Still coming back to it frequently.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: May as well drop a review to help the devs out - one of the better arena shooters to hit VR imo.  Gun crafting is fun and the random element keeps you coming back.  So far my only real complaint stems from the limited # of bosses and enemies, but the devs have dropped 1 update (so far) adding more content.  With a few more drops like that it has serious staying power in the library, but even as is it's worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: I reluctantly give this a positive review, and here's why.Graphics are great, gunplay is good, and the best part about this game is customising your weapons and loadouts - which fits perfectly in VR.  You can rotate, swap pieces in and out, and never have to open an inventory window or hit a rotation button.  Heck, you can attach a gun pointing sideways or backwards and hold your arm on an angle to shoot it in the direction you want.  This key game mechanic fits VR perfectly.Where it lacks is variety in bosses and enemy types.  There isn't too much variety in enemy types, and there are only 3 bosses.  They are the same after each level, and it feels like it could have been longer, and had more and different diverse boss fights, especially for a Rogue Lite you're supposed to run multiple times.But the primary reason for my reluctance, and biggest key detractor, is that it is more or less a standing wave shooter.  Yes, you have a small circle you can technically move/dash and lean around in.  But with this type of game, fully free movement would have really put it over the top and made it INCREDIBLE.  Games like Everslaught have tons of fast-paced moving, dashing, jumping, verticality, grappling hooks, etc.  They could have done something like that here.  If people feel sick, they can ease into it with comfort settings, or just choose to stand in one place and duck and dodge the incoming bullets.  I think this was a huge missed opportunity.All in all I support the dev for making the move to VR.  Many consider it too risky, or not worth the profit.  So for that reason, and the fact that it is still fun and works, I give it a thumbs up.  If you like wave shooters, definitely get this.  If you dislike them, this probably isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: You can't walk around! I expected it to be a FPS (my mistake) where you walk through the belly of a metal alien monstrosity. But it's a wave shooter. Nothing wrong with that if you like it but not for me (considering the price), unfortunately. There seems to be quite a shortage of good new VR games these days...Update (after developer reply):  developer thanks for your reply! I will certainly give it a second try. My review was mainly based on wrong expectations on my part and if you're into wave shooters it seems to be a good game. I also would like to support anyone who creates VR games, especially if you're a small team just like yourself. I can appreciate the time and effort that it takes to produce a game. That's why I think my initial review wasn't entirely fair and I've changed it into recommended. It would be good to have free movement in the future however ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly as advertised.While it is a wave shooter, it does allow for movement in your play area using either the movement controller or just physically moving out of the way. Your head is the only thing that can be damaged, so if you dodge your head from a projectile or melee path you can avoid a lot of the bullet hell.  Some enemy attacks are aoe based, chompers and sploders for example, and you either need to deal with them first or find shields.An hour and half in and there have been no bugs, no crashes nor any issues with tracking. It is designed that you will be doing multiple runs as items do not unlock till a run is finished.  If you played the first mothergunship then you will recognize enemy types and attack types right away.  If they do manage to make this immersive like the first one, it could be a fun upgrade. This stands pretty solid by itself as long as you don't have this deep seated hate for rail-like shooters... then you know buy this and complain about it being a rail shooter.   There is more movement options in this than most.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid gun creation, but i do really wish you could walk around and that sandbox mode was added at the release instead of it being a future update.I also miss the level mechanics from it's old PC where you could enter a short but mighty fine level you could get parts and stuff from, beat the boss and take the parts home if you survive it to play around with later or take onto the next level.Right now the game feels half baked and unfinished with how it is playing.To whoever reads this, i recommend waiting until some content updates have been released in order to get the most fun out of it, since the sandbox mode is announced to release later, and it being way more fun to play with the gunparts with you to the base as a reward for beating a boss.4/10 for now until they start to add some of the nice things from the previous game.NOTE: thanks for the devs for telling me, i will try the updates out tomorrow and see if it is any better! for now just imagine this review not existing :]

_childDocuments_.review: There is unfortunately not 1 positive thing I can say about this game. But I think I can summarize what I don't like into 5 parts.First being if you were a fan of the original mothergunship with it's premise of building an arsenal of guns. . . this ain't that. I came in knowing full well that it was gonna be a shiddy wave shooter. I knew this. I am not faulting it for this. What I AM faulting it for is the looting. There are like 6 types of rooms but you don't care about 4 of them. Any type the next door ISN'T a weapon parts room or atleast a shop, it feels like you just played the slot machines and lost, getting nothing for dealing with that room.And even THEN it's still bad. So there are these things called "weapon caps", they do SLIGHT SLIGHT augmentation to your gun. . . . which would be a good thing. . . IF YOU COULD EVEN FIND A GUN!!!! On the LUCKY chance you get a weapon room, 90% of the time. . . there won't even be any weapons! . I get nothing but stat-based caps. I don't care for caps! Idk why but the looting in the previous game didn't feel this bad. The worst part is. . . there is an easy fix to this. Just have caps be their own room separate from weapons. And have attachment point parts show up in both.The next part. It's slow. . . PAINFULLY slow. So much so that boss battles don't feel like boss battles. . . they feel like loading screens. I am just standing there, barely moving waiting what felt like 15 minutes for the bar to drain. This is fine in an action game. . . but this isn't an action game, this is a wave shooter. Meaning it's about landing your shots quick and precisely. . . the problem with that is their boss design aren't targets you have to be precise with nor are they quick. They are big floating targets. You can look away from them and just aim in their general direction and probably hit them. It will take you forever but it's not because your shots aren't landing. They are just tanky since you don't get any weapons.And even then it wouldn't be that bad. . . if actually fighting them was actually fun and or interesting. It's like fighting the DVD logo screen. Just hovering bouncing from corner to corner while it shoots 1 mile an hour bullets from 50 miles away. When I say this game is slow, I mean SLOW. There is free movement. . . barely, which you can use to dodge to the left or right at a snails pace. But since you are mostly just standing still in a circle, it doesn't exactly make you "want" to crouch or duck, it makes you just want to finish the fight and be done with it. Almost none of the attacks hit you cause of how slow it is (which goes against the nature of a wave shooter) and even when they do, it's cause it's either shooting at you from all directions all at once, or it's the 3rd boss that shoots you with cones that you have no idea where they are aiming at so just screw you the dev said to the player.3rd? Well, that would be progression, or the lack their of. See, after you beat a boss, in the old game, you bring your stuff back with you to add to your collection. There is no collection here, you die, you lose everything. You always start with nothing. Maybe there is progression in that you can actually bring a starting loading. . . but if you are playing an hour in and still can't get basic stuff. . . then that's just a bad game.I think that's all my issues, but generally, it's just not a fun experience. It's slow, where it's not as much challenging as much as it is a test of patients and the actual mechanics aren't enjoyable. I could complain about the controls being wack on the Index controllers where it wants us to use grip buttons on a controller that doesn't actually have a physical button, but that's not even worth mentioning. TL;DR:Even if we ignore the wave shooter aspect, it fails to do the basics that the original game got right. Clunky, slow, unfun, and just generally poor design choices, from the room types, to how it deals with it's loot all the way to mechanics and progression. Again, I'm really trying desperately here but there isn't one positive thing I think I can say about this game. Actually. I think I came up with one thing: I am within steams 2 hour mark, so I am able to refund it. Despite that, I don't think I will. That's because, although it's not exactly an "enjoyable" experience, it is atleast a "playable" experience. Like, something to do when you are desperate.Save your money. Get games like Compound or Ancient Dungeons instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this with high expectations, and came out disappointed. It has this feeling of being an early vr title, with little interaction of VR elements. If the game was more akin to Mothergunship proper (movement arena shooter), I think it'd feel more unique. As it stands, it feels low energy with little dodging, outside of some boss fights. Certain elements suffer for the players mostly fixed positioning, where mods like pierce are very niche, with the player not being able to properly maneuver and line up shots. The same goes for being able to place barrels are odd angles, which in a game where enemies come at you from more than one direction could have a certain utility, but here it's more a hindrance. And my biggest gripe, is the game simply doesn't give you enough parts. Gun part rooms are rare, and shops are often full health or upgrades, rather than parts. Only recomended if you're a big fan of wave shooter type games.

_childDocuments_.review: While I fully commend the attempt, Mothergunship: Forge doesn't really work as a VR title. Simply put - what make a VR game fun is the interactive component. Being able to pull back the bolt on a garand in Contractors, Pavlov, or H3 is fun because it immerses you. Combining ingredients in Cooking Simulator or Job Simulator is entertaining because of the creativity it allows for. Mixing gun components in Mothergunship... Well, I've seen that already in the base game, and in Forge I get the added element of... awkwardly dodging slow moving bullets while awkwardly trying to aim with 2 different weapons simultaneously at a horde of enemies. The key word is awkwardly.I want more titles in the Mothergunship franchise. I'd love for a non-roguelite attempt, and I definitely love the crazy weapon combinations one could make... but not in the VR medium.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say I am very close to recommending this game but it falls just short in a few key areas. The developers are still supporting the game and hopefully it will only get better and I will change this to a recommend in the near future.Co-op Mode is in beta currently. You have a small box to move in, no free style movement.You attach weapons and power-ups to your arms via Weapon Part upgrade rooms. You are moved to and from mini arena style maps in a bullet hell style shooter. You have 4 Hit points and if you lose them all your run is over. After each arena is defeated you will be given a choice of 1 to 3 rooms with different power-up options and this is where the problem starts. Rank SThe rooms provide either Weapon, Power-up, Slots to attach weapons and power-ups. You get to choose from 3.You want these over everything else all the time. Many of our runs end early because of one of the following;No weapons given (sometimes all the way until the 2nd boss)Common Weapons only (Rarity is Common, Uncommon, Rare, Legendary)Worthless Power-ups (Example would be AOE increase parts when you don't have an AOE weapon, which you likely wont as the game only gives you 3 choices per room)Not getting the X-Pistol (This weapon destroys enemy projectiles, seriously you need it the shields suck) Rank AThey give you Money for the shop, which is super important, just not nearly as important as a Weapon Room. Never choose any room over a weapon room. Rank BThese rooms are ok if your great on cash and there are no weapon part rooms available. If your forced into too many of them, just restart the run. Rank CThese give you access to a special store but doesn't guarantee that the store will spawn so many times you will just get stuck with the key until you die or finish the run. I would say about 1/3 of the time we get a key and then a key room to go into. The room is the same is a store room but everything is free, and many times will have useless items, so its not that great anyways. Rank CThese allow you to upgrade your weapons, power-ups, and slot boxes. These are deceptively nearly worthless.You need 3 of these to take a Common weapon to an Uncommon, or 9 to upgrade it to Legendary. There are not that many doors between bosses so you will never get enough of these to make any common weapon into something that is actually useful. And when you do upgrade a weapon it usually increases crit% or some secondary effect by 2-5%. Just go to weapon rooms and if Rare weapons are not dropping, RESET Rank F--These rooms are here to insult your intelligence. Some rooms will only offer 1 room, like exiting a shop. Sometimes its a purple gem room and if you squint a little bit, you can see a middle finger in the center of the gem.They will give you some extra points for stuff in the game menus, but you get them anyways just doing the runs normally, never ever go into these rooms if you can avoid them. They are never worth it and you will feel a little worse after doing them.These give you 2x whatever the room shows you on the door in red. So if your really lucky it will be a weapon room and solidify a great run, or it might be a purple gem room and you get two middle fingers to look at.This is probably where the game shines the most. There are a wide variety of enemies. Some heal, provide shields, or have some other effect that you have to contend with. Bosses can be a little bit over-kill on projectiles, but I honestly think if everything else in the game was fixed up, this wouldn't be an issue.1. The upgrade parts need to be more impactful. Either it only taking 2 instead of 3 to change a weapon rarity, or giving 2 per room and 4 per challenge room.2. Higher drop chance of rare equipment after bosses, I have been offered 3 commons after the second boss so many times its infuriating.3. More Health and Shield drops during a fight. It makes the game extremely frustrating that every little mistake is punished so harshly and you end up going into a boss room with 1 health.4. Offer a quick reset during a run. Its annoying to have to stand there and die on purpose or quit the game.5. Purple Rooms, get rid of them or change them to special gems for skins for the weapons or something like that6. Increase chance of the key room or just make it so that its a gaurunteed spawn 1 to 3 rooms after you get a key. A rare or legendary item should spawn in these rooms, they are currently not worth the hassle.7. Allow menu upgrades during Co-op, the game is already hard enough8. Hopefully the other game modes will be open to co-op when its done, currently they are not.9. More canister refill drops or the canisters should pause until they refill on their own. So instead of them being stuck empty during most of the fight, they should empty, and then start to refill but not activate again until they are full. This would create a situation so that the canisters turn off and on during a fight unless you get a refill drop. And make them a lot more impactful.

_childDocuments_.review: Argh, this one had so much potential! I was so happy when I started playing it, thinking I finally got a fun VR roguelike shooter. But alas, the illusion melted away relatively quickly. First off, you're greeted by a cheerful commander guy who's well written and has good voice acting. Then you meet some more characters... but the problem is that you never really get to interact with them. You just get pieces of info from them, and that's about it. Let me talk to them! Visit them! Do anything except just get dialogue quips!Then, the game makes you think it's like Hades. You have rooms with a reward sign: beat the room and this is what you get. Gun parts! Money! Upgrade hammers! Healing! Purple crystals that are totally not darkness! But uh-oh, what made Hades good was so much more than just that part. Besides, here the gun-building system just feels... I don't know, nothing seems to fit. Let me explain.You have connectors, barrels, ammo canisters and doodads. Connectors give you more room to stuff more parts, barrels do the pew-pew, ammo canisters give you bonuses as long as they're not empty (you can refill them), and doodads give you constant passives. All good, yeah? But then you have this issue that some connectors point sideways. What's the point of a gun with a sideways barrel? Of course, you can eventually get a different connector that points sideways too so you can "re-align" your barrels, but until then, you have a bit of an issue on your hands.Another thing: you have two hands, so that makes for two guns. Of course, you can have multiple barrels on every gun, so in the end it becomes far more than just two guns. But the problem is that you'll probably end up with different barrels on the same gun, maybe even wildly different ones: grenade launcher and a rapid blaster, for example. Why is this a problem? Because all of those guns will have their own fire rate, so the only way to deal proper damage at that point becomes to hold down the trigger button and never let go. It doesn't feel like shooting anymore, more like pointing a laser pointer of not-quite-death at stuff.And this is a real shame, because there is quite a nice amount of guns. But what's the point if in the end you'll end up holding the attack button anyway? Oh, a new barrel? Stick it on an empty slot and keep firing. No change, maybe a bit more DPS. Sorry, but considering this is the game's main draw, I can't help but expect more.Finally, there's the issue of the metagame. Not every roguelike needs to have meta progression, I'll be the first to say that. But here you have a lot of attention brought to the purple crystals which apparently unlock stuff, and your commander tells you to bring a lot of them back... but then you realise you're given a lot for simply doing the run anyway, and even then, they just end up getting tallied and eventually unlock a new weapon or a perk or something. And you have no control over it. You can choose which perk you go with - one at a time - but that's about it.There's also the issue of enemy design and variety, and probably more stuff besides, but I think I've made my point. There's definitely something going on here - and this game could be, in fact, a great one. But I feel like fixing everything and adding everything that I'd say is missing would take so much work, it's absolutely out of the question. Oh well, at least I got a minor workout dodging bullets, and Falcon Punching robo-biters was fun.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best, if not hte best 2-player co-op VR game there is. It's a roguelike in which you clear a room, choose an upgrade as a reward, then choose which type of room to go next and repeat until you make it to a boss. After boss there's a different style of rooms with a different boss at the end. Your character is mostly stationary - you have a circle area you can move around to avoid bullets and enemies shoot at you from distance or charge at you.The main feature of the game is building your own weapons. You get modules as rewards for clearing the rooms and attach them to your connectors however you want. If you play co-op, you can also give parts to your friend or take some from them. There are also game modes which modify how the weapon building works or what you get at the beginning. Or you can even save your builded weapon after a run and use them is a specific game mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Mothergunship: Forge is the perfect, Arcade-style VR experience. Dodge bullets, fire back, and assemble absolutely ludicrous guns. It's decent workout, pure fun to play, and at times laugh-out-loud funny.Physically attaching, detaching, and re-attaching weapon parts to build an armament is very satisfying, and also makes up the core of the game's roguelite engine. Weapon parts are the only way you get stronger during a run, either by attaching new barrels, ammo cannisters, or passive-power endcaps. However, each connector on your gun only has so many slots. This creates interesting choices: You have one slot left. Do you take the awesome weapon on offer, and risk not getting offered another connector for a while, or do you take another connector and open up some more room to make sure you don't have to forgo a later upgrade?There's a bit more strategy to the weapon assembly than just slapping things together. Connectors are weird shapes, so if you want that 4th barrel on your right hand to actually shoot forward, you have some rearranging to do. But you also have to consider that the path a bullet takes from your ammo cannisters (or hand) through the connectors also grants bonuses for each connector. It's not the deepest system, but it has enough depth to leave you fiddling with your weapons for a few minutes between rooms to find that perfect gun layout.The content variety is hit-or-miss. There are tons of parts, perks, and game modes to unlock for replayability, but there are also only 8 or so enemies (doubled if you count "now it's really big" as a different enemy) and just 4 bosses. It's enough if you can get replayability out of exploring new builds, but not enough if you need visually simulating environments or constant enemy surprises.Sometimes, though, I find it's worth doing a run just to hear the character banter between missions. There's not much dialog, but what's there is very well voice acted. There's some good humor in the writing, but the parts that made me laugh out loud came between sequences - I won't spoil the joke, but keep your eyes peeled.One word of caution, the game is notably less engaging played with locomotion. The bullets move pretty slowly, and you can dodge things mostly just tapping left and right on the joystick. It's much more engaging to play with locomotion disabled, forcing you to physically duck and dodge and be aware of your surroundings. It doesn't require a large space - mine is only 4" x 6" and I had way more than enough room to move - but more wouldn't hurt! It's still playable standing or seated, but is missing a little something if you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. Okaaaaaay.Really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun. And I'm throwing two words in there that Steam's gonna censor, just because Mothergunship is *that* fun.Do you hate your left thumbstick wearing out because the Valve Knuckles have them made out of cheap plastic? There's a dash option that lets you dash left and right instead. You're not moving far from your assigned circle anyway. Perfect.You wanna use frames to build a stupidly large contraption with a bazillion guns? Game lets you. Some passive attachments encourage 'dual wield' but honestly you shouldn't worry too hard on it. I generally have punch & passive stuff attached to my off-hand because a hand can't clench a fist for a punch if it's actively firing. Great system, all in all.Enemy placement is inventive too. Horde shooter games like these oftentimes become predictable with where the enemy would spawn. Not this one, though. Melee enemies take a predictable path, floating enemies take a minor arc towards you, but the turrets will just spawn bloody damn anywhere. Is there a turning wheel that dips into a liquid? A pump that pushes up and down? Yeah I've seen turrets just latch on there, frequently going out of view, incapable of shooting or being shot. It gives the combat a kind of dynamic where there's comfort in some predictability, but you still get some surprises.The treadmill of it all is pretty straightforward too, with modes being unlocked in rather obvious ways. Mode that favors melee? Have a high enough global total of punched enemies. Easy mode? Die twice. A modifier that gives you a starting forge upgrade point? Globally upgrade your guns x amount of times. Unlock more gun pieces? Just play the game as intended, you'll unlock plenty each run. There doesn't seem to be any inorganic feats you need to accomplish to get that loop of dopamine going.Mothergunship feels like if you took one of those VR proof-of-concept games that looked promising in the pre-2020's, then polished and developed their schtick like a real dev would.I don't say this a lot (even though a lot of VR reviewers do for *far* unworthier games), but this one's a must-have.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10I personally find it very hard to find games that are good rogue-like's or roguelites that have good replay ability everyone does it wrong making it become a game that could of been over 200 hours of game play into a game where if I play it for 40 hours ill be bored of the game already some even last less time making it down to 6 hours before I become bored. However, Mothergunship: Forge is not one of those games that does it wrong the concept of gun building every round and them having over 170 gun parts really does the trick. The versatility in game modes is amazing too if you want to go for hardcore just do nightmare mode. If you prefer to chill while having it still be how far can you get playing the game go endless mode. If you wanna just build a big A$$ gun go with the sandbox mode. TL:DR: If your into roguelikes or roguelites i would give this game a full on try.

It has coop, in case you subscribe to the fun with friends meme too(the difficulty scales whether or not you're in coop though, so beware if you're doing nightmare mode). _childDocuments_.review: This game is flippin' amazing! If you have a buddy to play through co-op that is. _childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly fun.  Customizing and upgrading your load out works seamlessly and gives you a lot of creative options, progression feels good, I haven't hit the point where I feel like I've played out the game yet and winning is just an inevitability or anything based on upgrades.  Gameplay is very similar to Space Pirate Trainer but with full customizability of the weapons that you get in a roguelike style dungeon.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game for vr, by far.  As well as my favorite roguelite.  The gunplay is good, level design is decent, but the gun crafting mechanics are immaculate!  You never end up with the same gun twice, and every build you make is special in its own way.  The various gamemodes keep you coming back, and there is even the ability to play online if you want.  If you are on the fence about buying MGF, do yourself a favor and take a chance on it.  I promise, you will not be disappointed.  And if you don't have a vr system yet, but are planning on getting one at some point, wishlist this game.  Every vr gamer should have this in their library, and it is a great game to get early on while you are still getting used to your vr system.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Simply amazing.You get new gun pieces for your arms every so often and strategize how to build the damn thing for each following room is not only inslanely fun but it gets right every design aspect one loves about rogue-likes. Combine that with VR friendly (but challenging) bullet-hell mechanics and enemy management and you have a game that just keeps you playing for hours on end.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Like most rouglites, it's a slow start at the beginning unlocking everything, but as you play more and figure it all out, the mechanics allow you do do wild stuff. The enemy variety is a little low, but considering it's a vr game that has a few unique bosses and is getting updates to a fun idea, I would say it's worth at least trying out, but I certainly love this game more than I thought I would when I started
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most fun I've had in VR in a long time.  I can't get enough of this game and it just keeps getting better with each update.  I love the new co-op options to share some of those juicy unlocks and modes to play together instead of only progressing in solo.  I love the concept, but do wish I could venture into the map and go on a punching spree like the 2D Mothergunship (Non-Forge) game.  However, the way it is set up is quite awesome and I crave playing this game all the time, as do my kids.  Maybe in the future we could get a "pause" function with a temporary multiplayer save setup so when it's time for dinner or bedtime we don't lose lots of progress when we play for hours at a time.  Thanks for all you do!
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: [Update]: Right, I'm mildly addicted to this game now. Great action, a huge range of gun components, an insane amount of rooms and surprises, a great variety of game modes and perks to change things up, and co-op gauntlet  campaign! If you like  and/or  and/or  and/or  get this game. It's such a good time, it is so well made, they deserve our love & support 🤣At first I was a bit disappointed that it wasn't the original game, with free locomotion inside each room, but holy rocket launchers, this game is a lot of fun! It is mainly a physical, mostly room-scale, wave shooter. That has become a derogatory term for VR games, but this is a supremely polished one that stands out, I'll try to elaborate why below.So yeah, if you have enjoyed other wave shooters, like Serious Sam: The Last Hope, this is definitely a game to check out. While I'm not a huge fan of rogue-likes/lites, which I guess this can be classed as, I've had a literal blast playing it so far, and will keep playing it too 🥰
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! With the recent updates, there are lots of items and different combinations for you to try. Yea, RNG will get you from time to time but see how long you can get with the build! Things can get interesting, you might get further than you think. The co-op is what I was really drew me to try this game and it did not disappoint. It has a lot of really neat features like sharing items back and forth and the ability to upgrade friends' items. _childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Its 2022, do we really need another wave shooter? YES!! This game is completely awesome.   It has dethroned Space Pirate as the best VR wave shooter.  This is a game that both VR newcomers and veterans will enjoy.This is a rougelike game where you build your guns as you progress.  There are hundreds of different pieces you can attach to your weapons that modify them in many different ways. Find a shotgun, toss a rubber canister on it so your bullets bounce around.  Is your rocket launcher/Saw gun shooting too slow, upgrade it or toss on a projectile speed modifier.  Chain gun have too much spread, put a magnetic canister so your bullets seek nearby targets.... you get the idea.   It feels like the devs have thought of every possible upgrade or gun.  You can build some truly devastating weapons.  And each run feels unique and won't be the same as the last.While this game's identity is rooted in building epic weapons, the boss fights might be the best part.  They take great advantage of VR as a medium  They will have you ducking, dodging and gasping in awe when you first encounter them.  When giant mechanical dragons lunge at you in VR, it just hits different, the sense of scale is staggering.To keep things fresh, there is also a plethora of game modifiers, that tweak nearly every aspect of the game.  Additionally, since the release of the game, the devs have added more gun parts, enemy types, stages, and now they even seem to be doing seasonal updates with the Halloween stuff.This is one of those games that just keeps on giving, and I could see myself coming back to for years to come.  The only downside is that it doesn't have cross play multiplayer with quest, so finding a multiplayer game could be a bit challenging, but I'm, sure with the help of discord you could do it easy enough.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: When I stumbled on this, I had no idea that I needed this in my life. Already enjoyed the gameplay loop of Mothergunship, so why not go into VR?I'll be totally honest, for the format and how it's designed? It works very well. It's not quite the same degree of bullet hell you'd expect from the original, but this is a great game as it's very accessible - even those not familiar but enjoy VR will find this easy to pick up and play, even with a limited space. It was a little daunting to learn how small the platform you navigate is, but it makes sense. Your actual hitbox is generally speaking, your chest and head. So in the grand scheme of things, not very big. So you don't need a huge space to bounce around dodging extremely fast projectiles. While a mode like that would be fun to have for VR vets, it doesn't detract from the gameplay.I've only got a small amount of playtime in, but it's worth the experience you get out of it for 20$. Seriously looking forward to future updates expanding the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: Mothergunship Forge is my new favorite VR shooter, and possibly even my favorite VR game of all time. The gun creation mechanics and wealth of game modes / perks make it insanely replayable, and a heck of a good time. Pretty chill on the easier modes/earlier levels, and turns into basically a VR bullet hell on the harder modes/later levels. An absolute must play for VR fans.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: See, normally when your gun takes up half the screen and obscures your vision so much that it gets you killed, it's bad visual design. Here, it's nobody's fault but your own, and it's glorious....Okay, but seriously, Mothergunship Forge is a roguelike VR thing based on the Mothergunship of old where you get to assemble your own guns piece-by-piece, and while this doesn't have quite so much jumping around, being able to build ridiculous boomsticks in VR and apply them directly to swarms of robots is something special. The multiplayer is a bit janky... okay, even the single-player is a bit janky... but that's what happens when you render hundreds of bouncing, chaining, homing bullets on two screens at once.
_childDocuments_.name: MOTHERGUNSHIP: FORGE

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite fun to make your own gun and destroy enemies with it and the bosses are fun to battle. There are still many things I haven't unlocked so there is a lot of content I've yet to discover which I have no doubt is really fun and puts a fun twist on the classic MGS experience. Overall if you want challenge, this game has it. If you want a calmer experience, this game has it. Would reccomend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a VR rogue-like, where instead of building your character you build your weapon instead. It's pretty enjoyable for a game you can describe in one sentence, building the gun lets your imagination run wild. Design it to look "reasonable" or just attach everything and make sure the barrel is facing the right way, there's no correct way to build it and that's what makes it so interesting.I personally would like to see the co-op get it's own campaign balancing, as the only co-op mode is a single room survival experience (a stark contrast to the solo campaign), and more enemy types. As a side note, punching enemies just feels great, but only 4 (2 if you don't count the elite versions) are even punchable.All in all, for a first step into VR territory, the gameplay is smooth, enjoyable, and works really well with the gun building concept. For a 20 dollar VR game, this checks all the boxes that say "worth it". Keep an eye on these guys, the updates for this or even another game are probably gonna be pretty sweet.7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I already own & enjoy the original Mothergunship. The TL;DR here is that I strongly recommend this game to VR players. It's a much longer experience with more progression than is typical in VR titles. If you've already played the original, it's very much the same kind of game with a few changes (mostly streamlining & altering mechanics to make it more suitable for VR). Pros: +Creating & customizing guns is absolutely incredible in VR, significantly faster & more fun than the flat-screen version+Gunplay is superb; no reloading or ammo, & all weapons have their own built-in laser sight  for intuitive aiming+Very replayable (since it's a rogue-like)+Good performance; high framerate with zero frame drops at the time of writing+Runs are filled with meaningful choices that greatly impact the rest of the runCons:-Lack of virtual body presence hurts immersion-Permanent progression is a bit too streamlined; all permanent unlocks be automatic without any player choice

_childDocuments_.review: FORGE feels like they took MOTHERGUNSHIP and trimmed the fat off, shedding its more complicated mechanics for, in my opinion, a much smoother experience. Gun crafting feels much more intuitive and less clunky with fewer limitations, you don’t have to worry about choosing a loadout or losing your gun parts, and rather than selecting ships from a map the game more closely matches what you would expect from an arcade-y roguelite FPS, taking notes from MOTHERGUNSHIP’s predecessor Tower of Guns.I’ve beaten the game once, and felt a little surprised that there wasn’t another level (I didn't even realize I was fighting the titular MOTHERGUNSHIP until I beat her). Regardless, I’m enjoying coming back to it time and time again and trying different gameplay modes and perks. If there isn’t already a hidden 4th level that I haven't discovered yet, my hope is that there will eventually be an update that adds another level (or two) along with a save-and-quit function to compensate for the longer play sessions.I love the characters, voice acting and writing, but I do think the game could benefit from a more fleshed out story à la the original game. These guys are familiar to me, so I like hearing them again, but I imagine a new player that hasn't played or beaten MOTHERGUNSHIP might not find them as charming as I do. Also, where’s Jasper?All in all, FORGE is an excellent wave shooter, the gun crafting mechanics and perks system add a level of variety that keeps me coming back in a way that is often difficult for VR games to do.

_childDocuments_.review: So far im enjoying it, only thing i'm sad about is there's no crossplay between steam/oculus.I dont know if there is a customizable game mode yet, but id love to do runs with certain enemies disabled or custom modifiers.Edit: Refunded so i could pick it up on the oculus store to play with friends on there. Still a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally not actually a fan of these "shooting gallery" type of VR games as they lack something that makes me feel like it really HITS. But if you can imagine mixing making that futuristic DLC of Pistol Whip (the one with the boss that fires immense amounts of bullets at you) with an overwhelming amount of gunfire on top of the wackiest gun crafting system that feels immensely satisfying you can get a good idea of what kind of game this is. 3.5 hours on day one and its a very solid banger, It straddles the line of finding just enough new stuff every run while running across enough familiar parts and items that you never get bored or lost in the immense variety. name: Azure Striker GUNVOLT 3
detailed_description: What lies beyond the path toward hope? The next installment in the high-speed 2D action Gunvolt series is finally here with Azure Striker Gunvolt 3. Balancing both an involving story and satisfying gameplay, Gunvolt 3 is the most extravagant entry in the series yet! Play as both new star Kirin and series protagonist Gunvolt as you switch between them on the fly while conquering Gunvolt 3's many stages and bosses. Story Mode+ which keeps the exciting action uninterrupted by the rich story. New to Gunvolt 3 are Image Pulses, collectable summons and equipment called forth from Gunvolt's own memories. Over 150 varieties are available to collect! ■Satisfying swordplay meets light-speed superpowers! Experience the exhilarating 2D action your own way! Take control of Kirin's stylish sword action or Gunvolt's devastating lightning powers to clear stages with show-stopping abilities! ■The thrilling near-future dystopian story plays out in real-time with 'Story Mode+'! Characters talk and banter without interrupting gameplay thanks to Story Mode+, allowing their personalities to shine and the story to develop without diluting the action experience. Full English voices are available along with the original Japanese! ■New songs from 'The Muse' Lumen heat up the battle! Put on a show with your gameplay to earn 'Kudos' points and the virtual pop idol Lumen will start a performance of her own, replacing the stage track with a vocal pop song! 7 brand new songs are included alongside a large selection of classic songs from the series. ■Kirin and Gunvolt's team-up creates a new power - 'Image Pulse'! Collect over 150 types of 'Image Pulses,' giving form to Gunvolt's memories. Image Pulses allow you to summon comrades and rivals from Gunvolt's past to attack, grant abilities, and more.
