_childDocuments_.review: Azure Striker Gunvolt 3, sorry, Septima Sealer Kirin could’ve worked great as a spin-off game instead of a mainline entry, but sadly, that’s not the case. Before reading any further, remember that this review includes story spoilers. Read at your own risk! This is also not entirely a negative review since the gameplay part is actually outstanding, but there are serious problems story-wise as well as from its technical aspects. Before stretching it out any longer, I’ll get right into it. Azure Striker Gunvolt 3 is such a misleading title for a game that you barely get to play as Gunvolt, and that is for a limited time unless you master his move set and memorize every single boss pattern. Kirin is in the spotlight this time around due to Gunvolt losing control over his power and going into Primal Dragon state which is supposedly a very dangerous being that is capable of destroying the world, but thanks to Sumeragi’s several Glaives, he stays under control until Kirin finds and frees him. Kirin’s Septima is capable of sealing other Adepts’ Septimas, thus she ends up sealing GV’s Azure Striker to keep him in check but ends up transforming him into a dog that can talk. This whole dog thing isn’t explained in any way at any point; therefore, I interpreted it as a sexual metaphor of the director. Oh, we have LOTS of those, by the way. I’ll get to them in a bit. Anyway, due to GV’s Primal Dragon state, we find out that there are some Adepts who got affected by his Dragon Radiation and went berserk. At this point, Sumeragi decides that GV isn’t a terrorist anymore, and with the help of Kirin, they start working for Sumeragi under a newly founded department called The Bureau of Dragon Saviors whose aim is to detect and take care of Adepts that got affected by GV’s Dragon Radiation. However, Kirin ends up recruiting them. I’m not gonna lie, they’re some very colorful characters and there’s huge potential, but the problem is that this whole game is a mainline entry instead of a spin-off. Naturally, everyone who made it up to this point will be expecting a follow-up to Xiao’s ending in GV2, but no. Instead, you’ll be greeted with a perverted Arabian Prince who has an organization of his own called ATEMS that is formed by him and his… wives. You heard that right. Even though the game refers to them as Zed’s Knights, it’s quite obvious that they’re not exactly that. There’s even a character that revolves around this prince’s sexual fantasies who is called Sistina. To elaborate it a bit further, she shoots dildos and butt plugs at you. Her desperation move is also called Relentless Libido. You’d naturally want to take this Zed guy down since he lacks the most basic moral judgments of a human being, right? But no… It gets worse. Much, much worse. He reveals that GV is not the original Primal Dragon, but something called Moebius, and this Zed guy ends up helping Kirin during the last fight. You even get to play as this perverted freak in a separate campaign. I really don’t want to spoil the ending, but it makes things even worse. So, that’s the mess of a story Inti Creates came up with in this game. No matter from what perspective you look at it, it doesn’t make any sense. Was there really no other way to introduce Kirin and other characters? What happened to the other characters that were in previous games? Where’s Copen? What happened to Mytyl? What was Xiao planning? You won’t find any answers to these questions sadly. Oh, before I forget, Lumen is in the game, but in the form of an Image Pulse which is the result of the combination of GV’s and Kirin’s Septimas. In other words, she’s just a materialized version of GV’s memories. Leaving that horrible story behind, let’s talk about the gameplay a bit. You almost play as Kirin all the time, but you can switch to GV if you feel like the game is too difficult for a reason if his Fetters Gauge is enough to allow you to play as him since he lacks any sort of HP bar. You can think of him as a backup plan because while using him, you’ll deal a huge amount of damage, but gain less kudos compared to Kirin. If you aim to play the game as intended, then you’ll have to refrain from touching the ground as long as possible and keep building up chains using Kirin. You’re probably already familiar with aerial combat from Luminous Avenger iX games, but unlike Copen, Kirin doesn’t have any sort of jetpack so it’s a lot harder to stay in the air. You unlock an aerial attack that acts as a jump after defeating a certain boss and you gain an additional air jump after using the Arc Chain successfully. It may sound difficult at first, but let me tell you that if Azure Striker Gunvolt 3 does anything right, it’s its gameplay and level design. There are also several active and passive Image Pulses that you can collect to aid you on your journey. However, if you’re thinking about playing as Gunvolt without having to deal with Kirin, you’ll have no other option but to memorize every single boss pattern and learn to keep GV’s Fetters Gauge at full. You can either use the special Image Pulse that lets you start most of the stages as Gunvolt or unlock D-nizer and Trial Modes to play as him without having to deal with Image Pulses. Although they’re the most ideal ways to play as GV, you’ll still have to deal with Fetters Gauge. In other words, there really isn’t a proper way to play as Gunvolt in a game called Azure Striker Gunvolt 3. What a joke. Speaking of a joke, there’s also a joke ending that you can unlock by collecting every single Image Pulse out there excluding the DLC packs of course. Do you want to go through all that trouble and get mocked by Inti? Go ahead. The future of the series doesn’t look bright, but one can hope regardless. I can only hope that whatever they have in store for us next, won’t be as shallow and disappointing as this one. Although Septima Sealer Kirin offers great things gameplay-wise, it fails to live up to its reputation when it comes to story. If you’re expecting a follow-up to Gunvolt 2’s ending, you won’t find any here. However, if what you’re after is good gameplay with new mechanics, Septima Sealer Kirin won’t disappoint. Sorry, were you looking for the review of Azure Striker Gunvolt 3? Oh, it isn’t out yet.

_childDocuments_.review: The day we've all been patient for, the long awaited Azure Striker Gunvolt 3 is here earlier then expected, now we have all Gunvolt game possibly made, available on Steam. (including the spin-offs series) This game takes place after the mainline games which are Azure Striker Gunvolt 1 & 2, if you haven't played those, no fear since you can play this game & still have an understanding to the story for the most part, it's recommended to play the previous first two games, to know the story precisely. Gamplay: This game introduces a new character Kirin, who uses her sword to slash enemies, similar to a Mega Man Zero, there's a new mechanic to her, you throw talisman on one or multiple enemies, then teleport into them with arc chain to kill them off at once to earn combos points. If you want to grind more points you have to avoid touching the ground similar to Copen's mechanics. You get to learn new moves as you progress each stages. The second character: the main series protagonist Gunvolt aka Azure Striker, plays much differently then in the previous games. Gunvolt is powerful & almost immortal, much like the first two games, you shoot & tag into one or three enemies & use your electric bolts or mimic Kirin's Arc Chain to finish off multiple enemies at once, you no longer have air strikes points & your flashfield is now automatic instead of holding the R Bumper Button, you  can also shoot diagonally, jump infinitely & air dash without equipments. Gunvolt no longer has a health bar instead you now have is this Feather Gauge, which is filled default at 100%, the downside to that is if that meter drains or if you use SP Skill, you will switch back to Kirin meaning you can use Gunvolt temporarily & wait until the meter is back to 100%. Copen (aka Acura) is no longer featured as a playable character here.Scoring & Difficulty: As with every Azure Striker Gunvolt game, (including the Luminous Avenger iX series) you have this Kudos System where if you reach 1K Kudos, Lumen start singing her new Jpop songs in the entire level. Normally if you get hit, you lose all your Kudos & Lumen stops singing however in GV3, they have changed it where if you take damage, your Kudos get locked & you have to earn points to unlock yourself & Lumen continues singing unless you stop grinding points . You are now forced to touch checkpoints bit it doesn't reset your Kudos anymore. GV3 also introduces a new S++ Rank which is a rank higher to S+ Rank, the requirements here are very high as you need to memorize the level & get an almost perfect run in every stage. You also have exclusive SS Rank for Gunvolt only if you equipped the proper image pulse through a gacha roll. The Kudos Mode: Gutless, Cautious & Fearless have now been replaced with Normal, Hard & Very Hard Modes. Conclusion & Thoughts: Overall I like GV3, it's not a perfect game & story could be better written but I did enjoy the story over Luminous Avenger iX2. I wish Kirin's gameplay was less linear & focused more on slashing enemies on ground rather staying on air but it get's the job done. I also wish Gunvolt had a health bar & wasn't so overpowered. The only nitpicks I have is that Gunvolt no longer runs or sprints instead dashes & that they removed the Sumeragi Plasma Legion Tank that was shown on GV3 first trailer. Currently the game is 10% off & you get all the Image Pulse DLC for Free with it if you buy the base game only until October 20th so get it while you can.As a side note, the full game runs much better then the Demo which had random occasional stutters & FPS drops, they are not present here or aren't as noticeable anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, got all the achievements and for the most part mastered the mechanics, don't expect me to be the final boss without cheesing him though :DFirst off, let's get the negatives out of the way.1. No regional pricing. At the end I buckled up and bought the game but this game, as FANTASTIC AS IT IS, is not worth 200 TL. 2. Mega Man Zero style special moves you get from the bosses kind of suck. I only use the upward slash and the spin slash attacks. The former only because it let's me do an extra double jump and the latter because it is a spin slash and I like those.And that's it. Those are the only problems I have with this game. Time for the positives!!!1. Fantastic controls. I always feel like I am in control of the characters, they are so smooth and tight. 2. Arc chain is amazing. THIS was a game mechanic I have been hoping to see in a 2d game for like the last 5 years. FINALLY, a fast and consistent way application! If you know what you are doing, you pretty much don't need to touch the ground ever!3. Arc chain is the main tag mechanic in this game BUT you don't need to tag enemies to kill them quickly in this game, unlike the previous gunvolt games. You do need arc chain to dodge a few boss attacks but you don't need to use it to beat the stages. The same also applies to tagging enemies. Your sword does a good chunk of damage without tagging enemies. FINALLY, a tag mechanic that doesn't limit you playing style!!!4. While the special moves you get from the bosses are quite lackluster, the image pulse mechanic more than makes up for it. You have your active image pulses which can be used to attack enemies or to support Kirin via healing etc... You also have passive image pulses that effect your stats. Overall a really cool and well implemented mechanic.5. Level design, presentation and boss fights are also really great and compliment the mechanics of the game. In conclusion, this is not only my favorite Gunvolt game but also one of my favorite platformers ever. Easily top 5.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not even feels like the next chapter in Gunvolt series. It's more like another spin-off filled with a bunch of weird decisions. Well, at least it's not as bad as iX2.Let's talk about the story first, so skip this paragraph if you want to avoid spoilers. Do you remember how Gunvolt 2 ended? Do you remember Copen, his sister, other characters and cliffhanger at the end? Well, forget about all of that. Because decades have passed since then and Gunvolt somehow turned into a dragon! Well, forget that too - now he's turned into a dog and fights with the adepts who turned into a lesser dragons. Oh wait, forget that as well - now an organization from another country is trying to steal some magic relics to control the almighty baby in order to take over the world! Wait, nevermind - the almighty baby is out of control anyway and now you have to beat it. This is literally the plot of Gunvolt 3. Which, to be honest, isn't that bad, but has nothing to do with the previous games whatsoever. Heck, Gunvolt isn't even the main character here! So I don't understand why this game is called Gunvolt 3 instead of Lightning Priestess Kirin or something.And what about that part where Gunvolt works for Sumeragi? We never saw a single Sumeragi representative through the entire game (except for that confused guy on the tutorial level). No one is forcing us to obey their orders. No one is trying to help us on the missions. No one sabotages our work. No one tries to drag us into some twisted plans. No one betrays us. And we're still fighting Sumeragi troopers and robots (because they went berserk) as if nothing ever changed. It doesn't even looks like Gunvolt is working for Sumeragi at all!Let's take a quick look at other issues:-Wait, what? No regional prices?-Gacha in a singleplayer 2D-platformer... Yeah, I know - GV1 and GV2 have something like a lootbox system, but it was removed in iX. It was a good decision, so I hoped that Intis realized how stupid these random rewards were and removed them once and for all. But now they implemented something even more stupid in GV3. Just wow.-Paid DLCs for those who don't want to waste their time on gacha. Just Inti Creates being greedy again, I guess.-Overpowered and unbalanced Gunvolt, who is not even the main character of this game, but a guest star or something.-No more rewards for high rank - now it's all about gacha.-Bad optimization. My laptop is not the most powerful gaming machine in the world, but I can run previous GV and iX games without any problems. But for some reason GV3 (a pixelated 2D-platformer, by the way) is lagging like crazy.Don't get me wrong - this game is not terrible. Gameplay is fun and dymanic - you can dash through the levels, slaying enemies on the fly. Pixel art and music are good, as always. There is also a lot of fun with new modes, characters, and secret battles after completing the story. So I can understand people who really enjoyed this game. But personally, I can't recommend Gunvolt 3 because of inconsistent plot and issues I listed above.

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt 3 is the most interesting of the series to me because it does a whole lot right but takes the story in a direction that although based on GV himself makes sense will probably bother some people, in fact I have seen it bother fans I know of but honestly speaking it's a bit of an over exaggeration that I feel we need to push past, it's fine, it works, it's very much the ZX of the gunvolt world in fact to a degree only kinda done a bit better character wise, the short of it is it's a great game with awesome gameplay and all around improvements in my eyes dood.Okay onto the detailed part of the review for those who want to know more, so to start you play as the new protag Kirin, who's playstyle although the same as GV in terms of having to tag enemies first is actually more like playing Zero (if you've ever seen the MMZ games if not a melee character rather than a ranged) but insanely fast and manoeuvrable but of course GV still exists with his usual abilities but now more powerful than ever! In a ways, I won't spoil seeing as it's new mechanics, they really changed things up and honestly in a fun way dood.Along with the new characters things were changed, now rather than accessories you have passive effect and attack skills of which they are quite generous in how many you can equip and can have some incredibly handy effects, Kudos no longer go to 0 when hit or using a skill (Fiiiiiinally!) instead they get sealed until you build up enough points to unseal them, this is extra great considering you now have levels of song based on how many kudos you get and how fast, this also means you aren't punished for using prevasion or skills which being main mechanics in the game were always a weird one to punish you for dood.The stages and enemy placements are all well laid out, in such a way in fact you could probably go through an entire level and literally never touch the ground outside of doors and next area points, which is great for score but also speed running a level as you can even go as far as using enemies as literal shortcuts rather than waiting around for moving platforms or the like which can help your score dood.Talking of score ranks are as insane to get as always, maybe hard helps with that but scores outside of achievements mean nothing now which I think is a great change, you don't get more of anything for higher ranks, instead you collect one of 6 items of which will net you three possible passive or attack abilities meaning you can play as casually or slow as you like and not feel punished for not being a speed running pro player who never gets hit like with the prior games dood.Final thing, there's voice acting now and I adore that, I like VA's, doesn't matter how corny they sound, just as long as they don't sound like they don't wanna be there, I think they did a good job on the dub personally but I know not everyone likes dubs XD but they are there and as far as dubs go are decent to good, the music is great too as well as the songs I mentioned prior dood.So yeah that's my review for GV3, if I were to think of fixes I'd say maybe not having the skills on the right stick might be nice but I also get that it's not easy to make that work all that well at times, still the amount of times I activated multiple special attacks when I only wanted to use one was kinda grating I admit, otherwise I can't see anything else I'd call bad, it was a blast of a game and I hope you all think so too if you ever pplay it ^-^7 thanks for reading dood ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: A'ight so lemme just say this, game is fun. If you're thinking of getting it, do it. That's the short story.Now here are my thoughts on the game as a whole as someone who's just recently 100%ed this game and been enjoying the series as a whole since it started.I'm a bit mixed (though mostly positive) towards this game. The gameplay takes some getting used to since it's probably the most fast paced in the series but is on point once you get used to it, the story however will leave you somewhat disappointed if you were looking forward to a follow up to the events of GV2. None of that is followed up on, in fact this game honestly feels like it's a soft reboot for the series, and to make things worse, GV gets shafted in his own game for a new character, Kirin. Now THANKFULLY, I think Kirin is a likeable character and good protag, she also has some fun banter with GV and I think the two make a good duo. They also bounce off what I think is the best supporting cast in the series pretty well once they join you. (#Caymanbestboi) But in the end this does end up making things feel as though this is more HER GAME than Gunvolt's, you can probably see how that'd be an issue when the name of the game is "Gunvolt 3". On top of that the story feels kinda weak and things just "happen" that lead up to the finale. The ending is mid at best too. You pretty much beat the final boss and the game just kinda rushes to the credits. And the true ending doesn't really help in fixing this either and leaves you asking what the heck even just happened. Initially I hated the true ending and thought the bad ending was honestly better, but after a recent update the true ending has been adjusted to provide more context as to what the heck happened. (Although for some reason, in my experience, the game doesn't always play this extra scene that adds said context) With that revealed, I'm more 50/50 towards it since it doesn't really fix anything but does help to confirm a suspicion of mine as to the direction they're going in with the next entry, which if I turn out to be right when Gunvolt 4 releases in 3054, will at least somewhat redeem the weird ending.Now the gameplay, it's honestly pretty great. Kirin's style is basically defeat as many enemies as possible without touching the ground or any walls. Maintaining air time is key to a decent score. This is super fun and all but I do have a nitpick or two. Firstly, I just wanna say that I feel as though Kirin's gameplay could benefit from her having a double jump. This isn't just for maintaining air time either but for avoiding certain attacks and/or some of the level design. Now I know there is an upgrade that grants you one, and there's another that grants unlimited jumping once fully leveled up. (Which is complete overkill btw) However you won't get those until going through the game on very hard mode which isn't unlocked until clearing the game. There are points when playing as Kirin where I feel she should have one by default, or at least unlock it by defeating one of the bosses. But I digress, it's really my only gripe besides some of the level design.[Recommendation: In the "Old Capital Temple" stage on normal difficulty, There is an upgrade that you can get that increases your jump height by 40% and another that increases it by 60%. I recommend trying to get the 40% one 'cause it's honestly perfect for helping with evasion and maintaining airtime while not having you jump too high like the 60% upgrade does. The 40% upgrade in particular also synergizes REALLY WELL with the double jump upgrade once you get it, PERFECT combo if you're going for the coveted S++ rank on every stage]Gunvolt's largely the same as you remember him but with some changes, most notably is that he's invincible now and that he can shoot in 3 directions just like Kirin. What you gotta do is maintain that fetters gauge by going for the type of combos you're used to as GV. That being tagging multiple enemies and then flashfielding them, alternatively you can deal with them the same way Kirin would with his own version of her arc chain. (Kirin's main method of attack) Deciding which to use depending on the stage layout and placements of enemies is key to maintaining and building up your fetters gauge. If you can't do that or get hit too many times, you switch back to Kirin, or get a game over if you're playing D-nizer mode. (Which is a GV only run of the game you can unlock after clearing the game and getting 3 Azure Striker ranks on 3 different stages) Besides that, GV's got some new moves that make him feel like a win button when used. (There are story reasons for this)Now the level/boss design, for the most part I'd say it's good. They seemed to favor vertical level design this time around which is something you don't see too often. But unfortunately this comes with the issue you'd expect from this type of level design... Not all of it's good.. Specifically in regards to the fact that bottomless pits are EVERYWHERE in this game. So much so that they made it so that they're not instant death in this game. I can promise you that you'll probably fall into one on at least 5 occasions in this game. (Most likely towards the end of the game) But I think the worst offenders are the "Stormy Magafloat" and "Megafloat Neptune" stages. (The later in particular is really annoying if you're going for an Azure Striker rank) And the final stages are mostly just bottomless pits. But that's just my opinion, you might find others more annoying over the ones I personally do. I'm also mixed on the boss design, overall I'd say it's fine (with two exceptions who I find very annoying) however most of the bosses don't seem to have any type of attack patterns in this game unlike previous entries, they just kinda throw everything they have at you, making boss fights feel mostly reactionary focused. (ESPECIALLY on hard mode and beyond) Not necessarily a bad thing per se but as someone who likes to re-fight bosses to learn their patterns and eventually start consistently no-hitting them, this becomes kinda impossible and more RNG based. That's my overall thoughts on this game, sorry for the massive 30 page essay, but if you've read until the end then you can tell I have a few thoughts on this game. I'm overall positive towards it, the gameplay is a solid 9 outta 10 for me, the story on the other hand... ehh, I wanna give it a 5 outta 10 but I'll give it a 6 for the adjustment they made to the true ending. With everything now said, if you're still thinking about getting this game after reading my review then do yourself a favor and do it! The gameplay alone is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: As of Blaster Master Zero 3 (with an exception being made for Luminous Avenger iX2 when it started getting review bombed by questionable design choices), , which is the only way many third-world countries with completely assblasted economies can still afford digital media with no extra cost to the publisher whatsoever.After being forced to watch Switch players try the game three months in advance, I was pretty excited to mess around with it myself...only to be given a massive middle finger in the form of  Said realization made me wonder, however:The answer:......yes lmao it's not even difficult my guyDon't take me wrong. The game is tight and I've gone and gotten at least a dozen hours out of every other game in the Gunvolt series, but my experience with these games is not the same as what you'd get from the average player that's just looking for a casual, start-to-finish, don't-bother-with-extra-challenges experience. They'd already get a lot less bang for their buck with the previous pricing, but asking average third-worlder joe to dedicate a chunk out of their monthly income for  over something much longer (like Elden Ring, The Witcher 3/Cyberpunk, Persona 4/5R, Devil May Cry 5 or literally any of the Yakuza games available right now) because daddy Inti Creates wants to squeeze as much money out of piss-poor countries as it can is unreasonable at best, downright mustache-twirling evil at worst.Do you actually want to hear my thoughts on this game? As mentioned before: I think arc chain is a pretty neat mechanic, but that's about as good as it gets with Kirin. I like sword guys. I like Zero. Kirin isn't Zero. She's got a 1-2-3 sword combo, sure, but when you're forced to tag an enemy upwards of six times with your ranged attack (that doesn't do any actual damage on its own) just so you can do optimal damage with (not three, mind you. Just TWO slashes of) your sword, then you're not really getting anything out of these two weapons and curbing player expression as a result.  Cool, right? No. Not really. I mean, he's broken in this game. Unlimited jumps and dashes, high sustained AND burst damage along with the opportunity to kill off bosses before they get to use their desperation moves means he absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥ on Kirin in both platforming AND combat, but that comes with the downside of his time in the field being limited by a gameplay resource. , however, and even if that was fixed, giving you temporary Easy Mode in a game that's already a walk in the park is just not a good mechanic overall.Wanna know what's even MORE braindead than Gunvolt?  The second half of Kirin's arsenal comes in the form of Image Pulses. Abilities coming from, in some way or another, the series' characters that can be Actively or Passively used and are unlocked as you complete stages. So far so good, right? Here's the catch: You don't get to pick and choose your unlocks. At all. Every stage draws its rewards from its own separate pool and the most you can do to maximize your chances to obtain the Image Pulses you want is collect the few medals hidden across each stage, which give you exactly one extra gacha pull per medal. Didn't get what you wanted? Play the stage again. Collect the medals. AGAIN. Did I mention the Image Pulse DLC packs? Go check 'em out. It'll be funny.Despite its flaws, I think there's some real good stuff here. Not nerfing Kirin's movement options (which was a thing that happened with Copen in iX2) or at least giving you ways to deal optimal damage to enemies besides "tag, tag, tag, tag, tag, tag>slash, slash" would go a long way in giving players different ways to express themselves with the current gameplay loop. Needless to say, the old rewards system needs to go. It doesn't work when your end of level rewards are Image Pulses, but I'll take a revamp too since that'll probably cost them less money and they're oh-so poor~Game's tight. Maybe I'll try out the extra challenges when I can own it for more than two hours, but I doubt that'll happen anytime soon. Who knows! I'll update when that's the case!

_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt 3 is... a mixed bag, to say the least. It has both the highest highs and the (debatably) lowest lows in the franchise, and this review would mostly be for people who are already familiar with the series.For those who have zero knowledge of the series, just get the game it's peak 2D actionThis title has the best gameplay the Gunvolt series has ever seen, taking design experience not only from itself, but I'm guessing from Megaman Zero also to flesh out the new character's playstyle (iirc they also brought in the gameplay director of Bloodstained to work on this game.) The result is a playstyle as explosive as Copen from Gunvolt 2 and iX 1, while increasing the depth of combat to bring forth the hardest bossfights this series has ever had. I won't go deeper into it, just be aware that the game allows for a lot of skill expression and replay value as this is the first Gunvolt game that allows you to change your character to the degree of allowing various approaches to playstyle.Most of my (and the community's) gripes would come from the fact that the story, one of the most important things when it comes to Gunvolt, get thrown out of the window. As a standalone story, Gunvolt 3 is... not that awful, I guess, but when taken as a package it used timeskip to just abandon all story elements set up in the materials preceding it. And that's such a shame when Gunvolt 3 managed to get so many other things in the story right. Gunvolt feels more like a real person and less of a generic shounen anime protag when we actually get to see how he views his past actions for once. _childDocuments_.review: Was on the fence about reviewing this one since I'd give this a mixed review if that was an option on this platform, but I'm leaning negative and most of these reviews are positive so I figured I'd at least give a different perspective. This is my first and only Gunvolt game. I got it on a whim when I was browsing the store and noticed that the new Gunvolt had ditched Gunvolt as the protagonist. Awesome, he looked bland anyways. Decent chance to try another Inti Creates title. The story was able to set me up pretty well despite having no clue who any of these people were. It's pretty disconnected from whatever else is going on in the Gunvolt verse since it's set 200 years in the future. The introduction stage was good overall, and was capped off with the sort of slower paced boss I can appreciate and learn the moves of. After the first stage, the game quickly lost me.The story in particular is not something I could enjoy at all. It's the sort of basic anime trite I can't stand. Outside of the main characters, Kirin & Gunvolt (more on that later), I don't even remember any of their names or character designs.  (or just the bare minimum, like Dr. Wily has 8 evil robots go beat them up sort of thing).As for the gameplay, Kirin is actually really fun to play as.  The chain teleports are also super cool, I loved marking enemies, doing a teleport stab, and then marking more enemies and doing it again without even landing. Of course the game constantly adds new moves to her moveset after completing stages in some rather stilted dialogue, like an upwards attack and a downwards attack. I'm not sure how many of them there were, I honestly couldn't keep track and thought the basic moveset was good already so I mainly stuck with that.And then there's Gunvolt. I'm honestly disappointed he's even in this game. From the trailer on the store page, I figured he was broken, but I assumed he'd be around in a more limited capacity. He's actually just a "Win Level" button that you can easily activate just by playing the game, or even waiting around if you have the patience for it. He's invincible, has infinite jumps, and does a ton of constant damage by auto-targeting marked enemies. You'll switch back to Kirin after his meter runs out, but he's easily enough to bypass every challenge the game throws at you without even trying. And if he wasn't enough, there's also a Vocaloid fairy that revives you and lets you beat bosses even if they literally just killed you. Besides the first boss, I never learned any of the enemy patterns because I didn't need to. Gunvolt and the revival crush boss battles for you. And even without them, I got a bunch of healing assists for Kirin that made it pretty damn hard to die no matter how bad I was playing with her.So I ended up finishing the game feeling... meh. For the price point, compared to other games that are absolute steals, it doesn't match up in the "Fun per dollar" metric whatsoever for me. But I still don't *hate* this game. Because Kirin's moveset is so damn cool.  So no Gunvolt win button, just stick with Kirin and play the floor is lava. I'm debating replaying this and doing exactly that. I imagine all the Gunvolt veterans ironically enough knew not to use Gunvolt and that's why they all had a better time than me. I suppose you'll be able to tell if my playtime for this ever updates. Of course with how insufferable I find the story and characters, that might be a while.

_childDocuments_.review: It might be weird not to play as Gunvolt much in his own mainline game, but man is Kirin's gameplay fun. In a similar way to Copen in Gunvolt 2, I think I like playing as Kirin more than Gunvolt. The story feels tangential to previous games but the cast as a whole is much more lively than either Gunvolt 1 or 2. It's a relatively short game if you just intend to play through the main story, but it’s packed with extras that can take a lot of time and effort to complete for even the most skilled of players. Generally, you'll enjoy this game the most if you engage with its scoring and ranking system. This pushes you to play the game in the most fun way - flying through stages without touching the ground. Outside of that, there's an , , extra stages, a boss rush, , time trials, , , and more. If you have even a passing interest in action-platformer games, you'd be doing yourself a disservice not to check out this game (and by extension, the rest of the Gunvolt series).Edit; While I recommend this game, I thought it prudent to also list my gripes with it. The most glaring issue is the means by which you earn Image Pulses (this game’s equipment). These are obtained randomly at the end of each stage depending on how many collectibles you found within it. In concept, this shouldn’t be too different to materials and medals in Gunvolt 1 and 2, but in execution it‘s tedious at best. The Image Pulse DLC packs are egregious in that they have no reason to be excluded from the main game. For a game titled “Azure Striker Gunvolt 3”, it is disappointing that there is no way to play as Gunvolt as he was in the previous games. You can only play a new, powered-up Gunvolt with infinite jumps, infinite air dashes, angled shots, altered Flashfield, Arc Chain, no SP, and no equipment, . .

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite part of the series, including all spin-offs.The new playable character, Kirin, is a blast to control. She combines bullit dashes and Gunvolt moveset to end up with a very fun gameplay style. You have good sword attacks, which after unlocks can combo almost like Megaman Zero games. You have thunder dashes into enemies tagged by talismans, and you can recover talismans while in air for infinite air time (as long as you're not getting hit). All unlockable moves are cool and useful.Instead of only unlocking boss moves you now get random skills at the end of the stage. I believe getting A or better on a stage always gives you the boss skill. The random skills you can get can be active attacks or passives or songs for your Muse. You can setup up to 4 active skills at a time and they have cooldown before they can be used again. Many of them are not too useful though.I am not a big fan of this gatcha-like mechanic for collecting upgrades. I was constantly getting the same things, which would be changed into upgrade currency. After beating the game with true ending you can use harder modes to get other upgrades, but it is still random. You can increase the amount of random skills you get by getting good enough score to have boss get additional phase, and by collecting all collectibles on the level. Still, it's random what you get, so you're expected to play a lot to collect them all. Still, there's a lot of variety so you can do a lot of builds, even if you don't unlock everything.The game follows typical for gunvolt formula of 1-4-1-4-1-4-x stages. The boss designs are quite forgetable, but for once you get side-characters that I might not forget before the next game.I like that the boss rush at the end is using different bosses than the ones you meet in this game. Getting true ending in this game is probably the easiest in the whole series, but you still might need to read online how to do it.While your main character is Kirin you get access to Gunvolt very early, and can use him in every stage. But he is almost god-mode, and using him means you get very little Kudos. The game sometimes will warn you that upcoming section is very hard and you should play as Gunvolt, but I didn't.The Kudos system also was changed (again), and at least on normal it never resets. You can activate checkpoints, get hit, whatever. Getting hit provides small penalty, where you get locked out of getting new kudos until you gather enough kudos to break the "kudo lock". It means even bad player like me can always activate Muse songs.They also removed all instant-death attacks and traps, at least on Standard difficulty. Spikes do almost no damage, falling off does only few percent of damage and teleports you to last place you stood at. I don't think any boss had an instant-kill. I haven't played on harder difficulties, so I can't say for sure.This game works almost flawlessly on Steam Deck. The only issue I had was small graphical glitch during introduction of the last boss. But I had to check on PC to make sure, since the glich could have been on purpose, considering what was happening.The story is OK. Probably OKayer than the rest of the series. I don't play this game for the story, but for once the chat with your pals between missions were fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Something strange has started happening in the Gunvolt universe's games. We saw it first with iX 2, then this game. I think a lot of people are overlooking the strange shift in story here, since unlike with iX 2, the gameplay for this one is very enjoyable. Unfortunately for me, the story is something I do hold dear.In iX 2 we got a strange isekai adventure where the only real tie back to the mainline world was that there were characters who had their own alternate universe versions there.In GV 3 we get decades passing by only for adepts to start turning into dragons? Then, in a very convenient fashion, we get a character who can seal that power with her own septima.Both of these are massive shifts from what we had in GV 1, GV 2, and iX 1. After some more thinking, I realized it's even a shift from many of Inti Creates' previous works. Inti Creates' has managed to create some great stories where race and class conflicts are at the core of the story, and the ways people are motivated to do things for or against that conflict.Mega Man Zero takes place in a setting where fully sapient robots are sacrificed to provide humans with the energy they desire, and you fight to end that pointless slaughter. Dragon Marked for Death follows a survivor of a dragon tribe and his goal to kill the king of the nation that slaughtered his people.We see similar things in the Gunvolt universe as well: GV 1 has Gunvolt fighting the Sumeragi Group which is attempting to control all adepts for public safety, but at the cost of freedom. GV 2 has Gunvolt fighting Eden which is trying to make a nation of adepts for adepts in order to oppose the rest of humanity. iX 1 has Copen/Acura fighting the new Sumeragi Group which has, for all intents and purposes, created that country Eden wanted to make, and after all this time, powerless humans have become a discriminated against minority.Unfortunately, it seems like Inti Creates is moving away from the story archetypes that worked well for them and these games, and now, their games feel more like strange fanfiction or side game stories rather than the main games they're supposed to be. It's a shame, but it seems like they want to move away from those types of stories and now they're floundering.I could point out many more specific issues, like how this is a Gunvolt game where Gunvolt doesn't have his own playable story missions, but I think all the real issues in this and iX 2 can be traced back to this single shift.That's why I have to give this a negative and hope we'll see better in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I said in my Luminous Avenger iX2 review where that game did raise my expectations for where this was going. And for the most part, yeah. Most of this review is going to be based on my time playing it on the Switch but I don't think there's too much different (outside of a small tid bit at the end and some... Odd instances of slow down on that system) so yeah if you see baby hours at the time of review that's why.GV3 delivers on being a high octane action platformer with the traditional tagging mechanic still intact and with a new protagonist in Kirin bringing her own take on it with close ranged sword combat also. There is something to be said about every Gunvolt game and the flow state you get into once you're familiar with the mechanics and are able to effectively tag enemies and both characters carry that extremely well.Visually the game is definitely one of Inti's finest looking games and in terms of audio the music is a banger from the stage themes and even the J-Pop for when you rack up a high amount of kudos from comboing from enemy to enemy.Top marks overall for having a good amount of replayable modes and features from harder difficulties, to an alternative Kirin playstyle and dedicated Gunvolt mode after beating the game also on top of equipment or "Image Pulses" in this game allowing you to be creative in terms of how you play. The game still has more content to come including a game mode called "Epilogue ATEMS" which aims to make a character named Zed playable... So far previews for that mode have been rough but at the time of writing I do have faith in it being fun in its own way......All the positives being said though, the game does drop the ball pretty hard in some slight yet meaningful ways especially if you're a fan of this series. First up, Gunvolt himself in the main story is more like a hyper mode than being one of the main characters to play. Despite this game being named Azure Striker Gunvolt 3, you're going to be playing as Kirin more than Gunvolt himself. This is mainly due to a story and mechanic perspective where Gunvolt is now pretty overpowered whenever he isn't a dog (yeah the dog in the banner is Gunvolt... Even the story tells you to roll with it). I do enjoy Kirin and I have really enjoyed Gunvolt in the past. While I do enjoy playing him here... Part of me does kinda wish there was some sort of nerfed Gunvolt option to play about like the previous 2 games.And secondly the story... Now there's definitely people here that will say you should not care for the story because of the series or whatever. I personally think that's a complete disservice to Inti and others that have interest in this series. I mean yeah this is a series with over the top anime tropes but traditionally the prior 2 Gunvolt games (even both iX games) weave in some pretty neat concepts, even if it's not too apparent or it is within a trope. Sometimes the most enjoyable stories aren't as deep as some highly regarded RPG stories.That being said though... Gunvolt 3 really drops the ball in story. I must stress first that it isn't the characters or banter that bring them down (though Story Mode + might be annoying enabled, more on that later) but more like despite the 3 there is not much connecting the previous games outside of Gunvolt, other not-so-present connections and the Image Pulses. The cliff hanger of Gunvolt 2's secret ending is just completely dropped and a certain character who probably should appear just doesn't despite everything feeling like it should... The ending itself is also one of the most endings of all time, true Morbius/10 material in those last moments.Story Mode + is also here again from the previous games. There are more options to tweak it to have it enabled with nothing cluttering the screen or at least be vaguely transparent, but primarily for English players it will definitely hinge on whether they are fluent in Japanese or if they are fine with the dub voices... Look I appreciate the fact the games are getting dubs now and for the record, this dub is better than iX 2's... By like the SLIMMEST margin of Gunvolt's dub voice being great but most of the other voices drop the ball in seemingly insignificant but (I think) very meaningful ways. I understand Inti isn't really fortunate in getting a lot of big voices but I do feel they should at least try pushing the dub actors/actresses they get harder to at least be on par or unique in the right ways.Despite some of the pains this game does give to long time fans, I still think Gunvolt 3 is still a truly great game. I will definitely be playing this game a fair lot to get as many S++ ranks as I can. I will probably goof off with the different Image Pulses to set up a challenge or just meme on a level for fun. I definitely hope for Gunvolt 4 they take what worked in this game and apply it to a more well balanced Gunvolt for next time. And of course, I'll still probably be simping for Kirin in many regards.Excuse me for I am about to morb out now.

_childDocuments_.review: Azure Striker Gunvolt 3, what praises can I not say about this game.If you have played any previous Gunvolt game, without a doubt you will enjoy this game. Compared to every game in the series the only one I feel even comes close in Gunvolt 2. Speaking of which, this game also has two (later updated to be 3 in a separate campaign) playable characters. Kirin and Gunvolt take up the main game and ZedΩ takes over the epilogue. Kirin by far is my favorite character to play as, both movement and combat wise taking many more notes from Megaman Zero and streamlining Copen's gameplay. Instead of a dash like Copen, she fires a projectile and once locked on the can instantly move next to the target dealing damage and it creates the most flow state like gameplay yet. Also like Copen, Kirin is able to augment her abilities and use other's abilities to aid her in battle with some of the later more completionist abilities being insanely strong.Even the story this time around, while still leaving a few minor holes, fleshes out the cast of characters the most even most if not all the bosses. Characterization like this has only been in supplemental material that isn't the easiest thing to experience in the west. All of the characters were great and the English Dub, unlike iX2 in my opinion, is fantastic; Sean Chiplock as Gunvolt being a real highlight for me. I only turned on the dub to try it out, but ended up playing the whole game with it. I seriously think you're missing out on some good moments without it.The epilogue story is kind of whatever to me though. The bonus story content is great sure, but ZedΩ gameplay, even if it is similar to Kirin and GV, lacks a good flow to it making it much harder that it should be. Maybe that was intentional, maybe I just never figured it out due to it's shorter length. At the end of the day, the epilogue is mostly a play it once for story kind of thing for me.As an added bonus to this review, I played a majority of this game on a Steam Deck and can say it is a great way to play the game with zero issues and good battery life performance; somewhere around 4 hours on a full charge.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Gunvolt is so powerful in this one they have to put a limited meter on him and also make him the potential game over condition.Very fun, very replayable, story complaints really aren't that bad. My only issue is that skill image pulses don't serve much purpose :vI like the new playable character so far. Very fun way to reiterate on Copen's "the floor is lava" design philosophy, featuring a mix of melee and ranged combat that is easier to swallow than iX2's Razor Wheel (though I will gladly defend iX2's approach to mixing ranged and melee any day of the week).Making GV a character you temporarily swap to allows the game to make The Azure Striker absolutely stark bonkers overpowered (more so than usual), which is cool lore-wise, but a little deflating when your Gunvolt meter runs out if you're not saving it for a boss fight or something.I understand the people that want more GV-centric gameplay, and to that I say, did you know GV2 has extra challenge stages in the "runner modes" menu featuring the bosses from 1? They're very cool.Back to 3 tho, I think Image Pulse is kind of a meme, novel idea, but it halfway through the game, it hardly feels it brings substantial changes to score-attack gameplay, it's a neat idea for casual play, but way more negligeable than the collectibles in 1 or 2 like a double jump or air dash. I find it as substantial as something like the stickers in Super Smash Bros Brawl, very minor variables that don't contribute to the whole equation in the long run.I'm sure DLC image pulses and late game ones let you snap the game in half, I did see a video of someone wiping the boss rush mode one command grab at a time, lol.I often hear the biggest complaint being about the story, and while I can parse a few already, like the game being more of a soft-reboot doing its own thing while ditching loose ends and themes found in the previous games. Half-way through the game, I remain cautiously optimistic, Gunvolt's characterization is intact and is supplemented by the supporting cast pretty well (though the dogvolt banter can be a little one-note sometimes), and after witnessing the character assassination fiasco that was Bayonetta 3, Gunvolt acting like Gunvolt in a Gunvolt setting is good enough for me.Also the music and graphics still slap.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so as a sequel to an established series, I feel this is disappointing and should've been the start of another spin-off series.But change of gameplay/narrative direction aside, this was easily my favourite in the series.So to address some of the notable changes, let's address the plot real quick.And as for the gameplay, it's less run n' gun and more the floor is lava.Tagging is still a major part of the gameplay, but instead of shooting up enemies, you instead jump to tagged enemies to take 'em down *mostly* instantly with your sword.Copen was already a big change for Gunvolt 2, but he was atleast optional unless you were going after the minor gameplay bonus that was the true ending, not to mention he had his own stages, adding a lot of content.Maybe Kirin will get her own spinoff series like he did, and this game could be the stepping stone for that, but as a Gunvolt game, it's mostly something else.To further address gameplay changes that prior fans might've liked, the Kudos system has changed a fair bit.Kudos is no longer lost upon getting hit, instead when you take damage, you get a lock on your score, basically nullifying an amount of point gain until the lock is broken. So while getting hit is still something you don't want to do, it is no longer an all or nothing/no hit kind of scenario, though stages still take a fair bit of effort to S++.Lastly, Gunvolt is a playable character, to an extent.You can choose to swap to him for a limited duration of time, and he's absolutely busted.With infinite jumps, air dashes, absurd damage and his classic tag n' flash action, this boy has never been stronger.But because he's so busted, and limits kudos build up due to being so busted, I found I only used him on bosses, and due to how they're designed and with how flashy GV is, it's kind of hard to see what bosses are doing, but that means very little when you have so much mobility and damage to deal with them.With that out of the way, onto the good stuff.I absolutely adore the way Kirin moves! Tagging enemies to instantly jump into them with talismans feels fantastic. It's an incredibly fast pace that treats enemies as more of a tool for movement than an actual threat, which feels really fun, especially when regular enemies in this series were never a threat.As mentioned before, the main way you accumulate kudos is to never touch to floor.Stages are designed in a way where while you can ride platforms, jump up walls, etc., they instead want you to jump between enemies to stay airborne until the stages forces you to use your legs.Gone are gear slots/materials, in favour of upgrades similar to what Zero would get such as downwards spin attacks, an upwards slash to help stay airborne, upgraded dashing options, just extra utility/moves to make stage replays more enjoyable and overall, far more natural extensions to your kit compared to the different guns Gunvolt had.But as another replacement for materials, there is oddly enough, a gacha-esque system, where you pick up items in the stage and collect mimics of former/current characters for more buffs like reduced damage, increased kudos, etc.Not bad, but not great, just kind of there to make things easier.To comment of thematics for a bit, the music's pretty great, not much more to say other than I found some of the variety of vocal themes was quite nice.And while I think the story may be lame and a waste of what the prior two games built up, I found the cast quite nice. They're nothing amazing but unlike the prior GV games, there is actually a fair amount of dialogue for them with defined personalities/relations. Seeing them in stages fighting in the background also makes them feel like they're more than just JPEGS that show up to give plot exposition.Lastly, and this is a big plus I wish GV2 had from the start.Story+ lets you disable the pop-up windows for dialogue mid-stage, even if it's your first run through.Though assuming you have story+ enabled, you don't have to read everything anymore, as there is now an english dub if you so choose to use it.Overall, while this may be a step away from the traditional Gunvolt gameplay, the core of building up Kudos and speeding through stages is still there.My only hope is that this is the start of a Kirin series similar to what Copen got with Luminous iX, but disregarding its status as a main entry aside, I had an absolute blast with this game, and I yearn to get S++ on these stages.Really fun game, I can recommend it even if it's your first time with the Gunvolt series.P.S. Postgame stuff

_childDocuments_.review: So far I've cleared the main story including getting the true ending, and I've cleared the bonus epilogue episode "Episode ATEMS" through it's story. Although a small portion of this time was spent replaying levels for fun, the whole process took me about 7 hours. I will not be spoiling the story in this review.The first thing I need to address here is regional pricing. The game was about $30 for me, but I've heard reports of the price being quite bloated in some countries. I am not aware of whether this issue has been resolved yet, but if you live somewhere where the price is absurdly high I can only recommend waiting for it to drop to somewhere more reasonable.Right off the bat, I had to configure my controller. Unfortunately, this proved to be the biggest inconvenience the game has to offer. The in-game configure tool is far too sensitive, making it something of a pain to configure my analog sticks properly. I had to go into the options menu and reconfigure multiple times due to this issue. For additional context, I use a Dualshock 4 through Steam Input, so I'm not sure if that contributed to the issue. Once I finally got it configured correctly however, I had no controller related issues from then on.The main playable character Kirin feels like a combination between multiple different playstyles Inti-Creates has worked on in the past. Her sealing talismans that she uses to lock onto opponents have a limited ammo supply similar to Copen's Bullits from previous Gunvolt and iX games. Also similar to Copen and GV2 in general, she can "reload" by pressing down twice while grounded. They will also restore themselves over time automatically, however if you have prevasion activated and it saves you from taking a hit, you will use up ammo that will not restore itself automatically, forcing you to reload.As for the ammunition itself, you can throw the sealing talismans straight forward, diagonally up, and diagonally down. This will do two things if it hits an enemy. First, it tags the enemy, allowing you to press a secondary attack button to instantly zip over to the enemy and attack them. If you choose not to attack them this way immediately, you can keep hitting them with talismans to increase the amount of damage that will be done, with most regular enemies being able to be one shotted this way. Sometimes it's better just to tag them once for speed and mobility reasons however.Kirin also has a sword that she uses for melee attacks. This is similar to Zero's Z-Saber from the Mega Man X and Zero series, or even Copen's Quick Razor from iX 2. You could also include the Empress from Dragon Marked For Death in this comparison if you wish. However, it most closely resembles Zero's gameplay, including the ability to learn additional attacks with it by defeating bosses. These also sometimes count as mobility buffs, so you can make good use of them even when there's no enemies around.Gunvolt himself is playable, but he exists as a sort of limited super power mode. You can swap to him at any time as long as his meter is at least 100% full. 100% is not the highest percentage, which isn't very intuitive at first, but it basically just amounts to something similar to like Super Sonic in the Sonic games where you need to collect 50 rings to transform, and then lose rings over time. He plays similarly to previous games, but is fully powered by default allowing him to jump around and dash infinitely. He even borrows a bit from Copen in that his dash can now target enemies so you can damage them. His dash is nowhere near as quick or far reaching as Copen's however, so you'll be making more use of the abilities he borrows from Kirin for mobility.Like previous Gunvolt and iX games, you collect "Kudos" or score from defeating enemies. Taking a hit will put you in the negative, but you get some wiggle room to work your way back up out of the negative to resume raising your score. At 1000 you will activate a muse state in which you get buffed somewhat while a song plays. This will last for quite a while. I assume that like previous titles there's also a random chance for this to activate on death, reviving you. However, I actually found it quite easy to not die in this game on regular difficulty and have not yet tried the higher difficulties, so I can't outright confirm this through experience.The most refreshing change, I think, is the rework to the upgrades system. It incorporates a sort of lootbox system in which you unlock upgrades through random chance from a pool attributed to each individual level. There are no microtransactions attributed to this system, you simply get to do another attempt at the end of each stage for a chance at what you want. It does however appear that the DLC for this game adds more possible rewards to the pool, I have not yet grabbed the DLC so I cannot say much about it yet.You still collect in-game money in this game, but you do not use it to create crafting materials or anything like that. Instead, it is used directly on any upgrades you have to upgrade them even further. In the bonus episode, you can also use it to unlock the upgrades to begin with.The game also features an English Dub option similar to iX 2. It's not the best voice acting in the world, but it's generally quite competent and gets the job done very well. It can be a bit cheesy at times, but I generally consider this a bonus. It adds to the campy "power of friendship" vibes the game is going for. Overall, I enjoy it. If you do not want it however, it can simply be disabled.All things considered, this is easily the most content heavy game in the series so far. Easily worth the $30 I paid for it. If you're a fan of these games or other games Inti has made in the past, this is an easy recommend. If you even just like 2D platformers, I'd say give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome, Fun, Fast Action Platformer. Combat has a unique style of Tagging enemies with ranged attacks and teleporting to them with your melee attacks (Arc Chain). The stages/enemy placements are set up in a way to make you think the floor is lava once you get used to this system. Air control feels really good and aerial actions/attacks go well with score combo chaining/killing enemies/platforming. The bosses are fast paced and have a clear moveset you'll need to learn to avoid getting hit.Mastering the stages/mechanics of the game is really fun, it feels satisfying to go to the next area without touching the ground if possible. Theres a Hardmode which enhances the bosses movesets. Passive And active skills exist in this game, you can basically use boss attacks or npcs attacks in combat, passives are really strong and open up new playstyles for scoring or just becoming very overpowered in mobility/combat. Theres a few characters to play as too, even though 1 of them is a reskin. Music is nice if you like anime opening songs i guess. Amazing game overall if you like Action Platformer genre, Arc Chain is such a fun system you'll zip zoom all over the place.

_childDocuments_.review: ...Why is Gunvolt a dog? Why is there a massive time skip? What is GOING ON in the screen most of the time? All important questions. I'm led to believe that this game is a mess, and doesn't feel like a suitable evolution of Gunvolt 2 or even Avenger iX2's gameplay, but it's still fun. Especially when you really figure out the mechanics. You kind of have to turn your brain off and accept this game's dialogue and anime...stuff. The screen is cluttered, especially when there's dialogue text on screen. The core gameplay is solid, but it has baffling mechanics: gacha system to unlock passive and active skills, Gunvolt is locked behind a time limited system and he's overpowered for no reason, the kudos system seems to be the easiest and most non-challenging one yet, the dialogue during boss fights is incredibly distracting to the point of being unfun. The story is also absurd, even if you've played all the Gunvolt games.I do feel that beneath a lot of the zany-ness is a deep, action platformer like previous Gunvolt games, but there's just so much GOING ON sometimes that it's hard to feel it. Gunvolt himself is basically god-mode + win button, which is SUCH a strange choice. Gone is the compact moment-to-moment gameplay of GV1 and 2, or even iX1, we're in GV3's world now. It's not all negative - the visuals are solid, the PC performance is good, voice acting is decent, music is great, and it's nice to be playing a Gunvolt game again. But man, I kind of wish it wasn't carried by that - it's an experience game primarily, quality game secondary. I'd argue that it's a better 2nd playthrough game, cause you can ignore story, dialogue and just focus on mastering the mechanics, it's more fun that way.If you were expecting a coherent story, a challenging experience, or even a sequel to Gunvolt 2, this honestly isn't it. But it is a fun anime action platformer with good jams. Take from that what you will.

None of these questions get answered really, and the story for this game is, at face value, very bland and uninspired.The gacha system, god the gacha system. Spend 4-10 minutes per stage, collecting a bunch of pointless trinkets so you have, if you're lucky, up to 5 chances to get random image pulses, most of which you won't use at all. The fact that the pool of IPs available in each stage has a ton of overlap, and that you'll probably just settle for the handful you come across, deincentivizes collecting the macguffins at all after a while. _childDocuments_.review: I played the Switch version for 25 hours prior to writing this review.I'm not really a fan of Gunvolt, I only like this game and Luminous Avenger iX. Gunvolt (the character) is really dull to play and I hate him. Thankfully Inti agrees so, after being cucked out of two-and-a-half games by Copen, he's been captured by Sumeragi, put into a machine and used to power the electrical grid for thirty years before— completely inexplicably— getting turned into a talking dog. Now he's your little pet and while you can swap with him at will so long as you have enough meter, you won't want to (unless you just want to push over the bosses) because he can't score as much. Instead, you're playing as Kirin, who is a ninja and a... a... g-g-girl?! *heart starts pounding out of chest like old cartoon*The gameplay this time is that you tag enemies using talismans and you press a button to teleport to the enemies you tagged in sequential order, either killing or damaging them depending on enemy HP and number of tags placed per enemy, before ending up on either side of the final enemy you tagged. Each time you use this teleport attack you regain one aerial jump. The objective is to stay in the air as much as possible to maintain a score multiplier, while taking as little damage as possible and finishing within the par time for the maximum time bonus (although this is less important than previous games, it's pretty lax). Bosses take a more traditional approach with attack patterns that you need to learn and more of an emphasis on your standard sword attacks, but they do force you to use your ability to teleport across to the screen to evade attacks. The biggest difficulty is your lack of a basic ranged attack which, in combination with the heavy score penalty for taking hits when you have a lot of score built up, makes for some violent incidents of gamer rage as any boss movement can suddenly screw you if you don't anticipate it. (Also, at the higher end, boss difficulty in this game is crazy. I'll beat merciless mode this time, I swear...)Overall this is a fast-paced game that relies on reflexes first and then memorisation as you replay levels for rank, and there aren't any really obtuse or weird mechanics that you need to read up online; as such, it's about as fun on a first playthrough as it is on subsequent plays and, although you could accuse the game of lacking depth, it piles on just about enough gimmicks to work. It helps that the levels are short. It's very easy to get put into a "one more go" mentality and then you find yourself trying to S++ a level for like an hour.Anyway, this game is nice and you should play it. Also Luminous Avenger iX (the first one). I hope they make a Luminous Avenger iX 3 and that it doesn't suck ass this time.edit: Having played for longer, this game is my favourite game this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed all achievements and fought all bonus bosses. S++ Ranks on almost all Hard Difficulty stages, with Hardest completed on almost every stage. Spoilers kept to a minimum in this review, no plot mentions.Amazing game, even though it very much is not a GV game. Playing as Gunvolt is a powerup only (aside from a special mode) and he has a constantly draining meter, and use of him reduces your Kudos gain compared to the wholly capable Kirin. Kirin is very very air focused, having access to a homing attack, named Arc Chain, that requires tagging with a high-velocity aimable projectile, and a double jump after each homing attack, as well as sword slashes which are pretty much window dressing. She can stock up damage by tagging the same enemy up to 7 times, or splitting those tags among as many enemies as she wishes, and then cash it all in with either a slash or Arc Chain. She gains her Kudos in a mixed method between Copen and GV, having a multiplier up to 4x for staying in the air between kills, and a linear Kudos bonus when killing multiple enemies at once with Arc Chain or her slashes. She also has a screen-nuking super attack similar to Copen, although notably it doesn't turn in Kudos. The right stick is dedicated to using Skill Image Pulses, which are equippable attacks or perks that have independent cooldowns. However, you almost always just want to use these for Healing, as damaging ones will not grant you Kudos. That being said, I hear there's one that can instant kill almost any boss...How do you get Image Pulses? Gacha, of course! Don't be afraid, the gacha system in this game has no pay to win elements (aside from DLC which adds new, powerful Image Pulses which are almost all worthless anyway). Instead of collecting Medals to get more materials like in GV1 and GV2, you can collect Image Chips throughout each stage, with most stages having 7. Collect 2 for a pull, collect them all for a bonus. Additionally, making it to the boss while above 7000 Kudos will usually cause the boss to revive for a bonus phase, and defeating the boss after that happens will give you an additional pull for a total of up to 5. You can get Skill Image Pulses, Passive Image Pulses that act as the equipment for this game, and Song Image Pulses which allow you to guarantee specific songs will play when you reach 1000 Kudos and 4000 Kudos.Speaking of Kudos, there aren't Kudos options in this game like previous installments. You have 1 Kudos mode, which, while you can't lose all of your Kudos without actually dying, causes you to receive a "Kudos Lock" when taking damage, which prevents you from gaining more Kudos until you pay off the Kudos Lock. Locks have higher values the more Kudos you already have, to a minimum of 10. I'd honestly prefer this system going forward, even if it has some flaws, as Kudos modes often prevented any mistakes whatsoever, and with a screen size and movement speed like the GV series, and an in-built mechanic to accommodate that doesn't play well with scoring, I'd prefer rankings being too lenient over too brutal to ever complete.My primary gameplay complaints are game length (which is obvious for an Inti Creates game tbh) and a lack of reason to use Gunvolt.GV is incredibly powerful, but I would've appreciated more ways to boost his damage output, as how it stands he's completely outpaced by a buffed up Kirin while also giving less Kudos.Additionally, not being able to switch out the LVL 3 Kudos theme to something else gets old very quickly, especially when certain Image Pulses give you insane Kudos generation (upwards of 100% bonus) causing you to spend most stages with >7000 Kudos for over half of them. "Traces" is an amazing song, but I wish "Memoria of He", "Ergo Sum", and returning songs like "Azure Door" and "Beyond the Blue", or even the level themes themselves got more spotlight without literally sacrificing damage output (there's an Image Pulse that gives an INSANE damage boost with LVL 3 Kudos, and its damage seems to be nullified if you have Mute Image pulses on to prevent "Traces" from playing). It takes 30 seconds at most for a buffed-up Kirin to reach 1000 Kudos in any given stage, and from then on it's all Lumen singing. Heck, even an option for a Song Image Pulse for Lola to switch out the singer would've been appreciated. All of this stacked on top of the new Kudos mechanics causing it to be incredibly difficult to actually lose your Kudos makes the entire soundtrack effectively null and void, but rest assured, it's good. Can you expect anything less than greatness from an Inti Creates soundtrack?All in all, I'm really looking forward to where this series goes moving forward, especially if we get another split series with Kirin similar to Luminous Avenger iX, as her playstyle is incredibly fun. Similarly to Copen, however, she really stretches the definition of the Platformer genre...PS: For some reason, this relatively graphically tame game lags on my device quite a bit in certain segments, especially when hooked with Discord. Not docking points for it, optimization for cross-platform games tends to be a bit sloppy nowadays. Make sure you surpass the Recommended system requirements listed on the store page, and not the Minimum, or you might experience slowdown in an already incredibly floaty game, causing the experience to be even easier than it already is.

_childDocuments_.review: You know what's weird? Gunvolt has my least favourite playstyle in the Gunvolt franchise.It's funny how far the series has...I wanted to say "evolved" but I'm not sure that's accurate. What used to be a fairly-paced Mega Man X-like where you jump, shoot, and electrify enemies to beat them, has now become a turbo Vergil festival.Kirin, the new protag, uses a sword and talismans instead of a gun and volts. Unlike Luminous Avenger iX 2, however, they kept the name Gunvolt for this game, because you can still play as Gunvolt technically; you know, if you really want to. Anyways, Kirin's talismans are used to tag enemies, but not quite in the same manner as Gunvolt used to; for every talisman that an enemy is hit with, a portion of their HP is "marked", and Kirin can then hit them with her sword to deal all of that marked damage at once. It's like if I shot you in the face seven times but you don't feel anything until I kick you in the shin.That's until the end of the intro stage. Once she meets up with Gunvolt and gives him a smooch (actually happened), the combination of their powers and spike of fanfic energy gives Kirin the full unbridled power of Nothing Personnel Kid, allowing her to teleport to every marked enemy and slash them all exactly once, dealing all marked damage in an instant. Luckily, this is more than just a cool gimmick; it's a genuine central movement mechanic that the stages and bosses revolve around, while still being an extremely cool and fun gimmick; because stages are laid out with this mechanic in mind, enemies and other tag-able objects are always placed within reasonable distance of each other, allowing you to chain multiple teleports and jumps to move across the stage extremely quickly without even touching the ground. Doing this is also Kirin's main method of building up Kudos and thus points. I'm gonna be honest: this is the first time in the Gunvolt series that I've actually  the stages and not just tolerated them to get to the bosses, and it's all thanks to this mechanic. Granted, I still prefer the bosses; which is why I'm so glad that they kept the boss missions feature from LAiX2; allowing you to fight bosses without having to go through their stage is a small but awesome convenience.If there's any shortcomings the game has, at least over its predecessors, it's that I feel the characters are kind of shallow and uninteresting--especially on Kirin's side. Another con I can think of is something that applies to pretty much every game in the franchise: "beating" the game is too easy. Normal mode bosses are pretty simple, and for some reason they made Anthem even more powerful than ever; when it activates, you don't revive as Kirin, you revive as a powered-up Gunvolt who can literally one-shot bosses. If you die as this Gunvolt you get sent back to the title screen, but I tried standing(or hovering, I guess) still in one of the bosses and it took five minutes for him to die. Anthem aside, you also have an assortment of unlockable and equippable passive and active skills, with effects such as healing, buffing, and dealing damage. So if you want an actual challenge you'll have to look to the hard and merciless modes--and ignore Anthem; don't use any passive/active skills for a cherry on top.Speaking of Anthem, there's another thing that, while it isn't exactly shortcoming, it also doesn't live up to its full challenging potential to my mind: bosses can Anthem too. Yup, the enemies have their own Muse and when you kill a boss they have a chance of reviving with a full health bar. The con? That "full health bar" is just aesthetic and the real amount is actually like a third of that. On top of that, they gain no power-up whatsoever. Kinda disappointing.But all in all, the stages are fun, the songs are boppin', and the boss fights are fantastic. Fun time all around.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is great, really it is, but it's not perfect, and that kind of has to do with the title more than anything.The gameplay is really good, Kirin is maybe the best playable character we've ever had (though I do still like iX1 Copen more), the level design is excellent, the story (in a vacuum) is pretty good, all the characters are likable, and the optional content after the game's completion is extremely fun. That said, while the story is, again, good in a vacuum, when you remember that this is a sequel to Gunvolt 2 it does feel a lot less...fulfilling. Gunvolt 2 left on a huge cliffhanger with it's hidden epilogue that doesn't go addressed here outside of a joke ending (that is kind of a massive pain in the ♥♥♥♥ to get). In fact, almost nothing really connects this to Gunvolt 2 outside of two boss fights and the fact that Gunvolt is still a playable character in this game.I think this game would've been infinitely better if it were a Gunvolt Chronicles game, rather than Azure Striker Gunvolt 3. That said, it's still an amazing game that I recommend everyone to play, even if you haven't played Gunvolt 1 or 2. I just kind of wish it was more connected to the games that came prior.Also, and small postgame spoiler warning here:

_childDocuments_.review: The most accessible 2d platformer I have ever seen.
