_childDocuments_.review: Gunvolt games rule.That said, the franchise is infested with weird decisions. Core mechanics change massively from game to game. Protagonists change from game to game. Timelines change from game to game. I like that the creators are experimenting, but I never really know what to expect.The throughline is buttery smooth gameplay and wildly fast level traversal. In 3, you mostly don't play as Gunvolt, but as Kirin who has a teleport and a Z Saber. Her lock on is throwing a fast ofuda, but you mostly don't need it unless you're trying to set up a teleport.I don't think I ever actually understood how to play this game, but it's very forgiving if you keep prevasion on and routinely ground stomp to keep your talismans stocked up. The exception, of course, is the last phase of the final boss. I ended up youtubing the ending because I couldn't quite figure out how I was supposed to dodge any of its attacks, and they all ignore prevasion.If you're a less casual player than me and you liked the other games in the series, I think you'll have a great time here. If you haven't played the other games, probably start with them first.I have no idea where the plot is going, but these games scratch that Zero series schmoovement itch, and they've always been worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: easy to pick up, very hard to master, but game offers plenty of help across the skill gap. very good gameplay, intimidating at first but definitely can be mastered. great same-file replayability but not much incentive to start a fresh save.gameplay loop is satisfying, but its very sharply divided between platforming through the stage and fighting bosses. the difficulty jump is cushioned by things like prevasion but you really feel it without that. i somewhat wish there was more room to use kirin's kit in the stages where 99% of the time you're tagging and zapping. bosses are overwhelming at first but all have patterns and can be learned given time which is afforded to you. the boss practice stages help a lot here.most active pulses can be safely ignored with some major exceptions but those exceptions are an option to grind up to make very hard mode easier. given you cant 100% a file without beating it, i appreciate this. passive pulses are nice to have and offer a ton of great bonuses and build variety. there's no "one size fits all" build, but you can tailor your loadout to maximize the one thing you really want - credits, damage, kudos, sustain, what have you.lots of bonus modes and characters to try out, though dont expect too much breaking the very solid formula thats already there. GV gets pretty sidelined because kirin is plenty enough on her own and he doesnt get nearly as much score, but he gets a (very difficult!) mode all to himself where he can shine. kirin xx is very fun to mess around with, though part of me wishes there was an unlock to enable passives on her - no point playing hard stages anymore with xx since you're basically playing very hard already.i full cleared the game a while ago but still playing to get better and simply because its just fun. use everything at your disposal and the game's not that hard to beat, but it really encourages you to try ditching those crutches and show you - hey, you can do this. the gradient from normal to hard to very hard mode helps with that, as do the boss practice stages, and if you really need it, there's still always an out. do not play for the story. there isnt one. gameplay however is magnificent, absolutely give it a spin.

_childDocuments_.review: In general, I don't recommend this game because it doesn't do enough steps forwards as the third game of the series:- Anthem can still not be disabled through menus (a RNG dependant, free revive mechanic).- The gatcha mechanics do not really solve the problem of previous games where you wouldn't get to craft a whole lot in a single, casual play-through, because you don't get to chose anything from what you get.- We finally get English voice acting, but it's pretty irritating at times, the voice actors are good, but it always feel like they didn't get proper direction.- Gunvolt, the namesake of the game, isn't it's own playable character, he acts more as a temporary enhance mode for Kirin, the actual protagonist of the game.This feels more like a spin-off experiment, like iX, then an actual sequel, which is why I can't recommend it. Gunvolt 3 is far from a bad game, but I personally feel it needs to improve in certain areas a lot more.

_childDocuments_.review: is the latest spin-off in the Azure Striker franchise.Kirin, the main protagonist, has an aggressive playstyle. Her gameplay loop is simple: tag enemies with her seals, then teleport attack to knock them out. The difficulty, of course, comes from being required to form large chains of uninterrupted KO's, ideally all without taking any damage. No need to worry, though. This game is still perfectly accessible even without high score considerations.While admittedly the plot gets quite underwhelming towards the end, the game makes more than up for it via character banter: since Kirin herself doesn’t like killing, about half of all characters eventually end up being recruited as part of her  support team. This is a large improvement over getting a new cast every single time a new entry in the franchise comes out, and this game handles intra-party banter well.The music was made by Inti Creates, so it’s going to be good like in all of their other games. All in all,  is a great start for a second set of spin-offs, and Kirin herself is very fun to play as. Here’s hoping for a .What about Gunvolt? Oh, he’s just another side character in a game supposedly named after him.

_childDocuments_.review: The Gunvolt series began in 2014 with the digital-exclusive 3DS game Azure Striker Gunvolt. In 2016, Azure Striker Gunvolt 2 continued the story of hero Gunvolt alongside his rival Copen. And now, in 2022, Azure Striker Gunvolt 3 finally picks up where 2 left off as an official sequel. New protagonist Kirin fights along side Gunvolt, allowing players to switch characters on the fly, adding a new element to the series’ high-speed 2D action gameplay. Familiar faces will return as “Image Pulses,” a new system that allows players to use characters from Gunvolt’s past in combat with over 150 varieties available! Thanks to the cooperation of Keiji Inafune (LEVEL5 comcept CCO), series executive producer / action supervisor, Inti Creates has evolved Gunvolt 3‘s action to exceed the expectations of modern players on the Nintendo Switch platform. Players will be blown away by the speedy and precise action on display in Azure Striker Gunvolt 3!

name: Fort Solis
detailed_description: Welcome to Fort Solis Responding to an unusual alarm call from a remote mining base, Jack arrives at the dark and desolate Fort Solis. With storm warnings imminent, he heads inside to make desperate contact. As the night grows longer, events escalate, spiral out of control and the mystery of what happened to the crew begins to reveal itself. The storms is approching, limiting Jack’s escape as he looks to hold out until morning arrives. Immersive Storytelling Fort Solis looks to deliver a high-fidelity experience designed to completely immerse the player in the cast and their long night. With performances from Roger Clark, Troy Baker and Julia Brown, Fort Solis looks to deliver emotion, fear, empathy and much more with every chapter. Supporting the core narrative are additional instances of story such as audio logs, surveillance footage of past or present events. Accompanying those are video logs recorded by all crew detailing the events before and perhaps even after that night the alarm was triggered at Fort Solis… A uniquely singular cinematic experience! The story is told across four chapters. Like a Netflix series, Fort Solis can be binged in one intense session, or played chapter by chapter like an episodic TV show. Grounded by the visuals Fort Solis brings to players, the next level of details, facial and body animations. With the help of Unreal Engine 5.2 Fort Solis realistic universe is brought to life! An isolated mining complex The skeleton of Fort Solis is built above and below ground. The base contains a variety of locations each with their own surface and sub surface levels. Players will be able to explore the isolated storm bearing surface, the creepy service tunnels absent of any light or the multiple departments that help Fort Solis function on a day-to-day basis such as Engineering, Medical and Communications. As the story unfolds locations can easily be revisited for additional story context or continue to serve as a backdrop to the fate that awaits Jack with each passing hour.

_childDocuments_.review: There was an old PS1/PC game called Martian Gothic: Unification. It was a mess in terms of gameplay and the Resident Evil like puzzles were nonsensical. But what it did have was a very interesting story about a team of Martian colonists that maintained radio silence suddenly, their final message was to 'stay alone, stay alive'. I highly recommend it, or at least watching an LP of it.Why do I bring it up in a review for Fort Solis? Well, simply put, I have for a long time hoped that one day we'd get a complete remake of Martian Gothic. Fort Solis is not it, but I do see some story similarities that had me hooked yet again. No spoilers here, especially because I'm still mid-playthrough and don't yet have the answers to what was going down at Fort Solis, but yet again it seems humanity was unprepared for what the Martian world could do to humans.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly amazing! This is exactly my kind of game! story-driven slow paced mature sci-fi plot. Fort solis has it all! But the walking speed is a problem. _childDocuments_.review: "Fort Solis" is an atmospheric space horror game with a tone reminiscent of "Alien: Isolation" and "Dead Space" but plays more like a simplified "Until Dawn". At its core "Fort Solis" is an exciting thriller with some interesting concepts and an intriguing story. The plot isn't entirely cliche either, with a number of subversive plot points I genuinely enjoyed!Despite this good core, the rest of the game feels underdeveloped. There were a number of bugs and accessibility issues that plagued the game through its entirety, including reading in-game text (where much of the story was located). Game mechanics ultimately boiled down to pressing two buttons and looking around. There were plenty of QTE events scattered throughout which all felt meaningless. I failed a QTE event and had a good outcome; I succeeded during another and felt like I lost. All this made me aware this game is more focused on dragging you along than letting you experience it for yourself.Though I have a lot of complaints about the game, I don't regret buying it for myself. I don't recommend purchasing the game in its current state, but I don't think you'll be too upset with yourself for taking the plunge into "Fort Solis".

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping to find a good story but was concerned about finding a bad one.What I didn't expect to find is such a complete failure to piece up any meaningful or even coherent story at all. The game tries to build mystical tension but never cares to resolve it. The author literally doesn't bother to fill the player in to let him assemble any remotely logical picture. All the critical pieces that would shed some light, are missing. This makes it feel, somehow, both extremely primitive and confusing at the same time. All the unfolding events are predictable a mile away, but your understanding of why all this is happening never really advances much from a vague "Something wrong happened here and it is related to plants".To add insult to injury, during final sequence, both protagonists you controlled during the game, all of a sudden and with no apparent reason, start acting like they just received divine revelation and finally realized the full picture. Which just made me yelling at the screen: "How about any of you, dipwits, finally explain to  what the whole drama is about?"What a waste of time.

_childDocuments_.review: READ before buying:I've never written a review on Steam before, but some of these reviews are seemingly unfounded and filled with bias, so here we go-- an unbiased take.Fort Solis is:A thriller/suspense >cinematic experience< with an unfolding storyline that gives to the player based on what the player puts into it. Yes, the game is fairly short when compared to other lengthy 'campaigns' from larger studios, but the depth in exploration (meaning collecting video logs and voice recordings) to unfold and understand the mystery of Fort Solis is what the game is about. Fort Solis is not:An FPS, shoot-em-up, RPG, fast paced, MMO, idle game. It is literally what is described by the developers in the description. You will not have nailbiting shootouts, ducking for cover under the fire of bullets, or turn based combat. All of these things are expectations of what people seem to WANT the experience to be. The game is best enjoyed if you don't WANT the game to be anything, and instead, ride alongside the adventure and mystery and try to uncover all of the secrets/unlockables throughout your playthrough that the studio created.Further detail:This game should not be approached with expectations of something that has been experienced before and compared against a game that another studio released (more on that later). All 5 played hours (at the time of writing) are from my first and only playthrough, and I will likely replay it again to pick up some things that I missed-- Though I felt as though I was being fairly thorough, so some unlockables appear to be fairly well hidden.The game offers sparse QTEs during cinematic moments, which if you're playing on KBM, are easy to miss due to the ambiguity of which key to press as it represents movement to avoid obstacles or using an item, neither of which are very clear to understand in the moment and the time window to react is fairly short, maybe only a second or two.(KBM player here) You cannot rebind action keys, but it really isn't that big of a deal. You can look around with your mouse, and the only other keys that are used are Q, W, E, A, S, D, F, B, Tab, and G like... once... oh and space bar in the menu-- I'm probably forgetting some other random key, but tl;dr, basically just left hand side of the keyboard, and the mouse (if you want to look around, but it isn't even really required most of the time).You can't run. This is true, but the game and atmosphere seems to play into this. Some moments appear to beg for running, such as when you're outside of the base in the storm on Mars, but if you're following the main objectives and not trying to do a completion playthrough, the walking pace mostly helps to build the suspense, especially in the beginning when there really isn't any urgency other than 'Oh, and alarm at Fort Solis, better see what's up'. As for not being able to run outside, the characters do state (quite early on) that being outside in the storm is painful, and the characters are shielding themselves from the barrage of dirt while outside.If you beat this game in 2 hours, I would guess that you're speedrunning an immersive experience that demands introspection and inquisition. Take your time. Unravel the story that ths game studio put together. Don't be afraid to backtrack and see if something changed or is now accessible after unlocking a key card, for example. A lot of the content in the game is fully optional (I will never be able to solve the rubicks cube in game), but these things build on the characters and their lore and are there if you choose to interact with it.Now to the performance issues-- I had none. Absolutely zero performance problems aside from stuttering during loading into new areas, but those were brief and I wouldn't really classify that as a performance issue due to optimization. I'm running 32g of ram, i7-7700k (ollllddd), and a 3080Ti. I was playing on High graphics settings on a 1440p monitor and it was a great experience. 4K is a different beast, so I can't speak to that, but I have no other frame of reference aside from what I have at my disposal.The voice acting is FANTASTIC. Some timing is a bit weird on delivery, but it seems like it's a coding wait() issue, not a delivery issue from the actors-- but I could be wrong. Sometimes, there will be overlapping audio if you rush into something without letting the current dialogue finish, so be weary of that as well.The atmosphere is sparse and tense-- No Country for Old Men type of ambiance. There is _some_ music, but it is very rare.The environment and attention to detail by the design staff is phenomenal.Overall, I would rate this a 9/10. This game is truly a labor of love from the development team and I really do believe it shows. Just remember, Fort Solis doesn't want you to rush through it, so (and this is from a video log in the game), 'All we have [on Mars] is time', so take yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is overall a really solid experience that I would recommend to anyone that likes deep and interesting stories, specifically in sci-fi. The story really hooks you and has you glued to your seat from start to finish (About 4 hours of playtime for me), with great voice acting and sound design. The story is told through 4 chapters, all at about an hour each, kind of like a Telltale game. Visuals were also really good, but there was unusually bad performance (was constantly getting dips to the 40s). For reference, I'm running max settings at 1440p (DLSS Balanced), on a RTX 3080 and 13900k. The story also ended very abruptly right as it started to get really good, so that was slightly disappointing, but I still had a good time with it.Gameplay is also very simplistic, with it mostly consisting of walking from point A to point B doing investigations, with the occasional QTE thrown in. I'm personally a fan of Walking Sims, so I don't mind this, but many won't like it. This is very unlike Dead Space or Callisto Protocol where combat drives the gameplay, because there's literally none of that here, so don't buy the game if this is a dealbreaker.All in all, if I had to rate the game as it stands, its a solid 7/10. I recommend you buy this game if you're into good stories in the sci-fi setting, and I would encourage to buy it to support the developers because they're very talented with this being their first attempt, and I think $20 is reasonable for a short, but high quality experience.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two ways to play this game. If you go into this as if your watching a movie then this is great, but if you play this with the mindset of other games then this is going to be a bit disappointing.Game as a film 9/10If you take the time to explore and truly figure out whats going on in Fort Solis your going to be rewarded with a great story and visual delight. _childDocuments_.review: The setting and scenario seems neat. But whomever decided on the control scheme for this game needs to be fired. I've played a lot of games with QTEs in them. Most of the time, the QTE prompts make sense. Spacebar here. Hold WAS or D there. Maybe an Enter every now and again or something. But the prompts in this game are so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird and I cannot get used to them. Moreso since they have times where you need to press two keys at once and they aren't even in order. I came across one where instead of pressing "W+E", they labeled it as "E+W". That's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. Out of all the QTEs I've come across in this game so far, I've only succeeded in like 2. They happen so quickly and with keys that don't make any sense, I barely even have time to register them before they disappear and I fail the damn QTE. The main character and his friend have this "I'm gonna constantly make jokes and rib at you" back and forth constantly and it just gets to be so annoying. It's draining. They go to a fort that clearly has some weird ♥♥♥♥ going on, yet they're like "Oh, look a poster for (future movie). I should go see that." to which his radio-bound partner will retort with something like "Aren't you too old for movies, geezer?" etc, etc. Bottom line, the QTEs make this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ miserable with the keys being terrible. Wish I could refund this. The horror tags on this game are misleading as hell.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted a game that was straight to the point and short. This is it. On top of that, it's one of the best looking games I've ever seen. The voice acting/performances are elite. Sound design is also just amazing. This is a cinematic experience. You are going along for a psychological thriller, not an action game. It's like a mini-series. Also, it was developed by 10 people...wild. You gotta know what you're signing up for with this one. It's nice to have a game that isn't some massive open world that will wreck 300 hours of your life. I will say that the slow movement is a gripe, but that was the developer's intent. You ain't running your way though this situation.There is a lot of ambiguity...A  LOT. I think it is a strength.  It keeps you wondering.  I want to see where this goes. This serves well as an introduction to something greater and I am down. PERFORMANCE: On a 4080, I-9, 32GB DDR5 5600 Mhz RAM, I'm getting 85-115 FPS with the settings on blast. It's either steady in the mid 80s or steady around 110. I have seen a few stutters, but nothing game breaking or immersion breaking. The game is demanding for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals were nice, considering the game was running in Unreal Engine 5. The only one gripe I had with the visuals was some shadow flickering that was present the entire game, which maybe had something to do with global illumination? I'm not sure. I googled it, but it seems it's a known issue that hasn't been patched.The story is average, I'd say. While you have an idea of why things happened the way they did, I feel there are a number of details missing that could help offer better detail to the story. One of my major gripes was the movement in the game. Even with the supposed increase to run speed patch, I felt it was still too slow.If you want to experience a newer game in Unreal Engine 5 and something that's only a couple hours long, then this could be a consideration, but I'd recommend buying it on sale. Overall, an average story, but not something you'd be missing out on if you didn't play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is a very short experience accompanied by nice graphics, an intriguing story that had me invested most of the way through, a almost pitch perfect atmosphere and likable enough characters (though I wish we had gotten to know them better). I encourage you to take your time to explore the facility, just go help gain a bit more understanding of the over arching narrative at play. Be warned, there are some character moments that some might not be a fan of (mostly jokes made between the two central characters, Jack and Jess). And this game is also not without its bugs, with me getting softlocked twice in normal gameplay. Though this was quickly fixed with a quick reload, so nothing too earth shattering. Overall, if you're looking for a quick game that'll tide you over for a night, I recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember my first experience with the red planet. Yes, it was some 60 years in the future from now, I disguised myself as a grumpy old man, trying to teach my protege Jessica. The disguise was flawless as I have been a grumpy old man since my teen years. This game was LITERALLY just walking, there wasn't even any running, so if you want to speedrun NAY speedwalk this, it will still take a bit of time I believe. Honestly, the story was a little weak, and felt quite Dead Spacey, especially the secret ending where Jack's prediction of zombies turns out to be... In addition, Jessica Appleton, had a nice apple bottom, if you know what I mean. The way the codes for the different vaults/safes were hidden was nice, although ONCE AGAIN, there was no 6969 code which was in fact a little disappointing as that would have been very very nice. ALSO there was one code which was 6 digits long that I painstakingly wrote on my notepad which turned out to be USELESS... or maybe I just didn't discover where to use it... ANYHOO! If you like walking and want to pretend you've done your 10k daily steps this game is for you! Other than walking and pressing 1 button 90% of the time, you'd be better off buying something else.Also the bumblybees were kind of cute, except the MASSIVE QUEEN BEE that chased me, that wasn't so cool!6/10 P.S. don't eat dirt or touch it or go outside or go to Mars, STAY AT HOME!

_childDocuments_.review: It's your regular Sci-Fi Space walking simulator with bits of mystery and horror. There are regular dialogues with a Story character like fan favourite game 'Firewatch'. Some parts require you to do QTEs and solve some minigames, The player has to watch some video/audio logs to learn more about the story, place and the characters which aren't mandatory but required for achievements. Overall i would say it's completely a cinematic based game with slow paced progression, as they say just like a Netflix show.The performance so far hasn't been upto the mark, my 4070 Ti is running it on Max Settings @FHD on just 65-75 fps on average and sometimes it goes above 85. With DLSS and DLSS3 Frame gen it runs above 100. I pity those who are playing on 2K or above. It's honestly terribly optimized with some bad shader lags as well. Graphics/visuals though are stunning and is a proper eye candy!!! Voice acting is top notch by Roger Clark. Had no crashes so far and i have played close to 2 hours.My Rating: 8/10 and is recommended for players who enjoy slow paced story based games and like to read stuff and know more about the characters and background.At full price i wouldn't recommend buying it as it's short from what i have heard from the early reviews. Get it when it's at least 40% off.Voted award for best Steam Deck game.

_childDocuments_.review: What first seems like an interesting sci Fi thriller quickly becomes a total slog. Playing the game is unsatisfying, slow, and clunky. The quick time events feel way too fast to do properly, but as far as I can tell they are completely free of consequences and the story continues in one direction regardless of your performance, aside from one single section.The story just ends, with little to no payoff and makes it seem like the team ran out of time to finish their story. I do like ambiguous endings that leave the player to decide what the real story is, but how they did it made it feel very rushed and unsatisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not just saying the thing above to grab your attention, I'm saying this because that's how I honestly feel after completing nearly 900 titles in the span of nearly two decades, on many different platforms and from many different genres. Fort Solis is not necessarily the worst because it does so many things so badly (although it indeed does). It's the worst because it's the first 'game' I've played that does literally nothing to fulfill any of the criteria that make something a video game.Games are about interactivity and player choice. It's a choice to shoot a goomba in Mario instead of jumping on its head. It's a choice to save the fish at the start of Detroit: Become Human. It's a choice in Dark Souls to decide how you want to gear up before the next boss. Fort Solis doesn't have ANY choices. In this... product, the interactivity consists of the following things: you either open doors, pick up items to be able to open doors, walk, partake in extremely bad quick-time events, or watch monitor screens. It's not a game when all you have to do is hit (A) to trigger a cutscene. It's the same as hitting Resume on your Blu-Ray player to continue your movie. Hell, even the bloody QTEs were unfailable, or at least that was my experience with them.Fort Solis sacrificed everything for the sake of creating a cinematic experience. Yet the irony is, that it fails MISERABLY as a movie too. Why? Because first, its characters don't grow or evolve throughout the whole 'story', and second, there is practically NO story! If you've seen the trailers, you've pretty much seen everything. Jack and Jessica receive a manual distress call from Fort Solis station so they go and check it out, and then NOTHING happens for 4 hours! They just randomly regurgitate the same boring points about a movie they've watched, and you run into some dead bodies, but you learn literally nothing aside from seeing some videos and emails on some PCs from the station employees who only talk about two things: soil experiments and Mars storms. And the ending, man, the ending, what an anticlimactic letdown.Fort Solis fails as a game, and it fails as a movie too. I don't know what it is, all I know is that I wanted to get drunk so much after I finally finished it. You know, instead of hitting (A) repeatedly in the game to make the character drink beer, because, oh, well, that's the most amount of interactivity it has. Oh, and it only takes 4 hours because 2 hours of that is just super-slow walking, otherwise, it would have only taken 2 hours. And yeah, there's no run button! I guess the developers thought it would have been hard to animate the characters running up the stairs, and it would have made the game less 'cinematic'.This is really just a side note because absolutely no one should buy and play (?) this. I know it's hard to believe, but the devs managed to make a game less optimized than Jedi Survivor. I have an RTX 3090 with an i5-13600KF, 32GB DDR5 6800MHz RAM and 6000/7000MB/s SSD. I can usually play highly demanding games at 90-120 FPS at 4K in DLSS Performance mode at High-Epic settings. This 'game' drops below 60 even with the lowest settings. In fact, there are barely any differences between the presets. It also crashed once, it has Unreal Engine micro stutters, the screen-space reflections are some of the worst I've ever seen (I can only see half of my character's reflection from a distance) and the shadows bounce from one spot to another on every surface, as if the walls were made out of water or something like that. Also, where is the ultrawide support from this so-called cinematic game? Oh, and be prepared for a locked FOV with a character that literally blocks half of your screen.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is thoroughly okay. The visuals are great and it has good bones, but they didn't flesh out the threat...at all. There's a hand tremor and a few mentions of odd behavior and that's it. The game never fleshes out what's happening to the crew, so the story boils down to one guy losing his marbles. In addition to that, some of the collectibles are incredibly hard to find. I like the surface walk segments, but with swirling dust everywhere and a decreased movement speed I am NOT going to check all the grey, angular surfaces to see which ones open to reveal collectibles.

_childDocuments_.review: If you understand the concept of "walking simulators" and their environmental storytelling, then give Fort Solis a try, it's a good one. I finished this in 1 session, took short breaks in between. Visuals, sound, (voice)acting and general atmosphere are fantastic and the game shows what artists can do with the UE 5.2 engine. Had no technical issues or bugs. The story is a matter of taste of course, but I enjoyed it very much and wouldn't mind a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Graphic and visuals are very good. Little clunky on character movements. Some difficulty on getting the character to face in the direction that you want. Achieved the bad ending  and on the second try I got the good ending. As long as you don't let the character movements discourage you and are really interested in the story and reaching the end this is a very good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: While the optimisation absolutely needs a bit of work, issues can be overcome by using DLSS, quality mode fixed any issues for me while not affecting visuals that much.Other than that, I believe many people just went into this game with wrong expectation. It is not a horror game, not in tradinitional way. Thriller is more fitting. More important is, it´s one of those movie-game experiences. If you love sci-fi and space stuff and you are ok with not many gameplay mechanics while the story and performances are great, than Fort Solis is for you. Otherwise wait for that other space game releasing soon.I am really satisfied with the game, especially with writing, main characters are very well voice acted and overall aesthetics and atmosphere are exactly my cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this game, it just isn't worth the money, even discounted 25%. The trailer is about as tense and exciting as the game gets, I mean, you're supposed to be investigating an emergency signal, there are dead people laying around and all you can do is move at a fast walk?! The game is very basic, Go here, Find this, Do that, move along, rinse and repeat. There is almost no problem solving to do and very little point in exploring, you'll go everywhere just following the storyline. The map turns out to be very small over all and unless you're at the point of the story where you need to be there, is largely unaccessible. Finally I just started the game up to find the keyboard controls have glitched to AZERTY from QWERTY and there is no way to change them, so thats game over.Really disappointed with this, the graphics are easily the best part of the game and its visuals are what you expect from Unreal, but as my dad used to say 'You can wrap a turd in gold leaf and make it look pretty, but underneath it's still a turd'. This game would normally be the first chapter of a much bigger game not a stand alone piece. Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: what an experience! the devs were onto something with this as a first project. very cinematic experience...awesome visuals to start. good sound fx, the same suspense as dead space, same ambience as the callisto protocol, and some good dialogue and mystery to keep you wondering throughout your walking. the price is a decent bit high for being so short but it's a new game on UE5 and it's what they need to get the ball rolling. got it for around $17 and i am happy for what i paid. felt like more of a movie that i was watching and itching to see what would happen next or what would come out to surprise or happen..or what i would find with a new video or audio log. great job devs..hoping to see more like this in the future!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: OK, here's my verdict.  It's worth it because it's the first Unreal 5 engine game that I have played and the quality quality of the mars environment was spectacular.  The game itself is a bit slow, with the character you play moving only at walking speed.  They did release a patch to speed walk, but it is still pretty slow.  Game play has you doing very little combat, and more of a clue - discovery - unlock door type game. It's certainly not an FPS. It does have you wondering what will happen around next corner, and there is definitely some core action you need to play through.  Walking around outside on the Mars surface was awesome.  The character scripting was ok, if not a bit empty, but as the game progressed, the dialog got more interesting and story unfolded,  To note, there are bugs and weird anomalies that I associate to Unreal 5 still being in development.  Some of the reflective rendering had shimmers which I also experienced in the editor.  Not sure if that is related to my video card, but I do have a MSI RTX 4080.  If you are into SciFi and want to experience what unreal 5 can do, then I would suggest you try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually striking. It's clear that a lot of love was put into the graphics. Unfortunately the story is lackluster and the characters relationship just reads like they tried to slap Hank and Delilah from Firewatch into it. Their emotional responses to events is bland/humorous when it should be one of shock/horror. They try to be whimsical when their crew mates have been killed. They just don't make sense.It becomes worse when they start retracing steps and asking "what's going on" when the game is almost over. They're like the annoying characters in horror movies that have watched everything but still don't know what's going on.I honestly wanted to love this game. I love horror, I love sci-fi. The graphics are this games only saving grace. I hope that this developer continues to make games. They obviously have a lot of talent. But I hope in their future games that they invest more in story telling and character development. Slow walking, quick time events, lackluster story just suck the soul out of a world that people clearly spent time trying to pour a soul into. Sadly it just isn't there.I would have loved a game that was Firewatch+SOMA. That seemed like a direction this game could have gone. But it's just a beautiful tech demo.

_childDocuments_.review: "Fort Solis" offers an enthralling gaming experience that resembles a gripping Netflix series, with a unique episodic format that allows you to dive into the story at your own pace. The game is divided into four captivating chapters, each serving as an episode in this intense narrative.In this dark and desolate world, you step into the shoes of Jack, who embarks on a journey to a remote mining base in response to an unusual alarm call. With an impending storm adding to the sense of urgency, you must venture inside Fort Solis to make contact and uncover the mystery shrouding the missing crew. As night descends and events unfold, the tension and mystery build, leaving you on the edge of your seat, all while the storm rages outside, limiting your escape options until morning breaks.What truly sets "Fort Solis" apart is its commitment to delivering a high-fidelity experience that immerses players in its characters and their long night of challenges. The storytelling in "Fort Solis" goes beyond the core narrative, featuring additional layers of the story through elements like audio logs, surveillance footage, and the haunting video logs left by the crew. These added dimensions enrich the overall experience and allow you to uncover more about the events leading up to that fateful night at Fort Solis."Fort Solis" doesn't just focus on storytelling and visuals; it also offers a richly detailed and multi-layered environment. The base itself is a complex structure, with both surface and sub-surface levels, including storm-battered exteriors, eerie service tunnels devoid of light, and various departments crucial to Fort Solis' operations, such as Engineering, Medical, and Communications. These locations become more than just settings; they evolve as the story progresses, providing additional context and a backdrop to Jack's ever-escalating challenges.In summary, "Fort Solis" is a masterful combination of storytelling, acting, and immersive world-building. The episodic format allows you to savor every moment, and the attention to detail in both narrative and visuals sets it apart as a must-play experience for those who seek an emotionally charged and gripping adventure. Dive into the world of "Fort Solis" and let its mysteries unravel before you as you uncover the fate that awaits Jack with each passing hour.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start off by saying  I don't review many games, on any platforms, but with this one I felt the need. I know it's gotten "mixed" reviews but I thoroughly enjoyed this game! The story is really good, I found myself fully immersed, reading every email I could find, happy when I found the next audio or video logs, and anxiously awaiting the next story sequence. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. Yes, I was hoping for some combat system, but the game isn't about that. Even without much action, there are tense moments in the game where you're directly involved.I enjoyed the storyline and the chemistry between the characters. The fact that all the characters look and sound like real people. The graphics, the atmosphere of the space complex, and the intrigue that keeps you engaged until the very last moment. And I have to highlight, as a Dead Space fan, I particularly enjoyed the storytelling without any editing cuts—it all looks very dynamic.Except for one thing—the main character's movement. Oh, how slow he moves. That's the main downside of the game for me. And a couple of moments where the character moves or crawls along long corridors, and absolutely nothing happens! No dialogue, no interaction with the surroundings. These moments really stand out and feel extremely boring.I hope the team will address this with new patches, at least by adding dialogues between the characters or some phrases. And they'll do something about the movement speed, it's just unreasonably slow :)Apart from that, thank you for the experience!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a mystery game where creators forgot to add an actual mystery. Instead you will get a bunch of vague mumbo-jumbo that does not actually mean or lead to anything. Given that the game has around 30 minutes of content in total that are prolonged by your character inability to run and excessive backtracking - that's just stupid. Like, it's not that much story to try to make it coherent. Basically the game tries to be bigger than it is by blatantly prolonging every action and deeper than it is by blurring the story with vague red herrings that lead nowhere. The red herrings would be a nice distraction in a game with more content but not as a replacement for the main story or a cover-up of the main story banalityP.S. And to add insult to injury the whole story hinges on a completelly manufactured premise that does not make sense to begin with

_childDocuments_.review: Only recommend to die-hard walking sim fans that enjoy a sci-fi setting. I really liked the visuals and production valve as it's a beautiful game and very well voice acted. I didn't enjoy the quicktime events which felt too quick on a controller but passable on a keyboard. Not a big fan of these though in general. The biggest negative for me was not having the ability to walk a bit faster which was quite frustrating. Didn't need a run button but just an option for a faster pace. I wanted to explore more but didn't want to have to walk all the way back to where I knew I had to go. The map animation on your hand is a bit too slow to keep pulling up and often didn't show you where your character was in relation to the world. Was easy to get lost in a few spots plus the slow walking pace made it a bit frustrating at times. The game is short, about 4 hours which is great for a straight playthrough if that's what you're looking for. Overall I'd give it a 6/10. For me personally, the price is fine for the production value you get.

_childDocuments_.review: #wyattdidnothingwrongThis game isn't a total disaster at all. The acting and voice work is very good, especially on the part of Wyatt. The script is great. It's obviously very nice to look at. The story is interesting and entirely plausible in a sci-fi kind of way; it's engaging and certainly gives you pause for thought when you realise exactly what surviving the situation might mean. I think the main problem for many is that Fort Solis clearly aspires to be a TV show. It says so, right there on the store page, describing the actions of the characters as "performances" and comparing itself to something on Netflix. The closest it comes to actual gameplay is quick-time events - with one major exception it doesn't even matter if you fail at these - or playing hunt the hidden object to access the audio and video logs that contain most of the backstory. On my part, I've no problem with walking sims; I've played many and loved some of them. They're totally upfront about what they're doing on the store page so nobody can claim to have been deceived by the marketing blurb. I do have a problem with the leisurely pace at which our protagonists (yes, plural: you switch characters halfway through, so if you're getting this as a huge Roger Clark fan don't expect to spend the whole game with Jack) drag their reluctant feet around the place while apparently in fear for their lives and those of others. Your joy at discovering a sprint button will be decimated as you realise that "sprinting" in this case means "moving like you're in rehab for a spinal injury but are making real progress and the doctors are optimistic". If you were to remove all the waddling about from the game, you'd be left with enough content for a movie rather than a TV series. And at £20.99, it's not a lot of movie for the money - I ran through the whole thing in just over 4 hours, including finding about 85% of the collectables, doing another loop of the base to take in the sights, redoing the last bit to get the alternate ending, and pausing the game while I made myself some noodles (satay, if you're curious). Completionists might add another hour of space dawdling at the very most, while those brainrotted into a short attention span and skipping all the collectables could plausibly finish it all in 2-3 hours. Plotwise, I'm not sure why more attempts to reason with the antagonist weren't made - it seems obvious that he's only the immediate threat rather than the real villain of the piece, and there's more than enough evidence left laying around the place that he might've been reasoned with in spite of his current condition. The climax also feels incomplete - I'm the right person to be charmed into liking a middling cinematic walking sim, but if I'm to care at all what's going on it might be good to finish the story properly, even if it's just in a note at the end. I won't spoil it for those who do play it but the consequences of your victory are left in an unknown state that could only really be resolved by a sequel, which unfortunately will probably never come. It's a shame. I'd have probably forgiven the flaws, even the constipated limping around, if they'd managed a satisfying ending to top it off.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not entirely sure how others are "experiencing issues" with higher end computers. I was expecting mutated creatures in space, and was met with something completely different which I will admit was a surprise.I am not a big fan of how the game ended overall, but would definitely recommend this to others. _childDocuments_.review: It's not that I wouldn't recommend AT ALL, but it's like an interactive movie instead of a game, which is fine, some players dig it, I do too in some cases, but this one just feels... lacking. It's unfortunate because it has such a good potential. I can see what they're trying to do with the story (though I still can't fully grasp what the lore here is supposed to be). Character developments have its ups and downs, movements are tediously slow which I think is intentional just so they could prolong such a short game, and some quick-time events prompts are ridiculously fast, it's almost like it's intentional and if so, why bother do quick-time event prompts? Just make it a cutscene for us to watch, lol. And the ending is just... well, let's just say it could've been more fleshed out, it's just really underwhelming.Strong points I can give for this game is the environment designs and its graphics. The foundation of the story is present for us to anticipate, so the potential is there. Reminds me of Callisto Protocol; has a potential, but just fall flat in certain areas. Just wish there's more to do rather than walk around and look for more hidden contents, which I doubt would clear the water for the story anyway.I'd love a follow-up to this game, but maybe a spin-off instead of a sequel. It'll be a great chance to re-do some concepts of the franchise and make it more enjoyable AS A GAME. As a movie though, this could be really great.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: Steam needs a button that's right in the middle.  I think this is somewhere in the middle of a Recommend/Not Recommended, but writing out this review I suppose I'd tell most people that I don't recommend it.The game looks pretty good.  It's obvious a lot of care went into the design of Fort Solis, even if a large portion of it is corridors and tunnels.  There's a lot of detail, just not much of a way to really interact with the environment.  The main characters look good, model wise and animations.  There are some animations during QTEs that look odd.  I think more could have been done to make it looked more "lived in."  It ultimately feels like a pretty empty location.Gameplay is particularly mediocre.  I'm not sure why they chose such an awfully slow walk speed without the ability to run or jog even..  My only guess is to pad the game's time to make it longer.  I think it was an awful choice.  I'd of been happy with a brisk walk, especially after the many times the game tries to instill a sense of urgency.Many interactions with the environment and objects lead nowhere, and the game ties you to this "find this before that" concept which means things that make sense to you will not be available unless you've done something the game wants you to do first.  I get it, as a way to drive the game narrative.. But it's not especially fruitful.Most of the interactions you will have will leave you clamoring for more information about what's going on at Fort Solis.  Or, what did go on.  This ties into my thoughts on the story, which is the really disappointing bit.A lot of my complaints for the game would be tolerable if the story wrapped up with a satisfying conclusion.  At the end of the game I still don't have a solid answer to what went wrong on Fort Solis.  Heck, there were promises about the game that just fall incredibly flat.In an interview with IGN, Tinsdale made some promises about your choices during cinematic events mattering, and the final scene having "many different ways."  Ah, yes.  That sounds cool.  That was one of the driving points for making me want to play this game.  What'd I get?  The ending really just depends on how fast you can push a button during a QTE.  That's very frustrating considering in most situations it doesn't really seem to matter what you do for the QTE.  The differences in what you see are very slight.

_childDocuments_.review: First, this is an on-rails walking sim; it doesn't attempt to be anything else. There is no run button, there is a walk faster button. Gameplay-wise, it reminds me a lot of Firewatch. Narratively, it's like someone threw The Martian and The Shining into a pot and gave it a good stir. Short run time, ends before the game over stays its welcome. graphics are on par with, let's say Starfield at medium settings. Positives: Stellar voice acting, atmosphere and story telling across the board. Progression despite the rails, doesnt feel confining.  The find it yourself style of level navigation is satisfying without being a difficult to decipher mess.Cons: controls are a bit clumsy, but again, there's no rush to get around. Quick times are unintuitive and unforgiving, but they don't come up often enough to slow the game pace and failing them only seems to result in your characters already bad day being ever so slightly worse. Biggest gripe is the organic style interface with all computer screens and notes can make reading some text difficult, especially if your rig isn't able to handle the full graphics settings. No replay value, seen it once seen it all.All said, not bad, perfect way to kill a rainy afternoon.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: After tweaking some settings like turning the maximum frame at 60fps rate off, my fps shot up to 120-140 on an RTX 4080. The game needs more optimization than it has now, which unfortunately seems to be the norm these days.You also have to be patient, since you are walking a lot and collecting hints. If you don't have patience then this is not the game for you. I'm going to give it a chance anyway, since the concept really appeals to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Standard story without twists. Comes with user interaction / minigames during action sequences, however ones acting does not impact the predetermined outcome. Atmospheric grand scale views are limited to the intro of chapter 1, after that one is stuck inside of dark corridors and the interior of a space station. Once they are running out of locations for the player to visit they force you to explore the very same corridors a second time by having you switch character. Yet the total playing time does not exceed 4 hours. The abrupt ending leaves many open questions, yet it does not feel like one has to expect a sequel. A lot of potential wasted.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a playable walking Sim-like Horror Movie. Inspired by games and movies like Dead Space and Moon you get a VERY strong atmosphere, very good voice acting and a thrilling story, even if the end was not 100% to my liking, as some decisions seemed a bit stupid.If you are not the impatient kind that needs to have stimulation every 5 seconds not to get bored, and if you like a slow paced, well cooked atmosphere, with superb voice acting this is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! I am only on chapter 3 at the moment and i am enjoying everything about it. If you love Atmosphere games with great sound (with good surround headphones) and graphics, then this game is for you at such a great price! This is not a "RUN and HIDE for survival" type of game and more along the lines of a Story/Mystery! If you liked Deliver us the Moon without puzzle solving then you should really try this game! _childDocuments_.review: I've decided to change my review to a recommend. On Second thought.The Things I don't enjoy aren't enough to make me not want to recommend this game. I look forward to, hopefully, more games from this/these companies in the future.Even though I like the game. I don't mind the game being a glorified movie for the most part. I enjoy cinematic games and cut scenes. However there really isn't a good reason for this game to be this graphically intense. I have a 2080 super and a i9-19300k and got about 40-50 frames on medium settings with regular fluctuations. I ended up setting max frames to 30 and mostly had it stable from there. I wouldn't say it looks any better than say, Starfield or even Aliens:Isolation. Another thing. The devs made an odd decision they tied screen resolution to whatever window mode you're using. To explain. I played on Windowed full screen and could only play on 2560x1440 if I pick windowed then I have other options, that's not something I've seen before.The writing and acting is amazing. I thoroughly enjoyed not just the banter but the way the characters interacted with each other and the world. The game does look good. Sound design is great. There isn't much in the way of music and that's fine. A lot of my play time was going back and forth. Get a new card go back to open doors to see whatever it is I was locked out of and figure out what is going on.There is no save option, You are entirely dependent on checkpoints.There is also QTE which are often annoying and not really enjoyable, they actually sorta make the game worse.. Your character moves at a casual walk unless the games wants you to move faster. The devs tried to explain this away by saying they want to maintain the atmosphere of the game but I wonder if it's just them trying to pad out the game time. There is a point in the game where your character says "♥♥♥♥ this, ♥♥♥♥ staying calm" and then calmly starts walking again. Fun fact: There is a short cut scene after the credits

_childDocuments_.review: Walking sim made with my name on it. Isolated horror with an engineer for a protagonist who tries to figure out what the heck is going on with a base that's gone dark. I loved a lot of the little quirks I found, and while there were a few puzzles I needed some external help with, I enjoyed the story enough to make up for it. Quite short, unfortunately -- and cliffhangers. I wish we'd gotten a little more info at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: Cinematic experience is totally present. Nice sci-fi ambience, dialogs are ok. I really liked the vlogs in the game. Probably lots of time spent on mo-cap to get that level of detail and micro expressions on some of the characters. Performance wise on my rig running on High@4K it was decent. No frame cap and had 70-170 FPS. Had some studders here and there when loading in upcoming scenary. Hard to tell if its devs or current build of UE5. I see the same stuff happening in Immortals of Avernus. This game left me wanting. It felt like a story better suited as a movie more than a game. After the first half hour or so it became quite apparent that the developers were trying to slow you down with just allowing you to walk around the place, trying to stretch the experience out as much as possible. When getting to the last act of the game I felt like that was confirmed even when voice queue was like "screw staying calm" - if anything I would expect the character to be able to run at this time.Considering how they frame the game as a cinematic experience, they are well on point. Everything is linear towards progressing to the next act. While you can roam a bit within the areas you have unlocked, most of the stuff you can interact with is related to background stories of the characters in the game, but not much of anything else. Rubrics cube was a fun addition, but that is about it. Like my title says it feels like a movie script with a bad game adaptation on an impressive game engine. They should have done a movie instead. Black Mirror: Bandersnatch was more engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is slowly pumping. The main character Jack Leary receives an emergency message from a nearby base and goes to investigate what happened. He doesn't know anything about what exactly happened, but reading notes and listening to audio diaries, as well as stumbling upon other, much more terrible finds, he realizes that something terrible has happened. His colleague and close friend Jessica Appleton often gets in touch with Jack: at first they just chat and joke about zombie series, but then the mood of their conversations changes dramatically along with how the hero learns more and more.The graphics in the game are excellent, there are minor drawdowns, in general, the frame rate is even. Gameplay-wise, this is the most reference walking simulator I've ever played. There is no running button in the game at all. At first, it doesn't bother, the animations of the character are good, but the whole game of unhurried walking may annoy someone. In fact, this is a beautiful adventure game with searching for objects, solving riddles, watching video diaries, etc. Don't expect shooting here, there's no horror here either, but the atmosphere in the game is present.The game is beautiful and made very technologically advanced. I really liked the atmosphere, which is most strongly influenced by the aesthetics of retrofuturism and liminal spaces created, without a doubt, by very talented artists. In addition, Fort Solis has fascinating music, which often gives goosebumps on the skin.Fort Solis is an exciting journey. Attempts to figure out what really happened at the Mars station encourage you to carefully examine every computer and listen to every message in audio diaries. There was no revolution in the narrative, but the game developers were able to tell their goal in the scenery of a fantastic thriller.Rating 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game hopeful that the plot would be worth dealing with the technical problems other people are seeming to have with the game. But I am not having technical issues - the game runs fine for me. Instead it is the plot and annoying QTE design that I am dinging the game for, in particular, the irony of mocking horror movie tropes like "clueless protagonist" while simultaneously hard-embracing them fully. In the sequence that made me finally quit playing the game, there were no less than four obvious opportunities the protagonists had to incapacitate the villain and they did nothing.The QTEs use small, non-obvious icons positioned away from where the action is occurring. Also, it's 2023, QTEs were maybe new and cool back in the 80s when Dragon's Lair was a thing, maybe, but nowdays they're just lazy and annoying game design, and, like most QTE-based games, the game eventually devolves into a sequence of scripted fights where your inputs don't actally make any difference plot-wise.... which is unfortunate. The plot was actually good up to that point.The one thing that does shine through here is the motion capture and voice acting - which just really cements my opinion that this should have been a 2 hour movie, instead of a 6-8 hour slog through bad QTEs.

_childDocuments_.review: I really did not like this game.  On the steam page it reads "The experience envisioned by the developers :A uniquely singular cinematic experience!The story is told across four chapters. Like a Netflix series, Fort Solis can be binged in one intense session, or played chapter by chapter like an episodic TV show."This right here should of told me the game would suck. First off, why are you comparing a video game to a netflix series? The developers don't realize that video games can be a superior form of media to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ netflix show. If they wanted to make a netflix episodic TV show then they should have done that instead. This "game" or whatever it is would have fit in perfect in the sea of garbage netflix original series! I like walking simulators. Walking simulators can be interesting and fun, although they are walking simulators there is usually some kind of gameplay, whether it be puzzles or exploration or w/e. This game has no kind of gameplay besides walk and press X. This game is boring, there is nothing to do in it besides walk around and look at little doodads and gizmos scattered around. For example you can interact with a rubix cube, or pickup some other object and the character makes a comment about it. Really cinematic rofl! The characters do nothing but walk. You cannot run, you can't jump, you can't do anything but press X and walk. And the walking...it is painfully slow. I think if you had the option to run, the time to complete the game would probably be halved. Because all you do is go from point A to point B. For the whole ♥♥♥ game. This is a game made by people that don't play video games. Maybe they have at one point but I do not believe the developers in charge of this project have played a video game, from start to finish, in the last 10 years.  Because if they had they would not have ever released something like this. They would say "hey we have a story and graphics but we seem to be missing the most important part of a game, the gameplay!" The game is marketed as "horror." Well there is not 1 single scare throughout the entire game. They really should change this to be like "interactive audiobook" or something because its not a game. There is no gameplay loop, there is no gameplay. The audio was well done, as in the sound effects and music and overall ambience. The story sucked, I couldn't even tell you any of the characters name and I finished this thing yesterday.  Oh yea I remember 1 characters name. Applebees or Applejuice or something stupid like that.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: They released a continuation of the story in the form of a powerpoint. No, that's not a joke. The continuation itself is an epilogue that only raises more questions than answers. The end was sequel bait enough - the powerpoint was more sequel bait. Like they even have money for a sequel. Still not recommended, but its even more aggressively no after releasing an epilogue in the form of a powerpoint.This story had me early on, but it never really seemed to go anywhere.The main draw of this really is the voice acting. This game has 10/10 voice acting and very good supporting graphics and sound design, so if you just want to hear some really good voice acting while playing a walking sim, this has you covered.The mystery of this game leaves a lot to be desired. I honestly don't think the stories final chapter/ending ties all the various plot threads and hints together like it should. The differences between the endings are minimal at best. There's not really any meaningful choices here. As for technical issues: I had two CTDs within the first 15 minutes, but after that I updated my Nvidia drivers and had zero crashes. Just update your drivers and the game should run fine.Performance isn't amazing, but this is a UE5 indie game with AAA graphics, so I'm willing to cut them some slack on that. And the environments frequently really are impressive. Its not anything super unique, but Fort Solis does look gorgeous. Ultimately, I still don't recommend this game. They really needed to explore the antagonists motivations a bit more, and maybe have more of an epilogue. I didn't rush this game (there are people that finished this in 2-3 hours), I went for every collectible/interactive object I saw, and I still don't feel like I really know much about what was going on at Fort Solis. There's a lot of theories I could present based on what happened, but its all just conjecture.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is an absolute gem of a game that captivated me from start to finish. The graphics are stunning, with breathtaking visuals that truly bring the desolate Martian environment to life. The attention to detail in the design is impeccable, making every corner of the abandoned base a visual treat.The story is equally impressive, weaving a gripping narrative that kept me on the edge of my seat throughout. The mystery and suspense are masterfully crafted, and the pacing is just right to maintain a constant sense of intrigue.However, if there's one drawback, it's that the game is a bit too short. I was left wanting more, which is a testament to how engaging the experience was. Overall, Fort Solis is a must-play for fans of narrative-driven games and psychological thrillers. Highly recommended!

But when the protagonist's walking speed is equivalent to my neighbor's 9-month-old crawling speed, I can't force myself to walk here and there. _childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis looks great, has a wonderfully atmospheric setting and am intriguing enough story to keep you going.  The problem is the pace of it.People said in their reviews that the story takes four hours.  It would be done in less than an hour if you can actually move with a modicum of urgency.  Your character is stuck in a casual walking pace.  Very, very slow, very, very casual walking pace.  And there's nothing you can do about it.  You're essentially following a predetermined path oh so slowly, you find items, documents and recordings that build up your understanding of what has happened and you keep going.  Very, very slowly.For atmosphere and setting it deserves a thumbs up.For the way it plays it deserves a thumbs down.You can watch a walkthrough on YouTube and save some money.  Or you can buy the game, support the developers but do make sure they know that they need to meet gamers half way.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is only 3,5 hours long and the story is extremely banal and predictable. Even if you read all the texts and notes you find during exploration there are no mysteries or riddles in the plot. Simply a straightforward narrative. Moreover, developers tried their best to prolong it through different tricks. For example, the character strolls even in an intense and possibly dangerous environment, he just can’t run. Not only it irritates but also it ruins the atmosphere of the game. After a scary interaction, the main hero walks as normal.I played short games such as Firewatch or The Invincible so I can appreciate the format and like it. But not in this case. I hope no one will make my mistake and buy this game, it’s not worth it. By the time you realise that the story is crap you wouldn’t be able to refund it as developers were smart enough to make long intro titles and suspense at the beginning which is enough to play for at least 2 hours.What a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: There will be an audience that appreciates Fort Solis for what it is, but even they may rue squandered potential. The premise and setting are simple but effective, thanks to the fantastic Martian atmosphere, understated horror, and great visuals. Well-known actors provide adequate performances in what is essentially a psychological thriller mixed with a walking simulator. But things fall by the wayside because of a narrative that is too ambiguous and an ending that brings no satisfaction. Some characters are not given enough and others have spotty dialogue. The game is only 3-4 hours long, with a painful walking speed and sluggish interactions that make it hard to stomach a replay. Fort Solis has appreciable qualities but needed better footwork before it was pushed out into the storm.*Neutral rating*

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game at all, and I hate to do it. I love walking simulators, for starters. I know that many people don't, but I really love the genre. On paper, this game has everything that I love. I love walking simulators, mystery and suspense, exploration, and the feeling of being alone. For these reasons, I love games like Firewatch, or games where you're alone in space and have to snoop around and think your way out of a situation. All of that aside, let me talk about performance. Granted, I have a good rig, so everyone's mileage may vary. I have a 4090 and experienced almost no performance issues. The only performance issues that I noted were that I noticed a slight drop in frames, for about a second or so, on three different occasions. That was the extent of it. Graphically, the game is decent, but it's not groundbreaking. We have many graphically beautiful games as of now, and this is indeed beautiful, but it's not a major selling point. The game utilizes shadows and dark tones very well. The cinematic drive towards Fort Solis itself was the prettiest moment in the game, in my opinion. After that, 90% of your time is indoors, where it looks like a typical base. The voice acting was quite good. There are only a small handful of voice actors in this game, however, they are all extremely professional and have done as well as they possibly could have with the source material that was given. The graphics and the voice acting were two of this game's strong suits. I have absolutely no complaints with the graphics, the voice acting, and most of the performance that I experienced as a day 1 player. However, like I said, I have a beefy PC, and all I had were three very minor frame drops that lasted a split second. Before going forward with addressing my qualms with this game, I'd like to first address the controversial walking speed, which has been a topic that I've seen on several online platforms. Yes, there is no option to sprint. You are walking at a pace that is similar to how one would take a stroll around the neighborhood. I have certainly encountered slower walking speeds than this before. It's not as abysmal as people have claimed it to be, in my opinion. This is a walking simulator, after all, and for a lot of the time there is no perceived threat. Thus, you are just very casually walking around an abandoned station, in a clunky space suit, and the walking speed is a very realistic pace. Your character isn't completely dragging his feet the whole time, but he also isn't in a massive rush to get from point A to point B. I personally didn't find the walking speed to be detrimental. I'm someone who usually hates not having a sprint option, but in this case, it really wasn't a big deal to me. You are almost always near an elevator or staircase, and the building that you are in is quite small. Fort Solis is a small building, and even in the times where I had to go back to an area to retrace my steps, it usually only took me a minute or two to get back to a completely different area of the building. You will get to where you need to go in no time at all, even without a sprint option. Where the game falls flat for me is the half baked story. I enjoyed snooping around the place, searching for documents to read, e-mail logs to delve into, and audio / video logs to collect. However, each and every single clue to solving this mystery is a very vague one. By the end of the game, you have pieced together dozens of vague clues, and as a result, you only have a vague idea of what's going on... somewhat. I'm trying to avoid spoilers at all cost here, which is why I'm not elaborating much further. Let's just say that many aspects of this story felt unfinished or disjointed. There is one singular common denominator throughout the entirety of the story. You can piece together that a certain thing happened at Fort Solis, however, the clues about said thing are extremely abstract and obtuse. Then, they throw in a few things that are sort of out of left field. Some audio logs and text logs mention things that sort of stray from the main narrative that the whole game focuses on. We don't get many answers, many objective truths, and they threw in some seemingly half-finished twists that had no further explanation outside of a video or voice log, and were never further followed up on. Towards the end of the game, I was left feeling perplexed. They kept every single clue to solving this mystery very vague, and I feel as though they did that to build a sense of intrigue and suspense. Did it work? Yeah, I definitely don't mind it when a thriller strings me along with breadcrumbs, and teases me by not giving me many obvious hints along the way... however, I usually only enjoy that sort of slow burn if there is some sort of grand and climactic reveal at the end. This didn't have that. You spend the entirety of the game collecting extremely abstract, disjointed, and murky clues. Then, the game sort of ends, leaving you with half-answered questions, a feeling of half-satisfaction, and a sense of half-understanding what any of this was about. It was reminiscent of some thriller and mystery shows that I've watched on TV. You know, the ones that dangle clues in front of your face the whole time, but never actually let you in on the big secrets, and then when it comes time for the season finale, you're expecting some sort of grand reveal, but it either ends on a cliffhanger or leaves you with a feeling of: "Meh... so, that happened." Yeah, this was like that.

_childDocuments_.review: Never heard of Fort Solis until a friend gifted it to me a little while back, decided to finally give it a whirl as he said he thought it was good. Unfortunately, can't say I share the same sentiment...I just felt this massive disconnect from everything happening the entire time and I wasn't invested enough to care about reading messages, listening to entire audio logs or watching the video entries after about half an hour, it just felt like quite a shallow experience. Voice acting was good and the visuals weren't half bad either for the most part I'll give it that.Fort Solis is essentially just a 3-4 hour walking simulator with QTEs for some reason, set on Mars, the premise starts out promising but fails to deliver anything interesting. Its mostly linear but for achievements you can backtrack a little to a few rooms when you get higher access. There are some random things you can interact with that I suppose was some attempt to add some kind of immersion, but considering the situation seem highly unnecessary for the sake of achievements, like using a punching bag, popping open a cold one or playing pool all while you're apparently "investigating" why the facility is baron of life. Even AFTER finding dead people they STILL keep saying stupid ♥♥♥♥ that just utterly obliterates and undermines the entire scenario.Probably would have given up at that half hour mark if they hadn't implemented the speed walk patch before I played it. In games like this, Immersion is ABSOLUTELY ESSENTIAL and it fails to hit the mark unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a common opinion that Fort Solis is a weak game but I actually enjoyed it very much. The design and graphics are beautiful, mocap is done very nicely. The story is interesting enough, and I liked that it didn't go for the standard cliches and just made a simple story about an experiment delivering a little more than expected. Yes, it's a walking sim, but it says so on the cover and in all reviews. I like that it's a thriller but in no way a horror game -- as much as I loved, say, Soma (a far better story!), sometimes I found it hard to enjoy because it succeeded in giving me the creeps viscerally; fortunately, there's nothing like that here. And the game doesn't overstay its welcome: the story takes about 5 hours, quite enough to develop it a little but not enough to get boring.The negatives exist too, of course. Running would be nice (although I didn't find fast walking to be too tedious, you don't have to cover long distances here). The QTEs are a joke: they are at the same time too hard (for me, at least) and completely unnecessary: failing QTEs doesn't change the outcome of a scene; why they are here at all is beyond me. And there is one completely inexcusable flaw: I spent at least an hour (out of 6) learning how to solve a Rubik's cube; and I did solve it, and the game didn't even give me an achievement for that! Shame on you, developers! Other than that, a very enjoyable experience, recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere and Aesthetics absolutely on point.Voice cast phenomenal.Gameplay a little frustrating. Thankfully only a few times they're needed.Story is so-so. Standard run of the mill sci-fi "where is everyone, oh ♥♥♥♥ that's a pool of blood, I'm not alone after all" type deal. There is the bones of a more interesting story there, but the game doesn't really capitalise on it. I had fun with it. Recommended on sale. Probably not for full price.
