_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is a visual masterpiece....I must say, when I read the initial reviews for Fort Solis, I was scared!BUT after playing it and completing it...WOW!From the title screen, I was amazed by the stunning visuals. This game was done with the Unreal Engine 5.2 and it's OMG, WOW! Sadly to get that WOW, let's be honest, you need to have a beefy GPU to be able to enjoy the visual! Even with my 4080, I had to turn DLSS Quality to get 4K 60+ (My game went from 70-100FPS, with some dips around 60). More optimization is strongly recommended and needed! I have the feeling that even playing at 1080p or 1440p, you'll need a good GPU. So if you do have GPU, you are in from a treat!  Probably one of the best looking game I ever seen and played!Fort Solis absolutely nails the suspense thriller atmosphere with a captivating narrative! If you are expecting a game full of action like Dead Space, this is not it! This is pretty much a walking simulator,  slowly exploring and unfolding the mystery at Fort Solis. Fort Solis is pretty much an interactive movie / game with some exploration!And that's what the developers said about it:"A uniquely singular cinematic experience!The story is told across four chapters. Like a Netflix series, Fort Solis can be binged in one intense session, or played chapter by chapter like an episodic TV show."Fort Solis got some great voice actings with amazing performances from Roger Clark, Troy Baker and Julia Brown. I really enjoyed all the exchanges between Roger and Julia. There's a few gems there!Fort Solis is a visual masterpiece, an amazing showcase of the UE 5.2 but it's not a perfect game!Here's some suggestion I would have love to see in the game (maybe for a sequel or a future project):- Adding the poossibilities to walk faster (Maybe with a NewGame+ mode, once you complete the game for the 1st time)- Adding a few jump scares here and there (with noise, etc.), to make the walking and exploration even more stressfull! The story itself got alot of horror movie references.- Adding an HDR mode- Fix the FPS drops here and there!- There's some QTE (not always easy or obvious) or little puzzles but nothing will have sadly a huge impact on the story!- It would have been cool to have multiple endings based on previous QTEs.If you like some slow but effective cinematic game, Fort Solis is for you (especially if your GPU can handle it).With 4 chapters and around 3-3h30 of gameplay, Fort Solis is really showing what UE 5.2 can do and I'm excited to see what's next from Fallen Leaf, Black Drakkar Games.9 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing through this.Maybe this game is a "waling simulator", but honestly it just contributes to the pace the game was intended to have.I enjoyed going through the detailed environments, immersing myself in the world-building done so far (which is expanded on  in a sort of epilogue short story the developers linked in a Steam announcement), and the little elements of mystery were also nice. In fact it was a mystery up until the end. Although the reveal wasn't very revealing, upon reflection I realized what's actually shocking is the lengths gone through by the physical antagonist. I won't spoil that, just keep it in mind if you play the game or have already played it.And there were two things funny about this game and how I ended up deciding to review it.First, I had no idea Roger Clark was voicing the main protagonist when I bought this game. A few minutes in, a little confused by the widely different accent, I was like, "Wait. Is this Arthur Morgan?" And it was. About ten minutes in I was so convinced I finally just paused the game and Googled it to confirm. I just initially bought this game because of the Sci-Fi, honestly.The second funny thing is I completely forgot to review this game for several months. The reason why I ended up remembering to write one is that Fallen Leaf actually responded to some comment on some post responding to someone unhappy with the post-release development pace. It was a little weird, especially since I had completely forgotten about it and this so happens to be a time where recent reviews are "mixed". But really I find it hilarious more than anything. This reminds me, I should probably write a few reviews for a couple other games....Oh! Yeah. Overall 9/10. I suppose the writing could've been done better overall, but obviously they put a lot of work into the atmosphere. That plus the environments and the voice acting are bulking this score up quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited for this game but agree with other reviewers. I don't mind the slow pace...I don't even mind the zero action. More like a narrative experience as we've seen with games like Gone Home. I'm fine with that. The visuals...the world building...the voice acting is seriously amazing and puts bigger studios to shame and I 10000% mean that. I wish more games put this much effort into the world building.I would have liked more detail from the video logs...what exactly is happening and why...it's all just too vague. You can't have a slow paced narrative game like this while also making the story vague in details. If the story was solid I think this would be a classic game that people would rave about. The non-running was annoying at first but I realized you would just run thru all the levels and miss all the little details. But man the lore in this world is something I do want more of. If there ever is a sequel I would say the story can't be so vague. It's a short game at around 4 hours...I'm all for supporting an indie studio. Would I suggest picking it up at this price...probably not but I would pick it up for a a bit cheaper. To me the game kind of had a "The Shining" feel and vibe to it at certain points but never really made it clear why everything is happening.

_childDocuments_.review: If I am honest, I didn't mind the story and I think I would of actually enjoyed the game otherwise but what I found absolutely immersion breaking was the quick time events. Don't get me wrong, I have played with this mechanic before in other games and had no problem with it but this game uses it extremely poorly. For starters I found them unreasonably quick, and it got so bad I wondered if perhaps I was using the wrong kind of controller when I was absolutely sure I got the input correct. It got to the point I felt no reason to press the buttons SPECIALLY when the prompts would switch between two button prompts, single prompt, bumper prompts and then in random places on the screen in less then a second. I missed a few because I didn't even see them until I saw the red! Then there was the consequences, ultimately there was no real reason for them and the only one that mattered was the end scene. I failed literally all of them before the very end scene and at the end I succeeded and got the 'good ending' most likely because of the movement sticks. It felt like I was being punished for not being quick enough but in the end it barely changed anything! Just made me feel punished for playing the game and I really don't understand why this mechanic was in the game and so poorly incorporated.I'm quite sad because I loved the interactions between the two main character and even some others but that was before the random quick time events, afterwards I was just too peeved to even enjoy it

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to write this review. I badly wanted to like this game, but I played it. I thought it was really not good. I found the gameplay so thoroughly uninteresting and dull that I LITERALLY couldn't even make it to the end of the game's story, a first for me. (I'm not one of those people who need everything to be extra fun and arcadey to enjoy a game). And I say this as someone who LOVED Disco Elysium, Death Stranding, and What Remains Of Edith Finch. So I don't exactly suffer from Goopy Goblin Gamer Brain, I can tolerate and enjoy many games people complain about having tedious, clunky, and cumbersome control schemes, like many older games that didn't age the best, as well as titles like Red Dead Redemption 2 known for it's slow and sluggish inputs. But just something about this game's controls and slow ass movement speed. It's like nails on a chalkboard torture to me. It's absolutely unbearable to play. On paper I should really like this game. They got Roger Clark (Arthur Morgan) and Troy Baker (Joel Miller and COUNTLESS other iconic characters), and Julia Brown (wasn't familiar with her work, but she's great too) in this game. All the performances were great. It's just that this game feels like it has zero vision in terms of any new or interesting thing to do with it's mechanics. It seems to genuinely wish it was a Netflix series with no ideas of how to turn it's concept into a thought provoking interactive experience. (Again I am not anti cinematic games, I LOVE Alan Wake 2, Red Dead Redemption 2, Silent Hill 2, The Last Of Us, Hellblade, Death Stranding, and many more of these types of games) I just think the execution here is SERIOUSLY missing something. I wonder if Fort Solis is a warning to indie studios who want to pursue AAA level photorealism and Naughty Dog/Rockstar levels of mocapped animation fidelity, but don't quite have the resources and budget levels to properly do it justice under the house of an engaging and well designed video game, because it genuinely feels like they poured all their resources into that one aspect, but had no resources or budget left to put into a strong core design foundation for this title. And then you get this awful experience where just walking through a hallway is so painfully boring and dreadful that you literally want to close the game and uninstall it. Also from what I have gathered, this level of fidelity also needs a ton of manpower to properly engineer and optimize for modern hardware, but I remember that even with my very solid RTX 3060 PC with a strong CPU and 32 GB DDR4 RAM, the game was running very poorly, even after I altered the settings and had upscalers going. I think that can be another downside of attempting this with a smaller studio. (Again, it makes me sad to even write this, I hope that Fallen Leaf could hopefully take some of this feedback and one day make a game that truly puts them in the spotlight as a special studio to pay attention to, but I just think they swung and missed with Fort Solis.) Sometimes you swing and miss as an artist or studio and that obviously is no fun. I consider this game a failure, but also see it as hopefully a powerful learning opportunity for Fallen Leaf that propels them to new heights one day.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a fan of this game. It's a walking simulator for sure, but the atmosphere is extremely cool (think near-future Mars sci-fi), the environments are beautiful, and the character performances are all fantastic, which are basically the three things that will make or break a game like this.The main two characters have great on-screen chemistry, and their dialogue is surprisingly authentic and endearing - the writers really captured the vibe of coworkers chatting about a job like normal people, incorporating a bit of banter without slipping into MCU-esque quippiness. Roger Clark nails the archetype of a slightly grumpy older employee who regards company regulations and red tape with a kind of benign dismissal; I've known enough of those in my own life that he immediately felt familiar to me within the first half hour of the game. His bemused fascination with "old" technology is a nice touch, as well.Julia Brown is great as a diligent up-and-comer whose dynamic with her peer might be summarized as "affectionate exasperation." Characters who spend most of the game just talking in your ear can easily become an annoyance, especially with the frequency of dialogue in Fort Solis, but she brings easy charisma to the role, and the quality of the script here is sufficiently high that I always enjoyed hearing her character's input.And of course, Troy Baker absolutely knocked it out of the park as Wyatt Taylor. No spoilers here, but there are a few critical story moments where the quality of facial capture really elevates his performance. Every scene that he's in is pretty riveting.Mechanically the game is perfectly fine - I had some minor performance issues, but the game sits pretty comfortably around 60fps on a 2080ti. Interactions with the environment are tactile and satisfying, the areas are large enough to feel believable without being a pain to get through, and the layout of the base is fairly intuitive. Minimal backtracking makes the slow walking speed more bearable, though I still hope they find a way to add a slightly faster option without messing up dialogue timings (surprisingly tricky with this style of game).All in all Fort Solis was easily worth the $25 asking price for me. It's important to go in with the right expectations, though: specifically, this is not a horror game, and 99% of the playtime really is just walking around an empty Mars base trying to piece together what happened via audio, text, and video logs. If you're on the fence about that framework, or are leery of walking simulators in general, you might wait for a sale. For everyone else: this is an easy recommendation for me, and congratulations to Fallen Leaf for a great release.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better visual novels I've played through. It's eerie, unsettling, and atmospheric like few games I've experienced. As a screenwriter, I'm always looking for great pacing, story, and execution (through acting & narrative) - this hits on all fronts. Yes, the movement is slow - is it game breaking? Absolutely not. In fact it's much more realistic. Do you think Ellen Ripley would be running through Nostromo when it was clear there was unknown foul play at large? Not every game needs/or should be a running simulator. I won't go into narrative elements, but I do think there's room for more story through a part two in the series. Incredible acting by the cast, really top notch, and hoping for more Fort Soils down the line. Lastly, while on the short side, this is a prime example of quality over quantity. 8.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is essentially a tech demo of UE5, supported by good acting performances. The main appeal to its gameplay is investigating and piecing together the various story threads strewn throughout the game, though most have little payoff other than the satisfaction of making narrative connections. The story's main draw is the moments of humanity in the characters, and a world that is unusually grounded and mundane but in a way that I personally found compelling.With the right expectations and mentality, I think Fort Solis is a good experience. However, I think the developers should let the player sprint when dialogue is not playing, and just force the player to walk during dialogue so it isn't cut off, which many other games do.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good interactive movie walking sim. Keeps tension and intrigue. Great art direction, writing, acting, and interactions. So much quicktime I thought it might be sponsored by Apple. :P A little camera jankiness that borderlines on bug (when you first enter the MU), collision issues/clipping which I am surprised have not been fixed by now. I am recommending it while it is on sale for $15, would not have bought for $25 and glad I didn't. Looking forward to seeing where they take this new IP.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game, but why did you make a walking simulator where walking feels like wading through mud? Between the slow walking speeds and difficulty rounding tight corners it doesn't exactly make for an experience that makes you want to explore your surroundings. Luckily it's not a deal-breaker as usually you only need to walk a few steps to the next story beat. Just make sure you disable camera smoothing.Lumen, the real-time global illumination system is freaking out pretty bad in some locations, giving super noisy and glitchy visuals. But almost all the environment lights in this game are static. If the developers used static, baked lighting it would've looked a lot better AND had better performance.As other have mentioned the story was pretty standard, but well executed with great voice acting and pretty good animations.I was quite surprised at the QTE mechanic, I thought everybody had agreed back in 2010 that we were done with that?I have to praise the level design, almost the whole game takes place in one location that keeps looping back on itself. There was only one passage where it broke down a bit (the long crawl).Anyway it's a decent game that you can easily finish in one sitting.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it for a couple of reasons, but good things first:- Good actors doing a good job ... given the thin story.- Good environment (3D modelling, lighting, effects, sounds, ...).- Starts off promising.Bad:- The graphics default settings it started with lead to repetitive "white screen of death" incidents, aka almost killed my GPU.- I played through in only 5 hours (would have been faster without the GPU issue).- The gameplay is basically just walk around, the occasional interact with object, and checking stuff out on your wristband. You just walk around and gather information while you're alone. All interactions with characters are basically interactive movies. You can't move and just helplessly watch (which doesn't match the characters and their background at all). Whenever you should better do something drastic immediately to survive in such scenes, you're only given a tiny fraction of a second to press a specific key you don't know before. Nevertheless the outcome is basically always the same ... and not in your favor.- The dark mystery part of the story doesn't make sense. -> IMHO a complete waste of time

_childDocuments_.review: Positive:- The game-play consists mostly of walking and quick-time events, however the environment and the story is immersive enough so that the walking simulator aspect did not bother me.- Looks and sounds absolutely amazing. I felt intrigued through the whole thing. Negative:- The story is interesting, however I felt like some elements were over-told, some important elements felt like clutter and fell by the wayside for me while playing it. Now thinking about it feels inconsistent.- There is an option to move faster, which is the same walking animation sped up. Felt and looked very weird, considering some moments of the story. I feel like a simple light jogging animation with the same speed would have made a lot of difference regarding immersion.- I suspect that some of the quick-time (potentially even every single one) does not affect the actual outcome of the scene. I missed quite a lot of them, which made me care less.Conclusion:- I absolutely enjoyed it, however it felt more of a cinematic interactive tech demo, rather then a game, which is not a problem, however may miss some people’s expectations.- Took me less than five hours to complete so I would suggest getting it at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I really wanted to like this game, the only good thing about it is the graphics. Everything else is poorly executed.Is there supposed to be a big mystery? Nope, the plot is as clear as day, and you get to role play the peril of stupid characters in typical horror movies. Shouldn't I at least have the means to defend myself before walking straight into such obvious, life-threatening danger? ..Nope. *Having the plot spoon-fed to you: Oh no.. what is happening?And let's not ignore the elephant in the room, you can only walk slowly at all times in this game. I wanted to believe that it was an artistic choice to build immersion, but there are so many immersion-breaking elements. I can't see this as anything other than a blatant method to prolong playtime.The game could be finished in less than 1 hour instead of 5. It feels more like a frustrating walking simulation, at no point do I ever feel any sense of horror. Do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there Dear Devs,Thank you for a lot of work put in this project. Fort Solis's environment is convincing and a huge effort was put towards designing station architecture (Artbook DLC - bravo). I love two main characters design and their voice over. Julia Brown & Troy Baker - You made the game worthwhile - respect!So why the negative? Because despite the fact that the plot is a crucial part of this game, in many places where there could have been alternative choices, we have only a linear story, that takes Player for only a couple of hours spin. Short game play alone is not a bad thing, but combined with only three known alternative endings, which none of them makes me feel like - 'good job, well done', unfortunately puts this title on the shelf of 'one-timers'. There are some graphical glitches like shimmering on objects in dark places (but that might be happening because of little number of lights sources - maybe) and some random artifacts on the rocky ground outside the base (again may be my machine only).As another downside I will mention sequences of buttons to be pressed to move forward in key moments, although some people may be OK with that, that doesn't work for me. Stressing myself over some random key sequence while a key scene is being played on the screen doesn't fit my best definition of fun... If there are no alternatives to the plot (for example different ending's for ), there is a chance a Player will not run the title again - so why in the first place take the most important parts of the story away from him?In my case - I will not come back, I will not play again... please tell me - why should I?

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is less than a game than an interactive movie.So it is more akin to the Dark Pictures Anthology than to Moon of Madness.There are no puzzles. You only have to push the right buttons. Here and then you have a very short time frame to press the correct one. But all in all it didn't seem like this had any effect. So it didn't matter whether I pushed the right button in the right time or not.That is the game.The walking speed is annoyingly slow for me. Admittedly I just placed Mass Effect before this game and I understand why the developers chose not to include the possibility to run.The main point is to create a tense atmosphere.The game does that really good. The video and audio logs and mails all add to that. I wasn't in the slightest annoyed by watching and listening to them.Unfortunately Fort Solis is more akin to a movie than a game also regarding length. It is awfully short.So if you want to buy an interactive movie with a really good atmosphere but less possibilities to interact than the Dark Pictures Anthology you might like Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: I first noticed this game when it was revealed at Summer Games Fest and it looked like it was right up my alley. I love Sci-Fi, I like horror/thriller, and I do enjoy good visuals. This game ticks those boxes so I wishlisted it right away and bought it on release. These are my thoughts after two playthroughs.The story here is the main focus of the game. And I found it very intriguing for the most part. You play as Jack Leary (voiced by Roger Clark) who is part of a two-person operation at a base on Mars called Fort Minor when an alarm beacon goes off for a distant base, the titular Fort Solis. You head off by yourself with your coworker on comms, Jessica Appleton (voiced by Julia Brown), to keep you company as you explore the base to find out what's wrong. The story has a good pace to it, it sets up a very creepy atmosphere that left me personally craving each next morsel of the plot. The majority of the story told here is told through audio logs, video logs and emails.I did enjoy the story quite a bit, and as it's the main attraction for this game that's a good thing. However it must be said that the ending is kind of underwhelming. I was reading every email, watching every video log, listening to every audio file and by the end of the story I was left slightly confused, still needing to put pieces together myself. It just felt lacklustre to me, however all of the build up and the journey to the end was very exciting and I will liken this to a 4 episode mini series as you'd find on Netflix.The gameplay here is mostly walking. That's what you'll be doing in this game. It's listed as a walking simulator on Steam and that is the perfect description for it. There are other small things you will need to do, such as find batteries to open doors and solve some simple puzzles. There are also quick time events in this game and geez they are pretty savage. The time you have to press some of them is extremely small. The QTE's don't really impact the story too much, save for some. I won't pretend that the gameplay is amazing here but as a walking simulator I expect no more than what was delivered. I did enjoy myself, taking my time exploring Fort Solis and looking at all the details in the environment. The game is very atmospheric so that helps a lot.Visually the game is striking. I loved the look of it, it paints a very grim and atmospheric picture for you to sink into. There's really nothing else to do other than sings it's praises in this category, however I will say that at times the characters dialogue and lips were out of sync, at least for me. This wasn't during cut scenes but during gameplay it was quite bad.The sound is amazing. All of the noises happening inside of the base with the low, intensely booming music backdrop give to the feeling of being trapped, that something is always waiting around the next corner. I really enjoyed the sound of this game. This game also knows when to keep quiet which is something not a lot of games these days seem to do. Sometimes less is more, especially for a game trying to keep up the tension. And not to mention the voice acting. It's really quite good, one of the better written and acted games I've played for quite a while. In particular I want to praise Julia Brown's performance as Jessica. She sounds extremely genuine which was very nice.I played the game on PC with an RTX 2080 Ti, an i9 9900K, 32GB's of RAM on Windows 10 with and SSD. For me the performance was a bit choppy. This game seemed to be able to hold a stable 60 at times but then it would suddenly hitch quite bad, most commonly when going into a new area. I ended up lowering the frame rate cap to 30 and that did make it a lot more bearable for me. I do not mind 30 FPS as long as it's stable so for me it was a lot better. But there is no denying that the game feels slightly unpolished or undertweaked for PC.As for bugs I didn't really come across any, none that stand out in my memory. The game seemed pretty bug free to me. The one exception to this is two instances where the controller inputs stayed on the screen and I'd have to open my wrist device and close it again to get rid of it. This only happened to me twice in about 10 hours of play.I really think this game is quite good for how much it costs. I live in Australia and new games tend to be $90 to $120 these days, a lot of money no matter how you look at it. I got this game during launch week so it was 10% cheaper than normal but even at full price it's only $40. For me the game is well worth that amount of money. You'd be paying the same for a mini series Bluray set at a retail store.The game has some issues but none that prevented me from enjoying my experience. I'd be keen to play a game from these developers again, or if they ever release a sequel of some kind. The graphics and audio is amazing, the story is good except for the underwhelming ending and I think if you enjoy some decent stories and have some love for taking your time and letting yourself sink right into a rich world full of mystery, you'll like this game. I definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am mostly posting a review because of the negative review bomb at launch. I was able to play the game through and did not experience any crashes. Graphics performance did leave something to be desired, but wasn't game breaking to me. I was excited to try this game after watching some pre-launch gameplay on YouTube. I really appreciate that the developers tried something a little out of the ordinary, and I think it paid off. The story telling is immersive, and the setting is beautiful. I did not intend to finish the game in one session, but I could not put it down. For anyone considering this, It is very much Dead Space a la Firewatch, and is more of a slow-burn cinematic experience. My only real complaints are that the quick-time events came on a little too fast for me, and there are a few parts of the game where I would've liked to have the option to run. Character movement was also a little meh, sometimes getting hung up in places where I shouldn't have. All in all, it's a good game for what it is and I hope to see more like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort SoulessThis is def a story driven walking sim. It is a sci-fi thriller which is what intrigues me. This is not comparable to Dead Space and reminded me more of Firewatch. The mechanics of the game is to walk slowly or press and hold left analog stick/shift to walk slightly faster. you use button prompts for looking at things like audio logs, posters, and video logs. There are also QTEs which don't matter until you are trying to do the alternate ending (which sucks btw). Just be aware there is no combat or anything like that. They have a powerhouse of voice actors and they def deliver with what is given to them dialogue wise. This game has a great setting being on Mars going through a research facility. The characters have heft to them when you are controlling them which comes off more sluggish than adding some sort of realism. The story itself is pretty interesting although short and unsatisfying. I do like the bit of ambiguity.Graphically this game looks great but has these moments where it looks very off. The software Lumen looks terrible. There is just too much visual noise it looks like walls are boiling or something. There is no option to turn it off. The options menu has very terrible graphical settings. There is also no ultrawide support. I also do not understand why we can not rebind buttons in the game menu or toggle the "1.3x walking speed" no you have to hold the button down. Performance wise I didn't have many stutters but they are there. I had a weird bug where I was stuck in a vent shaft when the button prompts just didn't work and had to reboot the game. I did not have any crashes. I also experienced very odd DLSS 3 ghosting or double imaging so I ended up not using it. I didn't have any crazy FPS drops either that I noticed which is surprising since this is a unreal engine game. I also had one big Stutter where the game literally stopped dead in its tracks and all a sudden the game changed my Xbox controller prompts to Playstation ones... okay? Overall performance is good I cant say its bad.Edit:So... this game feels like it should have just been a Netflix series bc I do not think this works as a game although, I think this would have been one of the few good Netflix series. as a Game... I do not recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed reviews? Absolutely undeserved! Many people play without understanding what game they are playing! It's like going to watch a romantic movie thinking it's an action movie instead! And then judge it as if it were an action movie! And obviously a romantic movie can only receive negative ratings from those who judge it as if it were an action movie!What is Fort Solis? It's not an action game for sure! Forget it! Are you looking for action, combats, shootings, easy fun, usual challenges and achievements, jump scares, hard puzzles, etc? Forget it! It's not the game for you!So, what is Fort Solis? It's a psychological sci-fi thriller based on thick deep atmosphere, great acting, good dialogues, very good story, compelling interactive narrative, impressive mo-cap animations, wise direction and one of the best graphics ever in a videogame.Not enough?I cannot believe the care developers put in the design of the Mars environment and sci-fi scenarios, better than many sci-fi movies. Extremely detailed and realistic graphics, impressive lighting and visual effects, state of the art soundscape: Fort Solis takes literally the player to Mars, period! You're not watching a movie: despite the poverty of narrative branches and a quite linear path , you can explore and contemplate the wonderful scenarios at your will and pace, you can decide what to do first and next. I played for 5 hours and I have not explored the whole map, I have missed several places, clues, audio and video logs and documents.This is a game you have to taste slowly as a vintage red wine, not fast as a lager beer.Some people pretend that a person wearing a bulky, heavy and rigid space suit on a low-gravity alien planet and a helmet equipped with an oxygen respirator should run and act like in an action film set on planet Earth! They make me laugh! They remind me of those players who expected the blind little girl to move quickly in the game Beyond Eyes! Is that the average intelligence of gamers? OMG! I'm still laughing! Fortunately Fort Solis is a realistic and serious experience with great care for such details. I really really enjoyed the direction of the whole experience, very serious, mature, realistic, plausible, with the right pace suitable for a psychological thriller set in space that pays a lot of attention to the characters rather than stupid action scenes at all costs or easy jumps scares or puzzles and challenges that are dissonant with the narrative.Actors are so incredible, I barely remember such good acting in any videogame; the quality of the mo-cap is so good that characters have life-like expressions you can barely distinguish from flesh and bone actors. Fort Solis reaches the next level of technical achievement thanks to wise implementation of the latest development tools, finally a next gen not-VR experience that put at good use my beefy PC!And believe me, story is so good, not what you expect, very smart, so ambiguos, I would say courageous, so far from every easy and blatant trend based on special effects or super powers; it's centered on human psychology, almost in contrast with the sci-fi context, I really appreciated it.It's not without complaints. There is no innovation in interactive narrative. Gameplay intertwines in a completely natural and fluent way with several but short and state of the art cinematic cut scenes, often triggered by Quick Time Events. It's ok, we are used to such kind of experience in games from Dontnod, Telltale, Quantic Dream; anyway I would like less cut scenes and QTE and more interactions where player doesn't lose control. I would like more innovative interactive mechanics. However narrative is good and compelling, you feel like the protagonist of a movie, immersed in the virtual experience, that's what matters more. No multiple choice dialogues in Fort Solis, it's not necessarily bad; in Quantic Dream or Telltale games they give you the chance to take important decisions, to influence the ending or to change relationships. However sometimes the outcomes are contradictory, it's like writing several stories and try to make them coherent. On the contrary, Fort Solis makes you the protagonist of a coherent story, the story that the developers took great care of and want the player to experience in an interactive and immersive way, as if you were the protagonist of a movie. There are two endings, but they are quite similar and they depends just on the outcome of ending QTEs. Not a defect in my opinion, I loved the story that the developers wanted me to star in. Thanks for the trip, I hope you can develop many more titles like this despite the conservatism and lack of maturity of the gaming market.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I had a great time with Fort Solis, and I don't think it deserves all the negative reviews. There are absolutely things to criticize here, but it seems like many of the reviews are about the "Walking Simulator" nature of the game. Indeed, the game is very linear, story-focused, and there's not a lot of "gameplay" in the traditional sense. It's more of an "interactive movie" type of experience: You are primarily walking around, reading emails and watching video logs, sometimes you need to find keys, and occasionally there are QTEs. It's also fairly short, at about 4 hours.Personally, I enjoy these types of games, I don't mind a shorter length (I prefer a tight and focused experience over a sprawling open world epic) and I don't think a negative review is warranted just because it's not a traditional action-focused game. So with that out of the way, let's start with what I liked about the game.I absolutely love the atmosphere and visuals in the game - it's a wonderfully realized sci-fi world, that immediately pulled me in and felt very immersive. Exploring the station was great, and I was always curious to see what I would discover next. There's a lot of nice world building and environmental story telling, and it feels like a believable place.Graphics, voice acting, and character models/animation are also stellar - it really does look great. And the characters are well done to, in my opinion.The story arc overall also felt well paced, starting out slow and calm, slowly developing a feeling of unease, then ramping up the tension. The final sequence truly had me on edge, it was quite intense due to the anticipation of something bad happening but it took a while until it actually did. This "horror of not knowing" aspect was very well executed. Overall, the game did a great job pulling me into the narrative and its world, and kept me hooked right until the end.Unfortunately, the ending itself left me a bit disappointed - which is my main gripe with the title. It's not that the ending itself is bad - it's mostly fine. The problem is that too many mysteries/open questions in the story are left unanswered. Basically, the whole time you're expecting a big revelation at the end, but it never comes. It doesn't matter if you find all of the optional audio/video logs etc., some key questions are simply not answered. I can only assume that the intention here was to leave things vague, to get players to theorize and come up with their own interpretations. And I get that some people really enjoy that kind of thing, but personally, I prefer a bit more closure.Without getting too much into spoilers, there is a thing in the game which is supposedly very dangerous, causing one of the characters to take extreme actions to prevent the danger. But it is never revealed what the danger actually is, not even hinted at aside from various characters talking about how "bad" it is. But they only allude to it being bad, without ever going into specifics. I really expected the actual danger to be revealed in the end, which would've put a lot of events into perspective and rounded everything out nicely. But instead, I was left wondering what it might be.Performance-wise, the game ran ok, but not great on my machine (2080 Ti, i7 9700k). At 1440p with DLSS Quality mode and max settings otherwise, I was getting between 35 and 70 FPS depending on the scene, but most of the time it hovered somewhere between 50 and 60. Thanks to my G-Sync compatible display, the framerate fluctuation was mostly not noticeable, and it's also not the type of game that really needs super consistent performance to play well. But if you don't have a VFR display, limiting the framerate to 30 might be a better option.What I found a lot more distracting was occasional stuttering, especially when entering a new area for the first time. I'm guessing this might be due to shader compilation, a typical issue with recent Unreal Engine games on PC. Would be nice if that could be fixed in a patch.There were also some odd artifacts with flickering shadows, and I had a game-breaking bug at one point where an interaction prompt didn't appear. Fortunately, restarting the game and replaying from the previous checkpoints fixed that. And I didn't experience any other bugs aside from this one instance.One final thing to mention is the QTEs. It turns out that with one exception, these have absolutely no impact on the outcome of the story, which feels like a missed opportunity. And another issue I have is you sometimes get a prompt in the middle of an otherwise non-interactive cutscene, which catches you off guard and thus is very easy to miss.Ok, so in conclusion - despite the disappointing ending, and some other issues, I still really enjoyed everything before that point, and I would recommend the game if you like this type of experience and aren't put off by the issues mentioned above. It's clearly a very ambitious effort by a small independent team, and I'm glad they took a chance on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is okay. It's not that good, but it's not bad either. The main things that are good about this game are voice acting and the graphics. The story is fine, not the best, but it gets the job done. The "gameplay" is pretty boring, however. It's a walking simulator with minimal interactions. Walking sims can be good, but this is on the more boring side of things. Hearing the characters banter is by far what I enjoyed the most, though, and the sci-fi setting is good, so I could recommend it for those reasons during a sale maybe.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: I have some big issues with Fort Solis but I'll give it a recommend. If Steam had a category of 'get this on a discount' that's where I'd place it with caveats. First, the positives:Now the critique:Overall I leave a recommend since I know how hard it is to just ship any kind of game and this is a great achievement for a small indie team. But at the same time, as a product you should have a good idea of what you're going in for. I hope the team is able to take the feedback from this for their next project.TLDR: It's a very high fidelity walking sim with a simple story that is acted very well. There isn't much interactivity but what is there is neat. YMMV if that's for you.

_childDocuments_.review: game is amazing. its a walking sim. and yes, there is no running. you walk. but the story, atmosphere, and graphics will have you engaged until the end. its not long which i found to be a good thing.(i hate endless storys) the price is appropriate for what you get. you can explore the entire map, indoors and outdoors. before you complete the story.  pushes gpu hard. uses UE5 tech. lumen and nanite so you need a 4090 honestly. with a 4090 i used dlss quality and frame gen to get 100 fps. which i find to be the best. native 4k ultra is only 40fps maybe 55 on the high. but dlss quality and FG in this game is perfect. and hardly a difference from native. story is thrilling and the lighting in this game is unreal.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to recommend this game because I love story driven games, especially those by indie developers, I cannot recommend this game. For the price of 32.50 CAD, I feel like the game should definitely be longer. As for the story itself, I felt like I was engaged and it was intense at moment, however it seemed to end abruptly without any explanation as to what just happened. Even with an extra hour of gameplay and more time to close out the story, would have done the game some good, rather than the abrupt ending. A final complaint I have is the optimization, as the game would run decently well on my 6800xt (yes I did update the software prior to playing), and yet the stuttering and framedrops were way to regular. I did enjoy parts of the game and I think this dev team did a good job at making the game immersive, beautiful and managed to snag some great voice actors, however the story was lackluster. Hopefully the devs will still continue on the storymaking path as even though there is room for improvement, they are not far off from making a great title

_childDocuments_.review: I had zero expectations going in and the game was nice for what it was. Besides they are really really QUICK like the only reason i noticed they made no difference is the second playthrough to collect all the achievements.Graphic wise its nice, unreal engine, atmosphere is there, i thought the rolling rocks were spacerats but ok.Biggest issue for many people in the reviews is the price and the ending. _childDocuments_.review: It's a game with much potential, and I think we get to experience some of it, but not all. The atmosphere, graphics, soundtrack, voice acting, everything is up to par here. _childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying this game is more for the story and exploration/immersion with great voice acting and audio design. If you are going into this with the hopes of spectacular gameplay you will be disappointed. The performance is not great. Graphically the game looks excellent, but you will be experiencing low fps and some stuttering when entering different areas of the game. I had the game crash 3 times within the first hour of playing, but after updating graphics drivers it hadn't crashed anymore.Although there is not much going on with the gameplay, it can still be annoying. Your character's movement feels very "heavy" and unresponsive. Although you don't need precise movements in this game, it still should've been improved. The use of QTE's seems unnecessary in this game. They pop up on random parts of the screen and can semi blend in if you aren't ready for it. Some of them are pretty quick as well, however I'm not even sure if completing them or failing them makes any difference honestly. Also maybe a preference, but the walking speed is slow and can be a little tedious getting from one section to the next.The story telling and banter between both protagonists in this game is something I enjoyed. Not only was the voice acting excellent, but the audio design and music was great as well. The sounds you would hear throughout the game made the game a lot more immersive. My one gripe with this is the end of the game seemed semi rushed, and it can be a little confusing in my opinion. I am also a big fan of the one take camera such as in God of War or Dead Space.I recommend this game if you are looking for more of a story than a game. Although the performance wasn't great, it was playable after updating drivers. If this concerns you I would recommend waiting until they sort these issues out.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a walking simulator that has a good atmosphere, beautiful visuals, and good acting, but it is a painful game in which the player is constantly stressed for the sake of the creator's self-satisfaction throughout the entire game.The walking speed is as slow as a turtle, and the camera keeps shaking, so even if you are used to playing games, you will get sick from 3D sickness after 2 hours of playing.There are no major events throughout the game, and you are just forced to walk along a long path, which is tedious from the very beginning of the game. Furthermore, the visibility of the map is extremely poor, and it is not even clear where the player is or which direction they are facing, let alone what the potential destination is.Then there are the sudden QTEs, which are instant death events that require the input of multiple button combinations that have never been touched before. The auto-save intervals are sketchy, and even the basic specification of a manual save is not implemented.The lack of intelligence and imagination of the creators of this game is all imposed on the player as stress.Now, when this is pointed out by many users, the production company releases a statement that is, to put it mildly, crazy, such as "This game is intentionally designed to be stressful so that you can enjoy this atmosphere, so please be patient. It's pathetic that they don't even realize that they are ruining everything.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game for £13. Completed it in 2.8 hours. Was it worth it? Only just.Firstly it feels like a tech demo more than a game, they spent more time on the graphics than anything else. The plot had so much potential but the way that it is unfolded makes no sense - I'm a regular player of story games like this and this is one of the only times where I've had to have the ending explained to me. Without spoiling anything, they throw some red herrings, and that's all good, but when it comes to the reveal - they just don't. They have video logs of the workers at Fort Solis and I expected a log near the end where there was some explanation for why what's happening at Fort Solis *is* happening and it just didn't happen. Like there was some transparency bias in telling the plot, as if the writer thought "Yeah everybody gets this, there's no need to outline it".Secondly, the plot is split between 2 characters. There's no problem with this as a format, however, you spend just enough time with both of them to not care too much about either. The game needed to be an hour longer at least so both characters get 30 minutes more of time to actually relate to them. This is a crime that's committed several times, not just for the 2 protagonists but also for the antagonist and all the workers at Fort Solis. It just needed more time to be worth the original ticket price.Minor peeve - For a game where you spend all the time walking around you'd think they spend more time on the "fast walk" animation - it just looks like the normal walk animation sped up - which looks completely unnatural.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this was an awesome experience, I really enjoyed my time with Jack and Jessica around Fort Solis. Sure, it isn't really a survival horror game like I first thought, it is a Sci-Fi Horror Thriller and this alone makes Fort Solis stand up in the crowd of Dead Spaces, Resident Evils and Callisto Protocols for example. But it is taking many elements from these games and tells a narrative story through video recordings of the Crew, CCTV footages, audio logs and e-mails and through the environment. The atmosphere and the overall graphics are gorgeous and can really distract you while you're slowly walking your way through the facility and the martian surface. At first the slow walking speed can be a little bit annoying, but I did get used to it after a while, even appreciating it for the pace the game is trying to achieve. In active gameplay there is nothing that requires you to sprint, though there are some scenes where your character moves or even runs automatically in respond to a small "cutscene".One negative thing that I'd like to point out are the QTE's that just happen and you've only got like a second to react to them. I only got some of them at the near end randomly correct which maybe got me the "good ending" but before, they were too random and too fast to react to. Just my opinion, could very well be a skill issue of mine with QTE's.The story is well written and is especially good with certain details. The characters are all extremely well animated and modeled and the voice acting is top notch. Having no HUD or whatsoever makes Fort Solis a overall very solid and super immersive, but also short lived experience with about 4 hours of playtime, maybe 5-6 if you really explore every corner of the game and do the backtracking into already visited levels after you acquired the highest security clearance. If you walk into this game without any expectations of having to fight various monsters or generally any realtime or turn based combat you will have a good time exploring Fort Solis and trying to find out what happened there.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you are interested in this game story (there is nothing else in here, really), better watch on youtube - at least you can change playback speed there.UPD: I've watched the story myself on stream. It is also a major letdown, reducing redeeming qualities of this game to somehow good visuals."So, let's make player walking speed abysmally low, without any form of sprint, so they spend more than 2 hours until they get to something remotely interesting, so they can't refund. Also, include 5 minutes of crawling in the vent where nothing happens, we gotta beat Callipso Protocol at least in something".Yeah, what about no.Another example that describes the game really well is a moment in the beginning when you take a vehicle and ride to the titular Fort Solis. No dialogs, no exposition through environment, no even control over car to keep player engaged somehow. You are left to stare at the car and brown-grey martian rocks in a silence for 3 minutes of NOTHING HAPPENING. Developers were really keen on making master-class at wasting player time.On the second note, if you rely on DLSS for your game to work on decent framerate (40 fps on i7 9700k + RTX 3070 without DLSS on, sick), can you at least ensure your upscaling does not create artifacts for 75% of all lighting in the game?On the third note, developers really nailed how to say "screw you" to M&KB players, because even if you go past extremely unresponsive camera with mouse and complete lack of controls rebinding, having B for cancelling (because, you know, "B" on gamepad is commonly used as "cancel" button) is just laughable.

_childDocuments_.review: I am into in-game photography. I am therefore a big fan of photo-realistic games, and especially of games with well modeled, detailed characters, atmospheric lighting, shadows, props, scenery, etc. I also do enjoy expressive animations and movement that look alive, character that have good hair and clothe models (in this case, they used a clever modeling to style the hair believably and yet have it all fit well within the helmet), and in-game scenematics that are real-time and not pre-rendered. Add to that my love of a good tense mystery, believable situations/decisions, good voice acting and a sci-fi, futuristic, Mars base and landscape, and well, I pretty much knew I was going to buy this game. The game play is short, and likely there is no reason to play through again unless you want to 100% it (because there is one item I cannot seem to collect after finishing the game). Most of my time in-game was spent screenshotting and I certainly got value and a good time from that. They should add an animation viewer to the model viewer in the bonus options after completing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I mostly only play games with Photomode in them. So once I found out this game had one I had to give it a try. The game is based on quick time events, where you punch buttons at certain points to interact with the environment. So as far as what you can do in the game that is pretty much it. The story is a thriller/horror base game that is not bad for the size of the game. At times it can be predictable, but then with pretty much all games like this you will eventually get that. My interest in this game is very much based around the photomode, which for what this game is, is better then most for a game this size. The texture quality is very good as you can get close to objects and you can aperture the object to keep its detail. If you are a virtual photographer then this game will give you unlimited amounts of shoots to take. The camera is worth mentioning that you can go from orbit cam to free cam. The distance of the cam is limited by the orbit but the orbit is not bad for distance.The one thing I don't like is that I always have to have the exposure at the highest to get a shot that doesn't look dark when I take it. As a virtual photographer I have put in 6 hours and have around 100 photos so far. I could see playing this game over again just to shoot things I didn't the first time around.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very enjoyable.  The visuals are absolutely beautiful, and despite having some crashes when I first started playing it, I updated to the latest Nvidia driver and added a -dx11 switch to the startup parameters.  After that the game ran very smoothly with no crashes for the rest of the game play.I7 11700RTX 308032G Ram1TB M.2 SSDIt is a very short game, but reasonably priced and well worth the money for what it delivers.  I felt that it started a little slow, but picks up. It is not a Hack and Slash game, or a Dead Space / Callisto clone, In fact  you have NO weapons for the entire game.   It's more of a Space Crime Drama where you are uncovering clues while investigating a distress signal from a research facility on Mars, or at least I assume it is mars.  Good voice acting and an easy to follow story line, that gets progressively better. I know that there were several negative reviews and some reported bugs on launch, and I almost didn't purchase this, but I am glad that I did.   The Developers are promising an upcoming patch to fix some of the reported problems.  I think they did a pretty decent job and definitely paid a lot of attention to details when it comes to both the planet and the base.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was basically a 50/50 for me, and I decided to side with recommending in the end because it's a small indie team, I think it's their first game, and so ultimately I'm hoping they can get some success from this, learn from the mistakes, and come back with something even better. _childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand the bad reviews this game's got. First of all, it's made by a team of 12 people. That's it. For what it delivers, it's impressive. And oh boy, it delivers. The voice acting, the atmosphere, the music are all top notch. The story is simple with a few twists, but for a walking simulator is enough. Exploring is nice, pace feels ok. Walking speed is perfect. If you dislike it, this game genre is not for you. Don't review bomb a game for something you don't even like in the first place. Just walk away. Second, for all of you cry babies that flaunt all of your 4090's around, it's sad to see you don't really understand how PC gaming actually works and/or is made. There is no way in hell a team of 12 can even make a game work perfectly on every configuration out there. There is no way they can make it work for all of you that never updated a driver in your life as well. And if you own a PC, you know it ain't that simple. It's not only about drivers. It's about optimizations made to your machine, from UEFI settings and UEFI updates, adjustments to temp profiles for your CPU/GPU to how stable an overclock actually is (you're all OC-ing your PC's, you just don't know it -- yeah, setting up a XMP profile for your ram is OC). There are a hell of a lot of things that can go wrong with a PC, even down to having different manufacturers for the memory chips that are soldered on your RAM disks, thus having different base clock speeds that can lead to a very unstable system if XMP is activated; this is just an example out of many, or that X cpu works best with that Y ram (stability wise) etc. And funniest of all, y'all get the latest CPU/GPU but when it comes to the motherboard, arguably the most important part of a PC and the most critical to be chosen very well, you cheap out and make compromises. Everyone expects a PC, even a top tier one, to behave perfectly. But that ain't the case. A console will behave perfectly. Because that hardware is specifically made with that architecture in mind for that X Y Z type of games, that, in turn, will be optimized as hell for just one platform (this is a whole lot easier for a developer to do). With all of the above being said, this game ran perfectly for me (average of 70-80 FPS) on a 3070 paired up with a ryzen 7 5800X3d and 32 gigs of ram, on the highest settings and in 2k. The game was very enjoyable and relaxing and I recommend it to everyone that likes this genre :)

_childDocuments_.review: I give the game a thumbs up with the caveat that it's not worth the full asking price. Its a decent game in some respects, but quite short and has some weird mechanics like useless quicktime events that don't change anything and don't cause you to fail if missed.I originally bought Fort Solis at launch for full price and got a refund as other reviews painted a bleak picture and I was annoyed a cinematic game didn't have cinematic ultrawide support. I recently bought it again for 10 bucks on a key site and for that price the game is worth it. It's essentially a drawn-out interactive movie with a lot of walking and information gathering between events. Nothing about Fort Soil stands out as bad, other than the dumb quicktime events and lack of any control over events as they unfold. It's a walking simulator with a muddy story that could be told in less than an hour, but a lot is left unclear and not fleshed out as well as it could have been despite the 4 hours of "gameplay." _childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is great, with amazing voice actors thrown in.  Would I recommend the game at full price?  Absolutely not until the developers fix the following:- Broken video logs that just show a white screen with no audio- The planetary storm disappears once you exit the tunnel (visual and audio) while your character keeps their hand up like they're in a storm (even inside the maintenance building)- Inconsistent audio (within the same scene audio sound crystal clear, then goes back to having a radio filter while your helmet was on the whole time)  - Moving around takes FOREVER -  we have established our characters can run, but only in cutscenes, and the "speed walk" animation just looks like you need to get to a toilet- The QTEs are too quick, and even when you press the key it registers only half the time- Don't turn the camera to see the character's face while speaking, zero effort in mocap and they look like they're mouthing out vowels in a dubbed filmOver half of the game's exposition is delivered through video logs, and they have willingly ignored a major bug that has been around since last year.  After completing the game I had to go online since I was so lost in regards to what happened before you responded to an alert.  The video logs are even broken in the extra content tab of the main menu.Playing the game in this state will leave you feeling like you just walked through a tech demo, with no substance.While playing I completely expected a bait and switch that showed this was a prequel set in the Dead Space universe and I would find a Marker in the dig site, but sadly it was not that smart of a story.  90% of the main character's choices don't make sense in the actual setting, and the voice acting direction did not increase any sense of urgency even immediately after scenes of finding bodies and blood - just more mundane sentences, quips, references to old horror movies, and even joking between the two.It has potential for a full length game, maybe even a series, but it appears to have been severely rushed and now the developers are not fixing the glaring issues bugging players still buying their product.  If they are going to make a full length fleshed out version in the future then PLEASE hire a good writer, directors, and animators - this title demands a better exploration.So in summary, definitely not worth more than $10 in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing this game I can say it really felt like a disappointment. I enjoy primarily narrative games like this, but this game just wasn't very good all the way around.While the lack of HDR and ultrawide support is disappointing, it doesn't keep you from playing the game and if the game is good on it's own merits, then I can forgive that. But this game doesn't stand on it's own merits unfortunately.While this game does indeed look very beautiful, that is about all it has going for it, except for the excellent voice acting from Roger Clark, Julia Brown, and Troy Baker. The story is not very good. It's a very generic slasher flick that never makes very much sense. I kept playing until the end hoping there would be a nice payoff at the end to make it worthwhile, but I was disappointed. The ending was especially bad as you literally do nothing to stop what's going on, there is simply a deus ex machina that occurs at the end to make everything alright. This game has the laziest kind of story telling, which is pretty bad for a story based game. The story got especially cheesy and predictable towards the end.Other reviews have mentioned this, but it's really important to emphasize how slowly you are forced to walk in this game. It makes the whole game agonizingly tedious to play. I literally started falling asleep in my chair at one point because the pace of the game is so bad. It makes the quick time event rough too, since you become completely disengaged with the game and start zoning out, so you miss them before you even realize one was occurring. It really feels like the developers made a game that could be beaten in 1-2 hours and decided to intentionally slow the player down just to pad out the game play length. I had heard this game was about 5 hours long, but I beat it in 3.5 hours, while trying to fully explore and find everything. There is so little actual game and story here, it is very disappointing. And the high quality graphics and good voice acting can't remotely come close to saving it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has always believed one of the possible futures of gaming was to provide an interactive cinematic experience, where you could play and experience the story as the main character, I find this game absolutely amazing. It does not deserve any of the hate it's receiving. A vast majority of the negative reviews seem to be from people who simply don't enjoy this genre. It would be like me buying an FPS, knowing full well I hate all FPS games and then leaving a negative review saying how bad FPS games are...The game is beautiful! It certainly feels as though they fully utilized the power of UE5. HDR support would have been a good idea, but the game's beautiful even without it. Aside from the extremely realistic graphics, the art design is top-notch as well. Everything feels suitably futuristic, while remaining grounded in realism.I just reached the 4th Chapter, so I won't comment on story as I still don't know where it's going. But it has kept me interested the entire time I've been playing it, so far. I may update after I've completed, as I've certainly been let down by endings before.I would also add that this game has the best voice acting of practically any game I've ever played. I've always been critical of voice acting in video games. It often feels as though everyone records their lines separately and with no interaction, leaving emphasis placed on the wrong words in sentences/statements. This game expertly delivers what feels like real conversation. So, kudos to the voice actors. Amazing job. I personally think that if you're a fan of Quantic Dreams' games you'll likely enjoy this game, too. Here's hoping for future releases from the developer. One thing they may try to add in future titles is the ability to alter outcomes through choice. Not that I don't enjoy just seeing a good story every now and then, but the biggest advantage to video games as interactive narratives is branching storylines.EDIT: I'm back to update the review after the ending. I feel one of two things regarding the plot after the game has ended:1. The plot was left just vague enough to let your imagination determine what was going on and fill in the blanks left by the developers.2. This feels like a prologue/prelude to a much larger, more complex story we could possibly experience at a later date.Either way, I enjoyed every minute of the game and hope there's more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be upfront and say I'm conflicted about this game. This is only the second game for which I've been compelled to write a review and yet would have loved an 'undecided button'.Atmospherically, the game was spectacular. The music, voice acting, sound effects and graphics were all excellent. Sure, there were some performance issues with the graphics moving between zones and I understand there is some ultrawide pain but only the first of those was an issue at all for me and it didn't really detract from the feel of the game. Besides, I'm sure that'll get patched at some point. But the look and feel of the base, the right use of atmospheric sounds and music, and the voice acting were all excellent.I do agree that the writing needed work. Ultimately, it's my experience that writing needs to be done by people with experience. People who've been scared out of their wits before and know how it felt, and what it made them do or say or how they acted as a result. Also, the writing should not be limited to dialogue - when the protag is scared, he or she should be running, or at least loping, and breathing more heavily than normal. Not ambling and potentially cracking jokes. The writing for this though felt disjointed at times which is a shame because it detracted from the atmosphere a bit.More than that though, and I'm going to do my best to avoid spoilers here, the story was almost completely inference. You read logs and emails, listen to audio files, watch video logs, and at the end you think you understand what's going on - kind of. I don't mind having the story inferred like that so long as all the bits you find all fill in a complete picture. Fort Solis didn't do that. It ends at a point where you find yourself asking 'but what happens next?' The sad part is that it does so in a way that can't ever really let you know. Fort Solis II would pretty much have to be something like a Resident Evil game to follow on, not a walking simulator / interactive movie like this game is. Changing the game genre that radically for the next episode would be plain insulting, not to mention a real challenge as far as character retention goes.Like many others, I found myself frustrated by this game. Arguably, you could have taken a lot of the walking out (or sped it up) and made it an actual movie. Put it on the Youtube DUST channel to critical acclaim. The walking took too long, the action sequences were almost twitch-gaming but with little logic in what button you were going to have to mash, and the performance issues with zone changes and the like took just a little of the polish off. Additionally, I'd have liked it to be more open world. If you have to do all that walking, let me see a lot more of the place!The physics of Mars storms have already been addressed by others so I won't touch on that other than to say that for a game of this detail, not applying the hard science of atmospheric dynamics on Mars was a little disappointing. Even a nod to the removal of perchlorates in the Martian soil to explain the 'compounds' (spoilers, don't ask for details) would have been a nice hard-science touch.That said, there was a lot of detail in the game that cannot be dismissed. The team that made this game put their hearts and souls into it, and it shows through. Even the sub-plot dealing with the hacking of vending machines was a great touch that (for me) added complexity to the relationship between the two protags. That and the good news she got just before her shift (only visible in her own messages on her multi-tool) add a richness and complexity to the story that would have made it excellent if it had not been for the lack of experience in human responses under stress and the fact that the game ends pretty definitively 95% of the way through the story. I've now got all story logs, achievements and items; going through them reveals no grand denouements to the storyline. As an aside, the ability to sort the story files into chronological order, preferably within character arcs would be a relatively simple task that would greatly add to the quality of life at the end of the game. Just saying.If there was an undecided button, I would click it for this recommendation. I currently give the game a 6/10 overall, but a 10/10 for atmosphere and 8/10 for the story.I'm also going to say (like some other reviewers have) that you might want to find a playthrough on Youtube to watch. I've actually done that and enjoyed it by not going through the actual interaction parts of the game. But, I strongly recommend that you BUY the game before doing so. I say this for two reasons. The first is that when you watch other people play the game, you're going to say to yourself 'hey, what's down that corridor?' Well, with your own copy of the game, you can find out.The second (and far more important) reason is this; despite its flaws, the game is worth watching, which makes it worth supporting, and the only way that the people on this team get better is if they are recompensed for their work and decide it's worth doing again. Personally, I think it would be criminal for the team behind this game to call it quits and walk away from doing this. They show great potential in what they do. And not 'great potential' in the way that when your wife says that when you're house hunting you instantly give a hard NO to the place as 'great potential' means that the place is a dump she's going to insist you use every spare weekend for the next 5 years fixing. I mean great potential in that with experience to sharpen and refine what they do, they're going to be making the most incredible games in the decades to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start this out by saying that going in, I really wanted to like this game. I feel like it has a lot of potential and it does have some good parts, but I feel like they're drowned out by other lackluster aspects. First thing's first, the game is GORGEOUS. If you're just looking for a super immersive Mars station to walk around in while not too focused on storytelling then this is definitely the game for you. The atmosphere is masterfully crafted for essentially every area in the playable map, and it really goes to show what UE5 is capable of. Creepy flickering maintenance tunnels, overgrown botany facilities, well-lived-in residential areas, etc. The voice acting is also superb as well, once again the legendary Roger Clark nails it, with fantastic performances by Troy Baker, Julia Brown, and other supporting cast members. I found the acting, both voice and motion, was extremely believable, especially in the pre-recorded video logs you can find. HOWEVERI also feel that even with these advantages the game fails to properly deliver its story both through gameplay and the narrative. The story itself isn't anything groundbreaking per-say, and has been seen before in other stories, but its execution left me a little confused. Unless you scour through every nook and cranny of the base for details on the story, you're not entirely likely to understand the whole plot, as I feel it's understood by the characters, but not the audience, and it leaves something to be desired. The gameplay isn't much to talk about either, mostly just a tense walking simulator (No running either, by the way. The fastest you can go is race-walk.)with solving a few minor puzzles and a heavy reliance on usually unprompted QTEs, which aside from being annoying if you're trying to focus on the action, seem to have very little influence on the story. On that note as well, the story is, as advertised, very linear, but in doing so it seems to give you the illusion of choices, while not having much of an effect on the plot itself. Overall I feel Fort Solis would probably have been better off as a TV series or film, which it feels like it's trying to be but is hindered by its own gameplay. On the surface I feel like the dev team definitely did a good job, and I do mean that, but at the end of the day the game did feel like it left something to be desired. That all being said, I am definitely curious to see what future projects this company goes on to produce, I feel like this game was on the cusp of being really good, and I'd like to see them get over that line.VERDICT-If it's on sale and you're in the mood for a shorter space sci-fi, I'd say go for it and see what you think for yourself. As it stands though I don't quite feel as though the bang is worth the buck, so to speak.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis, has many good things going on for it in the beginning. There's an alluring sci-fi mystery. A cast of very talented actors filling in the main roles. Unreal engine 5 promising new gen graphics and an amazing visual experience. Also a very short but at the same time, slow burn suspense story, building the game world and characters around you, promising.... things will happen....ohh.From there nothing happens.First, the cast. They are great, as expected. Troy Baker showing his acting chops, Roger Clark as well (Arthur Morgan) being out of the west and into space, and Julia Brown although very reserved at first, does come on her own towards the end, showing she can go all the way when the situation calls for it. They are great, but there's a lot of good supporting characters as well.The presentation of the game, with Unreal engine 5, looks very good most of the time. But it lacks somehow in certain areas. Some shadows look completely broken, while others look completely fine. This is a weird contrast which distracts you from time to time. The game being Unreal 5 supposedly has some kind of internal Ray Tracing (Lumen) but it is not clear how it is used in game. Our playable character Jack moves like a tank (in a bad way). Slow and not very maneuverable. In principle, it is fine for the narrative, since this is a slow-paced story. But it is annoying for exploration and looking at things, he is slow to turn, and lacks some basic functions like zooming in on objects (maybe I'm being picky here) but since the game has great art direction and good graphics, you do want to see things more closely sometimes.The story is... what? A million question marks in the end? And at the same time... not really? because maybe there isn't anything else to add, and the story is really that thin? Don’t get me wrong, I love a good slow burn, as long as things happen at some point… which, if we are talking about some tense scenes here and there you will find that on Solis, but aside from that… nothing going on here with the story. In a way, (and depending on how you look at it) the story ends as it begins. You do know in the end what happened at Fort Solis... but if that is all there is, then this was just a 15 minute short story with no development, no second layer of nothing to discover. Just, one thing and then another, and that's it. It wouldn't be that bad or disappointing if the narrative wouldn't be so long winded and slow just to arrive to the same thing... nothing to say, nothing new, just more of the same, an extended showcasing of madness. Again, in a way, everything is explained, but at the same time very limited on that explanation of what the issue was, and… not much sustance. And if I sound like I'm just repeating myself not saying anything new, is because the plot is very easy to spoil with just a few lines. Just like that.Maybe I'm just trying to give you a sense of how the game feels after you played it.
