_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult game to recommend. First, it isn't worth full price. I got it discounted and still feel like it is only worth buying on a very deep sale. Second, the performance is bad. Like, very bad. Constant stutters, FPS dips, and just all-around lazy optimization. Third, this is a walking simulator through and through. You pretty much get one playthrough and that's that. The "gameplay" is there to service the narrative and push the story forward. (And even still, the game is BEYOND clunky and surprisingly buggy.) So, really a game like this can only be as good as it's narrative which is unfortunately quite flawed despite a strong opening.Let's start with the positives: Roger Clark, Troy Baker, and Julia Brown all have excellent chemistry and the voice acting quite literally carries this game. The atmosphere and sound design work well to immerse you in what is happening. The story is a slow-burn and for the first two and a half chapters it is quite interesting. However, the story reveals it's hand far too quickly (especially if you're thorough with finding audio/video logs that flesh out the side characters and provide background as to what is happening). The mystery all but disappears by the tail end of the third and fourth chapters, and the game unfortunately devolves into generic slasher tropes where the protagonists are making nonsensical decisions (the ending is so poorly written that I had to play through it TWICE to believe it). Even top-notch voice acting can't save the game from sucking raw cheeks in the end. However, weirdly enough, this game was entertaining. This game is reminiscent of a series on Netflix that you binge in one sitting because you're bored and almost immediately forget about it. Overall, if you can immerse yourself in a dumb sci-fi story that doesn't quite stick the landing and turn your brain off for a few hours, then this is certainly worth your time for MAYBE five bucks.

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game for what it is - a walking simulator in and around a scientific / mining outpost on Mars, during a duststorm, with a decent mystery story behind. Do not buy if you expect anything else or the setting does not interest you. This is neither a horror game, nor by far as heart-wrecking and innovative as e.g. Alien Isolation - see it more like an interactive SF mystery movie. I played only at night, on a large OLED screen with surround sound, and with a relaxed mindset - would not choose to play this during the day, or on a small monitor. There is no "run" button in this game, forcing you to walk slowly - no problem for me, time to take in the atmosphere and nice graphics, and ponder the implications of the story. Graphics are really good (especially rock cliffs, the shadows and station interior), very detailed and fluent (at 4K with max settings, on a RTX 4090), the sounds and sound effects are good and fitting to the setting, voice acting, animations and cutscenes well done. Some QTEs and minor but logical riddles, I did not activate nor need any hints to play through.The only thing I was missing - a zoom function, to get closer and better see stuff lying around or read notes and book titles. Important stuff you can pick up and turn around, though.TLDR - chilled science fiction mystery movie in game format, can be completed in 2 night settings. Definitely not an action game. Recommend to buy on sale - if you are a fan of Mars themed games you can't go wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis appears to be a game developed by a team with a clear vision, unwilling to compromise. It does seem like they are talking feedback. My purchase was influenced by the Digital Foundry's coverage of the first batch of UE5 games. This is clearly a game that is making use of it being in the first wave. FINALLY we have circles. No more jagged edges.Honestly, this represented next-gen gaming for me. For instance, when playing Cyberpunk, the railings, still using decade-old technology, break the immersion for me. However, the quality had to grow on me; I wasn't immediately as impressed as I had anticipated. I found myself pausing to appreciate the visuals (using the built-in cinematic camera), which enhanced my immersion over time. This helped me get more immersed. I did play the game in one sitting.Another thing that impressed me was the facial animations. They were good i got no uncanny feeling from them. This meta human thing is pretty good.The story apparently is not talking place on mars. Which i had to tell myself again and again. It’s a different red planet. It uses the red planet because that was the example for UE5 nanite.Spoilers:The story begins with two engineers discussing zombies. In the back of my mind there was a constant questions are there going to be ones or is it a red heiring? I feel like the moment you discover the first body with the video logs you already know who the killer is. And then it just becomes the question where is this story going to go? For what it was i don’t feel it failed the execution. But i was hoping for that bit more. There is an epilogue but you can just ignore that.The soil just kept reminding me of the flood origin story. It felt a lot of this was soft sci-fi and needed a bit more hardcore. Ending scene i was hoping the monster they eluded to would show up. Also why shoot the guy with bullets why not tase him?There are few issues with the tone of dialog from the character that is sometimes off. When something has already happened. Or when a character comes across a body for the third time but then needs to puke? Sure there is a severed hand but she is an engineer. She has probably seen some gruesome things especially if you read the logs.The map layout was effective, it guided you through the whole station and i never feel cheated because i didn’t have clearance to open a room. I could always do it later. It does feel like they missed a map design mistake by the botanical garden not being more visible. It is a big mark on the map. And it is impressive but you only see it at the end as the final destination. I even confused the atrium for the garden. He event told me to find him in the garden. And i was looking for him at the atrium.Which brings me to gameplay. Regarding gameplay, it essentially functions as a walking simulator. They have added speed walking. It’s fine things go a bit faster although i would have liked to see a toggle. There is no going around it. You can have the same experience watching a let’s play. It’s ironic that they now have announced a film and tv. Because that came to my mind a few times. Why is this just not a movie. It’s simple to show UE5 tech and make money of the first wave. But apparently they have put in a lot more effort. Like mo-cap capping the whole climbing.Moving on to cut scenes, They look great. And then you have a quick time event. I missed 90% of those. They feel off. You get green near the end, but the next animation still makes it seems like it’s a failed state. But apparently they don’t matter. I haven’t seen one game over screen. Something that would have enhanced them would be slow mo.Some other thoughts i had:There are cars but no drive section? That felt like a cop out. But apparently they tried and couldn’t make it fit the story. Which seems like a down side of Top-Down design.The suite of the doctor kept changing and i don’t know if that’s story or my graphics settings. It was so weird.It kind of was obvious we would play as both protagonist after a while.Why 3d print an axe when you have all this other heavy gear laying around that nobody is using?Still don’t know if the tremors are anything. Because the woman protagonist was never exposed to anything in the facility. She always had her helmet on.The titans are small. When i think titan i think Bagger 288 not those small things they showed.The villain keeps saying it can’t get out. But he already sent two people with what could be diagnosed as radiation sickness to other places? How does that make sense. How is he going to stop them. To me this could all be chalked up to one man going insane.I played Jusant before this. And i was thinking it’s not going to be an empty canvas again where i won’t see any npc’s. Luckily this was not that. I haven’t gotten far in Jusant.Why do they hold their hand in front of there face when they are outside? They have a visor!You can switch keyboard layouts. Watched the dev stream. It feels like they have some spaghetti code in their game.In conclusion:The overall experience was ok. It’s great if you want to see what the UE5 can do.I have changed my dislike to a like. Because they are taking feedback. I wouldn’t buy it at full price. But it’s an ok experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I am BORDERLINE negative on this review.  It's almost good enough for me to give it a begrudging thumbs-up.I actually really enjoy walking simulators, and I particularly love "abandoning places where something has gone wrong" walking simulators.  This one, though, is tedious even by walking simulator standards.  And, the cynic in me, feels like a lot of the choices that make it a tedious experience are done solely to slow the pace of the game down, because if you moved at a normal game pace, or had even the slightest ability to walk quickly, the game would be done in an hour.This is how the "puzzles" operate as well - done out of a "need to do something" rather than having any logical sense - like, if every door needed a puzzle to unlock, fine.  But, the game breaks its rules, and some locks you just pop open, while others require an obnoxiously short timed QTE puzzle.And oh man, the QTE's in this game - they are next level.  You can be watching a 5 minute long cut scene, but don't you DARE let your guard down for even 1 second, because if you do, the random "D" key button press that will just pop up out of nowhere - lasting 1/2 of a second - and if you miss it, you get your leg smashed.  Even in the middle of fight scenes, I find it a bit obnoxious that your character will throw about 6.234 punches, and then out of nowhere, you are expected to hit a QTE to get that last one in, or else.SPOILER  I'm not sure if it was an intentional choice to have you end the game wondering what the heck just happened, but I sure did, and like I said - I'm into any game for the story first and foremost.Last criticism - this game could NOT find the tone it wanted to have.  You'd have this delightful banter between Jack and Jess before they realize that fecal matter has impacted the cooling units.  Then, after they are both horrified to discover corpses and gore, one second later, there is another quip.  Like...folks, pick the jokey casual tone, or the scratching strings, horrific atmosphere, and character development.  It felt uneven.I will end this on the major positive note of the game, which is the only thing that makes me feel borderline about it - the voice acting - particularly by Troy Baker (surprise, surprise.)  Althought he actor playing Jack kind of bounced back and forth between an irish-tinged accent, and an attempt at a Brooklyn accent (despite mentioning he was from Boston) he was still great in the role, and Jess was great too.  The side characters also did a great job of selling their characters through video/audio logs.  In that sense, I enjoyed Fort Solis.  Now, if I can only figure out what just happened in the game...

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game is a serviceable movie, if you play roughly like I did and don't use the awkward looking speed walk at all and stubbornly meander over to every interactable you see while life and death allegedly loom in the balance, you'll knock it out in around three hours. Do not spend your only $15 of game money for this Paycheck on Fort Solis, buy this if you really want to listen to T-Bakes and Roger Clark's voice acting for three hours with shiney visuals.I'm recommending this game because I'm soft, and I lack the stomach to be harsh with something that was clearly made with heart. Which is wishy washy, at best. To be clear, I got this game (As most likely have at this point) on sale, and I can say that even on sale, I feel a little robbed. Just a tiny bit.Not because the game lied to me, but because I didn't really believe it when it told me in no uncertain terms what to expect.I have nearly three hours in this game I spent around $15US on. The only reason I could possibly have to go back and add any more time to that? To see the alternative ending, which I'm not sure I'll be doing. Also there are collectibles in the form of character models to go back and unlock and look at, but if you've played any UE5 games recently, they will not be blowing your mind. They're good, and the game is visually solid. Incredible? No, but what is these days? Unreal has recently made incredible graphics mundane, for me at least.Someone said the game can be beaten by pressing W long enough, and they are unfortunately correct. The game, I feel like, is upfront about that.I personally think "Thriller" might be a stretch, but the story was relatively interesting even though it never felt like it paid off for me. It's tropey at the best of times, and a handful of story decisions irked me. That said, I was interested from beginning to end. All 2.9 Hours of it.Voice acting was great, by the way. Maybe I should have lead with that, but I feel like that is hardly surprising. Roger Clark and Troy Baker are hardly rookie talent, I don't know Julia Brown from anything else, but I assume she's well known since she's listed in the description. Either way she was also very good. Honestly, their solid performances are the primary shining point here, I believed the characters, even if I had no idea what was really going on.PS. Like has been said, the Tone is all over the place, and I can't feel any sense of urgency when my character's movement speed is "Casual Jaunt" or when I press shift "Awkwardly fast Jaunt". If you felt like Leon's "run" in RE2 Remake lacked purpose, our folks Jack and Jess must be absolutely blasted on Lorazepam for how slow they're going. Hard to feel "thrilled" when my characters can't be bothered to muster a jog even when the situation becomes clearly life threatening.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 5/9/2024: It's been a couple months since I played Fort Solis, and I've changed my mind - I absolutely recommend this game. I still remember certain scenes and situations that kept me glued to my screen wanting to know more. I loved experiencing the world and searching for answers. Sure, there was one bit that left me wanting, but that could very well be on me, not the game. I say give it a shot - I think you'll be glad you did. When I said this ticked all the boxes, I meant it. Original: I wanted to love this game so much. I love space, mars, and story-driven games.... this ticked all the boxes. Sadly, the piece I wanted the most - the story - did not flesh out enough by the end to leave me satisfied or excited for more. There were  dialogue lines that confused me because I didn't feel I'd learned enough information to relate or understand the drama. I kept pushing through because I thought in the end I would understand better. I didn't. There are plenty of awesome things in this game. The atmosphere they tried to create truly works. The dialogue, voice acting, and animations are fantastic especially at this price point. The devs should be proud.I just wish the story had fleshed out better and gone far deeper than it did because it left me feeling unsatisfied when the dots were connected.

_childDocuments_.review: ...During your investigation of the base, you’ll find audio logs, video recordings, and emails that shed some light for you. This is one of the most interesting aspects of Fort Solis. You’re discovering a lot about these crew members in these little interactions they have with one another, and how those interactions differ on the clock compared to after they punch out. The strongest throughline in the entire narrative is working relationships. Jack and Jessica are an example of a somewhat healthy relationship between co-workers. Shift things over to the Fort Solis crew and you start to see how red tape doesn’t stop when the workday ends.......As the mystery draws to a close, the game doesn’t quite land the ending. The twists and turns along the way were great, but the end just feels rushed. It also doesn’t help that the climatic encounter in the end plays out in QTE’s, some of which are just hitting the button to hide. It’s a weird moment that feels like it was tacked on at the last minute. Fort Solis is a mystery to me. It’s a beautiful game with well-developed characters, and fascinating themes it wants to explore. Yet, the things it does well are eclipsed by performance and pacing issues. I can’t help but think with some time under the hood this could be a classic narrative sci-fi thriller. In its current state I can’t recommend it.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely astounded at how much hate this one is receiving.To address some points I've seen made in these reviews:- The review claiming there is no story beyond what you see in the trailers is absolutely unhinged. That's ridiculously untrue. While I had my own problems with the ending and wish certain elements of the big reveal were stated more explicitly, there is absolutely an interesting story here, albeit one with some pacing problems.- It's correct that there is no run button. In parts of the game this can be a bit frustrating, though early on especially it's hard to find fault with it, as running all over the place really wouldn't allow for the very measured, quiet, dark atmosphere on display here. And this is truly among the more atmospheric games I've ever played.- Performance will definitely vary. At 4k, ultra settings on a 4080 with DLSS on, I was getting 70-80 fps. You might think that's ludicrous, but frankly this is an Unreal Engine 5 game and an AMAZING looking one at that. Seriously, the graphics here are absolutely state of the art. Not being able to run it doesn't mean it's terribly optimized, it may just mean your rig isn't quite up to snuff. I have no idea how it scales on lower end hardware, but be aware it doesn't even launch on steam deck, and it you don't have access to a card with DLSS you probably don't even want to bother unless you want to play at 30 fps. But again, I would put this more on the high fidelity visuals rather than poor optimization.Overall, this will not be a game for everyone. It's extremely cinematic, barely interactive at times, very demanding on the hardware and quite short at about 4 hours to complete. But it's also gorgeous, extremely atmospheric, wonderfully voiced and compellingly-written, and a quintessential example of a "really good 7/10" kind of game, in that it has some flaws but is unique enough to be worth a go for anybody interested in its concept and ok with the gameplay taking a backseat.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good graphics, excellent (really really good, top-notch) voice-acting. And that's about it. I don't regret playing it, I enjoyed it. But I can see that most people won't. There are three issues; camera-movement, story and quick time events.1- The camera angle and movement is not any good. You have to stop to get a good look around. It just does not flow. 2- Good suspenseful atmosphere leads to meh. The story is okay. It's not groundbreaking, and I do not mind a few loose ends and unanswered questions. But it does raise some questions about certain motivations and their justifications. (Even after collecting every audio and video log.) Anyhow, I probably had higher expectations. I can't in good conscience say that it sucks. It just needed a bit more elaboration, and a better sense of progression of the story.3- For me the worst part was quick time events. If you are going to do quick time events, they better lead to consequences. There are maybe 4-5 QTEs but they lead to absolutely nothing. They do not change the outcome of the action or of the story. Only one at the very end results in an alternate ending, and that's not a different ending at all with regard to outcome. Just a slightly different cut-scene with the exact same consequence. Why then?Oh, and essentially it's a walking simulator. If you do not like them, you don't. I like them, but I feel that this game could be so much more if Quantic Dreams made it. (Well, if you place unnecessary QTEs in the game, it's unavoidable to make that comparison to a studio that makes good use of them.) That's why it feels like the underachiever of a game despite good graphics, brilliant voice-acting, good atmosphere & suspense.

_childDocuments_.review: As I ventured into the captivating world of Fort Solis, I found myself drawn into a narrative-rich experience set amidst the desolate beauty of Mars. Developed by Fallen Leaf, this sci-fi thriller promised an immersive journey through the isolated mining post of Solis Planum, and it did not disappoint.From the moment I stepped into the shoes of engineer Jack Leary, responding to a routine alarm at the dormant outpost, I was enveloped in a gripping tale that unfolded against the backdrop of the red planet. The setting alone, on the far side of Mars, added a layer of intrigue and isolation that set the stage for the unfolding events.The graphics in Fort Solis are undeniably impressive, boasting stunning detail and realism that brought the Martian landscape to life. I found myself particularly enamored with the use of Reshade, which enhanced the visuals even further, complementing the already superb animations crafted through mocap technology. However, despite the visual splendor, performance issues did occasionally detract from the experience, with stuttering and texture pop-in disrupting the otherwise seamless immersion.The audio design in Fort Solis was another highlight, with a hauntingly atmospheric soundtrack that heightened the sense of tension and isolation. While I would have appreciated surround sound support, the music nonetheless succeeded in immersing me further into the unfolding narrative.In terms of gameplay, Fort Solis leans heavily into its narrative focus, eschewing traditional combat and puzzles in favor of a more contemplative experience. While this approach may not appeal to everyone, I found myself engrossed in the rich tapestry of story and lore scattered throughout the outpost. From notes and audio logs to video recordings, there was no shortage of content to absorb, making each exploration of Fort Solis a rewarding endeavor.That being said, I couldn't help but feel that the game could have benefited from a bit more interactivity. While the inclusion of button-pressing sequences helped break up the exploration, they occasionally felt tacked on rather than integral to the experience.As the narrative reached its climax, I found myself grappling with the moral implications of the story, echoing Dr. Ian Malcolm's famous quote from Jurassic Park. "Yeah, but your scientists were so preoccupied with whether or not they could, they didn't stop to think if they should." The ending, while potentially confusing for those who hadn't fully immersed themselves in the lore, served as a thought-provoking conclusion to Jack Leary's journey.Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with Fort Solis. It offered a unique blend of storytelling and gameplay set against the backdrop of a Martian mining outpost. While not without its flaws, including performance issues and a lack of interactivity, the game succeeded in delivering an immersive experience that left a lasting impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is a remarkable addition to the sci-fi gaming genre, set against the captivating backdrop of Mars. The graphics are exceptionally smooth and detailed, with an impressive level of attention to even the smallest elements. The Martian setting is immersive, making you feel as though you're truly there, surrounded by the eerie, desolate environment of an abandoned outpost.One of the game's standout features is its ability to evoke a sense of loneliness, despite the main character maintaining communication with a colleague via comms. This balance creates a subtle yet effective sense of fear, which is enhanced by the need to investigate an alarm that has disrupted the solitude. The atmosphere is masterfully crafted, capturing the unsettling feeling of exploring an abandoned facility.Movement within Fort Solis is deliberately slow, aligning with the developers' intention to create a tension-filled exploration experience. While you can't run, you can walk at a slightly faster pace, which suits the game's tone. However, a sprint option during certain moments would have been a welcome addition. The only instances where the protagonist is seen running are in cutscenes, which can feel a bit restrictive.Exploration is well-executed, with a map system that guides you without holding your hand. Although the map isn't entirely accurate, it gets the job done. Improvements could include clearer points of interest and security-level indications, but these are minor quibbles. The video and audio logs are particularly engaging, providing enjoyable insights into the crew's experiences and the events leading to the emergency.Despite the many unanswered questions, collecting all the logs and notes allows you to piece together a coherent story, though the developers clearly intended to leave some elements open-ended. This approach encourages players to think critically about the narrative rather than being spoon-fed information.Quick-time events are intense and leave little room for error, which might be frustrating for some players. However, they are not game-breaking, as failure often allows you to continue the story without needing to retry. The game's brevity is another point in its favor, with a complete playthrough taking around 5-6 hours. This short duration ensures a focused and immersive experience without unnecessary padding or repetitive quests.In summary, Fort Solis offers a compelling, atmospheric adventure that prioritizes story and exploration over combat and grinding. Its detailed graphics, well-crafted atmosphere, and engaging narrative make it a standout title, despite some minor flaws. It's a refreshing take on the sci-fi genre that leaves you pondering long after the credits roll. We need more games like this—short, focused, and rich in quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Fan of story-driven experiences? Science-fiction with the slightest 'hint' of horror? A slow thriller? Walking simulators?I really enjoyed this walking-simulator game. Lots of mystery and questions about the story, even after finishing the game. I sincerely appreciate this type of open-ended cryptic way of telling a story. Never really giving it a conclusion means your brain is racing for more of it. It feeds that drug called "curiosity".The game is drooling atmosphere! The music, the acting, the voices, logs. The attention to detail and scale. These are elements that make such a great story experience.Fort Solis is one of the greatest examples of how immersive strong voice-acting/acting can impact an interactive experience. The quality of the voice actors is just amazing! Troy Baker, who plays one of the important characters, really delivered in spades!But, no honest review would ignore the few flaws I found.While I absolutely love the theme, the story, and the "way" the story is told... ...the game does have a few issues. But fret not, these are only minor technical issues that don't break, nor affect the gameplay.Some textures, or lighting conditions, seem to exhibit some graphical flaws, like a bunch of shadows constantly "waving" over some textures (not all, only visible in some locations and settings). Also, even if motion blur was turned off, some of the transparency and movement create lots of slow motion blur in some instances.Again, these were minor grievances, and to be perfectly honest, it did not affect my appreciation for the game in the slightest.The one thing I disliked the most; QTE's. I HATE QTE's! Luckily, this game doesn't make you start sections over for failing. Often, the QTE's simply offer a slight change of cutscene, and in most cases, the ending of a cutscene is the same, regardless if you failed QTE's or not.Anyways, I highly recommend this game to fans of walking simulators. It's one you don't want to miss!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, even though I have tried to be understanding that this game was made by a small, very inexperienced team, I can't recommend it even at a discounted price. The performance issues alone make it unplayable to me. I still don't understand how game developers keep releasing stuttery mess like this and expect people to enjoy it, let alone support their next release. The game keeps dipping from 60-80 fps to 10 fps on R5 3060/RTX 3060 at 1080p in balanced DLSS and a mix of low/medium settings. It doesn't even look good enough to justify such a performance penalty for going with medium settings instead of low. I'm watching live developer gameplay as I write this review and even though it doesn't drop to 10 fps, it is still stuttering like crazy. I can't comment on a story and other game aspects since games in this state are just a pain to play and I wasn't able to force myself to run it for longer than 20 minutes.Update:After playing for over 4 hours, the only way to make the game playable is to set everything to low, lock the framerate at 40 fps and play on 1080p and DLSS in performance mode. This helped to reduce the constant stutter; unfortunately, the game still dips down to 6-10 fps every now and then. The game also suffer from constant flickering, shimmering and enormous amount of noise which has been reported multiple time by others. This makes the game look really bad, even at the highest settings and in 4K. _childDocuments_.review: Great experience - but not for everyone! I really love this project, but I would never recommend it to everyone, so be aware what you can expect from Fort Solis: My definition: This is not a game like many others and of course you can ask: "Is it even a game?" I would answer: "Maybe an hybrid. It's more a movie/series, than a game."  It also depends on the expectations you have. Are you looking for an Dead Space clone or an interactive movie like Detroit Become Human? Then this project is probably not for you. Bad things first: The optimisation is not good in this game so far. You will definitely encounter trouble while playing it. There are problems with keeping the fps stable (extremely in some areas) and having micro stuttering even on the best set ups. My set up runs the most games on max fluently, but if it even cause trouble on the very best pc's, I guess nobody will complete the game without having any issues. Normally, these issues are terrible to witness and can destroy the experience completely in games in general. But somehow not for me. Even I had the same troubles like others, I had a lot of fun playing the game. Maybe because it's more of a movie than a game, in which I need some good fps to have fun with fluent gameplay. In Fort Solis this didn't bother me that much. But I hope the devs will fix it for everybody including myself. It would be a shame, if this project would give them just a bad reputation, because they are really talented in what they are doing and I admire the work they did with only 10 people. It need to be mentioned, that the game is only 14 GB and around 20 bucks. Despite the issues, the players which are committing to the project and like to experience a Sci-Fi Thriller, should bring affinity to investigate and have fun with a very slow paced story. What others describe as boring, is a pleasure for me. I really like the slow investigation and movement. It's the complete opposite to my fast paced retro games and shooters and creates an atmosphere, that surpass other games with ease. Good things: The graphics are just gorgeous (check out my screenshots) and easily one of the best right now (especially due to the small file size). The ambient music, overall sound and the voice actors are phenomenal and add a lot to the movie like atmosphere. The animations are one of the best ever seen in a game and that's what I'm always talking about: We get so many good looking games, but the animations of the characters are generic, old and stiff and can't keep up with the rest of most games. In Fort Solis the body language is organic and natural and something moves all the time (not what you think :D). The characters have even micro movement when they are standing still (I love those details). The motion capturing is brilliant and you really feel the weight of the bodies. The same counts for the face animations. Never seen eyes looking around so naturally. It really adds life to the characters. If you have fun and excitement with movies like the martian or sunshine in a light version, this game can be definitely something for you. You will get an interesting experience for a few hours and a small price. Be aware with the issues (depending on your setup) and maybe wait for an patch. And of course you can check the game out and give it back, if it's not for you. I just wanted to test it and completed it in 2 sessions in around 7 hours (you can do it in 3 I guess, but I like to take my time with games like these). And never forget, it depends always on the expectations. If this project will run fluently someday, it's an 10/10 for me ;) Thx to the devs for this experience and keep on moving.Animated Steam Review:

_childDocuments_.review: All around the web you will encounter people saying, Fort Solis is a boring storyteller without any gameplay or fun. And well.. that's somewhat correct.Fot Solis is indeed a storyteller without any gameplay, but if it's fun, that's completely subjective.Ask yourself: do I like games in the likes of Dear Esther, Firewatch, The Suicide of Rachel Foster, etc.? If you can answer that with a yes, then perhaps this might be another decent title for you.Fort Solis is set on Mars, where you play as Jack (they could have also used another generic name, but anyways..). An engineer who's working for station Fort Minor during one of the many sandstorms on the red planet. Relatively close to Minor he finds the bigger station Fort Solis, where he's heading for to check in on the team located - but strangely there is no one to be found. The station appears to be empty and soon enough he even finds the body of one of the crew members - and so he starts his investigation about what the heck is actually going on here.With you in your earpiece there is Jessica, another employee for Fort Minor and your friend. The two talk alot during this story and share brief direct interations with each other along the way, albeit for the most part you will be completely on your own, exploring the station and some of its surroundings.The story unfolds with audio recordings, videos of former crew members, notepads and of course environmental storytelling, just as well as dialogues. And this is where the first complaints will arrive, as this is all that's gonna happen. You wander, you read, you listen and here and there you will tap some buttons for a quick time event.This is a typical walking simulator and if you don't like those - skip this. Simple as that.Where this shines is the story and the english voice acting. Both are pretty good, albeit not top of the list. Especially Jacks voice did not match for me and you may find that the story borrows some of its ideas from other sources like different games or even movies. I found that overall this did remind me a lot of the film "Sunshine", which I absolutely love. So this might be a reason why I give this game a pass.On a technical side this is definitely a double-edged sword.Yes, Fort Solis looks pretty good overall. But not fantastic. And given that the hardware requirements for this are rather hefty, this should either look even better or at least run the part.Since this is one of the first bigger UE5 titles, you will absolutely encounter stuttering here and there. It is unclear to me if this is related to the shaders or just because the game had to load the next assets, but these mostly show up when you traverse from one section of the station to the next. In that case at least they do not hinder gameplay and they were just annoying but not a reason to ditch the game as a whole.8GB of VRAM and 16GB of memory will suffice for this, but in case you do not own an RDNA3 or a modern RTX card, you will have to use both upscaling and frame generation to have a playable, stutterfree experience.I've played it on a 5600X with 6700XT and 32GB of DDR4 and was mostly fine. 1440p with  FSR2 ran decent, as long as you ignore the UE5 stutters mentioned before.Overall, if you'd like to spend roughly 4h exploring a space station and the game is on sale (I paid like 15 bucks), then this could be worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a tough one. It's close but I'll have to give it a "Not recommended" based on multiple factors, even if I love sci-fi mystery. The game does look quite good, however I have noticed some very irritating graphical artifacts where DLSS would create heavy ghosting even on "Quality" Preset, and Global Illumination causes intense light-spot flickering of the scene lighting, especially in the Atrium and some other areas. (Drivers are up to date!)Also without DLSS the game is practically unplayable for me at some 20 FPS in some areas. I had to even lower resolution to 1080p from 1440p, which I never needed to do until now.Adjusting other settings barely does anything for FPS, but the game will look like complete garbage on "Low".So it's either distracting graphical artifacts and smearing (not a fan of DLSS) or dogsh** performance.Granted, I "only" have a watercooled RTX 2080, but based on this experience I would not recommend this game to be played at anything less than this GPU, which can handle basically any other game I played so far, at comfortably smooth framerates in 1440p.On a positive note, no crashes or instability (if we disregard wildly different FPS in each area). Replayability: absolute 0Walking Speed: Even if literally your life depends on it - Snails pace, or about a nice slow cozy Saturday afternoon strollInteractivity is limited to be basically "press W" until you arrive at the next interactable object, then press "E", repeat. And some Quicktime Events, that barely change any outcome (except one time), but are annoying.An interactive movie if you will. Starts off strong, great mystery vibes and somewhat believeable (aside from the myth that storms on Mars are that powerful, but I digress).Then the characters even make fun of the typical tropes of the horror genre, until the point where they commit the exact same mistakes... oh well.Story flattens out in the mid to end and it's not really clear why things played out like they did.Which leads to...  It's just too damn high for what you are getting.You are looking at just about 3 hours tops if you just walk through the storyline. Maybe this increases to 6 or 7 getting all collectibles and achievements if you missed something. Not that there is a whole lot of interesting things to find aside from story tidbits.For 15€ maybe OK, more like 10. - Music: It's ok and fitting, but exceptionally forgettable, I don't remember a single track, melody or other fragment right after having played through the game... So why is there an OST for it? It's extremely generic.- Sound design: Pretty decent, nothing negative to say.- Animations: The MoCap is done well, looks natural aside from some unavoidable sliding when turning too quickly or interacting with stuff while walking or standing weirdly besides the object first.All in all, great atmosphere and design, but technical and graphical problems.Great premise, but ultimately too short and even with the minimal length failed to follow through with it's story and leaves a confusing aftertaste.Too expensive.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDRAlien Isolation without the Alien... so, just Isolation then.Well it's a thumbs up, but I have some complaints.Firstly, when I run windows in 4k, boot a game, and there's only one resolution option available (4k) I expect a 4k presentation. For some reason the whole game was still very low resolution (assuming 1080p by the 50-75% gpu usage) but with no other options available I just played the game as it was. After completing it I had a play, and found running in windowed mode (or tabbing out and in) gave me a vastly superior resolution (and suitably lower framerate). Thanks for ruining my eyes squinting trying to read messages at low res because for some reason you can't render a game at the resolution you force upon me. It's 2024, you're using UnrealEngine... this should just work out of the box... really?No HDR? It can be enabled with an .ini edit but no ingame option? In a game mostly set in the dark... no HDR. Expecting people to edit ini files? It's 2024, you're using UnrealEngine... HDR support is built in... really?The puzzles... oh no I need a passcode, oh there it is on the back of a photo right next to the computer and is the only other interactive element in the room. It's 2024, really?QTEs with catlike reflexes required in a game all about the slowness... really?The graphics are pretty and I appreciate the game is a walking simulator so there's time to "see" them more clearly (well, if you actually get the game running at the proper resolution) but the beautifully created map is wasted. I feel like letting people move quicker but adding more puzzles to get access to other parts of the station would've been a much smarter idea. More System Shock, less OAP marathon. When I did unlock higher access the idea of walking slowly back to the earlier doors didn't appeal much - especially as one L3 door refused to open despite me having L3 access. Super.Also worth noting it has DLSS and framegen, but the framegen added a tonne of artifacting so was next to worthless.So yeah, it only takes 4hrs, it's a nice enough walk and story but technical stuff got in my way and annoyed me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like space / mild sci-fi and are open to horror experiences in general, this might be for you. Although I would not call it a "horror" experience itself. Best comparison I might find here is first season of the Expanse, call it "dark suspense".The similarities go further than that. As other reviews point out, this is not an action game, more like a "cinematic" story and exporing experience. It may look very similar to Dead Space or Callisto Protocol in Screenshots, and in terms of technical quality and polish it easily rivals or surpasses those, but it is not the same. Gameplay consists of walking based exploration. Story and action, which exists, are experienced through seamlessly integrated cutscenes with simple quick-time events. This might not be something for the Dark Souls crowd. But if you think this looks cool while not necessarily wanting the actual stress of a Dead Space, this should have far better accessibilty. And with 4 hours of length, tbh., it's a dense and focused experience for anyone. The devs compare it to binging a (good) show, and that is not a bad comparison.Facts:Gameplay: walking/researching + quicktime eventsDuration: ~4 hoursAwesome tech, cutscenes, performancesPretty dense athmosphere Have I mentioned it looks awesome? It's such a blessing that today we can actually experience movie grade art design such as Alien or the Expanse in this quality.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅Intense atmosphere✅Graphically impressive➖Rough movement controls➖Strict QTE timersGame World: In Fort Solis (FS) you start the game immediately on the surface of Mars. You eventually come to learn that the year is 2080, just to provide a timeline. The world takes place entirely during the night on Mars and furthermore, during the storm cycle so the surface has an imminent storm incoming. Aside from the surface of Mars, you will also spend most of the time exploring Fort Solis itself, which is an older (2050s) installation. This area consists of what you might expect a spacestation to look like if it were on a planet. In a way I get a lot of vibes from The Martian as a possible visual inspiration. Because the vast majority of the game takes place either at night during a storm, or inside the space station, I wasn’t really able to explore the surface at all or even see out into space. Despite this minor gripe, I felt that the world of FS was incredibly engaging and immersive. Narrative: The narrative is subtle by intent and mostly told through video recordings. You take control of two engineers - first Jack, then Jess. You get an emergency lockdown signal coming from Fort Solis and you go investigate to try to understand what is going on and why it's on lockdown. You arrive to find it completely empty with indications of something sinister occurring. You then spend the rest of the story learning about the situation at Fort Solis. Full story SPOILERS:  Most of what I gathered from the plot was not very obvious and largely an assumption put together by the characters actions as well as some internet searching. The story was good, but it could have been presented much better. Perhaps if one of the characters explicitly stated the consequences of the situation they were in, it would have given the player more motivation instead of just going to the next area, which is how I felt at the end. It wasn’t really clear why I was doing what I was doing or for what reason. Length: I completed FS in about 3.5 hours. Mechanics: Since FS is a walking simulator, the mechanics are lighter here, as expected. Really there are only some button presses to learn information, a HUD with a map/emails/video logs, and some quick-time events that occur during major points in the story. Regarding the QTE specifically, they happen SO quick that I failed the vast majority of them, but there doesn’t seem to be any failure penalties aside from one part of the story. I feel that these could have been excluded, but perhaps the devs wanted something to be done during specific action scenes. Overall, I didn’t like the mechanics in FS, they felt fairly basic, flat, and uninspired even for a walking simulator. Difficulty: Easy. There seems to be no real way to fail. There is an alternate ending you can “fail” into, but that’s it. Quality: Despite taking place at night, being dusty, and largely full of dark mechanical corridors, FS is still pretty to look at. The characters look very nice. There is not much to say about the environment other than it's kind of boring. I mean it's just an old space station, it is hard to make it look beautiful, but at the very least the areas that I did explore did feel like they were lived in. The station seemed to show the wear-and-tear that I would expect a 30+ year old space structure to show. Performance: I kept a constant 60 FPS with no issues and hardly any dips. I did notice some animation bugs and even some collision bugs where a dead body was half in a wall. Still, overall good. i9-13900KF | RTX 4090 | 64GB RAM | 1440p @ 240hz | installed on SSDSound Effects: The sound is very well done. The environment is thoroughly creepy and the effects are well done. There’s not much aside from walking, doors opening, and general aging space station creaks, but this was well very well done. I thought the voice acting was good. I didn’t really like Jack’s VA due to his weird accent, but omg I could listen to Jess talk for hours. Reminds me of Tracer from Overwatch. Music: I…..didn’t even really notice anything here. Like it may have been subtle, but it just was barely present. The sound effects are good enough to carry this category, because I didn’t even notice any music. Doesn’t seem to be a good replay value other than some achievements and collectables. At the very least I like how there is an extra menu with all the things you can collect. I found Fort Solis to be a good walking sim with a good story. There are some definite horror vibes at the start, but like with many horror games and movies, once you learn what is going on, it doesn’t really become scary anymore. Whether that’s good or bad is up to the player, but I feel the strongest point of FS was when you are trying to piece together what is going on. As such, when you learn more about the activity on the station, you might be underwhelmed. You can find my curator page here:

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure whether to recommend the game or not, honestly.The title consists of 4 hours of an immersive story and unique - if at times VERY frustrating - keybindings. The polish of the game is fairly high and the setting is fantastic. It's clear that the developers are very talented. Unfortunately it feels that the ending ran over budget. Whilst the game looked great, it did not only not expand on its gameplay and story elements in its final hour, but rather removed some of its working formula, leaving it feeling a little empty.The ending also fell flat with no satisfactory conclusion, despite all the required elements being built on previously in order for the game to do so: The narrative threads left open left too many questions unanswered for satisfaction, or perhaps too many anemic theories not fleshed out. The game is supposed to be a mystery in that case, but personally I feel that the budget was the real answer to all of the possible outcomes raised. It just felt like there should be more.If you like mystery sci-fi and have the patience to explore this quasi walking-simulator with janky controls I would recommend the following:1) Pick up the game on sale2) Take your time and explore everything 3) Play the entire game from start to finish (4-5 hours)4) Take NOTES as you go5) Do not expect too many answers at the close!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with Fort Solis. I understand the problem with some of the complaints people have, but I think that if you go into this with the right expectations, you'll have a good time.This is by no means an action oriented, fast-paced adventure. It is a (very) slow, linear, walking simulator with gorgeous graphics and an interesting story. There are QTE's, but I'm not sure they actually have an impact on the overall story, maybe just in the way certain scenes play out. The voice acting is top notch. Character models look great. The way facial expressions relay emotion is done really really well.The game is pretty demanding on your hardware, but with a 40-series card Nvidia's Frame Generation tech should have you covered. In all honesty though, this is a cinematic experience, and you'll probably be fine even at 30 fps.The game also leaves the door open for DLC or a sequel, either of which I'd pick up in a heartbeat.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this game only because in my opinion it does have some positive attributes, and for some the positives may outweigh the negatives. However, it was a major disappointment for me. It's probably easiest to review this game in a pro v con manner.pros: -graphical style and atmosphere well thought out and executed.          -superb voice acting         -sort of, kind of, interesting story         -psychologically immersivecons: -clunky, annoying mechanics         -repetitive, unnecessary actions needed for unnecessary, irritating "puzzles".         -laconic, plodding play style         -terrible map presentation and map mechanics         -very little actual tension created as the story progresses, which does not work well with the quiet,          empty atmospherics. This is probably my biggest complaint, because I love the kind of subtle yet          disquieting atmosphere the game utilized, but you'd better be able to produce some narrative tension if          you're going to pretty much avoid any action other than walking around. The game didn't need fighting          or even complex QTEs, but it most certainly did need a story that got under your skin and started          crawling. The game falls flat as a Martian pancake in this regard.        -ending is vague and unsatisfying. I really wanted to like this game, because it had many of the basic ingredients of a good, possibly great psychological sci-fi thriller. But the development team obviously doesn't know how to cook with those ingredients. All the gameplay issues would fade away in my mind if the game had been able to produce a sense of emotional connection to the characters and the story, but it did not, and coupled with a fairly tepid story concept and an emotionally deflating ending, this one goes into the bin.

_childDocuments_.review: For Solis is a very good science fiction mystery/exploration game. The voice acting, visuals and character models are great. It's a very well-made game. You are an engineer for a mining firm on Mars. You receive a distress signal from Fort Solis, an old mining/research facility. When you arrive, the fort is locked down. You manage to get in and cannot find anyone. As you discover crew logs, journals and correspondence, you realise that something happened at the base. As you play through Fort Solis, you will discover what that is.This game was well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fort Solis

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is one of those hidden gems that unfortunately get overlooked amidst the wave of huge AAA games. And that's a shame, because it offers a truly great experience. The game oozes atmosphere and engulfs you in an intriguing narrative. Exploring the Martian mining colony is quite exciting, and the presentation that the game offers is truly stunning (especially the voice acting and the quality of the animations - some of the best motion capture work I've seen in a long time). That said - it's probably not everyone's cup of tea, with a very strong focus on narrative-driven design that might leave people wanting for a bit more action. I'm not particularly happy with the optimization of the engine. Sure, it looks great, but the framerate is uneven and I experienced a few freezes. But while it's not perfect, it definitely deserves a second look.

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis, the game that drops you on Mars like a lost tourist, is a wild ride. Picture this: you’re in a rusty mining outpost, and it’s so quiet you can hear your own existential crisis. The whole place screams “abandoned,” and the only company you’ve got is flickering lights and eerie audio logs. It’s like The Shining meets Interstellar, minus the friendly hotel staff.Roger Clark(yep, Arthur Morgan from Red Dead Redemption 2), Troy Baker(yep, Joel from Last of Us) and Julia Brown join the party, adding layers of emotion and suspense. So grab your spacesuit, buckle up, and prepare for a mind-bending journey!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game full of contradictions. There’s an argument to be made that the real advantage that games offer over non-interactive kinds of media is participation. That’s obviously on offer here: you push the stick, your character moves. You press X on the highlighted object, you examine it: in a sparse few places you even solve a puzzle. But Fort Solis is so determined that you experience it in exactly the way that the developers intended it that it often feels less like a game and more like a movie that you’re forced to interact with in order to drive the story forward. It’s entirely linear, with some optional backtracking for additional story. Your character walks at one speed; the speed that the developers believe is the best in order to preserve the atmosphere and presentation. That’s barely interaction: its forced direction.Choices don’t matter. I deliberately missed every quick time event in two spots and it didn’t change the outcome of the encounter. There are two endings but I have no idea how one gets one over the other. It’s very pretty and the voice acting is superb, but you’d be better served going elsewhere if you want to play a game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really found it hard to decide whether to give this game a thumbs up or down. I'm not one to downvote a game because I didn't like something that is primarily subjective in nature. I wish there was a neutral option. I will go ahead and hit the "Yes" button purely because I do feel the devs put a lot of love into this game, and perhaps it's just not resonating with me the same way it might with others. Pros:Short and sweet. About 4 hours to finish. Great atmosphere. Looks great graphics wise as long as your machine can handle it. I ran it on high settings fsr balanced on and it was pretty stable at around 70-80 fps. Need to really be observant and explore to get all the collectibles. I think I got around half. Characters were likable, mostly. Voice acting was phenomenal. Also Troy Baker. Cons:1-I can't say I'm motivated enough to do a subsequent play-through. It's kind of a one and done game unless you gotta get those achievements/collectibles. I understand that the devs were setting the pacing with only having one set walk speed, no run functionality, but it does kinda drag when nothing is happening, or especially when you backtrack. Not much of that is required fortunately. Would be nice to add in a run function as a unlock-able for beating the game so that going through again isn't as monotonous. 2-Character dialogue/exposition-Characters monologue nearly every time you interact with something. Not a bad thing, except I felt it really broke the immersion later on when things are supposed to be super tense, and you pick something up or look at something and the character says something in a really cheery voice or makes some kind of sarcastic response. Spoiler alert for the first chapter-You find a recently murdered person and not 5 minutes later the characters are making jokes back and forth. 3-Story-While not bad, I also can't say it had me hooked. I didn't ever really feel emotionally invested or attached to the characters. I felt more for the antagonist or at least was far more intriguing with their motivations rather than the protagonists which kind of left me unsure how to really feel at the end of it all. I also don't feel that I truly understood what exactly was going on. I know I missed some logs so it may just be on me. I may have to look into an in-depth analysis of the story to get it. 4-QTE's-I would prefer the game without them. Again, immersion breaking. especially when it felt like you were just meant to be watching a cutscene and the prompt just shows up on your screen out of nowhere. I mean, it does add a little interactivity, but with how minimal it is anyways, why even have them. It didn't even seem like missing one or hitting one really changed anything anyway. 5-pro or con depending on preference-I don't mind a good walking sim, but this is the walking sim champion. So if those kind of games aren't your cup of tea, you're better off just watching a playthrough on YT if the story at least interests you. I'd say the game is 75 percent walking, 20 percent reading/watching logs and other notes, and 5 percent pushing e.Specs: Ryzen 7700xRadeon 680032 GB @ 6000 Mhz1TB M.2

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it, and I'm gonna have to call this one of the most frustrating games I played this year. Fort Solis fails mechanically as a video game, and it fails even harder at story telling.While there's numerous issues with this title, I was willing to ignore every single one of them because I'm a sucker for good sci-fi; the art direction and world design really drew me in. The other thing the game does really well is drip feed you bits of its narrative, and my my, what a massive tease it is. It had me wrapped around its finger and I let it edge me along for 3 and a half hours, trusting that there's going to be some worthwhile climax at the end. Spoiler alert: this is not the case. Actual spoiler:For me around 40 fps average was bad enough, but it wasnt even a consistent 40 and it micro stuttered like hell. Had to enable frame generation just to get it to a playable state - dear devs, getting your game to an acceptable baseline is really not why this tech exists.QTEs out of nowhere with low contrast icons, but like whatever because as far as I could tell they have no impact on the outcome? Why are they even in there? Sluggish movement, poorly designed map, too much repetition, once the veneer of the game's narrative shatters all of its shortcomings that I put up with just become painfully obvious.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING THIS CONTAINS SPOILERSOkay, still here?  Cool, I'll break this down into 3 sections, Optimization, Gameplay, and Story.OptimizationQuite frankly there is none.  The game crashes 35% of the time when hitting continue, but continues to run in the background forcing you to kill it via steam or task manager.  Then the resolution is hard locked at 1366x1280 for some reason on every mode except windowed (this is not my display resolution in case you are wondering).  Then it has FSR2 which basically overrides all your display settings anyway, I found to get the game to play but actually be able to see what I was looking at required balanced.  However, even on the lowest settings you will still experience freezes and high CPU utilization.  Also experienced a lot of pop in and textures just vanishing on the higher settings.  At first I attributed this to perhaps something in the story but it was clear that was not a priority as mentioned below.GameplayDo you like quicktime events?  Cause that is the only gameplay in the game.  There were several moments that I thought I was going to get a puzzle and nope nada, closest thing is figuring out security codes of which there are 2 in the game.  One is so easy a baby could do it and the other as far as I know of no one has figured out yet without brute forcing it.  The thing about the qte's that is even more annoying is they don't really change much.  This breaks down into 2 types, A) progression stops until you solve the QTE the correct way, or B) you get a slightly different scene if you succeed vs fail but same situation overall.StoryOkay this is why you are here after all right?  Well don't waste your time.  No questions are answered.  The majority of the game involves the 2 protagonists joking about a zombie series they just watched, yet upon finding a dead body they ignore their instincts to GTFO.  This is even commented on in the game "You know it seems like you are trying to oneup the stupid protagonists in every horror film when they should clearly leave" < that's a direct quote from the game.If the game was trying to be tongue in cheek or had some clever twist it would be one thing, but there's no payoff.  They say something about the soil, but never point out what the problem with the soil was.  Why did Wyatt go from a caring father and doctor who wanted the program shutdown to brutally murdering everyone?  What was the deal with the soil that caused people to get aggressive (according to Wyatt)?  If Wyatt is supposedly still sane and is trying to contain the situation by killing everyone who comes in contact with it why does he cackle like a madman when Jessica runs away?  Why did he just capture Jack, but immediately went to trying to kill Jessica?  How is he teleporting all around the base?  None of the above questions will be answered and you will be left wondering.  Oh and in case you were wondering about the endings both are garbage.  It literally comes down to the second to last set of QTE's where you are running away.  If you mess up too many times while running, he catches you and in a fight you both die.  Otherwise he doesn't catch up until the hanger and you survive due to the cavalry finally arriving.  But Jessica dies due to getting cut by the same axe IN THE SAME SPOT that Wyatt had been cut by up to 5 times if you had completed the QTEs correctly, apparently leaving her too weak to do anything but an offscreen sacrifice that accomplishes nothing because it doesn't slow Wyatt down.All in all it has the same story plot beats of a B horror film, killer goes mad, kills everybody and stalks the rest and somehow can't be put down like a human being.  No payoff, no epilogue or satisfying conclusion.  Just dull sense of "why didn't he just leave after finding the dead body."TL;DRDo not buy if you have any interest in story or gameplay.  Only buy if you are wanting to support an indie company.

_childDocuments_.review: In the vast realm of gaming, it's not often that a title comes along that manages to forge a deep connection between players and their in-game personas. "Fort Solis," developed by a team clearly dedicated to immersion, successfully accomplishes this feat while also delivering stunning visuals and a unique game-play experience. While not without its quirks, the game manages to carve out a distinct niche in the gaming landscape.One of the standout features of "Fort Solis" is the remarkable way in which the development team has strived to weave an intricate bond between players and the main characters. From the onset, you're thrust into a narrative that's brimming with emotion and rich backstories, pulling you in and making you genuinely care about the characters' fates. This isn't just a game where you control avatars; it's an experience where you walk in the shoes of these characters, and every decision you make resonates with the weight of their destinies.Graphically, "Fort Solis" is a masterpiece. The level of detail present in every nook and cranny of the game world is astounding. From the subtle play of light and shadow,  every element has been meticulously crafted. This attention to detail not only enhances the overall immersion but also underscores the dedication of the development team to create a world that has a alien feel to it.Now, let's talk movement. The speed of the characters and their movement has been a point of contention among some players. However, when viewed through the lens of the game's overarching atmosphere of mystery and suspense, these design choices begin to make sense. The deliberate pacing and controlled movement contribute to a sense of tension and anticipation, aligning perfectly with the game's narrative tone. While it might not be everyone's cup of tea, it undoubtedly contributes to the game's unique appeal.It's worth noting that "Fort Solis" doesn't fit the mold of an open-world game. Instead, it offers an interactive walk-through experience that guides players through a carefully curated narrative. This focused approach allows the development team to maintain a high level of quality throughout, ensuring that every moment serves a purpose in the grand tapestry of the story. For what it sets out to be, "Fort Solis" excels admirably.And now, for a light-hearted moment – rest assured that in "Fort Solis," you won't encounter any frustrating boundary messages commanding you to return to your ship! While humor may not be the primary focus here "No pun attend" sorry Starfield!In conclusion, "Fort Solis" stands as a testament to the power of immersive storytelling and attention to detail. The development team's dedication to crafting a connection between players and characters shines through, even if the movement mechanics might take a moment to acclimate to. It may not be an open world, but If you're seeking an experience that leans into storytelling and atmosphere, "Fort Solis" is a captivating adventure worth embarking upon.

_childDocuments_.review: It's one of those games you really wanna recommend but you can't. There are things in the game that are great. The Graphics are amazing, the voice acting is great, the atmosphere is well built. But the problems of this game come down to how the game was handled at release and post release. Several people have reported game breaking  bugs, that the company has also acknowledged. For example if you quit game in the beginning of chapter 2, the next time you restart game you are forever stuck in an airlock with no way out. And there are other bugs like this during the game where you get permanently stuck somewhere just cos you didn't have time to play game from beginning to end in one session. The game was released exactly 3 months from today since writing this review, and they did make a few minor patches in the few weeks since the release but the patch is the only ones we got, and those were really minor fixes. You can of course finish the game, if you encounter said bug I described, you can restart the whole game from beginning. But Its really unacceptable you have to do that, you should be able to play the game through without game breaking bugs, especially since its a full release and not an early access.They have posted on forums that they are working on fixing these bugs and that they are a small team so it's slow. But I honestly find it unacceptable that they spent a lot of time post PC release working on Mac version of the game, while the PC version remains unfixed. Also a lot of people have asked on steam forums about the current state of the fixes, about when next patch will be released but I at least have not seen any comments from the devs since the one and only patch we got.As long as these bugs remain, and there is no further patches, I cannot recommend the game, tho I will make sure to update this review if they do release fixes on the biggest problems of the game.Edit: they did make 2 patches and not 1 as I originally said, tho again, both were minor bug fixes. They also announced a movie/tv series about the game....and something new for the game. I sure do hope its fixing game breaking bugs and not a paid dlc...

_childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is a standout title that offers a gripping, narrative-driven experience, perfectly suited for fans of intense, atmospheric thrillers. The game excels in creating a palpable sense of isolation and suspense as you explore the deserted Martian outpost. The voice acting is top-notch, with performances that breathe life into the complex characters and enhance the absorbing storyline.Graphically, the game is a marvel with detailed environments that beautifully capture the eerie desolation of Mars. The lighting and sound design further amplify the immersive experience, making every creak and shadow a source of heart-pounding tension.However, despite these strengths, Fort Solis isn't without its shortcomings. The game's pacing can feel uneven at times, particularly in the middle sections where the exploration tends to drag, potentially testing the patience of even the most dedicated players. Additionally, some of the puzzle mechanics are not as intuitive as they could be, leading to occasional frustration. QTEs are another area where Fort Solis could improve.In conclusion, despite some areas that could use polishing, Fort Solis is a must-play for those who appreciate a story-rich game with a strong emotional core and suspenseful atmosphere. The few issues it has do not overshadow the overall quality and thrilling experience it offers. Recommended for a dive into the mysteries that lie on the red planet!I wish it was longer than just 4 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: KEY POINTS of my long review: Great graphics, great acting, controls hinder gameplay, camera view is annoying, Story is a bit lacking but not terrible, not worth full price but worth checking out on sale, less than 6 hours of gameplay.Detailed opinionsStory 8/10 : Incredible idea for an edge of your seat story that just wasn't delivered in the best way. It's not bad it just feels like it's missing a good amount. The ending is just your run of the mill thriller movie ending but really my main complaint is how quick the story/game is. 100% completion in less than 6 hours and that's coming from me, a very slow player lol. A longer story would probably solve the issues I had with it.Graphics 10/10 : Beautifully designed environments and the character designs are incredible!Acting 10/10 : They did such a great job at making everything seem so natural. The facial expressions, the tones in peoples voices, the script etc. Great work.Gameplay 5/10 :           Camera view is too close to the character. It's like they couldn't decide between first person or 3rd person and decided to give you the feeling of sitting in a movie theater with a fat 7'3 dude sitting in front of the screen. Like I'm sure the visuals are awesome, sure wish I could see them beyond this dudes freaking back. You get used to it but it is annoying as hell.           Controls are immensely stupid. Play it with keyboard or controller, doesn't matter you'll hate it. You feel so restricted the entire time which makes 0 sense being in an environment meant for investigation and exploration. ALSO why TF can't you run? I get that running would make the game even shorter but in the situation these characters are in, they would realistically be running for their life. Again you get past it but seriously makes no sense.OVERALL : It is a good game and a good display of what the creators are capable of, referring to the visuals and acting, had  they spent more time on their story or at least just added more. I would not pay full price. This isn't worth more than 10 bucks imo.I really hope to see these guys make more games, I just hope they hear the players' opinions because they really do have the ability to be top tier creators.

_childDocuments_.review: . I think that had to said before anything else.I purchased this at . After downloading finished, I immediately launched and I did the obligatory time in the Settings Menu. I was shocked to discover that there was no way to change the key bindings. [:sadface:] . Another f.mod game. When will Dev's realise that not all PC Games actually use 'twin stick' controllers? We play using a Keyboard and Mouse.OK, disappointment aside, I finished setting up, returned to the main menu and launched. I then spent the next 4 minutes trying to get it to successfully launch only to be hit with an error message. Fail after Fail. So I went in search of help.Yep - every STEAM user's goto for quick fixes, for ports and/or new releases. Hmm. "Update to  nVidia drivers". OK, a little vague but I'll give it a go. AND....it still fails to launch.Since I couldn't get this to work on my $6,500 system (see My Profile) I hit  and watched a half dozen different play through's on both PC's and Xbox. My thoughts then led me down the rabbit hole, to preview other sites which have taken the time to do a breakdown of this Title. There were a LOT of points made, which are reflected in most of the reviews here on STEAM. My take after everything I've experienced AND from what I've watched and read? It seems this is a gem in the rough. If you listen to the feedback and change just three things, this would go a far way in making Fort Solis a real winner;I finally managed to get this title to launch, not on my main $6,500 system, rather my 6+ year old ROG 1050 Laptop. Yep - go figure!I played about 50 minutes which allowed for refunding the product if I wasn't sold. I wasn't.All of the above mentioned concerns (less performance issues, given the circumstances) are still relative except I would like to note these additional points;I found it particularly difficult controlling the antagonist using WSAD. Why? Because the movements of the antagonist has been written with twin Stick controllers in mind. This means that you need to 'roll' your keys in a circular motion as you do with the controller when you need to turn about. There is no instant DIRECTIONAL control you normally expect in  gaming.Then there was the surprise of the additional Keys. The 'B, T & G' keys are not even mentioned in the Settings but are integral in operating your wrist P.D.A. or trying to negotiate through . These will have the fingers of your LEFT playing TWISTER as you desperately try to successfully complete . I ended up using my RIGHT hand during these, which had me a little worried about taking my hand off the 'trigger' (mouse). Yes, I DO own a controller. However, if a  'game' is released I expect to be able to use native PC peripherals , with the use of Joysticks, Throttles & Rudders in the exception of Space/Flight Sims.Why are Events included on the PC, when walking swiftly or running isn't available? As a SDWS, is anything other the than 'E' key necessary? This is NOT a shooter. You never included the ability to drive the LMV down the canyon, the short distance from the Drill Site to Fort Solis. This only amplifies the 'On Rail' style implemented during most of the title.Fallen Leaf really set these two up from frame one. The idea of being a lead engineer responsible for the repair/maintenance of remotely controlled drilling platforms is a believable scenario. As the game starts, the gritty visual experience of Mars (as seen through the cameras of past and current drones) is replicated extremely well. The approaching storm is seen lurking in the background, like any sinister evildoer does.During the initial banter between Jack and Jessica, you can easily imagine their connection. As the game progresses you can't help but to bond with them, with an emotional connection slowly building with Jack as he searches through the dark corridors and rooms carrying out his investigation. You're constantly reminded of the immense storm outside, the only barricade being the thin walls of Fort Solis. The full story is extremely well written and could easily be adapted for Escape games. It's an amazing SDWS to play in a dark room with headphones.I thoroughly enjoyed the  playtime I experienced and will consider repurchase if the issues I raised are fixed. _childDocuments_.review: Fort Solis is essentially a very short walking simulator with a good atmosphere, very minor puzzle solving, great visuals and great voice acting. Tl;dr - I'd recommend this when it's on sale. That being said, the game falls flat when it comes to the storytelling aspect. Certain aspects of what has happened at the base aren't really made clear. It also doesn't help that the game feels very rushed with its progression; there's very little time for the game to allow different sections of the base to breath. A lot of the dialogue is clunky as well. I'm not sure if some things were lost in translation from Polish to English or what, but sometimes things that characters say just make no sense.Like many other games of this type there really is no replay value whatsoever. There are no kinds of branching narratives or alternate endings here. The story and level design aren't even really captivating enough to bring me back to experience again (like a good TV show for example).
