_childDocuments_.review: This game has many good things going on for it in the beginning. There's an alluring sci-fi mystery. A cast of very talented actors filling in the main roles. Unreal engine 5 promising new gen graphics and an amazing visual experience. So far the game feels very slow up to chapter 3 (it's where I left off), but the amount of interactables, references, ambiance, visual effects and graphics makes it a very interesting and captivating game so far, it gives you that eerie growing sense of dread, wanting more human interaction in it and when you finally get it it's not the happiest of moments lol (in a good horror sense)ConsJack moves like a tank (in a bad way). Slow and not very maneuverable. Jessica seems to be a bit better with controls and her camera angle also makes playing easier in my opinion, however both characters just feel like they are too clunky and turn too wide and there speed walk looks like their shuffling to take a mad dookie. The game definitely needs work in terms of rendering and visual bugs. It takes incredibly long to load and then there's the framerate drop/lagging which makes reaction triggers hard to do and when it comes to horror games, that is a huge no-no. As for visual bugs, many of the interactive consoles during cutscenes will disappear a dozen times when the player comes up to them, as well as entire vehicles also disappearing. Walls, doors, entities heads/hair disappearing or floating over curtains is also another constant issue I saw and it definitely breaks emersion and lags the game when it happens. A lot of the game in chapter 1-2 felt very much like filler and chapter 3 being more interactive when swapped to Jessica. Over all, there is more potential to this game and I sincerely hope the devs update it soon with some patches, because it definitely needs it. I do however still look forward to eventually finishing this game when I have the time and when some things have been fixed!

_childDocuments_.review: Want to know whether you should give Fort Solis a try? It depends if you are willing to taste something a bit different from what you are used to receiving from games. Setting optimization problems aside, as it is a known problem that I hope will be fixed soon (I have played Fort Solis on my quite ancient rig with Nvidia 1060, set the graphics on medium and while I certainly wasn’t able to enjoy its fullest potential when it comes to graphics, I only experienced a few slow-downs between the levels), let’s talk what that game truly is about - in my opinion.Fort Solis is a set of experiments questioning the status quo of what a game is. It sacrifices the gameplay for the sake of the story - but also sacrifices the story for the sake of experience. It tries to be as real as possible, which has its consequences, to name the two that were the most obvious to me:- the slow walking around, because who would run around all the time? Also, the jammed doors and long corridors are supposed to be a drag for the character, so it needs to be so for the player as well; - the vague story, because Jack and Jess (and therefore the player) are outsiders who try to unravel the plot from pieces of narrative created by characters who are inside the story. The logs, audio, and e-mails were not created to tell the story to us, they really try to imitate the communication that would be going on between people who live in certain conditions - we are only eavesdropping and trying to glue it together;Add beautifully and believably designed environments - both the dead, empty, and dusty surface of Mars and then wonderfully trashed labs, workshops, and crew areas, that make you believe someone really lives there. Then you watch or read or listen to the logs of characters and you see people that are alive - how they talk, how they stutter, their mimics and small gestures all gleaming with personality. The bare plot itself may not be something new, but what makes it stand out is how it comes to life through those people. It’s their story, not just a story. This part of the game truly amazed me - excellent writing and voice acting.We live in times when the era of telling stories gives way to a new age - thanks to modern technologies we can experience events in their whole. Fort Solis is an attempt to do this through the medium of a game. I won’t say the effect is perfect because it is not. But I enjoyed the game quite a lot. To sum up - there is only one way to play it: put the headphones on and immerse in it fully without expectations of what a game should be like. Experience it. You may like it or you may not, but it will be something new in your menagerie of experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a vivid example how NOT to make a game. It struggles in almost everything. It's not scary, it's not intriguing, it's slow and not fun. Also it's NOT a good showcase of Unreal Engine. People who said that obviously don't understand what they are talking about.There are 2-3 moments when character says out loud that he (or she, there are 2 playable characters) is in a hurry and it's dangerous to behave calm. But you don't have a sprint button. So after these words our hero just casually walks like nothing happened. Also the first character has to collect keycards to access different doors. The second one doesn't contact the first personally but has all these previously unlocked access levels. Magically, without explanation. Audio, text and video logs don't tell anything of relevance 90% of the time. Mini-games have really bad timings for button presses. QTE's can tell you to push stick left but character walks right. Cut-scenes are boring as hell and can't be skipped. There is literally zero twists in the story.It's a disaster. Someone actually invested in this and won't have their money back. There is no place for such products in gamedev. If you prolong your game by slowing the character it doesn't compensate the lack of content. It just shows your impotence as a designer.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game, short but sweet. Slowly discovering what happened by watching the video logs and listening to audio logs was very engaging and was a nice way of getting to understand the story. There are some quick time events but not many. I enjoyed getting lost in the world building and exploration. Overall it was a beautiful game and great voice acting. _childDocuments_.review: I love sci-fi, I love sci-fi horror and thrillers in space. I wanted to like this game a lot an be sucked into its world but...Why do I not recommend this game?- Considering depth of story, content, and length this game is barely worth 15 bucks.- Game is supposedly based on UE5, yet it looks and feels like an older version of Unity. Graphics, escpecially shadows look grainy on high quality settings and options like Motion Blur, Film Grain etc. turned off. A vast majority of textures look cheap like they were purchased from the UE store, looking bland and sallow. Blood in this game is bright red, which makes you wonder if it is red paint instead.- Horrible optimization, constant stuttering.- Horrendous game design choices: Map almost entirely useless, no live display of current location, no hints of which direction one is facing, either. Repetitive hallways, tunnels and rooms that all look identical and boring. NO sprinting, only slow walking throughout the whole playthrough. Annoying dialogues at the beginning with characters goofing around way too much when they should start being serious at some point. Insanely annoying QTE keybindings. Extremely linear gameplay.- Exploration extremely limited and not rewarding. Collectibles trite and expendable.- Atmosphere not gloomy and not scary enough (Inside the station for the most part)- Story not fully conclusive even after studying the plot afterwards.Positive:- Partially Atmosphere (Depiction of the planet Mars, certain sections inside the station)- Soundtrack and Sound Design- Voice Acting cast

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: Spoilers.Good:I really did enjoy the tension, atmosphere, and setting, its like a very mild 'Dead Space'. Voice actors we're also quite good.Graphics were great, and some of the little Easter egg elements were good fun.Bad:No ultra-widescreen support. The game is effectively a walking simulator, I don't really see a good excuse not to have made it compatible. (update) I get why they didn't go with this and its not a deal breaker for me, especially with an indie dev, it just would be nice to have.No way to tell your character to run or jog... we're in danger and running out of time, but all we can manage is a meandering walk. (update) I've read a number of responses by the developers around this, and I'm still unconvinced; there are cut scenes where the characters flat out sprint, adding the ability to jog, or even just walk a bit faster doesn't seem breaking in any way. There weren't any jump scares or moments I remember where it would have been a problem.The plot didn't make a great deal of sense, I never really had an 'ah ha!' moment where I felt like anything especially important had occurred or Wyatt's motivations make sense. Its like a very banal case of corporate espionage, with some hints that Helen has 'maybe' created something which might have negative side effects, and Wyatt got angry because management didn't like his interference. Generally speaking, the game had all the potential for a great/scary experience but falls flat on a number of points. The major reveal seemed very anti-climactic, and the ending was terribly contrived and unsatisfying. (update) On reflection, this is even more irritating, because the voice actors were so good and all the elements of a great sci-fi-horror-conspiracy-plot were there; but all the lead up and tension just falls apart because the 'conspiracy' is so unimpressive. We never get a straight answer about what damage the drill bay doors or if it was related to Helen's work. I also still don't have a clear picture for Wyatt's motivation, he comes off more as a disgruntled postal worker who shoots up the office, rather than someone who has uncovered some monumental conspiracy and is trying to ensure it never escapes the lab. We are "kind of" led to believe that compound 26 is(might be?) dangerous, but not immanently so, and there is never any real sense of urgency in whats going on.Finally, the whole wrap up of Jessica's story just seems like lazy writing. Which is annoying, because its clear the writers can do better. Its not just in how it ends, but the last few minutes of the process to get there are very contrived and not terribly well thought out. I think there was a huge missed opportunity here in terms of choice and consequence, and was left really wanting more. While the game is probably worth playing if you're a fan of the genre, I don't think I'd recommend it because of the fairly lack-luster plot, contrived ending, and poor quality of life decisions.

With storm warnings imminent, he heads inside to make desperate contact. As the night grows longer, events escalate, spiral out of control and the mystery of what happened to the crew begins to reveal itself. The storms is approching, limiting Jack’s escape as he looks to hold out until morning arrives.

name: Chants of Sennaar
detailed_description: Winner of Best Indie Game at the 2024 New York Game Awards and nominated multiple times at other ceremonies including The Game Awards and the BAFTA, Chants of Sennaar is a critically-acclaimed puzzle and adventure game developed by Rundisc. Divided since the dawn of time, the Peoples of the Tower no longer speak to each other, isolated by fear or mistrust. It is said that one day, a Traveler will find the wisdom to break down the walls and restore the balance. Travel the endless steps of a prodigious labyrinth, uncover the truth and unveil the mysteries of this fascinating universe where ancient languages are both the lock and the key. Inspired by the myth of Babel, discover an enigmatic and vast tower. As the Traveler, delve into a world full of mysteries, where Peoples have grown distant, unable to communicate with each other anymore. Begin your adventure in a prodigious tower inhabited by five distinct Peoples, observe, listen, and strive to mend the bonds of distrust. With a smart gameplay system, explore and solve various puzzles to uncover the mysteries of five different interconnected languages. Always guided by your trusty notebook, note each symbol, keep track of your surroundings, engage in conversations with people and unravel the meaning of every glyph. Each step will pave your way to the top of the Tower as each word will restore the link between People. Dive into an enthralling and colorful world full of secrets. Tumble headlong into a beautiful world inspired by impactful European comics authors where every floor of the Tower possesses its own visual identity, supported by distinctive technological levels, architecture and culture. Embark on a poetic and enchanting journey driven by a soul-stirring, lyrical soundtrack, made by Thomas Brunet.

_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: The overall concept and mechanics of unknown languages are amazing, fresh and fascinating! However "stealth" missions are boring, unnecessary and spoil mood of the game.PS noticed bad optimization of the game which trying to melt my notebook (this is ridiculous considering the primitive graphics in the game), for example, Rust on max don't giving such a load on my PCPSS transformation puzzle is overcomplicated, opposed to the all linguistic puzzles, formula is quite boring to decipher
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cool and very satisfying. I like how through exploring the tower levels, aside from translating and transcribing new languages you also get a look into the different core values of the different communities on each level of the tower. the graphics are simple but aesthetic and refreshing and I like the various color schemes in the game. overall I did not get stuck much but did feel challenged a few times. Still the main point I feel worth getting across is the satisfaction you get for every ounce of progress you make throughout the game. Also the game won't lock you out of achievements and will let you receive the fruits of your labor. You will be able to witness the transformation you as a player and a stranger to the tower managed to inspire while and after finishing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little game, to be played over the course of a week or binged over a weekend.This is a game with pleasant graphics and music, a nice story about the power of language, and some very wholesome interactions. Variable difficulty as explained below, the base game could be played by children. It took me 12 hours to fully complete the game, including all achievements.I STRONGLY SUGGEST YOU DON'T USE THE GLYPH VALIDATION. Use a pen and paper instead. I only filled in the first three pages, then I decided that this was too easy and didn't validate any more words. The resulting difficulty was perfect for me. I added my own guesses to the words, but didn't validate them. I validated every glyph in a row immediately before finishing the game.The main gameplay loop of finding glyphs with their meaning, then being able to understand sentences before finally translating from one language to another was extremely satisfying. More translation work, more complicated sentences and more words would have been amazing.The stealth sections seem superfluous, as do some other mini games, but those puzzles are easy enough and offer distraction from the bread-and-butter translating. Travel sometimes felt slow, because hints are strewn all over.I would have liked more complicated languages with more words and more text. Some sentences were hard to grasp because they were so short. Some glyphs had double meanings, but they were used too rarely to clearly grasp both contexts/meanings.The final language was a pushover, very disappointing. I would immediately buy a second game. I hope that a sequel would allow us to play without the validation feature, and have more words and more translation work. I could imagine a main story/quest to be completed, and then being able to dive deeper into the mythology of the different peoples by reading their holy texts optionally on the side.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. If you're super into con-langs, you might find it a bit underwhelming, but if you like puzzle games and have any interest in linguistics (or just think it sounds kinda interesting) this is the game for you.Completed the whole thing in about 10 hours. Got a little bored of all the walking by the end (especially in cases where I got a bit stuck) but the games pretty, so it wasn't too bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game recommended to me after finishing Return to the Obra Dinn and I was initially skeptical and came in with no expectations. What I ended up experiencing was a game that managed to capture every aspect of its execution perfectly, laying out a beautiful presentation that delivered on every front, from artwork to gameplay. One of the best puzzle / investigatory games I've ever played, only complaint is wishing it was longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Expensive, but exceptional. Wonderfully designed. You might figure out some words early, but the definite lock in will only happen once you should know the answer. A few spots of easy to miss symbols - three of the warrior symbols spring to mind - but overall well designed, clever, creative, and worth its price
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Even in a golden age of creative and polished indie games, this stands out. It really delivers on its premise with a clever interface that lets you focus on interpreting the languages, and holds your hand just enough to keep it light and fun while letting you feel smart. The world is charming and cozy, and funny at times. Short and sweet, highly recommended for someone who wants something that'll keep you using your brain but help you relax at the end of a long day.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: As far as language translation games go... yeah! It's cool! It's not, like. Particularly deep on that front - the languages you are translating all have their own rules and shapes and it's neat but they're also all, like, forty words big and share most of the same words, generally not too hard to work out (chapter 3 was the only time where this felt kinda challenging) and each language is pretty much tossed off upon entering a new zone, save for the last chapter of the game.And the last chapter is... a decision. You're basically given the entire last language for free as long as you've decently solved the previous ones and then you proceed to... not even use it very much, there's no puzzles to solve in the last zone and only a few doors to open, you're not even allowed to reestablish links yourself like you did for the other tower denizens. The entire last chapter feels kinda rushed and stripped back to ferry you along to the ending sequence faster. It's weird.Outside of the language-learning aspects, the puzzles are... pretty solid! Not very challenging (again) but they're often based off your knowledge of the language so it adds an extra layer at least. The stealth segments aren't exactly the highlight of the game but they're infrequent enough that I'm not too fussed by them. The game looks gorgeous, sounds pretty good too, and while the story is fairly minimal there's enough lore and culture implied by your interactions and exploration of the various levels of the tower that it's at least intriguing.My overall thoughts on the game are that it's - good! Not going to be as impactful or memorable as, say, Heaven's Vault, its most obvious comparison point, but I'm glad I played it, it was fun smiley face :) :)
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked games like The Witness or Tunic you may also like this. Buttt this game is not like those. Where those games are about "the layers", Chants of Sennaar plays it much more straightforward. You go around, observe, and draw deductions from your observations to inform your own understanding of the languages that you see. Oh and there is a lot of walking around without much happening in the meantime. Ultimately I liked this game but it feels that it goes too much out of its way to convenience the player. You are given an easy to game lock in feature (significantly easier than Obra Dinn's), some languages were just too easy (the game tells you the meaning after solving a mostly unrelated puzzle), and each language had far too few words in it for anything but the most basic communication. Unfortunately there really isn't a solution to these problems without either layering this sort of information (a la The Witness or Tunic) which adds far too much work for how much enjoyment an average player will get, or by alienating most of the target audience. The balance that Chants of Sennaar has struck is a good one that should satisfy everyone at least a bit, and for that I think it is an excellent game (and its also fun).I would like to see a hard version of this game, not as an extension to this one but like a sequel or something. A hard version where you get space for notes, but you have to take them yourself, preferably completely free-form (maybe just tell the player to get some paper). Where you can activate a lock in feature, but only after you have found all (or nearly all) the symbols, and already understand them well enough that you only use it to get the "true" meaning of the words. Where the phrases that you read are never properly translated to English (or whatever), you just get word translations, you have to make sense of the grammar yourself. Within Chants, I mapped out the entirety of an underground maze-like section, not because I had to (though it did help later on), but because it was fun. I think having an underlying part of the game that requires such tasks would be what is needed to make this game truly great. As it stands its just fun, which is why I still highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - 5 out of 5 StarsThis game took me approximately 18 hours to play and it felt like it was the perfect amount of time. It didn't overstay its welcome or leave me wishing it was longer, which is fantastic. The art, the puzzles and the story are amazing, unique and so much fun.The puzzles are definitely challenging and will take a bit of brainpower to think through. A few of the puzzle answers didn't make sense to me, which was frustrating, but overall, it's a nice challenge for puzzle players. I also really enjoyed the stealth parts and the few scary moments. The ending was lovely and the story resolves in a beautiful, touching way. I highly recommend for people like me who love language, puzzles, an interesting story and beautiful artwork.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game off of the recommendation of Game Makers Toolkit and it did not disappoint.The way that they handle puzzles and language learning is truly one of the best times that I've ever had with a game.A short but very sweet experience that I would highly recommend to anyone looking for a fun linguistic challenge.However the only thing that tripped me up is somehow I was not able to validate all of the symbols due to a random glitch. Other than that rest easy know that the money spent on the game is well spent
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: > Finished the game in around .A rare language puzzle solving game that nails its challenge. The languages has some clever deductions such as the shape, meaning and construction which makes it more rewarding to figure out. I also appreciate is how the game takes notes and images for the player where I did not need to use an external note taking device typical in hard puzzle games. Alongside the fixed/tracking camera, the visual aesthetic is quite pleasing specially the lines that provide shape and depth as plain large color blocks can be harsh on the eyes. With its low price, this game just provides so much value,As for issues though, I think some of the puzzles are guesswork due to being unclear or confusing. Some leeway is granted here given the nature of language but the last portion of the game really pushes that limit as well as the pacing. While deciphering a few languages are hard enough, I would like it if the languages have little commonality with each other but I cannot imagine the difficulty or design much less testing of more varied languages. Some of the other mechanics and mini-games such as stealth and inventory are underutilized or unremarkable. Although they are meant to vary the pacing, they could still be more memorable.Aside from those issues and loving the game, it does not reach that meaningful height to push the game to be truly great. I do like how sincere and positive the message is but I feel it does not emotionally or technically land. Language is cultural, social and geopolitical so the ending somewhat ignores those nuances. I also think a certain economic class was missing in the ending making it a bit muddled. Still the intent is good so I can let it slide but I am disappointed.The game does deliver on its core promise of a language solving game and for that I can very much recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A unique experience and absolutely one of my favorite games at this point. Using context clues to learn the unique languages, discovering the different grammar rules, and trying to translate between languages, all contributed to a fantastic game which my only complaint would be the game didnt have more gameplay for me to enjoy!Had my family and friends hearing me rave about it for over a month!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I wish my linguistic abilities would be greater to express how moved I've been by the beauty of this game. Every little aspect is simply beautiful. From the core idea to its mechanics, everything breathes poetry. Chants of Sennaar plays smoothly in a balance of complexity and simplicity. When you start, you will find that the basic components and rules are quite simple, but at the same time is from the interaction of these different mechanics that the complexity arises, making its gameplay an experience not so different from the way an actual language works. Overall, that allows for even the misunderstandings to be pleasurable, and the game, while pushing us up the ladders of dialogue between cultures, inadvertently ends up reaching a universal language of gaming appreciation.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. I see why this is recommended so highly on the Outer Wilds subreddit-- truly a game that you wish you could wipe your memory to play it for the first time again. A masterpiece. It says so much with shockingly few words. It's evocative, stylistically stunning, and haunting.I do wish that the automatic validation of words and definitions was toggleable somehow. I felt a lot of times like it happened too soon, and I would've preferred to draw more connections myself before having the game tell me definitively what the words mean, and it bothered me how easy it was to brute force a translation rather than try to understand. It's a nitpick though, and didn't detract from the overall experience (which was phenomenal) and I understand that not everyone is a conlang/linguistics nerd. But difficulty levels or something would've been nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: An outstanding puzzle game about translating languages. I had many moments of confusion, almost always followed by an extremely satisfying 'aha' when everything began to fall into place. I loved the world building as you play, and how the cultures strongly influence the languages. There were a few elements which felt out of place - Stealth and vaguely platforming sections, but they didn't detract from the experience very much. Plus, a great ending!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: An engrossing casual puzzle game centering around translating fictional languages. If that sounds excruciatingly hard, it's not; you can work backwards to validate the meaning of the glyphs in your journal if you get stuck. The translation mechanics feel a lot like the puzzle solving mechanics in Return of the Obra Dinn, another game I loved.It can sometimes be hard to trust a game with a novel premise, but trust me when I say this one delivered on my expectations! I was so enamored with this game that I beat it in two play sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game!!! Went through it on one breath and loved every second! heard about it as "duolingo dark souls" and it is somewhat true. Not as difficult as dark souls, but I did resort to looking up answers a couple of times. I loved noticing patterns inside of the language, such a delight learning different rules for each language. And the world dis just so beautiful!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough good about this game. Each language makes thematic sense based on their culture. The connection they have between each other is apparent based on the differences in language. The puzzles have a satisfying logic to them. You can pet a cat.Only minor criticism is that the 5th language is practically given to you, which makes the end feel a little rushed. Very fun. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I'm playing it as part of a video game club. I'm not sure I'd have picked this game up by myself, but I'm glad I did. The puzzles aren't overly obtuse and don't make you feel dumb. There's fun in figuring out a new language, although it's a very rudimentary/simple version of say duolingo. The art style and calming music is soothing as well. Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful puzzle game. For others who like linguistic puzzles, it may seem to start out very easy at first, but the languages definitely get tougher as the game goes on. That being said, the final language has a very different learning process due to the setting, so I don't know whether to fully count it as a linguistic puzzle.The setting is wonderful, with each area of the tower feeling very distinct from each other. The people inhabiting them feel real too - clearly a lot of thought was put into the worldbuilding. This also reflects in the linguistic section; you can really see which words are prioritized for each civilization, how their language and way of life shape each other. In fact, the game actively encourages you to think about how a word might have come about, which words it's similar to, etc. There was more than one time where I guessed a word based off the way it looked.Obviously, the languages aren't fully realized Tolkien-style. Even at the end, they lack a lot of the filler words and sentences never really stop being short and simple. That being said, this makes it very accessible to a wide range of people, even those unfamiliar with linguistic puzzles. And the game does shake things up at a few points, which I will leave as a surprise.The game also features puzzles of a more regular variety. These are fun too, though constantly running back and forth for some of them can get mildly annoying, it gives you more time to soak up the wonderful setting. At least a few of the puzzles are timing-based, relying on your ability to click fast enough. This isn't really a con in my book, I had great fun regardless, but is worth mentioning for the sake of accessibility. That being said, the controls never get more complicated than just clicking, which leaves it rather accessible to most.Overall it's going on my list of favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A really interesting approach to a puzzle game. If you enjoy linguistics, cultural anthropology, or mythology, then this is definitely worth checking out. I could talk about the well designed puzzles, or the overall variety the game achieves, but my biggest praise is the actual play-ability. The way the journal works to allow you to make notes and experiment with possible solutions, but not just giving you the answers, is absolutely wonderful. The mechanics of the game are simple, but really well designed for ease of play, while at the same time the game itself offers rewarding challenges and a nice story.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and satisfying as you slowly come to understand and translate alien languages. There are real moments of satisfaction and triumph as something about a language clicks into place. It is slightly marred by the sometimes tedious, sometimes frustrating puzzles.  This is par for the course as a point and click adventure game, but it left me wanting  everything to move a little faster. If you can enjoy the slower pace, you'll be very satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: played on ps5, hence the low playtime here.i really enjoyed this! the language translation mechanic at the center of the whole thing is great. if anything i wish that there was less guidance and that the game let you fail a little more often. the obra dinn style "confirming translation" mechanic gave some answers away too easily and took away from some of the joy of discovering components of each language organically.i also wish the game cut down on traditional point and click style puzzles a little more. there were a few puzzles that i got tripped up on simply because i didn't realize that i was supposed to be able to interact with or pick up a specific item in the environment, and a few times where i missed something and had to do a lot of manual backtracking just to scrape the environment looking for what i missed. it's fun when you're doing this to fill in gaps in the language, but when you're just looking for an item laying on the ground it starts to feel like busywork.aesthetically the game is really solid. the art direction is excellent and the soundtrack really fits the mood of the game. you can tell pretty early on that the overall message of the game is going to be something along the lines of "can't we all just get along" / communication solves all problems, which is a little trite and uninteresting, but hey, you can't expect all of your games to be philosophical masterpieces.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic! The art style is beautiful, the language learning element is so fun and interesting! There's sneaking, super fun puzzles, something for everyone! There seems to be a sort of ominous backstory, or at the very least something is going on, so that'll be fun to play out! Already one of my favourite games!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I played in the last few months. It could easily be the best game ever. I think I've never encountered anything similar. My best regards to everyone who contibuted to the creation of this game, you made me cry lol.If you love languages this game is for you, but it's not as simple as it may seem because every social group has its own language, and they even differ in grammar. Good luck trying to guess how to translate some of those words!For those who speak just one language: consider playing this game. It will make you re-evaluate your way of thinking and perceiving the world and the people around you. It's mind-blowing!100/10
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! Great short (too short!) experience with lovely graphics, perfectly balanced logic puzzles and cute critters (including those that shouldn't really be cute). Absolutely amazing idea enclosed in a really relaxing but still engaging playthrough. I loved every minute of it, even the moments when I struggled a bit (mostly due to getting lost or missing some doors...). The progress was very rewarding. Honestly, the only thing about this game that bugs me is that it left me wanting more! At some point I started getting really excited about the languages getting more complex and was super hyped to see how it will evolve. I have to say I was expecting a bit more when it comes to this (main) part of the game. I am definitely hungry for more and hope the developers will use the base idea of decoding languages again!I sincerely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: First off I love this game!I've already beaten it 3 times with my best time being just under 5 hours, with some mistakes here and there.If you really find language interesting, and enjoy puzzle games this game is certainly for you!I cannot stress it enough how wonderful this game is. Not to mention, if they do make some form of DLC for this game I will be so excitedTen outta Ten
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: If you like riddles and languages, this is the game for you. Some of the numerical ones I found quite tricky (but that is what the internet is for).All through the game you can feel how lovingly it was crafted.If this sets a precedent for a new game idea, I would be very happy.Could have played at least double the time and not gotten bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of "metroidbrainia" games like Outer Wilds or Obra Dinn, you'll probably like this one, though it is a bit more casual than either of those games. I think it has some weaknesses; lacking some QoL features that would make certain things much less tedious, and once you translate the languages a lot of the puzzles feel like just following instructions. But overall I enjoyed the experience and it did give me the "puzzle itch" where I'd be thinking about it after one session and have some idea I wanted to try at the start of the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece! Very unique and innovative concept, beautiful artwork and music, clever puzzles and great gameplay. I would strongly recommend it to anyone who likes puzzle games with a touch of surreal, weird environments (kind of like playdead games). Overall a great experience that was sadly overlooked by the mainstream media.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Great puzzle game, if decyphering languages sounds fun to you, this game is something for you.Didn't get stuck at any point, never felt unfair but still challenged me enough imo.My playthrough to get the good ending took me almost 8h, besides some achievements there's nothing more to earn after.This might seem a little low but i was glad about the playtime because it felt like just enough to have fun throughout without the base concept of the game overstaying its welcome. I've grown very fond of games respecting my timeoriginally bought it because it reminded me a lot of decyphering the language in tunic, didn't regret it, it's a great game with a novel concept, would highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this a somewhat easy puzzle game that weighs in with a strong art direction, music, and game design. The only real negative I have for this game is the movement system, which can get sticky around corners, bug out slightly near moving objects and be indecisive, which is a shame because a good majority of this game is running around, backtracking, and there are several sections where movement is time-sensitive.A couple of times the game didn't give me the opportunity to translate words I fully knew the meaning of and I had to consult a walk-through to find the 'trigger', and there was the occasional necessity of wandering around blithely for fifteen twenty minutes to find a metaphorical red key to stick in a red door. If you're like me, you will figure out 90% of a language very quickly and spend another thirty minutes re-visiting rooms to try and nail down one or two more.These are relatively minor concerns however, and I  recommend .If you like the very specific genre of 'relaxed translation puzzle game exploring weird cultures', I might suggest  as a second pickup, which focuses on one language with ten or twenty times the level of complexity as any one language seen here if you're hungry for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Chants of Sennar is a delightful game that kept me interested in the world with just the right amount of challenge. I felt like I always had enough information to solve puzzles on my own, but they weren't handed to me either. The art and sound design are gorgeous and you can tell a lot of care and love went into the production of this game. It nods to indie staples like Obra Dinn and Tunic (kinda) while fully standing on its own exploring unique gameplay ideas. I look forward to seeing more that Rundisc has to share with us!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Really great puzzle game. Took me 11 or 12 hours so it's not super long, but absolutely brilliant. The sort of puzzle design that will make you really struggle for a while and then when you figure it out you feel like a genius. The story is really sweet too, it's fun seeing the different cultures on each level of the tower and getting to help them with their problems. Art and music are beautiful too. Easily one of my favourite games I've played recently.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece, truly a masterpieceI've just finished my playthrough and I don't know where to start, really... This may seem to be a silly quirky game about translating non-existing languages but there's soooo much more to it! Creative gameplay mechanics, beautiful minimalist graphics with distinguishable colour palettes for each region and the ambient music that perfectly emphasises the atmosphere of the current location - these are only few reasons why you sholud play this hidden gem of a game.However, it is the story that shines the most. The worldbuilding is superb. Each of the Tower's peoples can be described with certain characteristics and the interactions among them really flesh out the world. The storytelling is really impeccable. As for the story it is a bit concealed and is told contextually with dialogue between various characters or using the world itself. Exploring the Tower actually feels like discovering an ancient civilization and uncovering its history. The story itself is really thought provoking, especially after experiencing the true ending of the game, and is filled with allegories to the real world.Reagrding the story (avoiding any spoilers) this game has got me hooked on for two evenings straight and  I'm just a few days before my final exams. Enough said I had to finish it before taking my tests and not after them since I couldn't think about anything else but this game - especially not about studying ;-)TL;DR: Once in a lifetime experience, a must-play
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: lovelovelove this game, just absolutely gorgeous and inventive and fun i want so many more games like this, i absolutely blew through it and now im replaying it to see how your perspective shifts when you already are familiar with a lot of the glyphs and puzzles i havent stopped thinking about this game all week
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fresh and unique puzzle game. Great art and puzzle design. The sounds are nice too although the UI sounds start to get very annoying near the end, but you can turn them off so that's fine. The only cons I can think of are, not allowing the player to organize the glyphs, it can be annoying to have to dig through them all the time if you don't have a photographic memory, being able to organize them in different ways would've been nice, and might've even helped with remembering the basic grammars. The other con is that the stealth is just really frustrating and slow in some areas. It really hurts the pacing of the game. Would love to see another installment of a game like this, but perhaps minus stealth. Overall, really enjoyed something completely new.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This is an innovative game that tickled my brain in all of the right ways! Piecing together a language through contextual clues is such a fun way to go about things. There were a few spots where I really struggled to make sense of things and got to feel so smart when I finally had the necessary breakthrough. And like many of the best puzzle games, Chants of Sennaar does not overstay its welcome. Once you figure something out, it moves on and doesn't beat you over the head with the same mechanic for the next few hours. The art and music are wonderful as well and contribute to the overall style of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played any other game like this. I love games that involve figuring out a language, and I love puzzle games, and this fuses the two beautifully! The languages are tightly integrated into the mechanics of the game, and with multiple languages, you're not just translating into English, you're learning about the cultures and connecting different concepts that hold a similar place for the different people.The gameplay for the last language feels unfinished (most of it is just handed to you, rather than having to figure it out), and I wish it were overall less eager to verify your translations, but these are minor nitpicks.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. Some of the puzzles were confusing at times and I need help to figure them out but I feel like the rest of the game easily makes up for that. I really want more content or even some sort of spin off game because it was really fun exploring the world just to figure out what one person is trying to tell you.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: : 4/5Chants of Sennaar is a very pretty and very entertaining experience which delivers an original gameplay experience about languages and how we as humans learn these through context and interaction.: 5/5Chants of Sennaar has an incredibly solid art style, some beautiful sights and wonderful sound design. It's always pleasant to navigate the world, and I'm only left wishing for more grand vistas of the tower in its entirety or the view from there as you climb.: 4/5Chants of Sennaar is about matching strange words to their meanings within a range of different languages by observing their use in context, inducing meanings or translating from other languages. This core loop was immensely satisfying, especially at first in my playthrough, but a lack of variety in the languages stupored the experience later on. I could feel more potential than was exploited here; while the developers play with using different grammars and sentence constructions, I feel the potential for even stranger combinations of languages could have made for even more interesting gameplay.I understand why they did not make the languages more distinct than they did - players must be able to translate between them at several points throughout the game, and more granular presentation than whole words or concepts would drastically raise the difficulty.I am ultimately left feeling a bit disappointed the languages did not go crazier than they did. There were some excellent moments, especially the revelation at the true ending which could perhaps not have been possible with stranger languages, but I still wish there was more meat to this since it was the most engaging part of the experience.:  4/5Nothing to write home about, but a neat story about human connection across cultures and assumptions. I was not left wanting more, but the narrative left no imprint on me neither. There are some excellent occasional touches, especially with regards to the words some of the people use against one another which really allow a more passive story to shine through, and these were the best parts of the narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: The game manages to capture elements that are true about actual language learning while still being fun and intriguing. There are very satisfying moments when you finally understand the language and/or get to progress because of your understanding. While there are some non-language-related stealth/timing sections that the game could have done without, they are easy and brief enough that I am okay with them. I really hope this game inspires a new genre of games that go even further with these language learning game mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: There exists a tower, a tower that was created to allow civilization to live on, but something has gone wrong. You have awoken from a tomb in a hidden room at the base of the tower with no understanding of the language of those who you run into. You will have to conquer the language and others to solve the mystery of the tower in Chants of Sennaar. You will be tasked with talking to those individuals who are willing to talk to you. You will also have to try to decipher the language written on walls, signs, and more. The more you interact with the language the better chance you have at figuring it out. You see, one of the main components of the game is that you, the gamer, will have to take guesses as to what each symbol represents. You will have “checkpoints” where you will take out your journal and try to place the symbol with a drawn representation to master the language.I will be completely honest with you, this is a game where you’re going to be note taking outside of the in-game note taking which is the foundational mechanic of the game. In each area you’re going to have to decipher up to 36 different symbols. These symbols can help you understand the residents of that level of the tower, as well as give you hints towards puzzles that you’ll have to undertake. The levels of the tower also increase in complexity. Later in the game, not only do you have to decipher the symbols, but you’ll also be tasked with utilizing stealth to get past certain sections of that level. There are other levels where you can easily get lost if you don’t follow directions you received somewhere else in the level.This is not a game for action loving gamers, this is the type of game for those who are looking to not only solve puzzles, but to rediscover lost languages. It, personally, took me close to 7 hours to get through the entire game. There were definitely some missteps, and there were times where I got lost, but there was always that burning desire to conquer the tower that seemed to stick with me throughout my playthrough. The one thing I will say is that even after deciphering the level’s language when tasked with translations to other level’s languages, there was definitely a level of frustration when it came to pluralized words. So if you do take up the call to conquer this specific tower, understand that sometimes direct translations, much like the world and the languages we interact with, don’t always run smoothly.I definitely recommend this game. I enjoyed it. It was something different, and a good change of pace. The translation/deciphering of languages did remind me of my time spent playing Heaven’s Vault, and that’s a good thing. So if you’re looking for a different type of game, and you have the brain power or brain configuration to decipher forgotten languages, I would highly recommend that you add this game to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: In Chants of Sennaar, you play as an unnamed character awakening one day at the bottom of a titanic tower. This Babel-like tower is home to several peoples, each living in their own part of the tower and speaking their own language. Your goal is to reach the top of the tower to uncover its secrets. To do so, you will need to understand the locals. The issue is, as you awake, you seem to be unable to understand all of these weird languages, and will be required to learn how to translate them.Chants of Sennaar is a great language-based puzzle game with a stunning art style. It has been rightfully compared to both Heaven's Vault and Return of the Obra Dinn: the former, because of its language-based puzzle solving mechanics, and the later, because of its theory confirmation mechanics - the game allows you to check your translations by filling in sets of translations all at once in the same way Return of the Obra Dinn would get players to lock in names and causes of death. To be fair, there are worst games to be compared to in such a favorable light.I cannot explain what I loved about Chants of Sennaar whitout first mentionning another game I played for tens of hours: Heaven's Vault. There is something about language-based puzzle games that I just find particularly appealing. However, I always had a small complaint about Heaven's Vault: although its glyph system made for a very interesting game, its language structure perfectly replicated the english sentence pattern. Sure, this made all these sentences easier to translate, and this was probably integral to the automatic sentence generation for players on their fourth or fifth playthrough. But this also meant that a whole part of the "language-based puzzle" was lost . Thankfully, Chants of Sennaar nailed that part quite well by playing on the sentence patterns. This was when I understood this game would scratch the itch I had since playing Heaven's Vault.There was however a mechanic I did not enjoy quite as much, and that is the infiltration part of the game. Sure, it was not really a difficult part of the game. However, this is not really something I personally enjoy in games - others may however like these stealth sections more than I did.Thankfully, the whole experience more than makes up for these stealth parts: I emphasized the language-based puzzles, but the whole game is a little gem. The art, the music, the general atmosphere they create, the puzzle-solving... Everything was nailed perfectly, all packed neatly in a 7 to 10-hour experience you should definitely try.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem of a game. I usually am not into puzzle games yet here am I, 7 hours in, constantly thinking about the beautiful setting of Chants of Sennaar. The rewarding feeling I get when I finally understand a glyph or a sentence is unparalleled. The soundtrack is beautiful, the art direction is gorgeous (I can't stop taking screenshots), the characters I encounter are endearing (most of them) and lively. And as mentioned above, the gameplay is so rewarding. I am 7 hours in and I am absolutely taking my time to finish this game, I want to enjoy if for as long as possible. (I was lucky enough to playtest a beta of the game a couple of years ago and got a key as a thank you, hence the "product received for free" checkbox)
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: It took me 12 hours to finish this but I wish there were many more. I never knew how much I love linguistic puzzles. One thing I'd like to say that grammar was a bit too much like English (except for Bards maybe - they have Yoda English:)). The music, sounds, visuals were top notch. Beautiful. I also liked both endings: one because it was stormy and the other because it was nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible adventure that did, sadly, get less fun over time. You go through five unique languages over the course of the game, but I had the most fun with the first one, as it really felt like I was piecing words together, and using the shapes of symbols to determine other ones, whereas as the game went on it became more of a brute-force simulator to try to guess what the symbol i had seen once two hours ago meant. Overall, an incredible game with outstanding visual style, but it wore a little thin near the end
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Chants of Sennaar is a work of art only possible in the medium of video games. I felt a sense of discovery and impact on the world in this game that I don't know if I've ever felt while playing a game before. Play this game or miss out on a one-of-a-kind work of art so unique that screenshots, videos, and reviews can only give you the vaguest sense of what it is like.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little indie game with a unique take on the adventure/puzzle genre. The art and music are absolutely gorgeous. World building leaves much to be desired, as the story is quite jagged and I felt myself not really understanding where I am. The 2nd "stage" of the game in particular I found very unfun because of how large and empty it is.The core game play loop, however, is brilliant. Piecing together languages using context clues and notes in your journal is fun and rewarding. Going back to previous conversations after learning new words and being able to make educated guesses on what certain words could be is amazing. Not to mention that each language is distinct in it's pluralisation, grammar structure, and direct translation. The game displays some of the complexity of languages and what makes them so different, and why translation can be so difficult.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: While I like linguistics I'm usually not even remotely into puzzle games but this game was still fabulous. Aside from any of the gameplay loops the art style is really visually striking and the soundtrack is amazing. The musical cues change when you're on track in finding where you need to be for a puzzle, the music conveys some of the sense of confusion you feel being dropped into a world where, especially at the start of each level, you quite literally cannot comprehend what anyone is saying.The game is short, I finished it in about 10 hours and that was with some pretty casual playing. I could've sat and binged but I wanted to take my time because the atmosphere of the game is really quite fun. I know there is some controversy in reviews of this game about the stealth sections and they do exist but they're relatively few and far between and also they're pretty simple. If you don't like stealth sections I would classify them as more of a nuisance than anything.I bought this on sale for $15 and easily has more quality/care put into it than plenty of $30 games so even the normal $19.99 price is a deal.tl;drgame good berecommend 10/10 would
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds you a bit of Outer Wilds while playing (highest possible praise). Some of the stealth stuff is a little clunky but I think it helps to think of those sections as just another type of puzzle. The language stuff is REALLY great and I'm hoping this is the kind of game a lot of other game devs are playing and taking inspiration from.Not a ton of optional/sidequest stuff but there are some cute/fun things to find as the game goes on, especially if you're headed toward completing the whole thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game. If you love this game, there is a nice chance you will find IOL questions interesting (though wayyy more challenging). However, I found some sections of the game that require quick reflexes quite annoying. It took me a lot of time to pass these sections, even with the help of walkthrough guides. It would be great if there is an option of skip those sections (e.g. replace them with animation), or have an easy mode available (e.g.  ). This would allow me to enjoy decoding the languages without interruption.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: If decoding fictional languages is your jam, then I think you'll have a really good time with Chants of Sennaar.PRO:- Decode not just one, but several fictional languages!- Languages are visually and grammatically distinct, and each one is internally consistent- Storytelling delivered by way of language design is a rad concept- Visual design is cool- Theme of building connections between people is coolCON:- So much walking- My god the walking- I could have gone for a bit more depth in the language stuff. More symbols, more puzzles. But that's just me.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are stunning and the game play kept me coming back to keep unraveling the story and the mysteries. I finished the game within a few days of purchase after about a dozen hours.As far as dislikes, this is the kind of game where if you don't notice a staircase/door/etc. you may get stuck walking around the world for ages trying to find what you missed. Because of this I did have to look up a guide a few times.I would recommend playing on PC rather than console as typing in the journal is a large component of the game. You can definitely get by without having a pen and paper out due to the journal automatically copying down anything you'll need to see later.The story line was satisfying and the ending unexpected! I'll certainly be recommending this game to my friends! Thank you to the Besties podcast for putting this on my radar!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I have always had a love of linguistics, so am naturally drawn to any game that allows me a chance to puzzle with languages. I will admit that I found myself quite stuck at the end of the game with a few of the puzzles, but in part I think that was me forgetting that each language also had it's own syntax for creating sentences. _childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Very challenging puzzle - there is alot of context clues that you have to look around for. It felt like a giant escape room where you had to go back and forth throughout all the escape rooms for hints and clues. I loved how it wasn't a puzzle where it was straightforward rather zig-zag and inter connected. I quite enjoyed binging this game for 3-4 days. An excellent game to use your braincells in.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game you finding how precious language is. When we are talking 2 different languages, can we  still understand each other? You probably have a time that you travel to other countries where speak different mother language as you do.  Plus, they may not speak English at all. You still can manage to convey them your message by a few easiest word "yes", "no", "thank you" or body language. Human are beautifully made with communication talents. So relaxing during my playtime.Definitely try to get to the true end. I love it so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this. The art is lovely, the gameplay is simple (I used a mouse but a controller might be a bit smoother for getting around quicker), and the story is compelling. I absolutely LOVE the languages aspect, would happily decipher many more - to be honest I was a bit disappointed when I finished deciphering everything, I was really getting into it. My only frustration is that I am geographically challenged in games just as much as I am in real life and I spent a looooot of time running around trying to find the places I had been and needed to revisit. If I play again I might try to find a map someone's put together or something, now that I won't need to worry about spoilers. _childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Really really fun and polished linguistic-themed puzzle game that made me binge play over 2 days until I completed all the achievements… The lore is beautiful and much darker than I expected, which as a result also made the heartwarming moments hit extremely hard. I loved the atmosphere, and the amazing level design in some places took me by surprise because I kind of went into this game thinking I’d mostly just be solving language puzzles. Finding some shortcuts within/across the five areas actually gave me a bit of the Dark Souls shortcut-opening joy. (They lowkey reminded me of the elevators in Undead Burg and Sen’s Fortress like yessss…) This game just went way over my expectations in so many different aspects. Please give Chants of Sennaar a play!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pure joy and a bit of a childlike wonder, at least it was for me. Intuitive and easy gameplay, better plays in company, when you all collectively are trying to guess the meaning of each symbol. Tbh I would gladly play something like that even more complicated, but it is quite fun as it is. Play Chants of Sennaar, you won't regret it! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Really good deduction-based puzzle games are few and far between, but Chants of Sennaar is one of the best exceptions. The language structures and vocabularies in the game are fairly simple, but this is in favor of a great feeling gameplay loop and helps to convey an enchanting narrative.Highly recommended for fans of mystery games like Outer wilds or Return of the Obra Dinn, and fans of other language deduction games like Heaven's Vault or Sethian, although this is more accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely lovely game with a great story and the language figuring out part is very intuitive and fun! Hoping there will be more games like this from the developer - I'm in awe.If you think about getting it, get it - you won't regret it. It's way longer than you'd expect and you get plenty of play time.It's smooth, fun and addictive. A perfect mix of thinking, action elements and gorgeous illustrations that make playing it such a joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that can basically be though of as an incredibly well done point and click adventure game where you're translating multiple languages to better understand the world, what's happening, and solve puzzles. Aside from a few quality of life changes I'll detail below, the overall atmosphere, music, and gameplay systems are integrated so smoothly together and I ended up finishing this game in two sittings. There's an amazing sense of exploration as you go through each environment, talking to people whom you at first don't understand. But as you steadily learn more of the language, it's exciting to go back to places you've been where you at first didn't understand some text or what people initially said. Overall it's a very tight and well made package where all of the game systems very naturally work together. The only things I would really like to see changed is how the words are organized in your journal. I wish there was some way to re-organize them to make some of the puzzles go by more smoothly. I spent a decent amount on some particular puzzles just searching for the right words by mousing over every single one. It may be a step too far but even a search function which could highlight the word I'm looking for would be very helpful.Additionally, some of the backtracking takes a little while, nothing obscene but there were some moments where I wish the game would hurry along either in terms of movement or some animations just taking a bit longer than I'd like. Lastly, a quality of life improvement I think would help the game overall, I would like if the game acknowledged your mouseclick with a little animation. There were some times I thought I clicked on something only for the character to stand still. All that said (and despite wanting to say more), I can heartily recommend this game especially if you're interested in something more atmospheric and want something a little cerebral.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful deductive puzzle game that scratches the same sort of itch as Obra Dinn and Outer Wilds (i.e. investigation/deduction games with cryptic information that leaves you to fill in the gaps yourself). It's full of lots of nice little details to give you information on the world and the people who live there without telling anything explicitly. For conlang enjoyers in particular there are probably quite a few features to enjoy regarding how the pictographs relate to each other and how their shapes relate to their meanings, but a lot of that went over my head.It was a good length for what I expected, too, taking me about 8 hours to complete the game and 100% achievements (my play time is a bit lower because I started by playing the demo, and save data carries over from the demo to the full game). I was slightly disappointed that the final language turns out to not be too much of a puzzle but on the other hand the game might have risked overstaying its welcome if you had to fully translate one more language right at the end.A strong recommend for anyone who enjoys deduction puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This game was promising but ultimately failed to deliver.The idea is that you're climbing the Tower of Babel, or something like it, learning each language as you go up. There are other puzzles and some timing/"stealth" bits but that's the main thing. The problem is simply that the game doesn't give you enough of a chance to do that, and doesn't give you enough to chew on when you are trying.You are periodically shown a journal page where you match glyphs to pictures depicting them. If you get everything right, the game confirms the meanings for you. In practice each time this happens you have probably been shown a mural or something making one or two glyphs' meanings obvious, will be able to narrow down the other one (e.g. you know it's a verb or a direction) and the last one can be solved by trying everything you haven't confirmed yet (which is generally not many). You additionally have help that a few key glyphs are somewhat pictographic, and a *lot* of scenes in the game where something is depicted or acted out and with a label or commentary. To be sure the game would be tedious and/or brutally challenging without a lot of what you might term "unrealistic" help, but all of this together means that the majority of the words can be guessed right the first time you see them or soon afterwards.There is only one language which makes any real attempt at getting you to work out a grammar different from that of English, and in general there is very little grammar that you need to work out and it's pretty obvious.When the game *does* let you stew a little and chew on some different grammar, you can see a unique and enjoyable challenge peeking through. But then you're on to the next language which is probably the worst of them all, because the lions share of the glyphs you have to work out are just numerals, and they're given to you almost straight away.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I came here from Aliens Rock. I was initially hooked by the unique puzzle-like mechanic but the music, art and atmosphere is what drew me into the whole world. It really makes you feel lost with how they stripped away the one thing that makes games easy to understand; language. Yet it also holds your hand and rewards you when you finally understand what each glyph means. I highly recommend this game for those who are trying out new and unique puzzles games and to those who especially love linguistic and logical puzzles as it challenges your understanding of syntax, grammar structure, and vocabulary.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful, interesting, fun game. To be fair, I could tell immediately from the screenshots and the description that I would love this game, and I did! I think all the success and good reviews are well deserved. Some of the stealth parts were a little annoying for me, but the game is very generous with checkpoints so I never really got frustrated. Other than that, everything was top notch. Sound design, world design, game design...Just a well polished game overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time reviewing a game, and probably the only time I will write a review. However i felt compelled to do so to convince others to play this game. I'm not a puzzle game person yet this game felt so rewarding. i have spent 20 hours of my life playing an incredibly beautiful and intrinsic game that constantly had me engaged. The journal system for translating languages was by far my favorite part. The steam page store doesn't do this game justice when i comes to the amount of content in the game. I've only done one playthrough at the time of this review and I have 20 hours. The soundtrack is also amazing. I love this game and I wish more people would play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little puzzle adventure game. Some of the puzzle solutions are kind of forced on you; I would have preferred if there was a little more nuance in how you deduced the solutions given the clues.Amazing art, acceptable sound, pretty good challenge and level flow. Could have used a map. Endings are a little meh, but still served to cap it all off.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Me not like puzzle/riddle. Me be not patient. Me like Sennaar. Me play hours plural. Me finish/complete Sennaar. Sennaar be pleasure/excitement.Jokes aside, this is an amazing game. I don't usually have the patience for puzzle games but I pretty much beat this one in a single sitting. Its concept is really well executed yet simple enough that the puzzles are never frustratingly hard or never reach any sort of moon logic that is often plaguing the genre. I always felt pretty overwhelmed when first accessing a new area, but through exploration, the pieces fell in place one by one and it was always a great feeling.On top of that, the presentation is top notch. The visual style is simple but colorful and there are some cool tracks in the OST.Even if you're not a fan of puzzle games, I'd still recommend you give this one a go. It's a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of self-contained puzzle games like OneShot, Chants of Sennaar is definitely for you. The way the game asks you to infer languages based off context is very fun and creative, but unfortunately this aspect does get a bit lost through the last 10% of the game. _childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little game. It strikes a great balance between being deep enough that solving the languages feels fulfilling but not so deep that it becomes a slog. The stealth sections can be very frustrating but thankfully there is no punishment for failing. A certain room in the fortress had me banging my head against the wall for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Chants of Sennaar

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Firstly, it's a beautiful game, the artistic style is just right for the game it is and is amazing to look at. Secondly I really enjoyed the unique puzzle game play it has to offer. There is something really neat about having to discover a language through context clues and actions of NPCs. It's so very human. I loved learning the language and then going back to find out what an NPC was trying to tell me before I figured out what they were saying. _childDocuments_.review: See, i never usually review games after i play them, i rarely fin that im fussed either way. But this game is a complete exception. I LOVED this game! _childDocuments_.review: I was very excited when I first saw this advertised on social media. I enjoyed the puzzle solving I had to do, as a linguistics nerd, I thoroughly enjoyed this game.
