_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal improvement over the first game. Keeps the same awesome combat system while adding a ton of quality of life improvements, making all the non-combat parts a lot more bearable. The dungeons are much less sprawling, and lots of fast travel points with a slimmed-down side quest system makes it all more enjoyable to play.Encounter design still feels like a missed effort; the combat mechanics are elegantly intricate, but the encounters really don't quite do it justice. More variety in generic enemies and more unique combats (and longer combats) to push the combat system more would have been amazing. Still, it's extremely fun despite the repetitive encounters.
_childDocuments_.name: The Caligula Effect 2

_childDocuments_.review: Way better than the first game. At first, I thought the combat going from 3 queued actions to 1 was going to overly simplify things, but attacks in this are more complex, with interesting triggered follow-ups. It keeps the move selections and timing as meaningful choices. Also, some character-specific "equipment" changes some abilities. These have been extremely useful, sometimes upgrading a move to have a complete followup attack, or even just adding an extra hit or two to the combo.The first time the game tempted me with an over-leveled enemy guarding treasure, I decided "why not?" and discovered that while any hit from something thrice my level was a one-shot, I could time things so I didn't get hit. Like somersaulting over the attacker after he'd already "locked on". Juggling the foe when I could, and not getting hit made it a very tense fight, but doable. Later on, I'm not able to do that as well, but that's because the foe +20 lv over my team summons 2 flunkies +16 lv over me, and that's just cheating, really. ;)The link system is way more usable now that locations are included. Although sometimes they're not... great, if you pay attention, you'll at least be wandering the correct map.The biggest upgrade over the previous title is probably the writing. Several characters are kind of adorkable, and the team tank is an absolute cinnamon roll of a human. And various foibles have positives and negatives. The first game was... not great in its handling of mental health & trauma. This game, the focus is much more on regrets, and you're not magically dealing with serious conditions through extremely questionable means. I mean, the first game, you "helped" someone with Munchausen Syndrome (fakes illness for sympathy) by showing them a possibly cursed book on method acting, so they'd fake it better? And/or actually making them honestly feel terrible? Eww. And worse, those quests were recycled. This game, I'm helping with errands, and often equipping specific traits to perform tasks. Like "Fair and Just" when I have to bear witness.About my only complaint is not knowing what impact the personality stats have on combat, only really important for the main character, as sidequests boost one aspect permanently.

_childDocuments_.review: good game 8/10 old school turn based rpgfun - music. 130ish side quests tracking. it has feeling like its trying to be persona game, but not as amazingbad - enemy variety, theres like handfull of enemies (5?) with handfull different variations of some of themugly - Wire.. it gives more depth to characters and even npc's. i just personally didnt like it and pretended it didnt exist

_childDocuments_.review: Big step up from Overdose -- which they make a lot of reference to during the game so while it's not recommended you play the fist one, you'd get a better picture, and I'm sure you'd enjoy this more if you did play the first game. Caligula's turn-based mechanics is something entirely new and refined from Overdose, and planning your moves right makes for a rewarding pay-out! The game is stylish, the characters are lovable right down to the NPCs and the music pops off. This game's a slow-burn and it's meant to be played with care and love.
_childDocuments_.name: The Caligula Effect 2

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you are patient and like JRPG. The story and characters get more interesting progressively.Good game, extremely good on the aspect of character illustration and music just like its predecessor.Quality of the latter half of the game vastly surpass the initial half with build coming in place and power spikes for characters kicking into play. Combat feels a lot more satisfying than early game dull hit and guard. Map design is slightly improved compare to Overdose however still vastly lacking in depth and running the map can be annoying. Some side quest are interesting but all are chore like nuisance, very painful to complete sometimes. But there are moments in this game that would strike your heart, for a anime JRPG it gets obnoxiously realistic in some part. The regret and demons we have to face in real life, the mask and facade we try to wear are teared into pieces with parts of the game. And that has the feeling of the old shin megami tensei.
_childDocuments_.name: The Caligula Effect 2

_childDocuments_.review: A big step up from the first game for sure.Most mechanics are the same, just refined and extended. The combat is pretty unique and I like the facts that if you plan your moves carefully, you'll never take any damage, help make you feel like your strategy matter. Although at times it might feel like the combat is taking forever and may bore you out when you have to do it many times for the grind.And then there's the music, top tier drug, similar to the first game. Stuff's so banger I got tired from just humming to the song rather than playing the game.The only gripe I had is probably the 3D model and animation, kinda stiff and not looking that good but doesn't bother me much.Buy it but don't expect a masterpiece or something, pretty decent game for the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review:
Dive into a reality-warping adventure from Persona scenario-writer Tadashi Satomi and director Takuya Yamanaka!

A virtuadoll named Regret has created the world of Redo in order to save people from their past regrets by unknowingly imprisoning them in a simulation. However, this "Paradise" is shaken to the core when a virtual idol named X breaks into Regret's virtual reality and restores a high school student's memories of the real world. In order to escape Redo, they form the Go-Home Club, a resistance group that seeks to fight against regret and her enforcers, the Obbligato Musicians.

name: Age of Mythology: Retold
detailed_description: Edition Comparison About the Game From the creators of the award-winning Age of Empires franchise, Age of Mythology: Retold goes beyond history to a mythical age where gods, monsters, and humans collide. Combining the best elements of the beloved Age of Mythology with modern real-time strategy design and visuals, Retold is an epic and innovative experience for old and new players alike. Secure your domain, command legendary monsters, and call upon the power of the gods to crush your enemies. Will you become Mythic? Call Upon the Gods Choose your gods from the Greek, Norse, Egyptian, and Atlantean pantheons. Devastate your enemies by summoning powerful lightning storms, earth-shattering quakes, and even the famed Nidhogg dragon. Or call upon nourishing rains and protective Dryads to help your people grow & prosper. Unleash the Monsters Unleash Centaurs, Trolls, Mummies, and more. From bejeweled crocodiles who harness the power of the sun to the mighty one-eyed Cyclops, you will command diverse units inspired by the world’s great mythologies. An Epic Mythological Universe Embark on multiple campaigns spanning 50-missions that take you across a vast, mythical world: besiege the mighty walls of Troy, battle Giants in the frozen wastes of Midgard, and discover the mysteries of Osiris in the shifting sands of Egypt. Become a hero of myth—or even a god. Better with Friends Play with your friends, either head-to-head or against the advanced AI on dozens of randomly generated maps and scenarios for limitless re-playability. * *Exclusive Premium benefits of 7 days Advanced Access and New Gods Pack available with Premium Edition and Premium Upgrade. New Gods Pack is a timed exclusive; may be available with future offers. Purchase the Premium Edition or the Premium Upgrade by August 27, 2024, for 7-days advanced access. Expansions 1 and 2 are available as released. Limitless Adventure, Solo or with Friends   Experience Age of Mythology: Retold like never before. In the main game, go head-to-head with friends or challenge the advanced AI across countless, randomly generated maps for endless strategic battles.  For a fresh twist, step into Arena of the Gods —an all-new mode where you take on the role of a legendary hero, facing 35 mythic skirmishes filled with divine challenges. Play solo or join forces in co-op*, battling through epic trials and exploring a whole new way to enjoy the mythological universe. Whether forging alliances or battling alone, each journey is uniquely thrilling and endlessly replayable.    New game mode:  Arena of the Gods   The gods are watching—embrace your destiny in the Arena of the Gods, a new Free Update* game mode now available in Age of Mythology: Retold ! Take on the role of a legendary hero and battle through 35 epic skirmishes, each filled with divine challenges. From the frozen Tundra to the heights of Mount Olympus, face world-changing twists and unlock godly blessings as you fight solo or with friends**.  *Requires Age of Mythology: Retold or Xbox Game Pass membership (Ultimate and PC only)  **Online console multiplayer requires Game Pass Ultimate or Core, sold separately.  Age of Mythology: Retold Premium Edition  Embark on a gaming journey of first-class offerings with the Age of Mythology: Retold Premium Edition.  Curated to offer an elevated gaming experience at launch and beyond.   The Premium Edition includes the full game, up to 7-day advanced access, New Gods Pack: “Freyr”, Legacy Deity Portrait Pack, Expansion 1 (all-new Chinese pantheon expansion) and Expansion 2 (additional new pantheon). *  Standard Game :  the complete Age of Mythology: Retold experience   Up to 7-day Advanced Access : Step into the divine realm before time itself with exclusive early unlock to the game available on Xbox, Steam and PC. *  New Gods Pack: “Freyr”:   Age of Mythology: Retold Premium Edition adds Freyr to the Norse pantheon.  Unleash the power of the Norse god of prosperity and fertility with the Freyr God Pack.  The blessings of Freyr will elevate your reign to unprecedented heights. Legacy Deity Portrait Pack : a nostalgic journey back to the origins of gaming greatness.  Relive the glory days of gaming with this special pack, which offers players the option to use iconic deity portraits from the classic game that captivated audiences worldwide.   (2) Upcoming Expansions : Prepare to embark on new epic sagas yet untold with two yet to be revealed and highly anticipated upcoming expansions. *  Expansion 1 :  All-New Chinese pantheon expansion Expansion 2 :  additional new pantheon expansion

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Empires cranked up to 11. If you like RTS, you will most likely enjoy this.The updated graphics bring the game to modern standards and the updated campaigns and gameplay flow very well. The developers already released a major update focusing on multiplayer improvements and campaign rebalancing and I am more than excited to see what is in store for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Units are responsive, graphics are fresh, and the balancing changes make for a unique experience. Main feedback in the beta was voice acting and artwork. The devs were able to muster up their forces and address both of those issues in full. There are a handful of issues with how the lobby browser works, matches crashing, and pathfinding - but those are in the works to be fixed. With new DLC on the horizon, for single and multiplayer alike this is well worth it's salt for old & new fans of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original, this game is very worth it (at least with 20% discount).Overall 9/10 quite good and a nice tribute to the original with enough differences to make it feel new, although I have a few complaints there have been some relevant updates and patches which for the most part have resolved all my complaints. The campaign Titan difficulty is a little harder than the original.BUT the music, the original voice actors and the saying by the units are extremely comforting. Thank you devs for bringing this back and with mod support.FYIEdited: Removed complaints after they were patched :D

_childDocuments_.review: Yep - If it was just nostalgia I wouldnt have as many hoursthis one looks better and has more effort put into it than the other remake of AOM (difficulty spikes up for a few random missions, and some loss of control with mission pop ups were the only annoying things)After Launch  - Arena of the gods mode (Free) is a little disappointing just beacasue it feels a little low effort, Kastor and Other Kastor for your co op partner and just seeing all the effects and buffs for each missions makes me want a more Rougelike or rougelite sort of mode with more heroes to choose from and like multiple stacking map effects . just makes me want more from the game mode.

_childDocuments_.review: I debated how I wanted to recommend this and kinda wish Steam had a neutral option, because I have mixed feelings about this. On the one hand, the game is a huge step forward in a lot of gameplay aspects from the original, new graphics, but also more refined gameplay. Being able to reuse god powers for favor, great; showing campaign objectives, great. But on the other hand, there are elements of the game that worry me long term in thinking that the studio is going to try to milk as much money as possible, $6 for the legacy portraits, really? A deity locked behind premium, gross. And there a sign of laziness too, instead of implementing a proper anti-cheat for multiplayer, the game will close itself if it detects a memory scanning program. And it doesn’t pop up a message saying X program caused it to close, so it can be hard to track down what program is causing it. And it does this for single player or campaign maps. If I want to cheat in a single player game, I should be able to. It's for those reasons I wouldn’t recommend the game right now, if you have the extended edition I’d recommend that version and wait a few months to see if they back off some of these aspects or if they double down.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite RTS games of all time. It is a massive upgrade to its older counterpart. You can play as Greeks, Egyptians, Norse, or Atlanteans so far since this games release. All of which have different ways to gain resource, differing trained units and mythological units. You can also build a gateway for titans which are massive mythological units. Your goal is to age up through resource, outwit, and outplay your enemy. Taking down their armies and buildings to either have them forfeit or make them. From the older game to this game I just really love everything about it! If you are a fan of RTS games or want to get your friends to play them, this is a great game to get started in RTS type of gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: I have so far only played all the available singleplayer missions, and played twice on ranked multiplayer, so I will only refer to singleplayer. I Lovethisgame! I have played the original year ago and it made me fall in love with Mythology as a whole till this very day. I tried my best to remain without bias as much as possible as I played. That was easy however, as the Retold version is an improvement through and through. This game was great a decade ago, Retold is only better! The god powers, the designs of the monsters, the new techs, the updated uproach to sea creatures. the visuals overall, the music, the designs of the maps in the missions. All of these are improved verions of what already was very good product. I can only honestly give one significant criticism, which in all fairness is a matter of taste, and I would be interested in an opinion of someone who has not played the original. I CAN'T STAND the voice acting. 85% of the characters are voiced sub par. The exception being Arkantos (thank you devs for listening to the audience at least that much) and maybe the Norse characters. Amanra holds her own for most of her apearance, but in the end her voiceacting seems lazy. Everyone else... abismal. Villans who used to be scary murderous monsters are now comic book villans that are only missing a top had and a mustache to twirl while they speak. Ajax, Agamemnon, Kastor (young and old) are simply unbearable. That can be easily fixed with a mod though.However annoying the voiceacting was, it mas but a tiny blemish on the entire experience, easily ommited and forgiven nearly instantly. This is a 10/10 example of how to do a Definitive Edition. Masterpiece.Cant wait for the DLC's :D Well Done To EVERYONE InvolvedI love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: People are not ready for how absolutly disgusting the AI is.If you like to play against the AI or play the campaign, get ready for some of the most absurd maphack you've ever seen. That and modified missions that have never been tested, not even once (hello mission 18, speaking of which why are the mummies and enemies allied now?).Want to play skirmish against the AI? Enjoy seeing them send armies at each other and never defend their bases. That's especially true in team games, where they don't care about their allies at all. It really feels like this AI is from 20 years ago.If you want to play against humans, I guess the game's fine, but these flaws are unacceptable for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: As promised, I am changing my review ! The developers DID in fact change the AI, and it is now FAR more manageable.Now, we have enemies that... play the game normally ! Do not all team up against the human ! I've had games where, out of the blue, computers quit because other computers destroyed them !However, they are STILL quite bloody broken when it comes to island maps. They still do not understand the concept of expansion. They drain their local resources dry and starve, unable to comprehend that more is out there. _childDocuments_.review: If you loved the original game, this builds on it in every single way, plus every god power you hoarded back in the day to use at "just the right time" can now be used infinitely, balanced with increasingly higher favor costs!Below is my review of "Age of Mythology: Extended" from 2015:While their previous titles, Age of Empires I and II, focused on history, Ensemble Studios opted to create a fantastical setting where three factions, the Norse, Ancient Egyptians, and Ancient Greeks collided. Player factions were further divided into three major deities, such as Zeus, Poseidon, and Hades for Greece. Following the footsteps of Starcraft, the three factions were asymmetrical in their playstyles, with the Norse favoring aggressive strategies, the Egyptians favoring late-game power, and the Greeks being middle-of-the-road. Technology paths were further divided by players choosing between two sub-deities at each level of the tech tree. Players could still train historical units like hoplites and pharaohs, but these would be alongside such mythical beasts as chimeras and valkyries. They could even evoke "God powers," with some bringing economic or combat support advantages, while others such as meteor strikes or earthquakes functioning as the game's version of the superweapons of RTS titles from the Command and Conquer series.Like many classic RTS titles, Age of Mythology features multiplayer and singleplayer skirmish modes with various rules as well as a full campaign, which follows the saga of the Atlantean hero, Arkantos. The campaign is actually quite good for an RTS, serving as both tutorial for players as well as providing a classic story of good vs evil, with many familiar figures from all three mythologies along the way. Multiplayer can be done vs other players or even AIs. The Extended Edition also includes content from the original game's Titans expansion, including a 4th faction, the Atlanteans, as well as the campaign. Most importantly a new mechanic, the Titans was introduced for all 4 factions, essentially each faction to construct a super-unit (the eponymous titan) capable of massive destruction.Age of Mythology first came about in the early aughts, alongside such RTS classics as Warcraft III (yes, Warcraft was not always a MMORPG!) and and Rise of Nations. While many later RTS titles would opt for "real-time tactics" gameplay as pioneered by the likes of Relic Entertainment's Dawn of War and Company of Heroes titles and Eugen Studios' "Wargame" series, Age of Mythology stands as a reminder of the classic RTS formula of "harvest / build / destroy."

_childDocuments_.review: I've almost played 100 hours since the pre-order early release.This won't be a review of Age of Mythology as a game, rather a review of the remaster in terms of what they did right and wrong in contrast to the extended edition.This is a great remaster as a whole, and much of the game's mechanics have improved significantly. I find the combat and researchable technologies/gods to be more balanced, even on higher difficulties. The graphics are much improved, yet the art-style remains faithful to the original; at times it's so faithful that I'm forgetting I'm playing a remaster. The changes in mechanics, such as including more Norse military and building, to using oracles to gain favour for the Atlantians are welcome additions that improve the gameplay. The soundtrack largely sounds the same with minor adjustments. The ability to use god power multiple times is amazing and allows for more use of various strategies. For example, I often wouldn't pick Osiris as a minor god for the mythic age because the son of osiris blessing could only be used once, but now I can make a small army of them and decimate my opponent, Performance is good too; had no issues. I also really liked the new UI. Pleasing to the eye, retains the original look and much easier to use and navigate. The god pack, freyr is really good, although might need some re-balancing as it's kinda OP right now. There are some issues however:CAMPAIGN ISSUES- They fixed Arkantos' voice acting, but the rest is pretty bad. I ended up using a mod to return the voice acting to the extended edition's. Amanra sounds awful and doesn't sound imposing and bad ass. Athena doesn't sound etherial and godly. Gargarensis sounds too broody and edgy. Not good.- Titan difficulty on some maps are almost impossible (All is not Lost, The Dwarven Forge and A long way from home are the worst). They need to be re-balanced. The AI should not have infinite resources and be able to spam endless armies in the space of seconds to minutes. Not fun and tedious. - Some of the maps feel smaller than before, but I don't know if this is true or not.- Due to being able to reuse god powers, some missions can be cheesed and need to be rebalanced to take into account the use of multiple god powers. Aside from all that, the campaign is great and still remains the best RTS campaign.MULTIPLAYER:- Unable to host or join games if you already played a multiplayer map. It will just say the lobby us full or the match has already started, or no one will join your hosted game. To fix this, exiting the game and reloading works, but this is not good as it has to be done every time you play a single match. I'm also getting sync issues on matches with more than 4 players.- Better filters, and an additional filter to filter out newer players (inexperienced) to experienced players, as I joined many matches where the other player didn't even know how to train a villager.OTHER:- There are two bugs; one where characters get stuck on terrain or buildings and have to be deleted. The other is where units get pushed by other units when they're traversing. - The artwork for the god portraits is much improved from the Beta artwork, however I still think that some of them could look better and some of they still look AI generated. I also don't like some of the art style choices made for the titans (Cerberus, norse titan, gaia, kronus), they look something out of league of legends or fortnight.Overall, excellent remaster, working properly (aside from MP) on day one and worth the price. Had a lot of fun and will continue to keep player. I'm very keen to see what they do with the other civs they're planning to bring. I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve ever wanted to command mythological beasts while laughing at the absurdity of your decisions, Age of Mythology: Retold is the game for you. It’s a polished return to the chaotic battlefield where gods casually grant miracles while you’re panicking because your villagers are chopping the wrong trees.The remastered visuals? Chef’s kiss. Watching a colossus casually yeet enemy buildings while my tiny human army flees in terror never gets old. It’s like they told the graphics team, “Make it majestic but slightly unhinged,” and they nailed it.The gameplay? Nostalgic perfection with just enough updates to remind you that you’ve matured (even if your strategies haven’t). The campaign is as dramatic as ever, with heroes so brave they don’t even question why they’re fighting alongside giant snakes and laser-shooting statues.But let’s talk multiplayer: nothing bonds (or destroys) friendships like summoning a literal meteor shower on someone’s carefully crafted town center. It’s peak betrayal, but with mythological flair. Your friend might hate you for a week, but hey, Zeus made you do it.And the gods? Each one feels like they’re personally invested in your success. Sometimes too much. Ever had a deity so generous you forgot to build an army because you were too busy summoning animals? Just me? Okay.In short, Age of Mythology: Retold is everything you loved about the original, with a dash of modern spice and a sprinkle of chaos. Play it for the nostalgia, stay for the epic laughs, and remember: when in doubt, spam myth units and blame the gods. They can’t be mad... right?

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology Retold is a refreshed version of the classic real-time strategy game Age of Mythology, originally released in 2002. This remastered edition aims to bring the beloved title into the modern gaming era with enhanced visuals, quality-of-life improvements, and additional features.Here are some key points from the review:Visuals and Audio: The game benefits from a significant graphical overhaul. The updated visuals are crisp and detailed, making the ancient mythological settings and units look more vibrant and immersive. The audio has also been enhanced, with improved sound effects and a refined soundtrack that helps to evoke the epic feel of mythological warfare.Gameplay: The core gameplay remains faithful to the original, which is a good thing for fans of the classic. The game retains its strategic depth, where players must manage resources, build armies, and harness divine powers to conquer opponents. The remaster introduces modern quality-of-life improvements such as better pathfinding, improved user interface, and more intuitive controls, which help to streamline the experience.New Features: Age of Mythology Retold includes additional content that wasn’t present in the original. This includes new campaigns, units, and gods, which add to the game's replayability. There are also updated multiplayer features that enhance the competitive aspect, making it easier to find and play with others online.Nostalgia Factor: For long-time fans of the original game, the Retold version offers a nostalgic trip with a fresh coat of paint. It successfully preserves the charm and strategic elements that made the original so beloved while addressing some of its older limitations.Potential Downsides: Some players might find that the game’s balance and mechanics feel outdated compared to modern RTS standards. Additionally, while the remaster updates the visuals and interface, it might not completely overhaul some of the more dated aspects of gameplay.Overall: Age of Mythology Retold is a solid remaster that caters to both nostalgic fans and new players interested in classic RTS games. Its updated graphics and additional content make it a worthwhile investment, though those looking for revolutionary changes might be a bit disappointed. It’s a respectful nod to a classic, with enough modern touches to keep it relevant.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game for almost 52 hours, 99% of this time was spent on the Campaign. Didn't play skirmish, customs or multiplayer. Finished all the campaigns on Titan difficulty. Devs did a great job, and didn't screw anything major up in this remaster.  - Does not have any major changes to the gameplay, except some improvements that should have been there in the base game i.e reusable god powers, manual usage of myth units' abilities, etc. - Visuals look great. Modern features like build queues are also very welcome, things like age up queues, free worker indicator/hotkey, etc. - The Soundtrack is a remix of the old one, and at first I wasn't sold on it, but it isn't bad and grows on you over time. I am sure you could also mod the original soundtrack or just play it in the browser if you don't like it. - If you loved the original, you will love this. It will remind you of the good ol' days when you came home from School, booted up the PC and Prostagma'd your way to victory. - The moment I heard Athena's voice in the campaign, I instantly disliked it. It just felt wrong. She sounds like she's going to make you a gyro, throw and break a plate and shout "MALAKA!". This isn't Assassins Creed: Odyssey, we don't need geographical authenticity in the voice actors and their accents, it's a game about MYTHOLOGY. The original voices were MUCH better, because you know, VOICE ACTING. As I kept playing the campaign, everyone except Arkantos sounded wrong. But the moment I heard Amanra's voice, I instantly quit out of the campaign, went into the mod section and downloaded the original voiceovers mod. WHOEVER MADE THAT MOD, YOU ARE A GOD SEND. - No achievements for completing the campaign on the hardest difficulty. Actually, very few campaign achievements. It feels like they wanted to do more but it got cut. There are achievements for doing something specific in the first 2 starting missions and for completing each campaign (and each civ in the main campaign). So yeah, nothing like "Complete this in 8 minutes" or "Collect all the relics" or "Make only X combat unit". - (All of this is on Titan difficulty) Some missions are very easy, some are ultra hard with no rhyme or reason as to why. In most RTS games, the difficulty scales with each mission as you are learning the mechanics. Some missions you complete them in 7 minutes, some missions are slog fests because the AI is too strong. Feels weird. - Keybinds: Basic RTS hotkeys are missing by default. Things like S to stop and A to attack move. Norse feels particularly weird as the hotkeys are dedicated to "slots" in the UI, so if you do change hotkeys of Stop and Attach Move to S and A, you will lose hotkeys for 2 buildings in the UI. It should be that buildings are behind a button press (a la any RTS worth their salt). However, props to the devs for adding keybind customization. UI: I had to go into a skirmish game and spend 20-30 mins to remove UI clutter and customize the UI to get it as close as possible to the original one. Still possible, but sucks you have to do it. Console Friendliness: Look, I get the Publisher is Xbox, but you don't need to shoehorn in console controls. Console peasants don't play RTS games. It's a waste of effort. Ask those plebs to buy a Keyboard and a Mouse and join the PC Master Race if they want to play RTS games so much. - Freyrs God Pack seems... I don't know what's the right word, greedy perhaps? You're selling a Major god with 3 minor gods, 3 myth units and 4 god powers that NO ONE ELSE HAS ACCESS TO. Like, explain to me how is this not pay to win? There are exclusive units, powers and tech that people pay real money for, and by default, anything new would be at least, slightly overpowered. So if you pay money you can now win more games? Until they nerf the god, but even then, it's not a level playing field. Also there's 0 singleplayer content with this God Pack.Overall, I enjoyed playing the game and it was money well spent, especially since I bought a pirated copy of the game in my youth. And now, will try my hand at some multiplayer games maybe. But so far, loved it. Ensemble Studios made an amazing game, one of the pillars of RTS games. I salute the devs who did a good remaster of an amazing game. The most variety in terms of difficulty. Most missions were extremely hard due to the AI sending large attack waves constantly. However, pro tip, AI does NOT REBUILD unit producing structures. Burst down barracks, temples and forts and attack waves stop. Campaign heroes are very strong, they can solo non-build missions. Mixed bag of difficulty, but less so than the Greeks. Barrack units suck, so your main job is to get to Citadel and spam Elephants. Screw Camels, just spam Elephants. With the right god, you can spawn 2 elephants for the price of 1. Get some ranged damage in Laser Crocs or a few Chariot Archers or if you're lucky, a Son of Osiris. Kind of an easy campaign, few missions were difficulty. THE LAST NORSE mission where you have to hold out was extremely hard, I had to abuse the campaign mechanics to get an extra 10 mins of setup time. The Thor Hammer was too hard as well, but luckily the AI sends 1 piece of the hammer to an undefended place if you just give it to them. VERY EASY CAMPAIGN, only 1 mission gave me trouble where you had only 1 temple of Kronos in Egypt. I first tried the last mission with army and just kited the titan to buy precious minutes then Gaia slapped him 5 times and he went down. Very Easy, 1 mission was kind of difficult but nothing like what I experienced in Greek or Egyptian or Norse campaigns.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game when i was a child and had a ton of fun playing the campaigns and skirmishes vs the AI. When i recently got the extended edition, i was disappointed at how the game felt. it felt really different from what i remembered and i didn't play EE that much. When I got to play in the open playtest, that did it for me! it felt like my nostalgia-infused memories of the original and its qol improvements make this remake feel like a perfect balance between the nostalgia for the old one and a fresh game for the 2020s.I'm also really happy about the camera zoom level. This may seem inconsequential to many, but the camera zoom range was very important to me. I couldn't get myself to enjoy AoE4 because of how weird the super zoomed-in camera made me feel, so it was a big relief to know that retold would let us zoom out a reasonable amount.I've played for over 100 hours already, and it doesn't get old. The multiplayer experience is reasonably good. There are still a few bugs that need to be addressed, but they don't make multiplayer unplayable by any means. The single player experience is ok. It could be better. The AI is very easy to beat in titan difficulty, but extreme and legendary feel very unbalanced. I recently learned those difficulties use the same AI as the titan difficulty, but it also essentially cheats, so that makes for a kind of wonky experience. If they improved the AI in a way that it played with the same rules but managed better strategies and provided a better challenge without needing to cheat, that would be perfect. I believe the AoE2 AI doesn't cheat and it provides a reasonable challenge at the higher difficulties, so doing that for retold should be possible, and i think necessary to make the single player experience better than "ok".The campaigns are really fun to play, the changes from the original are welcome, but it's too bad there are only 3 official campaigns right now. I would love to see two or three more campaigns, focusing on each pantheon/civ/culture and being as long as the fall of the trident.The visual aspect of the game is great, it's a 10/10 for me, it looks absolutely beautiful and isn't too demanding.God powers and myth units are still as silly and fun as they were in the original.Not much more i can say! If you played the original or the extended edition and enjoyed it, retold will provide you with hundreds of hours of fun. Overall I give this game an 8.5/10. docking a few points for the AI in single player(to note, this is the only game that i've found compelling enough to write a review about. it beat my expectations!)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: JUST BUY ITAbout 20 hours in, I can confidently say AOM Retold is a resounding victory. Fun, engrossing, and faithful to the original.Earnest Yuen, the Director of Production at World's Edge, said in various interviews that the team was aiming to "build the game [that is] in your head", i.e. the perfect version of AOM that we remember nostalgically in our minds. They have unreservedly succeeded in doing so.As a casual gamer who grew up with AOM and probably has > 2000 hours of AOM under the belt (900 hours on Extended Edition, plus countless hours on vanilla AOM and Titans, plus countless hours watching AOM on YouTube e.g. BoIT's channel), Retold is the modern version of this game that I love so much.There are minor issues, mainly that the voice acting in the Campaign doesn't have the soul and heft of the original. Athena's voice is no longer believable as a God, and the voices of some supporting characters also miss the mark a little. However, these minor points do not in any way detract from what is a beautiful and fun remake of an amazing game.Score: 12/10 (bonus points for listening to Beta community feedback: redoing God portraits and re-recording Arkantos' voice)

_childDocuments_.review: I've never thought this day would ever come. Age of Mythology, likely my most favorite game got remastered. The visuals can be noticed immediately. The game is truly gorgeous, offering a saturated palette of colours. The buildings and characters have their models completely redesigned, and the overall atmosphere is enhanced by a new soundtrack with instruments typical of the cultures you are currently playing. But there are many more changes than just the audiovisual. The game is smooth, it doesn't lag even with a large number of units on the battlefield, and I personally haven't encountered any bugs so far. Very interesting is the addition of the fifth age, which allows you to build a wonder and create titans. Among other minor changes, the population cap increase is awesome, making battles more epic. Another welcome change is definitely the removal of the favor limit. God powers can now be used again, for some favor, and that is a game changer. The Atlanteans, who are otherwise included in the expansion of the original game only, are a great plus as well. Another bonus is mod support and the map editor. The only downside of the game is the harvesting priority system, which should automatically manage villagers according to a preset ratio that can player choose. Unfortunately, villagers are often sent through the enemy territory to die, although they could've safely harvested much closer. And gaining favor isn't in this system at all. In the end, I was redistributing villagers on my own anyway, just like in the original game. This mechanics definitely deserves to get an upgrade. Overall, the game is absolutely great, whether you're a new player or a seasoned veteran, you definitely won't be disappointed. Zeus approves!

_childDocuments_.review: My family and I play this game, and have since I was a kid. The old game was great, lots of things to be desired though. Water walking titans, titan buffs perhaps, graphics upgrades obviously, god changes such as some not making any sense (Athenian wall going to... wait for it... Hera?). This game met all of those expectations flawlessly. Anything I ever wanted in the OG game was made better with this. Re-usable god powers, wonders being actually useful, you name it if you played the old game.However... I still do not recommend this game. I can no longer play a normal multiplayer game with more than 6 players, including AI (untested for anything less). The game goes out of sync within at least moments before building my Wonder (So relatively end game). This was normal until their latest patch which made their out of sync errors unrecoverable. I can no longer reload the save and continue playing, and this game has been out for over a month. I used to be okay with the errors, but bug fixing has seemingly gone from bad to worse.This game is owned by Microsoft. I will never, ever buy that Freyr DLC (Because its very small) for more than $5, because that's how much effort they really have put into the rest of the game. There is no need for the game to be this buggy, this late in the development stage. Do not play this until at least next summer, when the developers have finally put enough effort to fix the game. Until then, this game seems like a cash grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Good. Not great:I'm overall pleased with this remaster, but I do have some gripes with it. First the positives:The gameplay changes are overall well thought out. I like the idea of decoupling aquatic myth units from the god selection, being able to recast god powers for a substantial favor cost as well as removing the favor cap is a decent way of doing things in theory, even if this seems like it would be problematic for the Egyptian faction in particular (due to the 5 monument limit). I like the replacement of Hathor with Sobek (justice for Petsobek!). Overall the game design aspects definitely feel like they were done with care and precision. I don't entirely know how I feel about the creature rebalances, overall they seem good but the ability to manually trigger abilities may lead to competitive becoming a micro game, something I'm generally opposed to. But that's a preference thing. I generally like the new abilities, with the notable exception of the centaur's arrow rain looking and feeling kinda dumb.However:First, the campaign clearly was not rebalanced or rethought with the changes in mind. Hero Cheirobalistae completely trivialize the New Atlantis campaign, the opponents don't seem to realize you can build siege ships in classical age now, and they don't seem to reuse their god powers ever. Secondly, the voice over was changed. This one might be a "they changed it so I hate it", but while I can sorta forgive the new speech patterns, what I cannot forgive is the voice direction. Where are the voice effects that made Athena seem divine? Why do the voices seem so flat? And on that note, if you're going to have everyone re-record their voices, maybe rewrite the script? It's good that you dug up some unused voice lines to explain things in the Egypt portion, but doing that and not giving more context to the Super Greek Bros randomly splitting up in mission 9 just feels weird. Or retrigger it for that matter. "The greeks seek to disrupt our trade" my dude I'm a petrobolos shot away from the final objective. And finally: OH GOD THE PATHFINDING. It's so bad. The units obstruct each other so much, they crowd each other out on maximum range, they get stuck trying to get in melee, it's just bad. Please for the love of Thor fix this. TL;DR: Gameplay design good. Campaign worse but okay. Pathfinding atrocious.

_childDocuments_.review: There are three things to remember when playing the Norse.Instead of building granaries or storehouses, the Norse bring their resources to mobile drop sites known as Ox Carts. Ox Carts can be trained out of the Town Center, and ordered to move almost anywhere on the map.Another difference for the Norse is how they gain Favor.Instead of praying to their Gods, the Norse gain favor through battle. They simply fight, to please their Gods.Whenever a Norse soldier is fighting anything in the game, your Favor will increase.The final difference is that all Norse buildings are constructed or repaired by infantry units. Norse Gatherers can only build farms and collect resources.Any Norse infantry unit can build or repair buildings.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR as a causal player and huge fan of the original Age of Mythology, this is an overall great remake/remaster with lots of QoL changes and pretty graphics.Here are some various observations from my playing of the campaign and a few skirmish matches vs computersGameplayPositives-Being able to reuse god powers for a frick ton of favor allows for more variety of plays-Being able to see attack speed as well as exact numbers for damage multipliers is very nice-Upgrades are so much clearer on what they do, nothing says a generic “more resistant to blah”, it tells you “Reduces damage from hack attack by -15%”-The addition of more healing upgrades feel helpful, even though in reality its not super useful, but it's nice that they’re there.-Building a wonder has a purpose beyond winning supremacy games. I really like the powerful buffs it gives you for going to the now far higher effort to build a wonder-Lots of QoL changes like auto-making villagers at the start of the game, hotkeys everywhere, and more houses for more population-Switched from needing a market to advance to the mythic age to needing a hill fort/stronghold/fortress/palace, I think this is a good change because it always felt like you had to go out of your way to build a market in the original, but everyone should be building a fortress-You can finally set computers to be different difficulties wahoo. Also there’s even harder difficulties in chance you feel like going psycho-Maps show you a sample layout instead of a weird picture that tells you nothing about the map geometryNegatives-The units AI is as dumb as ever, they get distracted attacking the most random things and archers tend to stand behind and do nothing because the fight moved a micrometer forward (on defensive stance)-Aggressive stance units get distracted attacking a stupid wall or house instead of moving forward or attacking the enemy right in front of them-Sometimes all units aren’t correctly selected-Poison lasts too long and could be used for annoying micro-There are some funky special skills/upgrades, like why on earth would I want a (forced) free dwarf everytime I buy an armory upgrade because I picked Thor? Or there’s a lot of may summon a blank when fighting near thing or on death. It adds a luck factor that has no reason to be there.Neutrals-Being able to purposefully use a special unit’s ability is something? I’m sure there’s some cases where it could be useful, but I’m doubtful it’ll get much use-A lot of upgrades have been slightly changed from what they used to be-Units now get shoved out of the way, makes sense since that was frequently a problem in the original. I wish it didn’t look so floaty and weird though-Myth units are WAY stronger now, you might have to actually try and gather favor now-Multi use (Atlantean) god powers are nerfed because you only get one use before you have to start paying favor for them, even though in the original you always got multiple uses-That new Norse major god Freyr certainly exists, feels OP and weird that they get 3 personal minor gods that no one else gets-Titans can swim nowVisuals/AudioPositives-I like the character portraits in the campaign mode, it helps you get attached to them-Water looks great, especially with the discrepancy between crashing waves and calmer waters in bays and lakes.-Most units look nice with all of their added details-UI has a lot of added touches that change depending on which civilization you are, original had some, but here it's more obvious and cooler-Most of the audio is the original audio, which is of course very nostalgic and coolNegatives-Some artwork seems unfinished or just looks bad, a lot of units have the face part of the picture fully rendered, but the rest of the body looks bad. The small square image has a bad cartoon-ish style that doesn’t lend itself well to making units look cool-The animations in this game are very safe I would say. The original wouldn’t be afraid to have fast, sharp movements that could occasionally look dumb, most felt real and impactful. (Hydras attack used to whip its head to attack, now it just moves down at a “reasonable” speed)-Winged creatures have fallen into the trap of having “jelly wings” that don’t account for bones and joints in the wings. This leads to all flying creatures feeling float-y. Original had low poly count and therefore had wing bones, which made their flight cycles more realistic.-Some myth units and titans fall into the trap of having too much detail and too many things going on. Simple doesn’t mean bad.-The “remastered” old god portraits were clearly not done by an experienced artist. They often ruin the artistic intent of the original and just look plain bad.-Some sound effects definitely need to be reworked to be way quieter or removed. Picking up a relic sounds game changing and the enemy advancing to the next age sounds like you just lost the gameNeutrals-The changed voice acting is a mixed bag, mostly bad though. The actors speak with a lot less feeling, it may have been a bit excessive in the original, but it made everyone's intentions very clear. Its nice that they switched some sounds from stock sound to...probably more stock sounds but I can hope they're original-Kastor from the Atlantean campaign is somehow MORE punchable than the original-The lore description of many units has been shortened significantly, especially myth units. Sometimes this lore is just straight up wrong, but it's mostly correct. I miss the weird run on sentences and long paragraphs from the original.-The units icons are sometimes good, usually weird looking. It's an odd style choice, it doesn’t know whether or not it wants lineart and a cartoon-ish vibe, or lineless and realisticMisc.Positives-Main menu units change depending on far you’re in the campaign-They kept most of the cheats from the original and added some new funky onesNegatives-Water still moves when the game is paused for some reason-Can’t see enemies HP when they’re in view, I’m guessing this is a glitch-Can’t control the units on the main menu anymore, very sadNeutrals-Why did they randomly smite Hathor out of the game and replace her with Sobek? I liked her-The UI is definitely different

_childDocuments_.review: Since this is a decent upgrade of Age of Mythology, and I'm a huge fan of the original, the game was and still  is a "recommend" for me. However, there are some weird bugs on top of what others have mentioned, and I genuinely wish these would be fixed, since they're ruining our matches. Others might have point out these bugs too, but I didn't see them mentioned. So here goes:1. Once you drag select a number of units, you cannot isolate individual units or stacks of a certain unit from your selection. For instance, if you manage to rope in say 4 villagers in your army, those 4 villagers will be visible in the selection panel. You could click on them too. But nothing will happen, unlike in the original (or any rts game) where you'd naturally end up selecting that stack of 4 villagers. You'd have to deselect the whole crowd, find out where those villagers are hiding, and then physically relocate them before selecting the army again. This cannot be intentional, right?2. Every time I make an additional TC, all TCs start auto-queuing villagers. I usually end up with 50-70 idle villagers taking up my pop-cap unless I click on every TC and stop the production manually. Highly disruptive. Imagine waiting for backup archers, when you're told that you've reached your pop limit and there's 65 villagers standing around in the middle of a field, gazing at wild gnus, going Zzzzz...Still, I love the game in itself and would recommend. Just that I can understand if others may find these deal-breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Remake of an old game that, aside from a few glitches here and there, maintains what was great about the original while adding some much appreciated quality of life features such as key remapping, controller support and a much better camera to name a few. There are some things I'm not too fond of. The music it sounds like has been redone, and some parts just sound bad. Most tracks sound fine, but if you were an avid player of the original then you will probably notice pretty quick which ones don't sound the same. The spoken lines of dialog are completely redone with new actors and some of the line delivery felt a little off, but most was pretty good.Graphics look amazing and the way buildings crumble now is really fun. Lots of great additions and in my opinion definitely worth the $30 price tag. Especially when you consider how they are going to be adding new content to this game. Very exciting prospect. Definitely recommend and very excited to see what the future holds for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: A proper way to do a remaster!To my surprise, I couldn't even notice any worth mentioning issues, so I'll just list the stuff I liked: - Stayed very true to the original.- Looks up to date for modern standards.- Improves the user experience compared to original (unit control, variety of gameplay settings)- Runs well on the recommended system requirements.- Seems to be well polished, as I have not encountered any noticeable bugs.- Expands content to create new experiences without ruining the classic feel.- Even does some fan service (like legacy God portraits).Disclaimer: remaster does bring back couple of the original game's shortcomings, however those are mostly related to design decisions and the original was still a great game even with them.

_childDocuments_.review: When discussing video game remasters, this should be used as an example. _childDocuments_.review: A great revival of an old classic, easily my favorite RTS ever! The updates to the graphics are amazing but even more than that are the QoL improvements to bring this game into a more modern feel with gathering presets, auto-unit spawning, and unit collision. The god powers are better than ever and the ability to reuse them for a growing favor cost is awesome. Ever wanted to block a pass with nothing but Gaia trees? Well now you can! To top it all off though are the mods. Already there are tons of great mods for the game to improve things or add some fun maps, but THE BEST is the one to change the voices back to the OG cast ones. Right out of the gate, IF your big issue with the game was the voicelines, HAVE NO FEAR, you can fix it immediately with 2 mods! It does make you wonder why the developers didn't just use the OG voicelines anyway, but, what can you do? There are some issues, However, and this thing really needs some patch support. There's a weird bug causing the screen to flicker here and there and is really jarring visually, though it doesn't seem to effect gameplay too much.Some issues where the cursor gets locked into whatever the last action icon you sent your units to do, gather food, get favor, that sort of thing. Which isn't that big of a deal till you use the cursor to move the screen and it gets stuck like that and then every movement of the mouse is moving the screen. There's also some god powers that cause some major frame drops, though I've seen it effect people to a greater and lesser degree so hardware and what your running the game at settings wise definitely is a big factor. Other than those things, It's a great time to be an RTS fan. If your tired of AoE IV and loved the AoE III remake, this is right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah , it's what it says on the tin. A remake of Age of Mythology. Better than the HD version.Same game as before.Engine is functional and fluid.some stuttering and flickering but i suspect that's the AMD driver on my pc.The campaigns stay fairly true to the original , though i recall a mission where Arkantos has a dream and he plays as the bad guys destroying Atlantis.The portraits are a nice touch though why they made Amanra look 60 and cross like she smelled Arkantoses feta laced fart is beyond me. Voice acting is decent enough , though Kastor seems to be phoning it in.Also saw some bugs where ship combat sounds were still playing after both ships were destroyed.One thing that tick me off was unit spawning. This is what Spellforce 1 and 2 did because programming AI is hard . Same thing happens here . I saw two units spawn from a temple at once in a mission and attack me.In the mission where KAstor goes to mount Olympus the ruins of the barracks at beginning keep spawning units AFTER they were destroyed. Maybe somebody used a while loop instead of a for loop.Last nitpick - promise. The unit descriptions. In the previous games right clicking a unit or technology gave you some cool flavor text/backstory. Here ? Just endlessly loops unit production - which i found out after i had 20 Minotaurs. One unnecessary turd sticking to an otherwise decent release is the DLC for the Legacy Portraits. I mean , 6 euro for some dusty pics from mommy's attic ? common now.Hopefully the Chinese DLC is handled better than the HD version were it was severely panned.If it works well maybe we'll get more civs , Japan , India , Mezo-america etc.That would be cool.Multiplayer works well though i only played a few games with my mates. Worked fine so far.So yeah. It's good. Could use a tiny coat of polish but it is what players like myself wanted and true to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology is a game that was first released 22 years ago and served as a spin-off to Age of Empires, a franchise beloved by many players within the RTS genre. Now the game received a much needed love tap on the shoulder with a remake that stays extremely true to the original, but with a few little touch-ups here and there. There are three campaigns in total currently, Fall of the Trident, The Golden Gift and The New Atlantis. They already announced that they will release the China part as well as a DLC later and a second DLC which is supposed to bring a completely new campaign. There is also the option for a custom campaign, which is currently grayed out for me, but it does indicate the possibility of player made content to be available later. Depending on skill and chosen difficulty, a mission takes roughly between 20 and 40 minutes, sometimes even longer depending on how often it has to be restarted.The gameplay feels exactly the same as it did before, but with the difference that units behave slightly smarter than back in the days. You build up a base, recruit units, micro them in battle and counter the enemy units. Graphics and OST got improved, but nothing to write home about.A good remake that deserves to be played.

At least take the characters from the original game and tell it in a different way, so the price points feels justified, then maybe I will accept these new voices. The game play seems the same, but the UI is all different and they removed things that made the original much more efficient. It's a bad remake.

_childDocuments_.review: what a good remake.  I'm very happy.  While I did pre-order the game, I had no expectations going in. So far I am blown away.I have been a player of Age of Mythology since it first released in 2002.  I have played countless hours in the original version, then their first hd remaster / "extended edition" version of the game and now I plan on having countless hours in this version.I'm still being surprised by the new things they've added into this version of the game.  I won't spoil anything here so you can go find out for yourself but... It's neat.  If you've never played Age of Mythology, I highly suggest playing all three versions of the game, as all three have something to discover. :] It makes child me [and adult me] very happy and very proud. ♥Easily a 10/10 recommendation from me.I really hope you add the Chinese pantheon from the extended edition as well as some new ones we have yet to play. _childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the original Age of Mythology I would play it in custom mode making fake armies fight for hours and hours, Untold hits all the right notes while breathing fresh life into the classic. The nostalgia is undeniable, but the improvements make it feel like a modern experience. They kept so much of the original look, yet everything is noticeably cleaner and more polished.The God Powers are back, but now they feel even more impactful and strategic. Titans, while still a force to be reckoned with, are more balanced and not the unstoppable giants they once were. The game strikes a perfect balance between respecting the original and delivering something new and exciting. Whether you're a veteran or a newcomer, Age of Mythology: Untold is simply a joy to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology Retold is a remaster of one of my favorite childhood game that aims to improve the 2002 classic by adding quality of life features (such as the ability to toggle autocast on unit powers as well as the ability to cast them manualy or tool tips that tell you the damage modifiers of a unit against specific types) and balance reworks such as reusable god powers that cost favor to use again after a cooldown. The game also reworked elements already present such as Atlantean favor generation (they use oracles instead of town centers now), some unit match-ups (murmillos and ulfsarks are now all purpose instead of getting a bonus against cavalry) as well as adding all new units and a norse building (the norse changed a lot). The chinese have currently been removed from the game until a DLC that reworks them into something that I hope is much better is released (oh yeah they're doing brand new DLCs!)Ok so, they've made the OG game prettier, more user friendly and di balance tweaks. That's neat. What is amazing however is the decision to start adding new major gods, starting with Freyr for the Norse who comes with 3 new minor gods (as well as myth units for them), special missions to showcase those new gods (there is currently a single one for Freyr) and for some random reason they even added a roguelite mode which is appreciated even if it is unexpected.The one downside to this is that, to avoid the voices suddenly being different in its original content, all the characters have been recast and their voicelines have been replaced. The units sounds are still the same (we can still prostagma in the shade) but you'll have to download a mod to bring back the old cast. The new cast is fine, if a bit forgettable. tl;dr its a great remaster and I love what its doing to a game I realy like and I'm hyped to see what new content they release for it in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is this a great game, and a massive upgrade over the original, but the devs also listened to player feedback. Other than that, the gampelay is extremely satisfying, the balance seems pretty good, especially considering it just came out and there will definitely be more balance patches to come. I strongly recommend it to fans of the "Age Of" series, and also to strategy games lovers in general. It might even be a great introduction to RTSs for someone who never played before.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Some serious care was put into this remaster to the point where I would say it could potentially qualify as a remake. Legacy portraits are not modified, simply given a quality pass. Daniel Riordan reprises his role as Arkantos, the rest of the VA is done well also. Balance changes across the board, making the game play differently, but still in a familiar way. Potentially the best way to experience Age of Mythology.(Steam Deck Info)Performance holds up okay on Steam Deck at default settings, roughly 45 FPS on average. Mild ui issues, but a definite improvement from the original campaign playtest where the UI would slowly disappear one icon at a time. Played with mouse and keyboard. Text can be scaled up to a reasonably readable level.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Out of all of remastered RTS games we've gotten, so far this is one of the bests. Almost evrything feels so refresh and polished, seeing the redefined fantasy units and Gods are awesome. Music and voice acting sounds great. This game is what an actual remaster is supposed to be or feel like, now if someone could please remaster Armies of Exigo that would be amazing. Kinda wish Blizzard would have this kind of passion, especially for their RTS games.

Literally sounds like a cheap voice-actor from Fiverr. Also they've implemented large pop-up characters who speak along with closed captions during cut-scenes, it comes off as a cheap phone game.Other than that keen to put probably another 1,000 hours into this game.

I hope many of the old classic custom scenarios of the 2000s will return though, as I enjoyed them a lot.Overall (From what I've seen so far), a very good base game and its modern improvements built upon it make it better (I particularly like the addition of renewable god powers, making them less one-off gimmicks).
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: I remember my dad hooking this up in the basement so my brother and I and him could all play team games against opponents. What was that, 2005? I would have been 8.Lives up to the nostalgia quite well. They rebealanced a few things, like making god powers resusable at the cost of favor (you get 1 for free). I remember seeing one or two other rebalances I can't think of right now, but all have been for the better. There's nothing wrong with going back to play the original and if this didn't exist, I otherwise might have. But I'd personally say this is "better." I actually did fire up the old version last year and wasn't hit with nostalgia. I think nostalgia for me would come from playing this again with my dad and brother, which if my dad was as tech savy in his 50s as he was in his 30s, we probably would be!TLDR: Strictly speaking, I like it more than the original and the changes are good.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: I am having a great time returning to this game after 22 years. This remaster has been pretty good, there are a couple bugs with sound, changed up the game menu, added more settings/QOL updates and they have re-recorded all the dialogue of the campagins with new voice actors. I love the decisions they made with the visuals. It's not a full re-rendering into modern graphics, it still retains the blocky charm of the early 2000's, but the motion is all smoother, the textures look more detailed and the upscaling from the 2002 version also looks great. Crucially, the music remains identical sounding to the original. Along with most of the iconic lines and monster noises. Though, there are some updated/changed notification noises. They added villager auto-tasking, which I would not really recommend turning on, because it has a tendancy to just blindly send your workers to get any reasourse regardless of distance to drop point or potential hazards. So unless you have way too much going on, have control over large swaths of the map, and can't handle retasking all your workers constantly, I wouldn't recommend using it. Late game only, basically. This remaster really does feel like the superior way to experience this game now. It's not without it's flaws, but for fans of the original game, or early 2000's RTS games, this is a classic that won't disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from the voice acting being kinda stiff and lame, they did try to improve on it. If it bothers you that much, just wait for a mod to restore original voice actors. This is a high quality remaster and I am honestly so happy. I have very few complaints. There is a proprietary anti tamper to prevent memory manipulation, but thats really easy to bypass. I get why they did that, but they're going to annoy more casual players. The campaign is just as you remember it, but with way better visuals and kinda bad voice acting, but they brought back the original voice actor for Arkantos so that's a plus.Music and soundtrack has been upscaled or re-recorded to a higher bitrate and had some embellishments and slight tweaks to it, which I don't honestly mind. The gameplay is where most of the changes are. If you are like me and played the mainly skirmish against players, you'll be happy to know that the Norse Heiser rush and Atlantean Fast Heroic have been patched. I'm sure there are other broken things, but its far too early too tell. The new god power system seems like a gimmick as the amount of favor needed to cast a 2nd god power is ridiculous. To be honest, this requirement is going to favor experienced Egyptian players focusing on passive favor gen. Attack moves are now very responsive and actually work significantly better than in the original or the beta. Pathing has been significantly improved and you can command huge armies without units blocking eachother. Wonder Age has been readded allowing you to reuse god powers for cheap, empowering your myth units and allows you to rebuild titan gates. Odin now gets access to Braki as well as air units along with Norse getting a complete rework. The housing limit has been also increased to 16 which means you get a much larger population cap. Some myth units have gotten huge buffs like the minatour, Nemean Lion, Trolls and mummies getting an AOE that turn everything into a mummy. Myth units also get a big buff every time you level up like heroes. One of the biggest change is the naval combat, all 3 ship types are available in the classical age. For maps like Miggard this completely changes how the map plays. Lastly the Auto Queue has been removed from military units. You now have to hot key armies, but auto queue still remains for villagers. There's too many changes to honestly condense into one review, these are just my personal favorites right now. Game is 100% worth $30.
_childDocuments_.name: Age of Mythology: Retold

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology Retold is a hybrid of remake and remaster. Essentially, the game feels just as you remember it—and it looks as beautiful as you remember, too. In fact, it’s a stunning remaster of the original, without feeling out of place. It looks great, plays well, and runs smoothly. The campaigns are among the best the RTS genre has to offer. Age of Mythology offers a unique depth through its mythical units and god powers that you won't find anywhere else. And let’s be honest: THIS is how a remaster should look and feel! Microsoft has already proven with the Definitive Editions of the old Age of Empires titles that they understand the concept of "remaster," but somehow this one takes it to another level.I highly recommend it not just for old fans, but for anyone who enjoys RTS games.

_childDocuments_.review: Take this as sort of a neutral rating. It's a remake of a game I loved so in that regard, I was always going to like it. That said, it is flat out inferior to a 20-year old game. There are some baffling design choices that make me think the devs implemented the ideas in their heads without thinking it through.First thing are animals of set always leaving corpses. In the original, only villager kills would create a harvestable corpse, and with good reason. You can easily pollute the map with animal corpses which bugs out the pathfinding, especially when playing against the AI. The way the AI reacts to walls is also significantly worse. Sometimes, they recognize that they have to destroy it but other times, they just stand next to it, pelted by arrows until they die. This was never a thing in the original. Reusable godpowers.... You can block pathways with gold mines. While this isnt really an issue in PVP, it just seems obvious that if you allow reusable god powers, you'd force the mines to have a set distance from each other to be activated. Honestly, these seem like nitpicks but they had a great game to build off of --- and the base of it is still great. It always was. It's just the stuff they added is straight up bad.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology: Retold is the 2nd remaster (yep, games are getting that old now) and an equivalent to the Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition. I say this because while it brings the graphical fidelity to a modern level, it also adds new features that the original game didn't have. Both of those things have positives and negatives tied to them. I will primarily focus on what sets AoM:R apart from the original and the Extended Edition (the first remaster).The game play is largely improved as far as balance and flow goes. It is still the same mythology-based RTS everyone is familiar with from ages ago, but many aspects of how the gods play have been tweaked and a few new features have been added. Any God power can be used multiple times (not the same as before) with the first use being free and the next use(s) costing favor. This is probably the biggest change since some god powers can dramatically shift the flow of the game. There is a new age V (accessed by building a wonder) with many upgrades and costs (wonders are very expensive alone and rarely do games last that long unless it is a high player count game). There are new units and some units that have been given to gods that didn't have access to them previously (the new major god Feyr has the Draugr unit). There are several economic improvements to all or some pantheons with certain balances to others to make them feel closer in scale. For example, hero units can now be trained separately from others (training a Villager and Ajax at the same time). The Norse units can build the Ox Cart instead of using the Town Center to speed up production of units at the Town Center. Many formations and hotkeys from AoE II:DE has been carried over to AoM:R to speed up players. There are a ton of other changes that would take more than the allowed characters in a review, but overall, the changes are positive.The music is great and many will recognize unit sounds, combat, and ambiance from the original and the Extended Edition. There are more accessibility features than before. There are more graphical options with a much higher level of detail to immerse yourself in the world. I personally think some of the new artwork (major and minor gods and important character portraits throughout the story) are good overall, but some of them are just worse. Major story characters are still voiced, but many have new voice actors (I personally dislike the new Arkantos and Amanra voices). The negatives for Age of Mythology: Retold? Well, the price is going to be a big barrier for many, especially if you own Age of Mythology or Extended Edition. While this version is quite different and has a lot of new (and more DLC content planned) to it, it is still a hard sell. On top of that, RTS games are very much in the shadow of other genres and have limited followings these days (sadly). The online community is active enough (typically because of Age of Empires fans enjoy this game a lot too), but there definitely was a massive problem with this during the beta and launch time. There was a list of bugs that would prevent you from finding lobbies, joining lobbies, starting the game, and getting disconnected. Most of those issues are fixed now, but it was the main complaint when the game launched (it was pretty frustrating for me as well).In closing, if you haven't played Age of Mythology before, this is the best version, in my opinion. If you have played it, then I still highly recommend this game, but I would wait for a sale. I know more content will be added after this review (or the new, recently released mode, God Trials, that I haven't played), but I believe it will only add to the experience rather than take away. A 4th Norse god, Freyr, is in the base game with the Chinese pantheon being completely reworked and added in later plus more in the future.
