_childDocuments_.review: Alrighty... where to start. I'm almost 29 and I have been playing Age of Mythology since I was a little kid. I still own all physical copies of the game and still have the original computer I played it on purely for the memories. This game was the beginning of my professional gaming career and what ultimately got me into RTS games and Mythology. Having grown up on this game I am heavily biased towards it and extremely nit-picky about the small details. So let's get to it!I think we can all agree that the only campaign difficulty that is worth mentioning is Titan. Having not played this game in a long time and having long term hand injuries (military) Titan was relatively easy as it should be for someone like myself, but some missions were absolutely ridiculously difficult and I know people not as adept at the game would greatly struggle to do them. Having the AI spam attack you with insanely large armies every couple of minutes (think it was 3) is just silly. You  make a game harder without it being ridiculous. It's even worse when it's like 1 against 3 and you have limited resources and you have to break through massive cities to reach your destination. I love seeing an active ranked leader board. Some old names I remember as a kid, some I even played with as a kid, have been on it. I haven't played any ranked matches myself since my hands are messed up (massive APM reduction) but have watched quite a few of them being casted by FitzBro and had a great time watching them!Also please don't ask my old name... I really don't remember lmfao. I know I played some games with Akatsuki clan and a few other clans. I haven't tinkered with the Editor too much, but I did make a map based off a SC2. I do wish that you can use smaller water for fine details, and I wish it would do a better job following your mouse since at the moment the editor is like a small child with crayons, you try to stay in your perceived lines and for some reason it starts going outside the lines. Just some tuning would be great. I can't wait to see some of the old custom games come back. =) So I agree with everyone when people say the Voice Acting and Portraits aren't that great. The Portraits are clearly AI generated. Some of the voices try to hard to be unnatural. The voices give me Girl V-Tuber vibes basically. All you need to do is talk naturally, but putting extra oomph in bad pronunciation doesn't help. As a side note Amanra looks like a 90 year old twig compared to old Amanra who I actually thought was cute as a kid. Just uhh... thought i'd throw that out there. Overall I like how nearly every God seems to be pretty well balanced (ranging from C-A on my personal tier, though I think Set is easily S since it's pretty broken right now). There are some kinks that can easily be worked out, I would ask the ranked players. What I 100% believe needs to be reworked a tiny bit is Titan Difficulty. You can make them spam attack less and make it still be extremely hard as intended. If you need help, please, just ask the players. We've been playing for so long we kinda know the game a little bit. I am in absolute love with this anti-cheat. I remember back in the day there were some map hacks and some Cheat Engine cheats would work in ranked, but this completely stops that possibility. All of the major "trainer" makers seem to have thrown in the towel which is good. I also decided to test it by having one of those programs running and it immediately crashes the game on launch! It's amazing. Really great work from the devs on that one.With the new addition of Freyr I got to experience a new god on AoM since Atlanteans became a thing. That was pretty exciting to say the least. The god itself is... I am going to be completely honest the god itself is mediocre except on a few select maps and strats. It was exciting initially, especially in the Mythical Battles mode, but the more I played Freyr the more I preferred like Loki or Odin (Thor nice for the dwarves, but other than that Thor is also mediocre except on a few select maps). Now, with the release of Freyr, and the release of  in the future, I would like to start seeing more Major Gods and more Pantheons (with campaigns ofc). I don't mind if they're (pantheons) are sold as DLC for like $5 or $10. I do see one extra Pantheon being decided on other than Chinese, but I would like to state that you also have all of these to choose from (strictly pantheon):Just a thought!Overall I highly recommend the game. Despite some of the cons I pointed out, I have high hopes for this remaster. I highly doubt the devs would ever read this review, but if they do, please take what I said seriously in terms of pantheons. The community would LOVE to see more pantheons. After all, it's the Age of Mythology is it not? ;)

_childDocuments_.review: Retold is a love letter to the longtime fans of AoM. Where Extended Edition was simply just a modern reskin, Retold is effectively the Definitive Edition like for AoE2.Visual improvements go beyond special effects, where little things like the Citadels for each major faction have their own distinct appearances now, and aren't just the same Egyptian citadel with your major god statue. Considering the original game's 3D models and animations were very simple in order to be compatible across a wider range of PCs, it's incredibly refreshing to see these units and buildings we've known and love that have such improved detail on them.A lot of the audio has been redone and seems pretty good so far. The music still sounds familiar enough to ring nostalgia but still is new to your ears, much like AoE2DE's soundtrack. I ended up using mods for the redone campaign voice acting however, I can't stand to not hear the original lines as they were read back then, but that's entirely personal taste.There are plenty of other changes as well, from balancing to just making things much more fun. There's too many to go through in a review (nor have I even seen it all yet!), but to give a taste you can look at Ra and Isis' changes to what their monuments do for them. Empowering your monuments as Ra will let a fraction of the empowerment spread to nearby buildings, and as Isis it increases the range of blocking god powers.All in all, I call this a must-buy if you loved the original game. You won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Never played og AoM or AoE2 back in the day.  Tried out AoE4 this past year and absolutely adored it.  Fav RTS since Starcraft Brood War.  Loved it so much I was willing to buy AoM at full price instead of waiting for a sale.  This is coming from someone who mostly plays skirmish against AI.I recommend AoM:Retold but with some hesitation.If I had to compare it to AoE4, I would say AoM: Retold is a flashier, simpler, and more aggressive in gameplay design.The thrill of AoM comes from the fantasy presentation (including the mythological fan service and wicked animations) yes, but I think the most enjoyable aspects are the variety in effects from your choices in game.  Each major mythological god will have minor gods that are associated with it.  So as you age up during the game you will have to actively select minor gods/units/tech to get and deny yourself the perks of the one you didn't pick.  Making significant choices just feels plain good.The part that feels different (not that it's a bad thing) is that because this is a less defense-focused game - building walls and siege weapons feel way less important.  Everything just feels like the game wants you to  play aggressively - from the relics encouraging map exploration to beefier units all the way up to Titans being available as you age up.  I guess why I'm so mixed is because I enjoyed listening to podcasts as I played skirmish mode on silent in AoE4 and was able to zone out.  The other thing that I feel mixed about is the autoque.  It definitely makes the experience more fun, but has some bugs currently and diminishes some of the fun in Age 1 where it's all about micromanaging resources.The part that I absolutely hate are the graphics and lack of minor QoL features.  I'm not sure if this is engine related - but the overall graphics and style feel less polished compared to AoE4.  There are additional animations like the building being set on fire and units flying into the distance after being smashed, but the overall graphics feel less advanced than AoE4.  One of the things I was surprised about was how little minor gods actually impacted the presentation of the game.  For example, when I picked Aphrodite to be one of my minor gods,  I wished there was a voiced sultry line telling me that she was in my service (yes, I'm a little thirsty).  The lack of personalization with the minor gods outside of gameplay changes really is a bummer.Hope for the future: AoM Retold is a solid package.  I'm really excited for the Chinese pantheon as well as a new one (I'm hoping for a Lovecraftian one myself).  Also, I think having new major gods come as DLC would be absolutely amazing as well, although I'm not sure how that would work with some of the minor gods actually better fitting as major gods (such as Ares God of War).

_childDocuments_.review: I've been an Age of fan my entire life. I fondly remember the day I was given Age of Mythology by my childhood best friend, and we'd play LAN together. Then I remember the EXACT day Age of Mythology: The Titans expansion released, I was so excited.When the HD edition came out, I was disappointed. I was skeptical about the changes for Retold, but my skepticism has been thoroughly rocked by the sheer amount of quality on display. The rockstars at Forgotten Empires knocked this release out of the park and I eagerly await news for their upcoming DLC's.The reworks for each civilization are absolutely delightful, bringing modern quality of life and significant balance and content changes. Each civilization still feels like they originally did, while maintaining a number of new interesting changes that do not feel out of place. The pacing is solid, skirmish games are faster and more intense than ever before.While I personally wish they were able to keep all of the original voice actors for campaign, the fact that they pulled Daniel Riordan to voice Arkentos again mitigated a significant amount of that concern. Multiplayer is a breeze and there has yet in my experience to be any technical issues what so ever on or offline.I can pick some nits, but well and truly, I cannot recommend Age of Mythology Retold enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Some bugs here and there (cursor being weird, occasional short freezes, projectiles hitting water kinda just hang there, pathfinding being generally perplexing at times and the rare conga line here and there, some animation weirdness) the maps generally feel smaller. Not entirely on board with the new character models in the dialog (the eyes are cartoonishly big and the proportions generally feel off. And more importantly, why is Arkantos' nose smaller now?). The audio needs some adjustment or something, it's mostly ok but sometimes randomly a line is way louder, and speaking of audio, they did a great job with the voice acting but Arkantos and Ajax seem to be the only ones without appropriate accents in the cutscenes and it makes it feel off.Even with all of these and whatever other minor inconveniences I've encountered and forgot about I absolutely love this game. It delivers on everything one could expect and more, it manages to surpass the original while preserving its legacy in a respectful way. The original was my childhood and I've come back to it many times but I'm enjoying retold even more.If you liked the original, you should get this. If you like rts games in general, I strongly recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifetime lover of AoM (note my profile pic lol), Retold is excellent so far! The beauty of this classic in your heart is now better matched by beautiful graphics and some well-implemented gameplay tweaks and outright renovations. I particularly love the new favor system wherein all god powers are reusable at scaled costs. Getting into the "secret" fifth Wonder Age and repeatedly smiting your opponents with divine wrath is extremely fun! There is also a nice set of new maps to play on and more controls for setting up your game. The new Freyr god is super cool (although I wish his new minor gods had also been mixed into the original Norse gods so that they wouldn't be exclusive to Freyr) and I'm very excited to see and play the upcoming pantheons.Finally, if you're a true AoM nerd and enjoy spending hours in the editor making stuff, you will be relieved to know that 1) it still exists! and 2) there's a search feature now (thank the gods!).Could you keep playing the old game and still have a good time? Sure. But getting Retold will have you feeling 22 years younger again, engrossed in an awesome tale of gods and men.

_childDocuments_.review: I have about 300 hours ob steam on the original Age of mythology and probably 1000+ hours through disk version. This remastered version or "Retold" is a dream come true. The developers not only gave it the remaster version but much more. Age of Mythology Retold is an absolute triumph in the realm of real-time strategy games! This remastered classic breathes new life into the beloved original with stunning graphics, refined gameplay mechanics, and a fresh coat of polish that both long-time fans and newcomers will adore. The attention to detail in the updated visuals is breathtaking, bringing the mythical world to life in a way that’s both nostalgic and excitingly new.The core gameplay, which already was a standout feature in the original, remains engaging and strategic, with enhanced AI and quality-of-life improvements that make the experience smoother and more immersive. The inclusion of new content and balanced adjustments ensures that both veteran players and those just starting out have plenty to explore and conquer.The voice acting and soundtrack, true to their roots, evoke the epic feel of ancient legends while benefiting from modern audio clarity. The user interface is intuitive, making managing your empire and engaging in battles more fluid than ever.Age of Mythology Retold is a masterful revival of a classic, perfectly blending nostalgia with modern enhancements. It’s a must-play for anyone who loves strategy games or has a fondness for mythological tales. This remaster respects its legacy while boldly stepping into the present, making it a game that will enchant both the old guard and a new generation of players.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good remake of the original,I am happy with most of the changes, as it still holds that nostalgia, but it is more balanced I think.I am split on the artistic directions, as it looks a bit cartoony in some aspects and I personally liked old designs more, but it is not ugly or anything like that, just a bit inconsistent.Main issues are portrats and voice acting. Portraits are, as I've said a bit cartoony, and there are inconsistencies in artstyles, characters have different feel to them compared to the original,I don't like these: Arkantos, Agammemnon, Amanra, General Melagius, fanatic and destroyer.For voiceacting, Amanra feels too different, but that is not a great issue, but General Melagius looks and sounds too young, Krios sounds like a young boy for 80% of the time, and like the original for the rest, and he changes tone of his voice in the missions. Rest is mostly mistakes in the pronunciation of some words like "ship" to something that sounds like "sip" (mission 3 in new atlantis campaign) etc.Changes to gameplay I really loved:-Performance of units, dps and gather rate neatly displayed in UI-Research tells you exactly what it will do, same for the relics-Rechargable god powers and powers in general-Function of the Wonder-AI is not dumb (in previous games including Extended edition, it ignored walls altogether to go through open space, even if it was full of defensive buildings and units, and from what I could see, this was not the case in this version, but it will take me longer to know for sure if it is taking defensive buildings into consideration of pathfinding or it is something else) -Auto scouting-New attack move command-Naval myth units are now available for everyone regardless of minor gods you choose. Changes I find a bit weird:- Greek myrmidions now deal divine damage, yet other two major god 4th age units do not, combined with the fact that if you choose Hera you can slowly train them for free from all of your fortresses-Norse units still don't have a scouting unit, and if you don't have cavalery unit in your unit selection you cannot change unit stances or select patrolling. - Atlantian favor generation is reworked, but it is still unfair in comparison to others, maybe with exception of Norse generation, as you have to keep your Oracles far from eachother, and we still don't have "selet idle scout" button and they have to stand still to generate  favor, which is against scouting function. If I could suggest yet another rework, favor could be generated by manors. Overall good game in need of some finishing touches, and I think they did a good job of not just putting new visuals and calling it a new game, but a complete complex overhaul.8/10 I think? Certainly good enough for me, and I think newcomers will find it satisfying, but there is still a room to improve.I hope I didn't offended developers, this is just my personal take as a long time fan who owned it when it was for Win98, and I really want to thank you for giving a new breath to my most beloved game.

Same basic framework but enough changes that it is better than ever. Iffy voice acting some odd visual changes but great overall, AND SO MUCH ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ POTENTIAL!!!NON TLDR: Where to begin. Ultimately at it's core it's age of mythology. But It's overhauled to a point where this is the sequel we should have gotten.NEGATIVES- The voice acting is odd so far. Into the early first few missions of the Egyptian portion of the campaign and my biggest gripe is this: They clearly went for more accurate greek voices with most of the greek characters, why have Arkantos stay similar to his 'Oh we're greek so obviously we speak perfect english with no accent at all!' voice from the first game. Wedjet still be a slithery boy when not moving, and the Atlantean titan movement  Again just wierd.-DLC does not add new gods to exisiting pantheons. I will explain why I like this later, but I do think it sucks we are currently only able to play those new gods on the DLC.PROS-Solid game. The revamped user interface is intuitive and user-friendly, making it easier for both veterans and newcomers to dive into the strategic depth of the game.The inclusion of new content, such as additional campaigns and updated multiplayer features, adds significant replay value. Players can once again command powerful gods, lead legendary heroes, and engage in epic battles that are more dynamic and strategic than ever before. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or a newcomer eager to explore the ancient world, there’s something here to captivate and challenge you.In conclusion, Age of Mythology Retold is a triumphant homage to the original game, skillfully balancing nostalgia with modern enhancements. _childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology: Retold is what Warcraft 3: Reforged should have been—a faithful and improved game that honors the original while bringing it into the modern era.From the moment I started playing, I was overwhelmed with nostalgia. The music, the units, the gameplay—all felt just as I remembered. Initially, I had some doubts about the graphical overhaul, but after watching comparison videos of the original game, I was blown away by how much it has evolved. The transformation is truly remarkable.For those unfamiliar with Age of Mythology (AoM), let me explain why this game remains so captivating and entertaining:Age of Mythology is a Real-Time Strategy (RTS) game, meaning your actions and those of your opponents occur simultaneously, without turns or pauses. Success requires staying a step ahead of your opponent, and there are multiple ways to achieve this—by gathering more resources, advancing to a higher age, or building a larger army. But what sets AoM apart is the unique twist of incorporating heroes and mythological creatures.The differences in units might seem superficial at first, but they are integral to the rock-paper-scissors mechanic that underpins the game’s strategy. Every unit has its counter, adding a layer of depth and balance to the gameplay.On top of that, the game offers the favor of gods from three major pantheons—Greek, Egyptian, and Norse—each providing unique buffs, superpowers, and special units. This variety offers endless possibilities for experimentation and strategy.The game can be enjoyed in multiple ways: through skirmish games against the AI, where you can test out different gods, civilizations, and powers; through three engaging campaigns; or in online multiplayer matches. Plus, there's a thriving modding community that adds even more content and variety.One detail I particularly appreciate, which often goes unnoticed, is the beauty of the buildings. Each civilization’s architecture is distinct and easily recognizable, with certain structures, especially the wonders, featuring intricate and beautiful designs.All in all, Age of Mythology: Retold is a fantastic game for those looking to indulge in some strategic gameplay. It also serves as a wonderful gateway for introducing a new generation of gamers to the rich cultures and myths of ancient civilizations.

_childDocuments_.review: It's the best of Starcraft and Age of Empires:- three distinct factions. Each with their own unique units, sub factions, and macro mechanics.- fast paced but not too punishing combat. So far, I haven't encountered a match where my units were instantly wiped when I looked elsewhere for a few seconds.- players are incentivised to expand, or else they'll not get more population slots (more than 200!) and more worker production. Because of this, games are less turtly and you have to have map presence instead of merely walling off resources.- at first I was a bit skeptical about auto queue villagers but after trying it out, it's not as dumbed down as I thought. As for auto queue military, it's optional in ranked so harass and attention taxing tactics is still effective.- your opponent's faction and name are not shown so no checking the ladder and preemptive faction switching.Now for a bit on the negatives as of writing:- watching replays always crashes with a desync. You'll be able to watch the first few minutes and then a black screen of desync will appear. I wish this would be fixed for those who want to relive the glory of their wins and learn from their losses through replays.- queing for online matches sometimes disconnects so you have to re-queue again.- there is this hubub about the old portrait DLC and I agree that it's supposed to be free. It's like they want to milk the nostalgia of older players.- you have an elo or mmr rank but no bronze, silver, gold, etc ranking but maybe it's for the best.Haven't tried the campaign yet. The game is well optimized and looks great too. I have to wait and see if the next upcoming expansions (Chinese and.. I hope, Hindu myths) will be worth the premium upgrade. As someone who only bought the base game, the game's so worth it (I'm still regretting paying for Stormgate Early Access). _childDocuments_.review: As fans of real-time strategy games look back fondly on classic titles from the early 2000s, Age of Mythology often stands out as a shining gem. With its mythical creatures, divine influences, and rich historical tapestry, it captured the hearts of many. Fast forward to 2024, and we now have Age of Mythology: Retold, a remastered edition that promises to reignite the nostalgia while tempting a new generation of gamers. * Graphics, Sound & More *First and foremost, the visual upgrades are striking, with all-new graphics, animations, models, and lighting. This presents an appealing invitation to both newcomers and veterans alike. Also, while single-player campaigns seem more engaging with a remastered narrative, the voice acting fails to deliver at the correct tone of the original campaign.* Gameplay *At its core, Age of Mythology: Retold retains the beloved system of the original while implementing several refined mechanics that improve the overall experience. The resource management and build strategies feel tight and engaging, and the new hotkey layouts and improved UI design make the game more accessible than ever. Favor as a resource is now far more important by having no cap. It no longer feels like an optional or bonus resource, and if you ignore gathering it, you can be overwhelmed very early in the game. Also, attack move is better, but AI pathing still needs some improvements. * New Features *One of the most anticipated feature in Retold is the introduction of brand new minor gods and powers, with the addition of the norse god Freyr. The addition of new factions adds depth and variety, rekindling the excitement of  trying new strategies. The updated “God Powers” system has great replayability for all factions and it encourages players to explore different playstyles. Other changes worth mentioning are the navy rework, the norse new ranged hero Godi and great hall rework, larger population cap by raising the maximum number of houses to 16 and the overpowered late game bonus granted by building a wonder. * Final Thoughts *Overall, Age of Mythology: Retold is a touching tribute to the beloved classic that helped shape real-time strategy games. It expertly balances nostalgia with modern gameplay mechanics, though voice acting miss the mark in places, the improved accessibility and expanded options make this remaster a solid step forward. Whether you're a long-time fan or a curious newcomer, Retold delivers a “mythic” experience.

The soldiers often get completely stuck behind those in front of them and don't engage in battle, and sometimes their animations get stuck too, but that's just a graphical detail. It also sometimes happens that two soldiers push a free-standing unit in front of them, sometimes quite far. The villagers behave also poorly. When I have 5 idle villagers and I press the dot key and F, I only build one farm because all 5 go to build it. Another problem is that when I produce new units directly into the Sky Passage, they don't go inside and just stand in front of it. Or soldiers, when they have nothing to do, attack the wall, but when the enemy arrives, they calmly continue demolishing the wall, even though there is a slaughterhouse right next to them. In the old Age of Mythology, the units were much easier to control. I’m not sure if it was because of the shortcuts or because this is not final version yet. Hopefully, some updates will come that improve things a bit. I'm also not a fan of the repeating god powers. It would be nice if there was an option to turn them off before the game, just like the Titans. The god powers are too powerful and really disrupt the game. _childDocuments_.review: If you need only a summary it's this: it is an excelent remake worth the money, especially if it's your first time playing Age om MythologyBelow is more detailed description:Graphics: as expected the graphics are improved in every way. Ships and building are much more visual in their damage takes and their destruction (ships catch on fire and explode into splinters which is much more satysfying when they die via chrush/siege damage due to the crunch sound of the impact)Sound/voice acting: Sound of combat, miscelanious and such is preserved from the original since I imagine there was not much to do there. Siege attacks still crunch when hitting building, weapons clank in combat, the good old AoM. Voice acting is very much dependant on the listener: new voice actors by far and large do great to fantastic job emulating the old voice actors, only notable difference in major characters are Ajax and Gagarensis (but it's less about new VA being bad and rather more that the old VA were just that good). What IS very much appreciated is that there are new voicelines during campaing to provide sometimes tidbits of lore or ensuring smoother flow of the mission. And of course there is an mod for old VA so don't worry if you want the good old VA.Cinematics: Essentially AoM Retold is very much faithfull to the original and most that the cinematics got was a proper clean up and better visual overhaul.Gameplay: This one is a bit of a mixed bag. On one hand there are improvements with smoother and more interactive gameplay (keybind, stances, pathfinding and such). On the other hand sometimes things derp out (such as some of my units took one myth unit standing still on a LONG walk accidently). What is notable that quite a few things were invented: egyptian monuments are now much more important and are a part of strategy, new units were introduced to Norse and the most important thing is that god powers are now reusable with stacking favour cost enabling you to use wild and extreme strategies (like multiple Sons of Osiris)Is the Age of Mythology Retold worth your time and money? Depends if you liked the original or are you a fan of Age of Empires type strtegies. Where AoM Retold shines however is in the campaing. It is a expansive campaing that can also serve as entertaining tutorial if you want to get deep into each faction and have in my opinion a criminal amount of fun.The team behind AoM Retold so far have earned the respect of the community (fixed the god portaits, improved VA by leaps and bounds compared to early beta) so you can take a gample and I think you won't regret it. 2 new campaings are in DLC works so if you are patient you can wait a few weeks that the bugs are ironed out or wait until the DLC are out and get a more complete experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game for over 20 years and it has always been one of my favorites. It takes everything I love about Age of Empires, condenses it down to a handful of diverse factions like a Blizzard title would, and wraps it in a theme that I absolutely adore. I can say with 100% honesty this is one of the greatest remakes of any title I have ever played. It is perfect in almost every way, both in re-imagining the source work, and developing it in ways to make it better than it was before.Some bullet points:-Graphics: Amazing. I love the way every unit has been updated. This is exactly what AoM always should have been. My only very minor gripe is that while some animations looks flashy now, they lose a bit of their character. In particular is the death animations for ships, which simply explode instead of falling apart and sinking. But again, that is frankly a VERY MINOR complaint.-Gameplay: Perfect. Literally zero complaints. It plays almost exactly like the original game, and where it doesn't, it has been improved. Units and abilities from the original game that weren't very useful have been improved and developed to stand out more and be viable for once. Reusing god powers for a fee is a great change that really makes you think more about which powers you use. I love it all.-Music: In my mind Stephen Rippy and Kevin McMullan struck gold when they created the soundtrack for the original game, and I truly believe it is the greatest video game soundtrack of all time. It is rich and atmospheric, and I know every tune by heart. It manages to stick in your mind without getting in the way of the game. It is everything a video game soundtrack should be. Tilman Sillescu did a fantastic job updating the music of the game and adding his own flavor. It is the same, but different. Familiar, yet new. I personally still prefer the original out of nostalgia, but I think that his arrangements are just as great, and I do not find myself trying to replace it.-Optimization: The game runs just about flawlessly on my machine, and the new improvements to the engine allow you to field armies much larger than anything you could have in the original game. You can now select up to 100 units, whereas the cap for the original was 32 if I recall correctly, allowing you to truly dominate your opponents.-Artwork: You might see some complaints about horrible artwork in the game, but I must stress that these were images (shown in the first two trailers on the steam page as of the time of this review) in the beta version and the artwork in the full release is actually amazing. As far as I am concerned the art team did a fantastic job on the final release product. I question some of the design choices (making Gaia a wooden creature with no nose), but the quality is top notch.-Voice Acting: This is the big one. The voice acting in the beta was, frankly, quite bad. With the definitive editions of this series there has been a lot of "corrections" to the representation of certain characters and cultures that include changing names, words, and performances to be more accurate to the cultures represented. I support these changes wholeheartedly as I feel that they are in the spirit of the series, but at the same time I don't want them to come at a cost. The original release of Age of Mythology had a stellar cast that gave fantastic performances to all the characters in the campaigns, with truly top-notch voice acting. In Retold, however, all the characters were recast with actors that had proper accents (greeks no longer sound american etc). I like this idea in theory, but the new vocal performances are frankly quite weak. In response to the poor reception in the beta, they went and got the original VA for Arkantos, Daniel Riordan, to come in and reprise his role. It also seems that many other characters had their lines either recorded differently or they used different takes to improve the performance. It sounds better than it did in the beta, but I still think it pales in comparison to the original product. Luckily there is already a mod that replaces it all with the original voice acting, if you choose to do so.In conclusion: This game is amazing. I've played it for two decades, I'll probably play it for the next two decades. You simply will not find a better RTS out there, in my opinion. Well worth the $30 asking price, if not more.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: The game is seeing constant updates so this review might be outdated by the time you read it.Full-priced game that has less features than the old one. The main one being the lack of LAN mode.(Judging by AAA standards, which are low nowadays, but my point is that they have the necessary budget to tackle the issues mentioned bellow)Edit: I thought you couldn't save/load multiplayer games, but turns out you can, to load them, select the "saved game" game-mode when creating a multiplayer.Edit 2: - I've grown to like how oracles generate favor, in any case it was just a minor detail in my original review.- Added QoL suggestion about observer mode.Missing features:- Cannot host local(LAN) games, you can only play with others while online.Minor issues from the old game that weren't fixed (despite this one being in a new engine?):- Units can sometimes get stuck inside town centers.- AI that controls units (the one that makes yours units follow orders you give):  - Path-finding struggles with big-chunky units (like war-elephants), they will often keep bumping into each other.  - Questionable decision-making on attack commands: Units can stray away from the given order location indefinitely if they are chasing a unit that's faster than them (flash-back to 30 hoplites chasing a caravan across the map).  - Questionable decision-making on attack commands: buildings get completely ignored when there is at least a single enemy unit in vision, if you have 50 soldiers and 1 enemy villager spawns, they will all stop destroying the enemy's buildings to chase that villager.Some QoL suggestions:- Allow observer mode to flip the side of each player in the UI.- Allow players to change the side of their minimap on the UI.- Allow players to configure the opacity of certain UI elements, for example, the resource window of the alternative UI is very transparent.- Allow players to toggle-off the maximum population warning.- Allow players to toggle-off "unit-trained" sounds, or at least reduce their volume.- If you plan to keep supporting the villager AI feature, make it behave more efficiently and make norse-dwarvers be prioritized on gold-gathering.- Make it clear what each AI difficulty changes.- Some units/buildings/techs 's tooltips still aren't descriptive enough, use the extended edition's tooltip mod as reference. For example, the current tooltips don't show the values of the bonuses the pharaoh empowering ability gives.- The arrows FX are a bit too much.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology: Retold isn't a perfect remaster. Some of the new VAing is lackluster, especially compared to the original, there are some annoying pathing issues, and some of the DLC is way too expensive, especially considering its use of AI.However, despite these issues, in my opinion this remaster is everything I was hoping for and more. The graphics are pretty great, but that's something that should be a given. What I really enjoy are the changes to gameplay and the campaigns. Campaign missions have been given both minor and major changes, that still provide similar feelings to the originals.The most fun comes from the changes made to favor and myth units. Favor is no longer capped at 100, and you can build up almost as much as you like. While this can be used to mass myth units a lot easier, it can also be used to recast god powers (after a timer), and even summon more titans if your initial titan has been defeated. The addition of an entirely new age is also fun, even if it mainly serves as a buff to myth units in its current form. It would be cool to see unique buildings or units unlock in the future.I'm also interested in the amount of feedback the developers take, including redoing all of the god art and even redoing some Voice Acting, which couldn't have been easy only a few months from the full release, and I hope this remains active in the years to come.Overall, I can't reccomend this game more and if you're interested in trying out a classic or are interested in mythology or RTS games in general, I highly encourage you pick this up!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: a great Remaster for an often overlooked classicOn first look, the graphics have changed quite a bit. Not only in detail, which is expected for a Remaster, but in style. The colors are not as vibrant and bright as in the original, they seem mute and more realistic. The water is the best example, instead of a strong blue, it seems more like a grey-blue tone. It still looks good overall but definitely strikes a different tone than the original. I like the vibrant and bright graphics of the original, as almost every map had a positive mood.Gameplay is mostly unchanged; some units have their stats and/or costs changed for balance reasons. Some mechanics are changed or expanded, the Pharaoh of Ra can now enhance a monument, which in turn enhances all buildings in the vicinity. The Norse get two new units, the Hirdman is an anti-cavalry unit and the Godi fixes the lack of a range-hero unit.My biggest new feature is that every god power can be used multiple times. But not freely, the first usage is still free like in the original, afterwards you have to wait for cooldown and then pay favor to use them again. I really like this system; it encourages usage of the god powers while preventing a spam-fest. Cooldown and favor cost scale with the power and usefulness of a god power. Some god powers got some new utility, like Poseidon’s lure stone now also functions as drop off site for food.A big controversy is "Auto Everything": Back in the Titans expansion, a function for all buildings to automatically produce units was added, which was heavily discussed back then. It's back in Retold but modified. Every unit production can be automated by right clicking on the icon, but in the competitive multiplayer modes, it's deactivated by default. For villagers, it can be turned off in custom games, but enabled is also the default setting. I don't mind both options, as they have their downsides (and villager numbers are limited) and can be deactivated at least in custom games. What I dislike is that it is now also possible to queue techs and even age ups, even without having the necessary resources and they will be researched once they are accumulated. It cannot be deactivated and is a really powerful function, in my opinion outweighing the potential downside of taking resources for other things unintentionally. I wish the devs would add a function to be able to deactivate that as well.In terms of content, everything from the base game and its expansion pack is included. All gods, god powers, units and techs are available, with some additions to balance things. The additions from the Extended Edition are not included, which can be seen as a good thing as they are universally disliked. Chinese will feature in an already announced DLC and seem to be heavily reworked.Core of the game is the campaign, which is considered one of the all-time best campaigns in any RTS. "Fall of the Trident" includes all 34 missions, which are reconstructed closely to the originals, with some minor tweaks. Some of the difficulty spikes have been flattened a bit. Overall, it felt a bit more difficult than the original, most likely to offset the higher population cap and reusable god powers. Same goes for the smaller campaigns "The Golden Gift", which was a free bonus back in the day and "The New Atlantis" from the Titans expansion pack. They are solid campaigns, but quite a bit shorter, not reaching the same level of quality as the original one.Skirmish has all the things needed, all gods and maps from the base game are there. Some of the maps for skirmish and multiplayer are modified and those that are more game types like regicide are now turned into that, which can be played on any map. The new maps should be familiar to most Age fans, like Arena or Murkwood. 12 Players in a single match seems like a lot but ran smoothly for me thus far. Multiplayer seems solid, the problems with desyncs seem to be mostly fixed, but I hardly play any multiplayer and didn't encounter it myself in my limited testing.Overall, Age of Mythology Retold as a great remaster for an overlooked classic RTS. The new graphics are more detailed, I'm a bit indifferent about the change in style, but I also suffer greatly from nostalgia for the game. The changes to units make sense to balance things out, and I really like that god powers can be used multiple times. The price of 30€ (or your reginal equivalent) is in my opinion justified of the amount of content and upgrades. If you are a fan of classic RTS, especially Age of Empires, you should give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology Retold is a masterclass in game design, storytelling, and nostalgia. This beautifully crafted remake of the 2002 classic has exceeded my expectations in every way. The developers have skillfully updated the game while retaining its original charm, making it a must-play for both new and veteran players.The game's visuals are stunning, with vibrant environments, detailed character models, and impressive animations. The sound design is equally impressive, with an epic soundtrack and realistic sound effects that transport you to a world of myth and legend.Gameplay-wise, Age of Mythology Retold retains the addictive blend of resource management, base-building, and strategic combat that made the original so beloved. The new features and tweaks enhance the experience without overpowering it, making it feel both fresh and familiar.The campaign is engaging and well-paced, with memorable characters and storylines that draw you in. The multiplayer mode is equally enjoyable, with seamless matchmaking and a variety of game modes to suit different playstyles.Overall, Age of Mythology Retold is a triumph. It's a testament to the power of thoughtful game design and the enduring appeal of mythology and legend. If you're a fan of real-time strategy games, or just looking for an unforgettable gaming experience, do yourself a favor and dive into this incredible game.Pros:- Beautiful visuals and sound design- Engaging gameplay and campaign- Seamless multiplayer experience- Faithful to the original while introducing welcome updatesCons: NoneVerdict: Age of Mythology Retold is an instant classic that will captivate both old and new fans. _childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology has been a special game for me ever since I first played it as a kid. I remember being completely absorbed by its rich blend of mythology, strategy, and storytelling. Now with Age of Mythology: Retold, it feels like I’ve stepped back into that world but with a fresh coat of paint that makes everything even better.The magic of this game is how it brings the myths of the Greeks, Egyptians, and Norse to life. It’s not just about building armies and gathering resources; it’s about summoning gods, unleashing mythical creatures, and watching these legends play out on the battlefield. From calling down thunder as Zeus to sending Anubites into battle, every moment feels epic.What I love most about Retold is how it keeps everything I adored about the original, but adds just enough polish to make it feel modern. The updated graphics make the world look amazing, the UI tweaks make gameplay smoother, and overall it feels like I’m playing the game I loved, only better.There’s something so nostalgic yet exciting about diving back into the campaign with Arkantos, hunting down a cyclops, and saving Atlantis. Whether you’re a fan of the original like me, or discovering it for the first time, Age of Mythology: Retold is a perfect blend of nostalgia and mythological adventure. It’s more than just a strategy game—it’s a trip back to a world where gods and legends walk among mortals, and I couldn’t recommend it more.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm going to revise my negative review. After completing 80% of the Campaign under Titan Difficulty, The AI is still nasty, YES, always chasing your villagers and auto-spawn like hell, but I get it now: this is Age of Mythology, which is before chivalry was even invented, so I shouldn't expect my AI opponents to throw down their gauntlets like knights do. And nastiness is what the monsters in folklore are about - hell, where I come from, we even have a yaoguai that kidnaps kids for failing in exams, so I should call that "historical accuracy". The game often develops into a painful tug-of-war, YES - but that is because as an AOE 2 player, I just love to hit my keyboard 500 times to fill my units into the fray and call that a morning exercise, but AoM's villager-military ratio, unit movement speed etc. are so different that I simply can't play by old habits. Now I've found out the correct way of playing this game is protect your villagers, right-click to automate your unit production and control your heroes to focus fire on the powerful AI myth units - it doesn't feel half bad although my APM drops to noob level. All in all, AoM Retold is an enjoyable RTS with a lot welcomed change.  I keep my previous comment below to remember how I got infuriated by sucking at the game:=======================================================================I am a simple VS AI guy and I find AoM most annoying playing against higher difficulty AI among all the Age titles. The AIs' behaviors are so despicable that they always prioritize your villagers and settlements. The late game often develops into a slow-paced tug-of-war and, if you turn your attention elsewhere, e.g. to macro management or trying to deflect a base trade, which the AI often does, for five seconds, your units blindly chase moving villagers, break their formation completely and easily get picked out by enemy defenses. It's not like other Age titles don't have similar problems, but AoM just feels the worst to me for some reason. It should have been the most casual and fun one.

_childDocuments_.review: -Fantastic artstyle that stays true to the originals while also adding in new effects that don't pull away from the theme of the game-Gameplay loop is the same bar a few changes that make sense, such as the Wonder now allowing you to enter another age that makes your godpowers extremely strong-Units that previously were next to useless are now worth making, such as the healing units that Atlantis gets from one of their tech trees now having a group heal and a enemy debuff.-Introduction of a resource management system to auto-set your villagers is a great addition that allows you to micro more easily without losing track of where you left off-The much needed QoL features such as Titans not being useless on water maps and god powers being more than a one-time use are greatly welcomed and help to add depth to struggling Civ's due to their reliance on using a god power as a last resort.-The UI really needs to have some depth added to it, as at the moment it feels way too bare-bones-Certain UI elements feel like they were not sized, such as the minimap being raised away from two other bars, covering up an odd square of the screen that you can't change-Multiplayer is extremely unstable, out of the 4 games (Each upwards of an hour in length) that I've played with friends, we've had a d-sync on 3 of them, while the game has a recovery feature for this, I feel like it's almost a coinflip of if it'll happen or not so far.-During solo games the movement of units feels fluid and responsive, but online it feels like there is always at least half a second of delay between you clicking to move, and the unit moving. EE had this same issue and I was hoping it was down to an old game having its age show.-While I suspect that we'll find out down the line on what happened with the Chinese, so far there's been zero communication on where they went or what is happening with them, and personally I'd prefer people not have to buy a Civ yet again as DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, nostalgic, refreshing.Most people are familiar with this stellar RTS bursting forth from what is now a stale genre and it is massive fun to replay this classic title. The tweaks and reworks make this a joy to play but with some minor caveats. The AI will cheat, it will spawn inexplicable units from cleared areas, citing "A long way from home" in the Egyptian campaign as an example. Does it mar the experience ? not really, but it does make me shout "oh come on!"Graphics are gorgeous for an RTS, no hyperrealism here but charming and detailed. I cant comment on the voice acting because I skip most of the cutscenes. These games are about strategy not oscar winning dramatic scenes for me, and it is the strategy that holds the hook. I had no hesitation shelling out for the premium edition because AoM is just a quality experience and to have all the extras with it and early access, for me, it's a no brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: 🌟 Nostalgia-Fueled Godly Fun! 🌟Ah, Age of Mythology – the game that transported us to the lands of gods, mythological creatures, and devastatingly OP titans. If you were a fan of the original, you're in for a hearty dose of nostalgia. It’s like sitting by a warm hearth fire in Zeus’s living room, reminiscing about the days when you unleashed minotaurs and cyclopes on unsuspecting villagers. There’s something timeless about watching an army of heroic units and mythological beasts duke it out for supremacy, and it feels just as epic today as it did when I was a kid.But… oh mighty gods of Olympus, what has happened to the multiplayer?First, let me say this – yes, the game is awesome and very much worth the price of admission if you’re itching to ride that nostalgia train to glory. But be warned, brave warrior: the multiplayer experience is about as stable as a house of cards in a windstorm.🚪 Lobbies? Good luck finding them! The browser feels like a cluttered ancient scroll someone tossed into Pandora’s box – unorganized and chaotic. You’ll spend more time trying to find a game than you will actually playing it.🔄 Invites? Don’t get me started. It’s like the gods themselves are trolling you. You have to restart the game just to accept a friend’s invite, which, frankly, feels like trying to resurrect a dead hero over and over.📡 Connectivity issues? Oh, they’re there, looming over you like a vengeful god. Lag spikes, dropped connections, and an overall sense of “will this actually work?” – it’s a toll, folks.There are also a few bugs here and there. Nothing game-breaking, just the occasional weirdness that makes you wonder if Hermes is up to his usual tricks.Now, don’t let this scare you away entirely! The core gameplay is still as solid as the foundation of Mount Olympus itself. The single-player campaigns are beautifully nostalgic, the graphics are enhanced enough to please your eyes, and there’s still that sweet, sweet rush when you summon a god power and decimate your enemies.TL;DR: Age of Mythology is a gem, especially for those who have fond memories of its original glory days. However, if you’re planning to jump into multiplayer right away, you might want to wait for 1 or 2 patches for the gods to fix their meddling. But for the love of Zeus, it’s still worth grabbing if you’re ready to relive the mythic chaos. 🎮Recommended? ✅ But maybe let the gods patch the multiplayer first.Edit: Most of the bugs were fixed, multiplayer is really playable at this pointEdit 2: Arena Of The Gods was really underbaked, sad.

_childDocuments_.review: The remastered Age of Mythology brings back the nostalgic charm of the classic strategy game with updated graphics, engaging gameplay, and a captivating storyline that draws from various mythologies. The campaign and scenario missions are fun and immersive, offering both strategic depth and mythical wonder. For long-time fans of the original and newcomers alike, the game provides hours of entertaining play with an enjoyable mix of resource management, base-building, and mythological battles.However, the graphical improvements, while noticeable, don’t shine unless you have a high-end graphics card. On mid-tier setups, the visuals can feel average, which might slightly dampen the experience for some players. Despite this, the game’s core mechanics and design remain strong, and I still highly recommend it to any fan of strategy games looking for a mythologically rich experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently not worth 30 bucks. It's barely 'retold' with the same cheesy dialogue (which may be a plus for some for nostalgia), paper thin characters and little story point in doing optional objectives. There's some bugs fixed from the original, but a lot that are still present and a lot of new ones like not being able to unload troops from transports reliably. The Titan difficulty level is...not really that hard anymore. Maybe I've gotten better at the game since I first played it, but most of the Titan level missions are just kinda a slog rather than hard. The AI just hyperfocuses villagers which makes them very easy to beat. Your own units will focus enemy units rather than buildings that are attacking them and have to be manually tasked to attack production buildings, otherwise they will just focus constantly spawning new units and never make progress. I was hoping for a much bigger upgrade for being a 'retold' edition. Wait for it to go on sale or just play the original if you have it. The graphics upgrade isn't much.

_childDocuments_.review: I may be very biased as this is potentially my favourite video game of all time, the one that I grew up with as a child and the one that I never stopped playing 20 years later. But the "Retold" version of Age of Mythology is worth every single cent. So much love has been put in this game, so much good work in every aspect, in a successful attempt to recreate a game that is loved by so many and has such a loyal fanbase. I did not expect that AoM would ever be revived, let alone in such pride and glory. Thanks to each and every dev and I sincerely hope that the game will be supported for years to come!A few notes:- The graphics are amazing, so realistic and at the same time, if I hadn't been playing the OG game since release, it would be just as how I remembered it. No unecessary changes and such beautiful additions! I have no complaints whatsoever!-  Freyr is such a well-made and interesting addition, a unique main god to play with!- Best video-game soundtrack, I keep the main menu open even when I do not play just to listen to it!- Looking forward to discovering more mythical battles, potentially! Reginleif's Rally was great and challenging!ARKANTOS HAS AWAKEN!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR If you want this to still feel like Age of Mythology, you'll be disappointed. If you love the Age of Empires series as a whole, you'll probably like this. I *really* wanted to like this game. I love the OG Age of Mythology and the extended edition and have nearly 400 hours of game play. I was hoping this would be an updated version with better graphics, more maps, maybe some changes to the god benefits or gods, etc. Instead, they stripped the game of most of the ways it was different from the Age of Empires series. It is now just like the other Age of Empires but with an additional layer of complexity (god powers and myth units). IMO, what made Age of Mythology stand out was how it differed from the AE series. The remake feels disingenuous to the original Age of Mythology in favor of a series that already has like four editions!!! For some people, bringing Retold into the AE series game-feel will probably help. For me, it ruined the game and ultimately I requested a refund. Luckily I love Age of Mythology Extended Edition, and will happily continue playing. And honestly, for a game that is 20 years newer than the original Age of Mythology, the graphics just aren't all that.

_childDocuments_.review: AoMR is an excellent re-telling of Age of Mythology and a very welcomed addition to the series in so many ways!+ PROS + +++++++++ Improved Modern Graphics+ Really Good Storytelling+ Really Fun Gameplay+ Lots of nice looking Units+ Several Campaign Missions+ Skirmishes+ Titans are back+ God Powers are so much fun to play with and reusable too+ Multiplayer+ Bonus Points to devs for adding Controller Support+ Steam Achievements+ Game is getting 2 Expansions later- CONS - ----------- I wish that AoMR was retold in a similar method to AoE4 which would have made it a lot better- Not much gameplay right now, feels very lackluster and pails in comparison to AoE4- No WASD Panning Hotkey Support which should be a default for any RTS game for quick on the fly panning on map and it makes absolutely no sense why devs don't do that- There's a setting for Autoresource Control after aging up your Towncenter is not as helpful as it seems, often times, it will render your setup useless and will often really mess with your economy if you're not careful so then you have to either try again or set it back to None and fix it yourself, very frustrating and not as helpful as it could be- Units will often stand around doing nothing even with Enemies getting very close, default should be defensive if nothing else is happening and I sure as heck don't remember this ever being a problem in the other AoE games- Villagers will often get stuck on rocks trying to get trees and resources they'll never even be able to reach- Game Difficulty is unbalanced, Medium is not really challenging enough yet playing on Hard is almost Impossible= VERDICT ============= AoMR has a few big problems that will hopefully be improved upon and addressed in the near future but overall the game is outstanding and very fun to play just like the original! I strongly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best remake I have ever seen for a game. They took the original concept and improved upon it in many ways:1) Myth units and God powers now play much more significant role than before due to GP reusability, increased population cap, reduced myth unit population requirement, myth units now improves with each upcoming age, so your Sphinxes or Cyclops are not waste of population space in Mythic age.2) There are quality of life features that helps total beginners(villager allocation etc.) get a grasp of the game, but its not so good to make it a habbit to rely on it.3) Gods, units, techs, favor gathering etc. have been reworked. The game is similar enough to old AoM, but improved enough to feel fresh and new. This game has seen so much attention, has had so many changes and improvements, that they could had easily presented this as AoM2.Campaign.Voice acting is hit or miss - Arkantos original voice actor reworked his lines, so it sounds awesome, but on the other end is the old man Theocrat Krios, who sounds like 25 year old, and Gargarensis, who lacks the depth of the voice original voice actor had.Campaign levels are improved and in some cases quite different. They look better, surroundings are more purposeful, and some of the old cheese options do not work anymore.I highly recommend the game for everyone who is interested in RTS games. There are features for beginners(unit autoqueue, villager auto-allocation), the game has been reworked so well that it should please nostalgia players, and it is different from other Age games that more established RTS players could find it interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: not fit for release, the game feels rushed. it's straight up impossible to get into any multiplayer lobbies and the multiplayer menu is counter-intuitive. once you've spent over a hour trying to join a game, you'll be lucky to see it to the end because of desync. while the graphical updates are impressive, some of them (especially the appearance of upgraded myth units) are direct copies of workshop items in Age of Mythology: Extended Edition. voice acting was never checked for quality, so some lines blare while others are quiet, and overall they're not as good as in the original. for the game that has my favorite soundtrack of all time, which is hailed as one of the best video game soundtracks of all time, the strictly electronic cover of the organic, natural music of Age of Mythology, with no option to switch to the original soundtrack, is the biggest sin of all. this release gives the impression that the entire game has been ripped from it's original aesthetic and vision that Age of Mythology's original developers had - a commonplace occurrence in "remastered" games, resulting in a product that feels gentrified. i do however like the push to make Age Of Mythology more linear with Age of Empires within unit stats and counters, but please do something about the disgusting HUD. the game does have "mods", but they are strictly on the game itself, not on the steam workshop, and from my experience a majority of them are broken. either way, RIP Ensemble Studios.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I'm a little biased and maybe rightfully so since this was game was one of the center pieces of my childhood. I played through the campaign almost every year at least once. (Don't look at my Steam hours played since back in the day we took the "arrgh" way). I bought the Premium edition pre-release so I got to play it earlier and even though I wholeheartedly recommend it there are things that just don't sit well with me with this version.I will only mention the negatives since I would bet that 90% of sales will be made up of people who already own the original or have at least played it in the past.The cons:- VOICE ACTINGIt's just bad. There's no other way to say. - IN-GAME CUTSCENESThey added these "hand drawn" images of characters that are just off putting and the animations of actual 3D models in those cutscenes have taken a toll. They used to be ok, you could tell what was going on and they had more charm than they do now.- AUTO-QUEUE / AUTO-BUILD unitsI don't like it, I don't believe it has any meaning or adds anything in an RTS of this kind. "I don't want to click an icon every time I want to make a villager". Well then what's the whole point?- I'm not even sure what they call this but they added a "VILLAGER DISTRIBUTION PIE CHART" where you just click it and it automatically sends all villagers to gather a certain thing. For example I think the first AGE focuses more on FOOD and WOOD and very little GOLD. But as the ages advance they require more GOLD and less FOOD, so you would just click a PIE CHART and it would redistribute all villagers to fit that. I think that diminishes everything in an RTS and it makes me feel completely devastated and I can't even explain why. But it just sucks all enjoyment for the genre in whole out of me. Again, I am not sure why. Maybe I'm scared that this is the way RTS's are going since we didn't get a single good RTS game ever since SC2. AoE4 just didn't get it. Overall I really like the game still I just wish these things that I mentioned would be improved or taken out of the game. And before people attack me "oh you just want an APM game", no you really don't get it. I have never been a professional RTS player nor have I ever played competitively online or even ranked games and I don't consider myself very good since HARD is usually way too hard for me but come on - the whole point of RTS games is resource management and army building. And you're taking away resource management and adding auto-queue for army building. You're basically making a MOBA game but worse, since you don't have lanes and you don't play as cool heroes with cool powers.Short rant aside - yes, it's still worthwhile to play through the campaign and get some online matches in with friends. What we usually do with AoE2 is my brothers and my dad we pick a huge map and we play vs AI. 4v4 or 3v3 and we love it. Maybe we can do the same with AoM since it is my favorite of the Age of games.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game as a kid. I feel like I've been awaiting the release of AoM:R for at least four ages. It was my favorite in the franchise along with 3 growing up. I have very fond memories of the campaign, although I hadn't played it in nearly 20 years.As a remaster, Retold is fine. The new graphics preserve the art style of the original fairly well, but they don't look especially good on their own. I think AoE3DE looked better, honestly, but overall the new features and improvements are welcome. I don't really understand why they bothered to redo the VO, but you can replace it with a single click in the mod menu.But I deeply regret buying this, esp. in "Advanced Access," having now completed the main campaign. AoM's campaign has not held up. It's a toilet paper-thin story chaining together boring, repetitive macro missions where you spend 15+ minutes building up a base, again and again, before steamrolling the enemy. The missions are ludicrously overtuned, to the point that two felt impossible to me; I'm not the best RTS player in the world, but I've never seriously had difficulty beating any mission in AoE3, Dawn of War, WC3, or SC2: AoM is a whole different question. This difficulty didn't feel challenging. It felt unfair, every time. While I'm trying to secure a tree in the center of the map, I'm swarmed by mummies and elephant spam--with almost no time to prepare. After securing the forge and figuring the mission was over, more fire giants than I can possibly deal with spawn in--on the other side of the map, where I can't get to them in time to kill them before I lose the mission. Combined with the excessive macro components of every mission, it's just a miserable slog. The campaign is way overlong, with way too many missions, and in the end, the story is unbelievably shallow compared to AoE3 or WC3. AoE is obviously a macro-centric series. But campaign missions where you have to spend so long building up your base feel pointless. On mission 31, I built up my economy, then won fairly easy after I had everything in order. On mission 32, I immediately had to do it all over again. Nothing really had changed: there was no serious challenge. It was the same thing, all over. This drove me crazy. And if it wasn't for nostalgia, I would have given up after the Greek campaign ended.If you're competitive and interested in multiplayer, I'm sure AoM: Retold is a great deal, and you'll probably have a ton of fun playing online. But if you wanted to relive the campaign like I did, and you only are interested in singleplayer, I cannot possibly recommend this game to you. I really regret buying it. I haven't enjoyed my time with it at all.Edit: Having moved on to the Atlantean campaign, my memory held true in that it is VASTLY superior to the main campaign. The story and level design are infinitely superior; it's way more fun. I'm still not sure I can recommend this game for full price, but it might be worth picking up for the bonus stories.

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly the quintessential instance of "nailing" a remaster / remake. The game is not only fun and attracting loads of attention, it is more or less successful in every way that remakes and remasters try to be: The developers managed to update the game to make the UI and gameplay smoother; it expands beyond the scope of the original - there are 2 expansions coming out, and changes to date have been largely (except some overall minor content removed) welcomed, and will be followed by 2 pantheons ; meanwhile, the game balance feels great ; the game feels fun like it did as a kid in 2004 - it's really hard to fully articulate this accurately, but they have clearly done something right ; the hands-down most impressive aspect for me was the initial look, feel and impression. Very rarely does one pick up a remake of a 20 year old game and feel nearly the same experience that they did the first time they played it. But they really deliver this in AoM. Most remarkable for me personally, the game looked new like it did in 2003, the graphics feel sleek as they did back then, yet simultaneously, they  do not stray from the style or look of the originals.This is a departure from many remakes and ports over the last few years. AoM really delivers. While many PC remakes and ports were worse than the originals, AoM manages superbly to present a very rare, very unique juxtaposition: better, newer, and with more content than the original, while feeling identical. I cannot think of a single remake or remaster which manages this.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology Retold: A Classic RevitalizedThe announcement of Age of Mythology Retold sparked both excitement and concern among fans of the original 2002 game. Could this reimagining capture the magic of the beloved classic? After hours immersed in its mythical worlds, the answer is a resounding yes.Stunning Visuals That Honor the OriginalThe game’s visual overhaul is breathtaking. This isn’t just a remaster; it’s a thoughtful reimagining of a classic. Landscapes are vibrant and alive, with dynamic lighting and intricate details that bring rivers, temples, and mythological creatures to life. Iconic units like the Minotaur and Frost Giant are rendered in stunning detail, making them feel both nostalgic and fresh. The game masterfully balances modern graphical fidelity with the charm of the original aesthetic.Gameplay: Familiar Yet RefinedAt its core, Age of Mythology Retold stays true to its roots. The unique gameplay mechanics of the Greek, Norse, and Egyptian civilizations remain intact, preserving their distinct mythological flavor. Yet, the game is peppered with enhancements that make the experience more fluid and engaging.Improved AI: Enemies adapt to your strategies with a newfound sharpness, keeping the challenge alive.Quality-of-Life Improvements: Refined hotkeys, improved pathfinding, and intuitive controls streamline gameplay without sacrificing depth.Fresh Mythological Content: New additions keep the game exciting for longtime fans while enticing newcomers to explore its rich world.Aural ExcellenceThe re-recorded soundtrack, performed by a full orchestra, elevates the game’s atmosphere. Familiar tunes are brought to life with an epic scale, while voiceovers retain their nostalgic charm, now presented with enhanced clarity.Multiplayer and Community FeaturesMultiplayer receives a significant upgrade, offering stable, streamlined matchmaking for online battles. For the creative community, robust modding tools open up endless possibilities, ensuring Age of Mythology Retold remains vibrant for years to come.Final ThoughtsAge of Mythology Retold is far more than a simple remaster—it’s a heartfelt tribute to a timeless classic. By blending nostalgia with modern design, the game is a must-play for strategy enthusiasts and mythology lovers alike. Whether you’re a veteran or new to the series, this revitalized journey into mythological warfare is worth your time.Rating: 9.5/10The gods have smiled upon this reimagining, delivering a game worthy of its legendary status.

_childDocuments_.review: After I've sunk my teeth into this for 60 hours at the time of this review, I can say that this is an excellent remake, and a strong recommendation for newcomers and experienced RTS fans alike.  Stepping into Retold has been an absolute treat.  Everything feels buttery smooth, and I've not experienced anything like the lag which plagued multiplayer in the Extended Edition.  The game just feels *good* to play and control.  'Retold' is simultaneously the game we know and love, but also something new.  The altering and re-balancing of pretty much everything, from Major God bonuses, to individual units, will require some relearning, making things feel fresh even if you're an Age of Mythology veteran.The developers truly had a strong vision for how to make the 'Mythology' part of 'Age of Mythology' shine; and the game feels like such a letter of love not just to the original game, but to the mythologies that inspired it in the first place.  The campaign remains a highlight of the game, and took me dozens of hours to complete (including the campaign from The Titans expansion).  Whether you are after the challenge of Titan difficulty (which is no joke), or want a more chill time with an easier difficulty, you'll have a great time with this iconic campaign, with its levels rebuilt and redesigned from the ground-up in the new engine. Many visuals in the campaign have been drastically altered, pretty much all for the better!  This feels like what the original developers intended, but didn't have the budget or technology to realise in 2002.  For example, Niflheim, the Norse underworld, originally used the same 'volcanic/lava' tileset as the Greek Erebus.  But now in Retold, they've done justice to the icy realm that it is in the mythology.The asking price is surprisingly low for a modern-day remake, and the Premium Edition seems like a complete steal; if the two upcoming expansion packs are produced with the same level of quality as the base game.  It's a great time to be an Age of Mythology fan; it's almost surreal that we're getting brand-new expansion packs!With gorgeous new in-game art, reuseable god powers that create interesting decisions with Favor spending, new upgrades and balance changes that alter the dynamic of pre-existing units, updated controls, and new UI functionality with lots of customisation, (and more!), this is the definitive way to play Age of Mythology.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Mythology: Retold is an absolute triumph, breathing new life into the beloved classic while preserving all the magic that made the original so iconic. As someone who fondly remembers playing the original back in the early days, I was excited to see how the remastered version would shape up... and it certainly doesn’t disappoint!From the very first game, it’s clear that the developers have put in significant effort to enhance the visuals. The updated graphics are stunning, with beautifully reworked textures and intricate details that bring the mythological world to life like never before. The environments, character models, and animations are all crisp and vibrant, yet they still retain the charm of the original art style. Whether you're exploring the ancient Egyptian deserts, Greek temples, or Norse fjords, everything feels rich and immersive.The gameplay remains as captivating as ever. The core mechanics of real-time strategy, blending resource management, army building, and mythological abilities, have been perfectly preserved. For newcomers, Age of Mythology is as engaging and accessible as it was when it first launched (but of course, I recommend playing the campaign first to get a grip on things), while long-time fans will appreciate the polished updates and improvements. The gods and mythical creatures still add a thrilling layer of strategy, and the addition of new content (like the inclusion of The Titans expansion right from the start) offers even more depth and replayability. Also with a plan to revive the 5th race which were the Chinese (they were the added DLC race in the old game which was a total miss, and a quick money grab from the SkyBox studio, but I hope with these new devs we can expect something cool).The remastered audio is another highlight—new sound effects and a refined soundtrack make the game feel comfy, wild, immersive and just awesome (although I like the original soundtrack better without the tweaking the new has). The voice acting needs more work done (or maybe my nostalgia can't replace the old voice actors with the new ones), atleast they brought the voice actor of the original Arkantos :). The improved UI is sleek and intuitive, allowing for a smoother gaming experience overall.Multiplayer matches are as exciting as ever, offering a perfect mix of competitive and cooperative play. The game’s online community is vibrant, with a variety of modes to keep things fresh. Whether you’re playing a quick skirmish or a lengthy campaign, Age of Mythology: Retold ensures that there’s never a dull moment.Overall, Age of Mythology: Retold strikes the perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation. It takes everything that made the original a timeless classic and gives it a modern upgrade without losing the spirit of the game. Whether you’re a long-time fan or a newcomer to the franchise, this remastered edition is a must-play! It’s a testament to the enduring appeal of Age of Mythology and a shining example of how to bring a classic into the modern era.
