_childDocuments_.review: Hi, yes. I like this. It's an easy recommend for me, and I bought the DLC after about 20 hours to happily support the devs.If you're wondering if you might like this, some info that might help:I got here after a period bout of playing school management games (more recently,  and ), and this is better than any of those. This feels really satisfying to progress in.For more , this reminds me of  (one of my all-time favorites) and , maybe even , partly because of its visual design, yes, and partly because it really does simplify many things quite well. But it's also better than any of those if you like to be able to engage in more depth with things without getting to the complexity level of, say, . I'd tentatively say it's around  levels of complexity and depth, deeper when it comes to people management, a slight bit less when it comes to building optimization.This game manages the tricky balance of having a wealth of things to do and manage, a bunch of systems it allows you to engage deeper into, without ending up at a micromanaging hell that needs you to skip between a bunch of UIs all the time to try to figure out what the hell you have going on and that you want to do. It avoids the building and management creep the further you progress in career mode as well, which I love.One thing that is a shame is that it doesn't explain all that is available very well or in deep enough depth - for example, what's the meaning of a student's Club Skill and which stat influences victory during competitions? If I assign a teacher to be a Student Club's Coach, which skill matters more, their teaching ability or management ability? (You'll notice a bunch of these questions I have are about Clubs, because that's what I've been focusing on most, but there's more: how do I get butterflies, nevermind catch them, for this romantic student? How does weight affect students and staff both, if at all? So there's a lot that is happening, and not all of it is completely clear to its full depth. A Game Wiki that explains these things would be awesome. The lack of this hasn't ruined my experience, and the Steam discussion boards are a good source of info, but particularly for players that really thrive of min-maxing optimization, it could be more annoying than it has been for me (which isn't that much). Overall, you do not *need* to engage with the depth if you don't want to (you may however need to adjust your expectations as to how far you can take your school, or change some difficulty settings).Speaking of which, difficulty settings are fairly customizeable to a great degree, you can be min-max sweaty or chill nbd with a lot of freedom. It just may take a couple interrupted runs to understand how each setting may impact your playthrough (given the aforementioned lack of clarity on some things).Couple other notes: sound design is nice, I haven't disabled the music or anything else at all 30hrs in (a true rarity). Bugs are rare, and I didn't experience any game-breaking ones (just had to save and reload a handful of times when selecting things wouldn't register). Features like headmaster mode remind me of classic iconic games where you get to just walk around things you've built. There are a few different "mini-games" that mark the progress of time, which really helps break up the flow enough to prevent monotony from setting in - but thankfully these don't overstay their welcome, and are really just kind of a cute addition that I can appreciate.An important bit. Building is generally satisfying and easy, and you're able to upgrade existing built things without tearing them down to build newly researched ones from the get-go, which is great. One thing I wish there was is a Stash feature for buildings and/or rooms. I'd like to be able to move full rooms and try ways to fit them together with more freedom without having to build an empty building space big enough to hold a room just because I want to fit things together differently. Otherwise, the level of customizing you're able to unlock to build cool buildings is quite impressive - I'm not much of a builder in that sense myself, but I can easily see folks being able to pull off massive and impressive builds. In Career mode, there's a neat curve to the types of structures you unlock and how much you can customize them - at its end (or in Sandbox mode), you have a deceptively simple toolbox with a lot more parts and customization to it than you might realize unless looking further into it.As a "not that much of a builder" person, the fact that this has made me *want* to try to make cooler impressive buildings is pretty impressive. The initially generated buildings when you start up a new school have some inspiring features.Lastly,  is not a strict nightmare. So long as your buildings and rooms have accessible entries (accessible meaning reachable from outside), you can glue things right next to each other and trust that characters know and are able to move between things reasonably. This is more rare than it should be in management games of this size. This means you can make chock-full rooms without the irrationality of needing to account for the inability of a character to move in between a desk and its chair. If you do ever have a problem with a character getting stuck, the game notifies you and you can reset them with a single click. Nice!So, overall: a lot of QoL fit together, more depth than you'd think available so long as you bother to engage with the different things that exist, and an unfortunate lack of clarity on some specifics. Quite fun with a solid gameplay loop that can give you a challenge if you want it to, or be a chill pal to progress through. It's also surprisingly funny at times, not taking itself too seriously but allowing you to get invested in your students, clubs, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and fun game that probably should've been put to early access first. If you like city builders and other management sims, this'll be worth the 20 bucks for 15-20 hour run, but the game feels unfinished. Not in a "this is an unplayable glitchy mess," but more in the sense that it clearly has content and QoL that has yet to be added.-The game talks about clubs, but they're being added in a later update. Obviously this will change later, but it felt very weird to have a ton of facilities and sports available and not being able to make any clubs or sports teams,-Auto-teach AI is terrible, often forcing me to rearrange the schedule anyway to accommodate for some students' needs-Headmaster and Ms. Lin can only ever raise their proficiency to around 40 before they become a waste of time and resources. Considering how prominent and present they both are, it would feel better to have a way for them to raise their training threshold or just simply start them at a higher base.-The default refund value for stuff is 80% for some reason?? If you misplace something that's just a net loss of money. 100% should be the default-Only two locations, and one of them has the headmaster's office in a very awkward location behind the school-Rooms often have size requirements that do not match the actual room you need for them (the debate room is a big example)-Game doesn't punish you for filling rooms with nonsense in order to satisfy needs and aesthetic requirements, potentially leading to situations where you have immensely cramped areas if you're concerned with preserving as much space as you can (which you'll want to do early on)-Tons of bugs still need to be patched, even after hotfixes.Overall very fun and addicting game, but I did not feel like I was playing the full experience. I am praying this review ages like milk in a hot car because this is genuinely a very fun experience, but one I don't want to replay until more content is added.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful school simulator that puts you in the shoes of a headmaster striving to create a top-notch educational institution. Here's my take on this charming game:The game immediately put you in a warm and cozy atmosphere. The graphics and overall design contribute to a relaxing gaming experience. It's the kind of game that makes you feel at ease as you start building and managing your dream school.I love Let's School's simplicity. The mechanics are easy to grasp, there's no steep learning curve, and you can jump right into the fun without feeling overwhelmed.This game successfully combines the strategic elements of a tycoon game with the joy of building and managing a school. It keeps you engaged with a perfect balance of challenge and enjoyment. From creating classrooms to organizing extracurricular activities, every aspect of running a school is thoughtfully integrated into the gameplay.My only minor complaint is the limited map options. I found myself wishing for more landscapes and additional areas to expand my school. I hope the developers consider adding more maps in future updates!Let's School is a gem in the school simulation genre. I look forward to seeing how the game evolves with future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Academia School Simulator or the Kairosoft school game and found them wanting, then I have good news for you - this game totally surpasses it in every way.  Now it's worth mentioning that this is more of an Asian school system, so for us Americans we might find a few things odd (tea room?, no student lockers, students stay in a classroom and teachers rotate), but this is honestly one of the most satisfying simulators that I've played in a long time.  There is a good balance between micro- and macro-management.  The tone of the game feels optimistic, but isn't cheesy, which I've come to enjoy.Play the demo to get a good feel for the game, but realistically, at the low price that they're asking, this game is more than fairly priced.  What's more is that the developers have been pretty active in listening and responding to feedback, which I find surprisingly refreshing.  I think you'll be as pleasantly surprised as I was with this game.For the future, I'd hope to see maybe some sort of DLC or update that adds some American school flavoring (probably scheduling).

_childDocuments_.review: "Disappointing Micromanagement Overwhelms the Fun."Let's School presents itself as a charming and visually appealing game, but unfortunately, beneath its quirky exterior lies a frustrating amount of micromanagement. As a fan of simulators, I was eager to immerse myself in its world, only to find myself bogged down by excessive tasks that felt more like chores than enjoyable gameplay.The visuals are undoubtedly a highlight, with a unique art style that adds charm to the game. However, this aesthetic appeal can only carry Let's School so far when the gameplay itself becomes a tedious exercise in micromanagement. From managing schedules to overseeing every minute detail, the game's insistence on micromanaging every aspect of the experience quickly becomes overwhelming.As someone who enjoys simulation games for their immersive and strategic gameplay, Let's School falls short by focusing too heavily on micromanagement at the expense of enjoyment. Rather than feeling like a fulfilling simulator experience, it feels more like a burdensome chore, detracting from the potential fun that could be had.While Let's School may appeal to some players who enjoy the minutiae of management sims, for those seeking a more balanced and engaging gameplay experience, it ultimately misses the mark. Unless you have a high tolerance for micromanagement, this game may leave you feeling frustrated and disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Watched too much Japanese anime? Got a hankering to build an authentic anime school? Then this is the game for you - but it's remarkably a lot better than the premise to boot.Think Theme Hospital in a school setting, except they've worked out how to enable multiple floors and the students don't get Bubble Head. Management is a case of juggling timetables and activities, ensuring enough classrooms and specialist facilities (eg: chemistry labs, toilets, staff room and so on) exist to fill the needs of the teaching and then filling the remaining space with cleaning supplies. Some aspects are a little clunky, especially class management, but once you understand the Japanese system of three years, each denoted with a number, and then classes having a number afterwards,  it makes more sense (so 1-1 means the first class of the first year, 3-4 is the fourth class of third year).Building is probably most of the fun, along with the usual wait for research unlocks. Most of the environments are charming in their own way, with a unified aesthetic that works well, but the inability to interior decorate does grate a little, especially as the available carpets look so bad. I've also yet to work out whey pupils and staff will just walk through fences...What Let's School nails is the "one more minute" hook of the management genre. It's 1am before you realise it's time to go bed, with just one more cycle tempting you. For the price, it's an excellent little game with a few ongoing bugs and issues, but if you like management sims this'll scratch the itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I found Let's School to be an engaging and highly addictive management game that cleverly weaves in a perfect mix of creativity, strategy, and decision-making. I was constantly caught in the intriguing web of managing my virtual school and lost track of time more than once while playing.The freedom to design and structure your educational institution, along with the extensive range of educational equipment to choose from, promotes a sense of inventiveness that is both challenging and delightful. This unique aspect of the game successfully stimulates the players' urge to continually enhance and upgrade their facilities.The feature that sets Let's School apart is the diverse personalities of the students. The need to balance their various interests, meet their essential needs, and maintain the school's reputation proved to be a richly layered and satisfyingly intricate task. Overseeing the teachers' recruitment, teaching methodologies, and personal progression, added another level of engaging complexity.The detailed and well-planned discipline system of Let's School requires you to keep a watchful eye on your students, ensuring a safe and healthy learning environment. Handling real-world issues like absenteeism and bullying adds a touch of reality, making the gameplay even more immersive.The game's unique ways of representing student stress, such as the surge in eyeglass usage and weight issues, were an ingenious touch. Ensuring adequate sanitary facilities was another critical aspect of the game that added realism and a sense of urgency to my management role.The game's appealing aspect is the constant desire to add more furniture and refine the aesthetic appeal of the school. Offering elective courses and running various school events provide a meaningful impact on students' lives, which was rewarding and fulfilling.In conclusion, Let's School is a standout management game that impresses with its immersive gameplay, in-depth detail, and challenging school-running mechanics. It's an engrossing experience that you won't be able to put down for hours. A must-try for any strategy or management game aficionado who relishes a challenging yet rewarding creative endeavor.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games. Perfects the "room builder" genre with high customization and strong creative challenge. Very immersive, and different every time I play. And the artstyle is both detailed and adorable! Campaign mode is the perfect difficulty (with options to change it, of course) and the sandbox is so much fun. Unfortunately, there are some bugs. Most are small but sometimes I have to restart the game. Usually only if it's on for too long, and I've never lost a save file or had it corrupt from bugs. Restarting has always fixed the problem :)The translation is overall fantastic, but some inconsistencies in the tutorial made it hard to follow at first. After I understood, though, the game feels very smooth and easy to play. Game recently added more clubs via workshop support, which was my #1 want for the game. Yay! Now the thing I most want to be added is more maps & different starting building shapes. Looking forward to more DLC and updates but I'm happy with what's in the game now as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty decent game if you like management games and/or want a creative outlet for building and designing your own school. Art and graphics are cute, evocative and fairly atmospheric. I'd love some more ambient sounds effects like school children laughing though. There is a fair amount of awkwardly written English and missing spaces between words. It's not a good look for a finished game. I'm also not a fan of event where you need to hunt down hidden stuff in your school or events that need you to assign teachers like kids gaming (except world map), but these are minor things. _childDocuments_.review: This game was an enjoyable High School Simulation game that allows you to recreate your highschool experience.In all fairness it's more tailored to what I imagine Asian Highschool life is like and didn't really reflect the Australia Highschool system, but that being said I was able to use my IRL knowledge to help me problem solve throughout the playthrough which made this game pretty interesting.The game isn't that hard. Even in difficult mode I was able to finish the game pretty easily. That being said the challenge of this game was satisfying my OCD when it comes to class timetables teacher management and optimal classroom building and layout.I started playing the game pretty much the day it was released and in the short window I've already seen some good updates to the game. I definitely feel like this is a title too keep an eye on. That being said, if Simulation games are you're thing, its worth checking out.- In the future I would like to see better use of the "Teaching Policy" feature. Currently it resets the class study plan every new intake. The problem is the "auto" feature can over-train your students forcing you to research new curriculum to keep your students busy. More control over the pace in which the subjects are taught in general would be nice, but even just saving presets that you can copy and paste every semester would be nice.- Most other issues I can think of are probably just a reflection of the games early development, like the "earthquake" design having no impact and barely even noticeable if you arent looking for it. I've seen the developers are already working on changing this though so I don't think its a big deal.- More meaningful interactions with the other schools might be nice. Or a way to revive a fallen school would be good. Esp if you want their legendary teacher, but the school closed before you could afford them. I could list a bunch of potential improvements, but this isn't to say that the game isn't good as it is.All in all, its a solid simulation game and theres a demo as well if you're on the fence about if you want to play it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo and am ecstatic about the launch! *Gameplay Controls*Pros- Relatively easy and there are keyboard shortcuts that are pretty universal across PC games. Intuitive in nature if you have played similar time management games. Clear icons assist with easy navigation and multiple pathways to get to the same core components of the management pieces of the game. There is tons of space and clear systems within each “area” (e.g., building, building schedules, research, etc.). There is a straightforward “Headmaster’s Manual” that gives additional context.Cons- The responsiveness of mouse clicks on people is an intermittent problem. I’ve clicked on people and their individual profile card doesn’t come up. Sometimes clicking someone else and clicking back to that person works, sometimes it doesn’t. *Graphics*Pros- Personally, I love this art style and the clean and simple items make it easy to know exactly what and where everything is at a quick glance. Clear icons that pop up and hover over different rooms/areas really help when looking across the entire map. Cons- The characters do not abide by the laws of physics (walking through barriers (e.g., fences and railings, cutting through staircases) a.k.a shortest route.*Objectives*Pros- The game gives the player the option for objectives and has very clear tracking systems and multiple built-in objectives and rewards (like all students passing exams)! This provides layers to the gameplay, keeping you hooked. Reaching objectives involves lots of research and the research dependencies and rewards are cool and a part of the planning process for your gameplay.Cons- N/A. Expanded or new objectives in the distant future would be great.*Replay ability*Pros – Simply, yes. You can create and do whatever you want, you could play for a lifetime if you wanted.Cons- N/A*Difficulty*Pros – You can customize your game for the difficulty level of your choosing but the game by itself is a welcomed challenge. Making sure the people management, schedules, and facilities are up to standard is the core part of the game. Expanded aspects include exploring locations near your school, building relationships, promoting, and securing new admissions, etc.   Cons- Only teachers can be hired- which means having teachers assume the facility roles (cafes, security, researchers, storekeepers, etc.). It would be nice to have teachers and facility staff to improve the immersion.*Building Mechanics*Pros – YOU CAN JUST CLICK OR LONG HOLD THINGS AND MOVE THEM DIRECTLY IN LIVE GAME WITHOUT HAVING TO PAUSE OR EVEN GO TO BUILD MODE. If you have been playing any type of build games for a long time, you know this is a great feature. It is so simple to build and there really isn’t much else to it. Like with most games, it tells you what is required within the objects area, and you can search for items as well. Cons- Unable to shrink facility zones (the actual standalone building structure), made planning structures a bit more difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this not expecting much. Couple crashes and glitches, some mechanics not working right or worse. Imagine my surprise when this is actually a perfectly workable game. There are some weird things here and there and some room for improvements, but it's functional and quite fun.Starting a sandbox game without any prior knowledge, apart from having been to school myself, it's not impossible to grasp. There is even a minor tutorial of sorts in the sandbox, but just clicking through the various windows and resolving the problems the game informs you about teaches you most you need. It's not all intuitive, but most of it is and despite some mechanics being a bit overly micromanagement it can be handled if you pay attention.There is a slight imbalance between some mechanics being overly deep and others being a bit shallow. The whole wonders you can build I don't get what they are meant for, they don't seem to get used at all, much like the outdoor things. That you have to water your staff to make them work effectively is a bit strange, especially when they require water specifically and not just a vending machine for soda. Though the problem with that is more down to the way the build menu is organized and structured, lacking a bit in overview when you constantly have to scroll. This could really benefit some ui scale slider to reduce the ui scale and make more space in the build menu to show more items at once or add more categories.Hoping for a two more subjects making it in at some point so it's not just 4, which seems a bit lackluster compared to the rest of the game. Also the finance view needs a redesign, it's basically impossible to tell at a glance what is costing you money and what brings it in, even collapsed, when you basically omit all meaningful data, you only get a rough idea of the situation.Some of the items don't fit right in certain orientations or against walls, which makes them look odd and the average scale of people makes them so tall and wide that it ends up looking quite funky. The build area appears large at first, but if you want to build a larger campus with multiple buildings and facilities the space is actually quite limited. Hopefully some bigger maps in the future.The management aspect is really neat. Having to organize departments and working out a good structure makes sense, feels realistic and empowering. Just wish there was more indication of whether or not a management structure is helpful or not; some form of management quality percentage would be nice.Have to say though I did not expect even the small minigames and other mechanics to work this flawlessly. It's refreshing to play a game that might look like a yet another indie mess thrown together to fill a niche be actually working so well. Is it perfect? No, but if updates continue and some of the rough edges are polished it really could become a real gem. It reminds me a lot of the golden era of these tycoon games from the early 2000's when it was still about realism and engaging well-rounded gameplay. You don't need the best graphics when the game is fun to play. Graphics and models can be changed and modded, but that doesn't happen to games the play like garbage. It's only the games that are fun and invigorate creativity which build a fanbase that supports them.I really hope it will get the attention it deserves and the coming months and years will make it just better. There is already such a great basis here and so much stuff done well, leaving only minor things to clean up and polish to achieve cult status. Sounds overly flattering? Nah it's just that well made compared to all the other garbage on Steam. For $20 it's a perfectly okay price. If it is on sale it's a must-buy for anyone that's into tycoon management!

The systems are complex enough to spend a good deal of time optimising and perfecting, but at the same time, you're given a lot of forgiveness as you learn what you're actually doing.  The graphics are lovely, and there's a real sense of progression (though it's slow at first).I give this game a solid 8.5/10 and absolutely recommend it for anyone with even a passing interest in the genre! _childDocuments_.review: I grew up on Theme Hospital and Two Point Hospital was fun, so Two Point Campus felt promising. Turns out, it isn't very good. Unlike this game, which handles the same concept of creating a school, but instead of a copy-paste clone of a previous game, it's a small-time anime'esque evolution from a wooden hut to a concrete bunker straight out of your favorite anime.It's a great game. It's already very deep and complex but not overwhelming, which management games often are. _childDocuments_.review: A really fun school management game that combines the best of the harvest moon (now story of seasons) series and the sims. There are a few school management games on steam but I found this one particularly interesting. First you have the cultural aspect. While the game is fully functional in English, if you can see hints of Chinese culture in the items and general structure. For example, a core room is the tea room. However the students go back home before 10pm.  The setting works particular well since you start with decrepit wooden buildings and an outhouse and slowly catch up to modern facilities through staff research. I often have issues with the "blob" artistic style of these kinds of simulator but this one uses (bit art) humans so visually I prefer this style. The game doesn't currently support modding but that is something I am hoping for in the future. While you can choose your school crest and uniform, I think mod support there would really enhance the game. A mod to make it into a 6 year elementary school could also be interesting. Another fun hidden part of the game is, like the sims, your staff and students have needs and they can have a mental break down. It is kind of a hidden feature of playing badly but if you are the kind of person who tortures your sims, you might enjoy denying them toilets or maxing out their stress. I quite enjoyed this game and am looking forward to what this dev does next.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS ISN'T MY OFFICIAL FULL REVIEW -- I'LL BE UPDATING IT THE MORE I PLAY-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Initial Impressions:I got the game today after having it on my wishlist for quite some time since I figured it's been out long enough now that any annoying bugs or features that needed to be ironed out are probably taken care of by now, as things seem to go in the industry at large these days (games getting released way too early, etc). Along with the added trust that the vast majority of reviews are positive. I'm a huge fan of the sim/management genre, so I'm always happy to see a new addition on the scene.That said, I didn't have alot of time to play it today but I still feel as though I can still offer some useful points to anyone that might be considering the game (and to the team, if they happen to see this review).First, just to get it out of the way, the English needs some work. Most of it okay enough to understand what's being conveyed, but for a game that's not officially in Early Access, it's really not acceptable in my opinion. Obviously, it's not a major strike against it or anything since it has nothing to do with the substance of the gameplay...and like I say, it doesn't get confusing or anything (so far, from what I've encountered), so as long as they continue to smooth it out it's easy to look past.Second, animations need ALOT of work. When leg movement along with the walking speed doesn't match and looks "wonky" and things like that don't mesh it kinda ruins the experience a little, at least for me. Pathfinding and other general character/NPC movements are robotic and unnatural as well. If this was still in Early Access I wouldn't be mentioning it, but it's a detail that needs some attention I feel. Not game breaking, obviously...but does contribute to lessen the overall experience.I don't want this to sound like a negative review though, so let's switch gears for a second (lol). Overall, I love the art style and vibe of the environment. It's a very charming world to get immersed in (leaving out the immersion breakers mentioned previously) and the soundtrack fits it perfectly. Whoever made the music did some excellent work and should be proud of themselves. Same goes for the visual artists. Well done in those departments! :) Genuinely. I say that, but on the other side of it, some of the people models don't look like they're "final draft" versions. As one quick example, when choosing school uniforms when starting a game, they look disproportioned and unaligned; plus, some of the uniform variations don't fit properly and clip over/into spots where they shouldn't. This is the case in a few spots in the game. Again, if this was an Early Access game I wouldn't be mentioning it, but it's not so I am :)Lastly, since I don't want to take up too much of your time with the very little amount of experience that I have with the game so far, I'll just say that if you DO end up getting the game, skip the tutorial as it currently stands...unless they end up fixing/updating it before I get to update this review. It's very hard to follow and isn't always clear with what instructions it wants you to follow along with. The UI is designed well enough (although, not perfect yet) that you'd easily be able to figure things out on your own if you're familiar with this type of game. Save your time and jump in to the action without it :)Now...you might think that I'd be giving this a thumbs down considering the general tone of what I've brought up here today (and there's more that I could add), but I feel that it'd be too harsh -- officially, I'd give it a horizontal thumb, if that were ever a thing, lol. It's still a really great game as it is from what I've experienced in my short time with it so far (I'll definitely be playing more) and it appears as though the team is still actively putting in effort and working on improving it, so that wins alot of points in my books, personally. So let's see where it continues to go from here :) I'm curious to see!

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty, but I am not really sure what kind of game it is supposed to be. The scheduling system makes no sense at all. Students are difficult to move around from class to class. It is like the game wants you to keep all the students in one grade, in one room for all 4 years with one homeroom teacher. That's not how schools work. I can't give individual students individual schedules, so it works more like some kind of weird learning factory than a school. If you get a new student in the middle of the week they just have to hope they pass because they will only have 3 days of instruction instead of 5, which makes no sense.The game looks great and the building mechanics are solid and the game looks great, but the gameplay is horrible and confusing.  This game could be great, has potential, but it need to run more like a school and not some kind of strange day prison for students where they spend 4 years locked in one room, it's just not realistic, children change classes not teachers. It's like the creators have never actually been to a school or knows how one operates. Very strange.

Once you understand the marks every student needs to pass and you match the estimation, this game is just cake. The goal is clearcut, but I think it's just a little too clearcut. There are a lot of quality of life things that I think is also fully necessary. Having 280+ students and having to look through all of them to see who's sleeping is just...Really frustrating. Game's fun. Honestly, it really is a lot of fun. But it definitely needs some more variety right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting to really like this game. A quirky, cute little game about running a school is right up my alley. Unfortunately, what I actually encountered was such frustration that thinking about this game honestly makes me angry. I have tried to play Let's School twice. The first time, I was constantly blocked from advancing by an obtuse, badly-designed user interface with vital elements that are not mentioned in the in-game manual at all; a 'tutorial' that explains virtually nothing; and, in the end, a task that I could not complete because the game just flat-out does not work sometimes. You go to carry out a basic function, and the game can no longer perform that function. The buttons stop working. The second time I tried the game, this happened IN THE TUTORIAL. The game says to designate bathrooms, I go to do it, and room-building just isn't in the game any more. Clicking the interface does nothing. According to Steam, I've wasted 1.7 hours on Let's School, but it honestly felt like six. Oh, and by the way, the quality control is so bad that in the DEFAULT NAME for your character, the 'john' is not capitalized. This is trash.

_childDocuments_.review: Closest thing we can get to building an anime-like school. It isn't difficult per se but it can be overwhelming at first. Once you have an idea of what you want to do with the game, it becomes fun and if you don't know, working towards the goals is plenty satisfying.I've encountered a few issues with the game but they are not game breaking. Highlighting and selecting certain things can be a little annoying at times. There's some UI issue at times when I try to exit out of a plan/build phase as well.Though in saying that, any problems that are in the game (gameplay wise), you'll be notified at least what's going and how to resolve them which is plenty useful. It's a great game, I've lost track of time playing the game and I believe that's a good thing in terms of immersion. Lots of quality of life improves do get added over time. If you're on the fence about it but are interested in the game, I would recommend giving the demo a go. It's enjoyable and watching the school improve over time is satisfying to see.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game for people with low-end PCs or laptops. I have a low end PC that can handle Stormworks: Search and Rescue fairly well, a game that has slightly lower quality of graphics than this game. It can also run Age of Empires 4 with relative ease. Yet, it cannot run this game. As I play it, the Task Manager that I have up says that the GPU usage is mostly eaten up. Additionally, when this happens for extended periods, the game crashes. As such, if you have a low-end PC that can run other quality games like it, I would wait and see if your PC has a strong enough graphics card to be able to run it.Despite these limitations, it is a fun game. It gives you a chance to run your own school with a full immersion into both the creative and administrative aspects. As such, if your computer can handle the graphics, it is well made.

_childDocuments_.review: The game recommended setting :Processor: Intel Core i5 -7500 | AMD Ryzen 5 5600XMemory: 16 GB RAMGraphics: Nvidia GeForce GTX1060*My setting :Ryzen 7600Memory: 32 GB DDR5 CL32 6000MhzGraphics: Nvidia GeForce RTX3060TiThe last i checked, Ryzen 7600 is just as powerful as Ryzen 5800 for gaming, but less for creative works.So at the beginning of a new game i set the graphics setting to MAXI got 70 fps, and it stutters, the fps went up and down.OK i get it, somehow it is GPU heavy... I asked for how to make the game run 60 fps.I set everything to lowest possible. Good, the game run smooth.It doesn't looks much different with Max setting IMHO, just less (or no in my case) foliage and shadow.Until hitting the endgame. I have like 100 students and 25 teachers.It stutters, OK now it hitting my CPU. It went down like 50 fps. And doesn't feel smooth at all.I'm not claiming I know how to make an efficient game programming, but the performance I do feel substandard than games in the same genre. I love building games, it feels like you name it, i probably has it on my library.Including RimWorld people often sought the similarities.I think it is closer to Prison Architect than the RimWorld, as it doesn't have one thing integral, a story teller.Also you can't have limited control over the NPC like the RimWorld. There are things breaking the immersion.1. Like the NPCs stuck at the school gate when raining. The animation is like want to open an umbrella but they don't.Repeating all over.2. Students bypassing the wall like a ghost just to buy something from the school supermarket.3. Suddenly the students can't access the drink, toilet, and food. It just at the next door and i have like 50% more than the maximum capacity...And what i hate the most is the way the class is always randomized every new year....I've named the class like Evergreen 1, Evergreen 2, Evergreen 3 each to note their grade.But the game just ignore that and randomize it all over again, including the class name...WTF lah.Later, we could automatize the class selection for each district from where our students went from. So, for example now i could select the Evergreen 1-3 to be the select classes for any students from Archimedes district. Good, it will still be randomized but at least I'm hands free now.Good?No, because each district can only cater like 15 students at high popularity. It is like half the class capacity.And for idk reason, it can't be more than that.And they will hog the lab all by themselves. So for a district, you'll need :3 classes for each grade.6 labs for specialized study programMind you there are some labs that can be only build once like the computer lab, and the student lounge.And then what? Build it right ?Yes, I build a building each for each district.To get all of these up and running, i'll also need like 6 managers to cater all the enormous number of facilities. Yes, even the toilet, food store, cafeteria, playground, bike parking lot, etc. they all need managerial capacity.So at the end it is like I need around 10 teacher to cater 10 to 15 students. How it is not mind boggling. Better using personal tutor than this.The Student to Teacher ratio is getting ridiculous.Some of the Teacher is better renamed as Manager or a Worker than teacher.Some of them don't need to teach at all, like managing the shop, cafeteria, security?They can manage and teach at the same time but why? Without them, i didn't lack of teaching capacity. Because there're still managers, and homeroom teacher. I still end up profitable despite all of these ridiculous things, which is also mind boggling.My balance was like +180K with -60K expense. Played the standard difficulty, idk how it went at harder diff.My Cafeteria, School shop, and Sweets shop each generate more revenue than the student tuition fee.And the last straw is how everyone getting chubby at the end.Like everyone.I hate how they looked when chubby and giant at the same time.The Character is like 2 times the size normal, including the umbrella..... The umbrella looks squeezed up.And when my main character took the commemorative photo? It looks awful.And oh, some students just refuses to sit they sit, stand, sit, stand all over again. The hell is this.Someone said, oh, sell Tom Yum Goong at the Cafeteria. It will counter the effect.Fine it did work..... too well. Now the NPCs are Weak.Now the NPC looks like a straw man... Face palm....Also i want to point the chara customization? It only works at the beginning of the game.And the game doesn't have workshop content.So i must deal with all oddities happened, and the poor game performance at the late game.The game is cute, it looks pleasing. But the game hates me.Edit 1: My memory CL was wrong, went looking the box.Edit 2: The game have better performance now.So in comparison, it was like 150 occupants (students and teachers combined, minus pets) before stutters,after an update it raised to 250 occupants. And now i could say it can handle 350 safely in 60 fps, using my PC. And i'm playing the graphics at medium or high without worry a nuclear meltdown right now. This alone, changed the not recommended to recommended but I took my time to test things out before changing the review. I started a new game solely for that, a school with a lot of students.1. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start this off by saying I got this game only last week and already have 54 hours in it at the time of this review. I normally don't review games, but I absolutely had to say something about this one. It is by no means perfect, but it is probably the best game in the school simulation genre I have ever played. It far outpaces what Academia School Simulator wanted to be, and with charming graphics to go with it. There is so much detail and love put into so many different spots, and the mechanics are so easy to learn while simultaneously allowing for extremely complex strategies. It really feels like you are getting control over all the aspects of a school and creating your own narrative. I love the interplay of all the different departments and communities, and the various stat systems between teachers and employees and students. The building aspect is also a lot of fun. Gaining resources can be as easy or as hard as you want it to be, and even the harder aspects of the game are quite forgiving if you are just patient. It's so nice to see a game that makes the challenge less about trying not to fail, and more about trying harder to succeed. I do think the game could still use some polish on some mechanical systems, and definitely could use some attention to expanding on existing mechanics and content, but overall I believe this game is an amazing creation. I also love that they are giving attention to the game with very cheap DLC that delivers interesting new content that isn't just 100% cosmetic. Overall, I think the game and all its existing DLC are underpriced for what they deliver.I truly hope this game continues getting development and updates. I really don't want it to stall indefinitely or cease development at its current point. It is a really fun and complete game, but I think it has so much potential that could be elaborated on through reinvestment of resources, and I also think this game deserves way more hype and attention.Thank you so much for this game, and I hope to see more from you!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend it, but I'm also going to discuss my problems with the game. In no particular order...Let's School looks and feels like a fun, cozy school sim 75% of the time. The other 25% is WAY too complex. A lot of that could be fixed by redesigning some menus and making some things more clear, but a lot of it is ingrained in the game. They're doing a lot of things in very innovative ways, which I appreciate, but that often leads to frustration, confusion, or stress.In two different places you can see "students expected to pass" and see two very different numbers. One shows "students expected to pass at the end of the semester" and the other shows "students who would pass if the exam were right now."Also, the game often provides extra information in the most bizarre places. Maybe there's a reason for it, but I don't know why I care what university students want to go to after they graduate when viewing their exam results. That's fine information for a different menu.When you click on an item in a room it opens both the item's window and the room's window. If you want to remove the item, it's very easy to accidentally click on the "remove room" icon with the same icon (but different menu) and POOF the entire room disappears.They use flats and sharps to denote octaves. As a musician, this is very triggering. Not a big deal unless they don't fix it. (I have submitted feedback through official means)I get it, some people like added difficulty, but having disasters always on (you can only reduce the frequency) is a shame. There are plenty of other mechanics in the game to figure out and enjoy. Disasters add very little to the mix. You simply train your students every semester and you're good to go. All it does is costs you money and progress.The game's soundtrack is fine, but very limited. I lasted about 8 hours before muting it and making my own playlist.I'm still frequently confused by some icons because they are either too generic or too similar to another button.

_childDocuments_.review: Typical Asian Education System. If you ever played school tycoon, then you will like this game. You have to run a school where you have to manage all "things" regarding the school itself, such as the classroom, admission, teacher & staff recruitment, school organization management, and the lesson that your student will learn.I like the concept that you will choose a school that can give you the best facilities, teachers, and education system in order to escort you to your dream university. Based on that, then you have to decide, what lesson that your student should learn, and you also need to provide the supporting facilities such as lab, gym, library, etc. so your student can learn in-depth of the lesson that they try to learn. Easier said than done, there are so many challenges that we face in achieving all of that, such as bad behavior students, bad management, and sometimes natural disaster. These reality of school management has successfully captured by this game, even better than Two Point Campus in my opinion.What I found lack in this game is the competition. There are so many schools nearby but I feel that they are not improving their school quality at all. Moreover, I really expect that they will try harder to regain their popularity so that many new students will start to enroll more than from my school. I found it easier from time to time to persuade other people to join my school than any other school. And also, I don't think inter school communication give me any huge benefit.Overall, I really like this game. It surpassed my expectation regarding school management. At least when I compare it to school tycoon and Two Point Campus. The features provided are solid, abundant, and of course fun!!

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is simple, you suddenly get a school yeeted at you and a single teacher + your avatar (the boss) and you are told "git gud" and that's what you do, you make a room and then another one. And suddenly a day is gone and you are considering firing every single teacher and training them yourself. Because you realize training skill is the true value to aim for. Nothing matters besides that, if you can't train them further they might as well not exist. Anything under 100 teaching skill at 230% efficiency isn't even worth debating. And you see, that's the genius of this game. You can optimize, you can expand, you can go into the fine details and make a class for EVERY region you draw students from.The depth increases and you have a choice. Do you want to build NICE or do you want to build efficient? And that is where the 1 flaw of the game comes to shine. It isn't hard enough. No I don't mean it's easy to get money early on, or it's easy to manage everything at first. But once you understand what is going on the simulation at the core itself is too simple, doesn't bring enough push-back, not enough pressure. Students are paragons of health only very rarely hit by a flu (or broken legs if you accidentally upgrade their seats while the class is held). The game tracks a great many stats for each student, with traits, relations etc. so who you draw in makes a difference, bullies gonna bully, paragons of justice are gonna make your job easier. Frogs everywhere..... so many frogs. Psychological counseling exists in the game but I pushed to the absolute limit and tried my best at seriously not caring for any student whatsoever and I never got even 1 student to visit there. You are also sometimes restricted by the same thing students in real lif are restricted by, a break is only that long, and if it takes long to get to food, drink, toilets, then there won't be much time for other things. This in turn makes it extra difficult if you want to build pretty or "loose", as centralized layouts dominate for a reason. Even in our real life world.Ultimately there is not a single better made School Builder on Steam. This game oozes flair and can, at times, challenge you. It will at all times challenge that devil in your brain that wants to optimize and put everything into a self contained skyscraper.... and you can do that too. Although it is expensive and end-game stuff ;) The game is also extremely well optimized, never once dipping below 60fps (fps locked) even at most absurd student+teacher counts (beyond 300)There are a ton of fun hidden things to discover. Optimizations to achieve, research to do. It is truly a fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I had to learn about this game on a sale, this is basically made for... well, ME. Someone who loved Pocket Academy and Two Point Campus but wanted more micro level management. So before I built Japanese schools then British Universities, it's time I moved on to Chinese academies!I wondered if maybe this game would be a little too simple and then suddenly it was twelve hours later and the sun was coming up. It really hooks you in and doesn't let go. There's a lot of the more granular details I wanted in a game likes this, and because they tell you flat out "Do this or your students fail!" there's a goal that you suddenly find yourself striving for. It's a deceptively complex simulation that really rewards a player into the management side as well as the construction maniacs among us (yes there's a sandbox mode). There's some minor bugs here and there but the core product is solid and the devs are still adding new content, they just did a huge patch right in time for the sale that I bought this in. They're very responsive on their Discord too.More people need to discover this gem of a sim game!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying I quite enjoyed the game. My 50+ hours I put into over the course of a week or so is relatively evident of that. With that said, I couldn't shake the feeling that the game was overall incomplete. This game feels much more like it should be in EA rather than a full release. For starters, the least "complete" part of the game I feel is the club system. It's a school, and schools have clubs. Most schools have lots of clubs. Especially one's that have tons of students. You get 2. Basketball and Music. (3 if you count student council, but they don't do much other than attribute management points to said clubs.) When you start researching every tabs has tons of different options for including areas of the school. In the club section there are 4 things to research. The 3 aforementioned clubs, and decorations for your club room. That's it. There definitely should be some kind of expansion on this mechanic. Another thing that made it feel incomplete was the lack of variety in the different games and in my opinion vastly reduces replay value. You always start with the same 2 topics. Humanities and science. There are 4 total, but you never start a game with art or sports as one of your topics. Ms.Lin (your advisor at the start of the game) is always a humanities teacher, and the headmaster (You) are always a science teacher. This actually works out nicely for me in particular, being a science graduate, buuuut it would be nice to see the player be given the opportunity to choose their starting attributes. As a result, the starting town you get is always the same, just with slightly different names, occasionally different traits, and different tuition values. This always makes the start of the game (normally the first week or so) feel very samey. Staying on the topic of lack of variety, the overworld is another thing I find lacking. So you have 3 schools that you can choose from. A pretty standard school ground, one that is surrounded by streams, and one that is located in a cold snowy mountain. In my first game I played in the second map I listed. After you reach your first school reform, you can explore the over world map, where you can find new communities to recruit kids from, and other schools to trade with. The trading between schools is extremely barebones though, so I rarely touched that. At the top of the map, there is what appears to be a tap that says "Urban" implying that there are other locations. There isn't. I thought maybe when I tried the snowy mountain map, the map would be slightly different. Nope, it is exactly the same. Still the Urban map. Same schools, just moved to a different spot and slightly different communities to recruit from. Last thing I would like to point out were minor annoyances that I experienced with the game. I feel like once you reach a certain point in the game, your growth beings to vastly outpace the rate at which you obtain resources. These leads to just fast-forwarding to the end of the week so that your students can take your test to get an injection of money or the little attribute tokens for the 4 class types, so scaling feels a tad bit off. Another thing is the pop up messages in the bottom left. I don't need to be notified multiple times a day that there are new applicants or the 50 delinquent acts that happen a day. If I want to expel a student (Spoiler alert: I don't) or need to hire someone, I will. I don't need a notification for that each time, and should be able to turn them off. On the note about delinquency, another big issue with the game is how the security facilities work. So once you start having trouble-making kids, you have to start manually assigning teachers to break it up. That is at least until you have a security detail and cameras set up around the school. However, I began to find that my security office was occasionally too far from these incidents to go handle it. No problem, right? Just build another office closer to the problems, hire new employees, and no issue. Wrong. I give the new office a TV so that they can use the cameras, and...nothing. It always defaults to the first office, and there's no way to alter it, making the new office on the other side of campus effectively useless, unless you want to go back to manually assigning employees to delinquent acts. The last glaring issue that I felt playing this game is the lack of tool tips. Most items are pretty self-explanatory, but there are a few cases where you need to know certain things, and the game does not provide you enough information. Early in my play-through I found myself with a obesity epidemic sweeping through my school, and I could not figure out why. Apparently a burger sold in my cafeteria makes everyone fat, and thus you have to find the school with a particular item to trade so you can slim people down again. And eventually take both off the menu so that they can't order either. Except, once you do this, everyone becomes "weak" and thin like skeletons. Once you start having this fluctuation in weight (at least in employees, they students will eventually graduate and leave) it's almost impossible to get them back to normal weight. A lot will either be fat or skinny, with a few sitting in the middle. So, do I recommend this game? Eh, I got it on sale, and I think it's worth it at a reduced price if you enjoy sim/management games, but even at a $20 full price tag, I don't think it's worth it. So, if this sounds like a game you'd like, barring any major future updates (which based on the company moving forward with other projects, I find unlikely), wait until a sale to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: ( full review with screenshots:  )Let's School is a school management simulator that I won't call "School Tycoon" because there's no real campaign mode. Instead of the flood of scenarios you get in something like Two Point Campus, this has two maps, a bunch of difficulty settings, and three victory goals that you'll try to work towards. It certainly doesn't have the replayability that a more varied campaign would offer, but working on one increasingly complex school for the whole game also helps it avoid the repetitive tedium that killed Two Point Campus for me. Both games have a similar concept, but this is far and away the better game.The most basic loop you'll go through begins with building a classroom and assigning students from your feeder communities to it. These students have a three year goal of learning enough about two specific subjects, and you'll next assign teachers and classes to their class schedule in order to meet those goals. After that, you might find that the new students have pushed your bathrooms, cafeterias, management admins, or even HVAC over capacity and you'll need to build more of whatever is now lacking. You can send your classes on field trips to nearby communities in order to scout for more students, and those new students you find will have more ambitious goals and more complex needs. Meeting those requires doing research and upgrading your existing facilities, which you'll need more students to pay for. At a high level, that cycle continues until you win. Speaking of winning, there are three ways to do it. One route finishes when you graduate 20 students with the highest level goals, another needs 250 concurrent students and very high student/staff satisfaction, and the last needs 12,000 building score and having built an advanced wonder. These all sound fairly different, but because of the way the loop I described above works, I think you'd have to try pretty hard to complete one of them without being close to the other two. The best students need so much stuff to graduate that you'll need an advanced building and a lot of other students to fund it all, it's hard to have 250 students without a large building and a decent number of 5 star students, and if you have a 12,000 score building, you've probably filled it with something close to 250 students. The lack of variety here is the game's weakest point. That said, it's still receiving significant updates and it's possible that it'll have more variety between playthroughs in the future. The other big problem is the difficulty. Although it is reasonably customizable, if you're playing on the default settings, there's not much that can realistically stop you unless you just try to build too quickly. You can tell in advance what you need to do to graduate all your students with perfect grades, and doing that will give you more students and more money to keep the loop going. Occasional disasters are the only things that will mess with your plans, but earthquakes are mostly just annoying and fires will almost never happen as long as you've built a bunch of cheap safety items. This would have benefited from something like difficult short term bonus goals or more variability in student performance to add some risk to the game. --------For more reviews, see

_childDocuments_.review: A very well designed school management simulation, Lets's School will take from a puny hut of a school to a giant map complex and diversified academy of knowledge. I really love almost all about this game which for me recently became a star among tycoon games.So you begin by admitting a few pupils and with a few poorly specialized teachers and, step by step, you'll get to build many, many buildings: classrooms for science, literature, art and sport, stores and supermarket, cafeterias, specialized rooms for every taste, offices, modern spaces of learning like computer classrooms and projector rooms, dormitories and even wonders.Everything is unlocked by research, even the maps which give you access to more districts from where you recruit your subjects. You can also train your employees.The disasters, earthquakes and fires, are mostly annoying, but you can lose a lot of money because of them.I'm enjoying a lot playing this game that turned out to be a very nice surprise, being not too simple and not too complex or frustrating. It has a great sense of progression and I love to see how my (now) huge academy is extending and taking shape.Pros:- very good tycoon game- somewhat funny- very engaging and satisfying progression- relatively complex, with many buildings- replayable because you have three kind of goals (quantity or quality of teaching and aesthetics)- lovely graphics- cute cats and pandas- relaxing on slower speeds- a lot of content and devs are planning to add moreCons:- you can't really change the name of the classes (it only puts yours between brackets) which I find a very odd design decision. If you try to change the classes configuration, expect to acquire some strange bugs (like classes with the same name or randomly switching names every day).

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game to be very enjoyable and addicting is a similar way to games like Rimworld and Prison Architect and such hook me.  I've seen a lot of comparisons to Two Point Campus and, of course, that's fair -- but I think this game has a lot more depth to it.  When I play TPC, I always end up feeling like I am playing more of a puzzle game than a management sim. Like everything is being spoon fed to me I guess?  To be fair it's possible I just didn't play TPC long enough, but I put around 6 hours into TPC and it never quick clicked.  In this game I feel more like I'm given enough information to start, but left to learn things on my own.  It also opens up a lot at one point to where you are getting more involved in the world outside your school.  Lastly, I feel I "get to know" and care about my employees, which is something don't tend to get from TPC or even Prison Architect.  Somehow it makes me really care about the students and their success.  Anyway -- excellent game, highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: In short - a school tycoon type game that is heavily based on Japanese (and more loosely East Asian) middle and high schools. I played on the beta version that has the early implementation of extra-curricular activities and clubsPros: - Nails the East Asian high school vibe well- Good performance even at relatively high student numbers- Few bugs encountered for its current stage of development- A fairly robust building systemCons:- Students feel identical: their aspiration (i.e. the place they want to go after graduation, which directly influences your management choices) are always the same if they come from the same recruitment area. Their talents are always tailored to their aspiration too. Some randomisation here would definitely improve the gameplay loop.- The exam system is...weird. If two students score the same on their exam in a given subject, but one has a higher level aspiration requiring a higher final score at the end of year 3, he might still fail because the target is higher for him for some reason. - Relationships between students and teachers is as present as a system but underdeveloped at the momentOverall verdict:Still a pretty good school game overall imo despite its flaws. The club system looks promising, but its still in an early build on the beta and could definitely use some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game overall with a pleasing art style and adorable little things you can place around.There are quite a few annoyances in the current version of the game I'm playing that make the experience ever so slightly irritating, I encountered these with 8hrs of playtime and multiple sessions.- Game immediately crashes when you accept data collection for some reason, game starts perfectly fine when you decline although it asks you again everytime you relaunch the game with no way to turn it off.- Had a bug were for some reason when I click on the students it didn't pop up their status until I reloaded the save- Had a bug where I got softlocked and couldn't place anything after resizing a building and clicking a movable object until I reloaded the save- Have a bug on the scheduling page with the special courses where it overlaps with normal courses and the problem persists even when restarting the game- No way to mirror a blueprint you copied, at least as far as I know- Some events have no explanation on how to do them, not even a hint. (Like how to do cleaning chores, you'd have to unlock the specific research first and then set it on the schedule afterwards)- People getting stuck in empty buildingsAnd quite a few more very minor ones. Despite these flaws though the game is still  fun! It takes a bit of getting used to and you have to take your time or you go bankrupt quite quickly (I'm playing on hard mode so it makes sense). It's quite well paced with new stuff introduced to you slowly but surely.Hopefully the issues eventually get resolved since right now the game still feels a little underbaked in some aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game.Building mechanics are on point. You can edit rooms while being used and it keeps working. Plenty of possibilities and room for building your dream academy. _childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised when I purchased this game. I do enjoy a good simulation style game that I can play casually while I work or have my attention split with something else and this was a fantastic fit for that.The visuals are quirky in a good way and there is rather complex research and building system that you must navigate through in order to reach the end game. As you continue to play you need to get more money to be able to operate higher level facilities, this then requires you to take on students that pay more per term but have bigger goals to meet than students you would have taken on previously.It can take a surprisingly long time to reach the endgame but I didn’t find myself getting bored and enjoyed the slower progression. It never got too difficult either, but I didn’t find that this was a bad thing and I imagine many people playing this will be looking for a more laidback experience like I was.All in all, it was a nice little gem of a find that I enjoyed. If you like a solid simulation game this will scratch an itch for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and was pleased to find that it was much less glitchy compared to the Homeroom version. I wish that the discipline was a bit more effective. I also hope that there will be more decorative options added to the game at a later point since there isn't much to choose from. Otherwise, I really enjoyed playing and I recommend giving this one a try too!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's School does a fine job giving players a management sim they can enjoy. Let's School can sometimes feel simply functional and yet manages to stand out from the competition with momentary flashes of brilliance.Though easy to pick up, it can turn monotonous fairly quickly, even after you unlock new mechanics such as talking to other schools or exploring the regions around you. Let’s School does not feel like a game you can enjoy for hours on end, but you’ll certainly have a good time while you’re in the early stages. In that sense, it feels more like being a student than being a headmaster.Rate: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed this game!  Being a headmaster of a school that I've built has been a lot of fun... _childDocuments_.review: After 84 hours with this game, and getting the rarest achievement, I can say very confidently that I like this game... by a lot.What drew me into the game is the simple and yet hard to truly optimize mechanics. I micromanage a lot of the classes in the game, and that's just how I get the students to succeed! You can automate it after a certain time, and the game is just so appealing for those who likes management and tycoon games, which is also what I like, as well as the option for it in the first place. A lot of the game, like building to management, are also this way, and it's up to you to pick the one you like best.The graphics are quite good. They're pixelated but still somehow look good that way. Due to some hardware limitations, I can only run it on low graphical settings, and it doesn't look terrible at that setting. The music is literally just the same 5-minute track played over and over, and it's annoying after an hour.TLDR: I got this game at a 20% or so discount, but I'd be happy to pay the full price. It's good, fills a lot of time, lets you manage at your own pace... seriously, just get it.

_childDocuments_.review: So... It's good, but not perfect, or extremely amazing. It's fine and I enjoy it.I want to start with something positive, I love the game and this game have the potential to be very amazing with proper development. Like why the schedule can't be fully repeatable, why is there no way to check which students have how many demerits point, why I can't assign multiple admission to single class, and many other little things. _childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, it's addicting and fun if you like this sort of game. There's a lot to it but that may be exactly why it has the issues it does. It seems like it's not complete but will be amazing if it can ever get to that point.They claimed they fixed the issue with it prompting feedback on launch but it's still there for me and my friend who also has it. Saying yes crashes the game. Not everything is explained well, or it pops up as a dialogue box with no way to bring it back up. Clubs are not implemented yet. It would be nice if we could modify the graduation speed. One week for a semester and 3 semesters for graduation is fast when you consider the class subject progression. This is related to my next point.I unlocked a lot of the specialty classrooms but no one ever seems to use them. Even when I have students focusing solely on that subject their whole three semesters they still only seem to have classes in their main classrooms. So even if I build a beautiful school, it feels almost empty.There does seem to be some occasional bugs too.If some of this is user error and I can resolve, any feedback is appreciated but I feel like the game should give you some more information itself.I do really like the game and want it to update and become even better! _childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: I am really on the fence of this one to be honest. Let's start with the negatives.- I am writing this review because I was pressured by the game to do so, which feels really scummy.- This game is horribly optimized. At first I thought that this game may secretly be a crypto miner, because for some reason it is using 100% of my GPU (RTX 2060 Super!). This is unprecedented unless I am rendering something in Blender for example. It doesn't use any network connection though, so maybe (?) it is safe.- some minor stuff, for example a "headmaster mode" where you control your character in third person doesn't really work, cause usually there is a wall between the camera and your character.The positives are the very generic "It's fun!". But it really is, so if you don't mind a power bill of a crypto miner and think you will enjoy a school tycoon game, then I think this game is fine, but be careful and check the changelogs whether some of the issues have been fixed.Edit:After playing for more time I have noticed a lot more negative aspects, as such I would only recommend this on sale anymore:-no way to change textures of walls. This is especially bad on higher difficulties, because you are forced to use the steel foundation buildings to withstand earthquakes, but these buildings are extremely ugly. By comparison the wood and brick foundations look quite nice, but they are not viable because of earthquakes-setting up schedules is extremely annoying. You cannot easily set a teacher for one subject, instead it is only possible to either set them individually for each period, or you "assign to all periods", which in reality will only replace all the periods of a specific teacher. This is a bit confusing, so as an example:After quickly setting up a schedule, there are four teachers teaching science. Since I want the homeroom teacher to teach every science class, I want to replace them. I can either set her individually to each period, or I have to press "assign to all periods" three times, once for each teacher I don't want anymore.-Also room assignment is quite annoying. I am obviously fine with having room conflicts, it adds a bit of challenge. But the annoying part is that I will have to work with the schedules (which as I have mentioned is annoying), and it is also completely opaque when a room will be needed. For example some classes randomly need a chemistry room for second grade, while all my other classes used to only need the biology room, so once I set up a schedule that allows this, next semester suddenly all classes need the chemistry room. Overall it is simply very confusing for when which room is needed-some room requirements are a bit crazy. For example you need six beds for the infirmary. This seems excessive because it feels as if I am building a hospital ward. My middle school's infirmary only had a single bed as a comparison.-some game features still feel very bare bones. Maybe I am just stupid, but I can't figure out the point of the security office for example. Excursions and Interactions with other schools is also very basic.-Some minor things like: notification spam, lack of a planning tool

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's simple, but challenging, it's cute. _childDocuments_.review: This game is utterly delightful. That's the review.OK, fine, you want to know why you should (or shouldn't, idk it's your life) buy this game.Well, for one thing, it's a rock-solid entry into the Tropico-like (or Prison Architect-like) subgenre of builder game. If you've played and liked games like that, this is one more.For another, it has got a _ton_ of character. Because its developer, Pathea Games (best known for the My Time series, including my 2023 Game of the Year My Time At Sandrock), is based in Chongqing, China, they've gone with a distinctly Eastern vibe and style. The game's default currency is Japanese yen, and while you don't have to be a weeb to fall in love with the quirky visuals and "every high school anime you've ever seen" vibe with the students (I'm not a weeb, and I still smiled more than I perhaps should have), it does help.So there you go, really. This has something to offer just about anyone who's even tangentially interested in its subject matter.I do have a few small nitpicks—the translation leaves something to be desired (and some of the text is left in the original Chinese, but they're working on it), the mechanics aren't well tutorialized (if you've never played a game like this before, you will probably slam your head hard against it and bounce off its mechanics; go play Tropico 4 or Prison Architect first), and if you don't like pixel art, you're not going to like the simple visuals.But absolutely none of those things are enough to put me off recommending this game. It's excellent. Worth every penny of its $20 price tag, and better still if you can get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great - I really enjoyed it. It's a management sim where you build a school and take in students with different aspirations, and have to structure your classes around the students needs. you can automate student class assignments. It does lag a bit sometimes in very late game stages. i'm going to play it at least one  more time.I hope the developers will keep adding to the game - this is really a winner.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Good school management simulation.- Decent management gameplay.- Easy to approach.- Nice-looking art style.- Regular patches and updates which fix and improve the gameplay experience (e.g. add staffs).Cons:- Mediocre character design: Although the materials, equipments and buildings display good visuals, the character models and animations appear less refined, lacking in intricate details.- Repetitive gameplay: The core gameplay revolves around a repetitive cycle of constructing classrooms, facilities, and scheduling, which initially captures interest but eventually grows tiresome.Some ideas and suggestions:- Enhance and expand the expedition feature: Instead of presenting it as a simple text-based event, it can be transformed into an interactive gameplay element where players are responsible for organizing and leading real-time trips to diverse locations such as historical sites, other schools, jungles, beaches, or even foreign countries while completing various tasks and quests.- Introduce new functions for the facilities: In addition to serving as prerequisites for course unlocks, each facility can offer unique functions. For instance, the table tennis or basketball courts could be utilized for hosting sports events, the Assembly Hall could accommodate various other events like scholarship award ceremonies, graduation ceremonies, and career orientation sessions, while classrooms could be used for teacher-parent meetings, among other possibilities.- Build up the Student-Teacher-Parent relationship: Add more interactions among them. For example parents can have the opportunity to advocate for additional benefits for their children from the school and voice objections to disciplinary actions taken by teachers.
