_childDocuments_.review: I'm a pretty casual player and don't like a million complexities.  I found this game to be pretty entertaining with easy learning.  There's not much diversity to interactions or appearance, and you can tell there's a lot of copy paste with the students, but overall this is a very fun game for those who like management style games.  It's very cute in the Japanese style way and I really enjoy how positive things are-- like it's a happy game.  I also really like how often devs are sending out patches and updates.  While I wish there were more updates to keep it entertaining after the first or second run through, it's a pretty active team behind the scenes. Overall, I'd recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Right ahead, the game still has a few bugs, but so far I only encountered one game breaking bug. Due to daily autosaves, I didn't lose much by reloading. I would however recommend to not combine buildings to far after morning, that it would hurt to reload. (In my case it asked to combine them and just removed the price every time I pressed yes without actually finishing the combining and on no it deleted all buildings, with the rooms just floating outside, I didn't try, whether it would still work)But the Game is really fun to play. I really like the little takes, being allowed to customize your headmaster and school logo. And with a limit of seven levels to your buildings no one stops you from making a school full of towers or other building fun. I was slightly confused, that unlike all other rooms, sports rooms and the helipad are set down full equipped, but can be customized afterwards, but I asume it is to give you an idea of the size.I wish I had noticed sooner, that the departments in the management view are minimizable, since this view can get really hard to overview later in the game and sometimes the facilities on the edges aren't even accessible yet. This would be less annoying if the auto assigning of new facilities had some common sense or at least the order was saved. I can't count how man times my new facility was put in a department, that had no resources and completely unfitting policy, even though I had departments that could handle the load.But despite the bugs, it is a lot of fun :)

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was looking for something to scratch the school tycoon itch, this game was really a big surprise. It feels like many of the management sims nowadays for these types of games don't really care about realism, and while this game is far from realistic it stays far enough within the realm of seriousness that you can play it however you want. If you want to make a goofy school you can, and if you want to play a serious school you can, as well. While some of the content in the preview images isn't out yet, I look forward to the future of this game. With a bit of polish, this could easily beat out some of the bigger mainstream management sim titles.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Definitely addicting.Cons-----Micromanagement toward the end is a bit annoying. (Management Tree, Assigning Classes)The management tree is awful, you find yourself scrolling back and forth to move management offices, and sometimes you can't even click a class/resource to move it on the tree.There are only two maps.The game is incredibly easy, they need to add new mechanics to make a game over possible. The only event that was some what catastrophic was an earthquake that occurred before I updated the building material from wood to steel.Foot traffic doesn't matter (you can have a hallway that everyone walks through that's a single square wide with no penalty).

_childDocuments_.review: Boy howdy that learning curve is a doozy. I had to start this game from scratch three times before I was able to get a grasp of all the variables. But now that I have it has been a great game to play. It is really satisfying to get your school running smoothly and looking great. There is a whole lot of customization. You can have separate uniforms for each class, design your own logo, give each class and room a different name, also with their own logo, and you can make your school one giant building or a lot of little ones. There is also this part after a class graduates where you take a picture with them and you get to choose your pose and facial expression. That's fun. All the animations for the students and teachers are fun to watch, and it's cool how each student and teacher has their own portfolio. You can watch the students interact with each other and commiserate.There is one singular song in this game, so playing for long enough can get a little mind melting. You can always turn off the music and listen to something else, but it is nice to have something in game to vibe with. Moving around can get a bit frustrating, but that may just may be me being used to Sims controls/not used to PC controls.Also! There are cats!If anything could be amended I would ask for new/different/more music. The one song really grinds on you after a while.

As some other reviewers pointed out, the core gameplay challenge, keeping your school profitable and getting students passing exam scores, is not much of a challenge. _childDocuments_.review: There's alot of iffy parts overall - but its a 8.5/10 game just with alot of..."How does that work" issues. Things just seem to happen in some parts and that's honestly ok, it's a bunch of snags but the whole game itself is amazing. I'm sure with a comprehensive polish this game will far surpass alot of similar management games in it's genre. The fluidity of game play is 9.5/10 - very replayable mini gameplay loops. Get more students, learn to manage that in a increasingly larger school. Funny animations - funny interactions with NPCs - therefore the core of the game is fantastic. Placement, planning of rooms, and associated UI is a little rougher - 7/10 - very rough around the edges, but core is very good. But not too much fault here - UI is still very difficult but I hope it's looked into more. Visuals are like 8/10 - I get some of the animations are a joke but I'd like to see more pathing animations put in. Students still walk through walls every once in a while. Huge recommend from me and the devs deserve further attention.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan since the demo launched, and also got to be a part of the last couple of beta tests before launch.Game is great, but probably wait for an awesome Steam sale before purchasing.. maybe 30% or more.Game came out with a lot of bugs, but aren't really game breaking. I have not encountered a game breaking bug, mostly graphical which is annoying.I love to entertain myself in making a great environment  in city builders, one that really feels realistic and alive. While I can do that in the game, it does take a lot of effort to do so since the pathing behaviors of the characters in game are still flawed.You can spend hours and hours in building your pathways, entrances etc and no one would use it. The AI now has the sims using the shortest path available to go to specific places, even if it's the tiny little crevice in between school buildings. I have found a way to prevent that by overusing bicycle parking lots, which is the effort I was talking about earlier.. But adjusting the pathing AI would do wonders... Would make all the designing and planning worth it.If you are into just managing your school to get the maximum benefit for revenue etc, it can easily be done if you want to.. But game can be over in 3-4 hours this way. If you want to spend hours and hours planning and designing like I did, don't bother. Game is a 10 hour game max. I have spent 129 hours on this game just to end up being frustrated because my sims aren't going to the paths and doorways I set out for them unless I block off tiny crevices in the most awkward of ways.I am still recommending the game because it is a lot of fun when you start, I am hoping that Pathing updates are done and as well asset editor updates are done. _childDocuments_.review: First of all, if you liked Kairosoft's  games and you are here because  reminds you of those games, stop reading and go buy the game. If you enjoyed this game and don't know what Kairosoft is, go check on their games. They are available on steam and mobile stores.Let's School is a cozy school simulation game, clearly inspired by Japanese schools. It's quite easy to understand and the pacing is relaxing. You can also set yourself a custom difficulty, which is always a plus.You will begin with a run-down school which barely stands and soon be able to build a beautiful place for your students. They will need functioning places, like classrooms or a cafeteria, but they will also need them to be well lit and at a decent temperature (You will love the first cooling option the game gives you).Keep in mind that this high school might not be exactly like the one you remember. In this one, just like Japanese high schools, the students stay for years, which might not exactly fit other countries educational systems. Just so you can plan in advance the construction of classrooms. By the way, as of the  time of this review, classrooms will be set to the same group of students, so it's not possible to build one floor per year without having to manually move everyone.You will recruit students from different areas. Each area has all students pursuit the same goals, which is weird but works mechanically. I still prefer 's approach of a mixed bag of students but this allows you to focus on their goals and makes it easier for them to reach full marks. In my case, I built a full set of 3 classrooms for each area, so I could set a timetable fitting their expectations.One mechanic that seems a bit weird to me is the research. You will need free teachers to work on researching subjects to unlock everything needed to build and improve the school. Effectively, you can just build a sort of classroom for them to research, and that leads you to hiring teachers to just sit down there like students, which doesn't ring quite well with me.Another important feature is the management points. Each room costs management points and the Headmaster (that's you!) can only do so much. You will need to build extra departments to handle those rooms. It can be a bit of a mess, but it works well, because you can specialise those departments. I recommend to handle classrooms and research to them, because they can unlock perks to improve them.Students will move around, talk, play, fight and do some mischief. The conversations between them need A LOT more variety, but it's really nice to see them strutting around, minding their own business. The general ambien of the game is incredibly cute, a fact enhanced by the presence of cats.I find it visually stunning. Performance is top notch, even on Deck (more on that later) and the school itself and the variety of decorations are beautiful. The graphics are cartoony and simple but work very well and the outside look of the school can be beautiful.Let's School works well on Deck but the controls are a pain. I have played Two Point Hospital and Campus on Switch and I know this kind of games can work well on a portable, especially with a touchscreen, so I hope the devs will add actual Deck support at some point. It might not be their first priority after release, but it should be done at some point.I bought this game to have something to play until the release of Starfield and it's turning out to be a jewel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game as the fundamentals to be a good high school builder game. There are "communities" where you can draw students from. As they get good grades and graduate your influence in those communities grow. There's a management system, research; basically all the basics. But as of right now that's about it.There are many things that are lacking currently.- The research tree is rather small.- The building aspect of things is terrible and needs improvement. Rotating items in game is the biggest issue when it comes to building. You're also unable to center things if your room is odd-numbered (most items take up two tiles). Not to mention if you move rooms around, the camera acts funny like it's almost as though you're not moving the room with your mouse (which is how it should be), instead you're moving the room based on the W/A/S/D and where the room is relative to the camera placement at the time of moving the room. It's weird. Furthermore, the things you put on the walls of the room stay where they are even after the room is moved. So if you have decorations on the walls, they'll stay floating in the air until you demolish them, or until you get frustrated enough with being unable to place something the way you want it because something that's floating in the air is stopping you. Oh not to mention, despite most of the objects being two or more tiles, when you rotate something you're rotating the object on an axis, which makes placing large objects like stairs VERY frustrating to place.- Once you've built the infrastructure to make a successful high school, the game becomes too easy.- The management side of things, where different teachers hold different management figures is particularly frustrating because they're limited by their own "management figure", so you end up having to make eight+ management offices. In my current save, I have ten management offices for roughly 350 students. Not to mention, for whatever reason, these management offices have this weird fluctuation thing. I simulate one day and everything is fine, everything is below the max management number for the management office. But turn to the next day and for whatever reason I have two management offices that cannot handle their capacity, although it was fine the day before.- I also dislike how whenever a group of students moves to another year, the room they occupy goes with them. For example, if you make a classroom for Year Ones, that classroom will stay with that group of high schoolers meaning that you will need to create a new room for a new batch of Year Ones. This is annoying especially in late game because if your high school has its hands in every community in the game, you're constantly having to make new classrooms to accommodate all the new Year Ones. I would have liked it more if I had to make a new classroom for Year Two and Year three, so that I can keep my floors organized (Year 1 = first floor; Year 2 = second floor; Year 3 = third floor). This game has good fundamentals, however, it's still very new and I know that there will eventually be updates that will makes this game better. But as it stands right now, I wouldn't recommend it just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: The experience itself is great, spent nearly a 60 hours within the week. But here are my thoughts on some features that are broken or rather doesn't make sense to me.Sure this is a Japanese theme school organization and sim game in elementary school (grade 1, 2, and 3) or maybe it was compressed enough to be those year levels instead of highschool or senior (idk) also i considered it a elementary school since it has high demands on hand sanitation not to mention Comfort Room/restrooms are the place where you wash your hands not somewhere you'd place somewhere random to meet ends, hanging lunchboxes that were high demand in the mid game and a playground. sure lets keep those elements in mind. Hanging lunchboxes are on high demand during the midgame due to the admission of students mostly bringing lunchboxes instead of buying in a canteen, sure you can avoid them but most of the time you'd be addmitting anyone at this point when you go along and you're confident that they'll pass and discipline them enough to be a outstanding student, but making your classroom or somewhere else be placing those hanging lunchbox everywhere. It doesn't makes sense to me if its possible if you can just place it beside your desk, or within the person's bag which will save space and aesthetically pleasingHand sanitation, sure cleaning hands are "good" but how come that it is one of the major requirement for building a campus where there's accessible bathrooms that can be used for sanitation. Or a greater option will be having a shop that can sell sanitizers that can solve this.Playground, this is something you can solve with an arcade room, but some people wants a realistic feel of a Japanese school, and there is a rare case there's an arcade within the campus itself, sure playgrounds are great and there are also other decorations that can solve this issue but i don't see it as a feature that could make the students rebel for more playtime like is this like a sweat shop?Walls, this is a big issue for me, some walls or fences are just useless, they're not limiting the access of students within the area, especially when you're making a campus with strict pathways especially when you're trying to funnel students to a metal detector before going into class. So far metal detectors doesn't detect anything like guns, we're not in the US but it is realistic to have those walls be inaccessible to students.Security is when you make the students more disciplined and also finding bad students getting caught, but there is one feature on security that feels useless and also not placed right and those are the metal detector doors. Those metal detector doors are placed within a wall not a separate to a door, its the door itself. metal detectors are placed after a door or entrance, just like in hotels, malls, or universities, this should be a separate feature instead of being one with the doors and windows category.Lights are a bit more dim than it should be, sure the light levels are important and also depending on the kind of lighting it should be brighter and also more necessary, but most of the lights are dimmer than it should, making well lit hallways feels like there's always a deadspot no matter what kind of lighting you add.Auto scheduling doesn't solve the "auto" part, which is just a lazy thing to do, but if you're managing a campus of a thousand students, it'll be a complicated tedious task.  instead you'd be pressing that "auto" scheduling would help in these kinds of situation. but sadly still need improvement.The outside fence is something you can't remove, making parking lots and bicycle shed lacks a bit of immersion. Research is still not enough, you'd be finish on year two if you know what you're doing.Loans are way too forgiving, making the loan as a savior than a risk which is more of a risk realistically.Cherry/sakura trees are rare and once you remove them its gone forever, its sad.tiles are very blocky, and there are tiles that are blending with each other which is great but i wish this is applicable to some tiles and also having like a canal beside a sidewalk? maybe in the future.The steel wall can make the posters disappear, especially the promotional postersSome of the decoration glitch through the wall, but not entirely, just the sides like the cleaning ones and the shelves.Elevators are soo op, making the students just tp to one place to anotherSo far thats all. sorry for the broken english and grammar. Nonetheless I love the game and I'm very excited what this game has to offer in the future

_childDocuments_.review: "Let's School" is a cute little school management simulator where you assume the position of headmaster and operate your academy. As of this review there are currently two starting maps locations including a modern Japanese riverside, and a more traditional Chinese castle. Difficulty options are also provided before hopping into a new game. These range from starting funds, disaster frequency, and competing school intensity. The maps also list climate temperature and nearby purchasable plots which might give inspiration into new map types.       The gameplay is overall very balanced with both short-term rewards and long-term goals. Three Victory types are provided shortly after starting a new game, but all three can be worked on at the same time. Rooms must be built to teach the students and assigned a homeroom teacher. Spare teachers can be used to research new tech to improve existing rooms or unlock better ones. Managing the students' schedules is very convenient due to their exact knowledge points needed to pass being readily available to view.       The art style of the in-game models and on the menus help compliment each other. However the animations in the game are not perfect, but I feel they are great exactly the way they are.        I do recommend this game to anyone who wants to try out a new school sim well worth it's price.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: My experience with the game was fun at the start but had to restart after expanding too quickly. It simply becomes overwhelming without proper pacing. Once I did pace and plan my game, it became much more manageable. This should not be a requirement though.The end game is still lack luster and requires content. The biggest requirement for this game for me is having unique interactions between students and teachers. As many as they can be so it'll be interesting to simply look around the school.Here are some of my recommendations and Suggestions-I require more planning modes. I played my game with 100% refundable so that I could build anything I want then when I learn that I build it wrong, I can simply 'undo' and sell. Copying rooms is a great tool but sometimes it doesn't fit the floor plan and you'll be forced to sell everything. Losing money due to that sucks.`-Item movement improvement. It is so annoying having to hold left click before moving an object when you have to move an entire row of objects one block. It is so much easier to just sell then build again which you will lose money if not 100% refundable.-Bigger Lands. I personally don't like building up. I like building wide but with all of the facilities and wonders. I barely managed to fit them all. I want to build paths, maybe a personal building for each education type. A separate dorm building. The land is simply too small and the wonders are too big.-Bridges. I built a bridge connecting the 4th floor of two of my buildings using platforms and it looked terrible. Either I didn't explore it enough or the tools are just not there yet. -Money Research. After researching everything in the tech tree, the research room and its researchers become useless. They should be able to research and earn money instead.-Trading. Why is there a limit to the amount of cash and education points they have? Especially when they seemingly have unlimited when you go back to them. It is so annoying to trade 300 education points for 15000 cash multiple times.-The fundamental game is bad. What I mean here is that the game has fundamental problems that could be fixed in many ways or simply change entirely. An example is the teaching plans. Although it automates applicants and sets them into rooms, forcing each admission office to have 3 dedicated classrooms suck. This forces schedules to overlap and require the player so much more teachers which eats away at the profits. This technically works since teachers also staff the security, shops, and cafeteria. It'd be better to have different job types with their own stats but that would lead to several teachers not being assigned to anything. We could allow a mixing of students in the teaching plan and provide a secondary room when the primary room is full.This could also be fixed by changing how admissions work. I know it's part of the progress but having an entire class only have 6 students after I developed its teaching plan does not bring me joy. Maybe change how student application works. Add more details to the students and variety in each location as well as making more of them. Force us to accept bad students due to requiring money and allow us to pick and choose students that provide more benefits when the situation is steady. It should be okay to not accept all students.Better yet, we could choose all students and then we'll create a separate delinquent building where all the bad students are and give them special classes in their curriculum. This creates more variety in gameplay and some roleplaying, ie assassination classroom type of building separation.We could also just have random students with different goals in a single administration office. It shouldn't be that bad to start the game with an extra art and sports teacher.I didn't explore this much but the Headmaster POV should be capable of usage. We can interact with objects, students, and teachers but there was this one spot that was dirty and I really wanted to clean it myself using cleaning equipment nearby.All in all, good game but I don't see much replayability as of now. Will be waiting eagerly for future updates.

Knowing how to lay things out is a little difficult the first time, because you don't know how big rooms will end up needing to be after your school grows. _childDocuments_.review: Let's School, despite being a little bit rough around the edges, is a really fulfilling school management game. It kind of reminds me of some of Kairosoft's titles--however, this game is refreshingly complex compared to many of its rivals. For example, each facility placed increases administrative strain on you, the Headmaster--so you are compelled to create administrative departments, led by qualified school staff. And you get to name those departments, and give their leaders fancy titles. This can eventually lead to a sprawling (but oh-so-satisfying) bureaucratic apparatus of departments answering to departments answering to departments. Imagine the paperwork!I have to give serious props for the graphical design, and attention to detail. There are small things, like how each student has a book bag that they hang on their desks during classes, or how only certain students will actually bring their own lunches, and when they do, those lunches actually appear on the wall as objects. Or how the various forms of transportation students use to get to your school---by train or by bus or by bike---are rendered. It's all very... cute! And the art style is simple, vibrant, and comforting. Of course, you can tell that it's not strictly feature-complete. The end game is pretty aimless, for example. The game could do with some more challenge, especially once you overcome the initial financial difficulties. It is currently way too easy to schedule classes to guarantee everyone passes a given semester. And some mechanics--like school security, guidance counselling, extracurricular activities, and student relationships, are only half-implemented. But the potential is certainly there.As it is, Let's School is a lovely school management simulator, with great visual design, a lot of charm, and an okay simulation. Its difficulty leaves something to be desired, and its as-of-yet unimplemented features might turn you away, but honestly, I think it's absolutely worth the price on novelty alone. I have never attended a high school in Japan, nor any other country for whom this game was obviously inspired by. But I can't help but leave every session of this game feeling oddly nostalgic, like I've just relived a pleasant memory. Soooo... yeah! That's my take.

_childDocuments_.review: School management simYou play the head master of a primary/intermediate school semi quasi Chinese school. Build a school: The best part of the game, you build your school, either go wide or go tall. There are a lot of different types of class rooms and administration rooms and a few construction styles. You can build some really pretty schools with the tools provided. Manage a school: Hire staff, create a schedule and then start enrolling children. You then have one week to teach your kids before they have exams. The start of each new week brings a new season, which changes the environment visually and changes the students behavior, which is a nice way of keeping things fresh. Game length: Career mode involves money you run out of money, you lose. That’s fine. However you also have to research different class room types and various other things. That’s fine too. However towards the end of the tech tree it takes longer and longer to research anything. It’s designed to add difficulty sure, but it also felt like an intentional means of padding the run time. Another method of padding things out is expanding your ‘school range’, needing to send students out on expeditions to find new communities. The whole concept was just bizarre, and once more time consuming.  Animations: At 3x speed you’re not going to notice these things. But playing at regular speed you’ll notice the animation quality is lacking. Lots of clipping through walls, doors, other objects, sims move in robotic fashion and some animations are just plain missing. All of these things are minor but if you’re an attention to detail person this may irk you. Despite several annoyances and given the cheap price it’s hard to not recommend. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a super complex management simulator.  There are some research paths and the scheduling can be a bit of a pain at first, but overall its a relaxing and interesting game where you slowly build up your school trying to ensure that you have the facilities and teachers necessary to teach an ever increasing array of students with different goals and aspirations.  It definitely is fun though.If you enjoy games where you build something to achieve a management goal and then manage the rooms/people that are within your building zone this is a great game.  Just don't expect great graphics.  The designers went for a limited graphic engine in exchange for a more dynamic overall game.

_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: I have thoroughly enjoyed this game.  From starting out in a broken down, abandoned school campus to creating a powerhouse of educational efficiency, it has been fun the whole way through.  Learning to balance students' educational, entertainment, and social needs as well as teacher proficiency and satisfaction is key.  Getting a good group of researchers is key.  I have a lot of fun seeing the school upgrades unlock and then upgrading everything or building new parts to the school.   I enjoyed getting to creatively design the look of the grounds, the style of the roofing and siding.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: 8.7/10, would highly recommend. I really like the way the game incorporates 3-D thinking into the building mechanics, as well as the way field trips work.I detracted from my score since it doesn't appear you can swap out the WASD controls for the Arrow keys (which as a left-handed mouse user is pretty annoying), the hiring process can be a hassle since it seems you can only prioritize hiring by subject type (and you use the teacher candidate pool for all your staff hires, even for positions that don't directly relate to teaching), and money seems to be a pretty consistent bottleneck to expansion in a way that doesn't feel paced with everything else. These are ultimately pretty minor issues though, and can be worked around. There are a lot of quality of life features that help make most gameplay satisfying, like being able to move rooms or cloning them as needed, and with just a little more work this game would be perfect. I think adding things like intermural sports competitions with the other schools or an alumni network would just be icing on the cake at this point.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: Over 50 hours of game play...definitely worth the buy, If you like management type game. I love the games they produced and i was excited to try this one out.There's a lot of little bugs and glitches here and there but not major that is unplayable. One glitch that is pretty annoying to me at the moment, is when some of the students/staffs get stuck in unreachable places and there's is  no way to pick them up and set them down elsewhere but to build staircase or have a door for them to access it. Definitely take your time to go through tutorial and learn the game. There's the management side of the game (like managing your facilities to reduce the headmaster's workload) that wasn't included in the tutorial and I had to figure it out myself.  Sandbox is also a challenge, I do wish there are more decorative items in the future and also access hidden/unlockable building styles. roofing was a tough one with the limited option. Despite the little cons that I have, I still do enjoy this game. It's been a while that a management style game can make me get totally immersed in. Overall I would rate it 8/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very rough around the edges, but is an overall very enjoyable experience, 7.5/10 worth the $20. It might look like I don't like the game from my comments, but there is workshop planned and regular updates right now with a promising roadmap, so I do believe this game will eventually hit a higher point very soon.Personally I was hoping it'd be more complex, and there are a lot of systems that are bare bones. Things like students in one neighborhood all having the same goals and class requirements, modifiers that do almost nothing in the game like genius or forgetful, teachers that should have modifiers but don't (celebrities and rare spawn teachers), are just a couple of examples of not a lot being put into a system.Celebrity teachers are way to expensive for how good it is to just hold onto teachers and get good managers / upgrade classrooms. For the money it costs to get 1 celebrity teacher, you can get like 5 new teachers and upgrade a classroom to max stars and still have money leftover.There's a lot of cheese strategies to do in this game. Cleaning in this game is not punishing at all unless you completely neglect it. You really don't need to unlock the cleaning bots if you just place brooms in every room, because all staff members clean and you're going to have a ton of them walking around anyway. There's one poster that gives +8 stars to a room and decoration points, so instead of increasing the size of a room to allow for better furniture or decoration, you can just cover the walls and windows with this poster.Decorations in this game are not good for min-maxing. I like decorating my classrooms to look pretty and unique, but I like min-maxing more, and all my classrooms are copy-pasted and crowded but that's what is optimal.Security is so bad in the early game, but it doesn't even matter since you can manually stop truancy and it's really easy. There's too much punishment for expelling a kid (money lost vs no gain). Not saying you should implement gangs, but like maybe having troublemakers in a class should bring down overall conduct.Stacking managers is too powerful. As a joke, I had a sub-manager under my facilities director just called the Toilet Director. In my late game school he personally saved me about 90 points in other categories with good perks and eventually also became in charge of tea rooms.Water is too big of a priority. I hate making a tea room, just for me to slam down two big tea stations an hour later because I decided to admit 15 extra students.The UI/UX could use a lot of work, there are times that I'm often fumbling around in menus looking for teachers to train, but getting to the training menu takes a while and I was trying to find some shortcut.Just a couple of things to note above, I have more suggestions and issues with the game. I do programming / programming design professionally, so when the workshop comes out, I'll probably end up making mods that adds a lot of QoL and makes the game overall more difficult. But this game does have a lot of potential if it keeps receiving the care that it's currently getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: Man, it has been a long times since there was a decent school tycoon game. I remember when it game in that box full of random simulations games. They are also adding workshop access so soon there will be more decor options as well. Biggest draw backs: There are a few little things like the tram station or the fact it doesn't tell me students are missing a room to have class in until later, but these are minor irritations. I really do enjoy the game and believe I will continue to play it on and off for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game still have its fair share of bugs, updates are frequent and the core game is fun. A lot of improvements have been more eloquently proposed by others before or is on the roadmap, and the devs are receptive to it. A thing I would wish is for the ability to upgrade some of the early game decors - while lights and more necessary equipment have straight up upgrade and replacements, a lot of the decors don't and thus as space is a valuable resource it is more meta to just spam certain more space-efficient and high stat decor instead. Speaking of space efficient, sports facility can use an improvement since they are very large size, has little class size and can only be built outside (so thus can't be stacked) - leading to sports school having immense size bloat if they want to serve a larger population (thus making it difficult to create sport schools early game or make a multi-disciplinary school with the limited space you have). Perhaps they can be rebalanced or have the maximum school area bigger. Also, the ability to make multiple classes share the same facility in a period if their class subject line up would be nice. And an important point is to read every item description (especially shop items) when plopping them down - things that may just seem like flavor text may actually not be flavor at all! Turns out the metal detectors really do works magic and I just busted so many kids sneaking cigarettes and nun-chucks into school, and the joke about baguette being hard enough to use as a club is not a joke at all. Also most of the staff and students is now spherical because of bubble tea and burgers, and my attempt to get them to go on a diet hasn't been very successful.All in all, it is a very promising and surprisingly addictive game, and I eagerly awaits to see where it go  especially with the future roadmaps for clubs and extra curricular activities! Can't wait to   my students the Asian way by getting them all to go to compulsory cram school after class lol.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed it. There seems to be a decent bit of waiting for the week to end once you get things setup.There is some clunkiness in the game that I'll just mention here:- How can I view students by their demerits? It seems like I have to remember their name, then find them in the student list. - When building a room, there is 2 delete buttons. One deletes the room and everything in it and the other just deletes single items. They look the same, just their position is different. Luckily there is a confirmation on the former. - When copying a room, better hope you copied it near the center of the screen. Because if you copied from the option on the menu on the bottom right, you will quickly run out of space and drag your cursor out of the window.- Trees count as objects that stop you from placing outside buildings. I kinda get it, but it is also kinda annoying. - The management/department view doesn't zoom out enough imo, so you have to slide items over, then pan the screen and then slide them the rest of the way.- Whenever a classroom is unavailable, there isn't much notification except for the students being upset. Then you have to open the classroom schedule and look to see what room it is. If you have none of the rooms built at all, it will tell you, but if you already have it and just need another one, it will not say what you need on the quick view. _childDocuments_.review: Creative, charming, lots of fun management style gameplay, and can be challenging depending on your goals. _childDocuments_.review: It's fun! Definitely still needs some polish though - I researched clubs but are unable to do anything with that, for example. I also wish you could hire staff that wasn't just teachers - like janitors, security, lunch room/store runners, or people purely to work research or be management etc. It would make it much easier to have staff that stays focused that aren't also teachers that has to go off to take care of that, halting research for a bit because of their schedule. When you get a monopoly on schools the other schools start to close down, which I do dislike since there's things that they offer unique to their schools. It also erases the need for competition in those areas at some point, since once they're gone, a nondescript school will have some of the students, but isn't really a threat to you, meaning that you might ignore a certain neighborhood after they're completely yours because the need isn't there. Some more events would add to the school life as well. I also wish the headmaster was more interactive with the rest of the school life but that's more nit-picky than anything lol.Overall, it definitely could use some work, but I think it's enjoyable, even if you're not that great at city builders!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR good game, but not ready yet. wait for a good discount or when it's ready.The game is fun, the price is pretty fair, and there's plenty of content.But it is still somewhat unfinished. Some of the content was delayed, which is OK for stuff that are optional, like school clubs (although it is still very weird to keep the UI elements of it in the game, including the research tree telling you it is unlock-able when it isn't), but it's less OK for stuff that doesn't function correctly, like having a security building that you cant staff with actual security personal. You can place teachers there, but they don't actually do anything.The tutorial is also pretty lacking, and there is no real "endgame", which isn't that bad for a "creatuve" type of game but it does hurt it.The biggest problem is just the bugs. They don't make the game unplayable, but there are simply too many of them, and they make you question if the game even works the way it's intended, it's impossible to know if certain things really do what they say they do, or even do anything at all, either because of a lack of information or, again, because of bugs.The easiest example is the Teacher's desk: it has a green area in-front of it which you would think is where it is ideal for students to sit, but nothing in the game explains it, and when ignored nothing seems to change. I got 4 different answers from different people as to what it does (or if it does anything at all) and this problem shows up many, many times.On the bright side, the developers have already released multiple bug-fixes and they are planning on adding the content that was cut from the initial release, but I really wish they would've just delayed the game, or at least just make it an early access?Overall the game is still fun in my opinion, and if things continue the way they do right now it might get much better. If it interests you and its on sell, I recommend. Otherwise only buy if this is the type of game you absolutely must play and have no good alternatives left.(For context this review was written on 02/08/2023, about a week after the release)
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 30h in one week, I can safely say that I'm hooked.Good management-type game with a school setting that is delivered in a reasonable way. And I do not intend to make the game sound bad by calling it "reasonable" - it is a strentgh of the game. Various aspects of school life found their way into the game. It allows you to design shedules for classes, train/hire/motivate staff, influence relationships (bullying, friendships, even love interests), trade with other schools (special objects, policies, staff, ...) and much more. But it typically doesn't force you to do so. You can micro-mangage all that stuff, but the game doesn't hesitate you to do so.TL;DR: If you like managment games, enjoy the setting and don't mind casual (meaning: not-that-hardcorde-type) games - it's worth a buy. 20 Bucks seams pretty reasonable to me :)Pros/Cons:+ Micromanagement: Not really a "must", but a "can"+ School-Setting well done, yet not overwhelmingly complex+ plenty of options to design your school+ serious (not Two-Point Campus) (except the chemical laboratory, urgh)o atm mild bugs, but all of them resolvable by restarting the game :)- atm more like a beta (some features and 3D models still under development)- music (just disable it)- no campain and only two maps

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely a lot of fun. It's a simple game, with quite a bit of depth. You are a head teacher and your job is to build a good school. You have to make timetables, manage and train staff, increase levels of satisfaction within the school and neighbourhoods surrounding it.It's a pretty simple game, but there's always something to do. Money is easy to make, but I never have lots of it. Considering how much area there is to build on in this game, I think it'll be a long while until I'll make enough to be able to expand as far as I would want.In the beginning you start with a single class of Year 1s. You have quite a bit of money, but it doesn't last long as you'll want to upgrade and expand, build new rooms, hire more teachers etc. 1 Week = 1 Year. Every Friday there's an exam and students move up. So in Year 2, now you have two classes (Y1, Y2). The following week three classes (Y1, Y2, Y3). By now you will have to have researched advanced courses so students in Year 3 can study more and pass their final exams. Then you have graduation photos and make lots of money, if you did well, which is good as that will allow you to invest into more buildings.Upgrading buildings is simple and there's lots of flexibility. Genuinely, it's super calming and enjoyable for me.Timetables are pretty straight forward too and once you make one for each of the class, it doesn't need to be touched too much, because the game tells you if students will pass exam by the end of the week or not. It simplifies the game, but makes the rest of the school management fun and not too overwhelming, because honestly, there's always more stuff to do. Send students on trips. Find new schools. Open up more admission offices. Get more kids into your school.Make more money, expand your buildings and keep hiring more staff. Students might be bringing in banned items, they might be fighting or sleeping class and everything sort of needs your attention.It's light-hearted and failing is not impossible, but it's not easy. You will most likely be able to proceed with this game as long as you put effort into your building and keep a close eye on things happening around you. The tutorial is pretty damn good and intuitive. Introduces you will all mechanics as soon as they become relevant.All I can say, for the price, I expected this game to be very simple and boring, but I'm having a ton of fun and hours are just passing by.

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of Two Point Hospital, this game is a must-buy. But if you do not enjoy management games, this is probably not for you. Simple on the surface this game has a lot to it buried just beneath the surface and you can quickly find yourself overwhelmed if you are impatient. But if you stick it out and take on challenges as they come, you will get there. The key to this game is Training. As soon as you can build a Staff Training room, do so, and use it constantly. Especially for Research staff, another key, never stop the research if at all possible. Yes, some of your staff will be in a near constant state of low morale but just keep training them in Research and Management until they grow out of it. Another tip is to keep a constant watch on your class rooms schedule. Just because all students are passing at the moment does not mean they will be the next day. This is another reason you will have to Research all the time. To get those courses your students need, but don't worry if a few fail here and there, its all part of the learning the game. And all in all this is a good time sink of a game. You'll be spending hours on it before you realize.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal. It's a little rough around the edges, and how difficult and in-depth it goes it could really use a few QoL UI changes and probably an advanced tutorial, but I didn't mind figuring things out myself at all. This is a busy, difficult, micromanaging game with excellent visuals and a lot of heart. There are SO many mechanics, but it still manages to feel cohesive and enjoyable. The building is great, the game is endearing, and I honestly can't put it down. People comparing this to two point campus must be joking- I found that game so laughably shallow and dry. This is completely different, in a way that's actually fun and makes you care about what you're doing.Career mode is quite difficult, with steep difficulty increases and a LOT of managing that the UI at times fails to support- especially with staff- and many mechanics you have to figure out from failure and just getting a better grip on the game. The difficulty is a little deceptive- you are actually fully in control of the pace of the game. You choose when to admit new students and what students those are, you hire who you need, and build at your own pace- which is important because money is tight. The game by default really encourages you to keep growing (leading to more difficulty) but you are 100% in control. That being said, if you're looking for a chill management game, where you don't have to deal with "hidden" mechanics or put a lot of energy into figuring things out, this definitely isn't it. But honestly for the price point, getting the game just for sandbox mode is a great option, the building is simple but great. The difficulty of career mode can also be customized, so you can make it easier if you find it too overwhelming. I would absolutely recommend this game to pretty much anyone looking for a new management game, both on sale and full price. It's probably my favorite game right now! Excited to see what else they add (there's already so much!).

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful relaxing school builder. The game has some depth but it's introduced slowly throughout the tutorial. There's a lot to build, luckily the game allows you to also build up instead of only building sideways like in rimworld. You need to set a curriculum for each first year class (they will just keep their old one once they go a year further) and you need to plan the lessons well, based on teacher availability (if you can't hire more) and based on how many of them will pass the finals. The school year is a week long and on each friday evening the students take the exam. They have different aspirations on what they want to do after graduation. Some want to go to a science college (forgot the name xd) and thus need more xp from science class. The city will also pay you the better they do on the exam plus you gain reputation in the regions the good students are from so more will apply.The students also differ, some are forgetful and thus have reduced xp gain, some are rowdy and make a lot of trouble etc. Some are also richer than others and pay you higher admission fees. Rich parents though also have higher expectations from your school, not only on how well you teach but also on how good the star rating is (I think). The better a room is equipped the better it gets rated. There is a research system so you need to research new and more modern stuff.The game has some drawbacks I found, it's slightly unpolished though I didn't encounter any major bugs yet and the performance could be better, at least it likes to overheat my pc (very easy to do if gpu usage hits 60%) though I can run it by fiddling with the graphics settingsAll in all I can recommend it fullyYou compete with other schools in other districts for students. Those districts are explored by sending a class there to do a field trip.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a charming management sim with a wonderful aesthetic. At just a few hours of play time, I'm already enamored with it. It is a little rough around the edges, there are a few bugs, and some weird pathing and clipping issues, but nothing severe enough to detract from the enjoyment of the game. Things I like: + The general vibe is very relaxing.+ The game encourages you to adopt a cat, which you can name. The cat wanders the campus grounds and takes naps on desks, it's just great.+ The world is full of little details. I enjoy just looking around the map/level, watching buses go by, people walking around, leaves falling from trees, etc...+ The characters, both staff and students, are fun to watch go about their days. They get into arguments, form friendships, form secret gaming rings, etc...+ Headmaster mode: you can walk around your campus as headmaster, interacting with objects and encouraging staff and students.+ Vertical building is well implemented.Things I hope get added:+ More customization options for characters (uniform colors, etc...)+ Sensible pathing. Characters will walk straight through bushes and fences, not use paths you lay down, etc...+ Some of the game mechanics are very confusing at first. The tutorial could be stronger to help alleviate this.+ The initial flow of the game and research tree necessities feel a bit rushed. The game is very punishing if you don't prioritize researching the first tier of academic course improvements for instance.+ More cat interactions. Cat food, litter boxes, giving it treats, etc... Maybe a cat mode like the headmaster mode?? + More student / staff behaviors, events, and animationsOverall, it's a delightful game that is easy to sink time into. I hope it continues to improve because I can see myself playing this for a long time to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the Demo back in March I was a little worried about the game. At the time, it seemed a little more shallow than other similar games and I was hesitant to consider purchasing. Now that the game is released, I'm so happy to say I was incredibly wrong. Having also played Two Point Campus, this game honestly blows it out of the water. TPC tends to feel far more tedious and less relaxing, to the point I haven't played it since launch. Let's School improves on many of the things TPC failed at and allows for a far more rich and charming experience.The game starts slow, but definitely not boring, and after a few hours you'll be ramping up and managing so many little things that you won't know what to do first. Research feels rewarding! After your first year, if you're anything like me, you'll be scrambling to research the different courses and getting them up to level in time before your students need to sit their exams. It's just genuinely fun to actually have to think and foreplan this.My only gripe is how the Sandbox isn't a "true" Sandbox. I wanted to go in and try and build a School and quickly found that the settings didn't allow you to set your school level so getting the likes of staff with Service qualifications was impossible for the cafeteria. A tweak for this would be amazing!Can't wait to see what the team behind Let's School do next! <3A couple of things I'd love to see:1) Filters in the buy mode! When you start unlocking higher tiered furniture the catalogue becomes a little messy. It'd be nice to be able to filter through the newer stuff so you will only see them!2) Options for indoor wallpaper and flooring3) Colour variants for items4) More decorations5) A way to reject applications from Students.For a brand new game though, it's brilliant what you do get.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into simulator games, this is definitely one of the games you would want to give it a try.I wasn't expecting much when I saw the cover of this game. However, I decided to download the demo and give it a try since it's free. In this game you're able to roleplay as a principal and build your own school. There are many difficulties awaits you, including students behavior (Bullying, sleeping...) and natural disasters (Fire, snowing...).The reason why this is one of my favorite simulator games is because unlike other games, this one has so many outcomes and it just never ends so it's really worth the money. I'm not sure if you guys played internet café simulator 2 before, but it only took a day for me to unlock everything and get the best equipment. In this game you're able to focus on the aesthetics even if you got everything unlocked. Unlike internet cafe simulator which has limited space, this game has a open world where you can build anything everywhere. This game has so many possibilities and outcomes, even if you have unlocked everything, you are still able to improve your school and receive more applications.The interactions with students and teachers is also another reason why I would recommend this game. The interface is built really nicely and looks really polished. You are also able to look at the student view and experience your own school as a student. The most interesting factor of this game is probably exploring different places around the country and unlocking new types of student who studies different subject and have different ambitions. It is always exciting to build a new classroom with different courses for new students that you've discovered around the country.One of the downfall of this game is probably the tutorial. I feel like it's not enough for players to be able to understand what they're supposed to press on considering the fact that there's a lot of windows and options. However, once you've played the game for a while you will be able to obtain more knowledge for the game.If you would like to see students graduating from the school that you've created, then there's really no other better options than Let's School.

_childDocuments_.review: "Surely 20 cats roaming a classroom wouldn't be a detriment to student learning right?"One of the toughest things when building a simulation game is capturing the same spark and drive that would encourage someone to take on that job in the real world. Let's School hits the nail right on the head in that regard by combining an incredibly charming art style with genuinely sweet and adorable interactions that let the player really feel like they can take care of their students.In terms of building mechanics, the game follows the style of Theme Hospital, Two-Point Hospital, Two-Point Campus: build the building itself, then create room blueprints full of interactions for the simulated students. The amount of furniture available is fairly deep, with multiple quality levels to choose from, but rather narrow in scope. A lot of room for expansion could be reasonably expected.A student's academic year will last one week, with three levels to advance through. Those familiar with the inner workings of middle schools - Japan's education system in particular - will catch on quickly to the game flow and expectations. Players will need to manage staff and timetables to ensure their students are progressing through the courses that are set out for them by the communities they hail from. A good sim game will let you get into the nitty-gritty of things where you want and automate the rest - something that Let's School does with varying success. For example, while I enjoyed creating custom, carefully balanced timetables for every one of my classes, it was quite frustrating to see my work undone as automation systems overwrote things.Serious sim players may find the game rather easy and lacking in complexity, but Let's School's strengths lie in its charm and aesthetics. There is still lots of room in which the game can grow - expanded tech trees, wider array of furniture, and more varied class or course options to name a few - but Let's School offers a solidly built, charming simulation of running a Japanese middle school that will hopefully leave players with that soft and fuzzy feeling of helping kids.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: "Let's School" is a fun city builder/management game where you are appointed the headmaster of a failing school and need to develop it into a prestigious academic institution. The game-play parallels others games in the genre: meet the needs of your populace by building structures and designating rooms for various purposes, while also furnishing them appropriately so that they function properly. If you've ever played games like Prison Architect or the Two Point series, you'll generally understand the game-play.What makes Let's School unique from these other iterations is the art style; a pixel, blocky, cutesy aesthetic, and the depth to the school management. There are various students with their own goals and ambitions and your goal is to develop a curriculum to allow them to achieve that success. You not only need to manage students, assigning their teachers and classes, but you also have to recruit them, compete with rival schools, and ensure their needs outside of the classroom (recreation, temperature, food/drink, etc.) are met. I'm only briefly into the campaign, having graduated my first class (all kids trying to get into a low-end marketing school, all passed) but can definitely see this game developing into a much larger management sim where the staff you hire and rooms you develop becomes crucial for students trying to become some of the best in their field. In Let's School you develop your academy by researching innovations. These can be things as simple as a cafeteria, to more complex subjects, such as high-end, specified course programs. This element of the game pairs well with classroom management as you can be left scrambling with research to ensure your school's needs are met as your educational ecosystem grows larger. I don't think the game is perfect. While I developed bonds with some of my students, I was often left feeling very disconnected from most of them, although I'm not sure if that is part of a point the game may be trying  to make. There was a graduation photo which was cute though. Additionally, there are a few little things that could use improvements in the UI and more decoration/customization options would be appreciated. While I've only played briefly at the time of this review, I wanted to flag this newer game that I'd argue deserves your attention if you're a fan of this genre.8/10, Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's School

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare that a management game is as in-depth as I'd like it to be, and that holds doubly true for school-based management games, as many tend to be very shallow or in-depth with outdated mechanics or clunky systems. I quite enjoyed this game, both in the demo and the full game recently released, and found it to have very few game-breaking glitches, bugs or errors outside of minor translations.It's definitely worth the money to buy at full price, and there is a significant amount of gameplay even at this stage, with likely more to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of pathea games and as usual they never disappoint. It's a really fun and addicting school sim, kind of reminds me of pocket academy by kairosoft which I also played a lot on mobile. The game looks simplistic and charming but don't be fooled by it, gameplaywise there are a lot of things to do and management does gets more complicated once you delve deeper into the game. You have full control from designing your school, choosing your students, hiring teachers, even assigning the class schedules, heck you get to choose your student's uniform and school logo. All in all it's good and solid sim management game. As an early access game the foundation is good and I'm just expecting more content in the future. Knowing pathea games they do deliver so thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent school-management simulator.I've been following this since it's announcement last year, and the developers are really great in terms of taking feedback and listening to the community. For starters, the tutorial is a lot more structured and truly eases you into the game. Lots of UI elements were tweaked with the help of the community, and in general the game is a lot more easier to understand with all the complex systems it throws at you.For a lot of players, the aesthetic of the game is a strong reason to try it out. _childDocuments_.review: Let's school has, so far, been amazing. And will probably continue to be in the future! I've already clocked in a huge amount of hours playing it, but I'll provide a more cohesive review than just "It's grrreat", but before that the TLDR is 'play it' If you're a fan of this type of casual management simulator, it's a win all around. Now, for the cohesive review. Genre/Synapses: Casual/Simulation style asian inspired school-management game, similar to 'architect' style top down builder games and sim games like planet zoo or rollercoaster tycoon. Content rating: Family friendly, as far as I can tell. All ages could play this without much concern, content wise.Graphics/Aesthetic: Top down low poly count style graphics with a fun, original design for the characters, buildings and animations. Character portraits are a mix of drawn/pixel art.Gameplay: A bit of learning is required in regards to the UI, but not much at all. Once you have it down, it's easy to manage the different menus and gameplay elements to build the perfect school. For the most part you'll be managing student admission, faculty and the build/aesthetic of an asian style school building! Think planet zoo or planet coaster style gameplay. Performance: I'm using a AMD radeon R9 200 series graphics card and an AMD A10-6700 with no lag as far as student count, school decor and load times for different menus/starting the game. Performance is great. Minimal bugs, but it was also just released so patches will likely come soon for any bugs still in the game, if there are any. Overall opinion: This game is fun for the casual player, and I am definitely that type of gamer. I can have it in another tab no problem, or hyper-focus on it. Either way, it's still fun. Replay value is through the roof and the developer is notoriously great for releasing content, fixing bugs and producing great titles. I look forward to playing this non-stop from now on lol. 10/10 would suggest to friends and other potential players.

name: Tennis Manager 2022
detailed_description: JOIN THE DISCORD About the Game Put on the suit of a tennis coach and manager of a tennis academy. Immerse yourself in the most realistic tennis simulation, both on and off the court. Beat the odds and take control! Game description From the junior circuit to the professional circuit, access over 2,000 tournaments. Among the 5,000 players present, find the talents that will lead your academy to glory. Financial stability, contract negotiation, structural investments... Be clever in your management, reach your short and long term goals, and impress your board of directors. Surround yourself with the best staff (coaches, technical, physical, tactical and mental trainers, etc.) and design the training program that best suits your players' abilities, their expectations and your style! Perfect your speech in press conferences and show your board of directors, as well as your players, that you are the right man/woman for the job. Thanks to the 3D engine, immerse yourself in the heart of the match and coach your player in real time! Are you more of a serve and volley player or a baseline filer? Exuberant or totally passive? Take control, impose your style and guide your player to the top. Key features presentation The 2nd opus of the saga is here, with something new. CREATE YOUR OWN PLAYER Design your own player! Overpowered serve bot or inexhaustible marathoner? Extreme lifter or old school flat player? You can choose his style and shape him to lead your academy to titles and glory! NEW INFRASTRUCTURE SYSTEM Immerse yourself in the real life of an academy manager with a new infrastructure system that brings even more realism to your various investment decisions. You want clay court specialists? Then provide your structure with ochre training courts. You are not satisfied with the performance of your scouts? Then invest in your study center and boost their evaluation speed. You are the manager, you choose! ROUND ROBIN To win the Finals at the end of the season, you will have to go through the new group phase and hope to make the semi-finals. 2 groups of 4 players, the best 8 in the Race. This format is also used for the Next Gen Finals (under 21) and the Juniors Finals. Be sure to keep your scores high, as the title can be decided by a small difference! TEAM MANAGEMENT TOOLS Optimize your team management with new tools that are a must-have for any self-respecting manager! At a glance, you can now find all your team's key information (schedule for the week, next tournament, current form, status of commercial contracts, etc.), match history, detailed results, earnings per tournament or even the complete record of each player, and... new recruitment reports! What else? NEW CONTRACT MANAGEMENT / NEGOTIATION SYSTEM Negotiate with talent and skill the different contracts that will punctuate the life of your academy. Contracts and sporting objectives of players, agreements with equipment suppliers... The negotiation system has been reworked to reflect the reality of the business world. The agent of the academy becomes an essential actor to help you build your empire. IMPORT / EXPORT OF GAME PLAN One click to import Rafa's winning tactics against Roger in 2009, one click to export and become the star of the TM community. MATCH SIMULATION ENHANCEMENTS Take a seat on the court and vibrate with your player thanks to the improvement of the most realistic 3D simulation of the circuit. Improved AI, new behaviors (replacements, effects used, shot selection) and new animations (moves and moving shots). Closer to the court, more real, more emotional!

_childDocuments_.review: I do love the work and love the devs are putting into this game, but also a little greedy releasing a new one at this point.... don't get me wrong, it has potential and someday might become great, someday.... but right now it's nothing more than a little update, since the 2021 version feels more like a demo or a beta, they should have just kept improving that game for now, change the name to 2022 and just keep working on it until it feels like a finished, complete version of the game before moving on to a new one. If it's about making money, I really do not appreciate it since I paid almost full price (40 euros) for 2021 just to get a messy demonstration of how a tennis manager could look like. Again, I appreciate it gets attentions and improves on regular basis, but just keep it there, keep improving.... do not release an unfinished product after another.... and sorry, even if I am enjoying it myself, I cannot recommend at this point, with this price and what it offers. yeah, you gonna make some profit out of it too, but I also hope you are using the money to keep on working on the game.... dont let money get to your head, don't be greedy, make this game reach it's potential.... keep working and trying hard
_childDocuments_.name: Tennis Manager 2022

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun game with LOTS of major frustating mechanics...PROS:- Really fun to train players and coach them through seasons.- Feels very good to see a player that you scouted and trained reach a high ranking or win some championships.CONS: - We don't really know how the stats affect our matches, right now I have the #1 player, with more stats than my adversary (#110), the only advantage point for my adversary is that my player is in a weak shape and I'm being one sided beat for more than 200 matches (yeah, I refuse to lose to this adversary, so I keep loading until I win). I'm changing intensity levels, game plans and everything, but every time that I try to simulate my match I keep losing. You guys should put an option to show the percentage of victory chance on a simulation match for us to understand what's being effective or not, I feel that I'm blind and I need to randomly change everything until somehow I can win against some strong player...- The shape system inside the game is a total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, if my player has a weak shape I keep losing tournaments and cant get a better shape (to have an excellent shape I need to reach at least semi finals during the week).- The game keeps us blind during training modes, at first your hired players will progress really well, leveling 10, 20 or 30% each training week, than somehow it'll start leveling up by 0.1% and basically make training sessions utterly useless... - Recruiting 5 star staffs doesn't seem to add expressive changes through the game, I've filled each training staff for a player with 5 stars trainers (I also have 5 trainers for each section that allows us multiple trainers) and I don't really feel any difference, my players progress is almost insignificant at this point and it's almost the same to have a bigger high quality staff or not have any staff at all...- During training session it seems that you can only raise 3 stats, but the game doesn't teach you this, so if you follow the game's training suggestion you'll have an awfully week character... Also if you keep mixing lots of stats during each week training schedule you'll just spend some training slots for nothing, since only the 3 biggest growth stats count at the end of the week, totally ridiculous...- Graphs and models for players are horrible, it pains me to try to watch a match with those ridiculous models, in my opinion it's better to remove the option to watch a match and just let the user simulate the matches...- LOTS of complains about this, but the game usually crashes or start to get slow after a few hours, so you need to either restart the game or manually shut down your computer and restart it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tennis Manager 2022

_childDocuments_.review: It's got a good interface for a game of this type. If you're familiar with Football Manager or OOTP you'll be able to move around in this game pretty well. The matches look good.The problem for me is that you don't have enough control over what's going on. Or maybe not that you don't have enough control, but you don't have enough information given to you about why things are they way they are. So the players mental state is kind of a big deal in this game. In the matches I played, the player with the best mental state going in always won. That usually matches up with ability but not always. But you're given no indication of why a player feels the way he does.My one players mental state/morale dropped from 'OK' to 'Rock Bottom' over the course of two days. Why? I don't know. He didn't play a match during that time. I've got no way of turning it around. I just have to shrug and go, OK then, and wait for things to get better.My other player was in a tournament in which he was one of the strongest players. He destroyed the first two opponents and was in a match against someone who was about as good as he was. He went into the match Troubled and Anxious. Why? I don't know. My pre-match talk was whichever one told him to relax and it had no effect. Talking to him during the match had no effect either. So I'm sitting here watching him blast forehands into the net and miss his shots and I know that's his mental state because he wasn't playing like that before, and there's absolutely nothing I can do about it or avoid whatever caused it next time.Another thing related to personality is that you'll sign someone and then find out their expectations of what they can do are way out of line with yours. So that second player I mentioned up there with the bad mental state. He's 13, and he insisted that he play in the Mens tour. I had no option not to put him there, and only had the option to turn off Junior tour play and expectations for him.The match I was talking about up there? That was a Junior tour match. If he's crapping himself on the Junior tour how can he think he's ready for the men's tour? Regardless, that sort of thing should be resolved before you sign a contract.So basically this is a good game but ruined for me by these two arbitrary mechanics. Unfortunately these mechanics are a major part of gameplay so there's no ignoring them and I can't recommend this at any price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tennis Manager 2022

_childDocuments_.review: My first tennis manager game, I have played a lot of football manager and it is similar, you grow a created player/upcoming star or take on an established player, academy can be upgraded in sports,medical,youth & scouting and business, you have to keep an eye on your finances which is fun especially when your player starts to win grand slams and you get a percentage % of the winnings, grow your players and scout new ones, agents will get you sponsership deals for equipment and clothingThe game is very fun when you get used to the game mechanics, there are still some game breaking bugs however i imagine they will be patched out in due course
_childDocuments_.name: Tennis Manager 2022

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a lot of time playing other sim sports manager games (primarily Football Manager), and while this game has a lot of the makings of a good sim sports manager game, a lot of the finer details of the game are just not up to par. The quality control of these finer details is subpar. There are numerous typos throughout the game, the balance of the financial systems is just out of whack (especially early) and the game seems poorly optimized. The overall depth just isn't there from what one would expect from a sim sports manager game, in my opinion. Perhaps with more patches and experience, this game series will eventually get to the level of others (I recognize this is only the second iteration), but as it currently stands, I cannot recommend this game, especially at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Tennis Manager 2022

_childDocuments_.review: Fun manager game, my first Tennis manager game so I don't know how it compares to other games but I like this one.Easy to get into, not too complicated but also not too simple. You can manage everything yourself or automate things as you like.Some balancing issues in the beginning but patches have corrected most things so far.
