_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an elevated walking sim with absolutely gorgeous graphics and decent voice acting that takes inspiration from Blade Runner and the first season of Altered Carbon, then you've found it. Some of the mechanics can be finicky, but by the time the credits rolled I was super impressed with what I'd played. Wish you could jump back into a save file at any point and change the beats to see the other endings, but it's a minor gripe since the ride is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Wants to Die

_childDocuments_.review: For a UE5 indie project this was pretty impressive and well polished, really great visuals at max settings and cool cyberpunk atmosphere. The concept and world-building is highly reminiscent of Altered Carbon, but was compelling enough for the short amount of time you spend in it and liked the lead detective Karra. Was also cool how some minor dialogue options early on would be brought up again in conversations later, made it feel like it actually mattered what you picked even if it’s linearThat said I think its murder mystery while interesting at first, gets a bit muddled as it goes and kinda lost me by the ending. The investigative gameplay’s also just there to guide you through the story rather than having any substance on its own (similar to say Observer), but didn’t mind much since it’s just a couple hours
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Wants to Die

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody Wants to Die is a very interesting noir detective mystery with a twist. It has the look and feel of noir New York, but is set hundreds of years into the future. Humanity transfers their consciousness from body to body. Theoretical immortality is possible. But it comes at a cost. Bodies and the treatment are expensive. The poor end up in bad situations because of this system. You play a detective who has been in multiple bodies over time. Your beloved wife, years ago, died and could not be resurrected. You are brought back to investigate the murder of a prominent detective. You have a partner who communicates with you through your ear bud. Together you unravel a deeper conspiracy. The mechanics are not too difficult. It isn't tough to gather information from crime scenes, but it wasn't meant to be. Instead, the criminal investigations serve to unveil the narrative. It's quite satisfying. And the game looks fantastic. It's an amazing looking game. Fans of noir mysteries will really enjoy this.

_childDocuments_.review: So first thing I have to do is give huge credit to the voice actors, for a short narrative game like this if the voice performances are weak the whole thing falls apart. But the entire voice cast hits it out of the park, especially the lead trio of Philip Sacramento, Amanda Silvera and Keaton Talmadge. First time I've heard any of their work but their names will be on my radar in future. The term "Immersive" gets thrown around, but it really fits the bill for this game. The sound design from top to bottom, the visuals and atmosphere are 10/10 and if Altered Carbon/Blade Runner vibes are your jam and you enjoy taking your time with games you should enjoy this.  In terms of gameplay/puzzles it's fairly light more in line with something like Life is Strange in the Altered Carbon universe. I would have loved a "disable all hints/auto item equips" option as some people have mentioned it is a little too eager to remind you what tool to use in any circumstance even though there is only a few options.  The other thing that some might say is a bad thing, but for me is a huge positive in this era of live service games that go on forever, is the game is short. I took my time with it and it was around 7 hours, which to be clear is a huge positive in my book because I can play the game, enjoy the journey and then consider it finished. Won't be for everyone, but for those that enjoy those cyberpunk aesthetic and neon noir vibes should be in for good time.

_childDocuments_.review: An intriguing, gritty noir story set several hundred years in the future. The themes blended seamlessly with the environment, the characters, and mystery. _childDocuments_.review: First of all: If you like the original Bioshock setting mixed with Cyberpunk elements - retrofuturism meets art deco style - then you should take a look at this game! Oh, and there sure are the typical noir Max Payne-ish dark and cynical monologues and remarks we all certainly LOVE, am I right? [takes a drag on a cigarette while looking into an abyss of rainy nights and city lights]Nice game design with a very calm and atmospheric approach of crime investigations with a very interesting mechanic of reconstructing every bit by bit. Exploring the murder scenes is fun, the voice actors doing a fantastic job and the sound design combined with a great soundtrack and background music makes it very enjoyable. Visually using the Unreal Engine 5 in most cases the dev studio achieved a great looking game with some set-pieces that are candy for the eyes, also the story is a good reason to keep on playing because you want to know how it unfolds. With many different choices that can affect the story there also could be a reason to play the game twice or more - if desired.80/100

_childDocuments_.review: That's wild how after first ending and playthrough I was disappointed with story while after second ending I've found out I was dumb and trusted all I saw way too much. It's hard to describe it without spoilers but I think I would not have the same feeling if I did endings in opposite order even.Great plot twist in the end.I think some side stories could be developed a bit more but other than that it was a good game.Great graphics, atmosphere, soundtrack and created world.Sadly not a lot of decisions mattered I believe and the mechanic of connecting evidences also had one possible outcome. I think it would be more interesting with more story paths.Saying that I must admit I haven't unlocked some of optional dialogues/choices but I don't really know how I could do this even after 2 playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoiler Free*I really, REALLY enjoyed playing this game, the art style is beautiful, with ''classical-futuristic'' styling (if you crammed cyberpunk, sin city and altered carbon together), if you watched altered carbon, the storyline will give you core elements that'll remind you of it.*You really do need something 30 series cards or up (or AMD equivalent), tried my luck running a 1060, I got 30 fps on the lowest settings in 1080p most of the time, but one of the focal points of the game is its graphics*At the price-point, it's definitely worth sinking some time into.HOWEVER, a couple things prevent this very good game being an amazing one:- While the story feels super rich and full of questions that need answering, a lot of it kind of just gets smushed together towards the end parts of the game, some aspects really deserved their own missions/story expansion- You're reminded in game that choices matter, but there's only a couple choices that REALLY define the ending you'll get- There's no mission select when the game is finished OR multiple save slots, so if you want to go back and make different choices, not really going to happen unless you play it all over again- The game really holds your hand, if they could bring out an update to turn hints off and stop guiding as much it'd be considerably more interestingStill though, very good game, definitely worth a play, enjoyed every minute of playing!

_childDocuments_.review: So far i am really enjoying the game. Art Style is 15/10, the story so far is very good, I like the characters in the game, as far as i can tell this game also has multiple endings, OST is pretty fitting with Noir themes ( Would like some mix of more cyberpunk themes here and there but it still pretty good). Regarding the voice acting I think they were trying to go for something similar to "Firewatch" i dont think they managed the same level of quality but it is still pretty decent.Performancewise it does need some work, im running the game at 1440p TSR Ulta quality, Epic settings and it generally behaves decently ( >90 fps generally) but with some minor stutters when you change space but still perfectly playable.(i9 10900k, RTX 4090, 32Gb DDR4 RAM, Nvme SSD) Visually looks good with the regular visual issues i have encountered on every UE5 that uses Lumen.As the first game from this studio i have to say Bravo and i want to see more stuff from you guys!Pricing is very good 23€ on release seems fair taking into account the type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really tough one for me, and another moment where a simple "Yes" or "No" doesn't quite do it.I absolutely loved every minute of being in this world. It is EXACTLY the kind of vibe I like and the incredible graphics and art design immerse you in it flawlessly. The story is intriguing and the characters are good if not a little cliched.Where it falls down is the super-on-rails gameplay and the atrocious way the ending is handled.In regards to the gameplay; this is game where you play a detective, but never actually get the opportunity to do any detective work. Every step and tool you need to use is automatically chosen for you. A simple tutorial crime scene at the start where the mechanics are taught to you and then you would be free to experiment from there would have been much appreciated and enhanced the game greatly.As for the ending, I don't want to spoil anything. I somehow got the "bad(?)" ending (which, judging by the achievement unlock percentage, so did most people), which left me feeling like my entire playthrough was a waste. This game has no way of loading old saves or chapter select, so to get the good ending I'd have to play the entire thing again. Maybe I will in a couple of years or so, but this is not the kind of thing that endears players to your game. I get that stopping save scumming adds more weight to your choices but why not allow a chapter select once you've cleared the game?Also, while the story is intriguing, it really doesn't seem to have any pay-off. I got really excited by some of the possibilities it presented at times but it all seems to just fizzle out to nothing. Maybe that pay off comes with one of the other endings but I guess I'll never know.So why am I still recommending this after tearing strips off it for several paragraphs? Like I said, the world and tone of the game is incredible. A sequel to this game where they fix many of my complaints could be an absolute masterpiece. I'm also a big believer in finding the enjoyment in the journey rather than the destination. I think for fans of narrative walking simulators (I hate that name but it's kind of apt when the game is as on-rails as this is) it's a must play. Just be prepared for an unsatisfying ending.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 4 hours in, but WOW. Every since I played Still Wakes the Deep, I've really been enjoying narrative, thriller type games. Perhaps, as I age within the hobby; sometime I need a break from action, blasting, sword play, Devil May Cry, Call of Duty type games. I just want to sit back and solve a mystery.I heard about this game 2 weeks ago. I love detective/Noir like movies/games. Nobody Want to Die is hitting ALL the right buttons, thus far. The amount of "oh sh*ts" I've said under my breath. The story is so good.The graphics, are amazing. But graphics mean little if the art direction and story are subpar. That's definitely not the case here. This could have been a movie and I would've ran to the theater to watch it. I'm a fan of what the 50/60s imagined the future would look like. The world and environments in NWtD are surreal. Almost an intimidating vision of what we could become.Here we have amazing, again, Noir movie voice acting. Twists with every investigation (I love the sections in Jame's apartment). And the soundtrack...bought that after the minute I heard it.As I always say with the few games I've left a "review" for. I'm terrible at reviewing, let alone recommending/not recommending a game. As an artist, I feel I'm better at giving personal critic/praise on said art work. Critical Hit Games has created something beautiful and fresh to the eyes. A break from the recent cookie cutter sheets that games seem to be stuck on lately. I haven't even finished the game and already want a sequel, lol.

_childDocuments_.review: A Neo-Noir Cyberpunk MasterpieceThis game had me hooked from the moment I stepped into its gritty, futuristic New York of 2329. With a vibe that merges Cyberpunk 2077 and Bladerunner influences, the immersive atmosphere and storytelling kept me on the edge of my seat. Detective James Karra’s journey, alongside Sara Kai, unfolds like a classic sci-fi thriller with twists that dive deep into the city's dark secrets.While the storyline was compelling, I wish there was more freedom to explore the futuristic city, especially the apartment scenes. It would have been even better to drive through the neon-lit streets and dig deeper into the lore. But even with that, Nobody Wants to Die is a wonderful experience for any cyberpunk fan. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: It did not take long to "beat" and it wasn't particularly enjoyable.  It's certainly nicely done visually.  But the dialogue doesn't make sense, the characters are shallow, and the ending is a letdown.  I won't give spoilers but there are plot turns that maybe would have made more sense had I picked different conversation options.  The gameplay mechanics are also poorly conveyed and it takes half the game to figure out the nuance.  At that point, yeah, I wished I had looked for random non-investigation objects a bit harder.  If I played again and really did my best to find all the things and to take different conversation choices, I might get the "good ending".  It should not be up to the player to figure out what the devs think is a good choice in a morally gray conversation.  If you must do this kind of thing, at least offer ways to replay missions and give some hint as to where the pivot points are.  I don't have another 6 hours to spend on this game nor do I want to sit through another rendition of poor dialog with mediocre acting just to see how else the game might end.  With that in mind, it has a letdown of an ending and no replay value.  The world building is bad too.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game. I love the atmosphere, the story, the characters... I'll surely play it again to make different choices and see how it will end. Surely one of the best games of 2024 for me! To be more precise: the noir, dystopian atmosphere and visuals are great, mechanics of James' fancy gadgets are cool and not too sci-fy, they brought something new to the table when it comes to investigations. It felt like my choices had no value, which is frustrating because I ended up feeling like I wasted 5 hours for nothing other than to enjoy looking at an amazing futuristic city. Soaked in style and melancholy, counternotes to the plot that unfolds as you investigate the mystery.Lean on a railing and stare at its gritty beauty, a fallen angel working back towards the light. A game of substance and impact, one that will be in my top ten. Take a belt of whiskey, light up and get cracking, there's a mystery to solve.Edit - After playing more, all I have to say is move over Valve, this is a defining moment in gaming. Savoring this like a fine whiskey, don't want to rush through it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, buuuuuuut. Like most advertisement it looks a lot more interactive then it actually is. The "investigation" section are very much handheld. When you get to the point to connect the dots and build up the case I found these parts a bit disconnected. Story wise for me no big surprises but it is solid enough to be entertained. _childDocuments_.review: The general atmosphere, voice acting, graphical fidelity, the story and the dialogues are excellent, Nobody Wants to Die is very much likely to be my GOTY.I bought this game on the release day - I was browsing new games and this one looks interesting. Game is a top tier story based detective game, telling a future story in which people have the right to transfer their mind after death and live again in bodies that belonged to other people. The concept is not new but runs very well in this game, and I found some conversations are wise like *Spoiler Alert* .It's interesting to see what Manhattan looks like in 300 years. The skyscrapers are still there with endless flying vehicles, Central Park looks familiar with that fountain but the Liberty Statue with no head, with pollution and poverty clings to the city (Where are the AIs?). Player taking control of a traumatized detective, using gadget to manipulate time to restore crime scene to investigate suicide/murder case of Big Names and at the same time, try to figure out who poisoned his wife.The gameplay is fun and smooth, however you need to follow the lead and focus on the story because you will make decisions which lead to 2 endings. I tried both and liked both, though I hope there's another. A quick note about the end for myself: .I highly recommend this game. The only complaint is currently the game has no manual save, when you complete a run the save file is wasted, you'll need to play again or use other's save file to see another ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cross between Cyberpunk 2077 and Firewatch. Having just finished the game (took about 5h) I have to say I really did enjoy it, though a few pros and cons: Pros: - Pretty good story telling (even if a little hand holdy at times)- Voice acting was over all pretty great- Amazing visuals (UE5 + Lumen)- Amazing setting/style (Neo Cyberpunk 1920-30s)Cons: - Needs a pretty beefy computer. With a 5900x, 3070, and 64GB of memory, I was usually getting 40-60 fps with DLSS Quality at 1440p. Its UE5 with Lumen (I believe) so its pretty demanding.- Minor bugs and lack of some details in areas- Pretty linear and hand holdy at times- Ending can be ambiguous. I recommend checking out all the endings after you finish the game, as unless you get the "good ending" (which is pretty difficult) the ending can feel pretty empty or unfulfilling. After saying all this, I would recommend this heavily to anyone who liked the Cyberpunk 2077 detective stuff and liked Firewatch, which this feels like a direct 50/50 mix of, especially if you get this game on sale in the future.Edit: Coming back a couple months later, it's a bit more polished. Not as janky and had fewer of those minor bugs and glitches. Fps was also up ~5 from my previous experience, but this could also be some other factors, like misc system and driver updates. My hardware specs have not changed though.

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody Wants to Die starts out incredibly strong. A noir murder mystery about a world where people aren't supposed to die is a really strong concept. The problem is that by the end of the game, there are just too many things being juggled in the air. There's a potential supernatural element, there's a plot about your partner, there's a mystery about your character. If this was spread out across a longer game, it might have worked out. But by the time you reach the last couple of chapters, the game is speedrunning through every bit of plot that's been revealed.That said, it's a really impressive first outing for the devs, up until those last few chapters. I hope they have the chance to take this game and really build on it for whatever their next project is.

The investigation mechanics are cool but kinda clunky and what really annoyed me is how the game pretends to be a 'choices matter game' but only two choices affect the ending in the entire game, and there are only two endings. I think the game would have been a lot better had they just focused on one storyline rather than offering 'branching paths', especially since the branching dialogue is very hit or miss. Some lines are great, others are hot trash and the voice acting direction can vary wildly between sentences. The whole game feels poorly stitched together. Also, sometimes you can tell when a line was redone, cause the microphone quality and volume will change significantly from one sentence to the other.

Not sure if I'll continue or not...

_childDocuments_.review: Better than simply good, but not quite great. It's often low budget to the point where it's sort of cringe, like you can tell they didn't have the time/money to animate a lot of characters, so you only actually have face-to-face conversations with two people in the entire game, and rarely see actual living character models doing anything. The game goes out of its way to avoid situations where you might make a direct visual on a moving (alive) character. It's pretty embarrassing.However, the writing is generally quite good. It's not quite prestige TV level of quality, but it does its job and was a lot better than I was expecting. The world-building and aesthetics are very inspired; it's a detective noir, 1940s idea of what cyberpunk might look like. There are certain vistas in the game that are basically state-of-the-art in terms of graphical fidelity. So visuals/writing/tone are all solid, if constrained somewhat by the small budget.The gameplay is basically just walking sim with extra steps. You use this weird temporal reconstructor thing that reassembles physical events using clues you find lying around. It's pretty neat, but it's also on-rails and is something you'll basically meander through with zero effort. So gameplay is boring, but the main draw here is the story and atmosphere, so whatever.The game is also only 25 dollars, which is about right for something short like this. So it's not like you're getting ripped off. I'm satisfied with the experience and can now focus on getting the lump on my right testicle examined by a doctor.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game in the wider sense but an interactive movie, with graphics to die for. Be prepared to get your GPU challenged if you want the full fidelity. The setting itself is far more depressing than of Cyberpunk 2077 because apart from the PC's memories, the future perspective is barren and bleak. For the whole plot being settled in alternate future, the film noir/steampunkt/cyberpunk vibe works very nice and the devs really took a big spoon full of creativity to design the completely linear world. And by linear, I mean absolutely: the game literally runs on rails and hints you everywhere you have to go. There is no possible way you could do something wrong. The linear gameplay might maybe fend off some folks who do nothing under complete open world. On the other hand, having been "spoiled" with completely pointless open-world games (mainly by a publisher who is dealing with very serious crisis right now), such a scenario is refreshing as I am starting to convulse easily latzely when I hear from another game to be on the 100 hours plus side. It sometimes gives me back hope that there is still a way to get good game stories that are comparatively compact (the length is about 7 to 8 hours) and yet leave a staying impression.Definitely a recommendation if you like brain-twisted stuff and need some off-time from Ubisoft game labor...
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Wants to Die

_childDocuments_.review: I jumped into this one not really knowing what I was signing up for. I saw one trailer and thought to myself, it's been too long since Cyberpunk came out (even if I did play expansion on release day), so I pulled the trigger and dove right in.It is a story heavy game, almost an interactive movie in a way where you get to choose some dialogue options (and more unlocks as you search the locations in depth and choose other patch specific dialogue options). After about two hours I was missing the action, I was itching for very much and that is probably what made me break up this game into two days instead of finishing it in one.Yes it is very short, but runs great right on release and I can't ask for much more than that. Other than the fact that action is very lacking and game is so short you should no trouble finishing it in a day (think of it like binge watching a limited series), I can't say anything that is 'negative' about the game.Gameplay itself is spot on and has some really cool mechanics throughout. Once you've seen four tools you can use, you've seen it all, but because crime locations differ heavily it never gets old. Fast forwarding and rewinding time is a joy and the only gripe I would have would be that most of it is too easy with very heavy hand holding and every action pointed out on screen (might have to do with my settings more than anything though), but I can understand in the vein of pushing the plot along, because it is like a web with many different threads at times.Another thing is audio and graphics. _childDocuments_.review: Nobody Wants to Die is an engaging adventure game with great visuals and a really cool setting. Gameplay is pretty standard video game detective work with lots of familiar puzzle mechanics. UV lights to detect blood or fingerprints, X-Ray scanners to check internal anatomy and bullet trajectories, scrubbing through simulations of events, etc. Basically, everything you saw in Arkham Knight. Like most detective games, Nobody Wants to Die's puzzles are very linear and force you to reach the correct solution before you can progress. There's a ton of guidance to that end so it's pretty much impossible to get stuck. As this is very much a story-driven experience, I can't complain too much about that but if you're expecting a much more open-ended detective experience like Crimes & Punishments, you'll be disappointed.Writing is the most important part of the game and Nobody Wants to Die mostly succeeds on that front, though it kind of botches the endings. Throughout the game, there are several key choices you can make that will determine the ending you receive. However, there isn't always a logical correlation between cause and effect. After looking up the other endings online and seeing how to achieve them, I was left scratching my head because the only way to get the good ending is to make an illogical deduction while solving a case. The events in the other endings directly contradict that deduction too, making it all feel a bit contrived and arbitrary.Even though I was disappointed by the game's dubious implementation of choice and consequence, I still found Nobody Wants to Die to be a compelling, story-driven experience. The setting and premise really intrigued me and probably helped me overlook the game's faults. I'd really love to see this universe explored further but for now, I can recommend Nobody Wants to Die to anyone looking for a beautiful sci-fi noir adventure game.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome interpretation of a detective game, definitely has the most love in it compared to the other detective games on the market, and I'm already intrigued enough to do a 2nd play through just to see what the other choices do.Top-notch visuals, voice acting, and writing. The conversations don't feel forced, the humor is light but convincing, and the ambiance is perfect (sitting on the neon sign smoking a cigar was a great moment). The Blade Runner-inspired city has a lot of unique character to it and feels more alive than a lot of other open world games.Investigations involve a time rewind/fast-forward mechanic combined with clue finding and analysis, adding up to a pretty in-depth experience. Piecing together the clues later is satisfying, and I like the visual of the liquor bottles and papers spread across the floor after you're done. Gadgets feel intuitive and they work well, their mechanics are interesting and they give you the feeling of detecting clues instead of just looking around for markers. So far everything is at-your-own-pace, and that encourages exploration.All in all a very fun experience so far, with what seems like decent replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly inspired by Blade Runner, this game is a welcome change from the usual games on the market and comes with very nice graphics, a dense atmosphere and an interesting story. Here, you are a hardened detective who has to solve a murder case in a dystopian world that sucks you deeper and deeper into the vortex of intrigue. There are a lot of clichés, but that's exactly what makes the game entertaining. The gameplay is quite simple and the puzzles can hardly be called puzzles, but this at least keeps the game flowing and plays more like an interactive film. Unfortunately, you don't get a real detective feeling because the game takes you by the hand too much, but the time dialation function is an absolute eye-catcher. Even though basically every step to progress in the game is visualized and you hardly have to think about it yourself and just work your way through the levels in a linear fashion, it's still fun enough so that you want to keep following the story. I've finished the game in about 7 hours, but I'm already looking forward to a second playthrough. Genre-specific, the game offers us different storylines depending on the decisions we make or don't make in the game and I'm curious how the game will end this time.All in all, it is a great game at a really fair price and I hope it is successful enough that we can expect a second part with a little more freedom in our ability to investigate the crimes.

_childDocuments_.review: I am left with very mixed feelings. You might be triggered by my thumbs down if you loved this game, but please allow me to explain.I bought  yesterday on a whim, not really knowing what I was getting into. Stylistically, a dark mystery film noir in a futuristic dystopia is a setting that I am super interested in, so I was hooked right away. The game turned out to be a type of walking simulator with some form of gadget interaction that is very guided and linear at all times. The developers probably decided during playtesting that while the gadgets and the idea of reconstructing a crime scene in time is very interesting, leaving it to the players to choose the tools and approach would require a more dynamic environment, clues not marked with white icons and a system that extends past pressing LT and RT in the correct order. It is more than "just walking", though, and while it is linear and guided, the scenes were genuinely cool as long as I was feeling the story. Speaking of which... in the first few hours has a fascinating story. Nothing groundbreaking, but a solid noir story about corrupt politicians, a fallen hero and a murder case that gets more mysterious the more you look at it. Then, after three of those crime scenes, the story trips over itself. A side plot opens up about your partner, Sara, and another one about a mysterious voice starts to interfere heavily with the protagonist's sense of reality. Instead of solving crime scenes, you suddenly jump from set piece to set piece that open plot threads without tying them together in a manner that allows you to understand the connection, it's just force-fed to you with (admittedly fascinating) colorful visuals and exposition dumps at breakneck speed. Then you suddenly get Steam achievements announcing that you are close to the end of the game and you are completely stunned, like, that's it? What actually happened? Then the final chapter is about the side quest that tries to shoehorn the main plot and the murderer together into one big final revelation that is completely unexplained and falls so flat that I didn't even care about the game ending with a (presumably) bad ending as I didn't pull the trigger in one of those choices.Ah yes, choices. The game has choices. What do they change? Not sure. I hope they do change something and I just had a bad run because I didn't just want to murder people in cold blood (even if they were objectively bad people). My choice at the end seemed to allow the side plot to end on a high note for my partner, but the protagonist got ♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard and the main plot was completely unresolved. Would it have been different if I made different choices? I can only hope, so that I can try to understand the positive reviews. I would love to try, but ever since the end credits the game crashes hard when opening the main menu with an Unreal Engine access violation. Good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ job.As you might be able to read from my review, I am a bit annoyed at the game. The premise was so fantastic, the game is stunningly beautiful (even though I believe it should run better on my hardware) and the crime scene investigation is fun even if the gadgets and the clue interaction is so trivial due to being guided that it feels like the developers didn't have faith in their audience's ability to think for themselves at all, so everything had to be marked with icons and tutorials. And the story was good too, right up until after the crime scene with the politician's frivolous fetish sex party (yes, indeed), but then everything else is so rushed and underdeveloped that I must ask whether they ran out of time or money during development or had to meet some sort of deadline. At just over five hours total playtime, I feel a bit cheated considering the price as well.In the end, I think I have to leave a thumbs down for the wasted potential more than anything else, and the feeling of being cheated out of a good plot halfway through.

_childDocuments_.review: by  is set in a dystopian, retro-futuristic world where you play as a detective. When the game was first revealed, I let out a big sigh, expecting it to be yet another top-down shooter or strategy game with 2D characters delivering the story through text. Naturally, I dismissed it, not intending to explore it any further. But as months went by and my social media feed started buzzing with praise, I decided to give it a shot, especially when a sale came around. To my surprise, it turned out to be right up my alley. What follows is my take on the game, based on my preferences, but I’ll try to keep things as objective as possible.The story follows a typical noir detective narrative, complete with stylish dialogue that evokes the gritty, moody atmosphere of classic neo-noir films. While the plot isn't particularly groundbreaking, the environment and level design are masterfully crafted. It’s a testament to the potential of UE5, making me excited for future releases like Cyberpunk Orion and Witcher 4. However, despite the game's well-built world, the lore feels overly ambitious for its length, almost as though it’s trying too hard to be profound, making it feel forced at times. A refreshing aspect is the lack of combat, allowing players to truly immerse themselves in the role of the protagonist without being distracted by action sequences, which is a rare but welcome change for a game of this nature.One of the game’s notable drawbacks is how some mechanics and puzzles become repetitive and tedious. You’re required to sift through lengthy dialogue sequences just to solve certain puzzles, and it would have been a major improvement to have a skip option for these moments. Some of the mechanics feel reminiscent of Arkham games or Cyberpunk, but they don't bring much new to the table. At times, the game feels more like a tech demo than a fully realised experience, though there is still plenty to enjoy. For its price, Nobody Wants To Die justifies itself well, offering a unique experience that blends classic detective storytelling with immersive world-building. Whether you pick it up on sale or at full price, the content matches the investment, making it worth considering for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't heard of Nobody Wants to Die before its release, but when it popped up in my discovery queue on launch day, it immediately grabbed my attention. It's been a long time since I felt compelled to buy a game so soon after its release, and I don't regret it one bit! From the moment I started playing, I was hooked. The game delivers an immersive experience with a very well written story where you play as a detective tasked with solving murders.Pros:- Story: The game features a very well written story where you play as a detective solving murders. The narrative is captivating and pulls you in from the start. From the beginning, the game vaguely mentions events from your character's past, making you eager to discover everything about your own backstory.- Meaningful Choices: The choices you make throughout the game impact the story. Although I haven't finished the game multiple times to fully experience the extent of their effects, it's clear that decisions influence character interactions and plot developments, making each playthrough potentially unique.- Voice Acting/Characters: The voice acting is great, adding a richer and more immersive feel to the game. Each character is brought to life with distinct voices and each have their own struggles, enhancing the emotional impact of the story and making the world feel more authentic.- Stunning Graphics: The visuals are breathtaking. Every new location feels unique, making progressing to different locations a visually rewarding experience in itself, which is something I will never get tired of.- Performance: The game runs flawlessly on my PC, with no frame drops, glitches, or crashes. I have all settings on epic (except for motion blur, which is turned off), and it consistently maintains a steady 110FPS. PC specs are listed on my profile.- Interactive Environment: There are plenty of interactable objects beyond the obvious ones (dead bodies, blood etc). You can take your time investigating and discovering every corner of a room. Some crime scenes even have secret rooms with additional clues, which is great for thorough explorers.- Gameplay: The main detective work in the game is similar to Cyberpunk's brain dance, just more interactive. It’s incredibly rewarding to piece together clues and learn everything about the victims. The use of your UV light to follow blood trails, your X-ray to track bullet projectiles, or even to find hidden rooms adds an extra layer of depth and satisfaction to the investigative process. Additionally, every crime scene is detailed with a complex backstory to uncover, and as you investigate each scene, you gradually uncover more about the main story, making each discovery feel important to the overall narrative.- Tool Use: You don't need to switch tools manually using a tool wheel. Instead, a prompt appears, automatically switching to the right tool with one click. While this feature may not be groundbreaking, it has a positive impact on the gameplay.However there are a few things to consider:- Story: The story is the main focus of the game, and while it starts off strong, the ending left me feeling a bit puzzled. The conclusion seemed a bit confusing and didn’t fully answer all of the questions I had accumulated throughout the game. It’s possible that I might have missed some crucial details because I was keeping an eye on my Twitch chat during some moments, which could have affected my understanding of the story. As a result, I found myself feeling a bit disoriented and unsure about the ending.Investigation Mechanics: While investigating, you may need to maneuver around and find the right angle to reveal and interact with clues, which can be a bit awkward.- Repetitive Tools: While the detective work is engaging, the game relies on only three tools, which can become repetitive over time.- Replay value: The game features several possible endings (I believe there are three). While this could be appealing, it's unclear how much it actually affects gameplay or story. Although the first playthrough was genuinely entertaining, the game is not one you'll spend endless hours on. It may become repetitive if revisited immediately, but I’m looking forward to playing it again in the future.- System Requirements: While the game ran smoothly on my PC, it’s worth noting that its high system requirements might prevent it from running as well on other PCs. This could limit accessibility for some players and affect their overall experience.- 100% Completion: To achieve 100% completion, multiple playthroughs are necessary. While this might be frustrating for some, it’s not a reason to avoid the game.Overall, Nobody Wants to Die delivers an immersive and engaging experience with its captivating story, impactful choices, and stunning visuals. While it may have some repetitive elements, these do not significantly impact the game’s overall quality. It’s a beautifully crafted game that offers a rewarding detective experience and an intriguing narrative that keeps you hooked. Despite a few minor drawbacks, it’s a standout experience that’s well worth diving into.

_childDocuments_.review: A good piece for neo noir and cyberpunk enjoyers. For everyone else, maybe not. Nice visuals is a plus but you get used to it very fast and it does not matter much after like 30 minutes of gameplay. In a nutshell it is a walking simulator, and a story is very very linear (but still good). Gameplay is linear too, like never ending tutorial from the start till the end. I liked it in general, but I will think twice before recommending it to someone.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game from a new and relatively small developer, got me looking forward to their next project. Overall the game is really interesting. Gameplay leaves you wanting more, and unless you get the good ending you're gonna leave the experience somewhat frustrated. _childDocuments_.review: Take Blooper's Observer, Richard K. Morgan's Altered Carbon, a pack of Camel non-filters, a bottle of rye, and rain drenched neo-noir stylized world you get Nobody Wants to Die. I'm enjoying my time with this game and world. I'm hoping Critical Hit Games and PLAION expand on this world further. With that out of the way, I can see this game not being for everyone, especially for those expecting or preferring more action than talking and puzzles. All and all, I'm loving it and hope they expand more in this world.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game, as it felt more like a noir cyberpunk detective FMV. There were detective puzzles and toys to play with, but it all felt very lineair. Even so, the story, the voice acting was really good and enjoyable. You feel for the main character and the people he talks to. For those who are looking for a heavy rich story, you will find it, discover the truth behind whatever is happening in this distopia, and it really feels like ive been watching some sort of movie. The game does feel more like a walking sim, with extra features. Strong voice acting, amazing atmosphere, you feel completely immersed in this alternate futuristic noir cyberpunk world they built. Great sounds, fantastic visuals, and good soundtrack. But as great stories goes, i have finished the game in 5hours. Honestly, i think it was worth the price. Definitely loved the game and its story.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun narrative romp that looks gorgeous. Had some rough bits but generally progressed at a steady pace. Seems to have multiple paths and your choices effect future events and actions. I wish some story parts where expanded, maybe in the future. Had/Has a lot of leeway I feel, for a larger game. Seems clipped where the initial intention was for more a more fleshed out experience. Mixed thematic elements hint of some Sturm und Drang among the writers/developers and someone who wanted a more accelerated delivery. I smell Embracer.Additionally, I think it would be best to wait until this game discounted, given its short length etc...Will replay it with different choices when I have a few minutes to rub together.Anyhoo... had some scaling issues for some assets like giant keyboards and some other elements that where similarly jarring.  Obvious AI art assets popped up in the early parts of the game and then less so. boo. Pay a real live artist to do real assets. A lot of stunning vistas and other elements and then AI generated dross? One snap up and a circle....

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being a detective game, I didn't really need to think at all while playing this. In every crime scene investigation you are completely lead by hand every step. There is no way to fail at anything. You're pretty much just watching the story play out.There are only 2 endings, and the one you get only depends on actions you take during the final scene.If you're just planning on enjoying the settings and story, you could check it out. The story is still kind of interesting, but nothing you do really matters.

_childDocuments_.review: I was impressed at the beginning and very disappointed at the end. At first, the visuals and atmosphere of the game really captivated me, but after only an hour of playing the game, it started feeling dull and worn-out. Story-wise, there's not much more to find than a mishmash of “Altered Carbon” and “Blade Runner” without any interesting and/or new aspects. Even for a game that mainly relies on the development of a storyline, it´s mechanics are very repetitive. And the most disappointing part is the ending. It feels rushed and doesn't do a good job of clarifying anything regarding the storyline.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Wants to Die

_childDocuments_.review: The game was very atmospheric and cool, but I can definitely see room for improvement. Crowds in the distance look low res and 2D if you pay close enough attention and it feels like you are the only person in the city even though there are always cars zipping. I also noticed that the game didn't support 3440x1440 and 2560x*1440 was the only option so I think the whole time I played the game, the bottom of my screen was kind of cut off. Ngl, the ending I got kind of pissed me off cuz it felt so sudden and so open ended, but I understand that it might be alluding to future projects. I also don't want to have to sit through X amount more hours of all that talking to try and get the different endings. The pacing/storytelling sometimes jarred me with its sudden switches. Most annoying was how there were no real answers to anything ever. I was in a perpetual state of finding more mystery and never getting to the bottom of it. This felt more like a beta than a finished product. The audio balance was all over the place and could definitely use some improvement. Overall, it was more enjoyable than not, and I recommend it to people who are ok with a LOT of dialogue and little action, and lots of hand holding. I give it a solid 6.5/10. It has potential to be really mind blowing, just not yet with those loose ends and no conclusions to anything ever lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Clear time for one playthrough 6 hours unassisted, with additional exploring.NWTD is a beautiful game which interesting mechanics and a world that is fun to look at as a cautionary tale of the power of greed and the entrapment of immortality. The game is a trip to play and be a part of, like watching a movie.However, the story sort of takes a weird left turn towards the end of the game where I imagine they tried to throw a twist in. It wont work for everyone, making some endings you can receive feel unsatisfying. However, for the patient explorer, there are endings that tie things up in the game differently if you can find it in yourself to play through the game more than once.With no chapter select, I advise liberally backing up your saves after different decisions to avoid having to roll through heavily repeated gameplay in order to have all your questions answered.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little indecisive whether to give this a positive or negative review. I enjoyed it... at times. But the negatives just took so much from the overall experience.On the positive notes: - The atmosphere was great- The world building and overall visuals are great- I care about the main characters- The story was interestingBut...- The game had some major performance issues (BSOD thrice)- It's very linear and even though some choices prompts an "the story will be afftected by this", it really doesn't- .. Which makes it extremely weird when some situations plays out awkwardly even when you make the objectionable wrong choices. You spill the beans to the wrong person? No worry, they don't have time for you anyway- It's impossible to miss clues or deduce incorrect theories. It's not required to do any kind of thinking, problem solving or puzzle solving- The controls are SO. CLUNKY. I tried both kb+m and controller, and both sucked- The conclusion is thoroughly unsatisfying. I REALLY wanted to enjoy this, I feel like it was on the right track. But it's missing those elements that make LA Noire and Murdered: Soul Suspect really great. So.. no.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Wants to Die

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphic, amazing lore and good detective thriller story with decent voice acting and gameplay investigation mechanic. It would probably bore me if the game was longer than ~5 hours, but it was timed just right. All this wrapped in amazingly crafted sci-fi noir atmosphere and music culminated in very enjoyable experience from the start to the end.At the time of purchase, the game trailers and picture were giving me personally a bit misleading vibes. I though the game has more freedom and action. That is not the case.The game is pretty much linear walking simulator with investigation mechanics in prepared levels. Do not expect any complicated puzzles or something like that. It is very straightforward and the game holds your hands all the way through. You are there mostly just to enjoy the ride, but that is OK. It works. Could there be more to it? Sure. Does it need to be more? Not really. It is good as it is and definitely worth the asking price if you are into this kind of games.

_childDocuments_.review:
Lose yourself in the world of New York, 2329, where immortality comes at a price that someone has to pay. 

Following a near-death experience, Detective James Karra takes an off-the-books case from his chief with only the help of a young police liaison, Sara Kai, to assist him. Time reveals all as they risk everything in pursuit of a killer, uncovering the dark secrets of the city's elite.

See through the eyes of Mortality Department Detective James Karra on his hunt for a serial killer who targets the city's elite citizens. Investigate crime scenes using his time manipulation augmentation and advanced technology to reconstruct events leading up to each murder and uncover clues that lead to the horrifying truth behind the murders.

Lose yourself in a dystopian future through this meaningful and original interactive detective story, that explores the dangers of transhumanism and immortality.

name: The Cub
detailed_description: Challenging platform parkour inspired by classic SEGA games of the 90s - The Jungle Book, Aladdin, Lion King – but with modern twists and ideas. Platform parkour through the remains of humanity. Outwit evolved wildlife and dangerous hybrid flora. Crack environmental puzzles that keep you guessing. And stay one step ahead of the wicked humans who pursuing you in a twisted apocalyptic safari hunt. After the Great Ecological Catastrophe, the ultrarich flee to Mars and leave the rest to perish. But among them a small child who developed immunity to the hostile planet remains. Decades pass and those on Mars venture back to Earth to do recon. When they spot a small human child, The Cub, they immediately try to capture it. This sets off a journey of escape, exploration and discovery through the urban ruins of humanity coupled with frantic cat and mouse chases. Explore the ruins of humanity after the Great Ecological Catastrophe wipes out most of the civilization and leaves our remains to be reclaimed by an evolved mother nature. The story and clues of how and why humanity fell are strewn throughout the world. Crumbling brutalist tower blocks and abandoned genetics labs. Depleted chemical mines and overgrown battlefields. Each level has a story to tell. Accompanying you on the journey is Radio Nostalgia From Mars, a custom soundtrack that’ll crash land into your psyche. Sink into thought-provoking survivor stories from the few ultrarich living on Mars, while a smooth-voiced radio DJ keeps the show moving with a collection of chill apocalypse-wave tunes. Meticulously drawn and stylized to look like the classic animated films of the late 90s - Atlantis, Tarzan, Road to El Dorado - while also taking a page from Samurai Jack’s creator Genndy Tartakovsky's critically acclaimed series, Primal.
