short_description: From the creators of Golf Club Nostalgia and Highwater. Return to their whimsical, neon-lit apocalypse in a Jungle Book meets The Armageddon fusion. Parkour through the remains of humanity as a child being hunted, while catchy end-of-days tunes and curious survivor stories play on the radio.

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub is a post-apocalyptic platformer that is set in the same universe as the highly acclaimed Golf Club Nostalgia. I found it was mostly an improvement over its predecessor, but some of the platforming sections did leave more to be desired and the narrative barely scratched the surface. However, if you’re looking for that familiar and chill, Radio Nostalgia From Mars tunes, you will certainly find it here.You play as an unnamed young boy on a post-apocalyptic Earth who has been raised by wolves. Wealthy humans fled Earth long ago due to their own environmental destruction and overuse of resources and went to colonize Mars. Left behind to survive in the toxic environment were those underprivileged and who didn’t have the connections or wealth to secure a spot on one of the coveted rockets.However, when majority of humans left, it appears that Earth was able to flourish once more, and the protagonist can breathe the air without equipment. There are animals roaming around and nature is returning to the now abandoned cities and concrete jungles. All is well, except one day, Martians return to Earth looking to play some golf (yes, golf). Here, they discover the boy and are amazed by his seemingly natural ability to breathe the toxic fumes. This begins their hunt for him, believing he is the cure to be able to return to Earth once more and claim the land they believe to be rightfully theirs. Although the story is intertwined in the universe from Golf Club Nostalgia, it is a standalone game and can be enjoyed without playing the previous title. Note that there is a third part in the series, already released called Highwater. Throughout the game, the radio will be playing in the background, giving the game a more low-fi, chill vibe. Mixing with music and conversational pieces or monologues, and was generally interesting to listen to. The protagonist also explains his perspective through narrated segments between chapters. These segments are where most of the story is told to players (although there is lots of environmental storytelling). I would have liked to see some more depth in the commentary as it is very much shown that big, conglomerate companies such as Google, Amazon etc are the big bad guys and they destroyed humanity/Earth. That “they” and billionaires are the only ones who had the opportunity to escape Earth while the rest of the poor folk were left to die. There’s nothing wrong with this being the story, but it very much lacked any depth and was extremely surface level. This is what players and moviegoers have seen time and time again. No other perspectives are shown, no further descriptions, only that those rich Martians = bad and deserve to die.  Being only 3 hours long, it’s not surprising that so little is actually explored, but considering the inclusion of this narrative, I would have liked to see more effort to create a more three-dimensional reality. The Cub is a story-heavy game but with large platforming sections inbetween. For the most part, platforming is ok, but it does not feel very responsive nor reminiscent of the Classic SEGA games of the 90s (as mentioned on the store page). It’s fun with spikes to slide under, toxic goo to jump over and ropes to swing from. But sometimes, the character just will not connect with a handhold, even if you are jumping right into it. Do the exact same thing again and it will work. Its main problem was consistency, especially with in the plastic bag areas. There are tonnes of collectables to discover, and most will be very obvious in your direct path, only a few will require you to venture out. I enjoyed the collectables, specifically the books and newspapers as it helped get a glimpse into the last remaining days on Earth and sense what the general public’s perception was like.I did not find the gameplay difficult. Only slightly vexing in regards to the responsiveness of the controls and handholds, but as I played more, I became more accustomed with how the game operates. It just lacks the smoothness that other platformers have but I did get used to it. The Cub looks gorgeous with its light, pastel environments with watery hues mixed with bright neon signs. There is a lot of variety in environments from swimming underwater, to abandoned cities and houses or luscious, green open fields and all were very aesthetically pleasing.The soundtrack and of course, radio, is many players drawcard to the game and I was no different. The music is fantastic and especially memorable in some areas. Each song perfectly matched with the varied gameplay and the radio was fun to listen to. There are cutscenes between chapters, narrated by the protagonist which were interesting, but is mostly where the lack of depth is shown (as mentioned above). 3 hours Yes For achievements only. Note that although there is a chapter select, it does not state where missing collectables are or keep track of how many you collected each chapter.The Cub is a decent second entry into the Golf Club Nostalgia series. Featuring varied levels, environments and gameplay with a fantastic soundtrack and aesthetically pleasing visuals to boot. However, it is hindered by some unsatisfactory platforming elements and its short three-hour story leaves the narrative to only explore one perspective. Despite this, I enjoyed my short playthrough and am looking forward to trying the third and final entry to the series, Highwater.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: While the rich left for Mars, a young boy found himself lost, possibly left behind even, on Earth; an earth that has perished and one where the environment became toxic to humankind.One day some Martians decided to go back to their old home planet to play golf and hunt, just some casual rich people fun I suppose. They are baffled when they spot the child. A child that doesn’t have to wear a hazmat suit or helmet – impossible with the current conditions on Earth! And so, the chase starts, they need that kid as they believe that boy is the golden ticket to immunity and finally returning home.Of course, there is even more to the story than this summary, but I’ll leave it up to the game and the gorgeous, voiced, cutscenes to tell you the whole story. While it is fantastic that it is directly parallel to Golf Club Nostalgia, I would like to clarify that you do not need to have played that one if you want to delve into The Cub, it’s a perfectly stand-alone game on its own. But it might help you to understand a few things; like why there is so much talk about golf. As for me who did play it, I can only say it was enjoyable to experience a fresh viewpoint offered in a different genre of gameplay experience. Radio Nostalgia from Mars is back, baby! And just as in their first title, it will accompany you throughout the game from when The Cub finds a helmet. And they have once again done an excellent job with it. The smooth-voiced DJ keeps the show going between the soundtracks, just like you would hear on radio stations in real life.No matter where you are in the game, the soundtracks – or talking always match up perfectly to your scene and further enhance the ambient sense while elaborating on the tale.Talk about a unique mood-setter, right? I could not get enough of it despite that it was a very mixed collection ranging; from electronic, jazz, new age to – is, is that baby pop? Wait is baby pop a thing...? Where is my Google, I need to look this up. Yup, seems like it might be something designed specifically for this game as far as I can tell. That was a neat experience.The soundtracks throughout the whole game stayed new unless you replay scenes of course. There is not a single repeat or loop, at least not that I noticed. Another detail I find well thought out is when you are going underground or the helmet is removed for some reason, you will lose contact with the radio station until you resurface, or your helmet is back on. It’s often those little details that can give me a deeper immersion and I am all here for it.A first look: Not only the soundtrack is amazeballs, but I simply cannot get over how visually pleasing the game is either. Some of the locations looked familiar from the first game, making me return to fond memories. And there were also so many beautiful new locations I got to see and discover. This world the developers created is both beautiful and yet eerie. Created with a lot of eyes for detail; every location is unique. The bodies I saw lying around, the graffiti tags, destroyed buildings, the animals roaming free, how nature has evolved and slowly is claiming earth back and lost teddy bears. The devil is in the details as one would say. And one thing that will make you look around and pay attention even more is the fact they have added several collectables. Some are a little better hidden and some more straightforward.With the gloomy blue colours, the robust purple tones, and the flashy neon pinks, throw in some contrast of orange and reds – I can say this is a world I will not easily forget. Nor will I forget the gameplay anytime soon either because I struggled here and there. Dear lord, it made me grind my teeth a few times. And surely, I managed to die a lot of times, but that did not take away the fun for me. It was a bit of trial and error sometimes, a little bit of a learning curve, but regular checkpoints make sure my setback is never too insane. The store page promises ‘’ Challenging platform parkour inspired by classic SEGA games of the 90s - The Jungle Book, Aladdin, Lion King – but with modern twists and ideas’’. Given I never played any of those – I went in without having a clue what to expect.There definitely was parkour, and it was fantastic; I ran, climbed, slid, drove, pushed things around, double jumped, had to flee for my life, floated around with a plastic bag, swam, dove, had a jetpack flight, rode an animal, and even had to be a little bit stealthy and sneaky at times too. It was wild, it was exciting, and it was nice there was so much variation. It kept it crispy and fresh, and it had me fully hooked.The only point of critique I have is how it annoys me to bits that there is a cave where you can see all your collectables and there is a chapter select – super handy, but neither of them will show you in which chapter you’re missing collectables. I dislike having to go through the game repeatedly. It becomes too repetitive for my taste that way.And here we are, at the end of the review already. Who would have thought a post-apocalyptic game could be so stunning? Let us be honest, when I think of the word ‘post-apocalyptic,’ the first things I think about are zombies, destruction, disasters, alien invasions, and robot takeovers; far from a world that is coloured with soft and more eye-catching colours as I described a little earlier on. And in a way, The Cub felt like a serene place, one where I could see myself wandering in for more hours than I had already spent there. I was not ready to leave when the credits rolled, I wanted to stay; another game that left an emotional impact on me, another game of which I wished it was just a little – I’m lying, I wished it was a lot – longer.I saw that the devs are making a third part of this series that will have the title:– a new unique perspective on the overall world or story? I am excited already, given I enjoyed these two titles, so I am looking forward to that third part big time, whilst already secretly hoping for many more parts since I feel like that world has so much potential and so many more stories it could tell us and I would very much love that.Thank you so much for reading and see you in the next review!with love,Tchii If you liked the little scribble that I like to call a review – then please consider giving it a thumbs up. I would very much appreciate that.I received this game for free; I did not receive any compensation to write this review. The opinions represented here, as well as my experience with the game, are entirely my own and are not influenced in any way.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: + Interesting environment+ Nice soundtrack- Uninspired platforming- Game length is  too short to merit the price- No puzzling required, contrary to the tag- Uninteresting story that doesn't really make senseAs a fan of platformers, Cub intrigued me with its pleasant visuals and intriguing post-apocalyptic Jungle Book setting. But as I played the game, I realised there wasn't really anything unique about the game at all. Platforming is extremely generic with basic run, jump, dash, crawl, and grab controls—controls that remain the same throughout the game. The only real challenges of this game were annoying trial and error aspects, as you're sometime faced with split second decisions whether or not to jump, only to find out that jumping causes you to land into spikes. Or finding out that turning in the wrong direction while holding a parachute causes it to disappear.It might be that this was added to artificially inflate game time, because I completed the entire game in 70 mins without even trying. In fact, I actually took my time exploring every nook and cranny to locate collectibles, so imagine my surprise when the achievement for finishing the game showed up at the 70th minute mark.As for being "story-rich"? Yeah, I'm afraid that's not even close to accurate, because there's barely any story to speak of. The story is told primarily in the form of collectibles, but cursory glances of these collectibles tells me that it's just another generic story about capitalism and greed ruining the planet. I also could not understand why the humans returning from Mars saw a human child as an "it" rather than another human—it really made no sense.I suppose Cub isn't a  game per se, but it just offers so incredibly little in both quantity and quality that I pretty much felt bored from beginning to end, and mainly completed the game for completion's sake. For reference, Guacamelee! is a 10 year old platformer that's priced the same, but superior to this one in every single way.Feel free to give this game a play if you're looking for a very simplistic platformer to pass the time, but IMO, this is really just a $5 demo masquerading as a full fledged platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, it is too short and a bit too streamlined. It is good during its short playtime, but I saw the final credits after about three hours. I certainly had my fun with it, though. It's a platformer with Limbo vibes, and I enjoy such games. The puzzles are far less difficult than in Limbo, but there is more platforming (runnning and jumping). You play a little kid, living on a polluted, destroyed earth. Humanity has left for Mars, and when some of them return to explore earth, they want to catch you to examine you. So you run, and the game plays a bit like an endless runner. You are hunted and have to escape, dodging the environment, jumping, sliding and ducking. During some sequences, if you stop you die. You will die frequently anyway, but you always restart at the last automatic savepoint just a few seconds before, so this is no big deal. You wear a helmet from a deceased guy from an earlier expedition, so you hear the radio from Mars all the time. The soundtrack is great, the talking is fun. The levels are varied, sometimes there is a bit more jumping, sometimes a bit of sneaking or sometimes just climbing. There is also a mine cart sequence like in Indiana Jones, or a train wagon climbing like in Uncharted 2. I hated the bison riding sequence, but it was managable in the end. The difficulty is rather low, although it has some more taxing sequences near the end. A lot of collectibles can be found, gamepad support works fine.Nice little post-apocalyptical parkour platformer for a rainy day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Man, The Cub is insane and a work of art! Massive congrats to the team, this project is pure art and a labour of love. From an awesome OST music score that fits perfectly, to an epic radio station talk show that plays while you do your thing solving puzzles and platforming like warm butter to the pristine hand drawn art this is what video games are all about and it feels good.I will keep it short, if you love Inside, Somerville, Planet of Lana and other games like that instant purchase The Cub it is as good if not better in some aspects and 100% top shelf quality of the storey / puzzle platformer genera.During the demo I fell in love with the visuals, the 2D had drawn art is simply first rate and dope. The gameplay matches and is smooth and has very satisfying platforming and puzzles. I never thought it have a sound track and the music and the radio station where people just talk take the whole package over the top. Even the storey made me not want to skip and I listened with a hypnotic trance.As one that loves video games it makes me smile when you get a whole package like this and everything just works and fits together like a freshly solved rubix cube.Much love and respect to the devs, I salute you for your work of art, feels good man!If any of the words that I wrote form a picture that makes you happy or smile press that add to cart button and have your self an insane weekend while you play The Cub and remember I am the son of no one.Update: Jan 21 : so I have completed the game now and only have 3 achievements left to get.Ok, that was totally insane, a work of art and there is just so many hidden ideas, comments, warnings and it is just jammed packed with thoughts on our world and humanity. This game is mega deep Brah, that is what I love about these games and I just can't get enough of them.You really have to wonder what goes on in the minds of the devs that came up with this game and all the content in it regardless of how great all the platforming, puzzles, timing, art, music, etc are.An incredible ride which I will not forget and I truly appreciate, I almost feel like every video gamer should play through this game once and really take note what the devs are trying to say, the message is just as massive as how amazing the whole game was put together.Again, thanks devs for the The Cub I really appreciate it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. This is a follow up to Golf Club Wasteland (now called Golf Club Nostalgia), but with a new story wherein you play as an abandoned orphan who lost his mother during the chaos that had select people fleeing to Mars before people died from an environmental extinction event. You along with many other children were taken in and raised by wolves and were able to adapt to the toxicity of the Earth. In the previous game, you play as a pilot who came back to Earth to get in a round of golf, and although my recollection is a bit hazy, I believe that character makes a lengthy appearance later in this game as well. Anyway, researchers from Mars are back on Earth trying to figure out how to reclaim Earth since humanity is somewhat starved for oxygen on Mars. They see your character,  and set about trying to capture you so they can try to figure out how you've adapted to the Earth's previously mentioned toxicity. What follows is a platforming romp through post-apocalyptic Earth.With that as the story set-up, you keep baiting the aforementioned research team into less and less viable situations. However, you are also always hungry, and so you are also always on the lookout for some food in the form of delicious insects and remnants left by humanity. The platforming was fairly simple when it's just you gallivanting over and through obstacles. However, there are quite a few sequences where you are trying to avoid the researchers or their armed escort, and those are largely both pretty hectic and potentially frustrating as you (me/I) start dying or getting captured on repeat, lol. Still, each sequence is doable with enough practice and once you are familiar with certain triggers in each. I did think the Drone section in particular was quite the byatch, lol.Despite the inherently dark topic matter, this is a very charming game rife with lush set-pieces that really evoke an appreciation for how the world is presented. It's a stunner of a game visually. Additionally, and especially if you are familiar with the previous game, you will very much appreciate the radio station playing songs and offering commentary. It's as awesome as it should be and often hilarious while also being very on point to the way in which the world is today in real life.There are a lot of collectibles that function mostly as world building devices, from old newspaper clips and books to old television shows and actual notes from people mostly left behind when the exodus to Mars took place, or who died after coming back to Earth for whatever reason. There are also some teddy bears, because everybody needs a hug from time to time. :)I played this exclusively with an Xbox X controller and it was perfect played that way. Controls were tight and intuitive. I experienced zero technical issues with this game, and it all played as it should.If you played Golf Club Wasteland (Nostalgia), you should definitely play this, and even if you aren't particularly good at platformers (I'm certainly not), this is a game that offers a fun time with a lot of laughs, amazing tunes, and a cool story. It's a three-to-four-hour game, give or take a little based on your platforming skills. I'd recommend giving this one a look for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: In a society that’s solved world hunger and death, a new terrifying ecological disaster approaches and the best solution is to bring humanity to Mars. With civilization able to be sustained and reusable rockets built, they left Earth with a portion of the population and the ultra-rich with promises to come back to pick up the rest of humanity only to never return. Abandoned and left on a mutating planet, fighting broke out with others evacuating to safer cities. During the evacuation, a child was separated from his mother, and fearing the gunfire, fled into the forest to be raised by wolves. Decades passed, most of humanity failed to adapt, and the Martians can be seen returning to Earth to see if it’s habitable again… but mostly, to play Golf.  3 hours to complete, The Cub is a post-apocalyptic puzzle platformer with catchy radio music. There are three games so far that take place in chronological order that can be played separately – Golf Club Nostalgia, The Cub, and Highwater. While the platforming is a bit clunky, the game is pretty solid and worth playing if you enjoy storylines about surviving the aftermath of a collapsed society, no zombies. Not difficult to complete with easy collectibles and chapter-select for quick backtracking, I recommend playing The Cub if you want a short, chill, linear game to spend a couple of hours in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Just waaaaay too short for the price imho. I saw the entire story in less than 2 hours. And like 40 minutes of that was because I was stuck on two really infuriatingly annoying boss-esque areas. The story is pretty ok, if you played Golf Club Nostalgia, the story is a little better, as that is a prequel to this. Where GCN had replay potential due to the nature of the game (arcadey mini-golf), The Cub is a completely linear platforming adventure story, with nothing really to do, once you have spent 2 hours to play through the narrative.The one really positive aspect is all of the Radio show programming. Those contain both some really good bops in a variety of music styles and lots of interviews that help flesh out the world and backstory.But really you could save your $, and just pick up the soundtrack whenever that drops.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what is in for this game other than the graphics and music. Gameplay wise this is an up to 'ok' game, since its way to short for a plataformer. Somehow it feels like way too much tought was put into one place, leaving a lot to desire here.The game tries to sell on the 'music' and the radio aspects. And the, being real, the music is good sometimes, but it feels like the game doesn't know if it wants you to be enjoying it, or running around not carring at all for the radio, since levels are way to short and do little to try and 'challange' the player to stay and have a reason to hear the radio at all.Then there's the story... Oh boy... On the Demo version I tought the story was somewhat interesting, but with the full realase, it's clear the development studio needs to learn about 'pacing', and that sometimes: less is better. The game borderlines calls the player stupid by repeating the same piece of information/scene you just learned over a short period of time. One example os this, was with Charlie, when you first get to him: The game will show the Cub aproaching Charlie, clearly with some fear/curiosity, then will cut to the Cub narrating about his fear/curiosity, at the end you'll learn about Charlie wife that was left behind... Then when you get back to control the character and the game throws a piece of log at you with the same information, again, about Charlie's wife... Like to add salt to the injury the radio also starts talking about the same things lol. We just saw that, why mentioning it again? Somewhat I've left with a feeling that removing the Cub narrative would make things way better and less repetitive, especialy because the game already does a good work of conveying the Cub feelings and toughts in-game with gestures and expressions.Finally the platforming aspects. I believe the platform tag could be thrown out of the window, since it was poorly implemented. Controls are not consistent, you're supossed to be a nimble kid, yet momentum is not persisted between movements. One second you're dashing, sliding, the next you hit a corner and has to fully stops for an animation of the character climbing the corner to happen... Not to mention the game has a serious problem detecting colisions when mid-air... It's visible the devs had a hard time with this and forces the player to grab onto things. On the mining cart part, I would be flying over the cart (like way too high) and the game would lock-me into the cart, then other time would let me pass flying through the cart...Unfortunately this is one of those game that I'll never be back to finish, I've honestly gave-up near the end of the game as I was not having fun anymore and felt like a chore keep playing due to things mentioned aboved.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to sound harsh, and well... it is. This is by far the worst Limbo / Inside / Planet of Lana-esque game I've ever played. It basically fails on every note it tries to hit:Graphics - these look great, in screenshots. The thing is, in-game, they're still INCREDIBLY flat. This makes it difficult, if not impossible in some sections, to tell what is a physical thing that will kill you in the foreground vs. the background. It leads to just trial-and-error for the whole gameGameplay - oof. It's bad. I'm not sure if they wanted to make it a more ambitious, dynamic platformer and couldn't pull it off, or they wanted to make a much more streamlined simple platformer but decided to complicate it by making it a horrid mess. You can jump and literally see your sprite pass right through grabs and fall to your death. You can get wildly different results from identical button presses. Grabbing points and hitboxes are basically random. It's some of the worst platforming I've ever experienced, and I'm played those old 16-bit-era games this one mentions as inspirations. So many of your deaths are just not your fault the first time through.On top of that, checkpoints are sometimes a minute+ behind you, especially in glorified autoscroller sections (one could argue 95% of the game is, but the even more autoscrollery-autoscroller points), so you just wait through the little animated death scene for the 200th time and then do the exact same 1 minute segment you just did but now you know there's a "gatcha" from offscreen. Repeat until they decide the section is done.Sound - I get what they were going for with the music and the radio and it is like, close to getting it, but it's all just... off. Outside of one or two parts. That could be because it feels like the audio is designed to play at certain points as if you're making flawless progress, but it just plays no matter how much getting knocked back you do, so a lot of the dramatic moments just have nothing or something random playing. In a more streamlined game this would have worked a lot better.Collectibles - these are just insulting. Literally 95% of the "collectibles" are just right on your path, but the other 5% you have to find, through jumping off ledges and replaying levels, what weird little spot you have to go into. It just feels so utterly pointless to have so few off the path at all, yet they're naratively the same weight as the ones tossed at your face. Speaking of narrativeStory / Lore - I actually am pro a lot of what the statement of this game is. Giant tech companies are bad for us, the rich people leading them are among the worst of humanity, and capitalism is probably the eventual death of us all. But this game talks about it in such an immature, lazy way it makes me embarrassed to agree with it. It's got every trope in the world and somehow makes them worse than most other games. It's just bad. It's what a techbro would write if a techbro was anti-techbro. If you asked an AI to write you a story about kids left behind on earth it would be about as soulless. It references works of art and literature without apparently any emotion that should be involved in that.I didn't really enjoy Somerville but I'd rather replay that whole thing than try to finish off the achievements here, it at least had feeling behind it. Even if I hated the stealth sections so much (puzzle 2d platformers need to stop pretending stealth is an interesting puzzle, it's not), I appreciated the rest of the game. Here I just can't find anything to commend. The closest I can say is, at points, you can see glimpses of what it could have been, but it's just a hot mess instead.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: It's the end of the world as you know it, and Bezos/Musk/etc moved to Mars with their cronies.  A being-chased-while-running-and-platforming game - or as I kept thinking of it as I played it: a child-killing sim, par excellence.Pros:* Main char's voice actor is awesome, and the humor is delightfully right on the edge of acceptability.* Music is both unique and well-chosen, and the state-sponsored DJs are a hoot.* Level design is excellent.* Expect to die... a .Cons:* The hating on the rich, which I'm usually amused by, gets a bit heavy after awhile.TL;DR: If you want a semi-difficult pursued-while-platforming game, 8/10; else, avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub is a proper platformer and a beautiful game.I did not expect another game in the world of "Golf Club Nostalgia" and a kind of prequel/sequel, but here we go!Not only that, it is a completely different genre to the original game.The best parts of the first game can be found here as well: the post-apocalyptic setting, the Mars radio propaganda and music. Very enjoyable.The gameplay is not hard, unlike the 90s Lion King game, The Cub is more streamlined and polished.Meaning no softlocks or unfair/broken parts.Solid 5 hour game!Great ending to the whole story, unless we get another installment in this world?Good time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Quick rating: 6.5Longer review:The Cub continues the world building from Golf Club Nostalgia, a game I enjoyed a lot (apart from the Iron Will achievement).  The Cub is also a LIMBO-like...  a genre I greatly enjoy.  As such, I was very hyped for this game.  And, it's not bad.  But far from great.The Good: Art is really nice, the radio station is great, the story is enjoyable.  Gameplay is ok.The Not As Good: This game has tags of Puzzle, Precision Platformer, and Puzzle Platformer...  and I'd say it's none of these.  It is a platformer.  But it has 0 puzzles in it whatsoever.  And it's not what I'd consider a precision platformer... although some sections are a little challenging, mostly because the game can play a bit jank, not because it's really designed to be precision.The game is short.  I got all achievements + all in-game items for 100% in under 3 hours.  And that includes nearly an hour spent on doing Chapter 1 deathless... for those not achievement hunting, you may finish this game under 2 hours (or just a little over).At times, the foreground art can get in the way of visibility.  And ledge grabbing is fairly inconsistent on whether it'll work or not.All in all, the game is not bad.  I give it a recommendation, but not a glowing one.  If you like run-right chase sequences with a nice world and interesting story/music...  this will be a pleasant time for you.  A bit like the game Little Orpheus.  If that doesn't sound like your type of game... then I'd avoid or pick up on a steep sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere of this game is wonderful. Amazing art. Snappy animation. Delightful world building. For someone with generally a short patience with platformers, this one doesn't overstay its welcome, and it is usually generous with its checkpoints, which you will need.The politics are a little on the nose, and I would have appreciated a story that left a little more to the imagination, letting the player draw their own conclusions. Almost everything is satiric reference to current events, so I think this game will unfortunately date itself in about about one news cycle. But if you read it as a manifesto of the moment, then the game proclaims its message loud and clear.Definitely on the short side.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but there are a few things that make it just okay for me.I usually only post reviews when I really like a game, but I'll make an exception this time.The game is pretty straightforward in both its story and puzzles. The platforming isn't demanding, but the controls aren't precise either. I ended up dying in silly ways several times because of this. To be fair, many games in this genre have the same issue. The good thing is that the achievements for not dying are still easy to get in this game.I understand that the music working like a radio was meant for immersion (or at least I think that was the idea), making us feel part of the world, like we're there in the moment listening to the radio just like the kid. But for me, it didn't work. Having a chase sequence with 3-5 minutes of no sound at all made it tedious, not to mention that these sequences already felt long, repetitive, and slow to me.The puzzles are almost non-existent: Move this cube here, turn on the light there, interact with this thing over there… There was never a moment where I had to sit and think a bit.It's not a bad game per se, but there are so many excellent games in the same genre that this one ends up being just okay. That's why I still recommended it, though I think Steam needs a third neutral option for reviews.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub is the sequel to Demagog stuido's Golf Club Nostalgia, and is just as interesting and enjoyable.  Taking place concurrently with the events of GCN, The Cub is billed as a "parkour game", which frankly I find to be a little bit generous, as there is a bit of stiffness to the controls.  The Cub is a cinematic platformer with very deliberate movement and one hit deaths, similar to games like Limbo and Inside.  It has gorgeous 2D graphics that legitimately look like a hand drawn cartoon.  Much like GCN, your character has a helmet and throughout the game is listening to Radio Nostalgia from Mars, and the station is still entertaining and fascinating and very well done, however, because of who you are controlling in this game, it changes the context of things and makes it feel a little more sinister.  You only got a taste of the ruined earth environments in Golf Club Nostalgia, the Cub has you experiencing them much more fully, exploring fields and buildings and sewers, while trying to avoid those who would capture you and do you harm.  It is also much more interesting and exciting in terms of gameplay, as the simple golf in GCN was just an excuse to tour the world and its environments, but the platforming in The Cub is much more visceral and entertaining.  The story was well told and it was good to find out what happens to our pilot friend and the little boy from Golf Club Nostalgia.  If there is a negative to the game, it is that it is extremely short, I finished it with about 85% of the collectibles in about two and a half hours.  I look forward to playing Highwater, the third game in the trilogy.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 9/10The Cub is a beautifully illustrated platformer game with an amazing soundtrack with musical scores that are bound to get stuck in your head for a while. Each level offers a new enviroment to visit and (sometimes) challenging ways to get to the next spot in the game. The theme and story are written on a phenomenal level and it only leaves you hungry to learn more about this world and it's characters. As a fan of the GCN I have enjoyed seeing a familiar character as well as hearing the radio again. Just as with GCN I am adding my favourite tracks to my Spotify playlists so I can enjoy them more often! My only complaint is that the game could be longer so I could see more of what the world of The Cub has to offer : )
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't gotten very far yet, but so far the game is giving me everything I wanted out of it. Which is to say, narratively, it explores the same compelling themes as the first game. I was a bit skeptical about the sequel to Golf Club Nostalgia being a different genre, but this does let you see the world of Alphaville from a different perspective. Plus, they still found a way to integrate the amazing radio chatter from the first game, so I'm happy about that.The platforming is better than expected, even if it isn't going to rival Mario anytime soon. I'm also surprised how often the game gives you more than one route to achieve your objectives. Often times in cinematic platformers, you spend most of your time just kinda walking to the right, moving from set piece to set piece. This game does that too, but there's a lot of little hidden side routes, secrets, and optional paths to make the game interesting. I appreciate that.Seeing as I'm not that far in, I'll update this later on if my opinions change. But for now, I think this game is interesting enough that fans of the original should check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub is a straightforward 2D platformer that uses minor peculiarities to set itself apart. With a quirky radio station, diverse music, and some unusual flavor text, it manages to create a memorable post-apocalyptic setting, despite some oddly structured storytelling. The platforming works fine, but with a bit too much trial and error and not enough puzzles or variety. It impresses with its visuals, thanks to cool backgrounds, consistent use of colors, and crisp character designs. The game’s asking price is reasonable too at $15USD, for around three hours of gameplay. The Cub is not going to set the world on fire, but there is always room in the post-apocalyptic landscape for something a little different.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played! Beautiful artwork, awesome music, great storytelling, and challenging gameplay. Platformers aren't my usual game of choice, but there are soooo many things to love about this one. AND there are tons of collectibles to boot! If you're on the fence about getting this one, just do it! You won't regret it. Thank you so much Untold Tales for letting me review your game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Constantly feel that devs are trolling me:1) Occasionally height and width of jumps change randomly.2) Occasionally checkpoints punish me for nothing.3) Occasionally enemies are moving unpredictably.4) Occasionally jump puzzles show solutions only after death tries.5) Occasionally hitboxes of obstacles are weird.6) Occasionally the character doesn't grab a ledge.The rest of the game is pretty good, but gameplay problems ruin the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those times I'd much rather leave an informative review rather than picking a thumbs up or down. The game was very short with an interesting story with platforming mechanics that left me underwhelmed. Now I've never played any of the previous Demagog Studio games, and that lack of experience may have effected my view of this game. The music made for the game wasn't bad, some of the songs were much better than others, and some were very bizarre... I missed a couple achievements but collected everything in one short playthrough.You can view my entire review here:
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: This is by no means a precise platformer, with inevitable repetiton of some frustrating sequences, but the narrative is exceptionally flavorful. The story, art design, and sound design are polished and create a bizzare and absurd mood that drew me in. So many stunning and cinematic moments had me in awe of how well directed the experience was from start to finish. The post-apocalyptic message stands out to me as a unique spin on a familiar trope. Overall, this was a highly immersive experience for me and I hope Demagog Studios continues to give players ways back into this colorful world they have created.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed in this game, especially since some of the levels are inspired by my birth town. Also, music was well incorporated into game play and Radio Nostalgia is well placed story telling medium.As it stands in "About Game" section - Challenging platform parkour inspired by classic SEGA games of the 90s - The Jungle Book, Aladdin, Lion King – but with modern twists and ideas.Nothing to add here except that graphics and details are somehow unique and pleasant
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it a little but, but i can't recommend it.It has a very nice radio talk show, and the music kinda slaps. The setting and backstory is also interesting after you finish the game, making you think a little bit and draw similarities.But the gameplay is... i dunno, not really there? It is very short, the controls are not great even though they are simple, you die to some pretty lame stuff sometimes, and the checkpoints are often placed annoyingly far back so you have to do cutscenes or dialogue over and over.And then there is the message. The overarching theme is corporations are horrible so stand against them, greed is overflowing and exploitation of people and nature is rampant. That is good and all, but there is also the feeling that it wants to de-evolve society to a simpler one, and cast away alot of the scientific progress to do so. Might just be my understanding of it but i really can't agree with it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest - "The Cub" came out of nowhere. I really enjoyed the previous game from Demagog Studio - Golf Club Nostalgia - and just a few days ago, I received information on Steam that "The Cub" is coming. As I LOVED the universe set by Golf Club Nostalgia (because I played the game some time ago) it immediately piqued my curiosity, and I thought: "Alrighty, let me check it out!". And I am telling you - I am blown away! "The Cub" is a platformer masterpiece. The level design is top-notch, offering a perfect balance of challenge and fun. The visuals are stunning, creating a vibrant and immersive, postapocalyptic world that I couldn't get enough of. I can confidently say, if you're a fan of platformers, "The Cub" deserves a spot in your gaming library. It's a hidden gem that exceeded my expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: This really nailed the old school platformer feeling with modern graphics.  If you were a fan of the platforming it may feel a little short.  I was more into the story and it was a good length for me.The atmosphere and animation is a haunting and beautiful look in a post apocalypse world.  The story is a huge condemnation of our current trajectory in every way and it doesn't pull it's punches.  Despite that it is still somewhat uplifting and speaks to the determination and hope of our inner children.

_childDocuments_.review: Music is great, the idea of having a radio in your head is cool. The world is drawn amazingly. Bad that's it.Controls are glumpsy, simply could not grab a bloody cleave from time to time. Some death spots are not obvious. Won't be surprised if i knew i have more deaths in this game than in Elden RIng.Levels sometimes were too boring, could not wait to finish and delete.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub attempts to tell the story of a small boy The story starts out well and the music at the beginning is quite good. But for me things all go downhill from there. How far can you take a story and how well can you let the player experience it? That makes the difference between a good narrative game and a game that leaves me bored and non-plussed. The way I experienced this game left me scratching my head or rolling my eyes quite a bit. The gameplay is clunky and frustrating. Some things aren't obvious at first and it's like you have to die a few times before you actually notice what you need to do. For example, that you have to crouch through a small hole at the end of the room whilst an enemy that can kill you instantly is running at you to get to the next stage. Other times, you're just running along and poof and enemy is running at you at full speed or a projectile appears out of nowhere and you have a second or less to think before you die. Sometimes, parts of the screen are obscured by foreground elements that the player disappears behind.  In addition, I find myself getting stuck quite often because it's super difficult to get past several points in the game. Like unnecessarily difficult. There is no satisfaction from getting past those points either. It's like the devs just put it there for fun. Speaking of which, ever try playing a super difficult short less than 1 min long part of a game over 10 times just to realize after you finally get past it that you're led to a cutscene? The pacing of the game is also rather frustrating. Most of the time, just when I'm about to start enjoying playing, there's either a drop, something that can electrocute or kill me, an enemy or two chasing me or waiting up ahead for me or there's just some random obstacle that slows my running down somehow. On the topic of clunky controls, if you double jump whilst near an obstacle like a square platform, I realize my character always lands on his belly on the corner of the platform and climbs up. In my trials, I found that there is no ability to double jump and land on top of it. So.. no continuous free running if you encounter obstacles you need to climb over.All these little annoyances leads to a lot of frustrated sighs and eye-rolling along the way and after a while I began to get bore and question whether my time was worth playing this game just to get to the end. I forced myself to finish the game a month or more after the initial frustration and found the  ending disappointing and borderline stomach turning and not worth my time and effort to have gotten to the end.I wanted to like this game, but unfortunately, this isn't a game I'd recommend and if you really want to try it out, I'd only recommend buying this game on sale at a big discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack is bangin! First of all this is a pretty straight forward game with a unique story. Pretty much "post apocalyptic" everyone went to Mars and some were left behind on Earth. Those left behind evolved and those that went to mars came back and are considered "Aliens" now. Go figure. LOL!  The soundtrack and sound engineering is awesome in this game. The artwork is superb and the story is actually pretty dark as you progress but in a humorous way.  Not bad for a  just under a 3 hour game. I give The Cub a 7 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Full gameplay: I really enjoyed my short time playing this game (took me about 2.5 hours), it has a unique and cool art style with an interesting story. Gameplay mechanics are very basic but fun with some challenging moments in between. The game is very similar to Inside and Little Nightmares games but with different style, if you are a fan of those games I think you will like this one too. There are some great sound tracks in game but the radio implementation was really annoying in my opinion. Overall I think it was a good game with fun moments and beautiful art style and world design.I think this is where game shines, the art style and visuals of the game are really cool, it's not dark and gloomy like Inside and Little Nightmares, it's opposite of them, very colorful and bright. A fresh perspective on post catastrophe world which I really liked, although I wish the game had more creatures or monsters to show. Gameplay is very basic platforming stuff with jumping around and parkouring. Nothing hard or challenging. There are no fighting, just running from enemies or hiding. I think it's not bad but at the same time it would've been much better if they added some boss fights with some weird creatures that would fit in this world. The couple of enemies that the game have are very simple and you can easily run away from them or hide. I wish there were more enemy varieties and some combat or more challenging encounters in the game. I know usually these games work better with controllers but I used M/KB and had no issues. There were couple of moments that was frustrating which I think is very normal for platformer games. The game mention it has puzzles but I really didn't encounter any challenging puzzles. I think having some complex puzzles could've added to gameplay value.I think the game introduces itself very well, the mix of Jungle Book boy with Armageddon, I had doubt about this idea when I read it but to my surprise they worked very well together and I really liked this fresh idea and really hope to see continuation of this story in next games. The game tells its story by some cutscenes and lots of documents and videos that scattered around the world and you can find them. Also I love how the game make fun of lots of current situations.This is where the game had some issues I think, game had some very cool sound tracks, but my problem was specifically with the radio implementation in the game, it was very loud and intrusive. There were couple of cool discussions on the radio but in order to completely understand you need to stop playing and listen to them which I think was not very good idea, it overlaps with your gameplay and sometimes distracts you.  Didn't had any issues, game constantly run at 240fps on my PC without any bugs. I don't think there is any value in replayability unless you want to get the missing achievements.CPU: Intel Core i9-12900KMB: MSI Z690 Edge WiFi DDR4RAM: GSkill 32Gb DDR4 3600MhzGPU: Asus GeForce RTX 3090 StrixMonitor: Samsung Odyssey G7 32" 1440P 240Hz

_childDocuments_.review: Wow this game is amazing the art work and world they've created oozes charm and Intrigue. And the music is absolutely wonderful with lots of different genre's with very unique takes would love a vinyl of it personally, the story is a interesting one that has a few creepy twists with hidden collectibles that expand on it so please do look for them. Game play is your standard platforming 2d style game like the ones we used to get. Only issue was sometimes the game wouldn't give you enough indication on what to jump on and sometimes just relied on a lot of trial and error. That said I highly recommend this game and even though the year has started I can see it stay in my top 10 list for 2024. Congratulations to the devs for creating this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack and art design are beautiful. The game is short and sweet.Simple control mechanics and level design.Some collectibles were missed before I knew what to look for but I'm happy to jump back in and find them on a future playthrough. It was nice to play and beat a game in two short sessions. Not EVERY game needs to be dozens or hundreds of hours long. My backlog thanks you! Bought at a deep discount ($1.25CDN) from Fanaticle.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but overall it is a disjointed mess—ranging from the odd, radio-based "music" to the pixel-perfect platforming required of some sections. I ended up finishing it out of spite, regardless of the Donkey Kong Country-level of precision and split-second timing needed to progress for certain areas.It looks good and has a neat premise, but it plays like garbage and is unforgiving.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it and the Radio Nostalgia from Mars is a great storytelling device once again. But if you can't stand games that want you to die constantly and sometimes need a pixel perfect jump that you'll need to redo 20 times to make it then think twice. Controlling the character sometimes feels clunky, but overall it's a very competent and atmospheric game that I can gladly recommend. Just go and play Golf Club Nostalgia first for maximum appreciation.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit of a sucker for the sort of world built by Golf Club Nostalgia (FKA Wasteland) and this does more of that, so I was in day one.  I also appreciate the hand drawn art style of the game and the story for what it is is short and doesn't really overstay its welcome.  There were some jumps that took me some effort to stick while being pursued by enemy characters that I felt like could have been cleaned up some.  I also feel like I missed some collectibles because I took a path and I couldn't go back to take an alternate path due to slippery slopes or a ledge I couldn't jump to.  As I get older I can appreciate a 2-3 hour game on a Sunday night before the work week starts again, if this is too short for you for the price, then I get it, wait for a sale.Also it comes with another round of Radio Nostalgia From Mars, which was great in the first game and I occasionally listen to in the car, it's great.Fairly short game with a few frustrating bits, but overall pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub was a fun adventure game that was on my list for a while, and I finally grabbed it and played through it. Less than 3 hours, it's definitely a solid playtime that doesn't overstay it's welcome. It is challenging sometimes, but for the most part, very straight forward. The story was definitely better than I thought it would be, music was very good, the visuals were beautiful, and the gameplay ran at a solid 120+ frames a second and it was a beautiful sight to see the world that is destroyed after the catastrophic event. Definitely worth a look!
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand how this game has positive reviews. The art cycles between good and bad, and the rest of the game is terrible. The only part of the game I enjoyed was the notes that you have to go out of your way to collect. The rest of the game is either brain-dead platforming or trial-and-error tests of whether or not you'll quit the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Another mediocre limbo-like game where the only innovative mechanic (the radio AND its music) I found annoying. The story looked interesting enough and the graphics are pretty, but I just can't push forward when the gameplay and level design are so bland.If you're looking for something in the genre, try American Arcadia instead.2.5/5
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant, unexpected, and a throwback to the good old times. Think The Jungle Book meet Another World. Sort of.There's a definite re-use of Golf Club Nostalgia assets and ideas, and that's put to good use. The post apocalyptic atmosphere is emphasized by every single step you take, that can mean death. Danger is everywhere, be it creatures, or martians explorers, or the mutant biome. And the vibrant soundtrack, which tells nostalgia stories, is totally on spot. Controls are quite responsive, even tho there are a few double jumps that aren't really precise. I would've like a way to skip single lines of text, or a way to disable the sometimes obtrusive speeches.The game ticks at around 2-3 hours for the normal player, which isn't much, but the sights make those hours memorable.A must buy on sale.Actually if you look around the web you can find it for as low as a couple of euros, which is a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The exploration segments, gathering newspapers or other esoterica from the old world, are really enjoyable. But one of the worst game design decisions rears its head (and turns my thumb) here, which is "just die over and over again until you memorize everything which kills you." That whole school of thought, of having literally zero chance of getting a level right until it has killed you a dozen or more times, is rancid and unwelcome. Don't give me a split-second to make a decision, with no idea of the possible outcomes, and then punish me for picking tails instead of heads on a mental coin-flip.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but nice and atmospheric, cinematographic platformer, light on puzzles, rich on story. Radio Nostalgia from Mars is great, and tunes from it contribute probably half of the game enjoyment (rhythmical tracks help you to cope with retries). If you liked the games like Planet of Lana or Full Void, you may probably like this, although The Cub is more fast-paced, and focuses on platforming and parkour instead of puzzles, that's why you can complete it under 3 hours playing for the first time. As for downsides, some save points where placed sub-optimally (i.e. in one place you had to collect several items, and then proceed to the chase sequence, which made you die several times), and some sequences feel hard for the sake of it, but in general, I liked the game and recommend buying it when it's on sale. (Also the soundtrack is good, check it out).
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Earth suffered a catastrophe, and humanity took to the stars. A boy was left behind, and raised by anmals, as a cub. Humans return to visit, and decide to capture him. The game's a short, linear platformer across the crumbling cityscape. Move from left to right, finding optional mementos of the Old World in the process. The game's best parts are probably the writing and soundscape-the boy finds a helmet of a prior visitor and uses it to listen to Radio Mars, which gives  some insight into what the future expat earthling society is like. Game is pretty, plays well, and the platforming feels inspired by the Disney classics of the 90s (think Lion King). All in all, well worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy watching others play a game like this... Picked up this $15 at full price game in a $3 five game Fanatical bundle for $0.60 instead of the $5 to $6 common sale price at the time. So price wise this was a no-brain pickup and easily worth it.I'd describe it almost like its Steam page does... a combination of 90's classics such as The Jungle Book, Aladdin and The Lion King, but with modern twists and ideas. I'd also throw in Rayman and a little bit of Giana Sisters.It's strongest element is definitely its atmosphere. Very stylized, colorful and vibrant to look like those animated films from the 90's such as Atlantis and Tarzan. The game looks better and better as you progress.Another strong element is exploration and actually needs to be tagged as a Collectathon. Since you'll be constantly collecting messages, books, newspapers, teddy bears, luxuries and videos on a TV. I surprisingly ended up liking this about the game, since I read through and collected almost all of them in my first play-through.Its platforming is fine, that's the word I'll use. You'll know exactly what I mean the more you play it. It's a little finicky-ish at times and requires not only precision but patience.The soundtrack is pretty good but I'm not real big on the radio and what it's all about. It does suit the game but I'd rather the radio allow us to sort of change the station, if you know what I mean. It did grow on me as I completed the game but it's just different, I guess is the word to use on how the music in this game is. When music is actually playing that's the part of the soundtrack I like.There's not much puzzles about this game, so I wouldn't say its a strong tag or anything like that. And I'm glad to see this ring true in its list of tags showing puzzles lower on that list.It's story is minimal and the game has narrated cut scenes, which is fine I guess.There's more to this game that I won't spoil that takes place in the second half of the entire game. It definitely evolves into something you wouldn't expect and I enjoyed it a lot.P.S. Wait til you get to the Bison part, don't pull your hair out.

_childDocuments_.review: The old version of the demo made me cautiously optimistic while noticing some issues with the platforming. The new version of the demo improved on some aspects and I was ready to get the game day one but the reports of 2-3 hours of content discouraged me. The price of €15 seemed like too much based on that. Then the game released with a 33% discount and there was a bigger discount if you own Golf Club Nostalgia for a total of 46% off. I decided to get the game for €8 and I can definitely say it was worth it for that price. Saying the game is a platformer is not really accurate. While platforming is definitely part of the game, there are also a lot of chase sections, other sections that add variety, there are a lot of collectibles, there is also a strong focus on fleshing out the story with lore and cutscenes between every chapter. Platforming might be the weakest aspect of the entire package because you need to get used to certain quirks of the controls and the game requires you to deal with some sections one way only despite there being multiple ways. For instance, the game has issues with grabbing poles when you jump between them. Even though you have normal jump and high jump, thus allowing you to adjust your position, the game doesn’t always like that. There have been instances where I adjusted my jumps and I should be grabbing a pole but I still miss. It’s preferred you either use normal jump or high jump once depending on the distance between the poles. Once you figure this out, the game becomes enjoyable to control. It’s not a fluid platformer like other games focused on platforming and this is something to keep in mind. The game focuses on variety, atmosphere and telling a story through various means instead. The visuals and sound work together to successfully and uniquely get you invested. Seeing ruined buildings with details tells you a lot and the cutscenes are very effective and beautifully done despite the simplicity. The boy you control narrates the cutscenes very nicely and the host of the radio you listen to while playing is very soothing to the ears. The radio is not just there to flesh out the world but the radio also comments directly to what’s happening with the story as it develops and it’s quite brilliant. Then you have the collectibles. You can collect A LOT even though some of it is optional (not required for the achievements). You can find 22 books, 22 newspapers, 15 holo messages, 11 videos, 11 burps (food), 7 luxury items and 8 bears you can hug. The newspapers and books don’t have actual text, you mostly read the headlines with images to set the tone of the world. Those collectibles are already a lot for a longer game. So you can imagine where the focus lies when the game took me 3 hours on my first extensive run with only missing 4 collectibles and 3 achievements. Almost every collectible is easy to find. They’re not there to frustrate you but they’re there to enhance the story. You can check most of the collectibles found through the settings menu and the game also has chapter select right from the start. There are 8 chapters and a prologue. It makes sense why the game is this short and costs this much. The 3 hours are not much but the presentation and almost everything around it is of very high quality. The game has lots of animations and the music within the radio seems to be done by actual bands/singers. The songs are also extremely good. It was such an enjoyable journey that I went back to complete it a second time straight away without rushing things even after I got all the achievements. I ended up playing the game for 7 hours. The Cub makes me want to play Golf Club Nostalgia asap because I want to see more of this world. Getting the game purely for the gameplay and content might not be a smart idea. But the game is worth getting if you like what you’re reading. €15 might be too much unless money is a non issue to you. Less than €10 is safer despite me fully understanding where the budget went and why it costs €15.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: After spending just under an hour immersed in 'The Cub,' I can confidently say it is a great title. The game offers an unparalleled audio and visual experience that sets it apart. Its richness and innovativeness make it a standout, and as a bonus, knowing it hails from my own country fills me with pride. I'm excited to share a detailed review soon on . My only suggestion for the developers would be to consider adding multiple save slots for players to enjoy simultaneous sessions. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play platformers, they've never really appealed to me or my style of gaming before, but I made an exception for this one after loving Gold Club: Nostalgia. Its fun, the story is great and engaging, the art is absolutely beautiful, and the music? Oh, top notch. Excellent. I listen to the soundtrack from this and GC:N in my car quite often. It IS difficult and can be fiddly, especially the drone boss and the mine cart area, but its worth it for the story. It is pricey for the amount of hours you get out of it, but that art is worth supporting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: The Cub is in many ways a spectacular work of art, but a lot of that relates to design choices and storyline/background detail and animations. The game itself is quite simple, with retro style platforming in a very modern looking game devoid of any action or battle sequences. There are some stealth areas as well as moments where you're being chased, but the majority of the game is platforming and swinging. The controls are good without being great, and at times I wish I could have sprinted through areas. The music in the game is amazing, with the radio segments being unique and a fantastic way to progress the story. It really builds an image of how bleak mars is hearing the people speaking about missing home. Voice acting is good, as is the visual aesthetic of the game and the detail in area and level design is first class. Given all this though, I did finish the game in just over 2 hours which might put some off. I'm Beggles on Twitter if you want to chat Indies with me. Thanks for the game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really much a fan of golfing games, so I went into this completely blind and not knowing it's a kind-of spiritual successor to another game. But even if you skip that one, you're still in for a treat. This game's story is completely understandable without the backstory of that game, though you will more fully appreciate it withthe context.But enough about that. The Cub is a highly enjoyable 2D platformer with gorgeous graphics and great storytelling and presentation. If I had to compare it to one game, it's most similar to Planet of Lana, including the atmosphere and vaguely sci-fi story. I loved the aesthetics of this game as well as its soundtrack and ambience. Listening to the radio playing in the background did take the edge off of my frustration when I encountered areas where I frequently died (there are many sequences where extremely precise button mashing is required). All in all, if you're a fan of 2.5D platformers the likes of Limbo, Inside, and the aforementioned Planet of Lana, then this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of a more hopeful sequel to the golf game. There are three stories being told: through the radio broadcast, you hear gently about the desperate life former billionaires who are living on Mars are going through; through the environment you see the world that once was and what happened to those left behind; and the cub himself tells the story of the new generation of people who have adapted to life on post-apocalyptic Earth.The main draw for this game was still the radio broadcast, which is both funny and sad, and plays a pretty good variety of music that often reflects the themes of the game. The platforming mechanics are a bit stiff, but not too bad (I had trouble timing bounces for example). There were times I was stuck on some trial and error. Levels have a very good variety and there are a lot of unique sections, although some enemy mechanics return for the final gauntlet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Come for the post-apocalyptic parkour. Stay for Radio Nostalgia from Mars. What a fun ride. Yes, The Cub is a shorter game but the price reflects that. I picked this one up on a rainy afternoon and got completely absorbed in the funky fusion of genres. As many others have noted, the soundtrack alone is worth the price of admission, but the integration of the music with a good story and some fantastic art is where this one shines. Definitely a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: I was hooked on the demo... Played it multiple times since the first demo... And now we have the full game after a long wait...and boy was it worth the wait!!I love Golf Club Wasteland and still play it to this day, and The Cub just continues the magic of the geniuses at Demagog Studio.The Cub is just a sublime experience, from the level design, to the challenges, to the legendary music playing along throughout the game, delivered by it's very own radio station.Do yourself a favour and buy this game. It costs a fraction of a AAA game and will give you a lot more satisfaction! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those examples where you wish steam had a neutral rating. The cub isn't a bad game but it's far from a good one. Especially in the puzzle platformer genre where there are some real masterpieces (Gris, Unravel, INSIDE, inmost, ...) The reason for that is that the cub doesn't have any unique, creative or for that matter, fun game mechanics. Throughout the runtime nothing new is introduced to spice things up and there's barely any puzzles to speak off if any. Most of the challenges are simple platforming sections or chase sequences and these are often hindered by finnicky controls and bad ledge detection. The movement is thus servicable but not great and since that's what you're doing most of the time throughout very linear levels, the game gets quite boring. Luckily the cub doesn't overstay its welcome with a runtime of about 2-3 hours for the average gamer. This does make it so that the game isn't worth it at full price. I picked it up in a bundle with somerville (which i already owned) and combined with the launch discount i got it for a bit under 9 euros. For that price i can't really complain but i'm not particularly satisfied either. The game just didn't manage to grab me with its mechanics. And the story/music didn't captivate me either, luckily the game is well optimized with no lag or bugs/crashes. The visuals are also top notch and the reason i'm giving this game a thumbs up in the end but with an asterisk. Buy this in one of the bundles with either planet of lana or somerville (both great games really) and at a discount. If you can snag it for ten or lower then its worth it for one evening of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely little game and a strong third entry in Demagog's colorful post apocalypse world Music and environment art are the main highlights of this 3-hour performer. Writing is on point as always, with strong social and environmental messages and a lot of Tobe in cheek references to current world events.Gameplay is the weakest point, it mostly consists of genetic performing with several difficulty spikes in chase sequences Looking forward to what Demagog releases next ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game in about 3 hours. It feels a bit short because at the end I wanted more. But it's a very nice snack size game and also priced like one. Beautiful visuals and great soundtrack! The platforming and controls feel good and responsive. Hits the nostalgia sweet spot with the nods to Jungle Book and other classics in the hidden books and video's. Also seeing things like the giraffe remind me of playing The Lion King on my Mega Drive. The unforgiving and deadly environments keep you on the edge of your seat, but the main character always gives you a moment to relax or laugh after he makes a joke or does something funny. Would have loved to see some more puzzles and maybe a bossfights or two. Maybe in the sequel?
_childDocuments_.name: The Cub

_childDocuments_.review:
After the Great Ecological Catastrophe, the ultrarich flee to Mars and leave the rest to perish. But among them a small child who developed immunity to the hostile planet remains. Decades pass and those on Mars venture back to Earth to do recon. When they spot a small human child, The Cub, they immediately try to capture it. This sets off a journey of escape, exploration and discovery through the urban ruins of humanity coupled with frantic cat and mouse chases.

Challenging platform parkour inspired by classic SEGA games of the 90s - The Jungle Book, Aladdin, Lion King but with modern twists and ideas.

Platform parkour through the remains of humanity. Outwit evolved wildlife and dangerous hybrid flora. Crack environmental puzzles that keep you guessing. And stay one step ahead of the wicked humans who pursuing you in a twisted apocalyptic safari hunt.

name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider
detailed_description: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a side-scrolling action platformer that channels the golden age of classic 16-bit action games in a full-throttle quest for revenge. REVENGE OF THE MOONRIDER In the oppressed world of Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider, humanity finds an unlikely hero. After building an army of super soldiers as weapons of war, the authoritarians unwittingly seal their own fates by bringing online the ninja warrior known as Moonrider. Conceived as a tool to preserve the totalitarian state, the Moonrider instead rejects its intended purpose and wages a relentless battle for vengeance against its creators and fellow super soldiers. GEAR UP AND PREPARE TO BATTLE YOUR CREATORS The design of Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider puts the best classic action-game elements in the laser-precise sights of its starring ninja, ensuring snappy, responsive combat that’s supremely challenging. Powerful modifier chips are hidden and guarded throughout the adventure, allowing you to customize the Moonrider’s fighting style while gaining killer advantages and abilities. BEAUTIFUL PIXEL GRAPHICS COMPLEMENTED BY AN INCREDIBLE SOUNDTRACK The gorgeously desolated world of Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider flawlessly channels the halcyon days of the 16-bit era through intricate pixel art, inspiring a striking gauntlet across eight deadly stages. From start to finish, you’ll enjoy seamless platforming action for a tight, focused experience that never lets its blade get dull. Complementing these beautiful pixel graphics is an incredible soundtrack with a timeless, nostalgic vibe. The result is the quintessential retro experience. FEATURES ● Created by Joymasher, the studio behind the amazing retro games Oniken, Odallus, and Blazing Chrome ● Authentic retro-game feeling ● Discover special modifier chips throughout your adventure and use them to customize the Moonrider’s fighting style with killer abilities ● Incredible soundtrack ● Eight deadly stages to overcome

_childDocuments_.review: Great ninja action-platform game. Beware of the tags, this is NOT a metroidvania. Moonrider is a linear stage-based game, with some very light exploration elements (you can find hidden chips in most stages). This has more in common with games like Hagane, Ninja Gaiden, Strider, Shinobi, or even Mega Man X than any Metroid type game. And that's exactly what I want.I liked pretty much everything about this. The graphics and art style are fantastic, the soundtrack is great, the controls and mechanics are spot-on, there's a nice level of challenge, and the length is just right. The only things that I wasn't a big fan of were the vehicle stages - they play perfectly fine, but they go on too long for me, and they have quite a bit of dead air, with nothing happening. I feel like the game balance could use some fine tuning as well, since a few of the special weapons are extremely powerful, but maybe that's intentional. It's not much different from Mega Man in that regard. And the ranking & scoring system is a bit too basic, but that's sadly been the case for all of JoyMasher's games, so I've come to expect it. But none of that is a big deal, this is a great game and definitely my favorite from this studio yet. I'd absolutely recommend it to any fan of classic ninja action platform games, it's well worth the money.Here's my 100%* complete S-rank playthrough of the game if anyone wants to see how it's plays.
