_childDocuments_.review: Hmm....this is a side-scrolling slash-em-up that for old-skool fans from the megadrive / snes era is in the vein of Shinobi / Strider / Hagane / Mega man. For anyone who didn't grow up gaming on a 90s console: it's not a million miles away from the action of your typical metroidvania, albeit in a linear form with short levels packed with simple combat, platforming challenges and boss-battles.Vengeful Guardian Moonrider is a love-letter to those games of yesteryear, and whilst I adored this genre back in the day it unfortunately has a little bit too much in common for my evolved modern tastes. I thought this was going to be amazing, as this developers earlier title (Blazing Chrome) was a pretty slick retro effort, but this follow-up is clumsy by comparison. Do you perhaps expect your games to be slickly responsive? well....tough! That's not how it was "back in the day" and rather surprisingly they emulate that clunky-ness here, with controls that are a bit fiddly. The level design is supposed to be super-sharp to induce sweaty palms from an adrenaline pumping challenge, but often is too tight to be enjoyable when compounded by the loose controls.They're not sluggish to respond, yet are imprecise enough to make some of the more dense obstacles and enemy attack patterns rather irritating to overcome. And not in a good way! But, as in, urgh! This literally feels like playing a thirty year old game, both in terms of stodgy game-play mechanics and in the presentation which seems to think flickery graphics and an overly busy display makes for a good combination.On occasion I either couldn't see what the heck was happening, or it was a flashing mess that gave me eye-strain. This used to happen on old hardware due to it not being able to keep up with the action, whereas here it's just an ugly and badly conceived design choice for their presentation. I remember playing 'Axelay' on the Super Nintendo and it was a graphical showcase at the time, albeit one blighted by slow-down and bits of sprites disappearing as it pushed the SNES a bit too hard for it to cope. Although Vengeful etc doesn't have slow-down it does bizarrely have plenty of screen filling flickering explosions and effects, which to me is going too far in aping retro titles on hardware which shouldn't have this problem at all. It would seem to be a deliberate design choice and not one that I appreciate.So: the action is a bit woolly and the graphics are a bit "bleurgh!" on occasion, does it at least have good boss-battles? Eh....I guess they're okay. They're affected by the same issues as the rest of the game. Their attack patterns are generally not too bad, but I wouldn't say any of the ones I've fought were particularly enjoyable. Yes! They all look brilliant, as does the game in general, but I honestly wouldn't say the game-play is as polished as the graphical design. At under two hours played I'm debating getting a refund, which is not the position I expected to be in. I probably won't refund it as it's not awful, and will most likely drag myself around to finishing it at some point, but I honestly expected to like this much more than I actually did having played it. It's not bad, yet it isn't great either. A cautious recommended if you hoped for the spirit of yesteryear but with modern execution, as it somewhat surprisingly fails on the latter and is just as clunky as playing the likes of 'Strider' (which is significantly cheaper to buy) For anyone else: no doubt there are plenty of reviews gushing over this, so who the heck knows whether you will agree with them or not. I certainly didn't and it should have been my cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Yea...I think i am going to pass on continuing with this one.Here is the perfect example of a really cool looking game that hits all the retro vibes...and then you pick up the controller to find it just fails to be fun.First off the controls will fight you the whole way through. Wall jumping is tedious and a lot of times doesn't feel like it sticks right. Control of Moonrider feels like you are a robot, in an agile world...and I mean that in a very not so good way.  And it feels like he doesn't have much power to his attacks. Run can be a pain to start with the pad...and the dashing attack comes out way too often when you don't want it to due to its lack of power and long recovery...But there is the worse part....level design. They feel downright amateurish. Way too many blind jumps over pits that will do damage. And the levels DRAG!!!! For example, one level I did gave me two mini-bosses before the boss.....only to find out he was just a mini-boss too. So I continued on for another length and ran into a boss that took up the whole screen in his own room. Beat him and guess what.....yes, just another mini-boss. Continued on for a bit until I was so utterly bored with the level,  and I gave up.That is why currently, according to the achievements, there are only 73.1% owners of this game that have passed the first level, and 41.3% that have passed another level. Really take a moment to think about that. More than 1/2 of the people who have this game have not beaten more than one level. Then look at all the reviews. When talking about the difficulty, they aren't saying, "OMG this game is hard as nails!" So ask yourself, what is preventing over half the people from not passing 2 levels?But if you want...go ahead and get it. Its overpriced for what you get too....I grew up on these games. I remember Shinobi in the arcades. I remember playing Ninja Gaiden on NES. Go back and play those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Enormous love letter to Sega Genesis/Mega Drive's Shinobi's fans & an outstanding homage to the series.Huge Props to JoyMasher.Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a 16-bit side scrolling hack'n'slash with that retro vibe and old-school while fluid controls & gameplay. In a cyberpunk world & a corrupt government that rules it with fear & abuse, despite being an old pawn you decide to take Justice at your hands & go against'em! While kinda cliche & all that jazz, it has very few dialogues with more than fine lines but the game truly shines with its fast paced gameplay, precision platforming & discovering powerful secrets that let you modify your cyber ninja with further upgrades & abilities.Stages, while few, are long & hard  with different & variable enemies on each& cool looking bosses with great attack patterns. Most stages contain more than 2 bosses which is more than a worthwhile mention. There is great attention to detail regarding both the terrains & the animations while the soundtrack is phenomenal, 8bit harmonic & ambient truly befitting & completing this retro experience.Having played their previous games, Oniken,  Blazing Chromeand now Vengeful Guardian, I gotta say that I can't wait for their next project.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing retro 2D stage-based game that pays homage to the likes of Ninja Gaiden, Shinobi, The Ninja Warriors and Hagane.The formula to how you go about doing each stage and gaining power-ups is similar to that of the Mega Man games. Very linear in nature a lot more forgiving compared to those games I previously mentioned. Skills that let you find secrets, power-ups with minor invincibility. Including check-points between sub-bosses/main-bosses throughout each subsection of stages (so no worries if you used up all of your continues, you’ll be able to get right back into the boss fights.... somewhat). Most of said bosses have very little move-set with telepathic attack patterns that are easy to read, although that’s not to say it’s a bad thing. A game of this nature may be enjoyable if you’re the type who likes doing 100% speed-runs or want something that’s less stress inducing than the Mega Man X/Ninja Gaiden games (or worst.. Mega Man Zero 1 rank system *sudders*). I dare say it makes a good entry point for someone who want to test their skills on a retro-inspired 2D platformers for the first time. Give it a shot, it’s very short, has kick ass cyber ninjas and it's enjoyable. Also do yourself a favor, play this with the CRT filter on. This game does the CRT effect beautifully, makes me wish it was set on by default (like Steel Assault).

_childDocuments_.review: I've changed my opinion due to some apparent bugfixes that happened over the last few months. Controls seem to have been fixed from initial launch... that is, if I use Steam Input, it fixes everything so I'm not stuck using the analog stick (a Unity-ism). Previously this actually caused a jank baby jump animation when moving and attacking, creating really bad issues with attacks. It was some kind of interaction with pressing attack too many times too fast... like it was alternating between attack from Steam inputs and jump from the default interpretation of the PS5 controls. As of October 2024, this is no longer a problem.I came back to the game after a few months. Was originally sorta bored after the first few levels I played, and the previous control issues, and liked it enough to go ahead and S-Rank most things. It's very pretty if you're into pixel art. These guys do great work with their spritework, and this is no exception. It feels firmly out of the 16 bit era, and has that gritty washed out look so many Genesis games seemed to lean into. It plays sorta like Shinobi 3 with Strider basic attacks and Mega Man subweapon picks. The starter subweapon is really strong, as is the dash attack - though dashing has the Shinobi vulnerable leap portion too, so if you misjudge your distance and/or don't kill the guy, you're probably eating a hit. Basic attack can chain into a three-hit combo, while crouching and jumping are only single hits. You can usually out-DPS a boss by just mashing attack. The jump kick kills snipers no problem and also happens to do a number on the final boss. As far as collecting stuff goes...Every boss gives you a subweapon, but the fire dude's is the craziest, maybe a bit of a nod to Quick Man by being overpowered. It hits twice (potentially) and you get more of them than anything else for your subweapon energy, so it's the good default choice, useful in almost every situation.  As you go through levels you'll also discover chips to change your playstyle, though the two biggest ones are probably Long Sword and Acrobatic; that is, longer reach, and a double jump that makes S ranking incredibly easy. As a fan of PS2 Shinobi, I was excited to see you could also equip an Akujiki chip, which powers up with kills done in quick succession, though I would have preferred fully committing to the weapon with the life drain and a bar to show how long you've got before the effect is finished. In most cases, Akujiki did nothing, though, because it's so easy to kill basic enemies anyway. Getting rid of a drone in one jump attack was maybe a little better, but the long sword is way more versatile. You get the usual array of mods too... kill enemies for life energy, kill enemies for subweapon energy, take less damage but limit your rank, and so on. Level design is so-so, but it's varied, and the mental strain isn't too much if you want to S rank cuz you're just running and timing your dash attack. There's not a lot else to it. Patterns are easy to read, and there are only around 8 enemy types, so you'll know exactly what to do every time you see one. Levels take no more than 8 minutes each if you just keep dashing everywhere, so it's a quick game. Some little things like dead space on the bike sections are annoying, and having to press start to enter a level is a weird UX choice. .Odallus and Blazing Chrome are still far and away better in my opinion, but if you want an easy Shinobi III-like, this is the one to look at. If you like these dudes' other games, there's plenty of the same tropes... a mecha monkey, a laser tunnel or two. No polar bear though. For a better ninja game, I really liked Shadow of the Ninja Reborn, but Cyber Shadow was a more retro experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Moonrider is an incredibly tight game. If you're a fan of action platformers like Shinobi, Strider, Hagane, Run Saber, Megaman Zero, etc, you'll feel right at home. The movement and combat are incredibly fluid and intuitive, and everything just feels right. The soundtrack is incredible (though I do wish the level clear music was more triumphant/upbeat, it's still a great track) and the visuals are spot-on as usual for JoyMasher. Overall the game isn't super long, but the rank system and hidden secrets means there's reason to come back and replay past stages. There are only a couple of gripes that I have and they're incredibly minor to the point that they may not be worth mentioning. 1: I wish that the speedrun mode came back from Blazing Chrome. It was a fun little addition to have. Same with the mirror mode. 2: There are some balance issues with special weapons. The Darkportal ability is so far and away superior to everything else that you may choose not to use it just because it makes things THAT easy. This can be patched pretty quickly though.Overall, this is a great example of a game living up to the hype, and I'd be willing to put down some cash on DLC in the future if JoyMasher felt inclined to make it. Even if it's just costumes or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Modern retro games come in various styles. Some aim for faithful recreations, while others draw inspiration more loosely. Moonrider, in my opinion, sets the gold standard. It captures the essence of how we remember those games: a romanticized version, playing smoother, deeper, and more entertaining, with superior visuals and sound. It's exactly how we mistakenly remember our childhood games. Having played most of JoyMasher's previous titles, I can attest to their impressive progress!Most readers are likely familiar with Moonrider's inspiration from classics like Shinobi 3 and Megaman. The incorporation of Megaman elements is particularly interesting, adding a layer of complexity to what might otherwise be a linear experience. However, in Megaman, I found myself relying on guides to choose the right weapons. The trial and error of finding the best weapon for each boss suited the old design style - games that lasted for months, played by kids with ample free time.In Moonrider, it's unclear if the weapons are designed with specific bosses in mind. I didn't find any weapon particularly effective against certain bosses. My strategy involved alternating weapons to experiment, though the results were inconclusive. Nevertheless, the fact that I managed to finish the game suggests this design choice wasn't detrimental.Overall, I had a lot of fun with Moonrider. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the illegitimate child of Mega Man and Shinobi 3. It's honestly really great, except for it's length. Took me only 3 hours to beat. But then again it's also very cheap. I just hope there's more to come. If I have any critics for the game, is that it needs some QoL and unimportant fixes. QoL like, more infos at stage selection screen on how many secrets are left unfound after we beat it. The unfound secret is mentioned after beating the stage, why not also let us know in stage selection? Also, cmon, why must skin change requires a chip slot. But those aren't really anything game breaking. In any case, over all, I'd give this game a good 9/10. If the game could last like 10 hours, that'd be a good 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic throwback to retro action platformers of old such as Megaman X & Shinobi. Vengeful Guardian : Moonrider(That's a mouthful) is a fantastic action side-scroller with beautiful pixelated 16-bit art-style, solid gameplay, responsive controls, neat level design and good soundtrack. Boss fights are plentiful and varied (2-3 bosses per level), you gain various power-ups from said bosses, plenty of items to collect which affect gameplay and end level ranks which could encourage replays to get the S rank. The story is as cookie cutter as it can get but I didn't really mind that as they nail the retro aesthetic coupled with the grim cyberpunk vibes.The only negatives I can think of is that it's too short and the end level boss fights in particular are a bit too easy at times.Nonetheless 2023 is off to a great start. Mad props to JoyMasher. Looking forward to what they have in store for the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Shinobi gameplay, Mega Man X upgrade and map system. Lots of fun, great soundtrack, interesting stage mechanics.HOWEVER: The main stage bosses are too easy, easily killable by spamming attacks first try without learning the mechanics (which are cool so thats a super bummer). Even the mid stage bosses are harder. My only other gripe is the game seems made in a way where youre intended to take damage, and heal it afterwards in the stage, which feels...... weird.IF the main bosses were harder id give it an 8/10. but where it is, being a short game with the easy bosses its at a 6/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: What a neat but very short game for what it is , 3.5 hours for 100% it. Could have been faster but devs actually went and made some changes from their 1.0 version so no more Metal Man syndrome from Mega Man 2 , but it still heavily leans on to the robot masters concept. Pretty chill n' easy game but can be hard if you make it hard.Overall beautiful game that leans heavily into its influenced games of old , From Hagane, Shinobi, Mega Man, even the map screen brings me memories of Ranger X. Art style and soundtrack alone are enjoyable to finish the game and between finishing and completing it with achievements there's not too much about it so might as well go for it!The only complain besides being a bit short ( which I don't mind as other people do so take that as you will ) I would say difficulty is still a bit on the uneven scale, you can make it harder on you by imposing sword only runs or adding a chip that you obtain from one of the stages but it feels like it could have been an unlockable new game mode after finishing game rather than a chip, also RGB chip could be a feature instead of the upgrade chip?It's def more of make it your own challenge, but I don't mind it too much I just wished it had more separate options for that rather than being a upgrade chip related.Might be a bit pricey, but when its on sale for a 10$ , could be a good pass time while looking at some best implementation of fake CRT mode that I've seen so far , coupled with great art and soundtrack. I kind of wish CRT setting was available as a separate thing to buy as an overlay for my pc for other games now!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: So cool but I'm ♥♥♥♥ at it, or maybe just impatient with the bosses. Still recommended though.Hagane and Shinobi 3 finally have their own amazing retro nostalgia trip and it's really sick.Sprinkling in a bit of the Megaman X stage selection, secrets and special weapons, along with stage rankings for replayability and challenging yourself adds a lot to it as well. The art is awesome, the music is super good, and the gameplay is really nice, with QoL additions that Shinobi 3 sorely needed and was added in some of its romhacks.Also don't mind the hours played, I've been playing this on the Deck offline.Somehow feels more genuine that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This is a damn cool game with clear inspiration from Shinobi, Strider and Megaman. It's fast paced, full of action and plenty of death as well as destruction. It has a really good artstyle accompanied with probably the best CRT filter I ever experienced in these retro style games and what we have here is a game crafted with a lot of love and care.Soundtrack is really good, capturing 80's inspired synthwave and accompanies the action greatly while also being nice to vibe to outside of the game.There are, however, some nitpicks of mine with the game. Dificulty. It's way too easy and the only way to make it harder is to go for the other extreme with the One-hit-death mode. I would have prefered something in between to gradually move from until the OneHitDeath. With the base dificulty, boss fights are a joke and forgetable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a few things that could be tweaked (i.e. showing how many items are unlocked per each stage on the stage select screen, fixing some jarring screen transitions and grammatical errors), but overall I found the this title to be a lot of fun to run through. It takes inspiration from games like Shinobi III, Hagane, and the Mega Man X series, so if you like those types of games, this might be right up your alley. It is also pretty short (I finished it in less than two hours my first time through), but I definitely enjoyed the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: First off, let me ask you a few questions:-Are you into high speed dashing through levels and cutting enemies in half like in the MegaMan Zero games? That sweet moment to moment platforming mixed with super satisfying combat gameplay?-Wanna divekick loop your enemies with precision into oblivion?-Do you dig variety and a fair but challenging level design with plenty of bosses / sub-bosses?-Hidden capsules with upgrade chips spread across the levels? Boss weapons after defeating them?-Godlike pixel art presentation along with a terrific and memorable sountrack?-Boss intro with badass japanese voice lines were you have no idea what they're rambling about but enjoy it nonetheless?-90s Super Sentai aesthetics?-Strider? MegaMan X / Zero? Shinobi? Skate 4? Bloodborne Remastered?-Danilo Dias?If you said 'YES' to most or all of these questions, then you should buy Moonrider right now and enjoy your sweet time with it. This game is a freaking beast and definitely a must-play if you're into 90s / early 00s classic 2D action games.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: It's a JoyMasher game, so expect a certain level of love and respect for NES/Mega Drive/SNES/Neo Geo-era stuff. Always an enjoyable experience if you like the classics from that time period.Have got all of the trophies (not too much of an ask), probably their second best game after Odallus which is a classic under-rated Metroidvania before the genre really took off and became known as such.No criticisms aside from it being too short. Controls are tidy (despite what I've seen from other reviews), the higher tempo techno trance soundtrack stuff is solid and the Shinobi + Mega Man X descriptions are apt.Just a blast to play and a nice distraction for three or four hours, doesn't really have time to get old or repetitive so can see myself coming back to speed through a perfect run on another save slot.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: A very clean looking, retro throwback to the 8 and 16 bit ninja games of old. It has way more in common with Shinobi than it does Ninja Gaiden, with a very, VERY, light sprinkling of Mega Man (you can choose stages in any order and get abilities from defeating bosses, although they don't act as weaknesses to other bosses). The sprite art is really nice looking and the music is good. There are a couple of variations in gameplay throughout the game, but nothing too crazy. It can easily be finished 100% in a couple hours and maybe just a couple more to grab all of the achievements. It's not very hard in general. The controls can get kind of slippery due to various small issues, but nothing that ruins the game. I'd say it's a reasonably priced game for what it offers.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and can't wait to speedrun it. There is not a single thing I don't love about this game. If it looks good, it's because it is. Get it. Get it now and have a blast.A friend gifted this game to me as a disclosure, but I was gonna buy it anyway and then gifted a copy to someone else because I have to share the love.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: idk what to say about this. Everything is really good, except the gameplay. It feels like a third-rate Mega-Drive game, but with way better production values. It's obviously trying to be Shinobi 3, but the execution is a little off and the level design is ♥♥♥♥. As many others have said, the level bosses are pathetically easy... It's a shame because it's obvious that an insane amount of work went into this. I really wanted to like it. But it's bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Game is way too easy. It desperately wants to be Hagane, but doesn't seem to realise that the draw of that game was you had to practice and practice. This game can't resist giving you a health refill every 5 seconds. Bosses can be beaten by standing next to them and spamming the special attack button. There's a decent game here but the devs need to take off the kid gloves and let us actually play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: A MUST pick on a sale.Why do I start off like that? Because the game is too short! It is absolutely wonderful, with a great variety of environments, enemies, bosses and minibosses, not to mention the OST, but it took me 4 hours to get all achievements on it.I am thoroughly satisfied with the experience, it's just that I wish there either were more stages or we were able to play as a side character.Additionally, this is by far the easiest of Joymasher games. Which is both a good thing and a bad thing. Good because it is vastly more accessible than any of the previous titles, and bad because the infinite lives, combined with limitless continues and very, very generous checkpoints make walkthrough a bit too much of a breeze.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pure wasted potential. The overall presentation is great: very detailed and stellar pixel graphics that don't get old even after finishing the game, great enemy and boss designs, levels filled with character and detail, all tied off with a great and very fitting retroesque OST. Sadly, the game is really bogged down with very simplistic and mostly uninteresting level design, a lack of any real challenge after the starting level and (worst of all, in my opinion) bosses that are either very easy to take down or take needlessly long to whittle down with no real challenge whatsoever.Case and point: this game has all the style, but not a lot of substance. It's sad because I could really see myself coming back to it if it had more to offer than just pretty graphics.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Underwhelming for the price it asks you to pay.Visuals are the strongest point by far.Gameplay is quite solid although jumping might be a bit floaty than it should. You have access to a running attack and a divekick, the latter which feels a bit overshadowed by every other attack you can do.Defetaing bosses grants you new special attacks you can use at the cost of weapon energy. Most of these attacks are quite powerful, some kinda trivialize every single boss in the game.The stages are fun but the bossfight can be a joke once you know which special weapons are good.Troughout the stages you will find chips you can equip that will grant you special perks, allowing you to equip two at the same time.Once you beat the game once theres really nothing to do if you already got all achievements and found all chips.The Game is relatively easy and lacks any kind of unlockables like a hard mode and whatnot.Wait until its under 10 dollars because you wont be getting much out of it, but its visually cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian Moonrider is a mostly solid action game. It is made up of fairly short stages and doesn't take long to get through, instead promoting repeat play for score and clear time. Moonrider has a simple and satisfying move set, enemies are well designed, and stages are interesting, but the bosses are a mixed bag. Mid stage bosses are enjoyable enough, but the majority of end stage bosses can be completely blown through without much hassle with the exception of the final boss. There is an unlockable special move called darkportal that further trivializes these encounters and even goes so far as to make the mid stage bosses as ineffectual as the rest. The game also lacks any difficulty settings to potentially circumvent these issues. The bosses have cool move sets and the potential to be the highlight of the game, but as it stands they are way too easy to brute force and I never felt like I was actually fighting them. I was very excited for this game but came away unsure how to feel about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game that throws you back to Sega Genesis and Snes era. Such a great feeling to play a game made with this kind of passion for the old school ninja games like Shinobi and Hagane. Joymasher has only outstanding titles. I really recommend this game ! Congrats for the devs and thanks for this amazing piece of art.

_childDocuments_.review: This game beat my expectations going in. I just read some reviews that said it reminded them of Shinobi and Megaman, Who would have thought that putting those two games together would lead to something that maintains such a fantastic air of quality.The music is honestly the best part for me, it kept the action rolling along while bring you some excellent synthwave beats. Each boss has their own soundtrack as well keeping you playing to see hear all the bosses songs.Gameplay is slick and fast, it handles quickly and plays extremely well with a ps5 controller. This game also has special secrets per level that can boost your gameplay such as MP/HP Regen, one-hit kill (As in you're hit once and you die) and double jump to name a couple. This game also loves to change up the style of play to think of Batman returns and the batmobile sections and thats what you get, they are short, sweet, and have a rockin tune to blast to.I will say this though, sans the last boss all the others are too easy to cheese, I would put a hit limiter on the enemies or maybe refocus how they work so its just a smidge harder land a hit. I will be watching for speedruns of this game, its like its built for it.

Every boss can just be dropkick spammed. Kinda disappointing cause never got a chance to learn or even see some boss patterns.I guess maybe getting all S's might be a challenge but still... :D

_childDocuments_.review: === STORY ===In a dystopia ruled by a corrupt and tyrant government, you're the latest creation of their powerful cyber army but, you decide to turn on your former masters and fight for justice!The focus of the game is NOT the story so don't expect it'll go much deeper of what the premise tells you. There are some dialogues, a couple of cutscenes here and here from you where you can infer some stuff about the story and characters but just barely. Despite there some details I would liked to know more about, I don't think it's something that plays againt the game in general tbh.=== GAMEPLAY ===This is an action platformer kinda like Ninja Gaiden with some Megaman elements. What I mean with this is that you have different stages you can choose, each one with a boss you have to fight and, after defeating said boss, you get a power BUT, unlike Megaman, there not super-effective powers against certain bosses. They're just an extra to your arsenal.As for what you can do, you have your basic abilities: you can run, jump, a blade attack and you can do an aerial vertical/diagonal kick. Control response is good enough, no complaints there.=== VISUAL AND SOUND ===You like 80s-90s cyberpunk? You like samurai/ninjas? Well, you're in for a treat 'cause this game has plenty of it. The protagonist, bosses/enemies, everyone screams those aesthetics. Designs are pretty good, simple without going over the top. All that mixed with a nice 16-bit visual style.As for sound effect, they are good enough. As for soundtrack, it has a nice collection of synthwave tracks very pleaseant to hear while playing.=== FINAL THOUGHTS ===Pretty fun straight-forward game. It knows what it is and it offer what it promises in the right dose without overcomplicating itself too much with other extras. I only wish it could last longer but that just me.SCORE: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitated between a positive review, no review or a negative review. I think the current game evaluation (96%) is overestimated, so I opted for the negative review.First let's make things fair : visuals are stunning, and the music is delicious. You can really tell effort was made to give this game a unique atmosphere, while having some obvious references such as Ninja Gaiden.I don't think the controls are very good nor bad. They do take a little bit of time to get used to though. But I liked the fact that only 2 face buttons are used + 2 triggers for default mapping, so that everything is accessible with your standard hand position.Now the bads. This game needed some balancing. Because you can beat the levels in any order, it meant all bosses had to be "averaged" to consider you had at least one powerup. But it's not the case when you first meet one of them and it can be painful. And then, you stumble upon one or two overpowered chips that almost annihilates the game's diffculty. You can just damage tank the bosses now.Level design was overlooked. Health refill placements were sometimes too numerous or missing. Some rooms didn't really make sense and felt like they were put here to arbitrarily increase the game's length, without bringing any challenge. I may be a bit too harsh but such an approach would make sense considering the high price of the game.I will surely remember this game because of its overall charism. But I don't think I will ever play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a true SNES/Genesis game that got lost in the past. The precision, the feedback from landing blows, and the platforming all feel great. There is a real sense of momentum in the game. It is not easy by any means, but it is far from unfair. I can't help but make the Ninja Gaiden comparison, but it has that level of reward meets skill that is pretty rare these days. If this interests you in the slightest, get the game! If you want to jam out, get the OST too. It is pretty awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game overall, but nowhere near as good as JoyMasher's previous "Blazing Chrome" game as that game had Co-op (this one doesn't), extra playable characters (this one doesn't), better music overall (this one has 1 or 2 good level music, but the rest are forgettable) and the story in Blazing Chrome was more straightforward than this one.Still, I think Moonrider is an okay singleplayer side platformer overall, but given what I said above (as well as being on the shorter end), I would advise getting this game on a sale ($5 to $7 would be the ideal price for this game IMO).

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: This game is a little bit Contra, a little bit Mega Man and a little bit Strider. You're an oppressive robot gone rogue, who has decided to take on the oppressors. You'll have a number of levels to complete, most of which you can do in any order you like and at the end of each boss, you'll get a new secondary weapon, which you can select at will. The weapons vary greatly in strength and attack pattern and while some are better than others against certain enemies, you can use any of them at any time. There are also various upgrade chips hidden in the levels, of which you can equip two at a time.It's dripping with 16-bit style and challenge, though it's not as hard as JoyMasher's last title, Blazing Chrome, especially if you use certain upgrade chips. That's not to say there isn't a challenge here though, because this game will definitely test you, in the way 16-bit games were good at. The only thing I wish was here is co-op play, but it's still very solid as a single player experience.If you like modern retro titles like I do, this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Mega-Man meet Shinobi sounds great at first but...Graphics and AudioThe game looks amazing with a great soundtrack but that's about where the good stuff ends...DifficultyThis game is insanely easy and you're only going to get about 2 hours of content out of it before you've done it all. Even if you're exploring for every secret... maybe 3 hours. The mid-level bosses are harder than the end-level bosses. The final boss was a little more satisfying, but even then I only needed to restart once. MechanicsSpecial weapons take too much energy to be viable for more than just a boss fight. You're limited to 2 "upgrades" per level with no way to switch them up. These "upgrades" are essentially the same things you'd find in a standard Mega-Man game but instead of picking and choosing which ones you want to use they just become part of your standard load-out (double jump, armor, secret detection, etc). Another annoying aspect, no indicator to if you missed a secret in an area so if you're hunting for upgrades, you're going to have to play each level multiple times to see if you missed something. Just more tedious padding. ReplayabilityUnless you like doing the same thing over and over, good luck finding a reason to play it again.StoryThis aspect is also pretty lacking. The dialog is all cliche as hell and you just end up skipping it "blah blah same crap as any samarai movie blah blah" Conclusion:If you've got money to blow and want an easy-short-retro-like game. Sure, get it. Otherwise, skip this and buy The Messenger.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty sweet.I lack the background for most of its inspirations, seeing mostly Mega Man X DNA influencing the level structure, but the combat reminds me a lot more of Strider. It's got a smooth, fair difficulty that will chew you up if you're reckless, but basically no death feels unfair, even if it takes a few attempts.The soundtrack is fantastic, but given that Dominic Ninmark is at the helm that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone. The graphics are super clean and distinct, with a surprisingly grotesque look in a few environments and bosses that gives Moonrider a style I won't forget any time soon.The game could have done to be a little bit longer. Each of the main six stages are of a solid length, but with ONLY those six, and how short the endgame is, it feels like another one or two levels are missing from the experience.The game's story, while obviously not important to the enjoyment of the game, also feels a bit unfinished, as if there were some key backstories or establishing conversations that were cut. The character of Shinjen, for example, comes out of nowhere but is treated like the game's primary rival. This is despite the fact that I'm not certain he's even named anywhere inside the game itself. Add to that the fact that the boss fights begin with un-translated Japanese voice samples (which could have used subtitles to understand their context for those unfamiliar with the language) left me with a feeling that I was missing something. The story doesn't need much more than what's there, but what's missing sticks out a little.Nonetheless, the game is fantastic and worth the price of entry. It's short and sweet, and even if you're a bit unfamiliar with its niche in the genre like I was, there's plenty to love to get you in the door. Once you're in, I guarantee a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Side scrolling action game. Control a robotic enforcer or a fascist government that breaks free of his masters and fights the other robot guardians. Somewhat Mega Man X like with the stage selection, gaining an attack from each of the main bosses, and finding upgrades inside levels. You have a main three hit slash combo, a dash function you can do by double tapping left or right or by holding a button, dash attack, straight down or down and to the left or right aimed drop kick that bounces you off enemies, can duck and attack, and have access to a variety of sub weapons you can switch between. Stages have a good variety with some good backgrounds and the game controls well and it is satisfying to fight the game's enemies, of which each stage tends to introduce new ones.Where the game falls a bit short is maybe getting a bit too close to the Mega Man X style feel where stages can be way too easy without the enemies being meaningful challenges to you. You fight few enemies at the same time and it is often easy to even ignore or bypass them, which is actually helpful if going for higher stage rankings for achievements that require you to finish with faster times. The sub weapons also fall into the normal issue where most just aren't very useful and there is one in particular that is both great for stages and can finish off bosses in seconds.The equipable chips found in stages give you a variety of bonuses like regenerating health and MP over time, regenerating health and MP after a kill, longer attack range, double jumps, one that allows you to edit your color, one that causes you to die from one hit, etc. You can equip two of them at once. Losing all of your lives also unlocks one that reduces your max stage ranking but halves the damage you take. Nice to be able to customize yourself a bit but certain ones are obviously standouts in usefulness and there is nothing to out there that really changes up the gameplay.There are a few moments where you are riding on a motorcycle across a highway avoiding and shooting at enemies in a more horizontal shoot em up style, these stages look good but like going through the main stages you just aren't challenges by enemies and the subdued music can give them a dull feel as they do on.Solid game, just keeping some of the issues of the Mega Man games it somewhat emulates without having as many secrets and mechanics. Even going for an S rank on every stage is a quick and simple affair.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a good game.It has an interesting blend between the Shinobi games from SEGA and Rockman/Rockman X mechanics (even to the point of gaining powers from bosses or selecting the stage order). Controls are good, music is great, and pixel art is AMAZING. The style reminds me a lot of Contra Hard Corps on the Mega Drive. Gameplay is also great, it's what you'd expect of this type of blend: fighting lots of enemies with different attacks, exploring stages, finding hidden powerups in the form of chips, and enjoying cool boss fights a couple times per stage. And about chips: I love the fact that most provide alternative playstyles. You can recover health from killing enemies, passive energy regeneration for weapons, or even a double jump. Since you can only pick two, you need to think and prepare for the mission ahead using the right combination.With that said, there were some things that I found lacking:The powers obtained through bosses were underwhelming; the majority of them serve no discernible purpose. No interaction with enemies (like making them weaker with certain elements) or stages (like opening a shortcut) makes them worth using. A lacking fire boomerang that doesn't carry items, a shuriken shield that's not very protective... overall, I'd say the dash and the dark tentacle are the best ones.Picking the order of the stages is kind of detrimental to the story. In one boss dialogue, Moonrider is sure of himself, what he's doing, and what he is opposing. In the next one, he might be confused about what is going on or won't remember anything prior to his awakening.The level design is a bit lacking, to the point where you'll have a feeling of deja vu. You could make a drinking game out of how many times you're required to wall jump in a small gap between two walls in the ceiling, waiting for a platform or hazard.Overall, I recommend Moonrider to any fan of the genre. You can tell it's a passion project and a celebration of old-school action platformers, but it might leave you wanting more. And while most issues could be solved with updates, I don't know if JoyMasher wanted to replicate the feeling of a game released in the 90s, even to the point of bringing back the usual flaws of the time. I enjoyed my time with the game, and I hope we get more Moonrider in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start this review off with the question: Is this game worth it for the price?The answer depends if you'd consider yourself playing this game as a retro enthusiast, or a modern gamer. I recommend this game because I have quite a bit of experience with retro games, and most of my favourite games come from that era -- playing Moonrider just feels natural with a mixed elements from Mega Man X, Shinobi, etc. As a "modern-retro" game, it fits the bill quite well -- solid gameplay, great spritework, great OST. Game difficulty is on the easy side, with most bosses being easily cheesed with full health and basic attacks.Modern gamers (maybe even some retro gamers) will likely end up turning away from this game due to short game length, and lack of replay-ability features. I was able to complete the game within 2 hours, and there is not much to do once you complete the game besides getting all items, and all achievements. In this regard, I'd recommend waiting for a sale before picking the game up.Overall, if you have a soft spot for retro games, definitely check this game out. If you are looking for a game packed with features that'll keep you busy, there are better options out there.

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't think this game is awful, I can honestly say that I don't feel like lives up to much of the hype that it receives from other reviews.  There is a solid foundation here but it honestly it feels a little lazy/incomplete.  This game seeks to emulate several 16 bit era classics and it executes some of those concepts well in parts of the game, but fails to bring things all together into an enjoyable game.  It almost feel like they wanted to make this game difficult but then toned it down to make it more approachable to novice players.  I have picked this game up and put it back down several times because the segments that I enjoy from the game really excite me, but they are too few and far between to warrant a recommendation.  Definitely a C tier game.
