_childDocuments_.review: Fun platformer with great graphics and sound. Weirdly in depth story, but I like it. Gameplay takes a little time to get used to if you're expecting a carbon copy of Mega Man Zero/X, but are fine once you adjust (I wish the wall kick was just "press into wall" though instead of requiring an extra button press, though).To me, there are 2 main "weak points" with the gameplay: Length and Difficulty. For length, I personally didn't think only having 6 main stages was awful or anything, especially since they're all 2 parters. . I will say one of the guardian fights was a massive wasted opportunity considering the arena, but I won't spoil anything else. My main issue is with the last couple of stages, which feel very rushed. That feeling is probably exacerbated by my other point, the wack difficulty. One of the minibosses is harder than the final boss, I swear. No idea if this is more a "I got good at the end" situation or if it's some sort of oversight. I was getting mostly D or C ranks on the main stages and then proceeded to S rank all of the final stages. Oh well.The boss weapons are cool (Hey look, a dash attack that doesn't suck!), but most of the time your stock super attack is more than adequate, and the other parts of your moveset are also very capable of dealing with enemies. I spammed the running slash a lot, must be all that Pizza Tower I played. There's also the upgrade system, and finding and experimenting with new chips can be fun.I enjoyed this game a lot despite my gripes, and can't wait for what's next from the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Stylish and dark, Moonrider has the perfect balance between old-school "what even is this" difficulty and skill. The upgrade system is well crafted, the game is completely void of any filler. While the pixelated art could use some slight clarity, the mood, speed of gameplay, and especially the soundtrack elevate the game enough to warrant multiple playthroughs. Not to mention going for that S in every stage provides with a great sense of adrenaline and reward.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is not a run of the mill platformer, even if it may look a little like Ninja Gaiden, Probotector and Mega Man X had an influence on it. You play as the titular protagonist, a robotic being who escapes the clutches of the regime that had him made and takes down (former) comrades in order to liberate the fleshbags (humans) from tyranny.Thing is, it's not about the story. This game is all about the levels and especially the bosses. The visuals and the music complement each other fantastically. Controls are good and the boss weapons you get are fun. However, it's not a long game. It's more intended as a speedrunner's challenge in that sense: get through a level without dying and within 10 minutes and you can get an S-rank rating.Beyond that, I've but two gripes  with it: One, the boss weapons are not exactly useful, bar one. Dark Portal can trivialise most boss battles. The rest don't give enough oomph for the ammo cost, though they still have some use against regular enemies.Two, while there's one to two chips (extra abilities and functions) per regular stage, they are not easily found without the Detective chip eating up a slot, or having a walkthrough to show you where what is. Given that it has no other use and branching paths in stages are mostly filler rather than significant... I really wish the devs had relegated it and the Chameleon chip to their own slots rather than the two you have.That said though, Moonrider's a fun game with a good vibe. Just could've done with a bit more polish and a few more stages.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Very good 16-Bit Action Platformer reminiscent of classics like Hagane, Shinobi and Mega Man.You get several stages which are split in two levels. You can play through the stages in any order you want. If you beat a stage's final boss you'll get his special weapon which will be added to your arsenal. You first playthrough will be depeding on your skill 2-5 hours. Consequent playthroughs will be around the one and a half hour mark.The game is a bit on the easier side in this genre, but it is a great entry into the world of classic 2D Action Platformers and you can work your way up from here to more difficult games (like Cyber Shadow to name another modern game which is much harder).Only critique I have is that sometimes the game suffers from screentearing and there seems to be no V-Sync option.Other than that, a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Already from the Promotional Material to the first area cleared, this game has me hooked in what it's going for.Coming from the SEGA Genesis days of gaming this hits a strong Nostalgia Chord in me, only this time having a proper set up to fully engross myself in the games I'm playing.If you're looking for a Nostalgia hit, specifically from the SEGA Genesis era of gaming, then this game brings it in spades and has a Soundtrack I'm well intending to play even when I set the controller down!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have ever bought a game as fast as I have after seeing the trailer for Moonrider. There were so many callbacks and homages to my favourite game of all time, Shinobi III, that I could see in the trailer alone that I had to try it. This game plays fantasticly with all kinds of neat and memorable set pieces within the levels, many references not just to Shinobi but other games of the era as well. The control is responsive, the bosses are interesting to fight and the challenge isn't too terribly hard but still enough that you're probably going to die a few times. The art and graphics are great; it definitely nails the dystopian future aesthetic and the music is great with plenty of 80s style synths. If there is one downside it is that the story is what it is and the writing borders on cringe at times (And the typos are numerous and noticeable) but you're really not playing this one for the story. It's fun to play and it's all that matters.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game.A modern take on Shinobi 3 with some light Mega Man X influences. It controls like a charm, it looks fantastic, the sountrack is great.The game's difficulty is overall on the easier side, which is a welcome change of pace allowing for a smoother entrypoint for newcomers while score and time chasing will occupie more seasoned players. All in all, a very good package
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=================Fun but way too short 2-D platformer that feels like a demo, get it on a sale or not at all.Good Stuff==================- The pixel art in this game is below something like Blasphemous but it's commendable- The levels usually have a creative gimmick to them i.e. riding a bike or being constantly pursued by a mid-boss enemy ala the old Megaman X titlesBad Stuff==================- The game is offensively short, probably beatable in a single setting only missing 3 collectables, I clocked in at 2.5 hours with virtually no deaths so it feels intentional on the developers part- The difficulty, outside the final boss, is laughable. I can't imagine most players getting stymied on any part of this game- The hitboxes are a bit janky and you'll find yourself getting hit by stuff you probably shouldn't- The ability to hit projectiles is cool but inconsistent, you can only do it to a very small set of enemies- I know this isn't the forefront of a platformer but the story is...not good, just very poorly told.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: It's become a trend with Joymasher games. All style and very little substance. The art and visuals are great though and thats were it ends. Terrible controls, bad level design and heavy stage memorization just kills this game. Instead of playing a diluted version of great games that the developer is trying to imitate with Moonrider and Blazing Chrome. Here is a list of games that you should play instead :Megaman X Contra 3 : Alien Wars Metal SlugHaganeContra HardcorpsRevenge of the ShinobiShinobi 3 Batman Returns
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is one of the most "By the numbers" retro-style games you can possibly find. This game was made by the same people that did Blazing Chrome, an already "By the numbers" game, but in comparison Chrome wins by a landslide.I don't want to call "Moonrider" bad because it's not, but it's so damn safe in it's design and execution that while playing it you will be thinking how much more fun you would be having if you were playing the games that inspired it, (specially Ninja Gaiden or Shinobi III which are masterpieces).Aside from it's obvious ninja game inspirates, there's a fair deal of Megaman and "whatever was popular in the late 80's/early 90's". What I think hurts this game a lot is that does not just pays homage to those games, it outrights tries to copy them with flaws included.It's endearing when you play an old game that had a barebones story and limited gameplay, but doing it today feels just like a regular shortcoming, there's not tongue-in cheek commentary done about it, it's just played straight.The story is some barebones political revolution thing with no real explanation as to why things are happening, similar to Alien Soldier (this game wishes it was as tight). But Alien Soldier backstory is an excuse to throw boss fights at the player. In this game you keep getting information you could not give two ♥♥♥♥♥ about.For some retro-style ninja fix I would much rather play "The Messenger", which is a game that pay homages to retro games while building upon them instead of limiting itself just for nostalgia's sake. (Cyber Shadow might be another good alternative but I have not played it). "Moonrider" is a solid game but it does not stand out aside from early visual presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Game suffers from an identity crisis.  It doesnt know if it wants to be shinobi or megaman.  Example. the first boss is absurdly easy.  I then go to photonrider (or whatever his name is) level.  The level is of light-medium difficulty.  The boss is ridiculous.  He has no openings.  If you try to attack him for more than a second he will retaliate by jumping, slamming or jumping and shooting.  mind you, one third of your mobility/attacking is mid air...and if you're ANY WHERE in the air and  he's doing something he'll hit you.  I had at one point been a good 3 body spaces away and I just...died. mid jump as though he had shot.  Pick a lane man.  If I had some sort of semi ranged attack it'd be nice.  But you have to get into the bosses face to hit it; where he literally has all the advantage...and then jumps away...while attacking as PART of his escape move.  No thanks.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the apparent distinction of being literally unplayable on my computer due to a graphics card incompatibility. If you don't have the correct hardware, you get an error message during startup and the game closes. That's a major design flaw and I had no choice but to demand a refund. I could have used that money to buy a game I can actually play!I can play Warframe, PSO2, Crossout and Bloodstained without trouble, but this game doesn't even start because my graphics card doesn't work with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Way lower quality than I would expect from the folks at Joymasher. I had to refund because I was getting such low FPS on my laptop and constant frame rate issues even on my beefier desktop. The premise and OST for Moonrider are great, I just can't get the gameplay working as well as the demo last year, no matter what I do. Sad to refund, but maybe it will get fixed sometime down the road. I'd compromise and pick up the soundtrack for a few songs, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Fistst of all i was playing the game entirely on Steam Deck OLED. It runs fantastic,except minor stutterings here and there. I tried at 60fps/60Hz but it dropps sometimes to 58-59,Its not kuch but it creates micro stutters. I tried it at 90fpz/90Hz it still drops.Than at the end of the game (sadly) i tried 80fps/80Hz and the game ran smoothiy and stable.So if youre a Steam Deck OLED user, set thegame to 80FPS/80Hz for a smooth gameplay.Battery lasts about 6 hours more or less.As for the game itself,A bit short... But i really love it! Only thing i DIDN'T like are pseudo 3D stages.I beat the main game, without worrying to much about collecting stuff.I did collect things here and there and explored a bit, ibut i mostly wanted to beat the game.All in all, considering all i just wrote, it took me 4.4h.But the game is fantastic. I wish there are more things to explore, more levels or bigger levels, some plot tvists, new moves etc. Perhaps in Moon Rider 2? Who knows.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, I recommend it. The best part is the aesthetics and graphic design, reminiscent of the early '90s in 16-bit style, which is fantastic. While it never becomes monotonous, the new mechanics unlocked along the way are seldom useful, so our character's initial abilities are most likely the ones you'll stick with till the end. This leaves a desire for a bit more depth in gameplay (which, by the way, is very well executed).Contrary to what some have mentioned, the difficulty at the Normal level is quite appropriate.P.S. The CRT mode is almost imperative for a game like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin but this game is amazing. I am very blessed to have gotten the game for free, as I've personally been following the progress of the game since I saw the first level back on Youtube. The game brings back a lot of childhood memories of playing Hagane: The Final Conflict , only difference is that this game is just overall better. The controls are tight, animations are great, the levels are cool, music is on point, difficulty is just where it needs to be and just overall a fun game! Lots of love and effort was put into this project. If you're a retro gamer, like platformer hack and slash games from the 90's era, this game is right up your alley! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: Game is ultimate. It looks great, it sounds amazing, controls are for the most part very good, and the gameplay is phenomenal. Game is just right in length and there is much incentive to go fast. The Bad: I wish there was a slide, the dash attack has too much recovery, wall jumping is kinda rough, and the story cutscene text flies by way too fast. Maybe the bosses are bit on the easy side, but then I'm glad they aren't damage sponges with tons of ridiculous invincibility frames, more along the lines of Shinobi 3 where you can burst them down quick if you know what to do.The Ugly: This game is gorgeous, there is nuthin' ugly about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way too expensive for how short it is. $20 for a 2.5 hour game is ridiculous. I got it on sale for $15 and it was still too much. The combat and level design in this game are fine, but they don't make up for the ludicrous price tag this game possesses. If this game was $3, I can see myself considering it a 7/10 game, but with how short it is, it's quite simply not worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: If you miss the old 16 -bit Ninja games, then you found the right game for you.But be warned, this game is less Shinobi and more like Hagane on Snes, but this game fixes everything that was wrong with that game but making it feel a bit more SHINOBI 3 but not as much as expected.The game is both smooth as butter but stiff as a stick at the same time, jumping is very weird, it can be fixed but u will find out why it is not recommended in the game.Anw, great game, very well made, very good, just the bosses....they are so easy and u can easily beat most of them by just plain overpowering them if you chose to, but it is fine by me, no need for bosses that are hard as nail.Great graphics, good music, ok controls and good replay value, i recommend it for any Hagane/Shinobi 3 fans out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Don't waste your time on this game. There are no redeeming qualities about it. There is no difficulty to this game at all. You can face tank everything. I don't know how you can ripoff something like Megaman, where you have flawless blueprints, but this is what you come up with. The controls and movement are TERRIBLE. You're never going to use any other chips aside from double jump and detective unless you want to play through the game a second time, which I don't know why you would want to. By the time I completed the game I was at 95% completion with one chip missing. I know I 100%'d every stage so I went ahead and looked it up. You literally have to get a game over, which I never came close to, to get the chip I was missing. Don't even get me started on the basic, almost non-existent story. I'm not sure why there are so many positive reviews, I guess people will eat up any shovelware these days. Do yourself a favor and keep your money. This game isn't worth more than a few bucks let alone the insane price it's at.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid action platformer that takes a lot of influence from games like Megaman X. While everything is well made, theres a few points of missed polish like the stage selection not really telling you if you have already found items in that stage. It's maybe not as strong as their previous work, Blazing Chrome, but I don't regret spending my money on this game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent action platformer with great art and soundtrack, sadly though, it's pretty easy, very short and with not so great replay value. I think it's worth at least a single playthrough or a few more if you want to find and collect all chips or get the best score on all levels. I would only recommend buying the game during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.user: Turkey n' Shit こーりー
_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet love letter to the action/adventure games of yore you remember as a child. A beautiful homage and respect paid to both Shinobi and Mega-Man X.My only real complaint with the game is some of the balancing is questionable; mainly where the hentai sub-weapon from an old, cosmic world is concerned. It does entirely WAY too much damage and makes every single boss encounter in the game an absolute joke, allowing you to bypass fighting them long enough to encounter their entire animation/attack cycle(s). Seriously, it's busted. The only encounter where you can't 100% abuse this is the last boss, but even then, it's still fairly devastating.Baring that, the game is excellent, allbeit short. which is frankly expected at this price-point. I completed it in exactly 3 hours time, exploring for all the upgrades (I'm still missing one that isn't a level listed "item"... hrm) and S-ranking every stage, baring the last one because I simply didn't want to do that level again at that point.This game is going to be a real joy to watch during speed-running marathons, namely SGDQ later this year with any luck. I'd imagine some absolute mad-lad/lady is going to completely obliterate the game with the Glass-Cannon mod equipped (1-shot death).Worth it, ESP. at a discounted price-point if you own the developers/publishers other titles. I feel like this is their best work to date. Well done.Play their other games, ESP. Blazing Chrome! Exceptional love-letter to Contra.---Graphics - 8/10 (Art-Style is fantastic.)Gameplay - 9/10 (Aforementioned balance issues, otherwise near-perfect.)Controls - 10/10 (Controls are precise and fantastic. Movement feels wonderful, esp once you get some upgrades/abilities.)Soundtrack - 8/10 (I need to find the OST for this and listen with proper headphones. I found the music solid but maybe not as life-changing as some others have per their reviews.)Story - Subjective (It's about what you'd expect, but the narrative works.)Replay Value - Moderately-HighWouldn't mind updates to this game to allow you to play some other characters in the future. I would certainly come back.Overall - 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: The game is far too difficult with no real way to adjust difficulty outside of modification chips. The motion and controls as well are janky and inconsistent - a forward leaping attack that can cause damage if you touch an enemy in the first few frames just feels bad. Not worth the money, even on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: I suppose this is one of the first negative reviews. The game looks and sounds great with a cool setting. My issue is, for a platformer where reflexes are key to survival, the controls feel sticky and unresponsive at least on an Xbox controller. Sometimes it fudges running attacks and wall jumping. Unless this is an Xbox controller specific issue, you get way more fluid controls from a classic Megaman X, Metroid or Guacamelee.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Way too short for the money. I beat it in 2.4 hours. I'm missing like three hidden upgrades which would probably take another 20 minutes to get. For 20 bucks this is not worth it. It's just long enough that I can't get a refund. Ridiculously short. The game itself is a mix of Shinobi and Megaman X, which is a really a nice combo, but there is just not enough meat on the bone here. I feel pretty cheated with this one. Oh, and the English localization is pretty bad haha.EDIT: was able to get a refund. If this game was 5 bucks it would be worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a very good retro styled Hack and Slash action game and made by the same people that have made Blazing Chrome and Odallus: The Dark Call, okay then the story. In the far future the world is oppressed by a totalitarian state and their guardians, but the authorities signify their own destruction by bringing online the Ninja Warrior known as Moonrider, now Moonrider must defeat his own comrades in order to free the world from the iron grip of tyranny.Okay the likes, the gameplay is really good and takes inspiration from classic side scrollers like Strider, Contra and even Mega Man. Like you go around slicing enemies, deflecting laser blasts and wall jump like Strider, fight bio mechanical alien like horrors and ride a motorcycle just like contra, you can also select which stage to play and after defeating the boss of that area you gain their power just like in Mega Man.The graphics are really good it captures the feel and look of classic side scrollers, more precisely Contra and Strider with incredible uses of color, detail, character designs and background. The levels are all very good, nicely diverse with each level being just absolutely amazing to look at and explore from a laboratory to a forest to even a flying airship.The enemies and bosses are all fantastic each one has incredibly good designs that makes you think of video games like Contra and Strider, especially contra as the boss of the first level feels like it wouldn't be out of place in a contra game.The characters are good each one has its own unique look, like our main character he just looks absolutely badass. The story is good, it's a simple stop the bad guy story that does meditate a little bit on the nature of tradition, revolution and tyranny. The music is fantastic each level has an incredibly good soundtrack that fits the game so well. There's also some voice acting which is okay, it's in Japanese but it makes sense because an old games like contra there would be voice acting, but in the original Japanese.Okay the dislikes, the price for the game is a little bit too high for a game you can beat in around 3 hours, basically the game is $17. Also some levels can be a bit bunk mostly doing with enemy placements being incredibly cheap. Now that I told you this Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a very good retro styled Hack and Slash action game and made by the same people that have made Blazing Chrome and Odallus: The Dark Call, with good gameplay, vary good levels and fantastic enemies and bosses, alright do I recommend this game absolutely it's fantastic, I will say that maybe wait till it's on sale to save a few bucks though.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute little retro game. The graphics hit just the spot and the mechanics are fun. Bought the game after finishing Blazing Chrome (by the same developers), which I found to be a lot more difficult. On the one hand it was a bit of a relief, on the other hand the game wasn't quite as challenging and therefore less satisfying to beat. Still worth picking up, just don't expect it to be very difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Shinobi + Mega Man X = Vengeful Guardian MoonriderFantastic little romp! Short playtime, but don't let that deter you from a fanatically wrapped product. The quality and care put into this title shows in every pixel. Controls are intuitive and well tuned. The soundtrack is banging all the way through. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, similar to titles such as Hagane, Strider, or the Shinobi series. The controls are a little jank though in that the dive kick should be mapped to one of the many other available buttons instead of clumsily combined in the jump+attack (which is another attack if a direction isn't pressed). Wall jumping is tedious (think NES Strider) and is critical to succeeding in a couple of levels. They can be downright frustrating at times. The double jump upgrade you can acquire in one of the levels helps tremendously. Boss battles aren't bad as they can be beaten either by learning the pattern or spam attacking them.Overall, I'm giving this a recommendation, but be aware there are faults in the game; and better options.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Total play time is like 2hrs. The game encourages you to move fast and not kill enemy for some reason due to the large amount of health and energy pickups. Once you die a couple of times you get the shield upgrade which is like really OP and can make the difficulty much easier.The game's difficulty is weird too like if you have the dash or the tenticles it pretty much makes the boss shred like paper. I'd say its worth like 5-10 dollars if you want to get this game. Still recommended tho, I have had fun playing and it is a cool mixture of megaman and strider.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: A great looking and simple, albeit short homage to 16 bit consoles and the arcade era of games. Moonrider closely resembles Run Saber with Mega Man's level selection and boss weapons. The controls are very tight, and the artstyle just oozes cool. My biggest critique is that it is a very short game that can easily be beaten in under 2 hours. I recommend playing it, but wait for a sale to buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: You're a robot ninja that gets megaman style powers from killing bosses and you can repeatedly dive kick the ♥♥♥♥ out of anyone dumb enough to stand in your way. My only con is that I wish it was a little bit harder for veteran players since I was able to beat it without ever running out of lives. That said, it's a lot of fun to play through and it doesn't overstay its welcome. Definitely check this out if you're a fan of 90's action platformers!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider plays and looks phenomenal on the deck. It's main problem is the price and some boss fights not being on par with the others.Controls are tight, the music is really good, the story is oddly captivating, the visuals resemble gritty early 90's sci-fi anime, and overall the game is fun. Boss fights are usually engaging and challenging but there are a few bosses that don't hold up to the rest like one boss who stands still for a few seconds after an attack for no reason letting you get free hits or a submarine mini boss with a cannon that makes it annoying to hit the weak spot without taking damage unless you know to bring a specific chip into the level.It's a good time
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: While 16-bit-style action games are a dime a dozen these days, Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider truly stands out.The only complaint people seem to have about this game is that it's too easy. If you are like me though and are, on one hand, pretty good in games like these, but, on the other hand, also like to breeze through them without many roadblocks, then this is just perfectly balanced. Pretty much like the studio's last game, Blazing Chrome, actually, but just a bit more forgiving, due to its very powerful weapons and optional upgrades.Other than that, what this game excels in, is the sheer heft and haptics of the character. The absolute sweet spot between nimble samurai and heavy metal robot warrior.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels so authentic 16bit era. I loved how they didn't overdid the difficulty, instead adding optional equipment that can increase the challenge. It's really concise too and the CRT filter is the best I've seen ever, simply awesome. Instead of just trying to dumbly replicate a CRT TV 240p effect it does its own thing to effectively trigger the same psychovisual effect on your brain. If that last line sounds silly to you just take a quick look at the video below to see what I meant.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Frustrating at first, like many Sega Genesis games. You will get your butt stomped in once or twice... but then, once you get the hang of the button timings and attack positioning, the game opens up and becomes a lot of fun. The deliberate pace at which your character walks should inform how you play this game- it's not a button masher, and you will not be rewarded for flailing at your controller like it smoked all your meth.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Once upon a time, playing a good game that expected something of you -- as in, a game that's not mere entertainment, but something that you interact with -- could put you in a state, known as "The Zone".Most modern games act like this was never a thing. Heck, most devs would tell you that it isn't "essential" to game design. But I'd say that depending on what you are making, it is a mandatory component. As such, I took to retro experiences in order to get my fill of "The Zone". And the best thing that I can say abount "Moonrider" is that it put me in "The Zone".You know why you are here. You love Shinobi and Shadow Dancer, 90s pop-culture, ninjas, mechs and maybe even Megaman. And the devs knew that about you too. So they made "Moonrider" especially for us. While I'd define this game as "pure bliss" right now, I do admit that it is not perfect. I've numerous times fell victim to odd lag spikes, which cost me precious HP and the game's design simply lacking at times, because hidden moving platforms and respawning enemies just doesn't mesh well together. Furthermore, the game's level structure pretty much removes the typical learning curve, which left me banging my head for hours, because it took me longer than I'd like to admit to realize how this game wanted me to play it. TL;DR: watch the first level's intro closely and learn from it. But when it clicked? Pure bliss. And if you aren't as burnt out as I was when I picked this one up, your period is likely to be less than my "hours" spent in headbanging. Speaking of headbanging, I also didn't like the OST much until I realized what the composer actually did and since then, I've falled in love with the work. Guys, give us a record. We'll buy it. Please. Just do it. Not a CD. A record!! Also, a figure. Maybe a set of the mechs? I'd buy them. "Moonrider" was a wonderful surprise that I was excited about. Then life happened, I forgot about it and it is the only game I purchased during this year's Summer Sale. Why? Because I wanted this exact type of de-stress. And "Moonrider" delivered. It sparked that spark of joy, I went back and replayed Shinobi III and Shadow Dancer and I just... Love this so much. To wrap things up, I'll say the following: I did not click Uninstall when I beat this one, which is what I usually do. I will come back, with a vengeance. I will ace each stage. And I cant wait to get with friends over the weekend to eat pizza and try to beat eachother's high scores and look for secrets that probably don't exist. I don't care. I can vibe to this game. Because it has "The Zone". And that is of magnanimous importance. PS: Also, I really, really didn't understand anything about the plot. It was very confusing in its delivery, but I appreciated the set pieces, so theres that.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing JoyMasher games for a while, and there are a few things in common with all of their titles. First, they strive to replicate an authentic "retro" experience. Everything from the music, to the level design and difficulty attempt to emulate a time when games were difficult, hand crafted and fun in a way that sometimes wore its identity on its sleeves. Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is no different. In some ways, it is a refinement: everything is very lovingly made, and there is an attention to detail you don't usually see in retro style platformers. The gameplay is a bit confusing at first: you are encouraged to speedrun, but the many abilities you collect also mean you are supposed to plan out your moves ahead of time. The action is very satisfying. I'm not entirely convinced by the tank like nature of the protagonist. He seems to move quite slow, but then sprints if he has to, slashing away at things with abandon. Above all, the game rewards repeated playthroughs. There is that peculiar pleasure of memorizing a stage, not in a clinical way, but confidently. Much like a Souls title, in a sense. Long story short: a good time to be had here for retro game fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: THERE IS A DEMO AVAILABLE!!Give it a shot! It reeled me in!Gameplay was a mix of Ninja Gaiden and MegaMan X.A bit on the easier side (16-bit/retro platformers tend to be notoriously difficult), but I got the impression that this game is meant to be played fast & hard in a way that easily makes you feel like a badass. Very satisfying.Decent replay value to the stages as you look for powerups and try for S-Rank (felt to me like speed and not dying are the only qualifiers, so it's a pretty merciful endeavor for the most part). Each stage had their own gimmick to keep things fresh.Excellent pixelated graphics reminiscent of the Sega Genesis.Really good soundtrack with each stage theme having both high-energy and somber variants to them.===Main Complaints===-Again, a bit on the easier side, especially bosses; can easily brute force most fights with little regard to your HP.-Special weapons seem a bit unbalanced, one in particular absolutely decimates bosses nearly to the point of triviality.-There should be an option to make sprinting the default move speed; I had that button held down pretty much 100% of the time.-I encountered a couple bugs, but nothing that affected my ability to enjoy the game. Worst of them is the screen staying slightly dimmed after briefly darkening for the boss warning message. It goes away upon area transition, though. (Possibly related to FPS/refresh, based on my poking around.)-Map screen ought to show powerups found in each stage; the post-mission results screen is the only place to see this.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a throwback to the arcade-y, Sega Genesis era of gaming. The art style and theme remind me of Shinobi games a lot. It's a sidescrolling platformer with tight combat moves and glorious 16-bit graphics. The basic attacks are pretty limited but the selectable abilities add a nice bit of variety. Bosses are challenging, but doable.I'm having a good time with this game and would recommend it to fans of sidescrolling platform games.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: is an exceptionally fun, classically difficult 2-D side scroller with a consistently compelling 80's vibe that doesn't slip away throughout the entire game, as it influences the storyline, aesthetics, and soundtrack in equal measure.The game is relatively short, coming in at 2-3 hours to complete every level, and 8-9 hours to obtain all of the achievements (which requires a lot of restarting and perseverance, especially on tougher levels like the  .)Though this short length plays to the game's strength, as it's able to keep up the aforementioned 80's vibe, and present numerous distinct environments / stages to make your time investment worthwhile, with nothing overstaying it's welcome or feeling rehashed for the most part.If I had to knock the game for anything I'd argue that the skills you obtain from defeating bosses are not at all equal in their strength and usability, I personally used  and  to deal with anything that tried me on, even extending to  .Despite some balance gripes however, this game has an excellent hold on it's aesthetic style, while some of the bosses are eastern inspired robot warriors as you'd expect, others, especially the mini bosses, are heavily reminiscent of Gynoug (1991, Mega Drive). I wasn't expecting a dash of body horror whatsoever, and it really contributes to making  a unique experience, which throws so much diversity at you at a breakneck pace that, considering the playtime, it'd be a missed opportunity to not give it a shot.I'm no music expert, but I know when I like a soundtrack, and  uses it to retain immersion as much as possible, keeping you comfortably vigilant in Penrai. My favourite track  is Asura's Fleet (Act 1), I can see why Joymasher / The Arcade Crew chose to use it for the trailer, and trust me, playing the level that the track plays on takes the vibe to a whole new level, I love it, really a lightning in a bottle experience.Overall an excellent game, brimming with personality, goals to achieve, and a playtime that (almost) anyone can squeeze into their schedule, if you don't mind a little challenge and feel like being an acrobatic laser ninja for 8 hours, play  , you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: From Looks, to Gameplay, to Story, This Team GETS These GamesI cannot recommend these games enough. Blazing Chrome impressed me, and this one proves they understand the era of games they respect better than any other modern team I've seen. The graphics are perfect. Even the CRT filter looks exactly like the CRT I play my MIster on every week.Can't praise this team enough for what they're doing.  Even their story shows a grasp of modernizing 16 bit action better than anyone yet.  More than merely earning my financial support, they've earned my respect.My ONLY criticism so far is that the post-level cutscenes auto play, making it nearly impossible to not miss at least a little of what is said. They really really need an option to not move to the next text box without pressing the A button, or something.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel very proud, the people who worked on this game are of great excellence. _childDocuments_.review: As usual for Joymasher, the action is amazing and, just like with Blazing Chrome, the graphics and music set the tone perfectly. Dominic Ninmark is more at home on samples than on synths, like in Blazing Chrome, but the melodies themselves aren't quite as good as in that game. But my god the writing is so cringeworthy, especially the boss dialogue. Joymasher has never been good at writing dialogue between enemies, but they appeared to recognize this and dial it back for Blazing Chrome. One minor gameplay gripe too: a ranking system doesn't work great when items stay collected when you quit and restart a stage. I'm still recommending this because the player's moveset is practically perfect and the obstacles you'll face are quite varied and don't waste your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good videogame. In the presentation (visual/music/sounds/overall aesthetics) department it's a bang for its buck ten times over. For game structure - it's like a megaman, in that you have a stage select and each boss grants you unique weapon. All bosses have a weakness, but that weakness being they're all weak to the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing. A strong weapon's damage output is strong to everything :3So if you wish to play that way - you can absolutely equip yourself in a manner that pretty much guarantees that you'll complete the game.And after game is beaten - you can play more for steam achievements. No-damage taken is fun and actually made me plan and use different weapons. It's great.Wishlist:Hey devs, please add some sort of ingame rank/marker for beating each stage no-damage taken. I want some sort of marker/motivation for the effort.Also I feel like level design is under-explored. There's a section with lasers and elevator, I thought I'd need to do some timing wall jumps to pass, but all it amounted was just walking to a right position at a right time. Please do more interesting stuff with stage elements.Finally, seems that ranks don't matter. Was expecting that I'd unlock something if I got S rank on all stages, but it but it didn't do anything (besides steam achievement). Would be nice if it did. Ranking rework to consider things other than time it took to beat the stage would be great too (equipped chips, specials used, lives spent..).
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: As many have already mentioned, Vengeful Guardian Moonrider is an aciton platformer that is heavily inspired by the Shinobi series. It lets you play stages in any order with the exception of the first and last few. Each boss has a unique weapon you can use on later levels, the same as the Megaman titles. Each stage has hidden abilities you can find to improve yourself or make the game harder. It's not the most difficult game in the world, but the stages are all well designed and interesting, boss battles are more hit or miss, but not bad overall. I liked the fact that there was a variety of mini-bosses throughout each stage.It has some great art and music, although writing was poor and overall messy and incoherent. Sometimes text goes off screen before you can even read it. Story isn't anything to write home about either. It has a generic dystopian setting with a decent cast of enemies, but at the end of the day, somewhat forgettable.I think it's a great retro style platformer, but it doesn't really do anything you haven't seen before. I expected this going in, so I'm perfectly happy with what I got. I think what stands out the most was the level design. Some stages were really expertly crafted and I can't wait to see what JoyMasher does in the future. Great start to indie gaming in 2023!
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun. As everyone says, it does have NInja Gaiden, Super Metroid, Mega Man X vibes. I can't say it'll be an experience that I'll say is a GOAT, because it's not. But if you have some money on hand and want to burn about 2 hours of your time, go for it.One thing the devs could fix. The dash is finicky on whether it works or not. I could get it to work about 85% of the time, but it could use an improvement.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

I loved the art, the gameplay, the concept, the story, the cutscenes, the upgrades, the unique bosses with their voices in Japanese, the upgrades and the soundtrack, it's chilling.Since Oniken I'm always thinking about how their new games will be. You make us proud here in Brazil!

_childDocuments_.review: I played this demo back in the Fall of 2022, was anticipating a Fall release only to find out it wouldn't come out until January 2023. Well, it was certainly worth the wait. As an avid fan of old-school SEGA Genesis/MegaDrive games, like Shinobi which this game feels right on par with, this game is phenomenal. The Soundtrack is absolutely amazing, it was the first thing that pulled me into the game, when I heard the high-energy trailer track (Track 21 - Asura's Fleet Act 1), I knew this game was exactly what I wanted. Dominic Ninmark is a name I'm familiar with from his YouTube remixes, and his original work on this game does not disappoint. I'm eagerly anticipating Gravity Circuit, a Mega Man X style indie that'll release this year, his music on that is just as good. Highly recommend checking out his other works. Graphics and art style are amazing, but one thing in particular had me joyous with how good it was. The CRT filter they used in the game I personally think is phenomenal. Feels pretty close to how playing on an old CRT felt, playing through Shinobi, this game with the CRT filter is a must play. Plus it adds a reason to play through the game again, one time without the filter, and onetime with. It really does well emulating all the tricks older game devs/artists used to "smooth out" pixel art and make it seem almost hand drawn. Absolutely phenomenal work. The mechanics and controls feel right at home, in fact, sometimes they're just as frustraiting as the old Shinobi games! (In a good way! It's the intentional learning curve these games present to you, once you master it, they feel so satisfying) -Vehicle stages are alright. They're cool the first time, but there's a lot of "down time" where you're not really doing anything and it could be shaved off. Boss fight feels a bit too long. -Difficulty Balancing: Sometimes the difficulty curve feels reasonable, other time it feels like "how the hell am I supposed to kill this enemy/boss without getting hit?". It's not so much a massive issue as it is an annoyance that you have to work around. Other than that, I'd say some of the abilities/weapons are either overtuned or undertuned. -The voice acting. Before each boss battle, while a neat nod, you're stuck there for a good 5 seconds waiting for the voicelines of the boss to end. EACH. TIME. That's right, if you die, you must do it again, and again. Sure, "git gud" but also, I would much rather have it MMX style, where it just skips the whole dialogue/intro to the boss sequence and throws you right back into the fight to try again. The Voice Acting also just feels like it's too long in general. Especially since you can't skip it. You're forced to listen to it. This has to be my biggest "immersion breaker". This will also easily add 5 seconds per boss onto every speed run. Maybe they'll add a skip option in a patch, it'd be really nice to have that feature.-Broken English: This can obviously be fixed later on, and it's not like detrimental to the point that you don't understand anything, but there are some grammatical errors and typos here and there. Hopefully they get those sorted out with a couple of patches!All said and done, if you enjoy old-school side scrolling Shinobi-styled games, this is a must buy. If you enjoy banging sound tracks, this is a must listen. Play the game, you won' regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Been lookin forward to this since the demo. Love the aesthetic, gameplay, and soundtrack. Story is about what you expect but it's still does it's job. I'd say it clocks in at about 3 hours which I expected as well. Super fun, especially if you miss games like Ninja Gaiden and the like. The chip system is great though the one that lets you change colors I feel like should be more a post game unlock? Seems silly to have it take up a slot since it's cosmetic from what I could tell. I do agree with some complaints that it does seem to difficulty spike at times but I adjusted rather quickly. Though I do think the option to remove double tap to sprint would be a nice QoL feature. Overall 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: is like a snes game, and that carries a few cons against it but overall i liked it a lot, is a very straight forward game, you select a stage, kill the boss and get a new weapon, other than that you can find chips to equip hidden in the stages, they aren't super hidden and the game isn't very hard, it stands at a very comfortable level of challenge, along with the sprite art and the music is a very cozy game that you can replay and beat in a siting. Talking about more specific things, some of the upgrades and weapons are way too good, you can get hp and mp refills with every enemy you kill and that can make the stages a bit trivial, thankfully this doesn't work in bosses since there is no enemies to refill you there. There is also some part in the stages where things just jump at you but since the game is very forgiving with health is never a problem.while is a bit shallow in mechanics for the price i would 100% recommend it for people who like sidescrollers, is pretty fast paced and the level design is very fun, as well as some of the bosses, overall is a short sweet game.

You can brute force the bosses, which isn't ideal, but I don't find it to detract from the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good one.  I always get frustrated with enemy placement but they are placed strategically to deal damage and make it harder to avoid.  This reminds me of the classic retro games that frustrate you but not in a bad way.  It's challenging enough and you want to keep going to get through it.  Good one this.  Get it, support indie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider

_childDocuments_.review: A fun mix between Mega Man X and Strider. Controls are overall smooth and easy to grasp, but one minor issue I had was that I wish the sprint attack did not stop all your momentum and was instead a regular slash just to keep the pace up and minimise platforming mistakes. The upgrades are fun to play around with, but a lot of them are just variations of projectiles so I wish there was a little more variety. The presentation and soundtrack ooze that classic generation feel. Overall a fun way to spend an afternoon. It's not going to blow your mind, but it sets out to be a cool, fun experience and it nails it.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. The last boss lacks some flavor, like, the whole game is so damn beautiful and flashy, but the last boss doesn't have a nice final form with a big sprite or anything... _childDocuments_.review:
Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider is a side-scrolling action platformer that channels the golden age of classic 16-bit action games in a full-throttle quest for revenge.

REVENGE OF THE MOONRIDER

In the oppressed world of Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider, humanity finds an unlikely hero. After building an army of super soldiers as weapons of war, the authoritarians unwittingly seal their own fates by bringing online the ninja warrior known as Moonrider. Conceived as a tool to preserve the totalitarian state, the Moonrider instead rejects its intended purpose and wages a relentless battle for vengeance against its creators and fellow super soldiers.

GEAR UP AND PREPARE TO BATTLE YOUR CREATORS

The design of Vengeful Guardian: Moonrider puts the best classic action-game elements in the laser-precise sights of its starring ninja, ensuring snappy, responsive combat that’s supremely challenging.

Powerful modifier chips are hidden and guarded throughout the adventure, allowing you to customize the Moonrider’s fighting style while gaining killer advantages and abilities.

name: Haunted House
detailed_description: Chills and stealthy thrills abound In Haunted House, a reimagining of the classic Atari adventure! Players take control of Lyn Graves, the precocious niece of legendary treasure hunter Zachary Graves. Lyn visits her uncle’s mansion with her closest compatriots, only to find the house overrun with ghouls and monsters who quickly grab and spirit away her friends. In order to free her uncle and her friends, and capture all the supernatural foes, Lyn must find the shattered pieces of a magical urn and put them back together. Through procedurally generated room layouts, shifting walls, unpredictable enemy placements, and unique ghostly encounters, Lyn must creep, sneak, and dash her way through hordes of ghouls and eerie ectoplasms in order to locate her friends and uncle. Each urn shard is fiercely guarded by a bone-chilling boss — with 3D isometric stealth gameplay, Lyn must think on her feet to conquer each challenge. When she gets knocked out by a shadowy specter, she winds up back at the Haunted House’s entrance and must face an entirely new floor layout and enemy placement, ensuring each run is unique. Features Resurrected Roguelite: Haunted House doubles down on stealth and mystifying challenges while adding roguelite elements, ensuring no two runs are the same. All-Ages Thrill Ride: The whimsical, cartoonish art style only thinly veils the chills and thrills in Haunted House! Expertly riding the line between goofy and spooky, Haunted House features primarily stealth-based gameplay and light combat sequences. Unlockable Characters: As Lyn explores the Haunted House, she’ll free her trapped friends, who become playable characters you can use to dive deeper into the mansion. Each friend possesses different stats, so depending on who you explore the mansion with, it’ll be a new experience! Atari Easter Eggs: The game is full of collectibles and lore based on the original Haunted House and other classic favorites from Atari’s golden age. Sneaky Shivers: With combat de-emphasized, players must focus on stealth movement and solving challenges unseen in the shadows, along with utilizing the arsenal of traps and items at their disposal to distract the ghoulies hunting Lyn. Lyn must collect gems to power up the skills and perks that make her that much stronger during the next trip through the mansion’s labyrinth.

name: Amnesia: The Bunker
detailed_description: HALLOWEEN UPDATE This very special update brings a bunch of NEW FEATURES to Amnesia: The Bunker, really switching up the gameplay, adding new horrors and heaps of replay value. The new update comes with TWO completely new game modes: Shell Shock Mode: For the most Hardcore experience - a true test of guts. Custom Mode: Customize your experience with 30+ settings and parameters. Some of the new FEATURES available in the new modes are: New stalker behaviors that increases unpredictability A sublevel fuse system Hardcore version of the health system Randomized corpses and dog tags Randomized locker locations Revolver located in one of the lockers and not available from start New Training Grounds level for you to practice your skills Saving your progress costs fuel ...and much more! Note: Most of these are New Game+ features and are only accessible by completing the game on any difficulty once. About the Game Amnesia: The Bunker is a first-person horror game from the makers of SOMA and Amnesia. Left all alone in a desolate WW1 bunker with only one bullet remaining in the barrel, it’s up to you to face the oppressing terrors in the dark. Keep the lights on at all costs, persevere, and make your way out alive. A truly intense horror experience. RISING TENSION Immerse yourself in the multiple ways of tackling survival. In the shoes of the French soldier Henri Clément, you are armed with a revolver gun, a noisy dynamo flashlight, and other scarce supplies to scavenge and craft along the way. With randomization and unpredictable behavior, no play-through is the same. Hunted by an ever-present threat reacting to your every move and sound, you must adapt your play-style to face hell. Every decision will change the outcome of how the game responds. Actions bear consequences. ESCAPING THE NIGHTMARE Solve things your own way in a semi-open world. You must explore and experiment to make your way out. Figure out what’s going on down here - what has happened to the other soldiers? Where have all the officers gone? What diabolical nightmare lurks underneath this hellscape? Unravel the mysteries of the Bunker and get to know the nooks and crannies of this cruel sandbox to up your odds of survival. FEATURES Dynamic and ever-present monster that reacts to player actions. Constant tension - Time is not on your side. Tactile and physics based interactions with the world. Scavenge for resources and craft tools to aid your survival. Multiple solutions to problem solving in a non-linear open world.

You must explore and experiment to make your way out. Figure out what’s going on down here - what has happened to the other soldiers? Where have all the officers gone? What diabolical nightmare lurks underneath this hellscape? Unravel the mysteries of the Bunker and get to know the nooks and crannies of this cruel sandbox to up your odds of survival. FEATURES Dynamic and ever-present monster that reacts to player actions. Constant tension - Time is not on your side. Tactile and physics based interactions with the world. Scavenge for resources and craft tools to aid your survival. Multiple solutions to problem solving in a non-linear open world.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Dark Descent shook up the horror game scene 13 years ago, and Amnesia: Rebirth in 2020 seemed to sow the seeds of the story it planted for a chilling and climactic finale. So, Amnesia: The Bunker, a smaller and more independent chapter, did its job in getting me excited about this spooky franchise again. Even though many stealth and exploration basics remained the same from when I woke up as Daniel over a decade ago, this dark cat-and-mouse thriller proves you can teach an old infernal beast some new tricks.The Amnesia series by Frictional Games has three main features shared across all its games: firstly, all protagonists suffer from amnesia (hence the series name), needing to explore their surroundings and unravel what happened and how they're involved. Secondly, it's all in first-person style with a heavy focus on object interaction and puzzle-solving. Thirdly, the protagonist's fragility, unable to face monsters and having to hide until the danger passes. There's also a fourth feature, unfortunately not in all their games, which, for me, was the main reason for the success of their first game, Amnesia: The Dark Descent – the sanity meter, deteriorating when you stay in the dark, look directly at monsters or supernatural events, and when attacked. Only The Dark Descent and Amnesia: Rebirth, The Bunker's predecessor, use the sanity system, creating a real atmosphere of terror and urgency.So, let me define the game based on these features. Amnesia: The Bunker has a protagonist who's lost their memory. It's entirely focused on puzzle-solving. It has a fragile protagonist, but this time they can defend themselves, though not defeat monsters. And it lacks a sanity system, compensating with an excellent use of light and darkness systems, sounds, and silence. The terror the game provides is what makes it so good, on par with the quality of The Dark Descent and Rebirth, or even greater, I dare say.I can't say Amnesia is still an innovative horror franchise as it once was. The grander story it was building has unfolded with Rebirth. But Amnesia: The Bunker proves that smaller anthology-style episodes within its universe can still bring tension and scares. Frictional's bag of tricks is far from empty when it comes to making our hearts race and making us carefully ponder how to use the limited tools available. It's not a must-play experience, but as an Amnesia fan, it definitely satisfied my appetite for some gut-churning horror and a melancholic, dark narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: The Bunker takes a significantly more focused approach to gameplay, rather than the storytelling that Frictional Games has been famous for in their previous works. The primary antagonist in the game, called the "Stalker" has a dynamic kind of AI that is the subject of its well-deserved comparisons to Alien: Isolation's Xenomorph antagonists; It is a constant threat to you, and it reacts dynamically to your presence, stalking and hunting the player whenever they cause enough commotion. The more significant differences between them are manifested in the way the Stalker interacts with the world itself, and it can be a lot of fun trying to learn how it works and what to do in order to increase your chances of survival.It's hard to put into words how exceptionally well Frictional's recent Halloween update increased the replayability of The Bunker, giving the player the ability to significantly determine what their gameplay experience is going to be like. Some controls the player has can affect the AI directly, increasing/decreasing the Stalker's aggressiveness, presence, reactivity and overall predictability. Other controls affect the world more generically like the amount of resources that are spread out through the bunker, the amount of ammo present in the game, the rate in which the generator burns through fuel, the amount of time each crafted torch can last, and the length of time your flashlight lasts when you wind the thing up. I consider The Bunker to be essentially identical in quality to SOMA and Amnesia: The Dark Descent, despite the very different elements that each game emphasized. In terms of immersion and gameplay, it's by far the best of the three with its expertly crafted oppressive environments and varied per-playthrough experiences. The story is comparitively simple (especially compared to SOMA), and it isn't something the game tries to bother you with too much while playing. A player who doesn't care about the story of The Bunker at all will be able to get through the game without any real additional trouble, but a player who gathers and reads all the notes and photos will get helpful information about the events leading up to the player's awakening in the Bunker and they'll also get some hints as to who the antagonists are and how they work (yes the Stalker isn't the only problem).Concluding, I love The Bunker, The Dark Descent and SOMA all, and each for different reasons; The Bunker for its astoundingly well-crafted gameplay, SOMA for its immersive story telling, and The Dark Descent for its excellent balance between the two. Personally I'd recommend getting all three, and I hope Frictional takes The Bunker and expands on it.

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one thing historians, artists, scholars and survivors ever agreed upon, is that World War 1 was as close as you can get to .   The trenches were a literal meat grinder that spared no expense or pity on thousands and thousands of soldiers, who’s sole refuge were the layered bunkers and barracks. And in one peculiar french bunker, you awaken after a catastrophic event, trapped inside by rubble, and you are not alone. From the outset, you have only three goals. Find TNT, a detonator, and get the hell out. What makes The Bunker such a great experience is not only its non-linear exploration, it’s the plethora of mechanics added to the formula that gives the player agency, power and at the same time, a constant source of stress and dread. Aside from your hub, you can’t save anywhere. Every step you take is a second wasted from the generator that powers the dim lights of the bunker, every move might cost your life, and one mistake is all you need to be ripped to shreds. You are at the mercy of your wits in a constant cat-and-mouse hunt, using what little tools you find to slowly progress. When it comes to pure, survival horror, this game won’t leave you unsatisfied. Despite the age and rather poor texture quality, Frictional’s engine still delivers an excellent atmosphere, thanks to impressive sound design and hauntingly effective use of lights and effects. The only real flaw is the short length (depending on your bravery), however given how stressful the game is, it might be a positive.To put it bluntly, if you hated A Machine for Pigs, didn’t care for Requiem, and are a junkie for adrenaline that The Dark Descent gave back then, this is for you. This was an excellent return to form for the developer, and I am thankful they pulled off such a great experiment.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The game IS woefully short, but I don't necessarily think that's a bad thing. There's good gameplay here, and the compact and tight experience gives the player a better opportunity to become intimately familiar with the bunker, the monster, and the tools available. That said, since replayability is touted as one of the main features of this game, I would have liked to see more than "codes and resources are randomized every playthrough!" in terms of incentive. The game wears its Resident Evil influences on its sleeve, so why not have some neat unlockables you can get for extra playthroughs or meeting certain criteria(like a No-Save playthrough)? There's definitely some missed opportunity there.Regardless, even if I only get 3-5 hours out of this game, I still feel it's worth the price. It's one of the most tense games I've ever played. Frictional has accomplished exactly what they set out to do with this-- no more, no less.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a mixed relationship with the game. I have played all previous Amnesia games and remember them fondly. Even Rebirth who some people didn't like, was one of my favorites, since it was something different, more of the world to explore. And a lot of the previous games had a more sci-fi element to it, which I really missed in The Bunker. There is a monster in a bunker, and that's the whole premise. I was expecting more puzzles and more things to discover, a lot of it is just a game of hide and seek. It's still a good horror game don't get me wrong, it has the scary element really dialed in, and in a sense it's more of a return to how the original Penumbra games, so I see what they were going for. Problem is also that on normal difficulty, the game can be quite annoying at times, because you only have one spot where you can manually save the game and you may have to re-do a lot of the game if you get it wrong. So if you don't want the annoyance try the easier difficulty, since you can't change it later.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the gameplay of this one. The first Amnesia game to focus on the monster encounter and succeed. All the attempts before in the series felt cheap or scuffed. Not this one. There is clear inspiration from Alien Isolation and it couldn't be more of a love letter, I'd say. TLDR; great game for a fair price.First off, I highly recommend the hard mode. I started with normal, and the AI felt quite manipulable and left me alone for the most part. If you're playing for the story (which I have mixed opinions about expressed later) Normal might be the way to go. After my first play-through, I tried hard mode... and the difference is ridiculous. It feels like your being hunted and you constantly need to be on your toes and thinking about if you have an alternative way out of any room you enter. While in my first playthrough the beast didn't appear till I made a very loud noise (an explosive), on hard he immediately started to prowl. I was genuinely surprised when he came out of his hole unprompted.The story is neat to unravel and I love the setting and atmosphere, though the story feels a tad incomplete. Just when it seems like you're about to have that classic "amnesia reveal", it ends. Honestly kind of disappointed. Its also hard to keep track of the characters. A journal log of all the crew would be nice. You can sort the notes you collect by name, but not everyone wrote notes and its hard to remember people's rank or occupation. The dog tags also only are recorded if they have codes on them. Some sort of group photo of all the soldiers or a log like Obra Din would have been MUCH appreciated. The final act was... underwhelming. I will elaborate on that in spoilers...Spoiler: But minus the final act, I really enjoyed my time with this. I was pleasantly surprised after my first play-through when i was told that elements are randomly placed. That is a fun way to keep the game re-playable, especially to replay on hard where the game changes so much. Whenever I discovered something I didn't know I could do, it felt truly riveting and is informing my next play through. HIGHLY Recommended. A must play for anyone who's looking for a new "indie"-feeling horror survival. Frictional Games? More of this. More IN this. Add some more content. The game is great and needs a proper ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst being a huge follower of Frictional Games, Amnesia the Bunker did not disappoint. This entry is by far one of the most immersive and re playable experience yet. The atmosphere and bunker setting brings me straight back to their first game Penumbra: Overture which has always been one of my most favourite of Frictional Games.Amnesia: The Bunker is easily one of the most stressful horror games I have ever played which left me on edge throughout the entire game. Whilst required to keep the generator going at all costs, I have never been so afraid of a pocket watch before as the final count down reaches its last ticks before lights out.Whilst not being a huge fan of Frictional's previous installment Rebirth, Amnesia: The Bunker has won back the passion I had since The Dark Decent and is not afraid to experiment with new and risky gameplay elements such as providing you with weapons and grenades etc. Upon completion, I am looking forward to experience this wonderful game a second time in regards to the randomization of each play-through.Overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a brilliant horror experience and the WW1 backdrop is a unique setting that horror games need to explore more often.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Frictional Games are veterans when it comes to survival horror and so they know how to make a great game and Amnesia: The Bunker is no exception. They have consistently been innovating and putting out masterpieces like Soma, Penumbra and The Dark Descent. The Bunker was the only game in 2023 I was actually hyped for and, once again, Frictional delivered. In my opinion they have created the scariest and most terrifying horror game yet.This game freaked me out to the point I almost didn’t want to continue anymore. Let's begin with the fact the monster's behavior is entirely procedural, barely scripted and it follows you around for the entirety of the game. This made the monster very unpredictable and made the game so much scarier. Not the mention the absolutely awful and PTSD-inducing sound the monster would make when moving inside the walls. The monster's behavior is very different from all previous Frictional titles. Then there’s the hopelessness of being trapped inside a claustrophobic and desolate bunker in the middle of a ww1 battlefield, surrounded by the enemy. Everything felt authentic: the environment, the soldiers, the items, the acting etc. - this game really conveys the horrors of ww1. The amazing sound design also added to the immersion and, once again, Mikko Tarmia's soundtracks were phenomenal. I also like how some elements of the soundtrack reminded me of the Penumbra series soundtrack, as they shared a similar vibe.The game introduces several new mechanics, such as the generator, guns, grenades, inventory management and improves on older ones like crafting and stealth. The generator mechanic, with limited fuel, adds an extra level of stress as you are constrained by time. Planning your movements and objectives before leaving the administration office with the generator becomes crucial. Despite being armed, you are far from invincible, as the weapons only serve as a last resort with limited ammo. I must mention that the gun animations were exceptionally good for a horror game, surpassing even some modern-day FPS games. I also really liked the limited inventory space, forcing careful item management and decision-making when picking up items.There are so many more positive things I could mention about this game, but that would make this review a four-page-long essay... In conclusion, this game is a horror masterpiece!

_childDocuments_.review: The only Amnesia game I enjoyed. It does a great job with atmosphere, immersion, and scratches my itch for survival resource management. I have played all Amnesia games except for Machine for Pigs, and this is the only one I thought was worth my time. It did get a little boring during my final 2 hours because I had fully figured out the monster and was sprinting around the bunker even in the dark without a care in the world, but the beginning portion up unti about 80% of the way through is solid.Definitely recommend if you liked Alien Isolation, or enjoy games with resource management and immersion like Metro.The story was a little lacking and frankly very predictable. While graphically it does look dated, I found it actually helped make the game feel more gritty and atmospheric. I also liked being able to have multiple tools to deal with problems (locked doors, the monster, etc.) rather than having puzzles that were hit or miss (mostly miss) like Amnesia Dark Descent, or mindless walking where nothing happens the entire game like Amnesia Rebirth.I think this is a fairly accessible game to beginners to the survival-horror genre as well. I played on Normal and felt that the game was fairly easy, though I consider myself to be good at resource management and survival games. There are two difficulties below this, and New Game+ adds a lot of new things for when you become more adept with the game, or are a skilled gamer looking for a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot believe i'm saying this, but Frictional has let me down. People say Bunker is better than Rebirth? I say even Machine for Pigs is better than Bunker.The first victim is the very atmosphere.Remember wandering through dark corridors, without any idea of when the horror would arrive next? That perfect mix of both scripted and random encounters? They threw all that away, took the easy way and entrusted the narration to an ai-driven monster. Alas, chatgpt this is not.Now you know EXACTLY when the monster will arrive, which is either at regular intervals or when you make noise, with just a couple scripted appearances. Whatever the case, it will, unlike past enemies, patrol the area for AN ETERNITY, to the point that it tempts you to do out-of-game stuff, like cleaning the desk, petting the Cat, making a sandwich, cleaning the Fish tank, while your character sits in a closet.Then it will FINALLY go back in his tunnels... only to often immediately come back out and inflict you the same ordeal, sometimes more than once. I have rarely been this productive while playing a videogame. My desk is like crazy clean now.Oh, you can shoot it? Yeah, it takes like three bullets if you want it to go away (but it'll come back of course). And you almost never have that many in game. This isn't like alien isolation, where you have a reasonable amount of flamethrower fuel but dread the idea of running out. In The Bunker, you just don't use them against the beast because you'll be using any ammo you might see for a long time, for a rather modest payoff. Bullets that you could use to blast open locks for example. It almost makes you feel like, if you're spotted and can't get out, it might be better to die than to waste the bullets then possibly die anyway. And there goes the immersion.Speaking about writing: Bunker sees a massive drop in quality, substance and volume. There is next to no plot, the notes are everywhere and dreadfully unsubtle, and the protagonist is almost cardboard compared to Daniel or Simon, or Tasi, or even freakin' Mandus. There are no memorable characters, or lines, or character interactions whatsoever....And when you consider the effort they put in past endings, some of the moral, sentimental and philosophical choices you had to go through, what they did with the Bunker endings is possibly the worst offender. I'll leave it at that.Lastly, a sheer drop is also seen in game scale and structure: past titles were grand adventures that saw you cover quite the distance between point A and B. They had in common the presence of several hubs and a reasonable amount of backtracking, but all of that flew organically. Moving from one hub to another was a huge deal, often full of terrifying trials.Now? They completely took away the adventure: the masterfully narrated journey that made you feel like you were playing a novel in videogame form. There is a single hub now, nothing is story-driven, and the amount of backtracking is beyond insane.This isn't Amnesia. It's a poor man's alien isolation set in the Amnesia universe. It's a pre-cooked meal with artificially generated Amnesia flavor, from a company that used to be gourmet-level. I don't know who is running Frictional now, but they just nuked their own genre.Is this game good as a horror for the average gamer? Yes, it can scare. But as an Amnesia game, as an Amnesia fan, it is just painful.Bold new direction my a**hole.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very soft no. Honestly, this game is just not even scary. When you hear the monster snarl you don't even bat an eye.That leads me to my main issue with this game- the AI of the monster is poorly designed. The bleeding mechanic doesn't seem to even work. I just shouldn't have to coax out a monster just to have some fun to break the monotony of running back and forth.If you like achievement hunting this game has some fun for that here. But the librarian achievement is currently bugged and for whatever reason I didn't even get the achievement for beating the game so that's cool! Pls fix!!!
