_childDocuments_.review: Even though the game looked great at first and I was enjoying every minute, all the excitement and joy disappeared once I realized it's really just one big area and the player is supposed to go out, find a thing or two and go back to save the game.The idea of having two options - going there with lights on and off, which affects the monster, is great. But the whole game is so shallow and weird that it can't work as a standalone Amnesia game. It would be great as a mod or a DLC but this is a huge disappointment.I also managed to hit a point where I'm unable to progress without going through frustrating moments. Every possible way to destroy a door includes bringing a barrel from a remote location and the monster gets me sooner or later anyway. That also means that any possible way to be scared of the monster was annihilated byt the fear of losing progress.After several hours, the game is just not interesting anymore. It feels like "scavenge survival" mode in L4D2 - fun for a while but nothing you would buy a whole game for. I had no idea that one day I'll look back at Rebirth saying "this at least kinda felt like an Amnesia game" and I even enjoyed A Machine For Pigs so much more than Bunker. I have no idea what happened to a studio that's behind such masterpieces like SOMA and The Dark Descent but I'm not looking forward to anything from FG anymore unless it's a new Penumbra or something like that. The reason is that they seem to be a different company than what they used to be, not just because the games are different but because they don't seem to care about their community (platform / modding support) enough anymore.After all these years, remembering the old 2010 times playing Penumbra and TDD so extremely excited, here I come to be so disappointed by an Amnesia game I'm not even interested enough to finish. Another dissapointment comes from the fact that FG just threw all their Linux community overboard, after ~16 years, with no explanation. Sure, it works in Proton. Kinda. But that's not the point.I'll always remember TDD and SOMA as the best FG times. But it's probably time to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is a thoroughly impressive addition to the survival horror genre. Frictional have successfully integrated survival horror staples with their iconic world, lore, and monster horror design. The stalker is an excellent implementation of the unkillable monster antagonist in the vein of the Necromorph from Alien Isolation and Mr. X/Nemesis from Resident Evil. The generator mechanic is a fresh and inspired addition that turns the bunker into a dynamic, unpredictable environment that can change its tone at a moments notice. Randomized resource locations, traps, rats, locker codes, and customizable difficulty options mean the bunker can be revisited multiple times and remain uncomfortable and unfamiliar. What more can I say, other than that The Bunker is an incredibly complete survival horror package.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic horror game overall!  The setting of a World War I bunker is very well crafted and the monster is terrifying.  Gameplay is also great and gets more and more interesting as the game progresses (and you get new items).  The game is capped at 60 FPS due to physics engine limitations but I personally didn't notice it at all (and I frequently play other games at 120+ FPS).My only suggestion would be for the map to be at least somewhat procedurally generated (like SCP Containment Breach), which would help with the replayability greatly.  I know that was a major focus of this game due to its shorter length, but I still don't think randomizing items makes it that replayable.  However, overall, this will easily be one of the best horror games of 2023, and it's well worth the $25.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The BunkerNO SPOILERS (Just the basics)To preface the review; I have played all of the previous Amnesia games, so keep that in mind. I love Horror games and specifically Survival Horror games.Firstly this game differs from the past entries because it is by all accounts the most 'Survival Horror' this series has ever been. Preceding titles were more inclined to be what most people refer to as just 'Horror' or in some cases 'Horror walking simulators'. The story and atmosphere were definitely at the forefront, with a hint of survival mechanics included to varying degree.This game has more in common with classic games of the Survival Horror genre, like Resident Evil. You have a safe room, item chests, item management, crafting, puzzle Solving etc... all of which are hallmarks of the style. Their is also weaponry which you can use to fend for yourself, however they are mostly used for deterrence; you cannot kill the creature that stalks you. Make no mistake, this is not an action game.Stealth is very important. Visibility and noise are critical to your life so be careful. If you're discovered you'll need to run and hide. The beast that pursues you is cunning so you'll need to be smart about how you play the game.      More so than ever time is of the essence. A generator is used to light the bunker you're in, this is vital, because the monster hunts primarily in the darkness. The fuel depletes quickly over time, so you need to find more as you travel throughout the structure. This could possibly discourage players, although I quite liked it. Urgency is a product of any good horror game in my opinion.Above all, player initiative and self-reliance are probably the most important factors of this new entry in the Amnesia series. I loved all of the new changes to the formula. If this is a sign of things to come for the franchise, then I'm happy.A stressful, scary, inspired survival horror game.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: After the previous title, Amnesia: Rebirth, my opinion was that Frictional needed to innovate on gameplay.  While that game had a great setting and solid story, we were still working on the same mechanics from the Penumbra games that were now over ten years old.  This refers to gameplay focused on crouch-slinking around environments and all the monsters are coincidentally blind because their AI is so simplistic.  It also includes the tired genre of being completely unarmed against threats.  It was time to give the player some weapons and gadgets to expand the range of possible situations.  I am pleased to say Frictional has made major strides in both departments with Bunker.Monster AI has been improved, mostly in that it is much more aggressive in its awareness and pursuit of the player.  The monster can also do more interesting things like set ambushes for the player and react to light and sound in interesting ways.There is a plethora of new gadgets that the player must juggle in a limited inventory.  That’s right, inventory management is BACK and it’s great.  This includes guns, incendiary devices, noise-makers, and first aid.  This encourages the player to carefully consider their strategy, which leads to some great drama as the player weighs which items to take.  I LOVE the sound design of these gadgets.  For example, the gun is so loud and piercing and leaves your ears ringing.  Torches burn and crackle atmospherically.  The flashlight rattles rhythmically, always giving away your position.  Bunker also leans into one of the aspects of The Dark Descent’s design in that it centers around a “hub-area”.  The hub is a central area the player can plan, resupply, and regroup then go to a variety of areas to complete objectives in any order.  Bunker actually improves on this in that certain areas of this open-world can later be revisited when you get tools to open previously inaccessible areas.  Bunker also has a system of randomization to add replay value.As for the story, I won’t say too much but it was a little more bare-bones than I was expecting.  However, Bunker is able to make up for it by being a gameplay-focused experience.Overall this was a GREAT step in the right direction for Frictional and definitely worth a buy.  I had a lot of fun progressing.  It takes a little getting used to but once you start rolling its very addictive to progress.  I am looking forward to seeing how they take what they have built in terms of production design, AI, and gameplay and applying it to their next title.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic little horror game. Has some of the best sound design I've experienced for a horror game this decade. The immersive sim and randomly generated elements give this game so much replayability. After years of a dry horror scene being led by people who hate getting scared, The Bunker is a fresh take on survival horror that deserves praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A really well designed survival horror experience build on several complimentary systems. First off, there's the beast, constantly stalking you from within the bunker walls. Make too much noise and it emerges, at which point you will have to ward it off (with your limited resources) or hide. Hiding isn't ideal either as it wastes precious time. The beast will freely hunt in the dark, which is why you will want to keep the bunker generator working at all times. Of course, that too runs off limited fuel. To top it off, you have to deal with limited inventory space. Do you run to save time and generator fuel? Do you pick up the extra fuel canister or the grenade? Do you break down the door (making a ton of noise) or look for another way? Do you spend resources burning a corpse to prevent rats from coming and blocking your path? The whole game through is filled with decisions like that and it constantly makes you feel like you're juuuust barely scraping by on what you can find.Plays like a mix of the original Resident Evil, Alien Isolation and the first Amnesia. As such, if you enjoyed those games, I highly recommend this one.

I guess I thought of the wrong thing that would probably work...
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah it's good. Very scary. The looting aspect and continuous returning to a "homebase" made it always exciting, and I liked the lack of guidance you receive. It makes it feel as though you survived an encounter or found a key item because YOU are the skilled player! It also feels very optimised. My low rig survived at decent settings while streaming, so that's another plus. There's also workshop potential. Lots of replay value.Things I didn't like:The ending.Difficulty. Hard isn't hard enough once you realise how to manage fuel and just walk everywhere (though I am an amnesia veteran - so rad - so maybe my experience carried), although the dev team plans to add an "shellshocked" mode soon, so maybe this will be fixed.The ending's boss battle. This game is definitely attempting to uproot the traditional way horror games work. To me, it proved that the mechanics of horror can be altered and still achieve the same effect of horror. Although the story doesn't end in a satisfying way, the concept is there, and I support it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's strange how this studio peaked so hard with The Dark Decent and Soma, understanding that less is more as far as the monster appearances go. It's scary for like the first minute, and then just annoying, with the monster hunting you down more or less constantly while you're trying to solve the puzzles. no time to settle in the apprehension that something might attack you. You already know it will, so it just becomes about developing speed run strats and save scumming to manage your resources, at which point, any environmental storytelling that might be present goes out the window. I gave this game a chance to win me back to this studio after Rebirth, and it failed. Dark Decent and Soma are two of the greatest games ever made, and I just don't understand how the same people who put so much thought and care into making a game genuinely terrifying could now so consistently pump out such mediocrity. Very disappointed. I'm done with them.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. This is such an amazing game that even after reaching its finale, the game continues to occupy a significant part of my thoughts. The game so emotionally captures you in the process of passing it, you live with the game. Details in small things. For example: "You hear the monster walking, you hide in the closet and for a minute you hear how he breathes next to you. He destroys the boxes standing next to you, making you more terrified. You are waiting for the moment when he leaves. Meanwhile, a soundtrack with a dynamic heartbeat.The monster leaves and you quietly exit the closet.You take the first steps unsteadily and suddenly you hear the monster come back to you.You quickly run back to the closet and continue to wait for the attack to end.The growl of the monster is completely poisonous with you and the horror covers you . One minute.. Two minutes.. you are confident in the logic of the algorithms in the game and you are a little calm, sure that the monster will leave again. Suddenly the monster opens the closet door and kills you." How is it written in code? Just unbelieveble. It was so emotional. Thank you for the game to the entire development team and the whole team. This is one of the best horror games I have ever played. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a great horror game. The beast is very intelligent and it's a constant who outsmarts the other between you two. The noises it creates are also very nerve-racking. The encounters didn't feel scripted at any point whatsoever which is why it's so refreshing to play such horror game. The atmosphere is also what drew me to the game, a WW1 setting being trapped in a bunker and all of the areas are very distinct from one another. The story is simple and solid. Played on hard mode and finished in 6-7 hours total (in-game time was 5h). The game is not short in my opinion and well worth it. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: It's spooky season so let's kick it off with a bang.I was massively hyped for this game but didn't want to dive right in as I knew I wanted to save it for Halloween season, it was definitely worth the wait as this is an incredible horror game and has been one of my gaming highlights of this year.The amnesia games have always been quite nebula in their approach to lore and story, with later entries becoming more like walking sims with gameplay taking a backseat, sometimes it works like rebirth other times it's terrible like a machine for pigs. What bunker does it put gameplay upfront, so much so the game's subtitle is based on the star of the show which is the bunker itself rather than being something that will allude to the story. So is this just amnesia with guns? Well yes and no. You can think of this game as a mix between resident evil 7 and alien isolation whilst managing to be better than both of those games, it's short and sweet but has random elements to keep replays fresh and exciting, in other words the perfect recipe for a horror game. So let's talk gameplay. This is a massive departure form any of the other amnesia games, you are stuck in a bunker which is a semi open space in which you can freely explore, find key items and use the environment to your advantage. Yes you have guns but they are more tools than weapons. Ammo is scarce and they can be more useful in opening certain doors than actually fighting anything. This game really gave me og resi vibes. Whilst I wasn't particularly scared I was tense through my playthrough knowing a death could reset quite a bit of progress, what makes this worse is the ticking clock element of the generator that consumes gas as your explore, failing to keep this topped up will result in all the lights shutting off meaning you'll be alone in the dark with only a horrific monster for company. You don't want to crank your light either or really make any noise if you can help it for fear of alerting said monster to your presence.Story wise this is a slim offering, lore is present in the notes but soma this ain't, you won't find anything too deep here and honestly I don't mind that, it's nice to see frictional games emphasis gameplay for once and they still proved they are the best in the business when it comes to horror.Tense, scary and short in the best possible way, an absolute masterclass of the genre that I'll be replaying for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: it's great, scary, and has the most developed mechanics of any frictional games game yet. if you play amnesia for the story, dont expect to be wowed (i quite like the simple story myself) but gameplay-wise the tools this game gives you allow it to be super fun, while not necessarily sacrificing the power it has to be terrifying. though, i'd say my playthrough on normal mode allowed me to get away with a bit too much when it came to fighting back against the monster, as even though ammo and other resources seem scarce, there were hardly any encounters where i didn't have something that could scare it off. i haven't done a hard mode run yet, but i reckon if you're worried about the ability to fight back against the monster killing tension, you should probably run your playthrough on hard mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia The Dark Descent was the best amnesia game because it focused on both gameplay and story, Machine for Pigs undermined both of these aspects but it had at least a distinguishable identity. Rebirth lacked in gameplay but delivered in the story department, connecting it to the first game.The Bunker is the opposite of that, it focuses on the gameplay while diminishing the story, which is lacklustre. It is an Amnesia game and not one at the same time, very different from what we have had until that point. It is a full blown survival horror: resource management, stalker who is constantly hunting you and a set of tasks to complete.After a few playthroughs I warmed up to it though. The randomised elements after the first playthrough definitely help extending the fun, not to mention harder difficulty which I was not brave enough to try this time. And there is also a customisable difficulty with which you can mess if you want more experiences.I am intrigued what the next project of Frictional will be after this one, cuz when it comes to me, they can make many more Amnesia spin offs and I’ll make sure to give them a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Frictional games succeeds once more at bringing a scary as hell, immersive experience... only this time, you have to fight back (a little). Stealth is still key to surviving though, but you'll be equipped with a handgun, grenades and the loudest frigging flashlight on Earth to help defend yourself... or attract what lures in the bunker.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The best Amnesia experience since Dark Descent, The Bunker is truly a return to form for the series. I genuinely haven't been this scared by an Amnesia game in a while, and the way this new entry is designed makes the experience especially harrowing. Trapped underground in tight corridors and small rooms, a lone monster stalking you throughout, that can and will kill you the moment it finds you, and limited tools and inventory space to fend it off, it makes for a very stressful experience as you try to escape this hell. Overall, gameplay-wise, they take everything that made the original good and add more to it that just works for this game. Like the generator and save room system, where the majority of the map is built around a singular point that you will have to return to if you want to make this as easy as possible. Even then, fuel scattered about at random can make for challenging gameplay when the power inevitably blacks out. Besides the game, the story too is as compelling as the first in terms of regaining your memory and the setting it takes place in. The ending especially makes you wonder if you truly have escaped. But I won't say much more than that as this game has to be played, and for the price it is more than worth the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of the franchise, I must say that this game is a condensed version than what we're used to. It is pretty much devoid of story save for some mild beats and threads to connect, but what it lacks for in that aspect it makes up for with the horror experience. This game is designed to be finished within a few hours. I couldn't imagine it lasting over 5 hours. Resources are scarce and you must get out of your comfort zone to do anything. The most stress-inducing thing is the generator, which simply guzzles fuel and without it you're in extreme danger or sometimes not even allowed to progress. It's a pretty well laid-out game with decent level design and mechanics. I do wish there was more story like their previous works, but I can't judge it for what it wasn't meant to be. It's a quick and thrilling ride. I just hope you can handle the scares -- I was too stressed to even leave the saferoom my first time!

_childDocuments_.review: Just as with Rebirth, I discovered this game's release by accident, and bought it immediately. I am always excited by new projects from Frictional. I went in completely blind, and so I can say that this experience was entirely my own. So here are my thoughts:This installment of Amnesia is built around a very small play area that is packed with terror, atmosphere, and mechanical freedom and intrigue. Whereas with TDD, you had a whole castle to explore and would move from level to level through points of no return, the bunker setting has you returning to the same areas repeatedly with a safe room as your anchor. It's great concept and I think it was well executed.I read almost all the notes and collected all but one dog tag by the end, and I'm pleased with the story. I was able to put together what was happening.Amnesia is nothing without its monsters, so what do we have? Well, there are large, aggressive rats, and the stalker. There are also passive threats, such as tripwires rigged to various handhend explosives and utilities. Lets talk about how they all play together.The stalker is very noise sensitive, and in the enclosed bunker space, every pin drop can be heard. It makes for a tense atmosphere. Sometimes, there are scripted events to introduce you to new threats, but for the most part, the stalker only comes out when you make too much noise. This rewards a slower, more careful playstyle. Everything you interact with makes noise, especially your wind-up flashlight, which immediately introduces a nice compromise: create light at the cost of detection.In the darkness, the tripwires can be hard to spot. Some are lethal to you directly, and others are lethal to you because they attract the stalker. You can jump over them if timed right, but you cannot disarm them (well, maybe you could with the bolt cutters, but there were no more tripwires by the time I got them). The tripwires force you to pay attention to  where you'd walking. Carelessness will leave you worse for wear.The rats congregate at corpses which contain resources and dogtags which may have a code to unlock their corresponding locker in the storage room. You can kill the rats or scare them off. Get too close, and the swarm will attack and make a bunch of noise, which could draw out the stalker. Really neat mechanic. You are often provided tools to get the rats away, such as crafting a torch or a molotov. I didn't know I could make a torch until the end credits scoreboard.Oh yes, there is a scoreboard. I was confused by this. It seems out of place in an Amnesia game. This is supposed to be replayed. I don't think I will, though, any time soon, and here's why:This game was terrifying, but it was also suffocating. At first, when I knew nothing about the monster, every excursion sent my heart rate up. Because of the small map, the design makes these little explorations incredibly taxing. This draws things out. Ultimately, I reached a point where, to make progress, I had to stifle that fear by giving up and letting myself get killed. I saw the monster up close, saw how it killed, saw how it behaved, and then I wasn't scared of it anymore. I was then able to keep playing the game, now that the mystique was cleared.I didn't like doing this, honestly. it felt cheesy and I wish it weren't necessary for me to complete my objectives with cunning confidence.The greatest challenge offered by the game is fuel management and monster intelligence. The bunker has lights, but they are powered by a generator which you must refuel with resources found outside the saferoom. IF you run out of fuel, the lights go out. With the lights out, the monster will freely roam the bunker spaces and will be attracted by fewer significant player noises. The threshold for summoning the stalker is lower. This makes running out of fuel the biggest hurdle in the game. If you try to explore an area for the next objective in the dark, you will find yourself hiding for a long time. But hiding doesn't make it safe.The Bunker allows you to hide under tables, desks, and yes, wardrobes! Classic. But the beast is not so easily fooled. When searching a room, eventually, it will smash the table for tear open the wardrobe. Hiding is temporary and maybe be more dangerous than confrontation.So, how can you confront the beast? You are given many options. You have your revolver, whose bullet supply is very very scarce. There are grenades, which are best used to open doors (if there are no bricks around). Flares will distract the beast. Gas grenades are my favorite, since you can just put on a gas mask and watch all the rats and the stalker flee. Molotovs are good area denial. There's the shotgun, which you get in the endgame. You could lead the beast into a tripwire. The game almost encourages you to play aggressive instead of passively with the stalker. There are so few places to hide adequately. If you're not in the safe room, you could very well be killed.To finalize my thoughts, I think The Bunker is a really neat experiment and it's nice to see the developers trying something new. But exploring the space and dealing with the monster was not fun. It was slow and grueling and I was glad when it finally ended. I think it's still worth playing and experiencing for yourself, but I'm not eager to revisit this installment. Like Rebirth, the game introduces new mechanics to play around with in a classic Frictional style, and if you've been a fan over the years, you'll likely get something out of this experience. The game encourages creative problem-solving, so go on in and adapt. Just don't expect a fast pace.

_childDocuments_.review: An installment of Amnesia that I would consider as solid as The Dark Descent.The lack of human dialogue compared to previous games is a new but fresh addition.Originally feared that the gun mechanic might invalidate the monster's threat, very happy to see it used as more of a utility than an actual weapon.Movement feels very smooth, the animations of your hands are very well done.The beast also feels very fleshed out and life-like.Fuel management became the replacement to the Sanity system in previous entries.I'm not sure which one I prefer, Sanity had the benefit of being restored during gameplay, whereas Fuel must be found/farmed.Sanity caused me a lot more panic over Fuel however, because having a timer to know when it is about to decrease/fail is much more comforting than not. But I would understand if you think a timer would cause even greater terror seeing as it would be a point to stress out about.The greatest issue I had in the game was my very own brain,going as far as costing me to go fuel-less for the majority of the run and countlessly bitten by rodentsI understand, I was told that burning the bodies is the way to go. I was told numerous times.But I forgor. :skull:Very excited to see where custom stories will take it, keeping my hopes up for meme stories and serious ones.(also can someone tell me why the beast does not care for them? like are they friends???? does he enslave them to dig tunnels for him??????)

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILERS)Amnesia The Bunker ReviewStory 8/10I’m a huge fan of horror games and this is one of the best I have seen, an absolutely amazing game, but I have to say I love this way more than your usual horror games and the story on this game is pretty good for a horror game, how Lambert turns out to be the monster, and the way he reacts when you throw the rabbit doll at him he very clearly says “Blood on my hands…” while looking down at his hand and clenches the doll to his chest and says “Henri” then puts the doll away and returns back into one of his holes. Gameplay 10/10Keep in mind the game is pretty short it will only take 5-6 hours if you have a sense of where you are going it is pretty confusing at first but I got used to it quite quickly. Since the game is pretty short it is actually really good for replay ability. The map is pretty big and after you blow up the dynamite you basically get full access to every single area of the bunker, which gives a whole lot of time to get achievements.Horror 10/10 To me the horror is done so perfectly I love the atmosphere of the game and the monsters design is so horrifying. The monsters sound design in this is so good it makes the game so much more terrifying. _childDocuments_.review: I am going to be honest, I wanted to hate it.I didn't.The mechanics were pretty smooth for the most part. Graphics were smooth.The only hiccups were the loading areas in between segments of the bunker, but I can deal with that since it's a fairly short stutter and nothing major happens in those areas.Overall, Frictional Games did a very good job finally.  There was a decent amount of supplies to keep you going, but struggling at the same time.  Granted, I'd assume in a bunker during a war, there would be more guns and ammo to use, but hey, that's just my assumption.  Otherwise, they combined realism and horror with a good story. _childDocuments_.review: Terrific! Thought I was fairly immune to horror after playing so many, but The Bunker definitely reinvigorated some of that feeling as if you're new to them. It also does a remarkably good job of keeping the tension going throughout the entire playthrough unlike other games where it tends to fizzle out when you get too accustomed. They managed to strike a good balance between enemy encounters not being too frequent and not being too scarce and this helps prevent the player from both getting annoyed or bored. Everything related to immersion is also on point. The game never takes control away from you as cutscenes are limited to the short intro, intrusive gameplay elements are absent, and progression feels satisfying and rewarding as you don't get the rug pulled under you like in Rebirth.There are a couple things I think could've perhaps been done better, some of this is subjective and nitpicky and I understand you are a smaller studio and that this project wasn't meant to be as big or expansive as TDD or Rebirth so just take it as constructive feedback:1. Based on how the game was marketed, I expected the enemy to develop more dynamically as you play through in the sense that it's appearance would get somewhat altered, receives new mechanics, becomes more aggressive, or evolves countermeasures to deal with defensive actions from the player. It would've added another layer of dynamic tension so it's not just the same enemy type throughout. 2. A bit on the shorter side, I think I got around 5 and a half hours on my first playthrough and I explore fairly extensively and read notes. I wish there was more in general. 3. (Technical) When moving from one hub to another I sometimes had a slight stutter where the brightness would change then return to normal. Was a bit jarring and a smoother transition would be better. Don't think it's an issue on my end as my PC greatly exceeds the recommended specs, and I installed the game on an NVMe ssd. Overall, I'm very happy with my purchase and this game delivers brilliantly in tension, immersion and atmosphere. It's definitely the creepiest and most stressful experience I've had with a horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game captivated me with its unsettling atmosphere, evoking a strong sense of fear. One aspect that particularly stood out to me was the item management system, which added an extra layer of strategy. Additionally, being equipped with a weapon heightened the intensity and immersion of the experience.However, the game's non-linear structure presented challenges. It often left me torn between progressing and the urge to retreat to the safe room to save my progress. I died 40 times on the Normal difficulty, although I must admit that a lot of those deaths were due to my own recklessness. Waiting for the relentless antagonist to leave me alone in a closet for what seemed like an eternity tested my patience, only to find that the beast would occasionally discover me anyway.Looking ahead, I anticipate the next installment in the series. My hope is that it combines the item system and the combat mechanics with the seamless flow of Rebirth.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was really fun! I don't have too much to complain about. Guess I'll start with the strongest part of the game, being the atmosphere. Except for the final encounter, I was always on the edge with the beast. Even if I wasn't scared, he always left me pleading for mercy. Sadly his actual design is a bit of a let down, as nothing can compare to the horror the sound design produces in your head. Luckily you can never see him too well, so a good chunk of his design is left to your imagination.   The sound design is probably the best I've seen in any horror game. The whole point of the game is to stay quiet and avoid the monster, yet every footstep, every creak of the door, every flick of the revolver is loud and crisp, making you on the edge at all times. Constantly, the bunker is humming a deep, echoed silence, which makes the bunker feel so empty and lifeless. It's just you, Mr. Beastie Boy, and the rats. Whenever he came rumbling, my eyes widened. Even when you get to see brief glimpses of the outside world, your never relieved, as you immediately enter another hell. I've never had a physical reaction to gunshot in a game, but the way the bullets flew past me in the sniper's nest, put me in a state of shock. I instantly dodged the bullet in my chair, turning my head to it's direction.   Now let's chat about the Gameplay. On normal difficulty, it strikes a good difficulty balance. The Monster is very aggressive, but still gives you plenty of down time to recover. Throughout the play through, I was constantly worried about fuel and keeping the lights on, as when the lights go out, you can't see 2 feet in front of you, and any other source of light is either extremely limited or extremely loud. Not to mention, the gremlin in the walls can walk freely for much longer, as there's no light to scare him off. The game gives you many ways to fend him off though. Guns and explosives are satisfying to use, though normal grenades aren't very useful, as by the time they explode, le creature is already 2 feet in front of you and you missed your shot. While there are health kits, most of the time, he kills you instantly, so heath kits will mainly be used for rats and traps.  While the gameplay and atmosphere is fun, the story is put off to the side for this game, mostly hidden in notes scattered around the building and the surface story is very basic. This isn't a bad thing, as not every game need a complex and intriguing story, but compared to the previous titles, it's a bit of a let down. The last thing to mention is that the game is quite short. That's not an issue for me as I actually prefer shorter games. Right before the tension fades the game ends. My first playthrough took me 8 hours though I did get stuck in a few places. I'd say I could easily cut that in half if I knew what I was doing. Overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a condensed and horrific title I'd recommend anyone looking for a spooky game to play over a weekend. It's simple on the surface, yet gives the player incentive to replay it, as the mechanics blend together and let the player ♥♥♥♥ around. A solid 7.5 or 8. Not ground breaking, but extremely solid

_childDocuments_.review: "Amnesia: The Bunker" is the latest and most intense installment of the Amnesia series produced by Frictional Games. It takes everything that made the previous games so effective at horror and combines them into one finished product. It has the atmosphere of Dark Descent, the storytelling of Machine for Pigs, the mechanics of Rebirth, and a whole lot more. Most unique about this installment is that it relies on planning. You have the smallest inventory possible and only one save point in the center of the map. The Bunker really focuses on planning and decision-making more than any other game in the series. It is also the most graphically-robust game and is so realistic that it nearly doubles the effectiveness of the immersion this and the other Amnesia games provide. The game looks stellar yet at the same time runs smoothly (even on my semi-powerful laptop from 2020 which does not support RTX games) at all times and is a consistent experience through and through. The Bunker is the one game in the Amnesia series that focuses on survival more than any other installment; it's dropped the whole "puzzle" aspect of the previous games, but it relies on exploration now which is much more suited for this kind of approach. Set in a hole in the ground during WWI, "Amnesia: The Bunker" does a fantastic job at making you feel absolutely lost in the trenches. 9.3/10!

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game that fits well with the Dark Descent and Machine for Pigs in terms of gameplay, style, and story.Amnesia: The Bunker is a great game, I can't deny it. Any complaints or issues I have with the game are just based on how I played the game and what I should be expecting from this series after playing Dark Descent and Machine for Pigs. The gameplay is very fair and gives options to solve any problem. The rules aren't the same as every other horror game I've played, so there's reason to experiment and understand how this game works. I was upset a few times that I couldn't fit through something or kick away the rats, but those are the rules of this game and it shouldn't be played like something else. The game will also find ways to keep you on your toes so you don't get too comfortable or confident.The sound design and music is great. I found myself spending extra time in safe areas listening to the ambiance or music, increasing my immersion. The sound of a bottle rolling across the ground, gas grenades popping, hinges squealing, it all sounds great and fits in the environment. The voice acting for the characters was amazing as well, great choice of actors and their deliveries were perfect.For the story, it feels right for an Amnesia game. It's a setting I was aware of, but don't know much about so there's reason to pay attention. The writing for all the characters and voice acting had the right amount of emotion so it wasn't obnoxiously poetic, but had enough heart to where I was feeling something for them. Getting more information about the story was a treat, it made me want to explore and know more. The ending felt a little strange, but the Amnesia series has always given me that. A meaning I don't quite understand causing a hunger for more information. It makes me want to play it again or spend some time reading theories.Amnesia: The Bunker is a great game. All the qualities I examined were very well done and enjoyable in their own ways. It shouldn't be played like other games, not even like the other Amnesia games. Take it in as its own game with its own story and you will have a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the creepiest piece of media since a long long time. The reason for that is a subject we'll talk about. Mind you I only played on Hard. Can't speak for other difficulty options because they'll be different;This game is the most gut wrenching stomach curling muscle spasming heart exploding game I've ever played to this date. From start to finish this game is on another level. The sound design team should get some medals.Graphically it really delivers the feeling of the dusty WW1 bunker. There's almost nowhere safe. You have the pressure on you the moment you step outside and you have to plan accordingly.I really like how the game has heavily mechanic oriented rather than story. It's what separating this game from other horror games where you see almost all of them not focusing on gameplay as much as their stories. It's a huge plus. While the game can be short depending on diff and how you play it based on your randomized luck, the game doesn't drag and satisfies you enough for another playthrough. Which is very possible considering how randomization changes most of the items, traps and their locations.The game has a lot of potential for modding and I'll be diving into it as well. Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Just absolutely fantastic! This feels like a response to all the people doubting if Frictional could make a great horror game again (at least when it comes to gameplay) after Amnesia: The Dark Descent, and also one more focused on gameplay rather than story. The gameplay here is much more in depth compared to anything they have done before. You can actually fight back, which is a welcome change, even though I enjoy the way they have done it before as well. I also very much enjoy the more "im-sim" way of how they handle obstacles. Most things have a few different ways to get past and trying out what works in a given situation was very fun. May not be super deep, but deep enough imo. Even though the story really takes a backseat here, I found it very intriguing piecing together what happened in the bunker through the environment and the notes scattered all around. It was also pretty good which helped alot as I usually do not really read notes and stuff in games (except Frictionals). Some interesting twists and turns and also a nice tie in to the other games in the franchise.The majority of the horror in the game imo came from how stressful it was. Everything is super limited (both time and resources) and I never felt like I was in control of the situation throughout the game, which was also helped by the runtime I think. You also only have 1 real save spot and getting killed will remove all of your progress post save, which was sometimes really stressful when I had spent alot of time scavenging. The generator is such a smart mechanic and caused alot of stress when it was running out of fuel. This combined with the ever present monster was just superbly executed and I felt they did the whole "Alien Isolation" style even better than that one. Sure, the ai might not be as advanced, but I think the constant presence makes up for it. The sound design was absolutely superb as well and I will never forget the sounds of the monster stalking through the hallways. Absolutely the scariest one they have made so far.Some people may also say it is too short for the price, but I find its length to be a strength here. I find that horror games in particular need to be super careful when it comes to pacing, especially if they are longer. The more you get exposed to the horror, the more familiar it gets and thereby less scary. This I had a big problem with in Rebirth, but here it was just right I feel. Focusing more on replay value is also good with a bit of rng, and to further improve that they will release a Halloween update which looks very promising. It is also always quality over quantity for me and this game fits this description very well. This really showed me once more that Frictional is one of the greats in horror. An absolute must this Halloween season
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic survival horror / immersive sim - relatively short, but very replayable thanks to randomized elements and NG+ settings. I'm on my second playthrough right now, playing on the unlocked difficulty mode "Shell Shock" as opposed to my Normal difficulty first playthrough, and it feels almost like a different game at times, a suddenly torturous yet exhilarating one. There are so many unique gameplay systems and setpieces that make this short experience deeply memorable and, while not at all as story driven as past frictional works, the micro-story at play combined with the constantly tense atmosphere create something truly distinct and enjoyable. If you're at all interested in survival horror with elements of immersive sim, this is absolutely worth the price, and on sale it's a must. While judging by some reviews not every Amnesia fan was elated by The Bunker, I absolutely hope that Frictional continues down this design path, or at the very least keeps many elements of it. Great game, 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-AMAZING atmosphere. It really feels like you're trapped in a WW1 bunker with an eldritch monster.-Love the Frictional Games trademark physics interactivity-Puzzles are simple but logical and emergent, with sometimes more than one solution, and fun-Monster AI is fantastic. Its head did clip through a door and its threat was quite reduced once I figured it out (I was kinda hoping it would become more dangerous and like evolve or wtv, but no biggie).-Really liked the story here. Again, it's almost all thru notes and a select few are voiced, but it did have a twist I definitely did not expect but made sense and I liked it. Kinda wish there was at least ONE character I could talk with though (aside from that one dude that immediately gets ripped to shreds in the tutorial).-Graphics are a step above all previous games in their repertoire. Nothing amazing, but fantastic nonetheless.-Music is... well... does what it needs to, once in a while. I enjoyed the calm HQ musique (when you lock all the doors)... while it lasted... D:-Sound effects are superb. Shoot a gun or explode a nade, your ears will be ringing, just like in real life.-Most realistic gun handling in a first person shooter that I've ever played. Reloading next to an incoming monster is, fittingly, suicidal. -Game encourages you to be quiet. Some will or won't like this, but I did. I decided to forego the iconic dynamo flashlight since it made enough noise to wake up a neighbourhood and was rewarded for it by not having the beast pop out as often. It meant I sometimes couldn't see 2 feet in front of me, but I had a little lighter at that point and made the game more scary, but less stressful. Also I really liked that making a bunch of noise like shooting a gun or bashing a door open with a brick cause the monster to come running - I would formulate a plan to go hide in a closet or under a table and it was fun.-Short, but sweet. I never was stuck long enough to need to seek the internet for a solution - I figured ♥♥♥♥ out the whole way through and enjoyed it, which is more than I can say of most games...-Never had any crash or any bug to speak of (aside from some minor stutters when changing areas, but it's actually a blessing to be able to skip loading screens)-Monster tear me to shreds and I shrieke like a school girlCons-Short. Yes, it is short. If you're looking for a 20+ hr game, look elsewhere.-Ending(s) is... well... kinda garbage. Not gonna lie it seemed realistic I guess?... but a real downer and not satisfying.-Final monster boss is BS. Don't tell me this mo********er can take 4 shotgun hits pointblank in the face and still not back away to give me a sec to move some gosh dang boxes. This is a Frictional game I wanna move my boxes!... ... tried gas (wearing gasmask) and that was as effective as coughing in its general direction.  It still tore my face apart a couple times. I gave up and found a way to actually get another ending instead.-Monster as a whole could have done a bit more tbh. Maybe mutate, change appearance somewhat, get more behaviours and abilities and become smarter and more dangerous. Mildly disappointing. Also I guess I'm spoiling there's only one monster, my bad. Was expecting a tiny bit more. Then again, what it DID do was done perfectly, so I can't really complain.-Map is kinda smol as a whole, there ain't a whole lot to explore and once you've gotten the tools they only serve a couple of times then are useless.-Normal difficulty gives waaaaay too much resources. Before the end I had so much junk I was idly filling up drawers with excess items. I suggest going with hard difficulty if you don't mind being a little conservative with them.-There is a relative lack of item variety. Aside from quest items that just unlock a new section, you can pretty much try out all the gameplay items in the demo and you can count them on the fingers of one hand... aside from like 3 or 4 things. They could have added some rare or really rare stuff that you'd really need to look around for. Similarly, consequently, crafting is super bare-bones and limited.As a whole I'd rate the game a 8/10. Not the best horror game I've played, not *quite* as good or memorable to me as TDD, but definitely a step in the right direction. They innovated and I appreciate that.I hope Frictional makes many more games, each one with a cool particular take like this did.

_childDocuments_.review: Below are my thoughts after my first playthrough, doing my best to speak without the benefit of hindsight. Time Spent: Massively fun. I don't regret spending my time on it.Duration: Short but sweet - doesn't outstay its welcome (I clocked 4:40ish hours start to finish, minus breaks. Could have been more had I not gotten lucky at times, could've been less had I figured some things out more quickly). The game asks for very little time commitment to present to you what it has to offer.Horror factor: Masterful atmosphere - good balance between balance and calm, allowing just enough breathing room to where the game doesn't get exhausting, but not so much that it feels like the threat can be ignored. Threat fatigueI.e how quickly does the game's threat become tiring and annoying. The threat isn't annoying to deal with - If you play the game well, the game will treat you well. Survival mechanics:Dealing with the threat and mitigating harm is intuitive in a very 'common sense wins out' way - If doing something feels like it'll keep you safe, it probably will. If it feels like it'll put you in danger, it probably will.Progression mechanics:This is, in my opinion, where the games falls the lowest. The progression system of the game is well-paced and satisfying. The game, however, does a poor job at broadcasting this progression. The result is that one may find themselves completing objectives simply because they are 'the next step' despite not actually knowing why the objective actually ties into the overall experience until after the step is complete. This smells of poor writing rather than 'grand reveal.' There were moments (not many, but worth note nonetheless) where I felt as though the importance of an objective was not well explained. However, there were hardly any moments where I felt as though an objective existed purely to extend the duration of the game. Every objective served to enrich the experience. I just wish that such intention was better broadcast.World-building Gameplay integration:I.e how well does the story, world-building and the gameplay coexist in such a way that if you removed the 'game' aspect from puzzles and mechanics, these puzzles and mechanics wouldn't seem silly, such as 'a random sliding puzzle acting as a key to gain entrance to a room' per example.I believe that every puzzle, mechanic and task exists in near-perfect harmony with the logical boundaries of the world-building to produce a sense of immersion in the world of the game, all without sacrificing gameplay enjoyment for the sake of immersion. Everything feels like, were this experience real, the decisions made and obstacles in my path would make sense.Graphical design:Masterfully crafted. I personally experienced no immersion-breaking graphical defects, such as bodies clipping through objects or peering through tiles and textures. The GUI was also wonderfully-crafted, enjoyable to look at and easy to navigate. The underwater experience, however, while brief, did not appear to be particularly well cared for. It was evidently of lower priority than other aspects of the experience.Sound design:Spectacular. The atmosphere created through the sound in the way that it evolves based on location, threat index and stage in the game served to help build suspense, dread and immersion. The music was well-designed and the GUI, object and entity sounds were a treat to experience. Only note is that the Beast's audio cues do not lend themselves to immersion, as they can be heard through walls as though they do not exist, and the volume of the cues do not accurately represent the Beast's distance from the player often sounding way further or closer than it ought to for its actual distance.Overall, however, despite nitpicks, which are all my negatives are, really, the game is incredible. My favourite of the Amnesia series so far. 9/10. High 9.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is a great horror game. This game improves on previous iterations by Frictional Games, SOMA & Amnesia DD were much more story driven games but The Bunker really doubled-down on refining the gameplay. The gameplay in previous games involved picking up items and taking them to other places & occasionally hiding from the Monster. In The Bunker they give you many options to approach the game other than pickup item and take it somewhere. SPOILER WARNING:They give you the below tools to take on the game- Gun (with very limited bullets)- Pocket Watch- Flares- Grenades- Gas Grenades- Flashlight- Gas Canisters- Health Packs- Torches- Raw Meat- & more....How you use these different resources to avoid death and collect the necessary clues & items makes the experience completely different for each player. I would highly recommend this to any fan of horror games, it is more than hiding in closets from monsters, you need to use your wits and experiment to get past the games obstacles. Definitely one my top 3 horror games of the last 5 years. Well done Frictional and I look forward to your future games where you expand on the new game play introduced in The Bunker.

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of Frictional Games and the Amnesia Series.  Amnesia: The Bunker by far is the scariest and the best of the amnesia series. The game is rather short as a whole. I finished the game first time through in about 5 hours roughly. The overall gameplay of Amnesia: The Bunker was good. This is the first Amnesia game I believe to implement some kind of combat system since Amnesia: The Bunker has added guns as part of the game. Despite having guns, however, the ammunition is very scarce. This usually forces us to improvise and strategize.  Other than the combat system, Amnesia: The Bunker is similar to the other amnesia games where you either hide or run from any monster you encounter. The horror aspect of Amnesia: The Bunker was also very well done. The concept of the monster, the amount of areas the monster can pop out of, how it responds to how much noise the player makes, searching around the vicinity for the player, and deciding whether or not to waste valuable resources such as ammunition to slow the monster down always kept me on edge when playing through my first playthrough of the game. The overall story of Amnesia: The Bunker is always the best part of the game. The story is rather simple. Playing the game and exploring around the area finding notes hidden around to understand the story and what exactly happened is what I enjoyed most.  Overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a fantastic horror game. I definitely had a great time playing through it on my first playthrough.  I would say that Amnesia: The Bunker is one of the best and scariest horror games I have played. As I mentioned before, Amnesia: The Bunker is rather short, but I feel like the game has enough overall content for you to enjoy the game. I would definitely recommend this game. Even if you're not a fan of horror games, I would still recommend trying out this game and experiencing for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually don't understand the "very positive" reviews overall on this new amnesia title to be honest. Maybe it's because of new players coming to the franchise but as someone like me who played Amnesia since the beginning and started with Amnesia - The Dark Descent I must say that this title is somewhat underwhelming.Let me start with the positives:-  Sound FX- Environment- Crafting system- Atmosphere until its notNegatives with some more explanation:- The Monster: I played on normal mode and it was super annoying after the first 2-3 hours ingame. What should scare me, terrify me, hunt me in my dreams and should let me go insane ends up being so annoying that I wanted to RUSH through the game as fast as possible to finally beat it. As soon as you make the smallest noise its coming out, which is fine but the scripting behind it is terrible. It's actually babysitting the area/room you are currently located and instead of make me feel like I described above I just get bored and annoyed like "finally get the fk off and move on!". As soon as you encountered it 3-4 times all the magic is gone and it just annoys me. Especially with the so obvious scripted mechanics. You change the area with a loading lag and suddenly it teleports to the same area you want to investigate? Not much fun.- Backtracking and puzzles: In Amnesia backtracking was always somewhat a thing since you had a "safe space" and could investigate several rooms/ways in order to gather information or key items you need to solve puzzles. Which was GREAT! Puzzles in Amnesia was sooo fun combined with the horror and the fact you couldn't do much aside of hiding and running for your life. But the amount of puzzles in the bunker are very rare. They tried to build this mechanic around the crafting system which is somewhat fun but once you tried everything out it loses its fascination pretty fast. For example getting key items after obtaining some codes to unlock them. You end up using those tools a handful of times and thats it. The most annoying thing in this game however is dying after spending 30 minutes to 1 hour exploring the bunker without running back to your safe space to save the game and your progress. All you achieved before dying is GONE and you have to do it again. Finding key items, notes and so on.- Story telling: This was always the most important thing for me in Amnesia Games. Story telling. The first Amnesia had such a fascinating and oddly terrifying story which was told by notes of course but also by notes your protagonist was reading for you. Aside of that they also implemented some scenes where it seems you remember something that happened in the past (since you have amnesia) where you can listen to dialogues between yourself and other characters from the game. But not only that. You also had Sound FX connected to it which deepened the immersion of the flashback scene. If you look out for that in the bunker, well.. you can read your notes but thats mostly it. Some few notes were read by your protagonist and thats about it. The story itself is okay, rebirth was definitly better, dark descent too. Not only because of the way the told it but also because of the length. The bunker is actually very short which surprised me. The only reason it will take you 8-10 hours to beat it is just because of the monster babysitting you almost 24/7 in this game which artifically lengthens your playtime. There is however environmental story telling to some degree but the connection to older titles is rare. I won't spoiler but I can say there are a few connections to be fair.- Replayabillity: This was something they advertised a lot and I don't understand the fascination behind it. If there were multiple endings (it seems there are two? not sure yet) it would make sense but just procedural item changing won't do the trick for me. If the story is the same and I cannot change it why would I replay this game? Just to do different paths like I did before? Nope. The not so negative aspect:- Gameplay: As always in Amnesia. Feels like they never improved on that but for me that's not a big deal. It works.So overall when comparing this game to older titles I can't really recommend the game because the earlier ones are WAY better (aside of "a machine for pigs").It feels like this amnesia delivers on all fronts but less than what we got in the past. I understand that they wanted to change some mechanics and try out fresh and new ideas but PLEASE for the next installment don't cut the story telling. This is what made your games so good.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I'm going to recommend this game for a few reasons. First and foremost, I think Frictional Games is always going to be a promising studio because they're always willing to try something...even if it doesn't really end up working. Secondly, there's still no one else out there that can conjure up this sort of sustained dread like they do, and The Bunker is no exception.I think that if you're going to buy this game, you need to understand what you're actually getting. If you're looking for a full-length survival horror with a focus on atmosphere and narrative, like the original Amnesia, look elsewhere. If you're looking for a lengthy, writing heavy exploration piece like SOMA...well, this ain't it either.What Amnesia: The Bunker is, in actuality, is essentially one of Frictional Games' old formulas stretched out to be its own game. It's structured exactly like a section from The Dark Descent; you have a central hub, an obstacle blocking your path and 2-3 side areas that contain pieces of the puzzle that will unlock the way forward. The difference is, instead of unlocking the next hub and spoke area, the game just...ends. The Bunker will take on average 4-6 hours to complete, but it can probably be done in 1 or less on repeat playthroughs.Instead, A:TB tries to rely more on its mechanics rather than it's length. It's taken cues from Alien: Isolation in the sense that your progress is continually hindered by a (sort of) omnipresent monster. If you make too much noise or wait around in an area, odds are he'll come creeping around and disrupt your best laid plans.The problem is, in my view, is that there's simply not enough utility in all these systems. You get bullets and frags and gas grenades and throwable bait and distraction bottles and the like, but the only threats in the Bunker are the Stalker and...rats. That's it. You'll never need the Gas Mask unless you intend to walk into your own clouds or hit a gas grenade trip wire. You could build a torch to ward off rats from an item, but why would you when you can use the same ingredients to make a petrol bomb to burn the corpse? (Weirdly enough, this doesn't seem to attract the monster?) I had piles of bandages that I never used because the monster is almost always a one-hit kill, and the rats simply aren't present enough to be an enormous threat. The game needed an extra couple hours of run-time, more threats, more utility for the items, and absolutely more narrative. Way more. The lack of an engaging, horrifying story really hurt this game, and the tie-ins to the Amnesia IP are flimsy at best.But...it is only 25 bucks. Which for the dense, oppressive atmosphere and unscripted terror moments, might be worth it for most people. I'm sure the user-generated content will give this game the longevity it desperately needs.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: i LOVE the amnesia series, all of them are absolute masterpieces. i DO have to mention this one felt short i am MILDLY disappointed or maybe unsatisfied but that it also probably because i expected a storyline like the previous games. i absolutely recommend the game but be aware its not level rebirth!very short HOWEVER i cant complain cus most devs nowadays just price their games 60 or more and also insert some ingame money scams so even tho the game is very short i still believe its worth the money.(plis to give me more story next time tho friction xoxo)- Poro
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A short but good horror survival game. Yes it is actually a game and not a walking simulator. Think of it as a Amnesia Metroidvania. You wander around looking for tools and information you need to access areas that then allow you to access other areas working towards a goal that is given to you near the beginning of the game. Manage your resources and try to outwit the monster that is hunting you. They focused a bit more on replay value by randomizing items and codes on each playthrough but the map is always the same and the key goals are still always unchanged, so it is not that much different really.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty classic Amnesia/Frictional experience: the game looks, sounds, and plays great, perfectly evoking the horrific atmosphere that the whole genre relies on. The Bunker is very short - my first playthrough took me five hours - but because the items, traps, and codes you encounter are randomized each run, it is replayable, in case you want to find more things you missed last run. There are a lot of things to find, too. The bunker has several sub-maps that you need to break into rooms to unlock on your safe room's main map, and I did not unlock all of them. There are many side rooms I never entered and I'm sure plenty of notes and other lore I never saw either.Bottom line: is it worth 25 USD? Maybe. If you're going to replay it, yes. If not, wait for a bit of a sale. I'd definitely say it's worth 15 for one playthrough, maybe even 20.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Another pretty great game from Frictional Games, it's not the masterpiece that SOMA was but still an enjoyable experience.Pretty short if you focus only on the main objectives, but its roguelite elements in term of item spawning and on how you can solve the problems you face will at least make each replay differentMy only issue with the game is that I think the monster appears way too often on the highest difficulty thus reducing the fear factor and instead might start to get annoyingOverall if you're a fan of the Amnesia franchise this is a pretty interesting entry in the series
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite Frictional Games game to date. A nice blend of engaging mechanics with the tools you have at your disposal mixed with fantastic level design that is both claustrophobic but always leaves you opinions of navigation (even if they are extremely risky). Highly recommend. Can't wait for some good custom stories made by the community to keep me coming back to this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is the fourth game in the Amnesia series and it feels like a return to form that, although not lost, was a bit muddled over the years. I would go as far as to say that gameplay-wise it is the best Amnesia, and in general, the best Frictional's game we got to date. It does not reach the story heights of Dark Descent or the absolute apex that was SOMA, but what is here is servicable and does not deter from the opressive atmosphere present throughout. We are stalked by only one monster through the entire game this time but it is one that will test our wits more than once or twice. Addition of weapons seemed a bit odd to me at first but the way they are used in creative ways to deal mostly with environmental puzzles is a very welcome addition in the end. With a great atmosphere, gameplay and a non-demanding price (in today's climate at least), it is a game very easily worth a recommendation. Here's hoping we will see more Frictional soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Other reviews cover things in better detail than me, so the short version is essentially Alien Isolation blended with the Amnesia games, and the original Resident Evil titles.The creature feels both very intelligent (like the Xenomorph), yet also very RNG based simultaneously, which could be a little frustrating.  I had bad luck fairly frequently with just how often the creature decided to come out of his burrows and start to patrol, as well as the ridiculous duration of time it would just camp a place I was hiding, despite attempts at diversions.  The inventory system is very Resident Evil, I don't think I need to explain that one.The lighting, ambiance, soundtrack, visuals, narrative, and grotesque monster design are all Amnesia.I would seriously recommend this title if you're a fan of any of the three aforementioned game(s) series, or if you're not familiar with any of them, this is a great place to experience some terrific survival horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Bravo to the creators of this game. You guys did an excellent job. This is my first time ever playing an Amnesia game, and this was a fun thrill ride, with a surprise ending. The tension was great through out the game. And the cat and mouse aspect was an excellent addition. The game shows you that you can tell a perfectly good story and it does not have to be hours long for you to enjoy it. I thought 5 hours was a perfect amount of time to spend in this story, and the setting was excellent. I would highly recommend this game to anyone, and I am hoping the next game is similar to this. I would recommend a full price buy for this game, it is definitely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Dude, Frictional Games has been dropping the ball at every opportunity with every new game they make. Original Amnesia was amazing! Good mechanics, scary af, and mostly fair. Every new game following the original has been inferior in every way:1) Mechanics2) Story3) Controls4) Level DesignI've lost count of how many times I've been sucker punched by a mechanic without understanding what I was supposed to do to avoid it. So many dead ends where you just lose without the ability to avoid the danger. Such clunky controls that expect you to be perfect in every execution to play the game as intended. And how the hell can't I find ANY ammunition in a bunker, IN THE MIDDLE OF A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WAR!?I'm done holding my breath for another good Amnesia game. If I ever pick up another one, it'll be when it's in the bargain bin. Very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I was never a fan of the previous amnesia games, not that they were bad, far from it actually, i just really despised the hide and seek horror genre as it come to be known as,the bunker is however an actual survival horror game, puzzles, backtracking, item management, keys, hell even a pair of bolt cutters, the whole shebangand my god it is phenomenal everything about this game is so truly amazing an absolute must play for any survival horror or amnesia fans

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is not a very good Amnesia game. There is little grounding it in the lore of Amnesia. The WW1 bunker setting makes it feel a lot more like Penumbra than Amnesia. There aren't really puzzles. You get not one, but *two* guns, along with a litany of thrown weapons. That last point on its own feels a bit like sacrilege against the ethos of the subgenre that The Dark Descent was the progenitor of. Even if the weapon doesn't really do anything more than slow down the monster, having a way to defend yourself, even in such a meager way, really compromises a major facet of the game's atmosphere. The psychological impact of being truly defenseless is not felt when you're traipsing around the titular bunker armed to the teeth with more bullets and grenades than you can shake a stick at.So if you're here looking for the next good Amnesia game after the last two fumbled the original's good name into a pair of mediocre sequels, this is not it. It's a bad Amnesia game. But as a survival horror game -- it's pretty solid!The bunker itself is a really spooky environment. It's claustrophobic and poorly lit, even at the best of times. Your only light source in darkened areas is your hand-powered flashlight, which is loud as ♥♥♥♥ and will attract the attention of the monster, Jerome, whenever you crank it, and the charge lasts about 15 seconds. It's a terrible flashlight, by design. Its explicitly AIDSerific nature is meant to compliment the game's core mechanic, that being the generator that you have to keep fueled up in order to keep Jerome at bay and explore the bunker unmolested, but the fuel does not last terribly long. It simultaneously offers you respite from the darkness and the promise of (relative) safety from ol' Jerry, while also pushing you into exploring the unlit and unvisited areas of the bunker to find more resources. Everything you do puts you on a timer, and you feel the pressure of the clock ticking down on you constantly. Ending up stranded in the dark in one of the farther areas of the bunker is an almost guaranteed death sentence, or at the very least a guaranteed hectic run and gun back to the stash room to get the generator up and running again. It's a great source of tension.That core gameplay loop is actually compelling enough to carry the rest of the game almost on its own. It creates an atmosphere that is constant and oppressive, which goes hand in hand with the Frictional team's excellent map design and attention to detail. The bunker feels very lived in -- not just by its former human occupants, but also by our good friend Jerome. Let's talk about Jerome.The monster in Amnesia: The Bunker is both its greatest strength and its greatest flaw. The dynamic AI means that Jerome is a constant looming threat no matter where you are. You'll hear him skittering around inside the walls, growling and screeching, following you everywhere. Fire a gun or toss a grenade or run around too much in an unsafe area and it's a matter of moments before Jerome's on top of you and snacking on your innards. He's very similar to the Xenomorph from Alien: Isolation, though not nearly as consistent (or consistently irritating). There are holes in the walls all throughout the bunker which Jerome uses to stalk you around the base, which are themselves a serious source of tension, especially when placed directly next to your objectives. You can usually tell when he's nearby based on all the noise he makes, but every once in a while he decides to develop a mind of his own and go off script on you. He's supposed to hate the light and stay away from it, but he'll regularly come sniffing around where he's not welcome, spawning sometimes at complete random in fully lit areas. And Jerome is FAST AS ♥♥♥♥ BOIIIIINothing will stop him. Not doors, not tables, not closets, nothing. If you hear the "peekaboo I see you " noise, you've got about 1.5 seconds to pump a few bullets in him before he mulches your ass with his 1 hit kills, very much like the Xenomorph from Isolation. If he catches you, that's it.But here's the thing: Jerome cheats, and he's very dumb. He's supposed to have this mechanic where he can track you based on the blood trail you leave behind from being injured, but it doesn't seem to work 100% correctly. I've had instances where Jerome has smashed tables I'm under and closets I'm inside of despite having not seen me and having full health, and I've also had instances where I was nearly dead and bleeding out gallons per second while Jerome meandered past completely oblivious, lost in thought trying to decide what he's going to watch on Netflix tonight. He's also a big b with a tiny p most of the time and won't actually come out of his hideyholes in areas you've explored no matter how much sprinting, grenade tossing, or flashlight pumping you engage in, except on the odd occasions that he changes his mind about it and comes to say hello six feet away from your home base without any provocation whatsoever. I didn't really find myself constantly paranoid about Jerome like I was with the Xenomorph, because his rules are inconsistent, and he'll let you do whatever you'd like most of the time. It really saps a lot of the atmosphere by the end when it becomes a game of remembering where you have to go while some weirdo breathes heavily in the walls and occasionally screams at you rather than having to actually be mindful of the helldemon on your tail. This is itself curtailed somewhat by the game's short running time -- I beat it in just under 5.5 hours according to the in game timer, at least an hour of which was spent dying to a frustrating killbox in the penultimate area, and then dying over and over again attempting to figure out how to get out of the final arena. If one knew what they were doing and knew where things were, I could easily imagine this game being beaten in under 1.5-2 hours, probably less than that, due to how the game's mechanics are put together to only soft-gate your progress instead of hard-gating it. The game suggests some sort of replay value with randomized item placements and door/locker codes, as well as a big old stats screen at the end, but I don't really know how much mileage there is to get out of that, other than the time trial aspect of it.The story is nothing to write home about. None of the characters are really interesting, and the protagonist's involvement with the narrative's events are mostly incidental. Henri is not Daniel or Oswald, who were the prime movers of their narratives, tortured and conflicted characters whose actions set into motion all of the events of TDD and AMFP. He's not even like Tasi from Rebirth, who might have held a different role narratively to Daniel and Oswald, but at least had some greater motivation than "survive, idiot" and a connection to the other characters in the story. Henri is... I mean, he's just kinda there. You don't really learn much of anything about him, his amnesia is incidental, and he's not really the focus of the supernatural goings-on at the heart of the story. Nobody has any thoughts about Henri, and in turn Henri has little to say about any of them. His motivation is to escape the bunker. That's it.Maybe that's all you need to make a good video game, but I really expect a little more from an Amnesia game. There aren't even multiple *real* endings, a staple of the series, that's how barebones the story is. It's not great.But overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a tight, compelling experience, one which will keep you on the edge of your seat for most of its running time. $25 might be a bit high of a price to pay for something so short, but I still definitely recommend this game. Buy on sale when you feel like being spooked for a few hours.
