_childDocuments_.review: Man, I just don’t know with this game. I can’t say I had fun playing it. But also, after watching and reading more about it, I’m also convinced I may just have been playing it wrong. I’m unsure how much of the blame for that rests with me, and how much could be could be mitigated with better design and communication.I knew what I was getting into. I bounced off of Alien: Isolation, but respected what it was trying to do, so I wanted to give this a chance. I had read that The Bunker was only a few hours long, and I was in a halloweeny mood. Frictional’s SOMA is furthermore one of my all-time favorite games, though much more for its thoughtful meditations on consciousness and less for its hiding from beasties.It took me 11 frustrating hours to finish this. I think I just play these games far too conservatively. I ended the game sitting atop a mountain of generator fuel—having barely turned the thing on—and a stockpile of unused grenades. I forced poor Henri to assume a permanent crouch, and slip into a cupboard at the slightest noise. It took me over an hour of rummaging and experimentation in pitch-darkness, between long stretches of fearfully hiding under a bed, to figure out how to access the very first puzzle room. I read later that the monster can’t even emerge then, and that the noises at that stage were just to scare me.Inevitably, playing that way made my progress feel very slow, and every death feel like a large setback. Even though the knowledge I gained would always lead to quicker progress next time.I can’t help but wish that Frictional did more to encourage me to use more of my resources, and to play less fearfully. The game does explicitly tell you to experiment, and I did, but in practice, experimentation was resource-expensive and only very rarely resulted in progress. The game is much pickier than it claims about which key goes with which door. So, I moved much more slowly and behaved much more stingily than I needed to.On the other hand, abject terror, player disempowerment, and feeling like you need to stockpile everything you can to survive are a lot of what games like this are all about. There’s a paradoxical tension between encouraging the player to push ahead, spend consumables, and die a lot—sometimes in ways that seem unfair—and still preserve in them that delicious feeling of fear.For me, The Bunker skewed way too heavily toward the latter, and so I didn’t have much fun. But I also don’t really know how to solve that. I kind of liked that I was afraid to wind my flashlight, walk at normal speed, or perform any number of other mundane actions that were actually pretty safe. But, I guess, I could’ve had more fun if I realized all that safety sooner. It was a long 11 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A Frenchman bumbles around in the darkness while his landlord hunts him down because he's furious that he and his buds left the lights on all night.An exceptionally good game, I now have a bunker shaped hole in my heart. The sound design, adventuring, and thrills were all magnificent. The most gameplay heavy of all the Amnesia games but it still has plenty of story telling and note reading. I wish there were more puzzles, Amnesia games usually have crafting or physic based puzzles. Not this game though, it's mainly adventuring and figuring out where to go. I think the cat and mouse game played by Henri and the Stalker can be annoying at some points but there are plenty of tools at your disposal that the annoyance is minimal. Personally my GotY of 2023, I strongly recommend playing this.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Editing my review after finally beating the game. I'm honestly disappointed, it just didn't feel like an Amnesia game besides subtle nods to previous games.Do I recommend playing it? Sure. It's a good horror game, it scared me a ton.If you enjoy the story part of Amnesia games, you'll be disappointed. Many unanswered questions, and parts felt almost unfinished with how it rushed me through quickly.Overall, it was a good experience, just not as memorable as the previous games.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This was a terrifying and incredibly addicting and fun survival horror and definitely the best entry in the series since dark descent (Maybe even better?). This is a game about solving puzzles while one massive monster attempts to hunt you down, and you can adapt. But it is not gonna be easy. 9/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The Bunker is an absolutely Phenomenal entry in the Amnesia franchise, and a welcome change from the mediocrity of Rebirth, and the just bad Machine for Pigs. It does what it set out to do and it does it well, and it's story is very well written, with moments that will call back to the very first things you see in it. It has a number of call backs to the other games as well. The mechanics of the game are very well fleshed out, and lacks any major bugs, except one area where i managed to get the beast stuck. The only real complaint i have with the game, is that it's very short. I feel as though the game could have been better were it a little, or a lot longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Descent is one of my favorite horror games of all times, unrivaled by any other horror game I've ever played. Throughout my play through of TDD I was scared the entire time, always watching my back and fearful of what would come next. The puzzles of it were interesting and the monsters were well designed. Some time after, Machine for Pigs was released, and disappointed the series. It was a failure of a game and had nothing that made TDD an amazing and beautiful game. Many years later, Rebirth was released, and was close to the original feel of the game yet there was something missing. Every gripe I've had with every other Amnesia game since TDD was solved in this game.The Bunker brings back the original horror of the game, the fear of something always being there watching you. The atmosphere in this rivaled that of TDD. You could hear the monsters crawling around in the walls and you could see dust shake from the ceiling as it crawls around. The clicking of its nails against the concrete floor.This was one of the best Amnesia games, and honestly it was hard to decide between TDD and this one being my favorite. This one though has taken its place as my favorite horror game, with TDD being my second favorite. I surely hope the next game in this series is able to rival the same atmosphere and feeling this one had.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I played on hard, but in retrospect I should have gone with normal. Don't play it on hard unless you enjoy frustration. I don't. I expected a more challenging and enjoyable game, but hard only hampers your progress more. Play it on normal, that's clearly the proper balance for this game. They should have left out hard, because it's also less scary if you constantly die and have to try again.But I'm happy to say that frictional games has made another good horror game. I only wish they would have added some more story, because I'm a sucker for good stories!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite likely among the best horror games I have ever played. It's an interactive and dynamic horror puzzle game with a lot of interesting gameplay mechanics, probably among the more complex survival horror titles. Gameplay wise it's a mix between Resident Evil, Alien Isolation and the first Amnesia game. The game is pretty difficult and unforgiving at times so it takes time to figure out how things work in this game. You will die a lot if you start on Normal like I did but overall I enjoyed every second of the game and looking forward to more replays.10/10, can only recommendUpdate: The recent update made the game even more worthwhile to play. You can customize your playthrough much more and the new Shell Shocked difficulty was really good. The mode added a lot of spice to the already terrifying game.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I think this is the best of the 4 amnesia games.The immersion is insane, I was genuinely terrified at times which isn't something that happens a lot for me. The Dark Descent had great immersion until you figured out how the monsters worked, but in The Bunker even after I figured out how the monster worked I was ♥♥♥♥ scared at times. I actually found myself clenching my cheeks when moving around in the dark, praying to a god I don't even believe in that I didn't make a noise.The game is actually tricky at times, and some areas took me a number of attempts and/or running back with my tail between my legs because the monster showed up.One of the most difficult parts in my run (getting the code for the wrench locker) was able to be cheesed by just remembering the code on the dogtag you find at the end, which felt like an oversight to me but hey ho.Overall, this was an awesome game. I can't wait for the next installment!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I have yet to finish the game, and I can tell you already, I will be taking my time with this gem. The game captures the original feel of Penumbra games so well that it's hard to put into words exactly what has Frictional done right this time.The atmosphere and sound design is superb. Graphics and lighting are great too but lets you wonder what higher detail textures and models could do to a game like this. Gameplay mechanics are well done from what I have already seen. Overall this is my favorite take on Frictional horror game.Ever since Penumbra games, I have closely followed every Frictional release with one expectation: Will this game be scary enough to make you want to put it down, only to pick back up 15 min. later when you crave to know where will the story and events lead you to? This one really does. It's a perfect mix of mystery and horror.Thank you Frictional team for exploring and polishing your take on survival horror, it is one of a kind, for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia The Bunker proved to be a terrifying and amazing experience. the atmosphere is dense and thick creating a harsh and oppressive atmosphere all the more while a beast from the bunkers past lurks around the corners to kill you. popping in and out of holes around the map and creating a dynamic experience with how you interact with the world. it doesn't re-invent the wheel with a cat and mouse experience but it delivers on the TRUE experience of one. the dynamic AI that is provided you has given me some of the most adrenaline pumping experiences in any game with a lot of my encounters with the beast feeling like a full on action sequence that was meant to be apart of a scripted event. and even though this nightmare fuelled machine is out to kill you it can provide interesting benefits when it is out and about, some times destroying unbreakable block offs and busting down locked doors proves that even though its out to kill you if you smart enough can be manipulated to be used a tool.the additions of the weapons was a really nice touch; acting as a means of self defence but as a utility tool that can interact with the environment to help you. your movement feels very methodical and the weapons feel powerful, and going along with the scarce amount of ammo you will find along with how you need to manually reload it bullet by bullet emphasises that importance of every shot must count. i really enjoyed the generator mechanic too, acting as a means to give you some reprieve when exploring the bunker but i like how even though you have this reprieve the beast is still a threat if your reckless enough. i also like how you can sync up with the generator too and cool little touch is that if you explore a lot of the map turning on more lights it will in turn go through the fuel meaning the your little pocket watch will go out of sync and the black out will come sooner.it strikes this perfect balance of pure fear and excitement and giving you a perfect combination of tools at your disposal creating a grounded and dynamic sandbox which have led to some horrific and bad ass moments. and side note the sound design is amazing the way your guns make you go slightly deaf when you shoot them is really cool especially in heart pounding moments when your fending off the beast or when you using them to work with the enviroment too; along with the already terrifying atmosphere every sound made my ear twitch trying to figure out what was going on. when it comes to story there isn't a whole lot here which can be give or take depending on what type of player you are. you're given the basics in the intro/tutorial. but asides from that you'll get story through some of the enviroment but mainly the notes scattered around the whole map. personally i read all the notes i found and thought the story was interesting and good enough, nothing ground breaking but does provide some cool lore and some twists that i didn't see coming. but asides from that yeah give or take on whether you not you care about it which i think is good thing the story it self is interesting enough.quick cons would be that the game is a bit short but does make up for the replayability. the ending was a little underwhelming and going between main areas wasn't very seemless (but isn't too immersion breaking) and walking through the rubble can sometimes be a challenge to say the least. and the fps cap being at 60 isnt terrible just is an odd choice. (YOU CAN UNCAP IT THO, just go to files then documents, games, Amnesia the bunker, Main and look for text document with your username_110000117EBA5CF_user_settings.cfg. open with just normal notes, proceed through and find something that says refresh rate and replace it with your desired refresh rate mine being 144, side note if you still get 60fps even after changing you might need to set your v-sync to "false" in the file to) bearing in mind these cons they are actually just nit picks and aren't anything that ruin the game its just some slight annoyance.overall 4/5 highly recommend for horror fans or someone like me who's been waiting for a really good experience ever since soma
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad game by any means It has some truly cool stuff to offer. However The game does feel unnecessarily Frustrating at times taking away from the fear and inducing anger rather than fear. As a long time Horror Gamer I Don't believe It's a lack of skill. The Beast will almost 90% of the time find you no matter where you hiding and don't  get me started on the rats I understand why they are there but I feel they are way to unfair making game play frustrating yet again.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little horror game. I'm sure fans will struggle where to place Bunker among Frictional's other games, not as revolutionary as Dark Descent, not as heady and noetic as SOMA ect, but stands in direct response to the maximalism of Rebirth; Bunker feels like Rebirth's opposite, stripped down, minimalist, focused entirely on its few key elements. What impressed me most is how tactile every item is, and that design is the key to what made the game work so effectively for me. Like I was concerned when I saw we began with a revolver that this might be more of an action game, but when I discovered you had to manually flip out the cylinder and manually load each bullet before aiming to shoot I felt a lot of relief knowing this would be a very deliberate survival experience. Another example is having to wind up a pocketwatch to calculate how long the generator has fuel for, there is no UI icon for this, you have to pull out your little  pocketwatch to see how long until you're plunged back into darkness. Anyway I really enjoyed it and think it brings a lot to the table. I will say it is quite short though, so if you're the kind of silly goose who judges games based on dollars per hour of gameplay or whatever you'll be furious so don't do that to yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This game really finds that sweet spot of survival horror where you do have tools to defend yourself, but the ressources are very scarce so you never end up "fully geared" so that the monster is still dangerous and scary.  The story is great if you really take the time to read the notes you find since most of the story is told by those. The sound design is incredible and pairs really well with the game mechanic of the monster being attracted by sound so you end up being very cautious of the sound you make and the game renders it well creating a very oppressive atmosphere.  The game is short (5-7 hour a playthrough) but have a little wiggle room for replayability with difficulty settings, achievement and the fact that codes, items and traps are randomized for each playthrough. Overall very solid game 8/10

While not scary to those who are fairly numb to horror, it presents a perfect resource management challenge. coupled with a VERY well written story and a nice and cramped environment! and no matter what the RNG happens to throw at you in any difficulty, the fuel always seems to properly match what difficulty your playing.100% worth the money if you enjoy the previous amnesia games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game goes back to Frictional's roots -- the atmosphere feels both like Penumbra and The Dark Descent, but this time, the tension and scares come from your own decision-making. It's a break from Frictional's newer titles, but maybe that's exactly what the Amnesia series needed, because they've definitely succeeded - I'm freakin' scared.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Frictional Games went back to their roots with this one. Even with their departure from the usual sanity mechanic well-established in their other amnesia games, this game is genuinely terrifying at times with really good enemy AI, horrifying game mechanics, and goose-bump inducing WW1 bunker style environment. The fact the puzzles are randomly generated and there are multiple methods of achieving the same goals adds a lot of replay value that keeps the game alive for me. Each section of the bunker is different enough from the other mechanics-wise that kept the game interesting. The generator warrants an entire article on its own, but its management and value are probably some of the best parts of this game. When the power cuts off and you're deep in the bunker, the bone-chilling fear that ensues is genuinely unforgettable as you plunge into pitch-black darkness (no matter how high you set the gamma setting) with a loud flashlight and an attentive monster. The addition of custom stories gives it that Dark Descent feel that will give this game much needed longevity. Overall, frictional games hit home with this one as its a welcome step in the right direction. I don't this it's as groundbreaking as The Dark Descent or Soma, but it has its own special charm. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its relatively short length, this is probably my favorite of the series so far.  The new monster AI--while not perfect--creates a way more tense and unpredictable atmosphere (especially in subsequent playthroughs).  Same goes for the generator game mechanic, which feels like a proper evolution of the whole "inconvenient/unreliable light source" gimmick from previous entries in the series.  Remember the feeling of dread/terror when you ran out of oil/tinderboxes while exploring in DD?  It's kinda like that when the generator runs out of fuel...but way scarier (and without the nausea-inducing "sanity" effects).Overall, I really like where Frictional decided to go with this one.  The resource management/crafting is a welcome addition, and really makes things feel more immersive.  Item/code randomization on subsequent playthroughs is great too...the major/story items and goals don't change, but many obstacles/etc will require a different approach since the same tools/items might not be available.  For criticism, I don't really have much.  The game runs smoothly for me, and it seems well-balanced and well-polished (have played on Normal and Hard so far).  If I could change one thing it would be the length, as I completed my first playthrough on Normal in about 6.5 hours, and I didn't feel like I was rushing through. Compared to previous entries in the series, The Bunker is significantly lighter on the story/lore side of things too...though I feel it makes up for it with the overall gameplay experience.So, yeah definitely give this one a go if you like survival horror/immersive sim games, and especially if DD was your favorite Amnesia...you won't be disappointed.  I hope Frictional keeps going this direction for future titles...now that it's been tested and proven at Bunker scale, let's bring back some of the grandiose and dread-filled worlds that were so fun to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia The Bunker chooses to go back to the gameplay style of the first game in the series The Dark Descent, which came out more than 15 years ago... while that first game worked very well at the time it released (it was after all widely popular on the internet and it popularized watching someone else play probably for the first time) the perception of that game now is different.After Dark Descent frictional games released several more games with evolving gameplay mechanics and game stories while also updating the graphics. Soma was a great step forward with a compelling story, but more importantly Amnesia Rebirth, which came out in 2020 was a great step forward for this series. Amnesia Rebirth took the core gameplay mechanics of the first Amnesia and made it next level with a game that not only had deep lore and narrative, with great voice acting and dark imagery but also incorporated different playable levels within different visual styles, all part of the same dark story, a nonstop tale of horror located on the Algerian Desert.This new game in turn scratches all of the advances made on the previous game and goes back to doing the same thing that it was already done 15 years ago, which of course could be seen as a nostalgic return to the game that defined not only this studio but a whole new era in gaming.... The problem with that is, instead of coming up as a purist experience referring to the original Amnesia (that it was still present in Rebirth as well) in turn it comes out as a bare bones, stripped down Amnesia game which loses all the advances done in the last one, and it just looks like a spin off (in terms of story it refers to the world of Rebirth, but just as a passing word without ever going into any detail about it) and it terms of gameplay it just ends up being more annoying than anything else.The mystery of the creature is gone, and there's not any kind of novelty about it. The design is uninspired, the origins of it are expected at best, yawning at worst and the dark atmosphere is just gone.You will be scared, but mostly annoyed. The game world and story are just not interesting. They don't do anything besides putting you in a dreary situation and then adding ten obstacles to make you "game".Problem is the gameplay is nothing to talk about.Main gameplay mechanic is an energy generator which needs to be fueled constantly in order to illuminate the bunker itself. This could be an analogue mechanic to the lighter and the torches in Rebirth which added tension, but in this case, you have this one only generator for the whole complex which you have to come back constantly because it runs out of fuel literally every 5 to 15 minutes (in normal difficulty) and it just becomes your main activity for most of the game.You can explore the game in total dark, but then you miss out on seeing anything (of whatever little there is to see)At least the game offers you three difficulty levels including easy in which you are given more time for each generator recharge (but beware that it also changes other parameters such as creature behavior).Amnesia The Dark Descent was a game that despite its technical (and budget) limitations created an engaging story (regardless of being told mainly in texts and some abstract imagery).Amnesia Rebirth took all those elements from Dark Descent to the next level and went deep into the lore and added larger and more varied levels with more scenes with great voice acting as well.Amnesia The Bunker went ten steps backwards maybe thinking that "less is more" but in doing so tripped itself into a dark hole and it never came out.Here's hoping that Frictional games finds again the light that took them from Dark Descent to Soma and then Rebirth and are able to move forward into a new unexplored adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended! A tense survival horror game with a unique gameplay loop compared to the previous entries in the series. The difficulty settings were a welcome surprise. The decision to  was hilariously devious. The setting was great and very different for the genre. I always hope for more other-world lore and references to previous games, but after Rebirth gave me a ton, I am fine that Bunker kept it more subtle. This one was scary, especially before you get the hang of it, though I think Rebirth actually scared me more. Regardless, very fun. Mixing things up in the end was smart, to avoid letting players get too comfortable with the threats. As a long-time fan with a ton of nostalgia and love of the lore, I hope Frictional Games continue to put out quality games like this and explore the Amnesia universe further in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Horror fans are eatin' good this year, and it just keeps getting better with Amnesia: The Bunker!With a fresh gameplay take on Amnesia, bringing live-sim aspects to the series, this title stands out among the franchise. The campaign is short and sweet with the most replayability out of any previous title. From sound design to animations, the devs have nailed this spooky atmosphere, and the HPL engine keeps chugging along for each title to be timeless.Everyone at Frictional should be extremely proud of this one!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horrors I have ever played.It's not without its flaws, but they don't take much away from the game being amazingPros:-Genuinely horrifying-Beautiful-Wonderfully balanced with the amount of ammo and resources you get-The game doesn't have the issue that most survival horrors do where the player just has a peashooter gun that feels like it does nothing. Each bullet has a massive impact.-Difficult at points but not over the top-Surprisingly easy to run the game-Actually interesting notes / story (most games with a note system have me skipping the notes because they're either just way too damn long or don't add anything to the story and are just full of nothing-burgers)Cons:-Sometimes the monster sticks around for WAY too long, I found myself sitting around for half an hour at points waiting for it to disappear, thin 1-way hallways with minimal looping doesn't serve well for attempting to sneak around the monster. This is capable of being bypassed by making a distraction of some kind though.-Sometimes rats don't respond to your attempts to scare them off, being completely unphased by torches or gas grenades, causing you to waste additional resourcesThe cons are noticeable, however the amount of good that the game does is FAR beyond the cons, and it is still EXTREMELY good. People who enjoyed alien isolation are sure to love this too. I won't say that everyone will love it, because some are more nitpicky about super small things than I am, but I can say it is definitely a very enjoyable experience and I loved the entire game.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply fantastic. To me a genuine 10/10.The story is great to piece together, but never it's never spelled out for you. The atmosphere is phenomenal.It's scary and tense, and definitely makes you feel helpless, which makes your efforts to hurt/avoid the monster feel so much more rewarding. The visuals are amazing too. I never encountered any bugs, and any time I got caught I knew what I did wrong. I genuinely cannot think of a flaw in this game. _childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The devs really hit this game out of the park. Wonderful survival system, terrifying enemy, twisting claustrophobic tunnels, the whole works. The game stays scary the whole way through, without devolving into a shooter looter once you understand how the enemy ai works like some games do.I only give two complaints. The first one is that the game is a tad short, but the stunning execution of the hand crafted environment made up for it. As soon as I finished, I got the urge to replay again on a higher difficulty.The second complaint is that the inventory is just a little too teensy tiny. This is an intentional design decision, but it mostly just punishes new players who don't know when they need to carry certain key items like door grenades or wrenches. One or two more slots would have felt nice for normal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is a very effective horror experience. I feel like this is something which needs mentioning, as most of the discourse online (in my perception, at least) surrounding it doesn't ever touch on it. The game itself has a very thick, oppressive atmosphere, and having to use rare resources to do very simple things creates palpable tension. It is a very effective game in that aspect, as long as you play on Normal or Hard.The issues come, in my experience, from the length. To me the game was worth the asking price, but keep in mind I'm someone who plays games slowly and methodically, and I get very immersed in the game. If you're looking for an experience which emulates Amnesia: The Dark Descent in length and content, you're not going to find it. The game can be beaten very, very quickly if you don't explore much. I would argue the game is priced a bit too high, and if that puts you off, wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10This is my 1st Amnesia game I've ever played, let alone 100% completed. (All 44 Achievements)The game is extremely good, well made as well as fine tuned, the gameplay is really fun, balanced & fair. The only bugs or issues I ever ran into was two dog tags number codes for the lockers had not been saved so i had to go though 9999 number combos twice to guess the code for the two lockers but after the first playthough this was not an issue and due to the achievements i had played the game 4+ times and the issue/bug only happened in my first playthough so just make sure that you read/note the codes on the dogtags and make sure they are listed or saved.The sounds & music is really good & fitting, the physics & fighting for what little fighting you do is really well done, as for the stealth & hiding mechanics are top notch if your good at it, as for the hardcore modes they are surprisingly done very nicely as are more realistically fair then other game's hardcore modes. the lore and story are also very well done.You can get this at 50% off or more but i highly recommend this!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Remember how the monster encounters and chases in Amnesia: TDD would ultimately end and you would get a "calm" break in between? Yeah......The Bunker gives you no such breaks.This game is SCARY. Not only do you have a terrifying monster breathing down your back throughout the whole game, but you also have to worry about keeping the lights on. Said lights prevent (mostly) aforementioned monster from free roaming wherever it likes as it stalks you.The departure from the amnesia series traditional gameplay is a very fun and unique direction. It adds whole new elements within the game that make it arguably scarier than even TDD.I don't think this game is for everyone. However, if you are willing to learn and adapt to the new survival mechanics, then you might be in for the scariest gaming experience of the year!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I have not quite finished the game, although I am close on my first playthrough. This feels like a very tight and well polished experience, and much more akin to The Dark Descent in its feel than I think many would say of Rebirth and a Machine for Pigs. Progression is non-linear, there is instead a single level you are placed in and you can explore the areas in any order you want, barring any locked/blocked doors that require certain items. There are tons of items to collect, and multiple ways to go about completing your tasks, whether it be carefully and stealthily or loud and bombastic. There is also the added resource management of fuel, ammo, etc. This is incredibly well balanced though, there is just enough fuel to fill up the generator multiple times but its spread out such that you can easily run out if you dont ration correctly. Ammo as well is scarce enough that this avoids becoming an FPS, and while the monster for me stopped being "scary" I was still on edge because of its presence as I only had a couple of bullets to deal with it.All in all, a fantastic experience, and even with custom story support to increase the playabilityMy only gripe is that I am left absolutely wanting more of this gameplay and setting because it worked so well for me. Heres hoping there some kind of expansion on the idea!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5. I enjoyed the atmosphere and gameplay. My only nitpick was my frustration when in certain sections I should have known in advance to bring certain gear with me which the limited inventory space discourages. In part because of this, at times I was pulled out of immersion due to the resource and gear focus --- I tended to load the game relatively often to avoid waste, instead of seeing things through.

_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I have played Amnesia the Dark Descent on Playstation when I got it for free and I didn't particularly like it. The Bunker is quite different. It's a survival horror game, and that survival aspect is really what drew me in. After having finished the game, I am proud to say that this was a great experience. It's not exactly the hardest thing, you can just hide from the monster and it'll go away usually. Still, I played on normal and died quite a few times. I really did like the way you are given very few bullets, but for me I ended up stockpiling other resources in my saferoom. The generator doesn't keep the monster away (to my dismay), but it shortens the damned things' patrols. The ending makes sense, and I would love to see something in the same vein from the developers. This experiment of a game was a success in my book, and I hope they make more like this. Good work Frictional. Hope to see you in another review.

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. Love the environments, sound, audio. I read peoples comments in threads about the 60fps lock, but I don't see a problem with it.  People mentioned about it being a short game (four hours casual play), but that's a decent length for me. Replay value is decent. Locker combination is randomized to keep it a tad fresh.10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This game Is absolutely amazing, I love how you can go through the game and simply just escape the bunker or you can read the notes that your fellow comrades left behind  to fully immerse yourself  in the situation and gain an understanding of what happened while you were unconscious. The game play is fantastic, you have to scavenge around the bunker for supplies all while making sure your generator doesn't run out of fuel because if it does, you're screwed. This happened to me and it made the game extremely frighting, I was crawling around the dark trying to find ways to find fuel all while avoiding the beast that was hunting me down. There are moments in this game where you genuinely feel like you're in a horror film and its awesome.  I appreciate how the game makes you choose what supplies you want to carry with you because of your limited bag space, if you find something useful you may have to drop something that's less important than what you found, so the game puts you in a situation where you must make sacrifices. Luckily items don't despawn so you can always come back and pick it up later. My only wish is that this game was a little longer, I beat it in around 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely my favorite Frictional game. The story is great, the voice acting , sound effects, the atmosphere. And gosh was I scared the first few hours being trapped in a bunker with a "stalker".Interesting mechanics with the run reloading. But made it feel more real. Overall I highly recommend this game if you enjoy that not typical linear game style.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: After four playthroughs, I can comfortably say that this is one of the best horror games I've played. Frictional Games used everything they learnt from Amnesia TDD, Justine and other games like Alien Isolation to craft one of the most effective and interesting horror experiences. I can sit here and say I wish it was longer or had more replayability- I can comfortably beat the game in less than thirty minutes at this point- but for its price and what it was trying to do, Amnesia: The Bunker doesn't miss.What I Want more than anything for the future of this game is a mode with a randomized map and randomized objectives. Some interesting game modifiers like having a larger bunker or two monsters could go a long way to turn this from a 6 hour single experience for most players to an infinitely replayable and revisitable lifetime experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the game In one sitting I will divide this review into two sections one being horror (What makes it a good horror game) and interesting (What makes the game interesting basically) -   - Horror (What makes it a good horror game) 1) The monster isn't afraid of the light the game makes you think like you have a choice but you don't it comes out of it's hiding holes and will attack you if you make too much noise (Granted the lights do flicker when it's nearby which is possibly why it comes out).2) Your actions will have consequences the game says this, whatever you do you'll have to live with it an example being you weren't fast enough when using the generator and it ran out of fuel and now you playing the monsters game complete darkness. But hey it isn't that bad you got a noisy flashlight.3) The monster kinda acts like the alien from alien isolation which is pretty neat they both make noise when moving around the place and they camp a certain spot where they believe they heard the player. - Interesting ( What makes the game interesting) 1) The reason why this game is interesting is because it's set in WW1 and it's a horror game and I personally believe this is the first of it's kind. 2) Your actually allowed to fight back delay the inevitable what ever suits you fancy. 3) It's a fast paced horror game basically your on a time limit the time limit being the generator you have to run if you fast enough then the monster won't be able to hop out and kill you. This is all I can really think of and really all I can put by helping out players sort of and putting a good review without spoiling anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played many horror games but this game was a TON of fun. I really enjoyed the mechanics of having to avoid and hide from a creature using whatever tools you have at your disposal. Having to keep a generator fueled to keep the monster at bay added an extra challenge that almost felt like a mini game in a way. The fear I experienced when my generator went dark for the first time and I was far away from the safe room just for the monster to start hunting me was so scary and exciting. Once you play for a while the monster becomes a bit less scary as you understand its behavior more and more and how to deal with / avoid it. However, the game has a lot of difficulty customization that you can add to your game which adds good replay ability. The story and setting I found really cool as well. I had a ton of fun playing this, definitely one of the most fun horror games I have played I would really recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I felt sad when I beat this game, I was sad that it was over. We just don't get enough of these short but VERY sweet survival horror games. When this game says "If you think something might work, it probably does" it really means it. The climax of the game was something I beat in one try. Not because it was too easy, (It wasn't) but because I had an idea on how to beat it and it just so happened to work. And let me just say... the climax was VERY fulfilling... As someone who craves a horrifying creature feature, this definitely scratched the itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: God, I love this game. Only once or twice a year does a game grab my imagination and adoration like this. I dreamt about the game, I woke up giddy to get back to it, I thought about while I showered. I want to replay it at some point, but even if I only play it the one time, I won't forget this game for a long time.I don't like games where you can't defend yourself against enemies, which is why I have never played an Amnesia game before this. While the monster you are pitted against can't be killed, you are far from defenseless. In the beginning the game appears to be an Outlast (or perhaps Amnesia) style cat and mouse affair, as you come to understand the systems at play it morphs into a bloody-knuckle duel to the death. Although the game becomes less "scary" as you master its mechanics, the fear is replaced with equally visceral thrills.I could go on, but if you want a tight and focused survival horror which is willing to both beat the piss out of you and accept a beating in return, get this game. It's a steal at 25 dollars, they could have easily charged 40 and I would have been happy.

_childDocuments_.review: While it doesn't reach the story highs of SOMA or feel as tight overall in the game play department as The Dark Descent, what The Bunker manages to accomplish in terms of overall immersion reiterates once again that no one does it quite like Frictional.The combination of traditional survival horror game play, immersive sim elements, and Frictional's patented "i-can't-see-♥♥♥♥-holy-♥♥♥♥-what-was-that-noise, run-from-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" technology left me staring in slack-jawed amazement.My first play through was on Hard which I would absolutely not recommend to anyone as this type of game play just doesn't leave a good first impression when you're already trying to push the game to its limits.Play this EXACTLY how Frictional expects you to...- Normal Difficulty (or Easy if you're the reason your parents got divorced)- Lights OFF- Face DOWN- Ass UPTake your time. Immerse yourself in the game's world. Take your pants off.Become Henri.Become Amnesia.Become the Bunker.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like i was more stressed out or high in anxiety than scared.The Time attack mechanic of fuel was so stress inducing i was more focused on that and scaring myself than the actual monster. Maybe a final note before fighting the guy in that last level to help elude to more weird things would have been cool or something.Also your flashlight is useless, which this kinda killed the game for me, and the lighter is even more of a fail.I would be excited to see another attempt in this format, but with a little more of a mental/stress break and the levels a little more intertwined. _childDocuments_.review: It's rare that I abandon games in the middle, because I carefully choose what I play. Time is valuable! In this case it seemed I made a solid pick: I enjoy much of the Frictional Games catalog. But the bottom line is that I do not like .On the surface it seems to be less of a walking-sim, like the rest of the  series, and more survival horror, like Frictional's early  games. What you might not realize before buying is how brutally the bare-bones formula is applied here. What formerly was a gameplay element is now the entire game.Specifically,  is all about hiding from randomly distributed and randomly appearing enemies, looking for randomly located objects, and managing a tiny amount of resources with a very limited carrying capacity. And you're constantly on timers for dwindling fuel and batteries. It's just anxiety, all anxiety, all the time. There are some puzzles, but you're unable to consider them at your own pace.My gameplay loop essentially consisted of "raids" out of the (only) safe space: Go explore, collect some items until my pockets were full, return to safe space. Progress was slow and halting. The randomly appearing enemies were scary the first few times, but later just annoying as I would simply run away or hide until they moved on. The bottom line is that the enemies are arbitrary obstacles rather than satisfying challenges.Alas, the story is cliché and uncompelling from the very beginning. After getting tired of the gameplay loop in a couple of hours, I realized I didn't care enough to push through to the end. It would be just more of the same.Skip this one.I wish I could say: Play the demo first to see if you like it, but apparently Frictional removed the demo from Steam. It's easy to guess why:  is a game that lends itself to just a couple of hours of play, maybe for streamers to scream on camera and then move on. I imagine a lot of people played the demo, enjoyed it for what it was, but didn't feel a need to play a full game of it. So, no sale for Frictional. That's just the kind of game this is, better suited to be a free demo than a full experience. It's simply not what I'm looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: After just recently playing through the entire Amnesia series for the first time I must admit something; I think Amnesia: The Bunker is the best of the series. While it does suffer a couple of issues, it's the most engaging game Frictional Games has ever made in my opinion.The story this time is you play as a French WW1 soldier named Henri Clément. After a brief tutorial in which you , you suddenly wake up alone in the titular bunker; a vast underground labyrinth converted by your fellow countryman into their base of operations. From this point you notice something is severely wrong; the base is disturbingly quiet save for the sound of artillery fire hitting the ground above you rattling the whole complex. You soon come to realize why; there is a monster on the loose in the complex and most of your fellow countrymen have already been slaughtered by it. The few who survived escaped the bunker and decided that blowing up the only exit would be the best way to contain the beast. This is where Henri finds himself now; trapped in the vast complex he must assemble a bomb capable of destroying the rubble that blocks the exit. Frictional Games has taken more of a hands-off approach when it comes to the narrative in The Bunker and I quite enjoyed the way it was left up to the player to uncover the finer details of the story. It feels like a complete 180 when compared to Frictional Games' previous title Amnesia: Rebirth which really emphasized its narrative and the characters in it. Rest assured if you prefer to uncovered the story yourself rather than having it explicitly told to you, then you will enjoy this. As a huge fan of the narrative storytelling found in games like Metroid Prime & Prey (2017) for example, I loved the way the tale was told in The Bunker. The WW1 setting is also used extremely well here and I wouldn't mind having the next Amnesia game set in the same time period.So with your goal set (assemble the necessary components to build the bomb and escape) you must now scavenge the bunker for supplies, diary entries to piece the story together, and valuable tools that will allow you explore the furthest sections of the base. All the while you must avoid the beast as it stalks the halls. You have a couple of weapons you can use to temporarily scare the beast away from the area you're exploring, but it can't be killed and it will return before too long. If you've played Alien: Isolation then you'll be familiar with this type of gameplay. Much like the Xenomorph in that game, any loud or sudden noises will draw the attention of the beast and you must either hide or be prepared to engage it with what little firepower you have. There's an extreme emphasis on inventory management in The Bunker. So much so that one of its core mechanics is centered around it; the generator. In order to keep the lights running in the bunker (as well as other mechanisms that require power throughout the facility) you must keep the generator fueled with gasoline. If the generator runs out of gasoline the lights will go out leaving you more vulnerable to the beast. As such you'll be constantly deliberating with yourself whether to turn the generator on or off before you go out exploring the furthest sections of the bunker. Because gasoline too is a limited resource that you must only use when absolutely necessary.All of these mechanics (and a few others I intentionally left out for you to discover for yourself) come together to form what is in my opinion the best Amnesia game. The story is extremely interesting assuming you admire the time period it's set in as well as appreciate how the game leaves the finer details of its story up to you to uncover. The few issues I have with The Bunker is that I wish it was a bit longer and some of the immersive-sim elements aren't fully realized. For example: if there's a locked wooden door why am I not able to burn it if I throw gasoline on it and light it? Another minor issue is the graphics. I think the game looks good overall but I honestly think Amnesia: Rebirth looked better. Yes most of the time you're scurrying around in darkness so I get you're not gonna see as much detail in the environment as you did in the bright Algerian desert of Rebirth, but even with all lights on in The Bunker it just doesn't look quite as good. You would think a smaller environment with minimal open areas would allow for far more greater visual detail but alas that's not quite the case for The Bunker. Nevertheless Amnesia: The Bunker sets the bar even higher for the series moving forward and I for one can't wait to see what Frictional Games puts out next.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of frictional games, always buy their next game, and amnesia the dark descent is mine and a lot of other's favorite in the franchise. The bunker is a interesting turn from the previous's rebirth, in that it's less talking, less waiting, more playing.However, though this game is going in the right direction, away from rebirth but closer to the dark descent, it's still not good enough. You are set in a bunker in WW1, where there's something with you, something unknown that chases you but Instead of multiple monsters, there's only 1, instead of hallucinations and jump scares, there's none, other than the monster. In the original amnesia, there where many dangers around every corner, you never felt safe. In bunker, the only danger is the monster killing you, or you dying from your own mistakes.So when there's no monster, there's no scares, just darkness but with dark descent, there was always a scare around the corner. Most of my time was spent hoping to gain some progress, before returning to save without dying. Honestly, i wouldn't be able to watch someone else play it without falling asleep since nothing ever happens.Death is also less scary in this game and instead more annoying as you lose any progress gained before last save and the monster's actions are random, one time, hiding works, another it fails like throwing a dice. It's unpredictable and very annoying when it happens.Even worse, the "crafting" system is very poor, there's barely any items you can craft and at the end of the game, i had a ton of materials i never needed. they do say its random gen, so you could get one game with more and one with less but still, i kept feeling i had too many items for what was required.I'd give this game a 6/10. it kinda feels like a dumbed down rebirth, less talking and story but still a lot of walking back and forth to save every small progress that's made before getting insta killed by a big walking rat. it's also less scary than rebirth, never felt like i wanted to quit or even look behind me and i get scared easily! Wouldn't recommend. Hopefully we get some good custom stories though!

_childDocuments_.review: AMNESIA:Isolation Better than Rebirth for sure, A great return to form for Frictional.The mechanics are great and refreshing and handling a gun in Amnesia game feels strange and good. I kind of wish the game was a bit longer or more story heavy.The ambiance, the sound design, the story, the hovering presence of the monster were all done well......The monster is 100% Lambert.

_childDocuments_.review: If you finished this on shell shock with aggressive rats and without full subs or maxed gamma, I admire you! Hope you have great coping mechanisms for your newly acquired ptsd!  Does this game get frustrating at some point? Yes, absolutely. But it's still a very cool experience. And although I only planned to play for the story once, I still replayed it and had fun. If there will be any updates and new modes, I will totally play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia The Bunker IS survival horror. No other game I know of has been able to maintain tension and dread the entire game. Certainly not Resident Evil games. (which I do love by the way) The locations are DARK. You will receive a flashlight you have to pull to operate every 30 seconds or so that WILL attract the monster. Any other source of light is a GAMBLE as to whether or not you will receive it that playthrough. The monster is very effective and scary. I believe his AI is done very well; it is a gamble as to whether or not the monster will spot you in the place you chose to hide. But I think where this game really shines is the SOUND DESGIN. The sound of your footsteps in the bunker, the sound of the monster crawling throughout the walls, the sound of bombs exploding above you, the sound of shotguns pumping from mentally unstable people in the bunker - im sure I’m missing a few other notable sounds but it is all extremely EFFECTIVE. I believe the cherry on top is the reload animations and the way shooting feels. It is realistic and takes time unlike most FPS games. I highly recommend this game and believe it is priced very fairly. The only downside is that once you’ve finished the game once you never get that same sort of dread you experience the first time. Nonetheless this is a great game made by a smaller studio and I hope that we get something in the same vein in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good and chilling experience, definitely feels new and fresh, it gives a chilling experience because of the "beast" which is the monster that you see fairly early on when you enter the bunker where most of the times you find yourself in the dark, even though the generator is on there are some places where its dark and terrifying, the sound design is amazing and the story is also very good, 10/10 I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker offers a great horror atmosphere with decent replay ability, including a custom difficulty menu upon starting a New Game+. The backdrop of World War I is not a very common setting in horror games, and I absolutely loved it. The game also encourages players to experiment with different playstyles and offers many different solutions to bypassing obstacles and completing objectives. The story is mostly told through notes and clues hidden throughout the game, and allows the player to piece together the story over time. The voice acting and sound effects are quite good, and the game teaches the player to rely on audio cues and be vigilant. Overall, it was a blast to play this game, and I hope Frictional Games can keep up the great work.
