_childDocuments_.review: As an Amnesia Fan Im highly dissappointed.The game didnt catch me. It was scary in the beginning but it quickly lost the appeal when you sit under a bed and hope it waddles by quickly so you can get to it.Im a huge Anmesia Fan and was excited to see where the story connects here- well, lets just say it was very dissappointing.The only reason I finished the game was because I wanted to see the story to the end and i was very underwhelming.Would this have been a game on its own it probably would have been okay, scary, alot of replay value and very modable but its not an Amnesia Game.________Game Spoilers:As I said I dont see this as an Amnesia Game for several points:- the protagonist had Amnesia but it wasnt story relevant whatsoever- we had little to no connection to the other games- the dude in the basement was not really explained but talking to him would have been very fun/interesting/lore-intense(Yes I know he went crazy because of the book in the catacombs but still-)- no visit to the other world, no hinting towards Alexander, nothing ??? - the last room with the bridges hinted at something otherworldly, but there was nothing- if you hadnt played the other games you wouldnt know why Lambert wanted to induce more suffering, why he was changing etc- WORST of it all why was there no water level? That is THE scariest thing Amnesia!I do admit that it could be that I just didnt find these things but my point stands.I really, really love horror games but this one was simply not one of my favourites. I still am and will always be an Amnesia Fan but this game added nothing to a very interestng world.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I am not embarrassed to admit I've only beaten it on the VERY EASY setting. If you have the nerves to deal with having Big Homie after you on the harder difficulty levels, than you're a cooler machine than I am. And this game has many difficulty levels in addition to a custom mode which lets you hand tailor many parameters of the game to your taste.The Bunker takes place in the middle of WW1, and is very clearly in the same universe as the other games of the Amnesia Franchise. No new real ground is uncovered here as far as the story is concerned. Briefly you will read about, and then see things which are familiar, but the game and the character do not dwell on them. This game is all about SURVIVAL. It's about hiding. And running. And coming up with multi step plans QUICKLY and executing them PERFECTLY while the stakes couldn't be higher. The Bunker takes place during WW1 but is kind of indifferent towards the war as such. The characters are painted in only broad, minimal strokes. The way to enjoy this game is to try to place YOURSELF in Henri's boots, and then you will be too busy trying to survive to even worry about the story too much. I am hoping that future titles go back to exploring this amazing world Frictional has created a bit more, but I appreciate the fact that for The Bunker, they wanted to shake things up a bit and do a different take on the format we've all come to expect. Recommended for those familiar with the series. If this were to be your first exposure to Amnesia, you might not come back again.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Steam says that I've played this game for just under 7 hours, but I feel like I've played it for 20.There is so much dread in knowing that danger is around the corner, but apply that to every corner and you have a game that is extraordinarily intense.The story is nothing to scuff at, either. Especially for an Amnesia game, which from my point of view have always been games known more for their horror than their story. There are twists and turns, and every note you find adds some kind of detail to the world that you wouldn't get if the game just outright narrated it to you.What I find the most interesting is how the map is designed. Specifically, the whole map of the game is just one, big interconnected bunker (naturally, by the game's title). You will often revisit parts of the map several times, but it hardly ever feels as repetitious as it would be in inferior games. Every trip to an area is always dreadful thanks to the Monster's perpetual presence; you're never safe, and every approach, even to an area you've already explored, is usually different because of it. Safe to put it this way, this game is phenomenal. If you're a fan of the Amnesia series, this is a step up in ways that make the rest of the franchise look stale by comparison. Bonus points if you've played Alien: Isolation, which is the closest comparison I can make for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Genuinely one of the scariest games I've played in a very long time. There are plenty of interesting mechanics I could talk about, but the main one is the flashlight mechanic. It's the best in any game I've ever played. In most games it's just a regular flashlight that stays on forever, or it requires batteries you have to find, or it's a torch, a flare, a lantern that needs fuel, whatever. In this game your flashlight needs you to rev it like a generator. You pull a string for a couple seconds and it gives it the light, and you have to keep charging it periodically or else it goes out. Depending on how much charge you give it'll be brighter or dimmer, but if you want a full light you need to spend the precious time to charge it. The only issue is it makes a lot of noise, so the question is, do you risk making the sound and be able to see where to run away and not get lost or possibly spot the monster, or do you stay quiet and wander in the dark, potentially walking right up to the creature or getting lost? It's extremely intense when I hear the monster come in, it's pitch black, and I abandon trying to be stealthy and I spend 3 seconds charging my flashlight before sprinting away into the darkness in pure panic. It's such a great mechanic that creates a lot of risky and terrifying scenarios.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I prefer both A Machine for Pigs and Rebirth, but I really appreciate the different thing they tried with this one. It's very much Alien Isolation as a stripped down immersive sim Metroidvania. None of the "story" will make any sense if you haven't played at least Rebirth, but there's not much even if you have the background info. A fun, bite size experiment from Frictional that kind of looks back to Penumbra in a lot of ways.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really, REALLY great Survival Horror game. It focuses less on story(while still having a good story) and more on fleshed out mechanics that are satisfying and fun to play with. The game is more limited than it tells you in some senses, but it still provides more overall freedom than other games of its genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Just outstanding. Scariest game I have ever played, bar none. Blows Rebirth out of the water and almost made me poop my pants. Sound design (especially), graphics, general direction are all 10/10 and the story is sad, engaging, and haunting. Replayability is surprisingly high given the AI of the "Beast" as well as item placement. Speaking of, I'm due for a full replay on Halloween. 100,000% recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I had little hope for this game. Amnesia:Rebirth was a slap in the face to many fans, as it simply did not meet expectations and instead went against the Amnesia formula. However, Amnesia: The Bunker has ignited a renaissance of interest in the series and has met most, if not all, expectations from myself and the community. The claustrophobic and eerie tunnels once inhabited by the French, now a hunting ground for a seemingly durable predator, were the perfect choice and executed in a manner that is befitting of the title.The environment is well designed, and the atmosphere is impressive. The most notable addition is the ability to defend yourself from the threat. But that does not mean you can kill it. Ammunition is scarce and your last resort.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Really like this game. It quite cleverly sets up the atmosphere and gives you constant uncertainty of whats around the corner. There are quite limited supplies and something like fuel youll burn through very fast forcing you to explore more while being on the main quest. You are constantly given the option to play it safe and be happy with what you have or gamble and go out loud on a door maybe or a trap which adds more to the pressure. The map isnt that big but its quite nicely memorable. I think it has just the right length for it not to be too boring but also for you not to just finish it in one sitting (unless you dont sleep at night that is). Overall i definitely recommend the game. If you are hesitant just wait for sale.A note for achievement hunters at this point in time some achievements may be buggy forcing you to replay but it doesnt take long to do these achievements. But play the game first then focus on achievements its worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like Frictional Games have crafted a terrific new formula for the survival horror genre, much like when From Software crafted the Souls formula in Demons Souls and then Dark Souls.There's a lot of potential and I'm excited to see where FG can take this.As for Amnesia: The Bunker itself, it's an incredible experience. Tense, intimate and deeply unnerving. Frictional Games are masters of setting a mood. Exploring the map is a lot of fun, even with the monster creeping around you near-constantly. You get to know the map very well, so much so that you can quite easily navigate it in the dark if you're feeling brave and saving fuel for as of yet unexplored areas.The monster is scary, although not unreasonable. You start to understand it's nature quickly, and how to navigate around it. Not to say it still won't surprise or corner you! On my first run, I got caught by it a few too many times, and ended up .The story and voice-acting are solid. There's a lot of notes to pick up and read and was always excited to find more.I only wish the game were longer! I am on my second play through now, aiming to more fully explore every corner of the bunker this time. But I can't help but feel one final stage would have been ideal.Highly recommended to fans of the survival horror genre. And definitely don't just play easy mode, face your fears! (then run away and hide in the closet, like a true Amnesia veteran)
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Now this, this is absolutely amazing, after having completed the game myself, I can safely say that this is absolutely worth it, I could just simply recommend it and leave it at that, but oh boy there is a lot to unpackSet in the same universe as TDD, AMFP & Rebirth, with this game taking place only about 17 or so years after the events of AMFP, The Bunker is the next installment in the Amnesia series, the story is pretty good, the idea of a horror game set during the events of WW1 is brilliant, however, if you were expecting Rebirth levels of story, I'm sorry to disappoint, but this ain't it chief, the story is mostly told through notes, just like back in TDD, but other than that, it is not brought up much at all in the actual gameplay except for at the very start, which in my opinion works to its benefit, because unlike Rebirth, which leaned a little too heavy into prioritizing the story over the horror, this game is the complete opposite, leaning way more into the horror factor, which is perfectly captured, the Stalker is absolutely terrifying, every time I hear it move inside the walls around me, I freak out.Everything in the game is randomized, with only a couple of exceptions, every item, note & code is randomly placed throughout the bunker, giving the game a lot of replay value.The generator, while not to everyones liking, is an interesting implementation, sure, it may make the player feel like they have to rush through exploring, but I didn't feel that way, I found it rather intense, trying to get as much done as possible in time before the generator ran out, however, the same praise can not be given to the flashlight. The flashlight is.. not very reliable, I found myself leaving it behind more often than not, while it is nice that it does not require fuel, it makes a lot of noise while being wound up, which'll more often than not alert the monster, which, that is a fair trade off, I'm fine with the whole unlimited flashlight in exhange for making a lot of noise, , my biggest complaint is that it barely lasts for 20 - 30 or so seconds, if it lasted for maybe a minute to 1 and a half minutes at least, it would've been fine.I had a lot of fun playing through this game, I haven't had such a thrilling experience playing a horror game since I first played TDD. During my playthrough, I had.. a few blackouts, and let me tell you, it is some of the scariest feelings having to navigate through the dark, I was at one point forced to navigate through Maintenance during a blackout, where the stalker was out basically the whole time, that ♥♥♥♥ is scary, everything you do makes noice, and I mean .
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I can say it's a good one. For me, the best aspect of The Bunker is that it has actual gameplay, and it's not a sometimes scary, but most of the time boring walking simulator (*cough* A Machine for Pigs *cough*). You have to find resources, tools, combine them, manage your inventory, like in good old Penumbra. People tend to expect to relive the very feeling they had with The Dark Descent. They won't, because it's impossbile. If you keep that in mind, and don't try to look for faults during your playthrough, you'll have a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best horror game Ive played in years. It feels like a combination of Alien: Isolation, Resident Evil: Village and the best parts of Amnesia.This time instead of the Amnesia main character having a panic attack in the dark, you'll just experience one yourself if you're stuck in the dark.The sound design is insane, a glass bottle rolling across the floor has never sounded this terrifyingly loud while you're trying to sneak around.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game if you like survival horror / immersive sims.  Very similar to Monstrum / Alien Isolation. Not a straight hide & seek game though as you have some ways of (temporarily) fighting off the monster. They also just added a new mode that adds a ton of replay ability.  Highly recommend if you are into the aforementioned things.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love The Bunker, it's easily my favorite horror game.I love the setting, "The Bunker" makes you feel trapped and often vulnerable despite the tools you have in your disposal. The sound design in some parts of the game I can't get over, the revolver you get at the start of the game really has some unique weight to it that I haven't been this impressed with in many other places. I adore the story as well, I don't tend to read all these little notes in games like this but Frictional Games really captivated me with the story they created here. Basically, I think this game is incredible and an easy play for people who enjoy horror games or want to get into them. I feel honored I was able to play this game before I had it spoiled by watching any playthroughs of it first. I'll definitely try my best to force my friends to play this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic horror title!After 100% all achievements, including the BRUTAL Shell Shock Difficulty mode, it's safe for me to say that Amnesia: The Bunker is easily in my Top 5 Horror Games of All Time along side The Suffering, The Beast Inside, Silent Hill 2 and Darkwood.Something that REALLY won my heart with this one was the pure freedom of expression when it comes to figuring out certain situations. For example, you may come across a locked wooden door. How do you open it? Well, here are some (hypothetically speaking) ways you may open it:- Blow it down with a grenade- Shoot it with a shotgun (1 shots wooden doors)- Have The Stalker (main monster of the game) chase you and break it down for you- Go around to the next room and open the vents using a wrench- Go around to the next room and shoot the lock off from a hole in the wallAnd those are just SOME of the ways you might open a door. 10/10 horror game/sandbox game hands down. GET IT! DO IT!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia is back~! No, I'm serious this is a pretty good entry into the series and with the failure of Machine for Pigs and Rebirth this entry doesn't look to disappoint and it takes from Aliens as you avoid a beast in a bunker and honestly I've had no issues with this game at it's core and the game is VERY immersive and I enjoy that because honestly I feel this is a return to form and the "gun" doesn't take away from the game.I will say there were a few bugs and loading but beyond that games solid and I'd recommend it if you haven't played Amnesia and if you have well this is the Amnesia you've been waiting for.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: frictional games has made some of the best horror games ever they have never made a bad game..... until now!amnesia the bunker has to be the worst amnesia game ever infact i still say this should have been penumbra cause it would suit the title and the series so well. but i'm sure this will tie in with the other amnesia games but this is just awful the gameplay is fine kind of the story is great everything about it is good except the fact that you only have ONE! place to save there is no auto save what so ever even when picking up key items or doing important things like the old games which makes the game difficult to the point to where you spend hours and hours making no progress ON NORMAL DIFFICULTY!it has gotten to the point to where i literally cannot progress at all and i am stuck in an infinite loop of running back to point B dying spawning all the way back at save point dying again for the 5th time in a row than rage quiting. it really seems like games these days are forgetting about the casual gamers the gamers who just want to play and enjoy the game. i know i can put it on easy but since i am a youtuber who is recording this starting all over and making my way all the way back to where i am now is NOT an option. so if they could update the game and ad an auto save feature that would be fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: What an outstanding game. I loved every second of playing it.The Game play is so much fun, from managing resources, to sneaking around the enemy, to solving puzzles/problems in multiple ways all made me not want to stop playing. This game is SCARY, and not in the lazy jump scare way, I mean truly scary. With tension of when or if the beast will come out, find you, or get you combined with the dread of losing your progress for a particular supply run and the overall uncertainty of what will happen next craft the a perfect kind of horror that isn't seen in other horror games.Like the previous titles, once you figure out the monster's behaviour, the fear generally goes a way to an extent, but not so much for this game as the monster will dynamically react to your actions and has the best design in the whole series. Yeah, he is still scary after seeing him 100 times. The beast reacts to your actions and choices. Need to get a door open and are a little too loud doing so? He will come for you. Are the lights on and you are walking to fast or upset one too many rats? You need to hide. But even hiding is only one of the options when dealing with the beast. This game provides such a freeing experience allowing several different play-styles to thrive within it. This was an instant favourite of mine and boasts being the only other game in the series to truly contend for my favourite, which is saying a lot considering the Dark Descent is in this series. I could gush forever about what I love about this game but I'll leave it at that, experience it for yourself if you  have not. The game was so good I even went the completionist route with it.This game reinvents the franchise in a way that makes me want so much more just like this, with the addition of weapons, a dynamic antagonist and a nonlinear environment (that has key components randomised for a unique experience with every play-through), Amnesia: the Bunker is a game I need more of.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The Bunker was a great experience, fun mechanics and riveting gameplay. I took it pretty slow in the beginning then gained more confidence, only to be caught out by the monster. I was playing the game with spectators, whenever I would be far away and the genny went out we'd all go "oh noo".The monster does get more aggressive the more you fight it. I beat the game in a little under 5 hours, anyway Frictional it's time to start working on The Bunker 2!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker could have been a great game, but unfortunately they had to center it around a boring Stalker type enemy, neglect the story and have a defunct gameplay loop.WW1, trenches, bunkers, Stahlgewitter, gas attacks, No Man's Land. WW1 offers many possibilities for a first class survival horror game. Unfortunately, Amnesia: The Bunker does not deliver.This game and setting would have worked much better as a Soma like "Walking-Simulator" or Resident Evil kind of game. The "monster"...could it have been any more generic? Probably not. Whats even worse, the main gameplay loop just does not work. Keeping the lights on by using the generator only means you will not need your flashlight. In all key areas (and you only go into key areas basically) , the monster will appear anyway, even if the lights are on.So why even bother? Well, you don't have to use the flashlight and and it takes maybe 1 minute longer for the monster to appear. Like all Stalker type enemies the monster in this game always gravitates towards you and therefore ends up being just annoying. Rubber band AI.Amnesia: The Bunker is mediocre.It's not terrible and can be fun occasionally, but there is just too much wasted potential for a positive rating.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I'd rather have a great experience, such as I have had, in the story telling, atmosphere, in previous games :Amnesia, The Dark descent, Soma, Rebirth, Penumbra.Don't understand why the last game Rebirth was polarizing, it had a great diverse experience, varied locations, atmosphere, production values, and was frankly, an experience that still exists in my mind A Masterpiece. Fractional, I am the epiphany of a fan boi... and it gives me great grief to say...In comparison: This game is barren, drab, and pretty much empty experience of a game. Shame on you Fractional for turning your backs on a core target audience who wants games as an experience, a great book, or interactive movie experience, which you truly have delivered previously.This is an experiment of a game. You are stuck in a drab bunker with a lame, procedurally stupid monster, randomized codes and items don't make interesting story. Saving is done in the hub and is pretty old school in that sense that you will feel punished for dying and have to do same thing over and over again as a result of death. I love old school, but it is not something I related to Fractional Games = guys making interesting games as experiences and stories. This is just tedious back and forth.I'll just leave this evil horror review instead looking forward to your next game.This one feels like an ancient relic from the 90's that should be buried.In a bunker.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A terrifying cat-and-mouse experience. Survival requires bravery, attentiveness, and invention. If you're like me and you love any game where 1) you become intimately familiar with a map's layout and 2) you have to plan your next steps carefully, then you will find tremendous satisfaction with this game. If you're brave enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely underwhelming compared to TDD and Penumbra.The game is VERY short and shallow. Only one monster, only a couple of rooms, NO puzzles at all. You can cheese through the entire game with zero difficulty after figuring out how the monster works.A massive step-down from The dark descent, and honestly, it's not much better than Rebirth.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I love the design philosophy put behind this game, I hope some day another project continues on this and iterates further on this concept, the imsim approach is a lovely contrast to Rebirth. I think even Frictionals future more narrative focused games could take some small ques from this game as well although I think contrasting games between each others is more appealing overall. Either way, lovely titles and it might honestly be my favorite project you guys have crafted.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: While the shortest game in the Amnesia series, it's the best gameplay wise. Game relies on more randomness than scripted sequences which is a huge plus for any survival horror game. I would have preferred less of the monster "vents" though as it felt too much like Alien Isolation. Story here is very light compared to rebirth. I think the price is fair for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely well done survival horror game that checks all boxes for me.  It is tense, stressful, and absolutely terrifying at points.  It takes a lot of my favorite parts of the genre like limited inventory and puzzles, and puts them in amnesia's wonderful storytelling and gameplay.  If you are a fan of Resident Evil, Alien Isolation, and the first Amnesia game, check this out!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game! Headphones on, light off. No distractions. The game has a clear goal, and the mechanics are great and simple, and i particularly like how immersive it is. The only real drawback I found was there's a few particular points that when switching between areas, there's a little studder (while the next section loads), which removes the immersion, even though my pc far exceeds the recommended specs.A definite recommendation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: They've tried something new this time around and I think it works great.I was worrying about my fuel and ammo, all the while flinching at every sound. Both the sound design and the visuals are fantastic and got me on the edge of my seat. The skittering in the walls, the bomb-shells, the flickering lights. All fantastic.I actually took the time to properly read every note I found as well, which I sometimes get lazy with in other games.When you have no other recourse but to run or hide, it really becomes stale and eventually just less scary. Though having those weapons, even when incredibly sparse, it gives you hope and safety. Then really makes you weary of using them, is it the right to do so? The game makes you think with such, doubly so when navigating the bunker as a whole with your resources.It took me 5 hours for my first play through, but I think there's room for a lot of replayability for those wishing for it.After the last Amnesia which I didn't hugely enjoy, I feel like Frictional Games have earned some graces back from me.Unfortunately I can't recommend it since they forced me to play as a  French person.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: My game of the year 2023, FOR SURE. Amnesia: The Bunker and Alien: Isolation are the scariest games I've ever played not because of the monsters or the scares, but the way both put you in uncomfortable situations where YOU have control of how you are going to handle the given situation.I champion immersive sims to everyone I know, but this is one of the greatest immersive sims I've played and PLEASE, PLEASE, Frictional Games, continue to make games of this ilk from now on.Easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this game.. but it gets boring after your first encounter with the monster. Which also isn't very scary as you can learn its patterns quickly. Puzzles are basically non existent/ super easy, and running back to fuel the generator every 15 minutes gets old fast. Custom stories are our only hope now. 2/5 ★
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic horror experience taking place inside a bunker during world war 1. Replayable do to item placement and locker codes being random. It's not terribly long, but offers a very immersive and scary adventure. I think it's probably my personal favorite setting Frictional has chosen for one of their horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The old feeling that we were introduced to by Amnesia: The Dark Descent over a decade ago is finally back! I really enjoyed all aspects of this game, its narrative and mechanics. My only note on it is that it may be a good idea to play the first run in Normal difficulty, because I would've liked to take more time to focus on the story and exploring than the Hard difficulty allowed me to.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so good it honestly makes me sad how this is such a short experience. I've never played an amnesia game before but this was an absolute masterpiece and it deserves some good rewards at E3, not many horror games have been able to scare me but this shook me to my core in a way that kept me coming back for more. Definitely worth your money and more, hopefully DLC or a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Say what you will about certain titles from Frictional Games, I personally always found Amnesia and Penumbra great titles to come back to on occasion even if some of them fell short of their origin for whatever reason that may be, and though the shortest experience by far, The Bunker still delivered a great performance for both long time fans and new people alike.It's easy to just say "Stick to a formula that works" but then that leaves no room for experimentation and innovation in ideas, you just get the same rehash of an existing product so I think the difference between all of the Amnesia titles is actually a good thing in my opinion and I love each one in their own way. Really looking forward to their next Amnesia title if one ever comes around...and would quite happily pay for another shorter experience like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is truly a return to form for the Amnesia series as a whole in my opinion.Having played Dark Descent when I was still a kid, a Machine for Pigs and a bit of Rebirth, I can wholeheartedly say that The Bunker is like the Dark Descent but significantly better.A lot of people have have rose tinted glasses for Dark Descent and that's fine, it's still a phenomenal game in its own right, but for a modern audience and the strides they've made for the Beast AI that hunts you down in the Bunker, it's truly an amazing piece of art.Amnesia: The Bunker is a survival horror game set in 1916 in the French trenches during World War 1.Like previous titles, your character doesn't know what has happened beforehand and has to navigate their way through the French bunker alone to try and find an escape.There are multiple ways to solve a lot of the puzzles and there are plenty of areas for you to explore but the Beast is always nearby.One of my favourite parts of the game is keeping the generator working, the Beast tends to come out less when the lights are on but it requires fuel which isn't exactly in abundance, a fun part of the game for me was managing when to go out in the dark and when to put the generator on.You do have a gun in The Bunker and it has some use, with diminishing returns, but I found it just made me -feel- safe rather than actually making me safe.The sound and level design is great, it's definitely a game for headphones, playing it through speakers will put you at a disadvantage since your headphones can track which direction the Beast is lurking. Story-telling in the game is a lot more passive, you'll find notes and documents everywhere which helps create the world a little bit better from before the Beasts attack, to just afterwards. This might not be for everyone, as you can play the game without knowing any of the context from start to finish but if you're into finding out more, then the notes are all there.Amnesia: The Bunker is a true return in my opinion for the Amnesia franchise, this game is genuinely horrifying and although it's not super long, because of the randomisation aspects of items etc in the game, it does have replayability. The game will have you tense and on the edge of your seat the entire time. Don't be afraid to gaslight yourself into thinking you can take the beast head on if running for a room if you've been stuck in a corner scared for well over fifteen minutes.Overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a true horror game and deserves an abundance of praise, if you like horror, if you like genuinely feeling on edge and scared. You'll love this game.9/10 - As if the horrors of World War 1 weren't bad enough on their own terms.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The Bunker represents the absolute peak of the Amnesia series' ambitions. The game is terrifying yet so compelling, endlessy replayable, and trains you to be an expert at jury-rigging improvisational solutions on the fly - my favourite element of video games. The base layout of the bunker remains the same, but door locks, traps, item placements, codes, threats, etc. - all are randomized at the beginning of each run. This necessitates thst you be constantly on your toes as you discover the environment and avoid the beast roaming its halls.. It's roguelite-meets-survival horror, and it's utterly brilliant.It's poised to be receiving a near-infinite amount of user content through a combination of sophisticated game systems and powerful modding tools. Frictional has even facilitated the process of creating and sharing total conversion mods. I'm eagerly looking forward to seeing the crazy machinations that people will make with these building blocks.The game length is pretty short, so it might not appeal to those looking for a disposable experience, but anyone wanting meaningfully reactive mechanics to contend with will be pushing long past the short first run.This is without a doubt my GOTY of 2023, and I'm thrilled to see what other devs will do to progress the systems at work here! Please enjoy :)
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna go against the grain and hype on this one and state flatly that this is not a good game.  Despite some interesting ideas on where to take the amnesia series, this just wasn't fun. The rewards of gameplay, trying to figure it all out aren't really there. The location is too samey. The enemy appears and strikes way too often and so you're no longer isolated and doing puzzle work. But it's the mix of chase and puzzling that I like the most and it's absent here.  The random generation of certain things, I could see being good for keeping the game fresh and solving the lets play problem, but I don't like it. I'm constantly pulled out of the game rather than being invested. I think the enemy appears too much because of the small map, the difficulty has to ramp up to make up for the lack of interesting location.  I think there are some cool things here, but I suspect modders may make a better game that suits me more than the story told by the devs here.  I think. Good try but I just can't like this game. I lose immersion when I don't see the point. Challenges at a certain point have to have meaning and I'm not seeing any here.What I think is this game for me is worth rock bottom budget title. Launch day pricing was simply not appropriate here in my view. But if you liked it, great for you. Wish I did.All that aside, I do like the environment and texturing work they've done here. It really shows they are at an advanced level of environmental 3D game dev. I think a twist on the game I'd probably like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I feel that this is the best Frictional Games title so far. I have never played Rebirth and I've honestly heard mixed reviews on it so I wont be using it in this comparison. I walked into The Bunker remembering my childhood playing The Dark Descent. Its length contrasts to The Dark Descent quite a bit. The map is smaller, the story is shorter. This doesn't make it any less engaging. The endgame objectives are handed to you from the start and it is up to you, how you achieve them.The Beast is dynamic and scary. You don't always know where it will come out and it could either be hunting you or possibly investigating a noise you made. The suspense was unparalleled by other Amnesia titles because in this case, The Beast is actually hunting you, following your blood trails and listening for your footsteps. It will find you more frequently then previous Amnesia monsters.The graphics are very reminiscent of other Amnesia titles and made me feel right at home. The gameplay mechanics are very similar as well. The old-fashioned click-and-drag mechanics are all still there and you may occasionally find items tucked away in desk drawers. The frequency of which seems way toned down from past experiences. Maybe FG realized we don't explicitly love searching every desk in the game.Playing this game, I received (just less than) 1 hour of playtime for every dollar I spent. I feel that this should be the bare minimum expected results on any difficulty. The fact that I almost reached 25 hours of play can be attributed to a handful deaths which genuinely scared me, and a bit of experimentation on my end. These experiences were particularly fun and thrilling for me, standing out from other horror games quite a bit.I give this game a solid 7/10 and highly recommend it for horror and Amnesia fans alike. I've subtracted 3 points for the following reasons:(-1) Animations would sometimes break (particularly on creatures' heads) and cause them to flail about madly, totally ruining the immersion. Additionally, the animations on my first-person view models would occasionally break entirely (most frequently when I pulled my flashlight) and cause my hands to flail about. This was my only major graphical complaint for the game and it didn't affect the game functionality at all.(-1) The game's length is pretty short relative to other Amnesia titles. As mentioned previously, the map is smaller and the story is shorter. A good selling point is the game's cheaper price tag. $25 got me into this game and I feel like it was money well-spent. That being said, I was honestly hopeful the game would capture me for longer than it did on my first playthrough. On easier difficulties, I imagine that I would have spent significantly less time in the game and might have walked out feeling a bit disappointed.(-1) I feel like HARD difficulty was not anywhere close to hard enough. It needs to be tweaked or an additional difficulty should be added for true punishment seekers. I feel that The Beast should truly have been a force to be reckoned with. If it comes to hunt you, the likelihood of it finding you should be quite high unless you can distract it well. I found myself not using glass bottles or "noisy" items at all throughout my whole playthrough. Even on HARD, there was simply little-to-no need to do so in lieu of carrying more important items like bandages or torches. I feel like my experience on HARD was pretty on par with that of a NORMAL playthrough. I was hoping for a quite challenging experience that would have kept me focused for longer than it did.I am very excited for the fan-made custom content that will no doubt surface in the coming years. It will be a good reason to dust off this gem and play it some more!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that has not played any other amnesia titles, I bought this game because the concept intrigued me. I haven't played much or gotten far, but I must say, as someone who's been a horror fan from a very early age, I don't really get scared almost ever, but this game, THIS GAME, keeps me on the edge of my seat at all times, I crouch almost everywhere, I run for cover at any slight noise made. _childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, Frictional Games is back with a proper BANGER. They still got it! Amnesia: The Bunker is Frictional's take on the Alien: Isolation formula, and they honestly nailed it. An evolved Amnesia experience, with the setting, quality and atmosphere you'd expect from Frictional. The game carries its signature feeling of constant tension, anxiety and dread that we all grew to love so much from the original Amnesia: The Dark Descent. And now we get to be hunted by an AI-driven monster! Each footstep is painfully echoed through the claustrophobic and oppressive hallways of the bunker. Not to mention you have to manually crank up an old, creaky flashlight. Also, the game offers a fair bit of replay value, as New Game+ runs are customizable.If you loved Amnesia:TDD and/or Alien Isolation, you'll love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: one of the better recent survival horror games, frictional takes their strong sound design and places it as a central mechanic, creating some really tense moments. theres this insane pressure when you've got fuel burning in the generator to not let a single second be wasted, and each time you emerge from the safe room feels like its own expedition. the atmosphere is stupidly thick and dreadful. plus its about 5-8 hours a playthrough which is perfect for this sort of game, not to mention it has a lot of randomized elements so no two runs are the same. i'd say of every singleplayer game i've played this year so far, this ones really sticking with me, love this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The best Amnesia Sequel!Maybe even the best Amnesia game of them all!  The Bunker is a true return to the survival horror that we got from The Dark Descent. _childDocuments_.review: Introduction:Amnesia: The Bunker, a new game in the renowned Amnesia franchise, seeks to captivate players with its atmospheric horror experience. This analysis delves into the game's strengths and weaknesses, particularly focusing on its monster AI, level design, balance, and overall scare factor. While the game succeeds in establishing a moody ambiance reminiscent of the original Amnesia, it falls short in certain areas, especially in delivering a truly terrifying monster encounter.Monster AI and Level Design:Amnesia: The Bunker introduces a monstrous entity that poses a constant threat to players, aiming to create a sense of fear and suspense. Unfortunately, the game's monster AI often feels lacking in depth and complexity. Unlike Alien: Isolation's alien, which was competent and displayed intelligent behaviors, the monster in Amnesia: The Bunker falls short. Its actions may feel more superficial and predictable, reducing the overall tension and impact of encountering it.Furthermore, the level design in Amnesia: The Bunker may contribute to the underwhelming monster experience. While the game successfully establishes a moody and atmospheric setting within the bunker, the level design may feel unbalanced in terms of encounters with the monster. Players may find themselves resorting to repetitive strategies, such as auto-hiding or retreating to safe rooms, due to limitations in the monster's pathing behavior. This predictability diminishes the potential for creative problem-solving and dynamic gameplay moments.Balance and Problem-Solving Mechanics:A well-balanced game is essential for providing engaging and satisfying gameplay. In the case of Amnesia: The Bunker, players may encounter frustration due to the imbalanced distribution of essential resources, such as ammunition and grenades. The game's reliance on these items to progress can lead to moments of being stuck, forcing players to search extensively for specific items needed to proceed.Additionally, the game's problem-solving mechanics may not live up to the promises made during its promotion. Players may find themselves faced with a lack of clarity or misleading information regarding how to overcome obstacles. This ambiguity can hinder the immersive experience and cause players to feel stuck or uncertain about how to proceed, ultimately detracting from the game's overall enjoyment.Scare Factor:Creating a truly scary atmosphere is a delicate balance that requires effective sound design, visual cues, and psychological tension. While Amnesia: The Bunker successfully captures a moody ambiance akin to the original Amnesia games, it may fall short in delivering the same level of fear and terror. The monster, which was intended to be a central selling point, fails to leave a lasting impression due to its predictable AI and limited behaviors.Conclusion: 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horror games I've ever played, and probably the best of the Amnesia games (from a gameplay perspective). I can't recommend this enough, though it's not for the faint of heart.+ This is a survival horror game with an emphasis on SURVIVAL. It's rare for a game to make me feel like I'm up against a wall like this one has.+ IMO, the Beast is a much better stalker enemy than Mr. X or the Alien. It doesn't need to be tethered to the player like the Alien, because the bunker is small enough that you'll run into it regularly, and it's much cleverer than Mr. X.+ This is probably the most strategic horror game I've ever played. The Beast isn't random; it's a calculating foe who pays attention to your patterns and adapts to them. It doesn't cheat, and also has patterns of it's own which you can manipulate to your advantage.+ Intuitive gameplay that lends itself to complexity without complication. Like the loading screen says, if you think you can do something, you probably can.+ This game is a masterclass of making a lot with a little. The bunker itself is a relatively small area as far as horror games go, but the randomization, terrifying enemy, and oppressive atmosphere mean that your first playthrough will likely be a solid 5-8 hours.+ Excellent emphasis on progression. Basically, the map is one giant puzzle that you're slowly solving, with every minor puzzle solved a small celebration against the horrific atmosphere. This is something the Bunker does much better than Rebirth.+ Speaking of which, the Bunker has an intense, oppressive atmosphere like no game I've ever played. The only ones that come even close are Liquidators and Amnesia: The Dark Descent.+ World War I is a criminally underrated horror setting, which this game uses to great effect.+ As always with Amnesia, the music and sound design are 10/10.- While it has terrific gameplay, the story of the Bunker is very limited compared to the other titles in the series. Don't get me wrong, it makes excellent use of what it has, but ultimately, I was much more interested in the stories of the Dark Descent and Rebirth. Even the obtuse plot of Machine for Pigs had a lot more going on in terms of depth.- Henri is certainly the most limited Amnesia protagonist. He doesn't have the bright-eyed naivete of Daniel, the cruel sadism of , the eccentric genius of Mandus, or the quiet determination of Tasi. We learn almost nothing about him, there are no proper flashback sequences, and little voiceover. He's a soldier, and not much else.- While the other stories in the franchise still work if you haven't played their predecessors, the Bunker heavily relies on the player having existing knowledge of the setting. If you haven't played the Dark Descent, and  if you haven't played Rebirth, the Bunker is basically just a spooky World War I story that doesn't fully deliver on its potential.Other than the relative weakness of the story (which is still much better than most horror games out there), this is an easy recommendation. Pick it up and face the terrors of the bunker yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: Well, after that boring, obnoxious, woke, screeching purple haired feminist, abomination piece of trash that was Amnesia Rebirth this somewhat feels like a Frictional title again.This is essentially a Dollar Tree version of Alien Isolation but much of that unique "Amnesia" vibe is strangely missing (probably because it's a different team).Nevertheless it's still hella fun and immersive - even if very basic. _childDocuments_.review: I was very hyped to play another Amnesia, and even though I had fun playing it, it did not feel like a Amnesia game to me. It was too short, and not very challenging. Not even that scary.I loved Rebirth, and how fleshed out the character I played as was. Non of that comes back in this game. The character felt bland, and uninteresting. Didn't speak other then some journal entries. Very shallow.I liked the notes slowly revealing the story, but I would have loved for the character to have a personality.The gameplay wasn't all that great either. And just turned into: Fill the generator, and hoof it to your objective, come back and repeat for the next objective. The strongest point of the game for me was when I got lost in one of the sections in the dark, with a lot of progression items on me that I didn't want to lose. Overall, I would say that the game is fun, as a random indie horror game. But if you came in hoping for something coming close to a Amnesia game, you're going to be dissapointed. It's also way overpriced.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though Dark Descent is still my favourite game in the Amnesia series, The Bunker is a very close 2nd. It's a really eerie, creepy and amazing game that honestly is a lot of fun even on repeat playthroughs, what with the different endings and how the items are randomly generated in every single playthrough. If you like a horror game with a great atmosphere and one that doesn't solely rely on nothing but jumpscares, you could do much worse than this. Give it a shot, especially if you're a fan of the Dark Descent.

_childDocuments_.review: Length may be an issue, while steam claims I've done 11 hours as of the time of this review a lot of that was paused menu time because I played it with friends. The in-game timer states our first playthrough clogged at a little under 5h. Do however note I didn't get all the notes nor opened all the doors nor lockers, and my time in the roman ruins was quite short, so it might be more for you. Still, this is by no means a long game. BUT THAT SAID. This to me might be the best horror game I have ever played. Taking the title from its predecessor Amnesia: The Dark Descent. And I assure you I do not say this lightly. I'll be honest, I was scared when I started playing... scared that Frictional might have lost their mojo. The Dark Descent and Justine's expansions were damn near perfect for their time, but A Machine For Pigs was hot garb (tho that one was by The Chinese Room and not Fricitonal), Soma was horrifying in its themes but not particularly scary or tension filled in its gameplay, and Rebirth... Look, unlike Pigs I'm willing to concede Rebirth as being part of Amnesia's timeline, if only because Frictional actually made it. But I'd say it's straight up bad. I mean the actual worst game Frictional's ever made and probably the worst they'll make in a long time. And it most certainly isn't in any way scary.Point is... When this game popped up, I was worried. And then I started and I was genuinely terrified. I mean hoooooly moly this is undeniably the first game in years that has genuinely gotten me, and my friends, while playing together and commentating, to be genuinely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrified. It is an absolute mechanical wonder, the map has been micromanaged to ensure you're always vulnerable, the Beast's AI is surprisingly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good without any notable rubber banding outside of maybe spawning. The obstacles are extremely well placed to force you into triggering the beast sooner or later. The way the generator works is just *cheff's kiss* THIS GAME IS NEAR ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PERFECTION. I mean I am absolutely flabberghasted. It seems Frictional realized all the issues Rebirth had and learned how to do the opposite of that. Well. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Done. If I could clap in text I would.So yeah. If you're too preoccupied about length, maybe it's not for you. It also doesn't have that grand a story, hell most of its story is told through notes and ambient clues, which is how I like it. And in general don't expect Scorn or anything like that. But if you just want a relatively short, highly replayable, extremely well crafted mechanical horror game, well, this is for you no doubt about it. And it sure is for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A return to form from Frictional, The Bunker is terrifying and intense from start to finish. This has easily the most gameplay out of all their games. You're able to finally defend yourself against the monster, and it doesn't detract from the intensity or horror of the game. This is the biggest change, as there's a variety of ways to ward off the monster via grenades, explosive barrels, or shooting it. It runs away for some time but always returns, seemingly angrier each time. The environment is incredibly immersive and detailed, with some of the best audio design i've heard in quite a while. Each shot you fire is terrifyingly loud, echoing throughout the bunker and leaving tinnitus in your ears. Followed by knowing that thing is coming. The Bunker has taken on inspiration from immersive sims, and it absolutely fits this type of game perfectly. Puzzles/Obstacles can be tackled in various ways, and sometimes involving physics based ways of progression. It's reminiscent of older more realistic physics engines that games used to have. It feels amazing for this game, and adds a ton to immersion. If you like WW1 and horror, this is a must buy. If all their games are going to be reminiscent of this formula, count me in.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

I think the most annoying part of all is that the devs don't really provide a good sense of direction to get you going and its sort of a big mystery, the kind were a community would want to figure out all of the secrets instead of each singular player.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, very exciting and tense. Like the more Resident Evil aspects that have been introduced. I love how the player has to consider every action they take as most of them make a lot of noise and tempt the monster. The admin office is so comfy and the dread when you have to leave it to progress is so good. Really the only gripe I have is that it's on the shorter side.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best horror games ever made.In this entry both Amnesia and Penumbra meet at their very best to provide a truly terrifying experience. Everybody who knows me in real life knows that I'm not the type to get scared easily, in fact only a handful of very specific things have ever managed to make my stomach twirl. However, Amnesia Bunker managed to keep me on the very edge of my seat during my entire playthrough, I don't think I ever felt so much anxiety playing a videogame as I did here, I often found myself actually sweating out of nervousness and cussing the protagonist out whenever he made a loud noise. Out of all of the games I played none have captured that feeling of being hunted, of being stalked as perfectly as this one did, it seriously gives Alien Isolation a run for its money!Frictional also seems to have learned their lesson from Rebirth as this entry doesn't feature jumpscares (I honestly can't remember a single one) and the monster has a very unique design, speaking of the monster, I think Frictional did an outstanding job on the storytelling that leads to the true story behind the beast, The Bunker is one of those games you really MUST play more than once beecause you'll pick up on so many details and hints that you missed the first time playing through and it also makes you realize just how tragic the story really is.The only real problem I have with it is the ending which was very disappointing and clearly rushed, however I believe that the overall experience more than makes up for it.Normally I avoid using such strong words when giving my opinion on things but in this case I can say with full confidence that Amnesia: The Bunker is an absolute masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker re-establishes the Amnesia series as one of the most horrifying in the horror genre. Explore and escape the bunker, while being stalked by the beast, a mostrositiy, unsettling as it is unrelenting.This title includes more survival elements, I am used to from the other titles, making you use up your rare resources and pocket space carefully and plan your routes wisely.The beast seems like one of the most advanced AI I've seen in a horror title, yet, sometime comes off as dorky, while not being able to see you, while staring them dead in the eye from under a table.I played the game on hard, and found the name for that difficulty level appropiate, as resources were tight, especially in the beginning. A running generator was a rare commodity, I had to live without often at the start, and became increasingly more affordable, as the game went on.The many explosive traps that litter the bunker were a menace, that either killed me straight or attracted the beast to finish me off.But these grenade tripwires were barely an inconvinence, compared to the damned rats. I just didn't know how to deal with them blocking me off some virtal locations.All in all, I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone looking for an escape room -type game and good scare.

_childDocuments_.review: The newest entry from the Amnesia series, the devs decided to go back to the original roots and this brings closer to Dark Descent, you are stuck in a WW1 bunker and you are a french soldier, I know, very scary.It took me at a slow pace 7 hours to complete, short and sweet in my opinion, the sound design is well done. Imagine Alien Isolation but it's Amnesia and you are in a bunker pretty much, give it a try I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game honestly blew me away. There have been a lot of incredible survival horror games this year, many of them AAA, but Amnesia: The Bunker stands up among the best of them. The mechanics are perfectly woven together to build tension as you are constantly trying to avoid the monster, yet need to risk making noise in order to advance further into the bunker or acquire much needed resources. There's a large amount of player freedom and mechanical depth here, allowing for varied play styles and many ways to solve problems. The game is also the perfect length, clocking in at about 5 hours for my full play-through - short and sweet.With how much customization the game allows in regard to difficulty, plus the fact that it accommodates many different play styles, if you're even a slight fan of horror games I'd highly recommend checking this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better horror games I've played. It really balances things out by providing you with a multitude of options in how to deal with the enemies you encounter, without those measures feeling like cheats or ruining the tension and fear that comes with said enemies. It makes for a much more engaging game than if running/hiding was your only options. The sound design was superb and really was half of the reason the game really pulls you into Henri's experience. I highly encourage Frictional Games to incorporate this kind of run/fight/hide dynamic in any future installments of Amnesia, as well as an early 20th century setting, as both take the series to a whole new level.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing horror game with game design that compliments every aspect of it. This game has such an amazingly crafted art style which is so pleasing on the eyes. You may have to scale down the graphical settings, but it looks so incredibly good still. The visual style is edgy, but also heavily compliments the environment, with realistic looking human skin, which helps the monster's horror factor. It just compliments gameplay so well, and looks phenomenal.Despite the revolver and weapons you collect to scare off the monster, on easy, he'll flee after one shot. However, on harder difficulties, or all the way on hard, it won't be that easy. It may take up to three shots, and in hard, even on easy too, revolver bullets are harder to come across than you think. Along with this, it's always nice to find fuel for the generator, dog tags for new supplies in the lockers, grenades or more bullets, the game compliments the survival horror style. Along with this, the monster only comes out when you make too much noise, but will come out basically all the time when the lights are off, meaning your only hope is to fight back or run, not hide. Your vision distorts when the monster is near, helping alert you. Along with this, when the lights flicker, if your running, he may decide to come out, and you can see that from the holes, where his hand slowly comes out, and then he may decide to reveal himself. The gamemakes you feel anxious, like you need to be moving, like you can't waste time because your fuel is limited, it really adds an amount of stress and fear to the game, complimenting the environment the game gives off.There are probably gonna be a lot of spoilers in this section so I've covered them up. The story is incredibly in-depth, and has many different perspectives given, along with an intense plot-twist. You slowly understand what has happened down in the bunker by reading the many notes scattered around. They all are personal notes from people, so you really get to feel these characters' emotions and personalities, despite never really hearing or seeing them. The game's story compliments the horror environment, especially when reading the demented notes about the monsters' killings. There isn't much too talk about here, just that it does what most other categories and parts of this game do, use the music to compliment the game design and environment when in different scenarios and sections. However, you can hear the monster in the walls traveling to each hole whenever it hears a loud noise from you. You can hear its growls as it crawls around, the clanging of objects it knocks over, the game perfectly nails that atmosphere, and makes the experience always feel on edge.So far the achievements in this game have only showed me new areas and given me more intriguing information on the bunker, improve the depth of this story, and give me new perspectives, none of the achievements have felt like a chore to collect so far.Update: I have gotten every achievement, and can confidently say, none of them felt like a chore. Every achievement felt like it gave me a new way to look at the story and the game itself, and it just felt good. Beating the game in 28 Minutes to get an achievement is so interesting for me, plus it makes me realize how unnecessarily long I spent on my first save. All the achievements worked for me and they were all fun, even reading notes while getting every note was enjoyable, to imagine the stories each of these individual characters have. I love the game even more than i did before, and at almost 60 hours, I've finished a great game experience, and hope Frictional Games makes more games like this in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: The influence of Frictional Games on the direction horror themed games took over the past 16 years is undeniable. Their initial Penumbra tech demo from 2006 was a surprisingly fresh take on an adventure genre, with stealth and action aspects, physically-based puzzles and interactions and surprisingly solid horror atmosphere. All of which was developed further into Penumbra: Overture, the only game from the studio until now that was adhering to the pillars of the classic survival horror, focusing not only on exploration, adventure elements and stealth, but also allowing you to deal with enemies directly via combat and traps. But beginning with Penumbra: Black Plague, the team set a mission for themselves to make great narrative-driven titles and to achieve that, the survival horror mechanics had to go.After achieving great and unexpected success with Amnesia: The Dark Descent, team followed it up with no less great SOMA. Two fantastic story-driven horror themed stealth adventure games that always prioritized good atmospheric experience over the mechanical aspects of the gameplay. Then, just over two years ago, they’ve decided to revisit the Amnesia “brand” with the incredibly mediocre Amnesia: Rebirth – a game that went really far into the narrative, but without making it particularly engaging or interesting to experience. Amnesia: The Bunker seems like a direct reaction to that as it is the return to beginning and a curious attempt to reimagine what classic survival horror gameplay could be, while staying easily recognizable.The game has a very simple premise – you’re a French soldier in an underground bunker, World War 1 is raging outside, but inside everyone seems to be dead and a lone persistent and seemingly unkillable monster lurks in the darkness, so you have to find the way to escape the bunker. There’s more to the story, of course, as you will be finding notes and photographs of your fallen brothers in arms that explain what happened. But even the original Penumbra had far more story directly told to you, whereas in this game after you go through the intro section, you can easily skip every bit of story and escape without ever understanding what happened and why.This hands off approach is in everything this game tries to do. Sure, it does have resources and ammo for you to find, weapons, doors and keys, main pursuing enemy and also occasional swarms of rats as a simpler type of enemy to deal with and with elements like these you could easily imagine a typical Resident Evil game. But Amnesia: The Bunker attempts to mix in systems and emergent gameplay to these conventions, essentially adding a bit of an “immersive sim” aspect to it all. And now you can open doors in different ways – why search for a key when you can blow the door up? Why defuse the trap, if the trap can help you instead? What if the horrible monster that you don’t usually want to attract helps you if you play things right? It’s not as smart and as deep as the game wants you to believe and the amount of possible solutions is, in reality, quite limited. But what’s there is genuinely fun to experience and it does feel fresh.Oh and there’s a random element to it all as well. Most (or maybe even all) key items, notes and hints are always in the same spots, but resources, traps, codes and many little things are different each playthrough. Which makes the game feel more similar to the Granny games or Monstrum, and only a little bit Alien: Isolation. I’m not a fan of random/rogue elements in games in general, but here it’s just enough to keep every playthrough fresh, while remaining handcrafted and thought through. That said, the big bad monster behavior in the game is relatively primitive and it does cheat, sometimes leading to rather frustrating sequences. Still – dealing with him can be fun as you have to think on your feet and he’s not necessarily 100% deadly, as sometimes these types of enemies are.Still, the fact that the game really isn’t as smart as it advertises itself can lead to frustrations as well. Game doesn’t feel entirely consistent with itself and sometimes things happen that make no sense or some solutions that sound logical do not work. Items and notes can sometimes be placed in a spot that’s next to impossible to notice. You have to click on maps to “copy” them to your main safe room map, which sounds ridiculous given the size of those things – this extra step of “telling the game” that you know it is extremely awkward. The limitation for the storage box is really stupid, as you can just dump items on the floor right next to it with no penalty. You are best off doing quick expeditions out of the safe room then returning to save and check on fuel and even though the game clearly wants you to take more risks, there’s really no reason to do so. And there is no reason to ever carry around the stopwatch so it takes up valuable inventory space – it’s super easy to plan your exploration and then turn the generator on and off when not in use. Plus while the monster roams around less with light, he’s still coming out to investigate loud noises and having light on or off makes no difference at that point. Oh and I’d suggest binding the flashlight button to something easy to reach for as you will need to hold the button to charge it. And since it’s silly weak and holds for just a couple of seconds, you will be doing this a lot.While I cannot say that Amnesia: The Bunker truly nailed what it attempted to do and it is less easily recommendable than The Dark Descent, but it is a much needed fresh look at the genre that Frictional Games seemingly abandoned before and a really cool and inspiring game. If you love classic survival horror, are okay stealth focus and using weapons as problem solving tools rather than fun action tools, you should definitely check this game out. If you were the fan of adventure and narrative focused titles from the team – maybe this won’t click with you as much. But you still might as well give it a try, it’s a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Antagonist only has a single one-hit kill mechanic and is summoned constantly, everywhere, for seemingly no reason. The game tells you, verbatim, 'Try different things. If you think it might work, it probably will'. Cool. Shame every one of those little experiments causes noise which summons the beast. Scare off rats? Too much noise. Drop a box? Too much noise. Move some debris? Too much noise. Drag a box to block a hole? Too much noise. Cut a trap? Too much noise. Flip a switch? Too much noise. It's ridiculous. For giggles, I took my hands off my keyboard and sat motionless, crouched, in a dark corner of a room and let time pass. Magically, but not surprisingly, beast shows up and kills me. On the off chance he doesnt see you or kill you, youre only option is to shoot it (game provided basically no ammo), grenade it (good luck not killing yourself setting off grenades in a cramped and narrow bunker), or burn in (way too many limited resources/timing). You can also attempt to hide, but that seemingly does nothing. Sitting in a wardrobe with the door shut, motionless, still found. Hiding under a table. Still found. And the beast will sit there, wandering, outside the door for 5 to 10 minutes. You can (and will) be required to 'do nothing' for that time. Go take a piss, make a sandwich, fold some laundry and come back, maybe hes gone. And then, when you inevitably die to this invulnerable, omnisicient, hyper predator, you get the joy of respawning back at the 'save room' and losing the last 20-30 minutes and getting to repeat sitting in a wardrobe for 10 minutes over and over and over. I won't even get into the mind blowingly awful inventory (you get 6 slots, your gun, the flashlight, and lighter take up 3. Enjoy that.) or that the game literally tells you that 'The beast hates light' yet freely roams around, unhindered, with the genny on and the bunker lit up like a Christmas tree. In one case he appeared UNDER a lightbulb and smacked me in the face and killed me. What? And why do I need to crank this stupid flashlight about 6 times just to clear one medium sized room. The tedium of having to crank this thing constantly every 60 to 90 seconds is insane and gets old INCREDIBLY fast. Like I get that it adds tension theres some interplay between cranking and making too much noise, but my god literally every MINUTE? Come on. The game is not hard because its difficult, its just bad. Every mechanic and 'tool' at your disposal, every bright idea you have, every 'im smarter than him' is punished so rather than experiment, the opposite occurs, and you wind up just skulking around a dank WW1 bunker, crawling on your knees, flashlight off, in a last ditch desperate attempt to do anything you can to minimize the chances you're found. The game lies to your face, sends you off to do battle, gives you 3 inventory slots to do it, and limited time and light to do it. And when you die, you get to do it all over again, and again, and again, and again. Wish I could refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: The vast majority of horror games are just jumpscare simulators: no threat of death, just an endless stream of cheap jump”scares”. But, every now and then, there’s a diamond that stands out in the endless sea of trash, and this is definitely one of them.There’s countless things that I like about this game. The monster design has got to be the best one that Frictional Games has produced, and it fits so well into the WWI setting. The sounds it makes are chilling and eerily human, and the animations are so unsettling, that when paired with the mode, it sometimes just makes you want to look away.The randomised locker codes, loot locations etc. makes this game extremely replayable, which is why I have almost 24 hours on record at the time of this review.The revolver and shotgun are both very well designed. The long reload on both really emphasises just how rare the ammo in the bunker is as a result of the attempts to kill the Beast. The gunshots are deafeningly loud, and your lack of ear protection means that every shot will make your ears ring. Despite how powerful these guns feel and sound, I felt incredibly weak when using them - and that’s not a bad thing. Firing a single shot in the bunker rolls the dice on whether you’ll be killed or not. The Beast hates loud noises, so you can only imagine how irritating a gunshot is for him. I only use the revolver and shotgun when absolutely necessary, otherwise I just have the revolver out so that I feel a little bit safer. And now onto the ✨symbolism✨. The Beast is a metaphor for the horrors of war. All of those mangled corpses strewn throughout the bunker were killed by a threat that you rarely see. As to not spoil the end of the game, I’ll just say that the ending really signifies the fact that essentially nothing has changed.I highly recommend this game, and it’s criminal just how underrated it is. Get it even if it’s not on sale, it’s that worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first title in the Amnesia franchise I've played and I usually don't seek out horror games, but I got the chance to get it for free and I couldn't decline. I was not disappointed. After a while the story unfolds to lovecraftian depths as you uncover whatever was going on in this bunker and get caught up in forces that are beyond human comprehension.The game plays like Alien Isolation but with actual survival elements. You can and should be armed if possible but hiding and running is usually the better and more resourceful choice. Important resources ( i.e.  health kits and ammo ) are plenty on normal difficulty and can be stored outside of your inventory (they didn't respawn on my playthroughs).Pros:- Dense atmosphere- Immersive story telling- Plenty of options to deal with your enemies- A lot to discover and uncover with a story beyond the main characterCons:- Some of the key items that would be great for exploring () become available very late. at which point you no longer need them. - Its pretty short- The boss fight is underwhelming All in all I had a great time playing. Can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: *slight spoilers ahead*I love the atmosphere and overall idea of this game! But, for me, it comes off as very tedious with a very high amount of backtracking, way too much dialogue, and a finite amount of bullets that I fear you might soft-lock yourself out of the game if you spend them all on defense since your gun is also a puzzle-solver. For your light source, you have to manage finite oil for lighting overall in the facility but ALSO perma-crank your own light source you have in your hand - it's a real chore. The game says the monster only hunts when it's dark, but that's just not true as there's been times it roams with the lights on - so sometimes it just doesn't even feel valuable to use the lighting. Additionally, the monster just one-shots you so having all these heals feels useless. It's also faster than you with pretty much no where to hide. (can also just kill you where you hide if you do find one of the few places to hide)Finally, you only have 6 item slots at the beginning, which prolongs how tedious it is to accomplish basically anything since there's a lot of loot you need to pick up.  After looking at the hours my friends have in this game, the highest is 8 hours with the rest being around 1 to 3 hours - I think they all came to the same conclusion and moved onto other games.In my personal opinion, I give this game a 2/5 - I don't recommend it at all - I'd recommend Alien Isolation.

_childDocuments_.review: People like PewDiePie helped the Amnesia series gain popularity years ago. For so many years, the franchise has been riding on that tailcoat, with little actual development in distinguishing their style with anything especially innovative. The game is simply as follows: A non-threatening ever-present monster that only appears to hunt you when the generator shuts down or when you make enough noise while it is nearby hiding in one of the many holes around the bunker. That's all there is to it. 3 hours of a teleporting monster that isn't even terrifying with some pretty boring drawn out notes and voiced story from what you find of the previous inhabitants. What is the most terrifying aspect of this game? If you do not return to the generator to save often and end up dying, you will lose all of your recent progress. What a terrible experience it will be to have to play the game from an extra hour all over again rapidly and then run back to save your game. Play an actual horror game not a waste of your time and money.
