_childDocuments_.review: So far, I have completed the game ONCE and I plan on returning at some point to make a video or two (OrionsTale on YouTube). This is as of September 30, 2024.I usually leave the negatives first and save the positives for last. Remember that this is MY opinion and is based on MY experience so please look at other reviews before making a decision.Cons:- Pretty short (If you know what to do)- German Soldier Voices (except the prisoner's) are generic and hard to take seriously. Basically just them screaming "SCHNELL! SCHNELL!". However, you don't really hear it a lot, so it's easy to forget about.Pros:- No scripted jump-scares. Constant sense of dread.- Environmental storytelling done through written notes and observation. Little to no droning exposition.- Smart and unpredictable monster- Pretty good graphics- World War I setting (We need more horror games that take place during wartime, especially historical wars)- This game has a GUN... the most genius concept for guns in horror, honestly. It won't kill the monster, sure, but it is still an incredibly valuable tool.- The Generator system.- Actual inventory management your life will depend on.Rundown:Amnesia: The Bunker is actually terrifying. There are no scripted cheap jumpscares (aside from the beginning, though that's debatable whether it was intended to startle the player), no goofy writing, no dumb atmosphere. If you love real horror that isn't over-reliant on dead kids and jumpscares, you NEED to play this! Seriously.TL:DR - Game scary. Game Good. _childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is a phenomenal horror experience that had me on the edge of my seat the entire time. The decision to have the game set in WWI truly enhanced the experience. WWI is already a terrifying situation the be in and the game constantly has you questioning whether it is better to be outside where the war is or to be trapped with the beast. I loved less-linearized approach in the gameplay design. This gave the player freedom to strategize a plan and therefore either have the satisfaction of it working or suffer the consequences of failure. With that being said, I am looking forward to the custom stories for this game and would love for Frictional to continue with this style.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most replayable horror game I've ever experienced. One of the major downsides to horror games is that, once you've completed them, the scares are not so, well, scary, anymore. You go to replay a horror game and you know what to expect so you're prepared. You also know where everything at so you can speed through from start to finish, which also diminishes the sense of urgency. "Amnesia: The Bunker," though is an interesting exception because of how it's meant to be played. I really enjoyed this game, more so than 2020's disappointing "Amnesia: Rebirth." Granted, I do appreciate\ "Rebirth" more since the hype has is long gone, but the game is still slow-paced, too long, and ridiculously convoluted. Didn't like the "pregnancy simulator" aspect, either. Luckily, "The Bunker" has a much better pace and the story is more streamlined. There are some issues, though, as this game still didn't live up to my expectations. But first, the good aspects:The story is more straight-forward in "The Bunker" than "Rebirth," but the suspense to figure out exactly what happened and what was happening was such an intense and thrilling feeling. I was on the edge of my seat with each note and journal entry I found, and it left me guessing possible endings for the game (none of them were correct, unfortunately, but more on that later). I love games that can keep your interest from start to finish by feeding you the story bit by bit. "The Bunker" has excellent sound design, and you can clearly hear the monster moving around you and above you. It allows you to attempt to predict where he might appear, although, it's never a guarantee. Also, the game features a realistic "reaction" to guns and explosions. Whenever Henri fires a shot or blows up a barrel, there is a brief period of time where he is partially deaf, a noticeable ringing and muffled sounds around him being all you can make out. This isn't something I've experienced in any action game, and while it may seem weird at first, it makes a lot of sense and adds an extra challenge. The generator is basically the lantern from "Amnesia: The Dark Descent," but you can't take it with you. You have to try and keep it running at all times because, for one, it can be very dark and the wind-up flashlight is weak. The other reason is the monster is more like to come out if there's no power. I like the generator more than the lantern because you're forced to think carefully and plan your trips around the bunker. With the lantern, when you found oil, you were good to go. But here, you have to carry it back and hope you make it in time.Inventory management can be just as tricky as resource management. The more stuff you acquire, the more decisions you'll have to make. You can find pouches to expand your inventory, but it takes time to acquire them, and you may not find them all. This is where the need for fuel and resources will be a tense balancing act. You need fuel for the generator but you need your revolver, maybe a grenade or two, bolt cutters, the wrench, a healing item...sometimes you will just have to come back for items later so you can focus on the most important stuff first. I loved this aspect of the game because you needed to plan your trips out properly or else you'd struggle to get the stuff you needed when you needed it. Sometimes, it was trial and error, sometimes it was based on what i managed to find...it was so much fun, though.While certain key items are always in the same spot, other items will be randomized every time you start a new game. This also includes locker codes and some traps. This can go in your favor if you get good RNG, or you might find yourself struggling to survive due to unfortunate RNG. For example, during the first run on Normal, fuel was pretty scarce, but on my second run, I found much more. This keeps each new game unique since you aren't able to rely on everything being as it was like most games. "The Bunker" is semi-open world, as you do have some flexibility when it comes to navigating the place. Some things must be done in the right order to progress but you can sometimes choose what you want to do and when. This also keeps each new game interesting because you might try different routes just to see what it's like. I don't think I've played a horror game with any sort of open world features, but I'm not complaining.Now, for the things I didn't like:WARNING: Major spoilers ahead so avoid clicking on any hidden text if you don't want to ruin your first play through.The game has a plot twist -- well, two plot twists, really. The first was obvious based on some journal entries you find and putting 2 and 2 together. The monster  I figured this out pretty early, but it didn't necessarily ruin the experience. The other plot twist, though, was disappointing. Originally, I had been thinking this was an experiment gone wrong, or perhaps a classic case of unleashing something evil by being too nosy. However, I was wrong. As it turns out,  This part of the story simply fell flat to me. Something else that seemed odd was Henri's lack of commentary on...anything. He has temporary(?) amnesia but upon reading certain notes, especially his own from before the game's events, you'd think he'd say something, like be horrified or stunned. But no, he's silent and never physically shows any signs of distress as he reads the notes and journal entries. Something that Frictional Games really dropped the ball on was One thing I have mixed feelings about is the length of the game. It's quite short. Your first play through MAY be anywhere from 2-6 hours, depending on the difficulty setting you choose and how you make your way through the game. However, once you've played it, even with the randomized elements, it's pretty easy to make your way from area to area, collecting what you need to finish the game, without much trouble. You also know how the monster can behave, so you can bait him easily with explosive barrels and what not. However, the story for "The Bunker" is simple, and lacks the "deep lore" that "Rebirth" featured. Making "The Bunker" actually 8-10 hours could have been overkill. They would have had you make the story more complex and add more areas to explore. Not every game needs to be long, though, and horror games can be just as effective by being short and fast-paced. In fact, it kind of makes it scarier because the short length helps prevent repetitive scares from happening.The ending is a little abrupt. What happens next is left up to your imagination but I would have appreciated something a bit more...conclusive.Overall, "The Bunker" is a good game, and is better than "Amnesia: Rebirth." "The Bunker" is replayable for many reasons, and it's fun try to plan your way through the game each time with RNG in place. The biggest issue for me with this game was the reveal about what caused everything, including the monster.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like it's designed to be played in a very specific way. They wanted to make this an "Alien Isolation" but it lacks the freedom of choice when it comes to obstacles. Resources are very scarce and most of your actions will atract the monster's attention. I can't recommend this. It feels its interaction is "too scripted". Hiding spots are scarce and the monster finds a way to detect you. Even on normal difficulty, the game feels unfair.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker is a lot of fun, and I can say that it lived up to my hype. If I had to describe it in a phrase, it would be "Alien: Isolation but a roguelike". One playthrough was 7.6 hours, but in my defense I was playing on hard mode. While I do really like The Bunker, I would prefer a more narrative-focused game. The Bunker wears its survival horror influences on its sleeve, taking overt inspiration from pre-RE4 Resident Evil and Alien: Isolation, with more subtle influences from Silent Hill: The Room, Deus Ex, and Granny (really).Pros:-The Beast is really cool and easily improves upon the foundation set by Alien: Isolation. -The generator fixes the main issue with the Xenomorph of Alien: Isolation by letting you decide if the Beast will actively hunt you, but at a price. You can choose if you want to brave the darkness and save resources, or consume precious resources but have the Beast not patrol.-Randomization of codes and item placement allows for high replayability-Contains several immersive sim elements-Great environmental detail near the end of the game which scared the ♥♥♥♥ outta me-Excellently designed environmentThings that bug me but aren't actually a big deal:-Several visual glitches such as prop pop-in-The Beast became highly aggressive by the end of my playthrough, sometimes even ignoring the lights (this could be because I played on Hard mode)-Poor performance near water-No Machine For Pigs reference, although the lights do flicker when the Beast is around just like with the ManpigsCons:-Worryingly long load times-Doesn't really do too much with the greater lore of the Amnesia series. They could've easily connected it to A Machine For Pigs considering how important WWI was in that game's plot. References Rebirth a lot though :)Rating 8.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit undercooked. They have all the right ingredients to make a masterpiece - the Resident Evil inventory management, the Alien Isolation Monster, the Darkwood keep the generator on to keep the baddies away mechanic. The game stops being scary and becomes annoying fast. The rats + monster are very annoying early game. They severely over-promise on the interactivity and depth with the whole "if you think something is possible it probably is, so try it" thing. Molotovs using a whole fuel can is ridiculous. Ending is ass.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game and probably the best Amnesia since The Dark Descent. The game however is not perfect.Really interesting twist on the franchises main mechanics, though not all of them.I really liked that they revamped the usual lighting system of matches to light static light sources as well as an oil lamp you need to manage fuel for (as seen in DD and Rebirth) into an infinite use lamp that you have to noisily charge and that goes out very quickly, as well as a generator that powers the usual lights across the facility and keeps the Stalker away, though drinks petrol very quickly. My only gripe would be that I found the pocket lamp to be slightly predictable and impractical at times, because it didn't seem that I had to be careful of where the monster was, only where I was. This is to say that, there seemed to be certain corridors or stairways where it was always fine to charge the lamp and certain corridors where he would always hear me in the walls. This help contribute to the occasional feeling that there wasn't a Stalker who could be anywhere in the bunker, but one who was always aware of me and just waiting to be provoked, which I don't think is what was attempted.This is one gripe but it is of several, I think the mechanics in this game are a positive move forward for the series however, following whatever happened in Machine for Pigs and the kind of copy of the first game in Rebirth.I must say though that the ending was quite a disappointment, which is a shame because all of the previous entries have had incredibly strong endings so far, but I think this was an extension of how well defined all of the protagonists, Daniel, Manus and Tasi, were; they could have very fine ends to their stories that tied back around to some of their defining traits: for Manus, he had to rectify his attempt to control or even stop fate with the Machine telling him what he's going to be causing in that incredibly famous speech, for Tasi we got to see how her want for a child interacted with her want to save her child, and Daniel can be seen taking responsibility as he stops running and forces Alexander to do that same. Or at least, this is what I took from them. Though, I won't spoil the ending for this game.Overall, a very well put together survival horror that I enjoyed a lot, though I will say too that I only really ever found the first game to be at all scary (and maybe the city sequence in Machine for Pigs somewhat), and that trend isn't broken too much here.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is Bunker a return to form for the Amnesia series but its is also an evolution in all the right ways, taking all the criticism's of Amnesia: Rebirth and fixing them to create an extremely open ended and dynamic horror game with metroidvania aspects to it.In Amnesia the bunker you are trapped in a world war I French bunker and are the only survivor as there is now an immortal unkillable beast stalking you in the shadows. you are given a clear objective of escaping the bunker by blowing the entrance open with dynamite and to do that you need a plunger and a bundle of dynamite, how you get these and in what order is up to you but the game is far less cut and dry than it seems, the key items of your escape are typically locked behind inaccesible areas that require other items for you to progress which your must explore to find, all the while contending with the beast while simultaneously struggling to manage your constant need for fuel to power the lights which keep the monster at bay, creating a constantly tense atmosphere as merely standing around is a waste of your precious time. Guns and grenades are given new meaning as both weapons to fend of the beast temporarily but also to blast open looks, doors and other barricades or you can circumvent them through other clever means.the bunker rewards creativity but also rewards playing smart and becoming intimately familiar with the very creature that wants to rip your face off. by understanding the threat, you can combat it, and then learn what the hell has happened in this bunker as your amnesiac French brain cant remember and maybe, just maybe escape the nightmare and live to tell the tale.the Bunker is a truly amazing Horror Game with a perfect Length that never feels too short or too long and with randomised elements in item placement it can make every run different all over again. the Games length is perfect for repeat playthroughs and i am sure speedrunners will have a field day with this game.if you enjoy Horror games and the amnesia series as a whole, i implore you to play this game, it is a true gem of a title that shows that the amnesia series and frictional games has still got it.also you can gas a german. good day.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really have any expectations coming into this, with the only information i had was from a Jacob Geller video (specifically the "Three kinds of terror" video). Basically the only thing I knew was that this was an amnesia game, that you at one point could see the surface, and that you were unfortunately french. However, this game surprised me in many ways. The monster was utterly terrifying, and I was genuinely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ my pants sometimes in the first half of the game. The bunker atmosphere is also a cool addition, and with the fact that you were no less safe outside than you were inside (because it is literally ww1 outside). I was initially confused by the non-chronological storytelling of the notes, but it warmed up to me when i began piecing together what was happening. I love that this game focuses more on your choices than just making the monster an overpowering threat that cannot be stopped whatsoever. Would you use the few resources you have to evade it, or would you hide and hope for the best that the beast does not find you? The save system only helps to make this point come across further; you only have one save slot, and you can only save in one specific place, which only exacerbates the fear of your own choices when you are far away from the save point. However, there were some points where the game got a bit annoying, but I think that fault lies with me. For instance when I would stubbornly try to explore an area, and i would get caught, which only lead me to try and fail again multiple times just to not expend any resources.As for the story, I kinda like it. I like how you eventually begin to piece everything together at the end, and how you can relate to the main character at the start, who knows nothing because of (shockingly) amnesia. The ending was good, and i was initially shocked when you saw...All in all, I'll give this game a solid 9.5 out of ten. The only problem is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rats.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short but very sweet.The game won't waste your time with unnecessary stuff.  It's all about that Bunker after all.It is as others describe it, Alien Isolation with a bit of Resident Evil + Immersive sim.  Don't treat your opponent like the Alien though.Atmosphere of the Bunker is amaaaazing.  Loved every second of it.No performance issues or crashes.60fps locked.  If thats a deal breaker for you then lmfao, your loss.EDIT: Having played a bunch more, I've come to adore it.  It may by my fave Frictional game since DD.  While it does lack in overall story, it's gameplay i've found addicting.  Starting a new game and trying a different order to how I collect the equipment I need/want.  I really love the music.  While there is fairly little, it's all wonderful.The randomisation helps that a little, but I hope they add heavier randomisation.  Key items being in completely different sections of the bunker (Making sure it's impossible to be soft locked of course) would be amazing. _childDocuments_.review: I'm posting this review to hopefully increase the chance that we get more of *this* from Frictional. I was not particularly impressed by the presentation of 'The Bunker's' plot elements, but my time with this game is still some of the best I've spent on fiction. The Bunker is best described as a horror immersive sim. The level design is tight, the sound design is the best I've heard in a videogame, and the emotional experience of playing is best in class. The problems have creative solutions, the set pieces are their own reward, and mechanics are elegant. Despite me finding the general plot to be lacking in subtlety, even the writing impressed me throughout the game. I hope the lukewarm response to this game does not discourage Frictional from making more games in this vain. Amnesia: The Bunker is spectacular.

_childDocuments_.review: Shock of shocks, Frictional games made another Amnesia game and it only took three years for a sequel made by the same studio! And unlike the very mixed bag that was rebirth, this one is very very good. It's a bit different from the usual formula, and it's not perfect by any means, but it's probably my favourite of any new game that I've played this year, and it's absolutely terrifying.  If you don't believe me, let me tell you that you play as... I warn you, this is a bad.... a fr*nch soldier. Well now I know all the cowards in the audience have left, traumatised by the deep existential terror that there is indeed a fr*nce, a terrible realm full of "people" with deep nasal laughs  who devour poor innocent amphibians and very smelly cheese, I can actually talk about the game.So the setting is WW1, 1916 on the Western Front. You awake from a comatose state after seemingly trying and failing to rescue an injured friend from a deep shell crater, and find that the bunker in which you were serving has has suffered from a few issues besides being filled with "men" with a craving for croissants but croissants to be found and being stuck in the middle of a meat grinder masquerading as a war. The lights are off, the place in in disarray, and it quickly becomes clear that the lack of mimes for entertainment is the least of your worries. Something even more monstrous than the inhabitants has burrowed it's way into the bunker, and everyone inside is either dead or fled. You have one simple goal. Get out while you still can.It's a simple premise for a story, but it's executed incredibly well. Unlike it's predecessors, it's nonlinear, with most of the bunker open to you from the beginning. I love how much the developers have just absolutely embraced the setting. The atmosphere is some of the best I have seen. The bunker is relatively quiet, but the eternal rumble of distant guns never quite stops, the entire complex shaking when a shell lands nearby. Inside is dark and grungy, a world of concrete, mud and rust, and whilst I am a historian, I'll admit I'm no expert on WW1 bunker complexes, so I can't say for certain it's 100% accurate. What I will say is that it feels very authentic. There are no Battlefield style modern day technologies masquerading as experimental technologies here, it all feels very grounded, and it's really immersive. The items in game and various bits of scenic clutter feel very authentic to the setting.The sound design also absolutely carries the game beyond this. They also made the choice to randomise the location of most of the items in the game between play-throughs, so a walkthrough is of little use. I won't say why, but the brief section in the pillbox really sticks with me as hammering home the bleakness of the setting. The game also manages to marry it's setting to game-play perfectly. The bunker has a diesel generator that you need to keep refuelled to keep the lights on. It is legitimately amazing how comforting the mere act of turning the lights on in this game is, and it's not just a comfort thing. The beast doesn't like light, and keeping the generator on will discourage it from wandering the halls. The lights will also flicker when it gets near, so they do serve as a handy warning system. The generator drinks fuel like an irishman drinks.. well, anything with alcohol in it. It needs to be constantly fuelled, and it adds a lot of tension as you are always on a ticking clock, and coming back without fuel too many times means no power and having to go about in the dark. Your only portable light sources are a historically accurate dynamo flashlight with a ripcord, which has a tiny battery life and is also extremely noisy to use and a crafted torch, which requires sacrificing fuel to make, burns down very quickly and is also vital for scaring off rats so you won't want to use it just for light. Even with the lights on, the actual placement of lights is irregular, they can and will get broken and the bunker is still very gloomy, so you will be forced to rely on the flashlight a lot, afraid with every pull of the cord that you are going to attract attention. The developers deserve so much credit for the fact they made the more act of using a torch one of the most tense things in the game, and somehow made it historically accurate as well. Probably one of the biggest scares for me was going down a corridor with the power off, and pulling the cord only to realise that the creature was in the next room and I may as well have just rang a dinner bell.  The creature is never far from your thoughts. It has burrowed tunnels throughout the complex, and it seems to be able to feel vibrations, as the mere act of walking around will draw attention. You can frequently hear it sliding around inside the walls, the floor, the ceiling, (I did say the sound design was excellent) and whilst you are usually not sure of it's exact location, you can always be sure that it's never going to be far away, and when you do know where it is, between the erratic lighting and the fact you are almost certainly running in the opposite direction you are likely not going to see much of it beyond a limb or a silhouette. The fact it comes when you make a racket makes everything tense. Moving boxes and smashing open doors is something you'll need to do quite a bit and it's advisable to have an escape route and an emergency defence plan ready if you plan to do either. One area I was going through necessitated the breaking of multiple doors, each one which was then followed by a frantic run back to the safe room with roaring echoing through the halls behind me, and as the process went on the monster clearly memorised my escape route and started popping out of different holes to cut me off. I found myself trapped in a staircase and forced back down when it came out above me, and at one point it leapt through a closed inter-joining door to cut me off. You can lock yourself in this one room ,and it has some limited item storage, but it's of little comfort when you have to leave it constantly to scavenge for more fuel and supplies. Supplies are very limited, as is your carrying capacity. An active defence usually becomes a last resort, as whilst you do have a pistol, it is a six shooter which is slow to reload, and it doubles as a handy means of opening padlocks and blowing up barrels, so even in the event you actually have a surplus of bullets you won't want to use them. Creating molotovs means you have to sacrifice precious fuel, and you also need them for corpse disposal, and booby traps only work once. Even if you do manage to drive the beast away it will come back angrier next time. The item scarcity adds tension, and whilst you aren't completely defenceless like the other Amnesia games, I love the added flashes of frantic violence as you desperately try to defend yourself when hiding or running fails. So, as much as I like it, it's not perfect. It's not very long, My playtime was about 4 and a half hours, and whilst it was time well spent, I didn't expect it to be over as fast as it was. That run was actually my second, as my first I got soft locked out of the game an hour in when I got a glitch that wouldn't let me turn left or right and I had to restart, as reloading my save didn't fix it. The story is also strangely minimal. Frictional games are normally very well written, and whilst there is some nice flavour text it's quite sparse and I'd have appreciated a little bit more information on the inhabitants of the bunker and the sequence of events that lead to their deaths. I also find the lack of a rifle somewhat odd, as it was the most prolific weapon in the war and there doesn't seem to be one in the bunker. All in All, It's a great horror game and I very highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing.To begin, I'd like to start with what I love most about this game; the replayability. Few horror games have me just as tense as I was on the first play through as the ones that follow it, all thanks to the game's incredibly level of customisation and additional parameters you unlock after beating the game for the first time. These range from the monster's reactivity, a new fuze box system, and options to increase the monster's unpredictability (amongst many more!). The duration of the flashlight, for example, was one of the few complaints I had about the game but these settings now allow you to totally remove that issue by either extending it's life, making it infinite, or making it even shorter! It's all up to you. It is also massively helped by how all the items you find (with the exception of quest items) are totally randomized; meaning you're entirely encouraged to search each and every corner of the bunker as you move along. There's also a healthy plethora of workshop mods you can install to help change the experience even further! The Freddy Fazbear one sure is something...As for the game play, I think this is Amnesia at its peak. It removes the sanity system which I've always hated in horror games as it just became frustrating rather than adding anything to the experience. The survival horror aspect is also masterfully done here with each item you find within the bunker being pivotal to your survival. You never know when that measly little ball of meat might mean the difference between life and death! The generator is also a very fun mechanic and really makes you grateful for light. The presence of weapons also does little to bolster your courage. You might have a gun, but you also have hardly any bullets. If you're going to fight, make it count. You cannot kill this thing. As for the monster's gameplay, it's very simililar to Alien Isolation and I mean that as a very strong compliment (it's my favourite video game!) The monster has no set patrol patterns and its entirely possible to play the game without ever seeing it. But trust me, you know it's there. Storywise, this one doesn't have much to offer really but that isn't too much of a downside considering how much effort was put into the gameplay. If you want story, play either Rebirth or Machine For Pigs. If you want a thrilling horror experience, play this one! But that said, the story isn't weak either. It's simple but I feel like any other approach could have possibly weakened the overall outcome of the game as it allows the following playthroughs to not feel like slogs as you go through story elements you've seen before and instead you're thrown right into an experience which you quickly need to adapt to.Moving on, the game's atmosphere is AMAZING. From the sounds of artillery fire above you, the beast's horrifying howls, and then to the subtle but dread-inducing ambient music; Amnesia has never been better. Each sound tells you something and it's key to keep yourself ready for what they might be telling you. Additionally, the lighting is also fantastic and the monster's fear of the light makes it a fun game mechanic. Don't rely on that too much though. It's more hungry than it is scared of a lantern. Lastly, the game does have a tiny amount of flaws but they're nothing to put you off buying the game. A few examples are:- The game struggles with sound and elevation, making some things sound as if they're directly besides you whilst they're actually on a floor beneath you. There isn't many circumstances that this appears in but they're quite noticeable when they do.- The lighter item, specifically, is crucial to navigating the bunker it feels yet you're given it far too late for it to really mean anything. - The final section is a massive disappointment and feels as if the team was pressed for time when making it. However, since the rest of the game was so good it doesn't really matter. And the ending itself isn't bad either.Overall, one of the best horror games on the market and one I strongly recommend you try out! Looking forward to whatever Frictional might have next!

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia The Bunker is intense The atmosphere is chilling, keeping you on the edge of your seat. The gameplay is immersive, making you feel like you're in the midst of the horror. The graphics are pretty good except for how people look. Overall, Amnesia: The Bunker is a must-play for horror enthusiasts, delivering a thrilling and unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: , the latest Frictional Game in the  universe offers players a tantalising premise with their latest offering in the haunting world of the  series where for the first time the player is armed and is able to fight back. While the protagonist of the story you control certainly won't suddenly evolve into a game version of Rambo, this is survival horror after all with survival horror mechanics where often the best option is to still run and hide, the game falls somewhat disappointingly short in some crucial areas resulting in a moderately satisfying experience which leaves me wondering whether it isn't time for the company to retire the series for a little while.One of the game's strengths lies in its atmospheric design. The eerie ambiance and the dark, claustrophobic environments (that resemble a rats nest) effectively build tension and create an unsettling horrific atmosphere. The sound design, coupled with the visual aesthetics, contributes to the overall sense of dread, drawing players into its foreboding world. It also great to see developers building on what Creative Assembly gave us with , where the monster works very similarly to how the Xenomorphs behaved where it will actively hunt the player based on sound and location. Running, instead of crouching slowly along, when the monster is close by will attract its attention. Same logic applies to using items such as torches or flares which will draw the beast closer to the light source. However, where  struggles is in its execution of gameplay mechanics. The puzzles, while initially engaging, tend to become repetitive and predictable as the game has you backtracking quite a significant amount. The torch mechanic is frustrating as it barely illuminates the game's environments (I found this game incredibly dark making it a chore to navigate through,especially with its serpentine burrows that connect and loop back to other parts of the bunker). It becomes very easy to become very disorientated (which I suppose is what the developers are trying to achieve) and become lost. I get why they chose to only allow the torch to illuminate an area for a very short time (because it forces the player to make a sound by winding up the torch) but the novelty of it wore off very quickly as it became an exercise in frustration being constantly thrust into these incredibly dark environments and not being able to see where I was going. The game has a central hub where you can save progress, but this too ends up becoming a problem itself because if you die while out exploring for the next required item or solution to a puzzle all progress is reset to that last save. I died a lot in the dark (even while powering up the generator) but these constant deaths that reset all my hard work ended up geting on my nerves really fast. The monster that was stalking me quickly moved from harrowing and terrifying to irritating. The lack of innovation or variety in puzzle-solving methods also makes the game feel somewhat lacklustre. Additionally, the narrative, although promising at the outset, is so bare bones it's practically non-existent and what is there suffers from pacing issues and a lack of depth in character development. The story failed to grip me, leaving me detached from the overall experience. As someone who enjoys these games for their often disturbing narratives, this left me extremely disappointed. The potential for a compelling narrative is present but right now it feels like nothing more than an afterthought.On a positive note, the game does offer some genuinely chilling moments that can evoke genuine fear and tension. Running and hiding from the creature is still and incredibly intense experience and will make up the bulk of the players gameplay as they try to outwit and outsmart the creature. It is here where the game really does shine as it delivers some memorable and spine-tingling experiences, albeit inconsistently. Furthermore, the game's duration might feel shorter than expected, leaving players yearning for a more prolonged and immersive experience within this unnerving setting.:- Atmospheric Immersion: The game excels in creating a foreboding atmosphere, drawing players into a dark and chilling world through its haunting visuals and sound design.- Moments of Intense Fear: It delivers sporadic, heart-pounding moments that induce genuine fear and tension, offering a few memorable scares.- Claustrophobic Setting: The confined, claustrophobic environment effectively contributes to the overall sense of unease, amplifying the horror experience.:- Repetitive Puzzles with an insane amount of backtracking: The gameplay suffers from repetitive and predictable puzzles that are not on par with previous entries- Lackluster Narrative Development: The story, what there is, is incredibly thin on the ground. Coupled with pacing issues many players may find themselves falling into boredom despite the terror of being stalked by a creature.- Short Duration: The game's duration feels shorter than expected, leaving players longing for a more extended and immersive experience within its unsettling world.In summary,  presents an atmospheric horror experience with a strong foundation in its ambiance and unsettling setting. However, it falls short when it comes to mechanics, pacing issues within a paper thin story, and puzzles that are on the weaker side to solve. It's worth exploring for fans of the series seeking a moderately chilling experience , but if you aren't already a fan of the series, I gather this one will leave those that are not scratching their heads wondering what all the fuss is about. One for the die-hard fans.

_childDocuments_.review: For a little background, I'm a big FG fan. I loved The Dark Decent and Soma, I enjoyed Rebirth, and disliked AMFP (I know this was Frictional Games but I'm mentioning it anyways). When I think about good horror games, I instantly think of Frictional Games. I think they all have great atmosphere, interesting story, good monsters, and just fun gameplay while also being terrifying, and I think that Amnesia: The Bunker was a great follow up. It is a short game, yes, but it does what the developers intended and it does it WELL.This is one of many areas this game excels in. Throughout the game, you'll randomly hear (depending on where you are) gunshots, artillery blasts, soldiers yelling, and the monster scurrying through the walls of the bunker. It constantly keeps you tense, as well as reminding you that you are pretty much never alone no matter where you are. The glooming darkness of the entire bunker really makes your stomach sink whenever the generator runs out of fuel.  Atmosphere is something Frictional Games never disappoints with, but to me this was the some of the best I've seen.This is definitely the most fun Amnesia game there is. While I do still enjoy the puzzle walking sims, I think how they designed this game was still a little more fun. In this game you have a gun to defend yourself unlike the other games, but your defense is extremely scarce. You collect very few bullets throughout your playthrough and you might have to use a bullet to shoot a lock out or something else. There are other means of defense though, such as frag and smoke grenades and fire. There are also environmental traps that you can lure the Beast into. The game gives the facade that you have very little defense and keeps up the intensity, but if you use the environment, you can get even more of a chance. Another great new mechanic is the generator. The generator keeps the lights working, but you have to constantly keep refilling it with your finite resource of fuel canisters you find around the map, and the generator eats fuel QUICKLY. Now, you don't actually need to keep the generator going, but when the lights are out, the monster becomes much more active. He will start patrolling the area even if you made no sound. Plus, if you want to see you have to keep winding up your flashlight which is very loud. The generator adds another great layer of resource management to this game and running around the bunker in pitch black darkness will have you ***hole clenched.This game definitely kind of takes from newer Resident Evil games and Alien: Isolation. The inventory management, storage box, and how the monster works very much show that. You will sometimes be leaving items behind, run back to your storage box and dump everything, then run back in pitch black darkness for the item because you don't want to lose the item. Oh yeah, and there is only 2 save spots in the entire game, only 1 of which will be used 95% of the time. I think this was an amazing idea. It made the game challenging, but even more terrifying because you can't just save when you want. You have a singular safe room.The design of the monster, physically and intelligence wise, is just fantastic. The monster looks terrifying and having it jump in your face from the darkness was never fun. Intelligence wise, it isn't the smartest AI. It isn't Alien: Isolation levels of smart but I think for this game, it didn't need to be that smart.How the monster works gameplay wise was 100% inspired by Alien: Isolation. The monster is not always in the map, it is usually crawling through the ceiling or the walls, with random holes in every wall that it can jump out of or stalk from. If you make too much noise, like running or shooting your gun, the monster will pop up and start hunting you. I think using this design was perfect instead of making every monster a scripted scene such as in earlier games. It makes every run of the game or run through even an area completely different depending on what you do.Another thing Bunker did differently was putting the story on the backburner kind of. In the other games, you have a lot of notes that are explaining the back story, whats happening, who people are, and all that. And I mean a LOT of notes. In this game though, while they did do that, they did it on a much smaller scale. A lot of the notes simply go into the mental instability of the soldiers in the bunker, a lot of other notes were simply clues for things you needed to do in the game. While I appreciate and love the stories from TDD and Soma, I think putting gameplay over story in this game was the right choice. Staying in the dark and not knowing what is happening just like the soldiers.This game was amazing. I feel like it did most or even everything right. The game is kind of short yes, 4-8 hours depending on how you play, but I think that works perfectly. It doesn't over stay its welcome like other horror games where it stops getting scary because you are getting used to it. I whole-heartedly recommend this game for any survival horror lovers out there like me, especially for 25 bucks. Oh and the game has a lot of replayability with speed run potential, and the fact that every single code and item is random every play through. BUY IT.Amazing atmosphere, best gameplay out of amnesia games, story takes back burner behind gameplay but it works, the beast is terrifying, lots of replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: The gut-wrenching terror of looking for more fuel you haphazardly used all up, with one round in the chamber as your only means of defense, knowing that the slightest noise could spell death, has to be one of the most impactfully immersive feelings I've gotten from a horror game in years.Yes it's kind of short, it took me about 4 hours to complete, but when every single minute of that time is spent dreading looking around the next corner, you'll almost wish it would end sooner.But it won't. The only way to survive The Bunker is to blast open that door and pray it doesn't find you.I will admit I'm very biased towards Frictional Games and the gold they put out. But even if Rebirth left you skeptical, even if the length of the game seems disappointing, even if you think modern horror games won't scare you, play this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: I finished getting 100% of the achievements in amnesia: the bunker after 6 playthroughs of the game and I have to say... it's a masterpiece of horror game design. Truly incredible design work. The levels are deeply fleshed out, interconnected, and require a great amount of problem solving and thinking to figure out. You can also approach everything with multiple different strategies and it has the gameplay elements to support this kind of strategizing and adapting. It brings in elements they never had in other amnesia games (such as a weapon to defend yourself which is VERY different and unexpected since their whole gimmick is you are helpless and unarmed) and they all serve just to benefit the experience. The use of every bullet or bucket of fuel is such a hard choice that can either get you where you need to go or put you into a difficult to escape situation. Balancing resource management with well defined scares and an overall atmosphere that is just dripping in fear, the game really exceeded my expectations and kept me highly engaged for multiple playthroughs. I really appreciate the focus on game play with the story sprinkled throughout as intriguing yet not critical or necessary to complete the game. It felt satisfying to uncover the story of what happened in the bunker, but you are free to entirely ignore all of it and focus on getting the hell out if you so desire. WW1 as the setting is also a fantastic choice for a horror game because it puts you into the most terrifying situation humans have ever created: the hellscape of war. It does an excellent job of juxtaposing the monstrosity of humanity and the monstrosity of the thing lurking in the darkness of the bunker and really reinforces the fact that even if you escape from the bunker you will emerge from one hell only to end up right back in another. My only complaint is there isn't anything else like it. IF you want the best experience, play it on a harder difficulty 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, people who complain about the game being only "3 hours long" either played on easy or watched/read a walkthrough. If you play on normal, the monster is more aggressive and a bit harder to drive off with bullets than on easy, not the mention I've found only two save points through the whole game, whereas on easy, you've got way more save points, at least one per area. The game itself is one of Frictional Games' very best installments. Like, wow. After the slightly disappointing (for me at least) Rebirth, the Bunker decides to prioritize gameplay over story, and this is honestly the best game gameplay-wise that FG has ever made, ever. Maybe I don't enjoy it as much as SOMA or The Dark Descent but it's a solid top 3, nonetheless. It's far from an actual immersive sim like, let's say Prey 2017, but you do have at least a handful of possibilities, not just with how you can destroy doors, but you have more means of fighting the monster than just shooting it, there's also grenades, you can make molotovs rather in the game, pouring fuel on the floor and setting it ablaze.  You can hide, of course, if you do want to save up ammo. Throughout the entire game, I've found a couple of dozens of bullets for the revolver, so there's definitely room for usage for it, just remember, some bullets are hidden better than others. The game honestly scared me much more than all those funny pseudo-horror games for kids ever could that we recently got. I felt as scared as back when I first played TDD... and it was amazing. There isn't much audio, but what is there, sure as hell makes the job, especially the creepy noises the beast makes. It kept my hair straight for those first few hours of the game, by the end, I wasn't as scared but I was still a little tense. It was quite a ride from start to finish and I am looking forward to next playthroughs. Thank you, Frictional Games, for saving the horror genre once again. Can't wait for your next game!

_childDocuments_.review: great game. my 2th favorite game ever. liked this over the dark descent. i recommend doing shell shock like really, it makes you actully scared so much and makes you be resourceful so much and smart. when you do shell shock it makes you realize how all the mechanics work together + without having your revolver given to you, you act wayyyy more careful.

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter, experimental, and much harder and scarier than any previous Amnesia game, The Bunker represents a strong step in the right direction for the series. While Frictional's technology is lagging behind more modern offerings, their keen insight into what's scary has only gotten better with time, and here they're firing on all cylinders. With some randomness at play in terms of the items, traps and codes you find which are required for progression, as well as an entity that persistently hunts throughout the game, this is the first game in the series to offer genuine survival horror mixed with replayability. I would have liked to see a few more puzzles in the game, as well as a few additional ways to increase the sim-like behaviors in the game, this is a brilliant foundation to explore. The price point is also perfect for what is on offer.Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Much better than Alien Isolation. First, I thought there is no horror if a character has grenades and a gun, but they are actually more like  rather than defensive weapons. The stoty is short but actually great! You really  to read notes unlike most other games. It was a pleasure to read the whole story in chronological order and understanding it. _childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, I had hoped this to be good, but I'd never dreamed it'd be this good. To me, this is the best amnesia game they've ever made. I still liked SOMA more for the story and environment, but this is the best game in the amnesia franchise for me. Playtime is perfect (not too long, not too short). Atmosphere scared the living daylights out of me and the mechanics all worked together to make everything even more frightening. It's a shorter one than their other games, but I loved every second of it (read: I ♥♥♥♥ my pants every fifteen minutes).TL;DR: Highly reccomended if you liked any of the previous amnesia games even a little bit. _childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Initially the game is pretty scary because the sound design is well done, and the monster sounds like it's constantly right around the corner, waiting for you, or following you. You feel like you're hunted and you need to be ready to hide an any moment.This horror quickly falls off after about 10 minutes once you realize the monster spends most of it's time following you around and going "ooga booga" in the walls while not responding to any stimuli or caring what you're doing. It ignored the grenades exploding, breaking doors, making lots of noise, and only bothered to kill me when I purposely stuck my head in one of the holes to see if it'd actually do anything. The icing on the cake for me was when I touched a cloud of tear gas for 0.5 seconds, took damage, and the game told me I was bleeding and now I could be tracked unless I bandaged.Frictional Games captured lightning in a bottle with Amnesia: The Dark Descent, and to a lesser extent the Penumbra series, but has consistently failed to deliver anything more than a mediocre experience in the 13+ years and multiple titles since Amnesia: TDD in 2010.Give this one a pass. The game is not what you hope it will be.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia the Bunker in my eyes, is a great game. Whilst I'm not the largest fan of the Amnesia franchise I did thoroughly enjoy my time with the game though I haven't done the hard mode as of yet. My only gripes with the game were one the rats, they were very annoying with how sometimes you can get past them with ease, and others they'd bite you 3 or 4 times even though you did the exact same thing. They're annoying to put it in simpler terms. Whilst I do appreciate the replay ability aspect of the game with its rng in terms of items, I do wish that it could be turned off, at least for more important things like say pocket bags, it should at least be an option imo as at certain points you're just scurrying back and forth between spawn locations which can be tedious. The last gripe I had was the engine itself, it's showing its age and there were a few times where things like say the entrance to the tunnels was soft locked due to the box getting stuck inside a wall, though whether that's the engines fault or the way that's placed I'm not too sure so take that with a grain of salt that complaint. Otherwise I'd say this game is quite fun and enjoyable, enjoyable enough to make me speedrun it a few times even which I typically never do in a game and the speedrun is both rewarding and fun to pull of as the routes to take flow quite nicely together in my opinion. I'd say if you're looking for a fun somewhat horror filled experience of the Great War this would be it.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: You're alone in a bunker during WWI - you're buried inside ... with a monster.This plays very much like Alien: Isolation. Slightly less forgiving. Much smaller, but very well thought out map. Slightly overtuned on Normal difficulty. Some resources are way too abundant (healing items - the monster kills you in one hit, they are mostly pointless), some resources are too scarce (bullets - I shot 0 times at the monster, and was short on bullets all the time having shot a couple of locks or explosive barrels to open up level areas). The monster is mostly consistent in its behavior, which makes gameplay predictable once you get the hang of it. Unfortunately there are some sequences where the devs clearly 'want' the monster to come out, even though you give it no reason to. While understandable from a experience design standpoint, it's kinda meh when playing smart counts for nothing because the devs 'wanted' a chase sequence or force you into hiding at certain moments. That just makes it harder to learn what the 'default' behavior of the monster is - and navigating around this sucker is pretty much all you're doing in this game. And just like in Alien: Isolation, the monster is tethered to the player a bit too much. Want to distract the monster by throwing a grenade over there? Too bad, it will not necessarily go there, it's more likely to come to 'you' instead - even if you moved entirely out of 'scope' after throwing it. It's all knowing sometimes. Found a hiding place in a corner somewhere? The monster might decide to check this one particular corner for no reason. Reload.The game seriously lacks reliable hiding spots, and does not give you anything reliable with which to fight or outsmart the sucker, so you're basically trying to keep a low profile and when you have to make a ruckus, you plan your escape plan beforehand - since most hiding places are unreliable, that usually means making a beeline to the central safe-room of the bunker. This aspect could be much improved. There should be some reasonably available resource with which to deter the monster. It's not bullets. There's like 10 total in the game, about 3 of which you need to progress the story, and 3 are needed to deter a single monster attack - and you since you learn early on that bullets open locks (directly or indirectly) - why waste them on the monster? It will come back almost instantly anyway.The story is barely there, but in this amnesia title, the story is not that important, gameplay and player agency is. Which is a welcome change from Rebirth, which was almost entirely story-driven, but the story and protagonist were not delivering for long stretches of the game. This time the protagonist isn't pointlessly afraid of the dark and does not have excessive voiced lines. Only talks through his journal entries. There is some replay value as item placement and locker codes varies each playthrough. And you might want to go for a nice speedrun after learning how to progress the story. Clearly the devs went back to the roots on this one - and the game came out ... pretty great!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: 2023 really has been nothing short of a superb year for games (), and one of the biggest highlights has easily been Amnesia: The Bunker.While I don't think this reaches the absolute peaks of The Dark Descent - my personal favorite in the series, it is on the whole a much more consistent experience, being far less reliant on scripted events for scares. Instead, it relies on randomizing key items, traps and nests of rats to constantly keep your on your toes. This also has the added bonus of making the game highly re-playable, a rarity for a lot of horror games, Dark Descent included. Can we take a minute to talk about the audio design? Because good , The Bunker exceeds anything Frictional has done up to this point, which is saying a lot because basically everything they've put out starting from Penumbra Overture has had exceptional audio design. The Bunker though is on another level. The hollow reverb as you hear The Beast crawling, scratching and roaring through the interiors of the bunker, the chirping, chomping and hissing of the rats, the sounds of artillery going off above ground, shaking the entire bunker, causing dust to kick up and ceiling lamps to sway around violently. It is  done, and creates a soundscape that traps you into this desolate, horrifying, claustrophobic pit of Hell no man should wander into.The sound design also plays heavily into the gameplay loop. While I do think SOMA is the peak of Frictional's environmental and art design, The Bunker is absolutely in the leader ups. These environments are painstakingly detailed, well textured, dimly lit and full of atmosphere in a way you'd expect from studios who have triple the budget of what was spent to make this. Effects work like the aforementioned dust from above-ground artillery explosions, fire from molotovs and volumetric rays from artificial light sources is also absolutely stunning.Alright, I've gushed about this long enough. Do I like everything about this game? Not necessarily, it has some faults. Minor ones, but it adds up enough to create some annoyances.So remember what I said about the element of sound being heavily integrated into the game's core loop? While it starts off very strong and engaging, it does become easy to cheese once you find out the pattern The Beast operates on. In the game's defense, it does try very hard to throw you for a loop constantly, and the obscene amounts of darkness can cause you to run into traps accidentally, which make tons of noise and are guaranteed to attract the thing - but once you learn where the positions are, you can simply defuse or jump over the majority of them causing little noise. It becomes  easy to stay quiet.Another thing is that it's too easy to abuse saving in the game, which can take away a lot of the tension when you can just make a B-line for the  and stay safe until The Beast walks away.My last negative would have to be the See? Minor annoyances. They ultimately do not hugely degraded one of the best horror experiences I have ever played.This game is nothing short of a triumphant accomplishment, and it's a crime it wasn't nominated at The Game Awards for a single category. I don't personally care about the show, as I believe it's just 2+ hours of glorified advertising, but it still would've been a giant publicity boost for Frictional and their non-stop commitment to quality games. They deserve all the success they've worked incredibly hard to earn.If you're reading this, I highly encourage you to nominate The Bunker as GOTY during The Steam Awards. It's the reason why I'm writing this review in the first place!Absolutely stellar work, Frictional. Never stop doing what you do. You're a shining star in an industry currently full of stinkers right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Survival Horror gameplay with a cramped, claustrophobic setting: just you and what the game calls The Beast locked in a Bunker trying to outwit one another. Basic gameplay loop involves finding necessary materials to advance and making it back to your  saferoom to save your progress and gear up for another run. Each run from your safe-room to a new area of the map is a chance to pick up items you may not have seen/had room for, hone your spatial awareness and familiarity with a certain area, and get you one step closer to freedom. Highly recommend the game. Gameplay mechanics and atmosphere are top-notch, story is interesting, but not as much of a focus as say Amnesia Rebirth, or Soma, but if you've played every Amnesia entry till now there are some elements in Bunker's worldbuilding that definitely add to the overall lore Frictional has crafted. A great game that makes me excited to see how they go even further in future entries.

_childDocuments_.review: This game blends the puzzle solving of a Resident Evil game, with the randomization, granularity, and linearity of a Zelda randomizer, with the thrilling horror of a giant... thing that tries to kill you! My Normal difficulty run lasted 6 hours and 25 minutes, so expect each "run" of the game to be 4-8 hours depending on your skill and the luck of the seed I guess.Playing the game on Normal as a first playthrough was alright. The stalker (the monster's name) did have some mild tediums to kiting it away from where I was planning to go, but other than that and getting disoriented for half an hour in  you explore near the end of the game, the game had no major issues.The controls are super easy to learn. The shooting feels great. The physics are amazing. The game heavily encourages you to use your brain and whats given to you and to experiment, so if you've played games like Half Life, Breath of the Wild, or Noita, or some other game with commonsense physics (ie: shooting an explosive detonates it), this is another one of those you'll enjoy. The accessibility features are a nice touch for streamers amongst others. The replayability factor is super high as well thanks to the near infinite difficulty tweaks and sliders you can toggle once you beat the game the first time.If you like Zelda, Zelda Randomizers, Resident Evil, or really any puzzle and/or horror game, get this. Thank me later!9/10

_childDocuments_.review: After 100%ing this game and playing every difficulty, I can say that this is an amazing entry in the Amnesia series by Frictional. I feel that it scratched that immersive horror sim itch that I had since games like Prey and Alien Isolation, and I believe that this is a significant step from their earlier entry, Rebirth. Feels closer to what Amnesia The Dark Descent was than any other game so far by them and it did not overstay it's welcome, taking around 3-6 hours to complete depending on the difficulty and the method you play.It can also depend on RNG because Frictional made it so that New Game Plus randomizes items, and traps, making it kinda a new experience each time you play. Although I do wish that it also included changes to the layout of the map but I understand that would be exceedingly complicated to implement.The gunplay feels great, not too powerful to kill the beast and the tension, but strong enough that it did feel like a relief when I came upon some spare bullets. The shotgun though I think comes into play too late, because by the time you receive it, the game is practically done so it didn't feel like there was much point in having it.The monster is excellent, horror personified and definitely gave off those Xenomorph vibes from Isolation. It kept enough pressure on me throughout the various areas of the bunker where I felt unsafe but not too much where I got annoyed with its presence. The utility of the other items works extremely well.  The various types of throwables definitely are the highlight and I feel spices up the gameplay the most. The story is simplistic but not in a bad way. Unlike Rebirth where it was extremely heavy handed on the other world of Amnesia and its influence on the events of the prior games, The Bunker dials it back a bit to where it's not necessarily in the forefront but you do see some connections. For what it was, it did it's job and wasn't overly grandiose.  Some nitpicks of course; I don't understand why every box of ammo gives me one bullet. I think, for immersion sake, it wouldn't have harmed the difficulty nor the atmosphere if there were every so often 2-3 bullets per box.  I also wish there were more ways to stealthily open locked doors. There are a lot of loud options; You can use grenades, explosive barrels, heavy bricks, eventually the shotgun, and/or you can lure the monster to blow open doors. However all of these options lead to making the monster active, then it becomes a waiting game for them to leave their patrol elsewhere. Which isn't problematic. It helps the tension. I just think there are way too many doors locked that don't provide me the option to be quiet. Also I understand it's an Amnesia thing but it confuses me why the fuel canisters and bottles filled with fuel delete themselves after pouring them in the generator. They'd still be there if you pour em. They'd just be empty instead. But all in all, definitely worth its asking price and your time if you're either an Amnesia fan or someone who likes horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: An insanely well put together horror experience all the way through. The bits of story we get through notes, reminiscent of The Dark Descent, are well done, chilling, and saddening. The game play itself is The Bunkers strongest asset as well as the design for the monster AI, seemingly rivaling Alien Isolation. You'll dread hearing that generator shut down. Every time. Frictional has had ups and downs, this is FOR SURE an up. Couldn't recommend any more if I tried.

_childDocuments_.review: In Amnesia The Bunker you play as a french soldier in WWI who is trapped in a bunker together with a murderous creature. The gameplay is probably best described as a mini-version of Alien Isolation set in 1916. Amnesia The Bunker leaves most of the rather simplistic „walking simulator“ characteristics of past Amnesia games behind and plays much more like a survival-horror immersive sim or a stealth game. Probably the biggest novelty is that you can use actual weapons to defend yourself. Now there are basically no other enemies besides the monster itself and a couple of aggressive rats (except for one creepy enemy in one particular spot later in the game which i won’t spoil), so the weapons are actually more useful for blowing doors open with explosive barrels. There are only two guns (the second one i didn’t even find in my playthrough) with very few available bullets and all they do is chasing away the monster for a couple of minutes anyway. The few additional explosives (grenades and molotov cocktails) are similarly useless in combat and serve basically just the same purpose as the guns, that is blowing obstacles away and maybe getting rid of some of the rats, but against the monster they won’t do sh*t.The atmosphere is indeed pure terror. The first few minutes you just spent crawling through the trenches of WWI. This mainly serves as a tutorial for the controls, but it also sets the tone of how absolutely awful and horrible this place is that you are in now. When you wake up in the bunker completely alone and then proceed to sneak through the dimly lit tunnels and start to hear the monster rumbling in the walls or screaming in the distance, the atmosphere just gets amazingly terrifying. Of course, like in basically every horror game, the monster becomes a bit predictable and once you’ve explored the bunker, familiarized yourself with the layout enough and stocked up on helpful items, you’ll start to feel slightly more confident and the scare factor wears off a bit. But of all the horror games i‘ve played, this is one of the very few that manages to maintain a certain feeling of dread and uncertainty all the way through, especially when you start to uncover more and more of the unsettling story over the course of the game. The whole thing just has a perfectly paced suspense curve that smoothly goes from actual terror and immediate threat through the monster to a more creepy and gloomy vibe when you learn more about the unsettling backstory. On top, the sound does it‘s part very well: Even when you don’t hear the terrifying screams of the monster, the game constantly lets you know that you are completely f*cked, for example when it regularly makes you hear the loud bangs and booms of artillery fire outside the bunker. It’s as if the game tells you „even if you make it out of here, you‘re still in a world of sh*t and you‘re gonna die.“ Basically the only small weak point are the outdated grafics, but the atmosphere gets so intense that you barely notice them anymore after half an hour. Overall, Amnesia the Bunker is a phenomenal survival-horror game that for about a handful of hours won‘t fail to unsettle and terrorize you and you wouldn’t want it any other way. The varied gameplay mechanics are so much more engaging than the „walk-hide in closet-walk“ gameplay of some past Amnesia games and I liked it so much that i finished the whole thing in one session. If this game doesn’t manage to give you at least a small sh*t-stain in your pants, nothing does (or you are clinically dead). Just make sure that you‘ll play in the proper environment: At night, alone, with headphones on!_______________________________________AMNESIA THE BUNKERGenre: Survival-Horror / StealthRelease: Q2 2023( ) 0/8 Simply one of the worst games ever made. Don't waste any money on this.( ) 1/8 Bad. Seriously flawed with barely any redeeming qualities. Worth a couple of Cents at best, if at all.( ) 2/8 Sub-par. Only for hardcore-fans of respective genre / series. Don't pay more than 5 bucks.( ) 3/8 Meh-diocre. It‘s okay. Don't pay more than 10 bucks.( ) 4/8 Decent, but not for everybody. Don't pay more than 15 bucks.( ) 5/8 Good game, Must-play for genre- / series-fans. Worth 20 to 25 bucks max, if you are not a fan.(X) 6/8 Great game, universal recommendation. 30 bucks would be a steal for this.( ) 7/8 Outstanding game, a milestone of it‘s respective genre. Definitely worth its full prize.( ) 8/8 Simply one of the best games ever made. Get this, the prize doesn't matter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a f*cking masterpiece! Tension being there for the entirety of the game, feeling chills whenever you make even the slightest noise that may draw the monster from the French bunker.... The setting is great, WW1 is raging and you have been trapped in a bunker damned to either leave the bunker by blowing up the exit or die a gruesome death. -Generator is my favorite mechanic, you must keep it running if you want to survive. Beside main "quests" you are always carving for a couple of cans of fuel to find along the way just so you can buy time to leave this Hell.-Flashlight is my other favorite thing in this game. It runs forever, theoretically. You pull the little wire and it's working, but beware! It makes noise, and if you keep making more noise you know who's gonna show up..... Something to greet you with a gruesome death.Overall 10/10. Setting is good, mechanics are good, horror elements are there, paranoia, chills down your spine etc.From the technical prospective, it's excellent, no frame drops, no glitches, no bugs (at least I haven't found any yet).Much better from 90% of the AAA games in the recent time. The price tag stands along with the experience you get playing this! Totally worth every single dollar!P.S The game is short, I want more of this! I hope there will be expansion to this game, like a DLC or something.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were dissatisfied with Rebirth and it makes you hesitant to try this one out; don't be, It's a fantastic game, the atmosphere is amazing, and even though I'm a little skeptical when it comes to how it tries to scare the player, it is still far better than most other horror titles out there.Somehow in terms of sheer gameplay, this is probably the most fun game Frictional Games' made yet. You have a big open location with few sectors, and figuring out what you have to do is very satisfying, as well as is mastering the game on subsequent playthroughs.There are two downsides though:-The game is short, around 4 to 6 hours depending on your play style, and if you know what to do on subsequent playthroughs, that time will go dramatically down.-The story is probably the least interesting out of all the games this studio put out. Maybe it works together with the WW1 setting and an idea that you are essentially a nobody, but it still was a little disappointing.But yeah, It's still a wonderful title, and it makes me really excited for what this studio will do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia the bunker is a survival horror that takes place during the first world war. You find yourself awakening inside of a underground bunker that is filled with your dead comrades, rats, and a monster that stalks you.The gameplay has you searching the bunker for resources such as gasoline, bandages, bullets, and tools that you need to complete objectives. The entire time you play you will be resource managing the electric generator as it’s the only source to keeps the lights on. On a full tank you only get about 20min before you need to refuel it again. You also have a flash light but it’s a wind up and makes noise, and only lasts about 30 seconds.I really wasn’t a fan of the gameplay. The generator consumed entirely too much fuel in a short amount of time which kept you from being able to fully explore areas before needing to run back. The monster seems to find you very easily and will become a nuisance later in the game. You will die A LOT if you are the type that likes to fully explore, then die and have to repeat 30min of game. It’s not a bad game. It just wasn’t for me. It played good, it looked good, and I had no issues. It played great on steam deck and maintained 60 fps almost all the time.6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker sees you playing as a French WWI soldier stranded inside of a mysterious bunker. Armed with only a noisy wind-up flashlight and a revolver with one bullet, you'll have to carefully explore the bunker and gather tools and supplies to plot your escape, all while being relentlessly stalked by a horrendous beast of unknown origins. Having played all the other Amnesia games, The Bunker was actually a really welcome surprise entry to the series. Featuring a shorter story focused around a smaller location, The Bunker feels more rogue-like in its progression compared to the story-driven previous entries. While there is definitely a story that takes places over the course of the game, the pace of it is more directly controlled by the player and their preferred path of exploration. I thought the gameplay and atmosphere was extremely captivating, I felt incredibly immersed in the setting and driven to constantly explore new areas to get new tools to help me escape. The threat of the Stalker enemy coming in at any moment to disrupt your journey reminded me a lot of Alien: Isolation in how it incentivized careful, crafty exploration. There's a certain degree of random generation as well, making it so each "run" of Amnesia: The Bunker has a slightly different layout of key items and supplies, on top of very customizable difficulty settings to make different aspects of the game behave in new ways. If I had to give a few negatives for Amnesia: The Bunker, for one, since the pacing is so player-controlled, the story can feel rushed or too slow at times depending on the player's confidence and progression methods. Additionally, the Stalker enemy starts to lose its scare factor after a few encounters once you really learn how to manipulate its AI and work around it, so it becomes less of a fearsome enemy and more of a nuisance/obstacle in the path of wherever you're going. Finally, the ending (while appropriate for the setting) felt very abrupt, and I would've liked potentially a bit more plot resolution. Overall though, I really enjoyed Amnesia: The Bunker. This was a really pleasant experience that gave me a lot of opportunity to solve puzzles and problems my own way, and that degree of player freedom and control really makes me see why people enjoy doing multiple runs of this game. I think Amnesia: The Bunker is definitely worth its current price point, or at the least on a minor sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cruel crazy dating sim. What a twist!You have to live with monster in one bunker and you establishing relationships with him. Since you are living together you need to respect his wishes and avoid disturbance,  After some time you will lose your fear and learn how to respect the guy and avoid problems with him. He will become your unwanted buddy. If you ever rented room, not the whole apartment, you will understand me. So this is perfect simulator of living together with someone you don't know good enough. Be silent, cautious an FIND WAY TO GET OUT OF HERE.Non-linear nature of the game is perfect, you never know where you will meet again and you feel yourself in control  of such situations, and almost always it works. _childDocuments_.review: I think this is one of the most ingeniously designed horror games ever made. Just thinking about the game design and the decision making that said design encourages is fun and always gets me itching to run another playthrough. There are more complete packages as far as survival horror goes as the story in this game is light (a strength imo) and not anything too special, and the runtime is short (4-6 hours first playthrough), but just on a pure gameplay level the incorporation of immersive sim elements, randomization, and an intelligent AI stalker is extremely inspired and makes for a highly re-playable experience. The recently added custom difficulty and the option to make the stalker AI more unpredictable were amazing changes that got me to do three more runs of this game. I feel like this game is the antithesis of the walking/yapping/cheap jumpscare simulator that a lot of bad horror games are, it's almost pure gameplay from front to back. I really hope Frictional's next project uses the same design principles.
