_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horror games I've played. The atmosphere is terrifying, just like the beast that stalks you. Its a bit like alien isolation, though much shorter thankfully. The beast is attracted to sound so you are kinda forced to take things slow, especially on harder difficulties and you cant kill it.  Speaking of, The game is pretty challenging and i was surprised by how much the item randomization(on NG+) make the game more fun and re-playable.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: This was a sleeper-release for me. I hadn't heard anything about it, not trailers, advertising...or anything! I had no idea it was even in development.I randomly came across it, decided to give it a shot, and boy was I pleasantly surprised!It has similar mechanics to previous Amnesia titles, but with a bit of a twist to them. The attention to detail is also greatly appreciated. The lights flickering serving as a warning for when the Beast comes around. The trail of dust that falls from the ceiling serving as an indication of where the Beast is headed when roaming the in-wall/ceiling tunnels. It has pretty decent AI as well. The moments when the Beast comes around, it's always very intense and a lot of fun!The physics mechanics are all really good too imo, adding another level of puzzle solving to the game.The sound design, and use of directional audio is fantastic! A lot of horror games out there will just have random creepy ambient sounds that go off around you to keep you on your toes; or even have some piece of audio that plays in your right ear only no matter where you look (I hate that). But Amnesia The Bunker uses audio to its full advantage. It's very important to keep track of audio cues, and where they're coming from. They're very telling, and can keep you alive!The only semi-annoying thing about the game is the old pulley flashlight. Gets kind of annoying having to wind it up all the time. However, it's mitigated a bit by the generator that keeps the lights on. Also, cool note, they did make the flashlight a bit more interesting than it just purely being an object that allows you to see. It also makes noise, and noise can attract the Beast. So you kind of have to be a bit strategic in how you use it sometimes.Overall, I really enjoyed it. I recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Frictional has done it again!Another major, anxiety inducing trip!Indeed, this masterpiece checks all of the boxes: good tension, horror, powerful enemy presence, a story, voice acting, music and surprisingly, even difficulty settings, so everyone can enjoy it!My only complaint is that despite the initial long load, there is another quick load for each individual map segment and the map is not that big to justify these. Just a minor inconvenience, of course.Great Amnesia installment, without any doubt!
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: It's Alien: Isolation meets Resident Evil, except the game isn't nearly as long as Alien: Isolation, which makes it better IMO. The game is very immersive sim-like, there are almost always multiple ways to solve problems, and the game's claim of "If you think it's possible, then it probably is." was completely true 9 times out of 10. Upon beating the game you're given approximately 500 difficulty options to customize your next playthrough however you like, which makes this game one of the most replayable horror games I've ever seen. On top of this is a really great and detailed story that builds a world you can easily get invested in, which enhances the immersive sim qualities. My only real complaint is how stingy saving is: there's 1 main save station that you need to backtrack to all the time, and any death means going back to your last save, which often means picking up every single little item that you got in your last life but didn't save. That got fairly annoying over time, and this somewhat diminished the horror of the game for me. Everything else about this game is fantasic though, so if you like survival horror games, you've got a damn near perfect one right here.
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: A true MASTERPIECE! This game excels in its survival horror and immersive sim mechanics in a remarkable way. Throughout my entire playthrough, I was having anxiety, anticipating the monster's emergence (as it dynamically responded to my every action) and managing the fuel burning in the generator. While the monster's appearance is scripted 2-3 times, the game's short length is compensated by its infinite replayability:1) Every playthrough features randomized items, corpses, locker codes, and inventory upgrades, ensuring a unique and different experience each time.2) Upon completing the game, you unlock "custom mode", allowing you to modify the game with various modifiers to set the difficulty to your liking.The ability to skip the intro with each new playthrough is a welcome feature. Similar to one of my favorite games of all time, Half-Life, you experience the story through your eyes, with no cutscenes interrupting the gameplay.Furthermore, if you learn how the monster operates, you can try the modifier that makes it unpredictable, adding a new layer of fear and making the game scary all over again.You can also do the "missions" in different order (after you use the hand wheel) making the game more interesting.In summary, this is a genuinely scary horror game without resorting to jump scares, offering infinite replay value. All games should aim for this level of replayability.***EDIT: I forgot to mention that this game has also the workshop.***
_childDocuments_.name: Amnesia: The Bunker

_childDocuments_.review: Amnesia: The Bunker went further then my expectations. Although the game felt simply crafted but it took me longer to finish then Rebirth (Finished Rebirth in 3 days). The game is more focused on escaping like in an escape room but I liked that idea. This game feels also like it's another "Justine" to the Amnesia series. But after all, it is a really enjoyable game. Simple, well crafted and a saving grace for the criticized Rebirth.This game definitely did it better then Rebirth and A Machine For Pigs for me. Well done Frictional.

_childDocuments_.review: My perfect horror for now. Literally all I have dreamt about. All the mechanics are great.+ Open-world: For a moment I stopped seeing the game as a GAME. I felt as if I personally had to get through the bunker and was there on my own, without a scripted narrator;+ Multiple ways to solve problems;+++ The monster. It feels like it listens to me and hears every little sound. What a joy it was to step on a random pile of broken wood planks and hear the monster coming for me. It generates so many unexpected scenarios I was literally sharing each of my deaths with friends;+ Item spawns change (that brought more joy that I expected);+ Fantastic sound design;+ Marvellous physics and interaction with the world (I love you for that since penumbra);- After some hours of running and hiding the game feels more like going to work. _childDocuments_.review: Compared to other games in the series, The Bunker takes an extra step with additional ways of handling enemy encounters (no longer just hide and seek), a bit more nonlinear story progression and an option to make your exploration safer/easier for a limited amount of time at the cost of some resources.THINGS WORTH MENTIONING:-The total time I spent to 100% the game's achievements and mess around with out of bounds was 12 hours. I didn't get bored at any point and can confidently say that the 12 hours I spent playing the game were worth the price.-While the "easy" difficulty has multiple save points, "normal" and "hard" only have 1. When discovering this, I expected it to be a lot more problematic/frustrating than it ended up being as the save point is located in the center of the map so if I did end up dying I never lost more than 10-15 minutes of progress. (This additionally made me more careful, cautious and afraid of the things lurking in the shadow).-The sound effects are just right and the atmosphere is terrifying as the monster's introduction is superb and always leaves you wondering how scared you should be of what it's capable of doing to you and your surroundings.-The map is split into multiple sections, with each having it's own slight difference in theme and design, which keeps the map from feeling repetitive and stale.-Excluding the ending, backtracking is available throughout the entire game in one way or another, where the only con is spending more time with the bunker's residents. It's perfect for making additional runs to parts of the map for supplies, or double checking for missed collectables. Basically, you don't need to worry about missing something if you move to a different area.-Out of the Amnesia games, Bunker's notes gave me the most chills reading them, each one adding to the atmosphere and terror in the bunker. They give incredible insight on the story of why and how everything happened, it is so far the only game where I wanted more notes after each one I read.-There are a few more keybinds than other Amnesia games but nothing overwheling, settings are easy to adjust and will most likely take you less than 5 minutes to find your setting sweet spot.-And to top it all off, the good old Amnesia object interactions. They work just fine through the game but are also fun to use to get out of bounds and similar. I STRONGLY recommend messing around with the white Vinly disc cover in the save point room :)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the biggest gripes I ever had with Amnesia as a whole was that it was a horror game that didn't really have...Options. Your only way to go was forward, you'd only ever encounter monsters, and upon encountering monsters, you only had one option, and that was whatever the game wanted you to do at that moment. Run if it was a sequence where you were supposed to run, hide if it was a sequence where you were supposed to hide. Add in things like the sanity meter in a game where even looking at a monster for thirty seconds will then mean you're going to see monster hallucinations and suffer from who knows how many other downsides, and you have a recipe for a bad time unless you know exactly how the game wants you to play it.The Bunker, though? The Bunker is different, primarily because it's a take on the Amnesia formula that values options and flexibility over length. Instead of this one-way adventure through a giant mansion or a desert while being tracked by a multitude of monsters, The Bunker follows a much more simple formula: What if you were in a much smaller, open-ended area that trades out that multitude of monsters for one persistent, seemingly smart one? What if you could go in nearly any direction you wanted from the start? What if you had plenty of different options for how to solve an issue? What if you had a saferoom where you could take a break and gather your bearings while stockpiling and sorting your supplies? What if you had a generator that could take away the dangers of the dark with the tradeoff of constantly needing fuel to stay running?Encounter the monster? You can:#1: Shoot it, if you have the ammo.#2: Run from it, if you feel like you can survive the chase.#3: Hide from it, if you can break line of sight and find a way to isolate yourself.#4: Set it on fire, if you've got a molotov and a lighter.#5: Gas it, if you have a chemical grenade with you.#6: Lure it into a trap, if there's a tripwire nearby, you can jump over them, it can't.I'm technically getting into spoilers if I talk about too much else past this point, so I'll just say that the game focuses more on quality and variety within a smaller, open-ended environment that prioritizes putting you in situations where you have to think with your head to get out of them.Originally, if you told people back then there'd be an Amnesia sequel where they give you a gun, everyone would probably laugh at you, but I've found them adding fighting threats as an option instead of just running and hiding has done so, so much for the game as a whole. The monster is smart by Amnesia standards, it plays by its own rules you can learn if you pay attention, and that learning via observing permits you to better prepare yourself to survive future encounters with it.You'll probably die, I died several times playing this despite being pretty good at games like these, but at the same time, the deaths don't feel forced or unfair, and once you've learned the rules of the game, you'll get very, very good at it.Also in hindsight: I appreciate The Bunker because its puzzles are more...Emergent and less obvious. A door's locked, so you need to open it. Do you toss a grenade at it and blow it open, making a ton of noise and alerting the monster to you? Or do you brave the perils of several other hazards in order to circle around and open it, quietly, from the other side? You no longer have the days of having to solve some strange alien rotary lock cipher puzzle while a wraith is looking for you, it's simple: You need to get through a locked door, you need to clear a hazard out of your way, you need to distract the monster, you need to find a way to a key item, or, most commonly: You need to find a way to get out of an encounter with the 'Beast' alive and not torn in half.There are actually several skips you can pull off and shave off a ton of time if you know what you're doing, and intriguingly, a lot of these skips involve both alerting the monster and then knowing how to make a quick and timely escape.All in all? 8/10. I'm not a fan of the Amnesia series, but an approach and style to the formula like this made me one. Here's hoping Frictional realize the goldmine they've stumbled upon and expand the possibilities of future games going forward from here.And to certain people on the forums: 60 FPS is perfectly fine for a game, if you're going to bash the developers over a 60 FPS lock and say it's 'killing the game' when this is one of the most stable and remarkably well-optimized Amnesia titles to date that's also smashed numbers on release, here's a piece of advice: Please, for the love of god, shut up.

_childDocuments_.review: I put this game off for a bit because some reviews moaned on and on about constantly running back and forth trying to keep the fuel tank filled, however, I have no idea what they're talking about. The need to keep that thing fueled wasn't nearly as necessary as some of these other reviewers seemed to indicate. Others bemoaned shooting locks off doors. I honestly have no idea what these people are talking about. While, yes, these elements did exist, they weren't game destroying. Further, you DO NOT HAVE TO explore with the lights on. The monster still comes at you even with the lights on, albeit a bit less, but it still does. Other than the handful of situations where you need the electricity to move forward, resource issues just aren't as big an issue as certain reviewers just seemed to indicate. I'm rather annoyed I listened to them, because they caused my hesitation at buying this game sooner. Now that I've got that out of the way - overall, I enjoyed this game. The ending was questionable, but... I mean, it's an amnesia game. Of course it's questionable. In the game, you will find yourself trapped in an underground bunker while trying to evade a beast that cannot be killed. You will sneak and explore, trying to find the items you need, so that you can advance through the bunker and eventually escape. You will find yourself hiding in spots that you think are safe, only for the beast to find you and, if you're lucky, kill you quickly. This game does not quite capture the essence of the first Amnesia game, but it does a decent attempt for as small as it is. For a relatively short and simplistic game, I think it has decent replay value (items can change location, so you can't ever memorize things), and it's short enough that it doesn't quite feel like a chore as you attempt to beat previous completion scores.

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed all the Amnesia games and all but one Penumbra title. Whether the story or the game play takes priority, the series has always been solid for me. I'd say every Amnesia is worth experiencing just to make the memories, but the issue of terror induced by stress hasn't really been a part of the game since Dark Descent. Rebirth had moments, but I never made shamefully unmanly noises, had to pause because I was freaking the Hell out, or just realized my palms were soaked in sweat since Dark Descent. I went into this game 100% blind, and as soon as I realized it was resource management, crafting focused, and how the hunt worked, I was completely enthralled. The engine is the same as always, but it's focused on more than ever. Everything can break, everything can help you. There are times a brick is more valuable than a bullet. There are a ton of ways to approach this game and the tools let you pick and choose your level of risk. Choosing whether to venture in the dark, or keep the light on to buy a bit more time before the Beast shows. Realizing that the only solution you can think of will set off a bang and desperately considering hiding spots beforehand and wondering if he's learned your patterns...The Beast is drawn by noise by the way, and you'll quickly realize everything is loud, something as simple as bumping into a crate will send a shiver down your back, especially early game where you aren't intimate with the Beast yet. And as it goes on, you will get more confident and there is a beautiful rhythm between when the Beast controls your progress or when you're handling the Bunker and feel in control. He learn your patterns, and if you keep hiding in the same way, he will notice. And the audio design is all you really have to rely on as this game is dark even by Amnesia standards. The audio is also very accurate, you can track him through audio alone, and it's absolutely terrifying. Hiding from monsters is nothing new to Amnesia, but this is the first time I've felt sheer absolute terror because unlike prior games, the Beast can destroy almost anything, and is not as easy to cheese as enemies in prior games. I had three moments that the Beast tricked me, and put me into fight or flight, and despite the remarkably terror I managed to get away and felt the fear AND the reward at the same time and it's just so freaking FUN.  This game is fun, it isn't easy(but gets easier as you go) and isn't as accessible as others but it's just such a blast. It's not long but there are like fifty custom tweaks you can do for future runs, and I can't stop thinking about it and wanting to play it over and over again. It's simple, it's honest, it's scary, it rewards your creativity, and I loved every second of it. If you enjoyed Darkwood, the Penumbra series, or Witch Hunt, you will love this game and should buy it as soon as possible. Even full price, it's 100% worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review:
Left all alone in a desolate WW1 bunker with only one bullet remaining in the barrel, it's up to you to face the oppressing terrors in the dark. Keep the lights on at all costs, persevere, and make your way out alive. In the shoes of the French soldier Henri Clément, you are armed with a revolver gun, a noisy dynamo flashlight, and other scarce supplies to scavenge and craft along the way. With randomization and unpredictable behavior, no play-through is the same.

Hunted by an ever-present threat reacting to your every move and sound, you must adapt your play-style to face hell. Every decision will change the outcome of how the game responds.

name: DC's Justice League: Cosmic Chaos
detailed_description: Unite against chaos, in an all-new open world adventure where the Justice League go head-to-head with Mr. Mxyzptlk, a powerful prankster from the 5th Dimension. Suit up as Batman, Wonder Woman and Superman and go face off against some of the most powerful Super-Villains in the DC universe; including Bizarro, Starro the Conqueror, Clayface and many more in an epic battle to bring peace to Happy Harbor. DC’s Justice League: Cosmic Chaos gives you the freedom to play your way in action-packed missions, gruelling fights and daring challenges! Fly around Happy Harbor as Superman or propel yourself through the sky as Wonder Woman, the choice is yours! Play with friends or family in 2 player couch co-op Instant Action Mode and have the freedom to explore Happy Harbor, the home of the Justice League. Become Happy Harbor’s hero - with unlockable Elemental Attacks plus iconic moves and armor, including Superman's Heat Vision, Wonder Woman’s Truth’s Pull and Batman’s exploding Batarangs. Unravel mysteries that lead to Super-Villains, bounties, and secret locations Team up with friends and family in 2-player instant action co-op Play as Superman, Wonder Woman and Batman in action-packed missions and side quests

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely fun! If anyone has played Justice League Heroes on the classic xbox its kinda like that, a top down beat em up like marvel ultimate alliance but with the Trinity! They have classic RPG mechanics in here with a big skill tree that unlocks new abilities as you level up so you can mix and match abilities. You can unlock other justice league members to come out and fight with you but they have a cool down after they leave. The Free-roam is extremely fun with so many locations and mini dungeons to conquer. The games story so far is hilarious and fun, it also has couch co op and Online co op. _childDocuments_.review: A fun and simple Justice League Experience, despite it being designed for a younger audience, the game has a lot of charm and has decent world exploration and many references to the comics and the larger DC world. The game offers great voice talent as well to portray these character. However there are still a few minor stuttering issues here and there. A decent and fun experience for those who want a simple Justice League game for all ages with the flavor of DC's Golden-Silver Age of comics. 7.5-8/10!

_childDocuments_.review: I’d recommend this game to superhero fans and fans of the LEGO games.  I’d also suggest paying what you’re willing to pay for a LEGO game, too.That being said, I had a fun time playing this on Steam Deck.  This has a lot of good references for DC comics fans, and it’s family friendly since the aim here is for the kids.  The co-op is separate from the main story mode.  However, the mode that allows co-op has all abilities and costumes already unlocked, so it’s better for casual players and playing with kids who want to do everything in the game from the get go.This game has a Saturday morning cartoon feel to it, and that’s in large thanks to the voice acting, including Diedrich Bader returning as Batman.  Other voice actors you may recognize from other media.The game itself plays as a light action RPG, though more leaning into the action in that arcade style of dungeon crawling through the missions.  You unlock abilities as you level, you level the respective skill trees as resources are gathered from defeating enemies and unlocking treasure chests, and you can equip items to boost the characters and enhance their abilities.All 3 heroes have their own traversal in the over world, though in the levels and missions, these traversals are unavailable.Notable downsides is when playing this game, after a while something can glitch.  For examples, Superman’s heat vision stopped being hitting enemies, jellyfish villains would be invisible, or you may enter a vehicle and for some reason not be able to exit the vehicle despite using the button to exit.  The remedy to these is exiting the game and going back into it, possibly even resetting the game.  Thankfully the auto save feature means you don’t lose much progress when this happens.

_childDocuments_.review: As of 3/16, it says I've only been playing for 28 minutes, BUT I did just beat the game on Switch. (EDIT: I've played 20 hours on Switch.) I've played literally non-stop the past three days and have found almost every item, alongside unlocking every costume, and beating every mini boss. I just discovered that you can try out all of the costumes and items in the free-play couch co-op mode, but I've been on the grind with finding them in the story mode.The story itself is great, the voice acting is incredible, and the creators clearly love DC Comics. You play as Supes, Bats, and Wonder Woman, rotating between the three of them on the fly. Even though they have their own traversal options, you can even drive vehicles, which is hilarious. They aren't the only three members of the Justice League in the game however, as you can unlock various team members as sidekicks. (I won't list for fear of spoilers, even though it's pretty clear from the advertising.) I'm reviewing the game here because the publishers gifted me a copy for Steam (which was amazing of them!) Long story short, the Switch version has some performance issues, particularly with frame rate drops leading to lag and character attacks not registering. This was an issue specifically with Superman, where his heat vision wasn't making contact. So I was almost playing exclusively as Batman there towards the end of the game. There's also an issue where sometimes you can't get out of vehicles. Tip: if you drive into the water, it'll blow up the vehicle so you can get out, lol.The gameplay itself is simplistic but super addicting and the music is cohesive with the environment, making it one of the chillest action games I've played in a long time. Simply put, I cannot recommend this game enough. I truly love it.PS: The story is engaging, but play on "heroic" mode to make it more challenging.PPS: Did I mention you can ride a skateboard?

_childDocuments_.review: DC's Justice League: Cosmic Chaos caught me completely by surprise. By looking at the graphics, and the publisher, Outright Games, I honestly did not expect a lot going into this. I was expecting a boring lifeless cash grab on the Justice League IP, but what I got was a pleasant game full of character and deep cut DC comic references and a game that was clearly made with with deep love for the source material. Is the game perfect? Absolutely not, but I can honestly say that I thoroughly enjoyed my 12 hours spent getting all the achievements in this game and if you're a fan of the comics, looking for a game for a younger gamer, or just looking for a game you can play without thinking too much to have a good time with, then I can honestly say that I recommend this game if you can get it on a sale.The story is very simple, but perfectly fine for what this game is. The game starts off with Snapper Carr being elected mayor of Happy Harbor, the city where the game takes place. Suddenly out of nowhere Mr. Mxzyptlk appears, unleashing Starro the Conqueror upon the Justice League and the rest of the town. From there your mission is clear, save the affected members of the Justice League, and stop Mr. Mxzyptlk and Starro from taking over the world. It's nothing too special but it does a good job of giving you a reason to go from place to place and I think Mr. Mxzyptlk was the perfect choice for a villain in a game like this as it allowed all of these silly and fun things to happen that suit the game very well. Gameplay wise, Cosmic Chaos is very much a baby's first dungeon crawler, and it will certainly draw comparisons to Marvel's Ultimate Alliance games, which I think is warranted, but do not go into this expecting the same complexity in dungeon layout or combat as those games, as Cosmic Chaos is a much simpler game. Here you can only control 3 characters, and only 1 at a time but switching between them can be done instantly. Each character has a normal attack, ranged attack, special attack, and ultimate ability with additional members of the Justice League being able to be called in for some help once you've freed them from Starro's control. The enemies have elemental weaknesses pertaining to each of the 3 characters so you'll constantly be switching among them, although Superman is by far the best of the 3. The dungeons you go through aren't too confusing with slight variations from dungeon to dungeon to keep them from getting overly repetitive. There are side missions with more varied dungeons ending with boss fight with villains from Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman's rogue galleries, which was a nice treat. Overall, the gameplay is simplistic, but addicting, and the game won't be too challenging for younger gamers, and not overly easy for older gamers, especially since you can change the difficulty settings in the menu. You might be looking at this game thinking "wow, this looks like a great game to play with my child", well sadly, while there is co-op, you cannot go through the story mode in co-op which is a real shame. All you can do is run around the map and beat up bad guys, a real disappointment since this game seems PERFECT for a parent and child to play through together. While at first look, I didn't love the style of the graphics, they did grow on me over time. They do look exactly like those young reader comics I see for sale at my local comic book store so to be fair to them if that's what they were going for, they absolutely nailed it. The animations are all quite nice and all the different enemies you battle have distinct looks to them. The best part about the presentation though has to be the voice acting. The dialogue and constant banter between the main three of Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman was a treat to hear and while it did get a little bit repetitive towards the end of the game, it never annoyed me. The dialogue is full of references to the comics that will entertain older comic fans, and you can collect comic books across the map to unlock comics that reference the character's history in comics, including a personal favorite of mine, Kingdom Come Superman.Unfortunately, I couldn't do a proper review of this game without mentioning that yes, this game sadly does suffer from some bugs that are yet to be ironed out. One bug that I encountered made it unable for me to leave a vehicle once I entered it. this came up a couple of times, at one point forcing me to restart the game in the middle of a mission. A forum post shows that the developers have been aware of this issue since at least October, 2023, and it has yet to be fixed at the time of me writing this. A couple of times, I had enemies get stuck in walls or other parts of the environment, but I would still be able to kill them. Outside of a couple times where the voice acting didn't play for a few lines of dialogue these were the only bugs I encountered, and luckily none of them were game breaking, and although there were game breaking bugs at launch, it appears these were patched out luckily. DC's Justice League: Cosmic Chaos was a pleasant surprise for me, as a fan of the DC universe and comics. While it's not perfect, and the lack of ability to play through the story mode in co-op significantly hurts it I think, if you're looking for a relaxing fun, simplistic dungeon crawler, this game will certainly scratch that itch. I wouldn't pay full price for it, but getting it on a sale is definitely worth it if what you've read sounds fun to you. For more reviews, follow my

_childDocuments_.review: I've already gotten the platinum on PS5, but wanted to write a review here. This is probably Outright Games' best release. The devteam did a really good job. There's full voice acting which isn't the usual for Outright, sadly, but the art design is really nice. It has animated cutscenes that are really cool, the graphics have a nice style and look super polished.The gameplay itself is pretty basic, but it's fun. If you enjoy LEGO type gameplay and dungeon crawler dungeons then it's a good pick for you. The main criticisms I would place on the game is the dungeons. They're just a bit boring and same-y feeling. And it's a bit of a bummer you're limited to 3 (Batman, Superman, Wonder Woman) from the JL. It would've been nice to play as others like Flash, Green Lantern, Cyborg and Aquaman that are also in the game but regulated to support characters. But, I suppose it allows the story to be more focused. The story is highly amusing. There are tons of references to past DC moments weaved into the dialog that occurs ingame and during cutscenes. There's unlockable costumes which is a nice touch in an era of gaming where costumes are usually regulated to paying for DLC. There are different abilities you can use, you can change your elemental attacks, there's a kind of rock paper scissors element to the elements. It's not a huge deal most of the game, especially if you go for the story mode. I was trying that out on PC and it's very much easy. I don't think I took a single point of damage at all from that difficulty. So it's very accessible to younger players. I played normal on PS5 and it was balanced pretty well.The game's health items work kind of like Dark Souls, as tired as comparisons of that are. In that you have X amount of health items and you restore the charges at a little HP fountain looking thing. I really like that as opposed to buying healing items or finding them. And you can unlock more for use later. On normal I barely had to heal at all. There's a lot of equipment to choose from when you're equipping things and a lot are also references to DC things. A lot is missed on me, as I'm not *that* familiar with DC comics but if you are there's clearly a lot of love and attention put into the game.The voice actors are all really good for their roles. This is a licensed game deserving of a bit more love. It's really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Outright Games is often likened to a modern-day LJN, a reputation that is well deserved, and the developer PHL Collective has also made one of my absolute least favourite of their games (the Ben 10 one in particular) so while I did find the trailer and concept interesting, I wasn't sure what to think about this game. Having now completed it, I can honestly say it's a reminder that even the developers and publishers you're not too fond of may have a decent title once in a while.Right from the beginning of the game I felt a lot more care put into Cosmic Chaos than the other Outright Games titles I've tried. The first thing of note is the art style - it's unique to this game and very cute. You control 3 of DC's most iconic heroes: Superman, Batman, and Wonder Woman, with some other heroes acting as assists you can summon. There are plenty of events and cutscenes in the game, all fully voice acted. They got some pretty good voice actors as well, like Dana Snyder who steals the show as Mr. Mxyzptlk. Gameplay-wise, it's a beat em up with some simple puzzles, and like most of Outright's titles it's targeted for a younger/more casual audience. Fans will enjoy using each hero's power. You can throw enemies into traps with Wonder Woman's lasso, or fly through the sky as Superman. You can even drive vehicles, though this mechanic wasn't used in the game's story at all and was more of a bonus to make exploration more fun. I would heavily recommend waiting for a sale for this title if you are at all interested in it, though. While it can be fun and I enjoyed the time I had with it's main campaign, I wouldn't say it's worth the 50$+ price tag it's been given.

_childDocuments_.review: The best "Superman" and "Wonder Woman" game we will probably ever get.+ Top tier voice acting (Dana Snyder was perfect for his role).+ Solid script that is as fun for adults as for kids.+ The most simplistic, yet, enjoyable flying mechanic for Superman.+ Special attributes in the form of DC collectable items from many DC characters+ Side Missions that incorporate villains from Batman, Superman and Wonder Woman specific lore+++ The best achievement ever designed (inspired by Tony Hawk Pro Skater)+++ You compete on a game show reminiscent of MXC "Most Extreme Elimination challenge" (including a few of the original Takeshi's Castle games)...you have to respect that kind of call back in a modern game.I can't think of anything absolutely, glaringly wrong with the game.  Some may have a problem that it is not full of sex and violence, but the feel of the game comes from a more "Saturday morning cartoon" era.It really is the little things that the game takes into consideration that makes it feel like a work of love such as:= Being able to bounce on the trampolines and diving boards= Driving any of the cars or boats in the open map (as well as calling in the Batmobile, Wonder Woman's motorcycle, or Superman's spaceship)= A fully voiced radio station of talk shows and advertisements= The world feels alive with people milling aboutI randomly stumbled across this game and while not being a huge superhero fan, I had a great time playing through this.  Something about it is fun, breezy and colourful; and brings a smile to my face.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game to play with kids. It is designed to appeal to old timers (like me) who grew up reading the adventures of Superman, Batman and the Justice League and to kids who also are getting to know this rich universe. I play it with my daughter and she loved it. Until the game crashed, the screen became black and we lost all our progress. I researched and discovered this happened a lot, with many people, and in different parts of the game. The common factor is thar when it happens, you lose all your progress. We had to start all over again, When we got to the point where the problem happened (just after saving the Flash), I turned off steam cloud saving, and it worked. Since the game does not save without it, I turned it on again just before exiting the game, and by doing this, the problem was solved.Botton Line: you like DC heroes and have a small child who likes videogames, this game is very good. But it has some bad bugs, that require attention.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. The game is a little repetitive, and some of the quips that the characters utter will get on your nerve after you've heard them for the thousandth time. The game is geared towards younger players, but is fun for all. The script includes plenty of easter eggs for fans of the comics, and had a few good laughs. The gameplay reminds me of Justice League Heroes from the PS2. Out of the 3 characters that you can play as, I found Superman to be the best, then Batman, and the worst to be Wonder Woman. Superman worked best for me because his heat vision work really well as a long range weapon that recharged very quickly. I would say that this game is worth it if you are either a fan of the comics or someone who prefers more simplified, casual games.

name: Ten Dates
detailed_description: 📢 WISHLIST THE ISLE TIDE HOTEL About the Game Ten Dates is the sequel to the interactive rom-com, Five Dates. Misha, a millennial from London in search of that elusive in-person connection, tricks her best friend Ryan into going to a speed dating event with her. Each with their own five potential matches, Misha and Ryan must pluck up the courage and turn on the charm to date wildly different personalities. Throughout the game, your choices and interactions will either strengthen or weaken your relationship with your date. Amidst a branching, multi-directional chain of conversation topics and deep-dive questions, Misha and Ryan are faced with ice-breaker games, awkward scenarios and unexpected truths. Will either find love? A live-action romantic comedy with 12 hours of total footage Directed by Paul Raschid (Five Dates, The Complex) Authentic representation of groups including but not limited to; disability, neurodiversity and LGBTQ+ Real-time Relationship Status Tracking that influences the story as you play Pause your choices to interact with your community, your friends, or to just give you more time (optional) Ryan, a young urban heart-throb on a quest to find true love amidst the complexities of city dating. He wears his emotions on his sleeve and his words have the power to endear or alienate. Misha is a captivating city single searching for her perfect match. Her magnetic charm and quick wit leave a lasting impression on all who cross her path. With a sparkling personality, is she the missing piece to someone's love puzzle? A staple of the social scene, Bash is the ultimate lad, always ready for a good time with his friends. But is there more to him than just sports, beer, and crude jokes? Can you see through his exterior and discover the charming and endearing qualities within? Alpha and financially mobile, Brandy is the quintessential hustler. Keep up with her as she puts you to the test in a race to win her over. Learn about her journey and how she became a trailblazer in the city of London. Attractive, exciting, and devilishly charming, Ty is the ultimate bad boy with a hint of mystery. Will you be able to resist his rough exterior and see the potential for redemption within him? Or will his wild ways lead to heartbreak? A non-conformist rebel with a sharp wit. Explore the world of activism and arcane interests with this guarded, passionate firecracker. Meet the ultimate nice guy, dependable, kind and always ready to put a smile on your face. With a good job and a solid social life, he offers a pleasant dating experience. But is there more to him than meets the eye? Will you see through his surface-level charm and find the genuine interest he has in you? Get ready to break a sweat with this clean-living, driven athlete. Join her in her quest to break through society's slow acceptance of female sports and tackle the challenges she faces as a female athlete. The quirky and lovable coder with a sense of humour. As technology grows, so does Lucas's relatability. He may not be a dating expert, but his personable nature and trendy tech interests make him a standout in the dating scene. A PhD student with brilliance, charm, and a zest for life. Get ready for a thought-provoking journey as you join forces with this easy-going genius. A confident, approachable individualist with a relatable personality. Despite her un-curated exterior, Hazel hides a deeper story waiting to be uncovered. Join her as she navigates the dating scene and discovers what it means to be truly authentic. An urbane, suave, and smooth-talking event host. With his charm and effortless conversation skills, Derek will sweep you off your feet. A diverse cast includes Rosie Day (Outlander), Charlie Maher (Conversations with Friends), Meaghan Martin (Until Dawn, Camp Rock), Sagar Radia (Industry), Sam Buchanan (The Power), Kaine Zajaz (The Witcher), Ellie James (I May Destroy You), and Rhiannon Clements (Death On The Nile).

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I bought this game with high hopes after playing Five Dates. However, if you are a guy, the female characters in this game don't even come close to the acting of the female characters in Five Dates. Additionally, all of the characters in this game are quirky, which can be good to have some oddballs, but when everyone is quirky it becomes too much. Moreover, the mini-games in this game are not as fun as the virtual games like truth or dare. This version feels bland.I did think the concept of the relationship guide HUD was good, but overall it wasn't necessary. I'm not one to complain about a game, but when you start with an amazing game like Five Dates, you have to maintain that level. The developers really need to work on making this game as good as the prequel, or even better. Unfortunately, this game is just not there yet.

_childDocuments_.review: !! Solid 8 / 10 !!I loved five dates, so I woke up early on launch day to download. No early access here :)I played the first playthru as Misha, and played as if it was me - and ended up with a wonderful storyline with the character I would be most interested in , in real life. That made me happy.I love that the playthru options include hints on what the goals are, and not all of them are positive! So so much replayability.I love spending the time figuring out what options get you to some of the harder one.Some of the closed captioning is incorrect or has spelling/grammar mistakes and I do use the CC so this was a little aggravating. And I found a few bugs - things not checked off when met, etc .  But the music and graphics are great, the acting on both Misha and Ryan are top notch and I love the twist each character has that you meet. Appreciate the LBTQ+ inclusivity as well; it was not put in just for a checkbox but with a legitimate approach and depth.If you enjoy FMV, visual novels with choices and replayability, this is the game for you. Its exceptionally good for those who want to try dating sims but don't want the NSFW/sexual component. This is really about personality and compatibility.  Love it!

_childDocuments_.review: 𝖫𝖮𝖶𝖤𝖲𝖳 𝖯𝖮𝖲𝖲𝖨𝖡𝖫𝖤 𝖲𝖢𝖮𝖱𝖤: 𝟏 – HIGHEST 𝖯𝖮𝖲𝖲𝖨𝖡𝖫𝖤 𝖲𝖢𝖮𝖱𝖤: 𝟓➔ 👥  👱🏼‍♀️ 👱🏼‍♀️👩🏼‍🦳 | 2/3 (fun to stream or have friends watch) ➔ 🖥️  🖱️⌨️ (mouse and keyboard)Speed dating is a nerve-wracking thing for many people since you only have a few minutes to make small talk and leave a good impression. And whether it’s speed dating or regular dating, we’ve all been there -or be there- at one point and experienced it; The good, the bad, the ugly and the awkward. Ten Dates does an excellent job of portraying this, as well as all the different personalities you will encounter throughout your journey of finding “the one”.While it is true that some of the characters can feel over-the-top stereotypical, I rather like to view it from a different angle; it’s enlarged on purpose to celebrate how unique and different everyone is. With more diversity added, perhaps we all can find ourselves – partly or fully- in one or more characters; or it might make you think of someone you know, making the immersive experience greater. With 10 dates -5 for each main character, you can play as- the bachelors and bachelorettes are single and ready to mingle, showing you a little more about themselves and their stories on each date. After 3 successful dates, you get rewarded with a picture and tagline of the happy couple.I have a first-look video to give you a feel for some of the characters The gameplay itself is very simple; all you do is make choices when the prompt appears. There are two settings for this, the default setting that gives you a time limit makes it so that you aren’t stalling, and you must make your decision quickly. This makes the scenes and overall FMV experience feel smoother.The other option “streamer mode” can be turned on in the settings, when the prompt appears everything will pause, and you’ll have more time to think about your choice.But keep in mind, every action has a reaction. You could be setting yourself up for success but also for failure and it might take several tries to lead your dates to happy endings.Don’t fret when you failed, the game has a great skip button that’s almost near perfect. I’ve come to notice it skips most scenes you’ve seen but if you take a different answer from a prior run, it throws you on a different ‘path' and when you happen to get back to a scene you’ve seen before, it’s not skippable until a little later again, at least if you don’t go off the ‘path’ again. So, it felt a bit odd sometimes, leaving me puzzled and randomly trying my skip button till it worked again. While it’s not that big of a deal, I still would’ve preferred for it to just skip mainly because you always must restart from the very beginning and go through your dating venture.It made it so that I couldn’t fully go for it as I desired, and I felt forced to take breaks to avoid the repetitiveness and burning out, while all I wanted to do was just binge-play and take in the whole experience in one go. All. Of. It.All of this is accompanied by wonderful graphics and music. The splendid acting from all the characters shines through and makes the entire plot feel natural, easy and believable and does a great honour in showing how an FMV should be. Seamless, as if you’re right there in the movie with them, fully submerged in the experience.And not that it is an issue, but I think for one split second I caught a third wall break and I was living for it, the first thing I did was show a friend and we had a good laugh with it. Whilst the music and background noise felt so blended in, it’s there but it isn’t there. It’s like how it really would be if you’re engaged in a conversation with someone on a date while in a pub or a bar. Excellent job.The only small point of critique would be the diversity of scenery, a part of me longed to have more settings to avoid visual repetitiveness. While most achievements come naturally, I think I got unlucky missing a few and to be honest it was because I had played the previous game -five dates- that I got a hunch on how to get them, from that moment it wasn’t all too hard to pick them up quickly.Do keep in mind 100% achievements =/= 100% the game as there are a lot of scenes and some in-game bullet points to collect – not obligated but just for fun- It all depends on if you’re fine with having it played out and conquered all the achievements or rather take the full completionist route. I’ve had a marvellous time in the game, even when I struggled now and then because let’s be honest; it’s been a very long time since I’ve dated, and I almost forgot how to. The number of times I couldn't figure some characters out and chased them away - yikes!With no idea, if this is how speed dating goes -as I never did it- I still had a blast experiencing it this way; making me feel like it's now something I can strike out from my bucket list, oddly enough.I had a few good laughs, and I had a few sob moments that made me think ‘holy frek’ no wonder… It’s been a rollercoaster of emotions playing through and would recommend it to people who are a fan of FMV, rom-coms and dating sims.And it makes me curious to know what they will cook up for us next dating-wise. We’ve had phone dates due covid in ‘five dates’ and now speed dating as I’m not ready yet for this series to end, I need and crave more. So, I would say come on and surprise me!  With love,Tchii💻 𝐆𝐞𝐅𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐞 𝐑𝐓𝐗 𝟑𝟎𝟕𝟎, 𝐀𝐌𝐃 𝐑𝐲𝐳𝐞𝐧 𝟕 𝟑𝟕𝟎𝟎𝐗, 𝟑𝟐𝐆𝐁 𝐑𝐀𝐌✨ 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 𝐢𝐧-𝐠𝐚𝐦𝐞 𝐬𝐞𝐭𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 | 𝟏𝟗𝟐𝟎𝐱𝟏𝟎𝟖 𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧📝 No performance issues to report, everything went smoothly and perfectly. I received the product for free. I did not receive any compensation to write this review. The opinions represented here, as well as my experience with the game, are entirely my own and were not influenced in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten Dates, as a sequel to Five Dates, goes into a very similar direction and still is a FMV in which you make choices that will decide if your dates go well or not. This time just instead of an online date, it starts of as a speed date. The concept of a date is simple and something we all know which makes it easy to get into the characters and understand how they feel. Its also nice that the cast is quite diverse as it makes the dates a lot more different and makes it so that we all will find someone thats interesting to us at least to an extend. The choices you make also can change a pretty broad portion of the conversations and even the interests you pick in the beginning for the character you play do have some consequences in the dialogues.In general if you think you would enjoy this type of game then you most likely will actually end up liking it. I do have to say that the writing isnt super good and that some things in the conversations arent the most logical at times, but for the vast majority of the game the writing is more than okay.What I do not like that much though is that at parts I found it a little hard to follow some of the dialogue, which resulted in me at the choices sometimes not knowing what the question the character asked me actually was. It would have been great if the question, at least if possible, was stated with the subtitles or in general in text so it is easier to pick the right choice. This also would help when you play through it multiple times. It might also not be a problem for most of you, as long as you always concentrate on what is being said, but as I played it together with a friend we sometimes had to randomly guess the answer as we just didnt know what to pick.A second thing that actually really bugged me is, that you can get to the third date, have all the stats perfect and you can still fail to get into the relationship. Why even have the stats with the percentages shown, if they arent the one thing, that decides if you are successful or not. I was really suprised when I failed the last date with Hazel even though I got along great with her.Overall though, it is a fun experience to go through and this one in comparison to Five Dates, offers more content and has a more polished feel to it. So in short, I recommend it if you liked the first game, or if the description sounds interesting to you.

_childDocuments_.review: An interactive film with a branching plot. No spoiler review.The girl called her friend on a speed date. What will come of it?The gameplay is a visual novel, designed in the form of a movie with dialogues and the possibility of choosing options in them.First, let's define the hero. You can play as Ryan or Misha. We create a fairly detailed profile with a photo and a choice of character interests.And then we go to explore the plot.The heroes get into some kind of cafe and start conversations with the opposite sex. In the future, if a relationship develops with someone, then they will develop over the course of three dates. What is very vital - you can cause dissatisfaction with the interlocutor at any stage. Literally one wrong phrase and the game (or storyline) is over.There are 12 characters in total, 6 boys and 6 girls, including the two main characters.It is possible to view the statistics and progress of relationships with a particular character by pressing the S button. Endings can be both successful and not so good.Consider the pros and cons of the game, sum up.+ Interesting and not so common approach to graphics. The graph is good.+ Excellent music and soundtrack.+ In the mood, but an interesting plot.+ There was a feeling that from the screenshots and dialogues of the characters you can make a bunch of memes (not strong in this area, so maybe I'm wrong).+ You can make choices in dialogue thoughtfully (with a pause) or spontaneously (normal mode).+ Story events are interspersed with stylish video inserts.± If you do not poke around in all the endings, give answers in the dialogues without bothering, then the game is completed in a little more than an hour or even faster.- It seemed that the characters somehow sometimes behaved too feignedly with each other. It's a pretty subjective, fleeting feeling that only surfaced in a couple of episodes.This is a well-made, unusual quest. I liked the presentation in the form of filming with live actors.

_childDocuments_.review: Modern media could take a lesson from this interactive gameThis game is one of the most real depictions of human interactions today that I wish all movies and TV shows would take a lesson from.  It covers modern, controversial topics by providing real human responses and not just spouting polarized talking points.  It has a variety of styles included, such as people with different backgrounds, personalities, and demographics and yet they NEVER call any of it out.  It just is, which is the way it should be.  Example: One of the dates for the female protagonist has a physical genetic difference, and I did the first two out of three dates without even noticing at all that it existed.  When I finally noticed, an overwhelming sense of relief and appreciation came over me that I could play a game and have these things exist without people's identities being conflated with their personalities (let's call this the "as a person with _____ trait...[insert perspective I must have as a result]." syndrome).  The makers of this game deserve a medal for that alone.The realism of the game is so well done.  For example, your background changes your first impressions with the dates and can even put you well behind the eight ball before it even starts.  I thought that was so true to life.  My favorite part is that there is an extreme activist date that you basically have to do everything exactly right or you cannot successfully complete the three dates--both true to life (those kinds of folks have a "purity test" of sorts and won't associate with anyone who's not exactly like them) and also kind of like playing a pixel-perfect platformer (fortunately, though, skill isn't required but rather just memorization).  I'm not 100% sure, but I believe that even the star sign you select affects whether she will want to continue dating you (it definitely affects the scenes you get and I lost when I thought I did everything right but had an incompatible star sign, but I can't be sure).The only thing that bugged me about the story was some of the character's comments, but that's exactly the right thing that's supposed to bother you because people really do say weird things sometimes or have opinions you won't like.  If only every movie or TV show was organic like this and not preachy, the modern media landscape would be so much better.From a game perspective, there are only a few nitpicks I can think of:-Some decision trees lead to weird or even no transitions to the next interaction.  For example, I kept getting awkward moments and yet the person had a high score of liking me and then the next moment it would be great again.  Sometimes, the transitions were right for the moment where the person did a "RIGHT!" or some other way to acknowledge and transition away from the awkwardness, but sometimes there was a weird moment and then it'd jump to the next scripted discussion as if the previous moment didn't happen.  It was only a couple of times where it seemed strange, though, which is amazing given the dozens of variations that they have programmed and, therefore, have to connect.-As with the other games of this type, they let you tab along but won't let you tab forward with a scene immediately after a new scene even if the subsequent scene is identical.  It is only surprising because sometimes you're watching the exact same scene but because you selected a different profession or star sign, you have to watch it.-I loved the nuanced takes your character makes instead of being a caricature, but sometimes the options you select lead to a weird response that I don't think matches what I expected to say.  It's very rare--and sometimes I believe it's meant as a pleasant surprise--but occasionally I thought I was saying the opposite of what was actually said with my selection.  Again, this actually is a strength in two scenarios where you can date a footballer who will love if you say things that would normally tank a date (i.e., teasing and sarcasm) or date a guy who says the craziest stuff (strangely, I survived the final date with him even though I had a near-0% maturity score somehow).-I loved the way that they allowed you to make choices associated with your sexuality and it was so real instead of an identity, but it did unintentionally take a Kinsey-esque position on sexuality, which is uncommon in reality.  I much prefer this to the in-your-face, throw-sexuality-in-everyone's-face approach that everyone else takes, but I wonder if it'd be possible to choose your preference in the app and have it trigger the options instead of it looking like the one same-sex option was "turning" you.  Though I'd rather have it as-is than the alternatives that would've made me roll my eyes.-I'm not a woman, so I don't know from experience, but all of the male dates seemed pretty tame.  From what I hear, I figured at least one man would be more forward/aggressive.  Ironically, I'm glad how it turned out--I actually liked all of the guys in their own way once I got to know them--but I figured there'd be an equivalent to the money-loving option from the female dates.-For the game's sake, they had the woman protagonist get the contact info to contact the male dates, which is the only part that was completely unrealistic (stats show that men make the move the overwhelming majority of the time).  But that was purely for the sake of game mechanics, so it gets a pass there.In summary, whoever wrote the script for this did a fantastic job.  And the acting of the various personalities was phenomenal.  They all felt like three-dimensional characters--even the ones that did embody a set of traits associated with that type of person (e.g., the bad boy, the nice guy, the goth girl).  My favorite was how insanely well they did the introverted-borderline-Asperger's tech nerd.  I mean between the scripting and actor's mannerisms, they crushed that.  Funnily enough, being that type, I basically got 4 100% ratings plus succeeded all three dates on the first run--showing how well they nailed it.  I loved that they had the dates like things complementary to them and not just the same as them.  Masterfully done.If you're looking for a fun interactive game/entertainment experience to look into real dating interactions, I'd really recommend this.  If you're sick of the modern mind virus of everyone having to have the same opinions and spout the exact same talking points, this is a breath of fresh air with real people and nuanced, varied takes.  It also gives you the opportunity to really feel like you get to say what you'd actually think through your character and engage realistically vs. with an exaggerated view.  It covers all sorts of personalities and romantic situations naturally, meaning everything feels real and nothing is heavy-handed.  I can only say that I wish we had more media like this.  Oh, and I wish that Ryan and Misha could've gotten together--that would've been a cool secret option in addition to or instead of the whimsical secret date in Misha's scenario (though I deeply respect keeping some opposite-sex relationships platonic and not "'shipping" everyone for fan service).  If you like the genre, play this game.  If you want to see modern dating done respectfully, play this game.  If you want to experience realistic interactions, play this game.  It's what modern media should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten Dates is a sequel to Five Dates, this time with two main characters (a boy and a girl) who each date five people. Instead of video calls, the conversations now take place in real life in pubs, clubs and restaurants.In between events, the main characters discuss what is happening with each other, in a slightly bantering tone, but they both come across as sympathetic characters. Whereas in the previous game all the partners were considered to be "good people", in the sequel the spectrum has, shall we say, broadened. Because of this, both protagonists are totally incompatible with a number of potential partners, which is especially prevalent with the girl, and it results in some massively cringe/awkward conversations if you want to end the date successfully.The mini-games are similar to the ones in the previous game, except for Brandy's card game, which is outstanding. This mini-game was included in the demo and I thought all mini-games would all be this exciting in the final game, but unfortunately this was not the case.Of course some things improved, the UI has been refined, the quality of the videos is much better, but the skipping of scenes still leaves something to be desired: sometimes it jumps to the very end of the date (failing it), many times you have to re-watch sub-segments, and after the skip the choices don't always tell you what the question was when there is only a Yes/No answer.If you're a strongly heterosexual male like me, I still recommend trying the girl's path, because she's cute as hell and at least you'll see how much men can suck at dating.Overall it's recommended if you liked Five Dates, but I can't decide if it's better than that or not.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love FMV, as well as games where choices matter, you can't go wrong with this. What really, REALLY sets it apart is the acting. I've rarely seen such top-notch performances from an FMV title: a dating FMV could have seemed so forced but all 12 actors are excellent at making it feel natural and ad-libbed. Special shout out to the actress playing Misha, and the guy playing Bash... incredible depth and range to their performances (Bash's third date was genuinely quite emotional).The dates themselves are short but not shallow: the characters are well rounded and, while they fit certain archetypes (brainy/brawny/bad etc), it means that your choices never seem arbitrary. This isn't a guessing game: for the most part, the choices you make will play out as you expect them to and it's possible to intuit what the best choice might be. That's not to say that you won't get some unexpected reactions to your choices... there are surprises, to be sure, which just adds to the "human"-ness of it all. People are unpredictable!In gameplay terms, it overcomes the biggest FMV hurdle: you CAN skip dialogue if you've heard it before. This, plus a relationship screen, makes it really easy to track your past choices and try different paths without replaying huge parts of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten DatesThe title of the game might already give it away but we're going on dates!In this FMV game you see Misha tricking her best friend Ryan into going speeddating with her.You play as either Misha or Ryan while they meet all very different people during the event. The choices you make changes the story and your chances on a second date and or third date!The game is so much fun playing and watching. The actors did an amazing job with bringing across the different personalities. Some you're gonna love, some you're gonna hate, some are gonna surprise you.Achievements:These are all super easy to get. Some require you to do several playthroughs. But honestly that's not a problem at all because this way you can get through all the different dialogues. In my opinion there is also the opportunity to add a few more achievements like getting all of the objectives per date. And unlocking all dialogs with each person.The only thing that I'd like to see different is that it would tell you which dialogue options you already picked so you don't end up picking the same options on accident.What also would be great is having the option to start at the second or third date. So that whenever you made a mistake you don't have to do everything all over again.Overall I give this game a 7/10 Purely because there are small things that could be better and the fact whenever I pick the lewd option they walk away. Damn prudes!

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome British FMV dating sim! (IMHO better guy routes than the girls). I love the mashup of FMV/dating sim, hope more games do this! Lots of different personalities to choose, love the inclusion of LGBT options and male or female MC. The acting is great, the transitions are smooth, the music is catchy, the London nightlife transitions really help set the mood! Having three dates is a somewhat short snapshot of their relationships, but it works. Misha has great chemistry with everyone (especially Ryan-where's my DLC? :P). I might be biased since I like playing as female MC with male options, but I didn't much like Ryan's options. Or maybe it's just the one option that really threw me off. Overall though, I had a great time playing this game as Misha! Would love more like this!

_childDocuments_.review: Or Ten Dates is the follow up to Five Dates a full motion video dating simulator.Your best friend, who happens to be of the opposite sex, signs you up for a speed dating event that they are attending. You start the game by selecting which character you are going to play as, Ryan (male) or Misha (female). You then pick your profile picture and the industry you work in. Next you pick your interests, you select three out of the available options. Finally, you select your star sign.I recommend turning on Streamer Mode in the options. This allows you to take your time and make your decision. While this does disrupt the flow of the game it gives you more time to reflect on your choices, because choices really matter.At the speed dating event you will have five, five minute dates, four opposite sex, one "surprise" same sex. After you go through all five dates you do a wrap up with your best friend. After the wrap up you select up to two people to go on a second date. Depending on how your speed dating went will affect the people that you can ask on a second date.After the second date you will be able to ask one of the people on a third date, provided the second date went okay. At the end of the third date you decide if you're going to be an item, provided of course it went well. There is a brief follow up to let you know how things went after the third date.Ten Dates is like a choose your own movie. The acting is very good and the B-Roll of London and the food and beverages is beautiful.Intel i7-8086K Coffee Lake 6-Core 4.00GHz CPUCrucial Ballistix Sport AT 2666 MHz DDR4 RAM (16GB x 2)ASUS GeForce RTX 2080 Overclocked 8G GDDR6Or

_childDocuments_.review: Sure I’ll give it a thumbs up, but I will say that there were parts of this game that became very repetitive and annoying. Even when skipping scenes you’ve already seen, to get all of the accomplishments you have to go through the characters over and over again. The acting is fantastic, the characters are fun, and it plays out more like a TV show then a game, giving you a 90% reality show with a 10% gameplay. I wish there was also an option for the two main characters to get together because they were cute as hell. All in all, if you’re looking for immersive gameplay, this won’t be your cup of tea. If you’re looking for some entertainment in the form of reality TV, then sit back, relax and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: While the concept itself is great and it's clear a lot of hard work went into the writing, recording and creation of the game itself I honestly can't recommend the final product.After 3 successful dates the game just kind of ends with a "And they lived happily ever after." I might be missing something honestly but I really don't understand the 10 dates title. I was expecting more from this game in terms of exploring relationships and the differences between two people in said relationships.Throughout the dates you will learn small tidbits about a character such as they have a tense relationship with their father which really gives the impression that this is something you're going to have to deal with as a couple and that's going to effect the ending but that thread is simply dropped once you 'succeed' in the final date.Maybe I'm missing something entirely or just not getting the core appeal of this game but the effort just didn't match the final product for me personally. Props to the devs for working so hard and I'm glad to see other people liked it but ultimately it felt a little misleading.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten Dates comes off as more of a rom-com with exaggerated stereotypes and two main characters who are clearly in love with each other; well, clear to me but not Misha and Ryan who seem determined to ignore their own chemistry and take a shot at the speed dating scene.   I barely remember when speed dating was a thing here in the States.  You never hear about it anymore, but this game takes place in London, so maybe it’s still happening across the pond.Something you have to realize fast is that this is a game with clearly outlined goals, and you need to expertly thread the conversation needle through a diverse tapestry of overt stereotypes.  My main issue going into the game was I immediately started roleplaying like I was on the date, and I didn’t find any of my options all that appealing, physically or otherwise.  The only girl I found truly attractive was Kathleen.  There was something oddly familiar about her, and then I realized that Meaghan Martin, the actress who played her, was also Jessica in Until Dawn, not to mention a couple dozen other voice acting gigs in various video games.Ten Dates has a lot of replay potential, not only in finding a match and going the distance to update your relationship status, but also in checking off a series of objectives specific to each character.  This means a lot of new games and choosing different conversation topics and responses, and thankfully you can easily skip those video clips that will obviously repeat on future playthroughs.  The one thing this game does effectively teach is not to judge a person on first impressions.   While nearly none of these characters were initially “attractive” during the slightly superficial speed dating, things really open up on the second and third dates where you get to learn more about these people, their lives, and any shared interests. Ten Dates is a lot of fun, especially if you are into social interactions and enjoy complex relationship flowcharts where a single wrong response can ruin your social life...at least until the next new game.Read the full review at More Steam reviews on our Curator page -

_childDocuments_.review: The acting in Ten Dates is a mixed bag. Some of the actors are quite good, while others are a bit wooden. The dialogue is also a bit hit or miss, with some lines that are genuinely funny and others that are just plain awkward.However, I do appreciate that there are so many options to pick from in Ten Dates. There are ten different dates to choose from, each with its own unique personality. This gives the game a lot of replay value, as you can try different combinations of dates to see what different outcomes you can get. It's impossible to see all of the different endings in a single playthrough. I will say I am disappointed in the lack of diversity with the matches. In both Five Dates and Ten Dates there are no black matches. Overall, I think Ten Dates is a decent game. It's not the best I've ever played, but it's certainly not the worst. If you like dating games and you're looking for something to play on a rainy day, then I'd say it's worth picking up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Great successor to Wales Interactive’s previous game, Five Dates, which I considered the pinnacle of their FMV titles at that point. I didn’t know Ten Dates was coming out, but I picked this up without hesitation when I saw it and blasted through a playthrough as both the male and female protagonists (Ryan and Misha) in two and a half hours and enjoyed both thoroughly.Best asset is definitely the greater range of choice compared to Five Dates. Getting to be either male or female, with different date options for both, gives a greater variety compared to Five Dates’ straight, male player character. As a gay male, I don’t have any issue playing a straight person, but I appreciated that both protagonists in Ten Dates had a same-sex option if you wanted it, and I wasn’t unhappy with the way those options were presented and developed. However, if you’re someone looking for something with a greater LGBT+ emphasis then there’re several excellent visual novels elsewhere on Steam that deliver that better. Outside of that, the cast stories touch on a good number of topics in terms of the difficulties the people have been through, but the developer clearly dropped the ball on racial diversity as there's almost none.As protagonists, I found Ryan a little easier to get on with. Something I liked about the Five dates protagonist was that the player character didn’t present too much background so that you could overlay your own interests and preferences if you wanted without it feeling like you were fighting the character the developer created. Ryan similarly feels a little personality-less, in a good way, so you can play him however you fancy and he’ll roll with it. Misha comes off as more feisty and sassy with a dry sense of humour, which made her funnier to watch but harder to put myself in her shoes. I couldn’t decide if this was a good or bad thing, so take that how you will.  The “game” elements (the dates and choices) have seen the least change from Five Dates. Essentially, you dance through a series of questions where the NPCs attempt to pose questions that you can’t necessarily guess the outcome they’re looking for, which leads to natural-feeling outcomes where you maybe hit it off or not. The biggest change from Five Dates was that I felt there was a greater level of input from the dates. Five Dates felt like you had the reins a lot and the conversations focused more on what the NPC had to say, but I got the sense in Ten Dates that the NPC’s put me on the spot more. I don’t have a huge amount of playtime in Five Dates so maybe I'm misremembering, but I enjoyed the feeling in Ten Dates that the NPCs were as curious about me as I was of them. Overall, the gameplay pans out pretty similarly to Five Dates, but it’s no less satisfying, and I liked the mini goals each NPC had as an incentive to replay and pick them all up.Biggest gripe is definitely the lack of a skip function if you want to replay and try another path. There were some smaller gripes as well, firstly that I hit one instance of audio desync, which was resolved a few lines later (though it was very distracting while it was happening). More glaringly, there were  moments where the subtitles were either misspelled, didn’t match what was being said, and there was even one instance where it displayed the text for the alternative dialogue option instead of what it should’ve been showing. It’s a shame that this kind of stuff wasn’t caught, but it doesn’t really ruin the gameplay.All in all, very much enjoyable much like its predecessor, I found myself smiling and laughing along as I played, which is always a good sign. Neither game is a complex or challenging experience, but they’re both something a little different in the gaming market, and I think it’s an interesting romp if you fancy a change of pace. Wales Interactive’s offerings have been a bit hit-and-miss for me historically, but I love that there’re still studios dabbling in the FMV genre, and I’m more than happy to support that.

_childDocuments_.review: While I think games like these fill a really important role (especially in these days), a lot of the UI, ESPECIALLY in the UX department needs work.And most of those are actually related to replayability.A great example is when you are playing cards. And if you want to skip ahead to that section, it skips to a sequence where you don't get to hear what the previous card was. The game effectively asks you to memorize it since last time you played if you want to skip the sequence. It's also not very clear when a sequence can be skipped and not. Some very subtle icon or feedback would really help with that.On a personal note, I would have liked if the roster of a character was not revealed until you met the character.Or even have it revealed after you finish one playthrough. The moment I realized there were checks and stats, it went from feeling like intuitive flirting to a systems game.There's definitely a balance there.I still recommend the game on the basis of it being cheap, enjoyable and well acted! I'm surprised at how well some of the actors performed, when the script sometimes took them in weird directions. Which is fine! Some players are going to lack *game* so to speak.
