_childDocuments_.review: Lots of design choices that are at odds with each other. Like there are plot decisions you make by choosing which direction to walk in and it's not always obvious when you're making these decisions. That would be fine, except there are collectibles, which motivate trying to explore the entire level rather than being deliberate about the direction in which you are heading. You can't reload old saves, so you can't undo decisions made by accident.The thing that finally made me rage-quit was the transition from the Layers of Fear 1 stuff to the DLC/Layers of Fear 2 stuff. When you click on the books that represent the DLC bits, it warns you that you won't be able to back out into the meta story until the DLC is finished. It does not give you a similar warning when entering the Layers of Fear 2 bit. I accidentally entered the Layers of Fear 2 part, skipping the DLC, and there was no way to back out. Sure, you can do the DLC bits after the Layers of Fear 2 part, but then it's out of order. I can understand making accidental decisions permanent as a matter of realism or whatever, but in this case the in-game decision is whether to read a book or write a story. In real life you can switch between these activities at will. They should have at least had a similar warning popup for entering the Layers of Fear 2 part as they had for the DLC parts. Anyway, that was one frustration too far for me and I quit.The game is pretty though, and emotionally intense.

_childDocuments_.review: I am utterly torn on the final product. The graphical improvements add a lot of detail to the environment and give a little more of an added touch to environments, for example in Chapter 1, more paintings are "coming to life" and in the chapter about the daughter, the massive amount of toys lying about help add to the overall scene. It does feel like they tried to bring more scenes to life with the upgrades, even if it doesn't all come together perfectly.The lighthouse is a...well interesting take on tying things together but the Writer's story is so weirdly implemented throughout the game, it feels like you're being ripped out of individual stories to experience a small segment of the Writer's story who's supposed to tie it all together and it all just feels like it was wrapped together with a really weak link. The lighthouse itself sets up a very interesting environment for the likes of a psychological thriller, no better setting can define isolation and deterioration of the mind.The Painter's story is the highlight here, I LOVED the first game to death because it just nailed the aspect of an ambient horror experience. Like others have said, the lighting changes have had a mixed result. Sure, it's better looking but there's less creative contrast of light and dark which affects the overall ambience. There's just an overall lack of stylistic ambience that was achieved with the first game. The writing on the walls don't feel near as oppressive as the original and some original scares feel gutted, my favorites being the mimicked rooms with crayon lines, the "don't look back" painting, the basement piano scene, the doll running into a wall, some of these were just so iconic and now they're either gone entirely or severely weak compared to the original. The chase scenes felt so bad for this game, just like in the second title, they feel wholly out of place. I wasn't the hugest fan of the Actor's story or Layers of Fear 2, about all I can say is sure, the environments look even better than before but still, it didn't compare to the first game. It's relatively the same.Bug wise, it's mostly been fine outside of broken audio for scares like the piano scare in the house when picking up the music sheet or other scares not making noise so you're initially unaware of what occurred. Overall, I like the game, it's the definitive package, even if it's a weakened version. I got a loyalty discount so this game was cheaper for me and I think it was worth the money. My overall feeling is that while the attempt of the game is admirable, it just falls flat in some areas and totally alien as to what made the first game so great.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting a re-skin of the original with a little added, as most remakes are. This is a whole new game, especially for the first game. The painter's story becomes more cohesive, and more is added to make the experience less of a spooky walking simulator and more of a survival horror game. While I really enjoyed the original, this version was much more interesting and immersive. There is more added to all of the games to make the stories more cohesive. You get to play as two new characters: The Writer, who pulls the stories together, and The Musician, where you get a glimpse into the Wife's point of view. Overall this game is fantastic, beautiful, entertaining, and scarier than ever!Very few of the negative reviews have spent enough time in this game to have an accurate assessment of the game. Most of them have barely spent an hour, which isn't even enough time to get anywhere in the first game. I'd recommend playing this for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW IN FULLLayers of Fear 2023 is not a game, it is an experience that grabs you from the very depths of your soul and takes hold never letting go. It is still heavy on the themes and overall messages as well as symbolism and metaphors that make you feel cold by the time you finish it.But in a way, it has an uplifting sense of how you want these characters stories to end.So the best way to review these is to go one at a time on what each tale gives and offers you as a player.The Writer (Wrap Around Story Arc):Entirely new to this instalment, the Writer portions offer the player a succinct, harrowing and often times creepy as hell tale of love, loss, despair, hopelessness and longing. Having the story explained and at times explaining the narrative of the other tales as well, it fits and ties in perfectly for both new comers and old players of the series and offers many answers that were not given in the past. Discovering these twists are the backbone of this arc.You feel for the characters involved, the loss they have witnessed, the horrors they live through and to some the ending may seem to leave it open for another...but the more you think the more you know the story will never end.The best part by far having a sort of break in between both The Painters and The Artists stories that continues on, gives you hints and developments that you discover more as the Writer progresses.It's short adding up to about 30 mins to an hour of full experience, but honestly has to be the best part of the game!9/10The Painter (Layers of Fear 1):The entire first game that started it all, is the darkest part of Layers of Fear 2023You feel sick, you feel sad, you feel angry, you feel all these emotions as the story unfolds and ultimately is what pushes you to find out what will come of it all in the end.There are powerful metaphors and symbolism that are not fully explained and leave you the player to put the pieces together yourself. But be warned, the answers you seek are not necessarily ones you want to find out.The sad thing is with how emotionally charged this tale is, it is honestly one of the weakest entries that can be summed up in under 30 minsClocking in at around 5 hours or so the majority of this is well cheap jump scares....and I do mean cheap. Some hit you very well but ultimately it turns into a fun house where you just want something, anything to happen that isn't gonna smack you in the face with a loud startling noise. Everything and I do mean everything has a jump scare, from door openings, to windows closing, to the very steps you take and doesn't add anything to the plot, but instead takes away.The only good part is the writing, the voice acting and the twists of what really happened. But you just feel emotionally and psychically drained by the time this arc is over and not in a good way6/10The Daughter & The Musician (DLC Inheritance and NEW Final Note):Lumping these two together are essentially the final pieces of the puzzle to wrap up The Painters entire arc, answering questions thought lost by the end as well as new moments we had never seen before. The work better, feel better and play better than the Painter due to there creativity, care and full explanation and I honestly felt more for these two 1 hour or so DLC's more than anything happening in Layers of Fear 1 (The Painter)Bloober acknowledged this and gave a perfect way to wrap up the family of horrors. Seriously Final Note is emotionally charged, I would pay full price for that story. The daughters while quick feels like a sluggish add on that gave us new mechanics, but ended just as quickly without the full emotional depth you would expect. Still the way these two carry  themselves is impressive for short addons to an already full game.7/10The Artist (Layers of Fear 2):In my opinion a near perfect experience. Less jumps, less same same corridors, larger motives, bigger stakes, a more engaging story and overall the most emotion and feel for characters than I have ever felt. Every single step I wanted to know more, I wanted to uncover what happened, I wanted to see an ending worthy of this of sequel. While it does have a few slow moments and some very drawn out areas, this can be excused with that feeling of dread you face that is constantly hunting you. Each level you go down, feels like you are travelling deeper and deeper into the depths of hell and the only way out is to keep going.The puzzles make you think, the doors have reason for being there and you cant help but feel that claustrophobia closing in around every corner. The atmosphere is what drives this narrative. It grabs your attention and answers everything you need and even some special moments that expand it out if you are willing to search for them.It was probably the most fun walking horror simulator I have done in recent memory and has many special shout outs for those who love film and remember classic moments from years and years of Cinema. Hell, having that special booming, commanding voice in your ear, forces you to push on and never give up until the final curtain call.9/10Overall I enjoyed this horrific little romp through the mind of broken and desperate characters.There is a lot to find for collectable huntersMultiple paths that lead to different and in some cases true endings that can completely change your play styleThe graphics are gorgeous being an UNREAL ENGINE 5 game, it is hauntingly beautiful to walk through.The sound design is near perfect, with moments of dread, sombreness, panic, and emotional depth.You can tell that each voice actor did there very best to deliver a believable state of mindAtmosphere that grips you in a shaken state but you forces you to push onAnd a full story that feels worthy of its price and will keep people coming back for moreThere are some negatives to this though, both on a technical and mechanic frontDoors that seem to jam open or push you through unexpectedly Sounds that seem out of place or appear missing entirelyVoice actors lines (LAYERS OF FEAR 1 + DLC) that overlap and don't match with the subtitlesSubtitles that are missing entirelyWritten words that are not read out, and yet other paragraphs are in fullA really weird duplication bug that ruined the atmosphere fully, picking up an important object in both game and cut-scenes that just stay there, even though the character is holding it in there hand making you miss important moments because the chest you just opened contained another chest when the character is crying over whats in that chest and all you see is another chest is both hilarious and very disappointing given the majesty of this project.Some endings if not most don't fully give you a proper conclusion or way of summing upand strange frozen or buggy areas that are non responsive entirelyMost of these issues are all in the first half which kills the pacing and the enjoyment factor that can easily be fixed but felt like they cut corners, not sure if the same was done in Layers 1While the game is hauntingly beautiful, breathtaking, terrifying and shocking all rolled into oneThis is hard to recommend...You lose yourself in the scares and the jumps, but when you see the ending of only the first story...oooooof is it hard to swallow. Left me more depressed than anythingThe DLC's fixed that and felt a lot happier, and the sequel arc was justified.This is not for the faint of heart, I let it get to meI think from someone in the arts field it was a lot more painful to see, not to mention the themes contained within which are way to real in this world.This is a recommendation for those who can stomach the themes and look past the horrors within. While it isn't a game for everyone and should be handled as an experience more so, looking past its problems you will be glad you played it.But it is not for everyone8/10WATCH IT HERE: Decide for yourself

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game at a discount last year when it came out.  Having 100%'d the first 2 games, I figured that I was getting a remake of the first 2 games with a third "DLC" chapter thrown in.  After finally getting around to playing it this year for the spooky season, I was pleasantly surprised just how much content this game gives you.  The first game is completely redone.  Not only does it look a lot better, but it also adds a good amount of brand new areas to go through that weren't in the first game, which is a nice touch.  The second game feels more similar to it's original predecessor, but is still great.  The new writer story is good, albeit short.  There's also the original Inheritance DLC as well as 2 new DLC length stories to play through.  Between all of the new content, you're definitely getting enough new stuff for it to make up an entire third game.  If you liked either of the first 2 games, definitely pick up this one (especially if you can get it on sale!).  If you've never played the original games, I also recommend this, just don't be discouraged if it starts feeling long, as it's literally 3 games worth of content thrown into one.

_childDocuments_.review: The original "Layers of Fear" were not bad, but not great. The remake - or re-release, or whatever you want to call it - is also not great, and nearly crossing the line into "awful" territory. One of the advantages of the first game was its brisk pacing. It was over in 3-4 hours, just about when it was getting boring. This time it's lumped together with "Layers of Fear 2", 2 pieces of DLC, and a new overarching story, and it drags on for about 12 hours. None of the games gel together that well, the transitions between the stories feel jarring, and the new content seems like a bunch of scotch tape applied to stitch it all together. Some of the additions are kind of OK, for example, there's a very basic 'combat' mechanic that feels right at home here and makes the game more varied. Unfortunately, there are also unwanted additions - namely, glitches and bugs. I've experienced quite a few, and let me tell you, there's nothing like falling off the edge of the game world thinking that this might actually be a scripted scare. Overall, I think this package needed more time in the oven, and it almost makes me want to recommend "Layers of Fear" just because it was so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Just jumping in and graphics are fluid, sound design is beautiful (opening sequence from the original was always a favorite tune) and the creepy atmosphere is what I expect from this team. It is confusing, to say the least, that your eyes are telling you the top says one thing and someone in your ear is reading something else.  I am thrilled to see you can turn off voice overs, but just something I hope can be fixed in future updates, or explained why this happens.More to come...but so far I am definitely enjoying the overall experience.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of first-person psychological horror games and you’ve never heard about the original Layers of Fear, then this might be the best time to try this series in a brand new revamped version. This is not simply a remake, it’s a definitive collection that includes the first and the second games, the “Inheritance” DLC, but also completely new chapters such as “The Lighthouse” and “The Final Note” that further expand the story. In the first game you play as a Painter in the middle of an existential crisis. You will be exploring a Victorian mansion, trying to put the pieces together and learn more about his insanity. The DLC “Inheritance” is also included and allows you to play as the Painter’s daughter, learning all the secrets about her family. The remake also adds a new DLC called “The Final Note”, in which you take control of the Painter’s wife, a musician, giving a totally new perspective to the events. Then you have the second game, which is not a direct continuation of the same story. Here you play as an Actor who find himself trapped on an ocean liner, exploring the ship and discovering why he was chosen by the director himself to play the role. And finally, you will experience “The Lighthouse”, a brand new chapter in which you play as a secluded Writer who is trying to complete a book and connect all the stories together. You will play parts of this new chapter in-between the other games, unifying all the different storylines in one interesting plot with a common theme. Similarly to  and other horror games that play with your head, you will explore creepy environments and solve puzzles to overcome the obstacles that block your way. Most of the time, this will simply require finding hidden keys or codes to unlock doors or find story-related items. The whole experience is mostly linear, with few branches that effectively give the illusion of choice but bring you on the same path. To be honest, I played the original Layers of Fear back in 2016 and there were a few parts that I didn’t remember, so there are certainly things that have been changed or added in the remake, such as new sections, items and room layouts. One thing is sure, the puzzles are extremely guided and don’t require much thinking, which is a pity considering the variety of environments.There is also another problem, which understandably can be subjective, but for me it’s been very annoying: the game is not scary. It can be during the first two hours, when you can feel the tension of being inside a dark lighthouse or a creepy mansion, and then you get the first few frightening jumpscares that work pretty well, but then every room you enter starts to include one or more jumpscares and they become repetitive and predictable to the point that I got bored of seeing stuff suddenly flying, moving dolls, ghosts’ appearances or lamps that break. The game constantly uses the same method to frighten you: when you are facing a door or a wall, you can feel that something has changed in the environment behind you (there is like a visual glitch for one second) and when you turn around you simply get a jumpscare. Again, it’s fun and interesting for the first few hours when you don’t know what to expect but then it wears off really quickly. Fortunately, the team has introduced a new mechanic taken straight from : The Lantern. You can use it not only to illuminate dark areas, but also to destroy corrupted items and as a weapon against ghosts. Yes, there will be some sections in which you will run for your life while being chased by ghosts, adding a bit of dynamism to the gameplay. That said, Layers of Fear works more like a showcase of surreal things happening. Once you accept the absurd repetitiveness of the jumpscares you won’t feel any real tension or sense of danger. It becomes more like a story-driven and visually splendid walking sim with easy puzzle solving. I love that depending on the actions you make, such as closing and opening the same door again or watching a painting several times, you can trigger new jumpscares but again, it’s all pretty redundant.Speaking of actions, all the chapters feature multiple endings. The requirements for unlocking these are unknown to me, but I imagine they are somehow linked to the amount of “collectibles” you have found (there are quite a lot) and how you deal with the ghosts’ appearances. The game includes a chapter selection, so it should be easy to replay single parts and try to achieve the other endings. One thing that I should mention though is that despite finishing the Inheritance DLC with one of the endings, it didn’t get unlocked in the chapter menu (probably a bug).Since this collection is also a complete remake, the main differences you will find are in the graphics. The game is built on Unreal Engine 5 and utilizes the Lumen global illumination system. I went back to watch some videos of the original games to really understand the difference and it’s really huge. The environments are fantastic, very photorealistic and super detailed. Despite all the cheap jumpscares, I really enjoyed my time exploring these gorgeous, but unsettling, locations. The game is also decently optimized and features a good number of graphical settings, including raytracing, DLSS, XeSS (Intel Super Sampling) and TSR (Temporal Super Resolution), which work pretty well on Quality Mode with almost imperceptible quality loss but better performance overall. The game also uses binaural audio, which simulates a 3D effect and sounds much better on headphones. The only “bug” I found is the sound of rain that can be heard from inside the mansion, in the first game. It’s difficult to describe this issue, but sometimes the rain sounds weird, not realistic but more like a poor 3D effect.Layers of Fear strives to be frightening, but it actually ends up being a relaxing walk in the park, assuming you have enough experience with this kind of horror game, love art and surrealism. It’s not a bad game by any means; it’s a pleasant story-driven journey through the mind of twisted people consumed by their obsession for art, but I wish they could have avoided all those repetitive and ineffective jumpscares to focus on a more intimate and unsettling story. Anyway, this is the best package you can currently get for the series, with lots of content between the two games, DLCs and an entirely new chapter. Probably worth a try if you love being scared by a train of jumpscares or like me you simply enjoy exploring these atmospheric environments and dive into the twisted minds of the protagonists without fear.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial review was quite a negative one, however a few post-release patches added many changes and optional features that allow players to tailor the game to their own preferences. These include: - Option to disable voice-overs on notes - Option to disable text transcription by default (can be found at the bottom of accessibility)- Gamma / brightness adjustment slidersThese features really aid immersion and helps make the remake feel much closer to how the original games did. The game now also contains native ultrawide support, which can lead to some visual bugs due to how important perspective is in this game but it is entirely optional. Most major complaints I had initially have been addressed and the team deserves all the credit for taking community feedback so seriously and supporting the game post-release.There are still a few bugs and issues that I came across but they are somewhat minor:- As user 'Rostburken' in the comments of this review mentioned, some dialogue appears to start immediately one after the other, basically cutting the previous line early- Some pop-in issues and rooms not rendering until the player gets closer to it- Certain events appear to trigger early / at wrong times compared to the original game

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going give this a recommend, on the basis of, if you liked the originals or enjoy the genre, it's a good game. But it comes with a BIG caveat - I cannot recommend it for people like me, for health reasons.Opening this up with the fact that I deal with simulation sickness - some titles cause it worse than others. In spite of this, I was able to complete the original 2016 release (mild nausea, but nothing I couldn't pace out over time), so I figured, sure - I'll take a stab at the remaster, especially when they include accessibility options like we see here (head bob toggle, motion blur toggle, etc.) As far as games in that genre go, the original was fine, enjoyable even with some of the storytelling, even if it did end up feeling a bit more 'walking simulator with mild puzzles' rather than horror game to me. It was still interesting and enjoyable enough to justify the time and inconvenience - and if I could get through this remaster, I wager my view would be fairly similar.The problem is, I cannot get through the remaster - I disabled head bobbing, disabled motion blur, even disabled FSR (AMD card) - pretty much used all of the settings I could to minimize the sickness - but for some reason this version of the title has me almost wretching even after just the first 10-15 minutes. It's a mix of field of view, which is bad in both the original and this one, but feels worse here (even though the original had other motion sickness issues) - combined with a strange ghosting effect that was NOT present in the original - it's especially noticeable when looking at printed letters, if you rotate the object they will focus/defocus, and even the paper will leave a bit of a visual echo as it moves. This actually is happening with EVERYTHING in the game, it's just harder to consciously notice (but subconsciously, my body is noticing it, and that's what's causing the urge to vomit)This is also amplified in the "cutscene" sections when the game takes control of the camera - since people in this world can't keep  their head still - so all but a few in the bit I was able to get through for b-reel, resulted in me having to look away from the monitor.This game is good, but if you deal with simulation sickness, DO NOT BUY IT (the original will hit your simulation sickness too, but it was nowhere near as rough as the remaster). It is easily in my top 10 worst reactions to a game from this, in recent memory (including VR titles) - and this is from someone who makes part of their living reviewing a variety of titles, so I've come across some doozies, but can usually power through... this one, I cannot.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of horror games, but someone who did not play the original version of this, take my review for what it is.I definitely agree with others that this game was a walking sim, but that doesn't make a game inherently "bad". Although I was initially a bit on edge, perhaps from my history of playing horror games and not knowing what to expect from this one, that feeling of high alertness and caution eventually melted away to boredom and I just wanted the game to be over. The stories weren't very well laid out to offset the fact that basically the only mechanic in the game is opening doors and using a flashlight. There is definitely a Silent Hill inspiration to some aspects of the game, but overall it just felt like it tried too hard to be cryptic and got lost in translation, as it were. There was no twist or grand epiphany to the story that made it special or thought provoking.I would say buy this one on sale if you are out of other games to play.Also it seems like a lot of the positive reviews on this game are from people who only played the game for less then an hour total and/or received the game for free, so I have to question if the company solicited people to post dishonest reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review (I think).Okay so to be honest I was not able to finish this game by playing just this game. But in this case, maybe due to the game's nature (horror/spooky) I played other games too and then slowly came back to it. I do believe horror is tough to do anywhere, and this a good attempt.

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion of the game "Layer of Fear" (2023) is that it is incredibly stunning and immersive. Bloober Team has managed to create an atmosphere of horror and madness that keeps you on edge throughout.One of the strongest aspects of the game is its visual design. The graphics are impressive, with the use of dark and eerie tones blending with breathtaking visual effects. The environment around you changes and distorts, creating a sculpted and terrifying atmosphere. Every detail is well-crafted, adding to the realism and the sense of engulfing horror.The game design of "Layer of Fear" is also excellent. The decision to unfold the story in the isolated residence of the main character is very effective, creating a sense of confinement and isolation. You navigate through various rooms and corridors that shift and transform, while telling the dark story of the protagonist.The game's plot is mysterious and captivating. You discover letters, diaries, and objects that help you understand the deep psychology of the main character and the reasons behind his insane destructive mania. The intrigue unfolds gradually, compelling you to delve further into the dark world of the game.While the game primarily focuses on psychological horror, there are also some puzzles and gameplay mechanics that provide variety and interactivity. They are well-integrated into the story and do not disrupt the pace or atmosphere of the game.There are some moments where the path forward may be unclear, requiring you to search for a solution, but overall, the game provides enough guidance and hints to help you progress.The game is a fantastic choice for fans of psychological horror games. It immerses you in a dark and consuming world, offering visually stunning and emotionally engaging experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Layers of Fear

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing horror games with awesome stories that kept me immersed the whole way through. Graphics were some of the best I've ever seen and the gameplay, while slow, is still an improvement from the original games, with more interactive chases and scares. However, there were some moments where the gameplay did feel somewhat clunky (especially when opening doors in  more intense chase scenes) and the story was occasionally quite unclear and hard to follow (the second game is the best example of this). Overall, this is a 10/10 remaster and an 8/10 game, Very good!

_childDocuments_.review: "It's done!, I finished!", One more time I ended the game, the experience of playing Layers of Fear with all features of Unreal Engine 5 is awesome, this game was the first that I played in UE5. The light, shadows and environments is absolutely amazing, I'm really excited with all other games we will see using this engine.Talking about the remaster, I love the Layer of Fear 1 and your DLCs, all aspects of the story of the game is very interesting to me, some scenes was different from the original game and I liked all of them, this really add more depth for this masterpiece gameThe second one I unfortunely don't like, the story is some tedious, the environment don't give curiosity and seems really repetitive.I liked how the writter's story connect the first and second game, this is new and we never see before.Althrough the Bloober Team can't fix the second game even with the remaster, I loved this DEFINITIVE EDITION of Layers of Fear with all stories and a lot of content, this was made with love.Congrats Bloober Team and Anshar Studios for the work, you guys is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hot damn this is good! If this is the last Layers of Fear & the last psychological horror game from Bloober Team then it's good bang to go out on.Still only in the early hours of the stories of this review & played the first two games, but I like what I've seen so far.It's clear that the original content has been compressed yet it feels like nothing was removed, so alot of the fluff the first game had is gone now & it's more to the point. We have some new mechanics in the form of basic combat taken from Alan Wake thrown in to the first game. This goes alongside a pursuer taken from the second game, but the combat doesn't take it out, all you can do is temporarily stun her. Which is more enjoyable than just closing doors behind you.Story has lost some subtlety as the cost for getting a better idea of how the Rat Queen influenced everyone, but it doesn't takeaway from the psychological aspects or diminish them.The new Writer story had me worried that the events of the prior games were just going to retconed as the Writer wrote them as fiction. Thankfully this is not the case!Won't lie it's not that scary, the atmosphere didn't envelope me like Silent Hill 2, the Dead Space & Resident Evil 4 remakes, or Tormented Souls did. But the jump scares & the pursuer managed to get me a few times & the Rat Queen is creepy. It's still a walking simulator at the core but mighty good one.7/10 It's fans of the previous games that are going to get the most out of this, but there is still plenty to enjoy for everyone else if you don't mind a slow pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever Bloober and Anshar Studios get together,magic happens. This is another example - besides Observer Redux. The game is way scarier than it already was - and the visuals! Oh my God the visuals. Anshar and Bloober really know how to play with light, colour and sound. Some moments in the Actor Chapter were truly, truly, mesmerizing slash terrifying. This stuff takes my breath away. On the other hand, some of this scenes/characters have already been done in more aggressive and mind-blowing ways (Visage,Amnesia Rebirth, Outlast or Madison come to mind) and while I admire Bloober for what they have accomplished here, I don't think they are bringing anything really new to the scene. The new "layers" the title mentions are about visuals and some new dynamics and not much more. "In sound mind", an indie game that also deals with loss and despair and mental issues,was far more adventurous, scary and playable. A part of me considers this a missed opportunity for creating a real masterpiece. For instance, the decrease in quality and subtetlty in both The Musician and The Writer's Chapters are abysmal. I understand that you feel trapped because there's millions of chains everywhere. Do you need to repeat it every time, in every letter? They need better writers next time. All in all, as it stands, it is a more than welcome return from one of my favourite developers. I want more Anshar and more Bloober and I want it NOW.

_childDocuments_.review: Let us get this out of the way, I LOVED the original Layers of Fear (LoF) and did not like any of the add on's or LoF 2.  I was hoping the fresh coat of paint would make me really want to play the expansions again and the second installment, but I didn't.First, I did not encounter (very short play time) the new "Monster Chase" in the original game, but read that they added this new Mechanic where at times, something was chasing you in the original game.  I personally just don't like the chasing mechanic.  For me, its more frustrating and is not scary at all, its just annoying and forces me to rush sections instead of take in the ambiance or move my focus from something creepy to something...chasing me.Now, did the fresh coat of paint make me want to play anyways?  Well, not really.  It does look pretty, and its the first game that didn't bottom out my frame rate when I turned RTX on, however I really actually didn't notice any difference with it on or off.  But I can say, it looks more detailed and prettier.  So what gives, why don't I like it?For one, the voice overs sound bad.  Most of them sounded like they didn't care at all, just reading lines on a piece of paper.  Sections of the voice overs were just flat out missing too, like the entire first paragraph of a letter just skipped.I hated the new "Looking" mechanic.  In the original game when you picked something up, the background blurred and it was the only thing on screen and you can look at it from all angles.  Now, its animated in your hands and when you "rotate" your character just kind of flips it a little.  Mouse sensitivity also went very low when looking at something, I had to move my mouse 5 times as far as I should have to just move an object around.  The original viewing mechanic of having only that item on screen and blurring the background would have worked just fine.Looking in general also felt terrible.  Something is up with the camera, almost like there is a slight fish eye effect.  I didn't see anything in settings for it (and no idea why anyone would want to play like this) and if you look left or right, the camera would have a dome effect and your view would almost feel like it was going down a little.  If you look strait down it was like you would move your head 4 inches forward so you can never look strait down, like you are looking over a ledge.  This lead to having to backup all the time to try and open draws and look inside them.Opening draws was also touchy (this I might have been able to adjust to).  When I would click and hold and pull back I had to let go immediately or the game thought I was closing the draw and it would just slowly close on its own.  This might have something to do with the camera lurching forward when looking down, but it was annoying to have to constantly backup a bit if I was too close to something.If you never played the original and like the hide and go seek mechanics, this might actually be OK.  Some of the above I am sure you can adjust to and play this game fine.  But as a fan of the original and nothing after it, I would pass on this and just play the original if I feel the need.PS: I also didn't like 2, or the add on's for the original because they leaned WAY too heavy on "creepy" things like mannequins, dolls or rats (which I actually don't really find rats creepy).  But it was just "OH MY!  A room FULL of Mannequins, are you scared?"  "OH, did that scare you that when you looked back the mannequins are now looking at you?"  This has been done before, and was 100% predictable.  The original Escher like "impossible space" was captivating for me as it was, but that is just me.  If you loved 1, just play that because the graphics update is not really worth it.  If you liked 2 and the add on's more, you might actually like this one for the new mechanic.And yes, there was a new lighthouse Story, which I was actually looking forward to how they tied it all in, but I can just watch a lets play or something, I don't want to trudge through with mechanics I find frustrating to get the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Layers of Fear

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Layers Of Fear since the first iteration in 2016, I think this was a nice way to round the franchise of. Although the story is quite hard to follow and I can't say I fully understand it even after watching a youtube explanation of the story, you can still roughly work out what's going on at a basic understanding. The graphics are outstanding, the horror is 10/10 in my opinion as it is more than your average jumpscare fest. The game does an amazing job at taking a new perspective for horror games by inducing anxiety, disorientation and genuine discomfort. Surroundings change making you question whether something has been there the entire time. Even the slightest changes in a room make you question your own sanity. It's quite a disturbing game about sanity. Other than the difficult to follow story I would give it a 10/10 for horror for anyone looking for a genuinely disturbing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, I think the games are better appreciated in their original separate versions than compiled in this way.Although I really enjoyed Layers of Fear in its day, this remake proves that it hasn't aged very well, despite some interesting graphical improvements. The game isn't as scary and inventive as it was when it was first released, and the new features introduced by this remake range from average (the new scenario) to VERY bad (the new voiceovers, which are SO BAD they're funny, especially for the original story).But what's most annoying is that, now transformed into a "reworked compilation" (2 games + DLC linked by another, even different game that serves as a "central hub"), Layers of Fear has become even more repetitive than it was originally, with a story made totally confusing by a disparate accumulation of points of view. If you haven't played the original games (already not always very clear), the plot just becomes incomprehensible, with character changes for no reason at all, unclear switches from one game to another, and a huge (HUGE!) abuse of deliberately opaque written diaries. I encountered a small amount of game breaking bugs as well, most of them being tied to the LoF 1 DLC which likes to send me below the map.And again, I can't emphasize enough how lame the new voiceovers are. You just can't take seriously a story when it's told by such bad actors. :(

I enjoyed the  section though.Edit: Having now finished the main game, I find myself not caring much about the characters and the convoluted story. The Actor section was a major chore. _childDocuments_.review: How I rate/review and other info is  .  STEAM Game Normal, lazy✅	Artistic side is beautiful – art/graphic quality & style, atmosphere, music, ambiance✅	Main storytelling, daughter and mother side stories remain superb✅	Multiple endings depending on choices (event changes & triggering) for each story (Main story and “DLC extra stories”)✅	Plenty of collectibles and lore collectibles so exploration is rewarding✅	Walking sim part of the game remains exquisite (how it plays, feels and how camera tricks change your surroundings, how you find stuff/secrets, doorways etc…)✅	Life is made easier for completionists to see all endings/get all collectibles after finishing game once. (CHAPTERS SELECTION)✅	Some fun and unique puzzles & most are extremely easy❌	“creature banishing system” - The added “gameplay” elements felt unnecessary and removed the joy and awe I had from original game (will explain more in comments) (1)❌	Horror element weaker later on, extra stories ain’t much of horror and more of artist mental dilemmas❌	Exploration for collectibles is dice roll, as you don’t know whenever next spot locks you out due to progression or allows you to go back to previous room❌	Some game section with “kill chases” after you respawn after death end with spawnkilling if you don’t either instantly move or stay in place.(1) Let me get my main gripe out of the way first. The 2016 game what I loved about them was the amazing feeling, immersion and artsy walking sim it was. It was creepy, unique, sad, artistic but was so superb to walk around, see everything, move your camera around see stuff happen, change and so on. But with this remake what pissed me off so much and mainly ruined my fun a lot. Is the the actual F they decided to add “amnesia/outlast esque elements” … the whole gimmick of having light source with where I can focus light to “banish” monsters was more of an annoyance than tense, spooky or scary. In games where its main feature, it works, it creates tension while you deal with puzzles and progression. In this game it was just absolutely unnecessarily tedious and took the charm away the game used to have. New progression & collectibles with light focus I didn’t mind and liked actually.On the artistic side game remains superb. Graphic quality, art style, atmosphere, ambiance, music, storytelling is beautiful and unique.Main story I still enjoy a lot, rather sad tragic story with plenty of family dilemmas and fairy understandable how it unfolds and why most happens. As for side stories I did love the daughters “PoV” story and so did enjoy the mother’s story and they were as well fairly nicely understandable. Issue comes with lighthouse story and the after stories of those. The actors, director stories honestly, I couldn’t fully grasp. How much of them were about actual characters, how much of them were about script, how much about them were about mental dilemmas and by the end of these stories I were lost about who was even story going on about? But I did lose kinda interest and focus as well halfway going through world/setting of those stories anyways.One good thing with story is that, for ending hunting and extra collectibles hunting you don’t have to replay game from start 100 times but you have “chapters” selection where you essentially can resume game from certain chapters and do stuff differently to obtain different outcomes.Anyhow, plenty of lore collectibles, extra collectibles to find. And because how those game plays with your mind. Or well due to camera tricks, finding everything is rather challenging. But fun. Very trippy but absolutely love how this game does stuff with camera. Scenery can change every time you turn around, look stuff from certain angle, from 1 side of pillar or another and so on. BUT on the other side exploration is pretty much of a dice roll… because sadly quite often I ended up running in situation where I didn’t know whenever If I go through X point, can I go back or not? And if I can’t go back, I might end up missing side room… as this game relies on scripted moments a lot… there are plenty of moments you go through door, door locks behind you and goodbye your initial idea of checking the side room.Another dumb Issue I had on few occasions. If I died to a “chase” sequence and respawned. I got spawnkilled by mechanic again and again. On one occasion I had to INSTANTLY move to certain direction to avoid that issue and on second occasion I had to stand still like a rock and wait for death to pass before moving.Anyhow, in conclusion. It’s still beautiful game when it comes to its story telling and artistic side. And walking sim parts of the game are still one of the top notch of its genre. BUT…. The damn mob chases and ESPECIALLY the mob banishing system feels so damn out of place and simply annoying in this game. Not a single time it created tension or any extra horror element for me it simply created annoyance. In the end I loved the journey of main story, daughter story and mother story. Rest of stories, meh. ✅ Finished

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get into it, I wanna mention that the original Layers of Fear is one of my favorite games of all time. I've probably gone through it 7 or so times, and will occasionally revisit it just to experience the story and environment again. This review comes from a place of genuine love for the source material, and with a few updates it would definitely surpass the original.I'll start with the positives: the environmental design and new lighting is gorgeous. Bloober Team shows a tremendous mastery over their visuals and attention to detail in a way that's actually awe-inspiring; flickering lamps and candles create a much more dynamic experience as you trudge your way through the halls. It looks VERY good. The DLC is present and also receives a visual upgrade, and Layers of Fear 2 (a game I wasn't as big a fan of) seems to have gotten a glow up from the original version. There are also new sequences that are genuinely scarier and more interesting than what they replaced (the cat/dog/rat paper puzzle is now replaced with actually having to go through a maze of corridors, avoiding your wife, and unlocking actual doors that correspond to the animal). However, as an experience, it currently has a lot of issues that make it hard to recommend over the original to anyone.(I'm going to be mostly talking about the Painter's story, but also how it ties into the rest of the game briefly. The original game is still the most terrifying and engaging as an experience, and it's no different here. )>>>>SPOILER WARNING<<<< here are some major issues I have with the remake. - There is a TON of new dialogue in the Painter's story, recorded by the original voice actors, as well as getting voices for almost every letter you pick up. The Painter rambles to himself, the wife's apparition speaks a lot more, and you will hear narration from the writer who is framing the story as well. On a surface level, this isn't a bad thing... until you realize that, in the original game, there are many poignant and subtle moments that are completely destroyed by just how much talking you hear. I'm going to list a few examples. - The narration of the writer, as well as the existence of the Rat Queen as a character she is interacting with, feels extremely invasive. You are frequently reminded that you are experiencing this from an outside perspective, which completely destroys any sense of immersiveness. I found myself rolling my eyes whenever the writer talks dramatically about the painter and his wife, or when the rat queen talks to her about how much she enjoyed seeing him suffer, and also in relation to her... while I'm playing the first game's story, as the demented painter wandering his house. It's like if Layers of Fear was combined with the Muppets' Christmas Carol with how much narration there is at times. - The painter and the wife have too much dialogue during the actual gameplay. Besides him talking to himself in every other room, or her constantly talking and repeating of lines when she's chasing you, there's one part in particular that really stood out to me: the sequence where you push the wheelchair. In the original game, you can choose to slowly push the wheelchair through a burned, nightmarish hallway (helping her), or you walk around it through a pretty hallways (abandoning her). With no dialogue, this implication is very clear, and allows you to absorb the event. In the remake, the wife talks constantly, and if you push the wheelchair, she starts talking about how everything will be okay, how they'll be okay.... completely just laying it out for the player what the message was supposed to me. There's a lot less emphasis on metaphor and more on just straight up telling you what things represent because of this, and it's probably my biggest issue with the game. Poignant and subtle moments and obliterated by the sheer amount of dialogue from all parties. It would be nice to have an option that limits it to be more like the original game: no writer narration, no rat queen dialogue, and minimal dialogue from the painter and wife outside of whispers/memories/letters/ etc.   - The framing of the story is clumsy and offputting, especially in regards to how the writer interacts with these stories. I was extremely confused when, in her third chapter, she was suddenly talking about queens and rituals and tributes and getting her son back... events that I was not present for. I wondered if I had experienced a glitch at first, and it completely took away my investment of whatever she was going through.  - The sound design is really wonky. Ambient music will disappear completely when going to certain small side rooms, songs will play at the wrong time (like the theme playing during his original dialogue as the game starts, as opposed to just him speaking), certain events are very poorly timed with their sound effects or are just missing (the piano slamming and closing is several seconds delayed, light switches make zero noise and have indication you touched them, sometimes bookshelves falling over make no noise, windows slamming have delayed sound and zero animation, and jumpscare noises are extremely reduced). The sound effects and music not syncing are definitely a huge problem in a game entirely based on exploring a shifting, scary environment. The sound track alone feels a lot weaker than before as well (even Stumbling All Around gets an unfortunate nerf and is only really heard once in distorted reverse, which I imagine is due to licensing or something. You never even see the phonograph in the house until the extremely shortened bedroom sequence, which is also reduced). The sound design needs a SERIOUS pass through, and is definitely the worst part as of writing this review.  - The environmental puzzles and sequences do feel a bit neutered in parts of what was already a pretty easy game. Certain sequences take out any thought or effort to complete (one example being that, instead of pushing a bookshelf ladder across to reach a key, now you just pop away a memory distortion book and bam, there it is). I like that you don't have to open nearly as many shelves, but it's things like that which make me realize that it might have gone too far with scaling back the interactibility.   - The painter's room has a ton of issues. It doesn't transition very well whenever you interact with the painting, with visibly popping/changing to initiate the next chapter in a jarring way, and the design of the workshop severely lacks the visual impact it used to. It felt like it changed a lot less from chapter to chapter due it to just missing certain visual elements, like the daughter's lamp casting light shapes all over the workshop against a pile of dolls he brought in, or the wallpaper being jarringly different, or the huge mess of holes in the floor in later parts. The lack of decay in both the painter's workshop as well as the "real" house in general feels like a massive step down, especially since you frequently see the real house in a completely normal state now. What was originally the heart of the game is now one of it's least impactful parts, with wonky transitions, the narration from the writer, and just lacking any sense of distortion or change in many parts.Overall, I do like the game, just because of what it is, but I would be lying if I said it didn't feel like a somewhat limp representation of the original. While it's very pretty, it overcompensates with it's dialogue to the point where it takes away some of the environmental storytelling (this is a game of tell and show, as opposed to show, not tell), and it's sound design needs a serious pass over. With some adjustments, though, it would easily be the best way to experience these stories. And after some updates, I would immediately change this review, since again, I adore the original and would love to recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Layers Of Fear is a re-imagining/remake of the original two games and DLC with also two additional stories thrown in.The plot of Layers Of Fear involves taking the role of a writer, inside an isolated lighthouse where she must create novels on the lives on various tortured artists while she herself is one. This is all done under the influence of a dark evil "muse" like character who claims to have also influenced those she is writing about. The game involves living the lives of the artist his wife and daughter and an actor all of which have been vastly improved from their original iterations. The stories are all very dark and warped and while the new ones are comparatively short lived compared to the originals they are all relatively well done. Gameplay in this title is very cinematic, you must walk through corridors taking in breathtaking horror environments as you unravel what has happened, however gameplay has become more involved from the original releases giving clearer storytelling,  Alan Wake style combat where flashlights burn enemies and better more realised puzzles. Audio wise things are also great here to match the environments, great voice acting, lots of voice lines, terrifying sound effects and just an excellent horror audio feast.The game is very lengthy too, with easily 10+ hours for a single run with more to find other endings. As for cons, there isn't many really I really didnt like the original Layers Of Fear 2 for example but this up-dated version fixed most (not all) of my issues with it really making it a fun compelling experience something I didn't think was possible after playing it the first time round.Overall Layers Of Fear is a must for new players to the series and returning fans. A masterpiece of cinematic horror all tied up with a blood dripping bow to deliver the best experience possible with new and compelling gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I've previously reviewed Layers Of Fear (2023) when I had yet to finish Actor and Writer's Chapters. Now, after I played all chapters, including the newest Director's (Cut), I can give my personal opinion.I've been a fan of Layers Of Fear (2016) for a long time. When I heared a "remastered" edition, including all previous games and DLCs, was coming out, I knew I HAD to play (someone was may leading me to buy it? Maybe the same lady who led all these souls?). But let's go with order.Graphically talking, it's the best game I've ever played so far. I loved the 2016 game, this was a love letter to it with incredible lights and effects, probably Musiciant and Director's Chapters are those that really show this. Lights, shadows, everything is perfect. Maybe just some blood effects in Director's Chapter were a bit off, but over all, the work is excellent and has to be praised.When it comes to the more technical part, I have had some issues. So far, the Artist's Chapter was a complete remaster of the 2016 game: lights, animations, locations, everything was changed and improved, from the icons to the pick-up movements. Some great scenes were added, some very cool locations were changed, but everything worked fine I loved the result.I cannot say the same about the Actor's Chapter: half of the icons were simply pasted from the 2019 game (Layers Of Fear 2) and some pick-ups were not updated, ad there was not the animation of the hand picking the item but only it... floating in the air. I have to say the same with the Daughter's Chapter (DLC of Layers Of Fear 2016) that was only graphically improved, icons and animations were the same. Only once I saw a hand animation in this chapter. If we had to have a complete remaster of all games, I expect to find a complete remaster, not half of it. And if someone is saying "Actor's Chapter was done so because they wanted it", I can only tell you that in a short sequence (that is also in the 2019 version) there are updated icons.I know this is such a big product (2 games together, 5 chapters) and I'm grateful for what the devs have done to deliver such good experience. This was just a little (not so little as it happened for 2 full chapters) mistake that could be (or is already) fixed with a hotfix.In terms of the story, Layers Of Fear deliver a great experience: Actor, Daughter, Musiciant and Artist's Chapters are absolutely insane and have perfect timings. From the beginning to the end, it is a rollercoaster of horror, fun, riddles and insanity (which is a good thing). I gotta add also the newest Director's Chapter to this list as it's incredibly well written and performed. i loved every second of it even tho it lacks of chasing sequences and the ending should have been a little bit longer (I got the "bad" ending").About the Writer's Story... I expected something more. Basically, it's the mind all the chapters come from, from what I have learnt, and so it's right it doesn't have so much screen time... but the ending has a huge problem: timing. There is climax, there is suspence, there are new things we discover and that lead us to better understand all the other chapters... but the ending of the Writer's Story feels just so off. In a game that is focused on making the perfect piece of art... we really have such an ending?I get what was the purpose of this and it leaves the door open for what's to come, but the cutscene just need 1, maybe 2 minutes more to feel right and more "correct". I've been disappointed in this. It didn't ruin my experience, tho.But after all, Layers Of Fear is just a piece of art itself. From the lights to the mechanics (the new one is quite amazing, gotta say), from the stories to psychology, it is a little marble that I felt completely. I loved this game and I highly recommend to anyone.

You can name anything that comes to your mind if someone asking about some horror ideas and give you 0.5 sec to think and all of this stuff you can find in this series.It has nice graphics, mood is there, but as a plot heavy horror game - this suck so hard, you can't even imagine.This story can be a nice, very old horror novel, not something from 21st century. _childDocuments_.review: Layers of Fear 2023 draws many parallels with the painter protagonist of the original Layers of Fear.  In the original 2016 game, a painter loses his mind after his wife is caught in a terrible accident and he finds that the dashing of his harmonious home life impairs his ability to reach the same artistic heights he was able to achieve prior to the terrible event.  Much in the same way Bloober team has been trapped in a prison of its own design, incarcerated by in own initial success and each subsequent failure.  Since the release of Layers of Fear 2016, Bloober team has released the intellectually interesting but deeply flawed Observer, the flat and pretentious Layers of Fear 2, and the wholly derivative and underwhelming Blair Witch.  What was supposed to be a return to form and a coming home with a remake of Layers of Fear, instead devolves into a desperate, stabbing attempt at Bloober team reinventing the Layers of Fear mythos into something it is not and, in the process, undermining its already tenuous position as a premiere horror game developer.  In short, Layers of Fear 2023 isn't worth purchasing if you already bought, played, finished and enjoyed Layers of Fear 2016.  The game consists of five chapters of varying length and quality and a short, broken, unsatisfying ending.  The first chapter, the Painter's Story, is simply a reinvention of the original Layers of Fear 2016 game, with a new graphics engine, better lighting effects but, oddly, only equivalent graphics presentation.The game demands a slew of graphics technologies and graphics engine features that preempt gamers from running the title on moderately older hardware, but the title hardly looks better than its almost decade-old predecessor, built on Unity.  The story and game play have certainly changed in places, although, often, for the worse.  New chase scenes have been added that don't fit with the original game paradigm and the game doesn't really add new, cogent scares.  This is unfortunate since Layers of Fear 2016 was excellent and the Painter's Story is the only effectively scary and atmospheric chapter within Layers of Fear 2023.  Ultimately, if you've played Layers of Fear 2016, there's really nothing new here of value for returning players.  If you're a new player, you're better off getting the original for half the money.The other four chapters are parade of failed experiments, or intellectually lazy exploits that barely have any scares between all the combined portions.  One chapter, the Daughter's Story is an hour-long side tale about the Painter's grown daughter, voiced badly by a wooden voice actress and possessed of a long, introspective walking simulator with exactly 0 scares.  The next chapter is the Musician's Story, which is a 2-hour long tale about the Painter's wife during her mental deterioration and eventual suicide.  The story, written for wine moms, deals with post-part-em depression, the feelings of inadequacy the wife felt after the accident and her growing feelings of animosity towards her husband as he tried to hold their family together, respond to her needs and focus on his tenuously successful career.  Neither of the chapters add any real scares and only the Daughter's Story does much to alter the context of the Painter's Story.The last two chapters include the Actor's Story and the Writer's Story.  Actor's Story is a re-imagining of Layers of Fear 2 and it perfectly encompasses how Bloober team have misguidedly "lost the script" about what makes a good horror game.  While Layers of Fear 2016 had a simple, effective, creepily atmospheric every-man premise: "A painter loses his mind after his wife is disfigured and burned horribly.  His failure at his craft furthers his progression towards insanity and he eventually experiences a series of harrowing psycho-supernatural events as he feebly attempts to make amends for his mistakes", Layers of Fear 2 instead adds siblings on a ship, actors, secret societies, living mannequins, psychosis, hypnotism and about half a dozen other mismatched concepts that fall flatly on their face.  Worse is that the Actor's Tale, while sometimes atmospheric only has 2-3, chase driven scares, as the game flounders about, pretending to be an Amnesia mod.Layers of Fear 2 was a totally "skippable" title and the chapter 4 addition to Layers of Fear 2023 is no different.  The walking simulator is strange and sometimes unsettling but hardly harrowing.  The game lacks good scares or a cogent, seminal tale that most people can identify with, like its predecessor's grappling with the fear of losing one's mind.  In short, if the Painter's Story is Layers of Fear, then the Daughter's Story can best be categorized as Layers of Therapy and the Musician's Story can be identified as Layers of Grief.  The Actor's Story is at best Layers of Strange or Layers of Bizarre.  None of them add to the fear felt in the first chapter, despite accounting for 2/3 of the game's play time.The last chapter has gamers playing as a writer who lost her son and made a deal with dark powers by writing tales of misery and woe.  The tales are revealed to include all the prior chapters of the Layers of Fear IP.  This is a bit of letdown as Bloober Team retroactively undoes the impact of the Painter's Story to instead shove a short, minimally scary tale about Foxy Cleopatra and her dead offspring, into the center stage.  Worse still is that the chapter squanders a great setting (an abandoned lighthouse) and lacks any real ending, leaving players on an unsatisfying cliffhanger that feels insulting after Bloober team shamelessly repackaged its two prior Layers of Fear titles with a scant 3.5 hours of new, scare-free experiences.In short, Layers of Fear 2023 is a complete failure and the onus is on Bloober team to salvage its reputation.  It is currently developing Silent Hill and my sincere hope is that they sidestep all the pitfalls they keep stepping into, including story pretention, extreme abstraction, cultural narratives and general focus on experimentation over solid, tried-and-true horror creation techniques.  If you've played Layers of Fear 2016, you should save your money.  If you've never played the original Layers of Fear 2016, you should buy that instead of this title. It'll probably be half the price.  I gave this game a positive review but only because I have an unsettling feeling that Bloober team will eventually de-list the original Layers of Fear 2016 game and we'll all be left with only this pale reproduction.  In that eventuality, I recommend playing through the Painter's Story and maybe the Daughter's Story and then quickly uninstalling.7/10.A let down.  Silent Hill is their last chance...

_childDocuments_.review: Short review - Boring, lackluster gameplay with weak, barely existent horror elements, go play any other horror game, you can thank me later.The original Layers of Fear was a walking simulator type horror game where players walked along a corridor awaiting scary things to happen, which often failed to provide any reaction at all, with the exception of one scene involving a child which at least got a laugh out of me, while its use of non Euclidean space provided far more entertainment as an experience. A five hour experience that wasn't anything special, an awful horror game that relied too much on tired, samey jumpscares, and a story that felt so railroaded, you'd have to look up a walkthrough to see any other endings. Its DLC story added nothing to the story but features some awful fish eye lens tricks that genuinely ruins the experience, imagine walking around with a camera fully zoomed in and using that to navigate and you get the idea.Layers of Fear 2 was a significantly better game with a complete change of setting, gameplay changes pushing it away from the walking simulator genre with narrative choices and a monster giving chase, the monster is aggressive often putting you into a fail state that requires a little trial and error to know what to do in that situation, while it still lacked the horror element, it was a far more entertaining experience.And now moving onto Layers of Fear (Remake) a game that combines both of the previous games together, an additional story, and new gameplay features all wrapped up within the feature set of the Unreal 5 Engine.And its a disaster in almost every way.From a technical perspective, the games got serious issues, the famous Unreal Engine 5 "Stutter struggle" is there in all its glory, textures often fade into existence even when cracked up to maximum and the games "Ray Tracing" only appears as reflections and so rarely, you'll forget its even a feature, at least it doesn't impact performance to any major degree. A horror game that stutters takes you right out of the experience, a problem that still exists at the time of this review.Layers of Fear's Remake introduces you to "The Writer" yet another nameless protagonist to the series, who acts as an overruling hub for the main stories, featuring a square and three rooms to play with, shes a completely pointless character who currently adds nothing to the other two stories and introduces us to the series villain, a character so forgetful that she supposedly existed in the original games, but hey, at least you'll see her fail to jumpscare you over the length of the experience.So moving onto the first experience, a not at all faithful remake of the first game that takes out a number of scenes including the child scene and fails to replace them with anything exciting but hey, the game has "combat" now. Thats right, your previous walking simulator has some minor combat elements. Which can best be described as  borrowed from Alan Wake, you shine a Lantern at a scary thing with a bright beam and after 3 seconds, the "scary thing" melts into the floor and stays there before coming back for another round. Did i mention the Lantern has a limited life span? That drains while you have it out? So either you drain your lantern fighting a monster, or risk stumbling around long enough for it to recharge, it also has a Hud icon split into sections which means absolutely nothing, causing confusion, it looks like they planned to have a lantern which had to be refuelled but they scrapped it because it would be to difficult to build the game around.During my playthrough, I did completely different things, but ended up with the exact ending I got in the original game, confirming my suspicions that you basically have to follow a walkthrough to get any ending besides the "bad" ending.Onto the DLC, and its changed so little, I'm convinced nothings changed.Theres also a new storyline as the main characters wife, its lackluster and swaps out the lantern with a torch, its entirely forgettable and feels like its there to pad runtimeMoving onto the "remake" of Layers of Fear 2, and its barely been touched with the exception of adding a torch, the hud element returns with less sections and a light on the torch showing the power of the torch, why even have the hud element when it shows the power level on the torch? At least the torch has some additional features like the ability to move mannequins around and of course, stunning the monster, almost, the monster can't move, but it will still trigger a fail state if you get too close, did no one test that? Or did they just not care? Visually it barely looks better than the original, features no reflective surfaces for ray tracing making that feature a waste entirely, still better off playing the original and saving your money.As soon as Layers of Fear 2's remake is done? Drop to credits, no resolution to the writers story at all, Want a resolution to that story? Onto the "Directors Story" to get it.The Directors Story feels like it was created by a different studio entirely, one that actually cares about what its crafting, its horror elements actually do something, the Unreal Engine's effects are actually utilised with sparks and lighting effecting the environment and introduces a fetch quest where you have to acquire two items for a movie directorial shoot. And the director minigame is easily my favourite part of the game.The directorial minigame puts you in the seat of the director allowing you to switch items and characters around to do a scene of a horror film, do you want an ultra violent, grisly tale? Or a slapstick horror film? Or a combo of both since you have five scenes to edit and decide leading to the end of that story. Its short but far more enjoyable than the previous two remakes, it made me want a horror director game in a similar style and something a developer could easily make money from.And you finally get the end to The Writers story, a small 30 second cutscene and a cut to main menu, that's right, you don't even put the credits at the end of the game, you get the feeling the Directors story was rushed in by a different game studio.Overall, Layers of Fear remake for horror gamers is barely scary, there's far better horror games that do far more than this mess,

_childDocuments_.review: I was intrigued by this release, it looked interesting like an Amnesia-style horror game. The big thing that stood out to me is that this is an Unreal Engine 5 game, which is a big deal as so many different studios use this engine and UE4 has been such a point of frustration for the PC gaming community, thanks to games like Hogwarts Legacy and Jedi Survivor which are full of performance/optimization shortcomings, chiefly on the PC platform. It's like the publishers only care about the state of their console releases and us PC users can choke on shader compilation stutter. I don't blame the developers because they unfortunately don't get to make the call on when a game gets released, and they are often trying to do their best with the amount of time they are given. Unreal Engine 5 is supposed to be better and not be such a hot mess, even when developers don't have sufficient time pre-launch to get everything working properly. I can say that this game seems to run very well on my desktop PC (R7-5800x3d/rtx 3070/32GB DDR4 3200 CL16/installed on a Samsung 980 Pro Gen 4 NVMe), everything maxed out, including Lumen Ray Tracing @2954x1231 (closest I can get to a 1440p on my 21:1 ultrawide), I was getting about 90-100 fps using DLSS Quality mode.I know other people don't care what specs I have, I am only mentioning it so others know what kind of performance to expect and so they know that this game runs well on launch weekend, it's not a buggy/glitchy mess like many games have been lately.This game uses Lumen ray tracing, as well as Epic's Temporal Super Resolution. This game is absolutely gorgeous and I have really enjoyed playing it so far, it has been a while since a game's graphics/visuals has really impressed me like this. I highly recommend it if you want to play a moody horror game. You don't need to have played the originals as this is a remaster + new story. Anshar has done a great job with this and I think it's a steal for the $25 that I paid. One cool bonus, if you own a Mac with Apple Silicon, you can play this on that platform as well. It runs surprisingly well on my base model (8GB/256GB) M1 Macbook Pro. I did notice a conflict with cloud saves between Mac and Windows, but I have seen this before with other games, and cloudsaves work perfectly between Windows machines and Steam Deck.

This review will be changed should an official slider be put in, it's unacceptable.Completion edit: So I've done most of the content enough to basically be "done" with this game. It's possible to increase the FOV in The Actor via UUU5 for anyone wondering. In any case, some of the writing felt so rushed, it's heavily disappointing in that regard. The "letting go" secret ending for The Painter doesn't have any additional dialogue, and doesn't even play sound effects for the door being opened, and the scene outside the house (that you finally get to see for the first time) looks unfinished. The ending that wraps up the whole thing with The Writer is also highly anticlimactic, and as far as I'm aware is the ONLY ending. After ALL the various endings, secret or otherwise, throughout all the stories, the Writer only gets one, and it again feels like the most rushed, unfinished thing. They really set themselves up excellently just to fall flat at the end with so much wasted potential.I suppose the only thing that could redeem it is if they're looking at making a sequel that continues the Writer's story.

_childDocuments_.review: The work suffers from the inclusion of an inappropriate character who disrupts the purpose and structure of the piece. The authors could have achieved greater authenticity by creating a character reminiscent of classic literary figures such as Edgar Allan Poe or Mary Shelley. This character would have possessed a unique style and psychology, helping to better convey the emotional and intellectual state of the protagonist.The addition of a dark-skinned female writer is likely connected to an attempt to portray diversity and tolerance in society. However, in this context, it appears out of place and inconsistent with the overall concept of the work. Since the character does not match the external and psychological characteristics to the maximum extent, this intervention has negatively impacted the aesthetic integrity of the piece and diminished its value.Contemporary art, whether in films or games, should strive to remain true to its artistic values and qualities rather than conforming to societal demands. This allows for the creation of works that evoke deep emotions and reflect the talent and inspiration of the creators.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tech demo with a horror theme. PT was really popping off at the time so a bunch of devs tried to imitate its success, and this is goober team's take on it. Pretentious narrative with tons of scripted events. It's a boring walking sim more than anything. The story is not good. It's basically some edgy familial drama in the first game and its DLC, a boring story about an actor and horror mannequin tropes in the second game, and a lame wraparound story about the writer. It's all very cliche and tries so hard to make you think it's super deep. The story is told in a very grating way through these immersion-shattering voiceovers that feel so unnecessary. Outside of walking through hallways at a snails pace, you also pick up enough notes to fill a few novels. There's also your standard chase sequences where you can stun your opponents with your lamp/flashlight. Super basic and boring gameplay. After playing through this studio's other failed attempts at horror, I was hoping this could be the one exception in their catalog. People really gassed this one up back in the day, too. While it ain't as bad as Blair Witch, it's certainly not much better. I have zero hope for the SH2 remake and I highly suggest avoiding all of Bloober's titles. All have horrible depictions of mental illness using stereotypes, are all riddled with bugs, and are aggressively boring. Cool visual tricks can only take you so far.
