_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, I've played the original LoF 1 and LoF 2 and I enjoyed them thoroughly, and I was so excited when you announced a macOS port! I am REALLY happy that you ported the game to Mac and very thankful, and it's great that it released at the same time as the Windows version.UPDATE: I changed my review to recommended after Layers of Fear developers have fixed many issues I had brought up.FIXED: The resolution setting now worksFIXED: Game engine rendering is still being done in non-retina resolution, but the game is now changing the OS resolution to match the selected resolution setting (it's still not ideal/buggy, but at least it works now)FIXED: HDR is implemented and offers customization options to match your display's capabilities. Feels like it could be improved by having a separate slider for setting the black level (useful on OLEDs and mini-LEDs), but it works well enough now.There are still a few things I wish they did better:- The whole game runs in letterboxed 16:9 instead of the Mac screen's 16:10 (or 3:2) and has no option to change FOV. That's very annoying to me, I'd suggest playing on a 16:9 screen.- It's great that the game offers MetalFX upscaling (MetalFX is a *must-have* for all Mac games) but it has very little customization options: only offers two settings: "quality" and "performance", no ability to switch between temporal or spatial and no ability to choose resolution scaling. Personally I'd like to choose MetalFX Temporal at 2x upscaling. An example of great implementation would be No Man's Sky, which offers both MetalFX Temporal and MetalFX Spatial and many different settings to choose- The Mac port is missing ray traced reflections, but that has little to no impact on visuals and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Waterboard your trauma away."Solitude can be a lonely place.  Solitude can be a sentence.  Or it can be a companion.  It is whatever you make it.""No one understands them.  No one will understand you.""While I was learning how to live, I have been learning how to die.""How many times must a man die before he can live?""Your body can be rebuilt, but some wounds go deeper, so much deeper.""Once they lit a flame in their soul, there was no turning back.""The boy that never speaks, have you found a voice?""Finally, I understand, the way out, it's here, in me."Told through the perspective of a writer, painter, and a playwright, this game you will quite literally turn around and everything will change every five seconds, the entire game.  The story is loosely about writer's block, but also veers into the deeper aspects of what really truly makes psychological horror what it should be.  There's really no reason to be "scared" in this game, which further proves the distinction between these sort of horror sub-genres, unless you have no idea who you yourself are.  It's a different kind of unaddressed fear in some, and a masterclass at that.While there are a few references to some non-existent plays, there are some posters of real ones as well (Hamlet, The Tempest, King Lear, and the Twelfth Night), since they are all Shakespeare, it's likely a copyright reason for reference, I see no reason to need to know anything about them as I know a mild amount about them and see very little references to them, but they could still be there for the theater nerds.That being said, I would say you should probably see the movie Se7en before playing this if you haven't seen it.  There is very little relation to the movie in the story, but there is a clear reason to have seen the movie to understand why certain things are present in a very very small section of the game.  It is very worth knowing to catch those references which are not exactly direct.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a really fun experience that I would ultimately recommend playing. Sadly, the new Writer's story fell really flat for me and ended up way too vague and underdeveloped compared to the others. So this made it feel more like a hub world from which you play all the other games rather than a fleshed out narrative of its own that weaved in amongst them. However, despite that one disappointment, I must say I really enjoyed every other story included this remaster/remake (including the two new extras exclusive to this version). The Painter's story (LoF 1) was a beautiful tragedy that has haunted me long after completion, and the Daughter's (original DLC) and the Musician's (exclusive to LoF 2023) stories really flesh this narrative out even if they are technically optional experiences. Perhaps my favourite story was the Actor's (LoF 2) since it featured such a huge variety of set pieces and visual styles complete with a really intriguing narrative that (imho) had the superior storytelling. The Director's (exclusive to LoF 2023) story was interesting, if inconsequential, and definitely the least memorable of all the narratives, although it does raise some interesting questions as to the identity of the mentor figure from LoF 2. As for gameplay, this is essentially a walking simulator horror game with the occasional monster chase thrown in to break up the reading. Personally, I was perfectly fine with this design choice, as it's quite similar to other psychological horror games I've enjoyed such as SOMA, and it also allows the narrative and character writing to take centre stage. Speaking of which, the character writing in this game is phenomenal, really hooking you early on and making you ask all sorts of questions about the nature of the protagonists. It's also really good at respecting the player's intelligence, trusting you to make logical assumptions based on the little snippets of information you're provided with gradually through the notes and objects you pick up. It uses this to masterful effect by leading you down one particular interpretation of what's happening only to later provide you with information that contradicts your assumptions and throws your understanding of events on its head, often casting the ensemble in an entirely new and empathetic light. At this point, I should clarify that I have never played the original LoF games, so I am not sure how much of this content was present in the original games vs added in the remaster. However, my limited understanding is that the majority of LoF 2 is preserved (with narration by the Writer added between each chapter) and that most of LoF 1 was redesigned with a more explicit focus on the supernatural element that ties the games together as well as the inclusion of new monster chase sequences. There has also been voice acting added to most of the in-game notes (with only the occasional jarring difference between text and delivery), which helped my ADHD brain immensely with staying focused. Personally, I enjoyed all this content and found it very enjoyable for a first time player. As a final comment, the game is visually just downright gorgeous. The environments sometimes feel more real than real-life and the HDR lighting contrasts are pure visual eye candy. The gameplay was buttery smooth at max settings on my GTX 1070 at 1440p unlike some other UE5 games I've played, and imo really shows off the visual splendour possible with this engine. So ultimately, if you can accept the few shortcomings I've mentioned above, then I think you'll be in for a treat. This is a game I highly recommend playing and I know I will be spending many more hours in-game exploring all the little details of the narrative!

_childDocuments_.review: All good things come to an end. It's an unavoidable truth. This is none more true than for Bloober's break-through isometric Horror franchise "Layers Of Fear". This third instalment, which cryptically shares it's title with the 2016 original, this time follows multiple individuals down multiple paths. With a narrative this time focalized from many perspectives as opposed to the usual one or two, the story in some small way feels like an attempt at creating a Horror version of popular Oscar winning movie "The Hours".Beginning the game as new central protagonist 'The Writer', the first 15 minutes of the game is typical LOF fare: wander round a small localised area interacting with objects and experiencing mild supernatural phenomena. It is only AFTER the protagonist returns to her typewriter that things really start going as we are once more sent back to the beginning of the franchise and thrust into the wine-sodden, pain-smeared shoes of the protagonist 'The Painter'. Whether we are meant to see this as a jump to the past or whether the character is revealed to be fictional is not known at this stage, though the setting is an unmistakably familiar one with a lot of familiar story-beats and others (refreshingly) not so much. Currently at the 2 hour mark in my first play through and there are most notable difference is presence of mild combat. Rather than attempting to ignore the antagonist in the original LOF game, or flea from it like in the sequel, in this concluding chapter the player is encouraged to face the foe and to proactively make their own luck in progressing through the game. Some of these encounter segments can be a little frustrating but that's a minor complaint in the long run. Lastly, we come to the obvious topic of the graphic enhancements. The original LOF may not be universally popular but it was a definite milestone in 1st person Horror - just as much as higher profile titles like "Outlast" and "Resident Evil VII" - and it is pleasing to see this franchise at last receiving the 100% graphical makeover it deserves. Skin, wood and cloth textures all radiate their own feel and depth which benefits the experience to no end. A partial rehash of previous titles this may be, but it still manages to feel like something fresh as a result. At this stage, I can't really say too much more about this new 2023 version of "Layers Of Fear" other than I knew I was going to like it when a bought it - I know, sad fanboy - but wasn't expecting to be this impressed by the offering. Although I'm only less than a 10th of the way through at this stage, I already credit this as one of the best Steam titles of the year. It's been put forward for this year's award and it quite rightly deserves it's candidature. - 5/5 Stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending only because there isn't a neutral option and I think the positives outweigh the negatives.Positives are there is 2 games in one, plus DLC which is nice. Sound design and atmosphere is fantastic and the graphics are decent enough. Achievements are also fairly easy to get, and are fully guided if you care about that. The stories are pretty interesting, and thankfully it pretty much starts off with the Painter's which is by far the strongest story IMO. The environments are pretty interesting in all stories, and if you enjoy reading and piecing together the story yourself,  I think you'll get more out of the story than others. Some of the changes from the original are pretty cool, and I think added to how good the original was.Neutral - all stories are relatively short. Negatives are some of the puzzles don't make too much sense, the other stories are overshadowed by how good the Painter's story is (even if the others do have some good ideas, the execution doesn't do them justice), there can be quite game-breaking bugs which require a restart (falling through a void endlessly for example) - which can be very annoying if you have to do the same thing multiple times, though I did only experience these a handful of times. The scares are also pretty lame, just your standard jump scares for the most part. Most story isn't explicitly told to the player, so if you don't like environmental storytelling as well as searching for and reading notes, you probably won't like this.Overall it's decent, get it on sale if you want it.

_childDocuments_.review: Layers of Fear (2023) is a surreal walking simulator that includes Layers of Fear 1 and Layers of Fear 2 as well as some additional content (that I did not bother to play). Layers of Fear 2 is more dreamy with a less straightforward story compared to Layers of Fear 1. Overall Layers of Fear (2023) is a good game with an interesting and disturbing story, but unfortunately there are no real puzzles you have to solve, almost no items you have to find/use/combine (except for a few keys) and lots...I mean LOTS of doors. If you enjoy walking simulators that tell a dark and twisted tale then I would still recommend Layers of Fear (2023).

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece in the genre of horror games. Although a complete different direction that for example Outlast, this game packs some deeply twisted stories of the psychological pits of the human psyche.Beautifully designed, truely horrific ambienence and stories that really pull you in. Loved every minute of it.It is truely more of a walking simulator but it's worth every minute. _childDocuments_.review: As of late, I have been drawn toward the whole experience of playing psychological horror style games.  Started with Phasmophobia, the Demonologist, Devour, Escape the Backroom, LUTO and many others... However, then comes along Layers of Fear... a game that transcends traditional horror boundaries to deliver an experience that will leave you trembling and questioning your own sanity. This was a game I had with no prior history of or experience or even a yTube video to pre-screen the game play, I just dove right into it... I was sold on the "Graphics Beauty" of it (in Steam)... I love Unreal Engine, I love Corsair and I personally have a 'bomb' of a PC to push all boundaries of rendering and FPS. Personally, it was a slow start for me.  However, that only lasted a few hours… (and I’m glad I continued to play) The more I grew patience to listen and read a pounding of mystery letters right from the very beginning, the more I grew interest to give this game a real good shot!From the very moment you take your first hesitant step into the meticulously crafted Victorian mansion, a sense of unease begins to creep over you. This game is a masterclass in narrative delivery, utilizing a non-linear storytelling approach to pull players into a nightmarish slew of memories, emotions, and hidden traumas.The game's psychological manipulation is its true genius. Mirrors warp reality, corridors twist and elongate, and time itself seems to unravel before your eyes. It's not just the surroundings that warp – your own perceptions become unreliable allies.While the game's mechanics are relatively simple – exploration, observation, and interaction – the execution is where ‘Layers of Fear’ shines. Puzzles are intricately woven into the narrative, demanding your attention to detail and critical thinking. Every item you find, every note you read, and every door you open reveals another layer of the artist's mind, pushing you further towards the revelation of the horrific truth that lies at the heart of this twisted tale.Overall, I would hate to think that anyone who is in love with psychological horror style games would miss out on this masterpiece.  A true 5 out of 5 star this game demands.A note for the developers... You need to add to these wonder games more "JumpScare" scenes... Get the goosebumps going guys!!! This game would have received 6 stars if you had more JumpScares.Thanks Team Blobber.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say this right off the jump: If you've played the first two Layers of Fear games and aren't interested in playing them again with a very nice new coat of paint, you probably don't need this.The title is confusing, but the basics are that this release combines the first two Layers of Fear games, ties them together with a small additional narrative and redoes the whole thing in Unreal Engine 5. As a showpiece for that engine, this certainly does a great job as everything looks gorgeous and at least for me, it ran perfectly (i.e. mostly over 100fps) on a 3080 at 1440p with everything cranked and DLSS on Auto. The original games still look pretty good and this takes it up a further notch.The combination of the two games does make for a bit of a lopsided experience. The first Layers of Fear is shorter than the second one and it tells the story of three characters, whereas the second only tells the story of one. At the time, I felt the second game while good, overstayed its welcome narratively and could have told the story it wanted to in a lot less time and with less filler. None of that has been addressed here. The second game makes up well more than half of this package and while it's by no means bad, it is the weaker half. The additional story that is supposed to link everything together is also not very deep and could have offered a lot more in terms of character development and meta narrative.In terms of horror, this series has always played more like a haunted house that has a lot of cool tricks up its sleeve. It's not quite a walking simulator, but aside from some chase sequences, light puzzle solving and collectibles, it's mostly a linear progression through someone's increasingly mad state. It's unsettling and certainly impressive, but I wouldn't call it overly scary.Again, unless you're a super fan of this series or haven't played it before, I don't think there's much reason for you to pick this up. If you haven't played it though and want a dark story told in a really cool way, I highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: We've had lots of amazing horror content this year and this game is no exception. I not only play horror for the scares and gut wrenching moments but the story-line and how it develops and ties everything together. This was also high up on my list for months before the release because of it being re-made in EU5 (i did wait lol) for visual quality that did not disappoint at all!!! After a full play-through of all the stories within this game I can't help but admire how well things like depression, anxiety, and suicide were put into art form. The second the game starts you step into the mindset of these artists and you slowly go deeper into their motives, regrets, fears, and anguish. Besides the actual game play the audio/voice acting does so much for the story and I think this is one of those games that NEEDS a headset for the best first-time experience. All this is woven so well together which is the reason I'm writing this review- It's now my favorite horror game and I hope I can convince more people to try it. I'd love more expansions to the story or an entirely different story since I feel like this team could do just fine in another horror universe So If you're into psychology, horror, and the different motives that drive people - THIS IS FOR YOU! Finally, I want to take the time to thank the entire team and their attention to detail, coming back to remake the game in EU5, extremely reasonable pricing (100% got my money's worth & more), and the extremely captivating voice actors.

_childDocuments_.review: With only the faintest memories of watching youtubers play LoF1 and 2 when they came out I wanted to experience them for myself. Oh boy, where to start...some spoilers ahead;Layers of Fear, The Painter:The first game, Layers of Fear, started strong, the first two chapters felt coherent, had some understandable story telling and did a good job of setting up the character and rapidly deteriorating psyche of The Painter. Sadly this didn't last, as the chapters went on the game descended more and more into incoherent madness, and while yes that may be the point of the game, it doesn't make for a good experience when it devolves down to endless walking through ever-changing hallways (a mechanic that is overused and stops being interesting far too quickly) picking up notes to learn lore that never feels like it has a satisfying payoff especially with the addition of The Writer's story. The Lantern, the big change to the original game, is such a poorly done afterthought it killed any enjoyment I would have gotten from it. Multiple times I had the roaming enemy that you now have to 'fight' spawn on top of me and instantly kill me. Multiple times I walked out of the respawn room, only to have it spawn right in front of me, and because you need to hold down the lantern button for it to have any effect, it always takes too long and you end up being effectively spawn camped. Thankfully, there is an option to turn on safe mode and not have to engage with this poorly done afterthought of a mechanic that should never have made it into the game. I turned it on, and never took it off again. Also it's worth noting that the 'back out of interacting button' and 'take out the lantern' button, are the same bind. So closing a note or picking up an item always means you take out the lantern, another oversight. One thing I will say, is that some of the less crazy paintings in the game are actually really well done and some of them I wouldn't mind being able to get myselfDLC; Inheritance: I don't know I've ever had a worse experience in a DLC honestly. Meandering, aimless storytelling, meaningless interactions that fail to expand upon the established story in the first game, dream sequences that make no sense and obscure objectives that are easy to misunderstand, and a whole sequence that shrinks you down to child height. I admittedly thought we became a rat at first, given the abundance of rat themes in the game. Pointless padding that grows more annoying than anything, and I'm not going to talk about that Wyrm thing that roams about that one painting sequence. Not to mention endings that fail to provide any sort of satisfaction. If there was an option to skip having to play this DLC, I would have taken it.Musician's Story: This new addition felt better, at least at the start. It did a good job of establishing the mental state of The Musician after the trauma of the fire. And even though her whole angle of being trapped in her body was easy to guess at, I felt it did a good job of expanding upon her character.  However, this does not excuse the poor gameplay that comes along with it as once again, you get to use that new combat mechanic. I still had safe mode turned on from the first game, and let me tell you the most entertainment I got was from watching the roaming enemy melt whenever it got too close because it couldn't kill me. The notes you find, while some of them expand decently upon her as a character, some of them are read aloud by a woman with a grating, piercing voice that I couldn't stand listening to and had to skip. This highlighted another failing of the game, or highlights my failing at being able to find the keybinding, you can't reread notes once you've picked them up. I have no idea what her notes said, but I don't care to go back and find out honestly. The endings you get for The Musician as well don't feel amazingly done. You either get the canon ending, or a new one that just leaves more questions than anything.Layers of Fear 2, The Actor: My view of this one is maybe a little biased, as the constant rocking of the ship made me nauseous, but in any event,You start off directionless on the ship (and get given the how to open doors tutorial again, showing they slapped the story in without making such a basic adjustment from when it was its own product) and the setup is right away weaker than in Layers of Fear. While LoF had some basic guidance, a plot and a strong setup, LoF2 does not. And while I do honestly like the idea that the story is 'structured' around and like some of the set pieces and how it's done, it did not make for an enjoyable time. The majority of notes that I came across do not have any voice acting, a downgrade from the first game. At this point the jumpscares are so overdone that I stop even noticing them, in the first game I remember only one instance of a jumpscare getting me, and that was right at the start of the game. Throughout the franchise jumpscares and musical stings are so overused they lose any power they once had, and also they're so frequent that tension is never given a chance to build up properly, the exact thing jumpscares are supposed to work on. LoF2 is one great big walking sim, even more so than the other games, and while the others had notes, items, environmental storytelling, and paintings to examine, LoF2 lacks most of that and instead you walk through identical corridors and rooms through a large passenger liner at sea that made for quite a boring experience, so boring in fact, my friend I was experiencing the game with fell asleep during this part. The lighting for this one was bizarre, so often I'd enter a room that was washed out or blurred to the point it hurt my eyes because the lighting was so off balance. The character of the actor is honestly an interesting one and I liked the premise and some of the earlier story establishment for them, especially as some of the background notes and files that you can't pick up, but can zoom in on, give actual interesting text and background lore, though sadly not enough to matter. The flash light you get given, while interesting in the time windy aspect of it controlling the legions of mannequins you find, is functionally identical to the lantern of the first game, and that means that yes, combat is back. I again skipped it as it wasn't worth experiencing.The core themes of this game, touching on the aspects of Jungien psychology, different characters, personas, repressed memories and all that that reside within you is one that is honestly interesting to me and speaks to my hobbies and interests. That fact that you can choose to let the Actors 'shadow' loose, or repress it, is an interesting one. I also like they finally show faces in this one, albeit at the end.The Writer:The Writer... Considering her story is the one that's supposed to be tying this franchise together, to be giving the culmination to the story and mythos that's been established...it's a letdown. Her story is interspliced in small sections between the going on of the rest of the content. It admittedly started off alright, getting her established, getting a look at what her story and angle is. Her gameplay sections are mostly short. They offer some interesting if not totally clear bits of lore and world building but it all feels overshadowed by the man antagonist of the game (I started writing about her, but I ran out of room). Once again her sections rely too much on jumpscares and loud sound effects and music making it not only uninteresting, but also annoying. (especially in the section with the teleporting painting.) I don't remember most of what happened with her story I was so unimpressed with it. I do remember how it ended, and I do remember being just disappointed that there was no grand culmination, no final hurrah, nothing. I wanted a bang, and I got a whimper.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option for if I recommend this game because that is how I really feel, but if I had to make a decision, I guess I would recommend it. And that is hard for me to say because I LOVED the first two games, I thought they were amazing.The Good:The game looks beautiful. Visually it takes the previous games and recreates them from the ground up. It also changes the games slightly, adding some interesting parts and mechanics and I believe it is done well (not entirely necessary though). And the games themselves are still fun to play and explore, see the different endings. If you played the games previously, then you won't be scared, but the story is interesting. If you are new, give it a try, I think you will like them. Overall, playing a new version of Layers of Fear 1 and 2 was nice.The Bad:The new story... well, I struggle to even call it that. I was expecting a full, new story that tied the games together like it said, but really, that is not there. It kind of just feels like they jammed the two original games together and "The Writer" is a weak glue that holds them together. They didn't do anything with the writer, I know little about her, I don't care at all for her, and had no choices (that I know of) in the extremely limited time I played as her. Really, this is not a new game. This is just a bundle of the previous games remastered which would be fine... if they marketed it that way. Instead, I am disappointed. It was not entirely what I expected. Also, at first there were A LOT of glitches (my game crashed the first few times I tried to play) which had no business being there in what should have been a completed game, but I guess that's just par for the course now-a-days.At the end of the day, I enjoyed playing this game, it was good. Was I satisfied? Ehh, not really. If this series is actually going to continue, the developers are going to have to learn the same lesson as other game series in the past did, pretty graphics can't cover up a non-existent story.

_childDocuments_.review: Layers of Fear, a spine-chilling horror game, delivers an immersive experience that will leave players on the edge of their seats. As a fan of the horror genre, I thoroughly enjoyed my time exploring the twisted depths of the protagonist's mind in this psychological masterpiece. With its atmospheric setting, gripping narrative, and stunning visuals, Layers of Fear successfully captivates players and draws them into its macabre world.One of the standout features of Layers of Fear is its unique premise. Playing as a tormented painter struggling to complete his magnum opus, the game submerges players in a psychological journey filled with fragmented memories, bizarre visions, and supernatural occurrences. The narrative unfolds like an intricate puzzle, keeping players guessing and questioning their own sanity as they delve deeper into the mind of the protagonist. The game does an excellent job of building tension and fear through its clever storytelling techniques, creating an atmosphere that is both unnerving and captivating.Visually, Layers of Fear is a stunning piece of art in its own right. The graphics are exquisitely detailed, with a meticulous attention to lighting, textures, and environmental design. The Victorian-era mansion in which the game takes place is beautifully rendered, its decaying walls and hauntingly elegant decor adding to the overall sense of dread. The use of atmospheric effects, such as flickering lights and distorted perspectives, adds to the game's unsettling ambiance and further enhances the feeling of unease.The gameplay mechanics in Layers of Fear are relatively straightforward, focusing more on exploration and puzzle-solving rather than combat. The lack of traditional combat elements allows players to fully immerse themselves in the atmosphere and narrative without the distraction of constant action. Instead, the game relies on psychological tricks and mind-bending illusions to keep players engaged and terrified. Interacting with the environment, discovering hidden clues, and unraveling the layers of the protagonist's twisted psyche are all integral to progressing through the game.While Layers of Fear excels in many areas, there are a few minor drawbacks worth mentioning. The pacing can feel somewhat inconsistent, with moments of intense terror followed by periods of slower progression. Additionally, some puzzles may feel repetitive or overly reliant on trial and error, which can momentarily disrupt the otherwise seamless immersion.In conclusion, Layers of Fear is a hauntingly atmospheric horror game that provides a deeply immersive experience. Its engrossing narrative, striking visuals, and psychological twists make it a must-play for horror enthusiasts. Despite a few minor shortcomings, the game delivers a gripping and chilling adventure that will leave players questioning their own perceptions of reality. If you have a taste for psychological horror and appreciate intricate storytelling, Layers of Fear is an excellent choice that will keep you on the edge of your seat throughout its eerie journey into the darkest corners of the human mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: An update dropped today. I'll edit as I go through the game.--Don't get it.I say this as someone who has played the first original game + Inheritance and absolutely loved it. Layers of Fear 2016 was and is my favourite horror game. I'm only an hour in and I'm enjoying this one too. This isn't a remaster; they've added different scenes, changed how you make choices, and included notes not native to the first game.The voice-over and merging of the Painter's story with the Writer makes the differences more pronounced. However, this does make it feel like two stories are happening at once. This is, without a doubt, an entirely different experience than the 2016 game.I will note that the note voice-over only covers a few paragraphs and will skip others (usually at the start or end).The reason why I say not to get this: it's buggy. I've had to restart at least three times because the game didn't recognize a trigger for the next scene. Doors have glitched through me, items teleport to the other side of the room (not thrown - teleported), I've endlessly fallen, and got stuck on "press any key to continue" during a warning page. Restarting fixed all issues.Oddly, I was able to continue my game from my demo progress (chapter 5). This is all within 1.2 hours of the game.Overall, I'm absolutely enjoying it. It's a fun, new experience. It's a refreshing and interesting take on the original game (and the others, I'm sure). But the bugs definitely draw me out of the story and this game deserves better than that, especially if you're here for the first time. This story deserves a proper chance. Wait at least a few weeks for the developers to iron it out. Wishlist it and buy it later.

_childDocuments_.review: I played much of this elsewhere, so the short playtime is misleading. Ultimately I didn't feel like this was worthwhile enough to play if you've already played the others before. Yes, the new graphics are nice, and it's kind of helpful not to have every single cupboard interactable so you open things fruitlessly and waste time, but was that enough of a draw?If you've never played the games before, this is a great package deal (although I didn't like Layers of Fear 2 much at all the first time around), if you know that you're getting basically a spooky walking sim with some very light puzzles, but the value add here is minimal for those who already played it. Time would have been better spent crafting a new narrative entirely (and the lighthouse segment is not it, while I didn't end up finishing the game, I watched a playthrough of the lighthouse part and there wasn't enough meat there, quite frankly).There is also this bizarre choice not to have voice actors read the entire text up on the screen of a letter or article, they skip over sometimes key bits of it. If you're going to have voice actors read notes, have them READ THE WHOLE THING, otherwise instead of paying attention to either the text or the reading, I am distracted by the voice while having to backtrack to finish the text. What kind of design decision was that?And this kind of encapsulates my issues with Bloober. I think in general they are ambitious in their desires and I applaud them that, but every game from them feels like there is a lack of something, either in story, gameplay, or another aspect that doesn't gel and make the whole more than the sum of its parts. The developers commented on another review that this is more of a psychological horror and not meant to be filling you with dread, but really none of their products have managed to nail horror properly, and to say they aren't trying to frighten you during the games and that it's meant to be more of a tense atmosphere is disingenuous; there are many moments designed to unnerve and place you in a state of fear, but they aren't really that successful or rely on cliche to accomplish it.It does makes me concerned for Silent Hill 2's remake, as none of their games have truly wowed me, and, based on that, them attempting to remake the magic that was one of the greatest horror games of all time doesn't fill me with confidence.There's clearly a lot of aesthetic talent at Bloober Team, but they're missing a unified vision in their work that both understands and surpasses the genres they're working in.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played  back in 2016, when the demo was still available. Right away it was able to give me an atmosphere that I hardly found in other games of the same type. But we are here to talk about this "Remake" that in my opinion takes the value of the work to a different level than the original  initially was. Let's start in order and give some context to this new version of . In this fantastic package we find 1 side story, 2 main stories and 2 shorter stories related to "" the first major chapter of the saga. The second story, however, clearly refers to the second chapter of the franchise.All the stories in the game are combined into one side story, which is precisely that of the writer. I don't want to give any spoilers about this content exclusive to this edition. I will just say that the stories told in the video game come from the pen of this woman whom we will impersonate in some phases of the game.There is little to say; it is the  par excellence. In this edition it has become more massive with unique content and some interesting new mechanics. Connected to this chapter are the stories "Inheritance" and "The Musician" which give more insights to a story already greatly expanded by this edition.When  came out, I did not like it. It seemed too different from what I had now appreciated about the first . I abandoned it upon release without finishing it. It's probably also age but replaying it in this new edition I had to reconsider. A really well told story that reaches truly remarkable narrative peaks. If in  I had been afraid in  I felt anguish and felt heavily trapped. In conclusion  is a fine video game. Also worked with some precision and attention to detail. Creating such a product is not easy especially in the area of Horror where it is easy to fall into the mundane. In any case, it is not a game to be played in a hurry.  has its own pace and may not appeal to an audience accustomed to a more massive type of action. _childDocuments_.review: Did I like Layers of Fear?....Yes, but it's complicated.When it comes to horror games, it takes a bit to scare me outside of the occasional startle and jump. And Layers of Fear, while it had it's creepy moments, didn't leave me feeling afraid.What I like the most about horror games is exploring locales in a relatively spooky atmosphere, and that is what Layers of Fear does deliver in a competent way. The locations are interesting, the environments are very detailed-- presentation is basically the strongest point of this game. Given the well done realism and environments that can really pull you in, it's lovely. I can imagine how well this whole game would translate to VR-- given it's already been done with the original release of Layers of Fear.But-- that's about the most I can say about Layers of Fear. It's got great atmosphere and interesting places to explore. I don't really think that it really passes in a 'gameplay' sort of way. Walking Simulator aside, Layers of Fear's interactivity is rather limited compared to what the more modern releases in this type of horror genre would be like. It's a very... claustrophobic game, which, in a sense, is also good at making the player uncomfortable.The game itself also has some 'creases' at the seams, notably with a few nitpicky details. - Voice overs aren't consistent. Sometimes it reads the whole document, sometimes it only reads a portion of the document. Sometimes words that are censored out are skipped over, censored out with a garble-ish sound, or just replaced with a common 'they' or 'this date'. There is no golden standard that they all follow, so it's a bit jarring.- Minor spelling errors for subtitles. I can't recall what the word was exactly, but I do remember an english word being typo'd in a level select transition for the Actor section.-  Several times I've had to reload the latest save. Such as-- getting dropped out of the map on the Painter's story when I tried to double back into a room I came in from, leaving me falling into an abyss. Or how a sudden scripted shove clipped me into a table in the Painter's story. There is another example I can think of, but I can't go into detail without being somewhat spoilery.Layers of Fear is not without it's flaws, and I don't really know if I can easily recommend this to most users that are looking into the horror genre for the first time. I do think those who have an interest in exploitative games could find some enjoyment out of it, and with how much content is buried into this game, I'd imagine they'd be able to spend a couple nights with it and have an alright time.I'm left a bit indecisive on how I should rule my recommendation because of some of the factors I've laid out, but I'll let it pass due to I myself enjoyed the game enough to see it through to the end.

The Musicians Story was the one with the most glitches (soft locks), misplaced door, doors that lead into the void (i.e falling into an inescapable area) almost all of this happened in the library section which also plagued me with confusion on where to go and why certain places that were irrelevant weren't locked off like others were. _childDocuments_.review: Kind of liked it for a bit. But after having played it for about 6 hours I've reached a point where the game is getting very sluggish. It's more confusing than scary.The game lacks consistency. At first it was cool that the rooms and hallways were ever-changing. But after a while you realize you have no idea where anything is. Ever. If you enter a room there's a 90% chance the room you came from will disappear and turn into something else. So there's an inherent lack of stability to the environments.Now that wouldn't be a problem if the story being told was a bit clearer. But mostly it's just odd and confusing. You kind of get that there's a red line being followed throughout. But the bread-crumbs being served are incredibly symbolic to the point of seeming like nonsense.That's not to say it's all nonsense. Some of the written notes work pretty well and are decently voice-acted. The problem with those is that the progression is very, very slow. You'll be reading notes about the same thing over and over again, slightly rephrased and in different contexts. I don't need 20 notes telling me the same thing spread out over the course of 1 hour of gameplay.With some decent puzzles this might be remedied. But the puzzles are mundane at best. And sometimes it feels like the game just gives up on the puzzles and dissolves into just pushing buttons, walking and reading notes while weird stuff is triggered around you.With a better paced story, some more familiarity in the environments and better puzzles this could be a great game. Alas it isn't and I can't recommend it for the graphics and audio alone.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I absolutely love this.I have played the previous 2 in the series, and this remake does them justice.So far it feels like you kept all the best old bits, but didn't do a copy/paste.There's a bit in chapter 1 (LoF 1) that gets me every time, and I marvel you can make me jump out of my skin with such an innocuous thing.I had completed LoF 1 (Original) the night before this launch, and I was fully expecting it to happen again, then I was slowly gettingmore and more sure you might have removed it. Just about the time I was going to be sad about it, it happened and I jumped out of my skin!It's clear you folks care about the product; It shows in the work. I do agree with other reviewers that some of the voiceover work feels a bit hammy, but I believe narration can be turned off in the settings (haven't confirmed prior to posting this). The sound design is amazing though, and there are definite improvements (like the child's laughter).Once of the things I loved about the original game is a lot of the story-line can be more open to interpretation. With this new release, there is a little more backstory. I am not sure yet if I like this better or not. So far, it seems like the difference between: "For Sale: Baby shoes, never worn" and "For Sale: Baby shoes, never worn, because the baby died in the crib". The previous is far more dreadful (in my opinion) because it's an impression of a story...you get a glimpse of content and your mind rushes to fill in the blanks. Although, that being said, I do like the way you went about this; drafting a third storyline to incorporate the previous two.This game also feels a little more streamlined. There are far less empty cabinets to open, and it is far simpler to find everything. I am not sure if I like this or not either. There's times where I feel like I love it, and times where I miss the slower pace of discovery.There is one thing I definitely do not care for, and that is the chases and echoes. It's a bit tedious to be honest. It feels like it came from a different game.In terms of technical issues, I have not noticed any so far. The game runs smoothly for me on a 4 year old PC with graphics maxed.This game should appeal to newcomers and LoF veterans alike, and the price-point is perfect.It was also very kind of you to discount for owners of the previous games.Keep up the great work!

However, this game falls short on a few things listed below.1) There are glitches that you can see empty blue spaces.  The game crashed once on me when I opened a door and the hand wouldn't let go.2) This is by far the one thing that makes me so irritated about this game.  The script readings. It really sounds like you just got a couple of college interns to read scripts and said, "uhh.... try reading it with an accent."  "How about you read this as a pertinacious older man".  The first had 2 really good voice actors.  The DLC did a wonderful and believable job with it's voice acting.  Then you stepped it up and was like... GET TONY TODD!  Then it was like, these children don't care it's all about the graphics, just bring some friends in and have them read these lines. _childDocuments_.review: Speaking as a fan of the first two games, I thought this game was great! It does an amazing job in reworking the previous two games into one overarching narrative in a very novel and unique way. Bloober team seems to be very polarizing, and their style of "walking simulator" games are very hit or miss for many people. For me, I enjoy the immersive and story driven style of their games, and if you liked the previous two games, or any of their games in general, then I highly recommend this title. Having played the other games, I knew roughly what I was getting into, but I still found the story very intriguing, and the framing narrative with the writer was very well executed, and tied the sections together very nicely.   Graphically speaking, the game speaks for its self. It looks absolutely stunning in UE5, even without having nanite implementation, and the art direction is some of the best I have ever seen, as to be expected from Bloober team and this franchise as a whole. I will say that the best looking parts of the game are the painters story and the respective dlcs, as the actors story seems to be directly ported from UE4, just with the new lighting system that UE5 offers (lumen). It still looks great, just less so than the other parts of the game in my opinion. My only real issue with this game personally is I feel the voice acting at times has room for improvement. I would not say it is bad, but it can be tad unconvincing at times, most notably with the writer's voice actor. As far as the horror factor of this game, while it is not the scariest game I have ever played, it has fantastic atmosphere, and enough scares and intense sequences to keep you never knowing what to expect from you surroundings. as far as gameplay goes, it follows suit with the other games for the most part, however there is a very cool combat mechanic involving a lantern and later a flashlight in the other stories that I thought was very well done and implemented. It is very similar to the combat mechanic in the Blair Witch game, although I found this one far better executed than the Blair witch. Overall I would breakdown my ratings as follows. Story: 9/10Graphics: 9/10 overall (10/10 for the painters story)Horror: 7/10Gameplay: 8/10Overall score: 8.5/10I highly recommend this title if you are a fan of the other games or enjoy this style of horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't completed the game yet, but as someone who has played the original games I think I can already comment that this is easily worth it, especially if you own any of the original games for the incredibly generous 45% off offer. Simply put: Unreal Engine 5 is a beast. This game runs like a dream on mid-range hardware, and Lumen is an absolutely transformative technology here. So much of Layers of Fear is just about walking through spooky, atmospheric environs and visuals changing around you, and having best-in-class lighting sweetens makes it all work so much better. In a time when it feels like new games barely turn on, this is a win.Unfortunately, I had to use Flawless Widescreen for Ultrawide, but there is very little cost to doing so as it has worked *almost* flawlessly. Some artwork here is better than other stuff (the character model is disappointingly bland compared to the otherwise stellar technology supporting it). And, if you hated Layers of Fear -- this game won't change your mind on any of that. They have added an entirely new campaign of sorts that binds the stories from LoF 1 and 2 together. So far it's neat, and helps the value of the package even more, but I can't comment much further than that right now. I'll update this review if things change for me.

Layers of Fears is a first-person psychedelic horror chronicle focused on tense exploration and immersive storytelling - a new game built upon the foundations of Layers of Fear, LOF: Inheritance, and Layers of Fear 2 with a surprising new story and gameplay direction.

Created with the cutting-edge Unreal Engine 5 technology, the game will support Ray Tracing, HDR effect, 4K resolution, and make use of the Lumen system to offer the most immersive and visceral horror experience.

name: The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners - Chapter 2: Retribution
detailed_description: Continue Your Undead Tour Your tour through undead New Orleans continues in this new chapter to the Tourist’s story in The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners. Hunted by the seemingly unstoppable Axeman and facing off against the Tower’s latest push for total dominance, discover what connects these new threats together before it’s too late. New faces, places, weapons and gear all await you on your journey to a final showdown for the city's fate. Do you have what it takes to survive it all? All the great features you loved in the original The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners journey return here, refined and better than ever. Face off against countless walking dead with visceral physics based combat only possible in VR with an ever expanding collection of weapons, improvised or otherwise. Take on missions from different characters and factions all across NOLA, gaining resources and loot along the way. Survive your way and choose how you want to handle each new deadly encounter. Be a master of melee, an expert gunslinger, a stealthy shadow, and so much more. Be a Saint or Sinner. Choose to help or hinder who you like and define who you want your Tourist to be to the people of the city. Beware The Axeman Battle against a terrifying new foe more deadly than any walker or desperate survivor. Determined to chop you to bits, you'll need to fight with all you got or run for your life when this towering pursuer comes for you. Will you be able to solve the mystery of who this post-apocalyptic serial slasher is and put a stop to their reign of terror, or will you be just another victim on the chopping block? New Orleans Extended The city of New Orleans has much more for you to explore, both day and night! Find new locales and meet new locals throughout the New Orleans French Quarter, with all the loot, quests, and all the walkers you could hope to slay! Then when your morning journey is complete, prove your survival skills by jumping back on your skiff and exploring the city during the night! More loot, more undead, and more opportunities for adventure on every single map. Help (or Hinder) the Exiles Meet an all new faction of survivors in New Orleans. Rejected by the Tower and refusing to join the brutal Reclaimed, these men and women caught in the middle of the chaos can offer you incredible rewards if you take on their daunting tasks and help them establish their claim in this deadly place. Or you could find a way to take their resources by force, if the path of the Sinner is more appealing to you.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Saints & Sinners game was one of the most impactful VR releases back in 2020 and stands as a true classic now, at least in my book. Unfortunately, the sequel does not take it to the new level neither for VR gaming as a whole nor for the series itself.In fact, despite being sold as a separate game, technically Retribution is more like a DLC or an expansion pack. In essence, it is the same game with a different campaign + 3 new locations, a night mode and some new weapons and enemies. You can even import your save game from the original and get all of your inventory and materials. At the same time Retribution is pretty buggy: it is eight months after the release now, and - minor nuisances aside - there still are major blocker bugs in the game. I had to replay one of the final (and longer) missions because the closing dialog failed to start during the first run. This is, of course, frustrating. Also, the AI of the human enemies is almost non-existent at times. You can headshot the tower soldier and his buddy, who stands right next to him, just does not react at all. More like a shooting range than an action game, if you ask me.Despite all that, I am still giving Retribution a positive review. Thing is, if you loved the original, you are very likely to enjoy this one too. For starters, the core gameplay is still there and dispatching hordes of walkers still feels immensely satisfying and almost visceral, especially with some of the new weapons (sap gloves are my favorite but all the others are very good too). The new locations are done in much more detail than the original ones. They just feel bigger and much funnier to explore. The design of the missions is better than in the original game, largely due to the introduction of the night mode with the proper stealth component. And finally, it's a full-fledged game that took me 20 hours to complete the main story (could have been less if not for the bugs).Personally, I have enjoyed my experience with Retribution. It might not be better than the original, but it still delivers the proper Saints & Sinners gameplay in large quantities.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I'm loving it.I was really scared when I saw the first negative reviews flood in and I questioned my choice of purchasing the game immediately on release. True, when I launched it for the first time, it stuttered so hard I had to stop playing after five minutes.I wondered if perhaps I should refund the game. I'm a big big fan of the first one, and I was scared this one would be a letdown. Turns out, when you only play for ten minutes, you can't give a serious and well thought-out review (just like most of the ones I'm seeing here, being overly critical and disrespectful of the devs' work).So I took the time to play it again. I tweaked the settings, and simply changing the shadow quality to Medium and keeping the rest on Ultra made a big difference. I can play just like I played the first one now.Moving on to the actual game, of course, some bugs remain (some of them are actually hilarious, like doors doing a 360 through the wall). However, I know what Skydance Interactive can do, and they will not let us down. They patch stuff, they listen to bug reports, and they actually care about their product and their audience. Saying they don't is just blatantly disrespectful for their hard work to bring one of the only good, full-fledged VR games to our headsets.The story so far has kept me interested. The addition of new characters make the world feel livelier and gives the quests a better sense of purpose than the ones in the first chapter (which were already really good), and I really feel like I'm the Tourist. So far so good.I love the fact that it's an expansion of the first game. The new home base is crazy good, the new maps are a fine addition to the initial ones, and the story just evolves and doesn't keep up that old "good vs bad" cliché.Keeping my first save also feels kind of nostalgic since I haven't played in a while. I loved being able to move all my junk from the bus to my (now) neat storage shelves. I feel like I'm gonna have fun just organizing stuff and making a whole armory.Overall, despite the bugs and whatever people may say, keep in mind there's hardworking people behind this who are working to make it a more polished experience. I love this game, it's not perfect (might be soon), but it's a great sequel to an already great first chapter.

_childDocuments_.review: is well as its name suggests, is a direct sequel to Chapter 1 of Saints & Sinners. It picks up where you left off and continues the story while expanding upon the game in various ways.- Direct continuation of the story that is not bad- Dialogue system with choices are still apparent- The vibe of The Walking Dead is still there- The ability to import a save file from Chapter 1, meaning you get to keep all your items, resources and recipes from Chapter 1- Being able to scavenge both during the day and during the night- New maps that are fun to explore and look visually pleasing- New weapons, upgrades, attachements and so on.- Combat is still as great as it was- The character of Gerik was really damn good, he had great voice acting and was a menace.- Steam Achievements- The voice acting is sometimes really great, when at other times quite meh- The game lets you go out scavenging during the night, however if you are doing exile orders for example and want to sleep until nights, you'd had to sleep twice every single time you go back to your resting place. An option to sleep until night would have been a tremendous QoL feature- NPCs repeat the same voice lines over and over in the span of 5 minutes- Human enemies still drop broken weapons 90% of the time- The chainsaw was a letdown, though not that horrible- Launching the game in SteamVR causes the game to not recognize the correct VR inputs, I played on Quest 2 and the easiest workaround was to not launch the game within SteamVR but to use either Quest Link/Air Link.  - Had many bugs during my playthrough- Exile Orders are a hassle to complete, essentially fetch quests that are only available during the night and you have to put all the items in the lockers during one scavenge run otherwise its progress resets- Weapon durabilities are still quite low- Managing your inventory- The Checkpoint system is extremely flawed, especially towards the end- NPCs are as dumb as a rock with the peripheral vision of a fish Even though the game expanded upon the game in quite many ways it also felt like two steps back and one step forward. However, I still find the game really enjoyable and hopefully we may get a Chapter 3 as well in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge regression for the game, this "sequel" has clearly compromised the product for Facebook's VR hardware.Looks FAR worse in many ways (the blood in particular is laughably simple compared to the previous game) and yet runs terribly. Even on the lowest settings this runs far worse than Chapter 1 - perhaps an earlier iteration of the engine was used for this game's home hardware (Quest), or maybe it's CPU usage is more reliant on a single core. Regardless, refunded. Huge shame, loved the first game. I fear VR's having a hard time thanks to Facebook and Sony splitting up libraries for exclusivity deals - and instead of making PVCR games then scaling them down for consoles, we're instead getting garbage like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game only under certain circumstances. As a full priced game, it isn't really worth it. The game is more suited as a DLC. As a DLC it would be fantastic but it's a full priced game. I'd suggest getting this when it's on sale then it's worth it. The reason I say this is because despite being a separate game, it doesn't really change enough to justify being called a separate game. Same map, 3 extra locations, only 1 of them is actually interesting that being the tower. You got a whole bunch of new weapons which is nice and of course a new story. Main issue with the story is that your decisions from the first game? Yeah forget about it, they don't matter. I'd say the only good part of the story in this game is the Axeman and the Tower conclusion those moments were fantastic. The ending of the game was pretty interesting, left with another moral choice but it creates a pretty solid conclusion to the story. I can't really see where they can expand from here however. I don't think it's a bad game, it just feels like an incredible DLC but a disappointing full priced game. No hate against the developers. I would love to see more projects from them in the future, although with the way the story ends in this game I don't really think they can expand on this project further. Some additional points:For whatever reason when you make your way back to the reserve via the church you experience the most god awful lag spike I've ever experienced in a VR game. It's horrific and it lasts for quite a bit, however. This is the only occasion in which it happens and if you take the shortcut to the reserve it doesn't happen. Zombie spawning mechanics are god awful. You will kill some zombies, walk forward, turn around and zombies will be there. It really takes you out of the whole killing zombie things, I know the world can't be devoid of zombies but at least make them spawn naturally and not right behind you. Not a negative point, actually a good one. This game is quite a bit harder than the first. Not only for battles but for resources. I found myself struggling with resources and battles despite having gathered an huge amount in the first game. It's quite a challenge but that's part of the fun. _childDocuments_.review: Quick Review: Have you played the first game?Go play the first game [again].I pre-ordered this game back in March 2023 and it was so broken and buggy I thought “ok lets give them time to fix it”, that was almost a year ago and I don’t know what they’ve been doing.I have just completed it and outside of some of the things carried over from the first game, it is without a doubt one of the worst VR games I have played.Gone are many of the things that made the first game great, the tension of walking around trying to loot surrounded by zombies, replaced by infinite spawning zombies (some spawn right on top of you). Forced firefights against also infinitely spawning troops when you have limited resources and weapons that break. At first I enjoyed the night missions (carried over from the fantastic free DLC of the first game), but its just so buggy that many times as soon as you load into a map, all of the zombies on the map will just run at you, and at other times you will be able to sneak around without them noticing you at all.There are so many bugs and problems, invisible objects that cast shadows, weird shadows that won’t go away, missing textures, whole areas of the map not spawning, are just a few of the worse ones.Try to aim a rifle when it’s jerking all over the place when you are fully still, no wonder they added laser sights! Chainsaws… A weapon that spawns zombies all around you! The grenade launcher is very hard to aim and due to the smoke trails you cant even see where you hit, at times I fired it and nothing happened. I once had a uzi bug out and go tiny so it fit inside the palm of my hand, I could still fire it but had no way to aim.I swear all of the other interactions are way worse too, like accidentally pulling the backpack through my body when I was going for my waist item, pulling out whatever item when trying to loot or climb, the latter sometimes resulting in death or severe damage, not being able to interact with things. I wish they had options for the active area size and position of the item interactions as they seem so buggy now.Many missions are very badly made, buggy and often poorly described and implemented, “go and do a thing at a place”, googling is the last thing you want to be doing when you are trying to immerse yourself in VR. Item spawns also seem bugged out and common items will not spawn in the normal places anymore, if at all.The story is barely anything, just some minor disputes and then one big battle that ends in a let-down, there is one awful boss battle that is a crafting battle, yep you craft to defeat a boss.I have no idea what they were thinking, other than cashing in on one of the best VR games ever made. It would be meme worthy but its so bad nobody is even writing game guides for it, literally throw away trash.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about what I expect to be halfway through, maybe 33% of the way through. So far, it's a pretty good sequel. I have been waiting for this game ever since they announced it. I loved the first game so much and 100%'d it. I even did several playthroughs doing different play styles, such as a "genocide" route where I would murder everyone on sight, without interacting most of the time. The first game was so good and is likely my favorite VR game. This game, however, doesn't live up to the first game. This game still has a recommend from me because I love the physics and the style, but for anyone who is not as lenient as me, which is probably the general populus, you may not find this game as acceptable. For one, they kept pushing back the release date. First it was December, then February, then it released late March. With almost 4 months of waiting from the initial release, it had a lot of high hopes from me. Some of the problems I had with this game is that it's so buggy. Now i have a 3070, with my Valve Index, and i ran many games just fine. Blade and Sorcery, Pavlov VR, Bonelab, Half Life Alyx, and even the first game of Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners with NO problem. But for some reason this game has horrid lag spikes. Not only that but whenever i try to grab an item that's in front of me, such as the flashlight or the journal, it will auto grab my holstered weapons. It's very frustrating when I try to rush to grab my flashlight to see whats ahead of me down the stairs, yet it keeps grabbing the machete that's in my left holster, whether this is a bug or not, it's very annoying. The NPCs that you can talk to in the game are very forgettable, and most of the time, are just fetch quests. Dialogue sounds all the same and none of the characters stand out. Something else that is also very annoying, is the fact that all of them, no matter who, talk at such shambling speeds. Half the time while interacting with these characters, I want to shoot them out of frustration, but have to hold back since I want to 100% this gameWith so many negatives, It might seem dissuading to buy this game, which is why i should mention some of the positives. Now with these positives i'm going to list, they're good, but they don't outweigh the negatives. Night time travel. YES finally. This was one of the things that I wanted in the first game, and even had a mod to allow that. It has more dangers such as traveling elite reclaimed/tower members that will shoot on sight, and WAY more walkers, but pays off by having almost twice as much loot that are very useful for crafting, new trading posts that I will talk about, and also infinite stay time. Meaning you never have to leave because of the bells. As I have mentioned, there are now exile trading posts. These posts are scattered across each map (except for a select special few) and have their own dedicated journal spot. They give you loot by giving them certain requested items. Sometimes the loot can be mediocre, like a few flares, while other times its a lot of ammo, weapons, and even bombs. Yes these trading posts are a fun new mechanic in the game and allow you to have something on the side of the game. You are able to import the save file from the first game, to the new game. Thank GOD you can do this as several hours, if not tens of hours can be saved by being able to port your completed save. They added new crafting recipes, items, and ingredients to the game, so having to collect over twice as many ingredients from scratch is a little daunting, and Isn't my style of gameplay. The 2 new crafting tables allow more armor upgrades such as stamina for sprinting, kevlar armor, and heavy armor. But more than that, they have brought in 2 new types of guns to the game, SMG's and Sawed off shotguns. No not the double barrel shotgun that is from the first game. A pocket version of the weapon is available for a cheap price. These 2 new weapons are such a blessing for the game because pistols jam way too often, and melee weapons require you to get close to the enemy. They also added a laser sight, brass knuckles-esque gloves, and a chainsaw. While notable, aren't as cool as the new guns added. The laser sight does conveniently solve a lot of my previous issues with aiming, but doesn't let you put it on any gun, instead it only allows it on the 9mm pistol. Which makes sense, but I was really hoping for some variety. if you have also bought the payback DLC for an extra 10 dollars, you will also be given "The Blessing", "Fat Tuesday", Demon Storage Shelf, and collectable post cards. "The Blessing" is just a reskinned 9mm pistol, making it gold instead of the muddy silver color. Although cool looking, adds nothing to the game. "Fat Tuesday" is a reskin of the sawed off shotgun. Again, adds nothing, and doesn't even look too good. The Demon Storage Shelf is... alright? I mean it adds a cool shelf for your angel and demon statues that are collectables, but... there are so many shelves to choose from that you really do not need this shelf. The post cards are cool, but thinking about how little the DLC added; reskins, another shelf, and collectables? For 10 dollars? Not quite worth it.TL;DR this game is a good sequel, but not a good game. It has the same physics type gameplay from the previous game that is pretty much carrying all the flaws in it. This game did JUST come out so I'm sure the bugs are sure to be changed and fixed (hopefully).

_childDocuments_.review: Big, Big yikes. I tried my best to love this game and it just wasn't happening.According to other reviews, the Devs are aware of the game breaking bugs (In my experience they have yet to be fixed. The game is almost a year old now, get it together devs.)The few things I want to leave in this review are about the gameplay, bugs, and just bad design.I love that they expanded upon the crafting system and added new things, however there are many things left to be desired. For one, Fists should be on your character by default as weapons with the gloves as an "Upgrade". You cannot do any damage with your fists unless you have gloves. The "worn" weapons after you craft them are a bit of a bad design IMO. If you put in the supplies to craft earlier weapons, they shouldn't be worn, they can be of lower quality than future crafts, sure. But making them on the verge of breaking was highly disappointing. I loved the addition of laser sights, but scopes would've been nice as well.The design of the game is quite awful, the graphics are good, however good graphics don't make a game. The story is a bit bland and the missions are repetitive. Nighttime missions, despite being something new to the game, are very bad. You can hardly see 3 feet in front of you, and there is no moonlight. The flashlight helps very little when it comes to pitch black night missions.The character designs are just silly. The first 3 "Allies" you meet (after the prologue) I could not take them seriously. You have a  random Furry, Miley Cirus, and Lara croft. The only good character design IMO was Gerik.The missions are repetitive, confusing, buggy, and more of a chore than something fun to do. The game doesn't tell you at all what to do at many points and expects you to find everything on your own. I shouldn't have to use google to figure things out just to discover that a bug was making the mission impossible to complete. I waited a year to play this game as I was hoping the day one bugs would be fixed a year later. I wanted to see what would happen if I killed a "friendly" character in this game, their character model grew to an outlandish size and then the game crashed. Other bugs involve my character's arms being invisible, or sticking to everything. Grabbing items you don't reach for, or don't even have your hands near. Enemies have far too much health even on the easiest difficulty, and starting off this is a huge push back. The zombies don't die to headshots 80% of the time and when struck with a sword, it either bounces them back or "slaps" them.This game is like a pizza cooked by a man with no knowledge of cooking. The pizza is doughy, raw, and is missing toppings, including the cheese, and at the same time is somehow burnt. I hope the devs will fix the game and then possibly I'd change my review.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners - Chapter 2: Retribution is an amazing game. I've been playing for a little while, so here is what I'll say.Pros-Gorgeous game, looks very realistic while also having that comic style.-More walkers, makes situations overwhelming and immersive.-More weapons, all are fun to use such as the Bolted-Up gloves, Chainsaw, Vera Express, etc.-New locations. Personally, Bourbon Street is my favorite. Even if they are not as large as expected, they feel like they could go on forever and are huge.-Exile missions, footholds, and so on. Give more content to do aside from the story and scavenging.Basically, Chapter 2 has either improved most of the things in the first game or added new things,Now, onto the cons,Cons-Blood effects are not as good as the original. For some reason, it is a bright red. Unsure if this is a bug or it is an intended feature.-Depending on your system and settings, the game may not perform well. Examples can be low FPS. In my case, I use a Valve Index and the game runs well for me because of my system. I have not ran into issues so far.-Bugs. There are not a lot, but there definitely are some. For instance, one of Sable's soldiers ( Echo I think ) had his head turning at an unusual angle. In another part, he was like violently shaking or something while doing a sitting animation on a table. Another bug is when shooting a walker's head, it's head will be gone but the hair will still be there. All of these bugs are not game breaking, some can even be considered sort of funny. But these are things that should be fixed.Conclusion : When I was going into this game, I saw all of these negative reviews. I was skeptical, but gave it a chance. And I do not regret it at all. The game is visually appealing and stunning. Combat is fun. This is arguably better than the original if all of the current issues were fixed. I look forward to playing way more of this game. I would definitely recommend this game if you think you could run it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to get this out of the way for anyone checking back after the piss-poor launch:No, the game is not bug-free. Would I recommend it still? Yes.The Bad:I get the feeling QA either didn't happen or there wasn't enough of it. You will come across scenarios where you're left scratching your head wondering what to do. At best, these is a bit of a time-waste until you figure it out. At worse, you lose progress up until your last save (usually the last time you slept or traveled). There's also a myriad of random glitches and poor design choices, and the rare crash (I crashed at the 21 hour mark for the first time). The Good:When the game works, it's a genuine blast (and/or scare). The art style is beautiful and the game has some genuine charm when it tries. Combat is serviceable and satisfying, and while some weapons are obviously stronger than others (looking at you Nova), you can just as easily get away with using whatever tickles your fancy. The story is nothing to write home about (save for a few golden occasions) but it serves well on your first play-through, assuming you engage with it.The Worst (Spoilers): This next part deals with the story so if what I said so far sounds like a good time to you, just skip this and go play. You've been warned. To put it bluntly, your choices have very little impact on the story. The only changes are what quests you get to do, and if a certain character appears at the end. The only real choice you get is at the end which determines your ending. When you go through it for the first time you obviously don't notice this, but on a new run it is glaring. Not a deal breaker for me personally, but if you're looking for a meaningful story with impactful choices beyond "Good, Mean, Sarcastic" then this isn't it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of problems with this one, but the core of the game is good enough that I will recommend it, if (and only if) you have played and enjoyed the first game and if you can stomach some pretty dire bugs.The sequel to Skydance's rather popular zombie survival shooter picks up where the first game ended. You can even import a save to keep your progress and belongings. This at time feels more like an expansion than a new game as it is basically the first game with three new ares, some new weapons and a new campaign added on. But since the additions, including the new night scavenging mode, are pretty solid, it is still a good deal for fans of the franchise.The campaign takes about 14-15 hours to complete, so you can expect a similar amount of content as Saints & Sinners including the Aftershock DLC. Performance was solid for me (100-120 FPS on a RTX 2070 Super), at least after the first Hotfix. The patch unfortunately did not address other rather glaring issues. From graphical glitches and borked animations to crashes and invisible zombies, the state of the game is pretty rough. If you are looking for a smoother experience, it might be better to wait until a few patches have rolled out.All problems aside, Retribution is still a very solid experience with great feeling combat, good visuals, a satisfying gameplay loop and outstanding voice acting.
