_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that chapter 1 was a great game and I highly recommend that one. In short though, I highly recommend skipping chapter 2. I waited a while to get this because of all the gamebreaking bugs I saw being reported. Saw it on sale so decided to finally try it. It was impossible to get it working with my Oculus quest 3 to start, and I had to resort to custom bindings to get it working. Even then, I couldn't sprint, and my game had crashed. Experience wasn't better with the link or air link. I decided to refund it here and get it from the oculus store as it was made for that first, and is probably more polished.What I experienced was even worse than the steam VR version. The game's 2 initial loading logos were glitching into each other and after 3 mins of loading, it just crashed to my home screen. Tried it again. Same thing. The third attempt it finally loaded and I got into the game. So far, so good. smooth frames etc. The very first sequence begins and the guy talking to me as well as the first zombie were not fully rendering. their faces looked like rotten potato. One eye visible the other just a lump, lips paper thin and pursed idk what I was looking at. I get through that sequence and into the next little cutscene area. It is a small room with just me and 2 other NPCs. One of them had the rotten potato face too. I waited to see if it would ever load, and it never did.I ended up refunding that version as well because the game just lacks polish at every turn it seems. I felt at that point, it wasn't worth playing long enough to lose the ability to refund because from others reviews, there aren't many new maps and the story isn't the best either. It's a very unfortunate sequel to one of my favorite VR titles.UPDATE 6/7/24: just for the people that are curious, there have been 0 updates since my initial review, with the last official update being just over a year ago. There seems to be 0 intention to actually address the issues experienced. The devs responded to this on November 24th stating they have updates planned, but at 7 months from that message, with the first walking dead receiving graphical updates and this still being quiet, I just don't believe it's coming anymore

_childDocuments_.review: As a VR player who's more seasoned, I can't rate this game much good. Lacks customizing options for holsters, controls, etc. Guns/blades in holsters are easily lost because there is such a large spot to grab them, I'm often grabbing my weapon instead of what I want. Stamina system is almost completely unrealistic on anything besides story mode. It's like you're a fat man or couch potato with zero cardio training. Weapon durability, to get into a real fight you literally have to carry several copies of one gun into a fight, one weapon not even reliable enough to clear through the tower, even if you craft it yourself and it's brand new. Movement speed is painfully slow. Makes you want to sprint everywhere, and the stamina makes that near impossible. Everything you grab has "weight" but to a very unrealistic manner. I understand two handed melee weapons not working great but when I go to reload a shotgun it wobbles everywhere like a bobblehead. Realistically, I can hold a shotgun with one hand and keep it still at least. Not to mention tons attention to detail errors when it comes to the realism and accuracy of representation of firearms and other weapons and gear. Overall, it's a good concept game but they didn't give it the attention to detail it deserves. It doesn't have smooth play, and am often frustrated because these little things add up to a major downfall.

_childDocuments_.review: With ever increasing frequency, PC gaming is summed up by the simple logic of YMMV when it comes to the performance of pretty much any game these days (especially the ports).  As someone who was initially spooked by the Questification of this game, I wanted to do my part to spread the gospel that this game completely kicks ass and is a decided improvement on Chapter 1.   As others have said, it's more of a pricey DLC than a proper sequel but when it comes to getting another couple dozen hours with one of my favorite VR games, a direct continuation of Chapter 1 is my personal preference.  They doubled the # of crafting tables, expanded The Resting Place to the degree where now there's a slice of prime real estate to live in as compared to Chapter 1's "mattress stuffed into the back of a bus" approach.  I generally dislike crafting in games and S&S remains the only series that has ever made it genuinely tolerable.   Performance was a generally even 120 fps for me with a 3080 + 5850X3D.  A handful of 60 fps dips but none of the nasty stutters that some others have reported.  Graphics do not look Quest-y to me and imo look unchanged from Chapter 1 but to be fair, the art style of the game has always been a bit Questified in the first place.  Sometimes that's unfortunate but it doesn't bother me at all with this series.  Chapter 2 looks no better or worse than Chapter 1, just more of the same and I have no problem with that.  Being able to use my compiled resources from Chapter 1's 25 hour save was a really nice touch and it was slick to walk back into the bus and see my wall of weapons from the last time I played the first game.   Starting the upgrade tables at Ch 5 really helped out too.  If you loved chapter 1 then you'll love chapter 2, especially if your PC doesn't get the stuttering plague that mine thankfully avoided and will hopefully be fixed for all soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is a decent extension of the first Saints and Sinners game, although it does have some major areas for improvement. I'm recommending it, but barely. This game is fun to play, it's not entirely a bad experience, especially if you've already played the first. Get ready for an incoming essay lol, I have a lot of thoughts on this game, especially after 100%ing it!First off, the story isn't as polished or thorough as the story in the first game. If you look at this game as a standalone title, the story becomes even less impressive. Your choices within the story seem to have little to no impact - I wasn't expecting a Telltale level of variation, but the first game would have different factions on your side in the "finale" based on your in-game choices. There are many choices that the Tourist can make throughout the story that *seem* like they're going to be defining moments where the story might be changed. But those choices really don't matter, and don't change the outcome much at all. Especially the side plot of trading with the Exiles - doing those missions gets you some loot, which is cool, but nobody later in the story acknowledges the Tourist's influence.     (SPOILERS IN THE NEXT PARAGRAPH) For example, in the finale mission where the Tourist assaults the tower, the exiles and Father Carter *do* join the Tourist, provided that they aren't dead. Whistles, too. But Carter does nothing other than say a few lines - He doesn't react to the Tourist at all. Given that the last encounter with him before this could either end in him cursing the Tourist and calling them a demon, or thanking the Tourist for their help, to me it doesn't really seem fitting that he has zero reaction to the Tourist. He just stares at the Tourist like a dead fish, lol. Also, if Whistles is alive, she repeats the SAME one or two lines OVER AND OVER again in that section, which proved to get very annoying if I stayed in the area for more than thirty seconds. These are nitpicky, but they're small examples of the overarching bigger issue with this game - Characters within the game don't feel *real*, they don't react to in-game events unless it's absolutely required to move the main plot forward. It would've been awesome if the Exiles in the fight carried certain weapons or items gained from the trading network, if the Tourist does the trading network missions. Or maybe if Father Carter acknowledged the Tourist before the battle and gave some encouraging parting words. Or if the Pawn King and Des could be found in the tower if Des spares her father, since they were both blackmailed into joining The Tower. *Something* for people to acknowledge what the Tourist has done leading up to the finale in-game.Another issue in this game is the, uh... How do I say this... The fact that the game is pretty clearly unfinished? It's strange, in my experience with the original game, I had very few bugs or glitches. But this game is FULL of them, especially on the Quest version. Even within the PC version I'd regularly see entire floor textures vanish or move, making it look like the Tourist had gained the ability to fly, lol. Character's heads regularly spun on their necks, making them look possessed. Over the course of three full playthroughs, my game (PC version) crashed a total of eight times. Looking online, it's pretty clear that others have also experienced these bugs/graphic issues/glitches. They can be funny, but take you out of the immersion of the game, which kind of sucks if you're really into it and your adrenaline is pumping in a tense situation.This one is going to be one of my BIGGEST issues with this game. What I'm going to talk about next does have a lot of spoilers, but it's a crime that needs to be discussed. The Axeman. In the trailers/promo material for this game, he's set up to be this nemesis figure for the Tourist - I mean that in the literal sense of the word as well as a reference to Resident Evil 3's Nemesis. I read that the devs originally intended the Axeman to function like RE3's Nemesis, constantly encountering the Tourist and facing off in an intense game of cat-and-mouse. But in-game, he was reduced to this dude who just sometimes stands on rooftops and stares at the Tourist. He has no real impact on the Tourist - He leaves the bodies of dead tower soldiers around, but he doesn't really get in the Tourist's way, which is insane considering he thinks the Tourist destroyed his family and his #1 motive is killing them.      The boss fight with the Axeman is decent, it was honestly pretty fun. But a big issue is that you can "choose" his fate - Let him live, or kill him. Except making this choice does literally nothing in the story. There's no consequence to letting him live, there's no impact of killing him. The Axeman's story ends in a very meaningless way, imo. I also saw dev notes about cut content involving the Axeman - In addition to the way he was originally intended to function like Nemesis. Remember the scene in the trailers where he chases Father Carter into the speakeasy? Nope! Doesn't exist in-game! The Axeman pretty much never *actually* impacts the Tourist or characters that are meant to be close to them. Because of this, he's reduced to a non-threatening villain that doesn't have a whole lot of personal impact to the player or even the world around him. I think this is a huge shame, as the Axeman had *so* much potential. Potential to have an extremely meaningful story as well as an impact on the player's gameplay. But he didn't live up to that potential. On a more positive note, I do think that the new weapons added to the game are well-designed and satisfying to use. I'm not a personal fan of the hand grenades, but things like the chainsaw and elephant gun are SO fun! I also really appreciate how many references to other TWD content are sprinkled throughout the game - Item recipes you can find as well as physical in-game locations. It's very rewarding for long-term TWD fans to notice these little details.      (More spoilers ahead-) Also, the confrontation with Mama in the finale is well done. From a story perspective, anyways. Mama's perspective actually made me stop and think about the events of the story. I wondered - Could Mama be right? Could her crazy plot to bring walkers down NOLA actually be beneficial? I love that Mama is painted in a sympathetic light. In her eyes, betrayal after betrayal after betrayal led her to taking this course of action. While her mission is still completely immoral in my opinion, and the people who betrayed her had clear motives for doing so, the way her argument is structured really makes the player think. After that, it makes sense how she managed to convince the troops of The Tower to fall in line behind her. I also think her walking off of the Tower at the end shows just how much she really believes in what she's saying - Really hammering home just how far "off the edge" her past has driven her. Ha, get it? Edge? Okay, I'll stop now. In summary, Retribution has some good/entertaining elements. But its cut content and time constraints during development really hurt the end product. It's worth playing for the ending part of the story and the new weapons/mechanics, but the drawbacks of this game really hurt the overall player experience. The bugs, glitches, crashes, lack of meaningful story/impact from the Tourist's actions, as well as the Axeman's story really detract from what could have been an amazing product. The main takeaway I had after playing the game over and over again and seeing the cut content as well as the plans for this game was - "What could this game have been?" I had a lot of fun playing it, and I even liked the game a lot while I was experiencing it for the first time. But looking back, this game could have been so much more, and that's what detracts from it as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Saints and sinners 1 was a masterpiece, the only reason i bought a VR in the first place was to play that game specifically. I saw the reviews for this game and thought "Eh i'll give it a go" and while the gameplay, setting and story are just as good as the first instalment, the frustrating issues HEAVILY outweigh the positives.Specs:Quest 2GTX 3080Steam VR / Virtual DesktopPros:Gameplay - fluent like the first 10/10Story - pretty good so far (Only got 1 1/2 hours in due to issues below)Sounds - just as good as the first instalmentAll the pluses of the first game Cons:Controls - Horrendous, i've looked for 4 hours trying to get a control scheme, via the Devs approved control scheme, YouTube videos, forums etc, either you sacrifice the sprint (Which doubles the amount of time to get anywhere and makes the game quite boring when you're walking like you're elderly), or you don't move at all - which as of this review with the "Official" bindings selected, the left stick doesn't even move the player. (BTW if you've come to the reviews of the game to figure out the control scheme i'll help you out, it doesn't work, no one has a video, post or information where they can actually get the sprint to work like in the first game and you unfortunately just have to deal with it)Controls Pt 2 - This may seem small, however in the first game to pick up a gun from your holster, pick up items, weapons etc you had to hold the button to pick it up, immersing you a bit more since you felt like you were "Holding" the item. The only working control schemes i found and edited, it's a toggle button, so when aiming a gun at enemies you just press the button once and bam, you're continuously holding the gun, let go of the trigger, nothing happens, forget you're still holding the gun? fumble to put it away. Want to put the gun away after aiming and shooting, hover over your holster and press the button. It's a simple fix but in my opinion adds so much to the game actually feeling the weight of the gun, weapon, item and having to actually "Hold" it otherwise it's dropped - more realistic.Booting the game - As soon as you boot the game, you get a message along the lines of "Re calibrate controls" which shows a HTC Vive control scheme and if you don't have a Vive, you have to restart the game and hope it skips the "Re calibrate" - sometimes multiple times.Graphical - I noticed some minor graphical issues throughout my short playtime which i would stress is not a massive issue but considering the first game didn't have any (That i saw) i thought i'd mention it anyway.AI - The zombies perform just the same as the first game, no complaints there. However, my first encounter with the "Human" AI, they spotted me through a wall and started shouting at me, I thought "Okay maybe i made noise or something", decided to sneak to where they were and they were both looking in a random location, so i shot one in the head with a shotgun, looked at the second enemy and they had glitched walking about aiming a gun (With the knife floating where the gun is as well) and i could walk up to her, get in her way and she just kept shouting "I'll get you tourist" without ever attacking me. I ABSOLUTELY loved the Saints and Sinners 1, managed to 100% it and never had any issues with it, if the Devs read this PLEASE fix these issues, i can get past the graphics every now and again and hell, even the AI glitching out but the fact that it took me over half of my "Playtime" just to calibrate the controls so i can TRY to play the game is ridiculous. If you are thinking about getting this game, at the moment i wouldn't just based on these issues within the first hour of gameplay. When / IF they fix these issues i will HAPPILY update my review to be positive and more than recommend this game as i'm sure many others will. There will probably be a 3rd instalment of Saints and Sinners at some point i'm sure and with the current state of this game i will definitely not be buying it but if there is a labour of love shown and issues are fixed i am more than happy to take that gamble.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit2: Alrighty, so after the dev comment below I made dot-points of my criticisms of the game so we can see which issues were actually fixed.1) Left-handed mode not shown in menu2) Nothing new besides chainsaw and 2 guns (smg and something else?)3) Barely any enemies in-game4) Downgraded graphics5) Very quick progression6) Litte content in general (feels like a DLC rather than a full game)7) Terrible AI8) Barely any new assets/props9) Performance issues10) Crashed once1) NOT SOLVED! Despite this being an ini option it is still completely absent from the in-game menus2) Didn't notice any new weapons, although I forgot to mention a fist-type weapon which I haven't tried yet. Chainsaw is incredibly buggy and awkward to use (made for a right-handed user)3) Seems this has to do with the missions because I played a story mission with over a dozen zombies in-screen in a couple areas (bell section), better than last game but there are still barely enemies around as a rule4) Seems to have been little change, nothing noticable anyway5) I was already maxed out when I started playing and am only at day 5, though probably would've been different if I hadn't imported a save (the new stuff from Chapter 2 requires all-new resources so I prioritized those instead of the typical things I would have prioritized in the first game).6) Point remains, though I haven't finished the story yet. Got to the section where there is a bell hooked up to a generator, currently at day 5 (doing one story mission a day).7) AI still seems ridiculously dumb8) Haven't noticed any new props/background items except for a stack of sandbags which zombies could walk through (i.e there is no clipping on them, the zombies literally phase through the sandbags). This particular instances was a barrier for the player which you have to climb over, but the zombies just walk straight through.9) Seems fixed! Played on everything ultra with only a slight stutter as missions loaded10) No crashes, though I'd only ever crashed once before anyway.Edit: The joystick switch (from comments) worked! Why is this setting not in the game menu??? I needed to go to the .ini just to be able to play left-handed? In any case, I've played a few more hours and while I am enjoying exploring new areas, and the story seems more creative/involved than the previous game, I gotta say there is not really anything new besides a couple guns and the chainsaw, at least from what I can tell. I fully upgraded both the new workbenches after only two missions! I appreciate they added night-only resources to encourage you to explore at night-time (which has more zombies and poor visibility) but I won't be needing to do it ever again sadly. There are a couple attachments you can put on your weapons which is nice but honestly it's something which should've been in the original game.Overall I'd agree with the sentiment this is a DLC priced as a full game and am quite disappointed. Also the AI is the same if not worse which is really poor considering it was already quite basic in the first game. Limited number of enemies on the map at a given time is also boring but I think there can be mods to fix this (haven't seen any online yet).Original review below:I nearly refrained from purchasing this game but I thought I'd give it a go since there is the 2-hour grace period to account for developers' incompetence. Anyway, I am giving this a thumbs down mainly because there is STILL no way to swap joystick movement to the right controller, so left-handed players are once again left in the dust despite the years of criticism of the lack of this simple feature. Nevertheless the game is a good sequel and seems to contain 100% of the content from the previous game (in terms of weapons, collectibles and locations, from what I can see). The graphics are thankfully about the same as the original which is a relief, although the assets all seem copy+pasted with practically nothing new aside from a few instruments (hopefully I am wrong on  any case, I didn't personally have any performance issues after I turned Shadows and Post Processing to Medium (before that I was stuttering pretty badly so I'm guessing this has to do with an Ultra setting somewhere, despite the fact the quality difference was not really discernable for me).Also, I crashed right as I completed the first mission objective. Basically you must put this disc into a radio, and there is a blue square to indicate where to put the disc. I had the disc in hand and the instant it touched the blue square, the game completely froze (music was still playing). Waited about 2 minutes and it was still frozen despite mashing all the buttons, tabbing out and in again (a pain in VR) and whatnot, so I closed it and came to write this review.I'm past the 2 hour mark so I suppose I will play some more eventually and return to update the review if my thoughts change.Here are my specs:Windows 1032GB DDR4 RAMGIGABYTE RTX 3070R7 5800xOculus Rift S

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty damn upset to be writing this, but Retribution just... sucks. [LIGHT SPOILERS FOR CH1 + 2]Some of the new content here like the new items, locations and night mode are great but there still just isn't enough here to really warrant a standalone sequel to begin with. They've also made some strange changes to the existing locations, altering some lighting to be a comparative downgrade to Chapter 1 and even making Via Carolla (my favourite location) a completely overrun death trap with no way of getting it back to normal! Another absurd addition in Chapter 2 are these new posters dotted around for other Skydance productions; including a Netflix show poster and a couple Apple TV movie posters, which is an insane break to the immersion and timeline of the game world, seeing that this takes places in the 2000s!!!The story felt like a mound of wasted potential, casts of characters are introduced and are either killed off abruptly or softly forgotten in the campaign with no significant development, no solid ties to one another and no satisfaction by the time you reach the end of their story arcs. The game also acts like nothing you did in Chapter 1 happened, besides the unveiling of The Reserve. Everything is recapped in vague terms in an infodump in your journal, essentially stripping the player choice aspect, which is kind of the epitome of the name "Saints & Sinners." Speaking of which, that aspect is dumbed down further in Chapter 2's story, with player choice being few and far between and only ever having an impact on the predictable good or bad ending choice in the finale, a disappointing opposite of the harrowing set of endings in Chapter 1, that never really left you feeling good for yourself at all.By the end you get the feeling that the developers had some very grand and ambitious plans for the story, but they were likely shot down by higherups in a time crunch to get the game out the door.Then worst of all, the visuals and performance have been substantially downgraded, likely due to the fact they zeroed in on a Quest version to cash in on the 2022 Holiday season. Then come March 2023, they still didn't put much care into the other versions (especially PC) despite a 4 month delay. All new locations have this stink of leftover Questification; where texture detail and foliage/environmental props are noticeably lessened in new areas like The Tower and the optimisation is also extremely shoddy.To make matters worse, the post launch support has been kinda bad. To their credit, Skydance has fixed up the game to a reasonable extent mainly to the tune of progression blockers, crashing and major bugs. But in the current version of the game, I am still unable to complete Exile trades in The Shallows, and a couple of the other achievements have remained broken since the last patch in May 2023. There is also content they could have easily asset flipped from CH1 into CH2 that would have enhanced the experience a bit, like bringing back The Trial from CH1's Meatgrinder update. It's literally a super fun and fully finished component rotting in the games prequel, and the loading screen in CH2 even has leftover tips related to The Trial! The disappointment compounds further in that there seems to be no sign of any upcoming content updates like what CH1 had.The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners is my favourite VR game of all time; and I'm disappointed beyond words with just how hard Skydance fumbled Chapter 2. Lazy, terrible and downgraded. I hope the Questie cash-in was worth it, guys.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent installment in the Saints and Sinners Story. However, some of the plot points that are brought up in the story are not explored to their fullest extent. Several characters' story lines seem like they are cut short, and lack real purpose in the overall story of the series. Some game mechanics, such as the pawn shop, could have been more polished and could have played a bigger role in the overall gameplay. The game has a good amount of post-story content, certainly more than the first game. Also, the visuals from the first game seem to be definitely improved, with excellent shadows and lighting, especially for a Virtual Reality game. The new map nodes provide some excellent exploration, but could have been larger, deeper, or more claustrophobic to amplify the thrill of the game. As for the new weapons, some are useful, many are fun, but a few are downright useless. Overall, this game is very strong in gameplay, but falls short in the story and some mechanics are bland and unfinished.Note: Game is completely playable on PCVR, some minor annoyances but overall is in good health as of now, devs seems to fix mistakes relatively quickly.---{ Graphics }---☑ Beautiful---{ Gameplay }---☑ Very good---{ Audio }---☑ Very good---{ Audience }---☑ Teens☑ Adults---{ PC Requirements }---☑ Fast---{ Difficulty }---☑ Easy to learn / Hard to master---{ Grind }---☑ Isn't necessary to progress---{ Story }---☑ Decent---{ Game Time }---☑ To infinity and beyond---{ Price }---☑ Worth the price---{ Bugs }---☑ The game itself is a big terrarium for bugs---{ ? / 10 }---☑ 7

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this a bit longer I have to revise my review to a negative. This has turned into essentially a wave-shooter. The gameplay is very poor, with enemies spawning incredibly close to you very quickly even after you have cleared an area fully. Do that, and then wait about ten seconds and you'll have a complete respawn of the horde you just fought. It's just a nonsense shooter that is very light on story. Unless I can find a mod that makes this about something other than the mindless mess it has become I won't bother. Better just to play the first one again. This title is a perfect example of why Steam needs a rating scale, even something as basic as a 1-10. It is also a sad example of how bad the state of gaming has become, because I'm rating it "Yes" because the devs didn't completely destroy this sequel. In other words, "not totally ruined" is now somehow good  enough. On a 1-10 this title is a 5. So, so sad. The bad: TWDSSC2R (that's a mouthful) runs somewhat worse than the original while also having downgraded graphics in some ways. There are a lot of extremely poor textures (doors, clutter, etc.) I'm running on a 4090 and have had to drop my refresh to 75 and reduce the SS a bit. The original runs at 90, 150% SS on Wide FOV on my Pimax 8K-X with no hitching aside from the occasional texture load. That's at Ultra quality with mild reductions to shadows, post-processing, and effects. Low AA. At the same settings this one will give me 75hz, 120% SS, and continually hitches on stick-rotation (this is some kind of a bug with certain UE4 VR titles; Wanderer also suffered badly from this - rotation will be totally smooth when done full-body or when looking around with the HMD, but rotate with the stick and stutter stutter stutter.) So they've made a title that both looks and runs worse. BUT, they didn't completely destroy it, so thumbs up. The entire world also seems to be less dynamic; few drawers open, most fridges are just empty with missing doors (so far, I've played about 3 hours), and that kind of thing. The gore is also absurdly bad looking compared to the original. (Devs: Did you even bother to look at what you were doing? Compare the two side-by-side? What in the world made you think what you built here was OK?) Somehow they also haven't fixed the horrible problems with the holsters, so this remains a terrifying "Oh my God where did my weapons go!?" simulator (hint, you ejected them from your holsters while trying to pick something up from the ground)! The good: It runs OK and isn't completely ruined. The general vibe is still there and it still runs well enough to look decent, albeit not as good as the original. It definitely appears to be worth a playthrough, although the devs would have been far better off making this a modular expansion to the original (DLC) rather than a new title, as that way it would have had all of the performance, features and graphics of the original rather than being downgraded in all of these regards.

_childDocuments_.review: The story in the game started really slow and the only reason I kept playing is because the first game was so thrilling and immersive and you can import your previous save. It feels like every time I'm in a deep story mission my game crashes and all my progress is gone. my PC handled the last game flawlessly but the sequel seems to have buffer moments or sudden frame drops. It would have been better if they waited and took an extra couple months to finish the game. (I didn't know they already delayed, how useful that was.) I feel like I constantly grab the wrong item because my pouch hit-boxes are so sensitive. when ever I'm climbing a ladder or hanging, 90% of the time I accidentally grab my backpack or whatever item I have on me and fall to the ground. Also apparently walkers have super-senses and can hear and see me through walls. If I could I would refund this game. the game holds up well besides the incredibly dumb bugs and slow paced story and overall I'm disappointed.After reading other reviews i cant say I have personally YET experienced invisible enemies zombies/soldiers. During the story missions, enemies seem to spawn inside walls and try to shoot me. I have also experienced a Enemies trying to shoot me through walls even though they didn't see me yet and I haven't even explore that area.I love the new items such as the bolted up gloves and the sawed-off shotgun but BEWARE, this game is pretty much a re-skin. No new map areas to explore, mostly the same weapons and no new enemies besides clunky armored tower solders. Speaking of the new tower variant, its whole point is to be a tank for bullets, but they die from 1 head-shot with the semi auto pistol from far away. I have no clue why they would be this weak.All of the problems from the previous game seem to have come to the sequel. When you put 2 items near each-other all hell lets loose. There is also too much resource scarcity. At the beginning of the game I was already low on shafts and proteins. It seems like I can never find any and I understand its a zombie infested world but geez how hard should it be to find wood and old food.Honestly, I'm mad because I was playing on a long story mission before this review and all my progress got reset for the 3rd time. I would recommend you to buy this game a later time when all these problems are fixed. This is I think my only bad review I have made on my steam acc EVER, so sorry if I wrote too much.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead Saints & Sinners is still THE BEST VR Zombie game. That's only because there is no competition. Some issues;This game lacks serious QOL improvements. There's a LOT of smaller things that make the game painful at times. (Unloading your gear, messing with large objects)Weapon durability takes away the slasher part of this game and slows everything down to a crawl. (And weapons break way too fast)Weapon durability is more of an issue than conserving ammo. Inconsistency in what items can actually be used as weapons. (Bottles that don't break, items that aren't actually there)Items 'baked' into the worlds that aren't interactable, but they have the same model as the items that are.Zombies automatically know the best path to you, instead of hobbling or getting stuck on whatever is between you and them.If zombies cant pathfind to you, they stay in place and wave their arms around. Especially noticeable if you are on a higher elevation.Zombies infinitely spawn whenever you aren't looking, they don't just 'wander in'. An area you just cleared out while making minimal noise is once again full of zombies.Saints and Sinners 1 had a combat trials mode. This game doesn't have anything like that. (REALLY THOUGH. WHY NOT?)The dialogue and story is iffy at best. Simply an excuse to visit certain areas at certain times. The skip dialogue button is one of the things this game did right.On top of all that, it's just a copy/paste of the first game. Bugs. BUGS. BUGS. BUGS. Its still a zombie shooter game in vr. The combat is satisfying, and the crafting system is rewarding. I would have at-least liked SOME difference compared to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game, I really do. But the incessant amount of issues get in the way so much that it degrades the experience and makes it all the more frustrating when the game could freeze or crash at any point, killing any and all momentum and enjoyment there is to be had.The new weapons like the Devil's Paintbrush, the Sawn-Off Shotgun and the Chainsaw (ABSOLUTELY GODLIKE FEEL AND CONTROL) are fantastic additions on top of all the new items, environments, nighttime levels and set pieces in the story that make the game WORTH PLAYING. When the going gets good, IT'S ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GREAT. But that feeling is shot down faster than using the chainsaw against an armored enemy , forcing a restart and having to regain ALL progress LOST (same applies to random intervals in the story where the game freezes leaving me no choice other than to quit the game or end the process via task manager. Not to mention the hit detection when grabbing weapons, your flashlight, journal, etc. are somehow even MORE frustrating to grab when you're in the heat of the moment, leading to a lot of avoidable deaths that could have been mitigated if grabbing items weren't so cumbersome (an issue I've NEVER had when playing the first game 3 YEARS AGO).The fact the Quest 2 version was favored first and then added to Steam a few months later, one would be lead to believe the problems would be ironed out by the time it makes its debut, but honestly a delay would've been FAR more tolerable if it meant a quality product that actually functions. This "release broken now, fix it later" mentality should've died last generation, but as it stands I will set this game aside until most of the issues plaguing Saints & Sinners Chapter 2 are resolved.Peaks, Valleys and Roadblocks are the best words to describe my experience. There are moments of pure, unadulterated fun versus moments of anger, resentment and disbelief. It could have EASILY been superior to the first game, and the pieces and foundation are there, but it is far too unstable and rough for me to recommend it. And I am very disappointed. Wait for all the patches to fix the game, or buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Version: Too much needed to be changed and didn't get changed.  With the three-year gap, there's no excuse for being this similar.Long Version:Index player, 1080Ti graphics card (a bit weaker than a 3070).  I will say this game is only SLIGHTLY more optimized than the first - I remember the first game stuttering a lot more when I played, and I think I am seeing a slight bit of stuttering here.First Impressions:  This definitely feels like it should have been a DLC, rather than a full-fledged standalone game.  The Resting Place map (barring the expanded portion) is pretty much the way I remember it, right down to where the one food recipe is.  The combat is as I remember - maybe I am spoiled by other VR games but the guns still feel just as clunky as the first time (which might be a problem, with the plot that I've seen so far), forcing me to rely on melee.  That's tolerable given what the noise of firearms can do.The grabbing is just as wonky as I remember it.  Most VR games aren't anywhere near this clunky with grabbing items.  And THAT is the biggest reason that despite the fact I'll play this the whole way through, I'm giving this a thumbs down for the review.I can put up with the graphics issues given I put up with the first game's graphics problems.  But there's no excuse for the grab controls to be as imprecise as they are, especially several years after the first game.EDIT: Finally got to import my save with way too much of everything (turns out it was available on release day, I just never got the chance until now).  Naturally, the new crafting items call for new resources.  7-8 new resources, if I'm not mistaken.  And the graphics are in fact a bit more optimized than the last game.  Still not enough to change my review - things are just like I remember, especially with the grabbing controls.

_childDocuments_.review: If your favorite thing about the first one was killing zombies, get it because there's much more to kill (your character still has asthma so if you just want to kill, turn on the cheat mode in config and go to old town w/ infinite stamina. You'll need external trainers for anything else like infinite weapon durability). HOWEVER, combat feels less responsive half of time. Enemies getting knocked backwards when you try to decapitate them is very common. In every other way, it's worse and more buggy. Missions don't save your progress if you crash in the middle of them (this game is not stable, so this is likely).The game suddenly crashed for me during one of the last missions after going through the cellar+sewers. This segment takes a while because you can't see anything and there are lots of zombies that get in your way + a room you are encouraged to loot (this room has loot that is very hard to grab with your hands since they put it juuuuust out of reach). The segment took me about half an hour. I turned a corner into a room with a bunch of human enemies, the saving icon popped up for some reason and then never stopped loading. I closed the game after 5 minutes, rebooted, and was put back at the start of the mission.Also, night missions suck. I avoided them when possible, but a lot were forced nighttime only. If you're scared of the dark, they might be thrilling. For someone who isn't, it's more tedious than anything. I found myself having the manually crank up the brightness so I could actually see what I was doing, and then having to turn it back down for every other time so my retinas aren't burned out of my face by having it on max at day.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm changing my review from negative to positive after having finished the game today. I keep the old text below. Don't get me wrong - the next 15 hours still were a buggy and stuttering mess. I wasn't even sure if my progress was broken completely since the "Travel to Rampart at night" task would never disappear from my mission list. I have to admit that besides all technical problems the game loop is somehow addicting. Usually I'm not a fan of crafting or looting, but in this S&S 1+2 it's fun. And even more fun is killing zombies with a knife, shotgun or grenade :-). Scavenger hunts at night are spooky as hell and made the city even more terrifying. If you are willing to tolerate the obvious flaws, you'll get almost 20 hours of thrilling entertainment. Let's hope the engine will get fixed for Chapter 3...Some suggestions for improvement:- The grab radius for holster items is too large. It is really hard to grab a ladder without taking my knife or gun all the time. The radius should be dynamic and get much smaller when I look down (e.g. to climb down) and be large when the holsters are outside my field of view. The grab radii for lamp and map could be a bit larger or have a higher priority when my hands are near my torso. Instead of the lamp, I grabbed my gun most of the time.- Fix the human AI. If the game gets to difficult because of it, then reduce their number or give them limited ammo and/or close combat weapons.- I should be able to pick up and throw an armed grenade again- I should get some acoustic/visual warning if I accidentally lose my holster weapons while not looking at them- The girls in the bunker should not start shooting at me so shortly after accidentally drawing my gun- I'm also losing my gloves all the time and don't know why- Switching on the laser sight is really hard - I need several tries to find the switch (maybe larger radius?)- The chainsaw feels underwhelming. It should cut through hordes like butter without much resistance- And most important - fix the stuttering (caused by CPU spikes every few seconds) I'm sad to give this one a bad review, but the performance problems and ridiculous human enemy AI leaves me no choice. I consider myself an experienced VR gamer, but this game still gives me VR sickness. The regular stuttering after walking a few meters is bad enough (mostly CPU spikes), but after loading sub levels (like the recording studio) the image switches between freezing and unfreezing for almost half a minute. This feels really awful. I have a Ryzen 3700X, 32 Gigs of Memory, a  RTX 2070 Super and a SSD. All drivers, bios etc. is up to date. This should be enough to achieve a tolerable performance with medium or low details! The human enemies seem even more buggy than in chapter 1. They look in the wrong direction when attacking me or get stuck between doors. Sometimes I can't even shoot them due to invisible walls. There is a great game hidden inside this mess. Sneaking around and stabbing zombies is real fun. I can even live with the jankiness of the weapons and actually like their look and feel. But for me chapter 2 is definitely a worse experience than the first part...

_childDocuments_.review: REVISED REVIEW (now that the game is mostly fixed)!!!Great followup to the original. At first I was concerned when I saw that Chapter 2 uses the same map, with all 10 previous locations, and only adds 3 new locations. But now that I've played through the entire game, I can say there is enough new material here to justify the price. Overall, I highly recommend the game. Now for the pros and cons.PROS: 1. Allows you to import your save from the original game and have all your material and achievements from Chapter 1.2. Maintains the addictive replay value of scavenging and killing zombies,3. Despite only adding 3 new locations, there is enough new content to justify the price,4. Lots of new side tasks and hidden items to keep you playing after the main story ends.CONS1. Now that the game is mostly fixed, I don't have to mention the invisible zombies and constant crashes. But ghosts of versions past still haunts me.2. The dialogue is awful. Hackneyed, cliché, and overwritten. Especially the villains (Axeman and Momma). Their monologuing is like an AI writing sample (please hire a screenwriter or novelist next time, Developers).  Thankfully you can skip most of it. Though it means you miss most of the story line. 3. Unlike the original game, Chapter 2 has several night-only missions. But straining to see what's in front of you isn't so much scary as it is annoying. You don't want to make something so difficult that it stops being fun. Thankfully you can blast the brightness in the settings and that makes it tolerable.BUGS:There are still a lot of small bugs that frustrate. 1. Explosive arrows getting stuck in the invisible edges of barriers right in front of you happens way too often. 2. The inability to throw a grenade more than 20 feet. 3. The category of bugs that cause conversations with allies to unintentionally end in a bloodbath. Which often results in blocks that prevent you from completing tasks. Thus forcing you to reload and start over. QUESTIONS FOR DEVS:1. What's with the red fog making Villa Corolla andOld Town unplayable? I assumed this would develop in the story, but it never did, 2. Love the addition of beautiful Bourbon Street. But not enough access to all these buildings. Like the second floor balconies, for example. I would love more access in a future DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, IT IS BUGGY AND ABANDONED BY THE DEVELOPER!Updated on Dec-2023: It has been 7 months since the last update and guess what, it is still broken and abandoned by the developers.Update: It has been 2 months since last update and the game is still broken - this game is abandoned by the devs and you should NOT buy it expecting a finished game. With a heavy heart I cannot recommend this game.TD;DR:I like the game but it's a utter mass of bugs and crashes. The developers clearly did not put enough time testing and fixing the game before releasing it, even 4 patches in.  I paid the full price for this game and while I enjoy it, I cannot recommend buying it now - Maybe try it in 2024 when it is fixed and discounted.My 24 hours in review:Exprienced on Quest2, 3080TISo I jumped on the wagon a bit later than everyone else (2 weeks after release) and everything seems pretty much on par with this original game. It's OK but feels A LOT less polished than the previous chapter. I'm getting a lot of crashes during combat when using the Sap Gloves, which is the main issue for me. Now they released another patch (2023-05-23) which fixes the glove crash but broken achievements. It feels like they didn't really test the game properly to the high level which they did with the previous chapter. Shame.So after around 24 hours of gameplay, I greatly enjoy it but those crashes ruin the fun so much.Also, why no manual save option? I lost around 2 hours of progress due to the game crashing out of no where when gripping random stuff. I don't always have time to spend 30 minutes exploring a level.  This becomes a hassle which makes me plan my gaming sessions.======================  Gameplay and what was added.======================If you mastered the previous game, you will incredibly enjoy honing your skills again, just like riding a bike.Pretty much the same game, really feels like a DLC. You can now visit places at night which definitely increases the difficulty.They added around 3 new levels from what I seen so far.Two new workbenchs with stuff to unlock which were pretty easy if you import your save.They added punchy gloves, so you can now punch zombies, (Sap gloves crash the game, Use the Louisiana Kiss) they are overpowered AF, hold a zombie and punch it once and his head goes pop. It probably would be better if it took at least two punchs, seriously, what are these zombies made of? Pinatas break harder then the zombies.You get to carry over your original save which is nice, Although if you played the previous chapter you are most likely full of gear and guns so the game is pretty easy that way.[The way you do it requires you to start the previous game create and code and insert this code in this game, if you ask me - this is bad design. No reason why it couldn't just read the files from the previous install. ]======================Performance and Bugs:======================So far I played around 24hours. I didn't see any of the invisible zombie issue people have been talking about.I am about 24 days in the game and towards the endgame quests.The issues I saw so far:- Game crashed on me when I tried was crouching grabbing a zombie and somehow took the bag from my shoulder. This happened only once so far. - Game crashed when interacting with gloves. Sap Gloves make the game crash a lot. Happened at least 6 times.- Game crashed randomly when holding some lever.- Some dialog disappeared during the conversation with the NPC and it is not clear what happened.- Achievement have been broken by the last patch, clearly "kill X" when you get to kill him and it doesn't grant you the achievement, it's broken.- I encountered one invisible distant walls but that's not game-breaking so far.- One of the quest givers (it was static) was jittering (bad physics like) but not game-breaking..Maybe the last three patches improved upon it.Devs really need to fix this game, because it is so fun but frustrating due to bad testing from their side and crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: Much can be said about this game. Is it an enhanced Quest port? Maybe, some textures do look Quest-ish, some assets are low-poly, and physics are limited. Still this is the very best VR version of the game you can get - it's even better than the PSVR2 version.The PSVR2 version has limited or no dynamic shadows on npcs - see this vid at 4:05:The PCVR version is 55GB, while the PSVR2 version is about 32GB, so you might get the better textures too. Using Index, i9 10900K (10cores/20threads, 5.3Ghz), 32GB, and an oc'ed RTX 3090, I got solid 90 fps with res 200% (set using SteamVR, while keeping the in-game slider at 100%) and all other settings at the max, including antialiasing. With the PCVR version, you can probably increase res to 400% when the RTX 5090 arrives, might not be a bad idea :-)The dynamic shadows do look awesome, and while many textures are low-res, they look great from a distance, so don't get too close ;-)The game does feel like more of the same, but no harm done there, the original was a blast. The game feels like an 8/10, not more, not less.

Its not worth 50 dollars though.Had to get all the crafting recipes again because I started on a fresh save (uninstalled the first game long ago). Most of the old areas are completely devoid of any characters and only exist to house supply caches. The whole exile system feels useless because you can craft stuff that is either on par or better than what they have to give you. Just avoided it entirely until I had to do a single story quest for it.Human enemies are stupid. You can shoot a guy and his friend won't notice even from 5 feet away. Most of the armored enemies can be juggled/hit-stunned in the head with a pistol till they die. Gets easier to do when you can craft laser sights for pennies on the dollar. Was looking forward to the human combat in this game but was disappointed.The axe man is a big part of the marketing but plays such a small role in the games story until the end. Most of his character is left to "you were mean to me so I killed you" notes left next to dead bodies. Would have been cool to have him chase you through areas as you explored them but nah.I had to deal with the infamous invisible zombie only once. Had a bug where if I pistol whipped a zombie my game would crash, so I just avoided doing it. There's some horrible occlusion culling in The Tower area.Performance was OK. I have a 1070ti.

_childDocuments_.review: Most negative reviews you read are gonna talk about lag or other performance issues that will probably be patched out. I'm gonna get into why this game is just straight up terrible even when they manage to get it to run a consistent 30 fps.Boy I sure love the VR genre where we make games that wouldn't go for 15 dollars cost 40 the moment you have to put a headset on to play it. If you already own the first game don't bother, not enough new content to merit its price. If you don't own either game don't bother, there are so many other games in the headset that give you more bang for your buck and could probably be modded into a zombie game anyhow (see blade and sorcery, yes it doesn't have survival or crafting elements but the core gameplay loop is so much better because someone actually put their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ back into it). This is your typical example of big brand gaming, barely functional repetitive combat loop, lazy crafting to give the game some facade of complexity and a learning curve, and only skin deep level design. The levels are tiny, and could probably have been made in unity for an aspiring developers final project (I'd still only see it getting a C-), unlike other zombie survival games where the world feels large and impossible to navigate the dead infested New Orleans is pretty much a cakewalk. It was in the first game too, even without the easy start you get in the second.It's also just straight up boring, no slippery slope into scuffed situations like zomboid, survivors barely add a twist the gameplay unlike DayZ, and crafting is just there so they can advertise having crafting and is in no way deep or well implemented to the games function unlike 7 days. There is no satisfaction to taking down walkers, after your first couple kills (i got over it in the tutorial in the first game) you realize it's all the same motions. You can have whatever kind of melee weapon you want, stabbing skulls is the exact same. It's not like there isn't potential for fun, I've sunk my hours in and had my moments but it's hard to find when the devs don't want to make having fun easy. Or maybe this is another instance where someone pushing down from above ♥♥♥♥♥♥ the entire project. You also better believe that any attempts at changes to rectify this fact won't come for free, and will be hidden behind a DLC paywall because that's just how games work these days I guess. Either way, respect your dollar more. Don't buy this full price just because you want to fight zeds in VR, wait for someone to make a good game and set the industry standard or wait for one of them to go on sale. Until then, B&S has a zombie mod or if you're more looking for the open world approach there's always modded Skyrim VR (but that's another example of egregious overpricing for a game that already needs a headset). If the crafting is what you really want you might be screwed because outside of that one Minecraft version I can't even get to work properly and The Forest I have yet to find a single good survival crafting vr game. Yet another title I am happy to have bought a code for and minimized the money made off of me, Re: respect your dollar more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly just more of the first Saints And Sinners, which is all good if you really want more content, but I will admit this feels more like a DLC than a completely separate game. The story for the sequel was okay, nothing worth being invested in, but it's not like it isn't entertaining, It is definitely better at getting the player doing some stuff other than fetch quests for pump regulators and such. This really just feels like a game made for the sole reason of wanting more creative ways to kill zombies. I mean I was invested in this since I saw the chainsaw in the trailer, a chainsaw in a VR title like this is insanely awesome. Everything that I was really happy with from this game was in the weapons category and that's about it. Playing around with the gloves with bolts in them were fun, just because punching zombies to kill made combat very fun to mix up, the sawed off shotgun was a cool little way to have a shotgun as a sidearm, the sub machine gun is fun to run and gun with, but the chainsaw being able to slice back and fourth at any angle feels unreal in a game like this. One thing I will also say that sucks about this game is that it was basically a port from the quest, so it had quite a bit of glitches at launch. It sounds like it only got one bug fix since launch and was basically abandoned which sucks, but it is in slightly better condition than it was at launch. The only thing I really wished was added to this game was the round based mode from the first game. With this catalog of really fun weapons it would have been awesome to see something like that to play around with. All around Saints And Sinners Chapter 2 is great fun if you play for the weapons, but it could be a little cheaper and didn't need to be a completely new game, I enjoyed the time I played through it but really wish there was more reason for me to revisit it like more content or gamemodes.

_childDocuments_.review: Taken straight from my Part 1 playthrough video's description :I wanted to play this through to the end, but Virtual Desktop support stopped working after I already passed my refund period and immediately after recording Part 1. This has been my preferred wireless streaming method for years, and I continue to prefer it over Oculus AirLink. I had no issue the first time playing with VD, so this feels like a massive bait-and-switch to make it non-refundable. And after research, the developers seem to have no interest in supporting the game through Virtual Desktop. After recording Part 1, the controls switched from Oculus default controls to Vive wands, so I am unable to sprint or do other basic functions that would make it playable. I tried every other workaround under the sun, including custom, user-created Oculus controller profiles, to no avail. Seems like a small thing to fix, so as a matter of principle, I'm not continuing with this title until they give a crap about the largest demographic of VR users (Quest 2, Virtual Desktop). Seems like they just want to promote AirLink/Meta over satisfying the consumer. If I was a betting man, I'd bet on this being the reason the game's not even a full four stars across the board, when compared to the first.Sorry guys, I thought this would be a top title for the channel (was meant to be the debut title at least), but I refuse to be strong-armed into playing the way other people or industries want me to play, and I think companies should feel the weight of their bad decisions. I'll do my part by leaving this one at a negative review for now. It's a shame that the content itself can't be enjoyed past these minor, fixable technical issues, like they did with the first entry.  Either they've become lazy, or they're vying for exclusivity and preference to Oculus/Meta platforms. It's a shame.If you prefer Virtual Desktop with Quest headsets (the most popular setup), and want to continue to prefer them, I can't recommend this one in good conscience.2/5 - Can't even experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: too many people complaining about small bugs and delays on launch....this game is as good as the original and expands on it, you can visit old locations (and lots of new ones, AND visit them at night too) and complete parts of the old game as well...you can export your old save into the new game and start with your previous gear and items as well, to do this, first launch the original game and export the current save with the new button in the menu, bottom right... after that, take note of the code it shows, go into S&S2, select new game then import save, and input the code you wrote before.... and u start exactly with all the items u had before....as a hoarder myself i was very pleased to see my 10k+ resources, and dozens of weapons, where intact and ready to kill more zombies....in the end, you could see this as a paid DLC... it adds more to what there is already, and that's all you could ever ask for....

_childDocuments_.review: Hm. So far I'm enjoying it for the most part, but the story itself is a bit short. I think they tried to pad it a bit with the 'trade' missions that you can only do at night(Or they focused too much on those instead of writing more/better story), but busywork doesn't really make up for that. Sometimes I get the feeling that this game was meant to be DLC rather than a separate game given that most of the locations in it are the SAME LOCATIONS with the SAME ASSETS from the first game in almost every way with a few minor changes here and there. There are a few new locations, but not many at all. If correct, then why release it as new game??There are many bugs but they ARE being fixed as we, the players, report them. Really this should have been better tested before release, but I suppose "better late than never". Bugs of the past included: invisible armored zombies, crashing when you punched zombies's heads with the gloves, weapons getting stuck on the ground or falling through it, Bastion's world flickering in and out of existence visually but still existing physically, certain missions being uncomplete-able, the worn shotgun twitching all over the place (the better one still does this as of 4/7/2023), Quest Items vanishing, the Pawn King not messaging over the radio EVER, soda can grenades killing more than two-to-three enemies and crashing the game, data carry-over from the first game not working. The game not working for Quest 2 headsets at all! (And I'm sure there are more. Feel free to add them yourself in the comments).Good job fixing those at lightning pace, devs!I really wish we had a 'meh' option instead of just Yes or No specifically for the reasons of "I'm so far in the game but not done with it yet and my opinion might change" or "I don't like it but I don't hate it" reviews, which is my opinion on this game.

whole bunch of new items and weapons, and they really made a lot of improvements from the original game. for example, this game works way better from a narrative perspective, because this time you get an actual antagonist you meet at the beginning of the game, and the game builds it up throughout the narrative. in this game your main goal is to take down the tower, and collapse the corrupt faction thats been running new orleans. both those things are what i wanted from the first game. also the missions are way more diverse now, in the first game you basically had two different missions you would repeat over and over. it didnt get stale in my opinion, but it made the game kinda predictable. in this game though, pretty much every mission is unique. there are missions like "find a door code and use it to get into a building" or "sneak through a map infested with zombies to find someone" and many others. theres no repeats, its all different.now to be fair the game does have some negatives despite what ive said. for one thing the game is buggy and have given me times where i have had to restart a mission (multiple times) to finish it. the game can also crash randomly, also making you restart. which is weird because the last game wasnt buggy in my playthrough, i cant remember a single time thats happened, although to be fair i didnt buy it on release so they could have patched it before i bought it. theres also a new "trade network" mechanic in this game where you trade items with NPCs to get rewards, but i just couldnt get into it. im not that big of a fan of going to some location at night specifically to find someone, get the order, travel home, collect whatever junk they want, travel back to them, and get some crappy reward that you could have just scavenged or crafted yourself in the time it took you to do all that. i mean i know that the rewards eventually get better and you eventually get some exclusive stuff that you can only obtain via trading, but even then its just too much work for the payout. maybe if you only had to do it once to get the max reward it would be worth it, but i skipped that part of the game. also this last one is just a nitpick, but even if you load up a completed save file from the previous game, your choices from the last game will all be voided in this game. all the characters that you met in the previous games make no appearance, even if you didnt kill them. which sucks because i thought it would have been nice to have a conversation with casey or something for old times sake. but instead this is basically just a telltale game sequeloverall though its quite an improvement from the first game, definitely get it if you liked the first game. and if the studio ever decides to make a third game in the franchise, i would be all for it

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first title and the DLC that came free later on. That DLC made me play the first game again and I was really excited for Chapter 2. Now that I've finished Chapter 2 I feel like all I've done through this game is battle with this thought in my head that this is really really expensive DLC. I can't help but think that the price it currently is (£30) is to cover the development cost that went into the Quest 2 version of the game. So I should probably say if you're someone buying this in the future and getting it cheaper then I'd probably recommend this.So first off I should say the PC version came out 3 months after the Quest 2. It was supposed to be less than 2 months but it got delayed. You'd think the delay would be for polish and bug fixing, but it still released with issues. I think I got lucky that I didn't have as bad a time as anyone else but I did get the invisible invincible zombies later on too which was very very annoying. I think there are a group of people who would agree that there is a dip in gameplay and graphical quality to the sequel and that feels frustrating for the expensive price of the game. Thankfully though they took away the weight from the pistols so those are actually fun to use, that's actually a huge deal.Also they allow you to carry over your save file from the first game but this isn't explained well at all: you have to open the first game, generate a code from your save file, then remember and type this code in when you go to import your code for Chapter 2. I could be wrong but there are no story implications to this, it's simply to take your resources and weapons with you.There's also some features I really wish they implemented for users such as adjusting the size and placement of holsters. At least a third of my play time was going for my torch but picking up what was holstered, or going for my journal and not being able to grab it. Then also finding out later as I've had my hands to my sides that I've accidentally grabbed a weapon and dropped it on the floor -- super fun. And while climbing is a small part of the game it can be difficult to know if you're grabbing something or actually gripping it...sounds stupid but there's a part near the end where I died a few times because of this (it's more so some oddly designed route for climbing I feel, seems like it needed more QA).Now to get to the actual game. I think this game eventually becomes interesting for returning players past the half way mark so I find it hard to recommend, but for new players you might have a ball playing this (but really you should play the first game as it utilizes the existing locations better and has better story). If you don't want to know anything about it going forward then consider this spoiler territory so be warned. I loved my time with the first game and I think it had pretty good characters and a decent story that's building up, so I was hoping Chapter 2 would really push on this with its established world and gameplay. But that's not what you get at all, you seriously only get three new locations to explore and nothing really of interest happens until the last third of the game where things only just start to feel justified for the price. You can visit all the previous locations of the first game and frustratingly it seems like something you'd have to do anyway if you don't import a save so you can unlock some of the first games weapons and collect resources. And while the new locations are good and more interesting than the previous ones they only offer a glimpse into what a full on sequel could be and I think that's a damn shame. I also feel like one of the primary antagonists of this game who is a beefed up tank of a dude (and who I was really looking forward to going against) is a big missed opportunity in this game. It's my own fault for setting up expectations but I loved the idea of a sequel where this guy stalked you and actually made things a lot scarier. I thought the hotel might introduce this element and have him stalk and look for you but that didn't happen. He is just a tanky boss fight later and then it's over. I really enjoyed the final level and it was a good example of how this actually has some terrific guns and the shooting can be quite exciting. To this day the Nova might be my favourite shotgun in VR and is supremely satisfying to use. There's also a vista at the top of the tower that's quite breathtaking and really makes me wish for a game like this with larger levels. The area of the Tower feels like a glimpse of this at times and I hope one day we can get get a world that can offer the kind of size and depth of that.I've mainly written this review for anyone that loved the first game and needs more context of this one. The first Saints and Sinners is probably in my top 5 VR games ever made, so I was really looking forward to Chapter 2. But like another favourite of mine which is Boneworks, the sequel doesn't live up to the original in many ways but I did enjoy my time with Chapter 2 a lot more than I did with Bonelab. Wait for a price drop or a good VR bundle to enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll just get right to the point. The game doesn't suck, but it's really bad. Looking at the game's quality itself, it isn't bad, and it is 100% a playable game. But every single thing tied to the story sucks. I feel like I have to make this review, even though I have only played 2 hours.The rest I have to say below is just explaining why I said what I said above with spoilers from the first game.Right. The last thing that happened when I played the original Saints & Sinners is that my camp got raided by some losers, and I had to get all my stuff back. The thing is, in this game, you don't really get a new camp. Sure, the camp has gotten a little extra, but it's still the same location. Anyone would know where I am. When it comes to the crafting system, I expected there to be a new system since more items would make it wonky and uncontrolled. And it is. Running around to the different workbenches just feels unnecessary. I expected to have one bench and maybe a recepie book or just something more convenient.When it comes to other locations in the game, I really like that I am in the same world, same locations, different time. I can visit old places, but they have changed, and I like it. The cherry on top is that there are new locations too. Kind of expected, though.The introduction also left a lot to be desired. When I got thrown into action and then talked to the first dude, I just felt like there would be an alternative to live with him and set up camp in the hotel with that guy. Nope.Characters in the game are both great and meh. The first dude in the hotel seemed chill, and I like him. Even though I am not myself religious, I can agree with his beliefs since they do just make sense. I am also 100% not interested in taking down the tower, but I am forced to do so. I would like if I could have alternatives like, instead of fighting them head-on, they attack me first, and then I attack them type of ♥♥♥♥. _childDocuments_.review: An extremely great VR game engine severely damaged by poor game and extremely poor map design. Most of the content is just copy-pasted from the first game, despite you traveling to a new location in the story. The new maps, particularly the story instance maps at the end, are baffingly obscure in their puzzle elements, forcing you to abuse edge collisions to locomotion-walk forward past a section you'd normally Lara Croft-style shimmy or grab-climb through as a part of the actual linear way forward. As usual for VR, physics are just confusing and laggy - for example, the Lever-Action rifle doesn't work with your off-hand, so you have to reload it like a Break-Action rifle. Pistol racking is still way too stiff.If you've already played the first one, this is just more of the same with a few new thingies - not entirely worth full price. Despite the terrible game design, there's some extreme highs you can get with each raid. Once, I was in a raid so long my weapons all broke. I had to run my way through a small crowd of zeds, ducking and darting, grabbing bottles as I moved as improvised weaponry. Really, I haven't felt that gritty, violent, almost tactile fight-for-survival thrill since, like, The Raid.That, and pushing through human raider-infested zones with a pump-action shotgun in my left and my rifle balancing the shotgun in my right really makes you feel like a badass. There's no AUG - I couldn't roleplay as the Guvna.

_childDocuments_.review: The End of the Tour... Let me start off by saying I really enjoyed my play-through of the S&S 2. This game is all from the first game and more, so naturally if you enjoyed the first game, you'll enjoy this one. It contains the same locations from the first game, with the addition of the new locations to explore and an expanded resting place. Which comes with the added ability to now import your previous end game save from "The Walking Dead Saints and Sinners" which will carry over any decisions you made in the first game, as well as all your accumulated supplies from the bus. Which is totally worth the trouble, you can check out my guide on how to do this Here -----------------> To address issues of performance, as a whole, the game ran for me as well as the original game did years ago. My hardware hasn't changed, early 2020 gear. 2080rtx, i7, 16gb ram, nothing too special by today's standards and the game ran great. I played it on a Quest 2 using a Link Cable suspended from the ceiling. I only encountered a few problems, which didn't hugely affect gameplay (At least the way I was playing.)-Game would drop FPS if Headset disconnected or was put down (to piss let's say) and a game restart would usually be required to fix it, but not always.- Game had FPS drops upon first start up, however this was fixed by changing the graphics settings in game, everything from "ultra" down to "high" except for view distance. This fixed my FPS problems day one.- Some of the new Angel statues as well as the demon statues don't spawn at all, and therefore can't be picked up/collected. - A few of the achievements won't pop on steam, despite having completed their required tasks multiple times. (This is most likely a Steam port issue, rather than a game bug. but idk)- The game would oddly crash if I head shot an armored tower guard with the new Hunting Rifle. (I tested this to make sure it's not a fluke. Each time, I'd aim, line up the head shot, fire!, and be left with the frozen image of the gun going off and the death sound of the soldier.. Than Bug Reporting Screen, How Fun.) Annoying since this weapon is one of the most effective ways to kill them.- Some game "Mission Items" would not be removed from my backpack after completing the tasks. I couldn't use them for decor either so unfortunately I just had them in my backpack the whole time. -Long Loading Screens, most notably on start up. All small things that are annoying on there own, but don't affect the game as a whole right now. (Other than my disappointment that I can't 100% it on steam due to the achievement glitches.) SAD :-(Otherwise the game ran really well, and I am still having a great time with it. If you loved the first game, but are on the fence with this one because of all the reported performance issues, give it a try, you can always refund if your equipment doesn't agree with it. Hopefully they will release some patches to fix this steam issues soon. In closing I recommend picking this game up after you have enjoyed the first S&S game, and continuing the tourist's journey to the top of New Orleans. One Dead Walker at a Time.Game Rating:10/10Overall Rating Considering: 7/10**UPDATE** Achievement's have been fixed.Playing though again to check patches.
