_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Even though the first chapter had issues, it was still very enjoyable, but I cannot say the same about this one. I guess I'll start off with the good:1. It's pretty much like the first game, but worse. It has the fun combat, the looting system, new crafting recipes and weapons.2. The story had a ♥♥♥♥ ton of potential (I'll get into that later) and it had some interesting moments.Now the fun part:1. I don't even know where to begin - I guess I'll start with the performance. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible. Even if you turn every setting to the lowest one (which makes the game look like ♥♥♥♥) it will still perform poorly. Personally I've experienced screen-tearing and poor FPS.2. The enemy AI, just like in the first game, is absolutely abysmal. It's gotten a bit better in this one, but it still sucks. If an enemy spots you in a restricted zone, no one else will be alerted, unless they're very close. Nobody reacts to gunshots, the AI movement can be weird and all in all, it's not a very pleasant or immersive experience.3. The walkers are fine, but their spawn conditions are very unrealistic and annoying. At one point I was in an empty building, I went outside for a second and came back to a massive herd of walkers waiting for me. If you were to kill all of them in a room, they would just spawn for no reason. I understand that this game should be hard, and, apparently, only NASA supercomputers can handle at most 10 walkers on the map at one time, but I don't think that making walkers just magically appear behind you is the solution.4. It's buggy. If you spawn in and there's a flare just flying in the middle of a bus, I think you need to fix that.5. The gameplay and story was butchered. It had a lot of potential and a lot of hype (the Axeman, finally taking on the Tower), but it feels like It was done by a college student just before the assignment was due. It had some fun and interesting parts, but it could've been so much more. It didn't have the "punch" that the first chapter had.6. The exile missions... yeah no. You love the "pick this up and give it to me" type missions? Awesome! here's like 30 more, but you don't know where the items are and the rewards are usually ♥♥♥♥. I was expecting some kind of faction or a trade center, but it's just some NPC with a box and a list. And they don't impact the story ://All in all, I was very excited when it came out, but I left disappointed. They not only didn't address issues the first game had, but also created more of them.

_childDocuments_.review: As a purchasing recommendation I'd say, consider grabbing it only if it's on a steep sale. Maybe around $10-20. With its current Steam price tag, I cannot recommend it. However, brace yourself for the pain of seeing its lost potential. Go in with the mindset of playing it casually and intermittently, rather than expecting an engaging, seamless playthrough like the predecessorEven in the first game, I often found myself wishing for so much.. more. Like of course more meaningful decisions, which are virtually non existent. Perhaps more choices in interactions, or even just more interactions in general. It left me wanting for meaningful encounters with the world, as I could recall meeting only about three random people in the town who interacted with me (for 10-30 seconds) not only by using the generic threatening or antagonizing, comments or just immediately tried to kill me. Saints and Sinners Retribution disappoints despite its solid features, such as the well-crafted engine and immersive VR gameplay. The game's downfall lies in its frustrating design choices, notably the lazy zombie respawn mechanic. It feels like you move 3-5 meters forward, just to turn around and see Zombies that obviously materialized from another plane of existence. It shatters not only the immersion and feels like a cheap way to increase difficulty, but particularly in the tedious night missions, with their painfully poor visibility and monotonous tasks, it becomes extra annoying. In the end, this was the reason I lost interest and stopped playing.One of the most noticeable things missing.. is the lack of returning characters from the first game. For instance,  could have opened up an opportunity for a unique sidekick, someone who waits for you back at your base, adding a personal touch to the game. Instead, there’s nothing – a missed chance for continuity and deeper engagement. The game suffers from underdeveloped NPC interactions and a lack of continuity from the first game. The absence of any meaningful characters to connect with, creates a significant gap in the sequel's depth and engagement.In summary, Saints and Sinners Retribution, while built on a foundation of great potential, is spoiled by poor design decisions and narrative shortcomings. In a short summary: It's a missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a really mixed opinion about this game, at times i was really into it and then i was at the point where I wanted to just stop playing this game entirely. The devs have done a good job with actually listening to feedback and fixing bugs but bugs are still a thing in the game, and with time I think this game could be a lot more stable. The gameplay is a lot more immersive, having to actually use my brain to come up with combat strategies and having to manage my weapons carefully. The combat i found to be a lot more fun than the previous game with weapons like the SMG, chainsaw and sawed-off shotgun. SPOILERS AHEAD, now story on the other hand was pretty alright, at times I couldn't really tell what was going on. Most of the new characters i found to be pretty bland and generic. The pawn king  was an interesting character but I found him to be quite annoying, especially his missions. I thought the Dissidents were quite forgettable, I still don't even know their names. The villains though is were this game shines. Gerik was my favorite part about this entire game. Yeah he is an edge-lord and a stereotypical "big strong russian man" but I liked the story a lot and liked how they tied events from the last game into this one. Mama was questionable at times but I'm glad we finally got to see her after hearing so much about her in the first game. Mama is the perfect example of a cold hearted killer. The ending was pretty mixed for me, I am glad that we got the choice to choose between two endings and just like the first game, this game did not fail to have me questioning what I thought the right choice was, this time the choice was so much bigger, the fate of NOLA resting in my hands. I enjoyed this game and hope to see more of this series in the future, and for the love of Christ, please do not only release it on the meta quest 2 again. Overall if steam had a sideways thumb option for reviews, that's what I would give this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of mixed feelings about WD:SS2, but in the end I spent 15 hours playing it and enjoyed at least half of it.The game still has a rock solid core gameplay loop and great visual style, but it also has so many issues, both old and new ones.So first of all, yeah, it definitely should have been a DLC rather than a sequel. And it would have been an amazing endgame expansion, with lots of new content, including night time raids and long story campaign among other things. And there might have been much less bugs this way, but who knows.Speaking of bugs: they are plenty. From very frequent visual glitches, to much more annoying NPC dialogue stoppage, that requires reloading a save or choosing a violence to fix. My favorite bug is the head duplication after decapitation on an enemy, looks truly hilarious.Sadly, there were no updates for more than a year now, so there is very little hope for bugfixes.The other serious issue is braindead AI of not dead humans. It was an issue in the original, and it has not been improved at all, while becoming much more apparent due to increased number of enemies. Final mission (that has such an incredible view from the Tower, btw) is completely ruined because of the stupid AI, that can not perform in a massive combat scene.And last but not least: almost instant enemy spawn rates in a few certain missions (like the ending in nighttime Via Corolla or Tower ambush in the sewers), that make them a torture to play. Looks like the easiest issue to fix, yet it's still there.All and all, WD:SS2 is a huge letdown as a sequel, but still an enjoyable game, despite all its flaws.Works on Reverb G2

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome. I would 90% recommend it. This game is the perfect sequel to the first game.Do I have issues with it? Yeah, multiple.1. Save system. The game only saves at level transitions, now this was also a thing in the first game but it was nowhere near annoying as I found it in this game, you see this game features segments where you will be in one area for much longer, which means if you complete a specific boss-fight and are on your way back to your boat, and die with a bug which makes it impossible to recover your gear, you have to restart the ENTIRE LEVEL. Furthermore, if you have to leave your computer for a while you either have to keep the game open or bite the bullet and lose your progress. this sucks.2. The price tag. This game was great, but it is not worth it's base price, (£29.99), there is for sure more content in this game than the first one, but the game is largely just an expansion pack to the first game.3. A specific quest. This quest killed the replayability for me. The quest involves you finding some medical supplies in a hospital for someone. Sounds easy right? Yeah, no. I'm quite sure this wasn't just a me thing since other people reported this online too, but the spawn-rate for the equipment is horrible. I make no exaggeration when saying this: About 3 of my hours in this game were spent in that hospital constantly reloading my save to find the equipment I need. This quest has brought my motivation to replay this game from the top to about 1%.Thank you for reading my review, other than the listed issues, this game was awesome!

That's something that should have been fixed but it was the first mission so it only set me back 2 days. and the second major issue is that Zombies in this game take away stamina when you kill them with a bow or knife but shooting guns or explosions draw more of them to you. so if a continuous line of zombies corners you, you have 3 choices, use melee until your stamina runs out and you die, shoot guns and draw more zombies to you and die, or make a run for it and hope they don't catch you without stamina or you die. there's no way to get past zombies without using up ammo or stamina so once the game chooses to spawn more than 10-15 zombies at once It's just game over because even after killing hundreds of them they just keep trickling in at a rate slightly too fast to outrun or outkill. even left for dead had a system that gave you intermediate breaks to heal and reload between big fights. This game just doesn't have that. I know 90% of this review is dedicated to a minor annoyance but this makes the chainsaw the worst melee weapon in the game. if you are dealing with only a few zombies you can use a kitchen knife to stop them, and if there's a swarm the last thing you need is to run out of fuel after 15 zombies are dead and 15 more are closing in. even with these issues everything else works so well I'd still recommend it. Lots of VR games bite off more than they can chew but no system in this game works so poorly that it can't be used.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was about halfway through this game, my review was "If you liked the first game you'll like this one.", but now I changed my mind.If you played Chapter 1, you probably liked the maps, the puzzles, the scavenge hunts, and the combat, I did too, so I thought all they needed to do in the sequel was give us more of that.Except, everything good that was in Chapter 1 was copied and pasted in this glorified DLC, all the maps that are in Chapter 1 are nearly 100% unchanged, the same puzzles, the same safes with the same code locations.I thought that at least the new content would make up for this, but no. The gloves are useless because punching walkers doesn't stagger them, the safari rifle is just a buffed bolt action, the grenade launcher, does just that.The only thing I can say is amazing is the chainsaw, but it loses its charm quick.In Chapter 1, my biggest complain is that the human enemies were too stupid, never posed a threat, but that didn't matter too much because they weren't the focus, for the most part. In this game there are segments where you fight huge groups of humans at a time, and they serve to demonstrate how awful the AI really is.The new areas added are good, but not good enough to make up for the missed oportunities.The bugs are so obnoxious, my first playthrough was softlocked because I left a mission I had already completed before the game could tell me I completed it, and upon restart I realized the mission would never start again.The story is fine, I guess.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game really doesn't feel like a sequel.Yeah, you still live in the MAGIC SCHOOL BUS from the first chapter, but with two new workbenches, new toys, new people to meet , but the rest of it seems the same as it was in Ch 1.Don't get me wrong, the first parts of the story were good- at least the setup of it. The Axeman, at least in the trailers/what might have been expected prior to Ch 2's release on the quest, was supposed to be the "Mr. X"/Nemesis to the player, but playing to the end- the Axeman was never even an overlooming threat- as you only meet him face-to-face about TWICE in the game. No random encounters, none of it. He had potential yet Skydance wasted him with how the Axeman really played out.Overall, this game is on par to that of Aftershocks (a free post-game DLC) instead that of (dare I say it) a quarter-of-a-TOTK-level sequel.Do not buy.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, quick PSA: Turn on windowed mode. Solves 99% of sync issues and lag. If you gave this a bad review because of this issue then it's totally justified, fullscreen is stupidly laggy. Especially on some of the scripted missions with a lot of zombie/faction activity. That being said, there's still some bugs. Inventory management is annoying, you'll end up grabbing the wrong things, and if you're left handed then there's a 50% chance that throwing an object is going to make you place it in your backpack. Those bugs are manageable and can even be funny at times, but certainly is worth mentioning. I can't help but chuckle when I try to throw a knife only to end up seeing the inventory say the knife has been stored in my backpack... and then seeing the bolt-action rifle on my back impotently bounce off a zombie's face. The crafting system works like an RPG level system, and it is kind of structured like a looter-shooter. But the story is fun, the levels are spooky, you have a Hitman: Blood Money sort of freedom within each level and for the most part you do get a lot of freedom for different playstyles. Good things: + Working combat with good pacing+ Crafting economics are balanced+ Basically western Chernobylite + Fun climbing system + One of the few VR games where rifles have decent ironsights Bad things: - No modding support- Lots of invisible walls/unclimbable surfaces that feel contrived - Human AI have ridiculously low vision distance- Dull side missions- This DLC feels rushed and a bit unfinished (For instance not all bottles have been set up to work as weapons, details like that)- No customisable difficulty (Would be nice to see some settings for spawn density, loot degradation, weapon damage etc. Like in Project Zomboid.) - Because of how there's no mods or advanced difficulty settings, the sandbox/free roam after the main story falls very flat.Story (No spoilers beyond stuff you'll find out within the first introductory missions):Compared to the previous main storyline, this one is actually ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid. It's like politics without politics. The dissidents have no real opinions or intentions, so for all you know you're helping the Khmer Rouge rise to power. The tower is bad because they exile people even though that was a really common punishment prior to the invention of large scale societies and prisons. The only real political language used is "Authoritarian", but there's no actual evidence of that, and not to mention that in a zombie apocalypse you kind of have to be authoritarian. Between the bandits, the death cults, and the actual flesh eating plague, sometimes people will have to follow some rules. There's vague mentions of hunting and kill quotas in the first game, but the tower also admonishes these actions as things done by unsanctioned and corrupt functionaries. And the leader of the dissident comes off as basically yet another identical politician. Reverend Baptiste is the opposition, but all he ever does is to spout out quotes from what I can only assume is a planned sequel to the Unabomber manifesto. So you're stuck between 3 choices of ecofascism, bland liberal police state, or roll the dice on the "dissidents" whose vague ideals sound like the sort of garbage you'd see in a colour revolution... which 9/10 times in history eventually results in a bland liberal police state. If you're going to make a political story, then make a political story. Add real ideas with contradictions, and flaws, and difficult choices. "No system is perfect" is the warcry of the idiot. We have power grids, hospitals, airports and chemical plants. Pick a system, or millions will die. Doesn't matter if it's perfect or not. Either we keep ♥♥♥♥ organised, or dangerous things will happen. That's the real plot tension of politics, and they completely ignore that in favour of some wishy washy corporate "We don't want to be controversial" approach to politics where the dispositions basically boil down to aesthetics. Do you want the wacky looking faction, the creepy looking faction, or the serious looking faction? Very boring.

_childDocuments_.review: I have... very mixed feelings about this game. On the one hand, I enjoy the gameplay and love exploring the city; I always feel both extremely awesome and extremely terrified when I manage to escape a hoard of walkers or soldiers with nothing but a screwdriver and a half-loaded pistol. On the other hand, there is also a handful of problems that hold the game back from being a memorable experience.Starting with the pros, I really enjoy the addition of being able to explore the city at night. Night exploration forces the player use a different level of strategy, since a lot more walkers crowd the streets and are attracted to the player's flashlight. Therefore, you must survive using stealth, distraction, and a limited field of vision. It's also possible to scavenge backpacks from dead NPCs that spawn around the maps at night. It's a small detail that adds a bit of realism to the game, and, while it's not extremely likely to happen, you can find some pretty rare items or items that are hard to craft in the bags. The crafting benches have also been updated to provide some new and fun ways to destroy your enemies, living or dead. I had fun playing around with the chainsaw for a bit and absolutely obliterating walkers by slicing and dicing them into a pile of limbs, and the new laser guidance attachment for the firearms was particularly helpful for me because... uh... I kind of suck at aiming with them in this game. Overall, I don't really have an issue with any of the new mechanics, but I still have my gripes with the game that really dragged my experience through the mud.First of all, I'm a little disappointed that none of the choices that you made in the original game seem to carry over to the sequel. In fact, none of the choices you make in the first game seem to make a difference in how the sequel plays out. I imported an old save from the original game, but I also started a new file without the original game just to see what important choices there were that would affect the outcome of this chapter and was disappointed that nothing seemed to prompt me to choose what did (or, I guess, what I wanted to happen) in the first chapter. Even as I played through the game it became increasingly obvious that it was designed in a way that your choices would end up having more or less the same outcome in the story. I guess I can't really blame the developers for going this route though, as it would have been ambitious, to say the least, but having a game that has choices with major consequences is supposed to be... well, a major part of the game. Otherwise, it just kind of makes the player think, "Why did I waste all that time trying the good/bad/neutral guy when it didn't even matter?" It's just a big letdown for those who value the story as much as the gameplay. In addition, without getting too spoiler-y in this review, the two main story lines in this game were just very mediocre. They were enough to keep me engaged in my first play through, but after the game ended they just kind of made me think, "Huh... okay. I guess I'm finished now." The final confrontation was mildly engaging, but the climax of the overall story just felt like it happened long before the actual game ended. I valued the characters and the story of the first chapter much more than the ones in the second one. While this brought my experience of the game down a little bit, it wasn't nearly as much as all the bugs I encountered while I was playing.I just want to start this section by saying that in the very first mission of the game (when you're escaping the Hotel Eclair) I encountered a walker that was just slowly T-posing at me and it only got worse from there. I honestly thought the amount of glitches I encountered wouldn't be too noticeable, but they became pretty hard to ignore after the first few hours of gameplay. Some of the essential NPCs that were obviously supposed to be talking to me would turn their heads away at unrealistic angles and one kept glitching and moving through the table he was sitting on the entire time he was talking to me (again not even looking at me). Most of the time when a human NPC is decapitated, their helmet or hair stays attached to the body, but the head is gone. Several times there were buildings, walls, or objects that wouldn't render in (or would render in and out depending where you stood), creating empty spaces where you clearly see through the world and cast shadows where there were no objects to make them. Some of the new items are rendered way too big or way too small when you store them in the backpack, overlapping several of the other storage slots or making them near impossible to see or determine what they are at a glance. I've gotten stuck multiple times on curved staircases and had to use the railing to climb up (half of the time that didn't even work). I even once had to restart an entire mission that I was almost finished with because one of the essential NPCs got into a fight with a member of the Tower right before I could get to them and I couldn't pass along my item to them. For some reason, the encounter range had been moved to a point that was beyond my reach, so every time I moved towards the NPC to hand them the item the game would interpret it as me moving away and end the encounter. While I wouldn't count most of these as "game-breaking" glitches, they are very jarring and often very distracting, even blinding if a rendered object suddenly disappears and causes a sudden burst of light in a dark area. It's really a shame, because while the core gameplay and story is decent overall, the lack of polish is what's really killing the experience for me. Even in the first chapter, when this series was relatively groundbreaking for VR, I can't recall encountering many bugs at all, at least not to this level. If you want to make a good game, you have to immerse the players in the world deeply enough that they can believe that it's real. I don't mind the occasional glitch, especially when it gets a laugh out of me, but when it starts to break the immersion, that's when I start to lose interest.Overall, I don't hate this game, but I don't love it either. Probably a solid 6/10; fun enough to play through once but you might need to give it some time before you're ready to go back to it. A *LONG* time. I know I complained a lot about this game, but players new to the Saints and Sinners games will definitely get a kick out of it if they want to experience the zombie apocalypse and veteran players will probably find the new weapons, locations, and mechanics entertaining for a while. However, the number of bugs that need to be patched might deter both parties from picking it up more than once. I would recommend that all players start fresh with a new save file instead of importing one, especially if they have the Aftershocks DLC from the first chapter, as the amassed supplies collected from the import can make this one almost too easy. I probably could have exclusively used the custom Nova 1014 shotguns for the entire game without crafting any ammo for it and still have 50 rounds left over. I would also recommend getting this game when it's on sale, as $40 seems a little steep to be asking for the quality that it's currently at.

_childDocuments_.review: Retribution takes place following the conclusion of the events of the original Saints & Sinners game and the Aftershocks DLC.I highly recommend playing the first game, which is around the same price as this, before jumping into this one. This is due to the fact that outside of adding new workbenches, there is the ability to carry your game progress over from the first into this one, which allows you to crank the difficulty up a notch, if you wish.The additions are welcome, including the ability to scavenge at night for rarer materials with a blacklight, which highlight things used in crafting on the new workbenches.The story isn't exactly something to write home about, but where the game shines is in it's gameplay loop of sneaking and looting areas while avoiding or fighting the undead head on. Mechanically, this has not changed much since the first game, which is why I recommend both so you can get the full experience of getting all the gear and finding out which playstyle works for you the best.In all, this is honestly my favorite VR series to date, which is surprising considering Half Life: Alyx is in the same space and while it is gorgeous I didn't like it as much as S&S.Solid 8.5/10 from me. I wish the human AI was a bit more attentive, as they tend to ignore gunshots a bit too much, but otherwise an incredibly solid VR title.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those neutral rating games. Teetering between love and hate. Right now, I hate it. It feels like a rushed project with too many features half baked. The AI is particularly bad. NPC enemies will disengage without cause, or speak like they are attacking while staring off into the distance at idle. I understand the need for zombies to respawn to maintain a challenge and sense of threat, but this also isn't well done. 4 or 5 zombies will just stand there aimlessly bunched up like they spawned as one. Silently kill them with a bow and move a few feet, a bunch of zombies will come charging from across the map. There is no consistency, which takes away any sense of tactics, as they do not behave in a reasonably predictable way. Clear a house and go upstairs. Whoops, accidentally knocked over a bottle. 3 zombies upstairs and 3 down stairs in less than 3 seconds. I may be exaggerating. Maybe not.I just know those zombies weren't there three seconds ago when I cleared the house. Those are some fast zombies! It makes sense that making noise would draw the attention of zombies, but not manifest them from the ether. This happens far too often and in too close of a proximity. It take me out of the moment. Combat is sluggish and unreliable. I am a pretty good shot, but I often miss a walker 3 feet in front of me with multiple shots. Probably a get good situation, but I'm not that damn bad. I do like the sawed off shotgun. Biggest issue with combat feels like the contact points, as there is a good chance your basic human motion will not be executed in the game. It is satisfying when it does, however. This can lead to a bite, and the teleporting zombies grabbing you from behind even though the way was clear 3 seconds ago. So far in my journey, the game has leaned heavily on night missions. It is rather dark with local dimming enabled on the Quest Pro. This is good, if the dev team had ever used a flashlight before. The lighting from it needs a gradient between the light and the eternal void of existence.  I found a mod for this which actually improved the enjoyment of my sessions. Lots of darkness. There are some buggy textures, which often show up black, or objects stuck in the ground, etc. Conversing with NPCs can be an annoying task. Whoops, bumped my gun. NPC needs to start the conversation over. Maybe. Leave the room and reenter. Okay, can we talk now? Maybe? The amount of times I have had to restart a dialogue over the most minor of interruptions... I have also had to reload a save because the NPC decides to go bat... crazy, bouncing off the walls. I have taken to just holding my hands up in the air whenever I am talking to a npc. I may accidentally commit the greatest injustice of the zombie apocalypse by  bumping into them.The item holsters are nice and sticky, but more often than not I retrieve the wrong item than what I was reaching for. Going for the journal.. whoops, that's the flashlight. Going for my right holster... no I don't want to pick that up. Throw it away. Picked it up again. Where did my bat go? It's messy. Which gets me killed. Get good again.Going to still play it, as there are good things about the game, and I paid money for it. The world design is nice and it is a pretty game, which runs reasonably well using the Oculus Runtime. Not on OpenVR, though, which runs like trash and controls are sticky. I am not a pro gamer, but I put considerable time in the first game and have thousands of VR hours. It is just an effort of frustration that I am dealing with poorly implemented systems than the challenges of a well designed game. So, yeah, I am going to give it a thumbs down until they can improve it. Get good, developers. I joke... sort of.

As soon as i was able to buy it, i bought it, downloaded it and played it out the gate. the chainsaw is fun to use, the grenade launcher is an excellent addition, and the fact that you can complete footholds to get items you can't craft it a wonderful touch. And Holy Moly, the Atmosphere is amazing, the mood changes DRASTICALLY when you go out at Night. And that's okay, every game has bugs, ESPECIALLY on launch, it doesn't matter if it's a Triple A Dev Team or an Indie Team, games have bugs. And i have faith that they will patch and fix them, because it'd work against them NOT to do so. And i will admit, 40 bucks for the base game is abit steep and 50 for Deluxe even more so, but i believe in paying for a Developers Hard Work, and the bugs wont be there forever. All and all, i love this game, i had alot of fun and i look forward to playing it again and again, hopefully they add in The Trial Mode to this game, cause i wanna rip apart gaggles of walkers with my chainsaw. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played the first Saints and Sinners, the only thing that really makes it worth coming back for is the chainsaw. The rest of this is just recycled content that could be viewed online. You will not find yourself being chased by the Axeman like I had hoped. Welcome back to NOLA for more zombie slaughtering action! You've got new weapons, some new locations and some new characters to play about with in one of VR's finest titles.Pros:- More of the same satisfying combat from the first game, utilising the same weapon physics from the old title.- New locations, some of which lie within the city which is actually kind of interesting to explore- Brand new exciting weapons such as combat gloves, chainsaws, grenade launchers, UZIs and more!- The scavenging system from the old game makes a comeback with some new items to lootCons:- The premium package in this game is a ripoff. You're paying an extra £10 for 2 skins, a set of collectables that add nothing to the game and some shelves that ALSO add nothing to the game? Big waste of money, I regret not purchasing the default experience.- A lot of the quests are just glorified fetch quests, and characters are written just to fullfill this fetch quest loop. Even the first game had some more interesting scenarios than this...- A lot of the old game is recycled, from reused music and maps to reused enemies and locations. Some of which are entirely pointless when considering there's shortcuts to bypass them entirely.- Janky, just like the previous entry. But somehow a little bit more. I find myself constantly grabbing the wrong stuff from my body (e.g. a chainsaw instead of a ladder, or a journal instead of my gun). Zombies appear out of nowhere, usually out of view. Character facial expressions are sometimes just goofy.- The story, like the old entry, is bland. DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME IF YOU ARE LOOKING FOR STORY.- The poster boy, The Axe Man, barely shows up in the entire game. This was the biggest let down for me, as I only encountered him a handful of times, all in scripted scenarios. At least his music is good- Buggy (please note that my experience was shortly after launch. I hope that the developers have addressed some of the issues faced by the community and made it more playable for others!)Overall it's not a bad game, it's good compared to some VR titles! Just not great. As stated in the beginning, if you've played the first one, unless you are desperate for more content? It's not worth full price. Maybe wait for a sale or just skip this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the first entry in this series, this is a complete VR game, not a title with "VR support", that said, it earns at least a 5/10 from me as VR experiences are severely few and far between. However..This feels like a true continuation of the first game, coupled with what you'd expect from a full fledged expansion. There is a lot more to craft and upgrade and everything feels meaningful. I have played through the original twice, and really wish I had it installed before starting this one so I could import the consequences of my choices (few as they may be). It runs fine on a 3080, and the complaints about the changes to blood graphics seem to be completely misunderstood. This game added a visual chunk of flesh missing from walkers where you strike them that the first game didn't have, and I think that's where the confusion comes from. Human enemy AI is still bad, but the prevalence of weapons (particularly quite a few new guns) makes them much more fun to combat. The ability to scavenge at night adds a whole new depth to the game. It plays just like the first game, not sure why there are so many people insinuating that it's been dumbed down for Quest. With all of the new additions, the deeper connection between the player and the story through the Axe-man, a larger map, and just overall more of what qualities the first game had - I'd give this an 8/10 (especially compared to most of the generic cut and paste crap available for VR right now)

_childDocuments_.review: This game... is great.The walking SAS 2 takes the first game, and just makes it better in every way. This game assumes that you have played chapter 1, so it throws you right into the action. Graphically, the game looks as good or even better than the first game, especially at night. NOLA doesnt feel like an abandoned, destroyed place. its filled with plants and people everywhere, even if they arnt so nice.My main issue with the first game was the guns. the guns weighed too much, and your arms were too weak. THIS GAME FIXES THAT! When you pull up  a gun, it doesnt bob up and down like before. The zomies in this game are also a vast improvement over the first games. Stealth in this game is fantastic, even mores so at night. I never really sneaked around in the first game, but because of the difficulty in this one, I am forced too at time. It feels amazing to play.BUGS AND GLITCHESI have exprenced a few bugs here and there, but nothing game breaking. the only 2 I can recall of the top of my head aare1. when grabbing an item from one hand to another, while over your sholder, it will make the item little. this is because I assume the game registers it as you putting it in your backbag, but then your other hand. because of this it makes the item a small icon that would fit in your bax. interacting in any way fixes this (dropping the item, using item, ex.) all fix the bug. 2. A lighting error where sometimes your flashlight seems to not be able to light up anything, as if there is a black wall of smoke in the way of the light. how do you fix it? well its simple. toggle your blacklight, then toggle it back to flash light. it fixes your light by hitting one  FRAMERATEi play this game on a quest 2 airlink with my laptop. When loading into a new area, I sometimes lag down to maybe 5 fps. HOWEVER, this goes away after about 10 seconds and then the level will play out smoothly. framerate has been no isssue for me whatsoever.STORYOverall, its pretty good. I havent finished the game yet, but I am so intrested in teh axeman character. I have only seen him a few times, but he has seen me many. One of the best -arts of the game was when I was traveling through rampart at night. It was for a mission, wont say what because of spoilers. I had turned a corner into a path with the gym building at the end of it I think it was. the moon was right above the building, and you can see the figure of the axeman standing there, watching you. after only a few moments, he walked away and I havent seen him sense. This makes me wonder, how many times has he been right there, staring at me, and I missed it? he is always stalking the player, he makes that known. I cant wait to see more of that character and where it goes.OVERALLthis game is great. more action, more guns, more places to explore. so much better tahn the first game which I already loved. I went into this thinking it would be another dissapointment like BF2042, and Bonelabs. however, it has exceeded my expections and I am so excited to play more. NOLA, here I come!TLDR: game good, better than first. lag not happening, frame rate fine. me happy :)

_childDocuments_.review: First off I didn't have any of the performance issues a lot of other people seem to be having. I'm playing on an RTX 2070 Super and a Ryzen 5 5600x. Your mileage may vary.It very much feels like an extension of the first game, especially since they let you import your old save with all your gear and resources. Gameplay is familiar but still satisfying. Guns handle well and the melee weapons have a nice weight to them.I have encountered quite a few bugs though, especially enemy AI freaks out a lot and human enemies will just stand still looking at you, where walkers sometime get stuck on stupid things like chairs or cars. I also find grabbing the flashlight will grab the weapon in the left holster more times than not and that is very frustrating.Overall if you liked the first game and want more of it then I'd say this is a satisfying continuation, but a lot of the first game's issues and a host of new ones have been introduced. For now I'd only recommend buying this game if you really loved the first one, otherwise wait for a few patches.

_childDocuments_.review: After a bit more time with this game, I can say I'm pretty disappointed. It is not a "sequel" in a video game sense. It's the same engine, same mechanics, same graphics. It is more accurately described as a big DLC. It has a bunch more narrative content, some new items and weapons, but otherwise is the same same game as the first one. There are some differences, but they are not good.I chose not to carry over my game from part one because I enjoyed building up my character and items and wanted to do do it again. Well, this game makes some design choices that make that idea kind of a bad one. It is meant to be much harder, but really it's just cheaper and more annoying. First, enemies spawn much more frequently and closely than they did before. As in, they often spawn in the same room that you just cleared. Second, the scripted combat elements can be a bit ridiculous, even on the lowest difficulty setting. Third, weapons (even supposedly more durable crafted ones) are much crappier. For example, the 9mm pistol jams CONSTANTLY. Almost every other shot. As far as performance and bugs, I don't know. It seems to have gotten a bit better, but stuff they explicitly say they fixed isn't fixed. Moral of the story, this game is a mess. If you loved the first one, you'll probably buy this in spite of what I've said. If you haven't played the first one, get that one instead. It's literally the same game, but much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I consider the first game my favourite VR game of all time, so this is a pretty big let down. Sadly, this game is very buggy and almost unplayable with the constant crashes and the lack of optimisation.Let's get the main problem out of the way... this game should've been a dlc. There is not enough new content  to justify it being a standalone title. The game adds 3 new locations while reusing EVERY location from the last game. The only new content in this game are night time scavenges, a few new weapons + 2 weapon attachments, a small expansion to the graveyard safe space, 3 new locations (which feel heavily rushed / unfinished) and a new story. The night time scavenge and graveyard expansion could've 100% been a free update to the first game - while having the story, locations, weapons and such being a paid expansion. The only reason I could see them wanting to make this a new game would be for the upgrade to the games engine, however the games were made on the Unreal Engine which I know can be ported over to the updated versions (FNAF Security Breach for example was updated from Unreal 4 to Unreal 5).There are only around three new locations to scavenge in and they are severely lacking in quality when compared to the old locations from the first game. There are only a very few amount of drawers and cupboards that can be opened, for a game about scavenging for supplies, this is a pretty big let down. The locations that were ported over from the first game have not really been updated. The only thing that has changed is that 2 of the locations now have a bell that constantly goes off, making the areas inhabitable and basically not worth risking scavenging in them. Why they made these locations basically a deterrence for players while adding them in fully - big file size and all - I do not know. The Human AI in this game seems to either be broken, or just had little to no effort put into them. Enemy combatants will completely de-aggro off of you if you just simply move out of sight for a single second. This makes what is supposed to be one of the most dangerous and threatening enemy type in the game easier to deal with than the Walkers. The rest of their AI seems to have just been copy and pasted from the first game.The Walkers have had a new mechanic added to them in this game - the ability to fall off of elevated platforms. I like this change about their AI and is one of my favourite things to see happen in the game - my only wish would be for the feature to be more ragdoll physics based as opposed to the more animation based and able to happen from any ledge instead of a select placement of locations where they can fall. What I don't like however, is their new ability to phase straight through solid objects such as barricades and dumpsters. This is most prevalent on a night time mission where you return to Via Carolla. Another thing that can be kind of annoying with the Walkers is their "Instant Transmission", where they can just spawn right behind you in the span of 2-3 seconds when previously there was nothing there. A way they could make this less noticeable is by having the walkers spawn around corners where you can't see them, or just further away.While I'm not sure if this has always been a feature, Walkers now also eat the corpses of people you kill which while small, is a very nice little design detail.Scavenging at night isn't utilised in the game enough in my opinion. The only reason to do so is just for some of the new materials you need that are only available at night. Finding dead survivors and being able to take their loot isn't as rewarding as it should be with them only really having basic weapons that you could just easily craft, useless items or medicinal bandages (which are the only thing I really like that they drop). The new weapons are pretty cool. The chainsaw is fun to use, the new sawed off shotgun is also really fun to use and while I haven't had a chance to use the new smg yet - it seems like a pretty good option. There are also now weapon attachments in the game which I think is an amazing feature to have, there is a laser sight and a silencer. The laser sight is my favourite out of the two right now since I don't have to put as much effort into aiming a shot. The silencer to me seems pretty useless since I don't tend to use anything but melee weapons on the Walkers and since the enemy AI loses track of you so easily, I don't find much use for it in that regard (I tend to use the silencer just to make the gun look cooler).I haven't finished the story yet, but so far I think I'd have to say it's better than the first. There's a lot of characters with different goals, the characters aren't just on mission right offs like the first games and they seem more fleshed out. The issue I have with the characters however are their animations. The game makes their head lock onto you when speaking, which is a good thing mind you, but causes problems when they have an animation that moves their body (for example, the Pawn King opening the drawer for you causes his neck to elongate into an awkward position). The lip syncing is sometimes pretty good, but other times it is horrendously out of sync but this obviously isn't the biggest issue with the game. The game seems to use a new, or upgraded, lighting engine compared to the first game. With light rays and shadows being much more dynamic... that is if you can actually run the lighting on higher settings. The game feels extremely unpolished and unoptimized, with a lot of frame drops on some of the lower graphics. I have a 1080 TI which I feel should be strong enough to run this game pretty smoothly, but I currently have had to put lighting onto medium just to minimise these drops in frames, but even with this the game still drops frames fairly frequently. EDIT: I recently upgraded to a 4070 TI and there stills seems to be lag on high settings. This game lacks optimisation.From my time with this game, I have experienced countless bugs and crashes. Here's a list of what I can remember: -Walkers phasing through solid objects such as sandbag barricades and dumpsters -NPC's teleporting about a foot away from where they were just to immediately teleport back to where they were, then repeating the teleport every half a second. -Picked up an assault rifle just for my hand to decide to become sentient and start rapidly spinning -I lost my right arm after grabbing a drawer-Game crashed because I opened the options menu... 3 minutes into opening the game-Game crashed when I punched a Walker with the Sap Gloves... twice-Game crashed when I whacked a speaker in the hidden bar with a melee weapon... then again after going back and whacking a speaker with a gun-Game crashed when I was walking around Rampart at night... just walking -Some character + walker corpses despawn after walking a few steps away and turning back around which is kind of funny-My pistol shrunk after taking it off my hip and became non re-loadable, fixed after loading into a new areaThe devs do seem to be "listening" and asking for bugs to be reported... but end up doing nothing with this information as the game hasn't had any new patches since May 2023.In the games current state, I cannot recommend buying the game at all. The game seems to have been abandoned completely by its developers, even the review responses now seem to just be copy and paste of "Please join the discord to report problems", which is quite useless seeing as the game hasn't had an update since May 2023.
